title: Board of Veterans' Appeals (BVA) CUE Motion Pre-Filing Gate Checklist (38 U.S.C. § 7111; 38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1400–20.1411)
keyPrecedents: Disabled American Veterans v. Gober, 234 F.3d 682 (Fed. Cir. 2000)
Cook v. Principi, 318 F.3d 1334 (Fed. Cir. 2002) (en banc)
cFileTriggers: Drafting any motion to revise a final Board of Veterans' Appeals decision on the grounds of Clear and Unmistakable Error under 38 C.F.R. Part 20, Subpart O
killSwitches: 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c) ONE-SHOT BAR: Once the Board issues a final merits decision on a BVA CUE motion on a given issue, the claimant is barred FOR LIFE from filing another BVA CUE motion on that same issue!
38 C.F.R. § 20.1400(b)(1): Issue in the Board decision was appealed to and decided on the merits by a court of competent jurisdiction (CAVC / Fed. Cir.)
38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(d)-(e): Pleading Duty-to-Assist breach, inadequate reasons or bases, later medical diagnosis, weighing dispute, or later change in interpretation of law

toc.text: Gate 1: Exhaust Non-CUE Retroactive Alternatives First!
Gate 2: Jurisdictional Eligibility (38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1400, 20.1409(c))
Gate 3: Exclude the Five Categorical Non-CUE Traps (38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(d)–(e))
Gate 4: Temporal Record & Law-of-the-Era Audit
Gate 5: Strict Pleading Specificity (38 C.F.R. § 20.1404(b); *Andrews v. Nicholson*)

lines: **THE `38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c)` SINGLE-SHOT FINALITY TRAP (*Hillyard v. Shinseki*, 24 Vet. App. 343 (2011)):**

Unlike Regional Office CUE motions under `38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a)` (where distinct new CUE theories can be brought later), **`38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c)` gives a veteran ONLY ONE merits Board CUE motion per Board decision issue—forever.** If you file an incomplete or poorly researched BVA CUE motion and the Board denies it on the merits, **every stronger CUE theory you overlooked in that Board decision is permanently extinguished by res judicata!**
**NEVER file a Subpart O Board CUE motion until every box below is verified.**

blocks.text: Gate 1: Exhaust Non-CUE Retroactive Alternatives First!

Before touching `38 U.S.C. § 7111`, verify whether you can achieve the **exact same retroactive effective date** on an **open record under equipoise (`§ 5107(b)`)** without burning your one BVA CUE bullet:

items: **Are there newly associated or retrievable official Service Department Records (`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)`)?** Under *George v. Shulkin* and `§ 20.1411(b)`, a `§ 3.156(c)` reconsideration request goes to the **AOJ/RO**, overrides Board finality, allows new medical opinions, and **does not** consume `§ 20.1409(c)`!
**Is the veteran a *Nehmer* class member (`38 C.F.R. § 3.816`)?** *Nehmer* readjudication bypasses prior final Board denials of covered herbicide conditions automatically.
**Was the Board decision an unlawful rating reduction (`§§ 3.343, 3.344, 3.951, 3.957`)?** Check *Brown v. Brown* / *Kitchens* void *ab initio* challenge rules alongside CUE.

**Was the Board decision never validly mailed to the veteran or representative (`38 U.S.C. § 7104(e)`)?** Rebutting the Presumption of Regularity abates finality so the CAVC appeal window never started!

blocks.text: Gate 2: Jurisdictional Eligibility (38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1400, 20.1409(c))

items: **No Prior Merits Subpart O Decision (`§ 20.1409(c)`):** Search the entire VBMS eFolder / C-file to confirm neither the veteran (pro se!) nor a prior VSO/attorney previously had a Subpart O CUE motion **decided on the merits** as to this specific issue in this Board decision. *(Note: A prior CUE motion **dismissed without prejudice** for lack of pleading specificity under `§ 20.1404(b)` does NOT trigger the `§ 20.1409(c)` bar!)*

**Not Decided by a Court (`§ 20.1400(b)(1)`):** Confirm the specific Board issue was **not** appealed to and decided on the merits by the CAVC or Federal Circuit (including via Joint Motion for Partial Summary Affirmance, though a **Joint Motion for Remand (`JMR`)** that vacated the Board decision means that vacated decision is no longer a final decision—check the *post-remand* decision instead!).

**Correct Target Decision Identified (Subsumption Check):** Confirm whether a *later* Board decision reopened and readjudicated the exact effective-date/rating period or whether the target Board decision remains the final operative adjudication for that period.

blocks.text: Gate 3: Exclude the Five Categorical Non-CUE Traps (38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(d)–(e))
Confirm your motion does **NOT** rely on any of the five regulatory CUE exclusions:

items: **NOT a Delayed/Changed Medical Diagnosis (`§ 20.1403(d)(1)`):** A new 2026 nexus opinion or corrected diagnosis cannot prove CUE in a 1998 Board decision.
**NOT a Duty-to-Assist Failure (`§ 20.1403(d)(2)`; *Cook v. Principi*):** Do not argue the Board failed to obtain records or relied on an inadequate C&P exam.
**NOT a Weighing-of-Evidence Dispute (`§ 20.1403(d)(3)`):** If the historical record contained *conflicting* competent evidence on the disputed element, reasonable minds could differ—CUE fails.
**NOT Inadequate "Reasons or Bases" (`38 U.S.C. § 7104(d)(1)`; *Fugo*):** Failure to explain why evidence was rejected is a direct-appeal error, **never** CUE.

**NOT a Subsequent Change in Interpretation of Law (`§ 20.1403(e)`; *George v. McDonough*, 596 U.S. 740 (2022)):** Confirm the statutory/regulatory rule you invoke was settled and binding **on the date of the Board decision** (not created years later by a judicial reinterpretation or invalidated regulation).

blocks.text: Gate 4: Temporal Record & Law-of-the-Era Audit

items: **Verbatim Historical `38 C.F.R.` Pulled:** Attach or quote verbatim the **exact annual edition of `38 C.F.R.`** (checking Federal Register *effective* date vs. *publication* date in [38 C.F.R. Verbatim Snapshots & Redlines](/cfr)) in force on the day the Board Chair/VLJ signed the decision.

**Closed-Record / *Bell* Check (`July 21, 1992`):** — If the Board decision was issued **before July 21, 1992**, confirm every relied-upon document was **physically inside the C-file / before the Board** when decided (`VAOPGCPREC 12-95`; *Damrel*). — If the Board decision was issued **on or after July 21, 1992**, confirm any unassociated VA medical record preexisted the Board decision and bore a reasonably apparent relationship to the claim (*Bell v. Derwinski*).

**Manifestly Changed Payment Math (`§ 20.1403(a),(c)`):** Compute the `38 C.F.R. § 4.25` combined rating table (and `§ 4.26` bilateral factor / `SMC`) to confirm that winning this issue **actually increases the monthly dollar payment** (or unlocks SMC/TDIU/ancillary benefits) during the historical period!

blocks.text: Gate 5: Strict Pleading Specificity (38 C.F.R. § 20.1404(b); *Andrews v. Nicholson*)

Because pro-claimant sympathetic reading does **not** excuse omitting distinct CUE theories when represented by counsel (*Andrews v. Nicholson*, 421 F.3d 1278 (Fed. Cir. 2005)), confirm the motion explicitly sets forth **every viable CUE theory in one comprehensive filing**:

items: Claimant's full name, file number, and **exact date of the Board decision** (`§ 20.1404(a)`).
Exact issue(s) in the Board decision challenged (`§ 20.1404(b)`).

Clear, specific identification of **(a) the exact factual or legal error**, **(b) why the error was undebatable under extant law/record**, and **(c) persuasive reasons why the outcome would have manifestly changed** (`§ 20.1404(b)`).
Claimant's or accredited representative's signature (`§ 20.1404(c)`), filed directly with the **Board of Veterans' Appeals** (`§ 20.1404(d)`).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Safety Checklist Before Challenging an Old Board of Veterans' Appeals (BVA) Decision for CUE
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Challenging an older final Board of Veterans' Appeals (BVA) decision for Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) carries a high-stakes procedural rule that surprises many Veterans: under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c), once the Board issues a final decision on the merits of a CUE motion on a specific Board issue, no second CUE motion is allowed on that Board issue—even if an attorney later spots a much stronger legal error in the exact same Board decision. This checklist explains the five safety checks an accredited representative performs before ever filing a Board CUE motion.
record_clues: A prior final Board of Veterans' Appeals (BVA) decision in your C-file that decided the specific disability rating or service-connection issue you are questioning.

Any earlier letters or motions in your C-file mentioning 'Clear and Unmistakable Error' or 'motion for revision' (important to check whether one was already decided on the merits or dismissed without prejudice).
Historical VA Rating Code Sheets showing whether correcting the error would have changed your combined monthly compensation percentage on that date.
important_cautions: Single Merits Decision Limit (38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c)): Filing a quick, handwritten, or incomplete Board CUE motion that gets denied on the merits permanently closes future Board CUE motions on that Board decision issue (though a dismissal without prejudice for lack of specificity under § 20.1404 does not count as a merits decision).
If a federal court (such as the CAVC) already reviewed and decided that specific issue on the merits, the Board no longer has authority to revise it via CUE.
Arguments that VA failed to get records, provided a poor C&P exam, weighed conflicting medical opinions unfairly, or failed to apply a later change in law are excluded from CUE by regulation.
questions_for_representative: Can we check whether newly located service department records under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) can reopen this issue at the Regional Office (RO) without risking my one merits Board CUE opportunity?
Has any prior Board CUE motion ever been decided on the merits for this issue in my C-file, or was this Board issue ever decided on appeal by the CAVC?
Have we pulled the exact word-for-word 38 C.F.R. regulation in effect on the date of the Board decision and verified that the Combined Ratings Table math would have increased my monthly payment?

title: Historical & Modern VA Forms, Service Records & Rating Code Sheet Lexicon (1945–2026)
cFileTriggers: Decoding legacy carbon-copy Rating Code Sheets, hyphenated analogous diagnostic codes, SMC codes, or historical VA/military form numbers in a C-file
killSwitches: Auditing only claimant notification letters while failing to FOIA/Privacy Act request the internal VA Rating Code Sheets
Treating a VA Form 21-4138 or VAMC VA Form 10-7131 submitted ON OR AFTER March 24, 2015 as initiating a valid compensation claim

2. Official Military & Archival Records Triggering 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)

blocks.text: Deciphering a 50-year-old C-file requires recognizing obsolete form numbers, military archival documents, and internal VA Rating Code Sheet shorthand.

lines: **Always Obtain Every Historical Rating Code Sheet:** VA routinely mailed claimants only the cover letter (and, after 1990, the Rating Decision narrative) while keeping the internal **Rating Code Sheet** inside the C-file / VBMS eFolder. Only the Rating Code Sheet displays exact 4-digit Diagnostic Codes, effective dates, `38 C.F.R. § 4.25` combined math, `§ 4.26` bilateral factors, protection flags, `(Nehmer granted)` tags, and SMC letter/hospitalization codes!

blocks.text: 1. Evolution of Core VA Claim, Exam & Appeal Forms

rows: Classic formal application (frequently handwritten at separation). Compare **every symptom written by the veteran** against Rating Code Sheet #1—omitted lines may be unadjudicated pending claims (*Shea v. Wilkie*).
*Application for Disability Compensation and Related Compensation Benefits* (`Mandatory eff. Mar. 24, 2015`, `79 FR 57660`)

Prescribed standardized claim form post-March 24, 2015 (*Sellers v. Wilkie* requires identifying the claimed condition/symptom rather than "all benefits"). Audit every row against post-Feb. 19, 2019 AMA notices for silent omissions under *Hamill v. Collins*!
*Intent to File a Claim for Compensation and/or Pension, or Survivors Pension and/or DIC* (`Eff. Mar. 24, 2015`)

Replaced informal claims (`§ 3.155(b)`); locks in a **1-year retroactive effective-date placeholder** for the next complete formal claim (critical for PACT Act Aug. 14, 2023 ITF cutoffs, though note *Military-Veterans Advocacy* rules on concurrent Supplemental ITFs).

**Before March 24, 2015:** Operated as an **informal claim** (`former § 3.155(a)`) or **Notice of Disagreement (NOD)**! **On or after March 24, 2015:** Lay evidence only—**cannot** initiate a standalone claim or NOD!
*Veteran's Application for Increased Compensation Based on Unemployability (TDIU)*
Evidentiary development form—**NOT** required to initiate a TDIU claim! Under *Roberson* and *Rice*, TDIU is raised as part of an evaluation claim whenever record evidence shows unemployability.
*Examination for Housebound Status or Permanent Need for Regular Aid and Attendance*
Clinical trigger for statutory/factual `SMC(l)`–`SMC(o)` and `SMC(r.1)/(r.2)` (`38 U.S.C. § 1114`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.352`).
*Report of Medical Examination for Disability Evaluation* (`1940s–2000s`, pre-DBQ era)

Historical C&P exam form! Inspect **Section C / physical findings** for penetrating muscle scars, goniometer/qualitative spine findings, painful motion (`§ 4.59`), and examiner remarks on unemployability.
*Exchange of Beneficiary Information and Request for Administrative and Adjudicative Action* (`VAMC <-> RO`)

**Pre-March 24, 2015 Goldmine:** Internal VAMC-to-RO notice of hospitalization/outpatient treatment! Paired with `former 38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b)`, triggered an **automatic informal claim for increase** on already-SC conditions—and proves VA had **constructive notice of updated mailing addresses** (*Cross v. Brown*)!
Check mailing address on `21-2507` C&P scheduling slips for `§ 3.655` wrong-address no-show denials ([Playbook 02](/playbooks/02-wrong-address-defective-notice-cp-exams)).
*Appeal to Board of Veterans' Appeals (Substantive Appeal)* (`Legacy system through Feb. 18, 2019`)
Perfected a Legacy appeal after VA issued an SOC (`38 U.S.C. § 7105`). Audit VACOLS "withdrawn/closed" dismissals against timely `Form 9` filings under *Freund v. Collins* (2026)!
*AMA Supplemental Claim (`0995`), Higher-Level Review (`0996`), Board NOD (`10182`)* (`Eff. Feb. 19, 2019`)

Governed by `38 C.F.R. § 3.2500` 1-year continuous pursuit. Remember: if filing a `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)` service-record reconsideration on `20-0995`, **explicitly label it as a `§ 3.156(c)` reconsideration** so raters do not assign the `20-0995` date!

blocks.text: 2. Official Military & Archival Records Triggering 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)

items: **`AGO Form 53-55` / `NAVPERS 553` / `WD AGO Form 38`:** WWII separation and clinical physical reports (predating the 1950 `DD Form 214`).

**`DD Form 214` & `DD Form 215`:** Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty (`1950–present`) and official correction/amendment adding omitted awards (Purple Heart, CIB, CAR, Vietnam Service Medal).

**`DA Form 20` / `DA Form 2-1`:** Army *Enlisted Qualification Record* (`Vietnam/Cold War era`)—frequently proves exact unit assignments, MOS, Republic of Vietnam / Thailand / Korean DMZ dates, and combat campaigns (e.g., Tet Counteroffensive) omitted from a terse `DD-214`!

**Inpatient Clinical Packets vs. Outpatient Health Jackets:** Military hospitals filed **inpatient surgical/ward charts** separately by hospital and year at NPRC—often absent when the RO first requested STRs!

**Morning Reports, Muster Rolls, Operational Diaries, Ship Deck Logs & JSRRC / CRUR Reports:** Official unit records qualifying under `§ 3.156(c)(1)(i)` **even when they corroborate unit combat/exposure without naming the individual veteran**.
**`NA Form 13055` & Surgeon General's Office (`SGO`) Extracts:** NPRC 1973 St. Louis Fire loss certification and reconstructed hospital admission punch-card extracts (`§ 3.156(c)(1)(iii)`).

blocks.text: 3. Decoding Legacy & Modern Rating Code Sheet Shorthand

items:
**Hyphenated / Analogous Diagnostic Codes (`38 C.F.R. §§ 4.20, 4.27`):**
• Prior to modern VBMS formatting, raters typed **`7399-7346`** (or `7346-7319` / `5299-5257`). A **`xx99-xxxx`** code means an **unlisted condition rated by analogy (`§ 4.20`)** to the second 4-digit Diagnostic Code (e.g., pre-May 2024 GERD rated analogously to Hiatal Hernia `7399-7346`).
• Residual Etiology Hyphenation (`§ 4.27`): E.g., **`5317-7804`** or **`8520-5243`** denotes the etiological link + functional evaluation code.

**`SC` vs. `NSC` vs. `1151`:**
• `SC` = Service-Connected; `NSC` = Non-Service-Connected (used for pension or noted to deny linkage—audit `NSC` diagnoses on 1960s–1990s code sheets for missed `§ 3.309(a)` chronic or `§ 3.816` *Nehmer* conditions!); `38 U.S.C. § 1151` = Disability caused by VA medical care/voc rehab (paid "as if" service-connected).

**Bilateral Factor (`38 C.F.R. § 4.26`):**
• Paired service-connected disabilities affecting **both upper extremities** or **both lower extremities** combine first (`§ 4.25`), then receive **`+10%` of their combined value** before combining with non-bilateral disabilities.
• **April 16, 2023 Exclusion Rule (`88 FR 22914`, `38 C.F.R. § 4.26(d)`):** If including a bilateral disability in the bilateral factor calculation paradoxically *lowers* the rounded combined evaluation (e.g., `94.4% -> 90%` instead of `94.6% -> 95% -> 100%`), VA must **exclude** that bilateral disability from the bilateral factor and combine it separately to maximize the veteran's combined rating!

**Common SMC Code-Sheet Designators (`38 U.S.C. § 1114`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.350`):**
• **`SMC (K-1)`, `(K-2)`, `(K-3)`:** Statutory add-on (`§ 1114(k)`) for anatomical loss or **loss of use** of one creative organ, one foot, one hand, both buttocks, blindness of one eye (light perception only), or complete organic aphonia (up to 3 `K` awards stack on `0%–100%` or higher SMC subject to statutory rate caps).
• **`SMC (S-1)` (`§ 1114(s)`):** Statutory Housebound (`100%` single disability [or *Bradley* single-disability TDIU] + `>= 60%` separate combined SC disabilities) OR Housebound-in-Fact.
• **`SMC (L)` through `(O)` & Intermediate `(f)` Steps:** Aid & Attendance (`L`), anatomical/loss-of-use extremity/blindness tiers (`L½`, `M`, `M½`, `N`, `N½`, `O`). Under ***Barry v. McDonough*, 101 F.4th 1348 (Fed. Cir. 2024)**, `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(f)(3)` (half-step for separate `50%+` disability) and `§ 3.350(f)(4)` (full-step for separate `100%` disability) allow **multiple cumulative steps** up to `SMC(o)`!
• **`SMC (R-1)` / `(R-2)` / `(T)`:** Higher-level Aid & Attendance (`R-1`), skilled nursing/medical care (`R-2`), and Traumatic Brain Injury (`TBI`) Aid & Attendance (`SMC(t)`, paid at the `R-2` rate without needing `SMC(o)` prerequisites, and without needing licensed health-care professional care after *Laska v. McDonough*, `37 Vet. App. 460 (2024)`! See [Master SMC Treatise & Step Math](/docs/smc-complete-treatise-and-step-math), [Playbook 12](/playbooks/12-aid-and-attendance-smc-l-r1-r2-and-smc-t), [Playbook 13](/playbooks/13-ancillary-grants-sah-auto-clothing-dea-spina-bifida), and [`SMC & Ancillary Audit Worksheet`](/checklists/smc-and-ancillary-audit-worksheet)).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: How to Read Old VA Claim Forms, Military File Codes, and Internal Rating Code Sheets
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: When VA decided a claim decades ago, it usually mailed the Veteran only a short summary letter while filing the detailed 'Rating Code Sheet' inside the internal VA Claims File (C-file). That internal code sheet—along with older forms like VA Form 8-526, VA Form 21-4138, and hospital transfer slip VA Form 10-7131—holds the exact 4-digit Diagnostic Codes, hyphenated 'analogous' codes (such as 7399-7346), bilateral limb math, and Special Monthly Compensation (SMC) letters needed to understand how VA calculated your rating.
record_clues: Handwritten conditions listed on an original separation claim (VA Form 8-526 or 21-526) that never appeared as granted or denied on the first Rating Code Sheet.
Pre-March 24, 2015 statements (VA Form 21-4138) or VA Medical Center (VAMC) hospital notices (VA Form 10-7131) reporting worsening symptoms or an updated home address.
Hyphenated codes ending in '99' (for example, 5299-5257 or 7399-7346), which mean VA rated an unlisted condition 'by analogy' to a listed Diagnostic Code.
important_cautions: March 24, 2015 Form Cutoff: Before March 24, 2015, a written statement (VA Form 21-4138) or VA hospital admission report (former § 3.157(b)) could start an informal claim. On or after March 24, 2015, VA requires standardized forms (such as VA Form 21-526EZ or Intent to File VA Form 21-0966) to start a claim.

When submitting newly located military records under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) alongside a modern Supplemental Claim form (VA Form 20-0995), representatives explicitly note § 3.156(c) so VA evaluates the original claim date rather than only the new form date.
Summary award letters from VA.gov do not replace a full FOIA copy of your C-file when checking historical Diagnostic Codes.
questions_for_representative: Have we obtained all historical internal VA Rating Code Sheets from my C-file via a FOIA / Privacy Act request?
Did my original VA Form 8-526 / 21-526 list any symptoms or conditions that were left off the Rating Code Sheet without a decision?
What do the hyphenated Diagnostic Codes, bilateral factor entries, or SMC letter codes on my Rating Code Sheet mean?

blocks.text: Under `38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)`, the default effective date of an award of disability compensation cannot precede the date VA received the claim (or Intent to File) that resulted in the grant. When a veteran was wrongly denied or underrated decades ago and failed to timely appeal, **finality attaches** (`38 U.S.C. §§ 7104, 7105`).
Securing multi-decade retroactive compensation requires invoking a specific statutory or regulatory **exception to finality**—or proving that **finality never legally attached in the first place**.
1. Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE)

CUE is a collateral attack on an otherwise final Agency of Original Jurisdiction (RO/AOJ) or Board of Veterans' Appeals (BVA) decision. If established, the corrected decision takes effect **as if the original decision had been made properly on the date of the prior decision** (`38 U.S.C. §§ 5109A(b), 7111(b)`).
A. RO CUE vs. Board CUE (Critical Jurisdictional Split)

rows: Regional Office / AOJ (now via supplemental/motion filing to AOJ)
Directly with the Board of Veterans' Appeals
Multiple distinct CUE theories may be raised over time if not previously decided on the merits

**ONE-SHOT RULE (`38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c)`):** Once the Board issues a final decision on a CUE motion attacking a Board decision, **no further CUE motions** may ever be filed against that same Board issue!
Strict pleading requirements under `38 C.F.R. § 20.1404(b)`; dismissed without prejudice if facially non-specific, but *with* prejudice if decided on the merits
**Subsumed if BVA later decided the same issue on the merits** (`38 C.F.R. § 20.1400(b)`; *Manning v. Principi*, 16 Vet. App. 534 (2002))
Survives unless reversed/vacated by CAVC on that specific issue

lines: **Always Check Subsumption & Complete the Board Pre-Filing Gate First:** If a 1973 RO decision underrated a gunshot wound, and a 1985 BVA decision reviewed and affirmed that exact rating on the merits, the 1973 RO decision merged into the 1985 BVA decision. Attacking the 1973 RO decision via `§ 3.105(a)` is jurisdictionally dead; you must verify whether CUE existed in the 1985 BVA decision—and complete the mandatory [`Board CUE Pre-Filing Gate`](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate) before filing any `38 U.S.C. § 7111` motion!

blocks.text: B. The Strict Three-Prong Test (*Russell* & *Fugo*)
Under *Russell v. Principi*, 3 Vet. App. 310, 313–14 (1992) (en banc) and *Fugo v. Brown*, 6 Vet. App. 40, 43–44 (1993), the claimant must establish:

items: **Undebatable Factual or Legal Error:** Either the correct facts, **as they were known at the time**, were not before the adjudicator, OR the statutory/regulatory provisions **extant at the time** were incorrectly applied.

**Undebatable / Non-Judgmental Nature:** The error must be "undebatable"—reasonable minds could only conclude that the original decision was fatally flawed at the time it was rendered. Mere disagreement with how the adjudicator **weighed and evaluated** the evidence can *never* rise to CUE (`38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a)(1)(iii)`).

**Manifestly Changed Outcome:** Had the error not been made, the outcome would have **manifestly changed** at the time (i.e., resulted in service connection, a higher compensable evaluation, SMC, or an earlier effective date).

blocks.text: C. Constructive Possession (*Bell v. Derwinski* & The July 21, 1992 Cutoff)
In CUE claims, the "record at the time" normally means documents physically in the C-file before the adjudicator. However, under *Bell v. Derwinski*, 2 Vet. App. 611 (1992) and `VAOPGCPREC 12-95`:

items: **Decisions rendered ON OR AFTER July 21, 1992:** VA medical records generated by VA clinicians (e.g., VAMC treatment notes, VistA/CAPRI entries) and documents in VA's possession are **constructively part of the record** before the adjudicator—even if they were not physically associated with the paper C-file when the rating decision was signed, provided they existed prior to the decision and their relationship to the claim was reasonably apparent.

**Decisions rendered BEFORE July 21, 1992:** *Bell*'s constructive possession doctrine **does not apply retroactively** to CUE attacks on pre-July 21, 1992 RO or BVA decisions (`VAOPGCPREC 12-95`; *Damrel v. Brown*, 6 Vet. App. 242 (1994)). For pre-July 21, 1992 decisions, the document must have been **actually in the claims folder** at the time of the decision (though look immediately to `38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b)` informal-claim rules or `§ 3.156(c)` service records if the document was outside the C-file!).

blocks.text: D. Categorical CUE Bars

items: **Duty-to-Assist Failures Are NEVER CUE:** Failure to obtain medical records, schedule a C&P exam, or provide an adequate C&P opinion does not constitute CUE (*Cook v. Principi*, 318 F.3d 1334 (Fed. Cir. 2002) (en banc); *Caffrey v. Brown*, 6 Vet. App. 377 (1994)). It yields an *incomplete* record, not an *incorrect* application of law to a complete record.

**Retroactive Application of Later Judicial Interpretations:** A later court decision Changing an established VA interpretation generally cannot support CUE unless the court held that the statutory text was unambiguous from inception (*George v. McDonough*, 596 U.S. 740 (2022) — invalidation of a regulation years later does not make prior reliance on that regulation CUE).
**Benefit of the Doubt (`38 U.S.C. § 5107(b)`):** Failure to give the benefit of the doubt on equiponderant evidence is inherently a weighing error and cannot be CUE.

blocks.text: 2. Newly Associated Service Department Records (38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c))

`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)` is frequently **far more powerful than CUE** because it carries **no "undebatable" standard**, allows **full development and contemporary medical nexus opinions**, and still awards an effective date reaching back to the **original previously denied claim**.
Core Mechanics (38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)(1) & (3))

At any time after VA issues a decision on a claim, if VA receives or associates **relevant official service department records** that existed and had not been associated with the claims file when VA first decided the claim, VA **shall reconsider** the claim (`§ 3.156(c)(1)`).

items: **Effective Date Rule (`§ 3.156(c)(3)`):** An award made based *all or in part* on those newly associated records is effective on the **date entitlement arose** OR the **date VA received the previously decided claim**, whichever is **later**.
**Retroactive Ratings Schedule (`§ 3.156(c)(4)`):** Where retroactive evaluation spans multiple decades, VA conducts a staged rating analysis across the entire retroactive period!

blocks.text: Qualifying "Service Department Records"

items: Missing Service Treatment Records (STRs), inpatient clinical records (as distinct from outpatient health folders—a classic trap!), Dental records, Entrance/Separation physicals.
Unit morning reports, company rosters, ship deck logs, war diaries, after-action reports.
Joint Services Records Research Center (JSRRC) / Armed ForcesCenter for Research of Unit Records (CRUR) stressor verification reports.
DoD / military archival records (e.g., declassified chemical/radiation/herbicide exposure logs, Fort Sill or Edgewood Arsenal testing logs).
Reconstructed records following the 1973 NPRC St. Louis fire (*38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)(1)(iii)*).

blocks.text: Controlling Precedent

items: ***Vigil v. Peake*, 22 Vet. App. 63 (2008):** Clarified that the 2005 revision to `§ 3.156(c)` confirms effective-date retroactivity back to the original claim whenever the grant is based "all or in part" on the newly associated service records—even if a modern C&P nexus exam was also required to connect the service record to a current diagnosis.

***Blubaugh v. McDonald*, 773 F.3d 1310, 1314 (Fed. Cir. 2014):** Critical limitation! `§ 3.156(c)` applies **only when VA actually reconsiders** a prior denial based on newly associated records that remedy the reason for the prior denial (or bear on a contested element). Furthermore, if VA already associated and evaluated that service record in an *intermediate* reopening denied for lack of current diagnosis, `§ 3.156(c)` reconsideration is exhausted and will not carry a *later* grant back to the original claim.

***Emerson v. McDonald*, 28 Vet. App. 200, 208 (2016) & `M21-1 X.ii.2.B`:** Even if the service records were publicly available in an archive at the time of the earlier decision, what matters is when they were **associated with the veteran's VA claims file**. Crucially, *Emerson* and `M21-1` also compel `§ 3.156(c)` reconsideration of an original denial **even after VA already granted service connection on a later date via a liberalizing statute or rule** (e.g., `38 C.F.R. § 3.304(f)` PTSD stressor relaxation or the PACT Act)!

***Kisor v. Wilkie*, 969 F.3d 1333 (Fed. Cir. 2020), *reh'g en banc denied sub nom. Kisor v. McDonough*, 995 F.3d 1316 (Fed. Cir. 2021):** Defined "relevant" under `§ 3.156(c)(1)`—to be "relevant," the newly associated record must speak to a matter in dispute (i.e., relate to the basis of the prior denial rather than an uncontested fact).

blocks.text: 3. Unadjudicated & Still-Pending Claims

If a claim was legally filed (formally, informally, or reasonably raised) and **never validly adjudicated or noticed**—or if Legacy finality was abated within the 1-year appeal period—finality **never attached**. Even 40 years later, the veteran is pursuing an **open, original claim** under standard preponderance/benefit-of-the-doubt (`38 U.S.C. § 5107(b)`) rules—not CUE!
A0. Post-Decision Evidence Within 1 Year Abating Legacy Finality (38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b) — *Beraud* & *Lang*)

Under `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b)` (applicable strictly to **Legacy** claims prior to Feb. 19, 2019), new and material evidence received prior to the expiration of the **1-year appeal period** is considered as having been filed in connection with the claim that was pending at the beginning of the appeal period:

items: ***Beraud v. McDonald*, 766 F.3d 1402 (Fed. Cir. 2014):** If a claimant submitted evidence within 1 year of a Legacy RO denial and VA never issued a determination on whether that submission was new and material, **the Legacy RO decision never became final**—even if VA later granted a "reopened" claim decades afterward!

***Lang v. Wilkie*, 971 F.3d 1348 (Fed. Cir. 2020):** Combined *Beraud* with *Bell* constructive possession! If a **VAMC generated clinical treatment records** relevant to the denied/rated condition within **1 year *after*** a post-July 21, 1992 Legacy RO decision, VA constructively "received" that evidence within the 1-year appeal window under `§ 3.156(b)`. If VA never adjudicated whether those VAMC notes were new and material, **finality never attached to the Legacy rating decision**!

blocks.text: A. Defective Notice & Wrong-Address Mailings (Rebutting the Presumption of Regularity)

A rating decision or Statement of the Case (SOC) does not become final until VA mails notice to the claimant's **latest address of record** (and representative, if applicable) (`38 U.S.C. § 5104(a)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.103`). Similarly, VA cannot penalize a claimant under `38 C.F.R. § 3.655` for failing to report for a C&P exam if notice of the exam was defective.

items: **The Presumption of Regularity:** Courts presume VA properly mailed notice on the date of the letter unless the claimant produces **clear evidence** to the contrary (*Ashley v. Derwinski*, 2 Vet. App. 307 (1992); *Mindenhall v. Brown*, 7 Vet. App. 271, 274 (1994)).

**How the Presumption Is Rebutted:**
• The C-file contains **more than one address**, and VA mailed the decision or C&P scheduling notice to an outdated address after the veteran informed VA (including VAMC records under *Woods v. Gober*, 14 Vet. App. 214 (2000) and *Cross v. Brown*, 9 Vet. App. 18 (1996)) of a newer address.
• The envelope is in the C-file stamped **"Returned Undeliverable / Moved Left No Address"**, and VA failed to check other divisions/records in its possession for an updated address.
• **Representative Mailing & Systemic Irregularity (*Romero v. Tran*, 33 Vet. App. 252 (2021)):** *Romero* specifically addressed whether an SOC was mailed to a claimant's **representative** (not a wrong-address C&P exam). It held that nonreceipt **plus** clear evidence of **systemic VA mailing irregularity** (e.g., practitioner declarations, NOVA evidence, GAO reports) bursts the presumption and shifts the burden to the Secretary to prove actual mailing/receipt. *(Caution: *Marion v. Collins*, No. 24-6964 (Vet. App. Dec. 23, 2025) is a **nonprecedential single-judge memorandum decision** under CAVC Rule 30(a) holding that counsel's bare affidavit of nonreceipt of an HLR decision without systemic or C-file corroboration does not burst regularity—do not cite *Marion* as binding precedent).*

**VACOLS Systemic Sweeps (*Freund v. Collins*, No. 21-4168 (Vet. App. class certified Mar. 2026)):** Class action covering ~28,000+ legacy appeals improperly closed in VACOLS between Dec. 12, 1990 and Feb. 6, 2025 for a purportedly missing Substantive Appeal—always audit legacy appeals marked "withdrawn/closed" in VACOLS!

blocks.text: B. Pre-March 24, 2015 Informal Claims & 38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b) Hospital/Exam Reports

Prior to **March 24, 2015** (when `79 FR 57660` mandated standardized forms and created the Intent to File under `38 C.F.R. § 3.155`), **any written communication** indicating an intent to apply for benefits (`historical 38 C.F.R. § 3.155(a)`) could constitute an informal claim if it identified the benefit sought (and, for reopening/increase, if service connection was already in effect).

items: **The Golden `§ 3.157(b)` Rule (Repealed March 24, 2015, preserved for historical claims):** For any condition **already service-connected** (even at 0% noncompensable!), the **date of admission to a VA or uniformed services hospital** or the **date of an outpatient VA examination report** showing worsening **automatically operated as an informal claim for an increased rating**! If VA received or generated that VAMC treatment report in 1978 showing worsening of a 0% service-connected disability and never issued a rating decision on it, an unadjudicated increased-rating claim remained pending from 1978 (unless terminated by a subsequent formal adjudication of that exact condition).

**Reasonably Raised Claims & TDIU (*Roberson* & *Rice*):** Under *Roberson v. Principi*, 251 F.3d 1378 (Fed. Cir. 2001) and *Rice v. Shinseki*, 22 Vet. App. 447 (2009), VA must sympathetically read pro se submissions and evidence of record. Whenever a veteran seeks a higher evaluation for a service-connected disability and the record contains medical or lay evidence of **unemployability due to service-connected disabilities**, TDIU (`38 C.F.R. § 4.16`) is raised as part and parcel of the rating claim—no formal `VA Form 21-8940` is required to trigger the claim date (though VA will later request one in development).

blocks.text: C. The Implicit Denial Doctrine vs. AMA Abolition (*Hamill v. Collins*, 2026)

Historically, VA defeated decades-old pending claims using the judge-made **implicit denial doctrine** (*Deshotel v. Nicholson*, 457 F.3d 1258 (Fed. Cir. 2006); *Adams v. Shinseki*, 568 F.3d 956 (Fed. Cir. 2009)): if VA adjudicated Claim A in a decision whose surrounding context would lead a reasonable person to understand that related Claim B was also rejected (even without mentioning Claim B explicitly), Claim B was deemed "implicitly denied" and became final.

items: **Legacy Decisions (Before February 19, 2019):** *Deshotel* and *Adams* **still apply**—including to reasonably raised TDIU where a legacy decision denied a schedular rating increase (*Hampton v. McDonough*, 68 F.4th 1376 (Fed. Cir. 2023); *Steele v. Collins*, 135 F.4th 1353 (Fed. Cir. 2025), *cert. pet. pending*, `No. 25-1123`). Practitioners must analyze the timing, relatedness of conditions, and exact phrasing of the rating narrative/cover letter to prove a reasonable claimant would *not* have understood the silent decision to deny the pending claim (*Ingram v. Nicholson*, 21 Vet. App. 232 (2007); *Cogburn v. McDonald*, 809 F.3d 1232 (Fed. Cir. 2016)).

**AMA Decisions (On or After February 19, 2019) — *Hamill v. Collins*, 166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 4, 2026) (`No. 24-1543`) & *Cash v. Collins*, No. 24-1811 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 5, 2026):**
• ***Hamill*:** Landmark Federal Circuit decision holding that **the implicit denial doctrine is dead under the Appeals Modernization Act (AMA)** (arising specifically from an unaddressed AMA request to reopen a Character of Discharge determination—see [`Playbook 10: Character of Discharge, Insanity & Upgrades`](/playbooks/10-character-of-discharge-insanity-upgrades) and [`§ 3.12 COD Evolution`](/cfr/modules/character-of-discharge-3.12-evolution)). Because Congress amended `38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)` to mandate explicit identification of issues adjudicated, evidence considered, favorable findings, and reasons for denial, **VA cannot deny an AMA-governed claim by silence**. Any claimed or reasonably raised issue omitted from an AMA decision **remains legally pending and unadjudicated**! *(Note: Within 1 year of a silent AMA decision, file an HLR or Board appeal rather than a writ of mandamus—Hamill, fn. 6).*
• ***Cash*:** Under `38 U.S.C. § 7113(c)`, when a Board NOD (`VA Form 10182`) clearly identifies or incorporates probative evidence submitted during an AMA "in-between" window that is already in VA's possession, the Board must consider it without requiring physical resubmission.

blocks.text: 4. Ancillary Retroactive Vehicles
A. Mandatory Consideration of Special Monthly Compensation (SMC) & Multi-Step Bumps (*Barry*)

Under `38 U.S.C. § 1114`, entitlement to statutory SMC—such as `SMC(k)` (anatomical loss or loss of use of a creative organ, foot, hand, etc.), `SMC(l)` (Aid and Attendance), and `SMC(s)` (statutory housebound: a single 100% rating—including TDIU premised on a single disability under *Bradley v. Peake*, 22 Vet. App. 280 (2008)—plus additional independent disabilities rated at 60% or more)—**does not require a separate claim**.

items: **Mandatory Adjudication (*Akles* & *Buie*):** Under *Akles v. Derwinski*, 1 Vet. App. 118 (1991) and *Buie v. Shinseki*, 24 Vet. App. 242 (2010), VA is **obligated to adjudicate SMC whenever the medical evidence or rating percentages of record reasonably raise or establish statutory criteria**. Failure to award statutory `SMC(s)` when the combined rating code sheet itself showed a schedular `100%` + `60%` independent disabilities is a textbook, mathematical **RO CUE** (`38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a)`).

**Multi-Step Intermediate SMC Bumps (*Barry v. McDonough*, 101 F.4th 1348 (Fed. Cir. May 16, 2024)):** Overturned VA's longstanding single-step restriction on `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(f)(3)–(4)`, holding that veterans receiving base `SMC(l)–(n)` are entitled to **multiple** half-step (`§ 3.350(f)(3)`) and full-step (`§ 3.350(f)(4)`) intermediate rate increases (up to the `SMC(o)` cap) for each separate, independent `50%` or `100%` disability!

***George v. McDonough* (`38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`) CUE Caution:** Attacking a final **pre-2008** decision via CUE for failing to treat single-disability TDIU as the "total" rating under *Bradley*, or attacking a final **pre-May 2024** decision via CUE for applying a single-step cap prior to *Barry*, faces a substantial defense that *Bradley* and *Barry* changed the prevailing legal interpretation. Always look first for an **open/pending claim, `§ 3.156(b)` *Lang* non-finality, or `§ 3.156(c)` reconsideration** where *Bradley* and *Barry* apply retroactively across the entire open period without any CUE bar!

blocks.text: B. Cross-System Multiplier (Title 10 DoD, Not Title 38 VA): CRSC & *Soto v. United States* (2025)

lines: **Jurisdictional Boundary:** CRSC is military retired pay governed by **Title 10 (`10 U.S.C. § 1413a`)** and administered by the military branches/DFAS—**not** a Title 38 VA effective-date exception.

blocks.text: For military retirees (20-year or Chapter 61 medical retirees) whose retirement pay was offset by VA compensation and who qualify for CRSC under `10 U.S.C. § 1413a`:

items: Historically, the military branches capped retroactive CRSC payouts at **six years** prior to the CRSC application under the Barring Act (`31 U.S.C. § 3702(b)`).

In ***Soto v. United States*, 605 U.S. 360 (2025)** (decided June 12, 2025, 9–0), the U.S. Supreme Court held that `10 U.S.C. § 1413a` confers independent claim-settlement authority that **displaces the Barring Act's six-year statute of limitations**.

**Implementation & Forum Split:** On **August 20, 2025**, DoD issued implementation guidance directing military departments and DFAS to audit previously 6-year-capped CRSC awards; simultaneously, retirees with unpaid pre-6-year arrears exceeding **\$10,000** have pursued Tucker Act enforcement in the U.S. Court of Federal Claims (e.g., *Christopher Carey v. United States*). Screen every Chapter 61 or 20-year retiree after any retroactive VA combat-related win!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Legal Ways an Old, Unappealed VA Decision Can Still Be Reopened or Corrected
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Normally, if a VA rating decision is not appealed within one year, it becomes final—and filing a new claim years later pays benefits only from the date of the new claim. However, federal law recognizes several specific pathways that either bypass finality or show that the older claim never legally closed: (1) newly located official military or surgical records under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c), (2) older claims, VA hospital reports (before March 24, 2015), or timely Notices of Disagreement (NODs) that VA never properly finished or mailed, (3) improper reductions of long-standing ratings, and (4) Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) for undebatable errors in the law and record at the time.
record_clues: Military inpatient hospital folders from the National Personnel Records Center (NPRC), field medical cards (DD 1380), deck logs, or unit histories added to your C-file years after an earlier denial.
Envelopes in your C-file stamped 'Returned Undeliverable,' or VA Medical Center (VAMC) records showing a newer mailing address than the address VA used for a decision or C&P exam letter.

A timely pre-2019 Notice of Disagreement (NOD) in your file with no responsive Statement of the Case (SOC), or a post-February 19, 2019 Appeals Modernization Act (AMA) decision that silently skipped a claimed condition.
important_cautions: Checking non-CUE pathways (like § 3.156(c) service records or unfinished pending claims) first is often critical because those pathways allow VA to consider new medical opinions and apply the benefit-of-the-doubt rule, whereas CUE is strictly limited to the historical record.
Missing records or an inadequate C&P exam (duty-to-assist errors) cannot establish CUE, and later court reinterpretations of a rule generally cannot prove CUE in an older final decision.
Under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c), VA allows only one final merits CUE decision per prior Board of Veterans' Appeals (BVA) decision on an issue—never rush a Board CUE filing without full C-file review.
questions_for_representative: Before considering a CUE motion, could my older decision qualify for reconsideration based on newly associated military or inpatient surgical records under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)?
Does my C-file contain any unfinished pre-2015 informal claims, VA hospital reports, unissued Statements of the Case (SOCs), or returned mail envelopes?
If I am a military retiree with combat-related disabilities, should we also check Combat-Related Special Compensation (CRSC) back-pay rules with my service branch?

blocks.text: Positive statutory text stands at **Tier 1** of the Veterans Law hierarchy of authorities ([Authority Hierarchy, Temporal Versioning Policy & Citation Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)). When screening a multi-decade C-file or drafting a Clear and Unmistakable Error (`CUE`) motion under `38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a)` or `38 C.F.R. § 20.1404(b)`, practitioners routinely encounter obsolete statutory citations across **three distinct codification eras**:

items: **Era A (`March 20, 1933 – December 31, 1958`):** Executive `Veterans' Regulation Nos. 1(a)–12` promulgated under the Economy Act of 1933 (`Pub. L. 73-2`) and WWII readjustment acts (`Pub. L. 78-144`, `Pub. L. 78-346`).

**Era B (`January 1, 1959 – May 6 / August 5, 1991`):** Positive-law enactment of `Title 38, United States Code` (`Pub. L. 85-857`, `72 Stat. 1105`), employing legacy three- and four-digit section numbers (`§§ 101–5228`) cited throughout all `1959–1991` Regional Office (`RO`), Board (`BVA`), and early Court of Veterans Appeals (`COVA`) decisions.

**Era C (`May 7 / August 6, 1991 – Present`):** Modern chapter-aligned four-digit `Title 38 U.S.C.` numbering enacted via `Pub. L. 102-40` (`May 7, 1991`) and `Pub. L. 102-83` (`August 6, 1991`), augmented by the `1997 CUE Act`, `2000 VCAA`, `2008 VBIA`, `2017/2019 AMA`, and `2022 PACT Act`.

lines: **Why Exact Era Citations Matter in CUE & Pending-Claim Litigation:** Under `38 C.F.R. § 20.1404(b)`, a Board CUE motion is subject to dismissal if it fails to identify the governing statutory or regulatory provision **extant on the date of the challenged decision** ([Board of Veterans' Appeals (BVA) CUE Motion Pre-Filing Gate Checklist (38 U.S.C. § 7111; 38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1400–20.1411)](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate)). Always cite **both** the contemporaneous statutory citation and its modern bracketed equivalent—e.g., `former 38 U.S.C. § 314(s) (1976) [now 38 U.S.C. § 1114(s)]` or `Veterans' Regulation No. 1(a), Part I, par. I(a) [now 38 U.S.C. § 1110]`. Pair this statutory crosswalk with the [Master Chronological Matrix](/docs/master-chronological-matrix), [Procedural Vehicles for Piercing Finality](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality), [VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon), and the [Master Binding `VAOPGCPREC` Digest](/docs/vaopgcprec-index).

blocks.text: 1. Era A (1933–1958): Economy Act, Veterans' Regulations Nos. 1(a)–12 & WWII Readjustment Era
A. Statutory Architecture (Pub. L. 73-2 Through Pub. L. 85-56)

items: **Economy Act of March 20, 1933 (`Pub. L. 73-2`, Title I, `48 Stat. 8`):** Repealed the patchwork World War Veterans' Act of 1924 compensation tables and delegated sweeping authority to President Franklin D. Roosevelt to govern veterans' entitlement, rating schedules, effective dates, hospitalization, and definitions via numbered executive **Veterans' Regulations** (historically printed in `38 U.S.C.A. ch. 12A` prior to 1959).

**1934 & WWII Restorations (`Pub. L. 73-141`, `Pub. L. 78-144`, `Pub. L. 78-346`):**
• **Independent Offices Appropriation Act of 1934 (`Pub. L. 73-141`, `48 Stat. 509, 524`, Mar. 28, 1934):** Restored WWI presumptive service connection protections cut by the 1933 Economy Act.
• **Act of December 20, 1941 (`Pub. L. 77-361`, `55 Stat. 847`):** Enacted strong combat evidentiary relaxation rules—the statutory ancestor of modern **`38 U.S.C. § 1154(b)`**!
• **Act of July 13, 1943 (`Pub. L. 78-144`, `57 Stat. 554`):** Modernized presumption of soundness, line-of-duty, and wartime compensation standards in `Veterans' Regulation No. 1(a)` for WWII service ([1945–1961 Era Lens](/eras/1945-1961-post-wwii-korean-era)).
• **Vocational Rehabilitation Act of 1943 (`Pub. L. 78-16`, `57 Stat. 43`, Mar. 24, 1943):** Added **Part VII** to `Veterans' Regulation No. 1(a)` (ancestor of Chapter 31 VR&E).
• **Servicemen's Readjustment Act of 1944 ("G.I. Bill of Rights," `Pub. L. 78-346`, `58 Stat. 284`, June 22, 1944):** Added **Part VIII** to `Veterans' Regulation No. 1(a)` (education/training), created Boards of Review for Discharges and Dismissals (`§ 301`, ancestor of `10 U.S.C. § 1553` and `38 U.S.C. § 5303(b)`), and codified character-of-discharge bars (`§ 300`, ancestor of `38 U.S.C. § 5303(a)`).
• **Veterans' Benefits Act of 1957 (`Pub. L. 85-56`, `71 Stat. 83`, June 17, 1957, eff. Jan. 1, 1958):** Interim consolidation of compensation, pension, hospitalization, and administrative provisions immediately preceding full Title 38 positive-law codification in `Pub. L. 85-857`.

A. Positive-Law Codification (Pub. L. 85-857) & The Dec. 31, 1957 Savings Shield

On **September 2, 1958**, Congress enacted **`Pub. L. 85-857` (`72 Stat. 1105`)**, revising, codifying, and enacting all laws administered by the Veterans' Administration into positive law as **Title 38, United States Code ("Veterans' Benefits")**, **effective January 1, 1959** (`§ 2`, `72 Stat. 1262`).

items: **The `December 31, 1957` & `December 31, 1958` Statutory Savings Shields (`Pub. L. 85-56, § 2316(b)` & `Pub. L. 85-857, §§ 10–11`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.953(a)–(c)`):** Any individual receiving disability compensation on **December 31, 1957** (`§ 3.953(c)`) or receiving/entitled to Title 38 benefits on **December 31, 1958** (`§ 3.953(a)–(b)`) could **not** have that entitlement severed or terminated by reason of the 1957/1958 recodifications unless the original grant was procured by fraud, clear unmistakable error as to the laws in effect when rendered, or misrepresentation of material fact ([Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings), [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.105(d)–(i), 3.343, 3.344, 3.951, 3.953 & 3.957 (Rating Reductions, Stabilization & Statutory Protections)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.105e-3.344-3.951-3.957-reductions)).

blocks.text: B. Major Intermediate Enactments Inside Era B (1962–1988)

rows: Overhauled hospitalized incompetent veteran estate-limitation / withholding rules.
Created the **10-year service-connection protection shield** (`38 C.F.R. § 3.957`), barring severance after 10 years absent fraud or lack of qualifying military service!
Expanded `7-year` presumptive period for multiple sclerosis (`MS`).

Mandated issuance of a formal **Statement of the Case (`SOC`)** following a timely Notice of Disagreement (`NOD`). **Goldmine:** If a claimant filed a timely post-1962 NOD and VA never issued an SOC, the Legacy appeal remained **legally pending for decades** ([1962–1988 Era Lens](/eras/1962-1988-pre-vjra-closed-era))!

Standardized modern effective-date ceilings (`§ 5110(a)`), 1-year post-discharge filing (`§ 5110(b)(1)`), 1-year liberalizing law lookback (`§ 5110(g)` / `38 C.F.R. § 3.114`), and reduction effective dates (`§ 5112(b)(6)`). *(Kill-Switch: `§ 7` barred retroactive payments prior to Dec. 1, 1962 under newly liberalized provisions).*
Amended `former § 211(a)` to close the D.C. Circuit judicial-review loophole for benefits terminations; created POW statutory presumptions (`now § 1112(b)`).
Enacted the **1-year lookback for increased-rating claims** (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(b)(2)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2)`) where worsening is factually ascertainable within 1 year before claim receipt!
*Department of Veterans Affairs Act* — elevated the Veterans' Administration (`Administrator`) to a Cabinet-level Executive Department (`Secretary of Veterans Affairs`).

***Veterans' Judicial Review Act (`VJRA`)*:** Created the Article I **U.S. Court of Veterans Appeals** (`COVA`, renamed `CAVC` in `Pub. L. 105-368`, Nov. 11, 1998) and Federal Circuit review (`now § 7292`); mandated written BVA "reasons or bases" (`now § 7104(d)(1)`); repealed the `$10` attorney-fee limit after a first final BVA decision (`now § 5904`); codified equipoise (`now § 5107(b)`) alongside the temporary `1988–2000` **"well-grounded claim"** threshold (`former § 3007(a)` / `§ 5107(a)`) ([1988–2000 Era Lens](/eras/1988-2000-vjra-revolution)).

blocks.text: C. Special History: Transformation of the Judicial-Review Bar (Former 38 U.S.C. § 211(a) -> 38 U.S.C. § 511(a)–(b))

For 55 years (`1933–1988`), VA adjudicated claims in "splendid isolation" behind a sweeping statutory judicial-review bar. Practitioners researching pre-1991 federal cases or challenging extra-record agency actions must trace four statutory steps:

items: **Pre-1959 Origin (`Economy Act § 5` & `1940 Act`):** Section 5 of `Pub. L. 73-2` (`48 Stat. 9`, Mar. 20, 1933) and the Act of October 17, 1940 (`Pub. L. 76-866, § 11`, `54 Stat. 1197`) declared decisions of the Administrator on any question of law or fact concerning a claim for benefits "final and conclusive and no other official or any court of the United States shall have power or jurisdiction to review any such decisions."

**Era B Codification & 1970 Tightening (`Former 38 U.S.C. § 211(a)`):** Codified by `Pub. L. 85-857` (`72 Stat. 1114`, eff. Jan. 1, 1959) as **`38 U.S.C. § 211(a)`**, and expanded by **`Pub. L. 91-376, § 8(a)` (`84 Stat. 790`, Aug. 12, 1970)** to foreclose D.C. Circuit mandamus/APA suits challenging terminations of already-granted benefits.
• **Supreme Court Carve-Outs Before VJRA:** In ***Johnson v. Robison*, 415 U.S. 361 (1974)**, the Supreme Court held `former § 211(a)` barred review of decisions *under* a statute administered by VA, not facial **constitutional challenges** to Acts of Congress. In ***Traynor v. Turnage*, 485 U.S. 535 (1988)**, the Court held `§ 211(a)` did not bar testing whether a VA regulation violated an independent federal statute outside VA's exclusive domain (the Rehabilitation Act).

**VJRA Partial Opening (`Pub. L. 100-687, §§ 101–102`, Nov. 18, 1988):** Amended `former § 211(a)` to carve out four explicit exceptions—most crucially **(i) direct Federal Circuit APA review of VA regulations and general policy interpretations (`former § 223`, `now 38 U.S.C. § 502`)** and **(ii) exclusive judicial review of Board decisions via Chapter 72 (`COVA -> Fed. Cir. -> SCOTUS`)**.

**1991 Repeal & Enactment of `38 U.S.C. § 511(a)–(b)` (`Pub. L. 102-83, § 2(a)`, `105 Stat. 388`, Aug. 6, 1991):** Formally **repealed `former § 211(a)`** and restated the rule at **`38 U.S.C. § 511`**:
• **`§ 511(a)` (Channeling Rule):** The Secretary shall decide all questions of law and fact necessary to a decision under a law that affects the provision of benefits (`*Bates v. Nicholson*, 398 F.3d 1355 (Fed. Cir. 2005)`—broadly bringing attorney accreditation/fee disputes within BVA/CAVC appellate jurisdiction). Subject to `§ 511(b)`, the Secretary's decision is final and conclusive and may not be reviewed by any other official or federal district/regional circuit court (preserving District Court immunity against individual benefits FTCA/APA collateral suits).
• **`§ 511(b)` (Four Exclusive Statutory Exceptions):** (1) Direct Federal Circuit rulemaking/interpretive review under **`§ 502`**; (2) USGLI/NSLI insurance suits in U.S. District Court under **`§§ 1975, 1984`**; (3) Chapter 37 housing/loan suits under **`ch. 37`**; and (4) **Chapter 72 CAVC / Federal Circuit / Supreme Court appeals**.

blocks.text: 3. Era C (1991 – Present): The Two-Step 1991 Renumbering & Bidirectional Crosswalk
A. Precision Trap: Two Separate 1991 Statutes (May 7, 1991 vs. August 6, 1991)

Practitioners and even judicial opinions routinely attribute the entire 1991 Title 38 renumbering to `Pub. L. 102-83` or cite `May 7, 1991` for `Pub. L. 102-83`. Primary-source inspection of `105 Statutes at Large` reveals that Congress executed the 1991 renumbering in **two distinct Acts enacted 91 days apart**:

items: **Step 1 — `Pub. L. 102-40`, Title IV, `§ 402` (`105 Stat. 187, 238`, enacted & effective May 7, 1991):** *Department of Veterans Affairs Health-Care Personnel Act of 1991*. Section `402` renumbered **Parts IV, V, and VI** (`Chapters 51, 53, 55, 57, 59, 61, 71, 72, 73, 76, 81–85`)—converting claims (`§§ 3001–3023 -> §§ 5101–5123`), special provisions (`§§ 3101–3118 -> §§ 5301–5318`), attorneys (`§§ 3401–3405 -> §§ 5901–5905`), BVA (`§§ 4001–4009 -> §§ 7101–7109`), and COVA (`§§ 4051–4092 -> §§ 7251–7292`) on **May 7, 1991**.

**Step 2 — `Pub. L. 102-83`, `§§ 2, 4, 5` (`105 Stat. 378, 406`, enacted & effective August 6, 1991):** *Department of Veterans Affairs Codification Act*. Repealed and restated VA organizational/Secretary provisions (`Chapters 1, 3, 5, 7, 9`, moving `§ 210(c) -> § 501`, `§ 223 -> § 502`, `§ 211(a) -> § 511`), and in **`§ 5(a)` (`105 Stat. 406`)** renumbered every remaining benefit chapter in **Parts II and III** (`Chapters 11–42`, converting `§§ 301–363 -> §§ 1101–1163`, `§§ 401–423 -> §§ 1301–1323`, `§§ 501–562 -> §§ 1501–1562`, `§§ 601–664 -> §§ 1701–1764`, etc.) so that **the first two digits of every four-digit section equal its Chapter number**!

blocks.text: *(Consequently, a COVA or BVA decision issued in **June or July 1991** properly cites modern **`§ 7104` / `§ 5110`** alongside pre-August **`§ 314` / `§ 354`**!)*

blocks.text: 4. Landmark Post-1991 Statutory Additions (1997–Present)
These modern Title 38 sections **had no pre-1991 statutory section counterpart** (though several codified preexisting regulations):

rows: Enacted & eff. **Nov. 21, 1997** *(applies to decisions made **before, on, or after** Nov. 21, 1997 per `§ 1(c)`!)*

Codified `38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a)` RO CUE by statute and **overturned *Smith v. Brown*, 35 F.3d 1516 (Fed. Cir. 1994)** by creating statutory CUE review of final BVA decisions (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive, subject to `§ 20.1409(c)` one-shot res judicata and *George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)`).
Enacted & eff. **Nov. 9, 2000** *(applies to claims pending/non-final on or after Nov. 9, 2000)*

Abolished the `1988–2000` "well-grounded claim" gatekeeper; enacted statutory notice (`§ 5103(a)`) and duty to assist / C&P nexus exams (`§ 5103A(d)`). *(Kill-Switch: Duty-to-assist errors cannot constitute CUE under *Cook v. Principi*, `318 F.3d 1334 (Fed. Cir. 2002)`).*
Shifted paid attorney representation trigger forward from "first final BVA decision" to **filing of an NOD** on or after June 20, 2007.

`§ 5121A` allows an eligible survivor (`§ 5121(a)`) to **substitute into a deceased claimant's pending claim or appeal** within 1 year of death, developing new evidence rather than being frozen to the date-of-death file ([2000–2018 Era Lens](/eras/2000-2018-vcaa-legacy-modernization)).

Created 3 review lanes (`0995` Supplemental, `0996` HLR, `10182` Board) with **1-year continuous pursuit (`§ 5110(a)(2)`)**, shifted fee eligibility to **after initial AOJ decision (`§ 5904(c)(1)`)**, and mandated explicit decision notices (`§ 5104(b)` — *Hamill v. Collins*) ([2019–2026 Era Lens](/eras/2019-2026-ama-pact-modern-era)).

Extended herbicide presumption offshore to Republic of Vietnam `12-nautical-mile` territorial seas and Korean DMZ (`Sept. 1, 1967 – Aug. 31, 1971`), with retroactive effective dates back to prior post-Sept. 25, 1985 claims (`§ 1116A(c)`; `VAOPGCPREC 3-2019`).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Translating Old Law Numbers on WWII, Korea, and Vietnam VA Rating Papers (1933–Present)
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: If you read an older VA rating sheet or denial letter from the 1940s through 1991, the law section numbers look completely different from today's Veterans statutes. Congress reorganized and renumbered Veterans benefits laws in two major waves: first on January 1, 1959 (replacing presidential 'Veterans' Regulations' like Vet. Reg. No. 1(a) with Title 38 sections like § 310 and § 3010), and again in May and August 1991 (renumbering § 310 to § 1110 and § 3010 to § 5110 so the first two digits match each chapter). This guide translates those old numbers into today's sections.
record_clues: WWII or Korean War Rating Code Sheets citing 'Vet. Reg. No. 1(a), Part I' (wartime rates) or 'Part II' (peacetime rates, which historically paid 80% of wartime rates before 1973–1974).
1959–1991 VA Regional Office (RO) or Board (BVA) decisions citing former 38 U.S.C. §§ 211(a), 310, 314, 354, 355, 410, 3001, 3010, or 4004.
Decisions issued between May 7, 1991 and August 5, 1991—a 91-day window when procedural rules already used new 5000/7000 numbers while benefit sections still used old 300/400 numbers.
important_cautions: Renumbering a law section is not the same as changing what the law required: some modern rules (such as the 1988 creation of CAVC court review, the 1997 statutory Board CUE Act, the 2019 Appeals Modernization Act, and the 2022 PACT Act) did not exist in earlier eras.
Pre-1959 compensation awards that were already in place on December 31, 1957 or December 31, 1958 carry special statutory protection rules (38 C.F.R. § 3.953).
When reviewing a pre-1991 decision, an accredited representative checks both the old section number printed on the decision and whether the underlying wording was identical at that time.
questions_for_representative: What do the 'Vet. Reg. No. 1(a)' or three-digit Title 38 section numbers on my historical Rating Code Sheet correspond to in today's law?
Was the legal protection we are discussing already part of the law on the date of my older decision, or was it added by Congress in a later year?
Does my pre-1959 or long-standing rating qualify for statutory savings or 10-year / 20-year protection rules?

title: Playbook 01: Gunshot, Shrapnel & Penetrating Wounds (0% Scar vs. Muscle Group Injury)
keyPrecedents: Russell v. Principi, 3 Vet. App. 310 (1992) (en banc)
cFileTriggers: Rating code sheet showing 0% or 10% under DC 7800, 7801, 7802, 7804, or 7805 for 'GSW', 'SFW', 'MFW', 'shrapnel', 'mortar/grenade fragment', or 'punji/bayonet wound'
Purple Heart (PH) on DD-214, DA Form 1577, or casualty telegram
Operative note or separation exam mentioning 'debridement', 'through-and-through' (T&T), 'retained metallic foreign body' (MFB/SFB), 'fascia defect', 'muscle herniation', or 'adherent/depressed scar'
killSwitches: Wound was strictly superficial/subcutaneous without penetrating deep fascia or muscle belly
Combining muscle injury and joint limitation of motion for the EXACT SAME anatomical movement without meeting § 4.55(d)-(e) exception
Prior BVA merits decision evaluated the muscle code and weighed conflicting functional evidence
Quoting post-July 3, 1997 § 4.56(b) floor verbatim to attack a pre-July 3, 1997 decision via CUE
unfinalizedProposals: 90 FR 46542 (Sept. 29, 2025 proposed / unfinalized DC 7804 painful scars objective-evidence note)

toc.text: 1. C-File Red Flags (Audit Triggers)
2. Substantive Mechanics: Why Separate & Higher Ratings Were Mandatory
A. Muscle Groups (38 C.F.R. § 4.73, DC 5301–5323) & Verbatim § 4.56 Grading
B. Anti-Pyramiding & Separate Ratings (38 C.F.R. § 4.14; *Esteban v. Brown*)

blocks.text: One of the highest-yielding retroactive patterns in WWII, Korean War, Vietnam, and early Gulf/OIF/OEF C-files occurs when a combat veteran suffered a penetrating gunshot (`GSW`) or shell/grenade fragment wound (`SFW`/`MFW`) and VA assigned `0%` (or `10%`) under **skin scar codes (`DC 7800–7805`)** while completely ignoring **underlying muscle group damage (`DC 5301–5323`)** and **peripheral nerve injury (`DC 8510–8730`)**.
1. C-File Red Flags (Audit Triggers)
Scan the earliest post-discharge Rating Code Sheet and clinical records for:

items:
**Rating Code Sheet Notations:**
• `7804` / `7805` / `7801` / `7802` — `0%` or `10%` — `"Residuals, GSW right thigh"` or `"Scars, multiple fragment wounds"` (noting pre-Jan. 1, 1959 sheets cite `Vet. Reg. No. 1(a)` and `1959–Aug. 5, 1991` sheets cite `38 U.S.C. § 310` prior to `Pub. L. 85-857` / `Pub. L. 102-83` renumbering).
• Hyphenated scar codes (`7805-7804`) with zero `53xx` muscle group code anywhere on the sheet.

**Service Medical / Separation Physical Keywords (`SF 88`, `SF 600`, Field Medical Card `DD Form 1380`, Evac Hospital Summary):**
• `"T&T"` or `"through and through"` (entrance and exit wounds!).
• `"Debridement"` (surgical excision of devitalized muscle/deep tissue).
• `"Retained MFB"` / `"retained metallic fragments"` / `"shrapnel on X-ray"` inside muscle compartments.
• `"Loss of deep fascia"`, `"muscle hernia"`, `"depressed/adherent to underlying muscle"`, `"atrophy"`, `"weakness"`, or `"lowered threshold of fatigue"`.

blocks.text: 2. Substantive Mechanics: Why Separate & Higher Ratings Were Mandatory
A. Muscle Groups (38 C.F.R. § 4.73, DC 5301–5323) & Verbatim § 4.56 Grading

Always pull the exact edition of `38 C.F.R. § 4.56` in force on the rating date from [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 4.56 Muscle Injuries (Pre-July 3, 1997 vs. Current)](/cfr/38-cfr-4.56) (`62 FR 30235`, published June 3, 1997, **effective July 3, 1997**):

items: **Slight Muscle Disability (often `0%`, or `10%` in Group XIII `DC 5313` Posterior Thigh/Hamstrings):** Simple wound without debridement, no infection, clean healing, no retained intramuscular fragments, trivial functional effect.

**Moderate Muscle Disability (`10%` or `20%` depending on Muscle Group):**
• **Pre-July 3, 1997 `§ 4.56(b)`:** **Through-and-through (`T&T`) or deep penetrating wound** of relatively short track by single bullet or small shell/shrapnel fragment, *without* explosive effect of high-velocity missile, residuals of debridement, or prolonged infection, accompanied by lowered fatigue threshold or impaired tonus/power.
• **Post-July 3, 1997 `§ 4.56(b)` & `(d)(2)`:** `§ 4.56(d)(2)` carries forward the short-track `T&T` / deep penetrating wound criteria (*without* explosive effect, debridement, or prolonged infection) plus cardinal signs (`loss of power`, `weakness`, `lowered threshold of fatigue`, `fatigue-pain`, `impairment of coordination`), **AND `§ 4.56(b)` establishes an explicit floor:** *"A through-and-through injury with muscle damage shall be evaluated as no less than a moderate injury for each group of muscles damaged."*

**Moderately Severe (`20%`, `30%`, or `40%`) & Severe (`30%`, `40%`, or `50%`):**
• **Surgical debridement**, prolonged infection, sloughing of soft parts, and intermuscular scarring sit in **Moderately Severe** (`pre-1997 § 4.56(c)`; `post-1997 § 4.56(d)(3)`), while explosive high-velocity wounds, shattering/open comminuted fractures (`post-1997 § 4.56(a)`), extensive fascia/muscle substance loss, and scattered intramuscular metallic fragments sit in **Severe** (`pre-1997 § 4.56(d)`; `post-1997 § 4.56(d)(4)`).

blocks.text: B. Anti-Pyramiding & Separate Ratings (38 C.F.R. § 4.14; *Esteban v. Brown*)

Under *Esteban v. Brown*, 6 Vet. App. 259, 261–62 (1994) (construing the unambiguous plain text of `38 C.F.R. § 4.14` since 1946—making it **CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** safe without triggering *George v. McDonough*, 596 U.S. 740 (2022) / `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`), anti-pyramiding bars compensating the **exact same manifestation** twice, NOT separate manifestations of the same combat wound! A single GSW or shrapnel blast routinely supports **three independent, stackable ratings**:

items: **Cutaneous Scar (`DC 7800–7805`):** Superficial skin tenderness/pain on touch or instability (`DC 7804`), nonlinear surface area (`DC 7801/7802`), or head/face/neck disfigurement (`DC 7800`) — check the exact scar era in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 4.118 Scars & Disfigurement (DC 7800–7805, 1946–Present)](/cfr/38-cfr-4.118) (and note the Sept. 29, 2025 `90 FR 46542` `DC 7804` objective-pain proposal remains **proposed / unfinalized**).

**Muscle Group Injury (`DC 5301–5323`):** Loss of muscle power, lowered fatigue threshold, deep muscular ache on use. (Under `38 C.F.R. § 4.55(c)–(e)`, injuries to **different anatomical muscle groups** rate separately unless acting on the *same* joint in the *same* plane—and two injured muscle groups acting on the same joint combine by elevating the higher group to the next higher grade; *see also* *Tropf v. Nicholson*, 20 Vet. App. 317 (2006) and *Lyles v. Shulkin*, 29 Vet. App. 107 (2017)).
**Peripheral Nerve Injury (`DC 8510–8730`):** Numbness, paresthesia, sensory deficit, or motor denervation (`38 C.F.R. § 4.55(a)`).

blocks.text: 3. Legal Pathway Selection Decision Tree

items:
**Were the inpatient surgical / evac hospital records MISSING when VA originally rated `0%` scar?**
• **YES -> `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)` Reconsideration!** Request the inpatient clinical packet from NPRC (distinct from the outpatient STR jacket). Once associated, VA **must** reconsider the original claim, order a contemporary Muscle Injuries DBQ, and grant staged ratings back to the original claim date—**no CUE standard required**!

**Were the STRs / separation exam showing T&T wound, debridement, or muscle damage ALREADY IN THE C-FILE when the RO assigned `0%` under `DC 7804/7805`?**
• **YES (and never appealed to BVA on that issue) -> RO CUE (`38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a)`):** Argue the rater committed undebatable legal/factual error by failing to apply `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.55, 4.56, 4.73` to undisputed record facts (e.g., documented `T&T` wound through Muscle Group XIII `DC 5313` or Group XVII `DC 5317`, where a *Moderate* or *Moderately Severe* rating yielded `10%–40%`, manifestly changing the veteran's combined compensable evaluation under *Russell v. Principi*, 3 Vet. App. 310 (1992) (en banc)).

**Did the veteran get rated `0%` for the wound, and later VAMC clinic notes (pre-March 24, 2015) documented muscle weakness/retained-shrapnel flare-ups without a rating decision?**
• **YES -> Unadjudicated Informal Claim for Increase (`historical 38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b)`)!**

blocks.text: 4. Evidentiary Burden & Kill-Switches

items: **Combined-Rating Math Check ("Manifestly Changed Outcome"):** Before pleading CUE, verify the **Combined Ratings Table (`38 C.F.R. § 4.25`)** on the date of the challenged RO decision! If the veteran was `0%` overall, moving one muscle group from `0%` to `10%` manifestly changed payment. If the veteran was already `60%` (`58%` raw), adding `10%` (`58 + 4 = 62 -> 60%`) **did NOT change the monthly check** at that exact date unless it later pushed a combined threshold or `SMC(s)` over the line!

**Temporal `§ 4.56` Text Match:** Always quote the **pre-July 3, 1997** `38 C.F.R. § 4.56` text for decisions rendered before July 3, 1997 (note `62 FR 30235` was published June 3, 1997, so a June 20, 1997 decision is still governed by the pre-1997 text!), and the **post-July 3, 1997** text for later decisions. See [Muscle Injuries Historical Diff](/cfr/38-cfr-4.56#redline-diff).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Gunshot & Shrapnel Wounds Rated Only as a 0% or 10% Skin Scar
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: When a bullet or explosive fragment passes into or through the body, it can cause up to three distinct types of lasting disability: (1) a surface skin scar, (2) underlying muscle damage causing weakness or early fatigue, and (3) nerve damage causing numbness or tingling. In many older rating decisions, VA assigned only a 0% or 10% skin-scar code (Diagnostic Codes 7800–7805) without evaluating whether the wound damaged an underlying muscle group (Diagnostic Codes 5301–5323) or peripheral nerve.
record_clues: A VA Rating Code Sheet showing 0% or 10% under Diagnostic Code 7800, 7801, 7802, 7804, or 7805 for a gunshot wound (GSW) or shrapnel/fragment wound (SFW), with no 5300-series muscle code listed.
A Purple Heart on a DD-214, casualty report, or military award citation.

Service hospital, surgical, or separation exam notes mentioning 'through-and-through' (T&T), 'debridement' (surgical cleaning of damaged deep tissue), 'retained metallic fragments' on X-ray, 'fascia defect', or muscle weakness/atrophy.
important_cautions: Exact decision dates matter: VA overhauled the muscle-injury regulation (38 C.F.R. § 4.56) effective July 3, 1997 (published June 3, 1997 at 62 FR 30235), and updated skin-scar rules in 2002, 2008, and 2018. Meanwhile, a September 29, 2025 painful-scars notice (90 FR 46542) is a proposed rule only and is NOT enacted law.

If hospital surgical ward charts were missing when VA first decided the claim, requesting those official inpatient records and submitting them under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) is very different from filing a Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) motion.

Do not file a Board of Veterans' Appeals CUE motion lightly: under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c), once the Board issues a final decision on the merits of a CUE motion on a specific prior Board issue, no further CUE motions are permitted on that Board issue.
questions_for_representative: Can we request my complete VA Claims File (C-file), including every historical internal VA Rating Code Sheet, to see the exact 4-digit Diagnostic Codes assigned?
Did VA have my military inpatient surgical / evacuation hospital packet—not just my outpatient health jacket—when it issued the original scar rating (38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c))?
Based on the exact version of 38 C.F.R. § 4.56 in effect on my decision date, do my service records document muscle-group involvement or nerve symptoms separate from the surface skin scar?
Would an additional muscle or nerve rating have changed my combined monthly compensation percentage on that date under VA's Combined Ratings Table (38 C.F.R. § 4.25)?

Attacking a prior final decision via standalone CUE based solely on later judicial reinterpretations such as Burton (2011), Petitti (2015), Southall-Norman (2016), Saunders (2018), or Ingram v. Collins (2025) (barred by George v. McDonough, 596 U.S. 740 (2022) and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e))
