blocks.text: 1. Functional Loss, Painful Motion & Medication Canons (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.40, 4.45, 4.59, 4.10)

Every musculoskeletal joint evaluation rests on four interlocking regulations ([Verbatim Snapshot](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.71a-joints-arthritis-pre-and-post-2021)): **`§ 4.40` (Functional loss)**, **`§ 4.45` (The joints)**, **`§ 4.59` (Painful motion)**, and **`§ 4.10` (Functional impairment)**.
A. Functional Loss on Repetition, Flare-Ups & C&P Testing (§§ 4.40, 4.45, 4.59)

rows: Diagnostic codes predicated on limitation of motion (`DC 5201`, `5206–5207`, `5251–5252`, `5260–5261`, `5271`, `5235–5243`) are **not** capped by single-pass passive goniometer arcs: VA must evaluate **additional functional loss** caused by **weakness, fatigability, incoordination, or pain on repetitive use** and express that loss in terms of equivalent additional ROM degrees lost.

**Open-Claim / Appeal Remand Engine:** An examiner's failure to record *DeLuca* repetitive-use loss is an **inadequate-exam / duty-to-assist error**, which **cannot** constitute CUE under ***Cook v. Principi*, `318 F.3d 1334 (Fed. Cir. 2002) (en banc)`** (*unless* the C&P report already quantified the exact post-repetition/flare ROM degrees meeting a higher tier and the rater ignored them!).

Pain **alone** does not automatically equal the limitation-of-motion degrees at which pain begins! For pain during motion (e.g., knee flexion pain starting at `90°` with full movement to `130°`) to trigger a higher ROM tier (`DC 5260` `<= 45°`), the medical/lay evidence must show pain causes **functional loss equivalent to inability to perform movement beyond the compensable ROM cutoff** (e.g., pain preventing weight-bearing, squatting, or repetitive flexion past `45°`).

**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE):** Defeats naive CUE claims arguing *"pain began at `30°` flexion = automatic `20%` `DC 5260`"* where full active motion persisted without equivalent functional loss.

C&P examiners **must elicit flare-up frequency, duration, and functional impairment** from the veteran and provide a medical estimate of additional ROM loss during flares—even when the exam is **not** conducted during an active flare—unless the examiner explains why **medical knowledge as a whole** (not personal reluctance or lack of contemporaneous observation) renders any estimate speculative.
**Open-Claim Only (*Cook* CUE Bar):** Classic Board/CAVC remand hook against boilerplate *"cannot estimate flare-up loss without mere speculation because veteran not examined during flare"* DBQs.

To be adequate, a joint examination **must** (where feasible) test and record ROM across **four modalities** on **both the affected and opposite undamaged joint**: **(1) active motion**, **(2) passive motion**, **(3) weight-bearing**, and **(4) nonweight-bearing**.
**Open-Claim Only (*Cook* CUE Bar):** Never plead a *Correia* missing-modality DBQ defect as RO/Board CUE—file a Supplemental Claim, HLR, or Board/CAVC remand!

blocks.text: B. 38 C.F.R. § 4.59 Minimum Compensable Rating, *Saunders* Pain-Only SC & *Ingram* Medication Silence

`38 C.F.R. § 4.59` declares: *"It is the intention to recognize actually painful, unstable, or malaligned joints, due to healed injury, as entitled to at least the minimum compensable rating for the joint."* Five controlling precedents govern its reach:

items: **Not Limited to Arthritis (***Burton v. Shinseki*, `25 Vet. App. 1, 4–6 (2011)`**):** Although `§ 4.59` mentions arthritis in its opening sentences, its painful-motion rule applies across **all musculoskeletal joint and periarticular conditions** (sprains, strains, rotator cuff tendinopathy, meniscal tears, bursitis, surgical residuals), with or without radiographic arthritis.

**Objective Evidence of Painful Motion — No ROM Loss Required (***Petitti v. McDonald*, `27 Vet. App. 415, 424–26 (2015)`**):** `§ 4.59` does **not** require goniometer ROM loss reaching a schedular cutoff; it requires **satisfactory/objective evidence of actually painful motion** (e.g., examiner-observed grimacing, wincing, crepitus with tenderness on movement, guarding, spasm, or consistent documented painful arc), triggering at least the **minimum compensable rating** for that joint (`20%` under `DC 5201` shoulder; `10%` under hip/knee/ankle/elbow/wrist codes).

**Applies Even to Non-ROM Codes & Codes With a `0%` Tier (***Southall-Norman v. McDonald*, `28 Vet. App. 346, 351–54 (2016)`**):** `§ 4.59` is **not** restricted to range-of-motion diagnostic codes, nor is it defeated by the presence of a `0%` tier in the selected code (specifically holding `§ 4.59` applies to bilateral pes planus under **`DC 5276`**, elevating a `0%` mild flatfoot rating to the **`10%` minimum compensable tier** when objective painful motion of the foot/subtalar/tarsal joints is present!). *(Exception: If a Diagnostic Code has **no compensable tier at all**—such as `DC 5230` ring or little finger limitation of motion (`0%` max)—`§ 4.59` cannot invent a `10%` tier unless ankylosis or multi-joint arthritis applies).*

**Undiagnosed Functional Pain as a Compensable `"Disability"` (***Saunders v. Wilkie*, `886 F.3d 1356, 1361–68 (Fed. Cir. 2018)`**):** Overturning *Sanchez-Benitez v. West*, the Federal Circuit held that **pain alone—even absent a diagnosed underlying pathology—constitutes a `"disability"` for service connection under `38 U.S.C. § 1110`** whenever the pain causes functional impairment diminishing earning capacity.

**Baseline Unmedicated Joint Severity (***Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)`**):** Where a musculoskeletal Diagnostic Code does **not** explicitly factor medication into its criteria (true of virtually all joint ROM and instability codes in `§ 4.71a`), examiners and adjudicators **cannot discount the veteran's baseline joint pain, flare-up severity, or ROM loss** based on relief from prescription or over-the-counter medications (`NSAIDs`, meloxicam, celecoxib, intra-articular corticosteroid/hyaluronic-acid injections, gabapentin, or biologics).

lines: **Quarantine & Bitemporal Gate (*George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` & Rescinded `91 FR 7118`):**

* **Rescinded `§ 4.10` IFR Quarantine:** On February 17, 2026, VA promulgated an Interim Final Rule at **`91 FR 7118`** attempting to rewrite `38 C.F.R. § 4.10` to evaluate disabilities at their medicated level; **10 days later, VA formally rescinded `91 FR 7118` *ab initio* at `91 FR 9712` (Feb. 27, 2026)**. Never cite `91 FR 7118` as active law, and audit any musculoskeletal rating issued between February 17 and February 27, 2026!

* ***George* CUE Split:** Attacking a **pre-2011** non-arthritis `0%` rating via *Burton*, a **pre-2016** `DC 5276` `0%` rating via *Southall-Norman*, a **pre-2018** pain-only denial via *Saunders*, or a **pre-2025** medicated-ROM decision via *Ingram* as standalone **CUE** is **Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** (`38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`). By contrast, assigning `0%` to an **X-ray-confirmed arthritic major joint with undisputed objective painful motion** has violated plain regulatory text and ***Lichtenfels v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 484 (1991)`** for decades (**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive**)!

blocks.text: 2. Multi-Joint, Degenerative & Traumatic Arthritis + Fibromyalgia (DC 5002–5025)
A. Multi-Joint Active Inflammatory Arthritis (DC 5002) vs. Degenerative / Post-Traumatic Arthritis (DC 5003 & DC 5010)

Effective **February 7, 2021 (`85 FR 76453`)**, VA retitled `DC 5002` from *"Arthritis rheumatoid (atrophic) As an active process"* to ***"Multi-joint arthritis (except post-traumatic and gout), 2 or more joints, as an active process"*** (encompassing rheumatoid, psoriatic, reactive, enteropathic, and seronegative inflammatory polyarthropathies; `§ 3.309(a)` 1-year chronic disease).

rows: Rated **EITHER** *(whichever is higher—never combined!)*: · **1. Active Process:** · • **`100%`:** Constitutional manifestations associated with active joint involvement, **totally incapacitating**. · • **`60%`:** Less than criteria for `100%` **with weight loss and anemia** productive of severe impairment of health, OR **4 or more** incapacitating exacerbations/year. · • **`40%`:** Symptom combinations productive of **definite impairment of health** objectively supported by examination, OR **3 or more** incapacitating exacerbations/year. · • **`20%`:** **1 or 2** exacerbations/year in a well-established diagnosis. · **OR 2. Chronic Residuals:** Rate **each affected joint separately** on limitation of motion / ankylosis / `§ 4.59` painful motion (`DC 5003` post-2021 Note 1) and combine under `§ 4.25` (+ `§ 4.26` bilateral factor)!

**1. Compensable ROM or `§ 4.59` Painful Motion Present (`DC 5003` & `DC 5010`):** Rate **each affected joint separately** under its dedicated `§ 4.71a` joint code (`DC 5201`, `5252`, `5260`, `5271`, etc.)—including **`10%` (or `20%` shoulder) per joint** for objective painful motion under `§ 4.59` (*Lichtenfels v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 484, 488 (1991)`). *(Note: Effective Feb. 7, 2021 at `85 FR 76453`, `DC 5010` Post-Traumatic Arthritis directs rating directly under affected joint limitation/dislocation/instability codes combined under `§ 4.25`, decoupling `DC 5010` from `DC 5003`'s X-ray fallback below).* · **2. `DC 5003` Fallback Multi-Joint X-Ray Rule (ONLY When Affected Joints Have `0%` Noncompensable ROM AND Zero Painful Motion):** · • **`10%`:** *"X-ray findings"* *(MRI/CT accepted administratively under `M21-1`)* showing involvement of **`2 or more major joints` OR `2 or more minor joint groups`**. · • **`20%`:** Involvement of **`2 or more major joints` OR `2 or more minor joint groups`**, with **occasional incapacitating exacerbations**.

**`DC 5002` Note:** Chronic residual joint ratings and active-process ratings **cannot be combined** (`§ 4.14`)—VA must calculate both pathways and award whichever yields the higher combined evaluation! *(Systemic extra-articular manifestations—e.g., uveitis, interstitial lung disease, rheumatoid nodules, biologic skin/immunosuppression—are rated separately if non-overlapping).*

**`DC 5003` Note (1):** The `10%` and `20%` multi-joint imaging ratings are **never combined** with compensable limitation-of-motion ratings active on those same joints; they apply *only* as a fallback floor across remaining `0%` non-painful arthritic joints!

blocks.text: B. Major Joints vs. Minor Joint Groups (38 C.F.R. § 4.45(f)) & The *Lichtenfels* Asymmetry

Under **`38 C.F.R. § 4.45(f)`** ([Verbatim Snapshot](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.71a-joints-arthritis-pre-and-post-2021)), practitioners must strictly distinguish **Major Joints** from **Minor Joint Groups** when applying `DC 5003`:

items: **Six Paired Major Joints (`12` total):** **Shoulder, Elbow, Wrist, Hip, Knee, and Ankle** *(Note: Hands and Feet as a whole are NOT "major joints"—their constituent joints are minor joint groups!).*

**Minor Joint Groups:**
• Multiple involvement of **interphalangeal (`DIP`/`PIP`), metacarpophalangeal (`MCP`), and carpal** joints of the upper extremities *(each affected hand's multiple involved joints = `1` minor joint group)*.
• Multiple involvement of **interphalangeal, metatarsophalangeal (`MTP`), and tarsal** joints of the lower extremities *(each affected foot's multiple involved joints = `1` minor joint group)*.
• **Lumbosacral, sacroiliac, cervical, and dorsal (thoracic) spine** segments *(vertebrae count as minor joint groups for `DC 5003` when noncompensable under `DC 5235–5243`)*.

**The *Lichtenfels* Single-Joint vs. Multi-Joint Asymmetry (***Lichtenfels v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 484 (1991)`**):**
• **Painful Motion (`§§ 4.40 / 4.59`):** Painful motion of even **ONE single major joint** (e.g., right knee alone) earns **`10%`** (`20%` for shoulder under `DC 5201`)—and painful motion of **three** major joints (e.g., right knee, left knee, right ankle) earns **three separate `10%` ratings (`10% + 10% + 10%` + `§ 4.26` bilateral factor = `30%`)**!
• **Non-Painful X-Ray Arthritis (`DC 5003` Fallback):** Conversely, if a veteran has X-ray osteoarthritis in **four** major joints with full, **completely pain-free** motion (`0%` each), `DC 5003` awards **only ONE single combined `10%` rating** (`20%` with occasional incapacitating exacerbations)—**never** `10%` per non-painful joint!

blocks.text: C. Bone/Soft-Tissue Codes (DC 5013–5024) & Fibromyalgia (DC 5025)

items: **`DC 5013–5024` Cross-Hook (`85 FR 76453`):** Osteoporosis (`5013`), Osteomalacia (`5014`), Benign bone neoplasm (`5015`), Paget's disease / osteitis deformans (`5016`), Gout (`5017`, rated under **`DC 5002`**!), Intermittent hydrarthrosis (`5018`), Bursitis (`5019`), Synovitis (`5020`), Myositis (`5021`), Periostitis (`5022`), Heterotopic ossification / myositis ossificans (`5023`), and Tenosynovitis / tendinopathy (`5024`) are rated **as degenerative arthritis (`DC 5003`)** on limitation of motion / `§ 4.59` painful motion of affected joints.

**Fibromyalgia (`DC 5025`, enacted May 7, 1996 at `61 FR 20438`):** Requires **widespread musculoskeletal pain and tender points**, with or without associated fatigue, sleep disturbance, stiffness, paresthesias, headache, irritable bowel symptoms, depression, anxiety, or Raynaud's-like symptoms:
• **`40%`:** Constant, or nearly so, **AND refractory to therapy**.
• **`20%`:** Episodic, with exacerbations often precipitated by environmental or emotional stress or overexertion, **present more than one-third of the time**.
• **`10%`:** **That require continuous medication for control** *(Notice `DC 5025` `10%` explicitly mentions continuous medication, whereas `40%` requires refractoriness to therapy—an explicit statutory/schedular medication exception recognized in Ingram!)*.
• **Gulf War `§ 3.317` MUCMI & Anti-Pyramiding Interplay:** Fibromyalgia is one of the three named presumptive **Medically Unexplained Chronic Multisymptom Illnesses (`MUCMIs`)** for Southwest Asia / `38 U.S.C. § 1117` service ([Playbook 15](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera)). If associated IBS (`DC 7319`), migraines (`DC 8100`), or depression/anxiety (`§ 4.130`) are **NOT** used to justify the `DC 5025` fibromyalgia tier (because widespread pain/tender points alone satisfy `40%` constant/refractory), separate ratings for those comorbid conditions are permissible under `§ 4.14` (*Esteban v. Brown*, `6 Vet. App. 259 (1994)`).

blocks.text: 3. The February 7, 2021 Musculoskeletal Overhaul (85 FR 76453; Corrected 86 FR 8142)

Published **November 30, 2020 (`85 FR 76453`)** and effective **February 7, 2021**—with a critical technical correction published **February 4, 2021 (`86 FR 8142`)**—VA enacted the largest structural rewrite of `38 C.F.R. § 4.71a` since 1946 ([Verbatim Snapshot](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.71a-joints-arthritis-pre-and-post-2021)).
A. Side-by-Side Pre-Feb. 7, 2021 vs. Post-Feb. 7, 2021 Comparison Matrix

headers: Era 2: On or After February 7, 2021 (`85 FR 76453` & `86 FR 8142`)
rows: • **Temporary `100%`:** **`1 year` (`12 months`)** following implantation of prosthesis *(commencing after the initial `1-month` `§ 4.30` post-discharge total rating = **`13 months` total `100%`**)*. · • **Minimum Floor:** **`30%`** (`50%/70%/90%` Hip; `60%` Knee for chronic severe painful motion/weakness). · • **Partial Knee Replacements (*Hudgens* Window):** Covered partial/unicompartmental knee replacements **prior to July 16, 2015**!

• **Temporary `100%` Slashed:** Cut from `1 year` down to **`4 months`** following implantation of prosthesis **or joint resurfacing** *(after `1-month` `§ 4.30` grant = **`5 months` total `100%`** per Note 5!)*. · • **Minimum Floor:** **`30%` retained** for prosthetic replacement *(resurfacing is rated on ROM residuals under `5250–5255` or `5260–5262` after `4 months` without the `30%` prosthesis floor)*. · • **Note 2 (Revisions):** Revision surgery earns `4-month` `100%` only if **all original components** are replaced (partial revision uses `§ 4.30`). *(Note: Shoulder `5051`, Elbow `5052`, Wrist `5053`, and Ankle `5056` **retained `1 year` `100%`**!)*

Subjective three-tier scale for *"Recurrent subluxation or lateral instability"*: **Severe `30%`**, **Moderate `20%`**, **Slight `10%`** *(no brace or prescription device required; patellar subluxation often disputed)*.

Objective repair + prescribed device tiers + **Patellofemoral Note**: · • **`10%`:** Sprain, incomplete ligament tear, or complete tear (repaired/unrepaired/failed) with persistent instability **without** prescribed assistive device/bracing. · • **`20%`:** Sprain, incomplete tear, or repaired complete tear with persistent instability **AND** medical provider prescribes **brace AND/OR assistive device** (`cane/crutches/walker`). · • **`30%`:** Unrepaired or failed repair of complete ligament tear with persistent instability **AND** medical provider prescribes **BOTH** an assistive device **AND** bracing. · • **Patellofemoral Complex Note:** Recurrent patellar/retropatellar instability (`10%` w/ or w/o surgery; `20%` post-surgery + prescribed brace *or* cane/walker; `30%` post-surgery + prescribed brace **AND** cane/walker).
**No dedicated DC!** Rated by analogy (`§ 4.20`)—most favorably under **`DC 5276` (Flatfoot)** up to **`30%` unilateral / `50%` bilateral**, or `DC 5284` (`10/20/30%`).

Dedicated **`DC 5269`** *(initially printed as `DC 5285` in `85 FR 76453`, **formally corrected Feb. 4, 2021 at `86 FR 8142` to `DC 5269`** to prevent colliding with legacy pre-2003 `DC 5285` Vertebral Fracture!)*: · • **`10%`:** Otherwise, unilateral or bilateral. · • **`20%`:** Unilateral, **no relief from BOTH non-surgical AND surgical treatment**. · • **`30%`:** Bilateral, **no relief from BOTH non-surgical AND surgical treatment** *(Note 2: if recommended for surgery but **not a surgical candidate**, rate at `20%` or `30%`!)*. · • **`40%` (`DC 5167`):** With **actual loss of use of the foot** (+ mandatory `SMC(k)`!).
Qualitative adjectives only: **Marked `20%`**, **Moderate `10%`** (`M21-1` degree benchmarks were non-binding on BVA).

Codified explicit goniometer thresholds: · • **`20%` (Marked):** Dorsiflexion **`< 5°`** OR plantar flexion **`< 10°`**. · • **`10%` (Moderate):** Dorsiflexion **`< 15°`** OR plantar flexion **`< 30°`**.
Malunion rated on *"slight `10%` / moderate `20%` / marked `30%` knee or ankle disability"*; no explicit shin-splints text.

Malunion rated directly under **`DC 5256, 5257, 5260, or 5261` (knee)** or **`DC 5270 or 5271` (ankle)** (highest); added explicit **Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (`MTSS` / shin splints)** tiers (`0% / 10% / 20% / 30%`).
Historical `5-year` cure/discontinuance trap & qualitative active/inactive rules; `DC 5000` Note allowed discontinuing `10%` inactive rating after 5 years cure.

Retained `10/20/30/60/100%` osteomyelitis tiers (`100%` pelvis/vertebrae/major joints/constitutional; `60%` frequent constitutional episodes; `30%` involucrum/sequestrum; `20%` discharging sinus or active infection within 5 yrs; `10%` inactive following repeated episodes), modernized infectious/surgical cross-references.
`DC 5012`: `100%` active + **`1 year`** post-cessation of treatment; no `DC 5244` in Spine block.

`DC 5012` retitled *"Bones, neoplasm, malignant, primary or secondary"* (`100%` + **`1 year`** post-cessation of surgery/chemo/radiation, then residuals); added **`DC 5244` (Traumatic paralysis, complete or incomplete)** cross-referencing `DC 5109–5111` / peripheral nerves + `SMC`.

blocks.text: B. The *Hudgens v. McDonald* (823 F.3d 630) Partial Knee Replacement Timeline (Pre-July 16, 2015 vs. 80 FR 42040)

items: **Pre-July 16, 2015 Unamended `DC 5055`:** Prior to July 16, 2015, `DC 5055` covered *"Knee replacement (prosthesis)"* without specifying `"total"` vs. `"partial"`. In ***Hudgens v. McDonald*, `823 F.3d 630, 637–39 (Fed. Cir. 2016)`**, the Federal Circuit held that the unamended regulation did **not** unambiguously exclude **partial / unicompartmental knee arthroplasties** (and `11` of `14` Board decisions had granted `DC 5055` to partial replacements), resolving interpretive doubt in the veteran's favor!

**July 16, 2015 Interpretive/Final Rule (`80 FR 42040`):** On **July 16, 2015** (`80 FR 42040`, effective and applicable to claims filed on or after July 16, 2015), VA added an explanatory Note to `DC 5051–5056` stating `"prosthetic replacement"` means a **total** replacement of the named joint (*except* `DC 5054` hip, which covers total replacement of the femoral head *or* acetabulum), later reinforced in `85 FR 76453` (Note 3).

**Practitioner Audit Rule:** For any claim or continuous appeal **pending prior to July 16, 2015**, a partial/unicompartmental knee replacement qualifies for the **`1-year` (`13-month`) `100%` rating AND the permanent `30%` minimum floor** under *Hudgens*! For partial replacements performed under claims filed **on or after July 16, 2015**, claim **`38 C.F.R. § 4.30`** (`1` to `3+` months temporary `100%` surgical convalescence) followed by stacked knee residual codes (`DC 5257 + 5260 + 5261`). *(Note: Under George v. McDonough, attacking a final pre-2016 RO/Board denial of DC 5055 for a partial knee replacement via standalone CUE is barred by `§ 20.1403(e)`).*

blocks.text: 4. Upper Extremity Schedule (DC 5200–5230) & 38 C.F.R. § 4.69 Hand Dominance
A. Shoulder & Arm (DC 5200–5203): The 20% Minimum Floor & *Mariano* / *Cullen* Rules

rows: **Arm, limitation of motion of** *(Flexion and/or Abduction — Normal = `180°` per `§ 4.71` Plate I)*
• To **`25°`** from side: **`40%`** · • Midway between side & shoulder level (**`45°`**): **`30%`** · • **At shoulder level (`90°`):** **`20%`**

**THREE MASSIVE AUDIT RULES:** · 1. **Minimum Compensable Rating = `20%` (Both Major & Minor!):** There is **NO `10%` tier** under `DC 5201`! Therefore, under `38 C.F.R. § 4.59` (*Petitti*, `27 Vet. App. at 425`), **objective painful motion of either shoulder triggers a `20%` minimum rating—NEVER `10%`**! Assigning `0%` or `10%` for a painful shoulder rated under `DC 5201` (or `5003-5201`) is a textbook **RO CUE**! · 2. **Disjunctive Flexion OR Abduction (***Mariano v. Principi*, `17 Vet. App. 305, 313–17 (2003)`**):** Restriction to `<= 90°` in **either** forward flexion **or** abduction satisfies `DC 5201` (`85 FR 76453` codified explicit `25° / 45° / 90°` flexion/abduction parentheticals; *Mariano* also bars VA from ordering a second C&P exam solely to develop negative evidence against an adequate favorable exam!). · 3. **Single-Code Anti-Stacking Bar (***Cullen v. Shinseki*, `24 Vet. App. 74, 81–85 (2010)`**):** A veteran **cannot** receive two separate `DC 5201` ratings on the *same* shoulder (one for flexion + one for abduction).
• Dislocation / Nonunion w/ loose movement: **`20%`** · • Nonunion w/o loose movement / Malunion: **`10%`**
• Dislocation / Nonunion w/ loose movement: **`20%`** · • Nonunion w/o loose movement / Malunion: **`10%`**
Rate alternatively on impairment of contiguous shoulder joint (`DC 5201`) when higher (`20%+`).

blocks.text: B. Elbow & Forearm Multi-Plane Stacking (DC 5205–5213)

Unlike the shoulder (`DC 5201`), the elbow/forearm has **three separate movement-plane Diagnostic Codes** (`Normal` = `0°` extension to `145°` flexion; `85°` supination / `80°` pronation per `§ 4.71` Plate I):

items: **`DC 5207` (Forearm, limitation of extension):** Extension limited to `110°` (`50% / 40%`) \| `100°` (`40% / 30%`) \| `90°` (`30% / 20%`) \| `75°` (`20% / 20%`) \| `60°` (`10% / 10%`) \| `45°` (`10% / 10%`). *(Note **`DC 5208`**: Flexion limited to `100°` **and** extension to `45°` = **`20% / 20%`**, beating `10% + 10% = 19%` when no bilateral factor applies, though separate `10% + 10%` may combine favorably with `§ 4.26`—assign whichever is higher!)*

**`DC 5213` (Supination and pronation, impairment of):** Bone fusion/synostosis (`40% / 30%` unfavorable; `30% / 20%` favorable); pronation lost beyond middle of arc (`30% / 20%`) or beyond last quarter (`20% / 20%`); supination to `30°` or less (`10% / 10%`).

**Triple-Plane Elbow Stacking Rule (`§ 4.14` / *Esteban* / *Brady*):** Separate ratings under **`DC 5206` (flexion) + `DC 5207` (extension) + `DC 5213` (supination/pronation)** are permissible on the **same arm** whenever goniometer findings establish distinct limitations in each anatomical plane (mirroring `VAOPGCPREC 9-2004`; however, `§ 4.59` painful motion **cannot** be used twice to award `10% + 10%` where goniometer motion is noncompensable in both planes—that double-counts the same joint pain under *Brady v. Brown*, `4 Vet. App. 203 (1993)`!).

blocks.text: C. Wrist, Hand & Digits (DC 5214–5230, §§ 4.63–4.71) & 38 C.F.R. § 4.69 Hand Dominance Traps

items: **Wrist (`DC 5214–5215`):** `DC 5214` Ankylosis (`50%/40%` unfavorable, `40%/30%` intermediate, `30%/20%` favorable); **`DC 5215` Limitation of motion** (`10%` Maj / `10%` Min for dorsiflexion `< 15°`, palmar flexion limited in line with forearm, OR objective painful motion under `§ 4.59`).

**Digits (`DC 5216–5230`):** Evaluated across multi-digit ankylosis (`DC 5216–5223`), single-digit ankylosis (`DC 5224` Thumb `20%/20%` or `10%/10%`; `DC 5225` Index `10%/10%`; `DC 5226` Long `10%/10%`; `DC 5227` Ring or Little `0%/0%`), and single-digit limitation of motion (`DC 5228` Thumb opposition gap > `2` inches = `20%/20%`, `1–2` inches = `10%/10%`; `DC 5229` Index/Long `>1` inch fingertip-to-transverse-crease gap or `>30°` extension loss = `10%/10%`; `DC 5230` Ring/Little = `0%/0%`). Under `85 FR 76453`, multi-digit combinations impairing thumb-to-finger opposition/grasp convert directly under `DC 5216–5223` Notes (and complete loss of effective grasping/pinching triggers **`70%/60%` Hand Loss of Use (`DC 5125`) + `SMC(k)`** under `38 C.F.R. § 4.63`!).

**`38 C.F.R. § 4.69` Dominant-Hand (`Major` vs. `Minor`) Audit Rules (`62 FR 30235`, eff. July 3, 1997):**
• **Single Dominant Hand Mandate:** *"Only one hand shall be considered dominant."* Assigning `Minor` percentages to a veteran's documented dominant arm on `DC 5121–5125`, `5200`, `5201` (`25°/45°`), `5202`, `5205–5207`, `5213–5214`, `5301–5309`, or `8510–8519` is an **undebatable RO/Board CUE** (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive).
• **The Post-Injury / Post-Amputation "Dominance Flip" Trap:** When a naturally right-handed veteran suffers a devastating injury, nerve palsy, or amputation of the right hand/arm and adapts over years to write and eat with the left hand, C&P examiners frequently check *"Left-handed"* on modern DBQs—causing raters to **unlawfully downgrade the injured/amputated originally dominant right arm to `Minor`!** Handedness for the primary injured limb is governed by **pre-injury natural dominance** evidenced in entrance/service records (`DD 2808` / `SF 88`), NOT forced post-injury compensatory adaptation! *(And if the opposite minor hand breaks down from compensatory overuse, claim it as secondary under `§ 3.310(a)`!).*
• **Ambidextrous Reversal Rule:** Conversely, when evidence or VA testing establishes genuine **ambidexterity**, `§ 4.69` explicitly mandates: *"The injured hand, or **the most severely injured hand**, of an ambidextrous individual will be considered the dominant hand for rating purposes"*—meaning if the opposite hand later becomes more severely disabled, `Major` designation shifts to whichever hand yields the higher combined schedule!

blocks.text: 5. Lower Extremity — Hip (DC 5250–5255), Knee Multi-Code Stacking (DC 5256–5263) & Ankle/Foot (DC 5269–5284)
A. Hip & Thigh Triple-Plane Stacking (DC 5250–5255)

Like the elbow, the hip joint separates movement across **three independent anatomical planes** (`Normal` = `125°` flexion, `30°`/`0°` extension, `45°` abduction, `25°` adduction, `40°` external/`60°` internal rotation per `§ 4.71` Plate II):

items: **`DC 5251` (Thigh, limitation of extension):** Extension limited to `5°` = **`10%`**.

**`DC 5253` (Thigh, impairment of — abduction, adduction & rotation):** Loss of abduction beyond `10°` = **`20%`**; cannot cross legs (adduction) **or** cannot toe-out more than `15°` (rotation), affected leg = **`10%`**.

**Triple-Plane Hip Stacking Rule:** Under `§ 4.14` (*Esteban*) and `M21-1` V.iii.1.B, a veteran with goniometer-confirmed loss in multiple planes can receive **up to THREE concurrent ratings on a single hip (`DC 5251` `10%` + `DC 5252` `10–40%` + `DC 5253` `10–20%`)**! *(Again, `§ 4.59` painful motion without schedular ROM loss yields a single `10%` hip rating, not `10% x 3`).* Also check **`DC 5255` (Femur, impairment of)**: fracture nonunion w/ loose motion (`60%` / `40%` w/ brace), or malunion with marked knee/hip disability (`30%`), moderate (`20%`), slight (`10%`).

blocks.text: B. The Knee Multi-Stacking Goldmine (DC 5257 + 5260 + 5261 + 5258/5259)
No joint in the VASRD produces more under-rated code sheets—or cleaner CUEs—than the knee (`DC 5256–5263`):

headers: Binding Legal Rule & Concurrent Knee Stacking Permissibility
rows: Assigning a rating for knee instability (**`DC 5257`**) **AND** a separate rating for degenerative arthritis (`DC 5003`) or limitation of motion (**`DC 5260` / `DC 5261`**) on the **same knee** **does NOT violate `38 C.F.R. § 4.14`**, because instability and motion loss are distinct functional impairments.
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= July 1, 1997`):** Subsuming compensable ROM/arthritis into `DC 5257` (or vice versa) on undisputed C&P findings is textbook RO/Board CUE (`38 U.S.C. § 7104(c)`).

Clarifies `23-97`: alongside `DC 5257` instability, a separate `DC 5260`/`5261` rating is warranted whenever the veteran meets a compensable ROM tier (`DC 5260` flexion `<= 45°` = `10%`, `<= 30°` = `20%`, `<= 15°` = `30%`; `DC 5261` extension lag `>= 10°` = `10%`, `>= 15°` = `20%`, `>= 20°` = `30%`, `>= 30°` = `40%`, `>= 45°` = `50%`) **OR** has objective **painful motion under `§ 4.59`** (`10%`)!
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Aug. 14, 1998`):** Look at **`DC 5261` (extension lag)**: missing just `15°` of full straightening pays **`20%`**, and `20°` lag pays **`30%`**!
A veteran **may receive separate concurrent ratings under BOTH `DC 5260` (flexion) AND `DC 5261` (extension) for the EXACT SAME KNEE** when both flexion and extension meet compensable criteria!

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Sept. 17, 2004`):** Unlocks **triple-stacking (`DC 5257 + 5260 + 5261`)** on a single knee! *(Caution: Do not award `10%` `5260` + `10%` `5261` via `§ 4.59` painful motion alone if goniometer ROM is noncompensable in one or both directions).*

**Four-Code Unbundling + Post-TKR Stacking:** · 1. Meniscal codes **`DC 5258`** (`20%` dislocated semilunar cartilage with frequent episodes of `"locking,"` pain, AND joint effusion) and **`DC 5259`** (`10%` symptomatic cartilage removal) **do NOT categorically bar concurrent `DC 5257`, `5260`, or `5261` ratings**—provided the ratings do not compensate the exact same manifestation (`§ 4.14`, e.g., locking/effusion under `5258` vs. extension lag under `5261`, whereas `5259` painful motion overlaps `5260` painful motion). · 2. Even a **`DC 5055` Total Knee Replacement (`30%`/`60%`)** does **NOT** categorically bar a separate **`DC 5257` lateral instability** rating if instability is not already compensated under `DC 5055`'s chronic residuals!

**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** against pre-2017 final decisions rejecting `5258/5259` or `5055 + 5257` stacking on categorical grounds; **mandatory remand/increase weapon** on all open claims and AMA appeals!

Under **`DC 5257`**, knee instability (giving way / buckling / subluxation) is an **observable symptom that a layperson is fully competent to report**; the Board **cannot** categorically require positive objective Lachman, anterior/posterior drawer, or pivot-shift C&P testing to defeat credible lay reports of instability!

**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** on CUE; pairs powerfully with post-Feb. 7, 2021 `DC 5257` (where physician-prescribed bracing/cane + credible instability proves `20%` or `30%` despite a negative in-office drawer test).

blocks.text: C. Ankle (DC 5270–5274) & Foot Architecture (DC 5269, 5276–5284)

items: **Ankle (`DC 5270–5274`):** `DC 5270` Ankylosis (`40%` plantar flexion `> 40°` or dorsiflexion `> 10°` w/ deformity; `30%` `30°–40°`; `20%` `< 30°`); **`DC 5271` Limited motion** (`20%` Marked / `10%` Moderate—with explicit `< 5°` / `< 10°` and `< 15°` / `< 30°` cutoffs added **Feb. 7, 2021** at `85 FR 76453`); `DC 5272` Subastragalar/tarsal ankylosis (`20%`/`10%`); `DC 5273` Os calcis/astragalus malunion (`20%`/`10%`); `DC 5274` Astragalectomy (`20%`).

**Foot Schedule (`DC 5269, 5276–5284`) & The `§ 4.26` Bilateral Factor Trap:**
• **`DC 5276` (Flatfoot / Pes Planus, acquired):**
• **Pronounced** *(marked pronation, extreme tenderness of plantar surfaces, marked inward displacement/spasm of Achilles tendon, **not improved by orthopedic shoes or appliances**)*: **`50%` Bilateral** \| **`30%` Unilateral**.
• **Severe** *(objective evidence of marked deformity—pain on manipulation/use accentuated, indication of swelling on use, characteristic callosities)*: **`30%` Bilateral** \| **`20%` Unilateral**.
• **Moderate** *(weight-bearing line over/medial to great toe, inward bowing of Achilles, pain on manipulation/use)*: **`10%` Bilateral or Unilateral**.
• **Mild** *(symptoms relieved by built-up shoe or arch support)*: **`0%`** *(elevated to **`10%`** under `§ 4.59` if objective painful motion exists per Southall-Norman, `28 Vet. App. at 352`!)*.
• **CRITICAL `§ 4.26` Bilateral Factor Trap on Foot Codes:**
• **Single Bilateral-Tier Code (`DC 5276`, `DC 5278` Claw Foot `50%/30%`, `DC 5269` Plantar Fasciitis `30%/20%`, `DC 5279` Metatarsalgia `10%`):** When rated as a **single bilateral evaluation** with *no other* compensable lower-extremity SC disability, VA does **NOT** add a standalone `+10%` `§ 4.26` bilateral bonus onto that single number (because bilateral involvement is already built into `50%` vs. `30%`). **HOWEVER**, if the veteran holds **any separate compensable SC disability on either lower extremity** (e.g., `10%` right knee `DC 5260`), the `50%` bilateral `DC 5276` rating **DOES enter the `§ 4.26` bilateral-factor pool** (`50%` + `10%` = `55%` + `5.5%` bilateral bonus = `60.5% -> 60%`)!
• **Two Separate Unilateral Foot Ratings (`DC 5284` Foot Injuries, Other: `30%` Severe, `20%` Moderately Severe, `10%` Moderate; `DC 5283` Tarsal/Metatarsal Malunion; `DC 5280` Hallux Valgus `10%`; `DC 5281` Hallux Rigidus `10%`):** Because `DC 5284` has **no** built-in bilateral tier, bilateral foot injuries rated as **`DC 5284` Right (`30%`) + `DC 5284` Left (`30%`)** **AUTOMATICALLY trigger the `+10%` `§ 4.26` bilateral factor** (`30% + 30% = 51% + 5.1% = 56.1% -> 60%`!)—frequently **beating** a `30%` bilateral `DC 5269` plantar fasciitis rating!
• **Multi-Code Foot Stacking (`38 C.F.R. § 4.14`; *Esteban v. Brown*, `6 Vet. App. 259, 261–62 (1994)`):** A veteran with pes planus (`DC 5276`) **and** distinct non-overlapping foot pathologies—such as hallux valgus (`DC 5280`), hammer toes (`DC 5282`), Morton's metatarsalgia (`DC 5279`), tarsal malunion (`DC 5283`), or Achilles/ankle limitation (`DC 5271`)—is entitled to **separate ratings** so long as the exact same symptom (e.g., plantar tenderness) is not compensated twice (`§ 4.14`; note `DC 5281` Note explicitly bars combining hallux rigidus with `DC 5278` claw foot), capped per foot/below-knee at **`40%`** under `38 C.F.R. § 4.68`! *(Where pain on prolonged standing is uncompensated by `DC 5276`'s manipulation/use criteria, also evaluate `§ 3.321(b)(1)` extraschedular referral per **Yancy v. McDonald**, `27 Vet. App. 484, 490–96 (2016)`).*
• **Pre- vs. Post-Feb. 7, 2021 Plantar Fasciitis (`DC 5269`):** Under `DC 5269` (`86 FR 8142`), a veteran whose bilateral plantar fasciitis was **never recommended for surgery** caps out at **`10%`** (even if orthotics/injections fail!), whereas pre-Feb. 7, 2021 analogous rating under `DC 5276` allowed **`30%` or `50%` bilateral** without surgery! Always audit pre-Feb. 7, 2021 pending claims for protected higher `5299-5276` evaluations, and for post-2021 claims check **Note (2)** (*recommended for surgery, but medically not a surgical candidate -> `20%/30%`*) or **`40%` actual Loss of Use of the foot + `SMC(k)`**!

blocks.text: B. Mechanics & Exceptions of the 38 C.F.R. § 4.68 Amputation Rule Ceiling
`38 C.F.R. § 4.68` (*Amputation rule*, [Verbatim Snapshot](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.71a-joints-arthritis-pre-and-post-2021)) mandates:

lines: *"The combined rating for disabilities of an extremity shall not exceed the rating for the amputation at the elective level, were amputation to be performed. For example, the combined evaluations for disabilities below the knee shall not exceed the **40 percent** evaluation, diagnostic code **5165**. This 40 percent rating may be further combined with evaluation for disabilities above the knee but not to exceed the above the knee amputation elective level."*

items:
**How the Stepwise Distal-to-Proximal Cap Works:**
• **Below-the-Knee Cap (`40%` under `DC 5165`):** If a veteran has multiple SC disabilities strictly **below the right knee**—e.g., `DC 5271` ankle (`20%`) + `DC 5276` unilateral pes planus (`30%`) + `DC 8521` common peroneal nerve (`20%`)—their raw combination (`55% -> 60%`) is **capped at `40%`** (`DC 5165` below-knee amputation elective level; *unless* knee-action control is lost per `DC 5164` = `60%`).
• **Combining Below-Knee (`40%`) With Knee / Thigh Disabilities (`60% / 80% / 90%` Cap):** That capped `40%` below-knee block **then combines** with SC disabilities at or above the knee on the same leg—e.g., `DC 5257` knee instability (`20%`) + `DC 5261` extension (`30%`) + `DC 8520` sciatic nerve (`40%`)—up to the applicable above-knee elective amputation ceiling (`60%` middle/lower thigh `DC 5162`, `80%` upper third `DC 5161`, or `90%` hip disarticulation `DC 5160`). *(Painful stump neuroma after amputation receives the rating for the **elective site of reamputation** under `§ 4.68`, plus `§ 4.67` pelvic-girdle rules).*

**CRITICAL EXCEPTIONS THAT PIERCE OR SIT OUTSIDE `§ 4.68` (High-Value CUE / Audit Goldmines):**
• **Proximal Spine & Trunk Disabilities Are NEVER Capped by `§ 4.68`:** Thoracolumbar/cervical spine ratings (`DC 5235–5243`), pelvic fractures (`DC 5236`), and gluteal/pelvic girdle muscles (`DC 5317`) are **not** distal extremity disabilities and combine freely on top of the `§ 4.68` extremity cap!
• **Skin/Scars (`DC 7800–7805`) & Vascular Systemic Sequelae:** Painful/unstable superficial scars (`DC 7804`) or deep soft-tissue defects not solely affecting extremity propulsion, and systemic secondary conditions, require careful audit so raters do not unlawfully sweep non-musculoskeletal body systems under `§ 4.68`.
• **Mandatory Presumptive Secondary Cardiovascular Disease (`38 C.F.R. § 3.310(c)`):** Whenever a veteran has a service-connected **unilateral amputation of one lower extremity at or above the knee** (`DC 5160–5162`) OR **bilateral amputations of both lower extremities at or above the ankles** (`DC 5160–5165`), **ischemic heart disease (`DC 7005`) or ANY other cardiovascular disease** developing thereafter **MUST be held proximately due to the amputation as a matter of law** ([`§ 3.310` Snapshot](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.310-secondary-aggravation-evolution), [Playbook 14](/playbooks/14-secondary-service-connection-aggravation-obesity))! Denying secondary SC (or DIC under `§ 1310`) for IHD, hypertension, stroke, or heart failure in a qualifying `AKA` or bilateral `BKA` amputee is an **undebatable CUE (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive)**!
• **Multiple Annual Clothing Allowances (`38 U.S.C. § 1162`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.810` & *Sursely v. Peake*, `551 F.3d 1351 (Fed. Cir. 2009)`):** Whenever a veteran wears **multiple** prosthetic limbs or rigid orthopedic braces (e.g., bilateral hinged knee braces under `DC 5257`, an ankle-foot orthosis `AFO` + knee brace, or prosthesis + spinal brace) that each independently wear out or tear distinct articles of outer clothing (or uses skin medication staining garments), *Sursely* entitles the veteran to **multiple annual clothing allowances**—never just one ([Playbook 13](/playbooks/13-ancillary-grants-sah-auto-clothing-dea-spina-bifida))!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Musculoskeletal System Guide: Painful Motion, Multi-Code Knee Stacking, Implants, Amputations & Foot Rules
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Orthopedic claims are among the most common—and most frequently misrated—conditions in VA compensation. Beyond basic goniometer degree tables in 38 C.F.R. § 4.71a, VA raters must account for painful motion warranting at least the minimum compensable rating (§ 4.59), additional functional loss from pain, weakness, fatigue, and flare-ups (§§ 4.40 and 4.45), dominant ('Major') vs. non-dominant ('Minor') upper-extremity rules (§ 4.69), separate knee ratings when instability and limited motion coexist, prosthetic joint replacement minimums and convalescence (Diagnostic Codes 5051–5056), and post-February 7, 2021 foot codes like Plantar Fasciitis (Diagnostic Code 5269).
record_clues: A 0% joint rating when the VA examination noted objective painful motion—violating 38 C.F.R. § 4.59's rule requiring at least the minimum compensable percentage (10% for most joints; 20% for either shoulder under Diagnostic Code 5201 when arm elevation stops at shoulder level / 90 degrees).

A knee injury with documented giving-way/instability AND limited bending (flexion) or straightening (extension) folded into a single knee code instead of separate ratings under Diagnostic Codes 5257, 5260, and 5261 (VAOPGCPREC 23-97, 9-98, and Lyles v. Shulkin).
An upper-extremity injury where VA switched your naturally dominant injured hand to 'Minor' after you learned to compensate with your other hand (contrary to 38 C.F.R. § 4.69).

A lower-limb amputation (at/above one knee or both ankles) missing Special Monthly Compensation, multiple annual clothing allowances (§ 3.810), or automatic secondary service connection for later heart disease under 38 C.F.R. § 3.310(c).
important_cautions: Anti-stacking limits to keep in mind: while knee instability and knee motion can stack, a single shoulder cannot receive two separate Diagnostic Code 5201 ratings for flexion and abduction (Cullen v. Shinseki); non-painful X-ray-only arthritis across multiple joints under Diagnostic Code 5003 combines into a single 10% or 20% rating; and distal limb ratings cannot exceed the elective amputation ceiling in 38 C.F.R. § 4.68.

Bilateral foot ratings: when a single bilateral foot rating (such as 50% bilateral flatfoot under Diagnostic Code 5276 or 30% bilateral plantar fasciitis under Diagnostic Code 5269) is the ONLY compensable lower-extremity disability, it does not receive an extra standalone 10% bilateral factor unless another compensable lower-extremity condition exists.

Date gates and exam errors: the July 16, 2015 total-prosthesis rule (80 FR 42040; Hudgens v. McDonald) and February 7, 2021 musculoskeletal overhaul (85 FR 76453 / 86 FR 8142) depend on exact claim/decision dates, while existing ratings are protected under 38 C.F.R. § 3.951(a). Incomplete joint exam testing (Correia / Sharp) is a duty-to-assist issue for open claims/appeals—not Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) under Cook v. Principi—and George v. McDonough / 38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1403(e) and 20.1409(c) limit CUE motions.
VA's February 17, 2026 § 4.10 medication rule (91 FR 7118) was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712) and is not active law.
questions_for_representative: Did my VA joint examination test passive, active, weight-bearing, and opposite-joint motion (Correia v. McDonald) and estimate additional degree loss during flare-ups (DeLuca / Sharp)?

On my knee Rating Code Sheet, can instability (Diagnostic Code 5257), limited flexion (Diagnostic Code 5260), limited extension (Diagnostic Code 5261), or meniscal locking (Diagnostic Codes 5258/5259) be rated separately?
Did VA properly rate my naturally dominant arm under the 'Major' column in 38 C.F.R. § 4.69?

If I wear orthopedic braces, crutches, a walker, or prosthetics, have we checked eligibility for multiple annual clothing allowances (§ 3.810), Specially Adapted Housing (§ 3.809), or Special Monthly Compensation?

Counting diagnostic-only, screening, refraction, or routine tonometry monitoring clinic visits (where no active medical/injection/laser/surgical treatment is rendered or prescribed) as 'incapacitating episodes' under Note (1) to § 4.79

Claiming unilateral SMC(k) under 38 U.S.C. § 1114(k) / 38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a)(4) for unilateral 5/200 visual acuity (DC 6065) when the eye still perceives objects/hand motion/fingers at 3 feet (unilateral SMC(k) requires light perception only [LPO] or anatomical loss, whereas BILATERAL 5/200 triggers SMC(l)!)

Assigning DC 6090 diplopia evaluations to BOTH eyes separately (prohibited by 38 C.F.R. § 4.78(b)(1): diplopia is assigned to ONE eye only) or rating occasional/spectacle-correctable diplopia above 0%

*(For verbatim historical and current regulatory text of `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.75–4.79` [and former `§§ 4.80–4.84a`], see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.75–4.79 The Organs of Special Sense — Eye & Visual Impairment Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.75-4.79-eye-evolution) and [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.350, 3.352, 3.552(b), 4.63 & 3.810(a) (Special Monthly Compensation Ratings, Aid & Attendance, TBI SMC(t), Loss of Use & Multiple Clothing Allowances)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.350-3.352-smc-evolution); for `SMC(k)`–`SMC(o)` blindness step math and *Barry v. 1. Master Chronological Federal Register & Precedent Ledger (1946–2026)

rows: **Era 1 Baseline (`§§ 4.75–4.84a`):** Split anatomical loss / LPO / Snellen acuity across `DC 6061–6079`, muscle function `DC 6090–6092`, concentric contraction `DC 6080`, scotoma `DC 6081`, qualitative *"active pathology"* / unquantified *"incapacitating episodes"* across `DC 6000–6035`, and `30%` unilateral minimum for `DC 6029` Aphakia.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`< Dec. 10, 2008`):** Governs pre-Dec. 10, 2008 CUE audits and pre-Dec. 10, 2008 staged periods (including pre-2008 *Nehmer* diabetic retinopathy secondary to Agent Orange diabetes `DC 7913`).

Held that progressive hereditary eye diseases (**retinitis pigmentosa**, familial optic atrophy) are **compensable diseases**—NOT non-compensable static *"congenital or developmental defects"* under `38 C.F.R. § 3.303(c)`—and trigger the `38 U.S.C. § 1111` presumption of soundness when unnoted at entry.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= July 18, 1990`):** Categorical post-1990 RO/Board denials mislabeling retinitis pigmentosa, Stargardt's, or hereditary optic neuropathy as "congenital defects" violate binding `VAOPGCPREC` (`38 U.S.C. § 7104(c)`).

Liberalized **`SMC(o)`** (`38 U.S.C. § 1114(o)`) deaf-blind threshold from bilateral `LPO` to **bilateral SC visual acuity of `20/200` or less** when combined with bilateral deafness rated `>= 60%` (one or both ears SC).
**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) / CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Dec. 26, 2007`).**

**First Major Eye Overhaul (Era 2):** Consolidated `§§ 4.75–4.84a` into **`§§ 4.75–4.79`** (removing `§§ 4.80–4.84a`); consolidated visual acuity into **`DC 6061–6066` (`Table V`)** (retiring `DC 6067–6079`); enacted duration-based **General Rating Formula for Diagnostic Codes 6000 through 6009** (`>= 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 weeks` of prescribed-bed-rest incapacitating episodes/yr); codified Goldmann/automated Humphrey-Octopus perimetry (`§ 4.77`), `> 3.0 diopters` anisometropia (`§ 4.76(b)(1)`), near-vision step adjustment (`§ 4.76(b)(3)`), diplopia `1–3` step elevations (`§ 4.78(b)(1)`), and `10%` orbital prosthesis bump (`§ 4.75(e)`).
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`Dec. 10, 2008 – May 12, 2018`):** Running pre-Dec. 10, 2008 ratings protected under `38 U.S.C. § 1155`. Zero CUE reach before Dec. 10, 2008.

Reversed CAVC and held that **Leber's hereditary optic atrophy** (and any progressive genetic visual disorder) is a compensable *"disease"* under `§ 1110` / `§ 3.303(c)` entitled to `§ 1111` soundness unless VA proves both preexistence and non-aggravation by clear and unmistakable evidence.
**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** for CUE predating `VAOPGCPREC 67-90`/`82-90`, but reinforces CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive where post-1990 decisions defied `67-90`/`82-90`.

**Second Major Eye Overhaul (Era 3 — Treatment-Visit Count Formula):** Replaced archaic multi-week *"incapacitating episode"* duration blocks in `§ 4.79` with **annual clinic treatment-visit counts** (`1–2 = 10%`, `3–4 = 20%`, `5–6 = 40%`, `>= 7 = 60%` in past 12 months) for systemic immunosuppressants/biologics, intravitreal/periocular injections, laser, or surgery; **added `DC 6040` (Diabetic retinopathy)**, **`DC 6042` (Retinal dystrophy, incl. wet/dry AMD & RP)**, and **`DC 6046` (Post-chiasmal disorders)**; modernized `DC 6012–6013` Glaucoma.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= May 13, 2018`):** Claims pending on May 13, 2018 receive Era-2 staged ratings before May 13, 2018 and the higher of Era 2 or Era 3 from May 13, 2018 forward (*Karnas*). Zero CUE reach before May 13, 2018.
**`Pub. L. 116-154, § 2`** (*Ryan Kules and Paul Benne Specially Adapted Housing Improvement Act*, `134 Stat. 690`)

Expanded **`38 U.S.C. § 2101(a)(2)(B)(ii)` (`Ch. 21` `SAH`)** to cover **bilateral SC blindness with central visual acuity of `20/200` or less** in the better eye (eliminating the pre-Oct. 1, 2020 `LPO` / `5°` field threshold).

**Era-2 Note (`73 FR 66550`):** Period of acute symptoms severe enough to require **prescribed bed rest and treatment by a physician or other healthcare provider** (measured by cumulative duration).

**Era-3 Notes (1) & (2) (`83 FR 15321`):** Eye condition severe enough to require **a clinic visit to a provider specifically for treatment purposes**—e.g., **systemic immunosuppressants or biologic agents, intravitreal or periocular injections, laser treatments, or other surgical interventions**. *(Diagnostic, screening, or monitoring visits excluded).*
Pooled under `DC 6006` Retinopathy, `DC 6026` Optic atrophy, or analogous `DC 6080`.

blocks.text: B. The Post-May 13, 2018 Anti-VEGF Injection & Biologic Goldmine (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive)

items: **Why `83 FR 15316` Transformed Retinal & Uveitic Ratings:** Prior to May 13, 2018, veterans with **proliferative diabetic retinopathy (`DC 6040`)**, **neovascular ("wet") macular degeneration (`DC 6042`)**, **retinal vein occlusion (`DC 6006`)**, or **autoimmune uveitis (`DC 6000`)** who received monthly or bimonthly **intravitreal anti-VEGF injections** (*aflibercept [Eylea], ranibizumab [Lucentis], bevacizumab [Avastin], faricimab [Vabysmo]*) or **focal/panretinal laser photocoagulation** preserved `20/30` or `20/40` central acuity and were routinely stuck at **`0%` or `10%`** because outpatient injections did not cause "4 to 6 weeks" of continuous incapacitation.

**Kill-Switch Screen:** Purely **diagnostic, monitoring, refraction, OCT imaging, or intraocular-pressure checkup visits** where no active treatment procedure is performed or initiated **do NOT count** under Note (1).

blocks.text: 3. Central Visual Acuity (§§ 4.75–4.76, DC 6061–6066) & Four High-Yield Audit Traps

Under `38 C.F.R. § 4.75(b)`, every VA visual impairment examination **must** be conducted by a **licensed optometrist or ophthalmologist** using standard Snellen test types (`20 feet / 6 meters` distance; `14 inches / 35 cm` near) or equivalent.
A. Trap 1 — Unilateral SC Eye Presumed 20/40 (§ 4.75(c)) vs. 38 U.S.C. § 1160(a)(1) Paired-Organ Unlock!

items: **Default Unilateral Rule (`38 C.F.R. § 4.75(c)–(d)`):** When visual impairment of **only one eye** is service-connected, the visual acuity of the **non-service-connected (`NSC`) eye must be considered `20/40`** when reading across `Table V` (`DC 6063–6066`), capping unilateral functional visual impairment at **`30%`** (`DC 6064` LPO or `DC 6065` `5/200` paired with `20/40` = `30%`; `DC 6063` anatomical loss paired with `20/40` = `40%`, or **`50%`** if unable to wear an ocular prosthesis under `§ 4.75(e)`).

**The `§ 1160(a)(1)` / `§ 3.383(a)(1)` Paired-Organ Exception (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive):** Whenever the veteran has **compensable or noncompensable service-connected blindness/impairment in one eye** (`<= 20/200` or peripheral field `<= 20°` SC eye) AND suffers **non-service-connected (`NSC`) blindness in the other eye** (not due to willful misconduct) reducing the NSC eye to:
• Central visual acuity of **`20/200` or less**, **OR**
• Peripheral visual field widest diameter of **`20 degrees` or less**,

blocks.text: **`38 U.S.C. § 1160(a)(1)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.383(a)(1)` override `§ 4.75(c)` and mandate rating BOTH eyes together "as if" service-connected**—jumping the veteran from `30%` unilateral all the way to **`70%`–`100%` + `SMC(l)`–`(n)` + `Ch. 35` DEA** (*Kimberlin v. Brown*, `5 Vet. App. 174 (1993)`)!
B. Trap 2 — The > 3.0 Diopters Anisometropia Uncorrected-Acuity Rule (38 C.F.R. § 4.76(b)(1))

items: Normally, central visual acuity is rated on **best-corrected** distance vision.

**Critical Regulatory Carve-Out (`§ 4.76(b)(1)`):** When the corrective lens power (spherical equivalent) required to correct distance vision in the **poorer eye differs by MORE than `3.0 diopters`** from the lens required for the **better eye** (*and* the difference is **not** due to congenital or developmental refractive error—e.g., post-traumatic cataract extraction, unilateral corneal surgery/scar, scleral buckle), and the poorer eye (or both eyes) is SC, the rater **MUST evaluate the poorer eye using EITHER its uncorrected OR corrected visual acuity, whichever yields the higher combined rating**! Raters routinely overlook refraction diopter boxes on the Eye DBQ, creating clean **RO CUE** (`>= Dec. 10, 2008`).

blocks.text: C. Trap 3 — Corneal Contact-Lens Tolerance (§ 4.76(b)(2)), Near-Vision Step-Down (§ 4.76(b)(3)) & Intermediate Rounding (§ 4.76(b)(4))

items: **Corneal Irregular Astigmatism & Contact Lenses (`§ 4.76(b)(2)` — Crucial for `DC 6035` Keratoconus & `DC 6036` Corneal Transplant):** Even if rigid gas-permeable (`RGP`) or scleral contact lenses correct a keratoconus eye to `20/25`, VA may rate on contact-lens acuity **ONLY if the veteran *"customarily wears contact lenses"*!** If corneal pain, dry eye, or graft ectasia prevents customary contact-lens wear, VA **must** rate on **spectacle-corrected** acuity!

**Near-Vision Discrepancy (`§ 4.76(b)(3)`):** If corrected near vision (`14 in.`) is **`2 or more` scheduled steps worse** than corrected distance vision (verified by `>= 2` recordings + clinical explanation, e.g., posterior subcapsular cataract or accommodative palsy), rate the eye at **one step poorer** than measured corrected distance vision!

**Intermediate Acuity Rounding (`§ 4.76(b)(4)`):** Any Snellen measurement falling *between* two listed Table V benchmarks (`20/40`, `20/50`, `20/70`, `20/100`, `20/200`, `15/200`, `10/200`, `5/200`, `LPO`) **must** be rounded to the poorer Snellen benchmark permitting the **higher evaluation** (e.g., `20/60 -> 20/70`; `20/80 -> 20/100`; `20/150 -> 20/200`).

blocks.text: D. Trap 4 — Cataract Pseudophakia (DC 6027) vs. True Aphakia (DC 6029)

items: **`DC 6027` (Cataract of any type):** Preoperatively, rate under the General Rating Formula. Postoperatively, if an **intraocular replacement lens (`IOL` — pseudophakia)** is present, rate under the General Rating Formula (acuity/field residuals or post-op treatment visits—**no** automatic `30%` minimum!).

**`DC 6029` (Aphakia or dislocation of crystalline lens — NO replacement `IOL`):** When the natural lens is absent or dislocated **without** an implanted `IOL`, evaluate based on visual impairment, **elevate the resulting visual acuity level by ONE STEP poorer**, and enforce a **mandatory `30%` minimum evaluation** (unilateral or bilateral)!

blocks.text: E. Summary Reference: Table V Central Visual Acuity Benchmarks (DC 6061–6066)

rows: **`6063`** Anatomical loss `1` eye *(+`10%` if no prosthesis, `§ 4.75(e)`)*

blocks.text: 4. Visual Fields (§ 4.77, DC 6080–6081, DC 6046) & Muscle Function / Diplopia (§ 4.78, DC 6090)
A. Visual Field Perimetry Standards (§ 4.77) & DC 6080–6081 Equivalent Acuity Rules

items: **Approved Perimetry Equipment (`§ 4.77(a)–(b)`):** Examiners must use **Goldmann kinetic perimetry** OR automated perimetry with simulated kinetic Goldmann capability (**Humphrey Model 750**, **Octopus Model 101**, or later versions of these perimetric devices), testing **`III/4e`** target isopter (`IV/4e` for aphakic/pseudophakic eyes not well adapted to contact lens/IOL), documenting results for **at least `16` meridians `22½ degrees` apart for each eye** (`§ 4.77(a)`), averaging remaining field across the **`8` principal meridians `45 degrees` apart** (`§ 4.77(b)`), and—when additional testing is indicated—conducting either a **tangent screen** or a **`30-degree` threshold visual field with Goldmann `III` stimulus size**.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Eye & Vision Impairment Guide: Treatment Visits, Double Vision, Paired-Eye Rules & Hereditary Eye Diseases
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Eye disabilities often involve much more than a standard 20/20 chart reading. Under 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.75–4.79, VA evaluates central acuity, visual field narrowing or blind spots (scotomas/hemianopsia after TBI or stroke), double vision (diplopia, Diagnostic Code 6090), active clinic treatment visits (since May 13, 2018), facial disfigurement or prosthesis inability, and Special Monthly Compensation. In addition, federal courts (O'Bryan v. McDonald) and VA General Counsel opinions confirm that progressive hereditary eye diseases—such as retinitis pigmentosa or keratoconus—are compensable diseases rather than uncompensable 'congenital defects' if they first manifest or worsen during service.
record_clues: Diabetic retinopathy (Diagnostic Code 6040), macular degeneration or retinal dystrophy (Diagnostic Code 6042), uveitis (Diagnostic Code 6000), or glaucoma (Diagnostic Codes 6012/6013) rated 0% or 10% despite 3 or more active treatment clinic visits per year after May 13, 2018.

Post-TBI or post-stroke double vision (diplopia, Diagnostic Code 6090) accompanied by reduced visual acuity or visual field loss in the same eye where VA omitted the mandatory 1-, 2-, or 3-step visual acuity elevation under 38 C.F.R. § 4.78(b)(1).
A VA denial rejecting keratoconus (Diagnostic Code 6035), retinitis pigmentosa (Diagnostic Code 6042), or hereditary optic neuropathy as a 'congenital defect' under 38 C.F.R. § 3.303(c).

Loss of one eye to light perception only (30%, Diagnostic Code 6064) or anatomical removal (40%, Diagnostic Code 6063, or 50% if unable to wear a prosthesis) missing statutory SMC(k)—or bilateral 5/200 vision (Diagnostic Code 6065) missing SMC(l)–(n) and housing/auto grants.
important_cautions: Unilateral vs. bilateral SMC blindness thresholds: for a single eye, statutory SMC(k) under 38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a)(4) requires vision reduced to 'light perception only' (or anatomical loss), whereas bilateral 5/200 vision in BOTH eyes triggers higher SMC(l) and Specially Adapted Housing / Chapter 39 Automobile eligibility.

Diplopia (Diagnostic Code 6090) is assigned to ONE eye only (never stacked on both eyes simultaneously under § 4.78(b)(1)), and occasional diplopia or diplopia fully corrected by eyeglasses is rated 0%.

Exact overhaul dates govern historical reviews: December 10, 2008 (73 FR 66543) and May 13, 2018 (83 FR 15316) rules cannot prove Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) before their effective dates; pre-revision running ratings are protected by 38 C.F.R. § 3.951(a); and George v. McDonough / 38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1403(e) and 20.1409(c) restrict CUE motions.
VA's February 17, 2026 § 4.10 medication rule (91 FR 7118) was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712) and is not active law.
questions_for_representative: Did my VA eye exam perform automated Humphrey or Goldmann kinetic visual field testing—especially if I have glaucoma, diabetes, TBI, or stroke history?
If I have double vision (diplopia) along with reduced visual acuity or visual field loss in the same eye, did VA apply the step-up table in 38 C.F.R. § 4.78(b)(1)?
Was a progressive hereditary eye condition like keratoconus or retinitis pigmentosa mistakenly denied as a congenital defect?
Do my clinic records show active eye-injection, laser, or flare treatment visits since May 13, 2018 that support a 20%, 40%, or 60% rating under the General Rating Formula?
