1. Master Chronological Federal Register & Precedent Ledger (1946–2026)

rows: `1945 VASRD` (`38 C.F.R. § 3.952`; `29 FR 6718`, May 22, 1964; `41 FR 11298`, Mar. 18, 1976 ISO/ANSI puretone tables)

**Era 1 Spoken-Voice / Early Audiometric Schedule:** Evaluated auditory acuity initially by conversational voice distance (`1/3/5/10/15/20 ft`, Columns `A–F`) and later early puretone + PB word lists (`DC 6277–6297`); `DC 6260` Tinnitus required *"Persistent as a symptom of head injury, concussion or acoustic trauma — 10%"*.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`< Dec. 18, 1987`):** Governs pre-Dec. 18, 1987 hearing loss CUE audits; running pre-Dec. 18, 1987 awards protected from schedule-change reduction under `38 U.S.C. § 1155` / `§ 3.951(a)`.

**Modern Audiometric Overhaul (`§ 4.85`, `DC 6100`):** Replaced spoken-voice/legacy `DC 6277–6297` codes with **un-aided state-licensed audiologist testing** combining `1000–4000 Hz` **Puretone Threshold Average (`PTA`)** + **Maryland CNC Speech Discrimination** (`Tables VI, VIa & VII`, Roman Numerals `I–XI` -> `0%–100%` under unified **`DC 6100`**).
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Dec. 18, 1987`):** Mechanical math errors reading `Table VI`, `Table VIa`, or `Table VII` on undisputed audiograms are textbook **RO CUE** (`§ 3.105(a)`).

Enacted and refined **`38 C.F.R. § 3.385`** (*Disability due to impaired hearing*): `>= 40 dB` at any of `500–4000 Hz`, OR `>= 26 dB` at `>= 3` of `500–4000 Hz`, OR `< 94%` Maryland CNC speech recognition (`59 FR 60560` added the `< 94%` CNC prong).

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive:** Under ***Hensley v. Brown*, `5 Vet. App. 155 (1993)`**, `§ 3.385` governs *current* disability—**never** a bar requiring `§ 3.385`-level loss on a separation audiogram!

Under `32-97` & *Boyer*, unilateral SC hearing loss fixes the NSC ear at Roman Numeral `I` unless `38 U.S.C. § 1160(a)(3)` / `§ 3.383(a)(3)` applies: **pre-Dec. 6, 2002** required *total deafness* in both ears; **on/after Dec. 6, 2002**, `Pub. L. 107-330, § 103` liberalized `§ 1160(a)(3)` to **`>= 10%` compensable SC hearing loss in one ear (`Roman Numeral X or XI`) + `§ 3.385` NSC hearing loss in the other ear**!

**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) / CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Dec. 6, 2002`):** Huge CUE/effective-date unlock whenever a post-Dec. 6, 2002 `10%+` unilateral SC ear was not combined with a `§ 3.385` NSC ear!

**Overhauled `§§ 4.85–4.87a`:** Enacted **`§ 4.86(a)–(b)` Exceptional Patterns of Hearing Impairment** (`>= 55 dB` at `1000–4000 Hz`, OR `<= 30 dB` at `1000 Hz` & `>= 70 dB` at `2000 Hz`); **liberalized `DC 6260` Tinnitus** to *"Tinnitus, recurrent — 10%"* (deleting the head-injury/concussion/acoustic-trauma limitation + adding Notes (1) & (2) [redesignated Note (3) in 2003]); codified **`DC 6205` Meniere's `30/60/100%` + anti-pyramiding maximization Note**; separated `DC 6275–6276` smell/taste into `§ 4.87a`.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= June 10, 1999`):** Rater failure to apply `§ 4.86(a)` or `(b)` on post-June 10, 1999 audiograms is **one of the highest-yield math CUEs in Veterans Law**! Zero CUE reach before June 10, 1999.

Added **Note (2)** to `DC 6260` (*single `10%` evaluation whether unilateral, bilateral, or in the head*). **Federal Circuit reversed CAVC (`19 Vet. App. 63`)** and upheld `VAOPGCPREC 2-2003`, holding that **even pre-June 13, 2003 `DC 6260` authorized only ONE `10%` rating**!
**Adverse CUE Kill-Switch:** Defeats *all* bilateral `10% + 10%` tinnitus claims and CUE motions regardless of decision date.

Held tinnitus is an `"organic disease of the nervous system"` under `§ 3.309(a)` (*Fountain*); unnoted pre-service hearing shifts trigger full `§ 1111` soundness (*McKinney*); `§ 4.85` tables contemplate difficulty hearing/understanding speech, narrowing `§ 3.321(b)(1)` extraschedular (*Doucette*; *King*).
**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** for CUE against final pre-2015/2016 denials (`§ 20.1403(e)`), but decisive merits weapons on all open, supplemental, and AMA appeals!
**QUARANTINED — Proposed / Not Finalized:** Proposed eliminating standalone `10%` `DC 6260` tinnitus by folding tinnitus solely into underlying pathology codes.
**ZERO legal force.** `DC 6260` (`10%`) remains active binding law (see Section 6).

blocks.text: 2. Service-Connection Gate (38 C.F.R. § 3.385), Delayed-Onset Nexus (*Hensley*) & Soundness (*McKinney*)
A. Current Disability Threshold (38 C.F.R. § 3.385) vs. Delayed-Onset Acoustic Trauma (*Hensley v. Brown*)

Under `38 C.F.R. § 3.385`, impaired hearing constitutes a compensable/service-connectable **"disability"** for VA purposes when an audiometric examination by a state-licensed audiologist (`§ 4.85(a)`) shows **any one** of three disjunctive criteria in the affected ear:

items: Auditory threshold of **`40 decibels (dB)` or greater** at **any** of the five frequencies **`500, 1000, 2000, 3000, or 4000 Hz`** *(note: `500 Hz` counts for `§ 3.385` service connection even though `500 Hz` is excluded from the `1000–4000 Hz` `§ 4.85(d)` rating average; by contrast, isolated `6000 Hz` or `8000 Hz` notches alone do NOT satisfy `§ 3.385`!)*; **OR**
Auditory thresholds of **`26 dB` or greater** at **at least three (`>= 3`)** of the five frequencies **`500, 1000, 2000, 3000, or 4000 Hz`**; **OR**
Speech recognition score using the **Maryland CNC Test** of **less than `94 percent` (`< 94%`)**.

**The *Hensley* Separation-Audiogram Rule (*Hensley v. Brown*, `5 Vet. App. 155, 159–60 (1993)`):** VA examiners and raters frequently commit legal error by denying service connection solely because the veteran's **separation audiogram** was "normal" (did not yet cross `§ 3.385` thresholds). Under *Hensley*, **`§ 3.385` establishes ONLY whether the veteran has a *current* hearing disability at the time of the claim—it is NOT a requirement that `§ 3.385`-level hearing loss have manifested during active service!** A veteran with a sub-`§ 3.385` separation audiogram (or no separation audiogram at all, e.g., in-service high-frequency `4000–6000 Hz` threshold shift, combat artillery/flight-line exposure conceded under `38 U.S.C. § 1154(a)–(b)`) establishes direct service connection (`§ 3.303(a)`) via a medical nexus opinion linking current sensorineural loss to in-service acoustic trauma, reinforced by credible lay continuity (*Dalton*; *Jandreau*).

blocks.text: B. Presumption of Soundness on Entrance Audiograms (*McKinney v. McDonald*, 28 Vet. App. 15 (2016) (en banc))

items: Prior to 2016, VA routinely denied `DC 6100` claims on the theory that an entrance audiogram recorded elevated decibel numbers (e.g., `30 dB` at two frequencies or `45 dB` at `6000 Hz`) that did **not** meet `§ 3.385`, yet treated those sub-`§ 3.385` numbers as "noted preexisting hearing loss" shifting the `§ 1153` aggravation burden onto the veteran.

In ***McKinney v. McDonald*, `28 Vet. App. 15, 27–31 (2016) (en banc)`**, the full CAVC abolished that trap: because pre-entrance audiometric readings that do **not** cross `38 C.F.R. § 3.385` are **legally not a "hearing disability"** under VA's own regulation, an entrance exam recording sub-`§ 3.385` thresholds **does NOT "note" a preexisting hearing defect**! Consequently, the veteran enjoys the **full `38 U.S.C. § 1111` presumption of soundness**, requiring **VA** to prove by **clear and unmistakable evidence** *both* that a hearing disability preexisted service *and* that service noise did not aggravate it (*Wagner v. Principi*, `370 F.3d 1089 (Fed. Cir. 2004)`; [Soundness Treatise](/docs/service-connection-direct-soundness-aggravation)).

blocks.text: 3. Hearing Loss Rating Evolution (§§ 4.85–4.86, DC 6100): Puretone/CNC Tables & The § 4.86 CUE Goldmine

See [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.385 & 4.85–4.87 Impairment of Auditory Acuity, Vestibular Disorders & Three-Era Tinnitus (DC 6260) Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.85-4.87-auditory-tinnitus-evolution) for the complete verbatim `Table VI`, `Table VIa`, and `Table VII` matrices.
A. Mechanical Operation of 38 C.F.R. § 4.85 (>= Dec. 18, 1987, 52 FR 44117)

items: **Un-Aided State-Licensed Audiologist Exam (`§ 4.85(a)`):** Testing **must** be conducted **without hearing aids** by a state-licensed audiologist using **controlled Maryland CNC (`Consonant-Nucleus-Consonant`) 50-word lists** and **puretone audiometry**.

**Puretone Threshold Average (`PTA`, `§ 4.85(d)`):** Sum the puretone decibel thresholds at **`1000, 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hz` ONLY** and **divide by `4`** (rounding `.5` or `.75` to the nearest whole integer; `500 Hz` is **never** included in the `§ 4.85(d)` `PTA`! Under VA audiology exam protocol / `M21-1` `V.iii.2.B` and `Table VIA`'s `105+` ceiling, if threshold at any of the four frequencies exceeds `100 dB` or registers "no response," it is recorded as **`105 dB`**).

**`Table VI` vs. `Table VIa` (`§ 4.85(b)–(c)`; *Lendenmann v. Principi*, `3 Vet. App. 345, 349 (1992)`):**
• **Default (`Table VI`):** Intersect the ear's **Maryland CNC Speech Discrimination `%`** (`92–100%`, `84–90%`, `76–82%`, `68–74%`, `60–66%`, `52–58%`, `44–50%`, `36–42%`, `0–34%`) with its **`PTA`** (`0–41 dB` up to `98+ dB`) to obtain a mechanical Roman Numeral **`I` (normal) through `XI` (profound)** (*Lendenmann*; `Table VIA` splits `98–104 dB` [`X`] and `105+ dB` [`XI`]).
• **Mandatory `Table VIa` Puretone-Only Override (`§ 4.85(c)`):** When the audiologist certifies that the Maryland CNC speech test is **not appropriate**—due to **language difficulties (non-native English speaker), inconsistent/unreliable speech discrimination scores, cognitive/aphasic barriers, or conductive/mixed pathology rendering CNC invalid**—OR when triggered by **`§ 4.86`**, the rater **must** use **`Table VIa`** (puretone average alone)!

**Combining Both Ears on `Table VII` (`§ 4.85(e)`):** Intersect the **Better Ear** Roman Numeral (horizontal row `I–XI`) with the **Poorer Ear** Roman Numeral (vertical column `I–XI`) to assign a single **`0%` to `100%`** bilateral disability evaluation under `DC 6100` *(no `§ 4.26` bilateral factor applies because `Table VII` already combines both ears into a single `DC 6100` code)*.

blocks.text: B. The 38 C.F.R. § 4.86(a)–(b) Exceptional Patterns CUE Goldmine (>= June 10, 1999, 64 FR 25202)

lines: **Why `§ 4.86` Is One of the Highest-Yield Code-Sheet CUEs in Veterans Law (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive):** Veterans with severe noise-induced "ski-slope" high-frequency loss often score `92%–96%` on quiet-booth Maryland CNC testing (trapping them at Roman Numeral `I` or `II` = **`0%`** on `Table VI`!). Effective **June 10, 1999 (`64 FR 25202`)**, VA enacted `§ 4.86(a)–(b)` specifically to rescue these veterans—and evaluated **each ear separately**:

1. **Pattern A (`§ 4.86(a)` — Flat Severe `>= 55 dB` Pattern):** When the puretone threshold at **EACH of the four frequencies (`1000, 2000, 3000, AND 4000 Hz`) is `55 dB or more`**, determine the ear's Roman numeral from **BOTH `Table VI` and `Table VIa`** and assign **whichever Roman numeral is HIGHER**!

2. **Pattern B (`§ 4.86(b)` — Steep Ski-Slope `1000 -> 2000 Hz` Drop + Mandatory `+1` Numeral Bump!):** When the puretone threshold is **`30 dB or less` at `1000 Hz` AND `70 dB or more` at `2000 Hz`**, determine the ear's Roman numeral from **BOTH `Table VI` and `Table VIa`** (taking whichever is **higher**), **AND THEN ELEVATE THAT NUMERAL TO THE NEXT HIGHER ROMAN NUMERAL** (e.g., `IV -> V`, capped at `XI`)!

*Audit Check:* Pull every post-June 10, 1999 `0%` or `10%` `DC 6100` audiogram. Whenever raters plugged `1000–4000 Hz` numbers into `Table VI` while forgetting `§ 4.86(a)` or `(b)`'s `Table VIa` + `+1` Roman numeral elevation, file an immediate **RO CUE motion (`38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a)`)**!

blocks.text: C. Extraschedular Limits (*Martinak*, *Doucette*, *King*) vs. Paired-Organ Hearing (§ 1160(a)(3)) & SMC(k)/SMC(o)

items: **Mechanical Tables & Narrow `§ 3.321(b)(1)` Extraschedular Path:** Under ***Martinak v. Nicholson*, `21 Vet. App. 447, 453–55 (2007)`**, audiologists must still record the functional effects of hearing loss in daily life/work (`§ 4.10`). However, in ***Doucette v. Shulkin*, `28 Vet. App. 366, 371–72 (2017)`** and ***King v. Shulkin*, `29 Vet. App. 174 (2017)`**, the CAVC held that `§ 4.85` **already contemplates difficulty hearing and understanding speech** (including in background noise or group settings); therefore, `§ 3.321(b)(1)` extraschedular referral is triggered **only** by exceptional functional effects *outside* difficulty hearing—such as **otalgia (ear pain), aural fullness/pressure, dizziness/vertigo, or severe occupational/social sequelae not captured by secondary codes** ([Playbook 19](/playbooks/19-extraschedular-3.321b1-analogous-4.20-and-temp-total)).

**Two-Era Unilateral SC Ear (`VAOPGCPREC 32-97` / *Boyer*) vs. `38 U.S.C. § 1160(a)(3)` (`§ 3.383(a)(3)`) Paired-Organ Unlock:**
• **When Unilateral SC Ear Is `0%` (`Roman Numeral I–IX` when paired with `I` on `Table VII`):** Under **`VAOPGCPREC 32-97`** and ***Boyer v. West*, `210 F.3d 1351 (Fed. Cir. 2000)`**, an opposite non-service-connected (`NSC`) ear must be fixed at Roman Numeral `I` (normal) *(except prior to Dec. 6, 2002 where *both* the SC ear and NSC ear had **total deafness**)*.
• **Post-December 6, 2002 `§ 1160(a)(3)` Paired-Organ Breakthrough (`Pub. L. 107-330, § 103`, `116 Stat. 2821`; `69 FR 48149`, Aug. 9, 2004):** Effective **December 6, 2002**, Congress overrode the "total deafness" barrier! Whenever a veteran has **`(a)` SC hearing impairment in one ear compensable at `10% or more`** (`Roman Numeral X or XI` when paired with `I` on `Table VII`) **AND `(b)` NSC hearing impairment in the other ear that meets `38 C.F.R. § 3.385`** (not due to willful misconduct), VA **must evaluate BOTH ears together on `Table VII` "as if" service-connected**!

**Statutory `SMC(k)` Total Bilateral Deafness (`38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)`, `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a)(5)`) & `SMC(o)` Deaf-Blind Escalators:** Whenever bilateral SC (or `§ 1160(a)(3)` paired-organ) hearing loss reaches **`100%` under `Table VII`** (`Roman Numeral XI` bilaterally — deemed by `§ 3.350(a)(5)` under `Pub. L. 88-20` to establish *"deafness of both ears, having absence of air and bone conduction"*), VA **must** award mandatory **`SMC(k)`** (`+ $139.87/mo` in 2026) on top of `100%`! Furthermore, bilateral deafness rated `>= 60%` (one or both ears SC) combined with `<= 20/200` bilateral SC blindness jumps straight to **`SMC(o)` (`$6,877.12/mo`)** under `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(e)(1)(iii)` ([`System 02 Eye Diff`](/cfr/modules/02-eye-and-vision-4.75-4.79); [Master SMC Treatise](/docs/smc-complete-treatise-and-step-math)).

blocks.text: 4. Tinnitus (DC 6260): Three-Era Evolution, The *Smith* CUE Kill-Switch & *Fountain*/*Charles* Merits Wins
A. Three-Era Regulatory Text Comparison (1946 vs. 1999 vs. 2003)

rows: **`6260` Tinnitus:** *"Persistent as a symptom of head injury, concussion or acoustic trauma .......... **`10%`**"*
Required persistent ringing **plus** head-injury, concussion, or acoustic-trauma etiology (*upheld against statutory challenge in **Wanner v. Principi**, `370 F.3d 1124 (Fed. Cir. 2004)`*).

**`6260` Tinnitus, recurrent .......... `10%`** · • *Note (1):* Separate evaluation combinable with `6100, 6200, 6204`, etc., unless tinnitus already supports that code (`6205`). · • *Note (2) [now Note (3)]:* Objective tinnitus rated under underlying cause.

**Major Liberalization:** Eliminated the head-injury/concussion/acoustic-trauma prerequisite—unlocking `10%` for recurrent tinnitus from **ototoxic drugs (aspirin/NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, cisplatin, quinine/antimalarials), barotrauma, hypertension, TMJ, or idiopathic in-service onset**!

Added **Note (2):** *"Assign **only a single evaluation** for recurrent tinnitus, whether the sound is perceived in one ear, both ears, or in the head."* *(Redesignated objective-tinnitus note as Note (3)).*
Codified `VAOPGCPREC 2-2003` (`May 22, 2003`) confirming a strict **`10%` single-rating ceiling** regardless of bilateral perception.

blocks.text: B. CRITICAL CUE TRAP WARNING: *Smith v. Nicholson*, 451 F.3d 1344 (Fed. Cir. 2006)!

lines: **DO NOT FILE BILATERAL TINNITUS (`10% + 10%`) CUE MOTIONS (AGENTS Law 5 & Law 6):**

* Outdated secondary blogs occasionally cite ***Smith v. Nicholson*, `19 Vet. App. 63 (2005)`**, in which the CAVC *briefly* held that pre-June 13, 2003 `DC 6260` and `38 C.F.R. § 4.25(b)` required dual `10% + 10%` ratings for bilateral tinnitus.

* **THE FEDERAL CIRCUIT REVERSED THAT HOLDING IN *Smith v. Nicholson*, `451 F.3d 1344, 1350–51 (Fed. Cir. 2006)`**, deferring to VA's binding interpretation in [`VAOPGCPREC 2-2003`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index) (`69 FR 25178`) that **even under pre-June 13, 2003 regulations, `DC 6260` authorized ONLY ONE `10%` evaluation** whether perceived in one ear, both ears, or the head!

* **Practitioner Pivot:** Never waste a one-shot Board CUE (`§ 7111`) or RO CUE motion demanding bilateral `10% + 10%` tinnitus. Instead, capture `30%–70%+` in secondary compensation by filing **`38 C.F.R. § 3.310(a)` secondary claims** for **somatic symptom disorder / depression / anxiety (`§ 4.130`, `30%–70%`)** or **migraine headaches (`DC 8100`, `30%–50%`)** proximately caused or aggravated by relentless `DC 6260` tinnitus ([Playbook 14](/playbooks/14-secondary-service-connection-aggravation-obesity))!

blocks.text: C. High-Value Merits & Effective-Date Weapons on DC 6260 (*Charles*, *Jandreau*, *Fountain*)

items: **Lay Competence to Self-Diagnose & Report Tinnitus (*Charles v. Principi*, `16 Vet. App. 370, 374 (2002)`; *Jandreau v. Nicholson*, `492 F.3d 1372, 1377 (Fed. Cir. 2007)`):** Subjective tinnitus has no objective audiometric test; ringing in the ears is a classic observable symptom that **a lay veteran is 100% competent to perceive and report** both in service and continuously since discharge, triggering VA's `§ 5103A(d)` duty to provide an exam (*McLendon v. Nicholson*, `20 Vet. App. 79 (2006)`) even when STRs are completely silent!

**Tinnitus as a `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(a)` Chronic Nervous System Disease (*Fountain v. McDonald*, `27 Vet. App. 258, 265–72 (2015)`):** Even after *Walker v. Shinseki*, `708 F.3d 1331 (Fed. Cir. 2013)` restricted `38 C.F.R. § 3.303(b)` chronicity/continuity of symptomatology to `§ 3.309(a)` chronic diseases, the CAVC held in ***Fountain*** that **tinnitus associated with acoustic trauma (or nervous-system pathology) IS an `"organic disease of the nervous system"` under `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(a)`**—preserving both the **1-year post-discharge `10%` presumptive window** AND **`§ 3.303(b)` continuity of symptomatology** without requiring a separate medical nexus opinion if credible lay testimony establishes continuous ringing since service!

blocks.text: 5. Vestibular Disorders (DC 6204), Meniere's Stacking (DC 6205) & Complete Ear/Sense Schedule (DC 6200–6276)

headers: Current `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.87–4.87a` Criteria & Anti-Pyramiding / Maximization Rules
rows: Chronic suppurative otitis media, mastoiditis, or cholesteatoma

**`10%`** during suppuration or with aural polyps. **Note:** Rate `DC 6100` hearing loss, labyrinthitis (`6204`), `DC 6260` tinnitus, **`DC 8207` facial nerve paralysis**, and skull bone loss **separately**!
Chronic nonsuppurative / serous otitis media (`6201`); Otosclerosis (`6202`)

Rate hearing impairment (`DC 6100`) + `DC 6260` tinnitus if present. *(Note: Otosclerosis is a progressive hereditary/metabolic bone disease compensable under `§ 3.303(c)` & `VAOPGCPREC 82-90`—never a congenital defect!)*
**Peripheral vestibular disorders** *(labyrinthitis, BPPV, vestibular neuritis, post-TBI inner-ear vertigo)*

• **`30%`:** Dizziness **AND** occasional staggering *(cumulative conjunctive requirement!)* · • **`10%`:** Occasional dizziness. · • **Mandatory Objective-Finding Note:** *"Objective findings supporting the diagnosis of vestibular disequilibrium are required before a compensable evaluation can be assigned under this code."* (Satisfied by Romberg sway, nystagmus, Dix-Hallpike, VNG/ENG caloric testing, or observed gait unsteadiness!). Combine `DC 6100`, `DC 6200`, and `DC 6260` **separately**!

• **`100%`:** Hearing impairment with attacks of vertigo **and cerebellar gait** occurring **more than once weekly (`> 1/wk`)**, with or without tinnitus. · • **`60%`:** Hearing impairment with attacks of vertigo **and cerebellar gait** occurring **`1 to 4` times a month**, with or without tinnitus. · • **`30%`:** Hearing impairment with vertigo **less than once a month (`< 1/mo`)**, with or without tinnitus. · • **CRITICAL MAXIMIZATION & ANTI-PYRAMIDING NOTE (`38 C.F.R. § 4.14`; `DC 6205 Note`, `64 FR 25202, 25210`):** Evaluate Meniere's **EITHER** as a single `DC 6205` rating (`30/60/100%`) **OR** by separately rating vertigo (`DC 6204`, `10%/30%`), hearing loss (`DC 6100`, `0%–100%`), and tinnitus (`DC 6260`, `10%`) and combining them under `§ 4.25`—**WHICHEVER METHOD YIELDS THE HIGHER OVERALL EVALUATION!** *(E.g., when a veteran has `2` vertigo attacks/month *without* cerebellar gait—dropping `DC 6205` to `30%`—or mild `<1/mo` Meniere's with occasional staggering, unbundling `DC 6204 [30%] + DC 6260 [10%] + DC 6100 [20%] = 50%` beats a single `30%` `DC 6205` award!)* Never stack `DC 6205` *on top of* `6100/6204/6260` for the same ear(s).
**Malignant (`6208`)** / **Benign (`6209`)** neoplasm of ear *(other than skin only)*

• `6208`: **`100%`** during active malignancy/treatment + **6 months** post-discontinuance -> **mandatory VA C&P examination** before any reduction under `38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e)` (any premature reduction without exam is **void ab initio**, [Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings))! · • `6209`: Rate on impairment of function. *(Skin-only pinna basal/squamous cell cancers rate under `§ 4.118` `DC 7818`/`7800`).*
**`10%`:** Swelling, dry and scaly or serous discharge, and itching requiring frequent and prolonged treatment *(frequent tropical/humid-deployment & hearing-aid-occlusion secondary claim!)*.
**`0%`** *(audit immediately for accompanying `DC 6100` conductive/mixed hearing loss, `DC 6200` chronic suppuration `10%`, `DC 6260` tinnitus `10%`, and `DC 6204` barotrauma vertigo `10%/30%`!)*.
**Complete loss of sense of smell (`6275` Anosmia)**; **Complete loss of sense of taste (`6276` Ageusia)**

**`10%` each** *(combinable as **`10% + 10%`** when both complete losses have an **anatomical or pathological basis**—classic post-TBI cribriform-plate CN I shearing [`DC 8045`], post-rhinosinusitis/polypectomy [`DC 6510–6522`], or burn-pit toxic rhinitis residual!)*.

blocks.text: 6. Regulatory Watchlist & Quarantine Notice (RIN 2900-AQ72 — Proposed / Not Finalized)

lines: **QUARANTINE NOTICE — DO NOT CITE AS ACTIVE LAW (AGENTS Law 6):**

* **`RIN 2900-AQ72` (`87 FR 8474`, published February 15, 2022 — Proposed Rule, Not Finalized):** VA published a controversial **proposed** rule (*Schedule for Rating Disabilities—Ear, Nose, Throat, and Audiology Disabilities...*) proposing to **eliminate `DC 6260` as a standalone `10%` compensable code** and instead evaluate tinnitus solely as a symptom within an underlying diagnosed disease (`0%` if underlying hearing loss is non-compensable!). Following massive Congressional and VSO opposition (and subsequent Unified Agenda deferrals), **proposed rule `RIN 2900-AQ72` (`87 FR 8474`) remains unfinalized and not enacted.** Standalone `DC 6260` (`10%`) remains **100% active binding law** for all claims and appeals. *(Note: Even if VA ever enacted a future final rule, any running `10%` `DC 6260` award in effect prior to that effective date would be statutorily grandfathered against reduction under `38 U.S.C. § 1155` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.951(a)`!).*

* **Rescinded `38 C.F.R. § 4.10` Medication IFR (`91 FR 7118`, Feb. 17, 2026 — Rescinded `91 FR 9712`, Feb. 27, 2026):** VA's reactive medication Interim Final Rule was **rescinded ab initio** after 10 days; under ***Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)`**, because `DC 6204` (vestibular vertigo) and `DC 6205` (Meniere's) are silent on medication, examiners and raters **cannot** discount baseline vertigo/staggering severity for ameliorative meclizine, scopolamine, diazepam, or diuretic therapy!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Hearing Loss, Tinnitus & Balance Guide: Table VIa Exceptions, Paired-Ear Rules & Lay Noise Evidence
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Because VA hearing ratings rely on strict audiometric lookup tables (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.85–4.87), many Veterans with significant difficulty hearing in noisy rooms receive 0% or 10% unless every table rule and related condition is checked. This guide explains how Veterans establish noise exposure and continuous ringing through military occupational specialty and lay statements (Jandreau / Fountain), when VA must switch from Table VI to the puretone-only Table VIa (§ 4.85(c) speech-test unreliability or § 4.86(a)–(b) steep high-frequency loss), when severe hearing loss in one service-connected ear plus hearing loss in the other non-service-connected ear unlocks bilateral 'paired-organ' compensation (38 U.S.C. § 1160(a)(3); 38 C.F.R. § 3.383(a)(3)), and how dizziness/vertigo and Meniere's syndrome are evaluated.
record_clues: A denial of service connection for hearing loss solely because your separation audiogram did not yet cross 38 C.F.R. § 3.385 decibel cutoffs despite documented in-service noise exposure or threshold shifts (Hensley v. Brown).

A denial of recurrent tinnitus (Diagnostic Code 6260) discounting your consistent lay reports of ringing since service simply because Service Treatment Records were silent (Charles v. Principi; Jandreau v. Nicholson; Fountain v. McDonald).

A post-December 6, 2002 unilateral service-connected ear compensable at 10% or more (Roman Numeral X or XI when paired with I on Table VII) alongside § 3.385 hearing loss in the opposite non-service-connected ear where VA failed to award bilateral paired-organ compensation under 38 C.F.R. § 3.383(a)(3).

An audiology report stating Maryland CNC speech recognition testing was unreliable due to a language barrier or cognitive/clinical factor while the rater still used Table VI instead of mandatory Table VIa (§ 4.85(c)).
important_cautions: No dual bilateral tinnitus rating: the Federal Circuit reversed the earlier Veterans Court ruling in Smith v. Nicholson (2006), confirming that only ONE 10% rating is authorized under Diagnostic Code 6260 in any era, whether tinnitus is in one or both ears.

Paired-organ hearing threshold: under 38 U.S.C. § 1160(a)(3) and 38 C.F.R. § 3.383(a)(3) (expanded effective December 6, 2002; Boyer v. West), paired-organ relief for a non-service-connected ear applies only when the service-connected ear is independently compensable at 10% or higher (Roman Numeral X or XI on Table VII when paired with I)—not when the service-connected ear is rated 0%.

Extraschedular limits on hearing loss: difficulty understanding speech in background noise or group settings is already contemplated by the rating tables (Doucette v. Shulkin), whereas distinct uncontemplated symptoms—such as ear pain, vertigo, or secondary mental health/sleep conditions—require separate evaluation.

Unfinalized and rescinded rules: VA's February 15, 2022 tinnitus proposal (RIN 2900-AQ72, 87 FR 8474) remains a proposed rule that is not enacted law, and VA's February 17, 2026 medication rule (91 FR 7118) was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712).
questions_for_representative: Do my puretone decibel thresholds at 1000, 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hz trigger Table VIa under 38 C.F.R. § 4.86(a) or the +1 Roman numeral step-up under § 4.86(b)?

headers: Substantive Change Across `§§ 4.88a–4.88c` & Linked Part 3 Presumptions
rows: Established Era-1 infectious, tropical, treponemal, nonpulmonary tuberculosis (`§§ 4.88c, 4.89`), nutritional (`DC 6313–6315`), and `DC 6350` Lupus schedules (`DC 6300–6350`).
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`< Aug. 30, 1996`):** Governs WWII/Korea/Vietnam tropical (`§ 3.309(b)`) and FPOW nutritional (`§ 3.309(c)`) historical rating audits.

**Created `38 C.F.R. § 4.88a` & `DC 6354` Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (`CFS`):** Codified the 3-prong diagnostic exclusion/6-of-10 clinical criteria in `§ 4.88a` and the `10%/20%/40%/60%/100%` disjunctive evaluation schedule in `DC 6354`.
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Nov. 29, 1994`):** Zero CUE reach for `DC 6354` prior to Nov. 29, 1994; plain-text disjunctive `"or"` violations on/after Nov. 29, 1994 are reviewable.

**First Comprehensive System 04 Overhaul (Era 2):** Retitled *"Infectious Diseases, Immune Disorders and Nutritional Deficiencies"*; enacted/modernized **`DC 6351` HIV-related illness**, **`DC 6319` Lyme disease**, **`DC 6320` Parasitic diseases**, **`DC 6350` SLE** (`Note` alternative residual rule), **`DC 6304` Malaria**, and **`DC 6313–6315`**.
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`Aug. 30, 1996 – Aug. 10, 2019`):** Governs Era-2 infectious, HIV, Lyme, SLE, and nutritional evaluations.

Enacted **`38 C.F.R. § 3.317(c)`**, establishing presumptive SC for **9 infectious diseases** (`Brucellosis`, `Campylobacter jejuni`, `Coxiella burnetii` [Q fever], `Malaria`, `Mycobacterium tuberculosis`, `Nontyphoid Salmonella`, `Shigella`, `Visceral leishmaniasis`, `West Nile virus`) in Southwest Asia (`>= Aug. 2, 1990`) and Afghanistan (`>= Sept. 19, 2001`), plus explicit long-term residual tables in `§ 3.317(d)`!

**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) / CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Sept. 29, 2010`):** Note that `6` of the `9` diseases require `>= 10%` manifestation within **1 year** of separation, whereas **Malaria (`6304`), Visceral leishmaniasis (`6301`), and Tuberculosis (`6730`/`6311`) have NO 1-year cap** under `§ 3.317(c)(3)`!

**Second Comprehensive System 04 Overhaul (Era 3):** Enacted the **General Rating Formula for Infectious Diseases** (`100%` active -> `0%` resolved + mandatory separate residual organ ratings); added **`DC 6312` (`NTM`)**, **`DC 6325` (Strongyloidiasis)**, **`DC 6326` (Schistosomiasis)**, and **`DC 6329–6335`** (`Hemorrhagic fevers/Dengue`, `Campylobacter`, `Q fever`, `Salmonella`, `Shigella`, `West Nile`); updated `DC 6314`, `6319`, `6351`, and `6354`.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Aug. 11, 2019`):** Pre-Aug. 11, 2019 running awards are protected against schedule-driven reduction under **`38 U.S.C. § 1155` & `§ 3.951(a)`**; straddling pending claims receive the more favorable Era-2 vs. Era-3 evaluation (*Karnas*).

**PACT Act Gulf War `CFS` Expansion:** Eliminated the `Dec. 31, 2026` manifestation deadline, lowered the `§ 1117` compensable threshold to **`"to any degree"` (`0%+`)**, and expanded `MUCMI` (`DC 6354` `CFS`, `DC 5025` Fibromyalgia, `DC 7319` FGID) geography to include **Afghanistan, Israel, Egypt, Turkey, Syria, and Jordan** ([Playbook 15](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera)).

blocks.text: 2. August 11, 2019 Overhaul (84 FR 28227): General Rating Formula & Complete Infectious Code Table (DC 6300–6335)
A. The General Rating Formula for Infectious Diseases (38 C.F.R. § 4.88b)
Effective **August 11, 2019 (`84 FR 28227`)**, VA replaced repetitive acute/inactive phrasing across most bacterial, viral, rickettsial, and parasitic codes with a single two-step architecture:

items: **For Active Disease:** **`100%`** evaluation.

**After Active Disease Has Resolved:** Rate at **`0%` for the infection**, AND **rate any residual disability that is attributable to the infection separately under the appropriate body system** (`38 C.F.R. § 4.88b`).

lines: **Post-Infection Residual Unbundling Mandate (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive >= Aug. 11, 2019):** When an acute tropical, tick-borne, foodborne, or Gulf War infection resolves to `0%` under `DC 6300–6335`, VA **cannot** stop at `0%` if chronic post-infectious sequelae persist! Every `DC 6300–6335` Note explicitly cross-references signature post-infectious organ damage (matching the presumptive residual table in **`38 C.F.R. § 3.317(d)`**), which must be separately coded and combined under `§ 4.25`.

blocks.text: 3. Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (38 C.F.R. § 4.88a & DC 6354): Diagnostic Gate & Disjunctive "Or" Goldmine
A. Strict Three-Prong Diagnostic Prerequisite (38 C.F.R. § 4.88a(a)(1)–(3))

Before a veteran can be rated under `DC 6354` (including as a **presumptive Gulf War `MUCMI` under `38 U.S.C. § 1117` / `38 C.F.R. § 3.317(a)(2)(i)(B)(1)`**), a valid diagnosis of **Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (`CFS` / `ME/CFS`)** for VA purposes requires **ALL THREE** elements:

items: **Six-Month `< 50%` Onset Threshold (`§ 4.88a(a)(1)`):** New onset of debilitating fatigue severe enough to reduce daily activity to **less than `50 percent`** of the usual level for **at least `6 months`** *(note: once diagnosed, current rating severity can fluctuate across `10%–100%` under `DC 6354`)*; **AND**

**Clinical Exclusion Gate (`§ 4.88a(a)(2)`):** Exclusion—by history, physical examination, and laboratory tests—of all other clinical conditions that may produce similar symptoms *(watch for C&P examiners lazily blaming fatigue on controlled hypothyroidism, CPAP-treated OSA, or mild depression without checking whether `CFS` post-exertional malaise, tender lymph nodes, sore throat, and migratory arthralgias exist independently!)*; **AND**

**At Least `6` of the `10` Listed Clinical Criteria (`§ 4.88a(a)(3)(i)–(x)`):** `(i)` acute onset of the condition; `(ii)` low-grade fever; `(iii)` nonexudative pharyngitis; `(iv)` palpable or tender cervical or axillary lymph nodes; `(v)` generalized muscle aches or weakness; `(vi)` **fatigue lasting `24 hours` or longer after exercise** *(post-exertional malaise)*; `(vii)` headaches (of a type, severity, or pattern different from the pre-morbid state); `(viii)` migratory joint pains; `(ix)` neuropsychologic symptoms; `(x)` sleep disturbance.

blocks.text: B. Primary-Source-Verified DC 6354 Schedule & The Disjunctive "Or" Trap

headers: Prong 1: Nearly Constant Routine Daily Activity Restriction
rows: Debilitating fatigue, cognitive impairments (such as inability to concentrate, forgetfulness, or confusion), or a combination of other signs and symptoms which are **nearly constant and so severe as to restrict routine daily activities almost completely and which may occasionally preclude self-care**.
*(No incapacitation-weeks alternative at `100%`; evaluate `SMC(l)` Aid & Attendance or *Bradley* `SMC(s)` whenever `100%` is met!)*
Nearly constant symptoms which **restrict routine daily activities to less than `50 percent` (`< 50%`) of the pre-illness level** *(i.e., `> 50%` loss of routine daily activity!)*
**OR** wax and wane, resulting in periods of incapacitation of **at least `6 weeks` (`>= 6 wks`) total duration per year**.
Nearly constant symptoms which **restrict routine daily activities from `50 to 75 percent` of the pre-illness level** *(i.e., a `25%–50%` restriction of routine daily activity!)*
**OR** wax and wane, resulting in periods of incapacitation of **at least `4` but less than `6 weeks` (`4 to < 6 wks`) total duration per year**.
Nearly constant symptoms which **restrict routine daily activities by less than `25 percent` (`< 25%` restriction) of the pre-illness level**
**OR** wax and wane, resulting in periods of incapacitation of **at least `2` but less than `4 weeks` (`2 to < 4 wks`) total duration per year**.
Wax and wane resulting in periods of incapacitation of **at least `1` but less than `2 weeks` (`1 to < 2 wks`) total duration per year**; **OR symptoms controlled by continuous medication**.

lines: **THE #1 `DC 6354` LITIGATION & CUE TRAP — Physician-Prescribed Bed Rest Is NOT Required for Prong 1 (`20%` / `40%` / `60%` / `100%`):**
* Under `DC 6354` **`Note`**, *"incapacitation exists only when a licensed physician prescribes bed rest and treatment"* (modern medicine rarely prescribes multi-week strict bed rest for `ME/CFS`!).

* RO raters routinely misread that `Note` to deny **`40%` or `60%`** whenever no doctor prescribed bed rest. Under ***Tatum v. Shinseki*, `23 Vet. App. 152 (2009)`**, the semicolon **`; or`** separating Prong 1 (*nearly constant restriction of routine daily activities to `< 50%` [`60%`] or `50–75%` [`40%`] of pre-illness level*) from Prong 2 (*waxing/waning incapacitation*) is **strictly disjunctive**! A veteran whose `CFS` DBQ or lay/clinical record establishes nearly constant debilitating fatigue and brain fog cutting routine daily activities below `50%` of pre-illness capacity is legally entitled to **`60%`** with **ZERO** days of prescribed bed rest!

* **Anti-Pyramiding (`§ 4.14`) Comorbidity Check:** Can a Gulf War veteran hold separate ratings for **`DC 6354` `CFS` + `DC 5025` Fibromyalgia (`10/20/40%`) + `DC 8100` Migraines + `DC 9411/9434` PTSD/Depression + `DC 6847` Sleep Apnea**? **YES**, so long as the medical examiner delineates which distinct manifestations support each code without counting the *exact same* fatigue/cognitive/sleep symptom twice (*Esteban v. Brown*, `6 Vet. App. 259 (1994)`; *Joyner v. McDonald*, `766 F.3d 1393 (Fed. Cir. 2014)`).

blocks.text: 4. Immune Disorders (DC 6350 Lupus & DC 6351 HIV) & FPOW Nutritional Deficiencies (DC 6313–6315)
A. Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (DC 6350): Flare Schedule vs. Multi-Organ Residual Math

Under **`DC 6350` Note** (`38 C.F.R. § 4.88b`), VA **MUST** calculate the veteran's disability under **BOTH** methods below and award **whichever method results in the HIGHER evaluation** (never combining `DC 6350` itself with SLE organ residuals or `DC 7809` Discoid Lupus):

items:
**Method A — `DC 6350` Exacerbation Tiers:**
• **`100%`:** Acute, with frequent exacerbations, producing severe impairment of health.
• **`60%`:** Exacerbations **lasting a week or more, `2 or 3 times` per year**.
• **`10%`:** Exacerbations **once or twice a year** OR symptomatic during the past `2 years`. *(Notice: `DC 6350` has **NO `30%` or `40%` tier**—jumping straight from `10%` to `60%`!)*

**Method B — Combined Multi-Organ Residual Stack (`§ 4.25`):** Combine separate evaluations across every affected organ system: **Lupus nephritis (`DC 7502`/`7530`: `30/60/80/100%`)** + **Inflammatory lupus polyarthritis (`DC 5002`/`5003` + `§ 4.26` bilateral factor)** + **Cutaneous/discoid lupus or systemic biologics (`DC 7809`/`7806` — belimumab/anifrolumab/azathioprine/mycophenolate = `60%` under `§ 4.118`!)** + **Pericarditis/pleuritis (`DC 7002`/`6845`)** + **Neuropsychiatric lupus (`DC 9326`/`9434` or seizures `8910`)** + **Autoimmune hemolytic anemia / `ITP` (`DC 7723`/`7705`)** + **Secondary Raynaud's phenomenon (`DC 7117`)** + **Hydroxychloroquine (`Plaquenil`) bull's-eye maculopathy (`§ 4.79`)**! Whenever Method B combines to `70%+`, `80%`, `90%`, or `100%` (+ *Bradley* `SMC(s)` when one organ hits `100%` and others hit `60%`!), Method B crushes a `60%` `DC 6350` flare rating!

blocks.text: B. HIV-Related Illness (DC 6351) & Modern Antiretroviral (ART) Strategy

items:
**Verbatim `DC 6351` Tiers (`84 FR 28227`):**
• **`100%`:** `AIDS` with recurrent opportunistic infections (`Note (3)` — *Pneumocystis*, *Toxoplasma*, `CMV`, `MAC`, cryptococcosis, Kaposi's sarcoma, etc.) OR secondary diseases afflicting multiple body systems; HIV-related illness with debility and progressive weight loss.
• **`60%`:** Refractory constitutional symptoms, diarrhea, and pathological weight loss; **OR minimum rating following development of any `AIDS`-related opportunistic infection or neoplasm**!
• **`30%`:** Recurrent constitutional symptoms, intermittent diarrhea, and use of approved medication(s) (`Note (1)` includes research-protocol medications at an accredited medical institution); **OR minimum rating with `T4` (`CD4`) cell count `< 200`**.
• **`10%`:** Following development of HIV-related constitutional symptoms; **`T4` cell count between `200 and 500`**; **use of approved `ART` medication(s)**; OR evidence of depression or memory loss with employment limitations.
• **`0%`:** Asymptomatic following initial HIV diagnosis, without approved medication (`T4 > 500`).

**Crucial `Note (2)` Alternative Stacking Rule:** In the modern `ART` era (`Biktarvy`, `Triumeq`, `Dovato`), most virally suppressed veterans have `CD4 > 500`, placing `DC 6351` alone at **`10%`** ("use of approved medication(s)" per `Note (1)`)—unless they **ever historically suffered an `AIDS`-defining opportunistic infection or neoplasm (`Note (3)`)**, which locks in a **permanent `60%` minimum floor**! Even more importantly, **`Note (2)`** directs raters to **separately evaluate definite secondary/opportunistic malignancies (`DC 7715` NHL `100%`), `ART`-induced tenofovir renal tubulopathy (`DC 7530`), osteoporosis/avascular necrosis (`DC 5013`/`5255`), peripheral neuropathy (`DC 8520`), chronic diarrhea, HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder (`DC 9301`), or major depressive disorder (`DC 9434` — `30%/50%/70%/100%` under `§ 4.130` instead of `10%` under `6351`!)** whenever separate ratings yield a higher combined evaluation!

blocks.text: C. FPOW Nutritional Deficiencies (DC 6313 Avitaminosis, DC 6314 Beriberi & DC 6315 Pellagra)

For **Former Prisoners of War (`FPOWs`)** (`38 U.S.C. § 1112(b)(2)–(3)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(c)` — `Avitaminosis`, `Beriberi` [including **beriberi heart disease**, which encompasses **any** POW who suffered localized edema during captivity!], `Pellagra`, and any other nutritional deficiency; [Playbook 07](/playbooks/07-statutory-presumptions-chronic-tropical-pow-als)):

items: **`DC 6313` Avitaminosis & `DC 6315` Pellagra (`10/20/40/60/100%`):** **`10%`** nonspecific anorexia/weight loss/weakness/irritability; **`20%`** stomatitis, achlorhydria, OR diarrhea; **`40%`** stomatitis + diarrhea + symmetrical dermatitis; **`60%`** all `40%` symptoms + mental symptoms & impaired bodily vigor; **`100%`** marked mental changes, moist dermatitis, inability to retain nourishment, exhaustion, and cachexia.

**`DC 6314` Beriberi (Thiamine `B1` Deficiency — Active vs. Chronic Residual Goldmine!):**
• **Active Disease:** **`100%`** congestive heart failure, anasarca, or **Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome**; **`60%`** cardiomegaly, OR peripheral neuropathy with footdrop or thigh/calf muscle atrophy; **`30%`** peripheral neuropathy with absent knee/ankle jerks and sensory loss, OR weakness/fatigue/leg stiffness.
• **Post-Captivity Chronic Residual Stacking (`Note`):** Rate chronic **"wet beriberi" cardiomyopathy/heart disease (`DC 7000/7020` under `§ 4.104`)** AND **"dry beriberi" bilateral lower/upper-extremity peripheral neuropathy (`DC 8520` + `§ 4.26` bilateral factor, plus `SMC(k)` if complete footdrop!)** **separately** under their respective body systems!

lines: **QUARANTINE NOTICE — DO NOT CITE AS ACTIVE LAW (AGENTS Law 6):**

* **Rescinded `38 C.F.R. § 4.10` Medication Interim Final Rule (`91 FR 7118`, Feb. 17, 2026 — Rescinded `91 FR 9712`, Feb. 27, 2026):** VA's February 2026 attempt to override ***Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)`** was **rescinded ab initio** after 10 days.

* **System 04 Impact:** While `DC 6354` `CFS` (`10%`) and `DC 6351` `HIV` (`10%`/`30%`) expressly mention continuous/approved medication in their lowest tiers (*cf. McCarroll v. McDonald*, `28 Vet. App. 267 (2016) (en banc)`), `DC 6354`'s **`20%`, `40%`, `60%`, and `100%` tiers** and **`DC 6350` Lupus** are **completely silent on medication**—meaning raters and examiners **cannot** discount unmedicated flare frequency (`DC 6350` on corticosteroids/immunosuppressants) or stimulant-masked fatigue (`DC 6354` on modafinil/Adderall) under *Ingram*!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Infectious Diseases, Immune Disorders & Nutritional Deficiencies: 2019 Overhaul, Chronic Fatigue & Former POW Rules
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: This comparison guide explains how VA rates infectious diseases, immune disorders, and nutritional deficiencies under 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.88a–4.88c (Diagnostic Codes 6300–6354) before and after the August 11, 2019 overhaul (84 FR 28227). Many infectious illnesses—including Southwest Asia and Afghanistan presumptive infections under 38 C.F.R. § 3.317(c), tick-borne Lyme disease, and Southeast Asia parasitic exposures like strongyloidiasis or schistosomiasis—receive 100% during active infection and then step to 0% once the acute infection clears, UNLESS VA separately evaluates lasting organ, nerve, joint, or fatigue residuals. Meanwhile, Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (Diagnostic Code 6354), Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (Diagnostic Code 6350), HIV-related illness (Diagnostic Code 6351), and Former Prisoner of War beriberi/pellagra/avitaminosis (Diagnostic Codes 6313–6315) each follow specialized multi-tier rules.
record_clues: Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (Diagnostic Code 6354) denied 40% or 60% for lack of physician-prescribed bed rest despite nearly constant fatigue, cognitive difficulty, and post-exertional malaise cutting routine daily activities to 50–75% (40%) or below 50% (60%) of pre-illness capacity.

A Gulf War or post-9/11 Veteran (including service in Afghanistan, Israel, Egypt, Turkey, Syria, or Jordan under PACT Act § 405) denied presumptive service connection for Chronic Fatigue Syndrome or one of the nine § 3.317(c) Southwest Asia/Afghanistan infectious diseases (such as Q fever, brucellosis, campylobacter, malaria, or West Nile).

A post-August 11, 2019 rating dropping Lyme disease (Diagnostic Code 6319), Q fever (Diagnostic Code 6331), or West Nile (Diagnostic Code 6335) to 0% without separately rating residual Bell's palsy, arthritis, neuropathy, heart inflammation, or post-infectious fatigue.

A Former Prisoner of War with history of malnutrition, edema, heart disease, or painful burning feet omitted from presumptive service connection for Beriberi (Diagnostic Code 6314), Pellagra (Diagnostic Code 6315), or Avitaminosis (Diagnostic Code 6313) under 38 C.F.R. § 3.309(c).
important_cautions: Lupus anti-stacking rule (Diagnostic Code 6350): VA cannot stack a 10%/60%/100% lupus flare evaluation ON TOP OF separate organ-system residual ratings or discoid lupus (Diagnostic Code 7809); VA must compare both rating methods and award whichever single method yields the higher combined rating.

Bed-rest rule vs. daily-activity rule in Diagnostic Code 6354: claiming 'incapacitating episodes' requires a licensed physician's prescription for both bed rest and treatment, whereas claiming 'nearly constant' daily-activity restriction (20%, 40%, or 60%) does not require prescribed bed rest.

Exact amendment dates apply: Diagnostic Code 6354 was added November 29, 1994 (59 FR 60902), and new codes Diagnostic Codes 6325–6335 and updated HIV/infectious formulas took effect August 11, 2019 (published June 18, 2019 at 84 FR 28227)—none of which can establish Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) before their effective dates.

VA's February 17, 2026 § 4.10 medication rule (91 FR 7118) was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712) and is not active law. Also remember 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c)'s limit of one final merits CUE decision per prior Board issue.
questions_for_representative: Under Diagnostic Code 6354 (Chronic Fatigue Syndrome), did VA evaluate my nearly constant restriction of routine daily activities separately from the prescribed-bed-rest prong?
Did VA separately rate every lasting joint, neurological, cardiac, liver, or fatigue residual after an active infectious disease stepped down to 0%?
For Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (Diagnostic Code 6350), have we compared the flare-frequency rating against combining my individual kidney, joint, skin, heart, or blood residuals?
If I served in Vietnam/Pacific theaters or as a Former POW, should we check tropical parasitic residuals (Diagnostic Codes 6325–6326) or nutritional presumptions (Diagnostic Codes 6313–6315)?

blocks.text: This Reference module catalogs the Federal Register transitions (`1946–2026`), Diagnostic Code (`DC 6502–6847`) evaluation schedules, anti-pyramiding boundaries (`38 C.F.R. § 4.96(a)`), pulmonary function test (`PFT`) discrepancy rules (`38 C.F.R. § 4.96(d)`), and ***George v. McDonough* (`596 U.S. 740 (2022)`) / `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`** bitemporal gates governing **Body System 05 (The Respiratory System)** under `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.96–4.97`.

*(For verbatim historical and current regulatory text of `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.96–4.97`, see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.96–4.97 Respiratory System, PFT Rules, Sinusitis, Rhinitis, Asthma, COPD & Sleep Apnea Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.96-4.97-respiratory-evolution) and [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.1–4.31 Subpart A General Rating Policy & Two-Era § 3.321(b)(1) Extraschedular Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.1-4.31-general-policy-snapshots); for Subpart A rating policy and analogous rating rules, see [`Subpart A General Rating Policy Diff`](/cfr/modules/subpart-a-general-rating-policy-4.1-4.31) and [Playbook 19 (`§ 4.20` Analogous & Extraschedular)](/playbooks/19-extraschedular-3.321b1-analogous-4.20-and-temp-total); for PACT Act `38 U.S.C. § 1120` / `38 C.F.R. § 3.320` burn-pit presumptions, see [Playbook 15 (Gulf War, Burn Pits, PACT & TERA)](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera) and [`Part 3 Toxic & PACT Evolution Diff`](/cfr/modules/toxic-gulf-pact-1151-evolution); for secondary Sleep Apnea via obesity under `VAOPGCPREC 1-2017`, see [Playbook 14 (Secondary SC, Aggravation & Obesity)](/playbooks/14-secondary-service-connection-aggravation-obesity); for *Nehmer* respiratory cancers, see [Playbook 06 (*Nehmer* Herbicide Class Claims)](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc); for cor pulmonale and cardiovascular cross-hooks, see [`System 06 Cardiovascular Diff`](/cfr/modules/06-cardiovascular-system-4.100-4.104), [VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon), and [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).*
1. Master Chronological Federal Register & Precedent Ledger (1946–2026)

rows: Established baseline `§§ 4.96–4.97` (`DC 6501–6821`): qualitative dyspnea/attack descriptors for bronchitis, asthma, emphysema, bronchiectasis, and active/inactive tuberculosis (`§§ 4.96(b)–(c)`). **No diagnostic code existed for Sleep Apnea.**
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`< Oct. 7, 1996`):** Governs all pre-Oct. 7, 1996 respiratory ratings; pre-1996 Sleep Apnea was rated by analogy (`§ 4.20`) under `DC 6800`, `6516`, or `8108`.

**Comprehensive Respiratory Overhaul:** First complete revision since 1945. Enacted **`§ 4.96(a)`** coexisting-rating bar (`DC 6600–6817` & `6822–6847`) with upper-airway (`6502–6524`) carve-out; introduced `FEV-1`/`FVC`/`DLCO(SB)` PFT schedules; modernized Sinusitis (`6510–6514`), Rhinitis (`6522–6524` `30%` polyps), Asthma (`6602` inhaler/steroid tiers), COPD (`6604`), Interstitial/Restrictive (`6825–6845`), Sarcoidosis (`6846`); and **created `DC 6847` Sleep Apnea Syndromes (`0/30/50/100%`)**.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Oct. 7, 1996`):** Plain-text misapplication of `§ 4.96(a)` (e.g., subsuming `DC 6510` or `6522` into `6602`/`6847`), ignoring `DC 6522` polyps (`30%`), or ignoring `DC 6602` daily inhaled steroids (`30%`) is undebatable CUE on/after Oct. 7, 1996. Zero CUE reach before Oct. 7, 1996.

`71 FR 28586` made technical updates to `§ 4.97`; **`71 FR 52457, 52459`** added **`38 C.F.R. § 4.96(d)(1)–(7)`** codifying when PFTs/DLCO/post-bronchodilator studies are required or excused, resolving PFT metric disparities (`(d)(6)`), and barring compensable `FEV-1/FVC` ratings when both `FEV-1` and `FVC` exceed `100%` (`(d)(7)`).
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Oct. 6, 2006` for `§ 4.96(d)(1)–(7)`):** Plain-text `§ 4.96(d)` PFT rules govern decisions rendered on or after Oct. 6, 2006.

Added particulate-matter presumptions (`§ 3.320` asthma, rhinitis, sinusitis within `10 yrs` -> `Pub. L. 117-168` removed `10-yr` window and added `11+` burn-pit respiratory conditions & respiratory cancers of any type at any time post-service) ([Playbook 15](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera)).
**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114)** (`§ 3.114(a)` / PACT Act effective-date rules; **excluded** from `§ 3.816` *Nehmer* except for herbicide-exposed Vietnam/covered respiratory cancers!).
Construed intervening AOJ sinusitis increases (*Murphy*), explicit-medication DCs (*McCarroll* vs. *Ingram*), `§ 4.96(a)` predominant-DC elevation (*Urban*), and `§ 4.20` analogous rating (*Webb*).
**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** on CUE against final decisions predating each judicial precedent (`38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`); fully retroactive on open/pending/AMA `§ 5104(b)` claims.

**QUARANTINED — Proposed / Not Finalized:** Proposed restructuring `DC 6847` Sleep Apnea around treatment efficacy (`0%/10%/50%/100%`), revising `DC 6522` rhinitis, and adding **`DC 6605` Constrictive Bronchiolitis** (`89 FR 74162`).
**ZERO legal force.** Existing Oct. 7, 1996 `§§ 4.96–4.97` criteria remain binding law (see Section 7).

blocks.text: 2. Two-Era Architectural Comparison: Pre- vs. Post-October 7, 1996 (61 FR 46720)

See [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.96–4.97 Respiratory System, PFT Rules, Sinusitis, Rhinitis, Asthma, COPD & Sleep Apnea Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.96-4.97-respiratory-evolution) for verbatim historical and current text.

headers: Era 2: October 7, 1996 – Present *(`61 FR 46720`, pub. Sept. 5, 1996)*
rows: Subjective clinical descriptors (*"mild," "moderate," "moderately severe," "severe"* dyspnea on exertion, cyanosis, frequency/severity of asthmatic paroxysms, purulent expectoration).

Objective **Pulmonary Function Testing (`PFT`)** (`FEV-1 % predicted`, `FEV-1/FVC` ratio, `DLCO(SB) % predicted`, `VO2 max` exercise capacity), outpatient oxygen, cor pulmonale/PH, or explicit **medication regimens** (`§ 4.96(d)`).

**No dedicated Diagnostic Code.** Rated by analogy (`38 C.F.R. § 4.20`)—most commonly `6899-6800` (anthracosis/pneumoconiosis), `6599-6516` (chronic laryngitis), or `8199-8108` (narcolepsy / petit mal epilepsy `DC 8911`).

Dedicated **`DC 6847`** (`Sleep Apnea Syndromes: Obstructive, Central, Mixed`): **`0%`** asymptomatic -> **`30%`** persistent daytime hypersomnolence -> **`50%`** requires breathing assistance device (`CPAP`) -> **`100%`** chronic respiratory failure w/ `CO2` retention, cor pulmonale, or tracheostomy.

Rated on frequency of *"characteristic asthmatic attacks"* (`10%` mild/infrequent; `30%` moderate w/ weekly/biweekly attacks; `60%` severe w/ frequent attacks & moderate dyspnea; `100%` pronounced w/ emphysema/right-heart strain).

Objective **disjunctive (`"or"`) matrix**: `FEV-1` (`10/30/60/100%`) **OR** `FEV-1/FVC` **OR** **medication tier** (`10%` intermittent bronchodilator; `30%` daily bronchodilator *or* inhaled anti-inflammatory; `60%` `>=3`/yr systemic steroid courses; `100%` daily high-dose systemic steroids).
Split across `DC 6600` (Bronchitis), `DC 6603` (Emphysema), and `DC 6601` (Bronchiectasis); no unified `DC 6604` COPD code.
Added **`DC 6604` (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease)** evaluated alongside `DC 6600` and `DC 6603` under the **General Rating Formula for `DC 6600, 6603, 6604`**.
Legacy active/arrested ratings (`DC 6701–6724`) + statutory graduated two-year `100%` -> `50%` -> `30%` protections for pre-Aug. 19, 1968 awards (`§ 3.959`, `§§ 4.96(b)–(c)`).

Retained `§§ 4.96(b)–(c)` savings rules for legacy TB while adding modern **`DC 6730` (Chronic pulmonary TB, active = `100%`)** and **`DC 6731` (Chronic pulmonary TB, inactive = residuals)** (`1-yr` active `100%` treatment rule under Note).
Broad anti-pyramiding warnings against combining bronchitis, bronchiectasis, asthma, and emphysema.

Codified exact **numerical range lock** in **`38 C.F.R. § 4.96(a)`**: bars combining `DC 6600–6817` and `6822–6847` (plus `6819–6820` when lung/pleura involved), **explicitly leaving `DC 6502–6524` outside the bar!**

blocks.text: 3. 38 C.F.R. § 4.96(a) Anti-Pyramiding Matrix vs. Upper-Respiratory Carve-Outs (CUE Goldmine)
A. Exact Scope of the § 4.96(a) Single-Rating Lock

Under [`38 C.F.R. § 4.96(a)`](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.96-4.97-respiratory-evolution), VA's categorical ban on combining coexisting respiratory ratings applies **strictly** to the Diagnostic Code ranges enumerated in the text (*Tropf v. Nicholson*, `20 Vet. App. 317, 320 (2006)`):

rows: Deviated septum (`6502`), Nasal loss (`6504`), **Sinusitis (`6510–6514`)**, Laryngitis (`6515–6516`), Laryngectomy/Aphonia (`6518–6519`), Stenosis (`6520`), Pharynx (`6521`), **Allergic/Bacterial/Granulomatous Rhinitis (`6522–6524`)**

**EXEMPT FROM `§ 4.96(a)`!** May be rated **separately** from each other AND **separately** alongside any lower-respiratory or Sleep Apnea code (`DC 6600–6847`), subject only to `38 C.F.R. § 4.14` against compensating the *exact same* symptom twice (*Esteban v. Brown*, `6 Vet. App. 259 (1994)`).
**`DC 6600–6817` & `DC 6822–6847`** *(Trachea/Bronchi, TB, Vascular, Mycotic, Interstitial, Restrictive, Sarcoidosis & Sleep Apnea)*

Bronchitis (`6600`), Bronchiectasis (`6601`), **Asthma (`6602`)**, Emphysema (`6603`), **COPD (`6604`)**, TB (`6701–6731`), Pulmonary Vascular (`6817`), Actinomycosis/Mycotic (`6822–6839`), **Interstitial (`6825–6833`)**, **Restrictive (`6840–6845`)**, **Sarcoidosis (`6846`)**, **Sleep Apnea (`6847`)**

**STRICTLY NON-COMBINABLE WITH EACH OTHER.** Assign **ONE single rating** under the DC reflecting the **predominant disability**, with **elevation to the next higher evaluation** where the severity of the overall respiratory disability warrants such elevation.
Lung/bronchial cancer, pleural mesothelioma (`6819`), laryngeal/tracheal/sinus carcinoma (`6819`), benign respiratory neoplasms (`6820`)

• **With lung or pleural involvement:** **Cannot** combine `6819` & `6820` with each other OR with `DC 6600–6817` / `6822–6847`. · • **WITHOUT lung or pleural involvement** *(e.g., upper-airway paranasal sinus or laryngeal neoplasm)*: **OUTSIDE** the `§ 4.96(a)` lower-lung combination bar!

lines: **High-Yield PACT Act Triple-Stacking Audit (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive):**
A Gulf War / Post-9/11 burn-pit veteran (`38 U.S.C. § 1120`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.320`) can lawfully hold **concurrent, separate schedular ratings** for:
1. **`DC 6510–6514` Chronic Sinusitis** (up to `50%` — facial pain/tenderness, headaches, purulent sinus discharge/antibiotics) **+**
2. **`DC 6522` Allergic/Vasomotor Rhinitis** (`30%` for nasal polyps or `10%` nasal passage obstruction) **+**

3. **ONE Lower/Sleep Code**—e.g., **`DC 6847` Sleep Apnea (`50%` CPAP)** *or* **`DC 6602` Asthma (`30%/60%`)** (merged into a single predominant lower-respiratory rating under `§ 4.96(a)`, e.g., `6847-6602` at `50%` or elevated to `100%` if warranted).

**Plain-Text CUE Trigger:** Whenever a post-Oct. 7, 1996 Rating Code Sheet subsumes `DC 6510–6514` Sinusitis or `DC 6522` Rhinitis into `DC 6602` Asthma or `DC 6847` Sleep Apnea by misreading `§ 4.96(a)` as covering *"all respiratory codes,"* attack the final decision via **RO CUE (`38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a)`)** (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive). Also note that **`DC 6732` (Pleurisy, tuberculous, active or inactive)** sits in the gap between `6817` and `6822`, and extrapulmonary manifestations of **`DC 6846` Sarcoidosis** (ocular, cutaneous, cardiac, neurologic) are rated separately outside `§ 4.96(a)`!

blocks.text: B. Controlling Precedent on Predominant-DC Elevation: *Urban v. Shulkin* (2017)

items: In ***Urban v. Shulkin*, `29 Vet. App. 82, 87–89 (2017)`**, a veteran service-connected for both **`DC 6847` Obstructive Sleep Apnea (`50%` CPAP)** and **`DC 6602` Asthma (`30%`)** argued he should be elevated from `50%` to `100%` (or `60%` under `DC 6602`). The CAVC held that `38 C.F.R. § 4.96(a)`'s phrase *"elevation to the next higher evaluation where the severity of the overall disability warrants such elevation"* is evaluated **using the criteria of the predominant Diagnostic Code alone** (there, `DC 6847`, whose next higher tier above `50%` is `100%` requiring chronic respiratory failure with `CO2` retention, cor pulmonale, or tracheostomy), rather than mixing criteria across non-predominant codes.

**Practitioner Takeaway:** When `DC 6847` (`50%`) and `DC 6602` (`60%` for `>=3` systemic steroid courses/yr) coexist, **`DC 6602` (`60%`) becomes the predominant disability**, and severe coexisting CPAP-dependent OSA can be argued on direct appeal to warrant elevation to `DC 6602`'s next higher tier (`100%`)—or referral under `38 C.F.R. § 3.321(b)(1)` / `§ 4.16(a)` TDIU ([Playbook 19](/playbooks/19-extraschedular-3.321b1-analogous-4.20-and-temp-total)). *(Note: Challenging a pre-2017 final decision based on *Urban* nuances is Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) under `§ 20.1403(e)`).*

blocks.text: 4. 38 C.F.R. § 4.96(d) Pulmonary Function Testing (PFT) & Discrepancy Rules

Subsection [`38 C.F.R. § 4.96(d)`](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.96-4.97-respiratory-evolution) governs PFT administration and metric selection across **`DC 6600, 6603, 6604` (COPD/Bronchitis/Emphysema)**, **`DC 6825–6833` (Interstitial Lung Disease)**, and **`DC 6840–6845` (Restrictive Lung Disease)** (and informs `DC 6602` spirometry):

items: **Mandatory `DLCO(SB)` Rule (`§ 4.96(d)(2)`):** If the `DLCO(SB)` (diffusion capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide by single-breath method) test is **not** in the record, evaluate on alternative criteria **only so long as the examiner states why `DLCO(SB)` would not be useful or valid** in that particular case. Omitting `DLCO(SB)` without that medical explanation renders a C&P exam legally inadequate on appeal!

**Post-Bronchodilator & `> 100%` Rules (`§ 4.96(d)(4)–(5), (7)`):** Post-bronchodilator studies are required unless pre-bronchodilator PFTs are normal or the examiner states why post-bronchodilator testing should not be done (`(d)(4)`). Evaluate using **post-bronchodilator** results *unless* post-bronchodilator results are **poorer** than pre-bronchodilator results, in which case pre-bronchodilator values govern (`(d)(5)`). Under `(d)(7)`, if **both `FEV-1` and `FVC` exceed `100%`**, do not assign a compensable rating based on a decreased `FEV-1/FVC` ratio.

**The Discrepancy Resolution Rule (`§ 4.96(d)(6)` — Major Remand/Audit Trigger):**
• Whenever a veteran's `FEV-1%`, `FEV-1/FVC`, `FVC%`, and `DLCO(SB)%` point to **different percentage tiers** (e.g., `FEV-1 = 72%` [`10%`], `FEV-1/FVC = 65%` [`30%`], and `DLCO(SB) = 51%` [`60%`]), **`§ 4.96(d)(6)` strictly forbids the rater or Board from mechanically picking the lowest (or highest) number on lay intuition**.
• Instead, VA **must** *"use the test result that the examiner states most accurately reflects the level of disability."* For emphysema (`DC 6603`) and interstitial fibrosis (`DC 6825`), alveolar-capillary gas-exchange impairment makes **`DLCO(SB)`** clinically superior to `FEV-1`; if the examiner left the DBQ rationale blank and the rater picked the lower `FEV-1`, remand/HLR for a `§ 4.96(d)(6)` opinion (or apply `§ 4.7` higher evaluation if both metrics are equally valid!).

blocks.text: B. Three High-Yield Sinusitis & Rhinitis Litigation Traps

items:
**"Radical Surgery" vs. "Repeated Surgeries" (`DC 6510–6514` `50%` Tier):**
• **Radical Surgery:** Refers to open, obliterative procedures—classically a **Caldwell-Luc radical antrostomy**, Lynch frontalethmoidectomy, or osteoplastic frontal sinus obliteration—paired with **chronic osteomyelitis**. Routine outpatient **Functional Endoscopic Sinus Surgery (`FESS`)**, balloon sinuplasty, septoplasty, or endoscopic polypectomy is **not** *"radical surgery"* on its own.
• **Repeated Surgeries (`>= 2` FESS/Endoscopic Procedures):** However, **two or more `FESS` or sinus procedures** satisfy **"repeated surgeries"** under the *second* `50%` pathway whenever the veteran continues to suffer *"near-constant sinusitis characterized by headaches, pain and tenderness of affected sinus, and purulent discharge or crusting"* (*Tropf v. Nicholson*, `20 Vet. App. 317 (2006)`; *cf. Williams v. Wilkie*, `30 Vet. App. 134, 138 (2018)` (applying ordinary dictionary meaning to undefined VASRD terms)).

**Incapacitating vs. Non-Incapacitating Episodes (`DC 6510–6514` Note):**
• Under the Sinusitis **Note**, an **"incapacitating episode"** strictly requires **bed rest AND treatment by a physician** (prescribed/directed bed rest + `4 to 6 weeks` of prolonged antibiotics for `10%/30%`). Most modern outpatient urgent-care prescriptions (`7–14 days` of amoxicillin-clavulanate or doxycycline without physician-prescribed bed rest) fail the *"incapacitating"* prong—so practitioners **must** pivot to the **non-incapacitating episode** pathway (`3–6/year = 10%`; **`> 6/year = 30%`**), proving frequency through competent lay flare-up logs, OTC nasal irrigation/steroid records, and clinical histories!
• Under ***Murphy v. Shinseki*, `26 Vet. App. 510, 514–16 (2014)`**, if an RO grants an intervening higher sinusitis rating while an appeal is pending, the Board errs if it ignores the intervening grant or effectively reduces an established sinusitis rating without complying with `38 C.F.R. § 3.344` material-improvement protections ([Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings)).

**Recurrent vs. Resected Polyps (`DC 6522`):** If a veteran has a history of `30%` nasal polyps removed via polypectomy (`FESS`), VA **cannot** reduce `DC 6522` from `30%` to `10%/0%` without `38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e)` 60-day notice and a post-surgical exam confirming sustained absence of recurrent polyps (especially given high polyp recurrence rates in burn-pit/aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease!).

blocks.text: B. Doctrinal Deep Dives: Medication Rules, Constrictive Bronchiolitis, CPAP & Respiratory Cancers

items:
**`DC 6602` Asthma & `DC 6846` Sarcoidosis vs. *Ingram v. Collins* (`2025`):**
• Because `DC 6602` (`10%/30%/60%/100%`) and `DC 6846` (`30%/60%`) **explicitly incorporate medication regimens into their evaluation tiers**, they fall within the ***McCarroll v. McDonald*, `28 Vet. App. 267 (2016) (en banc)`** carve-out rather than ***Jones v. Shinseki*, `26 Vet. App. 56 (2012)`** or ***Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)`**—meaning a veteran whose PFTs are normalized (`FEV-1 = 88%`) by a daily Advair/Symbicort inhaler receives **`30%`** based on the medication tier itself, rather than speculative unmedicated PFTs!
• Conversely, codes that are **silent on medication**—such as **`DC 6604` COPD**, **`DC 6825` Pulmonary Fibrosis**, and **`DC 6522` Rhinitis**—remain governed by *Ingram v. Collins* (VA's reactive Feb. 17, 2026 `§ 4.10` IFR at `91 FR 7118` was **rescinded ab initio** Feb. 27, 2026 at `91 FR 9712`).

**Constrictive (Obliterative) Bronchiolitis — Current `§ 4.20` Analogous Strategy (*Webb*):**
• Although **constrictive bronchiolitis** is an express burn-pit presumptive illness under **`38 U.S.C. § 1120(b)(2)(B)`** and `38 C.F.R. § 3.320`, VA's proposed dedicated **`DC 6605`** (`RIN 2900-AQ72`, `89 FR 74162`, Sept. 12, 2024 SNPRM) remains **proposed / not finalized**.
• Today, constrictive bronchiolitis is rated **by analogy (`38 C.F.R. § 4.20`)**—typically `6699-6600`, `6699-6604`, `6699-6602`, or `6899-6825`. Crucially, small-airways constrictive bronchiolitis often presents with **normal spirometry (`FEV-1 > 80%`)** despite crippling exertional dyspnea (`VO2 max <= 20 ml/kg/min` or air-trapping on high-resolution expiratory CT)! Under ***Webb v. McDonough*, `71 F.4th 1377 (Fed. Cir. 2023)`**, raters cannot mechanically assign `0%` solely because spirometry is normal when cardiopulmonary exercise testing (`CPET` / `VO2 max`), inhaled steroid therapy (`6699-6602`), or `§ 3.321(b)(1)` extraschedular criteria demonstrate severe functional loss ([Playbook 15](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera), [Playbook 19](/playbooks/19-extraschedular-3.321b1-analogous-4.20-and-temp-total)).

**`DC 6847` Sleep Apnea `50%` `"Requires Use of Breathing Assistance Device"` Nuances:**
• The `50%` threshold turns on **medical necessity**—documented when a treating sleep physician, pulmonologist, dentist, or C&P examiner **prescribes or certifies that a breathing assistance device is medically required** (`CPAP`, `BiPAP`, `APAP`, `ASV`, `Inspire` hypoglossal nerve stimulator, or a custom prescription **oral mandibular advancement device** prescribed specifically as a breathing-assistance alternative to CPAP!).
• If a device is medically required and prescribed, inability to tolerate the mask due to claustrophobia, PTSD nightmares, nasal obstruction (`DC 6522`), or aerophagia does **not** negate medical necessity so long as a clinician confirms the veteran still medically requires positive-airway/breathing-assistance therapy.
• **Secondary SC Workhorse:** Sleep Apnea (`DC 6847`) is **NOT** a PACT Act `§ 1120` presumptive condition—making secondary service connection (`38 C.F.R. § 3.310(a)–(b)`) to SC **`DC 6522` Rhinitis / `DC 6510` Sinusitis** (upper-airway nasal resistance!) or SC **PTSD / Orthopedic conditions via `VAOPGCPREC 1-2017` Obesity** one of the highest-volume pathways in Veterans Law ([Playbook 14](/playbooks/14-secondary-service-connection-aggravation-obesity)).

**`DC 6819` Malignant Neoplasms of the Respiratory System (Herbicide & PACT Presumptive Powerhouse):**
• **Presumptive Triggers:** Herbicide exposure (`38 U.S.C. § 1116` / `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(e)` — lung, bronchus, larynx, trachea cancers -> **full `§ 3.816` *Nehmer* class retroactivity**!) AND Burn-Pit/PACT exposure (`38 U.S.C. § 1120` — **respiratory cancer of any type** and **head cancer of any type**, including paranasal sinus, nasal cavity, pharyngeal, laryngeal, tracheal, bronchial, lung, and pleural mesothelioma!).
• **Mandatory `100%` + `6-Month` Post-Treatment Floor (`DC 6819` Note):** Assign **`100%`** during active malignancy or any surgical, X-ray, antineoplastic chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or radiation procedure, **continuing for `6 months` following cessation of treatment**. Thereafter, VA **MUST schedule a mandatory C&P examination** to determine residuals (`DC 6844` post-lobectomy/pneumonectomy PFTs, radiation fibrosis `DC 6825/6845`, `DC 6518` total laryngectomy `100% + SMC(k)`, dysphonia, painful thoracotomy scars `DC 7804`, or chemo peripheral neuropathy `DC 8520`) **AND issue `60-day` pre-reduction notice under `38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e)`** (*Foster v. McDonough*, `34 Vet. App. 338 (2021)`—note that while omitting the mandatory exam or `§ 3.105(e)` notice renders a reduction **void ab initio**, *Foster* held `§§ 3.343(a)/3.344` stabilized-rating rules do not apply to temporary cancer Note discontinuances) ([Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings))!

blocks.text: 7. Regulatory Watchlist & Quarantine (RIN 2900-AQ72 — Proposed / Not Finalized)

lines: **QUARANTINE NOTICE — DO NOT CITE AS ACTIVE LAW (AGENTS Law 6):**

* **`RIN 2900-AQ72` (`87 FR 8474`, published February 15, 2022 NPRM; and `89 FR 74162`, published September 12, 2024 Supplemental NPRM — Proposed Rules, Not Finalized):** VA published two **proposed / unfinalized** rulemakings that would:

1. Overhaul **`DC 6847` Sleep Apnea** to eliminate the automatic `50%` CPAP prescription rating for newly evaluated claims, replacing it with `0%` (asymptomatic with *or without* treatment—e.g., CPAP fully controls symptoms), `10%` (incomplete relief with treatment), `50%` (ineffective treatment *or* unable to use treatment due to **comorbid condition** with end-organ damage), and `100%`;
2. Overhaul **`DC 6522` Rhinitis** and **`DC 6510–6514` Sinusitis**; and
3. Add a standalone **`DC 6605` Constrictive Bronchiolitis** code (`89 FR 74162` SNPRM).

**Neither proposed rule (`87 FR 8474` nor `89 FR 74162` under unfinalized `RIN 2900-AQ72`) has been enacted as a Final Rule.** Existing `DC 6847` (`50%` CPAP), `DC 6522` (`30%` polyps), and `§ 4.20` analogous rating for constrictive bronchiolitis remain binding law—and even if finalized in the future, `38 U.S.C. § 1155` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.951(a)` prohibit reducing any veteran's existing running `50%` `DC 6847` rating based on a schedule revision unless the disability itself materially improves under the *former* criteria!

* **Rescinded `38 C.F.R. § 4.10` Medication IFR (`91 FR 7118`, Feb. 17, 2026 — Rescinded `91 FR 9712`, Feb. 27, 2026):** Rescinded *ab initio* after 10 days; audit any February 2026 respiratory decision that cited `91 FR 7118`.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Respiratory System Guide: Burn Pit Asthma/Sinusitis/Rhinitis, Sleep Apnea CPAP Rules & Coexisting Lung Ratings
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: With PACT Act burn-pit presumptions (38 U.S.C. § 1120; 38 C.F.R. § 3.320) making asthma, chronic rhinitis, chronic sinusitis, COPD, interstitial lung disease, sarcoidosis, and respiratory cancers presumptive for covered Gulf War and post-9/11 Veterans, accurate evaluation under 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.96–4.97 matters more than ever. This comparison explains how VA evaluates PFT breathing numbers vs. inhaler/steroid therapy, why nasal polyps on CT or endoscopy establish 30% under Diagnostic Code 6522 Rhinitis, why upper-airway nose/sinus ratings stack separately with lower-lung ratings, and how Obstructive Sleep Apnea (Diagnostic Code 6847) interacts with coexisting lung disease.
record_clues: A Rating Code Sheet subsuming Chronic Sinusitis (Diagnostic Codes 6510–6514) or Allergic Rhinitis (Diagnostic Code 6522) into Asthma (Diagnostic Code 6602) or Sleep Apnea (Diagnostic Code 6847).
Allergic or Vasomotor Rhinitis (Diagnostic Code 6522) rated at 0% or 10% despite a sinus CT scan or ENT nasal endoscopy documenting nasal polyps (which warrants 30%).
Obstructive Sleep Apnea (Diagnostic Code 6847) rated below 50% despite a medical prescription for a CPAP, BiPAP, APAP, or oral mandibular-advancement breathing assistance device.

Total laryngectomy (Diagnostic Code 6518) or complete organic aphonia / loss of speech (Diagnostic Code 6519) rated 100% without concurrent statutory Special Monthly Compensation (SMC(k) under 38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a)(6)).
important_cautions: Endoscopic sinus surgery vs. 'radical surgery': routine functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS), polypectomy, or turbinate reduction generally counts as 'repeated surgeries' rather than 'radical surgery' (open obliterative procedures like Caldwell-Luc) under Diagnostic Codes 6510–6514.

Medication rules differ by code: because Diagnostic Code 6602 (Asthma) explicitly builds bronchodilator and corticosteroid medication into its 10%, 30%, 60%, and 100% tiers, it follows its explicit medication text (McCarroll v. McDonald), whereas non-medication codes like Sinusitis or Rhinitis cannot be discounted for temporary medication relief (Ingram v. Collins).

Do not confuse proposed or rescinded rules with active law: RIN 2900-AQ72 (87 FR 8474 & 89 FR 74162, proposing revised sleep apnea CPAP rules and Diagnostic Code 6605 constrictive bronchiolitis) remains a proposed, unfinalized rule (not enacted law), and VA's February 17, 2026 § 4.10 medication rule (91 FR 7118) was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712).

Pre-October 7, 1996 decisions used older qualitative lung criteria rather than Diagnostic Code 6847 or modern PFT tables, and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c) limits Board Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) review to one final merits decision per prior Board issue.
questions_for_representative: Have my Sinusitis (antibiotic courses / incapacitating episodes), Rhinitis (nasal polyps or >50% nasal blockage), and Asthma/COPD/Sleep Apnea all been evaluated under their distinct upper- vs. lower-respiratory rules?
Does a sinus CT scan or ENT exam show nasal polyps warranting 30% under Diagnostic Code 6522?

If I have constrictive bronchiolitis or burn-pit lung injury with normal spirometry (FEV-1) but abnormal diffusing capacity (DLCO) or exercise limitation, did the examiner address DLCO under 38 C.F.R. § 4.96(d)?
If both Asthma and Sleep Apnea are service-connected, did VA consider elevating the single lower-respiratory rating to 60% or 100% under § 4.96(a) (Urban v. Shulkin)?
