McDonough* (`596 U.S. 740 (2022)`) / `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`** bitemporal boundaries governing **Body System 06 (The Cardiovascular System)** under `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.100–4.104`.

*(For verbatim multi-era regulatory text of `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.100–4.104`, see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.100–4.104 Cardiovascular System Evolution Across Three Eras (Pre-1998, 1998–2021 LVEF/METs & Post-Nov. 14, 2021 METs)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.100-4.104-cardiovascular-evolution), [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.105(d)–(i), 3.343, 3.344, 3.951, 3.953 & 3.957 (Rating Reductions, Stabilization & Statutory Protections)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.105e-3.344-3.951-3.957-reductions), and [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.1–4.31 Subpart A General Rating Policy & Two-Era § 3.321(b)(1) Extraschedular Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.1-4.31-general-policy-snapshots); for `DC 7005` Ischemic Heart Disease `§ 3.816` *Nehmer* class retroactivity, `DC 7101` PACT non-*Nehmer* rules, and `10 U.S.C. § 1413a` CRSC *Soto* recovery, see [Playbook 06 (*Nehmer* Herbicide Class Claims & CRSC)](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc); for FPOW heart/stroke presumptions (`§ 3.309(c)`) and 1-year chronic cardiovascular diseases (`§ 3.309(a)`), see [Playbook 07 (Statutory Presumptions & POW)](/playbooks/07-statutory-presumptions-chronic-tropical-pow-als); for void reductions of grandfathered `LVEF` ratings, see [Playbook 05 (Void Rating Reductions)](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings); for survivor DIC on IHD/hypertensive deaths, see [Playbook 08 (Survivor DIC)](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical); for cor pulmonale and pulmonary hypertension cross-hooks, see [`System 05 Respiratory Diff`](/cfr/modules/05-respiratory-system-4.96-4.97), [`Subpart A General Rating Policy Diff`](/cfr/modules/subpart-a-general-rating-policy-4.1-4.31), [VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon), and [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).*
1. Master Chronological Federal Register & Precedent Ledger (1946–2026)

rows: Established Era-1 qualitative heart ratings (`DC 7000–7017` — congestive heart failure, angina on mild/ordinary exertion, cardiac hypertrophy/dilatation, NYHA functional equivalents), `DC 7101` Hypertension, `DC 7114` Arteriosclerosis obliterans, and `DC 7122` *"Residuals of frozen feet."*
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`< Jan. 12, 1998`):** Governs pre-1998 CUE audits and **pre-Jan. 12, 1998 staged periods** in retroactive *Nehmer* Footnote 1 & 2 `DC 7005` IHD awards!

**First Major Cardiovascular Overhaul (Era 2):** Replaced qualitative heart criteria with objective **`METs`**, **`LVEF`** (`<30% = 100%`; `30%–50% = 60%`), acute/chronic **CHF**, and **ECG/echocardiogram/X-ray cardiac hypertrophy or dilatation (`30%`)** + `10%` continuous medication; enacted `§ 4.100(a)–(c)` testing mandates; removed old `§§ 4.101–4.102`; modernized `DC 7101` (`160/100` + Note (1)) & `DC 7114` (`ABI` + claudication yards).

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`Jan. 12, 1998 – Nov. 13, 2021`):** Massive CUE goldmine whenever an Era-2 decision assigned `10%` (`>7 METs`) despite an echocardiogram/ECG in the record showing `LVEF 30%–50%` (`60%`), `LVEF <30%` (`100%`), or `LVH` (`30%`)! Zero CUE reach before Jan. 12, 1998.

**Overhauled `DC 7122` Cold Injury Residuals:** Retitled from *"Residuals of frozen feet"* to *"Cold injury residuals"* covering **any exposed part** (each hand, each foot, ears, nose — `10%/20%/30%` **per part** + `§ 4.26` bilateral factor) + Note (1) mandatory separate ratings for peripheral neuropathy, amputations, and scar carcinoma.
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Aug. 13, 1998`):** Bundling bilateral cold-injured feet/hands into a single rating or omitting Note (1) neuropathy on/after Aug. 13, 1998 is plain-text CUE.

Added **Ischemic Heart Disease (`IHD` — `DC 7005` & coronary/ischemic equivalents)** to `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(e)` herbicide presumptions, triggering full **`38 C.F.R. § 3.816` *Nehmer* Footnote 1 & 2 retroactivity** back to prior denied/inferred claims (extended to Blue Water Navy Jan. 1, 2020 via `Pub. L. 116-23`).

**Nehmer Retroactive Herbicide (§ 3.816) & CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive:** Requires multi-era staged ratings across Era 1 (`< 1998`), Era 2 (`1998–2021`), and Era 3 (`>= Nov. 14, 2021`) ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc)).

Held that because `DC 7101` (`10%`) expressly contemplates continuous antihypertensive medication, *Jones v. Shinseki* anti-mitigation rules do not entitle a medicated veteran with controlled BP to `20%+`.
**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** / adverse ceiling barring *Ingram* arguments above `10%` under `DC 7101`.

**Second Major Cardiovascular Overhaul (Era 3):** Enacted unified **General Rating Formula for Diseases of the Heart** (`DC 7000–7007, 7015–7017, 7019–7020`), **eliminating standalone `LVEF` (`<30%` / `30–50%`), standalone `CHF` episode counts, and `ECG`/`X-ray` hypertrophy** (retaining `30%` hypertrophy *only* when confirmed by **echocardiogram, MRI, or MUGA**); rewrote `DC 7009` bradycardia, `DC 7010` SVT (`>=5` vs. `1–4` interventions/yr), `DC 7114` PAD (`ABI`/`AP`/`TP`/`TcPO2` + `86 FR 62095` Note (2)), `DC 7008` hyperthyroid heart, and added `DC 7124` Raynaud's disease.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Nov. 14, 2021`):** Existing pre-Nov. 14, 2021 `LVEF` ratings are **statutorily grandfathered** under `38 U.S.C. § 1155` / `§ 3.951(a)`; claims pending across Nov. 14, 2021 receive Era-2 `LVEF`/`ECG` staged ratings prior to Nov. 14, 2021 and whichever schedule is more favorable from Nov. 14, 2021 forward if continuously pending (*Karnas* / `86 FR 54089` applicability clause).
Added **Hypertension (`DC 7101` / `DC 7007`)** as a herbicide presumptive condition for Vietnam, Thai, Korean DMZ, Johnston Atoll, Guam, C-123, and Blue Water Navy veterans.

**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (`>= Aug. 10, 2022`):** **NOT** a `§ 3.816` *Nehmer* class condition (`M21-1 VIII.i.2.B.1.c`), though PACT `§ 1305` / `§ 3.33` unlocks retroactive survivor DIC re-evaluations!

blocks.text: 2. Three-Era Heart Disease Evolution (DC 7000–7007, 7015–7020): 1946 vs. 1998 vs. 2021

See [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.100–4.104 Cardiovascular System Evolution Across Three Eras (Pre-1998, 1998–2021 LVEF/METs & Post-Nov. 14, 2021 METs)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.100-4.104-cardiovascular-evolution) for verbatim Era-1, Era-2, and Era-3 regulatory text.
A. Side-by-Side Structural & Threshold Matrix

headers: Era 1: `Apr. 1, 1946 – Jan. 11, 1998` *(1945 VASRD / `29 FR 6718` — Crucial for Pre-1998 *Nehmer* `DC 7005`!)*
rows: Code-by-code schedules (`DC 7000` Rheumatic, `7005` Arteriosclerotic/CAD, `7007` Hypertensive heart, `7015` AV block, `7016` Valve prosthesis, `7017` CABG).
Identical disjunctive criteria repeated under `DC 7000–7007, 7015–7017, 7020` + `§ 4.100(a)–(c)` testing mandates.
Unified **General Rating Formula for Diseases of the Heart** (`DC 7000–7007, 7015–7017, 7019–7020`, plus residual pathways of `7009, 7011, 7018`).

• **During & for `6 months` following acute illness from coronary occlusion or thrombosis (`DC 7005`)**, **OR** · • **Congestive heart failure**, OR angina/dyspnea at rest or on slightest exertion (*NYHA Class IV* — cold/bed/chairbound).

• **Chronic congestive heart failure (`CHF`)**, **OR** · • Workload of **`3 METs or less`** results in dyspnea, fatigue, angina, dizziness, or syncope, **OR** · • **Left ventricular dysfunction with an ejection fraction (`LVEF`) of less than `30 percent` (`< 30%`)**! *(Plus `3-month` `100%` post-MI [`7006`] or post-CABG [`7017`]!)*

• Workload of **`3.0 METs or less`** results in **heart failure symptoms** *(breathlessness, fatigue, angina, dizziness, arrhythmia, palpitations, or syncope)*. · *(**DELETED:** Standalone `LVEF < 30%` and standalone `"chronic CHF"`! Acute `3-month` `100%` post-MI [`7006`] & post-CABG [`7017`] and `1-yr` transplant [`7019`] retained under specific DCs).*

Following typical coronary occlusion/thrombosis, OR with history of **substernal anginal pain on mild exertion** / *NYHA Class III* marked limitation of physical activity (less than ordinary activity causes dyspnea, fatigue, or angina).

• **More than one (`> 1`) episode of acute congestive heart failure (`CHF`) in the past year**, **OR** · • Workload of **`> 3 METs` to `5 METs`** results in dyspnea, fatigue, angina, dizziness, or syncope, **OR** · • **Left ventricular dysfunction with an ejection fraction (`LVEF`) of `30 to 50 percent` (`30%–50%`)**!
• Workload of **`3.1–5.0 METs`** results in **heart failure symptoms**. · *(**DELETED:** Standalone `LVEF 30%–50%` and `> 1` episode of acute CHF in past year!)*

Following typical coronary occlusion/thrombosis with **definite medication/activity restriction**, OR **definite cardiac enlargement (hypertrophy or dilatation)** with characteristic anginal/dyspneic symptoms on ordinary exertion (*NYHA Class II*).

• Workload of **`> 5 METs` to `7 METs`** results in dyspnea, fatigue, angina, dizziness, or syncope, **OR** · • **Evidence of cardiac hypertrophy or dilatation on electrocardiogram (`ECG`), echocardiogram, or X-ray**!

• Workload of **`5.1–7.0 METs`** results in heart failure symptoms, **OR** · • **Evidence of cardiac hypertrophy or dilatation confirmed by echocardiogram or equivalent** *(e.g., multigated acquisition scan [`MUGA`] or cardiac `MRI` — **ECG and chest X-ray proof DELETED!**)*.
Mild CAD / post-anginal history with minimal functional limitation (*NYHA Class I–II*).

• Workload of **`> 7 METs` to `10 METs`** results in dyspnea, fatigue, angina, dizziness, or syncope, **OR** · • **Continuous medication required** *(e.g., daily beta-blocker, ACE inhibitor, ARB, statin/antianginal nitrate/ranolazine/P2Y12 antiplatelet for CAD)*.
• Workload of **`7.1–10.0 METs`** results in heart failure symptoms, **OR** · • **Continuous medication required for control**.

**`§ 4.100(a)`:** Must ascertain hypertrophy/dilatation & continuous meds. · **`§ 4.100(b)`:** Exercise `METs` mandatory unless contraindicated, `100%` assignable on another basis, or medically estimated. · **`§ 4.100(c)`:** If `LVEF` not of record, examiner must state whether needed.

**`§ 4.100(a)–(b)` (`86 FR 67654`):** **Removed `§ 4.100(c)` (`LVEF`)**! Retains `METs` testing or examiner interview-based `METs` estimation (`1 MET = 3.5 ml O2/kg/min`) when exercise testing is medically contraindicated (e.g., unstable angina, orthopedic/amputation inability to walk treadmill).

blocks.text: B. Three Multi-Six-Figure Audit & Litigation Goldmines Across the Three Eras

items:
**The `1998–2021` `LVEF` & `ECG/X-Ray LVH` CUE Goldmine (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive):**
• Between **January 12, 1998 and November 13, 2021**, VA cardiac DBQs routinely recorded interview-estimated `> 7–10 METs` (`10%`) for veterans on cardiac meds while VAMC cardiology notes, nuclear stress tests (`SPECT`/`MUGA`), catheterizations, chest X-rays, `12-lead ECGs` (*Sokolow-Lyon / Cornell voltage LVH*), or transthoracic echocardiograms in the C-file (or constructively in VAMC records under *Bell v. Derwinski*) documented:
• **`LVEF < 30%`** -> Mandatory **`100%`** (+ check *Bradley* `SMC(s)` statutory housebound!);
• **`LVEF 30%–50%`** (e.g., `LVEF 45%` or `"45–50%"` under `§ 4.7` / `§ 4.3`!) -> Mandatory **`60%`**; or
• **Left ventricular hypertrophy (`LVH`) or chamber dilatation** on **ECG, chest X-ray, or echo** -> Mandatory **`30%`**.
• Because the Era-2 criteria were strictly **disjunctive (`"or"`)** (*Tatum v. Shinseki*, `23 Vet. App. 152 (2009)`), assigning `10%` based on `METs` when `LVEF 45%` or `LVH` was undisputedly in the record is **undebatable plain-text RO CUE (`38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a)`)**!

**Transitional Protection (`38 U.S.C. § 1155` / `§ 3.951(a)`) & Straddling Claims (`Nov. 14, 2021`):**
• **Running Pre-Nov. 14, 2021 Ratings Cannot Be Reduced by the Rule Change:** Under **`38 U.S.C. § 1155`** and **`38 C.F.R. § 3.951(a)`**, no readjustment of the VASRD may be used to reduce any veteran's disability rating in effect on the effective date (`Nov. 14, 2021`) unless actual medical improvement is proven **under the *prior* (`1998–2021`) criteria** (e.g., proving `LVEF` actually improved above `50%` on sustained examination under `§ 3.344`!). Any post-2021 reduction of a grandfathered `60%` (`LVEF 40%`) rating to `10%` based solely on `> 7 METs` is **void ab initio** ([Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings)).
• **Pending Claims Straddling Nov. 14, 2021:** Under the `86 FR 54089` applicability clause and *Karnas v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 308 (1991)`, any claim filed *before* November 14, 2021 and pending on/after that date **must** be evaluated under Era-2 (`LVEF` / `CHF` / `ECG LVH`) for all periods prior to Nov. 14, 2021, and retains the higher Era-2 evaluation from Nov. 14, 2021 forward unless Era-3 criteria yield an even higher rating!

**Contraindicated Exercise `METs` Testing & Non-SC Orthopedic Confounders:**
• When SC knee/spine disability or amputation prevents treadmill testing, the examiner estimates cardiac `METs` from clinical interview of daily activities (`1 MET = sitting quietly; 3 METs = light housework/slow flat walking; 5 METs = climbing 1 flight of stairs/light yardwork; 7 METs = jogging/carrying heavy loads`). Watch for DBQ examiners erroneously writing `"No METs limit"` when the veteran avoids exertion *because* of angina/dyspnea, or conversely confusing orthopedic pain with cardiac dyspnea—demand a pharmacologic nuclear stress test + cardiology interview isolating **cardiac-symptom-limited `METs`**!

blocks.text: 3. Arrhythmias, Pacemakers, AICDs, Valves & Transplants (DC 7008–7020)

headers: Post-Nov. 14, 2021 (`86 FR 54089`) Rating Schedule & Era-2 Diffs
rows: **`100%`** during and for **`3 months`** following acute MI documented by laboratory markers/ECG; thereafter rate residuals under the **General Rating Formula for Diseases of the Heart** (mandatory C&P exam!).

**Post-Nov. 14, 2021 (`86 FR 54089`):** Rate under the **General Rating Formula for Diseases of the Heart** *(eliminated the quirky pre-2021 cross-reference to `DC 7900` hyperthyroidism when atrial fibrillation was present; cross-check `§ 4.14` against `DC 7900`!).*

**Added/Rewritten Nov. 14, 2021 (`86 FR 54089`):** **`100%`** for **`1 month`** following hospital discharge for implantation or re-implantation of an implantable cardiac pacemaker; thereafter evaluate under the **General Rating Formula for Diseases of the Heart** (*asymptomatic physiological bradycardia in athletes is non-compensable per Note*).
**Supraventricular tachycardia (`SVT`)** *(Includes **Atrial Fibrillation**, Atrial Flutter, AVNRT, WPW, Sinus Tachycardia!)*

• **Era 2 (`1998–2021`):** `30%` for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation or other SVT with **`> 4` episodes/yr** documented by ECG/Holter; `10%` for **permanent atrial fibrillation** (lone AFib) OR **`1–4` episodes/yr** documented by ECG/Holter. · • **Era 3 (`Nov. 14, 2021–Present`, `86 FR 54089`):** ·   – **`30%`:** Confirmed by ECG, with **`5 or more` (`>= 5`) treatment interventions per year**. ·   – **`10%`:** Confirmed by ECG, with **`1 to 4` treatment interventions per year**; **OR** confirmed by ECG with **either continuous use of oral medications to control** *(e.g., metoprolol, diltiazem, flecainide, amiodarone, sotalol)* **or the use of vagal maneuvers to control**. ·   – **Crucial Note (2) Trap:** A `"treatment intervention"` requires **IV pharmacologic adjustment, electrical/chemical cardioversion, and/or catheter ablation** for symptom relief! Thus, frequent self-resolving paroxysmal AFib episodes (>4/yr) without ER/hospital IV drugs, cardioversion, or ablation dropped from `30%` (Era 2) to `10%` (Era 3)—**audit grandfathered pre-Nov. 14, 2021 `30%` `DC 7010` ratings against unlawful reductions!** *(Also rate secondary anticoagulation strokes under `DC 8007–8009` or heart-failure cardiomyopathy under `DC 7020` if higher!)*

**Automatic `100%`:** For an **indefinite period** from date of inpatient hospital admission for initial medical therapy for sustained ventricular arrhythmia; **OR** for an indefinite period from hospital admission for ventricular aneurysmectomy; **OR** **with an automatic implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (`AICD`) in place!** · *(Mandatory C&P exam `6 months` post-discharge ONLY when NO `AICD` is in place; **so long as an `AICD` remains implanted, `100%` is locked in**—plus audit immediately for *Bradley* `SMC(s)`!)*

Benign (`1st-degree` or `Mobitz Type I / Wenckebach`) -> **General Rating Formula**; Non-benign (`Mobitz Type II` or `3rd-degree` complete heart block) -> **`DC 7018`** *(Note circular cross-reference in verbatim `§ 4.104`: `DC 7015` routes non-benign AV block to `DC 7018`, while `DC 7018` routes post-1-month residuals back to `DC 7010`, `7011`, or `7015` with a `10%` minimum—always demand evaluation under the **General Rating Formula** whenever `METs` `<= 7.0` or echo hypertrophy exceeds `10%`!)*.

• **`7016`:** **`100%`** for **`6 months`** post-hospital discharge for prosthetic valve implantation/replacement -> thereafter **General Formula** (mandatory C&P exam + `§ 3.105(e)` 60-day notice per *Foster v. McDonough*, `34 Vet. App. 338 (2021)`, though `§§ 3.343/3.344` do not apply to temporary post-surgical discontinuances). · • **`7017`:** **`100%`** for **`3 months`** post-hospital discharge for `CABG` -> thereafter **General Formula**. *(Note: Routine percutaneous coronary stenting/`PCI` without acute `MI` does NOT trigger `7017`'s 3-month `100%`, unless hospitalized `> 21 days` under `§ 4.29` or accompanied by acute `MI` under `DC 7006`!)*

**`100%`** for **`1 month`** following hospital discharge for implantation or re-implantation (*reduced from `2 months` in Era 2 via `86 FR 54089`!*). Thereafter evaluate as `DC 7010`, `7011`, or `7015` (with **General Rating Formula** fallback when cardiac workload/hypertrophy is higher), with a **MANDATORY MINIMUM `10%` evaluation** (`AICD` or combined CRT-D defibrillator/pacemaker MUST be rated at **`100%` under `DC 7011`**, NOT `10%` under `DC 7018`!).

**`100%`** for a **minimum of `1 year`** from date of hospital admission for cardiac transplantation; thereafter evaluate under the **General Rating Formula** with a **MANDATORY MINIMUM `30%` evaluation** (mandatory C&P exam!).
Evaluated under the **General Rating Formula for Diseases of the Heart** (`30%` minimum whenever echocardiogram/MRI confirms ventricular hypertrophy or chamber dilatation!).

blocks.text: 4. Hypertensive Vascular Disease (DC 7101) vs. Hypertensive Heart Disease (DC 7007)
A. DC 7101 Schedule & Note (1)–(3) Traps (38 C.F.R. § 4.104)

rows: *"Predominantly"* looks to the preponderance/majority pattern of readings across the rating period—raters cannot cherry-pick a single normal clinic BP to defeat predominantly elevated outpatient/VAMC readings.
Systolic pressure alone maxes out at **`20%`** under `DC 7101` (`>= 200`); `40%` and `60%` require diastolic elevation (`>= 120` / `>= 130`).
Diastolic pressure **predominantly `110` or more**, **OR** systolic pressure **predominantly `200` or more**
Isolated systolic hypertension (`>= 200` mmHg) reaches **`20%`** even when diastolic pressure is `< 100`.

Diastolic pressure **predominantly `100` or more**, **OR** systolic pressure **predominantly `160` or more**, **OR** minimum evaluation for an individual with a **history of diastolic pressure predominantly `100` or more who requires continuous medication for control**

• **Note (1) Initial-Diagnosis-Only Rule:** Hypertension or isolated systolic hypertension must be confirmed by readings taken **`2 or more times` on at least `3 different days`** *to establish initial diagnosis for SC*. Once SC is granted, VA **cannot** demand 3-day multi-reading confirmation on increased-rating exams! · • ***McCarroll v. McDonald*, `28 Vet. App. 267 (2016) (en banc)`:** Because `DC 7101`'s `10%` tier **explicitly addresses continuous medication**, *Jones v. Shinseki* (`26 Vet. App. 56`) and *Ingram v. Collins* (`38 Vet. App. 130`) do **not** apply to award `20%+` based on speculative unmedicated blood pressure. Conversely, if pre-medication STRs or historical medical records show diastolic readings predominantly `>= 100` and the veteran now takes lisinopril/amlodipine, **`10%` is guaranteed** even if current medicated BP is `118/74`! *(Rescinded Feb. 2026 `§ 4.10` IFR `91 FR 7118` — rescinded `91 FR 9712` — did not alter `DC 7101`).*
Diagnosed SC hypertension (`>= 140/90` on 3 days, or medicated without historical diastolic `>= 100` or current `>= 160/100`)
Still unlocks **massive secondary SC & survivor DIC value** (see Pivot below)!

blocks.text: B. The DC 7101 -> DC 7007 Upgrade Pivot & Secondary End-Organ Cascade

items:
**Mandatory Upgrade Pivot (`DC 7101` Note (2) & (3)):** Because most medicated veterans with `DC 7101` Hypertension are capped at `0%` or `10%` under *McCarroll*, **every `DC 7101` audit MUST check VAMC imaging and labs for end-organ damage**:
• **`DC 7007` Hypertensive Heart Disease (`30%` / `60%` / `100%`):** The instant an echocardiogram or cardiac MRI confirms **concentric left ventricular hypertrophy (`LVH`) or left atrial/ventricular dilatation** (a textbook consequence of chronic hypertension!), or cardiac symptoms occur at `<= 7.0 METs`, the veteran qualifies for **`30%` (or `60%/100%`) under `DC 7007` Hypertensive Heart Disease**! Under **`DC 7101` Note (3)** (`71 FR 52460`), *"Evaluate hypertension separately from hypertensive heart disease and other types of heart disease"* (*DeLisio v. Shinseki*, `25 Vet. App. 45 (2011)` scope of claim; Note (2) merges secondary isolated systolic hypertension into aortic insufficiency or hyperthyroidism).
• **Secondary Renal Dysfunction (`DC 7502` / `7530` Hypertensive Nephropathy):** Evaluate secondary hypertensive kidney disease **separately** (`30%`–`100%` under post-Nov. 14, 2021 `eGFR` / albuminuria criteria)!
• **Secondary Cerebrovascular Stroke (`DC 8007–8009`):** **`100%`** for 6 months + neurological/speech/extremity residuals (`10%` minimum; [System 13 Diff](/cfr/modules/13-neurological-tbi-nerves-4.120-4.124a)).
• **Secondary Hypertensive Retinopathy (`DC 6006`) & Erectile Dysfunction (`DC 7522` + `SMC(k)`):** Antihypertensive beta-blockers/thiazides and vascular endothelial damage routinely cause compensable `SMC(k)` loss of use of a creative organ!

**PACT Act `§ 404` vs. *Nehmer* Trap:** Remember that **`DC 7005` Ischemic Heart Disease** (`75 FR 53202`) **IS** a `38 C.F.R. § 3.816` *Nehmer* condition (paying decades of retroactive back pay + `10 U.S.C. § 1413a` CRSC uncapped under *Soto v. United States*, `605 U.S. 360 (2025)`!), whereas **PACT Act `§ 404` Hypertension (`DC 7101`)** is **excluded** from `§ 3.816` *Nehmer* retroactivity (`>= Aug. 10, 2022` liberalizing effective date under `§ 3.114(a)`, except for PACT `§ 1305` survivor DIC re-evaluations) ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc), [Playbook 08](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical)).

blocks.text: 5. Diseases of the Arteries & Veins: Aneurysms (DC 7110), PAD (DC 7114), Varicose Veins (DC 7120) & Cold Injury (DC 7122)
A. Peripheral Arterial Disease (DC 7114, DC 7115 Buerger's, DC 7117 Raynaud's Phenomenon vs. DC 7124 Raynaud's Disease)

On **November 14, 2021 (`86 FR 54089`)**, VA replaced Era-2 subjective claudication yardage (`<25 yds` / `<100 yds`) in **`DC 7114` Peripheral Arterial Disease (`PAD`)** (and cross-referenced `DC 7115` Thromboangiitis obliterans) with **four objective vascular hemodynamic metrics**—with **`Note (2)` formally corrected on November 9, 2021 at `86 FR 62095, 62096` (eff. Nov. 14, 2021)** so examiners do *not* falsely assign `0%` when calcified arteries skew `ABI`:

rows: Ischemic limb pain at rest, **OR** deep ischemic ulcers/trophic changes + **`ABI <= 0.4`**.
Claudication at **`< 25 yards`** on level grade at 2 mph + persistent coldness/trophic changes **OR** **`ABI <= 0.5`**.
Claudication on walking **`> 100 yards`**, diminished peripheral pulses, **OR** **`ABI <= 0.9`**.

lines: **Critical `DC 7114`, `DC 7110` & Raynaud's Audit Rules (`86 FR 54089` & `86 FR 62095`):**

1. **Diabetic / CKD Non-Compressible Calcified Vessel Trap (`Note (2)`, `86 FR 62095`):** In veterans with **Diabetes Mellitus (`DC 7913` — Agent Orange!)** or chronic kidney disease, medial arterial calcification (*Mönckeberg sclerosis*) makes ankle arteries stiff and non-compressible, producing **falsely normal or supra-normal `ABI` readings (`> 1.00` or `> 1.30`)** despite critical limb ischemia! Under corrected **Note (2) (`86 FR 62095, 62096`, Nov. 9, 2021)**, `ABI` is used *unless* the examiner states that `AP`, `TP` (Toe Pressure), or `TcPO2` is needed because `ABI` does not sufficiently reflect the severity of the veteran's `PAD`—and in all other cases where multiple tests exist, VA **must evaluate based on the test that provides the HIGHEST impairment value**!

2. **Bypass/Graft Residuals (`Note (3)`) & Separate Per-Extremity Ratings + `§ 4.26` Bilateral Factor (`Note (4)`):** Evaluate residuals of aortic and large arterial bypass surgery or arterial graft as `PAD` (`Note (3)`), evaluate **each affected lower or upper extremity separately**, and apply the **`38 C.F.R. § 4.26` `10%` bilateral factor** whenever both legs (or both arms) are compensable (`Note (4)`)! Also check **`§ 4.30` post-surgical convalescence (`100%`)** and **`SMC(k)`** if PAD culminates in toe/foot/leg amputation.

3. **Aortic Aneurysm (`DC 7110`):** **`100%`** if **`>= 5.0 cm` diameter**, symptomatic (precluding exertion), OR requiring surgical/endovascular (`EVAR`/`TEVAR`) correction—crucially, under `DC 7110` Note, **when surgery is required, the `100%` evaluation begins on the date a physician recommends surgical correction** (not waiting until hospital admission!), continuing through `6 months` post-discharge with a mandatory VA exam + `§ 3.105(e)` notice (*Foster*); **`0%`** if `< 5.0 cm` and asymptomatic (`60%` if precluded from exertion pre-2021).

4. **Raynaud's Split (`86 FR 54089`):** Strictly distinguish **`DC 7117` Raynaud's syndrome (secondary Raynaud's phenomenon)** (`100%` `>=2` digital ulcers + auto-amputation of `>=1` digit + attacks; `60%` `>=2` digital ulcers + attacks; `40%` characteristic attacks at least daily; `20%` `4–6`x/wk; `10%` `1–3`x/wk) from **`DC 7124` Raynaud's disease** (primary idiopathic vasospasm, which has **ONLY `10%` and `0%` tiers**: **`10%`** for characteristic attacks associated with trophic change(s) such as tight, shiny skin; **`0%`** without trophic changes!).

5. **Varicose Veins (`DC 7120`) & Post-Phlebitic Syndrome (`DC 7121`):** `DC 7120` cross-references **`DC 7121`**, rated **`100%/60%/40%/20%/10%/0%` per extremity** (+ `§ 4.26` bilateral factor) based on persistent edema, stasis pigmentation/eczema, intermittent vs. persistent ulceration, and relief by elevation/compression hosiery.

blocks.text: B. Cold Injury Residuals (DC 7122, 63 FR 37778, eff. August 13, 1998; Expanded 86 FR 54089, eff. November 14, 2021)

Enacted for **Korean War (Chosin Reservoir), WWII (Battle of the Bulge / Ardennes / Aleutians), Mountain/Arctic Warfare, and peacetime winter field-training** frostbite, trench foot, and immersion foot survivors (`38 U.S.C. § 1112(b)(3)(L)` FPOW cold-injury presumption; [Playbook 07](/playbooks/07-statutory-presumptions-chronic-tropical-pow-als)):

headers: `DC 7122` Cold Injury Criteria (`63 FR 37778`, eff. Aug. 13, 1998; expanded Nov. 14, 2021 at `86 FR 54089, 54097`)
rows: Arthralgia or other pain, numbness, or cold sensitivity **plus TWO OR MORE (`>= 2`)** of the following: `(1)` tissue loss, `(2)` nail abnormalities, `(3)` color changes, `(4)` locally impaired sensation, `(5)` hyperhidrosis, `(6)` X-ray abnormalities (osteoporosis, subarticular punched-out lesions, or osteoarthritis), *plus `[added Nov. 14, 2021]`*: `(7)` anhydrosis, `(8)` atrophy or fibrosis of affected musculature, `(9)` flexion or extension deformity of distal joints, `(10)` volar fat pad loss in fingers or toes, `(11)` avascular necrosis of bone, `(12)` chronic ulceration, or `(13)` carpal or tarsal tunnel syndrome.
Arthralgia or other pain, numbness, or cold sensitivity **plus ONE (`1`)** of the objective signs above (`1–6` pre-Nov. 14, 2021; `1–13` on/after Nov. 14, 2021).

**Arthralgia or other pain, numbness, OR cold sensitivity alone** *(subjective cold sensitivity or numbness of each affected foot/hand/ear/nose warrants `10%` PER PART without needing objective tissue/nail changes!)*

lines: **Multi-Rating Stacking Under `DC 7122` Notes (1) & (2) (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive since Aug. 13, 1998):**

* **Note (2) — Separate Per-Part Evaluation + Bilateral Factor:** Evaluate **each affected part separately** (e.g., Right Foot `30%` + Left Foot `30%` + Right Hand `20%` + Left Hand `20%` + Bilateral Ears `10%` + Nose `10%`) and apply the **`38 C.F.R. § 4.26` `10%` bilateral factor** to paired extremities!

* **Note (1) — Mandatory Separate Residual Stacking:** Separately diagnose and evaluate **`(a)` Peripheral Neuropathy (`DC 8520/8720` / `8515` — omitting sensory/pain symptoms already used to elevate `DC 7122` above `10%`)**, **`(b)` Amputations of digits/feet (`DC 5160–5173` + `SMC(k)`/`(l)`)**, **`(c)` Squamous cell carcinoma in cold-injury scars (`DC 7818`)**, and **`(d)` Secondary fungal infections (`DC 7813` onychomycosis/tinea pedis) or vascular thrombosis** whenever non-duplicative under `§ 4.14`!

blocks.text: 6. Regulatory Watchlist & Quarantine (91 FR 7118 — Rescinded 91 FR 9712)

lines: **QUARANTINE NOTICE — DO NOT CITE AS ACTIVE LAW (AGENTS Law 6):**

* **Rescinded `38 C.F.R. § 4.10` Medication Interim Final Rule (`91 FR 7118`, Feb. 17, 2026 — Rescinded `91 FR 9712`, Feb. 27, 2026):** VA's February 2026 attempt to mandate rating disabilities in their medicated state across all VASRD schedules was **rescinded ab initio** after 10 days.

* **Cardiovascular Impact:** As verified above, **`DC 7101` Hypertension** (`10%`), **`DC 7010` SVT** (`10%`), and the **General Rating Formula for Diseases of the Heart** (`10%`) *already* explicitly mention continuous medication in their text (*McCarroll v. McDonald*, `28 Vet. App. 267 (2016) (en banc)`). By contrast, cardiovascular codes that are **silent on medication**—such as **`DC 7114` PAD** (vasodilators/cilostazol), **`DC 7117` Raynaud's syndrome** (calcium-channel blockers reducing vasospastic attack frequency!), and **`DC 7122` Cold Injury** (gabapentin/analgesics masking cold pain)—are governed strictly by ***Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)`**, forbidding raters from discounting unmedicated attack frequency or baseline severity!

* **20-Year Protection Reminder (`38 U.S.C. § 110`; *Salgado v. Brown*, `4 Vet. App. 316 (1993)`):** Any Era-1 or Era-2 cardiovascular rating continuously in force for `>= 20 years` (even during periods when military retired pay was elected prior to `CRDP`/`CRSC`!) is **permanently immune from reduction below its lowest 20-year level** absent fraud.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Cardiovascular System Guide: Heart METs vs. Ejection Fraction, Hypertension vs. Heart Hypertrophy & Vascular Rules
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Cardiovascular claims combine complex medical metrics—METs exercise capacity, Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF), blood pressure readings, and ankle/toe vascular pressures—with high-stakes effective-date rules for Agent Orange Ischemic Heart Disease (Nehmer, 38 C.F.R. § 3.816) and PACT Act Hypertension (38 U.S.C. § 1116). This comparison explains the three eras of heart ratings (pre-January 12, 1998; the 1998–2021 LVEF + METs era; and the post-November 14, 2021 METs-centered General Heart Formula), when 0% or 10% Hypertension (Diagnostic Code 7101) must step up to 30%+ Hypertensive Heart Disease (Diagnostic Code 7007), and how implanted defibrillators, arrhythmias, peripheral arterial disease, and cold injuries are rated.
record_clues: A pre-November 14, 2021 Ischemic Heart Disease (Diagnostic Code 7005) or Hypertensive Heart Disease (Diagnostic Code 7007) rating assigning 10% based on >7–10 METs while ignoring an echocardiogram showing LVEF of 30%–50% (60%) or <30% (100%), or LVH/hypertrophy (30%).

A running pre-November 14, 2021 60% or 100% LVEF-based heart rating unlawfully reduced after November 14, 2021 without actual medical improvement (void under 38 U.S.C. § 1155 and 38 C.F.R. § 3.951(a)).

Service-connected Hypertension (Diagnostic Code 7101) rated at 0% or 10% when an echocardiogram or cardiac MRI shows left ventricular hypertrophy or dilatation—warranting evaluation as Hypertensive Heart Disease (Diagnostic Code 7007 at 30% or higher)—or secondary kidney/eye complications.

Sustained ventricular arrhythmia (Diagnostic Code 7011) rated below 100% while an Automatic Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator (AICD) is in place, or diabetic Peripheral Arterial Disease (Diagnostic Code 7114) rated on calcified ABI without toe pressure / TcPO2 testing.
important_cautions: Ischemic Heart Disease vs. Hypertension under Nehmer: Ischemic Heart Disease (Diagnostic Code 7005) IS a covered Nehmer condition eligible for pre-2010 retroactive effective dates under 38 C.F.R. § 3.816, whereas PACT Act § 404 Hypertension (Diagnostic Code 7101) is excluded from Nehmer class retroactivity (though previously denied survivor DIC claims can be re-evaluated retroactively under 38 U.S.C. § 1305).

Blood-pressure medication rule in Diagnostic Code 7101: the Veterans Court held en banc in McCarroll v. McDonald that Diagnostic Code 7101 contemplates controlled blood pressure on continuous medication at 10%, so higher 20%/40%/60% hypertension tiers require actual diastolic/systolic readings rather than speculative unmedicated estimates (also note Note (1)'s '3 different days' confirmation rule applies to initial diagnosis, not increased-rating exams).

Do not cite standalone LVEF for claims filed on or after November 14, 2021, or cite 1998 LVEF/METs rules for Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) before January 12, 1998, and remember 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c) permits only one final merits CUE decision per prior Board issue.
VA's February 17, 2026 § 4.10 medication rule (91 FR 7118) was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712) and is not active law.
questions_for_representative: If I have service-connected Hypertension (Diagnostic Code 7101), does an echocardiogram or cardiac MRI show left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) supporting a 30% or higher rating under Diagnostic Code 7007—or secondary kidney or retinal damage?
Did VA check both my METs workload and—for any claim period between January 12, 1998 and November 13, 2021—my Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF)?

If I have an implanted AICD defibrillator (Diagnostic Code 7011) or cold injury residuals in multiple extremities (Diagnostic Code 7122), are all separate ratings and Special Monthly Compensation rules applied?
If I am a Vietnam or Blue Water Navy Veteran (or survivor) with Ischemic Heart Disease, have we audited earlier claims and medical diagnoses for a Nehmer effective date under 38 C.F.R. § 3.816?

1. Master Chronological Federal Register & Precedent Ledger (1946–2026)

headers: Substantive Change Across `§§ 4.110–4.114` & Related Part 3 Rules
rows: Enacted foundational `§§ 4.110–4.114` (`DC 7200–7346`): qualitative `"mild / moderate / moderately severe / severe"` tiers, `§ 4.110` ulcer diagnostic standards, `§ 4.111` postgastrectomy syndromes, `§ 4.112` weight-loss general discussion, `§ 4.113` coexisting abdominal conditions, and `§ 4.114` non-combination range (`DC 7301–7329, 7331, 7342, 7345–7348`). **No dedicated GERD, Celiac, or Gastroparesis codes existed.**

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`< May 19, 2024` except liver `2001`):** Governs nearly eight decades of digestive ratings (`1946–May 18, 2024`), including pre-2024 GERD rated analogously under `DC 7399-7346` (`60/30/10%`) and legacy `DC 7319` IBS (`30/10/0%`).

**Liver, Hepatitis C & `§ 4.112` Weight-Loss Overhaul:** First codified quantitative `§ 4.112` substantial (`>20%`) and minor (`10–20%`) weight loss (`>=3 mos` below `2-year` pre-onset baseline); modernized **`DC 7312` Cirrhosis** (`100/70/50/30/10/0%`), rewrote **`DC 7345` Chronic liver disease without cirrhosis** and **created `DC 7354` Hepatitis C** (`100%` near-constant debilitating symptoms; `60%` `>=6 to <12 wks` incapacitating episodes/yr; `40%` `4 to <6 wks` OR substantial weight loss + `>=2` symptoms; `20%` `2 to <4 wks` OR minor weight loss + `>=2` symptoms; `10%` `1 to <2 wks` OR intermittent fatigue, malaise & anorexia, OR continuous medication; `0%` nonsymptomatic), and added **`DC 7351` Liver transplant** (`100%` -> `30%` min).
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`July 2, 2001 – May 18, 2024`):** Governs Era-2 liver/Hep C ratings; zero CUE reach before July 2, 2001 (`DC 7354` did not exist pre-July 2, 2001).

Amended **`38 C.F.R. § 3.317(a)(2)(i)(B)(3)`** to codify that **Functional Gastrointestinal Disorders (`FGIDs`)**—explicitly including **Irritable Bowel Syndrome (`DC 7319`), functional dyspepsia, functional vomiting, functional constipation, functional abdominal pain syndrome, and functional dysphagia** (excluding structural GI diseases)—are presumptive Gulf War `MUCMIs`.

**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) & CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Aug. 15, 2011`):** Plain-text error to demand an in-service nexus for `DC 7319` IBS in a qualifying Southwest Asia veteran on/after Aug. 15, 2011 ([Playbook 15](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera)).

Landmark precedent arising directly from **`DC 7319` IBS / anti-acid GI medication**: held VA **cannot** discount disability severity based on the ameliorative effects of medication unless the Diagnostic Code explicitly contemplates medication in its rating criteria (reaffirmed in ***Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)`**; *cf.* ***McCarroll v. McDonald*, `28 Vet. App. 267 (2016) (en banc)`** when a DC explicitly mentions medication).
**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** on CUE against pre-2012 final decisions (`38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`); fully retroactive on open, pending, `§ 3.156(b)–(c)`, and AMA `§ 5104(b)` claims.

**PACT Act Expansion:** `§ 406` (`38 U.S.C. § 1120(b)(2)(G)`) made **gastrointestinal cancers of any type (`DC 7343` — esophageal, gastric, small/large bowel, colorectal, anal, hepatobiliary, gallbladder, pancreatic)** presumptive for burn-pit-exposed Gulf War & Post-9/11 veterans; `§ 405` expanded `§ 1117` `FGID` geography to **Afghanistan, Israel, Egypt, Turkey, Syria, and Jordan** and eliminated the `10%` threshold / `2026` sunset.

**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (`>= Aug. 10, 2022`):** Liberalizing effective-date lookback under `38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)` + PACT `§ 1305` / `§ 3.33` survivor DIC re-evaluations ([Playbook 08](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical)).

**Comprehensive Digestive System Overhaul:** Reserved **`§§ 4.110–4.111`**; rewrote **`§ 4.112`** (`>20%` substantial / `10–20%` minor weight loss, Hamwi/BMI baseline, undernutrition, `TPN`/enteral support); updated **`§ 4.113`** & **`§ 4.114`** non-combination list; created **`DC 7206` GERD (`80/50/30/10/0%` stricture)**, **`DC 7207` Barrett's**, **`DC 7355` Celiac (`80/50/30%`)**, **`DC 7356` GI Dysmotility (`80/50/30/10%`)**, **`DC 7357` Post-pancreatectomy (`30%` min)**; updated **`DC 7319` IBS** to Rome IV (`30/20/10%`), consolidated **`DC 7326` IBD** (`60%` biologics; removed `7323`), introduced **`MELD` scores** in `DC 7312`, removed `0%` text from `DC 7336`, and retired 14 obsolete DCs (`7305–7306, 7315–7316, 7321–7324, 7330, 7334–7335, 7337, 7339–7340`).

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= May 19, 2024`):** Running pre-May 19, 2024 ratings (e.g., `30%/60%` GERD under `DC 7346`) are **statutorily grandfathered** under `38 U.S.C. § 1155` / `§ 3.951(a)`; claims pending across May 19, 2024 receive pre-2024 rules prior to May 19, 2024 and whichever version is more favorable thereafter (*Karnas*).

blocks.text: 2. 38 C.F.R. § 4.112 Weight Loss, Baseline Weight & Nutritional Support Definitions (>= May 19, 2024)

From `1946–July 1, 2001`, `§ 4.112` used qualitative prose (*"substantial"* vs. *"minor"* weight loss below *"normal/standard weight"*); on **July 2, 2001 (`66 FR 29486`, `RIN 2900-AK12`)**, VA first quantified `>20%` substantial and `10–20%` minor weight loss sustained `>=3 months` against a `2-year` pre-onset baseline weight. At **`89 FR 19735, 19742` (eff. May 19, 2024)**, VA reserved `§§ 4.110–4.111` and expanded [`38 C.F.R. § 4.112(a)–(d)`](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.114-digestive-pre-and-post-2024) to add *involuntary* weight loss, diminished self-care/work quality, the **favorable Hamwi/BMI baseline fallback (`(b)`)**, **undernutrition (`(c)`)**, and **`TPN`/assisted enteral nutrition (`(d)`)**—plugging directly into `DC 7203, 7206, 7301, 7303, 7308, 7328–7329, 7345, 7355–7356`:

rows: **Substantial Weight Loss** vs. **Minor Weight Loss** vs. **Inability to Gain Weight**

• **Substantial weight loss:** Involuntary loss **`> 20%`** of baseline weight **sustained for `3 months`** with diminished quality of self-care or work tasks. · • **Minor weight loss:** Involuntary loss between **`10% and 20%`** of baseline weight **sustained for `3 months`** with GI-related symptoms, involving diminished quality of self-care/work tasks or decreased food intake. · • **Inability to gain weight:** Substantial weight loss with inability to regain it despite following appropriate therapy.

Clinically documented **average weight for the `2-year` period preceding onset of illness**, OR (if relevant) weight recorded at the veteran's **most recent discharge physical**. **Favorable Fallback:** If neither is available or currently relevant, VA **must** use ideal body weight via either the **Hamwi formula** or **BMI tables**, **whichever is MOST FAVORABLE to the veteran**!

Nutrient deficiency from insufficient intake or malabsorption/inability to utilize or retain nutrients, characterized by failure to maintain normal organ functions/healthy tissues (signs include subcutaneous tissue loss, edema, peripheral neuropathy, muscle wasting, weakness, abdominal distention, ascites, and below-normal BMI).

• **`(d)(1)` Total Parenteral Nutrition (`TPN` / hyperalimentation):** IV catheter infusion of proteins, carbohydrates, fats, vitamins, and minerals bypassing GI digestion. · • **`(d)(2)` Assisted Enteral Nutrition:** Special liquid mixture delivered directly into stomach or small intestine via **nasogastric (`NG`), nasoenteral, gastrostomy (`PEG`), or jejunostomy (`J-tube`) tube**.

blocks.text: 3. Pre- vs. Post-May 19, 2024 Structural Diff Matrix: Major Digestive Conditions

See [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.110–4.114 Digestive System (DC 7200–7357, Pre- vs. Post-May 19, 2024)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.114-digestive-pre-and-post-2024) for verbatim historical and current `§ 4.114` schedules.
A. GERD (Former DC 7399-7346 -> DC 7206), Hiatal Hernia (DC 7346 -> 7203) & Barrett's (DC 7207)

headers: Era 1: `Apr. 1, 1946 – May 18, 2024` *(Rated by Analogy under `DC 7346` Hiatal Hernia)*
Era 2: `May 19, 2024 – Present` *(`89 FR 19735` — Dedicated `DC 7206` GERD & Revised `DC 7346`)*
rows: **`DC 7399-7346`** (GERD rated analogously under `DC 7346` Hiatal Hernia per `38 C.F.R. § 4.20`).

• **GERD:** Dedicated **`DC 7206`** (*Gastroesophageal reflux disease*). · • **Hiatal / Paraesophageal Hernia (`DC 7346`):** Expressly directs **"Rate as esophagus, stricture of (`DC 7203`)"** (identical `80/50/30/10/0%` stricture tiers as `DC 7206`!). · • **Barrett's Esophagus (`DC 7207`):** With stricture -> `DC 7203`; **without stricture** -> **`30%`** high-grade dysplasia, **`10%`** low-grade dysplasia (malignancy -> `DC 7343` `100%`).
**`60%`:** Symptoms of pain, vomiting, material weight loss, and **hematemesis or melena with moderate anemia**; or other symptom combinations productive of severe impairment of health.

• **`80%`:** Documented recurrent/refractory **esophageal stricture(s)** causing dysphagia + `>=1` of `(1)` aspiration, `(2)` undernutrition, or `(3)` `§ 4.112(a)` substantial weight loss (`>20%`), **AND** surgical stricture correction or **`PEG` tube**. · • **`50%`:** Documented recurrent/refractory **esophageal stricture(s)** causing dysphagia requiring `(1)` **dilatation `>=3` times/yr**, `(2)` **steroid dilatation `>=1` time/yr**, OR `(3)` **esophageal stent placement**.

**`30%`:** Persistently recurrent epigastric distress with **dysphagia, pyrosis (heartburn), and regurgitation**, accompanied by **substernal or arm or shoulder pain**, productive of considerable impairment of health (*no stricture or endoscopy dilatation required!*).
**`30%`:** Documented history of recurrent **esophageal stricture(s)** causing dysphagia which requires **dilatation no more than `2` times per year (`<=2x/yr`)**.
• **`10%`:** Two or more of the symptoms for the `30%` evaluation of *less severity* (e.g., chronic heartburn + acid regurgitation!). · • **`0%`:** Asymptomatic (`§ 4.31`).

• **`10%`:** Documented history of **esophageal stricture(s)** that requires **daily medications to control dysphagia** otherwise asymptomatic. · • **`0%`:** Documented history **without daily symptoms or requirement for daily medications**. *(Note 1: Stricture findings must be documented by **barium swallow, CT, or `EGD` endoscopy**!)*

lines: **Three Critical GERD Practice Rules (`§ 1155`, *Karnas* & `DC 7206` Medication Trap):**

1. **Grandfathering of Pre-May 19, 2024 `10%/30%/60%` GERD Ratings (`38 U.S.C. § 1155`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.951(a)`):** Hundreds of thousands of veterans hold `10%`, `30%`, or `60%` ratings under `DC 7399-7346` based on pyrosis, regurgitation, dysphagia, and substernal/shoulder pain *without* an `EGD`-proven esophageal stricture. Under `§ 1155` and `§ 3.951(a)`, VA **cannot** reduce those running awards unless sustained medical improvement is proven **under the pre-May 19, 2024 `DC 7346` criteria** ([Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings)). **Caution:** Do *not* reflexively file a post-May 19, 2024 increased-rating claim on a `30%` GERD veteran who lacks an esophageal stricture!

2. **Straddling Claims (`Karnas v. Derwinski`, `1 Vet. App. 308 (1991)`):** Any GERD or `DC 7346` claim (including ITFs, Supplemental Claims under `§ 3.2500`, HLRs, Board appeals, or `§ 5104(b)` *Hamill* pending claims) pending prior to **May 19, 2024** must be evaluated under `DC 7346` prior to May 19, 2024 and under **whichever schedule (`DC 7346` vs. `DC 7206`) is more favorable** from May 19, 2024 forward!

3. **Medication Split (*Jones*/*Ingram* vs. *McCarroll*) & Secondary GERD Gaps:** For pre-May 19, 2024 `DC 7346` periods, `DC 7346` was **silent on medication**—so under *Jones v. Shinseki* (`26 Vet. App. 56`) and *Ingram v. Collins* (`38 Vet. App. 130`), raters **cannot** discount heartburn/regurgitation controlled by omeprazole/pantoprazole (`PPIs`) or famotidine (`H2` blockers)! By contrast, post-May 19, 2024 **`DC 7206`'s `10%` tier explicitly requires *both* documented esophageal stricture(s) *and* daily medication** to control dysphagia (*McCarroll* carve-out)—note the regulatory gap where daily `PPI`-dependent GERD *without* an `EGD` stricture lands at `0%` under `DC 7206` unless accompanied by **`DC 7207` Barrett's dysplasia (`10%/30%`)**, secondary **`DC 6516` reflux laryngitis (`10%/30%`)**, or secondary **`DC 6602` reflux-aggravated asthma**!

blocks.text: B. Irritable Bowel Syndrome (DC 7319), Inflammatory Bowel Disease (DC 7326 Consolidating DC 7323) & Hemorrhoids (DC 7336)

rows: **`DC 7319` Irritable Bowel Syndrome (`IBS`)** *(formerly Irritable colon syndrome)*

• **`30%` (Severe):** Diarrhea, or alternating diarrhea and constipation, with more or less constant abdominal distress. · • **`10%` (Moderate):** Frequent episodes of bowel disturbance with abdominal distress. · • **`0%` (Mild):** Disturbances of bowel function with occasional episodes of abdominal distress. · *(**No `20%` tier existed!**)*

**Modified Rome IV Objective Frequency Formula (`30% / 20% / 10%` — `0%` eliminated!):** · Abdominal pain related to defecation during the **previous `3 months`** **PLUS `>=2` of 6 features**: `(1)` change in stool frequency, `(2)` change in stool form, `(3)` altered stool passage *(straining and/or urgency)*, `(4)` mucorrhea, `(5)` abdominal bloating, or `(6)` subjective distension: · • **`30%`:** At least **once per week (`>=1 day/wk`)**. · • **`20%` `[NEW!]`:** At least **`3 days per month`**. · • **`10%`:** At least **once** during previous `3 months`.

• **Massive Liberalization:** Post-May 19, 2024 `DC 7319` adds a **`20%` tier**, sets **`10%` as the minimum** once `3-month` criteria are met, and hits **`30%` at just `1 day/week`** (replacing `"more or less constant"` distress)! · • **Presumptive `FGID`:** Presumptive under `38 C.F.R. § 3.317(a)(2)(i)(B)(3)` for Gulf War & PACT `§ 405` theaters (and `§ 3.309(c)` for FPOWs!). · • **Silent on Medication (*Jones* / *Ingram*):** Both pre- and post-2024 `DC 7319` are **completely silent on medication**—raters cannot discount baseline stool/pain frequency masked by dicyclomine, hyoscyamine, loperamide, rifaximin, or linaclotide!
**`DC 7326` Crohn's Disease or Undifferentiated `IBD`** *(Consolidating **former `DC 7323` Ulcerative Colitis** & `DC 7325` Chronic Enteritis!)*

**`DC 7323` Ulcerative Colitis** (`100%` pronounced w/ malnutrition & numerous stools; `60%` severe w/ frequent exacerbations; `30%` moderately severe w/ infrequent exacerbations; `10%` moderate) while `DC 7326` cross-referenced `DC 7319` (`30%` cap trap unless rated by analogy under `7323`!).

**Unified `DC 7326` (`100% / 60% / 30% / 10%`; `DC 7323` removed):** · • **`100%`:** Severe `IBD` unresponsive to treatment + **`>=1` hospitalization/yr** + either **inability to work** OR recurrent abdominal pain w/ **`>=2`** of: `>=6/day` diarrhea, `>=6/day` rectal bleeding, recurrent rectal incontinence, or recurrent abdominal distension. · • **`60%`:** Moderate `IBD` managed outpatient with **immunosuppressants or other biologic agents**, + recurrent abdominal pain, `4–5/day` diarrhea, & intermittent toxicity (*fever, tachycardia, or anemia*). · • **`30%`:** Mild-moderate `IBD` managed w/ oral/topical agents *(other than immunosuppressants/biologics)* + pain, `<=3/day` diarrhea, minimal toxicity. · • **`10%`:** Minimal-mild managed w/ oral/topical agents + `<=3/day` diarrhea, no systemic toxicity.

• **Biologic Therapy `60%` Unlock:** Outpatient **infliximab (`Remicade`), adalimumab (`Humira`), vedolizumab (`Entyvio`), ustekinumab (`Stelara`), risankizumab (`Skyrizi`), tofacitinib/upadacitinib, or azathioprine/6-MP** anchors the **`60%` tier** (note conjunctive symptom elements—if a biologic puts stool count in remission while suppressing severe underlying IBD, check extraschedular/staged ratings or **`DC 7329` surgical resection/ostomy**!). · • **Surgical Colectomy / Ostomy (`DC 7329` = `40% / 60% / 100%`):** Under `§ 4.114`, surgical **colostomy or ileostomy** is evaluated under **`DC 7329` (Intestine, large, resection of)**—which awards **`100%`** for total colectomy w/ ileostomy, high-output syndrome & `>2` IV-hydration episodes/yr, **`60%`** for total colectomy (with or without permanent ostomy) without high-output syndrome, and **`40%`** for partial colectomy w/ permanent colostomy/ileostomy!

• **`20%`:** With persistent bleeding and with secondary anemia, OR with fissures. · • **`10%`:** Large or thrombotic, irreducible, with excessive redundant tissue, evidencing frequent recurrences. · • **`0%`:** Mild or moderate.

• **`20%`:** Internal or external hemorrhoids with **persistent bleeding and anemia**; **OR** **continuously prolapsed internal hemorrhoids with `>=3` episodes per year of thrombosis**. · • **`10%`:** **Prolapsed internal hemorrhoids with `<=2` episodes per year of thrombosis**; **OR** **external hemorrhoids with `>=3` episodes per year of thrombosis**. · *(Explicit `0%` text deleted; noncompensable `0%` governed by `38 C.F.R. § 4.31`).*

• **Pre-2024 Fissure Protection:** Note that pre-2024 `DC 7336` awarded **`20%`** for persistent bleeding **OR fissures**, whereas post-2024 `DC 7336` deleted fissures—grandfathered pre-2024 `20%` fissure awards are protected under `§ 1155`! · • **`DC 7720` Iron-Deficiency Anemia Trap:** Under `38 C.F.R. § 4.117` **`DC 7720` Note**, secondary iron-deficiency anemia caused by chronic GI blood loss (`DC 7336` hemorrhoids, `DC 7304` ulcer, `DC 7326` IBD) **cannot** be rated separately under `DC 7720`—it elevates `DC 7336` to **`20%`** (`DC 7304` to `60%`)!

blocks.text: C. Liver Diseases (DC 7312, 7345, 7351, 7354), Upper/Lower GI, Pancreas, Cancers & New 2024 Codes (DC 7355–7357)

headers: Post-May 19, 2024 (`89 FR 19735`) Criteria vs. Pre-2024 Historical Benchmark
rows: **Cirrhosis of the liver** *(Alcoholic secondary to PTSD under Allen, post-hepatitic, biliary, or `NASH`/`MASH`)*

**Replaced subjective Child-Pugh / ascites prose with objective `MELD` (`Model for End-Stage Liver Disease`) OR clinical complication tiers:** · • **`100%`:** **`MELD >= 15`**, **OR** continuous daily debilitating symptoms + generalized weakness & `>=1` of: **ascites, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (`SBP`) history, hepatic encephalopathy, variceal hemorrhage, coagulopathy, portal gastropathy, hepatopulmonary syndrome, or hepatorenal syndrome**. · • **`60%`:** **`MELD > 11 and < 15` (`12–14`)**, **OR** daily fatigue + `>=1` episode in past yr of variceal bleed, portal gastropathy, or hepatic encephalopathy. · • **`30%`:** **`MELD 10 or 11`**, **OR** portal hypertension signs (*splenomegaly or ascites*) + `>=1` (*"either"*) of weakness, anorexia, abdominal pain, or malaise. · • **`10%`:** **`MELD > 6 and < 10` (`7–9`)**, **OR** history of cirrhosis w/ `>=1` symptom (weakness, anorexia, abdominal pain, malaise). **`0%`:** Asymptomatic (`MELD <= 6`).
**Chronic liver disease without cirrhosis (`7345`)** *(Hep B, autoimmune, `MASLD`/`NAFLD` — Camp Lejeune hepatic steatosis!)* & **Hepatitis C (`7354`)**

• **`DC 7354` Hepatitis C** (created July 2, 2001, `66 FR 29486`, `RIN 2900-AK12`) now **directs evaluation under `DC 7345`** (retaining `7354` tracking code). · • **Post-2024 `DC 7345` (`100/60/40/20/0%` — eliminated legacy bed-rest `"incapacitating episodes"`):** **`100%`** progressive chronic liver disease requiring *both* parenteral antiviral *and* parenteral immunomodulatory therapy (+ `6 mos` post-cessation -> mandatory exam); **`60%`** continuous medication + **`§ 4.112` substantial weight loss (`>20%`)** + `>=2` of `6` symptoms (*daily fatigue, malaise, anorexia, hepatomegaly, pruritus, arthralgia*); **`40%`** continuous medication + **`§ 4.112` minor weight loss (`10–20%`)** + `>=2` of those `6` symptoms; **`20%`** chronic liver disease w/ `>=1` of `5` symptoms (*intermittent fatigue, malaise, anorexia, hepatomegaly, or pruritus*); **`0%`** asymptomatic/cured `SVR` post-`DAA` `Harvoni`/`Epclusa` without residual symptoms (*check extrahepatic **`DC 7544` viral nephropathy** or **`DC 7700s` cryoglobulinemia/NHL**!*).

**`100%`** from hospital admission for transplant surgery (`1-yr` mandatory post-discharge exam + *Foster* `§ 3.105(e)` 60-day notice); **`60%`** **while eligible and awaiting transplant surgery** `[NEW May 2024 tier!]`; **mandatory `30%` MINIMUM** post-transplant (or higher under `DC 7312`).
**Peptic ulcer disease** *(Consolidated gastric `7304`, duodenal `7305` & marginal `7306`; `DC 7307` Chronic gastritis also rates here!)*

• **Post-2024 (`100 / 60 / 20 / 10 / 0%` — NO `40%` tier!):** **`100%`** for **`3 months`** post-op for perforation or hemorrhage; **`60%`** continuous abdominal pain w/ intermittent vomiting, recurrent hematemesis/melena & manifestation of anemia, requiring hospitalization `>=1x` in past `12 mos`; **`20%`** episodes of abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting lasting `>=3` consecutive days, occurring **`>=4x` in past `12 mos`**, managed by daily prescribed medication; **`10%`** such `>=3`-day episodes occurring **`1–3x` in past `12 mos`**, managed by daily prescribed medication; **`0%`** asymptomatic or managed by intermittent medication. · • **Pre-2024 Trap:** Pre-2024 `DC 7304–7306` had a **`40%`** moderately-severe tier (`100/60/40/20/10%`)—any pre-May 19, 2024 `40%` award is **grandfathered under `§ 1155`**! Also remember `38 U.S.C. § 1112(a)(1)` / `§ 3.309(a)` **1-year chronic peptic ulcer presumption** (*Joyce v. Nicholson*, `19 Vet. App. 36 (2005)`).

**Post-2024 (`80 / 30 / 10 / 0%` — up from `50%` max pre-2024; NO `50%` tier post-2024!):** **`80%`** persistent partial bowel obstruction inoperable & refractory to treatment, OR requiring `TPN` for obstructive symptoms; **`30%`** symptomatic adhesions w/ recurrent partial obstruction episodes requiring **`>=1` hospitalization in past `12 mos`** + medically-directed dietary modification *(grandfathered pre-2024 `50%` awards protected under `§ 1155`!)*; **`10%`** symptomatic adhesions managed conservatively via outpatient care, medication, or diet; **`0%`** asymptomatic.

• **`7314` (`30/10/0%`):** **`30%`** `>=3` clinically documented RUQ pain/nausea/vomiting attacks in past `12 mos` OR biliary stricture dilatations; **`10%`** `1–2` attacks; **`0%`** asymptomatic. · • **`7318` (`30 / 10 / 0%` — NO `20%` tier post-2024!):** **`30%`** recurrent post-prandial/nocturnal abdominal pain + chronic watery bowel movements **`>=3x/day`**; **`10%`** intermittent pain + **`1–2` watery bowel movements/day**; **`0%`** asymptomatic *(pre-2024 `20%` moderate awards grandfathered under `§ 1155`!)*.

• **`7328` Small bowel resection (`80/60/40/20/0%`):** **`80%`** resection w/ undernutrition & anemia requiring **`TPN`**; **`60%`** resection w/ undernutrition & anemia requiring oral nutritional supplementation, continuous medication & **intermittent `TPN`**; **`40%`** resection w/ undernutrition & anemia requiring oral supplementation & continuous medication; **`20%`** resection w/ chronic diarrhea **`>=4x/day`**; **`0%`** asymptomatic. · • **`7329` Large bowel resection / Colectomy (`100 / 60 / 40 / 20 / 0%`):** **`100%`** total colectomy w/ ileostomy, high-output syndrome **AND `>2` episodes of dehydration requiring IV hydration in past `12 mos`**; **`60%`** total colectomy (with or without permanent ostomy) without high-output syndrome; **`40%`** partial colectomy w/ permanent colostomy/ileostomy without high-output syndrome; **`20%`** partial colectomy w/ reanastomosis and chronic diarrhea `>=4x/day` OR fecal leakage requiring pad `>=1x/day`; **`0%`** asymptomatic.

• **`7332` Sphincter impairment (`100/60/30/10/0%`):** **`100%`** complete loss unresponsive to prescribed bowel program requiring surgery or digital stimulation + meds + diet, **OR incontinence to solids/liquids `>=2x/day` requiring pad change `>=2x/day`** (*audit immediately for `38 U.S.C. § 1114(l)` `SMC(l)` Aid & Attendance!*); **`60%`** pad `>=2x/wk`; **`30%`** pad `>=2x/mo`; **`10%`** responsive to prescribed bowel program requiring special diet or medication, **OR** incontinence `<2x/mo` requiring pad `<2x/mo`; **`0%`** asymptomatic. · • **`7333` Anal stricture (`100/60/30/10%`):** `100%` inability to open anus/expel solid feces; `60%` `>=50%` lumen loss; `30%` `<50%` lumen loss; `10%` dietary management (*includes dyssynergic defecation / levator ani / anismus!*).
**Hernia** *(Femoral, inguinal, umbilical, ventral, incisional — excluding hiatal)*

**Unified all non-hiatal hernias (`60 / 30 / 20 / 10 / 0%`, plus `Note (1)` `100%` `2-mo` post-op convalescence):** Evaluates irreparable new/recurrent hernias present `>=12 mos` requiring **pain during `>=3` of `5` functional activities (`bending over, ADLs, lifting, pushing/pulling, or reaching`)** by size: **`60%`** **`>=15 cm`**; **`30%`** **`10 to <15 cm`**; **`20%`** **`4 to <10 cm`**; **`10%`** **`2 to <4 cm`**; **`0%`** `<2 cm` or without `>=3`-activity pain.
**Malignant neoplasms of the digestive system** *(Esophagus, stomach, colon, rectum, anus, liver, bile duct, pancreas)*

**`100%`** during active malignancy/treatment and for **`6 months` following discontinuance of surgery, radiation, antineoplastic chemotherapy, or other therapeutic procedure**; mandatory VA exam at 6 months + **60-day `§ 3.105(e)` advance notice required** before discontinuing `100%` (*Foster v. McDonough*, `34 Vet. App. 338 (2021)`). **PACT Act `38 U.S.C. § 1120(b)(2)(G)`** makes *all* GI cancers presumptive for Gulf War/Post-9/11 burn-pit veterans!

**Post-2024 (`100/60/30%` — `30%` minimum!):** **`100%`** maldigestion/malabsorption requiring dietary restriction + **pancreatic enzyme supplementation** (or daily debilitating pain requiring physician pain management / tube feeding); **`60%`** `>=3` abdominal/mid-back pain episodes/yr + **`>=1` hospitalization/yr** for pain management or enteral-tube/cyst complications; **`30%`** `>=1` episode/yr requiring ongoing outpatient medical treatment for pain, digestive problems, or cyst/pseudocyst/obstruction/ascites.
**Celiac disease** *(Confirmed by serum antibody test or `EGD` biopsy)*

**`80%`** malabsorption syndrome causing weakness interfering w/ ADLs + weight loss/wasting + nutritional deficiencies + systemic manifestations (*dermatitis herpetiformis, hypocalcemia, osteomalacia, vitamin deficiency, anemia, neuropathy*) + diarrhea from lactase & pancreatic insufficiency; **`50%`** malabsorption syndrome w/ chronic diarrhea despite medically prescribed gluten-free diet + nutritional deficiencies due to lactase & pancreatic insufficiency + systemic manifestations (*or biopsy villous atrophy*); **`30%`** malabsorption syndrome w/ chronic diarrhea managed by medically prescribed diet without nutritional deficiencies (*minimum compensable tier is `30%`!*).
**Gastrointestinal dysmotility syndrome** *(Gastroparesis — huge secondary to Diabetes `DC 7913`! — & `CIPO`)*

**`80%`** complete dependence on `TPN` or continuous tube feeding; **`50%`** intermittent tube feeding + recurrent ER treatment for obstruction/regurgitation/vomiting; **`30%`** `CIPO` or motility symptoms (*pain, bloating, early satiety/fullness, nausea/vomiting, constipation/diarrhea*) on ambulatory care + prescribed dietary manipulation; **`10%`** intermittent pain + epigastric fullness + bloating without structural GI disease (*captures **functional dyspepsia** under `§ 3.317`!*).

Evaluate under `DC 7347` Pancreatitis, `DC 7303` Upper GI surgical complications, `DC 7328` Malabsorption, `DC 7319`/`7326` Diarrhea, or **`DC 7913` Pancreatogenic Diabetes**, whichever yields highest rating — **mandatory `30%` MINIMUM**!

blocks.text: *(**Retired May 19, 2024 DCs — Grandfathered Only:** `7305` Duodenal ulcer & `7306` Marginal ulcer [`-> 7304`]; `7315` Cholelithiasis & `7316` Cholangitis [`-> 7314`]; `7321` Amebiasis, `7322` Bacillary dysentery & `7324` Distomiasis [`-> 7319/7326/§ 4.88b`]; `7323` Ulcerative colitis [`-> 7326`]; `7330` Intestinal fistulous tract [`-> 7328/7329`]; `7334` Rectal prolapse [`-> 7332/7333`]; `7335` Ano, fistula in [`-> 7332`]; `7337` Pruritus ani [`-> § 4.118 DC 7806`]; `7339` Ventral hernia & `7340` Femoral hernia [`-> 7338`]. Note: `DC 7303` replaced former `7308` phrasing for chronic complications of upper GI surgery [`80/50/30/10/0%`], while `DC 7354` Hep C directs rating under `DC 7345`).*
4. 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.113–4.114 Anti-Pyramiding Lock vs. Permissible Multi-Rating Stacking (CUE Goldmine)

Under [`38 C.F.R. § 4.113`](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.114-digestive-pre-and-post-2024) and the opening paragraph of [`38 C.F.R. § 4.114`](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.114-digestive-pre-and-post-2024), VA's categorical prohibition on combining digestive ratings is **strictly bounded by numerical Diagnostic Code listing** (*Tropf v. Nicholson*, `20 Vet. App. 317, 320 (2006)`):

rows: **`DC 7301–7329` inclusive, `7331` *(Peritonitis)*, `7342` *(Visceroptosis)*, `7345–7350` inclusive *(Liver/Hiatal/Pancreatitis/Vagotomy/Abscess)*, `7352` *(Pancreas transplant)*, and `7355–7357` inclusive *(Celiac, Dysmotility, Post-pancreatectomy)*** *(plus `7354` rated under `7345`)*

**STRICTLY NON-COMBINABLE WITH EACH OTHER.** Assign a **single evaluation** under the DC reflecting the **predominant disability picture**, and **elevate it to the next higher evaluation** if warranted by the severity of the overall disability! *(Watch `DC 7346` Hiatal Hernia: `7346` sits inside `7345–7350`, whereas standalone **`DC 7206` GERD** sits outside it!)*

**`DC 7200–7207`** — Mouth/Lip (`7200–7201`), Tongue loss (`7202`), **Esophageal stricture (`7203`)**, Motility/Achalasia (`7204`), Diverticulum (`7205`), **GERD (`7206`)**, and **Barrett's esophagus (`7207`)**

**EXEMPT FROM THE `§ 4.114` NON-COMBINATION LIST!** A veteran can lawfully hold **separate, combined ratings** for **`DC 7206` GERD** (or `DC 7207` Barrett's) **PLUS** a lower-GI or liver code from Group 1 (e.g., **`DC 7319` IBS (`30%`)**, **`DC 7326` Crohn's (`60%`)**, or **`DC 7312` Cirrhosis**), so long as the same symptom is not compensated twice under `38 C.F.R. § 4.14` (*Esteban v. Brown*, `6 Vet. App. 259 (1994)`)!
**3. Anorectal, Abdominal-Wall Hernia, Spleen/Transplant & Cancer Carve-Outs (`OUTSIDE` `§ 4.114` Lock!)**

• **`DC 7332`** (Rectum & anus, impairment of sphincter control `100/60/30/10/0%`) · • **`DC 7333`** (Rectum & anus, stricture `100/60/30/10%`) · • **`DC 7336`** (Hemorrhoids `20/10%`) · • **`DC 7338`** (Inguinal/ventral/incisional hernia `60/30/20/10/0%` + `Note (1)` `100%` post-op) · • **`DC 7343–7344`** (Malignant/benign neoplasms), **`7351`** (Liver transplant), **`7353`** (Anal/perianal injury)

**EXEMPT FROM THE `§ 4.114` NON-COMBINATION LIST!** Raters routinely commit **plain-text CUE (`38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a)`)** by lumping **`DC 7336` Hemorrhoids (`20%`)**, **`DC 7338` Inguinal/Incisional Hernia**, or **`DC 7332` Fecal Incontinence** into `DC 7319` IBS or `DC 7304` Ulcer! Only avoid duplicating the *exact same* symptom (e.g., rectal incontinence used for `DC 7326`'s `100%` tier cannot also be rated at `100%` under `DC 7332` per `§ 4.14`, whereas `DC 7319` IBS abdominal pain/diarrhea + `DC 7336` prolapsed/thrombosed hemorrhoids + `DC 7206` GERD **stack cleanly**!).

lines: **QUARANTINE NOTICE — DO NOT CITE AS ACTIVE LAW (AGENTS Law 6):**

* **Rescinded `38 C.F.R. § 4.10` Medication Interim Final Rule (`91 FR 7118`, Feb. 17, 2026 — Rescinded `91 FR 9712`, Feb. 27, 2026):** VA's February 2026 IFR attempting to abrogate ***Jones v. Shinseki*, `26 Vet. App. 56 (2012)`** and ***Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)`** was **rescinded ab initio** after 10 days.
* **Digestive System Medication Matrix:** Always check whether the specific digestive tier explicitly mentions medication (*McCarroll v. McDonald*, `28 Vet. App. 267 (2016) (en banc)`):

1. **Codes/Tiers SILENT on Medication (*Jones* & *Ingram* Govern Fully!):** **`DC 7319` IBS** (all eras — antispasmodics, antidiarrheals, laxatives, rifaximin), **pre-May 19, 2024 `DC 7399-7346` GERD** (`PPIs`/`H2` blockers), **`DC 7314` Biliary disease**, **`DC 7318` Post-cholecystectomy diarrhea** (cholestyramine/bile-acid sequestrants!), and **`DC 7336` Hemorrhoids** (hydrocortisone suppositories). Audit any decision—especially between Feb. 17 and Feb. 27, 2026—that discounted unmedicated symptom frequency!

2. **Codes/Tiers EXPLICITLY Incorporating Medication (*McCarroll* Governs):** Post-May 19, 2024 **`DC 7206` GERD `10%`** (stricture + daily meds), **`DC 7304` Peptic Ulcer `10%/20%`** (daily prescribed meds), **`DC 7326` IBD `10%/30%/60%`** (oral/topical vs. immunosuppressants/biologics), **`DC 7332` Sphincter Control** (meds beyond laxatives), and **`DC 7345` Chronic Liver Disease** (antiviral/immunomodulatory meds).

* **Proposed `38 C.F.R. § 3.317` Update (`89 FR 79815`, Oct. 1, 2024 — Proposed / Not Finalized):** Remains unfinalized, while positive statutory law in **`38 U.S.C. § 1117` (`Pub. L. 117-168, § 405`)** is already binding and self-executing for all Gulf War and expanded Post-9/11 `FGID` claims.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Digestive Conditions: Reflux (GERD), Irritable Bowel (IBS), Crohn's & Liver Rating Changes
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: VA significantly changed how it evaluates digestive conditions on May 19, 2024 (published March 20, 2024 at 89 FR 19735). Before May 19, 2024, acid reflux (gastroesophageal reflux disease, or GERD) did not have its own Diagnostic Code and was usually rated by comparison to hiatal hernia (Diagnostic Code 7346) based on heartburn, regurgitation, and chest or arm pain. Starting May 19, 2024, GERD has its own code (Diagnostic Code 7206) focused on esophageal stricture (narrowing) and dilation treatments, while Irritable Bowel Syndrome (Diagnostic Code 7319), Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis (consolidated under Diagnostic Code 7326), liver cirrhosis, celiac disease, and hemorrhoids gained updated rating tiers.
record_clues: A VA Rating Code Sheet showing pre-2024 GERD coded as '7399-7346' at 10%, 30%, or 60%, or post-May 19, 2024 GERD coded under Diagnostic Code 7206.
Upper endoscopy (EGD) or barium swallow reports mentioning esophageal stricture, esophageal dilation procedures, or Barrett's esophagus (Diagnostic Code 7207).

Gastroenterology notes documenting Rome IV abdominal pain with bowel changes for IBS (Diagnostic Code 7319), outpatient biologic infusions or immunosuppressants (such as infliximab, adalimumab, vedolizumab, or ustekinumab) for inflammatory bowel disease (Diagnostic Code 7326), or MELD lab scores for liver cirrhosis (Diagnostic Code 7312).
Gulf War or post-9/11 Southwest Asia / Afghanistan deployment records alongside a functional gastrointestinal disorder (such as IBS or functional dyspepsia) under 38 C.F.R. § 3.317.
important_cautions: Existing ratings are protected from schedule changes alone: under 38 U.S.C. § 1155 and 38 C.F.R. § 3.951(a), VA cannot lower a pre-May 19, 2024 running 30% or 60% GERD rating simply because the new Diagnostic Code 7206 requires an esophageal stricture. Conversely, claims pending across May 19, 2024 are evaluated under whichever version is more favorable for each period, while new claims filed on or after May 19, 2024 follow the updated schedule.

Anti-stacking rules depend on exact code numbers: 38 C.F.R. § 4.114 prohibits combining certain abdominal codes (such as IBS, ulcers, Crohn's, liver disease, and celiac disease) with one another, but upper-esophageal codes (Diagnostic Codes 7203, 7206, and 7207) and anorectal or hernia codes (Diagnostic Codes 7332, 7336, and 7338) sit outside that non-combination list when symptoms are distinct.

Do not rely on VA's February 17, 2026 medication rule (91 FR 7118): that Interim Final Rule was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712) and is not enacted law. Note, however, that specific post-2024 tiers that explicitly mention daily prescribed medication (such as the 10% tier of Diagnostic Code 7206) apply their written medication criteria.

Do not file a Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) motion citing post-May 19, 2024 digestive codes against a final decision issued before May 19, 2024, and remember that under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c), once the Board of Veterans' Appeals issues a final merits decision on a CUE motion for a specific prior Board issue, no second CUE motion is allowed on that Board issue.
questions_for_representative: Was my digestive claim filed or pending before May 19, 2024, so that VA had to consider both the pre-2024 criteria (such as Diagnostic Code 7346 for GERD) and the May 19, 2024 criteria?

Did VA improperly lump an upper-esophageal condition (like GERD under Diagnostic Code 7206) or hemorrhoids/sphincter impairment (Diagnostic Codes 7336 or 7332) into my IBS or inflammatory bowel rating despite the exact code list in 38 C.F.R. § 4.114?
If I receive biologic injections, infusions, or immunomodulators for Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, do my treatment records match the post-May 19, 2024 tiers under Diagnostic Code 7326?

If VA discontinued a 100% gastrointestinal cancer rating (Diagnostic Code 7343) after treatment, did VA wait at least 6 months, conduct a mandatory VA examination, and send 60-day advance notice under 38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e)?

headers: Substantive Change Across `§§ 4.115–4.115b` & Related Part 3 Rules
rows: Enacted Era-1 `§§ 4.115–4.115a` (`DC 7500–7531`): qualitative `"definite / marked / pronounced"` nephritis, cystitis, BPH, stricture, stone, and cancer schedules; **no standardized pad-count or `eGFR` dysfunction tables existed**.
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`< Feb. 17, 1994`):** Governs pre-Feb. 17, 1994 CUE audits and pre-1994 staged *Nehmer* prostate/bladder cancer periods!

Held that a veteran's **pre-existing or post-service elective vasectomy does NOT bar `38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)` `SMC(k)`** when the veteran subsequently suffers service-connected anatomical removal or complete atrophy of a testis (`DC 7523–7524`)!
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Mar. 23, 1989`):** Binding on all ROs and the Board (`38 U.S.C. § 7104(c)`).

**First Major Genitourinary Overhaul (Era 2):** Split `§ 4.115a` into **three standardized dysfunction matrices** (**Renal Dysfunction** [`BUN >80`/`40–80`, `creatinine >8`/`4–8`, albuminuria/edema, `DC 7101` HTN `>=40%`], **Voiding Dysfunction** [absorbent pads `>4` / `2–4` / `<2` per day; daytime/nocturia frequency; obstructed voiding `>150 cc` PVR / catheterization], and **UTI** [`30/10%`]) + redesignated **`§ 4.115b`** (`DC 7500–7542`), adding `DC 7528` 6-month post-treatment cancer exam rule, `DC 7508/7510` `30%` diet/drug stone rule, and `DC 7522` `20%` penile deformity w/ loss of erectile power.
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`Feb. 17, 1994 – Nov. 13, 2021`):** Governs 27 years of renal, voiding, `DC 7508`, `DC 7522`, and `DC 7528` ratings; zero CUE reach before Feb. 17, 1994.

Clarified `DC 7528` staged ratings vs. running awards: when VA assigns **retroactive staged ratings** in an initial grant after cancer treatment has already ended, `§ 3.105(e)` 60-day prospective notice does not extend the `100%` past the documented post-6-month clinical exam showing remission, *whereas* **running `100%` awards** require full procedural compliance.
**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** on pre-2010 CUE; governs all staged vs. running `DC 7528` audits.
***Williams v. Wilkie*, `30 Vet. App. 134 (2018)`** & ***Payne v. Wilkie*, `31 Vet. App. 373 (2019)`**

*Williams* held Era-2 `DC 7522` (`20%` *"penis, deformity, with loss of erectile power"*) encompasses **internal** as well as external anatomical distortion (e.g., post-prostatectomy internal tissue/nerve alteration!); *Payne* held **`SMC(k)` applies to multi-link secondary causal chains** and requires **no formal claim** under `38 C.F.R. § 3.155(d)(2)` when reasonably raised by the record!
**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** on CUE against final decisions predating *Williams*/*Payne*; massive value on pending/appealed/*Nehmer* pre-Nov. 14, 2021 claims!

Added **Bladder Cancer (`DC 7528`)** to `38 U.S.C. § 1116` Agent Orange herbicide presumptions—triggering full **`38 C.F.R. § 3.816` *Nehmer* Footnote 1 & 2 class-action retroactivity** (alongside long-covered **Prostate Cancer**, `61 FR 57586`, Nov. 7, 1996)!

**Nehmer Retroactive Herbicide (§ 3.816) & CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive:** Unlocks decades of retroactive `DC 7528` back pay + survivors' `§ 3.816(f)` estate benefits + `10 U.S.C. § 1413a` CRSC (*Soto*)!

Construed `DC 7528` Note: post-treatment termination of `100%` is a regulatory *"discontinuance"* rather than a traditional reduction—so **`§§ 3.343/3.344` do NOT apply**, **BUT VA MUST provide `38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e)` 60-day advance notice** (taking effect first day of month after 60 days from final notice)!

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive / Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e)):** Any running `DC 7528` `100%` award dropped without both a post-6-month exam AND `§ 3.105(e)` 60-day advance notice must be restored!

**Second Major Genitourinary Overhaul (Era 3):** Replaced `BUN`/creatinine renal tiers in `§ 4.115a` with **`GFR`/`eGFR` (`<15 = 100%`, `15–29 = 80%`, `30–44 = 60%`, `45–59 = 30%`, `60–89` w/ `ACR >=30` or structural/casts = `0%`) sustained `>=3` consecutive months**; added stent/nephrostomy (`30%`) & `>=6 mos` suppressive therapy (`10%`) to `UTI`; reduced **`DC 7522` ED to `0%` regardless of deformity** (preserving `SMC(k)`); **deleted `DC 7510` & removed diet/drug therapy from `DC 7508` `30%` stones**; narrowed `DC 7541` title to Diabetes Type I/II; and **added `DC 7543` (Varicocele/Hydrocele), `DC 7544` (Viral HIV/Hep B/Hep C renal), and `DC 7545` (Bladder diverticulum)**.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Nov. 14, 2021`):** Running pre-Nov. 14, 2021 awards (`20%` `DC 7522`, `30%` diet/drug `DC 7508`, `60%` HTN-based renal) are **statutorily grandfathered** under `38 U.S.C. § 1155` / `§ 3.951(a)`; straddling claims get favorable *Karnas* protection.

PACT Act `§ 406` made **reproductive cancers of any type (prostate, testicular, penile)** and **kidney cancer (`DC 7528`)** presumptive for burn-pit veterans (`>= Aug. 10, 2022`); **`90 FR 23, 30` (eff. Jan. 2, 2025)** enacted **`38 C.F.R. § 3.320a`**, adding **urinary bladder cancer, ureter cancer (incl. ureteric orifice & urachus), and related genitourinary cancers** as presumptive burn-pit conditions!

**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114)** (`>= Aug. 10, 2022` for `§ 1120` kidney/reproductive cancers; `>= Jan. 2, 2025` with `§ 3.114(a)` 1-yr lookback for `§ 3.320a` bladder/ureter cancers + `§ 1305` survivor DIC!).
