Era 3: `Nov. 14, 2021 – Present` *(`86 FR 54081` — `GFR` Sustained `>= 3 Consecutive Months` in Past `12 Mos`!)*
rows: Requiring **regular dialysis**, OR precluding more than sedentary activity from one of: `(a)` persistent edema and albuminuria; `(b)` **`BUN > 80 mg%`**; `(c)` **`creatinine > 8 mg%`**; OR `(d)` markedly decreased function of kidney or other organ systems, especially cardiovascular.

• **Chronic kidney disease (`CKD`) with `GFR < 15 mL/min/1.73 m²`** for at least `3` consecutive months during the past `12` months; **OR** · • Requiring **regular routine dialysis**; **OR** · • **Eligible kidney transplant recipient**.

Persistent edema and albuminuria with **`BUN 40 to 80 mg%`**; OR **`creatinine 4 to 8 mg%`**; OR generalized poor health characterized by lethargy, weakness, anorexia, weight loss, or limitation of exertion.
**`CKD` with `GFR 15 to 29 mL/min/1.73 m²`** (`CKD Stage 4`) for at least `3` consecutive months during the past `12` months.
**Constant albuminuria with some edema**; OR **definite decrease in kidney function**; OR **hypertension at least `40%` disabling under `DC 7101`**!
**`CKD` with `GFR 30 to 44 mL/min/1.73 m²`** (`CKD Stage 3b`) for at least `3` consecutive months during the past `12` months.
**Albumin constant or recurring with hyaline and granular casts or red blood cells**; OR **transient or slight edema OR hypertension at least `10%` disabling under `DC 7101`**!

**`CKD` with `GFR 45 to 59 mL/min/1.73 m²`** (`CKD Stage 3a`) for at least `3` consecutive months during the past `12` months *(Note: `GFR 45–59` sustained `>=3` consecutive months warrants **`30%` on `GFR` alone** without needing albuminuria or edema!)*.
**Albumin and casts with history of acute nephritis**; OR **hypertension noncompensable (`0%`) under `DC 7101`**.

**`GFR 60 to 89 mL/min/1.73 m²`** (`CKD Stage 2`) **AND** at least ONE of the following for `>=3` consecutive months during past `12` months: `(1)` structural kidney abnormalities (*cystic, obstructive, or glomerular*); `(2)` **albumin/creatinine ratio (`ACR`) `>= 30 mg/g`** *(microalbuminuria/proteinuria)*; OR `(3)` recurrent red blood cell (`RBC`), white blood cell (`WBC`), or granular casts.

lines: **Three High-Dollar Renal Dysfunction Audit Rules (`§ 4.115`, `§ 4.115a` Note & `38 U.S.C. § 1160(a)(2)`):**

1. **`eGFR` Lab Goldmine in Diabetic (`DC 7913 -> 7541`) & Hypertensive (`DC 7101 -> 7502/7534`) Veterans:** Every VAMC routine Basic/Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (`BMP`/`CMP`) prints calculated **`eGFR`** alongside serum creatinine, and `§ 4.115a`'s Note explicitly accepts **`eGFR` / creatinine-based approximations**! Whenever VAMC labs show `eGFR 45–59` (`30%`), `30–44` (`60%`), `15–29` (`80%`), or `<15` (`100%`) across `>=3` consecutive months in an Agent Orange Diabetic or PACT Hypertensive veteran, **file/audit secondary `DC 7541` / `DC 7502` immediately** (remembering `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b)` *Lang* constructive VAMC lab receipt in legacy claims)!

2. **The Unchanged `38 C.F.R. § 4.115` Nephritis–Heart Non-Combination Bar (and Its Two Carve-Outs!):** **`86 FR 54081` (eff. Nov. 14, 2021) did NOT amend `38 C.F.R. § 4.115`**! Under `§ 4.115`, ratings for **heart disease and any form of nephritis still CANNOT be combined**—instead, assign one predominant evaluation (elevating if warranted, or under `DC 7507` arteriolar nephrosclerosis evaluating under whichever system predominates)—**EXCEPT in two explicit carve-outs where heart and renal ratings DO combine separately:** `(1)` **absence of one kidney (`DC 7500`)** is the sole renal disability, **OR `(2)` chronic renal disease requires regular dialysis (`100%`)**! *(Note: Standalone `DC 7101` Hypertension without nephritis—or coexisting with non-nephritic voiding codes—combines normally, and pre-Nov. 14, 2021 `30%` or `60%` renal awards anchored on `DC 7101` `10%`/`40%` hypertension with normal `GFR >= 60` remain **statutorily grandfathered under `38 U.S.C. § 1155`**!)*

3. **Paired-Kidney Statutory Service Connection (`38 U.S.C. § 1160(a)(2)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.383(a)(2)`):** If a veteran has service-connected loss or kidney disease of **one** kidney (e.g., `DC 7500` unilateral nephrectomy for trauma/cancer at `30%` minimum) and subsequently develops non-service-connected `CKD`/failure in the **other** kidney (not due to willful misconduct), VA **must** compensate the combined bilateral renal impairment (`60%/80%/100%`) *as if* both kidneys were service-connected!

blocks.text: B. Voiding Dysfunction (60/40/30/20/10/0% — The Predominant-Area Trap!) & UTI (30/10/0%)

Under [`38 C.F.R. § 4.115a`](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.115a-4.115b-genitourinary-evolution), **Voiding Dysfunction** remained structurally consistent across `1994` and `2021`, divided into **three sub-tracks**—while **Urinary Tract Infection (`UTI`)** gained explicit stent/nephrostomy (`30%`) and `6-month` suppressive-therapy (`10%`) rules on November 14, 2021 (`86 FR 54081`):

headers: Rating Tiers & Exact Verbatim Thresholds (`38 C.F.R. § 4.115a`)
rows: **1. Urine Leakage / Continual Urine Leakage / Post-Surgical Urinary Diversion / Stress Incontinence** *(Highest Ceiling: **`60%`**!)*

• **`60%`:** Requiring the **use of an appliance** *(e.g., external Texas/condom catheter, urostomy/ileal conduit bag, artificial urinary sphincter)*, **OR** the **wearing of absorbent materials which must be changed MORE THAN `4` TIMES PER DAY (`>4/day`)**. · • **`40%`:** Requiring the wearing of absorbent materials which must be changed **`2 to 4` times per day**. · • **`20%`:** Requiring the wearing of absorbent materials which must be changed **less than `2` times per day** *(i.e., `1` pad/liner per day!)*.

• **Lay Competence Goldmine:** A veteran (and spouse) is **100% competent** to testify to how many adult diapers/pads (`Depends`, `Guards`, liners) are changed per day! Post-radical prostatectomy (`DC 7528`) veterans are routinely lowballed at `10%/20%` frequency when `2–4` pads/day (`40%`) or `>4` pads/day (`60%`) is documented in VAMC Prosthetics pad prescriptions! · • **Do NOT Let Examiners Require a Physician "Prescription" for OTC Pads:** The regulation requires *"requiring the wearing of absorbent materials"*, not a formal VA Prosthetics order.

• **`40%`:** Daytime voiding interval **less than `1 hour` (`<1 hr`)**, **OR** awakening to void **`5 or more` times per night (`>=5x/night` nocturia)**. · • **`20%`:** Daytime voiding interval **between `1 and 2 hours`**, **OR** awakening to void **`3 to 4` times per night**. · • **`10%`:** Daytime voiding interval **between `2 and 3 hours`**, **OR** awakening to void **`2` times per night**.
• **Disjunctive (`"or"`) Rule:** Nocturia alone (`>=5x/night = 40%`; `3–4x/night = 20%`; `2x/night = 10%`) satisfies the tier even if daytime intervals are completely normal!

• **`30%`:** Urinary retention requiring **intermittent or continuous catheterization**. · • **`10%`:** Marked obstructive symptomatology (*hesitancy, slow or weak stream, decreased force of stream*) **WITH one or more of**: `(1)` **post-void residuals (`PVR`) `> 150 cc`**, `(2)` uroflowmetry with markedly diminished peak flow rate (**`< 10 cc/sec`**), `(3)` recurrent `UTIs` secondary to obstruction, OR `(4)` stricture disease requiring periodic dilatation every `2 to 3 months`. · • **`0%`:** Obstructive symptomatology with or without stricture disease requiring dilatation `1 to 2` times per year.

• **Indwelling Foley vs. Appliance (`30%` vs. `60%`):** Watch the distinction between clean **intermittent self-catheterization** for retention (`30%` obstructed voiding) vs. requiring an external/suprapubic **urinary drainage appliance/bag** for continual leakage/diversion (`60%` urine leakage)!
**4. Urinary Tract Infection (`UTI`)** *(Updated Nov. 14, 2021 at `86 FR 54081`)*

• **Poor renal function:** Rate as **renal dysfunction** (`30%–100%`). · • **`30%`:** Recurrent symptomatic infection requiring **drainage by stent or nephrostomy tube** `[added Nov. 14, 2021]`, **OR** requiring **`> 2` hospitalizations per year**, **OR** requiring **continuous intensive management**. · • **`10%`:** Recurrent symptomatic infection requiring **`1–2` hospitalizations per year**, **OR** **suppressive drug therapy lasting `6 months` or longer** *(pre-2021 text said `"intermittent intensive management"` / long-term suppressive therapy without the strict `6-month` cutoff!)*. · • **`0%` `[added Nov. 14, 2021]`:** Recurrent symptomatic infection not requiring hospitalization, needing suppressive drug therapy **`< 6 months`**.

• **The `§ 4.115a` Predominant-Area Trap (`Kill-Switch`):** Opening text of `§ 4.115a` mandates that where diagnostic codes refer to these dysfunction areas, **ONLY the predominant area of dysfunction shall be considered for rating purposes** (*unless* distinct disabilities have non-overlapping symptoms under `§ 4.14`!). Thus, a veteran with `DC 7527` BPH who has *both* `3–4x/night` nocturia (`20%`) *and* wears `2–4` pads/day (`40%`) receives **ONE `40%` rating** (not `40% + 20%`)—always audit to make sure VA selected the **HIGHEST** dysfunction track (`60%` pads over `20%` frequency)!

blocks.text: 3. High-Value Diagnostic Code Audits (38 C.F.R. § 4.115b, DC 7500–7545)
A. DC 7528 Malignant Neoplasms of the Genitourinary System (Prostate, Bladder, Ureter, Kidney & Testicular Cancers)

items:
**Schedular `100%` & Mandatory `6-Month` Post-Treatment Exam Floor:**
• Under **`DC 7528`**, active malignancy of any genitourinary organ (prostate, urinary bladder, ureter, renal pelvis, kidney/renal cell carcinoma, testis, penis, urethra) warrants **`100%`**—and following the cessation of surgical, X-ray, antineoplastic chemotherapy, hormone/androgen-deprivation (`Lupron`/`Zoladex` — watch active vs. palliative continuous `ADT`!), or other therapeutic procedure, **the `100%` evaluation continues with a mandatory VA examination `6 months` following cessation of treatment**! *(Remember to check *Bradley v. Peake* statutory **`SMC(s)` housebound** whenever `DC 7528` is `100%` and other SC disabilities combine to `>= 60%`!)*

***Tatum v. Shinseki* (`2010`) vs. *Foster v. McDonough* (`2021`) Procedural Protection Split:**
• **Running `100%` Awards (*Foster v. McDonough*, `34 Vet. App. 338 (2021)`):** When a veteran is *currently receiving* a running `100%` rating under `DC 7528`, VA **cannot** terminate that `100%` rating without `(1)` conducting the mandatory post-6-month VA examination showing no local recurrence or metastasis, **AND `(2)` issuing `38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e)` 60-day advance notice** of the proposed discontinuance (with the lower residual rating taking effect `60 days` after the *final* decision notice, first of the following month!). However, *Foster* clarified that `DC 7528` post-treatment step-downs are regulatory *"discontinuances"*, so `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.343` and `3.344` sustained-improvement rules do **not** apply.
• **Retroactive Staged Ratings (*Tatum v. Shinseki*, `24 Vet. App. 139 (2010)`):** When VA grants initial service connection *retroactively* (e.g., an Agent Orange claim adjudicated two years after radical prostatectomy) and assigns staged ratings in a single decision, `§ 3.105(e)` prospective notice does not apply to historical closed stages—provided the medical record affirmatively establishes remission 6 months post-treatment.

**Mandatory Post-Prostatectomy / Post-Radiation Residual Triad (`Voiding` + `DC 7522 ED` + `SMC(k)` + `Digestive DC 7332`!):**
• Whenever `DC 7528` steps down from `100%` after radical prostatectomy, `TURP`, external-beam radiation, or brachytherapy, audit for **four concurrent entitlements**:
• **Voiding Dysfunction (`20%` / `40%` / `60%`):** Stress incontinence pad count (`2–4/day = 40%`, `>4/day` or sphincter/clamp appliance `= 60%`) or radiation cystitis frequency!
• **Secondary Erectile Dysfunction (`DC 7522`):** `0%` on/after Nov. 14, 2021 (`20%` **prior to Nov. 14, 2021** under *Williams v. Wilkie*, `30 Vet. App. 134 (2018)` whenever radical prostatectomy caused internal anatomical distortion!).
• **Mandatory Statutory `SMC(k)` (`38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a)`):** Loss of use of a creative organ—**even while `DC 7528` is at `100%`**, `SMC(k)` stacks on top of `100%` (and on top of `SMC(s)`!)!
• **Radiation Proctitis / Fecal Incontinence (`DC 7332` / `DC 7326`):** Pelvic radiation frequently causes chronic radiation proctitis/bleeding or anal sphincter weakness, which stacks **completely separately** under [System 07 (`§ 4.114`)](/cfr/modules/07-digestive-system-4.110-4.114)!

**Four Overlapping Toxic-Exposure Presumptive Gateways for `DC 7528` Cancers:**
• **Agent Orange / Herbicide (`38 U.S.C. § 1116`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(e)` — FULL `§ 3.816` *NEHMER* RETROACTIVITY!):** Covers **Prostate Cancer** AND **Bladder Cancer** (`Pub. L. 116-283, § 9109`, eff. Jan. 1, 2021 — audit all prior Vietnam, Blue Water Navy, Thai base, Korean DMZ, Guam, Johnston Atoll, and C-123 denials and survivor `§ 3.816(f)` estates!) ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc)).
• **January 2, 2025 Burn-Pit GU Cancer IFR (`38 C.F.R. § 3.320a`, `90 FR 23, 30`, eff. Jan. 2, 2025):** Establishes presumptive SC for **urinary bladder cancer, ureter cancer (including ureteric orifice and urachus), and related genitourinary cancers** for Gulf War (`>= Aug. 2, 1990` SWA/Somalia) and Post-9/11 (`>= Sept. 11, 2001` Afghanistan, Syria, Djibouti, Uzbekistan, Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Yemen) veterans!
• **PACT Act `38 U.S.C. § 1120(b)(2)(D), (H)` (`Pub. L. 117-168, § 406`, eff. Aug. 10, 2022):** Establishes presumptive SC for **reproductive cancers of any type** (prostate, testicular, penile) and **kidney cancer** for burn-pit-exposed veterans ([Playbook 15](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera)).
• **Camp Lejeune Contaminated Water (`38 C.F.R. § 3.307(a)(7)`):** `>= 30 days` (`Aug. 1, 1953 – Dec. 31, 1987`) establishes presumptive SC for **Kidney Cancer** and **Bladder Cancer** ([Playbook 07](/playbooks/07-statutory-presumptions-chronic-tropical-pow-als)).

blocks.text: B. DC 7522 Erectile Dysfunction & Penile Deformity, Male Reproductive Codes (DC 7520–7525, 7543) & VAOPGCPREC 5-89

headers: Pre-Nov. 14, 2021 (`59 FR 2523`) vs. Post-Nov. 14, 2021 (`86 FR 54081`) Rules & `SMC(k)` Hooks
rows: **Erectile dysfunction (`ED`), with or without penile deformity** *(Includes Peyronie's disease & penile scarring/trauma)*

• **Pre-Nov. 14, 2021 (`1994–2021`):** Titled *"Penis, deformity, with loss of erectile power"* — **`20%`** schedular rating **+ `SMC(k)`**! Under ***Williams v. Wilkie*, `30 Vet. App. 134 (2018)`**, *"deformity"* included **internal** distortion (such as radical prostatectomy surgical removal/alteration of internal structures), not merely visible external curvature (*Peyronie's*). · • **Post-Nov. 14, 2021 (`86 FR 54081`):** Reduced to **`0%` schedular** (*"with or without penile deformity"*), with Note directing penile scarring/deformity to `DC 7522` and **explicitly preserving `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a)` `SMC(k)` review**! · • **Grandfathering & *Payne* Rules:** Pre-Nov. 14, 2021 `20%` `DC 7522` awards are **grandfathered under `38 U.S.C. § 1155`**, and pre-Nov. 14, 2021 staged periods in *Nehmer* / pending prostatectomy claims still earn **`20%` + `SMC(k)`**! Under ***Payne v. Wilkie*, `31 Vet. App. 373 (2019)`**, `SMC(k)` applies to **multi-link secondary chains** (e.g., SC PTSD/SSRIs, SC Diabetes `DC 7913`, or SC HTN meds -> `ED`) and requires **NO formal claim (`§ 3.155(d)(2)`)** once reasonably raised in the record! *(Note: `PDE5` inhibitors like sildenafil/`Viagra` or tadalafil/`Cialis` restore temporary erection in some veterans—if `ED` prevents effective procreation without assistive medication/devices or medication fails/is contraindicated, audit `§ 3.350(a)` & *Ingram* carefully!)*
**Penis, removal of half or more (`7520 = 30%`)**; **removal of glans (`7521 = 20%`)**
Rate at **`30%`** (`7520`) or **`20%`** (`7521`), **OR rate as voiding dysfunction** if higher (`40%/60%`), **PLUS mandatory `SMC(k)`**!
**Testis, complete atrophy (`7523`: Both `20%`, One `0%`)**; **Testis, removal / orchiectomy (`7524`: Both `30%`, One `0%`)**

• **Mandatory `SMC(k)` (`§ 3.350(a)`):** Unilateral or bilateral SC removal (`7524`) or complete atrophy (`7523`) of a testis triggers **`SMC(k)`**! · • **`VAOPGCPREC 5-89` Vasectomy Rule (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive):** Prior elective sterilization (**vasectomy**) does **NOT** defeat `SMC(k)` when a veteran subsequently suffers SC anatomical removal (`DC 7524`) of a testis! · • **`DC 7524` Paired-Testis Note:** If **one** testis is removed due to SC injury/disease (other than undescended/congenitally undeveloped testis) and the **other** testis is absent or nonfunctioning from causes *unrelated* to service, assign **`30%`**!
Added Nov. 14, 2021 (`86 FR 54081`): **`0%`** schedular, with explicit footnote mandating **review for `SMC(k)`** if accompanied by testicular atrophy/azoospermia loss of creative function!

blocks.text: C. Stones (DC 7508 vs. 7511), Transplant (DC 7531), Systemic/Viral Renal (DC 7535, 7541, 7544) & Remaining § 4.115b Schedule

headers: Post-Nov. 14, 2021 (`86 FR 54081`) Rating Rules & Historical Diffs
rows: **Minimum `30%`**; OR rate as **renal dysfunction** (`60%/80%/100%`) if there is nephritis, infection, or pathology of the other kidney (*cross-check `38 U.S.C. § 1160(a)(2)` / `§ 3.383(a)(2)` if the remaining kidney has NSC disease!*).

• **Massive Nov. 14, 2021 `DC 7508` Diet/Drug Repeal (`86 FR 54081`):** From `1994–Nov. 13, 2021`, `DC 7508` (and former `DC 7510` Ureterolithiasis, consolidated into `7508` in 2021) awarded **`30%`** for recurrent stone formation requiring **`(1)` diet therapy, `(2)` drug therapy, OR `(3)` invasive/non-invasive procedures `>2x/yr`**. Effective **Nov. 14, 2021**, VA **deleted diet therapy and drug therapy** from `DC 7508`—requiring **invasive or non-invasive procedures (`ESWL` lithotripsy, ureteroscopy, percutaneous nephrolithotomy) `>2` times/year** for `30%`, or else rating as **`DC 7509` Hydronephrosis** (`30%` frequent colic w/ infection & impaired function; `20%` frequent colic requiring catheter drainage; `10%` occasional colic; severe -> renal dysfunction; *cf. Vazquez-Flores v. Shinseki*, `580 F.3d 1270 (Fed. Cir. 2009)`). · • **Grandfathering & `DC 7511` Quirk:** Pre-Nov. 14, 2021 **`30%` diet/drug `DC 7508` ratings are grandfathered under `38 U.S.C. § 1155`**! Curiously, **`DC 7511` (Ureter, stricture of)** *still* retains `1. diet therapy; 2. drug therapy; 3. procedures >2x/yr` for **`30%`** in `eCFR`! Also remember `§ 3.309(a)` **1-year chronic renal calculi presumption**.

**Cystitis (`7512`, incl. Interstitial)**; **Bladder calculus/fistula/injury (`7515–7517`)**; **Urethral stricture/fistula (`7518–7519`)**; **Prostatitis/epididymitis (`7525`)**; **BPH (`7527`)**; **Neurogenic bladder (`7542`)**; **Bladder diverticulum (`7545` `[NEW 2021]`)**

Rate as **voiding dysfunction** (`7512, 7515, 7517, 7518`), **UTI** (`7525`), or **voiding dysfunction OR UTI, whichever is predominant** (`7516` [suprapubic cystotomy = `100%`], `7519` [multiple urethroperineal fistulae = `100%`], `7527`, `7542` [huge secondary to Spine IVDS/radiculopathy, Diabetes, MS, or Parkinson's + check `SMC(k)`/`SMC(l)`!], and newly added `7545`). (`DC 7529` Benign neoplasms -> voiding or renal dysfunction).

**`100%`** from date of hospital admission for transplant surgery, continuing for **`1 year`** following hospital discharge (mandatory VA exam + *Foster* `§ 3.105(e)` 60-day notice); thereafter rate residuals as renal dysfunction with a **MANDATORY MINIMUM `30%` evaluation**!

**Chronic nephritis (`7502`), Pyelonephritis (`7504`), Arteriolar nephrosclerosis (`7507`), Dialysis (`7530`), Tubular (`7532`, `20%` min symptomatic!), Cystic (`7533`), Atherosclerotic (`7534`), Toxic (`7535`), Glomerulonephritis (`7536`), Interstitial/Gouty (`7537`), Papillary (`7538`), Amyloid (`7539`), DIC (`7540`)**

All evaluate under **`§ 4.115a` Renal Dysfunction** (`DC 7532` carries a **`20%` minimum** when symptomatic; `DC 7533` polycystic kidney disease is a compensable hereditary *disease* when aggravated or manifested per `VAOPGCPREC 82-90`; **`DC 7535` Toxic Nephropathy** explicitly lists **NSAIDs** [ibuprofen, naproxen, meloxicam prescribed for SC orthopedic pain!], antibiotics, radiocontrast, and heavy metals!).
**Diabetic Renal Involvement (`7541`)** & **Viral Renal Disease (`7544` — `HIV`, `Hep B`, `Hep C`)**

• **`DC 7541`:** `86 FR 54081` streamlined title from *"Renal involvement in diabetes mellitus, sickle cell anemia, systemic lupus erythematosus, vasculitis, or other systemic disease processes"* to **"Renal involvement in diabetes mellitus type I or II"** (rated as renal dysfunction; lupus/sickle-cell/vasculitis renal involvement still rates identically as renal dysfunction under `DC 6350` / `DC 7714` / `DC 7536`!). · • **`DC 7544` `[NEW Nov. 14, 2021]`:** Dedicated code for **HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C nephropathy** (rated as renal dysfunction—stacks separately from [System 07 `DC 7345/7354`](/cfr/modules/07-digestive-system-4.110-4.114) liver symptoms!).

blocks.text: 4. Regulatory Watchlist & Quarantine (91 FR 7118 — Rescinded 91 FR 9712)

lines: **QUARANTINE NOTICE — DO NOT CITE AS ACTIVE LAW (AGENTS Law 6):**

* **Rescinded `38 C.F.R. § 4.10` Medication Interim Final Rule (`91 FR 7118`, Feb. 17, 2026 — Rescinded `91 FR 9712`, Feb. 27, 2026):** VA's 10-day February 2026 IFR attempting to mandate medicated-state evaluations across Part 4 was **rescinded ab initio**.

* **Explosive *Ingram* / *Jones* Impact on `§ 4.115a` Voiding Dysfunction:** Neither the **Urinary Frequency** (`10%/20%/40%`) nor the **Urine Leakage** (`20%/40%/60%`) nor the **Obstructed Voiding** (`10%/30%`) criteria in `38 C.F.R. § 4.115a` mention oral medication! Millions of veterans with **`DC 7527` BPH**, **`DC 7512` Overactive Bladder / Cystitis**, or **`DC 7542` Neurogenic Bladder** take daily **alpha-blockers (`tamsulosin` / `Flomax`, `terazosin`, `alfuzosin`)**, **5-alpha-reductase inhibitors (`finasteride`, `dutasteride`)**, **antimuscarinics (`oxybutynin`, `tolterodine`, `solifenacin`)**, or **beta-3 agonists (`mirabegron` / `Myrbetriq`)** that artificially reduce nocturia, daytime voiding intervals, urinary urgency, and pad counts. Under ***Jones v. Shinseki*, `26 Vet. App. 56 (2012)`** and ***Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)`**, raters and examiners **cannot** discount unmedicated baseline frequency, nocturia, or incontinence! *(Contrast `§ 4.115a` `UTI` `10%`, which explicitly incorporates `>=6 months` suppressive antibiotic therapy under McCarroll).*

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Kidney, Bladder & Prostate Ratings: Comparing 1994 and 2021 Rules, Cancer Protections & SMC(k)
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: When VA evaluates prostate, bladder, or kidney conditions under 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.115a and 4.115b, most long-term ratings turn on functional categories—renal (kidney) lab function, voiding dysfunction (pad leakage, frequency, or obstruction), or chronic urinary tract infections—rather than the name of the diagnosis alone. Understanding the November 14, 2021 overhaul (published September 30, 2021 at 86 FR 54081) is especially important for Agent Orange (Nehmer), Camp Lejeune, and PACT Act Veterans with prostate, bladder, or kidney cancer (Diagnostic Code 7528), as well as Veterans developing diabetic or hypertensive kidney disease.
record_clues: Post-prostatectomy or radiation oncology records documenting urinary incontinence requiring absorbent pads (2–4 pad changes/day = 40%; more than 4 pad changes/day = 60%) alongside a Rating Code Sheet paying only 10% or 20% for daytime/nighttime frequency.

Active prostate, bladder, kidney, or ureter cancer (including Gulf War / post-9/11 urinary bladder and ureter cancer presumptions added January 2, 2025 under 38 C.F.R. § 3.320a, or Agent Orange prostate and bladder cancers under 38 C.F.R. § 3.816) reduced from 100% without a post-6-month VA exam and 60-day notice.
Urology prescriptions such as tamsulosin (Flomax), finasteride, oxybutynin, or mirabegron masking baseline urinary frequency or urgency on an exam.

Loss of one service-connected kidney (Diagnostic Code 7500) followed years later by non-service-connected disease in the remaining kidney, which triggers paired-organ protection under 38 U.S.C. § 1160(a)(2) and 38 C.F.R. § 3.383(a)(2).
important_cautions: Only the highest voiding category pays for the same condition: under 38 C.F.R. § 4.115a, VA cannot stack separate ratings for urinary frequency, obstructed voiding, and absorbent-pad leakage from the same prostate or bladder disorder—instead, VA must assign whichever dysfunction category provides the highest percentage.

Check the November 14, 2021 cutoff carefully: on claims filed on or after November 14, 2021, Diagnostic Code 7522 (erectile dysfunction) carries a 0% schedular evaluation (plus statutory SMC(k)) and Diagnostic Code 7508 (kidney stones) no longer pays 30% for diet or drug therapy alone, whereas pre-November 14, 2021 running ratings remain protected under 38 U.S.C. § 1155.

Post-treatment cancer reductions follow 38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e) notice rules rather than 5-year stabilization hurdles (Foster v. McDonough), meaning VA must wait 6 months after completing treatment, hold a VA exam, and give 60 days to submit evidence plus 60 days before lowering pay.

Do not cite the rescinded February 17, 2026 medication Interim Final Rule (91 FR 7118, withdrawn February 27, 2026 at 91 FR 9712) as active law, and remember that later court interpretations cannot be used to claim Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) against final decisions issued before those precedents (George v. McDonough; 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)).
questions_for_representative: Do my urology notes or lay statements show daily absorbent pad changes that support a 40% or 60% voiding rating under 38 C.F.R. § 4.115a rather than a lower urinary-frequency rating?

rows: Established Era-1 qualitative gynecological schedule (`DC 7610–7627`), evaluating mild/moderate/severe pelvic inflammation, prolapse (`DC 7621`), fistulas (`DC 7624–7625`), hysterectomy/oophorectomy (`DC 7617–7619`), radical/simple mastectomy (`DC 7626`), and gynecological malignancies (`DC 7627`).

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`< May 22, 1995`):** Governs pre-1995 CUE audits. Creative-organ `SMC(k)` applied from August 1, 1952 (`Pub. L. 82-427`), whereas breast loss alone carried **no** `SMC(k)` prior to November 1, 2000.

Binding General Counsel precedent holding that a **prior elective non-service-connected sterilization (tubal ligation or vasectomy) does NOT bar statutory `SMC(k)`** when a veteran subsequently suffers a **service-connected anatomical loss** of a creative organ (e.g., SC hysterectomy `DC 7617/7618` or oophorectomy `DC 7619`), because `§ 1114(k)` (`former § 314(k)`) compensates loss of bodily integrity independent of prior procreative function.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive:** Binding on all ROs and the Board (`38 U.S.C. § 7104(c)`). Any post-1989 rating denying `SMC(k)` on `DC 7617–7619` anatomical removal because of an earlier elective tubal ligation is undebatable **CUE**!

**First Major Gynecological & Breast Overhaul (Era 2):** Enacted `§ 4.116 Notes 1 & 2` (mandatory `§ 3.350` SMC check); replaced qualitative `DC 7610–7615` tiers with the **`30 / 10 / 0%` General Rating Formula** (continuous treatment); standardized `3-month` `100%` post-op floors on `DC 7617–7619`; modernized `DC 7624–7625` fistula pad counts and **`DC 7626` Breast surgery** (`80/50, 60/40, 50/30, 0%` + surgical definitions); and **created `DC 7628` (Benign GYN neoplasms) and `DC 7629` (Endometriosis `50/30/10%` w/ laparoscopy Note)**.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`May 22, 1995 – May 12, 2018`):** Assigning `0%` under `DC 7610–7615` when continuous oral contraceptives/hormonal/antibiotic treatment was required for control (`= 10%`), or omitting `SMC(k)` on `DC 7617–7620`, is plain-text CUE.

Amended **`38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)`** (`former § 3.350(a)(7)`) to grant statutory **`SMC(k)`** to women veterans for anatomical loss of one or both breasts (**complete mastectomy**: radical, modified radical, or simple/total mastectomy).

**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) & CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`Nov. 1, 2000 – Dec. 5, 2002`):** No breast `SMC(k)` existed before Nov. 1, 2000; during this 25-month window, lumpectomy/partial excision did *not* yet qualify.

**Broadened Breast `SMC(k)` (`§ 1114(k)` & `§ 3.350(a)` intro):** Removed `former § 3.350(a)(7)` and expanded breast `SMC(k)` to cover **`25%` or more breast tissue loss** (from a single breast OR both breasts in combination—capturing quadrantectomy, partial mastectomy, and wide local excision!) **OR receipt of radiation treatment of breast tissue**!

**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) & CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Dec. 6, 2002`):** Any decision on/after Dec. 6, 2002 rating `DC 7626` / `DC 7630` post-radiation lumpectomy at `0%` or `30%` without awarding **`SMC(k)`** (*Payne*/*Akles*) is textbook RO CUE!

**Second Major Gynecological & Breast Overhaul (Era 3 — Current Law):** Consolidated complete or incomplete pelvic organ prolapse into **`DC 7621` (flat `10%`, abandoning the proposed `POP-Q` stage threshold!)** and **removed `DC 7622` & `DC 7623`**; separated breast neoplasms into new **`DC 7630` (Malignant breast neoplasms `100%` + `6 mos`)** and **`DC 7631` (Benign breast neoplasms & other breast injuries)**; updated `DC 7627–7628` residual unbundling notes; and **enacted `DC 7632` Female Sexual Arousal Disorder (`FSAD` — `0%` + `SMC(k)`)**!

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= May 13, 2018`):** Pre-May 13, 2018 running `50%/30%` `DC 7621–7623` awards are **protected under `38 U.S.C. § 1155` & `§ 3.951(a)`**; post-May 13, 2018 `DC 7632` unlocks `SMC(k)` on open/new/secondary claims.

Enacted PACT Act burn-pit presumptive service connection for **`"reproductive cancer of any type"`**—expressly covering **female breast (`DC 7630`), ovarian, cervical, uterine, endometrial, vaginal, and vulvar cancers (`DC 7627`)** (`0%` floor, zero manifestation deadline). *(Note: VA sub-regulatorily added male breast cancer on June 17, 2024 at `89 FR 51224`, then prospectively rescinded male breast cancer effective **September 30, 2025**—leaving **female breast cancer `100%` untouched**; see Section 4 & [Playbook 15](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera)).*

**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (`>= Aug. 10, 2022`)** + `38 U.S.C. § 1305` / `§ 3.33` retroactive survivor DIC re-evaluations ([Playbook 08](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical)).
**QUARANTINED — Proposed / Not Finalized:** Proposed rule to eliminate the surgical laparoscopy requirement from the `Note` to `DC 7629` Endometriosis.

items: **`§ 4.116 Note 1` (Non-Compensable Physiological States vs. Compensable Complications):** Natural menopause, primary amenorrhea, and pregnancy/childbirth are **not** disabilities for rating purposes; however, **chronic disease, injury, or surgical complications of pregnancy/childbirth** (e.g., obstetric `DC 7621` pelvic organ prolapse, `DC 7624–7625` rectovaginal/urethrovaginal fistulas, chronic `3rd/4th-degree` perineal tear fecal/urinary incontinence, emergency cesarean adhesions/hysterectomy, or postpartum depression `§ 4.130`) incurred during active service **ARE fully compensable**!

**`§ 4.116 Note 2` (Mandatory `§ 3.350` SMC Audit):** Directs adjudicators to review **`38 C.F.R. § 3.350`** for Special Monthly Compensation whenever evaluating anatomical loss or loss of use of one or more creative organs or breast tissue.

Under **`VAOPGCPREC 5-89`**, a prior non-SC elective tubal ligation **never** bars `SMC(k)` upon SC removal of the uterus under `DC 7617` or `DC 7618`!

Codifies **`38 U.S.C. § 1160(a)` / `38 C.F.R. § 3.383`** paired-organ protection directly inside `DC 7619`! *(Note: `100%` 3-month convalescent floor does not apply to unilateral chemical/natural nonfunction without surgical removal).*

• **`DC 7621` Uterus, prolapse:** Complete (through vagina & introitus) = **`50%`**; Incomplete = **`30%`**. · • **`DC 7622` Uterus, displacement of:** Marked displacement & frequent or continuous menstrual disturbances = **`30%`**; With adhesions & irregular menstruation = **`10%`**. · • **`DC 7623` Pregnancy, surgical complications of:** With rectocele or cystocele = **`50%`**; Relaxation of perineum = **`10%`**.

**Unified `DC 7621` (`83 FR 15068, 15069`):** **Complete or incomplete pelvic organ prolapse** due to injury, disease, or surgical complications of pregnancy = **flat `10%`** *(Note: VA's Final Rule **abandoned** its proposed `POP-Q Stage II` floor—so **any** complete or incomplete prolapse warrants `10%`, plus mandatory separate evaluation of GU, digestive, and skin symptoms!)* · • **`DC 7622` & `DC 7623`:** **[Removed May 13, 2018]**.

**CRITICAL GRANDFATHERING & UNBUNDLING RULES:** · 1. **`38 U.S.C. § 1155` Shield:** Pre-May 13, 2018 running `50%` or `30%` awards under `DC 7621–7623` **cannot** be reduced to `10%` under the 2018 schedule! · 2. **Why `83 FR 15068` Set `DC 7621` at `10%`:** VA set structural prolapse at `10%` *specifically because* functional bladder, bowel, and skin impairments are **rated SEPARATELY** (`Esteban`): always stack **`§ 4.115a` Voiding Dysfunction / Stress Incontinence** (`60%` appliance or `>4` pads/day; `40%` `2–4` pads/day; `20%` `1` pad/day) **AND `DC 7332` Rectum & Anus Impairment / Fecal Incontinence** (`10%–100%`, [System 07 Digestive Diff](/cfr/modules/07-digestive-system-4.110-4.114))!

**`100%`:** Multiple urethrovaginal fistulae. · **`60%`:** Requiring appliance or absorbent materials changed **`> 4x/day`**. · **`40%`:** Absorbent materials changed **`2–4x/day`**. · **`20%`:** Absorbent materials changed **`< 2x/day`**.

*(Evaluated by analogy under `DC 7626` / `7628` prior to May 13, 2018).*

blocks.text: 3. High-Yield SMC(k), Analogous Pleading & Post-Cancer Unbundling Rules
A. The Dual-SMC(k) (K-2) Stacking Rule: Creative Organ (§ 3.350(a)(1)) + Breast Loss/Radiation (§ 3.350(a))

lines: **DISTINGUISH SINGLE CREATIVE-ORGAN `SMC(k)` FROM SEPARATE BREAST `SMC(k)` (`K-1` vs. `K-2`):**

1. **Within Creative Organs (`§ 3.350(a)(1)` = Max `1` `SMC(k)`):** Because `38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)` specifies *"anatomical loss or loss of use of **one or more** creative organs"*, concurrent SC hysterectomy (`DC 7618`), bilateral oophorectomy (`DC 7619`), and `FSAD` (`DC 7632`) authorize **only ONE `SMC(k)`** (`K-1`). Similarly, unilateral and bilateral breast tissue loss/radiation authorize **one** breast `SMC(k)`.

2. **Creative Organ + Breast Loss/Radiation = TWO `SMC(k)` Awards (`K-2` = `$279.74/mo` in 2026!):** In `38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a)`, *"anatomical loss of 25 percent or more of tissue from a single breast or both breasts in combination (including loss by mastectomy or partial mastectomy) or when breast tissue has been subjected to radiation treatment"* is a **separate statutory category** from *"one or more creative organs"*. Therefore, a woman veteran with **`DC 7630`/`7626` breast lumpectomy + radiation** (or prophylactic/therapeutic `BRCA`/cancer mastectomy + oophorectomy, or `DC 7626` breast radiation + SSRI-induced `DC 7632` `FSAD` / `DC 7620` chemo-induced ovarian failure!) is legally entitled to **TWO concurrent `SMC(k)` awards (`K-2`)** ([Master SMC Treatise](/docs/smc-complete-treatise-and-step-math))!

blocks.text: B. Navigating the DC 7629 Endometriosis Laparoscopy Gate (DC 7610–7615 & § 4.20 *Webb* Pivot)

Modern gynecologists routinely diagnose endometriosis clinically via transvaginal ultrasound, pelvic MRI, and empiric GnRH agonist/antagonist (`elagolix`/`Orilissa`, `relugolix`/`Myfembree`, `leuprolide`/`Lupron`) or continuous progestin response without subjecting the patient to invasive diagnostic laparoscopy. Yet until VA finalizes **`RIN 2900-AS39` (`90 FR 47266`, Oct. 1, 2025 — proposed / not finalized)**, the `Note` to `DC 7629` states: *"Diagnosis of endometriosis must be substantiated by laparoscopy."*

items:
**Practitioner Pleading Contract:** Never let an RO deny service connection altogether when surgical laparoscopy was not performed! Under ***Saunders v. Wilkie*, `886 F.3d 1356 (Fed. Cir. 2018)`** (functional impairment from chronic pain is a compensable disability even absent a specific pathological confirmation) and ***Webb v. McDonough*, `71 F.4th 1377 (Fed. Cir. 2023)`** (`38 C.F.R. § 4.20` analogous ratings cannot be defeated by demanding literal structural prerequisites unique to a listed code), **plead in the alternative**:
• Direct evaluation of chronic pelvic pain, dysmenorrhea, menorrhagia, or ovarian/uterine dysfunction under **`DC 7613` / `DC 7615`** (`10%` continuous hormonal/analgesic treatment; `30%` symptoms not controlled by continuous treatment); **AND**
• Separate secondary evaluation of dyspareunia under **`DC 7632` (`0%` + `SMC(k)`)**, secondary voiding frequency/dysuria under **`§ 4.115a`**, secondary IBS/dyschezia under **`DC 7319`** (`10%–30%`), iron-deficiency anemia from menorrhagia under **`DC 7720`** (*`former DC 7700` pre-Dec. 9, 2018*; note `DC 7720 Note` rates chronic blood-loss anemia via the underlying bleeding condition), and secondary depression/anxiety under **`§ 4.130`**.

blocks.text: C. DC 7630 Breast Cancer: Adjuvant Endocrine Therapy (Tamoxifen / Aromatase Inhibitors) & Residual Unbundling

items:
**The `6-Month` Post-Treatment Exam, *Foster* Notice & Adjuvant Hormone Therapy Dispute:**
• Under `DC 7630` (and `DC 7627`), the `100%` evaluation continues *"beyond the cessation of any surgical, radiation, antineoplastic chemotherapy or **other therapeutic procedure**"* until a mandatory VA C&P examination **`6 months` after discontinuance**, governed by **`38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e)` `60-day` advance notice** (***Foster v. McDonough*, `34 Vet. App. 338 (2021)`**—any premature reduction without a post-6-month exam AND `§ 3.105(e)` notice is **void ab initio**; [Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings)).
• **Audit Alert on `5–10 Year` Adjuvant Endocrine / Targeted Regimens:** Hormone-receptor-positive (`ER+`/`PR+`) and `HER2+` breast cancers are routinely treated for `1–10 years` post-surgery/radiation with oral Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulators (**`tamoxifen`**), Aromatase Inhibitors (**`anastrozole`/`Arimidex`, `letrozole`/`Femara`, `exemestane`/`Aromasin`**), ovarian-suppression **`goserelin`/`Zoladex` or `leuprolide`/`Lupron`**, `CDK4/6` inhibitors (**`abemaciclib`/`Verzenio`, `ribociclib`/`Kisqali`**), or anti-`HER2` immunotherapy (**`trastuzumab`/`Herceptin`, `pertuzumab`**). ROs frequently attempt to cut `100%` `6 months` after surgery/radiation by labeling tamoxifen/aromatase inhibitors "preventive/prophylactic." Always obtain an oncologist nexus statement explaining whether the agent is prescribed as **active systemic antineoplastic / cytostatic therapy to eradicate micrometastatic disease** (*sustaining `100%` under `DC 7630`!*), **AND**—even if `100%` eventually steps down—separately rate **every drug-induced side effect**: aromatase-inhibitor **polyarthralgia (`§ 4.71a` / `§ 4.59`)**, **secondary osteoporosis (`DC 5013`)**, **chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (`DC 8515/8520` + `§ 4.26` bilateral factor)**, **chemo-induced ovarian failure (`DC 7620 = 20% + SMC(k)`)**, and **tamoxifen endometrial thickening/polyps (`DC 7613/7628`)**!

**Mandatory Post-Mastectomy & Reconstructive Flap Unbundling (`DC 7630 Note` & *Esteban*):**
• The `Note` to `DC 7630` (`83 FR 15068`) expressly commands raters to evaluate non-overlapping residuals **in addition to `DC 7626` (`30%–80%`) + `SMC(k)`**:
• **Post-Mastectomy / Sentinel-Node Upper-Extremity Lymphedema:** **`DC 7121`** (`10% / 20% / 40% / 100%` under `§ 4.104`, [Cardiovascular Diff](/cfr/modules/06-cardiovascular-system-4.100-4.104)) + annual *Sursely* compression-sleeve clothing allowance if rigid/damaging (`§ 3.810`).
• **Shoulder / Arm Limitation of Motion & Nerve Injury:** **`DC 5201`** arm limitation (`20%–40%`), **`DC 8518`** long thoracic nerve (`winged scapula`), **`DC 8519`** thoracodorsal / intercostobrachial post-mastectomy neuropathic pain syndrome!
• **Reconstructive Muscle-Flap Donor Site Residuals (`TRAM`, `DIEP`, `Latissimus Dorsi` Flap):** Separate muscle-group ratings for abdominal wall (`DC 5319` Group XIX hernia/weakness) or back/shoulder (`DC 5302` Group II latissimus dorsi) harvesting ([Muscle Injuries Diff](/cfr/38-cfr-4.56#redline-diff)), **PLUS** painful/unstable donor & chest scars under **`DC 7801/7802` + `DC 7804`** ([Scars Diff](/cfr/38-cfr-4.118#redline-diff))!

blocks.text: 4. Toxic Exposure Presumptions: PACT Act (38 U.S.C. § 1120), Camp Lejeune, Radiation & Male Breast Cancer Reversal

items:
**PACT Act Burn-Pit Presumption (`38 U.S.C. § 1120(b)(2)(H)`, eff. Aug. 10, 2022):**
• Establishes presumptive service connection (`0%` floor, zero manifestation deadline) for **`"reproductive cancer of any type"`** in Persian Gulf (`>= Aug. 2, 1990`) and post-9/11 (`>= Sept. 11, 2001`) covered veterans—unconditionally encompassing **female breast cancer (`DC 7630`)**, **ovarian, fallopian tube, uterine/endometrial, cervical, vaginal, and vulvar cancers (`DC 7627`)**, plus **`38 U.S.C. § 1305` / `§ 3.33` retroactive survivor DIC re-evaluations** ([Playbook 08](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical), [Playbook 15](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera)).

**The Male Breast Cancer Sub-Regulatory Window & Preservation Rule (`89 FR 51224` -> Sept. 30, 2025):**
• On **June 17, 2024 (`89 FR 51224`)**, VA sub-regulatorily designated **male breast cancer (`DC 7630`)** as a presumptive PACT Act reproductive cancer (retroactive to Aug. 10, 2022), then **prospectively rescinded** that sub-regulatory presumption effective **September 30, 2025** (preserving all claims granted or pending under prior guidance while denying new post-Sept. 30, 2025 filings as non-presumptive).
• **Litigation Preservation:** For any male breast cancer claim denied after September 30, 2025, **always preserve both** `(a)` a statutory challenge that `38 U.S.C. § 1120(b)(2)(H)`'s plain text (*`"reproductive cancer of any type"`*) already covers male breast cancer as a matter of statute, **and** `(b)` direct toxic-exposure causation under **`38 U.S.C. § 1168` `TERA`** (`PFAS`/`AFFF`, `TCE`/`PCE` solvents, ionizing radiation, burn pits; [Playbook 15](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera))!

**Camp Lejeune (`38 C.F.R. § 3.307(a)(7)`, `§ 3.309(f)`) & Ionizing Radiation (`§§ 3.309(d), 3.311(b)(2)`):**
• **Breast cancer (`DC 7630`, female and male)** is a presumptive **Camp Lejeune contaminated-water disease** (`>= 30` cumulative days, Aug. 1, 1953 – Dec. 31, 1987; while female infertility and miscarriage are covered for `38 U.S.C. § 1787` healthcare/reimbursement and direct `TERA`/water-exposure nexus compensation claims; [Playbook 07](/playbooks/07-statutory-presumptions-chronic-tropical-pow-als)) and a primary **radiogenic malignancy** under `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.309(d)(2)(ii)` and `3.311(b)(2)` (alongside **ovarian cancer** under `§ 3.311(b)(2)`).

blocks.text: 5. Regulatory Watchlist & Quarantine Notice

lines: **QUARANTINE NOTICE — DO NOT CITE UNFINALIZED PROPOSALS OR RESCINDED IFRs AS ACTIVE LAW (AGENTS Law 6):**

* **`RIN 2900-AS39` (`90 FR 47266`, Published October 1, 2025 — Proposed Rule, Not Finalized):** VA published a **proposed** rule (*"Eliminating the Requirement for Laparoscopy To Establish Service Connection for Endometriosis"*) seeking to delete the diagnostic-laparoscopy prerequisite from `DC 7629`. **As of late 2026, `RIN 2900-AS39` (`90 FR 47266`) remains unfinalized** and has **zero legal force**; until a Final Rule takes effect, protect non-laparoscopic endometriosis claimants by pleading **`DC 7613`/`7615`** and **`38 C.F.R. § 4.20` analogy** (*Webb* / *Saunders*) in the alternative!

* **Rescinded `38 C.F.R. § 4.10` Medication Interim Final Rule (`91 FR 7118`, Feb. 17, 2026 — Rescinded Ab Initio at `91 FR 9712`, Feb. 27, 2026):** VA's 10-day IFR attempting to override *Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)` was **rescinded ab initio**. *(Note: While `DC 7610–7615` and `DC 7629` explicitly incorporate continuous-treatment control tiers into their text under McCarroll, post-mastectomy musculoskeletal/neuropathic residuals rated under medication-silent codes `DC 5201`, `8518–8519`, and `7804` remain fully protected by Ingram!)*

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Gynecological & Breast Conditions: Comparing Historical Rules, Endometriosis, Prolapse & Dual SMC(k)
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: VA's May 13, 2018 update to 38 C.F.R. § 4.116 (published April 9, 2018 at 83 FR 15068) reshaped how gynecological disorders, pelvic floor conditions, sexual health residuals, and breast surgeries or cancers are rated. Many Veterans and adjudicators overlook inferred Special Monthly Compensation (SMC(k)) after hysterectomy, ovary removal, breast radiation, lumpectomy removing at least 25% of breast tissue, or secondary Female Sexual Arousal Disorder (Diagnostic Code 7632) caused by psychiatric medications, Military Sexual Trauma, pelvic trauma, or diabetes—as well as separate post-mastectomy ratings for arm swelling (lymphedema), chest-wall scars, and nerve or muscle damage.
record_clues: A VA Rating Code Sheet granting Diagnostic Codes 7617–7620 (uterus or ovary removal/atrophy) or Diagnostic Code 7632 (Female Sexual Arousal Disorder) with no SMC(k) payment, or denying SMC(k) because of an earlier voluntary tubal ligation.

Operative or radiation summaries for breast cancer or breast surgery (Diagnostic Codes 7626 or 7630) showing mastectomy, 25%+ tissue removal, or breast radiation on or after December 6, 2002, alongside post-surgical lymphedema or nerve pain.

Gynecology or pelvic-floor physical therapy notes documenting pelvic organ prolapse (Diagnostic Code 7621) accompanied by stress urinary incontinence (absorbent pads) or bowel symptoms that were not rated separately.
Antidepressant (SSRI/SNRI) prescriptions for service-connected PTSD or depression, or PACT Act deployment histories paired with reproductive or breast cancers under 38 U.S.C. § 1120(b)(2)(H).
important_cautions: Proposed rule alert: VA's October 1, 2025 proposal to eliminate the laparoscopy requirement for endometriosis under Diagnostic Code 7629 (90 FR 47266, RIN 2900-AS39) is still a proposed, unfinalized rule and is NOT enacted law.

Understand the one-versus-two SMC(k) distinction: multiple reproductive conditions (for example, hysterectomy plus ovary removal plus Diagnostic Code 7632) yield a single creative-organ SMC(k) under 38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a)(1), whereas adding qualifying breast tissue loss (25%+ on or after December 6, 2002) or breast radiation unlocks a separate, second SMC(k) award.

Do not cite the rescinded February 17, 2026 medication Interim Final Rule (91 FR 7118, rescinded February 27, 2026 at 91 FR 9712) as active law, and check exact pre-2000, 2000–2002, and post-2018 effective dates before considering any Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) theory.

Never rush into a Board of Veterans' Appeals CUE motion: under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c), once the Board issues a final decision on the merits of a CUE motion on a specific prior Board issue, no further CUE motions are permitted on that Board issue.
questions_for_representative: Can we audit my Rating Code Sheet to verify whether VA overlooked statutory SMC(k)—or a second SMC(k) when both creative-organ loss and breast radiation or 25%+ tissue loss are present?
Did VA improperly deny SMC(k) after a service-connected hysterectomy or oophorectomy based on a prior elective tubal ligation, contrary to binding VA General Counsel precedent (VAOPGCPREC 5-89)?
Under post-May 13, 2018 Diagnostic Code 7621, did VA separately evaluate and combine my urinary leakage (under 38 C.F.R. § 4.115a) and digestive symptoms on top of the 10% prolapse rating?

If my breast cancer rating under Diagnostic Code 7630 stepped down after treatment, did VA separately evaluate post-mastectomy lymphedema, nerve injury, muscle-flap donor sites, and painful or deep scars?

Running pre-Dec. 9, 2018 100% rating for asymptomatic CLL (DC 7703) or TKI-controlled Chronic Myelogenous Leukemia (CML, former DC 7703 -> DC 7719) reduced after Dec. 9, 2018 solely because of the 83 FR 54250 schedule revision (void ab initio under 38 U.S.C. § 1155 & 38 C.F.R. § 3.951(a)!)

Post-treatment hematologic malignancy discontinuance (DC 7703/7709/7724 6 months; DC 7715 NHL 2 years; DC 7712 Multiple Myeloma 5 years) executed by automatic diary drop without a mandatory VA examination or 60-day § 3.105(e) notice (violates Foster v. McDonough, 34 Vet. App. 338 (2021))

DC 7712 MGUS or smoldering myeloma rated at 0% while omitting compensable secondary peripheral paraproteinemic neuropathy (DC 8520/8515), renal cast/light-chain nephropathy (DC 7502/7530), or osteolytic bone fractures
DC 7717 AL Amyloidosis scheduled for routine future examination or rated below permanent 100% (+ missing Bradley SMC(s) or multi-organ SMC(k)-(r) audit)

Gulf War / Post-9/11 veteran previously denied for leukemia, multiple myeloma, MGUS, myelodysplastic syndrome (DC 7725), or myelofibrosis (DC 7718) prior to the Jan. 10, 2025 38 C.F.R. § 3.320b burn-pit IFR (90 FR 1894)

Combat/trauma DC 7706 Splenectomy (20%) omitting separate ratings for Group XIX abdominal wall muscle injury (DC 5319), laparotomy scars (DC 7801/7804), or post-splenectomy pneumococcal/meningococcal sepsis residuals
killSwitches: Demanding a 100% initial evaluation for asymptomatic Rai Stage 0 Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) or monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis (MBL) on a claim filed ON OR AFTER December 9, 2018 (explicitly rated 0% under DC 7703 at 83 FR 54250)

Demanding a perpetual 100% initial evaluation for Chronic Myelogenous Leukemia (CML) in apparent remission on continuous TKI therapy (imatinib/dasatinib/nilotinib) on a claim filed ON OR AFTER December 9, 2018 (rated 30% under DC 7719 at 83 FR 54250)

Arguing that PACT Act § 404 Monoclonal Gammopathy of Undetermined Significance (MGUS, DC 7712 0%) triggers 38 C.F.R. § 3.816 Nehmer class-action retroactivity (expressly excluded from Nehmer; full symptomatic DC 7712 Multiple Myeloma and DC 7717 AL Amyloidosis ARE Nehmer class conditions!)

Claiming standalone disability compensation for asymptomatic Sickle Cell Trait alone without directly attributable pathological findings (barred by 38 C.F.R. § 4.117 DC 7714 Note, whereas Sickle Cell Anemia IS a compensable hereditary disease under VAOPGCPREC 82-90)

Evaluating secondary iron-deficiency anemia from chronic GI bleeding (ulcer, gastritis, hemorrhoids, colon cancer) separately under DC 7720 in violation of the DC 7720 Note requiring evaluation under the underlying blood-loss condition
Applying rescinded § 4.10 medication Interim Final Rule 91 FR 7118 (Feb. 17, 2026 — rescinded ab initio at 91 FR 9712, Feb. 27, 2026) to discount baseline severity on hemic codes silent on medication

McDonough* (`596 U.S. 740 (2022)`) / `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`** bitemporal boundaries governing **Body System 10 (The Hematologic and Lymphatic Systems)** under `38 C.F.R. § 4.117`.

*(For verbatim historical and current regulatory text of `38 C.F.R. § 4.117`, see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 4.117 Hemic & Lymphatic Systems (DC 7700–7725, Pre- vs. Post-December 9, 2018 & 87 FR 61248 Correction)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.117-hemic-lymphatic-evolution), [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.105(d)–(i), 3.343, 3.344, 3.951, 3.953 & 3.957 (Rating Reductions, Stabilization & Statutory Protections)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.105e-3.344-3.951-3.957-reductions), and [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.1–4.31 Subpart A General Rating Policy & Two-Era § 3.321(b)(1) Extraschedular Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.1-4.31-general-policy-snapshots); for Agent Orange `§ 3.816` *Nehmer* class retroactivity on B-cell leukemias, Hodgkin's, NHL, Multiple Myeloma, and AL Amyloidosis vs. PACT `§ 404` MGUS exclusions and `10 U.S.C. § 1413a` CRSC *Soto* recovery, see [Playbook 06 (*Nehmer* Herbicide Presumptions & CRSC)](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc); 1. Master Chronological Federal Register & Presumptive Ledger (1946–2026)

headers: Substantive Change Across `38 C.F.R. § 4.117` & Linked Part 3 Presumptions
rows: Enacted Era-1 `§ 4.117` (`DC 7700–7715`): hemoglobin-ladder `DC 7700` Anemia, `DC 7703` Leukemia, `DC 7704` Polycythemia vera, `DC 7705` Thrombocytopenia, `DC 7706` Splenectomy (`30%` -> later `20%`), `DC 7709` Hodgkin's, `DC 7714` Sickle cell anemia, and `DC 7715` Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (`59 FR 28260`, June 1, 1994). *(Multiple myeloma lacked a dedicated code prior to Dec. 9, 2018 and was rated by `§ 4.20` analogy.)*

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`< Oct. 23, 1995`):** Governs pre-1995 CUE audits and early *Nehmer* staged periods for NHL (`38 C.F.R. § 3.313`, Vietnam service) and Hodgkin's (`59 FR 5106`, Feb. 3, 1994).

**First Modern Hemic/Lymphatic Overhaul (Era 2):** Retitled section; standardized `DC 7700` Anemia hemoglobin cutoffs (`<= 5g/100ml = 100%` down to `<= 10g/100ml = 10%`); added **`DC 7716` Aplastic anemia**; set `DC 7706` Splenectomy at **`20%`**; codified `100%` active-disease + mandatory `6-month` post-treatment VA exam notes across `DC 7703`, `7709`, and `7715`.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`Oct. 23, 1995 – Dec. 8, 2018`):** Crucially, under Era-2 `DC 7703`, **both asymptomatic `CLL` ("watchful waiting") and TKI-treated `CML` received `100%`** as active incurable leukemias!

Added **Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (`CLL`)** (later expanded to **all chronic B-cell leukemias**, including hairy cell leukemia, at `75 FR 53202`, Aug. 31, 2010) to `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(e)` herbicide presumptions -> full **`§ 3.816` *Nehmer* class retroactivity**!
**Nehmer Retroactive Herbicide (§ 3.816) & CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive:** Any pre-Dec. 9, 2018 staged *Nehmer* period for diagnosed `CLL` (even Rai Stage 0!) commands **`100%`**!
**`77 FR 6466`** *(pub. Feb. 8, 2012; `RIN 2900-AN75`)* *(disambiguated from FRA rule `77 FR 13978`)*

**Created `DC 7717` AL Amyloidosis (Primary Amyloidosis):** Implemented VA's May 7, 2009 Agent Orange presumption (`74 FR 21258`) in Part 4 by assigning a **permanent, flat `100%` evaluation** upon diagnosis with **no scheduled future re-examination**.
**Nehmer Retroactive Herbicide (§ 3.816) & CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Mar. 9, 2012`):** Rating SC `AL` amyloidosis below `100%` or scheduling routine reduction exams is plain-text error.

**Second Major Hemic/Lymphatic Overhaul (Era 3):** Retitled *"The Hematologic and Lymphatic Systems"*; **repealed `DC 7700`** and enacted etiology-specific anemias (**`DC 7720–7723`**); split **`DC 7719` `CML`** (`30%`/`60%`/`100%` TKI tiers) from `DC 7703`; set **asymptomatic Rai Stage 0 `CLL` / `MBL` at `0%`**; created dedicated **`DC 7712` Multiple myeloma** (`5-year` `100%` floor for symptomatic myeloma + `§ 3.344(a)–(b)` protection vs. `0%` smoldering/`MGUS`); added **`DC 7718` (`ET`/myelofibrosis)**, **`DC 7724` Solitary plasmacytoma**, and **`DC 7725` `MDS`**.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Dec. 9, 2018`):** Running pre-Dec. 9, 2018 `100%` `CLL` and `CML` awards are **statutorily protected against reduction** under **`38 U.S.C. § 1155` & `§ 3.951(a)`**! Pending claims straddling Dec. 9, 2018 receive Era-2 `100%` prior to Dec. 9, 2018 (*Karnas* / `83 FR 54250` applicability clause).
Added **Monoclonal Gammopathy of Undetermined Significance (`MGUS` — `DC 7712` `0%`)** as a herbicide presumptive condition.

**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (`>= Aug. 10, 2022`):** **Excluded from `§ 3.816` *Nehmer* retroactivity** (`M21-1 VIII.i.2.B.1.c`), UNLESS `MGUS` progressed to symptomatic **`DC 7712` Multiple Myeloma** or **`DC 7717` AL Amyloidosis** (both of which ARE full *Nehmer* conditions!).
**`87 FR 61248`** *(pub. & eff. Oct. 11, 2022; **retroactively applicable as of Dec. 9, 2018**)*

**Correcting Amendment to `DC 7718`:** Fixed syntax/typographical omissions in the `100%` evaluation criteria and `Note (2)` for Essential thrombocythemia and primary myelofibrosis, retroactively applicable to December 9, 2018.

Enacted **`38 C.F.R. § 3.320b`**, adding **acute and chronic leukemias (`DC 7703`/`7719`), multiple myeloma including `MGUS` (`DC 7712`), myelodysplastic syndromes (`DC 7725`), and myelofibrosis (`DC 7718`)** as `PM2.5` burn-pit presumptive conditions for Gulf War / Post-9/11 veterans ([Playbook 15](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera)).
**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (`>= Jan. 10, 2025`):** Unlocks `§ 3.114(a)` 1-year lookback + PACT `§ 1305` / `§ 3.33` retroactive survivor DIC re-evaluations!

blocks.text: 2. Structural Overhaul Diff (Oct. 23, 1995 Era 2 vs. Dec. 9, 2018 Era 3, 83 FR 54250)

See [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 4.117 Hemic & Lymphatic Systems (DC 7700–7725, Pre- vs. Post-December 9, 2018 & 87 FR 61248 Correction)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.117-hemic-lymphatic-evolution) for verbatim Era-2 and Era-3 regulatory text.

rows: Single blanket **`DC 7700` (Anemia, hypochromic-microcytic and megaloblastic)** rated strictly by static **`gm/100ml` hemoglobin ladder** + clinical signs (`<= 5g = 100%`; `<= 7g = 70%`; `<= 8g = 30%`; `<= 10g = 10%`; `> 10g` asymptomatic `= 0%`).

**`DC 7700` REPEALED.** Replaced by four etiology/treatment-driven codes: · • **`DC 7720` Iron deficiency anemia** (`30%/10%/0%` IV infusions vs. oral iron; secondary blood-loss excluded per Note!) · • **`DC 7721` Folic acid deficiency** (`10%/0%`) · • **`DC 7722` Pernicious / Vitamin B12 deficiency anemia** (`100%/10%` + separate CNS/neuropathy!) · • **`DC 7723` Acquired hemolytic anemia** (`100%/60%/30%/10%/0%` immunosuppressives/transplant).

**Liberalization for Medicated Veterans:** Under Era 2, a veteran on lifelong B12 injections or oral iron whose medicated hemoglobin normalized above `10 g/dL` got `0%`; under Era 3 `DC 7720–7722`, continuous oral iron, high-dose folate, or B12 injections/nasal/sublingual therapy earns **`10%`** regardless of normalized hemoglobin!
Rated under **`DC 7703` Leukemia** -> **`100%`** throughout active disease or continuous treatment phase (including daily oral tyrosine kinase inhibitors [`TKIs`] like imatinib [`Gleevec`]).

Split into dedicated **`DC 7719` (`CML`)**: · • **`100%`:** Stem-cell transplant or continuous myelosuppressive/immunosuppressive therapy. · • **`60%`:** Intermittent myelosuppressive, OR `TKI` / interferon when **NOT in apparent remission**. · • **`30%`:** **In apparent remission on continuous molecularly targeted `TKI` therapy** *(blast crisis transforms back to `DC 7703` `100%` per Note)*.

**Massive `§ 3.951(a)` Reduction Shield:** Any veteran holding a running **`100%` `DC 7703` rating for `CML` on December 8, 2018** CANNOT be reduced to `30%` or `60%` based on the creation of `DC 7719` (`38 U.S.C. § 1155`; [Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings))!

Rated **`100%` under `DC 7703`** even during asymptomatic `"watchful waiting"` (Rai Stage 0) without chemotherapy because `CLL` remained an active, unremitted hematologic malignancy (`83 FR 54250, 54251`).

**`DC 7703`:** Explicitly assigns **`0%`** to **asymptomatic `CLL` or monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis (`MBL`) at Rai Stage 0**; **Rai Stages I–IV or any symptomatic/treated `CLL` receives `100%`** (+ `6-month` post-treatment floor).

**Huge *Nehmer* (`§ 3.816`) Staged-Rating Goldmine:** In any retroactive *Nehmer* or `§ 3.156(c)` `CLL` award reaching back before **Dec. 9, 2018**, Rai Stage 0 `"watchful waiting"` periods prior to Dec. 9, 2018 **MUST be paid at `100%`** (+ grandfathered at `100%` thereafter if continuously pending/awarded)!

Only **`DC 7704` Polycythemia vera** (`100%/40%/10%`) and **`DC 7716` Aplastic anemia** existed; **`MDS`** and **primary myelofibrosis / essential thrombocythemia** had to be rated analogously (`§ 4.20`) under `7716` or `7704`.

Revised **`DC 7704` Polycythemia vera** (`100%/60%/30%/10%` phlebotomy/biologics + separate thrombosis/stroke/gout/HTN); added **`DC 7718` Essential thrombocythemia & primary myelofibrosis** (`100%/70%/30%/0%`, corr. `87 FR 61248`) and **`DC 7725` Myelodysplastic syndromes (`MDS`)** (`100%/60%/30%` — **minimum `30%` floor** when ongoing biologic therapy or `1–3` transfusions/hospitalizations!).
Cross-check Camp Lejeune (`§ 3.307(a)(7)(iii)` `MDS`/aplastic anemia) and the **Jan. 10, 2025 `§ 3.320b` burn-pit IFR** (`MDS` `DC 7725` & myelofibrosis `DC 7718`)!

**Multiple myeloma had NO dedicated diagnostic code prior to Dec. 9, 2018** (rated by `§ 4.20` analogy, e.g., `7799-7703` or `7799-7715`); **`DC 7717` AL Amyloidosis** (`100%` permanent added Mar. 9, 2012).

**Added `DC 7712` Multiple myeloma:** **`100%`** symptomatic (**`5-year` post-diagnosis floor** + explicit `§ 3.105(e)` & `§ 3.344(a)–(b)` protection under `Note (2)`!) vs. **`0%`** asymptomatic/smoldering/`MGUS` (`ASH`/`IMWG` biomarkers per `Note (1)`); added **`DC 7724` Solitary plasmacytoma** (`100%` + `6-month` post-treatment floor); retained **`DC 7717` AL Amyloidosis (`100%` permanent)**.

Never leave `DC 7712` `MGUS` at a bare `0%` without auditing **secondary paraproteinemic peripheral neuropathy**, **renal disease**, **anemia**, and progression to **`DC 7712` (`100%`)** or **`DC 7717` (`100%`)**!

blocks.text: 3. Hematologic Malignancies, Post-Treatment Convalescent Floors & *Foster* Notice Traps
A. Side-by-Side Mandatory 100% Duration & Post-Treatment Re-Evaluation Matrix

A recurrent RO error in System 10 is **confusing the post-treatment mandatory `100%` duration across different hematologic malignancies** (not every blood cancer drops after `6 months`!), or terminating `100%` via an automated diary date without a C&P exam and **`38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e)`** notice:

rows: **Leukemia** *(Acute myeloid `AML`, acute lymphoblastic `ALL`, hairy cell, symptomatic `CLL` Rai I–IV; excludes `CML` `7719` & Rai 0 `CLL`)*

**`100%`** during active disease or treatment phase **+ `6 months` beyond cessation** of any surgical, radiation, antineoplastic chemotherapy, or other therapeutic procedures. *(Rai Stage 0 asymptomatic `CLL` / `MBL` = **`0%`** post-Dec. 9, 2018).*

**Mandatory VA examination** at `6 months` post-treatment cessation; any reduction requires **`60-day` `§ 3.105(e)` notice** (*Foster v. McDonough*, `34 Vet. App. 338 (2021)`, though `§§ 3.343/3.344` do not apply). Rate chronic chemo-induced peripheral neuropathy (`DC 8520`/`8515`), cardiomyopathy (`DC 7020`), cytopenias, fatigue, and psychiatric depression (`§ 4.130`) separately!
**`100%`** with active disease or during treatment phase **+ `6 months` after discontinuance** of surgical, radiation, chemotherapy, or other therapeutic procedures.

**Mandatory VA examination** at `6 months` + `§ 3.105(e)` notice. Audit post-mantle-radiation **secondary hypothyroidism (`DC 7903`)**, **coronary/valvular heart disease (`DC 7005`/`7000`)**, **pulmonary fibrosis (`DC 6825`)**, and bleomycin/vinblastine neuropathy!
**Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (`NHL`)** *(Includes indolent/follicular, diffuse large B-cell, mantle cell, cutaneous T-cell mycosis fungoides, Waldenström's macroglobulinemia)*

**`100%`** when there is active disease, during a treatment phase, **OR with indolent and non-contiguous phase of low-grade `NHL`** **+ `TWO (2) YEARS` after discontinuance** of surgical, radiation, chemotherapy, or other therapeutic procedures!

**CRITICAL `2-YEAR` FLOOR TRAP:** Unlike `DC 7703`/`7709` (`6 months`), `DC 7715` guarantees **`100%` for `2 full years` post-treatment**—AND low-grade/indolent non-contiguous `NHL` in `"watch and wait"` remains **`100%` indefinitely** (unlike Rai 0 `CLL`)! Cutting `NHL` at 6 months is undebatable **RO CUE** (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive).

**`100%`** for **symptomatic multiple myeloma** (`CRAB` end-organ features or `ASH`/`IMWG` myeloma-defining biomarkers per `Note (1)`), continuing for **`FIVE (5) YEARS` after the diagnosis** of symptomatic multiple myeloma (`Note (2)`)! *(Asymptomatic, smoldering, or `MGUS` = **`0%`**).*

**CRITICAL `5-YEAR` FLOOR + `§ 3.344` SHIELD:** Under `DC 7712` `Note (2)`, `100%` continues for **`5 full years`** from diagnosis before mandatory VA examination, AND any reduction is explicitly subject to **BOTH `38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e)` AND `§ 3.344(a) and (b)`** sustained-improvement stabilization protections! Even when `MGUS` or smoldering myeloma is rated `0%`, **separately rate** paraproteinemic neuropathy, light-chain renal disease (`DC 7530`), pathologic vertebral/rib fractures, and secondary mood disorder.
**Permanent flat `100%` evaluation** upon diagnosis (`77 FR 6466`, eff. Mar. 9, 2012; retained `83 FR 54250`).

**NO future examination scheduled.** Immediately audit for **`38 U.S.C. § 1114(s)` (`SMC(s)`)** (*Bradley* statutory `100% + 60%`) or **`SMC(l)–(r)`** by separately evaluating amyloid restrictive cardiomyopathy (`DC 7020`), nephrotic syndrome (`DC 7502`), autonomic/peripheral neuropathy, and GI malabsorption ([Playbook 12](/playbooks/12-aid-and-attendance-smc-l-r1-r2-and-smc-t))!
**`100%`** during active disease or treatment phase (including radiation, surgery, chemo, or autologous stem-cell transplant) **+ `6 months` after discontinuance** (`Note (1)`).

**Mandatory VA examination** at `6 months` + `§ 3.105(e)` notice; rate skeletal/neurological/radiation residuals separately, and monitor closely (`~50%+` risk) for progression to **`DC 7712` Multiple Myeloma (`100%`)**!

blocks.text: B. Toxic-Exposure Matrix Across DC 7703–7725 (Nehmer vs. PACT § 404 vs. § 3.320b Burn Pits)

items:
**Agent Orange / Herbicide Exposure (`38 U.S.C. § 1116`; `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.309(e), 3.816`):**
• **Full `§ 3.816` *Nehmer* Class Conditions (Footnote 1 & 2 Retroactive Back Pay + Uncapped `10 U.S.C. § 1413a` CRSC per *Soto v. United States*, `605 U.S. 360 (2025)`):** All **Chronic B-cell Leukemias** (`CLL` including hairy cell leukemia — `DC 7703`), **Hodgkin's Lymphoma (`DC 7709`)**, **Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma (`DC 7715`, plus `§ 3.313` Vietnam waters/shore)**, **Multiple Myeloma (`DC 7712`)**, and **`AL` Amyloidosis (`DC 7717`)** ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc)).
• **Non-*Nehmer* PACT `§ 404` Addition (`>= Aug. 10, 2022`):** **`MGUS` (`DC 7712` `0%`)** is presumptive for herbicide-exposed cohorts effective August 10, 2022 (`§ 3.114(a)`), **without** `§ 3.816` *Nehmer* class retroactivity—**EXCEPT** that if medical records show `MGUS` converted into **symptomatic Multiple Myeloma (`DC 7712` — `ASH`/`IMWG` `>= 60%` clonal bone marrow plasma cells, free light-chain ratio `>= 100`, `> 1` MRI focal lesion, or `CRAB` hypercalcemia/renal/anemia/bone lesions)** or **`AL` Amyloidosis (`DC 7717`)**, re-plead immediately as a **full *Nehmer* class claim**!

**Gulf War & Post-9/11 Burn-Pit Fine Particulate Presumptions (`38 C.F.R. § 3.320b`, `90 FR 1894`, eff. Jan. 10, 2025):**
• Effective **January 10, 2025**, VA added **acute leukemias, chronic leukemias (`DC 7703` & `DC 7719` — ALL types, myeloid and lymphoid!), multiple myeloma (including `MGUS`, `DC 7712`), myelodysplastic syndromes (`DC 7725`), and myelofibrosis (`DC 7718`)** as presumptive diseases for Persian Gulf (`>= Aug. 2, 1990`) and Post-9/11 (`>= Sept. 11, 2001` incl. Afghanistan, Djibouti, Syria, Uzbekistan) veterans ([Playbook 15](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera)).

**Camp Lejeune Contaminated Water (`38 C.F.R. § 3.307(a)(7)(iii)`):** `>= 30` cumulative days (`Aug. 1, 1953 – Dec. 31, 1987`) triggers presumptive SC for **adult leukemia (`7703`/`7719`), aplastic anemia and other myelodysplastic syndromes (`7716`/`7725`), multiple myeloma (`7712`), and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (`7715`)** ([Playbook 07](/playbooks/07-statutory-presumptions-chronic-tropical-pow-als)).

blocks.text: 4. Complete Non-Malignant & Myeloproliferative Schedule (DC 7702, 7704–7707, 7710, 7714, 7716, 7718–7723, 7725)

headers: Post-Dec. 9, 2018 (`83 FR 54250` / `87 FR 61248`) Evaluation Tiers & Key Practice Traps
rows: • **`100%`:** Requiring bone marrow transplant (`+ 6 mos` post-discharge + mandatory VA exam), OR infections recurring `>= 1` every `6 weeks` per 12-month period. · • **`60%`:** Intermittent myeloid growth factors (`G-CSF`/`GM-CSF`) or continuous immunosuppressives (e.g., cyclosporine) to maintain `ANC > 500/µL` to `< 1,000/µL`; OR infections `>= 1` every `3 months`/yr. · • **`30%`:** Intermittent myeloid growth factors to maintain `ANC > 1,000/µL`; OR infections `1 to < 4` times/yr. · • **`10%`:** Continuous medication (e.g., prophylactic antibiotics) OR intermittent myeloid growth factor to maintain `ANC >= 1,500/µL`.

• **`100%`:** Stem-cell transplant or chemotherapy/myelosuppressants (`+ 6 mos` post-discharge/completion + mandatory VA exam per `Note (3)`). · • **`60%`:** Phlebotomy **`>= 6` times/yr** OR molecularly targeted therapy (e.g., ruxolitinib `JAK1/2` inhibitor) to control RBC count. · • **`30%`:** Phlebotomy **`4–5` times/yr**, OR continuous biologic/myelosuppressive/interferon therapy to maintain platelets `< 200,000` or `WBC < 12,000`. · • **`10%`:** Phlebotomy **`<= 3` times/yr** OR intermittent biologic/interferon therapy. · • **Note (1) Separate Stacking:** Rate secondary **hypertension (`7101`), gout (`5017`), stroke (`8007–8009`), DVT/pulmonary embolism (`7121`/`6817`), or erythromelalgia/pruritus (`7825`) separately**! (`Note (2)`: leukemic transformation -> `DC 7703`).

• **`100%`:** Requiring chemotherapy for chronic refractory thrombocytopenia; OR platelet count **`<= 30,000`** despite treatment. · • **`70%`:** Requiring immunosuppressive therapy; OR platelets **`> 30,000` to `50,000`** with history of hospitalization for severe bleeding requiring `IVIG`, high-dose parenteral corticosteroids, and platelet transfusions. · • **`30%`:** Platelets **`> 30,000` to `50,000`** with mild mucous membrane bleeding requiring oral corticosteroids or `IVIG`. · • **`10%`:** Platelets **`> 30,000` to `50,000`**, not requiring treatment. · • **`0%`:** Platelets `> 50,000` and asymptomatic, or in remission. *(Note (1): **Separately evaluate `DC 7706` Splenectomy (`20%`)** and combine with `DC 7705`!)*

**Flat `20%` evaluation.** **Note — Separate Residual Stacking (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive):** Separately evaluate `(1)` any complications such as systemic infections with encapsulated bacteria (*S. pneumoniae*, *N. meningitidis*, *H. influenzae*), `(2)` **Group XIX abdominal wall muscle injury (`DC 5319`: `0/10/30/50%`)** for penetrating combat trauma ([Playbook 01](/playbooks/01-penetrating-wounds-scars-vs-muscles), [`Muscle Injuries Diff`](/cfr/38-cfr-4.56#redline-diff)), and `(3)` **painful or large laparotomy scars (`DC 7801/7802/7804`)** ([`Scars Diff`](/cfr/38-cfr-4.118#redline-diff))!

• **`7707`:** Rate for any peritoneal adhesions (`DC 7301`), muscle, or scar residuals. · • **`7710`:** Rate under `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.88c` or `4.89` nonpulmonary tuberculosis rules ([`System 04 Diff`](/cfr/modules/04-infectious-immune-nutritional-4.88b)).

• **`100%`:** **`>= 4` painful episodes/yr** in skin, joints, bones, or major organs (hemolysis/sickling with anemia, thrombosis, infarction) with residual symptoms **precluding even light manual labor**. · • **`60%`:** **`3` painful episodes/yr** OR symptoms **precluding other than light manual labor**. · • **`30%`:** **`1 or 2` painful episodes/yr** *(changed Dec. 9, 2018 from qualitative "repeated hemolytic sickling crises")*. · • **`10%`:** Asymptomatic, established case in remission, with identifiable organ impairment. · • **Hereditary Disease Law (`VAOPGCPREC 82-90` & `67-90`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.303(c)`):** Sickle cell anemia (and thalassemia / hereditary spherocytosis / G6PD hemolytic anemia) is a **compensable hereditary disease** whenever clinical symptoms first manifest in service or undergo permanent in-service aggravation (*O'Bryan v. McDonald*, `771 F.3d 1376 (Fed. Cir. 2014)`). By contrast, per **`DC 7714` Note**, **sickle cell trait alone**, without a history of directly attributable pathological findings (e.g., exertional rhabdomyolysis, splenic infarction at altitude, or renal papillary necrosis), is **not** a ratable disability.

• **`100%`:** Stem-cell transplant (`+ 6 mos` post-discharge + exam); OR RBC/platelet transfusions `>= 1` every `6 weeks`/yr; OR infections `>= 1` every `6 weeks`/yr. · • **`60%`:** Transfusions or infections `>= 1` every `3 months`/yr; OR **continuous immunosuppressive therapy or newer platelet-stimulating factors** (eltrombopag/romiplostim, per `Note (2)`). · • **`30%`:** Transfusions or infections `>= 1` per 12-month period. *(Note: Post-Dec. 9, 2018 `DC 7716` provides **`100% / 60% / 30%`** active tiers—removing Era 2's `10%` continuous-medication tier; cross-check `§ 3.309(a)` 1-yr chronic & Camp Lejeune `§ 3.307(a)(7)`!)*

• **`100%`:** Continuous myelosuppressive therapy, OR for `6 months` following hospital admission for stem-cell transplant, chemotherapy, or interferon (`+` mandatory VA exam per `Note (2)`). · • **`70%`:** Continuous or intermittent myelosuppressive, chemotherapy, or interferon to maintain platelets `< 500 x 10^9/L`. · • **`30%`:** Continuous or intermittent therapy to maintain platelets `200,000–400,000` or `WBC 4,000–10,000`. · • **`0%`:** Asymptomatic *(rate thrombotic/hemorrhagic/splenomegaly residuals separately; leukemic transformation -> `DC 7703`; Jan. 10, 2025 `§ 3.320b` burn-pit presumption!)*.

• **`100%`:** Stem-cell transplant or requiring chemotherapy (`azacitidine`/`decitabine`, `+ 6 mos` post-discharge/cessation + mandatory VA exam). · • **`60%`:** **`>= 4` blood/platelet transfusions/yr** OR **`>= 3` hospitalized infections/yr**. · • **`30%`:** **`1–3` transfusions/yr**, **`1–2` hospitalized infections/yr**, OR **ongoing biologic therapy** (epoetin/darbepoetin/lenalidomide/luspatercept). *(Transformation to `AML` -> `DC 7703` `100%`; Camp Lejeune & Jan. 10, 2025 `§ 3.320b` burn-pit presumptive!)*

blocks.text: 5. Regulatory Watchlist & Quarantine (91 FR 7118 — Rescinded 91 FR 9712)

lines: **QUARANTINE NOTICE — DO NOT CITE AS ACTIVE LAW (AGENTS Law 6):**

* **Rescinded `38 C.F.R. § 4.10` Medication Interim Final Rule (`91 FR 7118`, Feb. 17, 2026 — Rescinded `91 FR 9712`, Feb. 27, 2026):** VA's February 2026 attempt to override ***Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)`** was **rescinded ab initio** after 10 days. Where a `§ 4.117` code explicitly incorporates medication or treatment modalities into its rating tiers (e.g., `DC 7702`, `7704`, `7705`, `7716`, `7718`, `7719`, `7720–7723`, `7725`), evaluate strictly under the plain text of those treatment tiers; where a code is **silent on symptomatic/analgesic medication**—such as **`DC 7714` Sickle Cell Anemia** (where hydroxyurea, voxelotor, crizanlizumab, or opioid/NSAID pain regimens mitigate vaso-occlusive crisis frequency/labor impairment)—examiners and raters **cannot** discount baseline unmedicated impairment under *Ingram*!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Blood Cancers, Anemia, Splenectomy & MGUS: Comparing 1995 and 2018 Rating Rules
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Blood and lymphatic disabilities under 38 C.F.R. § 4.117 frequently intersect with Agent Orange (Nehmer), Camp Lejeune, radiation, and PACT Act burn-pit presumptions (including the January 10, 2025 rule at 38 C.F.R. § 3.320b adding acute and chronic leukemias, multiple myelomas, MGUS, myelodysplastic syndromes, and myelofibrosis). Because VA overhauled § 4.117 on December 9, 2018 (83 FR 54250, corrected October 11, 2022 at 87 FR 61248), checking whether a claim was pending or protected before December 9, 2018—and whether secondary organ or nerve complications were rated separately—can substantially change a Veteran's or Survivor's benefits.
record_clues: A retroactive Agent Orange (Nehmer) award for Rai Stage 0 Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (Diagnostic Code 7703) that assigned 0% to claim periods before December 9, 2018, or lowered a pre-2018 running 100% CLL or CML award solely because the rating schedule changed.
An automatic post-treatment rating drop on leukemia, lymphoma, or myeloma without an in-person or clinical VA examination and 60-day advance notice under 38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e).
A 0% rating for Monoclonal Gammopathy of Undetermined Significance (MGUS, Diagnostic Code 7712) where neurology or nephrology records show paraproteinemic peripheral neuropathy or kidney damage.
Combat or trauma spleen removal (Diagnostic Code 7706, 20%) without separate ratings for abdominal-wall muscle injury (Diagnostic Code 5319) or painful surgical scars (Diagnostic Codes 7801 or 7804).
important_cautions: Distinguish Multiple Myeloma from MGUS under Agent Orange Nehmer rules: full symptomatic Multiple Myeloma and AL Amyloidosis (Diagnostic Code 7717) are covered Nehmer conditions under 38 C.F.R. § 3.816, whereas PACT Act § 404 MGUS is a prospective statutory presumption and is excluded from Nehmer class-action back-pay rules.

Sickle cell trait versus sickle cell anemia: under the Note to Diagnostic Code 7714, asymptomatic sickle cell trait alone is not a ratable disability unless accompanied by directly attributable pathological findings, whereas sickle cell anemia is a compensable hereditary blood disease.
Do not rely on the February 17, 2026 medication Interim Final Rule (91 FR 7118)—VA formally rescinded it on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712), so it is not enacted law.

Check exact effective dates (October 23, 1995; March 9, 2012 for Diagnostic Code 7717; December 9, 2018 for the hematologic overhaul; January 10, 2025 for 38 C.F.R. § 3.320b) before alleging error, and remember 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c) allows only one final merits Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) decision per prior Board decision issue.
questions_for_representative: If my CLL or CML rating existed before December 9, 2018—or my Nehmer effective date reaches before December 9, 2018—did VA properly apply the pre-amendment 100% leukemia rule and 38 U.S.C. § 1155 protection?

Since my Multiple Myeloma (Diagnostic Code 7712) carries a 5-year 100% evaluation period, did VA apply both 60-day advance notice (38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e)) and 5-year stabilized-rating protections (38 C.F.R. § 3.344) before proposing any reduction?
Do my oncology or neurology records document secondary chemotherapy neuropathy, paraproteinemic nerve damage, kidney impairment, or Housebound / Aid and Attendance Special Monthly Compensation?
If I had a traumatic splenectomy (Diagnostic Code 7706), did VA separately evaluate my abdominal muscle group injury and surgical scar?
