rows: Established Era-1 qualitative skin schedules (`DC 7806–7819`): `DC 7806` Eczema (`50/30/10/0%` ulceration, exfoliation, exudation, itching), `DC 7816` Psoriasis (`50/30/10/0%`), `DC 7817` Exfoliative dermatitis (`100/50/30/0%`), `DC 7818` Malignant skin neoplasms, plus tropical/fungal codes (`7807–7815`).

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`< Aug. 30, 2002`):** Governs pre-Aug. 30, 2002 CUE audits. Under ***Pernorio v. Derwinski*, `2 Vet. App. 625 (1992)`**, BVA could not invent extra-regulatory physical-excoriation requirements to prove itching.

**First Major Skin Overhaul (Era 2):** Replaced qualitative Era-1 tiers with **`60 / 30 / 10 / 0%` Body Surface Area (`BSA`) / Exposed-Area `%` OR *"systemic therapy such as corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive drugs"*** (`12-month` duration); **removed obsolete `DC 7810` (Pinta), `DC 7812` (Verruga peruana), and `DC 7814` (Tinea barbae)**; enacted **`DC 7820–7833`** (infections, collagen-vascular, vitiligo, urticaria, vasculitis, acne, chloracne, alopecia, hyperhidrosis, malignant melanoma).

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`Aug. 30, 2002 – Aug. 12, 2018`):** Assigning `10%` when DBQ documented `20–40%` exposed-area involvement (`= 30%`) or `>=6 weeks` oral prednisone/methotrexate (`= 30%`) is plain-text CUE.

Overhauled **`DC 7800–7805` Scars & Head/Face/Neck Disfigurement** (8-characteristic matrix + `DC 7804` painful/unstable scar count; removed `DC 7803` — see [`Scars Diff`](/cfr/38-cfr-4.118#redline-diff)). Cross-impacts `DC 7807–7808`, `7818–7819`, `7828–7829`, and `7833` residual scar evaluations!
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Oct. 23, 2008`)** on scar/disfigurement residuals.
***Warren v. McDonald*, `28 Vet. App. 194 (2016)`** & ***Johnson v. Shulkin*, `862 F.3d 1351 (Fed. Cir. 2017)`**

*Warren* held `"such as"` in Era-2 `DC 7806` is illustrative, encompassing any systemic therapy akin to corticosteroids/immunosuppressives; *Johnson v. Shulkin* (rev'g `27 Vet. App. 497`) held **localized topical corticosteroid cream is *topical* rather than *systemic* therapy** unless applied on so widespread a scale that it acts systemically.
*Warren* is **Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** on CUE against final pre-2016 decisions; *Johnson v. Shulkin* enforces the plain boundary barring topical-cream CUE claims.

**Second Major Skin Overhaul (Era 3 — Current Law):** Codified **`§ 4.118(a)` route-of-administration definitions** of *systemic* vs. *topical* therapy (explicitly adding **biologics, retinoids, phototherapy, photochemotherapy, PUVA**); unified **General Rating Formula for the Skin** across `9` DCs (`7806, 7809, 7813, 7815–7816, 7820–7822, 7824`); rewrote `DC 7817` Erythroderma (`100/60/30/10/0%`), `DC 7825` Urticaria (`1st/2nd/3rd-line` therapy), `DC 7826–7827`, and reduced superficial `DC 7828/7829` acne/chloracne from `10%` to `0%`.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Aug. 13, 2018`):** Assigning `< 60%` when a veteran requires constant/near-constant systemic biologic therapy (`Dupixent`, `Humira`, `Skyrizi`, `Cosentyx`, `Otezla`) over 12 months is plain-text CUE! Pre-Aug. 13, 2018 awards are protected under `38 U.S.C. § 1155`.

Added **somatic `"melanoma of the skin"` (`DC 7833`)** and **neck cancers (`DC 7818`/`7833`)** as PACT Act burn-pit presumptions, and eliminated `§ 1117` Gulf War `10%` threshold & sunset for undiagnosed skin rashes ([Playbook 15](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera)).
**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (`>= Aug. 10, 2022`)** + `38 U.S.C. § 1305` / `§ 3.33` retroactive survivor DIC re-evaluations.
**QUARANTINED — Proposed / Not Finalized:** Proposed adding a note to `DC 7804` requiring objective exam demonstration of scar pain.

rows: Shared `DC 7806` template referenced by `DC 7809, 7813, 7815, 7816, 7820, 7821, 7822, 7824` *(Note: `DC 7814` Tinea barbae was removed Aug. 30, 2002)*.
Unified **General Rating Formula for the Skin** directly governing **`9` codes**: **`DC 7806, 7809, 7813, 7815, 7816, 7820, 7821, 7822, and 7824`**.

• **`DC 7806` (`50%`):** Ulceration or extensive exfoliation or crusting, and systemic or nervous manifestations, or exceptionally repugnant. · • **`DC 7816` (`50%`):** Generalized, with severe involvement of hands/feet or severe constitutional manifestations *(Note: `DC 7815` Pemphigus topped at `60%`)*.

**More than `40%`** of the entire body **OR more than `40%`** of exposed areas affected, **OR**; **constant or near-constant systemic therapy** such as corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive drugs required during the past 12-month period.

*At least one of the following:* · • Characteristic lesions involving **more than `40%`** of the entire body **OR more than `40%`** of exposed areas affected; **OR** · • **Constant or near-constant systemic therapy** including, but not limited to, **corticosteroids, phototherapy, retinoids, biologics, photochemotherapy, psoralen with long-wave ultraviolet-A light (`PUVA`), or other immunosuppressive drugs** required over the past 12-month period.

• **`DC 7806` (`30%`):** Exudation or constant itching, or extensive lesions, or marked disfigurement (*Pernorio*: no physical excoriation required to prove constant itching!). · • **`DC 7816` (`30%`):** Moderately extensive (`>10%` BSA) or chronic lesions of exposed parts.

**`20% to 40%`** of the entire body **OR `20% to 40%`** of exposed areas affected, **OR**; **systemic therapy** such as corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive drugs required for a total duration of **`6 weeks or more`**, but not constantly, during the past 12-month period.

*At least one of the following:* · • Characteristic lesions involving **`20% to 40%`** of the entire body **OR `20% to 40%`** of exposed areas affected; **OR** · • **Systemic therapy** (`corticosteroids, phototherapy, retinoids, biologics, photochemotherapy, PUVA, or other immunosuppressive drugs`) required for a total duration of **`6 weeks or more`**, but not constantly, over the past 12-month period.
• **`DC 7806` (`10%`):** Slight, dry, scaly, with intermittent itching. · • **`DC 7816` (`10%`):** Scattered, sparse plaques.

**At least `5%`, but less than `20%`** of the entire body, **OR at least `5%`, but less than `20%`** of exposed areas affected, **OR**; **intermittent systemic therapy** such as corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive drugs required for a total duration of **less than `6 weeks`** during the past 12-month period.

*At least one of the following:* · • Characteristic lesions involving **`5% to 19%`** of the entire body **OR `5% to 19%`** of exposed areas affected; **OR** · • **Systemic therapy** required for a total duration of **less than `6 weeks`** over the past 12-month period.
Slight, infrequent, or healed without disfiguring residuals.
**Less than `5%`** of the entire body and **less than `5%`** of exposed areas affected, **AND**; **no more than topical therapy** required during the past 12-month period.

*At least one of the following* *(where higher tiers are not met)*: · • Characteristic lesions involving **less than `5%`** of the entire body and **less than `5%`** of exposed areas affected; **and/or** · • **No more than topical therapy** required over the past 12-month period.

blocks.text: 3. *Johnson v. Shulkin*, *Warren v. McDonald*, & The 2018 Biologics / Systemic Therapy Revolution
A. Mandatory Citator Disambiguation (862 F.3d 1351 vs. 762 F.3d 1362; 28 Vet. App. 194 vs. 214)

lines: **DO NOT CONFUSE THE TWO *JOHNSON* LITIGATIONS OR THE TWO *WARREN* PAGES:**

1. **Skin Topical vs. Systemic Therapy (*Richard E. Johnson*):** Cite ***Johnson v. Shulkin*, `862 F.3d 1351 (Fed. Cir. 2017)`**, which **reversed** ***Johnson v. McDonald*, `27 Vet. App. 497 (2016)`** (`DC 7806` topical triamcinolone cream). Do **NOT** confuse this case with *Yancy Johnson*'s `38 C.F.R. § 3.321(b)(1)` collective extraschedular litigation in *Johnson v. McDonald*, `762 F.3d 1362 (Fed. Cir. 2014)` and *Johnson v. McDonald*, `28 Vet. App. 136 (2016) (en banc)`!

2. **Illustrative `"Such As"` Systemic Therapy (*Warren*):** Cite ***Warren v. McDonald*, `28 Vet. App. 194 (2016)`** for the substantive `DC 7806` holding that `"systemic therapy such as corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive drugs"` is illustrative rather than exhaustive (`28 Vet. App. 214` is a separate procedural jurisdiction opinion).

blocks.text: B. Era-2 (2002–2018) vs. Era-3 (>= Aug. 13, 2018) Therapy Rules & Biologic 60% Goldmine

items:
**The Pre-August 13, 2018 Doctrine (*Warren* & *Johnson v. Shulkin*):**
• Under *Warren*, `28 Vet. App. at 199–201`, any *systemic* treatment similar in nature to corticosteroids or immunosuppressives satisfied Era-2 `DC 7806`.
• Under *Johnson v. Shulkin*, `862 F.3d at 1354–56`, the Federal Circuit held that localized **topical** corticosteroid application (e.g., triamcinolone, hydrocortisone, clobetasol, fluocinonide, or tacrolimus cream/ointment) is **topical therapy** (`0%` therapy prong), **NOT** systemic therapy—*unless* the factual record proves a topical steroid was applied on such a massive, body-wide scale that systemic bloodstream absorption treated the body as a whole.

**The August 13, 2018 Route-of-Administration Bright Line (`38 C.F.R. § 4.118(a)`, `83 FR 32592`):**
• Effective **August 13, 2018**, VA codified bright-line definitions in `§ 4.118(a)`:
• **Systemic therapy:** Treatment administered **through any route *other than* the skin**—specifically oral, subcutaneous/intramuscular injection, intravenous infusion, suppository, intranasal, **plus** therapeutic **phototherapy, photochemotherapy, or `PUVA`** (`UVB`/narrowband `UVB`). *(Note: Systemic antibiotic/antifungal/antiviral courses count as systemic therapy when prescribed to treat the SC skin disorder—e.g., oral doxycycline/minocycline, oral terbinafine/itraconazole for `DC 7813`, or oral valacyclovir!)*
• **Topical therapy:** Treatment administered **through the skin** (creams, ointments, lotions, gels, foams, medicated shampoos, intralesional skin injections confined locally, or localized topical `UV` wand). Regardless of drug class (even potent Class I topical clobetasol or topical JAK inhibitor ruxolitinib/`Opzelura` cream), skin-applied medication is strictly **`0%` topical therapy** on or after August 13, 2018!

**The Modern Biologics & Oral Small-Molecule `30%` / `60%` Goldmine:**
• Modern dermatology treats moderate-to-severe **atopic dermatitis (`DC 7806`)**, **plaque psoriasis (`DC 7816`)**, **hidradenitis suppurativa (`DC 7820`/`7828`)**, and **bullous pemphigoid (`DC 7815`)** with maintenance **subcutaneous/IV biologics** and **oral targeted systemic immunomodulators**:
• **Biologics (Subcutaneous / IV):** `dupilumab` (**Dupixent**), `tralokinumab` (**Adbry**), `lebrikizumab` (**Ebglyss**), `adalimumab` (**Humira**), `etanercept` (**Enbrel**), `infliximab` (**Remicade**), `secukinumab` (**Cosentyx**), `ixekizumab` (**Taltz**), `brodalumab` (**Siliq**), `ustekinumab` (**Stelara**), `risankizumab` (**Skyrizi**), `guselkumab` (**Tremfya**), `tildrakizumab` (**Ilumya**), `bimekizumab` (**Bimzelx**), `rituximab` (**Rituxan**).
• **Oral Immunosuppressives / Retinoids / JAK-TYK2 / PDE4 Inhibitors:** `apremilast` (**Otezla**), `deucravacitinib` (**Sotyktu**), `upadacitinib` (**Rinvoq**), `abrocitinib` (**Cibinqo**), `methotrexate`, `cyclosporine`, `mycophenolate mofetil`, `azathioprine`, `acitretin` (**Soriatane**), `isotretinoin`, oral `prednisone`, and clinical **narrowband `UVB` / `PUVA`**.
• **Crucial Audit Rule (`0%` BSA Still Equals `60%`!):** Because the General Rating Formula is explicitly disjunctive (*"At least one of the following"*), a veteran maintained year-round on every-2-week `Dupixent`/`Humira`, monthly `Cosentyx`, or every-12-week `Skyrizi`/`Stelara` injections (which maintain continuous therapeutic drug levels across the entire 12-month period) **mandatorily qualifies for `60%`** (`30%` if `>= 6 weeks` total duration)—**even when the C&P examiner observes `0%` visible skin lesions on exam day because the biologic worked!** Assigning `0%` or `10%` based on cleared BSA while ignoring continuous biologic maintenance is textbook **RO CUE (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive)**!

**The Overlooked *Sursely* Annual Clothing Allowance (`38 U.S.C. § 1162`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.810`):**
• Even when a veteran receives only **`0%` or `10%`** because treatment is strictly *topical*, **every prescribed topical ointment/cream/lotion** (coal tar, anthralin, calcipotriene, tacrolimus, petrolatum-based triamcinolone/clobetasol, benzoyl peroxide, tretinoin) that **irremediably stains or damages outer garments** unlocks an annual tax-free **Clothing Allowance (`VA Form 10-8678`)**—and under ***Sursely v. Peake*, `551 F.3d 1351 (Fed. Cir. 2009)`**, **multiple** annual clothing allowances are payable if distinct SC skin/orthopedic conditions damage distinct types of outer garments ([Playbook 13](/playbooks/13-ancillary-grants-sah-auto-clothing-dea-spina-bifida))!

*(Remember **Exposed Areas** under `M21-1` & `§ 4.118`: **head, face, neck, and hands**—calculate exposed-area `%` as the percentage of total exposed skin surface affected, NOT as a fraction of whole-body Rule-of-Nines surface area!)*

headers: Evaluation Formula & Era-2 (`2002`) vs. Era-3 (`2018`) Rules
rows: **Dermatitis or eczema** *(atopic, contact, seborrheic, dyshidrotic, stasis)*
**General Rating Formula for the Skin (`60 / 30 / 10 / 0%`)** + alternate scar/disfigurement rating (`DC 7800–7805`) if higher.

Check Gulf War undiagnosed skin signs (`§ 3.317`), Camp Lejeune chemical exposure, jet fuel/`JP-8`/solvent contact, secondary stasis dermatitis to SC varicose veins (`DC 7120`), and `Dupixent`/`Rinvoq` **`60%`** biologic rule!
**Leishmaniasis:** American / New World mucocutaneous (`7807`); Old World cutaneous / Oriental sore (`7808`)
Rate as disfigurement (`DC 7800`), scars (`DC 7801–7805`), or dermatitis (`DC 7806`), depending on predominant disability.

**1-Year Tropical Presumption (`38 U.S.C. § 1112(b)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(b)`)** + Southwest Asia sandfly exposure (`DC 6301` governs visceral kala-azar leishmaniasis; [Playbook 07](/playbooks/07-statutory-presumptions-chronic-tropical-pow-als)).
**General Rating Formula for the Skin (`60 / 30 / 10 / 0%`)** + combine with `DC 7800` facial disfigurement or `DC 7830` scarring alopecia if non-overlapping (*Esteban*).

**Note:** Do **not** combine with **`DC 6350` Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (`SLE` `100/60/10%`)**—if systemic `SLE` is present, evaluate all lupus manifestations under `DC 6350`! *(Note: Oral hydroxychloroquine/`Plaquenil` year-round under standalone `DC 7809` = `60%` constant systemic therapy!)*
**[Removed August 30, 2002 at `67 FR 49590`]** *(modern tinea barbae is rated under `DC 7813` Dermatophytosis or `DC 7820` Skin infections)*.
Evaluate under `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.88c` or `4.89` (`100%` active TB -> graduated post-inactivity floors).
**Dermatophytosis** *(ringworm: tinea pedis, cruris, corporis, capitis, onychomycosis / tinea unguium)*

**Oral Antifungal Sleeper Rule:** A `12-week` oral **terbinafine (`Lamisil`)** or **itraconazole** regimen prescribed for recalcitrant SC toenail/foot fungus (`tinea unguium`/`tinea pedis`) exceeds **`6 weeks` of systemic therapy (`= 30%`)** over that 12-month period!
**Bullous disorders** *(pemphigus vulgaris, bullous pemphigoid, **porphyria cutanea tarda (`PCT`)**, dermatitis herpetiformis)*
**General Rating Formula for the Skin (`60 / 30 / 10 / 0%`)**; **Note (`83 FR 32592`):** Rate mucous membrane, ocular, or systemic complications separately!

• **`PCT` Herbicide Rule (`38 C.F.R. §§ 3.307(a)(6)(ii), 3.309(e)`):** Must manifest to **`>= 10%` within `1 year`** of last herbicide exposure (*IS* a `§ 3.816` *Nehmer* condition, unlike chloracne!). · • **Dermatitis herpetiformis:** Cross-check **`DC 7355` Celiac disease** (`89 FR 19735`).

**MANDATORY SEPARATE RATING NOTE:** `DC 7816` explicitly directs: *"Rate complications such as **psoriatic arthritis** and lesions of the mucous membranes or nails **separately**"*! Always audit `DC 7816` claims for **`DC 5002` Multi-Joint Active/Chronic Psoriatic Arthritis** (`20/40/60/100%` active flares OR separate ROM/painful-motion joint ratings under `§ 4.59` + `§ 4.26` bilateral factor; [System 01 Diff](/cfr/modules/01-musculoskeletal-joints-arthritis-implants-4.71a))!

**Dedicated `100 / 60 / 30 / 10 / 0%` Schedule (`83 FR 32592`):** · • **`100%`:** Generalized skin involvement **WITH systemic manifestations** (fever, weight loss, or hypoproteinemia) **AND** constant/near-constant systemic therapy (`corticosteroids, immunosuppressives, retinoids, PUVA, UVB, biologics, or electron beam therapy`) over past 12 mos, **OR** no current treatment due to documented failure of **`>= 2` treatment regimens**. · • **`60%`:** Generalized involvement **WITHOUT systemic manifestations** **AND** constant/near-constant systemic therapy over past 12 mos, **OR** documented failure of **`1` treatment regimen**. · • **`30%` / `10%` / `0%`:** Any extent of skin involvement requiring systemic therapy `>= 6 wks` (`30%`), `< 6 wks` (`10%`), or topical only (`0%`).

*Era-2 (`2002–2018`) Difference:* Under `67 FR 49590`, `DC 7817` awarded **`100%`** whenever generalized involvement had systemic manifestations (fever/weight loss/hypoproteinemia) *OR* required constant/near-constant systemic therapy—without requiring *both*! Grandfathered pre-Aug. 13, 2018 `100%` awards are protected under `38 U.S.C. § 1155`! Cross-check Sézary syndrome / cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (`DC 7818` / `7715`).
**Malignant skin neoplasms *(other than malignant melanoma)*** *(basal cell `BCC`, squamous cell `SCC`, Merkel cell, Kaposi's, cutaneous lymphoma)*

**100% Active / Systemic-Treatment Floor:** **`100%`** if requiring therapy comparable to systemic malignancies (**systemic chemotherapy/immunotherapy**, radiation **more extensive than to the skin**, or **surgery more extensive than wide local excision**), continuing until mandatory VA exam **`6 months`** post-treatment (+ `§ 3.105(e)` *Foster* notice). **Otherwise** (e.g., localized Mohs, curettage, cryotherapy, or wide local excision confined to skin): rate on **scars (`DC 7801–7805`), facial/neck disfigurement (`DC 7800`), or functional impairment**.

Check in-service solar UV exposure (flight line, deck, desert deployments), ionizing radiation (`38 C.F.R. § 3.311(b)(2)`), PACT Act **`38 U.S.C. § 1120` neck/head cancers**, and chronic burn/scar Marjolin's ulcer (`DC 7122` / `7804` secondary SC). Multiple facial Mohs scars frequently reach **`30%–50%+` under `DC 7800` + `DC 7804` painful scar count** ([Scars Diff](/cfr/38-cfr-4.118#redline-diff))!
**Benign skin neoplasms** *(lipomas, cysts, keloids, benign nevi)*
Rate as head/face/neck disfigurement (`DC 7800`), scars (`DC 7801–7805`), or impairment of function.
Painful multiple lipomas (`Dercum's`) or excised sebaceous cysts / keloids stack count-based painful scar ratings under **`DC 7804`** (`1–2 = 10%`, `3–4 = 20%`, `5+ = 30%`)!

**Skin infections (`7820` — incl. hidradenitis suppurativa / pseudofolliculitis barbae)**; **Cutaneous collagen-vascular (`7821` — scleroderma / dermatomyositis)**; **Papulosquamous (`7822` — lichen planus)**; **Keratinization (`7824` — ichthyosis / palmoplantar keratoderma)**
*(Added Aug. 30, 2002 at `67 FR 49590`; unified Aug. 13, 2018 at `83 FR 32592`)*: **General Rating Formula for the Skin (`60 / 30 / 10 / 0%`)**.

• **Pseudofolliculitis barbae (`PFB`, `DC 7820`/`7828`):** Check in-service shaving profile STRs + facial hyperpigmentation/scarring (`DC 7800`). · • **Hidradenitis suppurativa:** `Humira`/`Cosentyx`/`Bimzelx` biologic therapy = **`60%`**, PLUS stack deep axillary/inguinal/perineal scars (`DC 7801` + `DC 7804`) if non-overlapping!
**Chronic urticaria** *(defined in `83 FR 32592` as continuous urticaria `>= 2x/week` off treatment for `>= 6 weeks`)*

• **Era 2 (`Aug. 30, 2002 – Aug. 12, 2018`):** `60%` debilitating episodes `>=4x/yr` despite continuous immunosuppressive therapy; `30%` debilitating episodes `>=4x/yr` + intermittent systemic therapy, OR `1–3x/yr` despite continuous therapy; `10%` recurrent debilitating episodes `1–3x/yr` w/ intermittent systemic therapy OR continuous antihistamines/steroids. · • **Era 3 (`Aug. 13, 2018 – Present`, `83 FR 32592`):** ·   - **`60%`:** Chronic refractory urticaria requiring **3rd-line treatment** (`immunotherapy` [e.g., **omalizumab / `Xolair`**, **dupilumab**], `immunosuppressives` [cyclosporine], `plasmapheresis`) for control. ·   - **`30%`:** Requiring **2nd-line treatment** (`corticosteroids`, `sympathomimetics`, `leukotriene inhibitors` [**montelukast / `Singulair`**], `neutrophil inhibitors` [dapsone], `thyroid hormone`). ·   - **`10%`:** Requiring **1st-line treatment** (**antihistamines** — cetirizine, fexofenadine, loratadine, hydroxyzine, H2-blockers) for control.

**Massive Post-2018 Liberalization:** Under `83 FR 32592`, a veteran taking daily **montelukast (`Singulair`)** alongside Zyrtec for chronic hives qualifies for **`30%`** (2nd-line leukotriene inhibitor), and a veteran receiving monthly **omalizumab (`Xolair`)** injections qualifies for **`60%`** (3rd-line immunotherapy)—**without** needing Era-2 `"debilitating episodes"`!

**Era 3 (`83 FR 32592`):** **`60%`** persistent documented episodes refractory to continuous immunosuppressive therapy; **`30%`** recurrent episodes `>= 4x/yr` + intermittent systemic immunosuppressive therapy; **`10%`** `1–3x/yr` + intermittent systemic therapy, OR continuous systemic medication without recurrent episodes; **`0%`** or scars/disfigurement.
Distinguish localized primary cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis (`DC 7826`) from systemic ANCA/polyarteritis nodosa vasculitis affecting kidneys/nerves/lungs.

**Era 3 (`83 FR 32592`):** **`60%`** recurrent mucosal, palmar, or plantar involvement **impairing mastication, use of hands, or ambulation** `>= 4x/yr` despite ongoing immunosuppressive therapy; **`30%`** recurrent mucosal/palmar/plantar `>= 4x/yr` *not* impairing function + intermittent systemic therapy; **`10%`** `1–3x/yr` + intermittent systemic therapy OR continuous systemic medication.

Check secondary SC (`§ 3.310(a)` / `§ 1151`) when Stevens-Johnson / `TEN` was triggered by anticonvulsants (`lamotrigine`/`carbamazepine`), NSAIDs, allopurinol, or antibiotics prescribed for an SC disability, and rate ocular/corneal/mucosal scarring separately!

• **Era 2 (`2002–Aug. 12, 2018`):** `30%` deep acne `>=40%` face/neck; `10%` deep acne `<40%` face/neck or non-face/neck, **OR superficial acne with many comedones and papules and pustules**. · • **Era 3 (`Aug. 13, 2018 – Present`):** **`30%`** deep acne (deep inflamed nodules and pus-filled cysts) `>=40%` face & neck; **`10%`** deep acne `<40%` face & neck, or deep acne other than face & neck; **`0%`** **superficial acne (comedones, papules, pustules) of any extent** *(OR rate as `DC 7800` disfigurement or `DC 7801–7805` scars!)*.

**Grandfathering & `DC 7800` Pivot:** Pre-Aug. 13, 2018 `10%` superficial acne awards are **protected under `38 U.S.C. § 1155`**! For post-2018 acne, always evaluate **pitted/depressed/hyperpigmented facial acne scars (`>6 sq in`) under `DC 7800` (`10%–30%+`)** and tender cystic scars under **`DC 7804`**! Check steroid-induced acne secondary to SC systemic prednisone/testosterone.

• **`30%`:** Deep acne affecting **`>= 40%` of face and neck**. · • **`20%`:** Deep acne affecting **intertriginous areas** (axillae, anogenital region, skin folds of breasts or between digits). · • **`10%`:** Deep acne affecting **`< 40%` of face and neck**, or deep acne affecting **non-intertriginous areas** other than face and neck *(pre-Aug. 13, 2018 also included superficial acne with many comedones/papules/pustules!)*. · • **`0%` *(>= Aug. 13, 2018)*:** Superficial acne of any extent *(OR rate as `DC 7800` disfigurement or `DC 7801–7805` scars)*.

**DOUBLE AGENT ORANGE TRAP:** · 1. **`1-Year` `10%` Manifestation Gate (`38 C.F.R. §§ 3.307(a)(6)(ii), 3.309(e)`):** Presumptive SC requires chloracne to manifest to **`>= 10%` within `1 year`** of last herbicide exposure (audit STRs/post-Vietnam separation exams for retroauricular/malar cysts, `"cystic acne"`, or folliculitis misdiagnosed in 1966–1975—use `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)` if STRs were unassociated!). · 2. **Excluded from `§ 3.816` *Nehmer* Class Retroactivity** per `M21-1 VIII.i.2.B.1.c` ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc))!
• **`30%`:** **Unable to handle paper or tools** because of moisture, **and unresponsive to therapy**. · • **`0%`:** Able to handle paper or tools after therapy.
Check secondary SC to autonomic neuropathy, SSRI/SNRI psychiatric medications (`sertraline`, `venlafaxine`, `duloxetine`), PTSD hyperarousal, or hyperthyroidism (`DC 7900`).

**`100%`** during active malignancy or antineoplastic treatment **exceeding wide local excision** (e.g., systemic immunotherapy `pembrolizumab`/`Keytruda`, `nivolumab`/`Opdivo`, `ipilimumab`/`Yervoy`, targeted `BRAF`/`MEK` therapy, sentinel lymph node biopsy/dissection, radiation) + **`6 months`** post-cessation -> mandatory C&P exam & `§ 3.105(e)` *Foster* notice -> rate residuals (`DC 7800–7805` scars, lymphedema `DC 7121`, metastasis). *(If treated solely by wide local excision confined to skin, rate immediately on scars/disfigurement/function).*

**PACT Act Game-Changer (`38 U.S.C. § 1120(b)(2)(G)`, eff. Aug. 10, 2022):** Added **`"melanoma of the skin"`** (`DC 7833` — invasive AND *in situ* melanoma per VA PACT policy!) as a **presumptive burn-pit / Gulf War / post-9/11 somatic cancer** ([Playbook 15](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera), [Playbook 08](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical))!

Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)` was **rescinded ab initio**. *(Note: While the General Rating Formula for the Skin and `DC 7825–7827`/`7832` explicitly incorporate treatment/medication tiers into their text under McCarroll/Jackson, secondary orthopedic/neurological/psychiatric sequelae of skin disorders evaluated under medication-silent codes remain fully protected by Ingram!)*

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Eczema, Psoriasis, Hives, Chloracne & Melanoma: Comparing Topical vs. Biologic Skin Rules
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: One of the most common VA rating mistakes in dermatology claims happens when a Veteran takes a modern biologic injection, oral immunomodulator, or phototherapy regimen that successfully clears most visible skin plaques—and VA rates the condition at 0% or 10% based on small body-surface area at the exam while overlooking the 30% or 60% systemic-therapy tiers under 38 C.F.R. § 4.118. This historical comparison tracks how VA rated dermatitis, psoriasis, chronic hives (urticaria), Agent Orange chloracne, and skin cancers across the 1978, August 30, 2002, and August 13, 2018 schedules.
record_clues: A post-August 13, 2018 Rating Code Sheet paying 0% or 10% for dermatitis (Diagnostic Code 7806) or psoriasis (Diagnostic Code 7816) despite pharmacy refill logs showing year-round biologic or oral systemic therapy (such as Dupixent, Humira, Cosentyx, Skyrizi, Otezla, Rinvoq, or methotrexate).
Psoriasis (Diagnostic Code 7816) medical records documenting joint swelling, stiffness, or pain without a separate evaluation for psoriatic arthritis (Diagnostic Code 5002).

Allergy/immunology notes for chronic urticaria (hives, Diagnostic Code 7825) showing third-line omalizumab (Xolair) or cyclosporine (60% post-August 13, 2018) or second-line montelukast/steroids (30%).
A pre-August 13, 2018 running 10% superficial acne or chloracne rating (Diagnostic Codes 7828 or 7829) reduced to 0% after August 13, 2018 solely because the rating schedule changed.
important_cautions: Topical creams do not trigger 30% or 60% systemic tiers: localized steroid or calcineurin creams/ointments (such as triamcinolone, clobetasol, hydrocortisone, or tacrolimus) are classified as topical therapy rather than systemic therapy under Johnson v. Shulkin and 38 C.F.R. § 4.118(a), though they can qualify for annual Clothing Allowances under 38 C.F.R. § 3.810 if they stain or damage outer clothing.

Chloracne date and Nehmer rule: Agent Orange chloracne (Diagnostic Code 7829) requires 10%+ manifestation within 1 year of last herbicide exposure for presumptive service connection under 38 C.F.R. § 3.307(a)(6)(ii) and is excluded from special Nehmer class-action retroactivity.

Localized skin cancer procedures: simple Mohs surgery, cryotherapy, curettage, topical 5-FU, or wide local excision confined to the skin does not trigger the automatic 100% active-malignancy tier under Diagnostic Codes 7818 or 7833 (which requires more extensive surgery, systemic therapy, or extensive radiation).

Unfinalized and rescinded rules caution: VA's September 29, 2025 painful-scar proposal (90 FR 46542) remains an unfinalized proposed rule (not enacted law), and VA's February 17, 2026 medication Interim Final Rule (91 FR 7118) was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712).
questions_for_representative: Do my pharmacy refill records over the past 12 months prove constant or near-constant systemic biologic, immunosuppressive, or phototherapy use warranting 60% (or 6+ weeks warranting 30%) under 38 C.F.R. § 4.118?
If I have service-connected psoriasis, have we checked my records for a separate psoriatic arthritis evaluation under Diagnostic Code 5002?
Did VA unlawfully lower a pre-August 13, 2018 running 10% acne or chloracne rating without proving actual medical improvement as required by 38 U.S.C. § 1155 and 38 C.F.R. § 3.951(a)?
Have I applied by August 1 for an annual VA Clothing Allowance (or two allowances if multiple medications or braces affect distinct garments) under 38 C.F.R. § 3.810?

McDonough* (`596 U.S. 740 (2022)`) / `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`** bitemporal boundaries governing **Body System 12 (The Endocrine System)** under `38 C.F.R. § 4.119`.

*(For verbatim multi-era regulatory text of `38 C.F.R. § 4.119`, see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 4.119 Endocrine System (DC 7900–7919, Pre- vs. Post-December 10, 2017)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.119-endocrine-evolution), [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.105(d)–(i), 3.343, 3.344, 3.951, 3.953 & 3.957 (Rating Reductions, Stabilization & Statutory Protections)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.105e-3.344-3.951-3.957-reductions), and [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.1–4.31 Subpart A General Rating Policy & Two-Era § 3.321(b)(1) Extraschedular Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.1-4.31-general-policy-snapshots); for `DC 7913` Agent Orange Type 2 Diabetes, `DC 7903` *Nehmer* / Blue Water Navy / Thailand / PACT hypothyroidism, and `10 U.S.C. § 1413a` CRSC *Soto* recovery, see [Playbook 06 (*Nehmer* Herbicide Presumptions & CRSC)](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc); for multi-system secondary service connection, incremental aggravation (`§ 3.310(b)`), TBI pituitary deficiency (`§ 3.310(d)`), and intermediate obesity (`VAOPGCPREC 1-2017`), see [Playbook 14 (Secondary Service Connection & Obesity)](/playbooks/14-secondary-service-connection-aggravation-obesity); for PACT Act `§ 1120` thyroid/endocrine cancers, see [Playbook 15 (Gulf War, Burn Pits & PACT/TERA)](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera); for cross-system residual schedules, see [`Subpart A General Rating Policy Diff`](/cfr/modules/subpart-a-general-rating-policy-4.1-4.31), [`System 06 Cardiovascular Diff`](/cfr/modules/06-cardiovascular-system-4.100-4.104), [`System 13 Neurological & Peripheral Nerves Diff`](/cfr/modules/13-neurological-tbi-nerves-4.120-4.124a), [Master SMC Treatise](/docs/smc-complete-treatise-and-step-math), [VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon), and [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).*
1. Master Chronological Federal Register & Precedent Ledger (1946–2026)

rows: Established Era-1 qualitative endocrine schedule (`DC 7900–7915`): basal metabolic rate (`BMR`) thyroid criteria, qualitative mild/moderate/moderately severe/severe `DC 7913` Diabetes Mellitus tiers, `DC 7910` Hyperadrenia, and `DC 7911` Addison's disease.
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`< June 6, 1996`):** Governs pre-1996 CUE audits and pre-June 6, 1996 staged periods in retroactive *Nehmer* Footnote 1 awards.

**First Major Endocrine Overhaul (Era 2):** Eliminated obsolete `BMR` testing; created ongoing `10/30/60/100%` symptom/medication tiers for `DC 7900` Hyperthyroidism and `DC 7903` Hypothyroidism (`10%` for *"fatigability, or; continuous medication required for control"*); restructured `DC 7913` Diabetes (`10/20/40/60/100%` + Note (1) separate complications); **removed `DC 7910` Hyperadrenia**; added **`DC 7916–7919`**.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`June 6, 1996 – Dec. 9, 2017`):** Denying `10%` under `DC 7903` when record undisputedly showed continuous levothyroxine/Synthroid required for control, or omitting Note (1) diabetic neuropathy, is plain-text CUE.

Added **Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (`DC 7913`)** to `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(e)` herbicide presumptions, triggering **`38 C.F.R. § 3.816` *Nehmer* Footnote 1 & 2 retroactivity** back to post-Sept. 25, 1985 claims (extended to Blue Water Navy Jan. 1, 2020 via `Pub. L. 116-23` / *Procopio*).

**Nehmer Retroactive Herbicide (§ 3.816) & CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive:** Unlocks decades of staged `DC 7913` + secondary complication back pay and `§ 3.816(f)` survivor estate payouts ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc)).

Construed `DC 7913` (`40%`) as **strictly cumulative/successive** (*Camacho*, `21 Vet. App. 360`; *Middleton*, `727 F.3d 1172`), while construing Era-2 `DC 7903` (`30%/60%`) as **non-successive/disjunctive** permitting `§ 4.7` higher-tier approximation (*Tatum*, `23 Vet. App. 152`).

*Camacho*/*Middleton* enforce plain-text `DC 7913` limits; *Tatum* is **Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** on CUE against final pre-2009 `DC 7903` decisions, **but fully binding on open/staged *Nehmer* claims** covering pre-Dec. 10, 2017 periods!

Enacted **`38 C.F.R. § 3.310(d)`** establishing presumptive secondary SC for **diseases of hormone deficiency resulting from hypothalamo-pituitary changes** manifesting `>= 12 months` after moderate or severe SC TBI.
**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) / CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Jan. 16, 2014`).**

**Second Major Endocrine Overhaul (Era 3 — Current Law):** Replaced ongoing `10/30/60%` thyroid tiers in `DC 7900` and `DC 7903` (non-myxedema) with **`30%` for `6 months` after initial diagnosis -> `0%`**, coupled with **mandatory separate ratings for all chronic multi-system residuals**; clarified `DC 7913` (`"one or more daily injection(s) of insulin"` at `20/40/60%`; `"more than one"` at `100%`); modernized `DC 7904–7912, 7919`.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Dec. 10, 2017`):** Pre-Dec. 10, 2017 running awards are **grandfathered** under `38 U.S.C. § 1155` / `§ 3.951(a)`; claims pending across Dec. 10, 2017 receive Era-2 staged ratings prior to Dec. 10, 2017 and the more favorable rule thereafter (*Karnas* / `82 FR 50802` applicability clause).

Statutorily added **Hypothyroidism (`DC 7903`)** (alongside bladder cancer and Parkinsonism) as a covered Agent Orange presumptive disease—triggering **full `38 C.F.R. § 3.816` *Nehmer* class retroactivity**! *(Proposed CFR text update pending at `89 FR 9803`, Feb. 12, 2024).*

**Nehmer Retroactive Herbicide (§ 3.816) & CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive:** Any *Nehmer* award with an effective date **prior to Dec. 10, 2017** MUST be rated under Era-2 `DC 7903` (`10%` continuous medication / `30%/60%` *Tatum*) for the pre-Dec. 10, 2017 period!

Expanded herbicide presumptions (Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Guam, American Samoa, Johnston Atoll, C-123) for `DC 7913` & `DC 7903`, and enacted **`§ 1120` burn-pit presumptions** covering **neck/head cancers (thyroid & parathyroid carcinoma, `DC 7914`)**, reproductive cancers, and somatic cancers.

**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (`>= Aug. 10, 2022`)** + `38 U.S.C. § 1305` / `§ 3.33` retroactive survivor DIC re-evaluations ([Playbook 08](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical)).

Held that because `DC 7913` explicitly contemplates insulin and oral hypoglycemic medication, raters properly evaluate the medicated diabetic picture under `DC 7913` without speculating about unmedicated severity.
Forecloses *Ingram* anti-mitigation arguments on `DC 7913` itself, while leaving *Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)` fully intact for secondary neuropathy codes silent on medication.

See [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 4.119 Endocrine System (DC 7900–7919, Pre- vs. Post-December 10, 2017)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.119-endocrine-evolution) for verbatim Era-1, Era-2, and Era-3 regulatory text.
A. Side-by-Side Evolution of Hyperthyroidism (DC 7900) & Hypothyroidism (DC 7903)

rows: Qualitative `10/30/60/100%` tiers anchored to basal metabolic rate (`BMR`), tachycardia, tremor, exophthalmos, and weight loss.

**Ongoing Symptom/Medication Tiers:** · • **`100%`:** Thyroid enlargement, tachycardia `>100 bpm`, eye involvement, muscular weakness, loss of weight, and sympathetic nervous system, cardiovascular, or gastrointestinal symptoms · • **`60%`:** Emotional instability, tachycardia, fatigability, and increased pulse pressure or blood pressure · • **`30%`:** Tachycardia, tremor, and increased pulse pressure or blood pressure · • **`10%`:** **Tachycardia, which may be intermittent, and tremor, or; continuous medication required for control**.

**6-Month Initial Window + Mandatory Residual Unbundling:** · • **`30%` for `6 months` after initial diagnosis** · • **Thereafter (`0%` under `7900`):** Rate chronic residuals of disease or treatment (e.g., post-ablation hypothyroidism, tremors, anxiety) under appropriate body-system DCs. · • **Note (1):** Evaluate hyperthyroid cardiac disease (atrial fibrillation/HF) **separately under `DC 7008`** ([Cardio Diff](/cfr/modules/06-cardiovascular-system-4.100-4.104)). · • **Note (2):** Separately evaluate **Graves' ophthalmopathy** (diplopia `DC 6090`, visual acuity, or `§ 4.79`).
*Thyroid gland, toxic adenoma of:* `100% / 60% / 30% / 10%` mirroring `DC 7900` (`10%` for intermittent tachycardia and tremor, OR continuous medication required for control).

*Thyroid enlargement, toxic:* · • **Note (1):** Evaluate hyperthyroidism under **`DC 7900`**. · • **Note (2):** Evaluate neck disfigurement **separately under `DC 7800`** ([Scars Diff](/cfr/38-cfr-4.118#redline-diff)).
`20%` with pressure symptoms; `0%` without pressure symptoms.
`20%` with disfigurement of the head or neck; `0%` without disfigurement.

• **Note (1):** Evaluate symptoms due to **pressure on adjacent organs** (trachea, larynx `DC 6516–6520`, esophagus `DC 7203`) under appropriate body-system DCs. · • **Note (2):** Evaluate neck disfigurement **separately under `DC 7800`**.
Severe myxedema `100%`; lesser qualitative BMR/sluggishness tiers (`60/30/10%`).

**Ongoing Symptom/Medication Tiers (*Tatum* Disjunctive Rule):** · • **`100%`:** Cold intolerance, muscular weakness, cardiovascular involvement, mental disturbance (dementia, slowing of thought, depression), bradycardia `<60 bpm`, sleepiness · • **`60%`:** Muscular weakness, mental disturbance, and weight gain · • **`30%`:** Fatigability, constipation, and mental sluggishness · • **`10%`:** **Fatigability, OR; continuous medication required for control!**

**Bifurcated Myxedema vs. Non-Myxedema Rule:** · • **`100%` (Myxedema):** Cold intolerance, muscular weakness, cardiovascular involvement (hypotension, bradycardia, pericardial effusion), and mental disturbance (dementia, slowing of thought, depression). **Note (1):** Continues for **`6 months` beyond physician-determined crisis stabilization**! · • **`30%` (Without myxedema):** **For `6 months` after initial diagnosis**. · • **Thereafter (`0%` under `7903`):** **Mandatory separate evaluation** of all chronic residuals across affected body systems!
*(Added/clarified)* Asymptomatic/normal thyroid function = **`0%`**; otherwise rate as `DC 7900` or `DC 7903`.
With normal thyroid function (**euthyroid**) = **`0%`**. · • **Note:** Manifesting as hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism, evaluate as **`DC 7900`** or **`DC 7903`**.

blocks.text: B. High-Yield Thyroid Litigation & CUE Rules (§ 1155, *Tatum*, *Nehmer* & Residual Unbundling)

items:
***Tatum v. Shinseki*, `23 Vet. App. 152, 156 (2009)` (Pre-Dec. 10, 2017 `DC 7903` Non-Successive Rule):**
• In Era 2 (`June 6, 1996 – Dec. 9, 2017`), raters routinely denied `30%` or `60%` under `DC 7903` unless the veteran exhibited *every single* listed symptom (e.g., fatigability *and* constipation *and* mental sluggishness for `30%`). In *Tatum*, the CAVC held that Era-2 `DC 7903` criteria are **variable rather than strictly successive**, meaning **`38 C.F.R. § 4.7` ("more nearly approximates") applies**—a veteran with fatigability and weight gain or mental disturbance could qualify for `30%` or `60%` without exhibiting every symptom in that tier!

**The `Pub. L. 116-283` *Nehmer* Staged-Rating Goldmine (`Pre-Dec. 10, 2017` vs. `Post-Dec. 10, 2017`):**
• On **January 1, 2021**, `Pub. L. 116-283, § 9109` added **Hypothyroidism (`DC 7903`)** to `38 U.S.C. § 1116(a)(2)` as a covered Agent Orange presumptive disease. Under `38 C.F.R. § 3.816`, any Vietnam or Blue Water Navy veteran (or `§ 3.816(f)` survivor/estate) whose prior hypothyroidism claim—or prior claim where VAMC/private labs in the file already showed hypothyroidism ("Footnote 1" diagnostic lookback)—was received between **September 25, 1985 and December 9, 2017** is entitled to a retroactive effective date in **Era 1 or Era 2**!
• **Crucial Audit Check:** For the entire staged period **prior to December 10, 2017**, VA **must** apply Era-2 `DC 7903` (`10%` minimum for daily levothyroxine/Synthroid, `10%` under `DC 7900` for daily methimazole, or `30%/60%` under *Tatum*). Furthermore, once that pre-Dec. 10, 2017 running award is established, **`38 U.S.C. § 1155` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.951(a)`** bar VA from arbitrarily dropping the rating to `0%` on December 10, 2017 solely because the rating schedule changed ([Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings))!

**Post-December 10, 2017 Initial Diagnosis Trap & Mandatory Multi-System Unbundling:**
• For claims with effective dates **on or after December 10, 2017**, VA awards `30%` under `DC 7903` (or `DC 7900`) *only* during the **`6 months` immediately following initial medical diagnosis**—meaning a veteran first diagnosed with hypothyroidism in 2015 who files a non-*Nehmer* PACT/TERA claim in 2024 receives **`0%` under `DC 7903`**.
• **The Practitioner Counter-Move (`82 FR 50802` Mandatory Residual Cascade):** Under post-2017 `DC 7903`, VA **cannot** stop at `0%` when chronic hypothyroid symptoms persist despite levothyroxine replacement. Every chronic organ manifestation **must** be separately rated without triggering `§ 4.14` pyramiding:
• **Psychiatric / Cognitive (`§ 4.130`, `DC 9434`/`9440`):** Secondary depressive disorder, anxiety, or cognitive slowing (`10%–70%+`, [Mental Health Diff](/cfr/modules/mental-health-dc-9400-9411)).
• **Digestive (`§ 4.114`, `DC 7319`):** Chronic hypothyroid constipation / irritable bowel syndrome (`10%–30%`).
• **Cardiovascular (`§ 4.104`, `DC 7009` / `7002` / `7101` / `7008`):** Symptomatic sinus bradycardia, pericardial effusion, secondary hyperlipidemia/atherosclerosis, or hyperthyroid heart disease (`DC 7008`).
• **Neurological (`§ 4.124a`, `DC 8515` / `8520`):** Myxedematous carpal tunnel syndrome (`DC 8515`) or peripheral paresthesias (`DC 8520` + `§ 4.26` bilateral factor).
• **Skin / Hair (`§ 4.118`, `DC 7806` / `7831`):** Severe xerosis/dermatitis or alopecia ([Skin Diff](/cfr/modules/11-skin-dermatitis-psoriasis-biologics-4.118)).
• **Obesity Intermediate Step (`VAOPGCPREC 1-2017` / *Walsh*):** Hypothyroid metabolic weight gain -> obesity intermediate step -> **Obstructive Sleep Apnea (`DC 6847` CPAP = `50%`)** and weight-bearing knee/lumbar aggravation (`§ 3.310(b)`, [Playbook 14](/playbooks/14-secondary-service-connection-aggravation-obesity))!

A. Three-Era DC 7913 Criteria Comparison (1946 vs. 1996 vs. 2017)

rows: **Severe:** Large insulin doses (`>80` units), persistent glycosuria/acidosis, progressive loss of weight and strength.

Requiring **more than one daily injection of insulin**, restricted diet, and regulation of activities (avoidance of strenuous occupational and recreational activities) with episodes of ketoacidosis or hypoglycemic reactions requiring **`>= 3` hospitalizations/yr** or **weekly visits** to a diabetic care provider, **plus** either progressive loss of weight and strength **or** compensable complications if separately evaluated.

Unchanged substantive text (*"Requiring more than one daily injection of insulin, restricted diet, and regulation of activities..."* + `>= 3` hospitalizations/yr or weekly provider visits + progressive weight/strength loss OR compensable complications).
**Moderately severe:** Large insulin requirement, restricted diet, careful regulation of activities, poor control.

Requiring **insulin**, restricted diet, and regulation of activities with episodes of ketoacidosis or hypoglycemic reactions requiring **`1 or 2` hospitalizations/yr** or **twice a month visits** to a diabetic care provider, **plus** complications that would not be compensable if separately evaluated.

Clarified first clause to: *"Requiring **one or more daily injection(s) of insulin**, restricted diet, and regulation of activities..."* (+ `1–2` hospitalizations/yr or twice-monthly visits + noncompensable complications).
**Moderate:** Substantial insulin dosage and restricted diet, with fair sugar control.
*"Requiring **one or more daily injection(s) of insulin**, **restricted diet**, **and** **regulation of activities**."*
**Mild (with insulin/oral):** Small insulin dose or oral hypoglycemic agent and restricted diet.
Requiring **insulin and restricted diet**, **or**; **oral hypoglycemic agent and restricted diet**.
*"Requiring **one or more daily injection(s) of insulin and restricted diet**, **or**; **oral hypoglycemic agent and restricted diet**."*
**Mild:** Manageable by restricted diet alone, good sugar control.

blocks.text: B. Controlling Appellate Precedents on DC 7913 (*Camacho*, *Middleton* & *Jackson*)

items:
**Strictly Cumulative & Successive Criteria (*Camacho* & *Middleton*):**
• In ***Camacho v. Nicholson*, `21 Vet. App. 360, 366–67 (2007)`**, the CAVC held that `DC 7913`'s `40%` tier uses `"and"` conjunctively, requiring **all three elements**: `(1)` daily insulin, `(2)` restricted diet, **and** `(3)` **medically necessary** `"regulation of activities"`—defined parenthetically in the `100%` tier as ***avoidance of strenuous occupational and recreational activities*** (voluntary exercise to *promote* health does **not** satisfy avoidance of strenuous activities, and a physician/PA/NP must establish that avoiding strenuous occupational *and* recreational exertion is medically necessary to prevent hypoglycemia/hyperglycemia!).
• In ***Middleton v. Shinseki*, `727 F.3d 1172, 1178 (Fed. Cir. 2013)`**, the Federal Circuit affirmed that `DC 7913` is a **successive, cumulative rating schedule**, barring a veteran from invoking **`38 C.F.R. § 4.7`** (*"more nearly approximates"*) to leapfrog to `40%` or `60%` when daily insulin injections are absent—even if the veteran satisfies hospital/provider visit counts!
• **Modern GLP-1 / GIP Non-Insulin Injectable Trap:** Under `82 FR 50802`'s explicit text (*"one or more daily injection(s) of **insulin**"*), veterans treated exclusively with oral agents (`metformin`, `empagliflozin`/`Jardiance`, `dapagliflozin`/`Farxiga`, `sitagliptin`/`Januvia`, `glipizide`) **or non-insulin GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist injections** (`semaglutide`/`Ozempic`, `dulaglutide`/`Trulicity`, `liraglutide`/`Victoza`, `tirzepatide`/`Mounjaro`) **without insulin** cap at **`20%`** under `DC 7913` *(Note: Insulin pump continuous subcutaneous infusion delivers continuous daily insulin and satisfies the daily insulin requirement)*.

**Medication Contemplation Boundary (*Jackson v. McDonough* vs. *Ingram v. Collins*):**
• In ***Jackson v. McDonough*, `37 Vet. App. 87 (2023)`**, the CAVC held that because `DC 7913` explicitly incorporates insulin and oral hypoglycemic agents into its rating tiers, VA properly evaluates the medicated disability picture under `DC 7913` without speculating about unmedicated diabetic severity. **Crucial Distinction:** Under ***Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)`**, secondary diabetic complications rated under Diagnostic Codes **silent on medication**—most notably **diabetic peripheral neuropathy (`DC 8520` / `8515`)** treated with gabapentin, pregabalin (`Lyrica`), or duloxetine (`Cymbalta`)—**cannot** be discounted for medication relief!

blocks.text: C. DC 7913 Note (1) Mandatory Separate Complications Cascade (DeLisio Scope Rule)

lines: **`DC 7913` Note (1) & *DeLisio v. Shinseki*, `25 Vet. App. 45 (2011)`:**

* **Note (1)** mandates: *"Evaluate compensable complications of diabetes **separately unless they are part of the criteria used to support a 100-percent evaluation**. Noncompensable complications are considered part of the diabetic process under diagnostic code 7913."* (Note (2) bars ordering a glucose tolerance test solely for rating purposes once diabetes is diagnosed).

* Under ***DeLisio*** and `M21-1`, a claim for `DC 7913` Diabetes (or a `DC 7913` increased-rating claim) **reasonably encompasses** any diabetic complication shown by medical evidence during the pendency of the claim! Even when `DC 7913` sits at `20%`, unbundling Note (1) complications routinely drives combined ratings to **`80%–100% + SMC(k) + SMC(s)`** and triggers **`38 C.F.R. § 4.16(a)(1)` single-disability aggregation** (all secondary diabetic complications combine as **one** disability to clear the `40%` or `60%` schedular TDIU gate!).

rows: **4 Separate Ratings** (R leg + L leg + R arm + L arm) **+ `38 C.F.R. § 4.26` `10%` Bilateral Factor** on *both* paired extremities + `SMC(k)` if foot drop = LOU! *(Remember `§ 4.124a` `"wholly sensory"` moderate ceiling per *Miller*—document diminished ankle/Achilles deep tendon reflexes or toe/ankle weakness on DBQ to unlock `40%/60%`!)*
• **`DC 6040`** Diabetic retinopathy (`10–100%` on acuity, visual field, or incapacitating/treatment visits) · • **`DC 6027`** Cataract / **`DC 6012–6013`** Glaucoma

Post-May 13, 2018 (`83 FR 15316`), intravitreal anti-VEGF injections (ranibizumab/aflibercept/bevacizumab) or laser photocoagulation visits can support compensable eye ratings even when corrected acuity is preserved!

• **`DC 7541`** Renal involvement (`0/30/60/80/100%` via `eGFR` & albuminuria post-Nov. 14, 2021 `86 FR 54081`) · • **`DC 7522`** ED (`0%`) / `DC 7632` FSAD (`0%`) · • **`DC 7512`** Neurogenic voiding (`20/40/60%` pad/frequency)

• **`eGFR 45–59` (`>=3` mos) + albuminuria = `30%`**; `eGFR 30–44 = 60%`; `eGFR 15–29 = 80%`; `<15` or dialysis = **`100%`**! · • Diabetic `ED` (`DC 7522`) or `FSAD` (`DC 7632`) unlocks **statutory `SMC(k)` (`38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)`)** loss of use of a creative organ ([Master SMC Treatise](/docs/smc-complete-treatise-and-step-math))!

**`DC 7114` Note (2) Diabetic Calcified Artery Trap (`86 FR 62095`):** Diabetic medial arterial calcification produces **falsely normal `ABI > 0.90`/`1.30`**—VA **must** evaluate via **Toe Pressure (`TP`)** or **`TcPO2`**!
• **`DC 7820`/`7822`** Skin infections / necrobiosis · • **`DC 7308`/`7346`** Autonomic gastroparesis · • **`DC 5160–5173`** Amputations (`20–100%` + `SMC(k)/(l)/(m)`)

Below-knee (`DC 5165`) or transmetatarsal/ray amputations secondary to diabetic gangrene/osteomyelitis unlock **prosthetic `SMC(k)`/`(l)`**, `Ch. 39` Auto, `SAH`, and *Sursely* Clothing grants ([Playbook 13](/playbooks/13-ancillary-grants-sah-auto-clothing-dea-spina-bifida)).

blocks.text: 4. Parathyroid, Pituitary, Adrenal & Endocrine Neoplasms (DC 7904–7905, 7907–7912, 7914–7919)

rows: `100%` (`6 mos` post-surgery discharge); `60%` hypercalcemia/bone decalcification/renal stones; `10%` symptoms or continuous medication.

• **`100%`:** For **`6 months` from date of hospital discharge following surgery**. · • **`60%`:** Hypercalcemia indicated by at least one of: Total `Ca > 12 mg/dL` (`3–3.5 mmol/L`), Ionized `Ca > 5.6 mg/dL` (`1.4–1.75 mmol/L`), `CrCl < 60 mL/min`, bone mineral density `T-score < 2.5 SD` below mean, or fragility fracture of wrist, hip, or spine *(evaluated until surgical intervention or for `6 months` after pharmacologic therapy is initiated)*. · • **`10%`:** Symptoms despite surgery; OR hyperparathyroidism when surgery is not indicated and continuous medication is required for control. · • **`0%`:** Asymptomatic *(evaluate chronic nephrolithiasis/renal/bone residuals separately per Notes)*.
`100%` (`3 mos` post-initial diagnosis); `10%` or `0%` thereafter (or continuous calcium/vitamin D therapy).

**`100%` for `3 months` after initial diagnosis**; thereafter evaluate chronic residuals (nephrolithiasis, cataracts `DC 6027`, decreased renal function, paresthesias, congestive heart failure) separately.

`100%` active progressive (muscle wasting, osteoporosis, hypertension); `60%` proximal muscle wasting; `30%` striae, obesity, moon face, glucose intolerance, vascular fragility (`6 mos` post-initial diagnosis -> residuals).

**`100%`** active progressive disease (adrenal/pituitary enlargement, neurological/visual field changes, osteopenia, muscle wasting, glucose intolerance, hypertension, cardiovascular/psychiatric changes); **`60%`** loss of muscle strength and enlargement of pituitary/adrenal gland; **`30%`** striae, obesity, moon face, glucose intolerance, and vascular fragility; **`0%`** asymptomatic *(active `100/60/30%` evaluations continue throughout active disease for `6 months` following initial diagnosis OR until surgical/medical recovery, with chronic residuals—post-resection `DC 7911`, diabetes `DC 7913`, HTN `DC 7101`, osteoporosis, myopathy—rated separately; exogenous steroid-induced Cushing's is **secondary SC** under `§ 3.310(a)`!)*.
`100%` increased intracranial pressure/visual field, arthropathy, glucose intolerance, HTN/cardiomegaly; `60%` arthropathy, glucose intolerance, HTN; `30%` acral enlargement/long-bone overgrowth.
Retained **`100%`**, **`60%`**, and **`30%`** criteria. Cross-check pituitary adenoma surgery/radiation residuals and `§ 3.310(d)` post-TBI pituitary link.

**`100%`** polyuria w/ near-continuous thirst + `>2` dehydration episodes/yr; **`60%`** `1–2` episodes/yr; **`40%`** polyuria + continuous hormonal therapy; **`20%`** polyuria + oral/intranasal therapy.

**Sharply narrowed (`§ 1155` protection alert!):** **`30%` for `3 months` after initial diagnosis**; thereafter, if diabetes insipidus has subsided, rate residuals under appropriate body system, OR if persistent polyuria or **requiring continuous hormonal therapy** (desmopressin/`DDAVP`), assign **`10%`**! *(Pre-Dec. 10, 2017 `20%/40%/60%/100%` running awards are grandfathered under `38 U.S.C. § 1155`!)*
**[Removed June 6, 1996 at `61 FR 20446`]** *(adult adrenal hyperfunction evaluated under `DC 7907`, `7917`, or `7918`)*.

**`60%`** `>= 4` crises/yr; **`40%`** `3` crises OR `>= 5` episodes/yr; **`20%`** `1–2` crises OR `2–4` episodes/yr OR weakness and fatigability OR **corticosteroid therapy required for control** (Notes 1–3).

Retained **`60%`**, **`40%`**, and **`20%`** tiers (`20%` minimum floor whenever hydrocortisone/fludrocortisone replacement is required!). **Notes (1)–(3):** · • **Crisis:** Rapid onset vascular collapse (hypotension + shock) requiring **parenteral** corticosteroids/hospitalization. · • **Episode:** Less severe anorexia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dehydration, weakness, hypotension controlled w/ oral steroids. · • **Note (3):** Tuberculous Addison's has `100%` active disease (`§ 4.88b` / `§§ 4.88c, 4.89`); when inactive, `DC 7911` is **NOT combined** with the `50%/30%` graduated non-pulmonary TB ratings (assign whichever is higher!).
*(Added `61 FR 20446` as Pluriglandular syndrome)*: Evaluate according to major manifestations.

*Polyglandular syndrome (including multiple endocrine neoplasia, autoimmune polyglandular syndrome):* Evaluate according to major manifestations (Type 1 diabetes `DC 7913`, hyper/hypothyroidism, hypoparathyroidism, Addison's `DC 7911`, neoplasms `DC 7914/7919`).
**Neoplasm, malignant, any specified part of the endocrine system**
**`100%`** active malignancy/treatment + **`6 months`** following cessation of surgical, X-ray, antineoplastic chemo, or other therapeutic procedure; mandatory VA exam before rating residuals.

Retained **`100%`** active + **`6-month` post-treatment floor**. **Critical Audit Hooks:** · 1. **PACT Act `38 U.S.C. § 1120`:** Thyroid carcinoma and parathyroid carcinoma are **presumptive head/neck cancers**; adrenal/pancreatic islet/gonadal endocrine cancers are presumptive somatic/reproductive cancers ([Playbook 15](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera))! · 2. **Radiation (`38 C.F.R. §§ 3.309(d), 3.311(b)(2)`):** Thyroid cancer is a primary radiogenic malignancy. · 3. ***Foster* Notice Gate:** Under *Foster v. McDonough*, `34 Vet. App. 338 (2021)`, VA **cannot** reduce `100%` without a post-6-month C&P exam **and `60-day` `38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e)` advance notice**, and post-thyroidectomy hypothyroidism/vocal cord nerve palsy (`DC 8210`) / neck scar (`DC 7800/7804`) / hypoparathyroidism (`DC 7905`) must be rated separately!
**Neoplasm, benign, any specified part of the endocrine system**
Rate as residuals of endocrine dysfunction.
Rate as residuals of endocrine dysfunction (hormonal hypersecretion/deficiency, visual field loss from pituitary macroadenoma `DC 6080`, headaches `DC 8100`, surgical scar).
*(Added June 6, 1996 at `61 FR 20446`)*: Evaluate as malignant (`DC 7914`) or benign (`DC 7915`) neoplasm as appropriate.

Retained: Evaluate as malignant or benign neoplasm as appropriate (e.g., `DC 7916` galactorrhea/hypogonadism/ED `SMC(k)`/infertility/visual field; `DC 7917` Conn's refractory hypertension `DC 7101`/`7007` & hypokalemic arrhythmia; `DC 7918` paroxysmal catecholamine hypertension/tachycardia).
*(Added June 6, 1996 at `61 FR 20446`)*: **`100%`** active antineoplastic/surgical treatment + `6 months` -> mandatory C&P exam -> residuals.

**Restructured (`82 FR 50802`):** If **antineoplastic therapy is required**, evaluate as a **malignant neoplasm under `DC 7914`** (`100%` + `6 months` post-treatment -> mandatory exam -> residuals). **Note:** If **surgical treatment (prophylactic thyroidectomy) is administered without antineoplastic therapy**, evaluate as **hypothyroidism under `DC 7903`** (+ separate surgical scar/parathyroid/vocal-cord residuals)!

veteranOverlay.what_this_means: In endocrine disability claims under 38 C.F.R. § 4.119, the biggest difference in monthly compensation rarely comes from the base diabetes or thyroid percentage alone—it comes from mandatory separate ratings for secondary organ and nerve complications across the body. This comparison tracks the December 10, 2017 endocrine overhaul (published November 2, 2017 at 82 FR 50802), showing how Agent Orange (Nehmer) Type 2 Diabetes and Hypothyroidism claims, post-TBI pituitary hormone deficiencies, thyroid cancers, and multi-system secondary complications are evaluated.
record_clues: A 20% rating for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (Diagnostic Code 7913) where VA medical notes show tingling/burning feet or hands (diabetic neuropathy), diabetic eye exams (Diagnostic Code 6040), reduced kidney eGFR labs (Diagnostic Code 7541), peripheral arterial disease (Diagnostic Code 7114), heart disease, or erectile dysfunction (Diagnostic Code 7522 + SMC(k)) missing from the Rating Code Sheet.

An Agent Orange / Blue Water Navy retroactive hypothyroidism grant (Diagnostic Code 7903, added by Congress effective January 1, 2021 with Nehmer retroactivity) assigning 0% for pre-December 10, 2017 years despite continuous levothyroxine medication.

A diabetic Veteran denied Total Disability based on Individual Unemployability (TDIU, 38 C.F.R. § 4.16(a)) for 'no single 40% disability' even though multiple diabetic complications share a common diabetic origin and combine to 40% or 60%+ under § 4.16(a)(1).
Thyroid or endocrine cancer (Diagnostic Code 7914) dropped from 100% to 0% after surgery or radioactive iodine without waiting 6 months, holding a VA exam, and giving 60-day advance notice.
important_cautions: Non-insulin injectables versus insulin: oral medications (like metformin or SGLT2 inhibitors) and non-insulin GLP-1/GIP injections (such as semaglutide/Ozempic or tirzepatide/Mounjaro) do not satisfy the 'one or more daily injection of insulin' requirement for the 40% tier of Diagnostic Code 7913, which also requires restricted diet AND medical regulation of activities (Middleton v. Shinseki; Camacho v. Nicholson).

Medication rules differ between base diabetes and secondary neuropathy: because Diagnostic Code 7913 explicitly incorporates medication into its tiers, VA does not guess at unmedicated blood sugar (Jackson v. McDonough), whereas peripheral nerve codes for diabetic neuropathy are silent on medication (Ingram v. Collins). Never treat the rescinded February 17, 2026 medication rule (91 FR 7118, rescinded February 27, 2026 at 91 FR 9712) as active law.

Note on 89 FR 9803 (February 12, 2024): while VA's regulatory text update to 38 C.F.R. § 3.309(e) was published as a proposed rule, the underlying statutory Agent Orange presumption for hypothyroidism under 38 U.S.C. § 1116 has been active statutory law since January 1, 2021.

Do not file a Board CUE motion lightly: under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c), once the Board issues a final merits decision on a CUE motion on a specific prior Board issue, no second CUE motion is allowed on that Board issue.

blocks.text: 2. Organic Diseases of the Central Nervous System (DC 8000–8046, §§ 4.120, 4.124a)
A. Foundational §§ 4.120 & 4.124a Residual-Stacking Rule vs. Minimum Floors
Under `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.120` and `4.124a`, organic CNS diseases (`DC 8000–8046`) follow a **two-step evaluation architecture**:

items: **Separate Residual Evaluation:** Specific neurological residuals—loss of use or partial paralysis of extremities (`DC 8510–8530`), cranial nerve palsies (`DC 8205–8212`), impairment of vision/diplopia, hearing/vestibular vertigo, speech/aphonia (`DC 6519`), swallowing, anal/bladder sphincter control (`DC 7332` / `DC 7512`), or neurocognitive/mood disorders (`§ 4.130`)—are rated **separately** under their respective body-system diagnostic codes, plus applicable **`38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)–(s)` Special Monthly Compensation (`SMC`)**.

**Minimum Rating Floor Comparison:** Each organic CNS code specifies a **minimum percentage floor** (`10%`, `30%`, `60%`, or `100%`) when ascertainable residuals exist (or upon diagnosis alone for `DC 8004` and `DC 8017`).

blocks.text: 3. Traumatic Brain Injury (DC 8045): Two-Era Historical Diff (1946 vs. Oct. 23, 2008)

See [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.120–4.124a Neurological Conditions, Traumatic Brain Injury (DC 8045), ALS (DC 8017) & Peripheral Nerves](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.124a-tbi-and-peripheral-nerves-evolution) for the verbatim pre- and post-October 23, 2008 regulatory text and complete 10-facet matrix.

rows: Split strictly between **(1) Purely neurological disabilities** (hemiplegia, cranial nerve paralysis, epilepsies) vs. **(2) Purely subjective symptomatology** (`DC 8045-9304`).
Evaluates **three main areas of dysfunction**: **(1) Cognitive**, **(2) Emotional/Behavioral**, and **(3) Physical** (including subjective symptoms).

**Hard `10%` Ceiling Trap:** Purely subjective complaints recognized as symptomatic of brain trauma (headaches, dizziness, insomnia, memory/concentration complaints) were **capped at `10%` under `DC 9304`**, and **could NOT be combined** with any other brain-trauma rating in the absence of a diagnosis of multi-infarct dementia!

**`10-Facet` Table (`0% / 10% / 40% / 70% / 100%`):** Evaluates cognitive impairment and subjective symptoms across **10 facets** scored `0`, `1`, `2`, `3`, or `Total`. **Highest-Facet Rule:** The veteran's `DC 8045` percentage equals the **highest level assigned on ANY single facet** (`0 = 0%`, `1 = 10%`, `2 = 40%`, `3 = 70%`, `Total = 100%`)—never an average or sum!
None (unstructured `DC 9304` dementia schedule if organic dementia proven; otherwise `10%` max).

`1.` Memory, attention, concentration, executive functions (`0–Total`) · `2.` Judgment (`0–Total`) · `3.` Social interaction *(caps at Level `3 = 70%` via `0–3`)* · `4.` Orientation (`0–Total`) · `5.` Motor activity (with intact motor/sensory system — apraxia/initiation) (`0–Total`) · `6.` Visual-spatial orientation (`0–Total`) · `7.` Subjective symptoms *(cluster of headaches/dizziness/fatigue/malaise not otherwise separately rated; caps at Level `2 = 40%` via `0–2`)* · `8.` Neurobehavioral effects *(irritability, impulsivity, unpredictability, aggression; caps at Level `3 = 70%` via `0–3`)* · `9.` Communication *(comprehension/expression; `0–Total`: `0/1/2/3/Total`)* · `10.` Consciousness *(persistent vegetative state or coma = **`Total (100%)`** only)*.

**Crucial Era-1 CUE Loophole:** Separately diagnosed *neurological or physical conditions*—such as **Migraines (`8045-8100` up to `50%`)**, **Peripheral Vestibular Disorder (`8045-6204` up to `30%`)**, **Post-Traumatic Epilepsy (`8045-8910`–`8914`)**, cranial nerve palsies, or comorbid PTSD (`DC 9411`)—were **NOT** "purely subjective complaints" and had to be rated under their dedicated codes!

**Physical/Neurological + Note (1) Overlap Rule:** Distinct physical/neurological diagnoses (migraines `DC 8100`, seizures `DC 8910–8914`, tinnitus `DC 6260`, vertigo `DC 6204`, diplopia `DC 6090`, endocrine `§ 4.119`, skin/scars `§ 4.118`, bowel/bladder, ED `SMC(k)`) are **rated separately** unless the exact same symptom is already used to elevate a `DC 8045` facet (`§ 4.14`). Under **Note (1)**, comorbid mental disorders (`§ 4.130`) are rated separately *unless* manifestations cannot be delineated without speculation (*Mittleider v. West*, `11 Vet. App. 181 (1998)`), in which case VA assigns a single combined evaluation under whichever schedule yields the higher rating ([Playbook 18](/playbooks/18-tbi-facets-radiculopathy-and-nerve-stacking)).

• **Note (2):** Listed facet symptoms are *illustrative examples*, NOT mandatory cumulative checklists. · • **Note (3):** Distinguishes basic `ADLs` from `IADLs` (finances, shopping, meal prep, medication management, travel). · • **Note (4):** Initial in-service TBI severity label (*"mild"*, *"moderate"*, *"severe"* based on acute Glasgow Coma Scale / LOC / PTA) **does NOT cap or control** current residual ratings *(though initial severity DOES govern `§ 3.310(d)` secondary presumptions!)*. · • **Note (5):** Allowed veterans rated at `10%` pre-Oct. 23, 2008 to request review under the new table without proving worsening.

blocks.text: 4. Miscellaneous Neurological Diseases & Migraines (DC 8100–8108)
A. Migraines (DC 8100) — Controlling Precedential Matrix

rows: *"With very frequent completely prostrating and prolonged attacks productive of severe economic inadaptability"*

• ***Pierce v. Principi*, `18 Vet. App. 440, 445–46 (2004)`:** `"Productive of"` means **capable of producing** (NOT necessarily *currently producing* complete job loss); `"severe economic inadaptability"` denotes substantial work impairment (missed workdays, leaving shifts early, FMLA/sick-leave exhaustion, workplace accommodations, inability to work during attacks)—**continued full-time employment does NOT bar `50%`!** · • ***Johnson v. Wilkie*, `30 Vet. App. 245, 250–55 (2018)`:** `DC 8100` tiers are **successive and conjunctive** (making `§ 4.7` *"nearly approximates"* inapplicable across missing elements), so `50%` requires `(1)` very frequent (`>1/month`, contrasted against `30%` once/month), `(2)` completely prostrating (extreme exhaustion/powerlessness compelling cessation of activity), `(3)` prolonged, AND `(4)` productive of severe economic inadaptability. Crucially, the Board **cannot invent arbitrary, undisclosed numerical thresholds** (e.g., demanding weekly attacks or `>48-hour` duration) without articulating a reasoned medical or dictionary basis! · • ***Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)`:** Because `DC 8100` is completely **silent on medication**, raters and examiners **cannot discount baseline migraine frequency, prostration, or duration** based on ameliorative relief from abortive/prophylactic medications (sumatriptan/rizatriptan, gepants, CGRP monoclonal antibodies, Botox, topiramate, propranolol)! *(Watchlist: VA's Feb. 17, 2026 `§ 4.10` IFR at `91 FR 7118` was **rescinded ab initio** Feb. 27, 2026 at `91 FR 9712`).*
*"With characteristic prostrating attacks occurring on an average once a month over last several months"*
Requires characteristic prostrating attacks averaging **`1` per month** over the last several months (no economic-inadaptability requirement).
*"With characteristic prostrating attacks averaging one in 2 months over last several months"*
Averages **`1` prostrating attack every `2` months** over the last several months.
Diagnosed SC migraines/headaches with prostrating attacks less frequent than once every 2 months (or non-prostrating headaches).

lines: **Bitemporal CUE Gate on `DC 8100`:** Attacking a **final pre-2018** Board decision solely for violating *Johnson*'s anti-arbitrary-definition reasoning or a **final pre-2025** decision solely under *Ingram* is **Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** (`38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`). Conversely, if a post-2004 final RO decision denied `50%` *solely* on the stated ground that the veteran was employed despite conceding *"very frequent completely prostrating and prolonged attacks"* causing heavy sick-leave loss, evaluate under *Pierce* (`2004`).

rows: Rate as convulsive tic (`DC 8103`), except **severe cases: `60%`**.

Rated as Sydenham's chorea (`DC 8105`: `10/30/50/80/100%`) + separate cognitive/psychiatric/swallowing residuals. **Hereditary Disease Trap:** Under `38 C.F.R. § 3.303(c)` and binding [`VAOPGCPREC 82-90`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index), Huntington's chorea is a **compensable hereditary disease** (NOT a congenital defect) whenever adult clinical symptoms first manifest in service or are aggravated in service ([Soundness & Hereditary Treatise](/docs/service-connection-direct-soundness-aggravation))!

**Rated as for epilepsy, petit mal (`DC 8911`)** (`10%` minimum when continuous wake-promoting/anticataplectic medication is required; `20%/40%/60%/80%` based on weekly/semi-annual sleep attacks or cataplexy episodes!). *(Common CUE/Appeal Trap: Raters unlawfully rating narcolepsy at `0%` despite continuous modafinil/armodafinil/sodium oxybate therapy, violating the `DC 8911` `10%` continuous-medication floor!)*

blocks.text: A. The Three-Prefix Architecture & Severity Ceilings (§§ 4.123–4.124)
Every cranial and peripheral nerve carries **three parallel Diagnostic Codes** sharing the same final two digits, governed by distinct regulatory ceilings:

rows: Up to **Complete Paralysis** (`100%` of nerve's schedule). **Wholly Sensory Ceiling Note (`§ 4.124a`):** *"When the involvement is **wholly sensory**, the rating should be for the mild, or at most, the moderate degree."* Under ***Miller v. Shulkin*, `28 Vet. App. 376, 380 (2017)`**, this note is a **one-way ceiling** on purely sensory neuropathy—it does **not** create an automatic `"moderate+"` floor merely because reflex/motor signs exist.

**`38 C.F.R. § 4.123`:** · • **With organic changes** *(loss of reflexes, muscle atrophy, sensory disturbances, and constant pain, at times excruciating)*: Maximum = **`Incomplete, Severe`**. · • **Without organic changes:** Maximum = **`Moderate`**—**EXCEPT for the Sciatic Nerve (`DC 8620`), where the cap without organic changes is `Moderately Severe (40%)`!**

**`38 C.F.R. § 4.124`:** Characterized by dull/intermittent pain, tingling, numbness without motor/trophic loss -> Maximum = **`Moderate`**. · • **CRITICAL EXCEPTION (`§ 4.124` & `DC 8405`):** ***Tic douloureux* (trifacial / trigeminal neuralgia of the Fifth Cranial Nerve, `DC 8405`) may be rated up to `Complete Paralysis (50%)`**! Capping severe `DC 8405` trigeminal neuralgia at `10%` moderate is a classic plain-text **RO CUE** (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive).

lines: **Dominant (`Major`) vs. Non-Dominant (`Minor`) Handedness (`38 C.F.R. § 4.69`) & Combined Nerve Rule (`§ 4.124a`):**
