blocks.text: A. Physician Identification Gate (§ 4.121) vs. Competent Lay Seizure Logs

items: **Threshold Diagnosis Gate (`38 C.F.R. § 4.121`):** *"To warrant a rating for epilepsy, the seizures must be witnessed or verified at some time by a physician"* (satisfied by direct physician observation OR clinical/EEG verification accepting a credible medical history or eyewitness account; see [Verbatim Snapshot](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.124a-tbi-and-peripheral-nerves-evolution)).

**Lay Competence for Seizure Frequency (*Jandreau* / *Buchanan*):** Once a medical diagnosis of epilepsy is established, **lay witnesses (the veteran, spouse, roommate, or coworker) are fully competent** to testify to the **observable frequency, tonic-clonic convulsions, staring spells, tongue-biting, incontinence, and post-ictal exhaustion** occurring under *"the ordinary conditions of life"* (`§ 4.121`; *Jandreau v. Nicholson*, `492 F.3d 1372, 1377 (Fed. Cir. 2007)`; *Buchanan v. Nicholson*, `451 F.3d 1331 (Fed. Cir. 2006)`). Under `§ 4.121`, frequency **must** reflect ordinary non-hospitalized life rather than sheltered inpatient observation.

blocks.text: B. Seizure Classifications (DC 8910–8914) & General Rating Formula

items:
**Major Seizure Classifications:**
• **`DC 8910` (Epilepsy, grand mal):** Generalized tonic-clonic convulsions with unconsciousness.
• **`DC 8914` (Epilepsy, psychomotor; `§ 4.122`):** Rated as **major seizures** when characterized by **automatic states and/or transient episodes with loss of conscious control** (confusional/fugue episodes, automatisms); otherwise rated as minor seizures when brief and without loss of conscious control. *(Note: Chronic psychotic/neurocognitive disturbances secondary to epilepsy are rated separately under `§ 4.130`!)*

**Minor Seizure Classifications:**
• **`DC 8911` (Epilepsy, petit mal):** Brief interruption in consciousness/conscious control (absence staring, rhythmic blinking, myoclonic jerks, akinetic drop) *(also governs **`DC 8108` Narcolepsy**!)*.
• **`DC 8912` (Jacksonian and focal motor or sensory)** & **`DC 8913` (Diencephalic / autonomic):** Rated as minor seizures, *unless* a focal seizure progresses ("generalizes") into a tonic-clonic major seizure, which counts as a **major seizure**!

rows: Averaging **at least `1` major seizure per month** over the last year
*(Minor seizures alone max out at `80%` unless generalized/psychomotor automatic)*
Averaging **at least `1` major seizure in `3` months** over the last year
Averaging **at least `1` major seizure in `4` months** over the last year
**At least `1` major seizure in the last `6` months** OR **`2` in the last year**
**At least `1` major seizure in the last `2` years**
**At least `2` minor seizures in the last `6` months**
Confirmed diagnosis of epilepsy with history of seizures, **OR continuous anticonvulsant medication shown necessary for control**
Confirmed diagnosis with history of seizures, **OR continuous medication necessary for control**

blocks.text: *(Note: When both major and minor seizures are present, rate the **predominating type**—i.e., whichever category yields the **higher evaluation** under `§ 4.7`!)*
7. Regulatory Watchlist & Quarantine (RIN 2900-AQ73 — Proposed / Not Finalized)

lines: **QUARANTINE NOTICE — DO NOT CITE AS ACTIVE LAW (AGENTS Law 6):**

* **`RIN 2900-AQ73` (`89 FR 88917`, published November 12, 2024 — Proposed Rule, Not Finalized):** VA published a sweeping **proposed** overhaul of `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.120–4.124a` (*Schedule for Rating Disabilities: Neurological Conditions and Convulsive Disorders*) proposing to: `(1)` eliminate standalone neuritis (`§ 4.123`, `83xx`/`86xx`) and neuralgia (`§ 4.124`, `84xx`/`87xx`) codes in favor of unified nerve impairment schedules; `(2)` replace qualitative *"mild/moderate/severe"* incomplete peripheral paralysis descriptors with Medical Research Council (`MRC` `0–5`) muscle-strength testing and sensory-deficit matrices; and `(3)` modernize epilepsy and CNS diagnostic titles while retaining `DC 8100` migraine frequency tiers. **No Final Rule has been enacted.** All pending claims, appeals, and CUE motions remain governed strictly by the active `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.120–4.124a` schedules above.

* **Rescinded `38 C.F.R. § 4.10` Medication IFR (`91 FR 7118`, Feb. 17, 2026 — Rescinded `91 FR 9712`, Feb. 27, 2026):** VA's short-lived attempt to override *Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)` was **rescinded ab initio** after 10 days. Audit any `DC 8100` migraine or neurological rating issued in February 2026 to ensure *Ingram* is faithfully applied!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: TBI, Migraines, Parkinson's, ALS & Nerve Radiculopathy: Historical Rules & Rating Pitfalls
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Neurological disabilities under 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.120–4.124a span Traumatic Brain Injury (Diagnostic Code 8045), migraine headaches (Diagnostic Code 8100), Parkinson's disease (Diagnostic Code 8004), ALS (Diagnostic Code 8017), cranial nerve neuralgias, peripheral nerve injuries/radiculopathy (Diagnostic Codes 8510–8730), and seizure disorders. Because neurological conditions affect movement, sensation, speech, cognition, and daily safety across multiple body parts, VA rating sheets frequently under-rate them—by averaging TBI facets instead of taking the highest facet, dropping the 30% Parkinson's baseline when residual symptoms remain uncompensated, discounting migraines because medication dulls some attacks, or overlooking Special Monthly Compensation (SMC(k) for loss of use or SMC(t) for TBI Aid and Attendance).
record_clues: Headache logs, work leave slips, or neurology notes showing 'very frequent completely prostrating and prolonged attacks productive of severe economic inadaptability' for migraines (Diagnostic Code 8100, 50%) discounted because abortive/preventive drugs (triptans, CGRP blockers) helped some attacks or because the Veteran still held a job.

Agent Orange, Camp Lejeune, or post-TBI Parkinson's disease (Diagnostic Code 8004) where VA rated individual tremor, speech, or bladder residuals but deleted the 30% Diagnostic Code 8004 baseline despite remaining uncompensated Parkinsonian symptoms (such as masked facies, stooped posture, or bradykinesia).
Fifth cranial nerve trigeminal neuralgia / tic douloureux (Diagnostic Code 8405) capped at 10% despite 38 C.F.R. § 4.124's explicit exception allowing up to 50% for severe fifth-nerve neuralgia.

Traumatic Brain Injury requiring regular in-home supervision or Aid and Attendance to avoid institutionalization (SMC(t) under 38 U.S.C. § 1114(t), effective October 1, 2011) denied earlier because care was provided by a spouse or family member rather than a licensed medical professional (invalidated in Laska v. McDonough).
important_cautions: Unfinalized and rescinded rules caution: VA's November 12, 2024 neurological rulemaking (89 FR 88917, RIN 2900-AQ73) is a proposed, unfinalized rule and is NOT enacted law. Likewise, VA's February 17, 2026 medication Interim Final Rule (91 FR 7118) was rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712).

Later court reinterpretations cannot support CUE on older final decisions: under George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e), precedents like Duran v. McDonough (2023 on Parkinson's DC 8004), Johnson v. Wilkie (2018 on migraines DC 8100), and Laska v. McDonough (2024 on TBI SMC(t)) apply to open claims, timely appeals, Supplemental Claims, or § 3.156(c) service-record reconsiderations—not Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) against final pre-precedent decisions.

Check exact statutory and regulatory dates: the 10-facet TBI table took effect October 23, 2008; statutory SMC(t) for TBI took effect October 1, 2011; and the 100% minimum ALS rating took effect January 19, 2012.

Upper-extremity multi-nerve rule: when cervical radiculopathy affects multiple major nerves (radial, median, ulnar) in the same arm, VA's Combined Nerve Injuries Note requires rating them together under a Radicular Group code (Diagnostic Codes 8510–8513) rather than stacking separate single-nerve codes on the same arm.
questions_for_representative: Did VA discount my migraine rating under Diagnostic Code 8100 because I take prescription migraine medication or because I have not yet lost my job?

If I have service-connected Parkinson's disease (Diagnostic Code 8004), do I have ascertainable Parkinsonian manifestations not covered by separate extremity/organ codes that preserve the 30% Diagnostic Code 8004 rating?
If I need regular daily supervision, cueing, or physical help due to a service-connected Traumatic Brain Injury, should we file a Supplemental Claim or appeal for SMC(t) under Laska v. McDonough?

On my spine or nerve claim, did VA properly check upper-extremity Radicular Group codes (Diagnostic Codes 8510–8513), dominant-hand Major ratings (38 C.F.R. § 4.69), and SMC(k) if I have complete foot drop or hand loss of use?

McDonough* (`596 U.S. 740 (2022)`) / `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`** bitemporal CUE gates.

*(For verbatim historical `former § 4.132` (`53 FR 21`) and current `§ 4.130` text, see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125–4.130 Mental Disorders, Traumatic Stress (§ 4.129), Eating Disorders (DC 9520–9521) & Former § 4.132 Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.132-mental-disorders-pre-1996); for verbatim repealed `§ 4.16(c)` (`54 FR 4281`), see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 4.16 Total Disability Based on Individual Unemployability (1975–Present Evolution & Former § 4.16(c))](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.16-tdiu-evolution); for four-era `§ 3.304(f)` PTSD/MST stressor text, see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.303(a)–(d), 3.304(b) & (f), and 3.306(a)–(c) (Direct Service Connection, Chronicity, Congenital Defects, Presumption of Soundness, Aggravation & Four-Era PTSD / MST Stressor Evolution)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.304f-ptsd-evolution); for PTSD stressor and MST litigation strategy, see [Playbook 16 (PTSD Stressors & MST Corroboration)](/playbooks/16-ptsd-stressors-and-mst-corroboration); for comorbid TBI/PTSD *Mittleider* unbundling, see [Playbook 18 (TBI Facets & Nerve Stacking)](/playbooks/18-tbi-facets-radiculopathy-and-nerve-stacking) and [`System 13 Neurological Diff`](/cfr/modules/13-neurological-tbi-nerves-4.120-4.124a); for COD insanity (`§ 3.354(b)`) and personality-disorder misdiagnoses, see [Playbook 10 (Character of Discharge & Insanity)](/playbooks/10-character-of-discharge-insanity-upgrades); for `§ 3.344` unlawful mental-rating reductions, see [Playbook 05 (Void Rating Reductions)](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings); for HIV/pernicious-anemia neurocognitive cross-hooks, see [`System 04 Infectious Diff`](/cfr/modules/04-infectious-immune-nutritional-4.88b) and [`System 10 Hemic Diff`](/cfr/modules/10-hemic-and-lymphatic-4.117); and see [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).*
1. Four-Era Regulatory Evolution Matrix (1946–2026)

rows: **Three Separate Schedules** in `former § 4.132`: `(1)` **Psychotic (`DC 9200s`)**, `(2)` **Organic (`DC 9300s`)**, and `(3)` **Psychoneurotic (`DC 9400s`)**. · • **CRITICAL ERA-1 TRAP:** Psychoneurotic Disorders (`DC 9400–9411`) had **NO `70%` TIER** prior to Feb. 3, 1988 (`0% / 10% / 30% / 50% / 100%`)!

• **Two-Step `DC 9411` History:** While VA began administratively rating PTSD in **Oct./Nov. 1980** following DSM-III (`DVB Circulars 21-80-7` / `21-82-7`), `38 C.F.R. Part 4, App. A` formally codified **`DC 9411` on Feb. 3, 1988 (`53 FR 21`)**. · • **Top Era-1 Weapons:** `§ 3.156(c)` JSRRC/combat unit records overturning `1960s–1980s` *"personality disorder"* / *"nervousness"* denials; **`§ 3.309(a)` 1-yr chronic presumption for Psychoses (`DC 9200s` ONLY!)**; and `§ 3.344` void reductions.

Retained separate Psychotic / Organic / Psychoneurotic tables in `former § 4.132`, **ADDED the `70%` Severe tier** to Psychoneurotic Disorders (`0/10/30/50/70/100%` **social and industrial adaptability**), and formally codified `DC 9411` PTSD.

• **MASSIVE `1989–1996` CUE GOLDMINE — `Former 38 C.F.R. § 4.16(c)` (`Mar. 1, 1989 – Nov. 6, 1996`):** Whenever a **`70%` mental disorder was the veteran's sole compensable SC disability** and precluded substantially gainful employment, VA was **MANDATED** to assign a **`100%` schedular rating** (*Johnson v. Brown*, `7 Vet. App. 95 (1994)` — **CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive**)! · • Also check `100%` psychoneurotic disjunctive prong (*"or demonstrably unable to obtain or retain employment"*; *Gleicher*, `2 Vet. App. 26`; *Mitchem*, `9 Vet. App. 138`).

Redesignated `former § 4.132 -> § 4.130`; **unified ALL `DC 9201–9440` conditions into ONE General Rating Formula (`0/10/30/50/70/100%`)**; referenced DSM-IV Axis V **`GAF` scores** (`§ 4.125(a)` & `former § 4.130` introductory text); **repealed `§ 4.16(c)`**; **enacted `§ 4.129` (`50%` traumatic discharge)**, **`§ 4.128`**, and **`DC 9520–9521` Eating Disorders**!

• **Plain-Text CUEs (`>= Nov. 7, 1996`):** Omitting mandatory **`§ 4.129` `50%` post-discharge minimum** or **`§ 4.128` `100%` hospitalization convalescence**. · • **Stressor Liberalization:** **`38 C.F.R. § 3.304(f)(3)`** (`75 FR 39843`, corrected at **`75 FR 41092`** to **eff. July 13, 2010** — fear of hostile military/terrorist activity).

Adopted **DSM-5** diagnostic criteria (`§ 4.125(a)`); **eliminated `GAF` scores**; consolidated/renumbered `DC 9201–9440` titles; **kept the EXACT verbatim `0/10/30/50/70/100%` General Rating Formula** and `DC 9520–9521` Eating Disorders Formula!

• Governed by *Mauerhan*, *Vazquez-Claudio*, *Bankhead* (`2017` suicidal ideation -> `70%`), *Golden* (`2018`), *Martinez-Bodon* (`2022`), and *Ingram* (`2025`). *(Note: Post-2017 judicial interpretations like *Bankhead* are **Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** against final pre-2017 decisions under `§ 20.1403(e)`).*

blocks.text: 2. Substantive Gateways (§§ 4.125–4.128) & The Mandatory 38 C.F.R. § 4.129 50% Traumatic-Discharge Rule
A. §§ 4.125–4.128 Operational Rules (DSM-5, *Clemons*, Personality Disorders & 6-Month Hospitalizations)

items:
**Formal `DSM-5` Diagnosis Gate (`§ 4.125(a)`) vs. Broad Psychiatric Claim Scope (*Clemons*):**
• Under ***Martinez-Bodon v. McDonough*, `28 F.4th 1241 (Fed. Cir. 2022)`** (*aff'g* `33 Vet. App. 393 (2020)`), `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125(a)` and `4.130` make a **formal `DSM-5` diagnosis a mandatory precondition** to psychiatric service connection—distinguishing unlabelled physical pain under *Saunders v. Wilkie*, `886 F.3d 1356 (Fed. Cir. 2018)`. If an examination lacks `DSM-5` substantiation, `§ 4.125(a)` requires the rating agency to **return the report to the examiner**.
• Crucially, under ***Clemons v. Shinseki*, `23 Vet. App. 1 (2009)`** and `§ 4.125(b)`, a lay veteran's claim for `"PTSD"` encompasses **every psychiatric diagnosis reasonably raised by the record** (e.g., `DC 9434` Major Depressive Disorder, `DC 9400` GAD, `DC 9440` Chronic Adjustment Disorder, `DC 9421` Somatic Symptom Disorder)—often allowing the veteran to win direct SC under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.303(a)`** even when `§ 3.304(f)` PTSD stressor corroboration is contested ([Playbook 16](/playbooks/16-ptsd-stressors-and-mst-corroboration))!

**Longitudinal Assessment (`§ 4.126`) & Personality Disorders (`§ 4.127`):**
• **`§ 4.126(a)–(b)`:** Raters **cannot** base an evaluation on a brief lucid `"good day"` during a 20-minute telehealth DBQ; VA must evaluate longitudinal frequency, severity, duration, length of remissions, and social adaptability across work and personal relationships.
• **`§ 4.127`:** Intellectual developmental disorder and personality disorders are not compensable diseases per se (`§ 3.303(c)`), **EXCEPT** `(a)` when an SC mental disorder (`PTSD`/`MDD`) is **superimposed upon or aggravates** a personality disorder (`§ 3.310(a)`), or `(b)` when historical in-service *"personality disorder"* Separation Code entries masked incipient **schizophrenia (`§ 3.309(a)`), bipolar disorder, PTSD, or MST** ([Playbook 10](/playbooks/10-character-of-discharge-insanity-upgrades)).

**Extended Inpatient Psychiatric Hospitalization (`38 C.F.R. § 4.128`):**
• Whenever an SC mental disorder receives `100%` due to a **continuous hospitalization lasting `6 months or more`** (building on `§ 4.29` `>21-day` hospital `100%`), VA **MUST continue the `100%` evaluation indefinitely**, schedule a mandatory examination **`6 months` after discharge**, and apply **`38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e)`** before any reduction!

blocks.text: B. 38 C.F.R. § 4.129 Mandatory 50% Post-Discharge Minimum (Major Retroactive / CUE Trigger!)
Enacted **November 7, 1996 (`61 FR 52695`)**, `38 C.F.R. § 4.129` (*Mental disorders due to traumatic stress*) mandates:

lines: *"When a mental disorder that develops in service as a result of a highly stressful event is severe enough to bring about the veteran's release from active military service, the rating agency **shall assign an evaluation of not less than 50 percent** and schedule an examination within the six month period following the veteran's discharge to determine whether a change in evaluation is warranted."*

items:
**Four Practice Traps & Retroactive Goldmines Under `§ 4.129` (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive >= Nov. 7, 1996):**
• **NOT Limited to `DC 9411` PTSD:** By its plain text (`"a mental disorder"`), `§ 4.129` applies to **ANY `DSM` mental disorder** (`DC 9434` Major Depression, `DC 9400` Anxiety, `DC 9412` Panic Disorder, `DC 9440` Adjustment Disorder, `DC 9520–9521` Eating Disorder, or `DC 9201–9211` Psychosis) precipitated in service by a **highly stressful event** (combat, MST/personal assault, fatal crash, shipboard fire, mortuary duty)!
• **Administrative vs. Medical Separations (`"Bring About"`):** While `MEB/PEB/IDES` medical retirement or medical separation for a trauma-induced mental disorder is an automatic `§ 4.129` trigger, `§ 4.129` **also applies** when STRs/separation files show a trauma-induced mental disorder precipitated an administrative separation (e.g., `"condition not a disability"` / adjustment-disorder separation later recognized as SC PTSD/MST)!
• **Prospective `§ 3.105(e)` Protection vs. Retrospective Staged Ratings:** On a **running** post-discharge `50%+` award, VA **cannot** reduce below `50%` without conducting the mandatory 6-month VA exam AND issuing `60-day` **`38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e)`** notice (*cf. Foster v. McDonough*, `34 Vet. App. 338 (2021)`). Conversely, when `§ 4.129` is awarded **retroactively years later** as a historical staged rating, `§ 4.129` locks in **`>= 50%` for at least the initial post-discharge period** until post-6-month medical evidence affirmatively establishes sustained improvement, though prospective `§ 3.343(a)` hurdles do not block retrospective staged ratings (*Reizenstein v. Shinseki*, `583 F.3d 1331 (Fed. Cir. 2009)`).
• **Parallel `DoD` Medical Retirement Upgrade (`10 U.S.C. § 1216a` & *Sabo*):** Between `2001` and `2009`, military Physical Evaluation Boards unlawfully assigned `0%` or `10%` severance ratings for PTSD instead of `§ 4.129`'s **`50%` Temporary Disability Retired List (`TDRL`)** threshold (`>= 30%` = lifetime military medical retirement + `TRICARE` + `CRSC`!). Under **`10 U.S.C. § 1216a`** and ***Sabo v. United States*, `102 Fed. Cl. 619 (2011)`**, always screen `MEB/PEB` separation packets for a `PDBR` / `BCMR` medical-retirement upgrade alongside the VA claim!

blocks.text: 3. Controlling § 4.130 Precedents, Single-Rating Consolidation & Complete DC 9201–9440 Taxonomy
A. Controlling Precedential Architecture on § 4.130 (0% / 10% / 30% / 50% / 70% / 100%)

See [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125–4.130 Mental Disorders, Traumatic Stress (§ 4.129), Eating Disorders (DC 9520–9521) & Former § 4.132 Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.132-mental-disorders-pre-1996) for the verbatim `§ 4.130` General Rating Formula.

rows: The phrase **`"such symptoms as"`** makes the listed symptoms at each tier (`30%`, `50%`, `70%`, `100%`) **non-exhaustive illustrative examples**—raters may neither treat them as a mandatory cumulative checklist nor deny a higher tier when unenumerated symptoms produce equivalent occupational and social impairment.
Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) pre-2002; binding on all open/AMA claims.

`§ 4.130` is **predominantly symptom-driven**: evaluating a mental disorder is a **two-part inquiry** assessing `(1)` what symptoms exist, AND `(2)` their **frequency, severity, and duration** (`§ 4.126(a)`) to determine the resulting level of occupational and social impairment (`"deficiencies in most areas"` at `70%` vs. `"reduced reliability and productivity"` at `50%`).
***Bankhead v. Shulkin*, `29 Vet. App. 10, 20–22 (2017)`** & ***Golden v. Shulkin*, `29 Vet. App. 221 (2018)`**

**Suicidal Ideation = `70%` Hallmark:** The presence of **suicidal ideation alone**—including **passive suicidal ideation** (*thoughts of one's own death or wishing to be dead*)—signals `70%`-level impairment **without requiring active intent, a lethal plan, preparatory acts, or inpatient psychiatric hospitalization**! If the Board assigns `< 70%` despite documented suicidal ideation, it must explain why the veteran's overall symptom profile fails to approximate `70%`. (*Golden* reinforces alignment with DSM-5 symptom definitions).
**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** against final pre-2017 decisions; premier direct-appeal / HLR / Board remand weapon!
***Sellers v. Principi*, `372 F.3d 1318 (Fed. Cir. 2004)`** & ***Amberman v. Shinseki*, `570 F.3d 1377 (Fed. Cir. 2009)`**

**Single Mental Rating Consolidation (`§ 4.14`):** All comorbid `DC 9201–9440` psychiatric diagnoses (e.g., `DC 9411` PTSD + `DC 9434` MDD + `DC 9400` GAD + `DC 9421` Somatic Symptom Disorder + secondary substance-use disorder under *Allen v. Principi*) are consolidated into **ONE combined `§ 4.130` rating** reflecting total psychiatric impairment. *(See Section 3.C for mandatory separate physical/neurological/eating-disorder carve-outs!)*
***McCarroll v. McDonald*, `28 Vet. App. 267 (2016) (en banc)`** vs. ***Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)`**

**Psychotropic Medication Rule:** `§ 4.130`'s **`0%` and `10%` tiers explicitly mention continuous medication** (*"or symptoms controlled by continuous medication"* = `10%`), whereas **`30%`, `50%`, `70%`, and `100%` are silent on medication**. Thus, if SSRIs/mood stabilizers genuinely control symptoms down to mild/asymptomatic levels, `10%` applies (*McCarroll*); however, whenever residual symptoms persist above `10%` (panic attacks, depressed mood, sleep impairment, suicidal ideation), **`30%–100%` are silent on medication**, barring examiners from discounting partially medicated severity under *Ingram* (`91 FR 7118` rescinded `91 FR 9712`)!
Audit both `§ 4.130` residual severity AND **secondary medication side-effect claims**!

blocks.text: B. Complete DSM-5 Diagnostic Code Taxonomy (DC 9201–9440, 79 FR 45093 / 80 FR 14308)

items:
**Schizophrenia Spectrum & Other Psychotic Disorders (`DC 9201–9211` — *ONLY* category eligible for `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(a)` 1-Year Chronic Disease Presumption!):**
• **`9201`** Schizophrenia *(DSM-IV subtypes `9202–9205` removed Aug. 4, 2014)* \| **`9208`** Delusional disorder \| **`9210`** Other specified and unspecified schizophrenia spectrum and other psychotic disorders \| **`9211`** Schizoaffective disorder.

**Delirium & Neurocognitive Disorders (`DC 9300–9326`):**
• **`9300`** Delirium \| **`9301`** Major or mild neurocognitive disorder due to HIV or other infections \| **`9304`** Major or mild neurocognitive disorder due to traumatic brain injury *(evaluated via `DC 8045` `10-facet` TBI schedule per `§ 4.124a`!)* \| **`9305`** Major or mild vascular neurocognitive disorder \| **`9310`** Unspecified neurocognitive disorder \| **`9312`** Major or mild neurocognitive disorder due to Alzheimer's disease \| **`9326`** Major or mild neurocognitive disorder due to another medical condition or substance/medication-induced *(note: `former DC 9327` Organic mental disorder, other removed Aug. 4, 2014)*.

**Anxiety, Obsessive-Compulsive, Trauma/Stressor, Dissociative, Somatic, Mood & Adjustment Disorders (`DC 9400–9440`):**
• *Anxiety & OCD:* **`9400`** Generalized anxiety disorder \| **`9403`** Specific phobia; social anxiety disorder (social phobia) \| **`9404`** Obsessive-compulsive disorder \| **`9412`** Panic disorder and/or agoraphobia \| **`9413`** Unspecified anxiety disorder.
• *Trauma & Stressor-Related:* **`9410`** Other specified trauma- and stressor-related disorder \| **`9411`** **Posttraumatic stress disorder (`PTSD`)** \| **`9440`** Chronic adjustment disorder.
• *Dissociative:* **`9416`** Dissociative amnesia; dissociative identity disorder \| **`9417`** Depersonalization/derealization disorder.
• *Somatic Symptom & Related:* **`9421`** Somatic symptom disorder \| **`9422`** Other specified somatic symptom and related disorder \| **`9423`** Unspecified somatic symptom and related disorder \| **`9424`** Conversion disorder (functional neurological symptom disorder) \| **`9425`** Illness anxiety disorder.
• *Bipolar & Depressive:* **`9431`** Cyclothymic disorder \| **`9432`** Bipolar disorder \| **`9433`** Persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia) \| **`9434`** **Major depressive disorder (`MDD`)** \| **`9435`** Unspecified depressive disorder.

blocks.text: C. Breaking Out of Single-Rating Consolidation: High-Value Secondary & Comorbid Physical Unlocks

Because *Amberman* merges all `DC 9201–9440` diagnoses into one rating, firm case value multiplies by pleading **non-`§ 4.130` physical, neurological, and medication-induced secondary conditions** (`38 C.F.R. § 3.310(a)–(b)`):

items: **SSRI / SNRI / Antipsychotic Sexual Dysfunction (`DC 7522` Erectile Dysfunction `0%` or `DC 7632` Female Sexual Arousal Disorder `0%`) -> Mandatory **`38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)` (`SMC(k)`)** monthly add-on!**

**Psychotropic Weight-Gain / Trauma-Inactivity Obesity Intermediate Step (`VAOPGCPREC 1-2017`) -> `DC 6847` Obstructive Sleep Apnea (`50%` CPAP), `DC 7913` Type 2 Diabetes, `DC 7101` Hypertension, & `DC 7346` GERD** ([Playbook 14](/playbooks/14-secondary-service-connection-aggravation-obesity)).

**Stress/Hyperarousal Bruxism & Temporomandibular Disorder (`DC 9905` `10%–50%` + `§ 17.161` VA Dental)**, **Tension/Migraine Headaches (`DC 8100` `30%–50%`)**, and **Irritable Bowel Syndrome (`DC 7319` `10%–30%`)**.

**Comorbid `DC 8045` TBI (`§ 4.124a` Note (1)):** Rated **separately** whenever a qualified specialist can delineate TBI cognitive/neurobehavioral facets from psychiatric symptoms without speculation (*Mittleider v. West*, `11 Vet. App. 181 (1998)`; [Playbook 18](/playbooks/18-tbi-facets-radiculopathy-and-nerve-stacking)).

blocks.text: 4. Eating Disorders (DC 9520 Anorexia Nervosa & DC 9521 Bulimia Nervosa, § 4.130 Notes 1 & 2)

Enacted **November 7, 1996 (`61 FR 52695`)** and expressly carved out of the `DC 9201–9440` General Rating Formula by **`38 C.F.R. § 4.130` Note 2** (which refers to the codified **`Rating Formula for Eating Disorders`** heading as the *General Rating Formula for Eating Disorders*; see verbatim text in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125–4.130 Mental Disorders, Traumatic Stress (§ 4.129), Eating Disorders (DC 9520–9521) & Former § 4.132 Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.132-mental-disorders-pre-1996)):

headers: Structural Criteria Summary (`DC 9520` Anorexia Nervosa & `DC 9521` Bulimia Nervosa — Verbatim SSOT in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125–4.130 Mental Disorders, Traumatic Stress (§ 4.129), Eating Disorders (DC 9520–9521) & Former § 4.132 Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.132-mental-disorders-pre-1996))
rows: Weight `< 80%` expected minimum + `>= 6 weeks`/yr incapacitating episodes + `> 2` hospitalizations/yr for parenteral nutrition or tube feeding *(conjunctive `"and"`)*.
Weight `< 85%` expected minimum + `>= 6 weeks`/yr incapacitating episodes.
Weight `< 85%` expected minimum + `> 2` to `< 6 weeks`/yr incapacitating episodes.
Diagnosed purging/weight-resistance behaviors + incapacitating episodes of up to `2 weeks`/yr.
Diagnosed eating disorder (`DC 9520`/`9521`) without physician-prescribed incapacitating episodes.

lines: **Structural Cross-Reference & Audit Hooks (`Note 1`, Comorbid `§ 4.130` & Physical Residuals):**

1. **`Note 1` Bed-Rest Prerequisite:** `Note 1` defines an `"incapacitating episode"` strictly as *"a period during which bed rest and treatment by a physician are required"*; coupled with the `< 85%` / `< 80%` weight cutoffs at `30%–100%`, normal-weight `DC 9521` Bulimia Nervosa or DSM-5 Binge-Eating Disorder (`§ 4.20` analogy) rarely exceeds `0%` or `10%` under the Eating Disorders table alone.

2. **Comorbid `§ 4.130` & Secondary Physical Cross-References:** Because `Note 2` separates `DC 9520–9521` from `DC 9201–9440`, comorbid trauma/mood disorders (`DC 9411` PTSD / `DC 9434` MDD, e.g., post-MST under [Playbook 16](/playbooks/16-ptsd-stressors-and-mst-corroboration)) are evaluated on distinct non-duplicated symptoms under **`§ 4.130` (`30%–100%`)** (`§ 4.14`; [Playbook 19](/playbooks/19-extraschedular-3.321b1-analogous-4.20-and-temp-total) for `§ 3.321(b)(1)` extraschedular). Common secondary physical sequelae (`§ 3.310(a)`) include dental enamel erosion/tooth loss (`§ 4.150` + `38 C.F.R. § 17.161` VA Dental), esophagitis/GERD/stricture (`DC 7206`/`7346`), hypokalemic cardiac arrhythmias (`DC 7010`/`7011`), secondary amenorrhea/infertility (`DC 7613` + `SMC(k)`), and osteoporosis (`DC 5013`).

lines: **QUARANTINE NOTICE — DO NOT CITE AS ACTIVE LAW (AGENTS Law 6):**

1. **Unfinalized Proposed Rule `RIN 2900-AQ82` (`87 FR 8498`, published February 15, 2022 — Proposed / Not Finalized):** VA published a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking proposing to replace both the `§ 4.130` General Rating Formula for Mental Disorders and the Separate Eating Disorders Formula with a **5-domain `WHODAS 2.0`-inspired functional matrix** (`cognition`, `interpersonal interactions`, `task completion`, `navigating environments`, `self-care`), eliminating `0%` in favor of a **`10%` minimum floor** and removing total occupational impairment as a bar to `100%` while employed. **`RIN 2900-AQ82` (`87 FR 8498`) has NEVER been finalized and has ZERO legal force as of late 2026.** Never cite `RIN 2900-AQ82` on any pending claim, appeal, or CUE motion; apply active `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125–4.130` exclusively.

2. **Rescinded `38 C.F.R. § 4.10` Medication Interim Final Rule (`91 FR 7118`, Feb. 17, 2026 — Rescinded `91 FR 9712`, Feb. 27, 2026):** VA's February 2026 IFR attempting to override *Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)` was **rescinded ab initio** after 10 days. Audit any psychiatric evaluation issued in February 2026 to ensure `30%–100%` criteria were not unlawfully discounted under rescinded `91 FR 7118`.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Mental Health Disorders (1946–Present): PTSD, Depression, Traumatic Separation & Medication Side Effects
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Under 38 C.F.R. § 4.130, VA evaluates almost all non-eating mental health conditions—including PTSD, major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety, panic disorder, bipolar disorder, and psychotic disorders—under a single General Rating Formula (0%, 10%, 30%, 50%, 70%, or 100%) based on overall occupational and social impairment. This historical guide compares the pre-1988, 1988–1996 (former § 4.132 and former § 4.16(c)), November 7, 1996 (DSM-IV), and August 4, 2014 (DSM-5) rules, while flagging common errors such as discounting passive suicidal thoughts, overlooking the 50% post-discharge floor under 38 C.F.R. § 4.129, denying non-PTSD mental diagnoses when a Veteran filed for 'PTSD,' or missing secondary physical conditions caused by psychiatric medications.
record_clues: VA mental health or C&P exam notes recording passive or active suicidal ideation (such as 'thoughts of being better off dead') where VA assigned 30% or 50% because there was no active plan or psychiatric hospitalization (contrary to Bankhead v. Shulkin on open claims/appeals).

Military Medical Evaluation Board / Physical Evaluation Board (MEB/PEB) separation records for a trauma-induced mental disorder on or after November 7, 1996 where VA assigned less than 50% from discharge in violation of 38 C.F.R. § 4.129.

An older 'PTSD' denial where a VA examiner diagnosed major depression, generalized anxiety, or chronic adjustment disorder instead of PTSD and VA stopped without evaluating whether that acquired psychiatric diagnosis was connected to service (Clemons v. Shinseki).

Prescriptions for SSRIs, SNRIs, or antipsychotics accompanied by weight gain/obesity leading to obstructive sleep apnea, teeth grinding/TMJ (Diagnostic Code 9905), or sexual dysfunction (Diagnostic Code 7522 or 7632 + SMC(k)).
important_cautions: Single combined mental health rating rule: under 38 C.F.R. § 4.14 and Federal Circuit precedent (Amberman v. Shinseki), VA generally assigns one combined mental health percentage covering overlapping psychiatric diagnoses (such as PTSD plus depression plus anxiety), and Federal Circuit precedent (Martinez-Bodon v. McDonough) requires a formal DSM-5 diagnosis to establish psychiatric service connection.

One-year post-discharge chronic presumption limit: under 38 C.F.R. § 3.309(a), only 'psychoses' (Diagnostic Codes 9201–9211) qualify for the automatic 1-year post-discharge chronic disease presumption—PTSD, anxiety, and non-psychotic depression require direct, stressor-presumptive (§ 3.304(f)), or secondary service connection.

Quarantined proposed and rescinded rules: VA's February 15, 2022 proposed 5-domain mental health schedule (87 FR 8498, RIN 2900-AQ82) remains an unfinalized proposed rule (not enacted law), and VA's February 17, 2026 medication Interim Final Rule (91 FR 7118) was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712).

Check historical dates and *George* limits before considering CUE: suicidal ideation did not enter the 70% regulation until November 7, 1996, and under George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e), a later court interpretation like Bankhead v. Shulkin (2017) cannot establish Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) against a final pre-2017 decision.
questions_for_representative: Do my VA therapy notes or C&P exam document suicidal ideation, near-continuous panic/depression, or inability to maintain work and family relationships matching the 70% or 100% tier of 38 C.F.R. § 4.130?

If VA denied my earlier PTSD claim even though the examiner diagnosed depression or anxiety, can we review whether Clemons v. Shinseki or newly obtained military stressor/personnel records (38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)) apply?

Have we checked my medical records for secondary conditions caused or aggravated by my psychiatric condition or medications—such as jaw clenching/TMD (Diagnostic Code 9905), sleep apnea via medication-induced weight gain, or SMC(k)?

If I had continuous inpatient VA or approved psychiatric hospitalization lasting more than 21 days (38 C.F.R. § 4.29) or 6+ months (38 C.F.R. § 4.128), did VA pay the mandatory temporary 100% evaluation?

Brown*)**, PACT Act `38 U.S.C. § 1120(b)(2)(B)` head/neck/oral malignancies (`DC 9918`), and ***George v. McDonough* (`596 U.S. 740 (2022)`) / `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`** bitemporal boundaries governing **Body System 15 (Dental and Oral Conditions)**.

*(For verbatim multi-era regulatory text of `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.149–4.150` and `§ 3.381`, consult **[Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 4.150 Dental & Oral Conditions and TMD Matrix (DC 9900–9918, 1994 vs. September 10, 2017)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.150-dental-tmj-evolution)**, [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.105(d)–(i), 3.343, 3.344, 3.951, 3.953 & 3.957 (Rating Reductions, Stabilization & Statutory Protections)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.105e-3.344-3.951-3.957-reductions), and [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.1–4.31 Subpart A General Rating Policy & Two-Era § 3.321(b)(1) Extraschedular Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.1-4.31-general-policy-snapshots); for `§ 4.59` painful motion and *Ingram* anti-mitigation rules, see [`Subpart A General Rating Policy Diff`](/cfr/modules/subpart-a-general-rating-policy-4.1-4.31) and [`System 01 Musculoskeletal Diff`](/cfr/modules/01-musculoskeletal-joints-arthritis-implants-4.71a); for secondary bruxism/TMD causation (`§ 3.310`), see [Playbook 14](/playbooks/14-secondary-service-connection-aggravation-obesity); for PACT Act head/neck/oral cancers, see [Playbook 15](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera); for cranial nerve, taste/smell, and facial scar unbundling, see [`System 03 Auditory & Taste/Smell Diff`](/cfr/modules/03-auditory-hearing-tinnitus-4.85-4.87), [`System 13 Neurological & Cranial Nerves Diff`](/cfr/modules/13-neurological-tbi-nerves-4.120-4.124a), [`Scars & Disfigurement Diff`](/cfr/38-cfr-4.118#redline-diff), [Master SMC Treatise](/docs/smc-complete-treatise-and-step-math), [VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon), and [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).*
1. Master Chronological Federal Register & Precedent Ledger (1946–2026)

rows: Established Era-1 dental/maxillofacial schedule (`DC 9900–9913`), qualitative temporomandibular limitation (`DC 9905`), maxilla loss (`DC 9910`), bony tooth-substance loss (`DC 9913`), and former `§ 4.149` barring compensable ratings for treatable carious teeth/periodontal disease.
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`< Feb. 17, 1994`):** Governs pre-1994 CUE audits.

Held that a veteran's claim for **service-connected dental disability compensation inherently and simultaneously raises a claim for VA outpatient dental treatment eligibility** under `38 U.S.C. § 1712` (`former § 612`) and `38 C.F.R. § 17.161` (`former § 17.123`)—barring ROs from closing a noncompensable tooth claim without adjudicating treatment-purpose SC!

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive / Pending Unadjudicated Claim:** An RO decision denying compensable `§ 4.150` pay while failing to adjudicate `§ 3.381` / `§ 17.161` dental treatment leaves the outpatient dental claim legally unadjudicated (and post-Feb. 19, 2019 triggers *Hamill* `§ 5104(b)` non-finality!).

**First Major Dental & Oral Overhaul (Era 2):** Enacted objective millimeter inter-incisal table in **`DC 9905`** (`0–10 mm = 40%`, `11–20 mm = 30%`, `21–30 mm = 20%`, `31–40 mm = 10%`; lateral excursion `0–4 mm = 10%`); **removed `DC 9910`** (replacing it with **`DC 9914–9916`** maxilla codes); modernized `DC 9900–9913`.
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`Feb. 17, 1994 – Sept. 9, 2017`):** Notice that `31–40 mm` vertical opening equaled **`10%`** and `21–30 mm` equaled **`20%` WITHOUT any dietary restriction**!
***Woodson v. Brown*, `8 Vet. App. 352 (1995)`**, *aff'd in part, dismissed in part*, **`87 F.3d 1304 (Fed. Cir. 1996)`**; ***Simington v. West*, `11 Vet. App. 41 (1998)`**

*Woodson* confirmed routine in-service extractions without bony trauma do not self-evidently prove post-service compensable dental pathology (`§ 3.381`); *Simington* delineated service-trauma dental SC (`Class II(a)`) vs. compensable `§ 4.150` bony loss (`DC 9913`).
Enforces the statutory divide between `§ 4.150` monthly compensation and `§ 3.381` / `§ 17.161` VHA dental treatment eligibility.

**Removed and Reserved `38 C.F.R. § 4.149` & Overhauled `38 C.F.R. § 3.381`:** Relocated the noncompensable treatable-caries / periodontal-disease rule out of `Part 4` (`§ 4.149 [Reserved]`) into **`38 C.F.R. § 3.381(b)`** (*service connection of dental conditions for treatment purposes*).
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= June 8, 1999`):** Clarified Part 3 vs. Part 4 boundary without altering substantive noncompensability of simple caries/periodontal disease.

**Second Major Dental & Oral Overhaul (Era 3 — Current Law):** Enacted `§ 4.150 Notes (1)–(2)`; replaced `DC 9905` with the **two-axis Vertical Opening (`0–34 mm`) × Mechanically Altered Diet (`10%–50%`)** matrix (`normal = 35–50 mm`); expanded **`DC 9900`** to cover **osteonecrosis (`ONJ`/`MRONJ`) and osteoradionecrosis (`ORN`)**; merged `DC 9906–9907` into **`DC 9902`** (`10%–70%`) and **removed `DC 9906, 9907, 9912`**; and **created `DC 9917` (Benign oral neoplasm) & `DC 9918` (Malignant oral neoplasm `100%` + `6 mos`)**.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Sept. 10, 2017`):** Pre-Sept. 10, 2017 running `DC 9905` awards (`e.g.`, `10%` at `35–40 mm` or `20%/30%/40%` without diet restrictions) are **grandfathered under `38 U.S.C. § 1155` & `§ 3.951(a)`**; pending claims straddling Sept. 10, 2017 receive Era-2 staged ratings prior to Sept. 10, 2017 (*Karnas*).

Enacted PACT Act burn-pit presumptive SC for **`"head cancer of any type"` and `"neck cancer of any type"`**—capturing **all oral cavity, lip, tongue, floor-of-mouth, palate, gingival, mandibular/maxillary jaw, oropharyngeal, and salivary gland malignancies (`DC 9918`)**!

**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (`>= Aug. 10, 2022`)** + `38 U.S.C. § 1305` / `§ 3.33` retroactive survivor DIC re-evaluations ([Playbook 08](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical), [Playbook 15](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera)).
***Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)`** *(rescinded IFR `91 FR 7118` voided at `91 FR 9712`)*

Because **`DC 9905` TMD is 100% silent on medication**, adjudicators and C&P examiners **cannot discount** jaw ROM impairment for ameliorative effects of muscle relaxants (`cyclobenzaprine`, `tizanidine`), NSAIDs, corticosteroids, or masseter `Botox` injections!
**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** on CUE against final pre-2025 ratings; **fully binding** on all open, pending, Supplemental, HLR, Board, and CAVC claims!

blocks.text: B. Controlling DC 9905 Notes, Measurement Traps, § 4.59 Painful Motion & Secondary Bruxism

items:
**Mandatory `DC 9905 Notes (1)–(3)` (`82 FR 36080`):**
• **`Note (1)` (Non-Combination of Vertical + Lateral):** Ratings for limited interincisal vertical movement **shall NOT be combined** with ratings for limited lateral excursion (`0–4 mm = 10%`); assign whichever single evaluation is higher.
• **`Note (2)` (Normal Unassisted Vertical Opening = `35 to 50 mm`):** Examiners must measure **maximum *unassisted* vertical opening** (inter-incisal gap in millimeters using a millimeter ruler/Boley gauge—**never** passive examiner-forced prying of the jaw!).
• **`Note (3)` (Mechanically Altered Diet Definition & Physician-Verification Gate):** Mechanically altered foods are foods altered by **blending, chopping, grinding, or mashing** so they are easy to chew and swallow (`4` recognized texture levels: **full liquid, puree, soft, and semisolid**). **Crucial Gate:** *"To warrant elevation based on mechanically altered foods, the use of texture-modified diets **must be recorded or verified by a physician**"* (or treating dentist/oral surgeon—a veteran's uncorroborated lay statement of eating soft soup/smoothies without provider chart documentation/verification will fail at the Board; **always have the treating dentist or PCP record the texture-modified diet in the clinical treatment plan before the C&P exam!**).

**The `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.40, 4.45 & 4.59` Painful-Motion `10%` Floor & *DeLuca*/*Mitchell* Flare-Ups:**
• The temporomandibular joint is a **synovial musculoskeletal joint**! Even when a veteran's unassisted interincisal opening measures **`>= 35 mm`** (`"normal"` under `Note (2)`) and lateral excursion exceeds `4 mm`, **actually painful motion (`§ 4.59`)** during jaw opening, closing, lateral excursion, or mastication (*Burton v. Shinseki*, `25 Vet. App. 1 (2011)`; *Petitti v. McDonald*, `27 Vet. App. 415 (2015)`) **mandates at least the minimum compensable `10%` evaluation** under `DC 9905`—and examiners must also estimate additional millimeter loss during masticatory **flare-ups** and repetitive motion (`§§ 4.40, 4.45`; [System 01 Diff](/cfr/modules/01-musculoskeletal-joints-arthritis-implants-4.71a))!
• **Why Even a `10%` `DC 9905` Award Is Worth Tens of Thousands of Dollars:** Crossing from `0%` to **`10%` under `DC 9905`** immediately qualifies a veteran (even one whose combined VA rating is `< 100%`) for **Class I Lifetime Comprehensive VA Outpatient Dental Care (`38 C.F.R. § 17.161(a)`)**—covering **all** oral health, crowns, implants, root canals, and prosthodontics for life, **not just the TMJ**!

**The Secondary Bruxism Intermediate-Step Doctrine (`PTSD` / `MDD` / `TBI` / `SSRIs` -> Bruxism -> `DC 9905` TMD + Tooth Attrition):**
• Under `M21-1` (`Part V, Subpart iii, Ch. 14`), **bruxism** (involuntary sleep/awake teeth grinding and jaw clenching) has **no standalone Diagnostic Code** and is treated by VA as a *symptom* rather than an independent compensable disability when claimed in isolation.
• **The Winning Secondary Strategy ([Playbook 14](/playbooks/14-secondary-service-connection-aggravation-obesity)):** Plead bruxism (triggered by **SC PTSD hyperarousal, MDD/anxiety, TBI, or SSRI-induced bruxism** from `sertraline`/`fluoxetine`/`venlafaxine`) as the **causal intermediate step** (`38 C.F.R. § 3.310(a)`) producing **`DC 9905` Temporomandibular Disorder (`10%–50%`)**, secondary **cervicogenic/tension/migraine headaches (`DC 8100`, `10%–50%`)**, and secondary **tinnitus (`DC 6260`, `10%`)**! Once `DC 9905` reaches **`>= 10%`**, **Class I (`§ 17.161(a)`)** automatically unlocks full VA restorative dental care for every bruxism-fractured or worn-down tooth!

blocks.text: 4. Compensable VASRD (§ 4.150) vs. VHA Outpatient Dental Care (38 U.S.C. § 1712, 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.381 & 17.161) & *Mays v. Brown*

Because standard VHA health care (`38 U.S.C. § 1710`) **excludes** routine dental care for most `< 100%` veterans, unlocking VHA outpatient dental eligibility under **`38 U.S.C. § 1712`** and **`38 C.F.R. § 17.161`** is often worth **$20,000–$80,000+ in lifetime implants, crowns, prosthodontics, and periodontal care**. Under ***Mays v. Brown*, `5 Vet. App. 302, 306 (1993)`**, **every claim for dental disability compensation automatically raises a claim for `§ 3.381` / `§ 17.161` outpatient dental eligibility**:

headers: Scope & Frequency of Authorized VA Dental Care
rows: **Any `>= 10%` compensable SC dental or oral disability** (`DC 9900–9918`—including a **`10%` `DC 9905` TMD / secondary bruxism** rating!).

**LIFETIME COMPREHENSIVE DENTAL CARE:** *Any* dental treatment reasonably necessary to maintain oral health and masticatory function (**unlimited repeat episodes**, **all** teeth, zero application deadline!).

**The `10%` `DC 9905` Golden Key:** Winning **`10%` for `DC 9905` TMD** (including via `§ 4.59` painful motion or secondary to PTSD/bruxism) converts a veteran with `10%–90%` combined ratings into a **lifetime full-mouth `Class I` dental beneficiary**!

**`0%` noncompensable SC dental condition** (`§ 3.381`) shown in existence at discharge after `>= 90` (`Gulf War/post-1990`: `>= 90/180`) days active service, **applied for within `180 days`** of discharge, provided `DD-214` (`Block 17`) does **not** certify complete pre-separation dental exam & treatment.
**One-time correction** only of those specific noncompensable dental conditions existing at separation (unless upgraded via `Class II(a)` or `Class I`).

Strict **`180-day` post-discharge filing bar** and `DD-214` dental-completion bar (*Woodson*) defeat most late `Class II` claims—**pivot immediately to `Class II(a)` trauma or `DC 9905` `Class I`!** *(Note: `38 C.F.R. § 3.381(d)` bars treating routine in-service fillings/extractions as aggravation of pre-entry caries unless additional pathology developed after `>= 180` days of service).*

**`0%` noncompensable SC dental condition adjudicated as resulting from COMBAT WOUNDS or SERVICE TRAUMA** (`§ 3.381(a)(3)–(4)`; *Simington v. West*, `11 Vet. App. 41 (1998)`—e.g., fractured/avulsed tooth `#8`/`#9` from rifle butt, parachute landing, vehicle crash, training blow, or MST assault!).

**LIFETIME REPEAT DENTAL CARE FOR TRAUMATIZED TEETH:** Any treatment reasonably necessary to correct and **maintain** the service-traumatized tooth/teeth and replacement prosthesis/implant (**NO `180-day` deadline; unlimited repeat care**!).

Audit **service dental records (`SF 603` / `DD Form 2813`)** for any tooth fractured, luxated, root-canaled, or extracted due to **physical trauma** (or associate missing dental STRs via **`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)`**, [Playbook 03](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c))!
**Former Prisoner of War (`FPOW`)** of any duration (`38 U.S.C. § 1712(a)(1)(F)`).
**LIFETIME COMPREHENSIVE DENTAL CARE:** Any needed outpatient dental treatment (`Class I` equivalent!).
Veteran with a dental pathology professionally determined by a VA physician/dentist to **directly and materially AGGRAVATE an associated SC medical condition**!
Ongoing dental treatment for all dental conditions having a direct and material detrimental effect on the associated SC medical condition.

**HIGH-YIELD CLINICAL BRIDGE:** Applies to **head/neck radiation xerostomia**, **Sjögren's syndrome (`DC 6351`)**, **SC bulimia nervosa (`DC 9521` acid enamel erosion)**, **medication-induced severe xerostomia** (anticholinergics, tricyclics, opioids, CPAP dry mouth), **SC prosthetic heart valves / endocarditis risk**, and poorly controlled **SC diabetes (`DC 7913`)** aggravated by periodontal infection!

Veteran rated **`100%` schedular** OR paid at the **`100%` rate via `TDIU` (`§ 4.16`)**! *(Note: Temporary `100%` ratings under `§§ 4.29/4.30` or temporary active cancer `100%` do NOT confer permanent Class IV after the temporary `100%` ends, though active cancer care receives medically necessary hospital/Class III/VI dental clearance).*
**LIFETIME COMPREHENSIVE DENTAL CARE:** Any needed outpatient dental treatment for all teeth!
Remind every newly granted `100%` schedular or **`TDIU`** client (`P&T` not even required while `100%`/TDIU is running!) that they immediately qualify for **full `Class IV` VA dental care**!

**`Class V`:** Active **`38 U.S.C. Chapter 31` VR&E** participant needing dental care to achieve vocational rehabilitation / prevent interruption. · **`Class VI`:** Veteran scheduled for inpatient/outpatient VHA medical care (e.g., joint arthroplasty, cardiac valve surgery, organ transplant, head/neck radiation, bisphosphonate start) where dental pathology would **complicate medical care**.
Medically/vocationally necessary dental care to complete `Ch. 31` (`Class V`) or clear the medical complication (`Class VI`).
Essential stopgap for `< 100%` veterans awaiting `TDIU` or `DC 9905` adjudication!

lines: **QUARANTINE NOTICE — DO NOT CITE RESCINDED IFRs AS ACTIVE LAW (AGENTS Law 6):**

* **Rescinded `38 C.F.R. § 4.10` Medication Interim Final Rule (`91 FR 7118`, Feb. 17, 2026 — Rescinded Ab Initio at `91 FR 9712`, Feb. 27, 2026) vs. *Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)` on `DC 9905` TMD:** VA's 10-day February 2026 IFR attempting to displace *Ingram* was **rescinded ab initio**. Because **`DC 9905` Temporomandibular Disorder contains ZERO mention of medication** (its two axes measure *unassisted vertical opening* and *mechanically altered diet*, NOT pharmacologic control), ***Ingram v. Collins* applies with full force to `DC 9905`!** Whenever a veteran takes **muscle relaxants (`cyclobenzaprine`, `methocarbamol`, `tizanidine`, `baclofen`), prescription NSAIDs/corticosteroids, or therapeutic `Botox` (`onabotulinumtoxinA`) injections into the masseter/temporalis muscles** that artificially widen jaw opening on exam day, the examiner and Board **must** account for the baseline unmedicated functional loss of jaw motion and cannot use medication-induced relief to deny a `10%–50%` `DC 9905` evaluation!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Jaw Disorders (TMJ/TMD), Bruxism, Oral Cancer & VA Dental Care Classes: Historical Guide
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Access to comprehensive VA dental care is strictly limited unless a Veteran is rated 100% disabled/TDIU, is a former Prisoner of War, or holds a compensable (10% or higher) service-connected dental or jaw disability (Class I under 38 C.F.R. § 17.161). Many Veterans with service-connected PTSD, anxiety, depression, Traumatic Brain Injury, or SSRI medication side effects experience severe jaw clenching and teeth grinding (bruxism) that causes Temporomandibular Disorder (TMD, Diagnostic Code 9905)—which not only pays 10% to 50% monthly compensation under 38 C.F.R. § 4.150, but also unlocks full VA outpatient dental care.
record_clues: Dental notes mentioning 'bruxism,' 'wear facets,' 'nightguard / occlusal splint,' jaw clicking/locking, or masseter muscle tenderness in a Veteran service-connected for PTSD, depression, anxiety, or chronic pain.

A TMD (Diagnostic Code 9905) exam where muscle relaxants, anti-inflammatories, an occlusal splint, or Botox injections masked baseline jaw restriction (Diagnostic Code 9905 is silent on medication under Ingram v. Collins).

A VA denial of a dental compensation claim that stayed completely silent on whether the Veteran qualified for noncompensable VA outpatient dental treatment under 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.381 and 17.161 (Mays v. Brown).

Post-treatment oral, tongue, salivary-gland, or jaw squamous cell carcinoma (Diagnostic Code 9918—a PACT Act presumptive head and neck cancer) omitting separate ratings under § 4.150 Note (2) for radiation bone necrosis (Diagnostic Code 9900), difficulty speaking, loss of taste or smell, cranial nerve palsies, or facial scars.
important_cautions: Bruxism is an intermediate symptom, not a standalone Diagnostic Code: VA does not have a 4-digit code for 'bruxism' alone; instead, bruxism is claimed and evaluated as the causal link or symptom establishing secondary Temporomandibular Disorder (Diagnostic Code 9905) or aggravating another ratable condition.

Simple tooth decay and gum disease do not pay monthly compensation: cavities, periodontal disease, and missing teeth replaceable by bridge/denture/implant without jawbone-body loss are noncompensable under 38 C.F.R. § 3.381(b), though they may qualify for specific VA dental treatment classes.

Do not stack vertical opening and lateral excursion inside Diagnostic Code 9905, and remember that post-September 10, 2017 dietary elevation requires physician-recorded or physician-verified mechanically altered diet restrictions.
Never cite VA's rescinded February 17, 2026 medication Interim Final Rule (91 FR 7118, rescinded February 27, 2026 at 91 FR 9712) as active law.
questions_for_representative: Do my dental records show jaw clenching/bruxism caused by my service-connected PTSD, depression, or medications that has led to ratable Temporomandibular Disorder (Diagnostic Code 9905)?

Did the C&P examiner test both unassisted jaw opening and objective painful motion (38 C.F.R. § 4.59), and account for whether muscle relaxants, splints, or injections temporarily masked my jaw stiffness?
When VA denied monthly compensation on my dental claim, did VA separately adjudicate my eligibility for outpatient VA dental care under 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.381 and 17.161?

After oral or head-and-neck cancer treatment under Diagnostic Code 9918, did VA separately evaluate every speech, swallowing, jawbone (Diagnostic Code 9900), nerve, taste/smell, and facial-scar residual under § 4.150 Note (2)?

blocks.text: 2. Current Verbatim Text: 38 C.F.R. § 3.1000(a)–(h) (Uncapped Accrued Benefits)

lines: **§ 3.1000 Entitlement under 38 U.S.C. 5121 to benefits due and unpaid upon death of a beneficiary.**

**(a) Basic entitlement.** Except as provided in §§ 3.1001 and 3.1008, where death occurred on or after December 1, 1962, periodic monetary benefits (other than insurance and servicemembers' indemnity) authorized under laws administered by the Department of Veterans Affairs, to which a payee was entitled at his or her death under existing ratings or decisions or those based on evidence in the file at date of death, and due and unpaid will, upon the death of such person, be paid as follows: *(Authority: 38 U.S.C. 5121(a))*
* **(1)** Upon the death of a veteran to the living person first listed as follows:
* **(i)** His or her spouse;
* **(ii)** His or her children (in equal shares);
* **(iii)** His or her dependent parents (in equal shares) or the surviving parent.
* **(2)** Upon the death of a surviving spouse or remarried surviving spouse, to the veteran's children.
* **(3)** Upon the death of a child, to the surviving children of the veteran entitled to survivors pension, compensation, or dependency and indemnity compensation.
* **(4)** Upon the death of a child claiming benefits under chapter 18 of this title, to the surviving parents.
* **(5)** In all other cases, only so much of the accrued benefit may be paid as may be necessary to reimburse the person who bore the expense of last sickness or burial. (See § 3.1002.)
**(b) Apportionments.**

* **(1)** Upon the death of a person receiving an apportioned share of benefits payable to a veteran, all or any part of such unpaid amount is payable to the veteran or to any other dependent or dependents of the veteran. *(Authority: 38 U.S.C. 5121(a)(1))*

* **(2)** Where at the date of death of the veteran an apportioned share is being paid to or has been withheld on behalf of another person, the apportioned amount remaining unpaid for periods prior to the last day of the month before the veteran's death is payable to the apportionee.

**(c) Claims and evidence.** A claim for survivors pension, compensation, or dependency and indemnity compensation, by an apportionee, surviving spouse, child or parent is deemed to include claim for any accrued benefits. (See § 3.152(b).)

* **(1)** If an application for accrued benefits is incomplete because the claimant has not furnished information necessary to establish that he or she is within the category of eligible persons under the provisions of paragraphs (a)(1) through (a)(5) or paragraph (b) of this section and that circumstances exist which make the claimant the specific person entitled to payment of all or part of any benefits which may have accrued, VA shall notify the claimant:
* **(i)** Of the type of information required to complete the application;
* **(ii)** That VA will take no further action on the claim unless VA receives the required information; and

* **(iii)** That if VA does not receive the required information within 1 year of the date of the original VA notification of information required, no benefits will be awarded on the basis of that application.

* **(2)** Failure to file timely claim, or a waiver of rights, by a preferred dependent will not serve to vest title in a person in a lower class or a claimant for reimbursement; neither will such failure or waiver by a person or persons in a joint class serve to increase the amount payable to another or others in the class. *(Authority: 38 U.S.C. 5121(c); 5112(b))*
**(d) Definitions.**

* **(1)** *Spouse* means the surviving spouse of the veteran, whose marriage meets the requirements of § 3.1(j) or § 3.52. Where the marriage meets the requirements of § 3.1(j) date of marriage and continuous cohabitation are not factors.

* **(2)** *Child* is as defined in § 3.57 and includes an unmarried child who became permanently incapable of self-support prior to attaining 18 years of age as well as an unmarried child over the age of 18 but not over 23 years of age, who was pursuing a course of instruction within the meaning of § 3.57 at the time of the payee's death. However, upon the death of a child in receipt of survivors pension, compensation, or dependency and indemnity compensation, any accrued will be payable to the surviving child or children of the veteran entitled to survivors pension, compensation, or dependency and indemnity compensation. Upon the death of a child, another child who has elected dependents' educational assistance under 38 U.S.C. chapter 35 may receive accrued survivors pension, compensation, or dependency and indemnity compensation, payable on behalf of the deceased child.
* **(3)** *Dependent parent* is as defined in § 3.59: *Provided*, That the mother or father was dependent within the meaning of § 3.250 at the date of the veteran's death.

* **(4)** *Evidence in the file at date of death* means evidence in VA's possession on or before the date of the beneficiary's death, even if such evidence was not physically located in the VA claims folder on or before the date of death, in support of a claim for VA benefits pending on the date of death.

**(e) Subsistence allowance.** Subsistence allowance under the provisions of 38 U.S.C. ch. 31 remaining due and unpaid at the date of the veteran's death, is payable under the provisions of this section.

**(f) Dependents' educational assistance.** Educational assistance allowance or special restorative training allowance under 38 U.S.C. ch. 35, remaining due and unpaid at the date of death of an eligible surviving spouse or eligible child is payable to a child or children of the veteran (see paragraphs (a)(2), (a)(3) and (d)(2) of this section), or on the expenses of last sickness and burial (see paragraph (a)(5) of this section.) Benefits due and unpaid at the date of death of an eligible spouse are payable only on the expenses of last sickness and burial (see paragraph (a)(5) of this section).

**(g) Veterans educational assistance.** Educational assistance allowance under 38 U.S.C. chapters 30, 32, or 34, and 10 U.S.C. chapter 1606 remaining due and unpaid at the date of the veteran's death is payable under the provisions of this section. *(Authority: 38 U.S.C. 5121)*
**(h) Clothing allowance.** Clothing allowance under 38 U.S.C. 1162 remaining due and unpaid at the date of the veteran's death is payable under the provisions of this section.

lines: **§ 3.1010 Substitution under 38 U.S.C. 5121A following death of a claimant.**

**(a) Eligibility.** If a claimant dies on or after October 10, 2008, a person eligible for accrued benefits under § 3.1000(a) listed in 38 CFR 3.1000(a)(1) through (5) may, in priority order, request to substitute for the deceased claimant in a claim for periodic monetary benefits (other than insurance and servicemembers' indemnity) under laws administered by the Secretary, or an appeal of a decision with respect to such a claim, that was pending before the agency of original jurisdiction or the Board of Veterans' Appeals when the claimant died. Upon VA's grant of a request to substitute, the substitute may continue the claim or appeal on behalf of the deceased claimant for purposes of processing the claim or appeal to completion. Any benefits ultimately awarded are payable to the substitute and other members of a joint class, if any, in equal shares.

**(b) Time and place for filing a request.** A person may not substitute for a deceased claimant under this section unless the person files a request to substitute with the agency of original jurisdiction no later than one year after the claimant's death.
**(c) Request format.**

* **(1)** A request to substitute must be submitted in writing. At a minimum, a request to substitute must indicate intent to substitute; include the deceased claimant's claim number, Social Security number, or appeal number; and include the names of the deceased claimant and the person requesting to substitute.

* **(2)** In lieu of a specific request to substitute, a claim for accrued benefits, survivors pension, or dependency and indemnity compensation by an eligible person listed in § 3.1000(a)(1) through (5) is deemed to include a request to substitute if a claim for periodic monetary benefits (other than insurance and servicemembers' indemnity) under laws administered by the Secretary, or an appeal of a decision with respect to such a claim, was pending before the agency of original jurisdiction or the Board of Veterans' Appeals when the claimant died.
* **(3)** A claimant for accrued benefits, survivors pension, or dependency and indemnity compensation may waive the right to substitute in writing over the claimant's signature.

**(d) Evidence of eligibility.** A person filing a request to substitute must provide evidence of eligibility to substitute. Evidence of eligibility to substitute means evidence demonstrating that the person is among those listed in the categories of eligible persons in § 3.1000(a)(1) through (5) and first in priority order. If a person's request to substitute does not include evidence of eligibility to substitute, the agency of original jurisdiction will notify the person that evidence of eligibility must be submitted within 60 days from the date of the notification. Failure to furnish evidence of eligibility within 60 days will result in the denial of the request to substitute.

**(e) Decisions on substitution requests.** Subject to the provisions of § 20.1302 of this chapter, the agency of original jurisdiction will decide in the first instance all requests to substitute, including any request to substitute in an appeal pending before the Board of Veterans' Appeals.

* **(1) Notification.** The agency of original jurisdiction will provide written notification of the granting or denial of a request to substitute to the person who filed the request, together with notice in accordance with § 3.103(b)(1).
* **(2) Appeal of denial.** The denial of a request to substitute may be appealed to the Board of Veterans' Appeals pursuant to 38 U.S.C. 7104(a) and 7105.
**(f) Adjudications involving a substitute.** The following provisions apply with respect to a claim or appeal in which a survivor has been substituted for the deceased claimant:

* **(1) Notice under § 3.159.** VA will send notice under § 3.159(b), "Department of Veterans Affairs assistance in developing claims," to the substitute only if the required notice was not sent to the deceased claimant or if the notice sent to the deceased claimant was inadequate.
* **(2) Expansion of the claim not permitted.** A substitute may not add an issue to or expand the claim. However, a substitute may raise new theories of entitlement in support of the claim.

* **(3) Submission of evidence and other rights.** A substitute has the same rights regarding hearings, representation, appeals, and the submission of evidence as would have applied to the claimant had the claimant not died. However, rights that may have applied to the claimant prior to death but which cannot practically apply to a substitute, such as the right to a medical examination, are not available to the substitute. The substitute must complete any action required by law or regulation within the time period remaining for the claimant to take such action on the date of his or her death. The time remaining to take such action will start to run on the date of the mailing of the decision granting the substitution request.
* **(4) Board of Veterans' Appeals procedures.** The rules and procedures governing appeals involving substitutes before the Board of Veterans' Appeals are found in parts 19 and 20 of this chapter.
**(g) Limitations on substitution.** The following limitations apply with respect to substitution:
* **(1) A claim or appeal must be pending**—

* **(i)** A claim is considered to be pending if the claimant had filed the claim with an agency of original jurisdiction but dies before the agency of original jurisdiction makes a decision on the claim. A claim is also considered to be pending if, at the time of the claimant's death, the agency of original jurisdiction has made a decision on the claim, but the claimant has not filed a notice of disagreement, and the period allowed by law for filing a notice of disagreement has not expired.

* **(ii)** An appeal is considered to be pending if a claimant filed a notice of disagreement in response to a notification from an agency of original jurisdiction of its decision on a claim, but dies before the Board of Veterans' Appeals issues a final decision on the appeal. If the Board issued a final decision on an appeal prior to the claimant's death, the appeal is not pending before VA for purposes of this section, even if the 120-day period for appealing the Board's decision to the Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims has not yet expired.

* **(2) Benefits awarded.** Any benefits ultimately awarded are limited to any past-due benefits for the time period between the effective date of the award and what would have been the effective date of discontinuance of the award as a result of the claimant's death.

* **(3) Benefits for last sickness and burial only.** When substitution cannot be established under any of the categories listed in § 3.1000(a)(1) through (a)(4), only so much of any benefits ultimately awarded may be paid as may be necessary to reimburse the person who bore the expense of last sickness and burial.

* **(4) Substitution by subordinate members prohibited.** Failure to timely file a request to substitute, or a waiver of the right to request substitution, by a person of a preferred category of eligible person will not serve to vest the right to request substitution in a person in a lower category or a person who bore the expense of last sickness and burial; neither will such failure or waiver by a person or persons in a joint class serve to increase the amount payable to other persons in the class.

* **(5) Death of a substitute.** If a substitute dies while a claim or appeal is pending before an agency of original jurisdiction, or an appeal of a decision on a claim is pending before the Board, another member of the same joint class or a member of the next preferred subordinate category listed in § 3.1000(a)(1) through (5) may substitute for the deceased substitute but only if the person requesting the successive substitution files a request to substitute no later than one year after the date of the substitute's death (not the date of the claimant's death). *(Authority: 38 U.S.C. 501, 5121, 5121A)*

lines: **§ 3.816 Awards under the *Nehmer* Court Orders for disability or death caused by a condition presumptively associated with herbicide exposure.**
**(f) Payment of benefits to survivors or estates of deceased beneficiaries**—

* **(1) General.** If a *Nehmer* class member entitled to retroactive benefits pursuant to paragraphs (c)(1) through (c)(3) or (d)(1) through (d)(3) of this section dies prior to receiving payment of any such benefits, VA shall pay such unpaid retroactive benefits to the first individual or entity listed below that is in existence at the time of payment:
* **(i)** The class member's spouse, regardless of current marital status.
* *Note to paragraph (f)(1)(i):* For purposes of this paragraph, a spouse is the person who was legally married to the class member at the time of the class member's death.
* **(ii)** The class member's child(ren), regardless of age or marital status (if more than one child exists, payment will be made in equal shares, accompanied by an explanation of the division).

* *Note to paragraph (f)(1)(ii):* For purposes of this paragraph, the term "child" includes natural and adopted children, and also includes any stepchildren who were members of the class member's household at the time of the class member's death.
* **(iii)** The class member's parent(s), regardless of dependency (if both parents are alive, payment will be made in equal shares, accompanied by an explanation of the division).

* *Note to paragraph (f)(1)(iii):* For purposes of this paragraph, the term "parent" includes natural and adoptive parents, but in the event of successive parents, the persons who last stood as parents in relation to the class member will be considered the parents.
* **(iv)** The class member's estate.

* **(2) Inapplicability of certain accrued benefit requirements.** The provisions of 38 U.S.C. 5121(c) and § 3.1000(c) requiring survivors to file claims for accrued benefits do not apply to payments under this section. When a *Nehmer* class member dies prior to receiving retroactive payments under this section, VA will pay the amount to an identified payee in accordance with paragraph (f)(1) of this section without requiring an application from the payee. Prior to releasing such payment, however, VA may ask the payee to provide further information as specified in paragraph (f)(3) of this section.

* **(3) Identifying payees.** VA shall make reasonable efforts to identify the appropriate payee(s) under paragraph (f)(1) of this section based on information in the veteran's claims file. If further information is needed to determine whether any appropriate payee exists or whether there are any persons having equal or higher precedence than a known prospective payee, VA will request such information from a survivor or authorized representative if the claims file provides sufficient contact information. Before releasing payment to an identified payee, VA will ask the payee to state whether there are any other survivors of the class member who may have equal or greater entitlement to payment under this section, unless the circumstances clearly indicate that such a request is unnecessary.

* **(4) Bar to accrued benefit claims.** Payment of benefits pursuant to paragraph (f)(1) of this section shall bar a later claim by any individual for payment of all or any part of such benefits as accrued benefits under 38 U.S.C. 5121 and § 3.1000.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Exact Legal Rules for Accrued Benefits (§ 3.1000), Survivor Substitution (§ 3.1010) & Nehmer Payees (§ 3.816(f))
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: This reference module compiles the three core VA regulations governing unpaid lifetime benefits after a Veteran's death, including their key historical turning points: (1) 38 C.F.R. § 3.1000 (Accrued Benefits), showing the December 16, 2003 statutory repeal of the old 2-year back-pay cap and the 2015 constructive-possession definition of 'evidence in the file at date of death'; (2) 38 C.F.R. § 3.1010 (Substitution), implementing 38 U.S.C. § 5121A for deaths on or after October 10, 2008—including the rule that a timely DIC or Survivors Pension application automatically counts as a request to substitute; and (3) 38 C.F.R. § 3.816(f) (Nehmer Agent Orange survivor and estate payments), including the December 2, 2021 amendment requiring full payment to newly identified eligible payees.
record_clues: A Veteran's death on or after December 16, 2003 (when Congress repealed the old 2-year limit on accrued back pay) or on or after October 10, 2008 (when Congress enacted § 5121A open-record substitution).

A VA Form 21P-534EZ survivor claim filed within 1 year of death while a Veteran's claim or appeal was pending—which § 3.1010(c)(2) treats as an automatic request to substitute even if no separate VA Form 21P-0847 was filed.

A pre-December 2, 2021 Nehmer Agent Orange decision that denied an eligible family payee because VA had already paid part or all of the award to someone else (removed effective December 2, 2021 at 86 FR 68409).
important_cautions: Priority Line Does Not Pass Down Upon Waiver (§ 3.1000(c)(2) & § 3.1010(g)(4)): Under standard accrued and substitution rules, if a surviving spouse is alive and eligible, lower-priority relatives (such as children or dependent parents) cannot step in even if the surviving spouse chooses not to file or waives substitution.

Death During the 120-Day CAVC Appeal Window: If the Board of Veterans' Appeals issued a final decision BEFORE the Veteran died and the Veteran passed away during the 120-day judicial appeal window, VA agency substitution under § 3.1010 does not apply—an accredited attorney must invoke CAVC Rule 43 judicial substitution (Breedlove) alongside a protective VA filing.

Deemed Substitution Waiver Notice (Reliford v. McDonald): VA cannot close out a pending claim purely on limited closed-record accrued rules without first giving the survivor proper notice of their right to substitute and submit new evidence.
questions_for_representative: Did my timely VA Form 21P-534EZ DIC/pension application automatically trigger substitution under 38 C.F.R. § 3.1010(c)(2), and did VA notify me of my right to submit new medical evidence before deciding?
Were VA Medical Center or federal records constructively in VA's possession at the date of death under 38 C.F.R. § 3.1000(d)(4)?
For a Nehmer Agent Orange back-pay audit, how does the December 2, 2021 amendment to 38 C.F.R. § 3.816(f)(3) affect eligible family or estate payees?
