blocks.text: Spine evaluations under `38 C.F.R. § 4.71a` hinge on **two closely spaced regulatory effective dates** in 2002–2003 (plus minor note/title updates effective **February 7, 2021** at `85 FR 76453`):

items: **September 23, 2002 (`67 FR 54345`, published Aug. 22, 2002):** Revised **Intervertebral Disc Syndrome (`former DC 5293`)** to introduce the physician-prescribed bed-rest **Incapacitating Episodes** formula (`60/40/20/10%`) vs. combined chronic orthopedic and neurologic manifestations.

**September 26, 2003 (`68 FR 51454`, published Aug. 27, 2003):** Removed `DC 5285–5295` entirely and enacted `DC 5235–5243` under the **General Rating Formula for Diseases and Injuries of the Spine**, establishing objective goniometric range-of-motion (ROM) cutoffs and **Note (1)** mandating separate evaluations for objective neurologic abnormalities (radiculopathy, bowel/bladder impairment).

blocks.text: 1. Era 1 Verbatim Text: Pre-September 26, 2003 (Former DC 5285–5295, 2001 GovInfo CFR Edition)
*Governs spine decisions from April 1, 1946 (as updated March 10, 1976 at `41 FR 11294`) through September 25, 2003 (except `DC 5293` from Sept. 23, 2002 – Sept. 25, 2003, shown in Section 2).*

lines: ### THE SPINE
**5285 Vertebra, fracture of, residuals:**

* With cord involvement, bedridden, or requiring long leg braces — **100** *(Consider special monthly compensation; with lesser symptomatology rate on residuals of cord involvement or limitation of motion.)*
* Without cord involvement; abnormal mobility requiring neck brace (jury-mast) — **60**

* In other cases, rate on limitation of motion, muscle spasm, or other manifestations; **add 10 percent for demonstrable deformity of vertebral body** *(Note: 10 percent added to compensable or 0% limitation-of-motion rating for radiographic compression/deformity of vertebral body).*
**5286 Spine, complete bony fixation (ankylosis) of:**
* Unfavorable angle, with marked deformity and involvement of major joints (Marie-Strumpell type) or without other joint involvement (Bechterew type) — **100**
* Favorable angle — **60**
**5287 Spine, ankylosis of, cervical:**
* Unfavorable — **40**
* Favorable — **30**
**5288 Spine, ankylosis of, dorsal:**
* Unfavorable — **30**
* Favorable — **20**
**5289 Spine, ankylosis of, lumbar:**
* Unfavorable — **50**
* Favorable — **40**
**5290 Spine, limitation of motion of, cervical:**
* Severe — **30**
* Moderate — **20**
* Slight — **10**
**5291 Spine, limitation of motion of, dorsal:**
* Severe — **10**
* Moderate — **10**
* Slight — **0**
**5292 Spine, limitation of motion of, lumbar:**
* Severe — **40**
* Moderate — **20**
* Slight — **10**
**5293 Intervertebral disc syndrome** *(Pre-September 23, 2002 text)*:

* Pronounced; with persistent symptoms compatible with sciatic neuropathy with characteristic pain and demonstrable muscle spasm, absent ankle jerk, or other neurological findings appropriate to site of diseased disc, little intermittent relief — **60**
* Severe; recurring attacks, with intermittent relief — **40**
* Moderate; recurring attacks — **20**
* Postoperative, cured — **0**
**5294 Sacro-iliac injury and weakness:**
**5295 Lumbosacral strain:**

* Severe; with listing of whole spine to opposite side, positive Goldthwaite's sign, marked limitation of forward bending in standing position, loss of lateral motion with osteo-arthritic changes, or narrowing or irregularity of joint space, or some of the above with abnormal mobility on forced motion — **40**
* With muscle spasm on extreme forward bending, loss of lateral spine motion, unilateral, in standing position — **20**
* With characteristic pain on motion — **10**
* With slight subjective symptoms only — **0**

blocks.text: 2. Interim IVDS Revision: September 23, 2002 – September 25, 2003 (67 FR 54345, DC 5293)
*Effective **September 23, 2002** (and carried forward as `DC 5243` on September 26, 2003):*

lines: **5293 Intervertebral disc syndrome:**

Evaluate intervertebral disc syndrome (preoperatively or postoperatively) either on the total duration of incapacitating episodes over the past 12 months or by combining under § 4.25 separate evaluations of its chronic orthopedic and neurologic manifestations along with evaluations for all other disabilities, whichever method results in the higher evaluation:
* With incapacitating episodes having a total duration of at least six weeks during the past 12 months — **60**
* With incapacitating episodes having a total duration of at least four weeks, but less than six weeks, during the past 12 months — **40**
* With incapacitating episodes having a total duration of at least two weeks, but less than four weeks, during the past 12 months — **20**
* With incapacitating episodes having a total duration of at least one week, but less than two weeks, during the past 12 months — **10**

*Note (1):* For purposes of evaluations under 5293 [now 5243], an incapacitating episode is a period of acute signs and symptoms due to intervertebral disc syndrome that requires bed rest prescribed by a physician and treatment by a physician.

blocks.text: 3. Era 2 Verbatim Text: September 26, 2003 – Present (68 FR 51454 & 85 FR 76453, DC 5235–5243)
*Published August 27, 2003 (`68 FR 51454`), **effective September 26, 2003** (with minor `DC 5235–5244` title/paralysis routing updates effective **February 7, 2021** at `85 FR 76453`):*

lines: **General Rating Formula for Diseases and Injuries of the Spine**
*(For diagnostic codes 5235 to 5243 unless 5243 is evaluated under the Formula for Rating Intervertebral Disc Syndrome Based on Incapacitating Episodes):*
With or without symptoms such as pain (whether or not it radiates), stiffness, or aching in the area of the spine affected by residuals of injury or disease:
* Unfavorable ankylosis of the entire spine — **100**
* Unfavorable ankylosis of the entire thoracolumbar spine — **50**
* Unfavorable ankylosis of the entire cervical spine; or, forward flexion of the thoracolumbar spine 30 degrees or less; or, favorable ankylosis of the entire thoracolumbar spine — **40**
* Forward flexion of the cervical spine 15 degrees or less; or, favorable ankylosis of the entire cervical spine — **30**

* Forward flexion of the thoracolumbar spine greater than 30 degrees but not greater than 60 degrees; or, forward flexion of the cervical spine greater than 15 degrees but not greater than 30 degrees; or, the combined range of motion of the thoracolumbar spine not greater than 120 degrees; or, the combined range of motion of the cervical spine not greater than 170 degrees; or, muscle spasm or guarding severe enough to result in an abnormal gait or abnormal spinal contour such as scoliosis, reversed lordosis, or abnormal kyphosis — **20**

* Forward flexion of the thoracolumbar spine greater than 60 degrees but not greater than 85 degrees; or, forward flexion of the cervical spine greater than 30 degrees but not greater than 40 degrees; or, combined range of motion of the thoracolumbar spine greater than 120 degrees but not greater than 235 degrees; or, combined range of motion of the cervical spine greater than 170 degrees but not greater than 335 degrees; or, muscle spasm, guarding, or localized tenderness not resulting in abnormal gait or abnormal spinal contour; or, vertebral body fracture with loss of 50 percent or more of the height — **10**
*Note (1):* Evaluate any associated objective neurologic abnormality, including, but not limited to, bowel or bladder impairment, separately, under an appropriate diagnostic code.

*Note (2):* (See also Plate V.) For VA compensation purposes, normal forward flexion of the cervical spine is zero to 45 degrees, extension is zero to 45 degrees, left and right lateral flexion are zero to 45 degrees, and left and right lateral rotation are zero to 80 degrees. Normal forward flexion of the thoracolumbar spine is zero to 90 degrees, extension is zero to 30 degrees, left and right lateral flexion are zero to 30 degrees, and left and right lateral rotation are zero to 30 degrees. The combined range of motion refers to the sum of the range of forward flexion, extension, left and right lateral flexion, and left and right rotation. The normal combined range of motion of the cervical spine is 340 degrees and of the thoracolumbar spine is 240 degrees. The normal ranges of motion for each component of spinal motion provided in this note are the maximum that can be used for calculation of the combined range of motion.

blocks.text: 4. High-Value Pre-2003 vs. Post-2003 CUE Traps

items: **Pre-2003 `DC 5285` "+10% Demonstrable Deformity" Bonus:** Under former `DC 5285` (prior to Sept. 26, 2003), a veteran with X-ray-confirmed compression fracture / demonstrable deformity of a vertebral body was entitled to **add `10%`** on top of limitation-of-motion ratings—frequently overlooked by RO raters!

**Pre-2003 `DC 5292` (`10%` Slight) vs. `DC 5295` (`0%` Slight Subjective):** Where a pre-2003 exam documented actual limitation of motion of the lumbar spine (`DC 5292`, minimum **`10%`** for *Slight*) and the rater assigned `0%` under `DC 5295` (*"slight subjective symptoms only"*), audit for CUE or failure to maximize!
**See Also:** [VASRD Historical Diff: Spine & Musculoskeletal Joints (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.40, 4.45, 4.59, 4.71a)](/cfr/modules/orthopedic-spine-joints).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Neck & Back Ratings Across Three Eras: Pre-2002 Qualitative Rules, 2002 Disc Rule & Modern Degree Cutoffs
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: How VA rates neck (cervical) and back (thoracolumbar) disabilities under 38 C.F.R. § 4.71a changed dramatically in 2002 and 2003. Before September 23, 2002, VA used Diagnostic Codes 5285–5295 with descriptive labels ('slight', 'moderate', 'severe' limitation of motion, recurring disc attacks, or lumbosacral muscle spasm on extreme bending). On September 23, 2002, VA revised Intervertebral Disc Syndrome (former Diagnostic Code 5293) around physician-prescribed bed rest ('incapacitating episodes'). Then, effective September 26, 2003 (68 FR 51454), VA enacted today's General Rating Formula for Diseases and Injuries of the Spine (Diagnostic Codes 5235–5243; Diagnostic Code 5244 added February 7, 2021), using exact goniometer degree measurements (such as forward back flexion of 30 degrees or less = 40%) PLUS Note (1) requiring separate ratings for objective nerve radiculopathy, bladder, or bowel complications.
record_clues: A post-September 26, 2003 back exam recording thoracolumbar forward flexion of 30 degrees or less (40%), or 35–60 degrees (20%), or muscle spasm causing abnormal gait/spinal contour (20%), where VA assigned a lower percentage.

A post-September 26, 2003 neck or back exam noting radiating nerve pain, numbness, or weakness in the arms or legs (radiculopathy) or neurogenic bladder/bowel symptoms omitted from the Rating Code Sheet despite Note (1).

An older Rating Code Sheet dated before September 26, 2003 showing Diagnostic Codes 5285–5295 (such as Diagnostic Code 5285 for a healed vertebral fracture, which carried an extra 10% for demonstrable deformity).

Confusion on a modern code sheet between legacy Diagnostic Code 5285 (vertebral fracture, retired in 2003) and the brief November 2020–February 2021 Federal Register typo that temporarily printed 5285 before correcting Plantar Fasciitis to Diagnostic Code 5269.
important_cautions: Never mix pre-2003 and post-2003 spine rules: goniometer degree cutoffs (such as <=30 degrees = 40% or <=60 degrees = 20%) took effect September 26, 2003 (published August 27, 2003 at 68 FR 51454) and cannot establish Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) in final decisions issued before September 26, 2003.
Notice the one-year interim disc window: Intervertebral Disc Syndrome bed-rest rules took effect September 23, 2002 (67 FR 54345), one year before the broader September 26, 2003 spine overhaul.

Under Chavis v. McDonough, 'ankylosis' (50%/40%/30%/100% frozen-spine tiers) involves functional or bony fixation of a spinal segment, though later judicial interpretations cannot establish CUE in older final decisions under George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e).
Remember 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c): once the Board of Veterans' Appeals issues a final merits decision on a CUE motion for a specific Board issue, no second CUE motion is allowed on that issue.
questions_for_representative: Which spine rating era governed on the date of my VA decision—pre-September 23, 2002 (Diagnostic Codes 5285–5295), the 2002–2003 disc transition, or the post-September 26, 2003 General Rating Formula (Diagnostic Codes 5235–5244)?
Did my spine examiner test and estimate additional range-of-motion loss during painful flare-ups and repeated weight-bearing movement under DeLuca v. Brown and Correia v. McDonald?
Did VA assign separate peripheral nerve ratings under Note (1) for every affected nerve in my arms or legs, plus any bladder or bowel nerve involvement?

If I have Intervertebral Disc Syndrome, would rating under physician-prescribed bed-rest incapacitating episodes or under the General Rating Formula + nerve radiculopathy yield a higher combined evaluation?

title: Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.75–4.79 The Organs of Special Sense — Eye & Visual Impairment Evolution

Applying the December 10, 2008 eye reorganization (73 FR 66543) retroactively to prove CUE in a final pre-December 10, 2008 decision governed by former §§ 4.75–4.84a

blocks.text: 1. Three-Era Structural Overview (1946–Present)

*Source: `29 FR 6718` (published **May 22, 1964**, codifying the 1945 VASRD effective **April 1, 1946**), verified via `govinfo.gov` (`1996–2008` annual `38 C.F.R.` editions) and `38 C.F.R. Part 4, Appendix A`.*
Prior to December 10, 2008, VA's eye regulations spanned eleven separate sections:

items: **`§ 4.75`** (*Examination of visual acuity*), **`§ 4.76`** (*Examination of field vision*), and **`§ 4.76a`** (*Computation of average concentric contraction of visual fields*).
**`§ 4.77`** (*Examination of muscle function*), **`§ 4.78`** (*Computing aggravation*), and **`§ 4.79`** (*Loss of use of one eye, having only light perception*).

**`§ 4.80`** (*Rating of one eye*), **`§ 4.83`** (*Ratings at scheduled steps and distances*), **`§ 4.83a`** (*Impairment of central visual acuity*), and **`§ 4.84`** (*Differences between distant and near visual acuity*).

**`§ 4.84a`** (*Schedule of ratings—eye*): Contained `DC 6000–6092` and Tables I–V. Acute inflammatory eye conditions (`DC 6000–6009`) were rated qualitatively on active pathology/intercurrent episodes rather than a standardized multi-tier episode formula, and post-lens-removal aphakia (`DC 6029`) carried a minimum `30%` rating (`29 FR 6718`).

blocks.text: Era 2 (2008-12-10 -> 2018-05-12): 73 FR 66543 Reorganization & Bed-Rest Duration Formula
*Enacted at `73 FR 66543` (published **November 10, 2008**, **effective December 10, 2008**).*

Removed `§§ 4.76a, 4.80, 4.83, 4.83a, 4.84, and 4.84a`, consolidated the diagnostic schedule into `38 C.F.R. § 4.79`, codified the modern visual-impairment preface in `§§ 4.75–4.78`, and introduced the **General Rating Formula for Diagnostic Codes 6000 through 6009** tied to total duration of incapacitating episodes (`>=6 weeks = 60%`, `>=4 weeks = 40%`, `>=2 weeks = 20%`, `>=1 week = 10%`), where an incapacitating episode required **prescribed bed rest** and treatment by a physician or other healthcare provider.
Era 3 (2018-05-13 -> present): 83 FR 15316 Clinic-Visit Formula & Modern Retinal/Neuro-Ophthalmic Codes
*Enacted at `83 FR 15316` (published **April 10, 2018**, **effective May 13, 2018**).*

Eliminated the obsolete bed-rest requirement, retitled and expanded the formula to the **General Rating Formula for Diseases of the Eye**, and substituted an objective count of **documented incapacitating episodes requiring treatment visits for an eye condition during the past 12 months** (`7+ = 60%`, `5–6 = 40%`, `3–4 = 20%`, `1–2 = 10%`), while adding dedicated diagnostic codes for Diabetic retinopathy (`DC 6040`), Retinal dystrophy (`DC 6042`), and Post-chiasmal disorders (`DC 6046`).
2. Verbatim Eye Preface: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.75–4.78 (Current Text)

*Source: `ecfr.gov` / `govinfo.gov` (`[73 FR 66549, Nov. 10, 2008]`, with `§§ 4.77–4.78` amended at `[83 FR 15320, Apr. 10, 2018]`). Note that `§ 4.76` consists of paragraphs `(a)` and `(b)(1)–(4)` (there is no paragraph `(c)` in codified `§ 4.76`).*
38 C.F.R. § 4.75 — General Considerations for Evaluating Visual Impairment

lines: **§ 4.75 General considerations for evaluating visual impairment.**
**(a) Visual impairment.** The evaluation of visual impairment is based on impairment of visual acuity (excluding developmental errors of refraction), visual field, and muscle function.

**(b) Examination for visual impairment.** The examination must be conducted by a licensed optometrist or by a licensed ophthalmologist. The examiner must identify the disease, injury, or other pathologic process responsible for any visual impairment found. Examinations of visual fields or muscle function will be conducted only when there is a medical indication of disease or injury that may be associated with visual field defect or impaired muscle function. Unless medically contraindicated, the fundus must be examined with the claimant's pupils dilated.

**(c) Service-connected visual impairment of only one eye.** Subject to the provisions of 38 CFR 3.383(a), if visual impairment of only one eye is service-connected, the visual acuity of the other eye will be considered to be 20/40 for purposes of evaluating the service-connected visual impairment.

**(d) Maximum evaluation for visual impairment of one eye.** The evaluation for visual impairment of one eye must not exceed 30 percent unless there is anatomical loss of the eye. Combine the evaluation for visual impairment of one eye with evaluations for other disabilities of the same eye that are not based on visual impairment (e.g., disfigurement under diagnostic code 7800).

**(e) Anatomical loss of one eye with inability to wear a prosthesis.** When the claimant has anatomical loss of one eye and is unable to wear a prosthesis, increase the evaluation for visual acuity under diagnostic code 6063 by 10 percent, but the maximum evaluation for visual impairment of both eyes must not exceed 100 percent. A 10-percent increase under this paragraph precludes an evaluation under diagnostic code 7800 based on gross distortion or asymmetry of the eye but not an evaluation under diagnostic code 7800 based on other characteristics of disfigurement.

**(f) Special monthly compensation.** When evaluating visual impairment, refer to 38 CFR 3.350 to determine whether the claimant may be entitled to special monthly compensation. Footnotes in the schedule indicate levels of visual impairment that potentially establish entitlement to special monthly compensation; however, other levels of visual impairment combined with disabilities of other body systems may also establish entitlement.
*(Authority: 38 U.S.C. 1114 and 1155)*

blocks.text: 38 C.F.R. § 4.76 — Visual Acuity (>3 Diopters Anisometropia & Near-Vision Rules)

lines: **§ 4.76 Visual acuity.**

**(a) Examination of visual acuity.** Examination of visual acuity must include the central uncorrected and corrected visual acuity for distance and near vision using Snellen's test type or its equivalent.

**(b) Evaluation of visual acuity.** (1) Evaluate central visual acuity on the basis of corrected distance vision with central fixation, even if a central scotoma is present. However, when the lens required to correct distance vision in the poorer eye differs by more than three diopters from the lens required to correct distance vision in the better eye (and the difference is not due to congenital or developmental refractive error), and either the poorer eye or both eyes are service connected, evaluate the visual acuity of the poorer eye using either its uncorrected or corrected visual acuity, whichever results in better combined visual acuity.

(2) Provided that he or she customarily wears contact lenses, evaluate the visual acuity of any individual affected by a corneal disorder that results in severe irregular astigmatism that can be improved more by contact lenses than by eyeglass lenses, as corrected by contact lenses.

(3) In any case where the examiner reports that there is a difference equal to two or more scheduled steps between near and distance corrected vision, with the near vision being worse, the examination report must include at least two recordings of near and distance corrected vision and an explanation of the reason for the difference. In these cases, evaluate based on corrected distance vision adjusted to one step poorer than measured.

(4) To evaluate the impairment of visual acuity where a claimant has a reported visual acuity that is between two sequentially listed visual acuities, use the visual acuity which permits the higher evaluation.
*(Authority: 38 U.S.C. 1155)*

blocks.text: 38 C.F.R. § 4.77 — Visual Fields

lines: **§ 4.77 Visual fields.**

**(a) Examination of visual fields.** Examiners must use either Goldmann kinetic perimetry or automated perimetry using Humphrey Model 750, Octopus Model 101, or later versions of these perimetric devices with simulated kinetic Goldmann testing capability. For phakic (normal) individuals, as well as for pseudophakic or aphakic individuals who are well adapted to intraocular lens implant or contact lens correction, visual field examinations must be conducted using a standard target size and luminance, which is Goldmann's equivalent III/4e. For aphakic individuals not well adapted to contact lens correction or pseudophakic individuals not well adapted to intraocular lens implant, visual field examinations must be conducted using Goldmann's equivalent IV/4e. The examiner must document the results for at least 16 meridians 22 1/2 degrees apart for each eye and indicate the Goldmann equivalent used. See Table III for the normal extent (in degrees) of the visual fields at the 8 principal meridians (45 degrees apart). When the examiner indicates that additional testing is necessary to evaluate visual fields, the additional testing must be conducted using either a tangent screen or a 30-degree threshold visual field with the Goldmann III stimulus size. The examination report must document the results of either the tangent screen or of the 30-degree threshold visual field with the Goldmann III stimulus size.

**(b) Evaluation of visual fields.** Determine the average concentric contraction of the visual field of each eye by measuring the remaining visual field (in degrees) at each of eight principal meridians 45 degrees apart, adding them, and dividing the sum by eight.

**(c) Combination of visual field defect and decreased visual acuity.** To determine the evaluation for visual impairment when both decreased visual acuity and visual field defect are present in one or both eyes and are service connected, separately evaluate the visual acuity and visual field defect (expressed as a level of visual acuity), and combine them under the provisions of § 4.25.
*(Authority: 38 U.S.C. 1155)*

blocks.text: 38 C.F.R. § 4.78 — Muscle Function (Diplopia Step Adjustments)

lines: **§ 4.78 Muscle function.**

**(a) Examination of muscle function.** The examiner must use a Goldmann perimeter chart or the Tangent Screen method that identifies the four major quadrants (upward, downward, left, and right lateral) and the central field (20 degrees or less) (see Figure 2). The examiner must document the results of muscle function testing by identifying the quadrant(s) and range(s) of degrees in which diplopia exists.

**(b) Evaluation of muscle function.** (1) An evaluation for diplopia will be assigned to only one eye. When a claimant has both diplopia and decreased visual acuity or visual field defect, assign a level of corrected visual acuity for the poorer eye (or the affected eye, if disability of only one eye is service-connected) that is: one step poorer than it would otherwise warrant if the evaluation for diplopia under diagnostic code 6090 is 20/70 or 20/100; two steps poorer if the evaluation under diagnostic code 6090 is 20/200 or 15/200; or three steps poorer if the evaluation under diagnostic code 6090 is 5/200. This adjusted level of corrected visual acuity, however, must not exceed a level of 5/200. Use the adjusted visual acuity for the poorer eye (or the affected eye, if disability of only one eye is service-connected), and the corrected visual acuity for the better eye (or visual acuity of 20/40 for the other eye, if only one eye is service-connected) to determine the percentage evaluation for visual impairment under diagnostic codes 6065 through 6066.
(2) When diplopia extends beyond more than one quadrant or range of degrees, evaluate diplopia based on the quadrant and degree range that provides the highest evaluation.
(3) When diplopia exists in two separate areas of the same eye, increase the equivalent visual acuity under diagnostic code 6090 to the next poorer level of visual acuity, not to exceed 5/200.
*(Authority: 38 U.S.C. 1155)*

Era 2 (2008-12-10 -> 2018-05-12): Duration & Bed-Rest Formula (73 FR 66543)
*Enacted at `73 FR 66543, 66550` (published **November 10, 2008**, **effective December 10, 2008**); verified from `govinfo.gov` (`2009–2017` `38 C.F.R. § 4.79` editions).*

lines: **General Rating Formula for Diagnostic Codes 6000 through 6009**
Evaluate on the basis of either visual impairment due to the particular condition or on incapacitating episodes, whichever results in a higher evaluation.
* With incapacitating episodes having a total duration of at least 6 weeks during the past 12 months — **60**
* With incapacitating episodes having a total duration of at least 4 weeks, but less than 6 weeks, during the past 12 months — **40**
* With incapacitating episodes having a total duration of at least 2 weeks, but less than 4 weeks, during the past 12 months — **20**
* With incapacitating episodes having a total duration of at least 1 week, but less than 2 weeks, during the past 12 months — **10**
**Note:** For VA purposes, an incapacitating episode is a period of acute symptoms severe enough to require prescribed bed rest and treatment by a physician or other healthcare provider.

blocks.text: Era 3 (2018-05-13 -> present): Clinic-Treatment-Visit Formula (83 FR 15316)
*Enacted at `83 FR 15316, 15321` (published **April 10, 2018**, **effective May 13, 2018**); verified word-for-word from `ecfr.gov` (`38 C.F.R. § 4.79`).*

lines: **General Rating Formula for Diseases of the Eye**
Evaluate on the basis of either visual impairment due to the particular condition or on incapacitating episodes, whichever results in a higher evaluation.
* With documented incapacitating episodes requiring 7 or more treatment visits for an eye condition during the past 12 months — **60**
* With documented incapacitating episodes requiring at least 5 but less than 7 treatment visits for an eye condition during the past 12 months — **40**
* With documented incapacitating episodes requiring at least 3 but less than 5 treatment visits for an eye condition during the past 12 months — **20**
* With documented incapacitating episodes requiring at least 1 but less than 3 treatment visits for an eye condition during the past 12 months — **10**

**Note (1):** For the purposes of evaluation under 38 CFR 4.79, an incapacitating episode is an eye condition severe enough to require a clinic visit to a provider specifically for treatment purposes.

**Note (2):** Examples of treatment may include but are not limited to: Systemic immunosuppressants or biologic agents; intravitreal or periocular injections; laser treatments; or other surgical interventions.
**Note (3):** For the purposes of evaluating visual impairment due to the particular condition, refer to 38 CFR 4.75–4.78 and to § 4.79, diagnostic codes 6061–6091.

lines: **QUARANTINE — RESCINDED INTERIM FINAL RULE (`91 FR 7118`, Feb. 17, 2026 -> Rescinded `91 FR 9712`, Feb. 27, 2026):**

Following *Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)`, VA briefly issued an Interim Final Rule on February 17, 2026 (`91 FR 7118`) attempting to amend `38 C.F.R. § 4.10` to evaluate disabilities as ameliorated by medication, before **rescinding that Interim Final Rule on February 27, 2026 (`91 FR 9712`)**. Practitioners must **never** cite `91 FR 7118` as active law, while noting that `DC 6012` (Angle-closure glaucoma) and `DC 6013` (Open-angle glaucoma) independently codify an explicit `10%` minimum floor whenever continuous medication is required.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Eye & Vision Regulations (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.75–4.79): Comparing the 2008 & May 13, 2018 Rating Schedules
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: VA's eye and vision schedule (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.75–4.79) evaluates vision loss across three dimensions—central visual acuity, visual fields (peripheral vision), and eye muscle function (double vision / diplopia)—plus active eye diseases. VA overhauled these regulations twice: first effective December 10, 2008 (73 FR 66543, standardizing Goldmann/Humphrey visual field charts and rating flare-ups by prescribed bed-rest duration), and again effective May 13, 2018 (83 FR 15316, redefining 'incapacitating episodes' around clinic visits specifically for active treatment—such as eye injections or laser therapy—rather than bed rest, and adding dedicated codes like Diagnostic Code 6040 Diabetic Retinopathy and Diagnostic Code 6042 Retinal Dystrophy).
record_clues: A post-May 13, 2018 eye rating of 0% or 10% based on reading an eye chart when ophthalmology records show repeated clinic visits for active treatment (such as anti-VEGF eye injections, laser procedures, or biologics: 1–2 visits = 10%, 3–4 = 20%, 5–6 = 40%, 7+ = 60% in 12 months).

A unilateral service-connected eye rating where the non-service-connected eye was NOT assigned the standard 20/40 baseline (§ 4.75(c))—or where severe vision loss in the non-service-connected eye (<=20/200 acuity or <=20 degrees peripheral field) should have triggered full bilateral 'paired-organ' compensation under 38 U.S.C. § 1160(a)(1) and 38 C.F.R. § 3.383(a)(1).

An optometry refraction showing more than 3.0 diopters difference in lens strength between the two eyes (acquired anisometropia) where VA rated the poorer eye on corrected rather than uncorrected vision (§ 4.76(b)(1)).
Blindness of one eye (light perception only or anatomical loss) or concentric field contraction to 5 degrees or less adjudicated without Special Monthly Compensation (SMC(k) or SMC(l)–(o)).
important_cautions: Strict effective dates govern historical eye reviews: the clinic-treatment-visit formula took effect May 13, 2018 (published April 10, 2018 at 83 FR 15316), and the modernized acuity/field reorganization took effect December 10, 2008 (published November 10, 2008 at 73 FR 66543). Neither rule can prove Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) in final decisions issued before its effective date.

Post-cataract lens implants vs. true aphakia: when an intraocular lens implant (pseudophakia) is placed during cataract surgery, the condition is rated under Diagnostic Code 6027 rather than the 30% minimum aphakia rule of Diagnostic Code 6029 (which applies when the natural lens is absent without replacement).
Routine monitoring or eyeglass refraction checkups where no active treatment is rendered or prescribed do not count as 'incapacitating episodes' under § 4.79 Note (1).

VA's February 17, 2026 § 4.10 medication rule (91 FR 7118) was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712) and is not active law. Also remember 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c) allows only one final merits CUE decision per prior Board issue.
questions_for_representative: Over the past 12 months, how many ophthalmology clinic visits specifically provided active treatment (such as injections, laser therapy, or prescribed acute flare treatment) under the post-May 13, 2018 General Rating Formula?

If I have vision loss in one service-connected eye and severe non-service-connected vision loss in my other eye, do I qualify for paired-organ bilateral compensation under 38 U.S.C. § 1160(a)(1) and 38 C.F.R. § 3.383(a)(1)?
Does my eyeglass prescription show more than a 3.0-diopter difference between my eyes requiring uncorrected acuity rating under 38 C.F.R. § 4.76(b)(1)?
Have we checked Special Monthly Compensation (SMC(k) or SMC(l)–(o)) and Specially Adapted Housing / Automobile grants for severe visual acuity or visual-field loss?

rows: `29 FR 6718` (`38 C.F.R. Part 4, App. A`; Tables amended `41 FR 11292` & `43 FR 45348`)
Evaluated hearing acuity via spoken-voice whisper/conversational distance tests (and early audiometric conversion tables); ear diseases and `DC 6260` housed in `former § 4.84b`.

Replaced spoken-voice tests with state-licensed audiologist **Maryland CNC** speech discrimination + `1000/2000/3000/4000 Hz` puretone threshold average and new **Tables VI, VIA, and VII** (`DC 6100`); redesignated ear schedule from `§ 4.84b` to `former § 4.87a`.

**1999 Ear Schedule Reorganization, `§ 4.86` Exceptional Patterns & `DC 6260` Era 2**

Added **`§ 4.86(a)–(b)`** exceptional hearing patterns; moved `DC 6200–6260` from `former § 4.87a` to **`§ 4.87`**; liberalized `DC 6260` to **`Tinnitus, recurrent — 10`** regardless of trauma etiology and added `Note (1)` (separate evaluation) and `Note (2)` (objective tinnitus exclusion) (`§ 3.114(a)` floor **June 10, 1999**).

blocks.text: 1. Verbatim Threshold Definition: 38 C.F.R. § 3.385

*Source: `ecfr.gov` / `govinfo.gov` (`[59 FR 60560, Nov. 25, 1994]`, **effective December 27, 1994**; originally promulgated at `55 FR 12348`, Apr. 3, 1990, effective May 3, 1990). Note that `§ 3.385` includes **`500 Hz`** for establishing service-connected disability, whereas `§ 4.85(d)` uses only `1000, 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hz` for rating percentage calculation—meaning a veteran meeting `§ 3.385` is entitled to service connection even when Table VII yields a `0%` noncompensable evaluation under `DC 6100`.*

lines: **§ 3.385 Disability due to impaired hearing.**

For the purposes of applying the laws administered by VA, impaired hearing will be considered to be a disability when the auditory threshold in any of the frequencies 500, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000 Hertz is 40 decibels or greater; or when the auditory thresholds for at least three of the frequencies 500, 1000, 2000, 3000, or 4000 Hertz are 26 decibels or greater; or when speech recognition scores using the Maryland CNC Test are less than 94 percent.

blocks.text: 2. Verbatim Hearing Evaluation Rules: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.85 & 4.86

*Source: `ecfr.gov` / `govinfo.gov` (`[64 FR 25206, 25209, May 11, 1999]`, **effective June 10, 1999**, revising the audiometric framework enacted at `[52 FR 44117, Nov. 18, 1987]`, **effective December 18, 1987**).*
38 C.F.R. § 4.85 — Evaluation of Hearing Impairment (DC 6100)

lines: **§ 4.85 Evaluation of hearing impairment.**

**(a)** An examination for hearing impairment for VA purposes must be conducted by a state-licensed audiologist and must include a controlled speech discrimination test (Maryland CNC) and a puretone audiometry test. Examinations will be conducted without the use of hearing aids.

**(b)** Table VI, “Numeric Designation of Hearing Impairment Based on Puretone Threshold Average and Speech Discrimination,” is used to determine a Roman numeral designation (I through XI) for hearing impairment based on a combination of the percent of speech discrimination (horizontal rows) and the puretone threshold average (vertical columns). The Roman numeral designation is located at the point where the percentage of speech discrimination and puretone threshold average intersect.

**(c)** Table VIa, “Numeric Designation of Hearing Impairment Based Only on Puretone Threshold Average,” is used to determine a Roman numeral designation (I through XI) for hearing impairment based only on the puretone threshold average. Table VIa will be used when the examiner certifies that use of the speech discrimination test is not appropriate because of language difficulties, inconsistent speech discrimination scores, etc., or when indicated under the provisions of § 4.86.

**(d)** “Puretone threshold average,” as used in Tables VI and VIa, is the sum of the puretone thresholds at 1000, 2000, 3000 and 4000 Hertz, divided by four. This average is used in all cases (including those in § 4.86) to determine the Roman numeral designation for hearing impairment from Table VI or VIa.

**(e)** Table VII, “Percentage Evaluations for Hearing Impairment,” is used to determine the percentage evaluation by combining the Roman numeral designations for hearing impairment of each ear. The horizontal rows represent the ear having the better hearing and the vertical columns the ear having the poorer hearing. The percentage evaluation is located at the point where the row and column intersect.

**(f)** If impaired hearing is service-connected in only one ear, in order to determine the percentage evaluation from Table VII, the non-service-connected ear will be assigned a Roman Numeral designation for hearing impairment of I, subject to the provisions of § 3.383 of this chapter.

**(g)** When evaluating any claim for impaired hearing, refer to § 3.350 of this chapter to determine whether the veteran may be entitled to special monthly compensation due either to deafness, or to deafness in combination with other specified disabilities.
**(h)** Numeric tables VI, VIA*, and VII.

blocks.text: Reference Structure of Tables VI, VIA & VII (§ 4.85(h), DC 6100)

items: **Table VI (*Numeric Designation of Hearing Impairment Based on Puretone Threshold Average and Speech Discrimination*):** Intersects speech discrimination rows (`92–100%`, `84–90%`, `76–82%`, `68–74%`, `60–66%`, `52–58%`, `44–50%`, `36–42%`, `0–34%`) with puretone threshold average columns (`0–41`, `42–49`, `50–57`, `58–65`, `66–73`, `74–81`, `82–89`, `90–97`, `98+` dB) to yield Roman numerals **`I` through `XI`** for each ear.

**Table VIA (*Numeric Designation of Hearing Impairment Based Only on Puretone Threshold Average*):** Maps puretone threshold average (`1000–4000 Hz` mean) directly to Roman numerals **`I` through `XI`** (`0–41 = I`, `42–48 = II`, `49–55 = III`, `56–62 = IV`, `63–69 = V`, `70–76 = VI`, `77–83 = VII`, `84–90 = VIII`, `91–97 = IX`, `98–104 = X`, `105+ = XI`).

**Table VII (*Percentage Evaluations for Hearing Impairment (Diagnostic Code 6100)*):** Intersects the better-ear Roman numeral (`I–XI`) with the poorer-ear Roman numeral (`I–XI`) to assign a single schedular rating from **`0%` to `100%`** (e.g., when the better ear is `I`: **`I + I–IX = 0%`** and **`I + X–XI = 10%`**; `II + V–XI = 10%`; `XI + XI = 100%*`, with footnote referral to `38 C.F.R. § 3.350` for Special Monthly Compensation).

blocks.text: 38 C.F.R. § 4.86 — Exceptional Patterns of Hearing Impairment

lines: **§ 4.86 Exceptional patterns of hearing impairment.**

**(a)** When the puretone threshold at each of the four specified frequencies (1000, 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hertz) is 55 decibels or more, the rating specialist will determine the Roman numeral designation for hearing impairment from either Table VI or Table VIa, whichever results in the higher numeral. Each ear will be evaluated separately.

**(b)** When the puretone threshold is 30 decibels or less at 1000 Hertz, and 70 decibels or more at 2000 Hertz, the rating specialist will determine the Roman numeral designation for hearing impairment from either Table VI or Table VIa, whichever results in the higher numeral. That numeral will then be elevated to the next higher Roman numeral. Each ear will be evaluated separately.
*(Authority: 38 U.S.C. 1155)*

blocks.text: 3. Three-Era Verbatim Evolution: DC 6260 (Tinnitus)
Era 1 (1946-04-01 -> 1999-06-09): Trauma/Concussion Etiology Restriction (former § 4.84b / former § 4.87a)

*Source: `29 FR 6718` (May 22, 1964), redesignated from `§ 4.84b` to `§ 4.87a` at `52 FR 44117` (Nov. 18, 1987, effective Dec. 18, 1987); verified from `govinfo.gov` (`1996–1998` `38 C.F.R. § 4.87a` editions) and `VAOPGCPREC 2-2003`.*

lines: **6260 Tinnitus:**
Persistent as a symptom of head injury, concussion or acoustic trauma — **10**

blocks.text: Era 2 (1999-06-10 -> 2003-06-12): Liberalized *"Tinnitus, Recurrent"* (Notes (1)–(2), 64 FR 25202)

*Enacted at `64 FR 25202, 25210` (published **May 11, 1999**, **effective June 10, 1999**; redesignated to `38 C.F.R. § 4.87`). Removed the head-injury/concussion/acoustic-trauma etiology restriction (`38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)` liberalizing floor **June 10, 1999**) and enacted `Note (1)` (separate evaluation) and `Note (2)` (objective tinnitus exclusion). Although the explicit single-evaluation note did not yet appear in the text, in **Smith v. Nicholson**, `451 F.3d 1344 (Fed. Cir. 2006)`, the Federal Circuit upheld **`VAOPGCPREC 2-2003`** (May 22, 2003), holding that both pre-1999 and 1999–2003 `DC 6260` authorized only a **single `10%` evaluation** regardless of whether tinnitus was bilateral.*

lines: **6260 Tinnitus, recurrent** — **10**

**Note (1):** A separate evaluation for tinnitus may be combined with an evaluation under diagnostic codes 6100, 6200, 6204, or other diagnostic code, except when tinnitus supports an evaluation under one of those diagnostic codes.

**Note (2):** Do not evaluate objective tinnitus (in which the sound is audible to other people and has a definable cause that may or may not be pathologic) under this diagnostic code, but evaluate it as part of any underlying condition causing it.

blocks.text: Era 3 (2003-06-13 -> present): Explicit Single-Evaluation & Objective-Tinnitus Notes (68 FR 25822)
*Enacted at `68 FR 25822, 25823` (published **May 14, 2003**, **effective June 13, 2003**); verified word-for-word from `ecfr.gov` (`38 C.F.R. § 4.87`).*

lines: **6260 Tinnitus, recurrent** — **10**

**Note (1):** A separate evaluation for tinnitus may be combined with an evaluation under diagnostic codes 6100, 6200, 6204, or other diagnostic code, except when tinnitus supports an evaluation under one of those diagnostic codes.
**Note (2):** Assign only a single evaluation for recurrent tinnitus, whether the sound is perceived in one ear, both ears, or in the head.

**Note (3):** Do not evaluate objective tinnitus (in which the sound is audible to other people and has a definable cause that may or may not be pathologic) under this diagnostic code, but evaluate it as part of any underlying condition causing it.

blocks.text: 4. Verbatim 38 C.F.R. § 4.87: Key Ear & Vestibular Diagnostic Codes (DC 6200–6211)

*Source: `ecfr.gov` / `govinfo.gov` (`[64 FR 25210, May 11, 1999]`, **effective June 10, 1999**, as amended at `[68 FR 25823, May 14, 2003]`). Under `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a)`, complete loss of both auricles (`DC 6207`) also warrants review for Special Monthly Compensation (`SMC(k)` / `§ 3.350`).*

lines: **§ 4.87 Schedule of ratings—ear.**
**Diseases of the Ear**
* **6200 Chronic suppurative otitis media, mastoiditis, or cholesteatoma (or any combination):**
* During suppuration, or with aural polyps — **10**
* *Note:* Evaluate hearing impairment, and complications such as labyrinthitis, tinnitus, facial nerve paralysis, or bone loss of skull, separately.
* **6201 Chronic nonsuppurative otitis media with effusion (serous otitis media):** Rate hearing impairment.
* **6202 Otosclerosis:** Rate hearing impairment.
* **6204 Peripheral vestibular disorders:**
* Dizziness and occasional staggering — **30**
* Occasional dizziness — **10**

* *Note:* Objective findings supporting the diagnosis of vestibular disequilibrium are required before a compensable evaluation can be assigned under this code. Hearing impairment or suppuration shall be separately rated and combined.
* **6205 Meniere's syndrome (endolymphatic hydrops):**
* Hearing impairment with attacks of vertigo and cerebellar gait occurring more than once weekly, with or without tinnitus — **100**
* Hearing impairment with attacks of vertigo and cerebellar gait occurring from one to four times a month, with or without tinnitus — **60**
* Hearing impairment with vertigo less than once a month, with or without tinnitus — **30**

* *Note:* Evaluate Meniere's syndrome either under these criteria or by separately evaluating vertigo (as a peripheral vestibular disorder), hearing impairment, and tinnitus, whichever method results in a higher overall evaluation. But do not combine an evaluation for hearing impairment, tinnitus, or vertigo with an evaluation under diagnostic code 6205.
* **6207 Loss of auricle:**
* Complete loss of both $^{1}$ — **50**
* Complete loss of one — **30**
* Deformity of one, with loss of one-third or more of the substance — **10**
* **6208 Malignant neoplasm of the ear (other than skin only)** — **100**

* *Note:* A rating of 100 percent shall continue beyond the cessation of any surgical, radiation treatment, antineoplastic chemotherapy or other therapeutic procedure. Six months after discontinuance of such treatment, the appropriate disability rating shall be determined by mandatory VA examination. Any change in evaluation based on that or any subsequent examination shall be subject to the provisions of § 3.105(e) of this chapter. If there has been no local recurrence or metastasis, rate on residuals.
* **6209 Benign neoplasms of the ear (other than skin only):** Rate on impairment of function.
* **6210 Chronic otitis externa:**
* Swelling, dry and scaly or serous discharge, and itching requiring frequent and prolonged treatment — **10**
* **6211 Tympanic membrane, perforation of** — **0**
$^{1}$ Review for entitlement to special monthly compensation under § 3.350 of this chapter.

blocks.text: 5. Quarantine Warning: Unfinalized Proposed Rule RIN 2900-AQ72 (87 FR 8474)

lines: **QUARANTINE — PROPOSED / NOT FINALIZED (`RIN 2900-AQ72`, `87 FR 8474`, Feb. 15, 2022):**

On February 15, 2022 (`87 FR 8474`), VA published a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (*Schedule for Rating Disabilities—Ear, Nose, Throat, and Audiology Disabilities; Special Provisions Regarding Evaluation of Respiratory Conditions; Schedule for Rating Disabilities—Respiratory System*, `RIN 2900-AQ72`) proposing to eliminate standalone `10%` service connection and evaluation for recurrent tinnitus under `DC 6260` and instead evaluate tinnitus solely as a symptom of an underlying service-connected pathology. **As of late 2026, `RIN 2900-AQ72` remains an unfinalized proposed rule with no published Final Rule or enacted effective date.** Practitioners and AI agents must **never** cite `87 FR 8474` as active law; `38 C.F.R. § 4.87`, `DC 6260` (`10%` standalone evaluation) remains fully in force.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Hearing Loss, Vestibular Balance & Tinnitus Regulations (38 C.F.R. §§ 3.385 & 4.85–4.87) Across Eras
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: VA evaluates hearing loss mechanically using two measurements from a licensed audiologist's exam: controlled Maryland CNC 50-word speech recognition and puretone decibel averages across 1000, 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hz (introduced December 18, 1987). Effective June 10, 1999 (64 FR 25202), VA added two critical 'exceptional hearing pattern' rules in 38 C.F.R. § 4.86(a)–(b) that allow puretone-only Table VIa when high-frequency drop-offs mask severe real-world hearing difficulty, updated Meniere's syndrome (Diagnostic Code 6205) and vestibular dizziness (Diagnostic Code 6204), and broadened recurrent tinnitus (Diagnostic Code 6260) beyond head injury or acoustic trauma—before clarifying on June 13, 2003 that recurrent tinnitus receives a single 10% evaluation whether heard in one or both ears.
record_clues: An audiogram meeting VA's disability threshold in 38 C.F.R. § 3.385 (such as >=40 dB at any frequency 500–4000 Hz, >=26 dB at three or more frequencies, or <94% speech recognition) that VA denied outright instead of granting at least 0% service connection.

A post-June 10, 1999 audiogram showing >=55 dB loss at ALL FOUR frequencies (1000, 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hz) [§ 4.86(a)], OR <=30 dB at 1000 Hz with >=70 dB at 2000 Hz [§ 4.86(b)], where VA used Table VI instead of checking Table VIa (including the +1 Roman numeral step-up under § 4.86(b)).
A pre-June 10, 1999 tinnitus denial because the ringing did not stem from a specific concussion, head injury, or single acoustic trauma.

Meniere's syndrome (Diagnostic Code 6205) rated at 30% without checking whether separate ratings for vertigo (Diagnostic Code 6204), hearing loss (Diagnostic Code 6100), and tinnitus (Diagnostic Code 6260) produce a higher combined evaluation.
important_cautions: Single 10% cap on recurrent tinnitus in every era: under Note (2) to Diagnostic Code 6260 (effective June 13, 2003) and the Federal Circuit's decision in Smith v. Nicholson (2006, upholding VAOPGCPREC 2-2003 for pre-2003 claims), VA assigns only ONE 10% rating for recurrent tinnitus regardless of whether ringing is perceived in one ear, both ears, or the head.

Anti-pyramiding rule for Meniere's syndrome: VA must award WHICHEVER method is higher—either Diagnostic Code 6205 (30%/60%/100%) OR separate ratings for hearing loss, vertigo, and tinnitus—never both stacked together.

June 10, 1999 date cutoff: the exceptional hearing pattern rules in 38 C.F.R. § 4.86(a)–(b) took effect June 10, 1999 (published May 11, 1999 at 64 FR 25202) and cannot prove Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) in final decisions issued before June 10, 1999.

Rumored tinnitus changes are NOT law: VA's February 15, 2022 audiology notice (RIN 2900-AQ72, 87 FR 8474, proposing to eliminate standalone 10% tinnitus) remains a proposed, unfinalized rule and is not enacted law. Also remember 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c) allows only one final merits CUE decision per prior Board issue.
questions_for_representative: Can we check my audiogram decibel numbers at 1000, 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hz to see if I qualify for Table VIa exceptional hearing patterns under 38 C.F.R. § 4.86(a) or (b)?

If my audiogram met 38 C.F.R. § 3.385 thresholds (or my separation exam showed an acoustic shift before crossing § 3.385 under Hensley v. Brown), should service connection be established even if Table VII initially yields 0%?
If I have Meniere's disease, have we compared the single Diagnostic Code 6205 rating against separate ratings for vertigo, hearing loss, and tinnitus?
Do my tinnitus or hearing symptoms cause secondary sleep disturbance, migraines, depression, or anxiety under 38 C.F.R. § 3.310?

rows: Redesignated former `§ 4.88a` as `§ 4.88b` (and former `§ 4.88b` as `§ 4.88c`), added `§ 4.88a` codifying VA's diagnostic criteria for Chronic Fatigue Syndrome, and added `DC 6354` (`100/60/40/20/10%`).

Revised `§ 4.88b` (`DC 6300–6354`), including `DC 6304` Malaria (permitting endemic clinical diagnosis initially, blood smears on relapse), `DC 6309` Rheumatic fever, `DC 6313–6315` Avitaminosis/Beriberi/Pellagra, newly added `DC 6319` Lyme disease, `DC 6350` Lupus (`100/60/10%` + higher-of-residuals Note), conjunctive `10%` `DC 6351` HIV tier, and `DC 6354` CFS Note defining incapacitation.

Enacted the **General Rating Formula for Infectious Diseases** (`100%` active -> `0%` resolved + mandatory residual ratings across body systems), updated `DC 6304` (modern antigen/PCR diagnostics), `DC 6309`, `DC 6319` (explicit Bell's palsy, radiculopathy, ocular, cognitive residuals), and `DC 6351` HIV (making `10%` prongs disjunctive — e.g., `"use of approved medication(s)"` alone — and adding `Note 3` AIDS-defining opportunistic infections). **Archival Withdrawal Note:** VA expressly withdrew the Feb. 5, 2019 NPRM (`84 FR 1678`) proposal to rename/restrict `DC 6354` CFS, preserving the substantive `DC 6354` criteria intact.

blocks.text: 1. Verbatim 38 C.F.R. § 4.88a & § 4.88b DC 6354: Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (1994–Present)

*Source: `ecfr.gov` / `govinfo.gov` (`38 C.F.R. § 4.88a`, added at `59 FR 60902`, Nov. 29, 1994; `38 C.F.R. § 4.88b`, `DC 6354`, added at `59 FR 60902`, amended at `61 FR 39875`, eff. Aug. 30, 1996, and formatting/heading retained at `84 FR 28227`, eff. Aug. 11, 2019).*
38 C.F.R. § 4.88a — Diagnostic Criteria for Chronic Fatigue Syndrome

lines: **§ 4.88a Chronic fatigue syndrome.**
**(a)** For VA purposes, the diagnosis of chronic fatigue syndrome requires:
**(1)** new onset of debilitating fatigue severe enough to reduce daily activity to less than 50 percent of the usual level for at least six months; and
**(2)** the exclusion, by history, physical examination, and laboratory tests, of all other clinical conditions that may produce similar symptoms; and
**(3)** six or more of the following:
* **(i)** acute onset of the condition,
* **(ii)** low grade fever,
* **(iii)** nonexudative pharyngitis,
* **(iv)** palpable or tender cervical or axillary lymph nodes,
* **(v)** generalized muscle aches or weakness,
* **(vi)** fatigue lasting 24 hours or longer after exercise,
* **(vii)** headaches (of a type, severity, or pattern that is different from headaches in the pre-morbid state),
* **(viii)** migratory joint pains,
* **(ix)** neuropsychologic symptoms,
* **(x)** sleep disturbance.
**(b)** [Reserved]

blocks.text: 38 C.F.R. § 4.88b, DC 6354 — Evaluation Criteria for Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (CFS)

lines: **6354 Chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS):**
Debilitating fatigue, cognitive impairments (such as inability to concentrate, forgetfulness, or confusion), or a combination of other signs and symptoms:
* Which are nearly constant and so severe as to restrict routine daily activities almost completely and which may occasionally preclude self-care — **100**

* Which are nearly constant and restrict routine daily activities to less than 50 percent of the pre-illness level; or which wax and wane, resulting in periods of incapacitation of at least six weeks total duration per year — **60**

* Which are nearly constant and restrict routine daily activities from 50 to 75 percent of the pre-illness level; or which wax and wane, resulting in periods of incapacitation of at least four but less than six weeks total duration per year — **40**

* Which are nearly constant and restrict routine daily activities by less than 25 percent of the pre-illness level; or which wax and wane, resulting in periods of incapacitation of at least two but less than four weeks total duration per year — **20**
* Which wax and wane but result in periods of incapacitation of at least one but less than two weeks total duration per year; or symptoms controlled by continuous medication — **10**
**Note:** For the purpose of evaluating this disability, incapacitation exists only when a licensed physician prescribes bed rest and treatment.

blocks.text: 2. Era 1 Verbatim Text: August 30, 1996 – August 10, 2019 (61 FR 39875)

*Source: `61 FR 39873, 39875` (published **July 31, 1996**, **effective August 30, 1996**); verified word-for-word from `govinfo.gov` (`2018` `38 C.F.R. § 4.88b` edition). Note that `DC 6313–6315` and `DC 6350` were unchanged in substance by the August 11, 2019 rule and appear in full in Section 3 below.*

lines: **6304 Malaria:**
* As active disease — **100**

* **Note:** The diagnosis of malaria depends on the identification of the malarial parasites in blood smears. If the veteran served in an endemic area and presents signs and symptoms compatible with malaria, the diagnosis may be based on clinical grounds alone. Relapses must be confirmed by the presence of malarial parasites in blood smears.
* Thereafter rate residuals such as liver or spleen damage under the appropriate system.
**6309 Rheumatic fever:**
* As active disease — **100**
* Thereafter rate residuals such as heart damage under the appropriate system.
**6319 Lyme disease:**
* As active disease — **100**
* Thereafter rate residuals such as arthritis under the appropriate system.
**6351 HIV-Related Illness:**

* AIDS with recurrent opportunistic infections or with secondary diseases afflicting multiple body systems; HIV-related illness with debility and progressive weight loss, without remission, or few or brief remissions — **100**
* Refractory constitutional symptoms, diarrhea, and pathological weight loss, or; minimum rating following development of AIDS-related opportunistic infection or neoplasm — **60**
* Recurrent constitutional symptoms, intermittent diarrhea, and on approved medication(s), or; minimum rating with T4 cell count less than 200, or Hairy Cell Leukoplakia, or Oral Candidiasis — **30**

* Following development of definite medical symptoms, T4 cell of 200 or more and less than 500, and on approved medication(s), or; with evidence of depression or memory loss with employment limitations — **10**
* Asymptomatic, following initial diagnosis of HIV infection, with or without lymphadenopathy or decreased T4 cell count — **0**
* **Note (1):** The term “approved medication(s)” includes medications prescribed as part of a research protocol at an accredited medical institution.

* **Note (2):** Psychiatric or central nervous system manifestations, opportunistic infections, and neoplasms may be rated separately under appropriate codes if higher overall evaluation results, but not in combination with percentages otherwise assignable above.

In addition to `DC 6304`, `6309`, and `6319` below, the **General Rating Formula for Infectious Diseases** governs `DC 6300` (Vibriosis), `6305` (Lymphatic filariasis), `6306` (Bartonellosis), `6307` (Plague), `6308` (Relapsing fever), `6316` (Brucellosis), `6317` (Rickettsial, ehrlichial, and *Anaplasma* infections), `6318` (Melioidosis), `6320` (Parasitic diseases otherwise not specified), `6329` (Hemorrhagic fevers), `6330` (*Campylobacter jejuni* infection), `6331` (*Coxiella burnetii* infection / Q fever), `6333` (Nontyphoid *Salmonella* infections), `6334` (*Shigella* infections), and `6335` (West Nile virus infection). By contrast, standalone evaluation schedules govern `DC 6301` (Visceral leishmaniasis: `100%` active + `6 months` post-treatment + mandatory VA exam), `DC 6302` (Leprosy: `100%` active + `6 months` post-treatment + mandatory VA exam), `DC 6310` (Syphilis: rate residuals under appropriate body system), `DC 6311` (Tuberculosis, miliary: `100%` active + `§§ 4.88c/4.89`), `DC 6312` (Nontuberculous mycobacterium infection: `100%` active throughout treatment + mandatory VA exam), `DC 6325` (Hyperinfection syndrome or disseminated strongyloidiasis: `100%` active + mandatory VA exam), and `DC 6326` (Schistosomiasis: `0%` acute or asymptomatic chronic disease + rate residuals separately).*
General Rating Formula & Infectious Diseases (DC 6304, 6309, 6319)

lines: **§ 4.88b Schedule of ratings—infectious diseases, immune disorders and nutritional deficiencies.**
**General Rating Formula for Infectious Diseases:**
* For active disease — **100**
* After active disease has resolved, rate at 0 percent for infection. Rate any residual disability of infection within the appropriate body system.
**6304 Malaria:** Evaluate under the General Rating Formula.

* **Note 1:** The diagnosis of malaria, both initially and during relapse, depends on the identification of the malarial parasites in blood smears or other specific diagnostic laboratory tests such as antigen detection, immunologic (immunochromatographic) tests, and molecular testing such as polymerase chain reaction tests.
* **Note 2:** Rate under the appropriate body system any residual disability of infection, which includes, but is not limited to, liver or splenic damage, and central nervous system conditions.
**6309 Rheumatic fever:** Evaluate under the General Rating Formula.
* **Note:** Rate under the appropriate body system any residual disability of infection, which includes, but is not limited to, heart damage.
**6319 Lyme disease:** Evaluate under the General Rating Formula.

* **Note:** Rate under the appropriate body system any residual disability of infection, which includes, but is not limited to, arthritis, Bell's palsy, radiculopathy, ocular, or cognitive dysfunction.

blocks.text: Nutritional Deficiencies / Former POW Presumptive Conditions (DC 6313–6315)

lines: **6313 Avitaminosis:**
* Marked mental changes, moist dermatitis, inability to retain adequate nourishment, exhaustion, and cachexia — **100**
* With all of the symptoms listed below, plus mental symptoms and impaired bodily vigor — **60**
* With stomatitis, diarrhea, and symmetrical dermatitis — **40**
* With stomatitis, or achlorhydria, or diarrhea — **20**
* Confirmed diagnosis with nonspecific symptoms such as: decreased appetite, weight loss, abdominal discomfort, weakness, inability to concentrate and irritability — **10**
**6314 Beriberi:**
* As active disease:
* With congestive heart failure, anasarca, or Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome — **100**
* With cardiomegaly, or; with peripheral neuropathy with footdrop or atrophy of thigh or calf muscles — **60**

* With peripheral neuropathy with absent knee or ankle jerks and loss of sensation, or; with symptoms such as weakness, fatigue, anorexia, dizziness, heaviness and stiffness of legs, headache or sleep disturbance — **30**
* Thereafter rate residuals under the appropriate body system.
**6315 Pellagra:**
* Marked mental changes, moist dermatitis, inability to retain adequate nourishment, exhaustion, and cachexia — **100**
* With all of the symptoms listed below, plus mental symptoms and impaired bodily vigor — **60**
* With stomatitis, diarrhea, and symmetrical dermatitis — **40**
* With stomatitis, or achlorhydria, or diarrhea — **20**
* Confirmed diagnosis with nonspecific symptoms such as: decreased appetite, weight loss, abdominal discomfort, weakness, inability to concentrate and irritability — **10**

blocks.text: Systemic Immune Disorders (DC 6350 Lupus & DC 6351 HIV-Related Illness)

lines: **6350 Lupus erythematosus, systemic (disseminated):**
* Not to be combined with ratings under DC 7809.
* Acute, with frequent exacerbations, producing severe impairment of health — **100**
* Exacerbations lasting a week or more, 2 or 3 times per year — **60**
* Exacerbations once or twice a year or symptomatic during the past 2 years — **10**
* **Note:** Evaluate this condition either by combining the evaluations for residuals under the appropriate system, or by evaluating DC 6350, whichever method results in a higher evaluation.
**6351 HIV-related illness:**
* AIDS with recurrent opportunistic infections (see Note 3) or with secondary diseases afflicting multiple body systems; HIV-related illness with debility and progressive weight loss — **100**
* Refractory constitutional symptoms, diarrhea, and pathological weight loss; or minimum rating following development of AIDS-related opportunistic infection or neoplasm — **60**
* Recurrent constitutional symptoms, intermittent diarrhea, and use of approved medication(s); or minimum rating with T4 cell count less than 200 — **30**

* Following development of HIV-related constitutional symptoms; T4 cell count between 200 and 500; use of approved medication(s); or with evidence of depression or memory loss with employment limitations — **10**
* Asymptomatic, following initial diagnosis of HIV infection, with or without lymphadenopathy or decreased T4 cell count — **0**

* **Note 1:** In addition to standard therapies and regimens, the term “approved medication(s)” includes treatment regimens and medications prescribed as part of a research protocol at an accredited medical institution.

* **Note 2:** Diagnosed psychiatric illness, central nervous system manifestations, opportunistic infections, and neoplasms may be rated separately under the appropriate diagnostic codes if a higher overall evaluation results, provided the disability symptoms do not overlap with evaluations otherwise assignable above.

* **Note 3:** The following list of opportunistic infections are considered AIDS-defining conditions, that is, a diagnosis of AIDS follows if a person has HIV and one more of these infections, regardless of the CD4 count—candidiasis of the bronchi, trachea, esophagus, or lungs; invasive cervical cancer; coccidioidomycosis; cryptococcosis; cryptosporidiosis; cytomegalovirus (particularly CMV retinitis); HIV-related encephalopathy; herpes simplex-chronic ulcers for greater than one month, or bronchitis, pneumonia, or esophagitis; histoplasmosis; isosporiasis (chronic intestinal); Kaposi's sarcoma; lymphoma; mycobacterium avium complex; tuberculosis; pneumocystis jirovecii (carinii) pneumonia; pneumonia, recurrent; progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy; salmonella septicemia, recurrent; toxoplasmosis of the brain; and wasting syndrome due to HIV.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Infectious Diseases, Chronic Fatigue Syndrome, Lupus & HIV Regulations (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.88a & 4.88b)
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Sections 4.88a and 4.88b of Title 38 govern Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (Diagnostic Code 6354), tropical and Southwest Asia/Afghanistan infectious diseases (malaria, Lyme disease, Q fever, brucellosis, West Nile), Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (Diagnostic Code 6350), HIV-related illness (Diagnostic Code 6351), and Former Prisoner of War nutritional deficiencies (Diagnostic Codes 6313–6315). Effective August 11, 2019 (84 FR 28227), VA enacted a General Rating Formula for Infectious Diseases (100% during active infection, stepping to 0% once resolved while requiring separate ratings for any lasting organ, joint, nerve, or heart residuals), made the 10% criteria for HIV-related illness disjunctive (including continuous approved antiretroviral medication), and preserved Chronic Fatigue Syndrome without enacting proposed restrictions.
record_clues: A Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (Diagnostic Code 6354) decision denying 40% or 60% solely because no doctor prescribed bed rest—overlooking the alternative 'or' pathway for nearly constant debilitating fatigue and cognitive/physical symptoms that restrict routine daily activities to 50–75% (40%) or less than 50% (60%) of pre-illness levels.

A post-August 11, 2019 rating for Lyme disease (Diagnostic Code 6319), malaria (Diagnostic Code 6304), Q fever (Diagnostic Code 6331), or rheumatic fever (Diagnostic Code 6309) dropped to 0% after acute treatment without separately rating chronic arthritis, Bell's palsy, nerve radiculopathy, heart, or fatigue residuals.

Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (Diagnostic Code 6350) rated at 10% or 60% on flare frequency alone when separately combining kidney, joint, skin, lung, heart, or blood residuals would produce a higher rating under the Note.
An HIV-related illness claim (Diagnostic Code 6351) adjudicated on or after August 11, 2019 assigned 0% despite daily prescribed antiretroviral medication (which satisfies the post-2019 10% tier).
important_cautions: Two distinct prongs in Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (Diagnostic Code 6354): if relying on the waxing-and-waning 'periods of incapacitation' prong, the Note requires both bed rest AND treatment prescribed by a licensed physician; if relying on the 'nearly constant' daily-activity-restriction prong, prescribed bed rest is NOT required.

Anti-pyramiding rule in Lupus (Diagnostic Code 6350): VA cannot combine a Diagnostic Code 6350 flare rating WITH discoid lupus (Diagnostic Code 7809) or separate lupus organ residuals—instead, VA must calculate both methods and award whichever yields the higher overall evaluation.

Withdrawn proposal vs. enacted date: VA expressly withdrew its February 5, 2019 proposal (84 FR 1678) to tighten Chronic Fatigue Syndrome rules when issuing the June 18, 2019 Final Rule (84 FR 28227, effective August 11, 2019). Post-August 11, 2019 codes cannot prove Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) in pre-August 11, 2019 final decisions, and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c) allows only one final merits CUE decision per prior Board issue.

Former POW nutritional rules: Beriberi (Diagnostic Code 6314, including beriberi heart disease and dry beriberi peripheral neuropathy), Pellagra (Diagnostic Code 6315), and Avitaminosis (Diagnostic Code 6313) carry specific presumptive rules under 38 C.F.R. § 3.309(c).
questions_for_representative: For Chronic Fatigue Syndrome under Diagnostic Code 6354, do my medical and lay records show 'nearly constant' restriction of routine daily activities (<50% for 60%, or 50–75% for 40%) even without prescribed bed rest?
After an infectious disease like Lyme disease, Q fever, West Nile, or malaria resolved to 0%, did VA separately evaluate every lasting joint, nerve, cardiac, or post-infectious fatigue residual?
If I have Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (Diagnostic Code 6350), would rating my affected body systems separately yield a higher combined percentage than the 10% or 60% flare-count tier?
Do Gulf War / Southwest Asia / Afghanistan presumptions under 38 C.F.R. § 3.317(a) or (c) apply to my condition?

blocks.text: 1. Verbatim Special Provisions: 38 C.F.R. § 4.96(a)–(d)

*Source: `ecfr.gov` / `govinfo.gov` (`[34 FR 5062, Mar. 11, 1969; 61 FR 46727, Sept. 5, 1996; 71 FR 52459, Sept. 6, 2006]`). Observe carefully that `§ 4.96(a)`'s bar on combining coexisting respiratory ratings covers `DC 6600–6817` and `DC 6822–6847` (plus `DC 6819–6820` when lung/pleura are involved), leaving Nose and Throat codes (`DC 6502–6524`) outside `§ 4.96(a)` unless symptoms overlap under `§ 4.14`.*

lines: **§ 4.96 Special provisions regarding evaluation of respiratory conditions.**

**(a) Rating coexisting respiratory conditions.** Ratings under diagnostic codes 6600 through 6817 and 6822 through 6847 will not be combined with each other. Where there is lung or pleural involvement, ratings under diagnostic codes 6819 and 6820 will not be combined with each other or with diagnostic codes 6600 through 6817 or 6822 through 6847. A single rating will be assigned under the diagnostic code which reflects the predominant disability with elevation to the next higher evaluation where the severity of the overall disability warrants such elevation.
**(b) Rating “protected” tuberculosis cases.**

**(1)** Public Law 90–493 repealed section 356 of title 38, United States Code, which had provided graduated ratings for inactive tuberculosis. The repealed section, however, still applies to the case of any veteran who on August 19, 1968, was receiving or entitled to receive compensation for tuberculosis. The use of the protective provisions of Pub. L. 90–493 should be mentioned in the discussion portion of all ratings in which these provisions are applied. For application in rating cases in which the protective provisions of Pub. L. 90–493 apply, the former evaluations pertaining to pulmonary tuberculosis are retained in § 4.97.
**(2)** In cases protected by the provisions of Pub. L. 90–493, the graduated ratings of 50 and 30 percent for inactive tuberculosis will not be elevated.

**(c) Special monthly compensation.** When evaluating any claim involving complete organic aphonia, refer to § 3.350 of this chapter to determine whether the veteran may be entitled to special monthly compensation. Footnotes in the schedule indicate conditions which potentially establish entitlement to special monthly compensation; however, there are other conditions in this section which under certain circumstances also establish entitlement to special monthly compensation.
**(d) Special provisions for the application of evaluation criteria for diagnostic codes 6600, 6603, 6604, 6825–6833, and 6840–6845.**
**(1)** Pulmonary function tests (PFT's) are required to evaluate these conditions except:
**(i)** When the results of a maximum exercise capacity test are of record and are 20 ml/kg/min or less. If a maximum exercise capacity test is not of record, evaluate based on alternative criteria.
**(ii)** When pulmonary hypertension (documented by an echocardiogram or cardiac catheterization), cor pulmonale, or right ventricular hypertrophy has been diagnosed.
**(iii)** When there have been one or more episodes of acute respiratory failure.
**(iv)** When outpatient oxygen therapy is required.

**(2)** If the DLCO (SB) (Diffusion Capacity of the Lung for Carbon Monoxide by the Single Breath Method) test is not of record, evaluate based on alternative criteria as long as the examiner states why the test would not be useful or valid in a particular case.

**(3)** When the PFT's are not consistent with clinical findings, evaluate based on the PFT's unless the examiner states why they are not a valid indication of respiratory functional impairment in a particular case.

**(4)** Post-bronchodilator studies are required when PFT's are done for disability evaluation purposes except when the results of pre-bronchodilator pulmonary function tests are normal or when the examiner determines that post-bronchodilator studies should not be done and states why.

**(5)** When evaluating based on PFT's, use post-bronchodilator results in applying the evaluation criteria in the rating schedule unless the post-bronchodilator results were poorer than the pre-bronchodilator results. In those cases, use the pre-bronchodilator values for rating purposes.

**(6)** When there is a disparity between the results of different PFT's (FEV–1 (Forced Expiratory Volume in one second), FVC (Forced Vital Capacity), etc.), so that the level of evaluation would differ depending on which test result is used, use the test result that the examiner states most accurately reflects the level of disability.
**(7)** If the FEV–1 and the FVC are both greater than 100 percent, do not assign a compensable evaluation based on a decreased FEV–1/FVC ratio.
*(Authority: 38 U.S.C. 1155)*

blocks.text: 5. Quarantine Warning: Unfinalized Proposed Rule RIN 2900-AQ72

lines: **QUARANTINE — PROPOSED / NOT FINALIZED (`RIN 2900-AQ72`, `87 FR 8474` & `89 FR 74162`):**

On February 15, 2022 (`87 FR 8474`), VA published a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (*Schedule for Rating Disabilities: Ear, Nose, Throat, and Audiology Disabilities; Special Provisions Regarding Evaluation of Respiratory Conditions; Schedule for Rating Disabilities: Respiratory System*, `RIN 2900-AQ72`) proposing to eliminate automatic `50%` CPAP evaluations under `DC 6847` unless treatment is ineffective or contraindicated with end-organ damage, and to revise rhinitis/sinusitis criteria. On September 12, 2024 (`89 FR 74162`), VA issued a Supplemental Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (`SNPRM` under `RIN 2900-AQ72`) proposing a new `DC 6605` for constrictive (obliterative) bronchiolitis. **As of late 2026, `RIN 2900-AQ72` remains an unfinalized proposed rulemaking with no enacted final rule or effective date.** Practitioners and AI agents must **never** cite `87 FR 8474` or `89 FR 74162` as active law; the enacted `1996/2006` `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.96–4.97` criteria above—including the `50%` CPAP evaluation under `DC 6847`—remain in full legal force.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Respiratory System Regulations (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.96–4.97): Breathing Tests, Sinusitis/Rhinitis, Asthma & Sleep Apnea
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Effective October 7, 1996 (61 FR 46720), VA modernized its respiratory rating schedule (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.96–4.97) around objective Pulmonary Function Test (PFT) numbers (FEV-1, FEV-1/FVC, FVC, and DLCO diffusing capacity), inhaler/steroid medication tiers for Asthma (Diagnostic Code 6602), dedicated formulas for Sinusitis (Diagnostic Codes 6510–6514) and Rhinitis (Diagnostic Code 6522), and Sleep Apnea Syndromes (Diagnostic Code 6847, awarding 50% when a CPAP or breathing assistance device is medically required)—followed on October 6, 2006 (71 FR 52457) by § 4.96(d)'s rules on when PFTs can be excused and which PFT score governs. Crucially, § 4.96(a) prevents combining multiple LOWER-respiratory codes (Diagnostic Codes 6600–6817 and 6822–6847), while leaving UPPER-respiratory nose and sinus codes (Diagnostic Codes 6502–6524) completely separate to combine!
record_clues: A Rating Code Sheet that improperly folded upper-respiratory Chronic Sinusitis (Diagnostic Codes 6510–6514) or Allergic Rhinitis (Diagnostic Code 6522) into a lower-respiratory Asthma or Sleep Apnea rating—violating the plain numeric boundaries of 38 C.F.R. § 4.96(a).

Coexisting service-connected Asthma (Diagnostic Code 6602) and Obstructive Sleep Apnea (Diagnostic Code 6847) rated flatly at 50% without evaluating whether combined lower-respiratory severity warrants elevation to the next higher tier (60% or 100%) under § 4.96(a).

Asthma (Diagnostic Code 6602) rated at 10% despite daily use of an inhaled anti-inflammatory corticosteroid or daily bronchodilator (which meets the 30% tier), or rated at 30% despite three or more courses per year of oral/injectable systemic steroids (which meets the 60% tier).

A respiratory cancer (Diagnostic Code 6819, a PACT Act presumptive condition) reduced from 100% after treatment without a mandatory VA examination 6 months after treatment ended and 60 days' advance notice under 38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e).
important_cautions: Lower-respiratory non-combination rule (§ 4.96(a)): VA cannot assign separate stacked percentages for two lower-respiratory conditions within Diagnostic Codes 6600–6817 and 6822–6847 (for example, Asthma + COPD + Sleep Apnea); instead, VA assigns one rating under the predominant code with potential elevation to the next higher tier.

October 7, 1996 and October 6, 2006 date gates: Diagnostic Code 6847 (50% CPAP Sleep Apnea) and modern FEV-1/DLCO tables took effect October 7, 1996 (published September 5, 1996 at 61 FR 46720), while § 4.96(d) PFT rules (including § 4.96(d)(7), barring compensable ratings from FEV-1/FVC ratio alone when both FEV-1 and FVC exceed 100% predicted) took effect October 6, 2006—neither can establish Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) before its effective date.

Sleep apnea CPAP rules have NOT changed: VA's February 15, 2022 proposed rule and September 12, 2024 supplemental notice (RIN 2900-AQ72, 87 FR 8474 & 89 FR 74162) remain proposed and unfinalized (not enacted law); the 50% CPAP rule under Diagnostic Code 6847 remains binding law.
Remember 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c): once the Board of Veterans' Appeals issues a final merits decision on a CUE motion on a specific Board issue, no further CUE motions are permitted on that issue.
questions_for_representative: Did VA keep my upper-respiratory Sinusitis (Diagnostic Codes 6510–6514) and Rhinitis (Diagnostic Code 6522—30% with nasal polyps, 10% without polyps with >50% obstruction) separate from my lower-respiratory Asthma or Sleep Apnea rating?

On my Pulmonary Function Test report, if FEV-1%, FEV-1/FVC, and DLCO (SB) pointed to different rating levels, did the examiner explain which test best reflects my disability under 38 C.F.R. § 4.96(d)(6)?
Do my pharmacy records show daily inhaled corticosteroids/bronchodilators (30%) or three or more annual systemic steroid courses (60%) under Diagnostic Code 6602?
If I have both Sleep Apnea and Asthma/COPD, did VA evaluate elevation to the next higher percentage tier under 38 C.F.R. § 4.96(a)?
