1. Legacy 38 C.F.R. Parts 19 & 20 (57 FR 4088, 1992) vs. AMA Overhaul (84 FR 138, 2019)

items:
**Era 1 (Post-VJRA Legacy Baseline):**
• **Federal Register Citation:** `57 FR 4088` (`Part 19` at `57 FR 4104`; `Part 20` at `57 FR 4109`)
• **Publication Date:** `1992-02-03`
• **Effective Date:** `1992-03-04`
• **Transitional / Pending-Claim Rule:** Restructured legacy `38 C.F.R. Part 19` into separate AOJ appellate processing (`Part 19`) and Board Rules of Practice (`Part 20`) following `Pub. L. 100-687` (`VJRA`). Remains **actively in force today** for all un-opted appeals of AOJ decisions issued **prior to `2019-02-19`** (`38 C.F.R. §§ 3.2400(b), 19.2`), including `~28,000+` `VACOLS`-swept appeals restored under ***Freund v. Collins*, `No. 21-4168 (Vet. App. class certified Mar. 2026)`**.

**Era 2 (Appeals Modernization Act Overhaul):**
• **Federal Register Citation:** `84 FR 138` (`Part 3` at `84 FR 167–172`; `Part 19` at `84 FR 177`; `Part 20` at `84 FR 178–193`; `RIN 2900-AQ26`)
• **Publication Date:** `2019-01-18`
• **Effective Date:** `2019-02-19` (`Pub. L. 115-55, § 2(x)`, `131 Stat. 1115`)
• **Transitional / Pending-Claim Rule:** **Strict Statutory Partition (`Karnas v. Derwinski`, `1 Vet. App. 308 (1991)` Inapplicable to Structural Track):** Applies to all claims in which VA mails notice of an initial AOJ decision **on or after `2019-02-19`** (`§ 3.2400(a)(1)`), plus Legacy claims affirmatively and **irrevocably** opted into AMA via `RAMP` or within `60 days` of a post-Feb. 19, 2019 `SOC`/`SSOC` (`§ 3.2400(a)(2), (c)`).

headers: Era 2: **AMA System (`84 FR 138`, Eff. `2019-02-19`, as Modified by Courts)**
rows: Single linear track (`38 U.S.C. § 7105` `[pre-AMA]`): `1-yr` `NOD` (optional `DRO` election under `former § 3.2600`, `66 FR 21871`, eff. `2001-06-01`) -> VA issues `SOC` (`§ 19.29`) -> `VA Form 9` Substantive Appeal.

Three modular `1-year` lanes (`38 U.S.C. § 5104C`; `§ 3.2500(c)`): `(1)` **HLR** (`VA Form 20-0996`, `§ 3.2601`), `(2)` **Supplemental Claim** (`VA Form 20-0995`, `§ 3.2501`), or `(3)` **Board Appeal** (`VA Form 10182`, `§ 20.202`). Issue-splitting across lanes permitted (`§ 3.2500(d)`).

Two-step perfection: `(1)` `NOD` within `1 year` (`VA Form 21-0958` mandatory `>= 2015-03-24`, `79 FR 57660`); `(2)` **`VA Form 9`** within **`60 days` from `SOC` mailing OR remainder of `1-year` post-decision window, whichever is later** (`§ 19.52(b)` `[former § 20.302(b)]`).

Single-step perfection (`38 U.S.C. § 7105(b)(1)`): **`VA Form 10182` (`NOD`)** filed directly with the Board within **`1 year`** of AOJ decision notice (`§ 20.202(b)`). `SOC`, `SSOC`, and `VA Form 9` abolished for AMA claims.
*Not applicable* (single unified Board docket; hearing could be requested anytime prior to decision under `former § 20.700`).

**`38 C.F.R. § 20.202(c)(2)`:** File new `10182` by **later of `1 year` from AOJ decision notice OR `60 days` from Board receipt of initial `10182`** (barred if evidence/testimony already submitted). Board **cannot** decide prematurely before window expires absent waiver (***Williams v. McDonough*, `37 Vet. App. 305 (2024)`**); late switches/delays barred (***Brack v. Collins*, `No. 25-1205 (Fed. Cir. Sept. 8, 2026)`**, *aff'g* `37 Vet. App. 172`).

**Open Continuous Record (`former §§ 19.37, 20.800, 20.1304`):** Evidence accepted continuously throughout appeal (`90 days` post-certification under `§ 20.1304`, or afterward upon good cause / before decision). Triggered mandatory `SSOC` (`30-day` response, `§ 19.38`) unless waived under *Bernard v. Brown*, `4 Vet. App. 384 (1993)`.

**Sealed Statutory Windows (`38 U.S.C. § 7113`; `§§ 20.301–20.303`):** · • **Direct (`§ 7113(a)` / `§ 20.301`):** Closed as of AOJ decision. · • **Evidence (`§ 7113(c)` / `§ 20.303`):** With `10182` or within **`90 days` post-NOD receipt**. · • **Hearing (`§ 7113(b)` / `§ 20.302`):** At Board hearing or within **`90 days` post-hearing**. · • Board weighs window evidence **in first instance** (`§§ 20.300(a), 20.801`) without `SSOC` or *Bernard* waiver!
*No gap existed*—all post-AOJ submissions entered the continuous appellate record (and `§ 3.156(b)` abated finality if submitted within `1 yr` without an `NOD`, *Beraud* / *Lang*).

• ***Cook v. McDonough*, `36 Vet. App. 175 (2023)`:** Gap submissions (between AOJ decision & `10182`, or between `10182` & Board hearing) do not auto-enter record, though VLJ/Board must give accurate exclusion/resubmission notice (`§§ 20.205(c), 20.705`). · • ***Cash v. Collins*, `No. 24-1811 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 5, 2026)`:** When `VA Form 10182` **identifies or incorporates by reference** probative gap-period evidence already in `VBMS`, Board **must consider it** under `§ 7113(c)` without physical re-upload!
**`"New and Material"` (`former § 3.156(a)`):** Must relate to an **unestablished fact** necessary to substantiate the claim **AND raise a reasonable possibility of substantiating the claim**.

**`"New and Relevant"` (`38 U.S.C. § 5108(a)`; `§§ 3.156(d), 3.2501(a)(1)`):** Lower threshold—not previously in actual record + **tends to prove or disprove a matter at issue** (or raises unaddressed theory).
**Continuous** throughout AOJ and Board proceedings until final BVA decision.

**Terminates at AOJ decision notice (`§ 5103A(e)(2)`)** during HLR and BVA review—*except* mandatory **`§ 3.2601(g)` / `§ 20.802(a)` remand** for pre-decisional DTA error (`Full § 5103A` re-attaches in Supplemental Claims, `§ 3.2501(b)`).
• Reopening after BVA/CAVC affirmance **reset effective date** (`§ 7291`). · • **Implicit Denial (`Deshotel` / `Adams`)** extinguished unmentioned related claims.

• **`§ 5110(a)(2)(D)–(E)` & *MVA v. Sec'y*, `7 F.4th 1110 (Fed. Cir. 2021)`:** `1-yr` Supplemental Claim after **BVA OR CAVC** decision preserves initial effective date (`§ 3.2500(b)` Fed. Cir. bar & `§ 3.155` Supplemental `ITF` exclusion **invalidated**!). · • ***Hamill v. Collins*, `166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. 2026)`:** Implicit denial **abolished** for AMA decisions under `38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)`!

items: **Pre-1997 Baseline:** In ***Smith v. Brown*, `35 F.3d 1516 (Fed. Cir. 1994)`**, the Federal Circuit held `38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a)` applied solely to RO decisions, leaving veterans with no statutory CUE motion against final Board decisions (only discretionary Chairman reconsideration under `38 U.S.C. § 7103`). Congress responded by enacting **`Pub. L. 105-111` (`111 Stat. 2271`, enacted & effective `1997-11-21`)**, codifying `38 U.S.C. § 5109A` (RO CUE) and **`38 U.S.C. § 7111`** (Board CUE).

**Era 1 (`Subpart O` Enactment):**
• **Federal Register Citation:** `64 FR 2134, 2139` (`RIN 2900-AJ15`)
• **Publication Date:** `1999-01-13`
• **Effective Date:** `1999-02-12`
• **Transitional / Pending-Claim Rule:** Applies retroactively to revise *any* prior final Board decision regardless of how many decades earlier the Board decision was rendered (`§ 20.1400(a)`), judged strictly against the record and law extant when that Board decision issued (`§ 20.1403(b)`).

**Era 2 (AMA Conforming Amendments & *George* Validation):**
• **Federal Register Citation:** `84 FR 138, 191–192` (`RIN 2900-AQ26`)
• **Publication Date:** `2019-01-18`
• **Effective Date:** `2019-02-19`
• **Transitional / Pending-Claim Rule:** Updated internal `Part 20` cross-references and conformed `§ 20.1411(b)` to AMA `§ 5108` Supplemental Claims without altering substantive CUE burdens; **`§ 20.1403(e)` upheld 6–3** in ***George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)`**.

rows: All final Board merits decisions are subject to revision except issues which have been **appealed to and decided by a court of competent jurisdiction** (`CAVC`/`Fed. Cir.`); subsumes underlying RO rating decision on the same issue.
Unchanged substantively—remains the threshold jurisdictional check on [`Board CUE Pre-Filing Gate`](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate).

Codified absolute bars against pleading `(1)` **changed medical diagnosis** without factual record error, `(2)` **Secretary's failure to fulfill the duty to assist** (*Cook v. Principi*, `318 F.3d 1334`), or `(3)` **disagreement as to how the facts were weighed or evaluated**.
Unchanged—still defeats every DTA, *McLendon*, *Nieves-Rodriguez*, and `§ 5107(b)` equipoise theory pleaded as CUE.

*"Clear and unmistakable error does not include the otherwise correct application of a statute or regulation where, subsequent to the Board decision challenged, there has been a change in the interpretation of the statute or regulation."*

**Affirmed by U.S. Supreme Court in *George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)`:** Even when a regulation (`former § 3.304(b)` soundness rebuttal in *George*, `§ 3.350(f)` single-step cap in *Barry*, or `§ 3.352(b)(2)` in *Laska*) is later invalidated as contrary to statute, a prior final Board decision applying that regulation while in force is **immune from CUE**!

• **`§ 20.1404(b)`:** Must set forth clearly and specifically the alleged factual/legal error, exact extant law, and why result would have **manifestly changed** (*non-specific motions dismissed without prejudice*). · • **`§ 20.1409(c)`:** **STRICT ONE-SHOT RES JUDICATA**—once there is a final decision on a `Subpart O` motion on a given Board issue, *"that issue may not be reviewed again under this subpart."*
Unchanged (`84 FR 191` updated cross-references to `Rule 803`/`§ 20.803` etc.). **Never** file a half-researched Board CUE motion!
Referenced `"reopening"` a previously disallowed claim based on `"new and material evidence"` under `38 U.S.C. § 5108`.

**`84 FR 192`** replaced `"reopen"` / `"new and material"` with filing a **`"supplemental claim"`** under `38 U.S.C. § 5108` (`new and relevant`), clarifying a `Subpart O` CUE motion is distinct from a `§ 5108` Supplemental Claim.

blocks.text: 3. Four-Era 38 C.F.R. § 14.636 (Former § 20.609) Attorney & Agent Fee Evolution (1862–2026)

Eligibility to charge a `38 U.S.C. § 5904` (`former § 3404`) contingency or hourly fee—and eligibility for `20%` direct VA withholding from past-due benefits (`§ 5904(d)`)—is governed by **four distinct statutory/regulatory eras**:

rows: **Capped at `$10` per claim** across all VA stages (upheld in *Walters*, `473 U.S. 305 (1985)`). Criminal misdemeanor (`§ 5905`) to charge `> $10`.
**ONLY AFTER a first final Board (`BVA`) decision** on the issue, **AND** attorney/agent had to be **retained within `1 year`** of that BVA decision (`NOD` had to be `>= Nov. 18, 1988`).
**After a Legacy Notice of Disagreement (`NOD`) is filed ON OR AFTER `June 20, 2007`** (`Pub. L. 109-461, § 101(i)`). *(Pre-June 20, 2007 NODs stay under Era 2 post-BVA rule per `§ 14.636(c)(3)`!).*
**After VA issues notice of an initial AOJ decision on the claim (`>= Feb. 19, 2019`)** (`§ 14.636(c)(1)`). Zero fee permitted on an original initial `21-526EZ` claim prior to first AOJ decision.
Required a prior final BVA decision on the underlying issue + `1-yr` retention (or final BVA denial of CUE).
Required filing a post-June 20, 2007 `NOD` after RO denied reopening/CUE (unless earlier final BVA/NOD on same `"case"` covered downstream work).

• **`Feb. 19, 2019 – July 29, 2021` (`84 FR 174`):** `§ 14.636(c)(1)(i)` purported to **ban** fees on `>1-yr` Supplemental Claims & `CUE` motions until VA first denied that Supplemental/CUE filing. · • **`July 30, 2021 – Present` (*MVA v. Sec'y*, `7 F.4th at 1135–41`):** **INVALIDATED `§ 14.636(c)(1)(i)`!** Fees ARE lawful immediately on **all** `>1-yr` `§ 5108` Supplemental Claims and `§§ 5109A/7111` `CUE` motions whenever an earlier initial AOJ decision on the claim existed (even decades ago)!
• **`<= 20%`** of past-due benefits eligible for direct VA withholding (`§ 5904(d)`) & presumed reasonable. · • Fee agreements filed with BVA (`former § 20.609(g)`).

• **`<= 20%`:** Presumed reasonable (`§ 14.636(f)`) + direct VA withholding (`§ 5904(d)`). · • **`20.01% – 33.33%`:** Neutral (no presumption; direct client collection only—VA will **not** withhold `>20%`!). · • **`> 33.33%`:** Rebuttably **presumed unreasonable** (`§ 14.636(f)`). · • Oversight moved from BVA to **VA OGC** (`30-day` filing rule, `§ 14.636(g)(3)`).

Same `<= 20%` direct-pay / `<= 33.33%` reasonableness structure (`§ 14.636(f)–(h)`); fee base governed by `"cash-in-hand"` net past-due payout rules (*Snyder*, `489 F.3d 1213`; *Ravin*, `956 F.3d 1346`; *Gumpenberger*, `973 F.3d 1379` — [Playbook 20](/playbooks/20-backpay-offsets-crdp-crsc-severance-recoupment)) + mandatory `Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c)` `"same-work"` EAJA refund.

blocks.text: 4. Non-VA Emergency Medical Reimbursement (38 U.S.C. § 1725; 38 C.F.R. §§ 17.1002 & 17.1005): 2001 -> 2018 (*Staab*) -> 2023 (*Wolfe*)

Under `38 U.S.C. § 1725` (enacted by `Pub. L. 106-117, § 111`, `113 Stat. 1553`, Nov. 30, 1999, eff. `2000-05-29` for non-service-connected emergency treatment of active `24-month` VHA-enrolled veterans, distinct from `38 U.S.C. § 1728` SC/`P&T`/`Ch. 31` emergency care), VA's Other-Health-Insurance (`OHI`) exclusion regulations underwent two major judicial invalidations and Federal Register overhauls:

items:
**Era 1 (Pre-*Staab* Total / Partial `OHI` Exclusion Era):**
• **Federal Register Citations:** `66 FR 36467` (pub. `2001-07-12`, eff. `2001-08-13`) & `77 FR 23615` (pub. `2012-04-20`, eff. `2012-05-21`, implementing `Pub. L. 111-137`, retro. eff. `2009-07-19`)
• **Rule & Judicial Invalidation:** `Pub. L. 111-137` amended `38 U.S.C. § 1725(c)(4)(D)` so VA became secondary payer while barring reimbursement for `"any copayment or similar payment"` owed by the veteran. Despite `Pub. L. 111-137`, VA retained `former 38 C.F.R. § 17.1002(f)` barring *all* reimbursement if a health-plan contract covered *any fraction* of the ER visit—**invalidated** in ***Staab v. McDonald*, `28 Vet. App. 50, 54–56 (2016)`** as frustrating Congress's `2010` amendment!

**Era 2 (Post-*Staab* Interim Final Rule — Sweeping Deductible & Coinsurance Ban):**
• **Federal Register Citation:** `83 FR 974` (`RIN 2900-AQ08`, *Reimbursement for Emergency Treatment*)
• **Publication Date:** `2018-01-09`
• **Effective Date:** `2018-01-09` *(Interim Final Rule)*
• **Rule & Judicial Invalidation:** Amended `§ 17.1002(f)` to strike `"or in part"`, **but simultaneously amended `§ 17.1005(a)(5)`** to prohibit VA from reimbursing `"any copayment, deductible, **coinsurance**, or similar payment"`! In ***Wolfe v. Wilkie*, `32 Vet. App. 1 (2019)`** (`Rule 23` class action) and ***Wolfe v. McDonough*, `28 F.4th 1348, 1354–60 (Fed. Cir. 2022)`**, the Federal Circuit held that while fixed **copayments** and **deductibles** are `"similar payments"` barred by `38 U.S.C. § 1725(c)(4)(D)`, percentage-based **coinsurance** (`e.g., 20%` of a `$250,000` ICU/air-ambulance bill = `$50,000`!) is **NOT** a `"copayment or similar payment"`—invalidating `83 FR 974`'s coinsurance ban! *(Note: Wolfe, `28 F.4th at 1358–60` vacated CAVC mandamus because class members had an adequate direct statutory appeal pathway through BVA to CAVC).*

**Era 3 (Post-*Wolfe* Final Rule — Coinsurance Payable; Copayments & Deductibles Excluded):**
• **Federal Register Citation:** `88 FR 10835` (`RIN 2900-AQ08`, *Reimbursement for Emergency Treatment*)
• **Publication Date:** `2023-02-22`
• **Effective Date:** `2023-04-24`
• **Transitional / Retroactive Filing Window (`§ 17.1004(f)`):** Opened a special **`1-year` retroactive claim window (through `February 22, 2024`)** for veterans whose `OHI` emergency claims met `§§ 17.1002–17.1003` criteria back to February 1, 2010!

rows: **Excluded (`$0`)** — upheld as `"similar payment"` in *Wolfe v. McDonough*, `28 F.4th at 1356`.
Denied under `83 FR 974` (**invalidated** in *Wolfe*, `32 Vet. App. 1` & `28 F.4th 1348`).
**Uncovered Emergency Services** (`e.g., non-covered air ambulance / out-of-network balance`)
Denied if `OHI` paid any other line item (*Staab* error).
**Reimbursable** up to `§ 17.1005` payment schedule (**extinguishes provider balance-billing liability** under `38 U.S.C. § 1725(a)(2)(A), (e)` & `38 C.F.R. § 17.1005(a)(4)` once VA pays!).

blocks.text: 5. Era-Specific CUE Traps & *George v. McDonough* Bitemporal Gate Matrix
Always screen historical `Part 19/20`, `Part 14`, and `Part 17` errors against ***George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)`** and **`38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`**:

rows: **Board Refusal on an Open/Timely Appeal to Consider Gap-Period Evidence Identified on `VA Form 10182` (*Cash v. Collins*)**
**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** *(Direct CAVC / Timely Appeal)*

On any timely appeal to CAVC (`120 days`) or pending Board docket, ***Cash v. Collins*, `No. 24-1811 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 5, 2026)`** compels vacatur whenever `10182` incorporated `VBMS` gap evidence under `§ 7113(c)`. Conversely, attacking an unappealed **final pre-2026 Board decision** via `Subpart O` CUE faces `§ 20.1403(e)` / *George*—file a `1-year` `§ 5110(a)(2)(D)` Supplemental Claim (`20-0995`) instead to preserve the full effective date without CUE!
**Silent Omission of a Claimed or Reasonably Raised Issue in an AMA Decision `>= Feb. 19, 2019` (*Hamill v. Collins*)**
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** *(Pending Unadjudicated Claim — No CUE Needed!)*

Under `38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)` and ***Hamill v. Collins*, `166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. 2026)`**, implicit denial does not exist in AMA—the omitted issue **never became final** and remains an **open, pending claim** adjudicated under `§ 5107(b)` equipoise ([`Procedural Vehicles`](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality))!
**Unlawful `VACOLS` Administrative Closure of a Perfected Legacy Appeal (`Dec. 12, 1990 – Feb. 6, 2025`, *Freund v. Collins*)**
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** *(Pending Legacy Appeal — No CUE Needed!)*

Because `VACOLS` closed the appeal without a Board decision or valid `§ 20.205` withdrawal, **appellate finality never attached**—demand immediate Legacy docket restoration under ***Freund v. Collins*, `No. 21-4168 (Vet. App. Mar. 2026)`**.
**OGC / RO Refusal After `July 30, 2021` to Honor a Valid `§ 5904` Fee Agreement on a `>1-Year` Supplemental Claim or `CUE` Motion (*MVA v. Sec'y*)**

Once the Federal Circuit **invalidated `38 C.F.R. § 14.636(c)(1)(i)` on July 30, 2021** (`7 F.4th at 1141`), that subparagraph ceased to exist in law; any post-July 30, 2021 fee-eligibility denial invoking `§ 14.636(c)(1)(i)` is reversible error / CUE ([`Award & Withholding Checklist`](/checklists/award-letter-and-withholding-audit-checklist)). *(Pre-July 30, 2021 final unappealed fee denials face George / `§ 20.1403(e)`).*
**VHA Denial `>= Apr. 24, 2023` (or Open Post-*Wolfe* Appeal) Refusing `§ 1725` Coinsurance Reimbursement**
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** *(Post-`2023-04-24`)* / **Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** *(Pre-`2022` Final Denials)*

Post-`88 FR 10835` (`2023-04-24`), `§§ 17.1002(f) & 17.1005(a)(5)` expressly authorize coinsurance reimbursement; open/timely-appealed pre-2023 denials also win under *Wolfe*, `28 F.4th 1348`, whereas unappealed final pre-*Wolfe* denials that missed the `Feb. 22, 2024` window face *George* on CUE (screen instead for **`38 U.S.C. § 1728` service-connected/`P&T` eligibility**, which **never** had `§ 1725`'s `OHI` deductible/copay bars!).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Legacy vs. Modern (AMA) Appeals, Representation Fee History & Emergency Coinsurance Rules
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: VA's procedural rules changed dramatically across four eras—especially on February 19, 2019 when the Appeals Modernization Act (AMA, 84 FR 138) replaced the old open-record Legacy appeal system (Statement of the Case + VA Form 9) with three distinct review lanes and strict 90-day Board evidence windows. This historical comparison tracks: (1) Legacy Part 19 open-record rules versus AMA Part 20 closed/windowed dockets, (2) Board Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) rules enacted February 12, 1999, (3) when accredited attorneys and claims agents can legally charge fees across pre-2007, 2007–2019, and post-February 19, 2019 rules (38 C.F.R. § 14.636), and (4) non-VA emergency medical coinsurance reimbursement after Staab and Wolfe (38 C.F.R. §§ 17.1002 and 17.1005).
record_clues: The date of the initial VA Regional Office decision: decisions noticed BEFORE February 19, 2019 stay in the Legacy system unless opted into AMA, whereas initial decisions noticed ON OR AFTER February 19, 2019 are governed by AMA.
A VA Form 10182 Board appeal citing or incorporating medical evidence that was already uploaded to VA's file between the Regional Office decision and the Notice of Disagreement (Cash v. Collins).

A Regional Office or VA General Counsel letter refusing to recognize an accredited representative's contingency fee on a non-continuous Supplemental Claim or CUE motion based on invalidated language in 38 C.F.R. § 14.636(c)(1)(i) (struck down in Military-Veterans Advocacy v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs).

A non-VA emergency care bill denied under 38 U.S.C. § 1725 because Medicare or private insurance left 20% coinsurance unpaid (reimbursable under Wolfe v. McDonough and the April 24, 2023 rule at 88 FR 10835).
important_cautions: Do not mix Legacy and AMA evidence rules: an AMA appeal of a post-February 19, 2019 decision does NOT keep an open evidentiary record up to the Board decision—evidence uploaded outside the selected AMA Board docket window can be ignored unless properly submitted or preserved via a follow-on Supplemental Claim.

Fee-trigger dates protect Veterans: nobody may charge a fee on an initial claim before VA issues an initial decision (38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(1)). On older Legacy cases, the fee trigger turned on whether the Notice of Disagreement was filed on or after June 20, 2007 (Pub. L. 109-461) versus before June 20, 2007 (requiring a prior final Board decision).

Strict Board CUE finality bar: under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c), once the Board issues a final decision on the merits of a CUE motion on a specific prior Board issue, no second CUE motion is allowed on that Board issue—and under George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e), later judicial invalidations of regulations cannot establish CUE against earlier final decisions.

Emergency reimbursement scope under § 1725: percentage-based coinsurance is reimbursable under 38 C.F.R. § 17.1005 after Wolfe, whereas fixed copayments and annual deductibles remain excluded under § 1725(c)(4)(D) (unless the Veteran qualifies under 38 U.S.C. § 1728 for a service-connected emergency or 100% P&T status).
questions_for_representative: Is my appeal governed by the pre-February 19, 2019 Legacy open-record system or the post-February 19, 2019 AMA system, and should a remanded Legacy appeal stay in Legacy?
If medical evidence was uploaded to my VA file in an 'in-between' period before my VA Form 10182 Board appeal, did we clearly incorporate it or select the Evidence Submission docket?
Does our representation agreement comply with 38 U.S.C. § 5904 and 38 C.F.R. § 14.636 (accredited representative, post-initial-decision trigger, <=20% direct-pay cap, and 30-day filing)?
If VA denied my non-VA emergency room coinsurance bill under older rules invalidated by Staab or Wolfe, what review options remain open?

Citing VA's unfinalized July 10, 2020 proposed standalone definition of 'moral turpitude' (85 FR 41471, proposed rule — rejected and NOT adopted in final rule 89 FR 32361, 32363–32365)

blocks.text: This Reference module tracks the eighty-year statutory evolution of Character of Discharge (`COD`) bars (`1944–Present`), maps a clause-by-clause comparison between pre-June 25, 2024 `38 C.F.R. § 3.12(a)–(k)` and the **June 25, 2024 Final Rule (`89 FR 32361`, `RIN 2900-AQ95`, published April 26, 2024, effective June 25, 2024)** (`§ 3.12(a)–(l)`), and defines the strict bitemporal boundary between prospective `38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)` reopenings and the **five retroactive pre-2024 pathways**.

*(For verbatim pre- and post-June 25, 2024 text of `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.12, 3.13, and 3.354`, see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.12, 3.13, 3.354, 3.400(g), 3.6 & 3.301 (Character of Discharge Evolution, Insanity, Upgrades, ADT/IADT & Line of Duty)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.12-3.13-3.354-cod-insanity); for operational pleading strategy, see [Playbook 10 (COD, Insanity, `§ 3.13` & Upgrades)](/playbooks/10-character-of-discharge-insanity-upgrades), [Playbook 11 (Guard/Reserve ADT/IADT & LOD)](/playbooks/11-guard-reserve-adt-iadt-and-line-of-duty), [Playbook 03 (`§ 3.156(c)` Service Records)](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c), and the [COD & Guard/Reserve Intake Audit Checklist](/checklists/cod-and-guard-reserve-intake-audit)).*
1. Chronological Statutory & Regulatory Architecture (1944–Present)

Under `38 U.S.C. § 101(2)`, basic eligibility as a `"veteran"` requires discharge or release `"under conditions other than dishonorable."` In *Garvey v. Wilkie*, `972 F.3d 1333, 1337–41 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`, the Federal Circuit confirmed that `38 U.S.C. § 5303(a)` sets mandatory **statutory** floors while `38 U.S.C. §§ 101(2) and 501(a)` empower VA to promulgate supplemental **regulatory** bars in `38 C.F.R. § 3.12(d)`.

rows: *Servicemen's Readjustment Act of 1944* ("G.I. Bill"), `Pub. L. 78-346, §§ 300–301` (`58 Stat. 284, 286`, June 22, 1944); `1946` VA regs (`11 FR 8731`)

• **`§ 300`:** Enacted the original five statutory bars—conscientious objector refusing duty/uniform/orders, sentence of a general court-martial (`GCM`), officer resignation for the good of the service, deserter, and alien requesting release during hostilities—while carving out the statutory **insanity exception**. · • **`§ 301`:** Created military Discharge Review Boards (`DRBs`, ancestor of `10 U.S.C. § 1553`). Simultaneously, VA codified the administrative COD bars (`escape trial by GCM`, `mutiny/spying`, `moral turpitude`, `willful and persistent misconduct`, and `aggravated homosexual acts`).

• Codified `"under conditions other than dishonorable"` in **`38 U.S.C. § 101(2)`**, retirement-without-break protection in **`38 U.S.C. § 101(18)`** (paired with regulatory `38 C.F.R. § 3.13(a)–(b)` conditional-discharge rules), and statutory bars + insanity (`§ 3.354`) in **`former 38 U.S.C. § 3103(a)–(b)`** (see [Three-Era Statutory Crosswalk](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk)). · • **Pre-Oct. 8, 1977 Upgrade Rule (`former § 3.12(f)`, `now § 3.12(g)`):** Any regular `10 U.S.C. § 1553` DRB upgrade to Honorable or General issued **before October 8, 1977** set aside `(c)` and `(d)` bars **except `(c)(2)` (`GCM`)** and `1977 SDRP` / Proclamation `4313` upgrades.

Enacted four transformative changes alongside the Carter-era Vietnam `SDRP` / Proclamation `4313` clemency review: · 1. **Added the `6th` Statutory Bar (`former § 3103(a)`, `now § 5303(a)` / `§ 3.12(c)(6)`):** Barred benefits for an OTH discharge issued for **continuous AWOL of `>= 180 days`**, *unless* VA finds **"compelling circumstances"** warranting the prolonged absence. · 2. **Post-Oct. 8, 1977 `DRB` Gate (`former § 3103(e)(1)–(2)`, `now § 5303(e)(1)–(2)` / `§ 3.12(h)–(i)`):** Restricted `10 U.S.C. § 1553` DRB upgrades issued **on or after October 8, 1977** (`§ 5303(e)(1)` / `§ 3.12(h)`) and `SDRP` programs (`§ 5303(e)(2)` / `§ 3.12(i)`) so DRB upgrades set aside **`(d)` regulatory bars ONLY (never `(c)` statutory bars!)**, and only if issued on an individual case basis under published, historically consistent uniform standards (`10 U.S.C. § 1552` BCMR upgrades under `§ 3.12(f)` remained conclusive over *both* `(c)` and `(d)`!). · 3. **Multi-Enlistment Unconditional-Discharge Rescue (`Pub. L. 95-126, § 3`, `91 Stat. 1108` -> `38 U.S.C. § 101(18)(B)` & `38 C.F.R. § 3.13(c)`):** Statutory safeguard deeming a service member **unconditionally discharged or released** upon completing an obligated enlistment where an intervening reenlistment prevented issuance of a `DD-214`. · 4. **Chapter 17 Healthcare (`Pub. L. 95-126, § 2`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.360`) & Oct. 1, 1982 `ELS` (`§ 3.12(l)(1)`):** Preserved Chapter 17 care for non-`§ 5303(a)`/`BCD` line-of-duty disabilities and made **Entry Level Separations (`ELS`)** automatically "under conditions other than dishonorable."

• **`Pub. L. 102-40` (May 7, 1991)** renumbered `former 38 U.S.C. § 3103` to **`38 U.S.C. § 5303`** (`Pub. L. 102-83` conformed Secretary references Aug. 6, 1991). · • CAVC and Federal Circuit decisions defined `§ 3.12(d)(4)` minor-offense protections (*Cropper*, *Stringham*), broad non-criminal `§ 3.354` insanity (*Zang*, *Gardner*, `VAOPGCPREC 20-97`), GCM clemency limits (`VAOPGCPREC 10-96`), and `§ 3.12(d)` validity (*Garvey*).
**Final Rule, `89 FR 32361–32373`** (`RIN 2900-AQ95`, proposed July 10, 2020 at `85 FR 41471`; RFI Sept. 9, 2021 at `86 FR 50513`; **published Apr. 26, 2024, effective June 25, 2024**)

• Retitled `§ 3.12` (*Benefit eligibility based on character of discharge*); **eliminated former `§ 3.12(d)(5)`** (homosexual acts); bifurcated `§ 3.12(d)` into `(d)(1)` (non-exempt) and `(d)(2)` (exempt); replaced subjective minor-offense guesswork in `(d)(2)(ii)` with **objective `2-year` / `5-year` *Manual for Courts-Martial* (`MCM`) spacing and punishment rules**; created unified **`§ 3.12(e)` Compelling Circumstances Exception** covering `(c)(6)` AWOL, `(d)(2)(i)` moral turpitude, and `(d)(2)(ii)` willful & persistent misconduct; and redesignated former `(e)–(k)` as **`(f)–(l)`**. *(No subsequent 2025 or 2026 NPRM or IFR has altered `§ 3.12`).*

blocks.text: 2. Clause-by-Clause Diff: Pre-June 25, 2024 § 3.12(a)–(k) vs. Post-June 25, 2024 § 3.12(a)–(l)

*(Link to [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.12, 3.13, 3.354, 3.400(g), 3.6 & 3.301 (Character of Discharge Evolution, Insanity, Upgrades, ADT/IADT & Line of Duty)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.12-3.13-3.354-cod-insanity) for verbatim regulatory text blocks).*

rows: **Heading:** `§ 3.12 Benefit eligibility based on character of discharge.`
Clarifies that VA determines Title 38 benefit eligibility ("Honorable for VA Purposes" / `HVAP`) without altering the military `DD-214` itself.
Replaces `"veteran"` with `"former service member"` prior to establishing status; Honorable and General (Under Honorable Conditions) discharges remain binding unless a statutory bar in `(c)` applies.

Substantively unchanged (`38 U.S.C. § 5303(b)`): if the former service member was **insane (`§ 3.354`)** at the time of committing the offense(s) leading to discharge, **ALL statutory `(c)` and regulatory `(d)` bars are defeated**—including a General Court-Martial!
Unchanged (`38 U.S.C. § 5303(a)`): conscientious objector who refused to perform military duty, wear the uniform, or comply with lawful orders.

Unchanged (`38 U.S.C. § 5303(a)`): discharge/dismissal by **sentence of a General Court-Martial (`GCM`)** (includes Dishonorable Discharge, Officer Dismissal, or a Bad-Conduct Discharge adjudged by a *General* Court-Martial—**NOT** a *Special* Court-Martial `BCD`!).
Unchanged (`38 U.S.C. § 5303(a)`): resignation by an **officer** for the good of the service.
Unchanged (`38 U.S.C. § 5303(a)`): discharged/released as a deserter (requires affirmative record proof of intent to remain away permanently under Art. 85, UCMJ, not mere AWOL).
Unchanged (`38 U.S.C. § 5303(a)`; cross-referencing `§ 3.7(b)`): alien during hostilities where affirmatively shown the service member requested release.

Pre-2024 `(c)(6)(i)–(iii)` housed narrow AWOL-only compelling-circumstances factors directly inside `(c)(6)`. Post-June 25, 2024 **`(c)(6)(i)`** points directly to the expanded **`§ 3.12(e)`** compelling-circumstances framework; **`(c)(6)(ii)`** preserves pre-Oct. 8, 1977 upgrade rules.
**`§ 3.12(d)(1)`** *(Undesirable discharge to escape trial by GCM)*
**`§ 3.12(d)(1)(i)`** *(Discharge in lieu of trial by GCM)*

Grouped under **`(d)(1)` (*Compelling circumstances exception is NOT applicable for*)**. Modernizes `"undesirable discharge"` to `"discharge under other than honorable conditions or its equivalent in lieu of trial by general court-martial"` (e.g., Army Ch. 10 / USMC SOTS **only** when charges were referred to or threatened with a **GCM**, *not* a Special Court-Martial!).
**`§ 3.12(d)(3)`** *(Offense involving moral turpitude — generally felony conviction; **NO** compelling-circumstances exception)*

Moved into **`(d)(2)` (*Compelling circumstances exception IS applicable for*)**. Retains `"includes, generally, conviction of a felony"` *(Note: at `89 FR 32363–32365`, VA explicitly **declined** to finalize its `85 FR 41471` proposed standalone moral-turpitude definition so as not to widen the bar, while unlocking full `§ 3.12(e)` mitigation!)*.
**`§ 3.12(d)(4)`** *(Willful and persistent misconduct — subjective minor-offense proviso; **NO** compelling-circumstances exception)*
**`§ 3.12(d)(2)(ii)`** *(Willful and persistent misconduct — **objective `2-yr` / `5-yr` MCM thresholds + `§ 3.12(e)` exception!**)*

**Two massive liberalizations:** · 1. **Objective `MCM` Definition & Spacing:** Defines **"minor misconduct"** as an offense whose maximum *Manual for Courts-Martial* (`MCM`) punishment if tried by GCM **would NOT include a dishonorable discharge or confinement `> 1 year`**. A single offense is *never* persistent; persistence requires: `(A)` two minor offenses within **`2 years`**, `(B)` a minor offense within **`2 years`** of a more serious offense, or `(C)` two more serious offenses within **`5 years`**. · 2. **Full `§ 3.12(e)` Mitigation:** Even if spacing is met, `(d)(2)(ii)` is overcome by `§ 3.12(e)` compelling circumstances!
Completely repealed as obsolete and discriminatory (`89 FR 32366, 32372`); any actual non-consensual assault/coercion is evaluated neutrally under `(c)(2)`, `(d)(1)(i)`, or `(d)(2)`.

Unified mitigation test governing `(c)(6)` AWOL, `(d)(2)(i)` moral turpitude, and `(d)(2)(ii)` willful & persistent misconduct: · • **`(e)(1)` Service Quality/Length:** Service exclusive of the AWOL/misconduct period. · • **`(e)(2)(i)–(vii)` Seven Mitigating Reasons:** `(i)` **Mental or cognitive impairment** (clinical diagnosis *or* evidence that **could later be medically determined** to show PTSD, depression, bipolar, schizophrenia, **substance use disorder**, ADHD, impulsivity, or cognitive disability); `(ii)` **Physical health** (trauma / **medication side effects**); `(iii)` **Combat or overseas hardship**; `(iv)` **Sexual abuse/assault (`MST`)**; `(v)` **Duress, coercion, or desperation**; `(vi)` **Family / third-party obligations**; `(vii)` **Age, education, cultural background, and judgmental maturity**. · • **`(e)(3)` Valid Substantive UCMJ Defense.**
Redesignated `(e) -> (f)` with updated cross-references. Honorable or General upgrade by a `§ 1552` BCMR/BCNR sets aside `(c)` and `(d)` bars conclusively.

Redesignated `(f) -> (g)` with updated reference to `(i)(1)–(3)`. Pre-Oct. 8, 1977 `§ 1553` DRB upgrades to Honorable/General set aside `(c)` and `(d)` bars **except `(c)(2)` (`GCM`)** and `(i)(1)–(3)` special programs.

Redesignated `(g) -> (h)`. Post-Oct. 8, 1977 `§ 1553` DRB upgrades set aside **`(d)` bars ONLY (not `(c)` statutory bars)** provided `(h)(1)–(3)` individual-review and uniform-published-historical-standard rules are met.
Redesignated `(h) -> (i)`. Clemency/SDRP upgrades require an affirmative `Pub. L. 95-126` uniform-standard review.
Redesignated `(i) -> (j)` with updated reference to paragraphs `(h)` and `(i)`.

Redesignated `(k) -> (l)`: `(l)(1)` **Entry Level Separation (`ELS`)** = automatic other-than-dishonorable; `(l)(2)` **Void enlistment** & `(l)(3)` **Dropped from rolls** = reviewed under `(c)` and `(d)`.

blocks.text: 3. Bitemporal & Effective-Date Trap Matrix: 89 FR 32361 Floor vs. Five Retroactive Pre-2024 Pathways

lines: **THE JUNE 25, 2024 LIBERALIZING-LAW CEILING (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(g)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)`):** Under the applicability clause of `89 FR 32361` (`Apr. 26, 2024`) and `38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)`, when a previously final COD denial is overcome **solely** because of the liberalized June 25, 2024 criteria (e.g., applying `§ 3.12(e)` compelling circumstances to a `(d)(2)` bar or applying the new `2-year`/`5-year` MCM spacing rules), **the effective date CANNOT precede June 25, 2024** (Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114))! Even if the veteran files within 1 year of June 25, 2024 (`§ 3.114(a)(1)`) or files years later (`§ 3.114(a)(3)` `1-year` lookback), `§ 5110(g)` forbids any award date prior to the effective date of the liberalizing regulation (**June 25, 2024**), and *George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` / `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)` bars citing `89 FR 32361` as CUE against a pre-June 25, 2024 decision!

blocks.text: Whenever a veteran has an earlier denied claim or prolonged disability stretching back years or decades before June 25, 2024, **never settle for a June 25, 2024 effective date** without screening all **five retroactive pre-2024 pathways** below ([Procedural Vehicles for Piercing Finality](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality)):

headers: How It Unlocks Pre-June 25, 2024 Retroactive Back Pay
rows: Reopens any prior final COD denial as a change in law (`38 C.F.R. § 3.2501`). If filed `June 25, 2024 – June 25, 2025` (or pending on June 25, 2024), effective **June 25, 2024** (`§ 3.114(a)(1)`). If filed after June 25, 2025, effective up to **`1 year` prior to receipt of the reopening claim** (`§ 3.114(a)(3)`), **never earlier than June 25, 2024**.

`38 U.S.C. § 101(18)(B)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.13(a)–(c)`; *Holmes v. Brown*, `10 Vet. App. 38 (1997)` *(note: pre-VCAA preponderance threshold abrogated in favor of `§ 5107(b)` equipoise by Newman v. McDonough, `35 Vet. App. 310 (2022)`)*

Whereas `§ 3.13(a)–(b)` treats an uncompleted-obligation discharge as `"conditional,"` **`38 U.S.C. § 101(18)(B)` and `§ 3.13(c)`** rescue a veteran who completed an initial obligated tour (or discharged early under `(a)(3)` to reenlist) without a physical break in service (`DD-214` Block 18 `"Immediate Reenlistment"`)—deeming the earlier period terminated by an **unconditional discharge or release** under conditions other than dishonorable, insulating all Period 1 disabilities from a later OTH/BCD in Period 2 (absent `§ 6104` treason/subversion forfeiture)! Overlooking an undisputed back-to-back reenlistment in the C-file is **textbook RO/BVA CUE (`§ 3.105(a)` / `§ 7111`)** back to the original denied claim!
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** *(especially via `§ 3.156(c)` or open/pending claim)*

`§ 5303(b)` has been positive statutory law since `1944`! Under *Zang*, *Gardner*, and [`VAOPGCPREC 20-97`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index), VA insanity is **broad and non-criminal** (rejecting *M'Naghten* right-vs.-wrong tests and requiring no direct causal nexus so long as disease-driven behavioral deviation existed concurrently with the misconduct). Associating unobtained brig/stockade, inpatient psychiatric, or unit records under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)`** carries the insanity grant—and full compensation—all the way back to the **original denied VA claim**!
`38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)`; *Hamill v. Collins*, `166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 4, 2026)`

*Hamill* **literally arose from a veteran's unaddressed AMA request to reopen a COD bar** ([Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log))! Because `38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)` abolished implicit denials for all AMA decisions (`>= Feb. 19, 2019`), any post-Feb. 19, 2019 claim or COD reopening issue that VA silently omitted or brushed past without explicit `§ 5104(b)` findings **remains legally pending and unadjudicated**—allowing `89 FR 32361` to govern the still-open claim from June 25, 2024 *and* pre-2024 merits (`§ 3.354`, *Cropper*, `§ 3.13`) to pay back to the original pending AMA claim date!
`Former 38 C.F.R. § 3.12(d)(4)` (`pre-June 25, 2024`); *Cropper v. Brown*, `6 Vet. App. 450, 452–53 (1994)`; *Stringham v. Brown*, `8 Vet. App. 445 (1995)`
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** *(Judged strictly under pre-2024 text)*

Even before June 25, 2024, `former § 3.12(d)(4)` stated that a discharge for a *minor offense* was **not** willful and persistent misconduct if service was otherwise honest, faithful, and meritorious (*Cropper*), and `former § 3.12(c)(2)`/`(d)(1)` applied **only** to *General* Courts-Martial, **never** *Special* Courts-Martial! Where a pre-2024 rater committed an undebatable legal error under **extant pre-2024 law** (e.g., treating a Special Court-Martial `BCD` or an `ELS` under `former § 3.12(k)(1)` as an automatic statutory bar), attack via `§ 3.105(a)` / `§ 7111` CUE (completing the [Board CUE Pre-Filing Gate](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate) first).

• **Standard Upgrade Effective Date (`§ 5110(i)` / `§ 3.400(g)(1)–(3)`):** For an *original* VA claim filed within `1 year` of the upgrade taking effect, effective on the date the `DRB`/`BCMR` application (`DD-293`/`DD-149`) was filed with the service department (`§ 5110(i)`; `§ 3.400(g)(1)`); for a *reopened disallowed* VA claim, effective on the **latest** of `(1)` date the military-upgrade application was filed, `(2)` date of receipt of the disallowed VA claim, or `(3)` `1 year` prior to VA reopening (`§ 3.400(g)(1)–(3)`). · • **`§ 3.156(c)` Accelerator:** If the `BCMR`/`DRB` proceeding or archival FOIA also uncovers **preexisting official service department records** (missing STRs, inpatient charts, CID/NCIS MST files, unit logs) never associated during an earlier VA denial ([Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon)), plead **`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)(3)`** alongside `§ 3.400(g)` to pierce `(g)(3)`'s 1-year cap and reach back to the **original VA claim date**!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: What Changed on June 25, 2024 in VA's Character of Discharge Rules (Before-and-After Guide to 38 C.F.R. § 3.12)
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: For sixty years before June 25, 2024, VA's Character of Discharge regulation (38 C.F.R. § 3.12) gave raters broad, subjective power to bar Veterans with Other Than Honorable (OTH) discharges for 'willful and persistent misconduct' or 'moral turpitude'—and allowed 'compelling circumstances' consideration ONLY for continuous AWOL of 180 days or more. Effective June 25, 2024 (89 FR 32361), VA dramatically modernized § 3.12: it repealed the obsolete homosexual-acts bar entirely, set an objective 2-year / 5-year spacing and Manual for Courts-Martial severity test for 'willful and persistent misconduct,' and created a new § 3.12(e) 'compelling circumstances' exception weighing physical/mental health (PTSD, TBI, MST), combat hardship, age, and length of service for BOTH prolonged AWOL and regulatory misconduct bars.
record_clues: A pre-June 25, 2024 VA denial finding your OTH discharge 'dishonorable for VA purposes' due to 'willful and persistent misconduct' based on minor or widely spaced Article 15s, or due to 'moral turpitude.'

Service or post-service records showing behavioral changes after combat, head trauma, Military Sexual Trauma, or family crisis that were never weighed as 'compelling circumstances' under the old rule.
A separation under old 'homosexual policy' or aggravated acts provisions (repealed from § 3.12(d)), or a back-to-back reenlistment overlooked under § 3.13.
important_cautions: Why Reopening vs. CUE Matters Here: Because the June 25, 2024 overhaul (published April 26, 2024 at 89 FR 32361) is a prospective liberalizing rule, previously denied Veterans can file a new Supplemental Claim (VA Form 20-0995) right away—but the 2024 rule cannot be used to claim Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) on a pre-June 25, 2024 decision, and compensation granted solely under the 2024 change cannot take effect earlier than June 25, 2024 (§ 3.114(a)).

Unfinalized 2020 Proposal Was Rejected: In its July 10, 2020 proposed rule (85 FR 41471), VA floated a new standalone regulatory text defining 'moral turpitude,' which VA expressly declined to adopt in the 2024 final rule—leaving VAOPGCPREC 6-87 governing moral turpitude.

Statutory & Non-Mitigable Bars Remain Excluded From § 3.12(e): General Court-Martial sentences (§ 3.12(c)(2)), OTH discharges in lieu of General Court-Martial (§ 3.12(d)(1)(i)), mutiny/spying, desertion, conscientious objector bars, and officer resignations for the good of the service are NOT eligible for § 3.12(e) compelling circumstances (check § 3.13 prior enlistments, § 3.354(b) insanity, or § 1552 BCMR relief instead).
questions_for_representative: Was my pre-June 25, 2024 Character of Discharge denial based on a category—like 'willful and persistent misconduct' or 'moral turpitude'—that is now eligible for 'compelling circumstances' review under new 38 C.F.R. § 3.12(e)?
Looking at the dates and maximum punishments of my minor UCMJ offenses, would they even count as 'persistent' misconduct under the new objective 2-year / 5-year rules in § 3.12(d)(2)(ii)?

Alongside a post-June 25, 2024 Supplemental Claim, do I also have an earlier honorable enlistment under § 3.13 or newly associated service records under § 3.156(c) that could support an even earlier effective date?

title: VASRD Historical Diff: Mental Disorders & PTSD (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125–4.130, DC 9400–9440)
cFileTriggers: 1960s–1980s combat veterans denied for 'personality disorder', 'immature personality', or 'nervousness' prior to/shortly after 1980 PTSD recognition
Pre-Nov 7, 1996 mental health reductions violating § 3.344
Post-Nov 7, 1996 ratings treating § 4.130 symptom list as an exhaustive checklist or ignoring suicidal ideation (Bankhead = 70% floor trigger)
killSwitches: Pleading Mauerhan / Bankhead suicidal-ideation 70% CUE on a pre-November 7, 1996 decision (suicidal ideation entered the § 4.130 70% symptom criteria on Nov 7, 1996!)
Assuming proposed RIN 2900-AQ82 (10% minimum floor / domain model) is active law (NOT finalized as of late 2026)

toc.text: Historical Evolution Matrix (1945 – 2026)

blocks.text: Mental health evaluations evolved through four distinct historical phases (plus a pending unfinalized proposal). For the complete Body System `14` reference (`DC 9201–9521`, `§ 4.129` `50%` traumatic-discharge rule, and Eating Disorders `DC 9520–9521`), see [VASRD System 14 Historical Diff: Mental Disorders Complete Reference (1946–2026), Former § 4.132 Four-Era Evolution, § 4.129 Traumatic Discharge 50% Rule, § 4.130 Precedents & Eating Disorders (DC 9201–9521)](/cfr/modules/14-mental-disorders-4.125-4.130) and [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125–4.130 Mental Disorders, Traumatic Stress (§ 4.129), Eating Disorders (DC 9520–9521) & Former § 4.132 Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.132-mental-disorders-pre-1996). Because subjective evaluation of psychiatric severity involves weighing evidence, **pure percentage CUEs (`30%` vs. `50%`) are very difficult**, whereas **unlawful reductions (`§ 3.344`)**, **`former § 4.16(c)` `1989–1996` `100%` mental CUEs**, **`§ 3.156(c)` JSRRC/combat stressor reconsiderations**, and **unadjudicated TDIU (`Roberson`/`Rice`)** are massive winners.
Historical Evolution Matrix (1945 – 2026)

rows: **1945 VASRD / DSM-I & DSM-II:** Separate schedules for Psychoses (`DC 9200s`) vs. Psychoneurotic Disorders (`DC 9400` anxiety reaction, `9405` depressive reaction). **No PTSD code existed!**

Psychoneuroses often capped below `100%` in early versions unless psychotic/total industrial incapacity; evaluated via **social and industrial inadaptability** (`none 0%`, `mild 10%`, `definite 30%`, `considerable 50%`, `severe 70%`, `total 100%` after 1960s harmonization).

**Opportunity:** Combat veterans misdiagnosed with "anxiety neurosis" or "personality disorder" where missing combat records (`§ 3.156(c)`) later verify trauma, OR psychoses (`DC 9200s`) manifesting within **1 year of separation** (`38 C.F.R. § 3.309(a)` chronic disease presumption—Note: **only psychoses**, not neuroses/PTSD, are `§ 3.309(a)` 1-year chronic diseases!).

**DSM-III (1980) / DSM-III-R (1988):** Added **`DC 9411` (Post-traumatic stress disorder)** to `38 C.F.R. § 4.132`. Separate rating tables remained for Psychotic vs. Organic vs. Psychoneurotic (`DC 9400–9411`).

**Critical Trap:** Do **NOT** cite modern `§ 4.130` symptoms (like "suicidal ideation" or "panic attacks more than once a week") for pre-Nov. 7, 1996 decisions! Pre-Nov. 7, 1996 `§ 4.132` hinged on `definite / considerable / severe` industrial impairment. **Best Weapon:** `§ 3.344` unlawful reductions of `50%/70%/100%` PTSD ratings and `§ 3.157(b)` VAMC PTSD hospitalizations!

**DSM-IV (`38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125, 4.130`):** Unified **ALL** mental disorders (except eating disorders `DC 9520–9521`) into **one General Rating Formula for Mental Disorders** (`0/10/30/50/70/100%`); referenced **GAF (Global Assessment of Functioning)** scores.

Introduced non-exhaustive symptom examples (*Mauerhan*, 2002): · • **`30%`:** Occasional decrease in work efficiency. · • **`50%`:** Reduced reliability and productivity; panic attacks `>1/wk`. · • **`70%`:** Deficiencies in **most areas** (work, school, family, judgment, thinking, or mood), **suicidal ideation** (*Bankhead*!), obsessional rituals, near-continuous panic/depression. · • **`100%`:** Total occupational and social impairment.

**Key Precedents:** *Mauerhan* (symptoms are examples, not rigid checklists); *Vazquez-Claudio* (symptom severity/frequency/duration drive occupational impairment); *Bankhead v. Shulkin* (presence of **suicidal ideation** strongly points to at least `70%`, though weighing nuances normally make *Bankhead* a direct-appeal remand smash rather than CUE).
**DSM-5 (`38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125, 4.130`):** Adopted DSM-5 diagnostic criteria and **eliminated GAF scores**; renumbered several `94xx` categories (`DC 9411` PTSD unchanged).
**Identical `0 / 10 / 30 / 50 / 70 / 100%` General Rating Formula** text to the Nov. 7, 1996 rule!

Also cross-check **July 13, 2010 PTSD Stressor Liberalization (`38 C.F.R. § 3.304(f)(3)`, `75 FR 39843` as corrected at `75 FR 41092`)** (fear of hostile military/terrorist activity confirmed by VA psychiatrist)—liberalizing rule (`§ 3.114`) effective no earlier than July 13, 2010 unless `§ 3.156(c)` unit records apply!

Proposed 5-domain WHODAS model (`cognition`, `interpersonal`, `task completion`, `life activities`, `self-care`) with **`10%` minimum floor** and elimination of total-unemployability bar to `100%` while working.
Never apply `RIN 2900-AQ82` to any current or historical claim; monitor Federal Register for any future Final Rule publication.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: PTSD & Anxiety Ratings (DC 9400–9440): Pre-1980 Labels, the 1996 Checklist Trap & Stabilized Protections
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (Diagnostic Code 9411) was not added to the psychiatric manual (DSM-III) or VA's rating schedule until 1980, meaning many Vietnam, Korean, and WWII combat Veterans were originally diagnosed in the 1960s and 1970s with 'anxiety reaction,' 'combat fatigue,' 'nervousness,' or mislabeled with a noncompensable 'personality disorder.' This focused historical diff explains how Diagnostic Codes 9400–9440 evolved across the 1980, February 3, 1988, November 7, 1996, and August 4, 2014 updates—and why VA raters cannot treat the symptom list in 38 C.F.R. § 4.130 as a rigid all-or-nothing checklist.
record_clues: 1960s–1980s military separation or VA rating sheets denying 'nervousness' or 'immature/inadequate personality' despite combat awards, casualty exposure, or post-combat nightmares and hypervigilance.

A post-November 7, 1996 Rating Decision denying a 50% or 70% mental rating because the Veteran did not have every single example symptom listed in 38 C.F.R. § 4.130 (violating Mauerhan v. Principi), or overlooking documented suicidal ideation.

A reduction of a PTSD or anxiety rating held for 5 or more years based on a single routine C&P exam without proving sustained improvement under the ordinary conditions of life and work (38 C.F.R. § 3.344).
Combat decorations, unit deck logs, morning reports, or hostile-activity deployments that were never associated with the file when an older PTSD claim was denied (38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)).
important_cautions: Exact November 7, 1996 symptom date: suicidal ideation and today's occupational/social symptom examples were enacted in 38 C.F.R. § 4.130 effective November 7, 1996 (published October 8, 1996 at 61 FR 52695). You cannot cite post-1996 symptom examples or later cases like Mauerhan or Bankhead to claim Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) in a final pre-November 7, 1996 decision.

Unfinalized proposal warning: VA's February 15, 2022 proposed rule to replace the § 4.130 formula with a 5-domain model and 10% minimum floor (87 FR 8498, RIN 2900-AQ82) is still an unfinalized proposed rule and is NOT enacted law.

Look for missing official military records first: if combat citations, unit action reports, or inpatient psychiatric ward charts were missing when an older PTSD claim was denied, submitting official service department records under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) avoids the strict legal bars of CUE.

Under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c), once the Board of Veterans' Appeals issues a final decision on the merits of a CUE motion on a specific prior Board issue, no further CUE motions are permitted on that Board issue.
questions_for_representative: If VA denied me decades ago for 'nervousness' or 'personality disorder' before PTSD was recognized, do newly obtained military unit records or combat logs trigger retroactive reconsideration under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)?
Did VA treat the symptom examples in 38 C.F.R. § 4.130 as a mandatory checklist instead of evaluating the overall frequency, severity, and duration of my occupational and social impairment?
If VA lowered my long-term PTSD or anxiety percentage after 5 or more years at the same level, did VA violate the stabilized-rating rules of 38 C.F.R. § 3.344 (making the reduction void)?
If my 70% PTSD or anxiety rating prevents me from holding substantially gainful employment, has VA adjudicated entitlement to a 100% payment rate via TDIU under 38 C.F.R. § 4.16(a)?

title: VASRD Historical Diff: Spine & Musculoskeletal Joints (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.40, 4.45, 4.59, 4.71a)
cFileTriggers: Post-Sept 26, 2003 spine DBQ showing forward flexion <= 30 degrees (40% lumbar!) or ankylosis while rater assigned 10% or 20%
Post-Sept 26, 2003 spine exam documenting lower/upper extremity radiculopathy omitted from rating code sheet
Painful motion documented on joint exam while rater assigned 0% noncompensable (violates 38 C.F.R. § 4.59 minimum compensable rating!)
Dual knee ratings ignoring separate DC 5257 instability + DC 5260 flexion + DC 5261 extension (VAOPGCPREC 23-97 & 9-98)
killSwitches: Citing goniometer degree cutoffs (e.g., forward flexion <= 60 degrees = 20%) for a spine decision rendered BEFORE September 26, 2003
Pleading Correia / Sharp inadequate C&P exam testing as CUE (exam inadequacy is a duty-to-assist error barred as CUE by Cook v. Principi)

toc.text: 1. Spine Evolution: Pre-Sept. 26, 2003 vs. Post-Sept. 26, 2003 (DC 5235–5244)
2. February 7, 2021 Musculoskeletal Overhaul (85 FR 76453)
3. Three Classic Orthopedic Code-Sheet CUEs (38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a))

blocks.text: Orthopedic claims turn on three VASRD overhauls—**September 23, 2002 (Interim Spine IVDS `DC 5293`, `67 FR 54345`)**, **September 26, 2003 (Full Spine General Rating Formula, `68 FR 51454`)**, and **February 7, 2021 (Musculoskeletal System, `85 FR 76453`, corrected Feb. 4, 2021 at `86 FR 8142`)**—plus timeless functional-loss and anti-pyramiding rules that generate clean **math/code-sheet CUEs**. For verbatim historical spine text across all three eras, see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 4.71a Spine Evolution (Former DC 5285–5295 vs. Modern DC 5235–5243)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.71a-spine-evolution); for complete `DC 5000–5284` joint, arthritis, prosthetic-implant, amputation, and foot/knee stacking schedules, see [VASRD System 01 Historical Diff: Musculoskeletal Joints, Arthritis, Prosthetic Implants, Amputations & Foot/Knee Stacking (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.40–4.73, DC 5000–5284)](/cfr/modules/01-musculoskeletal-joints-arthritis-implants-4.71a) and [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.40, 4.45, 4.59, 4.67–4.69 & § 4.71a Joints, Arthritis, Prosthetics, Knee & Foot Evolution (Pre- vs. Post-Feb. 7, 2021)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.71a-joints-arthritis-pre-and-post-2021).
1. Spine Evolution: Pre-Sept. 26, 2003 vs. Post-Sept. 26, 2003 (DC 5235–5244)

*(Note: On Sept. 26, 2003, old spine codes `DC 5285–5295` were renumbered to `DC 5235–5243`! When `85 FR 76453` Nov. 30, 2020 initially attempted to reuse `DC 5285` for Plantar Fasciitis, VA formally corrected Plantar Fasciitis to **`DC 5269`** at `86 FR 8142` Feb. 4, 2021 so `5285` remained reserved for legacy vertebral-fracture corporate records!)*

headers: Era 2: Sept. 26, 2003 – Present *(General Rating Formula for Spine, `DC 5235–5244`)*
rows: **Lumbar / Cervical Limitation of Motion & Vertebral Fracture**

Old **`DC 5292`** (Lumbar), **`DC 5291`** (Dorsal `0/10/10%`), & **`DC 5290`** (Cervical) used qualitative adjectives: · • **Lumbar (`5292`):** Slight `10%` / Moderate `20%` / Severe `40%` (Ankylosis `5289`: Fav `40%` / Unfav `50%`) · • **Cervical (`5290`):** Slight `10%` / Moderate `20%` / Severe `30%` · • **Vertebral Fracture (`former DC 5285`):** Added **`+10%` for demonstrable deformity of vertebral body** on X-ray!

**Objective Goniometer ROM Cutoffs:** · • **`10%`:** Thoracolumbar flexion `>60° to 85°` (Cervical `>30° to 40°`), combined ROM, muscle spasm/guarding/localized tenderness not altering gait. · • **`20%`:** Thoracolumbar flexion **`>30° to 60°`** (Cervical `>15° to 30°`), OR combined ROM `<=120°`, OR spasm/guarding severe enough to cause **abnormal gait or abnormal spinal contour**. · • **`40%` (Thoracolumbar) / `30%` (Cervical):** Forward flexion **`30° or less`** (Cervical `15° or less`), OR favorable ankylosis. · • **`50%` / `40%`:** Unfavorable ankylosis of entire thoracolumbar / cervical spine (`100%` whole spine).

Old **`DC 5293`:** Rated `0/10/20/40/60%` based on recurring attacks, sciatic radiation, and mild/moderate/severe/pronounced persistent symptoms (**included neurologic manifestations inside `5293`** unless rated higher separately!).

**`DC 5243` ( updated Sept. 23, 2002 & Sept. 26, 2003):** Rated **EITHER** under the General Rating Formula (ROM) **OR** on total duration of **incapacitating episodes** requiring **physician-prescribed bed rest** over past 12 months (`>=1 wk = 10%`, `>=2 wks = 20%`, `>=4 wks = 40%`, `>=6 wks = 60%`), whichever yields the higher overall result (*Chavis*, 2021)!
Often bundled into `DC 5293` IVDS prior to 2002/2003 unless peripheral nerve rating alone exceeded IVDS.

**Note (1) Mandatory Separate Rating:** **ANY associated objective neurologic abnormality** (e.g., lower-extremity sciatic `DC 8520` / femoral `DC 8526` radiculopathy, bowel/bladder sphincter impairment) **MUST be rated separately**!

blocks.text: 2. February 7, 2021 Musculoskeletal Overhaul (85 FR 76453)

rows: Subjective grades of recurrent subluxation or lateral instability: **Slight `10%`**, **Moderate `20%`**, **Severe `30%`**.

Objective surgical/brace tiers: · • **`10%`:** Sprain/incomplete ligament tear/repair with persistent instability **without** prescription of assistive device/bracing. · • **`20%`:** Persistent instability **with** physician-prescribed brace *or* assistive device (`cane/walker`). · • **`30%`:** Persistent instability requiring **BOTH** prescribed brace **AND** assistive device (or unrepairable multi-ligament instability).
**12 months** (`1 year`) of temporary `100%` convalescent rating post-arthroplasty (`13 months` pre-2015 calculations), then `30%` minimum.

Reduced temporary `100%` post-surgical convalescence from 1 year down to **4 months** following arthroplasty; retained **`30%` minimum** evaluation thereafter (`50%/60%+` for chronic severe residuals).
Rated by analogy (typically `DC 5276` flatfoot `0/10/20/30/50%` or `DC 5284` other foot injury).

Dedicated **`DC 5269`** (`86 FR 8142`, Feb. 4, 2021, eff. Feb. 7, 2021): `10%` (unilateral/bilateral otherwise), `20%` (unilateral, no relief from both non-surgical & surgical treatment, or surgical non-candidate per Note 2), `30%` (bilateral, no relief from both non-surgical & surgical treatment, or surgical non-candidate per Note 2; `40%` actual loss of use of foot under `DC 5167` + `SMC(k)`!).

blocks.text: 3. Three Classic Orthopedic Code-Sheet CUEs (38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a))

items:
**Ignoring `38 C.F.R. § 4.59` Painful Motion Minimum (`0%` Joint Error):**
• Under `38 C.F.R. § 4.59` (and *Lichtenfels v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 484 (1991)` / *Burton v. Shinseki*, `25 Vet. App. 1 (2011)` / *Petitti v. McDonald*, `27 Vet. App. 415 (2015)` / *Southall-Norman v. McDonald*, `28 Vet. App. 346 (2016)`), **actually painful, unstable, or malaligned joints** supported by objective evidence of painful motion are entitled to **at least the minimum compensable rating (`10%`)** for the joint—even if goniometer flexion/extension numbers fail to hit the `10%` schedular ROM cutoff! When a C&P exam explicitly records objective painful motion of a shoulder (`20%` minimum under `DC 5201`!), hip, knee, or ankle, and the rater assigns `0%`, audit immediately for **RO CUE** *(Note `§ 20.1403(e)` / George v. McDonough bitemporal gate: plain-text arthritic painful-motion CUE is safe since 1946/Lichtenfels, whereas non-arthritis `§ 4.59` CUE predating Burton (2011) or `DC 5276` CUE predating Southall-Norman (2016) is Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE))*!

**Failure to Stack Knee Codes (`VAOPGCPREC 23-97`, `9-98` & `9-2004`):**
• Binding VA General Counsel Opinions hold that a veteran with **both** knee instability (`DC 5257` — `VAOPGCPREC 23-97` & `9-98`) **and** painful/limited flexion (`DC 5260`) **and** limited extension (`DC 5261` — `VAOPGCPREC 9-2004` & *Lyles v. Shulkin*, `29 Vet. App. 107 (2017)`) is entitled to **separate concurrent ratings** without violating `§ 4.14` anti-pyramiding!

**Post-Sept. 26, 2003 Spine Goniometer Math Error or Omitted Radiculopathy:**
• DBQ records thoracolumbar active forward flexion of `25°` (`<= 30°` = **`40%`**) and rater mistakenly awards `20%` -> **undebatable RO CUE**.
• Post-Feb. 19, 2019 AMA spine DBQ documents sciatic radiculopathy and AMA rating decision silently omits it -> **still legally pending under *Hamill v. Collins* (2026)**!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Quick Comparison: Spine Degree Rules (2003), Joint Painful Motion & Multi-Code Knee Evaluations
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: This focused orthopedic comparison highlights the four most common rating transitions across back, neck, and joint claims under 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.40, 4.45, 4.59, and 4.71a: (1) the September 26, 2003 shift from descriptive spine codes (5285–5295) to goniometer degree cutoffs (5235–5243) plus mandatory separate nerve ratings under Note (1); (2) the rule in § 4.59 awarding at least the minimum compensable percentage whenever a joint has objective painful motion; (3) functional loss during flare-ups and repeated weight-bearing movement; and (4) separate knee ratings for instability plus limited flexion and extension.
record_clues: A post-September 26, 2003 back examination recording forward flexion of 30 degrees or less (which triggers 40% for the thoracolumbar spine) or ankylosis while the Rating Code Sheet assigned 10% or 20%.
A post-September 26, 2003 neck or back exam noting radiating nerve pain, numbness, or tingling in the arms or legs (radiculopathy) with no separate peripheral nerve code on the Rating Code Sheet.
A joint exam documenting painful motion where VA assigned a 0% noncompensable evaluation despite 38 C.F.R. § 4.59.

A knee Rating Code Sheet assigning only one code despite documented joint instability (Diagnostic Code 5257) alongside compensable loss of flexion (Diagnostic Code 5260) or extension (Diagnostic Code 5261).
important_cautions: Do not apply modern spine degree cutoffs before their effective date: the General Rating Formula for Diseases and Injuries of the Spine took effect September 26, 2003 (68 FR 51454) and cannot establish Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) in final pre-September 26, 2003 spine decisions.

Incomplete examination testing vs. CUE: if a VA examiner failed to test weight-bearing/passive/opposite-joint motion (Correia v. McDonald) or failed to estimate flare-up degree loss (Sharp v. Shulkin), that exam defect is a duty-to-assist error addressed in open claims, Supplemental Claims, or appeals—not CUE against a final decision (Cook v. Principi).

Existing ratings in force before the February 7, 2021 musculoskeletal update (85 FR 76453 / 86 FR 8142) cannot be lowered solely due to the revised schedule under 38 U.S.C. § 1155 and 38 C.F.R. § 3.951(a).

Under George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1403(e) and 20.1409(c), later judicial interpretations cannot establish CUE in older final decisions, and only one final merits CUE decision is permitted per prior Board decision issue.
questions_for_representative: Does my post-September 26, 2003 spine DBQ show flexion degrees or abnormal spinal contour that meet a higher rating tier on their face?
Did VA overlook separate Note (1) peripheral nerve ratings for sciatic, femoral, or cervical radiculopathy recorded on my spine exam?
If VA assigned 0% for an arthritic or injured joint despite documented painful motion, how does 38 C.F.R. § 4.59 apply to my claim?
Should we seek a new orthopedic examination or private medical opinion in a Supplemental Claim if my prior VA exam omitted flare-up or weight-bearing range-of-motion estimates?
