Parts 1 & 3` regulatory transitions (`1962–2026`) across five high-dollar financial domains: `(1)` increased-rating lookbacks and Intent-to-File (`ITF`) standardization (`§§ 3.155, 3.400(o)(2)`), `(2)` Legacy finality vs. AMA continuous pursuit (`§ 3.2500`), `(3)` military separation and disability severance recoupment (`§ 3.700(a)(2), (a)(3) & (a)(5)`), `(4)` the **October 18, 2018 Wartime Pension net-worth and `36-month` lookback overhaul (`83 FR 47246`, `§§ 3.274–3.279`)**, and `(5)` the **December 29, 2022 -> January 26, 2026 (`90 FR 54234`) overpayment waiver deadline alignment (`§ 1.963(b)`, `former § 1.963(b)(2)`)**.

*(For verbatim regulatory text snapshots, see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.114, 3.400, 3.2500, 3.654, 3.665, 3.700 & 3.701 (Effective Dates, Liberalizing Laws, Continuous Pursuit, Drill/Incarceration Adjustments, Severance/Separation Recoupment & Benefit Elections)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.114-3.400-3.700-effective-dates-offsets), [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.274–3.279, 3.272(g), 3.353, 3.105(h)–(i), 3.500(b), 1.963 & 1.965 (Pension Net Worth & 36-Month Lookback, Deductible Medical Expenses, Competency Due Process & Overpayment Waivers)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.274-3.279-3.353-1.965-pension-competency-waivers), and [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: Former 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.155(a) & 3.157(b) Informal Claims (Repealed March 24, 2015)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.155-3.157b-informal-claims-pre-2015). For appellate synthesis and operational workflows, consult the [`Master Effective-Date & Staged-Rating Treatise`](/docs/effective-dates-and-staged-ratings-treatise), [Playbook 20 (Offsets, `CRDP`/`CRSC` & Severance Recoupment)](/playbooks/20-backpay-offsets-crdp-crsc-severance-recoupment), [Playbook 21 (Overpayment Waivers, Competency & Wartime Pension)](/playbooks/21-overpayment-waivers-incompetency-and-wartime-pension), and the [`Award Letter & Withholding Audit Checklist`](/checklists/award-letter-and-withholding-audit-checklist)).*
1. 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.155, 3.157(b) & 3.400(o)(2): Informal Increase Triggers vs. Standardized Intent to File (1975–Present)

rows: • **`Former § 3.155(a)`:** Any written communication indicating an intent to apply and identifying the benefit sought (*Shea v. Wilkie*, `926 F.3d 1362 (Fed. Cir. 2019)`). · • **`Former § 3.157(b)`:** Any VAMC or uniformed-services outpatient examination or hospital admission report for an already SC disability (`0%` or compensable) operated **automatically** as an informal claim for increase (*Pacheco v. Gibson*, `27 Vet. App. 21 (2014) (en banc)` — **first** report showing worsening anchors pending date!).

Earliest date within **`1 year` prior** to receipt of formal or informal claim as of which worsening is factually ascertainable (*Harper v. Brown*, `10 Vet. App. 125 (1997)`; *Gaston v. Shinseki*, `605 F.3d 979 (Fed. Cir. 2010)`; *Dalton v. Nicholson*, `21 Vet. App. 23 (2007)` for TDIU).

• **Prospective Repeal:** Eliminated non-form informal claims and **repealed `§ 3.157` in its entirety** for communications/reports `>= Mar. 24, 2015` (*Sellers v. Wilkie*, `965 F.3d 1328 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`). · • **`§ 3.155(b)` ITF:** `VA Form 21-0966` (or `va.gov`/phone ITF) holds a `1-year` placeholder. · • **Single-Active-ITF Rule (`§ 3.155(b)(4)–(6)`):** Max **1 active ITF** per general benefit (`compensation`, `pension`, `survivors`); **consumed** immediately by first complete claim; duplicate ITFs before consumption are void!

Amended `§ 3.400(o)(2)` to measure earliest factually ascertainable worsening if a **"complete claim or intent to file a claim"** is received within `1 year` from such date (reaching up to `~24 months` before a timely perfected formal claim, **never** `> 1 year` before the ITF itself).
**Era 3A: `Feb. 19, 2019 – July 29, 2021`** · *(Initial AMA Exclusion of Supplemental ITFs)*
Amended `§ 3.155` introductory text (`"Other than a supplemental claim..."`) to **exclude `§ 5108` Supplemental Claims (`VA Form 20-0995`)** from the `§ 3.155(b)` ITF placeholder system.
`§ 3.400(o)(2)` continued to accept ITFs for initial/increase `VA Form 21-526EZ` claims, while VA refused ITFs for `20-0995` Supplemental Claims.
***Military-Veterans Advocacy v. Sec'y of Veterans Affairs*, `7 F.4th 1110, 1142 (Fed. Cir. July 30, 2021)`**

**JUDICIAL INVALIDATION:** Struck down `§ 3.155`'s exclusion of Supplemental Claims—**restoring `VA Form 21-0966` ITFs to `§ 5108` Supplemental Claims** (particularly `>1-year` non-continuous Supplemental Claims under `§ 5110(a)(3)` and protective post-CAVC filings!).
Both `VA Form 21-526EZ` increase claims and `VA Form 20-0995` Supplemental Claims consume and benefit from an active `§ 3.155(b)` ITF.

blocks.text: 2. 38 C.F.R. § 20.1103 (Legacy) vs. 38 C.F.R. § 3.2500 (AMA Continuous Pursuit, 84 FR 170)

rows: Single linear track: `1-year` NOD -> VA issues `SOC` -> `60-day` / remainder-of-1-year `VA Form 9` Substantive Appeal.
Choice of three `1-year` lanes (`§ 5110(a)(2)(A)–(C)`; `§ 3.2500(c)`): `0996` HLR, `0995` Supplemental Claim (`new & relevant`), or `10182` Board NOD.

Appeal to CAVC within `120 days` (`§ 7266`). Filing a `§ 5108` reopening at the RO **forfeited** the original claim's effective date (effective date reset to reopening unless `§ 3.156(c)` or CUE applied).

Appeal to CAVC within `120 days` **OR** file a **`§ 5108` Supplemental Claim (`20-0995`) within `1 year` of BVA decision (`§ 5110(a)(2)(D)`; `§ 3.2500(c)(3), (h)(1)`)**—**preserving the initial effective date**! *(HLR barred after BVA).*
**FINALITY BREAK (`38 U.S.C. § 7291`):** CAVC affirmance makes the BVA denial final; any later reopening gets **only the date of reopening** (absent `§ 3.156(c)` or CUE).

**CONTINUOUS PURSUIT PRESERVED (`§ 5110(a)(2)(E)`):** Filing a `§ 5108` Supplemental Claim (`new & relevant`) within **`1 year` after CAVC decision** preserves the initial effective date even after a CAVC affirmance!
Barred concurrent RO adjudication of the exact issue pending before Fed. Cir. (*Cerullo*).

`84 FR 170` originally barred concurrent Supplemental Claims during Federal Circuit appeals (`§ 3.2500(b)`), creating a fatal gap because `§ 5110(a)(2)` lacks a post-Fed.-Cir. clause. ***MVA v. Sec'y*, `7 F.4th at 1134` INVALIDATED `§ 3.2500(b)`**—counsel **can and must** file a protective `20-0995` / `21-0966` within `1 year` of the CAVC decision while appealing to the Federal Circuit!

blocks.text: 3. 38 C.F.R. § 3.700(a)(2), (a)(3) & (a)(5): Separation Pay & Disability Severance Pay Recoupment (1996 -> 2002 -> 2008/2009)

*(Link to [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.114, 3.400, 3.2500, 3.654, 3.665, 3.700 & 3.701 (Effective Dates, Liberalizing Laws, Continuous Pursuit, Drill/Incarceration Adjustments, Severance/Separation Recoupment & Benefit Elections)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.114-3.400-3.700-effective-dates-offsets) for verbatim `§ 3.700(a)(2)–(3), (5)` text and [Playbook 20](/playbooks/20-backpay-offsets-crdp-crsc-severance-recoupment) for `CRDP`/`CRSC` and recoupment refund procedures).*

headers: Recoupment Base (`Gross` vs. `After-Tax Net` & Flat-Rate Tax Schedule)
rows: **GROSS PRE-TAX RECOUPMENT:** VA recouped `100%` of gross Readjustment Pay (`75%` rule for certain pre-1981 awards, `(a)(2)`), Nondisability Separation Pay / `SSB` (`(a)(5)`), and Disability Severance Pay (`DSP`, `(a)(3)`) without deducting federal income taxes withheld.

• **Non-Severance Rating Isolation (`§ 3.700(a)(3)`):** For `DSP` (`10 U.S.C. § 1212`), VA withholds **only** the monthly compensation attributable to the *severance disability(ies)*—compensation independently payable for *other* SC conditions cannot be recouped! · • **No combat-zone `DSP` exemption** existed yet.

**AFTER-TAX NET RECOUPMENT ONLY:** VA is barred from recouping federal income tax withheld from post-Sept. 30, 1996 Readjustment Pay (`§ 3.700(a)(2)(iii)`), Separation Pay / `SSB` (`§ 3.700(a)(5)`), or `DSP` (`§ 3.700(a)(3)`). · • **IRS Supplemental Flat-Rate Withholding Schedule** *(used when W-2/DFAS tax proof is absent)*: `20%` (`Oct. 1996 – Aug. 6, 1997`) -> `28%` (`Aug. 7, 1997 – Aug. 6, 2001`) -> `27.5%/27%` (`2001–2002`) -> `25%` (`May 28, 2003 – Dec. 31, 2017`) -> **`22%` (`Jan. 1, 2018 – Present`, TCJA)**. *(Audit **Pub. L. 114-292** / *St. Clair v. United States*, `778 F. Supp. 894 (E.D. Va. 1991)` tax refunds where DoD improperly taxed combat/VA-linked `DSP` (`26 U.S.C. § 104(a)(4)`): if DFAS taxed `DSP` at payout, VA recoups only the net `75%/78%` while the veteran separately claimed the IRS refund!)*

• Non-severance rating isolation (`§ 3.700(a)(3)`) applies in full. · • **CRITICAL BRIGHT-LINE KILL-SWITCH:** Members separated under Chapter 61 **before January 28, 2008** remain subject to after-tax `DSP` recoupment even if injured in Iraq/Afghanistan combat!
Retains after-tax net cap (`25%` through 2017; **`22%`** `2018–present`) for *non-combat* `DSP` and all nondisability Separation Pay / `SSB`.

**ZERO RECOUPMENT (`10 U.S.C. § 1212(d)(2)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.700(a)(3)`):** **NO deduction/recoupment** of Disability Severance Pay is permitted if the veteran was separated under `10 U.S.C. ch. 61` **on or after January 28, 2008** for a disability incurred in line of duty **in a combat zone** (`DD-214` / PEB `DA Form 199` code `V1`/`V3`/`10a`/`10c`) **OR** incurred during performance of duty in **combat-related operations** as designated by the Secretary of Defense (armed conflict, hazardous service, instrumentality of war, or simulated war)!

blocks.text: 4. 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.274–3.279: Needs-Based Wartime Pension Net Worth, 36-Month Lookback & UME Overhaul (83 FR 47246, Eff. Oct. 18, 2018)

On **September 18, 2018**, VA published **`83 FR 47246–47275` (`RIN 2900-AO73`, effective October 18, 2018)**, replacing nearly sixty years of subjective "corpus of estate" pension adjudication (`38 U.S.C. §§ 1522, 1543`) with objective Medicaid-aligned rules ([Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.274–3.279, 3.272(g), 3.353, 3.105(h)–(i), 3.500(b), 1.963 & 1.965 (Pension Net Worth & 36-Month Lookback, Deductible Medical Expenses, Competency Due Process & Overpayment Waivers)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.274-3.279-3.353-1.965-pension-competency-waivers); [Playbook 21](/playbooks/21-overpayment-waivers-incompetency-and-wartime-pension)):

rows: **Subjective Multi-Factor Corpus Test:** No fixed dollar cap (informal RO rules of thumb `$50k–$80k` routinely reversed on appeal); weighed liquid assets against income, family expenses, medical costs, and **table life expectancy** (`whether corpus would be consumed during claimant's lifetime`).

**Bright-Line Medicaid `CSRA`-Indexed Cap (`§ 3.274(a)–(b)`):** Indexed annually on Dec. 1 by Social Security COLA (`$123,600` on Oct. 18, 2018 -> **`$163,699` for `Dec. 1, 2025 – Nov. 30, 2026`**). · • **Formula (`§ 3.274(b)`):** **`Net Worth = Countable Assets + Annual Income for VA Purposes (IVAP)`** (after deducting annualized `§ 3.278` unreimbursed medical expenses; if `UMEs` reduce `IVAP` below `$0`, `IVAP` counts as `$0`, never negative!).
Excluded single-family dwelling plus `"such contiguous land as is reasonable"` based on local zoning/custom without a strict acreage cap.

**`2-Acre` Residential Lot Cap (`§ 3.275(b)(1)`):** Excludes primary residence (even if claimant moved into assisted living / nursing care!) **plus residential lot area up to `2 acres` (`87,120 sq. ft.`)**. Marketable value of land **exceeding `2 acres`** counts as an asset *unless* excess land is legally/physically **unmarketable** (zoning ban on subdivision, landlocked). Also excludes personal effects and daily family transportation vehicles (`(b)(2)`).

**ZERO LOOKBACK / ZERO PENALTY:** Uncompensated gifts or irrevocable trust/annuity transfers made **even `1 day` before filing** removed assets from net worth so long as the claimant completely relinquished ownership and control (`VAOPGCPREC 33-97`)!

**PROSPECTIVE-ONLY `36-Month` Lookback (`§ 3.276(a)–(b)`):** · 1. **100% Exemption for Pre-Oct. 18, 2018 Transfers (`§ 3.276(b)`):** VA **strictly disregards ALL asset transfers made BEFORE October 18, 2018**! · 2. **36-Month Window & `"Covered Asset"` Threshold (`§ 3.276(a)(2)–(3)`):** Reviews uncompensated transfers (gifts, irrevocable trusts, immediate annuities lacking residual liquidation value) within `36 months` preceding claim receipt—**PENALIZING ONLY the `"covered asset"` portion** (the dollar amount by which pre-transfer net worth would have exceeded the bright-line cap! If a claimant had `$100,000` total net worth and gifted `$50,000`, `"covered asset" = $0` and **penalty = `0 months`**!).
*Not applicable (no transfer penalty existed prior to Oct. 18, 2018).*

• **Single Uniform Monthly Divisor (`§ 3.276(e)(1)`):** Regardless of whether claimant is a single veteran, married veteran, or surviving spouse, divide `"covered asset"` amount by **`MAPR for a Veteran with 1 Dependent in need of Aid & Attendance ÷ 12`** (**`$34,488 ÷ 12 = $2,874/month`** for `Dec. 1, 2025 – Nov. 30, 2026`; round down fractional cents/months per `(e)(1)`, starts first day of month after last transfer per `(e)(2)`!). · • **Maximum Penalty Cap (`§ 3.276(e)`):** Capped at **`5 years` (`60 months`)**. · • **Cure Window (`§ 3.276(e)(5)`):** Full/partial return of transferred assets within **`60 days`** of penalty notice (with `90-day` proof window) recalculates or extinguishes the penalty!
Governed by scattered `former § 3.272(g)` and `M21-1` instructions leading to inconsistent RO disallowances of assisted-living room-and-board and family-caregiver payments.

**Codified `UME` Catalog (`§ 3.278(c)–(d)`):** Deducts unreimbursed medical/custodial expenses exceeding `5%` of baseline `MAPR`: · • **Nursing Home / Memory Care / Assisted Living (`(d)(3)`):** `100%` of facility charges (including **meals and lodging**) are deductible as `UMEs` whenever the facility provides or contracts for health care or **custodial care** (assistance with **`>= 2` Activities of Daily Living [`ADLs` under `§ 3.278(b)(2)`: bathing or showering, dressing, eating, toileting, transferring, and ambulating within the home or living area]** OR supervision due to cognitive/physical impairment), OR when a `physician/PA/CNP/CNS` states in writing that the individual must reside in the protected facility to obtain third-party/family care (`(d)(3)(iv)(B)`)! · • **In-Home Attendant (`(d)(2)`):** Deductible (even for an unlicensed family caregiver!) when claimant needs `A&A`/`Housebound` or has a `physician/PA/CNP/CNS` written statement of need for health care or custodial care. *(Cross-ref `§ 3.279` consolidating statutory exclusions).*

blocks.text: 5. 38 C.F.R. § 1.963(b) (Former § 1.963(b)(2)): Overpayment Waiver Deadline & The 2023–2025 Statutory-vs.-eCFR Lag Trap (90 FR 54234)

rows: `38 U.S.C. § 5302(a)` (`Pub. L. 101-237, § 311`, `1989`, reducing earlier 2-year window to **`180 days`**)
**`"within 180 days"`** in `former § 1.963(b)(2)` following date of notice of indebtedness (`58 FR 3840`, Jan. 12, 1993)

Strict **`180-day` statutory bar** for `VA Form 5655` equity-and-good-conscience waiver (`§ 1.965`). *(Missing `180 days` forced counsel to attack underlying **debt validity**—e.g., `38 U.S.C. § 5112(b)(10)` sole administrative error or void `§ 3.105(e)` reduction, which has **no 180-day limit**!).*

**`Pub. L. 117-328, Div. U, § 254`** (*Joseph Maxwell Cleland and Robert Joseph Dole Memorial Veterans Benefits and Health Care Improvement Act of 2022*, `136 Stat. 4459, 5464`, enacted **Dec. 29, 2022**) — amended `38 U.S.C. § 5302(a)` by striking `"180 days"` and inserting **`"one year"`**!
**STALE `eCFR` PRINTED `"180 days"`** in `former § 1.963(b)(2)` *(unamended in `38 C.F.R.` for 37 months!)*

**CRITICAL STATUTORY-SUPREMACY TRAP:** Positive statutory law ([Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)) controlled immediately upon enactment (`Dec. 29, 2022`)! Any Debt Management Center (`DMC`) or Committee on Waivers and Compromises (`COWC`) refusal to adjudicate a waiver filed between **`Day 181` and `Day 365`** on a post-Dec. 29, 2022 debt notice violated `38 U.S.C. § 5302(a)` and is **reversible error / CUE**!

**`"within one year"`** in undivided **`§ 1.963(b)`** — Final Rule, **`90 FR 54234`** (`RIN 2900-AS18`, *Extending Deadline for Debtor To Request a Waiver*, **published Nov. 26, 2025, effective January 26, 2026**)

Consolidated `former § 1.963(b)(1)–(2)` into undivided `38 C.F.R. § 1.963(b)` conforming to `§ 5302(a)`'s **`1-year`** waiver deadline. · • **CRITICAL `30-Day` Stay Distinction:** While a debtor now has **`1 full year`** to request a waiver, filing within **`30 days`** of the first DMC collection letter remains essential to **freeze monthly benefit withholding** pending waiver adjudication ([Playbook 21](/playbooks/21-overpayment-waivers-incompetency-and-wartime-pension))!

blocks.text: 6. Era-Specific CUE Traps & *George v. McDonough* Gate Matrix

Always screen historical offset, pension, and effective-date decisions against ***George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)`**, **`38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`**, and the [`Board CUE Pre-Filing Gate`](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate):

headers: Why It Succeeds (or Fails) & Optimal Remedy
rows: **Recouping Combat-Zone `DSP` on a Chapter 61 Separation `>= Jan. 28, 2008` (`10 U.S.C. § 1212(d)(2)`)**

Unambiguous statutory prohibition since **Jan. 28, 2008** (`Pub. L. 110-181, § 1646`). Audit `DD-214` separation date (`>= Jan. 28, 2008`) + PEB combat code; demand full refund of illegally withheld compensation via CUE / administrative audit ([Playbook 20](/playbooks/20-backpay-offsets-crdp-crsc-severance-recoupment)). *(Kill-Switch: Fails if separated `<= Jan. 27, 2008`).*

Unambiguous statutory cap (`Pub. L. 104-201, § 653`) since **Oct. 1, 1996**. Whenever VA withheld `100%` gross instead of deducting federal tax (`20%/28%/25%/22%`), recover the over-recouped tax slice via `§ 3.105(a)` CUE or post-award audit ([`Award Letter Audit Checklist`](/checklists/award-letter-and-withholding-audit-checklist)).
**Imposing a `§ 3.276` `36-Month` Transfer Penalty on a Gift/Trust Executed `Before Oct. 18, 2018`**

`38 C.F.R. § 3.276(b)` (`83 FR 47246, 47271`) explicitly exempts **all** asset transfers prior to **October 18, 2018**. Penalizing a pre-Oct. 18, 2018 transfer—or penalizing a post-Oct. 18, 2018 transfer where pre-transfer net worth was below the CSRA cap—is undebatable **RO/Board CUE**!
**Dismissing a `Day 181–365` Waiver Request on a Post-`Dec. 29, 2022` Debt Notice as "Untimely" Under `Former § 1.963(b)(2)`**

Unlike judicial reinterpretation (*George*), here **Congress directly amended `38 U.S.C. § 5302(a)` on Dec. 29, 2022** (`Pub. L. 117-328, Div. U, § 254`), rendering the unamended `"180 days"` text in `former § 1.963(b)(2)` (`2023–Jan. 25, 2026`) void as contrary to positive statute on the day of the decision!
**Attacking a Final `Feb. 19, 2019 – July 29, 2021` Decision Refusing a Supplemental ITF via CUE (*MVA v. Sec'y*)**

Barred as CUE under *George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` and `§ 20.1403(e)` because raters faithfully applied extant `84 FR 170` regulatory text prior to its July 30, 2021 invalidation (`7 F.4th 1110`). Screen instead for `§ 5104(b)` *Hamill* non-finality or `§ 3.156(c)` service records ([Procedural Vehicles](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality)).

`79 FR 57660` was strictly prospective from March 24, 2015 (*Shea v. Wilkie*). Any pre-March 24, 2015 VAMC examination/hospitalization report for an SC condition never adjudicated in a subsequent final rating remains a **pending unadjudicated claim for increase** ([Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon))!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Key Date Cutoffs: Informal Claims (2015), Severance Offsets (1996/2008), Pension Transfers (2018) & Debt Waivers (2022/2026)
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Across VA compensation, wartime pension, and overpayment law, a handful of sharp calendar cutoffs determine whether an older medical visit counts as a claim, how much separation pay VA can recoup, whether gifting assets triggers a pension penalty, and how long you have to request a debt waiver. This historical comparison maps four major rule shifts side-by-side: (1) March 24, 2015 (when Intent to File replaced informal claims and VA hospital-report claims under former 38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b)), (2) October 1, 1996 and January 28, 2008 (after-tax separation/severance recoupment caps and combat-zone severance exemptions under 38 C.F.R. § 3.700), (3) October 18, 2018 (bright-line pension net worth and 36-month transfer lookback under 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.274–3.279), and (4) December 29, 2022 / January 26, 2026 (expansion of the overpayment waiver window from 180 days to 1 year under 38 U.S.C. § 5302(a) and 38 C.F.R. § 1.963(b)).
record_clues: A pre-March 24, 2015 VA medical center outpatient exam or hospital admission showing worsening of an already service-connected disability (including a 0% rating) that VA never adjudicated as an informal claim for increase under former 38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b).

A VA Award Letter recouping gross pre-tax separation or severance pay received after September 30, 1996, OR recouping Chapter 61 combat-zone / combat-related disability severance pay for a separation on or after January 28, 2008.
A VA Pension denial applying a 36-month transfer penalty to a gift or trust created before October 18, 2018, or where total net worth was already below VA's bright-line limit.

A Debt Management Center or Committee on Waivers and Compromises letter dismissing a waiver request filed 181–365 days after a post-December 29, 2022 debt notice based on the outdated 180-day regulation.
important_cautions: Prospective military separation cutoffs: the combat-zone / combat-related disability severance non-recoupment rule (10 U.S.C. § 1212(d)(2)) applies strictly to service members separated on or after January 28, 2008, and the after-tax net recoupment cap applies strictly to separation/severance payments made after September 30, 1996.

March 24, 2015 claim-form cutoff: VA medical records generated ON OR AFTER March 24, 2015 do NOT automatically initiate a claim for increase—though pre-March 24, 2015 informal claims that VA never adjudicated remain viable (Shea v. Wilkie).

October 18, 2018 pension transfer cutoff: pre-October 18, 2018 asset transfers are exempt from the 36-month penalty period, whereas uncompensated transfers of excess assets ON OR AFTER October 18, 2018 can trigger up to a 5-year pension penalty.

Judicial invalidation vs. CUE: while the Federal Circuit invalidated VA's ban on Intent to File for Supplemental Claims in Military-Veterans Advocacy v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs (July 30, 2021), George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e) bar using that later court ruling to claim Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) against final pre-July 30, 2021 decisions.
questions_for_representative: Do my pre-March 24, 2015 VA medical center records contain an unadjudicated informal claim for increase under former 38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b)?

Did VA calculate my separation or disability severance recoupment using my net after-tax payout (post-September 30, 1996), or exempt my Chapter 61 combat-related severance pay if I separated on or after January 28, 2008?
If VA denied my Wartime or Survivors Pension due to an asset transfer, did the transfer happen before October 18, 2018 or stay below the bright-line net-worth threshold?
Was my overpayment waiver filed within 1 year of a debt notice dated on or after December 29, 2022 under 38 U.S.C. § 5302(a)?

Filing a standalone CUE motion against a final pre-Nov. 26, 2008 decision (Bradley), a final pre-May 16, 2024 decision (Barry), or a final June 7, 2018 – Sept. 5, 2024 decision (Laska) that faithfully applied extant VA regulations/VAOPGCPREC (barred by George v. McDonough, 596 U.S. 740 (2022) and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e))

blocks.text: This Reference module maps the 93-year statutory and regulatory evolution of **Special Monthly Compensation (`SMC`)** from `Veterans' Regulation No. 1(a)` (`1933`) through `former 38 U.S.C. § 314` (`1959–1991`) and modern **`38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)–(t)`** (`38 C.F.R. §§ 3.350, 3.352, 3.552`), isolating exact **Federal Register publication vs. effective dates** and ***George v. McDonough* (`596 U.S. 740 (2022)`) / `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)` bitemporal CUE gates**.

*(For verbatim regulatory text of `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.350` and `3.352`, see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.350, 3.352, 3.552(b), 4.63 & 3.810(a) (Special Monthly Compensation Ratings, Aid & Attendance, TBI SMC(t), Loss of Use & Multiple Clothing Allowances)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.350-3.352-smc-evolution); for doctrinal rate-step architecture, see [Master SMC Legal Treatise & Step Math](/docs/smc-complete-treatise-and-step-math); for operational pleading, see [Playbook 12 (`SMC(l)`, `SMC(r)(1)–(2)` & `SMC(t)`)](/playbooks/12-aid-and-attendance-smc-l-r1-r2-and-smc-t), [Playbook 13 (Ancillary Grants)](/playbooks/13-ancillary-grants-sah-auto-clothing-dea-spina-bifida), [Playbook 04 (Unadjudicated TDIU & Mandatory SMC)](/playbooks/04-unadjudicated-tdiu-informal-claims-smc), [`Surviving Spouse & Helpless Child Evolution Diff`](/cfr/modules/survivor-marriage-dependency-evolution), [`SMC & Ancillary Audit Worksheet`](/checklists/smc-and-ancillary-audit-worksheet), [VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon), and [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).*
1. Master Chronological Evolution Matrix (1933–2026)

rows: `E.O. 6156` (June 6, 1933) under `Pub. L. 73-2`: **`Vet. Reg. No. 1(a), Part I, par. II(k)–(p)`**

Established foundational wartime anatomical loss / loss of use (`LOU`), blindness, and regular Aid & Attendance (`par. II(l)`) tiers above `100%` *(peacetime `Part II` paid `80%` until `1973`; see [Statutory Crosswalk](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk))*.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive:** Cite `Vet. Reg. No. 1(a), Part I, par. II(...)` on pre-1959 code sheets (`38 C.F.R. § 20.1404(b)`). Protected on Dec. 31, 1958 by `Pub. L. 85-857` (`38 C.F.R. § 3.953`).
Added anatomical loss or **loss of use of one or more creative organs** to `par. II(k)` `[now § 1114(k) / § 3.350(a)(1)]`.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Aug. 1, 1952`):** Omitting `SMC(k)` when C&P/STRs establish SC orchiectomy, prostatectomy, hysterectomy, or SC erectile dysfunction is classic CUE (`Akles v. Derwinski`, `1 Vet. App. 118 (1991)`).

`Pub. L. 84-629` added loss/`LOU` of **both buttocks** (`§ 3.350(a)(3)` inability to rise without assistance); `Pub. L. 85-782` enacted original **`SMC(r)`** additional A&A allowance `[carried into former § 314(r), now § 1114(r)(1)]`. *(Note: `Pub. L. 85-652`, eff. Sept. 1, 1958, amended `LPO` blindness in `(m)`).*
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Aug. 1, 1956` / `Oct. 1, 1958`):** Cannot claim `SMC(r)` for periods before October 1, 1958.
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive:** All `Jan. 1, 1959 – Aug. 5, 1991` ratings are governed by **`former 38 U.S.C. § 314`** ([Statutory Crosswalk](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk)).

Added **`former 38 U.S.C. § 314(s)` `[now § 1114(s)]` (`SMC(s)`)**: `(1)` statutory `100%` single SC disability + `60%+` independent SC disability(ies), OR `(2)` permanently housebound-in-fact (`§ 3.350(i)`).

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Sept. 1, 1960`):** Pure math omission of `SMC(s)` when code sheet shows **schedular `100%` + `>= 60%` separate combined SC** is airtight RO/Board CUE! *(Zero `SMC(s)` entitlement before Sept. 1, 1960).*

Added total bilateral deafness (`absence of air and bone conduction`, **`§ 3.350(a)(5)`** & `§ 1114(o)`) and **complete organic aphonia** (`constant inability to communicate by speech`, **`§ 3.350(a)(6)`**) to `former § 314(k)`.

**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) / CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= July 1, 1963`):** E.g., post-laryngectomy (`DC 6518`) or organic aphonia (`DC 6519`) total speech loss mandates `100% + SMC(k)`!
Divided `former § 314(r)` into **`SMC(r)(1)`** and **`SMC(r)(2)`** (`38 C.F.R. § 3.352(b)`), creating the top-tier skilled health-care allowance for veterans otherwise requiring institutionalization.
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Oct. 1, 1978`):** `SMC(r)(2)` did not exist prior to October 1, 1978.

**`5-89`:** Prior elective sterilization (vasectomy/tubal ligation) **does not bar `SMC(k)`** for subsequent SC **anatomical** organ loss. **`30-97`:** Preexisting NSC paraplegia **does not bar `SMC(n)`** for `§ 1151` bilateral hip amputation ([`VAOPGCPREC` Index](/docs/vaopgcprec-index)).
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Mar. 23, 1989` / `Aug. 29, 1997`):** Binding on ROs and BVA under `38 U.S.C. § 7104(c)`—violation on undisputed surgical facts is CUE!
Renumbered `former 38 U.S.C. § 314(a)–(s)` to **`38 U.S.C. § 1114(a)–(s)`** *(91 days after `Pub. L. 102-40` May 7, 1991 Part IV–VI renumbering)*.
**Pure Recodification:** Zero substantive rate/criteria change, *but* essential for exact-era CUE citation precision.

**Stage 1 (`Nov. 1, 2000 – Dec. 5, 2002`, `former § 3.350(a)(7)`):** Required **complete mastectomy** of one or both breasts. · **Stage 2 (`>= Dec. 6, 2002`, `§ 3.350(a)` intro — removing `former § 3.350(a)(7)`):** Expanded to **loss of `>= 25%` of tissue** from a single breast or both breasts combined (wide local excision / lumpectomy) **OR radiation treatment of breast tissue**!

**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) / CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive:** Check exact surgery/radiation vs. rating date! A `2001` lumpectomy with radiation did *not* qualify until **Dec. 6, 2002** (`Pub. L. 107-330`), whereas denying `SMC(k)` for breast radiation after Dec. 6, 2002 is statutory error!
Liberalized bilateral blindness acuity in `38 U.S.C. § 1114(o)` (when paired with total bilateral deafness) from `5/200` to **`20/200` or less**.

***Bradley v. Peake***, `22 Vet. App. 280 (Nov. 26, 2008)`; **`75 FR 11229` (Mar. 10, 2010)** withdrawing `VAOPGCPREC 6-99`; *Buie*, `24 Vet. App. 242 (2010)`; *Gazelle*, `868 F.3d 1006 (Fed. Cir. 2017)`

Invalidated `VAOPGCPREC 6-99` (`64 FR 52375`, June 7, 1999): **`100%` TDIU attributable to a SINGLE SC disability** satisfies the total-disability prong of `§ 1114(s)` regardless of award sequence (*Buie*), provided remaining SC disabilities combine (`§ 4.25`) to `>= 60%` (*Gazelle*).

**SPLIT BITEMPORAL SCOPE:** · • **Final `June 7, 1999 – Nov. 25, 2008` denials:** **Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** (*George* / `§ 20.1403(e)` shields faithful application of `VAOPGCPREC 6-99`; use `§ 3.156(b)–(c)` or pending claims!). · • **Decisions `>= Nov. 26, 2008` / `Mar. 10, 2010`:** **CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** if record undisputedly showed single-disability TDIU + `60%`!

Added **`38 U.S.C. § 1114(t)`** paying the **`SMC(r)(2)` rate** for SC TBI residuals requiring regular A&A absent which residential/institutional care would be needed. **6.5-year CFR lag:** `§§ 3.350(j), 3.352(b)(2)` published May 8, 2018 (`83 FR 20735`), adding an extra-statutory `"higher level of care"` hurdle.

**CRITICAL TEMPORAL SPLIT:** · • **`Pre-Oct. 1, 2011`:** **Hard statutory bar** (`Pub. L. 111-275, § 601(c)`). · • **`Oct. 1, 2011 – June 6, 2018`:** Governed directly by `38 U.S.C. § 1114(t)` (ignoring `§ 1114(t)` due to missing CFR rule was error, though watch *George* if attacking `June 7, 2018 – Sept. 5, 2024` final denials—see *Laska* below).

Invalidated VA's single-bump cap on `38 U.S.C. § 1114(p)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(f)(3)–(4)`: veterans at base `SMC(l)–(n)` earn **multiple cumulative `½`-steps (`50%+` SC) and full steps (`100%` SC)** up to the `SMC(o)` ceiling!

**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) for pre-May 16, 2024 final ratings:** Cannot prove CUE on final pre-*Barry* single-step ratings (`§ 20.1403(e)`), **but** applies retroactively to *all* open appeals, `§ 3.156(b)–(c)` reconsiderations, *Hamill* AMA omissions, and current Supplemental/increase claims!
***Laska v. McDonough***, `37 Vet. App. 460 (Sept. 6, 2024)` (`No. 22-1018`, *originally docketed as Haskell v. McDonough*)

**Invalidated `38 C.F.R. § 3.352(b)(2)`'s `"higher level of care"` requirement** for `SMC(t)`: under `38 U.S.C. § 1114(t)`, SC TBI veterans need prove **only regular A&A (`§ 3.352(a)`)** without which hospitalization, nursing home, or residential institutional care would be required—**no skilled nursing/licensed-professional threshold**!

**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) against final `June 7, 2018 – Sept. 5, 2024` denials:** Under *George*, faithful application of extant `§ 3.352(b)(2)` defeats standalone CUE, **but** *Laska* unlocks full `SMC(t)` back to **`Oct. 1, 2011`** on every pending appeal, `§ 5121A` substitution, `§ 3.156(b)–(c)` claim, or post-Sept. 6, 2024 `20-0995` Supplemental Claim!

blocks.text: 2. Side-by-Side Structural Threshold Diffs (Pre- vs. Post-Judicial / Statutory Shifts)
A. 38 C.F.R. § 3.350(f)(3)–(4) Intermediate & Full-Step Bumps (Pre-Barry vs. Post-Barry, May 16, 2024)

headers: Post-May 16, 2024 Controlling Law (*Barry v. McDonough*, `101 F.4th 1348`)
rows: **`§ 3.350(f)(3)` (`½`-Step per `50%+` Independent SC Disability or Combination)**
Capped veteran at **one single `½`-step** regardless of whether they had `2`, `3`, or `4` separate `50%+` SC disabilities/combinations.

**Unlimited cumulative `½`-steps** (one `½`-step for **each** separate, independent `50%–90%` permanent SC disability **and** for any `§ 4.25` combination of leftover `< 50%` permanent SC disabilities combining to `>= 50%`), capped at **`SMC(o)`**.
**`§ 3.350(f)(4)` (`1` Full Step per `100%` Independent Schedular SC Disability)**
Capped veteran at **one single full step** AND prohibited combining an `(f)(3)` `½`-step with an `(f)(4)` full step.

**Cumulative full steps + `(f)(3)`/`(f)(4)` stacking** for each separate `100%` schedular (*not `§ 4.16` TDIU*) SC disability (e.g., base `SMC(l)` A&A + independent `100%` PTSD `[+1 step -> M]` + independent `50%` Sleep Apnea `[+½ step -> M½]` + independent `50%` Radiculopathy `[+½ step -> N]`, capped at **`SMC(o)`**—which in turn unlocks **`SMC(r)(1)`** under `§ 3.350(h)` if A&A is present!).
Prohibited counting the base `SMC(l)–(n)` disability twice.

**Strictly preserved:** Under *Breniser v. Shinseki*, `25 Vet. App. 64 (2011)` and *Amberman v. Shinseki*, `570 F.3d 1377 (Fed. Cir. 2009)`, a disability used to establish base `SMC(l)–(n)` **cannot also** power an `(f)(3)` or `(f)(4)` bump!

headers: `SMC(t)` Post-*Laska* (`>= Sept. 6, 2024`, Controlling Statutory Meaning of `§ 1114(t)`)
rows: **YES** (must first reach `SMC(o)` or maximum `(p)`/`(n½ + k)` rate + A&A under `§ 1114(r)`)
**NO** (requires SC Traumatic Brain Injury residuals only)
**NO** (requires SC Traumatic Brain Injury residuals only)
**Higher level of care (`§ 3.352(b)(1)`):** Daily personal health-care services by (or under regular supervision of) a **licensed health-care professional**
Unlawfully demanded **`§ 3.352(b)(2)` "higher level of care"** (daily skilled/professional services)

**Regular Aid & Attendance ONLY (`§ 3.352(a)`):** ADLs, cognitive/supervisory cueing, or protection from daily hazards provided by a **family caregiver or lay attendant**—**NO skilled/professional care required**!
Absent skilled care, would require **hospital, nursing home, or other residential institutional care**
Absent **regular A&A**, would require **hospitalization, nursing home care, or other residential institutional care** (including assisted-living / TBI group-home supervision).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: How Special Monthly Compensation (SMC(k) Through SMC(t)) Evolved From 1933 to 2026
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Because VA's duty to consider Special Monthly Compensation (SMC) whenever the medical record reasonably raises it goes back decades (Akles v. Derwinski), auditing an older Rating Code Sheet requires knowing exactly when Congress created or expanded each SMC tier. This historical guide traces every statutory milestone from 1933 Veterans' Regulation No. 1(a) and 1958 former 38 U.S.C. § 314 through modern 38 U.S.C. § 1114: the September 1, 1960 birth of Housebound SMC(s), the 1958/1978 creation of SMC(r)(1) and SMC(r)(2) Aid & Attendance, the 1981 three-extremity bump, the 2000/2002 breast SMC(k) rules, the 2007 deaf-blind liberalization, the October 1, 2011 enactment of TBI SMC(t), and the 2024 court breakthroughs in Barry v. McDonough and Laska v. McDonough.
record_clues: Older WWII, Korean, or Vietnam Rating Code Sheets citing 'Vet. Reg. No. 1(a), Part I, par. II' or '38 U.S.C. § 314' (renumbered to § 1114 on August 6, 1991).
A 1999–2010 rating decision denying Housebound SMC(s) on single-disability TDIU based on withdrawn VAOPGCPREC 6-99 (overturned by Bradley v. Peake in 2008).

A 2011–2024 Traumatic Brain Injury rating denying SMC(t) under VA's June 7, 2018 rule (83 FR 20735) for lack of skilled professional care, or a catastrophic SMC(l)–(n) rating capped at one § 3.350(f) step bump.
important_cautions: Match Historical Statutory Citations on Old Decisions: Before January 1, 1959, SMC sat in Veterans' Regulation No. 1(a); from 1959 through August 5, 1991, it was numbered 38 U.S.C. § 314; and SMC(s) did not exist prior to September 1, 1960 (Pub. L. 86-663), while SMC(t) did not exist prior to October 1, 2011 (Pub. L. 111-275).

Open Claims vs. Final Decisions After Court Invalidations: Under George v. McDonough, 596 U.S. 740 (2022) and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e), judicial decisions overturning VA's prior regulatory/GC interpretations—such as Bradley (2008), Barry (May 16, 2024), and Laska (September 6, 2024)—apply retroactively inside open, pending, timely appealed, or § 3.156(c) claims, but cannot prove Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) against older final decisions that applied then-standing rules.

Never Double-Count Overlapping Impairments: Under Amberman v. Shinseki and Breniser v. Shinseki, the same underlying disability cannot be counted twice to build both base SMC and additional step bumps.
questions_for_representative: Was the specific SMC tier we are investigating already enacted by Congress on the date of my historical VA rating decision?

Did an earlier VA decision stay completely silent on reasonably raised SMC—leaving an unadjudicated/open issue where modern court precedents like Bradley, Barry, or Laska can apply without hitting the George v. McDonough CUE bar?
If my case involves an older pre-1991 decision, have we cross-referenced the exact former 38 U.S.C. § 314 text in force on that date?

headers: Bitemporal CUE vs. Open-Claim Posture (*George v. McDonough*)
rows: *Essentials of evaluative rating*; *Interpretation of examination reports*; *Evaluation of evidence*
Requires evaluating current exams in light of the **entire recorded medical & industrial history** (*Schafrath*).

**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** on weighing disputes; **CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** only if undisputed probative evidence in the record was completely ignored with outcome-determinative effect.
Applies `38 U.S.C. § 5107(b)` equipoise to the **degree of disability** within a Diagnostic Code (*Bufkin*).
**Never CUE** (`38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(d)(3)` — failure to give benefit of the doubt cannot constitute CUE); open-claim/appeal tool reviewed for clear error at CAVC (*Bufkin*).
Awards higher evaluation when disability picture **"more nearly approximates"** higher tier (*Tatum* vs. *Camacho*/*Middleton*).
**Generally Open-Claim Only:** Subjective "more nearly approximates" judgment calls cannot support CUE (*Russell*/*Fugo*), unless all objective criteria of the higher tier were undisputedly met.
Excludes static structural defects, refractive error, personality disorder, and intellectual disability (mirrors `§ 3.303(c)`).

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= July 18, 1990`):** Misclassifying a progressive hereditary **disease** as a noncompensable `§ 4.9`/`§ 3.303(c)` defect violates [`VAOPGCPREC 82-90`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index) ([Causation Treatise](/docs/service-connection-direct-soundness-aggravation)).
Anchors ratings to functional ability under **ordinary conditions of life, including employment**; bars uncodified medication discounting (*Jones*; *Ingram*).

**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** for pre-2025 final decisions under *Ingram*; **immediate HLR/Supplemental/Appeal audit** for ratings issued during the rescinded `91 FR 7118` IFR window (`Feb. 17–27, 2026`).
Separates progression of prior condition from correction of diagnostic error; protects prior SC (*Read v. Shinseki*).
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** if VA severed SC without `§ 3.105(d)`/`§ 3.957` compliance; diagnostic code reclassification preserving SC is **not** a severance (*Read*).
Bars compensating the **exact same manifestation** twice (*Brady*), while mandating separate ratings for **distinct actual symptoms** (*Esteban*; *Morgan*).

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** when VA double-counted identical symptoms OR refused a mandatory separate rating (e.g., Spine Note 1 radiculopathy, [`VAOPGCPREC 23-97`/`9-2004`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index) knee instability + flexion + extension) on undisputed C&P facts.
Governs constitutional/individual total impairment, `§ 4.16(a)–(b)` TDIU, protected/static trauma employment termination (`§ 4.18`), and coexisting misconduct insulation (`§ 4.17a`).

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** on `§ 4.16(a)(1)–(5)` single-disability aggregation math errors; **Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** on `§ 4.16(b)` extraschedular referrals ([VASRD Historical Diff: TDIU (§ 4.16), May 2024 Digestive (§ 4.114) & Pending Sleep Apnea/Tinnitus Proposals](/cfr/modules/tdiu-digestive-respiratory-diffs)).
**Strictly prohibits** considering advancing age in evaluating SC disability compensation or TDIU (`§ 4.16`).
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** if a rating narrative explicitly discounted an SC evaluation or denied TDIU on the face of the decision due to the veteran's advanced age.
*Analogous ratings (`§ 4.20`)*; *Application of schedule (`§ 4.21`)*; *Use of diagnostic code numbers (`§ 4.27`)*
Three-factor analogy test (*Lendenmann*); no rigid literal-identity barrier (*Webb*); `xx99-xxxx` hyphenation (`§ 4.27`).
**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** for *Webb* (`2023`) and initial choice among competing plausible analogous codes.
*Aggravation baseline deduction (`§ 4.22`)*; *Attitude of rating officers (`§ 4.23`)*; *Central Office correspondence (`§ 4.24`)*
Deducts *ascertainable* entrance schedular % on `§ 1153` aggravation (**zero deduction if `100%` or unascertainable**!).
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** when VA deducted an arbitrary/unascertainable entrance percentage or deducted from a `100%` evaluation in violation of `§ 4.22`.
Whole-person efficiency (`100 - remaining efficiency`), `.5` rounding, `+10%` paired-extremity bonus, and **Apr. 16, 2023 `§ 4.26(d)` exclusion** (`88 FR 22914`).
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** for pure `§ 4.25` arithmetic/rounding errors, omitted mandatory `§ 4.26(a)–(c)` bilateral bonus, or omitted `§ 4.26(d)` exclusion **on/after Apr. 16, 2023**.

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** when VAMC/surgical records in the record at adjudication undisputedly met objective `>21-day` hospital or cast/surgical criteria (or omitted `>=2008` *Bradley* `SMC(s)`).
Mandatory `0%` SC evaluation whenever a DC lacks an explicit `0%` tier and compensable criteria are unmet.
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** if VA denied service connection outright solely because current symptoms did not reach a `10%` compensable threshold!

blocks.text: 1. Evidentiary & Interpretive Canons (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 4.6, 4.7, 4.21)
A. Longitudinal Historical Context (§§ 4.1, 4.2, 4.6 & *Schafrath v. Derwinski*)

Sections `4.1`, `4.2`, and `4.6` form an indivisible evidentiary triad (verbatim text in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.1–4.31 Subpart A General Rating Policy & Two-Era § 3.321(b)(1) Extraschedular Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.1-4.31-general-policy-snapshots)):

items: **`§ 4.1` (*Essentials of evaluative rating*):** Percentage evaluations measure *"average impairment in earning capacity"* in civil occupations (`38 U.S.C. § 1155`), requiring accurate, fully descriptive examinations emphasizing limitation of activity, with **each disability viewed in relation to its entire history**.

**`§ 4.2` (*Interpretation of examination reports*):** Adjudicators must interpret individual C&P examination reports *"in the light of the whole recorded history, reconciling the various reports into a consistent picture so that the current rating may accurately reflect the elements of disability present."* If an exam report lacks sufficient clinical detail for evaluation, **it is the mandatory duty of the rating official to return the report as inadequate**.

**`§ 4.6` (*Evaluation of evidence*):** Every element in any way affecting the degree of disability must be considered; ignoring favorable medical or lay history in the C-file to rely exclusively on an isolated, unrepresentative "good day" C&P snapshot violates `§§ 4.1, 4.2, and 4.6` (*Schafrath v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 589, 594–95 (1991)`).

blocks.text: B. Reasonable Doubt on Evaluation Tiers (§ 4.3 & *Bufkin v. Collins*)

Under `38 C.F.R. § 4.3` (implementing `38 U.S.C. § 5107(b)`), whenever a reasonable doubt arises regarding the **degree of disability** after careful consideration of all procurable and assembled data, such doubt **will be resolved in favor of the claimant**.

items: **Appellate Standard of Review (*Bufkin v. Collins*, `604 U.S. 369 (2025)`):** At the AOJ and the Board of Veterans' Appeals, `§ 4.3` / `§ 5107(b)` operates as a potent substantive tie-breaker whenever competing medical exams or symptom accounts stand in approximate balance. At the CAVC, however, *Bufkin* holds that the Board's approximate-balance determination is reviewed deferentially for **clear error** (`38 U.S.C. § 7261(b)(1)`), making inadequacy-of-reasons-or-bases challenges under `§ 4.2` / `§ 4.6` / `§ 7104(d)(1)` far higher-percentage CAVC remand vehicles than pure equipoise reweighing.
**Absolute CUE Bar (`38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(d)(3)`):** By explicit regulation, VA's failure to apply the `§ 4.3` / `§ 5107(b)` benefit-of-the-doubt rule **can never constitute CUE**.

blocks.text: C. 38 C.F.R. § 4.7 (*Higher of Two Evaluations*): Disjunctive vs. Conjunctive vs. Successive/Cumulative Criteria

`38 C.F.R. § 4.7` states: *"Where there is a question as to which of two evaluations shall be applied, the higher evaluation will be assigned if the disability picture more nearly approximates the criteria required for that rating. Otherwise, the lower rating will be assigned."* Together with `38 C.F.R. § 4.21` (confirming it is not expected in atypical instances that all cases will show every specified finding, so long as rating coordinates with functional impairment), `§ 4.7` is the primary weapon against hyper-literal "checklist" denials—**except** when blocked by a **successive/cumulative conjunctive rating structure**:

rows: **1. Successive / Cumulative Conjunctive Criteria (`"and"` cascading upward)**
***Camacho v. Nicholson*, `21 Vet. App. 360, 366–67 (2007)`**; ***Middleton v. Shinseki*, `727 F.3d 1172, 1177–78 (Fed. Cir. 2013)`**

**`§ 4.7` CANNOT Bypass Missing Prongs:** Where each ascending tier explicitly incorporates *all* requirements of the preceding lower tier **plus** an additional criterion joined by `"and"`, the veteran **must satisfy every cumulative prong**. Failing a required lower-tier element (e.g., `"regulation of activities"`) forecloses `§ 4.7` even if the veteran has the higher tier's extra symptom!

**`DC 7913` Diabetes Mellitus:** `20%` (`insulin AND restricted diet`) -> `40%` (`insulin, restricted diet, AND regulation of activities`) -> `60%` (`40% criteria + episodes of ketoacidosis/hypoglycemic reactions`). Under *Middleton*, ketoacidosis hospitalizations *without* regulation of activities cannot yield `40%` or `60%` via `§ 4.7`!

**`§ 4.7` FULLY APPLIES:** Even when a tier lists multiple symptoms joined by `"and"`, if the rating tiers are **not** structured as rigid upward-cascading cumulative steps, the Board **must apply `§ 4.7`** to decide whether the veteran's overall severity more nearly approximates the higher tier despite lacking one listed symptom!

**Pre-2017 `DC 7903` Hypothyroidism** (*Tatum*: `10%` vs. `30%` tiers listed distinct symptom clusters rather than incorporating lower tiers verbatim, requiring a `§ 4.7` approximation analysis); **Pre-May 2024 `DC 7346` Hiatal Hernia/GERD** (`30%` vs. `60%`).
**3. Exemplar / Holistic Occupational-Impairment Formulas (`"such symptoms as"` / `"or"`)**
***Vazquez-Claudio v. Shinseki*, `713 F.3d 112, 116–18 (Fed. Cir. 2013)`**; ***Bankhead v. Shulkin*, `29 Vet. App. 10, 21–23 (2017)`**

**`§ 4.7` & Symptom-Driven Holistic Assessment:** Listed symptoms are **non-exhaustive examples** demonstrating the frequency, type, and severity of occupational/social impairment. Presence of a higher-tier hallmark symptom (e.g., passive suicidal ideation at `70%` under *Bankhead*—requiring no plan, intent, or hospitalization!) compels rigorous `§ 4.7` analysis of overall impairment.

**`§ 4.130` General Rating Formula for Mental Disorders (`DC 9400–9411`)** ([VASRD Historical Diff: Mental Disorders & PTSD (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125–4.130, DC 9400–9440)](/cfr/modules/mental-health-dc-9400-9411)).

blocks.text: 2. Functional Impairment & The Ameliorative Medication Doctrine (38 C.F.R. § 4.10)

Under `38 C.F.R. § 4.10`, the basis of disability evaluations is *"the ability of the body as a whole, or of the psyche, or of a system or organ of the body to function under the ordinary conditions of life, including employment."*
A. *Jones v. Shinseki* (2012) & *Ingram v. Collins* (2025): Prohibition on Uncodified Medication Discounting

For decades, VA examiners and Board members routinely depressed orthopedic, gastrointestinal, neurological, and dermatological evaluations by measuring range of motion or symptom frequency *while the veteran was heavily medicated* without accounting for baseline unmedicated severity:

items: ***Jones v. Shinseki*, `26 Vet. App. 56, 61–63 (2012)`:** Analyzing `DC 7319` Irritable Bowel Syndrome, the CAVC held that **unless a Diagnostic Code specifically contemplates the ameliorative effects of medication in its rating criteria, VA may NOT deny a higher disability evaluation by relying on relief provided by medication**—because doing so impermissibly adds uncodified criteria to the Rating Schedule.

***Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)`** *(Federal Circuit appeal `No. 25-1972` voluntarily dismissed Mar. 30, 2026)*: Extending *Jones* squarely to **musculoskeletal range-of-motion and functional-loss evaluations (`38 C.F.R. §§ 4.10, 4.40, 4.45, 4.59, 4.71a`)**, the CAVC held that because goniometric joint/spine Diagnostic Codes do not mention medication, **C&P examiners and adjudicators MUST ascertain and discount the ameliorative/masking effects of pain or anti-inflammatory medications** so the veteran is compensated for baseline functional impairment ([VASRD Historical Diff: Spine & Musculoskeletal Joints (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.40, 4.45, 4.59, 4.71a)](/cfr/modules/orthopedic-spine-joints)).
• **Contrast Explicit Medication DCs:** Where a Diagnostic Code *explicitly* builds medication into its text—such as `DC 6602` Asthma (intermittent vs. daily inhalational bronchodilators/corticosteroids), `DC 7101` Hypertension (`10%` continuous medication), `DC 7913` Diabetes (insulin/oral hypoglycemics), or `§ 4.124a` Epilepsy—the specific DC criteria govern.

blocks.text: B. Quarantine Alert: The Rescinded 10-Day § 4.10 Interim Final Rule (Feb. 17–27, 2026)

lines: **Quarantined & Rescinded Agency Rulemaking (`91 FR 7118` -> Rescinded at `91 FR 9712`):**

* On **February 17, 2026**, VA published an immediate-effective Interim Final Rule (**`91 FR 7118`**, *rescinded*) attempting to amend `38 C.F.R. § 4.10` to overturn *Ingram* and *Jones* by evaluating disabilities solely at their medicated level.

* Following immediate congressional and veterans-bar backlash, VA **formally rescinded the Interim Final Rule ten days later on February 27, 2026 (`91 FR 9712`)** and voluntarily dismissed its appeal in *Ingram* (`No. 25-1972`, Mar. 30, 2026) ([Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).

* **Mandatory Firm Audit Rule:** **Never** cite `91 FR 7118` (rescinded) as active law. Conversely, **flag every RO, HLR, or Board decision issued between February 17, 2026 and February 27, 2026** (or relying on a DBQ completed under temporary Feb. 2026 M21-1 guidance) for immediate **Higher-Level Review, Supplemental Claim, or CAVC remand** under *Ingram*!

* **Bitemporal *George* Gate:** Because *Ingram* (`2025`) clarified judicial construction of `§ 4.10`, attacking a **final pre-2025** rating decision via CUE faces `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)` / *George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` (Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)), whereas *Ingram* governs **100% of open, pending, timely-appealed, `§ 3.156(b)–(c)`, and new increased-rating claims**!

blocks.text: 3. Change of Diagnosis (§ 4.13) & Avoidance of Pyramiding (§ 4.14)
A. 38 C.F.R. § 4.13 (*Effect of Change of Diagnosis*) & *Read v. Shinseki*

When VA changes a previously assigned diagnosis, `§ 4.13` requires certifying whether the new diagnosis reflects **(1) progression of an earlier diagnosis**, **(2) development of a new and separate disease**, or **(3) correction of a prior diagnostic error** (where prior factual findings are reviewed as a whole).

items: ***Read v. Shinseki*, `651 F.3d 1296, 1300–02 (Fed. Cir. 2011)`:** When VA reclassifies the Diagnostic Code of a disability in force for `10+` years under `§ 4.13` to reflect an updated/corrected diagnosis of the *same underlying symptom complex* **while maintaining service connection**, that diagnostic reclassification is **NOT a severance of service connection** violating `38 U.S.C. § 1159` / `38 C.F.R. § 3.957` (though any reduction in percentage must still satisfy `§§ 3.105(e)` and `3.344`—see [Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings)!).

blocks.text: B. 38 C.F.R. § 4.14 (*Avoidance of Pyramiding*): Symptom Overlap vs. Etiology

`38 C.F.R. § 4.14` commands: *"The evaluation of the same disability under various diagnoses is to be avoided ... The evaluation of the same manifestation under different diagnoses is also to be avoided."* Few VASRD provisions are more frequently misapplied by RO raters to suppress lawful separate ratings:

items: ***Brady v. Brown*, `4 Vet. App. 203, 206 (1993)` & *Amberman v. Shinseki*, `570 F.3d 1377, 1380–81 (Fed. Cir. 2009)`:** The anti-pyramiding rule bars compensating a veteran twice for the **same functional manifestation or symptomatology**—even if doctors attach two separate diagnostic labels (e.g., PTSD + Major Depressive Disorder sharing identical occupational/affective symptoms under `§ 4.130`).

***Esteban v. Brown*, `6 Vet. App. 259, 261–62 (1994)` (The Symptom-Overlap Test — NOT an Etiology Test!):** Reversing the Board's refusal to assign three separate ratings for a single facial trauma injury (`DC 7800` disfiguring scar, `DC 7804` painful scar, and `DC 5325` facial muscle injury), the CAVC established the bedrock rule of `§ 4.14`: **conditions sharing a common etiology or single injury MUST be rated separately whenever none of the symptomatology justifying any one evaluation is duplicative of or overlapping with the symptomatology of the others**!
• **High-Yield Separate-Rating Multipliers (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive when omitted on undisputed C&P facts):**
• **Gunshot / Shrapnel Wounds:** Muscle injury (`DC 5301–5323`) + painful/unstable/areal scar (`DC 7801–7804`) + peripheral nerve damage (`DC 8510–8730`) ([Playbook 01](/playbooks/01-penetrating-wounds-scars-vs-muscles), [VASRD Historical Diff: Scars & Skin Disfigurement (38 C.F.R. § 4.118, DC 7800–7805)](/cfr/38-cfr-4.118#redline-diff), [VASRD Historical Diff: Muscle Injuries (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.55, 4.56, 4.73, DC 5301–5323)](/cfr/38-cfr-4.56#redline-diff)).
• **Single Knee Triple/Quadruple Stacking:** Lateral instability (`DC 5257`) + limitation of flexion (`DC 5260`) + limitation of extension (`DC 5261`) + symptomatic meniscal tear (`DC 5258`/`5259` where distinct locking/effusion symptoms exist) ([`VAOPGCPREC 23-97`, `9-98`, `9-2004`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index); *Lyles v. Shulkin*, `29 Vet. App. 107 (2017)`).
• **Spine + Radiculopathy + Bladder/Bowel:** Orthopedic ROM (`DC 5235–5243`) + each affected lower/upper peripheral nerve (`DC 8520` sciatic, `DC 8526` femoral) + neurogenic bladder/bowel (`§ 4.71a` Spine Note 1).

***Morgan v. Wilkie*, `31 Vet. App. 162, 166–68 (2019)` (Actual Compensated Symptoms & Duty to Maximize):** Anti-pyramiding under `§ 4.14` applies **only to *actual* symptoms already compensated** under an assigned rating—**never** to uncompensated manifestations or hypothetical criteria listed in a Diagnostic Code that the veteran was not rated for! Under *Morgan*, VA's duty to maximize benefits requires adjudicators to **exhaust every non-pyramiding separate schedular Diagnostic Code** (`§ 4.14`, `§ 4.20`, `§ 4.7`) before reaching `§ 3.321(b)(1)` extraschedular analysis.

blocks.text: 4. Total Disability, Age, Analogy & Code-Sheet Math (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.15–4.27, 4.31)
A. Total Disability, Age Prohibition & Aggravation Deductions (§§ 4.15–4.19, 4.22)

items: **`§ 4.15` (*Total disability ratings*) & `§ 4.16` (*TDIU*):** Distinguishes general/schedular `100%` impairment (measuring average impairment across civil occupations) from individualized unemployability (`§ 4.16(a)–(b)`), taking into account `§ 4.18` static-trauma employment failures and `§ 4.17a` (which prevents a coexisting willful-misconduct disability from blocking P&T/TDIU if innocently acquired disabilities independently meet total criteria). *(For complete `§ 4.16(a)(1)–(5)` single-disability aggregation CUE rules and `1975–1996` historical text, see [VASRD Historical Diff: TDIU (§ 4.16), May 2024 Digestive (§ 4.114) & Pending Sleep Apnea/Tinnitus Proposals](/cfr/modules/tdiu-digestive-respiratory-diffs) and [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 4.16 Total Disability Based on Individual Unemployability (1975–Present Evolution & Former § 4.16(c))](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.16-tdiu-evolution)).*

**`§ 4.19` (*Age in service-connected claims* — Categorical Bar):** *"Age may not be considered as a factor in evaluating service-connected disability; and unemployability, in service-connected claims, associated with advancing age or intercurrent disability, may not be used as a basis for a total disability rating."* Conversely, VA **cannot deny TDIU or discount an SC rating** by claiming a 72-year-old veteran is retired or unemployable due to advanced age if SC disabilities alone preclude substantially gainful employment ([`VAOPGCPREC 75-91`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index))!

**`§ 4.22` (*Rating of disabilities aggravated by active service*):** Mirrors `38 U.S.C. § 1153` (`former § 353`): VA may deduct the pre-service entrance degree of disability **ONLY if**: `(1)` the entrance severity is **affirmatively ascertainable** in terms of the Rating Schedule (if unascertainable, **zero deduction** may be made!), **AND** `(2)` the current post-aggravation disability is **less than `100%`** (**if the disability reaches `100%` total, ZERO deduction is permitted**!).

blocks.text: B. 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.20 & 4.27: Analogous Ratings (*Lendenmann* & *Webb v. McDonough*)

When a veteran's service-connected disease or injury is unlisted in the VASRD, **`38 C.F.R. § 4.20`** forbids conjectural or unsubstantiated analogies (`"Conjectural analogies will be avoided, as will the use of analogous ratings for conditions of doubtful diagnosis, or for those not fully supported by clinical and laboratory findings"`) and instead mandates rating under a **"closely related disease or injury"** in which not only the **functions affected**, but the **anatomical localization** and **symptomatology** are closely analogous. Under **`38 C.F.R. § 4.27`**, unlisted analogous evaluations are formatted on the Rating Code Sheet as hyphenated `xx99-xxxx` codes (e.g., `7399-7346` or `8599-8520` — see [VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon)).

items: ***Lendenmann v. Principi*, `3 Vet. App. 345, 350–51 (1992)`:** Codified the mandatory **three-factor test** requiring the Board to compare competing candidate Diagnostic Codes across **(1) functions affected, (2) anatomical localization, and (3) symptomatology**, providing written reasons or bases why the chosen code is the closest match.

***Webb v. McDonough*, `71 F.4th 1377, 1381–83 (Fed. Cir. 2023)` (Eliminating the Literal-Prerequisite Trap!):**
• **The VA Error:** VA rated a veteran's medication-induced erectile dysfunction by analogy to `DC 7522` (`7599-7522`, pre-2021 text providing `20%` for *"Penis, deformity, with loss of erectile power"*) at `0%`, claiming the veteran could not receive `20%` because he lacked physical *penile deformity*.
• **The Federal Circuit Holding:** Vacating the CAVC, the Federal Circuit held that **requiring an unlisted disability rated by analogy under `§ 4.20` to strictly satisfy every literal diagnostic or anatomical prerequisite of the listed Diagnostic Code renders analogous rating illusory**! Once a listed DC is selected as closely related under `§ 4.20`, the unlisted condition need only approximate the functional/symptomatic impairment of that tier, **not** extraneous anatomical preconditions inherent only to the named disease. *(For operational code-selection strategy, see [Playbook 19, Track B](/playbooks/19-extraschedular-3.321b1-analogous-4.20-and-temp-total)).*

blocks.text: C. 38 C.F.R. § 4.25 Combined Ratings Table & § 4.26 Bilateral Factor (Including the Apr. 16, 2023 § 4.26(d) Rule)

VA never adds disability percentages arithmetically (`50% + 30% != 80%`). Under **`38 C.F.R. § 4.25`** (*Table I*), ratings are combined sequentially from **highest to lowest** based on **continuing whole-person efficiency**:
$$\text{Combined Raw Rating after Disability } i = C_{i-1} + \text{round}\!\left(R_i \times \frac{100 - C_{i-1}}{100}\right)$$

items: **Sequential Whole-Person Lookup (`§ 4.25(a)`):** Start at `100%` efficiency. A `50%` disability leaves `50%` efficiency. A second `30%` disability impairs `30%` of the remaining `50%` efficiency (`15%`), yielding **`50 + 15 = 65%`** raw combined value (note: in Table I, each pairwise step rounds to the nearest whole integer before combining the next disability!).

**Final `10%` Rounding Rule (`§ 4.25(a)`):** After *all* disabilities are combined, convert the final exact integer (`0–99`) to the nearest multiple of `10`: values ending in **`1` through `4` round DOWN** (e.g., `64% -> 60%`, `94% -> 90%`), while values ending in **`5` through `9` round UP** (`65% -> 70%`, **`95% -> 100%`**!).

**Mandatory `10%` Bilateral Factor (`38 C.F.R. § 4.26(a)–(c)`):**
• **Trigger:** Compensable (`>= 10%`) service-connected disabilities affecting **both upper extremities**, **both lower extremities**, OR **paired skeletal muscles** (`§ 4.26(a)`). *(Upper and lower extremities are distinct pairs; spine trunk ROM `DC 5235–5243` is NOT an extremity disability, whereas bilateral sciatic radiculopathy `DC 8520` IS!)*
• **Order-of-Operations Rule (`§ 4.26(c)` — CUE Trap!):** Bilateral disabilities **must be combined FIRST** in descending order via Table I; then **exact `10%` of that combined bilateral value** is added (before `10s` rounding, rounded to the nearest integer—e.g., `30%` R knee + `20%` L ankle = `44%` + `4.4` bilateral factor = `48.4 -> 48%`), and that **`48%` single composite unit** is then sorted and combined in descending order with all non-bilateral disabilities!

**Historical Evolution — The April 16, 2023 `§ 4.26(d)` Bilateral Exclusion Rule (`88 FR 22914`):**
• **The `94% -> 90%` Rounding Paradox:** Because Table I rounds intermediate integers at each step, adding a `10%` bilateral factor can shift an intermediate number so that the final raw score lands at **`94%` (`-> 90%`)** whereas combining the exact same disabilities *without* the bilateral factor lands at **`95%` (`-> 100%`)**!
• **Worked Mathematical Proof (`88 FR 22914` Preamble Archetype):** Suppose a veteran's non-bilateral disabilities (`80%` Heart + `50%` PTSD + `30%` Sleep Apnea) combine to **`93%` raw**, plus paired bilateral lower-extremity ratings of **`10%` Right Knee** and **`10%` Left Knee**:
• **WITH Bilateral Factor (Pre-Apr. 16, 2023):** `10%` R + `10%` L = `19%` + `1.9` (`10%` bonus) = **`21%`** bilateral unit. Combining `93%` with `21%`: $93 + (21 \times 0.07) = 93 + 1.47 = 94.47 \rightarrow \mathbf{94\% \rightarrow 90\%}$!
• **WITHOUT Bilateral Factor (`§ 4.26(d)` Exclusion):** Combine `93%` + `10%` R = $93 + 0.7 = 93.7 \rightarrow 94\%$; then `94%` + `10%` L = $94 + 0.6 = 94.6 \rightarrow \mathbf{95\% \rightarrow 100\%}$!
• **Bitemporal Effective-Date Gate (`88 FR 22914`, published Apr. 14, 2023, effective April 16, 2023):** Enacted **`38 C.F.R. § 4.26(d)`**, mandating exclusion of bilateral disabilities from the bilateral factor whenever inclusion lowers the combined rating. **Prospective liberalizing rule (`38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)`) effective April 16, 2023**—cannot support CUE prior to April 16, 2023, but **IS mathematical CUE** if omitted on or after April 16, 2023!

blocks.text: D. 38 C.F.R. § 4.31 (*Zero Percent Evaluations*)

Whenever a Diagnostic Code omits an explicit `0%` tier (for example, `DC 8100` Migraines prior to `0%` or modern `DC 7319` IBS at `10%/20%/30%`, `DC 6260` Tinnitus at `10%`, or `DC 5276` Pes Planus), **`§ 4.31` mandates assigning a `0%` service-connected evaluation** whenever service connection is established (`current diagnosed disability + in-service incurrence + nexus`) even if compensable (`10%+`) severity criteria are unmet. Denying service connection outright for lack of `10%` severity violates `§ 4.31` (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive).
5. Temporary Total (100%) Schedular Evaluations (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.28, 4.29, 4.30)

Originally structured in the 1945 VASRD and modernized in 1989 (**`54 FR 4281`**, pub. Jan. 30, 1989, **eff. Mar. 1, 1989**; technical updates at **`54 FR 34981`**, Aug. 23, 1989), Sections `4.28`, `4.29`, and `4.30` assign temporary schedular evaluations without requiring permanent `100%` criteria (verbatim snapshots in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.1–4.31 Subpart A General Rating Policy & Two-Era § 3.321(b)(1) Extraschedular Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.1-4.31-general-policy-snapshots); full litigation and *Bradley* `SMC(s)` audit workflow in [Playbook 19, Track C](/playbooks/19-extraschedular-3.321b1-analogous-4.20-and-temp-total)):

headers: Effective Date, Prosthetic Interplay (*Hudgens*) & `§ 3.105(e)` Reduction Rules
rows: **Prestabilization Rating from Date of Discharge from Service** — Unstabilized disability with severe impairment at separation (`unhealed/incompletely healed wounds or injuries` where material impairment of employability is likely).

• **`100%`:** Severe disability where continuing employability is **not feasible or advised**. · • **`50%`:** Severe unhealed/incompletely healed disability where material impairment of employability is likely. · • **Duration:** Runs **12 months following discharge** (scheduled re-exam between months `6` and `12`).

Effective **day following separation** (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(b)(1)` when claimed within 1 year of discharge). **Exclusion:** Never assigned if the veteran immediately qualifies for an equal or higher regular schedular `100%` evaluation (`§ 4.28`).

**Hospital Treatment or Observation (`>21 Days`)** — Inpatient treatment or observation for an **SC disability** in a **VA hospital or VA-approved hospital** in excess of **21 continuous days** (even if originally admitted for an NSC disability, once SC hospital treatment is instituted and continues `>21` days under `§ 4.29(b)`; `<21` days needing prolonged convalescence referred to Director under `§ 4.29(g)` / `§ 3.321(b)(1)`).

• **`100%`** beginning on the **first day of continuous SC hospitalization** (`§ 4.29(a)`–`(b)`), with physician-approved temporary releases not breaking continuity (`§ 4.29(a)`). · • Terminates **last day of the month** of hospital discharge (or release to non-bed care) OR **last day of the month** of termination of SC treatment/observation (`§ 4.29(a)`), plus optional `1, 2, or 3` mos post-discharge convalescence (`§ 4.29(e)`) and `1, 2, or 3` further mos with VSCM approval (`§ 4.29(f)`).

• **1-Year Claim Window (`§ 3.400(o)(2)`):** Post-Mar. 24, 2015, claim/ITF must be received within **1 year** of hospital admission/treatment to capture day-1 retroactivity (*pre-Mar. 24, 2015 VAMC admissions triggered automatic informal claims under `former § 3.157(b)`!*). · • **`SMC(s)` Unlock:** Triggers mandatory statutory **`SMC(s)`** if separate SC disabilities combine to `>= 60%` (*Bradley v. Peake*, `22 Vet. App. 280 (2008)`).

**Convalescent Ratings (`100%` Post-Surgical or Cast Immobilization)** — Treatment in a VA or **any** hospital/outpatient surgical center for an **SC disability** resulting in: · **(1)** Surgery necessitating **at least 1 month of convalescence** (`§ 4.30(a)(1)`); · **(2)** Surgery with **severe postoperative residuals** (incompletely healed surgical wounds, therapeutic immobilizing casts, crutches/wheelchair inability to navigate, or strict house confinement) (`§ 4.30(a)(2)`); **OR** · **(3)** **Immobilization by cast, without surgery, of one or more major joints** (shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip, knee, ankle) (`§ 4.30(a)(3)`).

• **`100%`** from date of hospital admission or outpatient surgery/cast application. · • **Initial Duration:** **`1, 2, or 3 months`** from the **first day of the month following hospital discharge or outpatient release** (`§ 4.30`). · • **Extensions:** Extendable by **`1, 2, or 3` additional months** (`up to 6 mos total`) under `(a)(1)–(3)` (`§ 4.30(b)(1)`), and **`1` to `6` further months** (`up to 12 mos total`) under `(a)(2)–(3)` with VSCM approval (`§ 4.30(b)(2)`).

• **Joint Replacement Interplay (*Hudgens v. McDonald*, `823 F.3d 630 (Fed. Cir. 2016)` & `85 FR 76453`):** Under *Hudgens*, **partial knee replacements** qualified under pre-Feb. 7, 2021 `DC 5055` (`1-year` `100%`) for claims filed/pending before VA's interim rule (`80 FR 42040`, July 16, 2015); effective **Feb. 7, 2021 (`85 FR 76453`)**, total joint replacements (`DC 5054/5055`) carry a `4-month` `100%` period while partial/resurfacing procedures fall under `§ 4.30`. · • **`§ 3.105(e)` Reduction Trap:** Expiring a fixed `§ 4.30` period back to the **pre-surgical running baseline** is exempt from `§ 3.105(e)` (`§ 4.30` text), **HOWEVER**, reducing a veteran **below** their pre-surgical baseline evaluation—or discontinuing a post-treatment cancer `100%` without `§ 3.105(e)` 60-day notice under `DC 7528` Note (*Foster v. McDonough*, `34 Vet. App. 338 (2021)`, which enforces `§ 3.105(e)` notice while holding `§§ 3.343/3.344` stabilized-rating rules inapplicable to temporary cancer discontinuances)—is **void *ab initio***!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: How VA's Whole-Person Math, Anti-Pyramiding, Medication & Bilateral Rules Work Across Eras
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: VA disability percentages do not add up by simple addition; instead, 38 C.F.R. § 4.25 uses 'whole-person remaining efficiency' math, enhanced by a 10% bilateral factor when compensable disabilities affect paired arms or paired legs (§ 4.26). This comparison guide explains how Subpart A's core doctrines operate and how they changed over time—including why distinct symptoms of the same injury can earn separate ratings without 'pyramiding' (§ 4.14; Esteban v. Brown), why VA cannot penalize Veterans for taking symptom-controlling medication when the Diagnostic Code does not mention medication (§ 4.10; Ingram v. Collins), how analogous codes work (§ 4.20; Webb v. McDonough), and how April 2023's § 4.26(d) rule fixed a rare rounding quirk at 94%.
record_clues: A Rating Code Sheet omitting the 10% bilateral factor on compensable left-and-right arm or leg conditions (§ 4.26(a)–(c)), or rounding a combined raw 94% down to 90% on or after April 16, 2023 when excluding a bilateral condition reaches 95% -> 100% (§ 4.26(d)).

A VA denial refusing to assign separate percentages for distinct, non-overlapping effects of a single injury—such as knee instability plus limited bending, or a painful scar plus muscle or nerve damage—by broadly citing 'pyramiding' (§ 4.14).

A VA exam or decision lowering a rating because daily medication masks pain, reflux, voiding frequency, or migraines under a Diagnostic Code that says nothing about medication—especially any decision issued during the February 17–27, 2026 window before 91 FR 7118 was rescinded.

A temporary 100% hospital (§ 4.29) or surgical convalescent (§ 4.30) period where separate permanent service-connected disabilities combined to 60% or more, yet VA omitted statutory Special Monthly Compensation at the housebound rate (SMC(s) under Bradley v. Peake).
important_cautions: Higher-of-two-ratings (§ 4.7) vs. cumulative criteria: when a Diagnostic Code uses 'and' or builds successively on lower tiers (such as the 40% tier of Diagnostic Code 7913 Diabetes Mellitus requiring insulin, restricted diet, AND regulation of activities under Middleton v. Shinseki), § 4.7 cannot skip a missing mandatory element.

Do not rely on unfinalized or rescinded proposals: VA's February 17, 2026 § 4.10 medication rule (91 FR 7118) was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712), while proposed changes to sleep apnea/tinnitus (RIN 2900-AQ72), mental disorders (RIN 2900-AQ82), and painful scars (90 FR 46542) remain proposed and unfinalized (not enacted law).
Diagnostic code re-labeling under 38 C.F.R. § 4.13 when a condition's medical name evolves is different from severing 10-year protected service connection under 38 C.F.R. § 3.957 (Read v. Shinseki).

Under George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1403(e) and 20.1409(c), later judicial reinterpretations such as Webb (2023) or Ingram (2025) apply to open claims and appeals rather than Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) motions against older final decisions, and only one final merits CUE decision is permitted per prior Board issue.
questions_for_representative: Are all distinct, non-overlapping symptoms of my service-connected injuries—such as orthopedic limitation, joint instability, scars, and nerve pain—separately accounted for under 38 C.F.R. § 4.14?
Does the April 16, 2023 bilateral exclusion rule in 38 C.F.R. § 4.26(d) affect my combined rating if my raw score sits near 94%?
If I received a temporary 100% hospitalization (§ 4.29) or surgical convalescent (§ 4.30) rating while holding other 60%+ disabilities, did VA pay statutory SMC(s) during those months?
Should we challenge an unfavorable analogous '-99' code or medication-discounted exam through a Supplemental Claim, Higher-Level Review, or Board appeal?
