Part 3` status thresholds governing **surviving spouse recognition** (`38 U.S.C. §§ 101(3), 103(a)–(d), 1304, 1318(c)`; `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.1(j), 3.50–3.55`) and **helpless child dependency** (`38 U.S.C. §§ 101(4)(A)(ii), 103(e), 1313–1314, 3562`; `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.55(b), 3.57, 3.356, 3.707, 21.3023`).

*(For verbatim `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.22` and `3.1000–3.1010` snapshots, see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.22 & 3.312 (Hypothetical § 1318 Total-Disability DIC Evolution & Service-Connected Cause of Death)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.22-dic-hypothetical-evolution) and [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.1000, 3.1010 & 3.816(f) (Accrued Benefits, § 5121A Substitution & Nehmer Survivor/Estate Payouts)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.1000-3.1010-accrued-substitution); for operational litigation strategy, see [Playbook 08 (DIC & `§ 1318`)](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical), [Playbook 09 (Accrued, Substitution & *Nehmer*)](/playbooks/09-accrued-benefits-substitution-nehmer-estates), [Playbook 06 (*Nehmer* `§ 3.816`)](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc), and the [48-Hour Survivor Post-Mortem Triage Checklist](/checklists/survivor-post-mortem-triage-gate)).*
1. Surviving Spouse Validity, Cohabitation & Duration Thresholds (38 C.F.R. §§ 3.1(j), 3.50–3.54)
A. Choice-of-Law Validity & Same-Sex Marriage Evolution (38 U.S.C. § 103(c); 38 C.F.R. § 3.1(j))

rows: `38 U.S.C. § 103(c)` [pre-1991 unchanged section number; see [Statutory Crosswalk](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk)]; `38 C.F.R. § 3.1(j)`

A marriage is valid if valid under the law of the place where the parties **resided at the time of marriage** OR where the parties **resided when the right to benefits accrued** (includes ceremonial, common-law, tribal, and proxy marriages if recognized by that jurisdiction).

Executive Branch ceased enforcing DOMA § 3 (`Sept. 4, 2013`), but `38 U.S.C. § 103(c)` state-residency language temporarily blocked VA recognition where couples resided in states banning same-sex marriage both at marriage and accrual.

Eliminated all state-residency marriage bans nationwide under `§ 103(c)` and `§ 3.1(j)`. *(Bitemporal CUE Note: Under George v. McDonough, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` and `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`, Obergefell cannot be used to prove CUE in a final pre-June 2015 denial that applied extant § 103(c) law—use liberalizing/supplemental pathways or Instruction `01-22` below (Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE))).*
Secretary Instruction `01-22` (`87 FR 68904`, pub. Nov. 17, 2022, eff. Oct. 11, 2022)

Where unconstitutional state/federal bans prevented a same-sex couple from marrying early enough to satisfy the **1-year** DIC/pension duration rule (`§§ 1304, 1318(c), 1541(f)`) or **8-year** DIC kicker (`§ 1311(a)(2)`), VA counts a documented pre-*Obergefell* **"marriage-type" relationship** toward marriage duration!

blocks.text: B. Deemed Valid Marriage vs. Continuous Cohabitation Rescue (38 U.S.C. §§ 101(3), 103(a); 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.52, 3.53)

rows: Attempted marriage invalid due to a **legal impediment** is deemed valid if: · 1. Married `>= 1 year` before death, OR **any period** if a child was born of/before the purported marriage (`§ 3.54(d)`), · 2. Claimant entered marriage **without knowledge of the impediment** (`§ 3.52(b)`), · 3. Continuous cohabitation to death (`§ 3.52(c)` / `§ 3.53`), AND · 4. **No rival legal surviving spouse** files and establishes entitlement to gratuitous death benefits (`§ 3.52(d)`).

• ***Dedicatoria v. Brown*, `8 Vet. App. 441 (1995)`:** Ignorance of the impediment is tested **solely at the moment the purported marriage was contracted** (discovering the veteran's prior undissolved marriage *later* does NOT defeat `§ 3.52`!). · • ***Colon v. Brown*, `9 Vet. App. 104 (1996)`:** "Legal impediment" includes a jurisdiction's **non-recognition of common-law marriage**, provided the claimant genuinely lacked knowledge that a ceremony/license was legally required. · • ***Lamour v. Peake*, `544 F.3d 1317 (Fed. Cir. 2008)`:** VA must adjudicate `§ 103(a)`/`§ 3.52` sympathetically alongside applicable `VAOPGCPREC` opinions.

Required for *all* surviving spouse claims (`§ 3.50(b)(1)`). Living apart at the veteran's death **does NOT break continuity** if: · • Separation was due to **misconduct of, or procured by, the veteran without fault on the surviving spouse's part** (e.g., veteran's PTSD volatility, domestic abuse, substance abuse, desertion, infidelity), OR · • Separation was by **mutual consent** for health, medical institutionalization, nursing care, work, or convenience with **no intent by the surviving spouse to desert**.

• ***Gregory v. Brown*, `5 Vet. App. 108 (1993)`:** Invalidated VA's former continuing-fault rule; **absence of fault on the surviving spouse's part is judged strictly at the time the separation occurred** (post-separation conduct while estranged does not retroactively create fault at separation!). · • **`§ 3.53(b)` Presumption:** The surviving spouse's statement as to the reason for separation **shall be accepted** in the absence of contradictory information in the file; state desertion laws do not control.

blocks.text: C. Critical Statutory Diff: Marriage Duration Rules (§ 1304 Direct DIC vs. § 1318(c) Total-Disability DIC)

lines: **DO NOT CONFUSE `38 U.S.C. § 1304` WITH `38 U.S.C. § 1318(c)`:** When a marriage lasted **less than 1 year** before the veteran's death and no child was born to the couple, the **15-year post-discharge rule** rescues `§ 1310` service-connected-death DIC (`§ 1304` / `§ 3.54(c)(1)`) but **DOES NOT EXIST** under `§ 1318(c)` (`§ 3.22(d)`) total-disability non-SC-death DIC!

rows: Any **ONE** of three paths: · 1. Married **before or within `15 years`** after termination of the period of service in which the injury/disease causing death was incurred or aggravated (`§ 3.54(c)(1)`), OR · 2. Married for **`1 year` or more** (`§ 3.54(c)(2)`), OR · 3. Married for **any period of time** if a **child was born** of the marriage or born to them before the marriage (`§ 3.54(c)(3)`).

Biological child born on or after the marriage date, or born to the veteran and spouse before the marriage (includes a fetus advanced to the point of gestation required to constitute a birth under the law of the jurisdiction where the fetus was delivered; excludes stepchildren or adopted children for `§ 3.54(d)` waiver purposes).

Only **TWO** paths (**NO 15-year post-service path!**): · 1. Married to the veteran for **`1 year` or more** immediately preceding the veteran's death, OR · 2. Married for **any period of time** if a **child was born** of the marriage or born to them before the marriage.
Same `§ 3.54(d)` definition (also review Secretary Instruction `01-22`, `87 FR 68904` if same-sex marriage bans prevented 1-year duration).

blocks.text: 2. Multi-Era Remarriage Termination, Restoration & Age-Cutoff Diff (38 U.S.C. § 103(d); 38 C.F.R. § 3.55(a))

headers: Effect of Remarriage (or "Holding Out") on DIC & Ancillaries
Restoration / Age-Retention Rules & Critical Temporal Traps
rows: Remarriage—or living with another person and openly holding oneself out as their spouse ("inferred remarriage")—**permanently terminated** widow(er) status.
**Permanent bar** unless the purported remarriage was **void** or **annulled** (`§ 3.55(a)(1)`). Death or divorce of the second spouse did *not* restore DIC or pension.
Remarriage or holding out terminated DIC/pension while ongoing, **subject to full restoration** upon termination.

**Full Restoration Era:** Termination of remarriage by **death or divorce** (free of fraud/collusion) OR cessation of open cohabitation/holding-out **restored both DIC and Survivors Pension** (`§ 3.55(a)(2)`).
Repealed `§ 103(d)` restoration for claims filed after **Oct. 31, 1990**.

**Grandfather Rescue Exceptions (`§ 3.55(a)(2)`):** Restoration *remained available* during `1990–1998` if: · 1. Claimant was a **former surviving spouse whose remarriage had already terminated before Nov. 1, 1990**, OR · 2. Legal divorce/annulment proceedings were **commenced before Nov. 1, 1990**!
Remarriage barred DIC while ongoing (except CHAMPVA at **age `55+`** eff. Feb. 4, 2003 under `Pub. L. 107-330`), **but restoration upon termination returned for DIC**.

• **Oct. 1, 1998 (`§ 3.55(a)(3)`):** Termination of remarriage by death, divorce, or annulment (or cessation of cohabitation) **restored Chapter 13 DIC** prospectively from Oct. 1, 1998. · • **Dec. 1, 1999 (`§ 3.55(a)(4)`):** Restored `CHAMPVA (§ 1781)`, `DEA (ch. 35)`, and `VA Home Loan (ch. 37)` upon termination. · • **TRAP:** **Survivors Pension (`ch. 15`) WAS NEVER RESTORED** post-OBRA 1990 unless an Era 3 pre-Nov. 1, 1990 grandfather exception or void/annulled rule applies!
Remarriage **on or after attaining age `57`** **NO LONGER BARS** `Chapter 13 DIC`, `CHAMPVA (§ 1781)`, `DEA (ch. 35)`, or `VA Home Loan (ch. 37)`!

**Pre-Dec. 16, 2003 Transition Cutoff Trap (`Pub. L. 108-183, § 101(e)` / `§ 3.55(a)(10)(ii)`):** · • Spouses who remarried at age `57+` *before* **Dec. 16, 2003** had to submit a written application received by VA **before December 16, 2004** (*Frederick v. Shinseki*, `684 F.3d 1263 (Fed. Cir. 2012)`, *rev'g* `24 Vet. App. 335 (2011)` — strictly enforcing `§ 101(e)`'s 1-year filing bar against pre-Dec. 16, 2003 remarriages!). · • By contrast, spouses who remarried at age `57+` **on or after Dec. 16, 2003 / Jan. 1, 2004** face **NO 1-year filing bar** (`38 U.S.C. § 103(d)(2)(B)`; `§ 3.55(a)(10)(i)`).
Remarriage **on or after attaining age `55`** (occurring **on or after January 5, 2021**) **NO LONGER BARS `Chapter 13 DIC`** (or `CHAMPVA § 1781`)!

**THREE CRITICAL TRAPS (`Pub. L. 116-315, § 2009` & `87 FR 68360`):** · 1. **No Pre-2021 Grandfathering (`§ 3.55(a)(9)(iii)`):** VA (`87 FR 68360, 68363` & `M21-1 VII.i.2`) applies the age-`55` DIC rule strictly to remarriages occurring **on or after January 5, 2021**. A spouse who remarried at age `55` or `56` in `2018` remains barred from DIC while that marriage continues (whereas a spouse remarrying at age `55` on `Jan. 6, 2021` retains DIC!). *(Appellate Preservation Note: `Pub. L. 116-315 § 2009` amended the second sentence of `§ 103(d)(2)(B)` directly without an explicit pre-enactment cutoff clause unlike `Pub. L. 108-183 § 101(e)`—preserve statutory-text challenges on direct appeal against `87 FR 68360` if encountered).* · 2. **22-Month Regulatory Lag Audit (`Jan. 5, 2021 – Nov. 14, 2022`):** Because VA did not update `38 C.F.R. § 3.55(a)(9)` until **November 15, 2022** (`87 FR 68360`), raters and VLJs during `2021–2022` (or citing stale pre-Nov. 2022 CFR editions) sometimes denied post-Jan. 5, 2021 age-`55+` remarried spouses by quoting unamended `§ 3.55(a)(10)` age-`57` text—a **textbook CUE / statutory error** under controlling `38 U.S.C. § 103(d)(2)(B)` ([Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log))! · 3. **`DEA` & `Home Loan` Still Require Age `57` (`§ 3.55(a)(10)`):** `Pub. L. 116-315 § 2009` inserted `"chapter 13 or"` into the second sentence of `§ 103(d)(2)(B)` alongside `§ 1781`, leaving `Chapter 35 DEA` and `Chapter 37 Home Loan` governed by the **age `57`** rule (`§ 103(d)(2)(B)` sentence 1 & `§ 3.55(a)(10)`)!

blocks.text: A veteran's biological, legally adopted, or qualifying stepchild (`38 C.F.R. § 3.57`) who became **permanently incapable of self-support prior to attaining age `18`** qualifies for **lifetime** dependency additions (`§ 1115`), supplemental DIC (`§ 1314(c)`), or standalone surviving-child DIC (`§ 1313` / `§ 1318`).

rows: • **`§ 3.356(a)` Origin Cutoff:** The physical or mental defect causing permanent incapacity for self-support **must have existed before the child's `18th` birthday** (even if the formal diagnostic label—e.g., schizophrenia, autism spectrum disorder, severe bipolar I, intellectual disability, refractory epilepsy—crystallized shortly after age 18, provided pre-18 medical, school IEP/504, or lay records prove incapacity existed prior to 18). · • **`§ 3.356(b)` Functional Benchmark:** Evaluated solely on whether the child can **earn their own reasonable support through their own competitive efforts**. Intermittent, casual, sheltered-workshop, heavily accommodated family employment, or post-18 college/special-education enrollment **does NOT automatically defeat** `§ 3.356` permanent incapacity! *(Under Dobson, Board determinations under `§ 3.356` are factual findings reviewed for clear error—build a thorough pre-18 functional record).*

**SEVERE ASYMMETRY WITH SURVIVING SPOUSES:** While Congress restored remarried surviving spouses' DIC in `1998` (`TEA-21`), **Congress NEVER repealed the `OBRA 1990` marriage-restoration ban for children (`38 U.S.C. § 103(e)`)!** · • Any valid marriage of a helpless child terminated **on or after November 1, 1990** (unless divorce proceedings began before Nov. 1, 1990, `§ 3.55(b)(2)`) **permanently extinguishes** VA child status—even if the child later divorces or is widowed! · • **Sole Rescue (`§ 3.55(b)(1)`):** Child status survives/resumes **only** if the child's marriage was **void *ab initio*** (e.g., lack of mental capacity to contract marriage under state law!) or **annulled** by a court of competent jurisdiction free of fraud/collusion (`§ 3.400(u)`).
**`Chapter 35` DEA vs. Helpless Child Concurrency & Sequencing Trap**

• **Recognized Helpless Child Concurrency (`38 C.F.R. § 21.3023(b)`):** Unlike regular `18–23` school-attending children, an adjudicated **helpless child (`§ 3.356`) MAY receive `Chapter 35` DEA educational assistance or special restorative training CONCURRENTLY with disability compensation, DIC, or pension** (barring duplicate same-parental-line multi-parent awards on/after June 9, 1960). Raters who terminate an adjudicated helpless child's DIC upon `Ch. 35` DEA payment commit clear legal error! · • **CRITICAL SEQUENCING TRAP (`§ 3562` & `§ 21.3023(a), (c)`):** For a regular `18–23` schoolchild (`§ 21.3023(a)`), negotiating the first `Ch. 35` DEA check/EFT is an **irrevocable lifetime bar** to future schoolchild `18–23` dependency/DIC payments (`§ 21.3023(c)(1)`, save VA misinformation under `(c)(2)`). Therefore, if a disabled 18-year-old commences `Ch. 35` DEA **before** `§ 3.356` helpless-child status is established—and VA later denies `§ 3.356`—the child is **permanently locked out** of schoolchild DIC/dependency rates! Always file and document `§ 3.356` helpless-child status (`VA Form 21-534EZ` / `21-686c` + pre-18 IEP/medical records; see [Forms Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon)) **before** negotiating a `Ch. 35` DEA payment, and frame any post-18 `Ch. 35` enrollment as accommodated or **Subchapter V Special Restorative Training** so examiners do not mischaracterize school attendance as competitive employability.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Surviving Spouse Marriage Rules, Age-55 vs. Age-57 Remarriage Protections (§ 3.55) & Adult 'Helpless Child' Benefits (§ 3.356)
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Before VA even looks at a Veteran's cause of death, VA checks family relationship rules that have changed repeatedly across decades. This guide explains: (1) how a surviving spouse satisfies marriage-validity, 'deemed valid' marriage (§ 3.52), 'continuous cohabitation' separation exceptions (§ 3.53), and marriage-length rules (§ 3.54); (2) how surviving spouses who remarry at age 57+ (for remarriages from January 1, 2004 through January 4, 2021) or age 55+ (for remarriages on or after January 5, 2021) keep their monthly DIC checks under 38 C.F.R. § 3.55; and (3) how an unmarried adult son or daughter who became permanently incapable of self-support BEFORE turning age 18 ('helpless child' under 38 C.F.R. § 3.356) can qualify for lifetime dependency or survivor DIC benefits.
record_clues: A survivor denial stating you were 'living apart at the time of death' even though the separation was due to the Veteran's PTSD/misconduct, medical care, or mutual agreement without fault on your part (§ 3.53).

A surviving spouse who remarried at age 57 or older on/after January 1, 2004, OR remarried at age 55 or older on/after January 5, 2021 (including during the 2021–2022 statutory lag window before VA updated § 3.55 on November 15, 2022), or whose earlier remarriage ended by death, divorce, or annulment.

A marriage lasting slightly under 1 year before the Veteran's death where a child was born to the couple before OR during the marriage (§ 3.54(d)), or where a same-sex couple was legally barred from marrying earlier prior to Obergefell.

School IEPs, pediatric/adolescent medical charts, autism/intellectual disability evaluations, or early psychiatric records showing a Veteran's adult child became permanently unable to support themselves before their 18th birthday (§ 3.356).
important_cautions: Exact Remarriage Date Cutoff (Age 57 vs. Age 55): Congress lowered the DIC retention remarriage age from 57 to 55 in Pub. L. 116-315, § 2009 effective strictly for remarriages occurring ON OR AFTER January 5, 2021 (codified in CFR November 15, 2022 at 87 FR 68360). Remarriages between January 1, 2004 and January 4, 2021 remain governed by age 57, and Chapter 35 DEA / VA home loan retention under § 3.55(a)(10) remains at age 57.

Marriage Length Difference (§ 1310 vs. § 1318): While direct service-connected death DIC (§ 1304) allows a marriage within 15 years after service even if under 1 year long, 10-year total-disability DIC (§ 1318(c)) requires EITHER 1 full year of marriage OR a child born of the marriage.

Critical Chapter 35 DEA Bar for Disabled Young Adults (38 U.S.C. § 3562): If an 18-to-23-year-old disabled child cashes a Chapter 35 DEA education check BEFORE establishing § 3.356 helpless-child status, electing DEA permanently bars standard schoolchild DIC/dependency payments if § 3.356 is denied—and marriage of a helpless child after October 31, 1990 generally ends child status unless void or annulled.
questions_for_representative: Based on the exact date of my remarriage and my age on that wedding date, do I retain DIC under the age-57 (2004+) or age-55 (January 5, 2021+) rule—or qualify for reinstatement because an earlier remarriage ended?
If my spouse and I lived apart before death, does the record show separation without marital fault on my part under 38 C.F.R. § 3.53?

If we were Same-Sex partners prevented by state law from marrying long enough to meet the 1-year or 8-year DIC marriage requirements, can we request consideration under VA Secretary Instruction 01-22?

Before my disabled 18-year-old child applies for or cashes Chapter 35 DEA education benefits, should we adjudicate lifetime § 3.356 helpless-child status first to avoid the 38 U.S.C. § 3562 election trap?

blocks.text: 1. Total Disability Based on Individual Unemployability (38 C.F.R. § 4.16)
A. Historical Federal Register Milestones & CUE Temporal Traps

*(See full verbatim `38 C.F.R. § 4.16(a)–(c)` snapshots in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 4.16 Total Disability Based on Individual Unemployability (1975–Present Evolution & Former § 4.16(c))](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.16-tdiu-evolution) and binding TDIU General Counsel opinions in [Master Binding VA General Counsel Precedent Opinion (VAOPGCPREC) Digest (1989–Present)](/docs/vaopgcprec-index)).*

items: **September 15, 1975 (`40 FR 42535`):** Promulgated the foundational two-paragraph `§ 4.16(a)` (`60%` single / `70%` combined with `40%` anchor + 5 single-disability aggregation categories) and `§ 4.16(b)` (extraschedular Central Office referral) structure.

**March 1, 1989 (`54 FR 4281`, published January 30, 1989, effective March 1, 1989):** Overhauled `§ 4.16` and added **former `38 C.F.R. § 4.16(c)`**, mandating an automatic `100%` schedular evaluation whenever a veteran's *sole* compensable service-connected disability was a mental disorder rated `70%` that precluded substantially gainful employment. *(Former `§ 4.16(c)` remained in force from **March 1, 1989 through November 6, 1996**, when VA removed it via `61 FR 52695`, published Oct. 8, 1996, **effective November 7, 1996** — see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125–4.130 Mental Disorders, Traumatic Stress (§ 4.129), Eating Disorders (DC 9520–9521) & Former § 4.132 Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.132-mental-disorders-pre-1996)).*

**September 4, 1990 (`55 FR 31579`, published August 3, 1990, effective September 4, 1990):** Amended `38 C.F.R. § 4.16(a)` to codify that marginal employment generally exists when earned annual income does not exceed the U.S. Census Bureau poverty threshold for one person.

**Bitemporal CUE Gate (*George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)`; `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`):** Never project post-Sept. 4, 1990 poverty-threshold text backward onto a pre-Sept. 4, 1990 CUE motion, and distinguish plain-text regulatory errors (`§ 4.16(a)(1)–(5)` math, CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive) from later judicial elaborations (*Ray*, *Ortiz-Valles*, *Cantrell*), which govern open, pending, `§ 3.156(b)–(c)`, and appealed claims.

blocks.text: B. Schedular Thresholds (§ 4.16(a)) vs. Extraschedular Referral (§ 4.16(b))

items:
**Schedular `§ 4.16(a)`:** Requires inability to secure or follow a **substantially gainful occupation** (*Ray v. Wilkie*, 31 Vet. App. 58 (2019) — has both an *economic* and a *non-economic* physical/mental ability component!) PLUS:
• **One** disability rated **`60%` or more**, OR
• **Two or more** disabilities with at least one rated **`40%` or more** and sufficient additional disability to bring the **combined rating to `70%` or more**.
**The Overlooked Five "Single Disability" Aggregation Rules (`§ 4.16(a)(1)–(5)`):**

blocks.text: For the `60%` single-disability prong (or the `40%` anchor prong!), **multiple disabilities count as ONE single disability** if they arise from:

items:
One **single common etiology** (e.g., all residuals of Diabetes Mellitus—neuropathy + retinopathy + nephropathy!),
• A **single accident or injury** (e.g., car crash or IED blast!),
• Disabilities affecting a **single bodily system** (e.g., orthopedic, digestive, respiratory, neuropsychiatric),
• **Multiple injuries incurred in action** (any combat wounds across *multiple* wars/engagements combine as **ONE** disability to hit `60%` or `40%`!), OR
• Multiple disabilities incurred as a **Prisoner of War (POW)**.
• **CUE Goldmine:** Raters routinely deny schedular `§ 4.16(a)` TDIU because a veteran has `30%` right knee + `30%` left knee + `20%` lumbar (`64% -> 60%` combined, no single code at `40%`), completely overlooking that all three affect the **musculoskeletal system (`§ 4.16(a)(3)`)** or stem from **combat (`§ 4.16(a)(4)`)**, satisfying the **`60%` single-disability rule** on the face of the code sheet! *(Note: While `§ 4.16(a)(1)-(5)` aggregates disabilities to qualify for TDIU, it does NOT aggregate them into a "single 100% disability" for statutory `SMC(s)`—Gazelle v. Shulkin, 868 F.3d 1006 (Fed. Cir. 2017)).*

**Marginal & Protected Employment (`§ 4.16(a)`):**
• Income below the U.S. Census Bureau poverty threshold for **one person** (`55 FR 31579`, eff. Sept. 4, 1990) is marginal employment by law and **cannot bar TDIU** (*Ortiz-Valles v. McDonald*, 28 Vet. App. 65 (2016)).
• Income *above* the poverty threshold **still qualifies as marginal** if earned in a **protected environment** (e.g., family business or heavily accommodated role shielded from competitive market productivity demands—*Cantrell v. Shulkin*, 28 Vet. App. 382 (2017)).

**Extraschedular `§ 4.16(b)`:** Requires mandatory referral by the RO to the **Director, Compensation Service** whenever a veteran falls below `§ 4.16(a)` percentages yet evidence shows unemployability due to SC disabilities (*Bowling v. Principi*, 15 Vet. App. 1 (2001)). *(Note: RO/BVA lack jurisdiction to grant `§ 4.16(b)` in the first instance without Director review, and failure to refer under `§ 4.16(b)` is normally a procedural/record-weighing error rather than CUE).*

blocks.text: 2. May 19, 2024 Digestive System Overhaul (89 FR 19735, Published March 20, 2024, Effective May 19, 2024 — 38 C.F.R. § 4.114)

*(For the complete System 07 `DC 7200–7357` structural diff—including `§ 4.112` weight loss/parenteral nutrition, `§§ 4.113–4.114` non-combination boundaries, `DC 7326` IBD biologics, `DC 7312/7345` MELD liver rules, and `DC 7355–7357` Celiac/Dysmotility/Post-pancreatectomy—see **[`VASRD System 07 Digestive Diff`](/cfr/modules/07-digestive-system-4.110-4.114)** and verbatim **[Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.110–4.114 Digestive System (DC 7200–7357, Pre- vs. Post-May 19, 2024)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.114-digestive-pre-and-post-2024)**).*

headers: On or After May 19, 2024 (`89 FR 19735`, Pub. Mar. 20, 2024)
rows: Rated by analogy under **`DC 7346` (Hiatal Hernia)**: · • **`10%`:** Two or more symptoms of `30%` group of *less severity*. · • **`30%`:** Persistently recurrent epigastric distress with dysphagia, pyrosis (heartburn), and regurgitation, accompanied by substernal or arm/shoulder pain. · • **`60%`:** Symptoms of pain, vomiting, material weight loss, and hematemesis/melena with moderate anemia.

Dedicated **`DC 7206` (GERD)** — tied strictly to **esophageal stricture & dysphagia**: · • **`0%`:** Documented history without daily symptoms or daily medication. · • **`10%`:** Documented history of **esophageal stricture(s)** requiring daily medications to control dysphagia otherwise asymptomatic. · • **`30%`:** Recurrent esophageal stricture(s) causing dysphagia with dilatation `<=2x/yr`. · • **`50%`:** Recurrent/refractory stricture(s) causing dysphagia with dilatation `>=3x/yr`, steroid dilatation `>=1x/yr`, or esophageal stent. · • **`80%`:** Stricture + aspiration/undernutrition/substantial weight loss + surgical treatment or PEG tube.

**`DC 7319` (Irritable Colon Syndrome):** · • **`0%`:** Mild (disturbances of bowel function with occasional episodes of abdominal distress). · • **`10%`:** Moderate (frequent episodes of bowel disturbance with abdominal distress). · • **`30%`:** Severe (diarrhea, or alternating diarrhea and constipation, with more or less constant abdominal distress) — **Note: No `20%` tier existed!**

**`DC 7319` (IBS — Rome IV Criteria; added `20%` tier!):** Abdominal pain related to defecation over past 3 months + `>=2` of 5 stool/bloating/mucorrhea symptoms: · • **`10%`:** At least **once** during previous 3 months. · • **`20%`:** At least **3 days per month** during previous 3 months. · • **`30%`:** At least **1 day per week** during previous 3 months. *(No `0%` tier—minimum is `10%` if frequency met!)*

lines: **Transitional Protection (`38 U.S.C. § 1155`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.951(a)`):**
* Veterans already rated `10%`, `30%`, or `60%` for GERD under `DC 7346` before May 19, 2024 **cannot** have their rating reduced solely because `DC 7206` now requires esophageal strictures.

* For claims **pending across May 19, 2024** (note `89 FR 19735` was published **March 20, 2024**, effective **May 19, 2024**), VA must evaluate pre-May 19, 2024 periods under `DC 7346` (`DC 7319` old text) and post-May 19, 2024 periods under whichever version (`DC 7346` vs. `DC 7206` / old vs. new `DC 7319`) is **more favorable** to the veteran!

blocks.text: 3. Bilateral Factor Exclusion Rule (38 C.F.R. § 4.26(d), Effective April 16, 2023)

Historically, adding the `10%` bilateral bonus (`38 C.F.R. § 4.26`) could paradoxically **hurt** veterans near the `95% -> 100%` rounding boundary due to intermediate rounding in `§ 4.25` Table I. Effective **April 16, 2023** (`88 FR 22914`, published **April 14, 2023**), VA enacted **`38 C.F.R. § 4.26(d)`**: whenever including bilateral disabilities in the `10%` bilateral factor results in a *lower* combined evaluation (e.g., `94% -> 90%` instead of `95% -> 100%`), VA **must exclude** those bilateral disabilities from the bilateral bonus calculation so the veteran receives the `100%` combined rating!
4. Unfinalized Proposals & Rescinded IFR Watchlist (Active Law Still Governs as of Late 2026)
Practitioners frequently encounter client or rater confusion over **proposed / unfinalized** or **rescinded** VASRD rules (see [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)):

items: **Obstructive Sleep Apnea (`DC 6847`, `RIN 2900-AQ72`, `87 FR 8474`, Feb. 15, 2022):** **Current active law STILL awards `50%`** whenever use of a breathing assistance device such as **CPAP** is medically required (`30%` persistent daytime hypersomnolence). Proposed Feb. 2022 rule remains **unfinalized / not enacted**.

**Tinnitus (`DC 6260`, `RIN 2900-AQ72`, `87 FR 8474`, Feb. 15, 2022):** **Current active law STILL awards a standalone `10%`** for recurrent tinnitus. Proposed Feb. 2022 rule remains **unfinalized / not enacted**.

**Mental Disorders (`38 C.F.R. § 4.130`, `RIN 2900-AQ82`, `87 FR 8498`, Feb. 15, 2022):** Proposed domain-based WHODAS overhaul remains **unfinalized / not enacted**; `0/10/30/50/70/100%` General Rating Formula remains active law.

**Painful Scars (`DC 7804`, `90 FR 46542`, Sept. 29, 2025):** Proposed note requiring objective evidence of pain upon examination/demonstration remains **unfinalized / not enacted**; existing `DC 7804` criteria remain active law.

**Rescinded Medication IFR (`38 C.F.R. § 4.10`, `91 FR 7118` -> Rescinded `91 FR 9712`, Feb. 17–27, 2026):** VA's 10-day Interim Final Rule (`91 FR 7118`) attempting to overturn *Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)` was **formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (`91 FR 9712`)**—audit any decision rendered Feb. 17–27, 2026 that discounted medicated symptoms!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Total Unemployability (TDIU), the May 2024 Digestive Overhaul & Unfinalized Rating Proposals
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: This comparison module connects three major Part 4 rating transitions: (1) how Total Disability Based on Individual Unemployability (TDIU, 38 C.F.R. § 4.16) evolved from 1975 through the March 1, 1989–November 6, 1996 70%-mental-disorder rule (former § 4.16(c)) and the September 4, 1990 poverty-threshold / protected-workplace rule (§ 4.16(a)); (2) how VA's May 19, 2024 digestive overhaul (38 C.F.R. § 4.114) reshaped acid reflux (GERD, Diagnostic Code 7206) and Irritable Bowel Syndrome (Diagnostic Code 7319); and (3) how to separate enacted VASRD rules from unfinalized Federal Register proposals.
record_clues: A Rating Code Sheet showing a single disability rated 60% or higher—or multiple disabilities combining to 70% or higher with at least one at 40% (including grouped conditions sharing a common cause or body system under § 4.16(a)(1)–(5))—alongside medical or vocational records showing you could not hold substantially gainful work.

A TDIU denial because you earned wages below the U.S. Census Bureau poverty threshold for one person, or worked in a family business or sheltered/heavily accommodated job ('protected employment' under § 4.16(a) and Cantrell v. Shulkin).

A GERD or Irritable Bowel Syndrome claim pending across May 19, 2024 where VA applied only one set of criteria instead of checking both pre- and post-May 19, 2024 rules, or reduced an existing pre-2024 GERD rating without actual medical improvement.
Confusion over online rumors claiming VA eliminated standalone tinnitus or 50% CPAP sleep apnea ratings—when those proposals remain unfinalized.
important_cautions: Only service-connected disabilities can establish unemployability under 38 C.F.R. § 4.16(a)–(b); VA cannot count non-service-connected health conditions toward TDIU.

Historical TDIU dates matter: the Census poverty-threshold definition of marginal employment took effect September 4, 1990 (published August 3, 1990 at 55 FR 31579), while former § 4.16(c) (mandating a 100% schedular rating when a 70% mental disorder was the sole compensable disability causing unemployability) was in force only from March 1, 1989 through November 6, 1996.

Existing pre-May 19, 2024 digestive ratings (such as 30% or 60% GERD under former Diagnostic Code 7399-7346) are protected against reduction due to schedule changes under 38 U.S.C. § 1155 and 38 C.F.R. § 3.951(a).

Watch out for unfinalized or rescinded rules: proposed changes to Sleep Apnea and Tinnitus (RIN 2900-AQ72), Mental Disorders (RIN 2900-AQ82), and Painful Scars (90 FR 46542) remain proposed and unfinalized (not enacted law), and VA's February 17, 2026 medication rule (91 FR 7118) was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712).
questions_for_representative: Do multiple service-connected disabilities in my file share a common etiology or single body system under 38 C.F.R. § 4.16(a)(1)–(5) so they count as one disability toward the 60% or 40% schedular TDIU threshold?
Did an earlier increase claim alongside evidence of job loss reasonably raise TDIU under Roberson v. Principi and Rice v. Shinseki?
If my GERD or IBS claim was pending across May 19, 2024, did VA evaluate both the pre-May 19, 2024 and post-May 19, 2024 criteria to award the more favorable rating?
If I work part-time below the poverty threshold or receive special accommodations from a family/sympathetic employer, what documentation helps show marginal or protected employment under § 4.16(a)?

blocks.text: This Reference module tracks the primary-source statutory and `38 C.F.R. Part 3` evolution across three major non-herbicide compensation regimes—**Persian Gulf War illnesses (`§ 3.317`)**, **fine particulate matter / burn pits (`§§ 3.320, 3.320a, 3.320b`)**, and **VA medical/rehabilitation injuries (`§§ 3.358, 3.361–3.363`)**—isolating exact **Federal Register publication vs. effective dates**, **statute-vs.-CFR lag periods**, and ***George v. McDonough* (`596 U.S. 740 (2022)`) / `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)` bitemporal CUE boundaries**.

*(For operational pleading contracts, see [Playbook 15 (Gulf War `§ 3.317`, Burn Pits & `§ 1168` TERA)](/playbooks/15-gulf-war-mucmi-burn-pits-pact-tera), [Playbook 17 (`38 U.S.C. § 1151` Malpractice & `FTCA` Offsets)](/playbooks/17-section-1151-va-malpractice-and-ftca-interplay), [Playbook 06 (*Nehmer* & *Soto* CRSC)](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc), [Playbook 07 (`§§ 3.309(a)–(d)`, ALS, Radiation & Lejeune)](/playbooks/07-statutory-presumptions-chronic-tropical-pow-als), [Playbook 08 (Survivor DIC & `§ 1305`)](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical), [Playbook 13 (Ancillary Grants)](/playbooks/13-ancillary-grants-sah-auto-clothing-dea-spina-bifida), [`Part 3 SMC Evolution Diff`](/cfr/modules/smc-statutory-and-regulatory-evolution), [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) Service Department Records (Pre-Oct. 6, 2006 vs. Current)](/cfr/38-cfr-3.156c), [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.350, 3.352, 3.552(b), 4.63 & 3.810(a) (Special Monthly Compensation Ratings, Aid & Attendance, TBI SMC(t), Loss of Use & Multiple Clothing Allowances)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.350-3.352-smc-evolution), [Three-Era Statutory Crosswalk](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk), [Master `VAOPGCPREC` Digest](/docs/vaopgcprec-index), [VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon), [Procedural Vehicles Piercing Finality](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality), and [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).*
1. Family I: 38 C.F.R. § 3.317 (38 U.S.C. §§ 1117–1118) Persian Gulf War Evolution (1994–2026)

rows: Created **`38 U.S.C. § 1117`** & **`38 C.F.R. § 3.317`**. Covered **undiagnosed illnesses ONLY** (`>= 10%` severity), originally within a `2-year` post-Southwest-Asia departure window *(extended repeatedly at `62 FR 23138`, Apr. 29, 1997; `66 FR 56614`, Nov. 9, 2001; `76 FR 81834`, Dec. 29, 2011; `87 FR 6038`, Feb. 3, 2022)*.

**CRITICAL `1994–2002` CUE TRAP:** Before **March 1, 2002**, any *known clinical diagnosis* (even `CFS`, `fibromyalgia`, or `IBS`!) defeated `§ 3.317`! Never plead CUE on a pre-Mar. 1, 2002 denial of a *diagnosed* `MUCMI`.

Expanded `"qualifying chronic disability"` (`§ 3.317(a)(2)(i)(B)`) beyond undiagnosed illnesses to include **diagnosed Medically Unexplained Chronic Multisymptom Illnesses (`MUCMIs`)** (**`CFS`**, **fibromyalgia**, and **`IBS`**), while excluding partially explained illnesses (`diabetes`, `MS`, **`§ 3.317(a)(2)(ii)`**).

**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (`Mar. 1, 2002` floor)**; **CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (`>= Mar. 1, 2002`)** if AOJ/Board demanded a medical nexus (*Gutierrez v. Principi*, `19 Vet. App. 1 (2004)`) on `>= 10%`, `6-month` `CFS`/`fibromyalgia`/`IBS`!

Added **`38 C.F.R. § 3.317(c)`**: presumptive SC for **`9` infectious diseases** (`brucellosis`, *Campylobacter jejuni*, `Q fever`, `malaria`, `TB`, nontyphoid *Salmonella*, *Shigella*, `visceral leishmaniasis`, `West Nile virus`) + secondary long-term sequelae (`§ 3.317(d)`), **adding Afghanistan (`>= Sept. 19, 2001`) STRICTLY for `§ 3.317(c)` infectious diseases**!

**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (`Sept. 29, 2010` floor).** Note `1-year` post-separation manifestation rule for `7` acute pathogens vs. `no time limit` for `visceral leishmaniasis` & `TB` (`§ 3.317(c)(3)`).

Replaced standalone `"irritable bowel syndrome"` in `§ 3.317(a)(2)(i)(B)(3)` with **"functional gastrointestinal disorders (`FGIDs`)"** + explanatory Note covering `IBS`, functional dyspepsia, functional vomiting/constipation/bloating, and functional abdominal pain syndrome (*excluding structural IBD*).
**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (`Aug. 15, 2011` floor)** for non-`IBS` `FGIDs` (note `31-day` gap between July 15 publication and Aug. 15 effective date!).
***Joyner v. McDonald***, `766 F.3d 1393 (Fed. Cir. 2014)`; ***Stewart v. Wilkie***, `30 Vet. App. 383 (2018)`
***Joyner*:** Pain alone without somatic pathology qualifies as an undiagnosed illness. ***Stewart* & *Goodman* (`870 F.3d 1383`):** Case-by-case medical test for non-enumerated `MUCMIs`.
Check *George* (`§ 20.1403(e)`) before attacking pre-2014 pain-only denials via CUE; fully retroactive on all open/pending/`§ 3.156(c)` claims.

`(1)` Replaced the legacy `10%` threshold and `Dec. 31, 2026` sunset in **`38 U.S.C. § 1117(a)(1)`** with **"became manifest to any degree at any time"** (`0%` floor & permanent eligibility); `(2)` Enacted **`38 U.S.C. § 1117(f)`**, adding **Afghanistan, Israel, Egypt, Turkey, Syria, and Jordan** to `§ 1117` `MUCMI` & undiagnosed-illness coverage!

**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (`Aug. 10, 2022` floor)** for `< 10%` `MUCMIs` and the `6` newly added `§ 1117(f)` countries (*except* `§ 1305` survivor DIC re-evaluations!). Positive statutory text overrides stale `eCFR` `§ 3.317(a)(1)(i)` (`89 FR 79815` remains *proposed / not finalized*).
Zero burn-pit or `PM2.5` presumptions; claimants had to prove individualized particulate exposure and medical nexus.
Pre-2021 denials cannot be attacked via CUE for omitting post-2021 presumptions; use **`§ 3.156(c)`** + direct `§ 1168` nexus to reach pre-2021 dates!

Enacted **`38 C.F.R. § 3.320`**: presumptive SC for **asthma, rhinitis, and sinusitis (`rhinosinusitis`)** (`Southwest Asia` `>= Aug. 2, 1990`; `Afghanistan, Syria, Djibouti, Uzbekistan` `>= Sept. 19, 2001`), **RESTRICTED by a harsh `10-year` post-separation manifestation cap**!
**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (`Aug. 5, 2021` floor)** for claims meeting the `10-year` cap prior to Aug. 10, 2022.

Added **`9` rare respiratory cancers** (squamous cell carcinoma of larynx/trachea, adenocarcinoma of trachea, salivary gland-type tumors of trachea/lung, adenosquamous/large-cell/sarcomatoid lung carcinomas, typical/atypical lung carcinoid) at **`0%` floor & zero manifestation limit**.
**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (`Apr. 26, 2022` floor)** — `3.5 months` *earlier* than the Aug. 10, 2022 PACT Act floor!

Enacted **`38 U.S.C. § 1119`** (`Aug. 2, 1990+` incl. **Somalia**; `Sept. 11, 2001+` incl. **Afghanistan, Djibouti, Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, Uzbekistan/K2** + airspace), **`§ 1120`** (`11` cancer categories + `12` respiratory diseases, **`0%` floor**, **abolishing the `86 FR 42724` `10-year` cap**!), and **`§ 1168` `TERA`**.

**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (`Aug. 10, 2022` statutory floor)** for living veterans (*Nehmer* `§ 3.816` **inapplicable**); **CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** post-Aug. 10, 2022 if rater applies `10%` floor or `10-yr` cap; **`§ 1305` full retroactivity** for prior denied DIC!

`89 FR 51224` added **urethral cancer**, **paraurethral gland cancer**, and **male breast cancer** (`eff. June 17, 2024` / PACT alignment). **Eff. Sept. 30, 2025**, VA prospectively rescinded sub-regulatory presumptive status for **male breast cancer** (grandfathering pre-Sept. 30, 2025 awards).

**Bifurcated Window:** Pre-Sept. 30, 2025 grants protected; post-Sept. 30, 2025 male breast cancer claims must preserve statutory `§ 1120(b)(2)(H)` (`"reproductive cancer of any type"`) + `§ 1168` TERA nexus!

Codified **`38 C.F.R. § 3.320a`**: presumptive SC (`0%` floor, zero time limit) for **urinary bladder cancer** (incl. overlapping sites) and **ureter cancer** (incl. ureteric orifice & urachus) in `§ 1119(c)` veterans.
**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (`Jan. 2, 2025` floor)** unless direct `§ 1168` TERA nexus or `§ 1305` DIC applies.

Codified **`38 C.F.R. § 3.320b`**: presumptive SC (`0%` floor, zero time limit) for **acute leukemias, chronic leukemias, multiple myelomas (including `MGUS`), myelodysplastic syndromes (`MDS`), and myelofibrosis** in `§ 1119(c)` veterans.
**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (`Jan. 10, 2025` floor)** (`§ 3.114(a)` 1-year lookback to Jan. 10, 2025 if diagnosed by that date).

Statutory text contained **NO fault requirement**, yet VA enforced an *ultra vires* fault rule in **`former 38 C.F.R. § 3.358(c)(3)`**. Struck down unanimously in ***Brown v. Gardner*, `513 U.S. 115 (Dec. 12, 1994)`** (`§ 3.358` revised at `60 FR 14222`, Mar. 16, 1995).

**SPLIT BITEMPORAL GATE:** · • **Final pre-Dec. 12, 1994 denials:** **Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** (*George* / `§ 20.1403(e)` bars standalone CUE; check `§ 3.156(b)` 1-yr VAMC notes!). · • **Decisions `Dec. 12, 1994 – Sept. 30, 1997` (or still-open pre-Oct. 1, 1997 claims):** **CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** under *Gardner* no-fault standard!

Restored **proximate VA fault (`§ 3.361(d)(1)`)**, lack of **`§ 17.32` informed consent**, OR **"event not reasonably foreseeable" (`§ 3.361(d)(2)`)** for medical/exam claims received **`>= Oct. 1, 1997`** (`Ch. 31 VR&E` kept no-fault causation). Codified `§ 3.361(f)` contract-care exclusions and `§ 3.362(b)–(d)` gross vs. survivor FTCA offsets.

**Reopening Trap (`38 C.F.R. § 3.361(a)`):** Any claim to reopen a denied pre-1997 `§ 1151` claim received **`>= Oct. 1, 1997`** is governed by `§ 3.361` fault/unforeseeability! *(Note `30-day` gap between Aug. 3, 2004 FR publication and Sept. 2, 2004 CFR effective date).*
Extended **`38 U.S.C. § 1151(a)(2)`** no-fault coverage to **`38 U.S.C. § 1718` Compensated Work Therapy (`CWT`)** (`§ 3.361(d)(3)`).

Enacted **`38 U.S.C. § 1151(c)`**, confirming `§ 1151` eligibility for **`Ch. 21` `SAH`/`SHA`** and extending **`Ch. 39` Auto/Adaptive Equipment** (`§ 3.808(b)`), plus **`§ 3.362(e)`** designated-purpose FTCA offsets (*contrast Alleman, `349 F.3d 1368` [`S-DVI` barred] & Mintz, `6 Vet. App. 277` [`§ 2307` barred]*).
**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) (`Dec. 10, 2004` statutory floor for `Ch. 39` Auto & `§ 3.362(e)`).**

*Viegas*: defective VAMC equipment/restroom grab bar = compensable unforeseen event. *Roberson*: 2-prong diagnostic-delay burden. *Hatfield*: total failure to attempt `§ 17.32` consent defeats *McNair* minor-deviation defense.
Apply *George* (`§ 20.1403(e)`) screen on CUE against pre-*Viegas* (`< Feb. 7, 2013`) facility-defect denials; fully retroactive on all open/Supplemental claims!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Date-by-Date Rule Changes for Gulf War Illness, Burn Pit Presumptions & VA Medical Injury Claims
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: When reviewing older denials involving Gulf War illnesses (38 C.F.R. § 3.317), airborne particulate and PACT Act presumptions (38 C.F.R. §§ 3.320–3.320b), or injuries caused by VA medical care (38 U.S.C. § 1151; 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.358 and 3.361–3.363), the exact year of the claim or decision changes which legal standard applied. For example, diagnosed multisymptom illnesses like fibromyalgia and irritable bowel syndrome were added to § 3.317 effective March 1, 2002; Afghanistan joined § 3.317(a) multisymptom coverage on August 10, 2022; and VA medical injury claims shifted from a 'no-fault' standard to a negligence/unforeseen-event standard for claims received on or after October 1, 1997.
record_clues: A 1995–2002 Gulf War denial rejecting chronic fatigue syndrome, fibromyalgia, or irritable bowel syndrome because it was a 'diagnosed' illness before Congress expanded 38 U.S.C. § 1117 effective March 1, 2002.
An August 5, 2021 through August 9, 2022 denial of asthma, rhinitis, or sinusitis under 38 C.F.R. § 3.320 because symptoms first appeared more than 10 years after military separation.
A post-2024 claim involving urinary bladder/ureter cancer (§ 3.320a, effective January 2, 2025) or leukemias, multiple myeloma, or myelodysplastic syndromes (§ 3.320b, effective January 10, 2025).

An older 38 U.S.C. § 1151 (or former § 351) VA hospital injury claim filed before October 1, 1997 that may still have remained pending—preserving the pre-1997 no-fault standard under Brown v. Gardner and 38 C.F.R. § 3.358.
important_cautions: Watch Federal Register publication dates versus effective dates: functional gastrointestinal disorder rules published July 15, 2011 (76 FR 41696) took effect August 15, 2011, and VA's post-1997 § 1151 regulations published August 3, 2004 (69 FR 46426) took effect September 2, 2004 (implementing the October 1, 1997 statutory cutoff).

Reopening a finally denied pre-October 1, 1997 § 1151 medical-injury claim on or after October 1, 1997 triggers the modern fault/unforeseen-event standard under 38 C.F.R. § 3.361(a)—so representatives check first whether the pre-1997 claim actually remained pending before filing to reopen.

VA's October 1, 2024 notice updating §§ 3.317 and 3.320 (89 FR 79815) remains a proposed rule that is not finalized, though the PACT Act's statutory text in 38 U.S.C. §§ 1117, 1119, and 1120 is already binding law.

Prospective statutory or regulatory expansions cannot prove Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) in final decisions issued before those rules took effect, and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c) permits only one final merits CUE decision per prior Board decision issue.
questions_for_representative: Was my earlier Gulf War or burn-pit denial based on an old geographic, 10-year manifestation, or 10% severity rule that Congress or VA later removed?

If I had a VA medical-injury claim before October 1, 1997, did any unaddressed submission or post-decision medical record under former 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b) keep that claim pending under the pre-1997 no-fault rule?
How do the effective-date limits in 38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a) compare with submitting newly obtained official service records under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)?
If I am pursuing a PACT Act cancer claim, how do both the statutory presumption in 38 U.S.C. § 1120 and a direct 38 U.S.C. § 1168 TERA nexus opinion work together?

title: Zero-PII 6-Gate Post-Grant VA Award Letter, Offset, Ancillary & § 5904(d) Fee-Withholding Audit Checklist
statutes: Pub. L. 104-201, § 653 (after-tax recoupment cap, eff. Oct. 1, 1996)
keyPrecedents: Jackson v. McDonald, 635 F. App'x 858 (Fed. Cir. 2015) (nonprecedential), rev'g Jackson v. Shinseki, 26 Vet. App. 460 (2014)
Military-Veterans Advocacy v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs, 7 F.4th 1110 (Fed. Cir. 2021)
cFileTriggers: Every favorable RO Rating Decision, Higher-Level Review grant, BVA grant implementation, or VA Award Letter (audit within 7 calendar days of VBMS upload!)
Rating Code Sheet assigning the C&P examination date as the effective date instead of date of claim, ITF, or 1-year § 3.400(o)(2) lookback
First-time >= 30% combined grant or newly granted 100% P&T / TDIU award missing spouse/child dependency additions or Ch. 35 DEA effective-date backdating
Award Letter withholding table showing Military Retired Pay (DFAS AEW hold), Disability Severance Pay, Separation Pay, Drill Pay, Incarceration, or Overpayment Recoupment
Direct-pay 20% attorney fee decision (§ 14.636(h)) or overlapping CAVC EAJA award requiring Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c) lesser-fee client refund calculation
killSwitches: Writing any client name, SSN, VA claim number, bank routing number, or unredacted Award Letter text into a repository copy of this checklist

Treating a partially favorable grant (wrong effective date, low initial stage, or omitted SMC) as 'closed' and letting the 1-year AMA continuous-pursuit window (§ 3.2500) or 120-day CAVC NOA window (§ 7266(a)) expire

Failing to submit VA Form 21-686c within 1 year of a newly crossing >= 30% rating notification (§ 3.401(b)) or failing to file Ch. 35 DEA (VA Form 22-5490) within 1 year of initial P&T notice (§ 21.4131)
Failing to audit and release a stalled DFAS Audit Error Worksheet (AEW) hold on a >= 50% CRDP retiree's retroactive back pay and 20% direct-pay attorney fee

Retaining both an EAJA fee and a § 5904(d) contingency fee for the exact same CAVC representation without refunding the lesser amount to the client (violates Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c) and 38 C.F.R. § 14.636)

Missing the 30-day stay request on an accompanying overpayment demand (which freezes monthly recoupment!) or the strict 1-year statutory waiver deadline under 38 U.S.C. § 5302(a) & 38 C.F.R. § 1.963(b) [former § 1.963(b)(2)] (Pub. L. 117-328, Div. U, § 254, eff. Dec. 29, 2022; 90 FR 54234, eff. Jan. 26, 2026; 180 days on pre-Dec. 29, 2022 notices)

Preconditions (Pull From VBMS Before Auditing the Award Letter)

items: **1. Internal Rating Code Sheet** *(never rely solely on the claimant notification letter!)*
**2. VA Award Letter + `Payment Summary` / `Withholding` Schedule** *(monthly rate table from effective date to present)*
**3. `DFAS Audit Error Worksheet (AEW)` / `DD-214 Block 18` / `DFAS RAS`** *(if military retiree or separated with severance/separation pay)*
**4. RO Direct-Pay Fee Entitlement / Allocation Decision (`38 C.F.R. § 14.636(h)–(i)`) & Executed Fee Agreement**

blocks.text: Gate 1: Effective-Date & Staged-Rating Audit (38 U.S.C. § 5110; 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.114, 3.400)
Cross-check every granted Diagnostic Code's effective date against the [Master Effective-Date & Staged-Rating Treatise](/docs/effective-dates-and-staged-ratings-treatise):

items: **1.1 "Date of C&P Exam" Error (*Swain v. McDonald*, `27 Vet. App. 219 (2015)`):** Did the rater lazily assign the date of the VA/private DBQ examination instead of the date the claim was received (`§ 5110(a)(1)`) or the earlier date medical/lay evidence shows the disability or worsening arose?

**1.2 Unconsumed Intent to File (`VA Form 21-0966`, `38 C.F.R. § 3.155(b)`):** Did an active `ITF` filed within 1 year prior to the `526EZ` / `0995` go unapplied—or did an earlier claim consume the first `ITF` while a second `ITF` remained valid?

**1.3 Increased-Rating `1-Year` Pre-Claim Lookback (`§ 5110(b)(3)` `[former § 5110(b)(2)]`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2)`):** On any increased-rating grant (including initial `TDIU` on already-SC conditions!), did VAMC, private clinical, or lay employment records show an ascertainable increase in severity **within the `1 year` *preceding* the claim/ITF**?

**1.4 `1-Year` Post-Discharge (`§ 5110(b)(1)`) / `1-Year` Post-Death (`§ 5110(d)`) / `1-Year` Post-`§ 1151` Injury (`§ 3.400(i)`) Lookbacks:** Verify day-after-discharge, first-of-month-of-death, or date-of-malpractice-injury backdating when filed within 1 year.

**1.5 Liberalizing Law (`§ 5110(g)`; `§ 3.114(a)`), PACT Act (`Aug. 10, 2022`), *Nehmer* (`§ 3.816`) & `§ 3.156(c)` Service Records:** Verify raters did not assign the `20-0995` Supplemental Claim date when `§ 3.114(a)` (`up to 1 year` pre-claim back to statutory enactment), `PACT Act § 1305` prior-DIC re-evaluation, *Nehmer* Footnote 1 (`>= Sept. 25, 1985`), or `§ 3.156(c)(3)` original-claim reconsideration controlled!

**1.6 Staged Ratings Across Multi-Year Appeals (*Fenderson v. West*, `12 Vet. App. 119 (1999)`; *Hart v. Mansfield*, `21 Vet. App. 505 (2007)`; *Singleton v. Shinseki*, `659 F.3d 1332 (Fed. Cir. 2011)`):** Did VA assign a low initial stage (`10%` or `30%`) for earlier years and `70%`/`100%` only recently despite longitudinal records supporting higher earlier stages—or stage *downward* without affirmative medical evidence and adequate `§ 7104(d)(1)` reasons or bases (*Singleton*)?

**1.7 Silent Omission Check (*Hamill v. Collins*, `166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. 2026)`):** Compare every contention on the `526EZ` / `0995` / `NOD` against the decision's `§ 5104(b)` findings—any unaddressed issue remains legally pending!

blocks.text: Gate 2: Combined Math (§ 4.25), Bilateral Factor (§ 4.26(d)), TDIU & Mandatory SMC(k)–(t) Audit

items: **2.1 Whole-Person Combined Table (`38 C.F.R. § 4.25`):** Recompute every historical epoch independently (`x.5` rounds **up** to the next `10%`, e.g., `94.5% -> 95% -> 100%`; `94.4% -> 94% -> 90%`).

**2.2 Bilateral Factor Inclusion vs. `§ 4.26(d)` Exclusion (`eff. Apr. 16, 2023`, `88 FR 22914`):** Verify paired upper- or lower-extremity SC disabilities received the `+10%` bilateral factor—**AND** for periods `>= Apr. 16, 2023`, verify VA excluded a bilateral pair under `§ 4.26(d)` if including it paradoxically dropped `95%` (`100%`) down to `94%` (`90%`)!

**2.3 Inferred `TDIU` (`§ 4.16(a)–(b)`) & Mandatory `SMC` Sweep ([`SMC Audit Worksheet`](/checklists/smc-and-ancillary-audit-worksheet)):** — If combined `< 100%` (`>= 60%` single or `>= 70%` combined with one `40%+`) and evidence shows unemployability, did VA adjudicate or defer `TDIU`? — Did the code sheet award **every mandatory statutory `SMC`**: **`SMC(k)`** (`ED`/`FSAD`, breast tissue/radiation, extremity `LOU`, aphonia, single eye, deafness), **Statutory `SMC(s)`** (`100%` single disability or *Bradley* single-disability `TDIU` + `>= 60%` independent SC), **`SMC(l)`–`SMC(o)`** + ***Barry* (`101 F.4th 1348`)** multi-step `§ 3.350(f)(3)–(4)` bumps, or **`SMC(t)`** (*Laska*, `37 Vet. App. 460`)?

blocks.text: Gate 3: Dependency (§ 3.401(b)) & Ancillary Benefit Unlocks (Playbook 13)

items: **3.1 Dependents (`38 U.S.C. § 1115`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.401(b)`):** Whenever an award first crosses **`>= 30%` combined** (or retroactively backdates `>= 30%`), verify spouse, minor children, `18–23` school-children (`VA Form 21-674`), `§ 3.356` helpless children, and dependent parents (`VA Form 21P-509`) are paid from the **exact `>= 30%` effective date**! **Action:** If missing, file **`VA Form 21-686c` within `1 year` of the rating notification letter** (`§ 3.401(b)(3)`) to capture `100%` of multi-year retroactive dependency back pay!

**3.2 Spouse Aid & Attendance Add-On (`38 U.S.C. § 1115(1)(E)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.351(a)(2)`):** At `>= 30%` combined, if the veteran's **spouse** needs regular A&A (nursing home, dementia, ADL assistance), file `VA Form 21-2680` + `21-686c` for an extra `~$195+/month` (pro-rated from `30%`–`100%`).

**3.3 `100% P&T` / `TDIU P&T` Ancillary Trigger Packet *(Excluding `§ 1151`-Only Grants per [Playbook 17](/playbooks/17-section-1151-va-malpractice-and-ftca-interplay))!*:** — **`Chapter 35` `DEA` (`VA Form 22-5490`):** Confirm the code sheet explicitly grants `Basic Eligibility to Dependents' Educational Assistance` with the **earliest `100% P&T` effective date**; advise spouse/children to file **within `1 year` of P&T notice (`38 C.F.R. § 21.4131`)** to lock in retroactive tuition/stipend semesters! — **`CHAMPVA` (`VA Form 10-10d`)**, **`VALife` (`38 U.S.C. § 1922B`)**, **State `100% P&T` Property-Tax Exemption** (have client take the VA Summary of Benefits letter to the County Tax Assessor immediately—many states bar retroactive tax-year refunds!), and **Federal Student Loan Total & Permanent Disability (`TPD`) Discharge**.

**3.4 Catastrophic Grants:** Screen **`SAH`/`SHA`/`TRA` (`VA Form 26-4555`, `~$117,000+`)**, **`Ch. 39` Auto (`VA Form 21-4502` / `10-1394`, `~$25,000+` + `Pub. L. 117-333` 30-yr/10-yr repeat eligibility)**, and ***Sursely* Multiple Clothing Allowances (`VA Form 10-8678`, `Aug. 1` annual cycle)**.

blocks.text: Gate 4: Military Retiree (CRDP/CRSC), Severance (§ 3.700), Drill Pay & Incarceration Withholding Audit (Playbook 20)
Inspect every dollar withheld in the Award Letter's `Withholding` column:

items: **4.1 Military Retired Pay & `CRDP` / `CRSC` Check (`10 U.S.C. §§ 1413a, 1414`):** — **`20+` Year / `TERA` / Gray-Area Retiree Rated `>= 50%` (or `100% TDIU`):** Confirm `CRDP` triggered automatically; calendar a **`45-day` `DFAS AEW` follow-up** until VA & DFAS release the held retroactive compensation! — **Chapter 61 Medical Retiree (`< 20` Years Service) OR Any Combat Retiree:** Remember `< 20-yr` Ch. 61 retirees get **ZERO `CRDP`** (`10 U.S.C. § 1414(b)(2)`)! Immediately file/amend **`DD Form 2860` (`CRSC`)** with the veteran's military branch to claim **uncapped retroactive tax-free `CRSC` arrears** under ***Soto v. United States*, `605 U.S. 360 (2025)`** ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc))!

**4.2 Disability Severance Pay (`10 U.S.C. § 1212`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.700(a)(3)`) & Separation Pay (`§ 3.700(a)(5)`) Three-Prong Check:** — **Prong A (Combat Non-Recoupment):** Did the veteran separate under Ch. 61 **on or after `Jan. 28, 2008`** for a disability incurred in a **combat zone** or **combat-related operations** (`§ 1212(d)(2)`)? If YES, VA recoupment must be **`$0.00`**—challenge any withholding immediately! — **Prong B (Non-Severance Isolation Math):** For `DSP` (`§ 3.700(a)(3)`—unlike `ISP`/`SSB` under `§ 3.700(a)(5)`), verify VA withheld **at most** the lesser of `(1)` the initial standalone severance rating or `(2)` `Total Combined Rate minus Non-Severance Combined Rate` (e.g., `$0/mo` withheld when `70%` non-severance + `10%` severance still rounds to `70%`!). — **Prong C (Post-Sept. 30, 1996 After-Tax Net Cap):** For *any* `DSP`, `ISP`, `SSB`, or Readjustment Pay paid **after `Sept. 30, 1996`**, verify VA deducted federal income taxes withheld at separation (`Pub. L. 104-201, § 653`) rather than recouping the gross `DD-214` figure!

**4.3 Reserve Drill Pay (`§ 3.654`) & Felony Incarceration (`§ 3.665`):** — Confirm drill-pay adjustments waive **only `1/30th` per drill/AT day** (e.g., `63 days/yr`), NOT a full-year award suspension. — If incarcerated `> 60 days` post-felony conviction (*Mulder*), verify no reduction occurred during pre-trial detention or **halfway house / work-release (`§ 3.665(b)`)**, file **`VA Form 21-0788` dependent apportionment (`§ 3.665(e)`)** immediately for spouse/children, and verify day-of-release full restoration (`§ 3.665(i)`).

blocks.text: Gate 5: 38 U.S.C. § 5904(d) 20% Direct-Pay Fee Base & EAJA Same-Work Offset Audit

items: **5.1 Mandatory `30-Day` Filing Compliance (*Ravin v. Wilkie*, `956 F.3d 1346 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`):** Confirm VBMS reflects timely filing of `VA Form 21-22a` and the compliant `<= 20%` direct-pay fee agreement within `30 days` of execution (`38 C.F.R. § 14.636(g)(3)`), and that all compensated work occurred *after* an initial AOJ decision on the claim (`§ 5904(c)(1)`).

**5.2 Recompute Exact `"Past-Due Benefits"` Base (`38 C.F.R. § 14.636(h)(3)`):** — Sum `(Newly Awarded Monthly Rate [incl. SMC & Dependents] − Prior Paid Monthly Rate)` from the granted effective date through the date of the award decision (`up to date of award implementation` per VA fee-calculator rules). — **`DFAS AEW` Hold Check:** If `100%` of retro was temporarily held pending a `DFAS AEW` on a `CRDP`-eligible retiree, do **not** close the fee ledger until DFAS returns the `AEW` and VA issues the supplemental **Fee Release** disbursing `20%` of the restored net cash! — **Incarceration vs. Debt-Invalidation Distinctions:** Under ***Snyder v. Nicholson*, `489 F.3d 1213 (Fed. Cir. 2007)`**, `§ 5313` incarceration reductions do *not* shrink the gross `"past-due benefits awarded"` base (payable from non-apportioned retro); conversely, under ***Gumpenberger v. Wilkie*, `973 F.3d 1379 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`**, invalidating a VA debt yields direct-pay fees **only** on dollars VA actually withheld and restored in cash (*note also nonprecedential* *Jackson v. McDonald*, `635 F. App'x 858 (Fed. Cir. 2015) (nonprecedential)`).

**5.3 Mandatory `EAJA` + `§ 5904` Same-Work Client Refund (`Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c)`, `106 Stat. 4513`):** — Did the firm previously receive an **`EAJA` fee (`28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)`)** for the CAVC appeal that remanded this exact claim, and does the `§ 5904(d)` fee agreement cover that **same work** (as opposed to distinct post-remand agency advocacy cleanly segregated by contract, or where EAJA is offset)? If EAJA and `§ 5904` overlap for the same work, **calculate and disburse the lesser-of-the-two refund to the veteran immediately** upon receipt of the `§ 5904` payment and log the trust/operating check in the file!

blocks.text: Gate 6: Critical Post-Award Jurisdictional Deadlines (Calendar Before Closing!)

rows: **`30 Days` from debt notice** to request waiver/dispute **and FREEZE monthly benefit recoupment**; **`1 Year` statutory deadline** (`Pub. L. 117-328, Div. U, § 254`, eff. Dec. 29, 2022; `90 FR 54234`, eff. Jan. 26, 2026; `180 days` pre-Dec. 29, 2022) to file `VA Form 5655` + waiver request!
**`60 Days`** from AOJ fee allocation notice to challenge a default fee split before VA releases withheld funds (`120 Days` for OGC fee-reasonableness review motion under `§ 14.636(i)`).
**Adverse / Partial BVA Decision (Denied Earlier Effective Date, Higher Stage, or `SMC`)**

**`120 Days`** from BVA mailing date to file **CAVC Notice of Appeal** **OR `1 Year`** from BVA decision to file a `VA Form 20-0995` Supplemental Claim (`new & relevant`). *(Trap: In **Legacy** claims, CAVC affirmance breaks continuous prosecution; in **AMA**, `§ 5110(a)(2)(E)` allows a `20-0995` within **`1 year` after CAVC decision**, whereas appealing further to the **Federal Circuit** requires a protective `20-0995`/`21-0966` within 1 year of CAVC judgment per **MVA v. Sec'y**, `7 F.4th 1110`!)*
**Partial RO / HLR Grant (Wrong Effective Date, Missing `SMC`, Unlawful `§ 3.700` Withholding, or RO Fee-Base Error)**
**`1 Year`** from RO/HLR notification letter to file AMA `HLR` (`20-0996`), `Supplemental Claim` (`20-0995`), or `Board NOD` (`10182`).
**`1 Year`** from threshold rating / P&T notification letter (`VA Form 21-686c` & `VA Form 22-5490`).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: After You Win: 6-Point Checklist to Audit Your VA Award Letter, Back Pay & Ancillary Benefits
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Even when VA mails a 'favorable' Rating Decision granting service connection or a higher percentage, errors frequently hide inside the payment math. VA may pick the C&P exam date instead of your claim or Intent to File date, miss staged ratings across earlier years, miscalculate combined percentages or the post-April 16, 2023 bilateral exclusion rule (38 C.F.R. § 4.26(d)), omit inferred Special Monthly Compensation (SMC), forget spouse/child dependents upon crossing 30%, hold back retired pay or over-recoup severance pay, or misstate attorney fee / EAJA offsets. Auditing every grant promptly protects both your lump-sum back pay and your appeal deadlines.
record_clues: A newly issued VA Rating Decision, Higher-Level Review grant, Board grant implementation letter, VA Award Letter monthly payment table, and the internal VA Rating Code Sheet.
An effective date matching the date of a recent C&P exam rather than the Intent to File date, claim date, or 1-year pre-claim lookback for increased ratings (38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2)).

Crossing 30% combined for the first time without spouse/child/parent dependency additions (1-year window on VA Form 21-686c under 38 C.F.R. § 3.401(b)), or crossing 100% Permanent & Total without Chapter 35 DEA education and CHAMPVA notices.

Award Letter 'Withholding' lines for Military Retired Pay (DFAS Audit Error Worksheet hold), Disability Severance Pay, Separation Pay, Reserve Drill Pay, Overpayment Recoupment, or 20% direct-pay representation fees.
important_cautions: A partial win still starts strict appeal clocks: if your percentage is too low for an earlier period, your effective date is wrong, or SMC was omitted, you must appeal within 1 year (for a Regional Office / HLR grant under 38 C.F.R. § 3.2500) or within 120 days to the CAVC (for a partial Board denial under 38 U.S.C. § 7266(a))—otherwise the unfavorable part becomes final!

One-year family benefit deadlines: when a rating first crosses 30% combined, submit VA Form 21-686c within 1 year of notification to backdate dependent pay to the rating's effective date (38 C.F.R. § 3.401(b)); when first granted Permanent & Total disability, dependents should check the 1-year Chapter 35 DEA filing window under 38 C.F.R. § 21.4131.

Mandatory EAJA lesser-fee refund: if an attorney represented you at the CAVC and received an Equal Access to Justice Act (EAJA) award for the same work that produced your VA back pay, federal law (Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c)) requires the attorney to refund the smaller of the two fees dollar-for-dollar to you.

If an accompanying letter demands repayment of an overpayment, remember the 30-day stay window (which freezes monthly withholding) and the 1-year statutory waiver deadline under 38 U.S.C. § 5302(a) and 38 C.F.R. § 1.963(b) (180 days for pre-December 29, 2022 notices).
questions_for_representative: Can we compare my VA Award Letter line-by-line against the internal VA Rating Code Sheet to verify my effective dates, staged ratings, combined math (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.25 and 4.26(d)), and any inferred Special Monthly Compensation?

Now that my combined rating is 30%+ (or 100% Permanent & Total), have we filed VA Form 21-686c for my dependents and checked CHAMPVA, Chapter 35 DEA, VA dental care, clothing/auto/housing grants, and state property-tax exemptions?

Are the military retired pay (DFAS CRDP/CRSC) or separation/severance recoupment withholdings on my Award Letter accurate under 38 C.F.R. § 3.700 (after-tax cap or post-January 28, 2008 combat-severance exemption)?
If a 20% contingency fee was withheld from my past-due benefits, does it match my net retroactive increase—and am I owed a dollar-for-dollar refund of any prior CAVC EAJA fee covering the same work?

title: C-File & VBMS eFolder Chronological Audit Protocol
keyPrecedents: Russell v. Principi, 3 Vet. App. 310 (1992) (en banc)
cFileTriggers: Initial intake of a 1,000–15,000+ page VBMS eFolder or legacy FOIA C-file
killSwitches: Skipping early Rating Code Sheets or DD-214/OMPF boxes and reading only recent AMA decisions
Defaulting to CUE on a judicial-reinterpretation theory barred by George v. McDonough, 596 U.S. 740 (2022) and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e) when an open-claim or § 3.156(b)-(c) vehicle exists

toc.text: Pass 1: Service Profile & Presumptive / Class Triage (15 Minutes)
Pass 2: Chronological Claims vs. Adjudications Ledger (30 Minutes)
Pass 3: Substantive Code-Sheet & Bitemporal Notice Audit (30 Minutes)

blocks.text: Never audit a C-file backwards from today's rating alone. Six-figure retroactive recoveries are won by reconstructing the **exact timeline of claims, evidence association dates, rating code sheets, and mailing addresses** from separation forward.
Pass 1: Service Profile & Presumptive / Class Triage (15 Minutes)

items: **Service Dates, Branch & Retiree Status (`DD-214`, `DD-215`, `AGO 53-55`, `NGN 22` — see [`Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon`](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon)):**

Did the veteran have **90+ days continuous wartime/post-1946 active service**? *(Unlocks `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(a)` 1-year chronic disease, `§ 3.309(b)` tropical, `§ 3.309(c)` POW, and `§ 3.318` ALS `20%` minimum presumptions—run [Playbook 07](/playbooks/07-statutory-presumptions-chronic-tropical-pow-als)).*
Is the veteran a **20-year retiree or Chapter 61 medical retiree**? *(Flag immediately for uncapped **CRSC back pay** under Soto v. United States, 605 U.S. 360 (2025)).*
Any **Purple Heart**, CIB, CAR, Combat Medical Badge, Parachutist/airborne wings, or Prisoner of War status?
**Geographic / Toxic Exposure Footprint:**

**Republic of Vietnam (land, inland waterways, OR 12nm offshore Blue Water Navy):** Flag **ALL** post-Sept. 25, 1985 claims and medical diagnoses against `38 C.F.R. § 3.816` (*Nehmer* — noting `M21-1 VIII.i.2.B.1.c` excludes chloracne, hypertension, and MGUS from `§ 3.816`).
**Korean DMZ, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Guam, Camp Lejeune, SW Asia / Post-9/11 Burn Pits:** Cross-check `§ 3.307(a)(6)` vs. PACT Act (`38 U.S.C. §§ 1116, 1119, 1120`).
**Completeness of Service Records (`STRs` & `OMPF`):**
Are **inpatient clinical hospital packets** missing (only outpatient jacket in VBMS)?
Any **1973 NPRC Fire** memo (`NA Form 13055`)?
When were STRs, deck logs, or JSRRC stressor reports **date-stamped into the C-file**? *(Compare receipt dates against EVERY prior denial for `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)`!).*

blocks.text: Pass 2: Chronological Claims vs. Adjudications Ledger (30 Minutes)
Build a two-column chronological ledger (`Claim / Evidence Trigger` -> `VA Disposition & Mailing`):

items: **Discharge / First Claim (`VA Form 8-526`, `21-526`, `21-526EZ`):**
List **every single word/symptom** written by the veteran on the very first application.

Compare item-by-item against Rating Code Sheet #1 (translating pre-Jan. 1, 1959 `Veterans' Regulation No. 1(a)` citations under `Pub. L. 85-857` and `1959–1991` `300`/`3000`/`4000` statutory citations under `Pub. L. 102-40` & `Pub. L. 102-83`). Were any claimed conditions **left completely off** the rating decision?
**Pre-March 24, 2015 Informal & Inferred Claims:**
Audit every `VA Form 21-4138`, handwritten letter, VSO memo, and congressional inquiry before **March 24, 2015** (`79 FR 57660`).

Once *any* condition became service-connected (even at `0%`!), scan VAMC admission summaries and VA outpatient clinic reports prior to **March 24, 2015** showing worsening without a follow-on rating decision (`historical 38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b)`).
Check every increased-rating claim for mention of **job loss, SSDI, VR&E infeasibility, or inability to work** (*Roberson* / *Rice* unadjudicated TDIU).
**Post-February 19, 2019 AMA Explicit Notice Audit (*Hamill v. Collins*, 2026):**

For **every** AMA decision (`2019–present`), verify whether any claimed issue on `21-526EZ`/`20-0995` OR any reasonably raised issue on a C&P DBQ (e.g., radiculopathy, scars, TDIU, SMC) was **omitted from the decision notice**. Under `38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)` and *Hamill v. Collins*, `166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. 2026)`, omitted AMA issues remain **open and pending**!
**NOD / SOC & `§ 3.156(b)` Post-Decision VAMC Audit (Legacy Claims Before Feb. 19, 2019):**
Did the veteran send *any* written disagreement within 1 year of a rating notice where VA **never issued a Statement of the Case (SOC)**? *(Appeal remains open indefinitely!)*

**The *Lang* 1-Year Post-Decision VAMC Check (`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b)`):** Did a VAMC generate relevant clinical records within **365 days *after*** a post-July 21, 1992 Legacy RO decision without VA determining whether they were new and material (*Lang v. Wilkie*, `971 F.3d 1348 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`)? *(Legacy decision never became final!)*
**BVA Subsumption & Mandatory Pre-Filing Gate:**

List all BVA decisions (`date`, `issues decided`, `remanded vs. denied vs. dismissed`). Never file an RO CUE (`§ 3.105(a)`) on an issue later decided on the merits by BVA—and **never** file a Board CUE (`38 U.S.C. § 7111`) without first clearing [Board of Veterans' Appeals (BVA) CUE Motion Pre-Filing Gate Checklist (38 U.S.C. § 7111; 38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1400–20.1411)](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate) (`38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c)` one-shot rule)!

blocks.text: Pass 3: Substantive Code-Sheet & Bitemporal Notice Audit (30 Minutes)

items: **Combat / Penetrating Wounds:** Any `0%` or `10%` scar (`DC 7800–7805`) for a GSW, shrapnel, grenade, or penetrating wound? -> Run [Playbook 01](/playbooks/01-penetrating-wounds-scars-vs-muscles) (`DC 5301–5323` muscle groups + peripheral nerves).

**Address & `§ 3.655` No-Show Audit:** Any missed-exam denial or unappealed adverse decision? Compare cover-letter address against every prior/contemporary address in C-file and check for `"Returned Undeliverable"` scans -> Run [Playbook 02](/playbooks/02-wrong-address-defective-notice-cp-exams).

**Rating Reductions / Severances:** Did *any* percentage ever go **down** on a subsequent code sheet? Check `§ 3.105(d)–(e)` 60-day notice, `§ 3.344` 5-year stabilization, `§ 3.957` 10-year severance bar, `§ 3.953` Dec. 31, 1957/1958 savings protection, and `§ 3.951(b)` 20-year floor -> Run [Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings).
**Math & Mandatory SMC Audit:**
Check Combined Ratings math (`§ 4.25`), Bilateral Factor & April 16, 2023 Exclusion Rule (`§ 4.26(d)`), and `§ 4.59` painful-motion `10%+` joint minimums.

Whenever veteran hit `100%` (or single-disability TDIU under *Bradley*) + `60%` independent disabilities, verify `SMC(s)` was paid; if at `SMC(l)–(n)`, verify **multi-step bumps** under `§ 3.350(f)(3)–(4)` (*Barry v. McDonough*, `101 F.4th 1348 (Fed. Cir. 2024)`)!
Check `SMC(k)` for radical prostatectomy, ED secondary to DMII/PTSD meds, or loss of use of foot/hand.
**Bitemporal & Primary-Source Cutoff Verification:**
Is a CUE motion reliant on VAMC records *not* physically in the paper C-file? Confirm decision date is **on or after July 21, 1992** (*Bell v. Derwinski*; `VAOPGCPREC 12-95`).

Does the theory rely on a **later judicial reinterpretation** (e.g., *Bradley* in 2008 or *Barry* in 2024)? Under *George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` and `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`, route through an **open/non-final claim** (`§ 3.156(b)–(c)`, defective notice, pending claim) rather than CUE against a prior final decision!

Confirm exact Federal Register **effective date** (not publication date!) and verbatim VASRD text using [38 C.F.R. Verbatim Snapshots & Redlines](/cfr), [38 C.F.R. Historical Redline Comparisons](/cfr), and [Authority Hierarchy, Temporal Versioning Policy & Citation Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: How Accredited Representatives Review a Complete VA Claims File (C-File) From Oldest to Newest
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: A Veteran's VA Claims File (C-file, stored digitally in VA's VBMS eFolder) can run from a few hundred pages to more than 15,000 pages—and digital scans are often uploaded out of chronological order. Reading only your most recent VA decision letter misses half the story. This protocol shows how experienced advocates sort a C-file from your military entrance exam forward: matching every DD-214 and inpatient service record against every historical internal VA Rating Code Sheet, spotting unanswered Notices of Disagreement or pre-2015 informal claims, checking returned-mail envelopes, and identifying whether an earlier effective date can be pursued without resorting to a high-hurdle Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) motion.
record_clues: You only have VA's summary notification letters at home and have never seen your internal VA Rating Code Sheets (which list exact 4-digit Diagnostic Codes, effective dates, and combined-rating math).
Your DD-214, Purple Heart / combat awards, or military hospital records list injuries or deployments that never appeared on your earliest VA rating decisions.
You remember filing an old claim, statement, or appeal years ago that seemed to disappear without a formal Statement of the Case (SOC) or explicit decision.
important_cautions: Request the Full C-File First: Notification letters sent in the mail frequently omit Diagnostic Codes, bilateral-factor math, and the exact inventory of service records VA actually reviewed.

Check Open-Claim & Service-Record Routes Before CUE: Under George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e), CUE carries the strictest legal burden in Veterans Law and excludes duty-to-assist errors and later court reinterpretations—whereas 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) newly associated service records, void reductions, Nehmer herbicide rules, and pending claims allow full weighing of the evidence.

Protect Board CUE Finality (38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c)): Never file an unreviewed Board CUE motion before completing a full C-file audit, because the Board allows only one final merits CUE decision per prior Board decision issue.
questions_for_representative: Have you downloaded and reviewed my complete VBMS eFolder—including every historical Rating Code Sheet from my very first claim forward?
Can we build a simple timeline comparing every claim or appeal I filed against every decision VA mailed, checking for unanswered filings or wrong-address mailings?
Were any military inpatient packets, unit logs, or personnel records added to my C-file after an earlier denial (38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c))?
Before considering any CUE motion, have we ruled out lower-burden pathways like § 3.156(c), void rating reductions, Nehmer, or an open AMA issue?

killSwitches: Storing completed worksheets with veteran PII inside a git-tracked folder (always save completed client worksheets outside the repository!)
