lines: **PII Rule:** Copy this template to your secure local/encrypted case folder **outside** this Git repository before filling in client-identifying details.

blocks.text: This worksheet enforces the mandatory **6-Step Operational Screening Order** (aligned to Case Screen) so you never default to CUE when an open/pending-claim or `§ 3.156(c)` pathway is available.
Header: Service Profile & Cross-System Flags

items: **Case / Matter Reference (Anonymized ID):** `____________________`
**Active Service Period(s):** `____________________` (`>= 90` continuous days? `[ ] Yes [ ] No`)
**Herbicide / Toxic Exposure Zone(s):** `[ ] RVN Boots-on-Ground` `[ ] RVN Blue Water (12nm)` `[ ] Korean DMZ` `[ ] Thailand` `[ ] Laos/Cambodia/Guam` `[ ] Camp Lejeune` `[ ] SW Asia/TERA`
**Military Retiree Status (Title 10 CRSC Gate):** `[ ] None` `[ ] 20-Yr Regular/Reserve` `[ ] Ch. 61 Medical Retiree` `[ ] TDRL/Severance`

blocks.text: Step 1: Finality, Mailing & Implicit-Denial Audit (Test BEFORE CUE!)

headers: Exact Issues Claimed or Reasonably Raised
Notice Mailed to Latest Address of Record?
Returned Mail or Better VA Address?

items: **NOD Without SOC Check (`1963 – Feb. 18, 2019`):** Did the veteran file a timely written disagreement with **no SOC ever issued**? `[ ] Yes (Appeal Still Pending!)` `[ ] No`

**`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b)` Post-Decision VAMC Check (*Lang v. Wilkie*, 2020):** Did a VAMC generate relevant clinical records within **1 year *after*** a post-July 21, 1992 Legacy RO decision without VA adjudicating whether they were new and material? `[ ] Yes (Legacy Decision Never Final!)` `[ ] No`
**VACOLS Sweep Check (*Freund v. Collins*, 2026):** Was a legacy appeal closed (`1990–2025`) in VACOLS for a missing Form 9 despite timely action? `[ ] Yes` `[ ] No`

**Silent Omission Regime:**
• `[ ]` **AMA Decision (`>= Feb. 19, 2019`):** Implicit denial **abolished** (*Hamill v. Collins*, 2026; `38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)`). Omitted issue is **legally pending**!
• `[ ]` **Legacy Decision (`< Feb. 19, 2019`):** Run *Deshotel* / *Adams* / *Hampton* reasonable-notice test.

blocks.text: Step 2: Newly Associated Service Department Records (38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c))

items:
Were **any** official service department records associated with the C-file *after* an earlier denial?
• `[ ]` Inpatient hospital clinical records (distinct from outpatient STR jacket)
• `[ ]` Unit morning reports / ship deck logs / command chronologies
• `[ ]` JSRRC / CRUR stressor report or retroactive `DD-215` combat award
• `[ ]` 1973 NPRC Fire reconstructed extracts (`SGO` index cards, pay/hospital records)
• `[ ]` Declassified DoD exposure logs (`§ 3.156(c)(1)(iii)`)

**Relevance & `(c)(2)` Check:**
• Existed at time of prior decision? `[ ] Yes [ ] No`
• Speaks to a disputed element in prior denial (*Blubaugh* / *Kisor*)? `[ ] Yes [ ] No`
• Did veteran withhold identifying unit info in Claim #1 (`§ 3.156(c)(2)` / *Mayhue*)? `[ ] No (Good)` `[ ] Yes (Blocked)`

blocks.text: Step 3: Pre-2015 Informal Claims (§§ 3.155, 3.157(b)) & Unadjudicated TDIU

items:
**Pre-March 24, 2015 `§ 3.157(b)` Hospital/Exam Trigger:**
• Date SC first granted (even at `0%`): `____________`
• Pre-`3/24/2015` VAMC admission or VA outpatient exam showing worsening with no rating follow-up: `____________`

**Reasonably Raised `TDIU` (*Roberson* / *Rice*):**
• During an open/increased-rating claim, did the record reflect unemployability (`SSDI`, `VR&E` infeasibility, medical/lay job-loss statements)? `[ ] Yes [ ] No`
• Check `§ 4.16(a)(1)–(5)` single-disability clustering (common etiology / single body system / combat injuries `>= 60%` or `>= 40%` anchor): `____________________`

blocks.text: Step 4: Special Regimes — Void Reductions & *Nehmer* (§ 3.816)

items:
**Rating Reduction / Severance Check:**
• Did any evaluation ever drop (`e.g., 70% -> 30%`)? `[ ] Yes [ ] No`
• Was rating in effect `>= 5` years (`§ 3.344`), `>= 10` years SC (`§ 3.957`), or `>= 20` years (`§ 3.951(b)`)? `____________`
• Did VA send 60-day advance proposal notice (`§ 3.105(e)`) and prove sustained improvement under ordinary conditions of life and work (*Brown* / *Kitchens*)? `[ ] Yes` `[ ] No -> VOID AB INITIO!`

***Nehmer* Class Check (`38 C.F.R. § 3.816`):**
• RVN / Blue Water Navy veteran with a covered herbicide condition previously denied (or diagnosed in medical records during a claim) on/after **Sept. 25, 1985**? `[ ] Yes [ ] No`

blocks.text: Step 5: Last-Resort Collateral Attack — Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE)

items:
**Subsumption & One-Shot Gate (See [Board of Veterans' Appeals (BVA) CUE Motion Pre-Filing Gate Checklist (38 U.S.C. § 7111; 38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1400–20.1411)](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate)):**
• Did BVA ever decide this exact issue on the merits? `[ ] No -> AOJ CUE (§ 5109A)` `[ ] Yes -> BVA CUE (§ 7111 — ONE-SHOT LIMIT!)`
• Has BVA *already* decided a prior CUE motion on this Board issue? `[ ] No` `[ ] Yes -> BARRED BY § 20.1409(c)!`

**Record Scope (*Bell v. Derwinski* Gate):**
• Challenged decision date: `____________`
• `[ ]` **Before July 21, 1992:** Restricted strictly to documents **physically in the C-file** on decision date (`VAOPGCPREC 12-95`).
• `[ ]` **On or After July 21, 1992:** Includes VA-generated medical records constructively in VA's possession.

**Law-of-the-Era & Disqualifier Gate:**
• Exact CFR edition & verbatim section pulled from Verbatim CFR Snapshots / `govinfo` / FR? `[ ] Yes [ ] No`
• Does theory rely on Duty-to-Assist / inadequate exam (*Cook* bar)? `[ ] No (Good)` `[ ] Yes (Dead)`
• Does theory rely on a later judicial invalidation/reinterpretation (*George* bar)? `[ ] No (Good)` `[ ] Yes (Dead)`
• **Combined Math Check (`§ 4.25`):** Would fixing the error have changed the rounded `10%` combined monthly payment on that date? `[ ] Yes` `[ ] No (Check when later ratings crossed a threshold!)`

items:
**Mandatory `SMC` (`38 U.S.C. § 1114`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(f)`; *Akles* / *Buie* / *Bradley* / *Barry*):**
• `[ ]` `SMC(s)`: Single `100%` (or post-2008 single-disability TDIU) + separate `60%+` combined disabilities
• `[ ]` `SMC(k)`: Anatomical loss or loss of use of creative organ / foot / hand / eye
• `[ ]` `SMC(l)–(n)` + **Multi-Step Bumps (*Barry v. McDonough*, 2024):** Additional independent `50%` (half-step `§ 3.350(f)(3)`) or `100%` (full-step `§ 3.350(f)(4)`) disabilities up to `SMC(o)`

**Downstream Title 10 `CRSC` (*Soto v. United States*, 605 U.S. 360 (2025)):**
• If military retiree (`20-yr` or `Ch. 61`) + combat-related nexus -> Route post-grant to branch CRSC board for **uncapped retroactive DFAS arrears** (no 6-year Barring Act cap!).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Printable Preparation Worksheet for Your First Meeting With a VSO or Accredited Attorney
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Walking into an appointment with a Veterans Service Officer (VSO), accredited claims agent, or VA disability attorney can feel overwhelming when your medical and claims history spans years or decades. This blank offline intake worksheet shows the exact dates and document facts an advocate needs to organize your history: your service branches and deployments, every past VA claim and rating decision date, your 4-digit Diagnostic Codes, whether any ratings were ever reduced, whether military records arrived late, and whether you also receive military retired pay, severance pay, or Combat-Related Special Compensation (CRSC).
record_clues: Your DD-214s (or NGB-22 / Reserve orders), award citations, and any Record Correction or Discharge Upgrade decisions.
Dates and outcomes of your earliest VA claims, Rating Code Sheets, Statement of the Case (SOC) packets, and any Board of Veterans' Appeals decisions.
Dates when you stopped working due to service-connected conditions, or dates of VA hospitalizations and surgeries lasting more than 21 days or requiring convalescence.
important_cautions: Protect Your Personal Privacy: Never post or upload worksheets containing your Social Security number, VA claim number, date of birth, or unredacted medical letters onto public forums or shared online folders. Keep completed copies securely in your private offline records or share them directly with your accredited representative.

It Is Okay to Mark 'Unknown': If you do not yet have your complete VA Claims File (C-file) or internal Rating Code Sheets, mark those items 'Unknown' so your representative knows to file a Privacy Act / FOIA request or inspect VBMS first.

Never Pay Unaccredited 'Claim Sharks': Under federal law (38 U.S.C. § 5904), VSOs assist free of charge, and only VA-accredited attorneys or claims agents may charge regulated fees after an initial VA decision has been issued.
questions_for_representative: Can you verify your VA Office of General Counsel (OGC) accreditation and pull my electronic VBMS eFolder so we can fill in the missing Rating Code Sheet dates together?
Based on the service eras, decision dates, and conditions on my worksheet, which missing records (such as NPRC inpatient files or Social Security records) should we request first?
Are there any active 1-year AMA or 120-day CAVC deadlines running right now on my recent decisions that we need to protect first?

CAVC Rule 33 Staff Conference memo or draft Joint Motion for Partial Remand (JMPR) circulated by VA Office of the General Counsel (OGC Group VII)

Adverse CAVC panel or single-judge decision evaluated for 60-day Federal Circuit appeal under 38 U.S.C. § 7292

New VA representation intake requiring VA Form 21-22a + § 5904 fee-agreement execution and 30-day § 14.636(g)(3) filing, or post-remand VA grant requiring a Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c) EAJA client refund
killSwitches: Entering any client name, SSN, VA file number, CAVC docket number tied to unredacted PII, or bank routing data into a repository copy of this checklist
Filing a BVA Motion for Reconsideration AFTER the 120-day CAVC Notice of Appeal window has already expired (fails to revive CAVC jurisdiction under Rosler v. Derwinski, 1 Vet. App. 241 (1991)!)

Challenging a VA C&P examiner's professional competence/qualifications for the first time at the CAVC without record evidence of irregularity (waived under Francway v. Wilkie, 940 F.3d 1304 (Fed. Cir. 2019) (en banc)!)

Signing a narrow Rule 33 JMPR without a Carter non-waiver reservation clause or without an administrative-error predicate (forfeits unmentioned theories on remand under Carter and destroys EAJA prevailing-party status under Sumner / Robinson v. O'Rourke!)
Waiting 90 days (60 + 30) to file a CAVC EAJA application after a consent JMPR order that issued an immediate mandate under CAVC Rule 41(b) (fatal expiration of the 30-day EAJA deadline on Day 31!)

Appealing a CAVC affirmance to the Federal Circuit under 38 U.S.C. § 7292 on factual or law-to-fact grounds (barred by § 7292(d)(2)) OR failing to file a protective AMA Supplemental Claim (VA Form 20-0995) within 1 year of the CAVC decision (MVA v. Sec'y, 7 F.4th 1110 (Fed. Cir. 2021)!)

Missing the 30-day fee-agreement filing rule under 38 C.F.R. § 14.636(g)(3) (Ravin v. Wilkie) or retaining both EAJA and § 5904 fees for the same work without refunding the lesser amount to the claimant (Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c); Carpenter v. Principi)

Pull and verify these exact artifacts **before** docketing a judicial appeal or executing a fee agreement:

Complete BVA Decision + Mailing Date Envelope / Caseflow Dispatch Stamp** *(verify exact `§ 7266(a)` Day-0 mailing date and confirm the veteran was alive on the decision date—post-death BVA decisions are void nullities under [`Survivor Post-Mortem Triage Gate`](/checklists/survivor-post-mortem-triage-gate)!)*

blocks.text: Bitemporal Pathway Gate (Rank Lowest Legal Burden First — Open-Claim vs. CUE)

rows: **Within `120 Days` of Adverse / Partial BVA Decision**

**1st Choice: CAVC Notice of Appeal (`38 U.S.C. § 7266(a)`)** (`$50` fee or `IFP` declaration) — preserves open-claim status, captures new favorable judicial precedents, and shifts hourly fees onto the government via `EAJA`! *(Optional AMA alternative/sequential fallback: `VA Form 20-0995` Supplemental Claim with new & relevant evidence within `1 year` under `§ 5110(a)(2)(D)`).*
**Full `Open-Claim` Retroactivity:** Judicial reinterpretations or invalidations (e.g., *Barry*, *Hamill*, *MVA v. Sec'y*) apply in full!
**Day `121` to Day `365` After AMA BVA Decision *(Missed `120-Day` NOA, No Equitable Tolling)***
**AMA `VA Form 20-0995` Supplemental Claim (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)(2)(D)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.2500(c)(3)`)** supported by **new and relevant evidence** (e.g., private nexus/DBQ opinion).
**Preserves Original Effective Date (`Open-Claim`)!** *(Note: Unavailable in pure Legacy appeals unless opted into AMA or eligible under `§ 3.156(c)`).*

**1st Choice:** `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)` newly associated official service department records (if applicable). **2nd Choice:** `VA Form 20-0995` Supplemental Claim (prospective effective date, immediately fee-eligible under *MVA v. Sec'y*). **Last Resort:** One-shot `38 U.S.C. § 7111` Board CUE ([`BVA CUE Gate`](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate)).
**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) on CUE:** `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)` & *George* bar attacking final BVA decisions via `§ 7111` CUE using later judicial reinterpretations!

blocks.text: Gate 1: Board Finality, 120-Day NOA Clock, *Rosler* vs. § 5110(a)(2)(D)–(E) Parallel Track & Equitable Tolling Audit

items: **1.1 Jurisdictional Finality & Adverse-Ruling Check (`38 U.S.C. §§ 7252(a), 7266(a)`):** — Confirm the BVA issued a **final denial** (or partial grant denying an earlier effective date, higher staged rating, `TDIU`, or `SMC`). **Trap:** Purely remanded BVA issues are non-final and non-appealable to the CAVC (*Breeden v. Principi*, `17 Vet. App. 475 (2004)`)—appeal *only* the finally denied/under-granted issues!

**1.2 Exact `120-Day` Calendar Math (`38 U.S.C. § 7266(a)`; `CAVC Rules 4 & 26`):** — Count **`120 calendar days`** from the stamped mailing date on the BVA decision (`38 U.S.C. § 7266(a)`). Verify whether a defective BVA mailing address (or failure to mail a copy to accredited POA) prevented the `120-day` clock from starting under *Ashley v. Derwinski*, `2 Vet. App. 307 (1992)`.

**1.3 *Rosler* Chairman Reconsideration Tolling vs. AMA Supplemental Parallel Track:** — ***Rosler* Tolling (*Rosler v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 241, 249 (1991)`):** Filing a motion for BVA Chairman Reconsideration (`38 U.S.C. § 7103`; `38 C.F.R. § 20.1001`) **within `120 days`** of the BVA decision abates finality and restarts a fresh `120-day` CAVC NOA clock once the Chairman denies reconsideration *(filing reconsideration on Day `121+` does **NOT** revive CAVC jurisdiction!)*. — **AMA Post-BVA (`§ 5110(a)(2)(D)`) & Post-CAVC (`§ 5110(a)(2)(E)`) Supplemental Track (`38 C.F.R. § 3.2500(c)–(d)`):** Remember `38 C.F.R. § 3.2500(d)` bars pursuing two AMA lanes *simultaneously* on the exact same issue—file the CAVC `NOA` within `120 days` first (preserving `EAJA` + judicial error review!), knowing that even if CAVC later *affirms* an **AMA** BVA decision, **`38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)(2)(E)`** still grants **`1 year` after the CAVC decision** to file a `VA Form 20-0995` Supplemental Claim with new & relevant evidence while keeping the original effective date! *(Legacy Trap: `§ 5110(a)(2)(E)` does **NOT** save a Legacy CAVC affirmance!)*

**1.4 Equitable Tolling Audit When Day `120` Passed (*Henderson v. Shinseki*, `562 U.S. 428 (2011)`):** — Because `§ 7266(a)` is non-jurisdictional (*Henderson*), immediately assemble sworn declarations + corroborating records if the claimant satisfied **both** `(a)` **extraordinary circumstances** beyond control *and* `(b)` **reasonable diligence**:

**Mental or Physical Incapacity (***Barrett v. Principi*, `363 F.3d 1316, 1321 (Fed. Cir. 2004)`**; *Arbas v. Nicholson*, `403 F.3d 1379 (Fed. Cir. 2005)`):** Medical/lay proof that psychiatric or physical illness rendered the veteran incapable of rational thought/deliberate decision-making or physically unable to handle affairs during the window.
• **Stop-Clock vs. Full-Period Diligence (***Checo v. Shinseki*, `748 F.3d 1373, 1378–80 (Fed. Cir. 2014)`**):** Under *Checo*'s **"stop-clock"** rule (homelessness, hospitalization, disaster), the veteran need only prove causation and diligence **during the extraordinary impediment period** (not the remaining unimpeded days)!
• **Case-Specific Postal / Filing Obstacles (***James v. Wilkie*, `917 F.3d 1368, 1373–75 (Fed. Cir. 2019)`**):** Rejects rigid categorical "garden-variety neglect" bars (e.g., *pro se* veteran placing timely NOA in residential mailbox with flag raised on Day 120 where USPS failed to pick up mail).

blocks.text: Gate 2: Favorable-Finding Lock (*Medrano* / § 5104A) & Issue-Preservation Gate (*Francway*; *Maggitt*)

items: **2.1 Lock Every Binding Favorable Finding (*Medrano v. Nicholson*, `21 Vet. App. 165, 170 (2007)`; `38 U.S.C. § 5104A`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.104(c)`):** — Catalog every explicit or implicit favorable factual finding in the RO/HLR/BVA decisions (e.g., conceded stressor/exposure, in-service injury, current diagnosis, lay credibility). Under *Medrano*, **the CAVC will not—and the Board on remand cannot—disturb favorable findings** (and under AMA `§ 5104A` / `§ 3.104(c)`, AOJ/BVA favorable findings bind all subsequent VA adjudicators unless rebutted by **clear and unmistakable evidence**!).

**2.2 C&P Examiner Competency Preservation Check (*Francway v. Wilkie*, `940 F.3d 1304, 1307–09 (Fed. Cir. 2019) (en banc)`):** — Did prior counsel or the claimant challenge the VA C&P examiner's professional qualifications/competence **before the Board**? Under *Francway*, the presumption of competency attaches **unless challenged at the agency/BVA level** (absent independent record evidence of irregularity)—if unpreserved below, pivot your CAVC attack to **inadequate medical rationale / inaccurate factual premise** (*Nieves-Rodriguez* / *Barr* / *Dalton*), which requires **no** competency challenge!

**2.3 Issue-Exhaustion & *Robinson* `EAJA` Preservation Gate (*Maggitt v. West*, `202 F.3d 1370, 1377–79 (Fed. Cir. 2000)`):** — Distinguish `(a)` arguments demonstrating **Board error on the record** (`§ 7104(d)(1)` failure to address reasonably raised record theories under *Robinson v. Peake*, `21 Vet. App. 526 (2008)`, *aff'd sub nom. Robinson v. Shinseki*, `557 F.3d 1355 (Fed. Cir. 2009)`) from `(b)` brand-new discretionary arguments never raised below (*Maggitt*; *Scott v. McDonald*, `789 F.3d 1375 (Fed. Cir. 2015)`). — **EAJA Trap (*Robinson v. O'Rourke*, `891 F.3d 976 (Fed. Cir. 2018)`):** Remember a *Maggitt* remand solely for the Board to address a **brand-new argument raised for the first time at CAVC** (where the Board committed zero error below) yields **`$0` EAJA fees**!

blocks.text: Gate 3: Outright Reversal (*Deloach* / *Horn* / *Gutierrez*) vs. Rule 33 JMPR Drafting Gate

items: **3.1 Screen First for Outright Reversal (`38 U.S.C. § 7261(a)(4)`; *Bufkin v. Collins*, `604 U.S. 369 (2025)`):** — Never reflexively sign a remand when the undisputed record mandates **outright CAVC reversal**! Screen for:

**Unrebutted Favorable Medical Evidence (***Deloach v. Shinseki*, `704 F.3d 1370, 1380–81 (Fed. Cir. 2013)`**):** All competent medical opinions of record favor the veteran (or the sole negative VA C&P exam is legally worthless/non-probative while a positive, adequate nexus/TDIU opinion stands uncontradicted), leaving the Board's denial *"clearly erroneous"*!
• **Failed Government Burden on Presumption of Soundness (`§ 1111`) or Rating Reduction (`§§ 3.343–3.344`) (***Horn v. Shinseki*, `25 Vet. App. 231, 243–44 (2012)`**; *Brown v. Brown*, `5 Vet. App. 413 (1993)`):** When VA fails its affirmative clear-and-unmistakable rebuttal burden under `§ 1111` (*Horn*) or reduces a protected rating unlawfully, **outright reversal and restoration—NOT remand to give VA a second bite to manufacture negative medical opinions—is mandatory**!
• **Uncontroverted Schedular / `SMC` / `TDIU` Criteria Met (***Gutierrez v. Principi*, `19 Vet. App. 1, 9–10 (2004)`**):** Undisputed Board/clinical findings already satisfy `100%` of the higher Diagnostic Code or `SMC` criteria as a matter of law.

**3.2 Mandatory 4-Clause `CAVC Rule 33` `JMPR` Drafting Checklist:** — Before signing any Joint Motion for Remand (`JMR` / `JMPR`), verify all **four protective clauses** appear verbatim or in substance in the joint motion:

**Clause A — Explicit Administrative-Error Predicate (*Sumner v. Principi*, `15 Vet. App. 256 (2001) (en banc)`; *Kelly*; *Zuberi*):** State explicitly that *"Vacatur and remand are warranted because the Board erred under `38 U.S.C. § 7104(d)(1)` [and/or `§ 5103A`] by failing to provide adequate reasons or bases..."*—**locking in `EAJA` `"prevailing party"` status!**

**Clause B — *Medrano* Favorable-Finding Lock (*Medrano*, `21 Vet. App. at 170`; `38 U.S.C. § 5104A`):** Explicitly list and preserve every favorable Board/AOJ finding (`"The parties agree that the Board's favorable findings that [X, Y, Z] shall not be disturbed on remand"`).

**Clause C — Anti-*Carter* Non-Waiver & Open-Submission Clause (*Carter v. Shinseki*, `26 Vet. App. 534 (2014)`, *vacated on other grounds sub nom. Carter v. McDonald*, `794 F.3d 1342 (Fed. Cir. 2015)`):** State explicitly that *"The enumeration of specific errors herein shall not limit the scope of the Board's review on remand, Appellant waives no additional arguments, theories, or issues raised by the record, and Appellant retains the right to submit additional argument and evidence on remand"* (`Quarles v. Derwinski`, `3 Vet. App. 129 (1992)`; `Kutscherousky v. West`, `12 Vet. App. 369 (1999)` / `38 C.F.R. § 20.802`).

**Clause D — *Stegall* Compliance Directive (*Stegall v. West*, `11 Vet. App. 268, 271 (1998)`; `38 U.S.C. § 7112`):** Require expedited remand adjudication (`38 U.S.C. § 7112`) and explicit compliance with the JMPR's terms (creating automatic *Stegall* error if the Board ignores any directive on remand!).

blocks.text: Gate 4: EAJA (28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)) 30-Day Post-Mandate Filing, Net-Worth, CPI-U & *Richlin* Billing Gate

items: **4.1 Calendar the Exact `30-Day` EAJA Deadline Immediately Upon Disposition (`28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)(1)(B)`; `CAVC Rules 36, 39, 41`):** — **Consent `JMPR` / Stipulated Immediate Mandate (`CAVC Rule 41(b)`):** **ZERO `60-day` wait!** File the complete EAJA application **within `30 calendar days` of the `JMPR` order date**! — **Contested Single-Judge (`nonprecedential, CAVC Rule 30(a)`) or Panel Judgment (`CAVC Rule 36`):** Calendar **`60 days` (`§ 7292(a)` appeal period -> `Rule 41(a)` mandate) + `30 days` (`Rule 39(a)`) = `90 days` from judgment** *(knowing premature post-judgment EAJA filings are held and deemed timely at finality, and timely filings may be amended under **Scarborough v. Principi**, `541 U.S. 401 (2004)`).*
**4.2 Mandatory 4-Prong Pleading & *Ratliff* Assignment Packet:**

Allege `(1)` **Prevailing Party** status, `(2)` Government position **not substantially justified** at both BVA and CAVC stages (*Patrick v. Shinseki*, `668 F.3d 1325`), `(3)` **Net Worth `<= $2,000,000`** declaration (or cite docketed CAVC `IFP` grant), and `(4)` **Itemized `0.1-hr` billing statement** + **executed Client `EAJA` Fee Assignment** (*Astrue v. Ratliff*, `560 U.S. 586 (2010)`).
**4.3 *Mannino* `CPI-U` Midpoint Math, *Richlin* Paralegal Rates & *Jean* Fees-on-Fees:**

Compute attorney rate = `$125.00 × (Midpoint Regional/National CPI-U ÷ March 1996 Base CPI-U)` under ***Mannino v. West*, `12 Vet. App. 242 (1999)`** (verify midpoint date = exact halfway date between first and last billed appellate entries!).

Bill supervised paralegal and law-clerk hours at **prevailing market rates** under ***Richlin Security Service Co. v. Chertoff*, `553 U.S. 571 (2008)`** (never payroll cost!), include `1.5–3.0 hrs` for preparing the EAJA application itself (***Jean*, `496 U.S. 154`**), and claim `$50` CAVC filing fee expense (if not waived via `IFP`).

blocks.text: Gate 5: Federal Circuit Jurisdictional Gate (38 U.S.C. § 7292) vs. Rule 23 Class & TRAC Mandamus Triage

items: **5.1 Strict `38 U.S.C. § 7292(a) & (d)(2)` Pure-Law Framing Audit (`60-Day` NOA Clock):** — Unless raising a **bona fide constitutional claim**, **`38 U.S.C. § 7292(d)(2)` strips the Federal Circuit of jurisdiction** to review any challenge to a **factual determination** OR **application of law to the facts of a particular case** (including clear-error `§ 5107(b)` equipoise weighing after *Bufkin v. Collins*, `604 U.S. 369 (2025)`)! — **Pre-Filing Test:** Can the Question Presented be stated purely as *"Whether the CAVC misinterpreted the legal standard of `38 U.S.C. § [X]` / `38 C.F.R. § [Y]` by requiring [legal element Z]..."* without disputing how the Board weighed evidence? — **CRITICAL AMA EFFECTIVE-DATE SAFETY NET (*MVA v. Sec'y*, `7 F.4th 1110, 1131–35 (Fed. Cir. 2021)`):** Because `38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)(2)(E)` preserves continuous-pursuit effective dates for `1 year` after a **CAVC** decision—and does **NOT** reset a new `1-year` Supplemental Claim window after an unsuccessful **Federal Circuit** appeal—calendar a hard **`330-day` post-CAVC-decision stop-date** to evaluate filing a protective AMA `VA Form 20-0995` Supplemental Claim if the Federal Circuit appeal remains pending or risky!

**5.2 `CAVC Rule 23` Class Action & All Writs Act (`28 U.S.C. § 1651(a)`) Mandamus Triage:** — **Unreasonable Agency Delay (`TRAC` Six-Factor Test — *Martin v. O'Rourke*, `891 F.3d 1338, 1344–49 (Fed. Cir. 2018)`):** Plead concrete human-health/financial welfare prejudice (`TRAC` Factor 3 & 5) and rule-of-reason benchmarks—never rely on a rigid "unreasonable per se" month count, and never file mandamus when an adequate ordinary AMA appeal exists (*Cheney*; *Hamill* fn. 6). — **Systemic Class Relief (`CAVC Rule 23` — *Skaar* & *Beaudette*):** Under ***Skaar v. McDonough*, `48 F.4th 1323, 1331–35 (Fed. Cir. 2022)`**, CAVC `Rule 23` classes in `§ 7252` appeals can include **only** claimants who obtained a final Board decision (or have a ripe appealable Board decision within the `120-day` window / equitable tolling), *unless* challenging a systemic deprivation of BVA review itself as in ***Beaudette v. McDonough*, `93 F.4th 1361 (Fed. Cir. 2024)`** (opening BVA/CAVC review to `PCAFC` caregiver appeals)!

blocks.text: Gate 6: 38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(1) Era Trigger, *MVA v. Sec'y* Eligibility & 30-Day § 14.636(g)(3) Filing Gate

items: **6.1 Confirm Active Accreditation & Post-Accreditation CLE Compliance (`38 C.F.R. § 14.629(b)(1)(iii)–(iv)`):** — Verify the signing attorney/agent holds active OGC accreditation and completed `3 hours` of qualifying CLE **within the `12 months` *after* initial accreditation** (never pre-accreditation!) + `3 hours` every `2 years` thereafter.

**6.2 Verify Statutory `§ 5904(c)(1)` Fee Trigger (`Legacy` vs. `AMA` *MVA v. Sec'y*):** — **Original `VA Form 21-526EZ` Contention (Never Previously Decided):** **STOP — `$0` Fee Permitted** until VA issues its initial `§ 5104` AOJ decision! — **AMA `HLR` (`20-0996`), `Board NOD` (`10182`), *ANY* `Supplemental Claim` (`20-0995` — whether `< 1 yr` OR `> 1 yr`!), OR *ANY* `RO`/`BVA` CUE Motion (`§§ 5109A / 7111`):** **IMMEDIATELY FEE-ELIGIBLE** upon retention because a prior initial AOJ decision already exists on the issue (***Military-Veterans Advocacy v. Sec'y*, `7 F.4th 1110, 1135–41 (Fed. Cir. 2021)`**)! *(If VA RO staff deny direct-pay fees citing invalidated `38 C.F.R. § 14.636(c)(1)(i)`, immediately file an HLR/NOD citing **MVA v. Sec'y**, `7 F.4th at 1141`!)* — **Legacy Appeal (`June 20, 2007 – Feb. 18, 2019`):** Confirm a valid Legacy `NOD` was filed `>= June 20, 2007` (covering downstream continuous-case `TDIU`/rating stages under *Cameron v. Shinseki*, `26 Vet. App. 109 (2012)`).

**6.3 Execute & File Fee Agreement in the Correct VA Office Within `30 Calendar Days` (`38 C.F.R. § 14.636(g)(3)`):** — **`<= 20%` Direct-Pay Contingency Agreement:** Upload/transmit `VA Form 21-22a` + signed fee agreement **to the `AOJ` / VBA Centralized Mail Intake (`QuickSubmit` / VBMS)** **within `30 days` of execution** and save timestamped proof of receipt (*Ravin v. Wilkie*, `956 F.3d 1346 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`). — **Non-Direct-Pay Agreement (`> 20%` up to `33 1/3%` [neutral middle band evaluated under `§ 14.636(e)`, vs. `<= 20%` presumed reasonable and `> 33 1/3%` presumed unreasonable under `§ 14.636(f)(1)`], hourly, or flat):** File with **`VA Office of the General Counsel (022D)`, 810 Vermont Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20420** **within `30 days` of execution**!

blocks.text: Gate 7: Post-Grant Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c) "Same Work" EAJA Refund & § 5904(d) Withholding Audit

Run this gate within **`7 calendar days`** of every favorable post-remand VA award alongside the [`Post-Grant VA Award Letter & Withholding Audit Checklist`](/checklists/award-letter-and-withholding-audit-checklist):

items: **7.1 Audit `20%` Direct-Pay Past-Due Calculation & `DFAS AEW` / *Scates* Holds ([Playbook 20](/playbooks/20-backpay-offsets-crdp-crsc-severance-recoupment)):** — Recompute `20% × Sum(Newly Awarded Rate − Prior Paid Rate)` across every retroactive month (`§ 14.636(h)(3)`), verifying full inclusion of `SMC`, dependents (`§ 3.401(b)`), incarcerated gross awards (*Snyder v. Nicholson*, `489 F.3d 1213 (Fed. Cir. 2007)`), and post-`AEW` `CRDP` releases (*contrasting* uncollected debt balances under *Gumpenberger v. Wilkie*, `973 F.3d 1379 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`). — **Multi-Counsel / Discharged-Counsel Notice (`§ 14.636(i)`; *Scates v. Principi*, `282 F.3d 1362 (Fed. Cir. 2002)`):** If a prior discharged attorney claims part of the `20%` pool, calendar the **`60-day` disbursement window** and file a **`120-day` *quantum meruit* reasonableness motion with `OGC (022D)`** (`§ 14.636(i)`) limiting prior counsel strictly to actual contribution!

**7.2 Execute Mandatory `Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c)` `"Same Work"` Client Refund (*Carpenter* & *Shaw*):** — Did the firm (or any fee-sharing co-counsel) collect `EAJA` fees (`28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)`) for CAVC remand litigation on this claim stream? — **IF YES (Unified Representation Model):** Compute **`Refund_Due_To_Client = min(EAJA_Fee_Received, §5904_Fee_Received)`** (*excluding* reimbursed out-of-pocket court filing expenses), **disburse `100%` of that smaller fee directly to the claimant immediately upon clearing the `§ 5904` payment**, send a written settlement accounting letter citing `Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c)` and *Carpenter v. Principi*, `15 Vet. App. 64 (2001) (en banc)`, and archive the cleared check/wire confirmation in the firm compliance ledger! — **IF NO (Segregated Referral Model):** Confirm in writing that CAVC referral counsel took *only* `EAJA` (`$0` `§ 5904` share) and agency counsel took *only* `§ 5904` (`$0` `EAJA` share) with **zero inter-firm fee-splitting**!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Appealing to the Veterans Court (CAVC): Deadlines, Remand Agreements & Fee Protections
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Taking a denied Board of Veterans' Appeals decision to the U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims (CAVC) involves strict court deadlines and safeguard rules that every Veteran and representative should understand up front. This 7-gate checklist covers the 120-day CAVC appeal deadline, protecting favorable Board findings, avoiding waiver traps in Joint Motions for Partial Remand (JMPRs), the 30-day Equal Access to Justice Act (EAJA) fee deadline (where the government pays your court attorney fees when VA erred), 60-day Federal Circuit appeals, protective 1-year AMA Supplemental Claims after an adverse court ruling, and mandatory EAJA client fee refunds.
record_clues: A final adverse or partially favorable Board of Veterans' Appeals decision stamped with a mailing date (starting the 120-day CAVC Notice of Appeal window under 38 U.S.C. § 7266(a)).
A draft Joint Motion for Partial Remand (JMPR) negotiated between your CAVC attorney and VA's Office of the General Counsel.
A CAVC remand judgment or immediate-mandate consent order (CAVC Rule 41(b)) opening the strict 30-day EAJA fee-application window under 28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)(1)(B).
A VA Form 21-22a appointment, a 38 U.S.C. § 5904 contingency fee agreement, and post-remand VA Award Letters showing both prior EAJA fees and direct-pay contingency withholding.
important_cautions: Protect the 120-day CAVC clock: a Motion for Board Reconsideration pauses the 120-day CAVC deadline ONLY if filed within the 120-day window (Rosler v. Derwinski), whereas filing an AMA Supplemental Claim does NOT pause the 120-day CAVC deadline.

JMPR waiver & immediate-mandate EAJA traps: a Joint Motion for Partial Remand should explicitly preserve favorable Board findings (Medrano), reserve unmentioned arguments for remand (avoiding the Carter v. Shinseki waiver trap), and rest on administrative error (preserving EAJA fees under Sumner / Robinson). Also note that consent JMPR orders issue an immediate mandate under CAVC Rule 41(b), meaning the attorney's 30-day EAJA clock expires on Day 30—not Day 90!

Post-CAVC 1-year continuous-pursuit safeguard: if the CAVC affirms a Board denial (even if you appeal pure legal issues within 60 days to the Federal Circuit under 38 U.S.C. § 7292), filing a protective AMA Supplemental Claim (VA Form 20-0995) or Intent to File within 1 year of the CAVC decision preserves your effective-date chain (38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)(2)(E); Military-Veterans Advocacy v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs).

Fee compliance & Board CUE caution: direct-pay fee agreements (<=20%) must be filed within 30 days (38 C.F.R. § 14.636(g)(3); Ravin v. Wilkie), attorneys must refund the lesser of overlapping EAJA and § 5904 fees to the Veteran (Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c)), and under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c), once the Board issues a final merits decision on a CUE motion for a prior Board issue, no second CUE motion is allowed on that Board issue.
questions_for_representative: What is the exact 120-day CAVC Notice of Appeal deadline from my Board decision's mailing date, and will my CAVC representation be covered by Equal Access to Justice Act (EAJA) fees if we win a remand?

Before signing a Joint Motion for Partial Remand (JMPR), does the motion lock in my favorable Board factual findings (Medrano), allow me to submit new medical evidence and raise additional arguments on remand (Carter), and preserve EAJA eligibility?

If the CAVC does not remand an issue, what is my 1-year deadline from the CAVC decision to file a protective Supplemental Claim (VA Form 20-0995) with new and relevant evidence under 38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)(2)(E)?
If we win an EAJA fee at the CAVC and later win past-due benefits on remand at VA, how will you document and pay my mandatory dollar-for-dollar lesser-fee refund under Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c)?

title: Character of Discharge (OTH / BCD / Uncharacterized) & National Guard / Reserve Active-Service Intake Audit Checklist
cFileTriggers: Intake prospect presenting an Other Than Honorable (OTH), Undesirable, Bad Conduct (BCD), or Uncharacterized DD Form 214
DD Form 214 Block 18 showing 'Immediate Reenlistment' or 'Continuous Honorable Active Service' preceding a final adverse separation
DD Form 214 Block 25/26/28 listing Pattern of Misconduct, Drug Rehab Failure, In Lieu of Court-Martial, Personality/Adjustment Disorder, or Entry Level Separation
National Guard or Reserve prospect presenting only an NGB Form 22 without a federal DD Form 214, Title 10/32 orders, or Line of Duty (DA Form 2173 / AF Form 348) packet
Prior VA denial for 'Not a Veteran', 'No Qualifying Active Service', 'Character of Discharge Bar', or 'Willful Misconduct'
killSwitches: Litigating 38 C.F.R. § 3.12 misconduct before checking DD-214 Block 18 / OMPF contracts for an unbroken multi-enlistment unconditional discharge or release under 38 U.S.C. § 101(18)(B) and 38 C.F.R. § 3.13(c)!

Pleading 38 C.F.R. § 3.12(e) compelling circumstances against a General Court-Martial sentence (§ 3.12(c)(2)) or discharge in lieu of GCM (§ 3.12(d)(1)(i))—only § 3.354(b) insanity, § 3.13 prior period, or § 1552 BCMR relief overcomes those bars!
Treating an NGB Form 22 alone as proof of Title 38 federal active duty (pure State Active Duty under governor authority is NOT qualifying Title 38 service)
Claiming disease service connection (other than § 106(d) acute MI, cardiac arrest, or stroke) on pure Inactive Duty Training (IADT / weekend drills) under 38 C.F.R. § 3.6(a)(3), (d), (e)
Invoking the § 1111 presumption of soundness on Active Duty for Training (ADT) before first proving an in-service disease or injury was incurred or aggravated during ADT (Biggins / Smith / Donnellan)
Expecting pre-June 25, 2024 retroactive compensation when reopening a final COD denial solely under the liberalized 89 FR 32361 criteria (§ 3.114(a) floor)

toc.text: Preconditions (Mandatory Intake Packet — Never Rely on Member-1 Short Copy!)
Gate 1: Forensic DD-214 (Member-4) & NGB-22 Block-by-Block Decode
Gate 2: Multi-Enlistment 38 C.F.R. § 3.13 Unconditional-Discharge Screen *(Check BEFORE Litigating § 3.12!)*
Gate 3: Statutory vs. Regulatory Bar Triage & Dual-Track VA + DoD Upgrade Strategy
Gate 4: National Guard / Reserve Active-Service & Line-of-Duty (LOD) Audit (38 C.F.R. §§ 3.6, 3.301)
Gate 5: Immediate Chapter 17 Healthcare Access, Ancillaries & § 5904 Fee Check

lines: **ZERO CLIENT PII RULE:** Never type veteran names, SSNs, VA file numbers, service numbers, or unredacted `DD-214` / `NGB-22` blocks into repository files—execute all case-specific intake audits offline! General practitioners and VSOs routinely turn away disabled veterans with "bad paper" or `NGB-22`-only National Guard records; running the five sequential gates below separates dead statutory bars from **high-value `§ 3.13`, `§ 3.12(e)`, `§ 3.354(b)`, *Hamill*, and `ADT`/`LOD` `§ 3.156(c)` fee cases** in under 30 minutes.

blocks.text: *(Cross-references: Verbatim snapshot [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.12, 3.13, 3.354, 3.400(g), 3.6 & 3.301 (Character of Discharge Evolution, Insanity, Upgrades, ADT/IADT & Line of Duty)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.12-3.13-3.354-cod-insanity); [`Part 3 COD Evolution Diff (89 FR 32361)`](/cfr/modules/character-of-discharge-3.12-evolution); [Playbook 10 (COD, Insanity, `§ 3.13` & Upgrades)](/playbooks/10-character-of-discharge-insanity-upgrades); [Playbook 11 (Guard/Reserve ADT/IADT & LOD)](/playbooks/11-guard-reserve-adt-iadt-and-line-of-duty); [Playbook 03 (`§ 3.156(c)` Service Records)](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c); [Procedural Vehicles for Piercing Finality](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality); [Master `VAOPGCPREC` Digest](/docs/vaopgcprec-index); [Three-Era Statutory Crosswalk](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk); [Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon); and [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).*
Preconditions (Mandatory Intake Packet — Never Rely on Member-1 Short Copy!)

items: **Obtain `DD Form 214` (`Member-4` or `Service-2` Long Copy) for *Every* Period of Service:** `Member-1` deliberately omits Blocks `23–30` (Character of Service, Separation Authority, `SPD` Code, Reentry Code, and Narrative Reason)!

**Order Full `OMPF` + Military Justice / Separation Packet (`SF-180` / `milConnect` / Archival FOIA):** Pull enlistment/reenlistment contracts (`DD Form 4`), Administrative Separation Board (`AdSep`) notification/waiver memos, `UCMJ Art. 15` (`NJP`) logs, charge sheets (`DD Form 458`), court-martial promulgating orders, `CID`/`NCIS`/`OSI` reports, and inpatient/brig clinical jackets.
**Pull Complete VBMS eFolder:** Inspect every prior VA Administrative Decision ("Character of Discharge Determination"), Rating Code Sheet, and post-Feb. 19, 2019 AMA decision notice.

blocks.text: Gate 1: Forensic DD-214 (Member-4) & NGB-22 Block-by-Block Decode
Audit six exact blocks on **every** `DD-214` (and compare against any `NGB Form 22` *Report of Separation and Record of Service*):

items: **Blocks `12a–12h` (*Record of Service*):** — Check `12c` (*Net Active Service This Period*), `12d` (*Total Prior Active Service*), `12e` (*Total Prior Inactive Service*), and `12f` (*Foreign and/or Sea Service* — combat/TERA trigger!). — **CRITICAL `NGB-22` TRAP:** An `NGB-22` proves separation from a state's Army/Air National Guard (`ANG`), **NOT** Title 38 federal active duty (`38 C.F.R. § 3.6(a)–(b)`). Always cross-check whether federal mobilizations or `IADT`/`ADT` basic training generated separate `DD-214`s!

**Block `18` (*Remarks*):** — Scan immediately for **`"IMMEDIATE REENLISTMENT"`** or **`"CONTINUOUS HONORABLE ACTIVE SERVICE FROM [YYYYMMDD] TO [YYYYMMDD]"`** (triggers **Gate 2**!). — Audit any **`"LOST TIME"` / `"TIME LOST UNDER 10 USC 972"`** date ranges: count whether any single unauthorized absence (`AWOL`) reached **`>= 180` *continuous* days** (`38 U.S.C. § 5303(a)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.12(c)(6)`). Multiple shorter AWOLs totaling `180+` cumulative days **do NOT** trigger the `(c)(6)` statutory bar!

**Block `24` (*Character of Service*):** — `Honorable` or `Under Honorable Conditions (General)` -> **Binding pass** under `§ 3.12(a)` (unless a rare `(c)` statutory bar applies or post-Oct. 8, 1977 `DRB` upgrade requires `§ 3.12(h)` verification). — `Under Other Than Honorable Conditions` (`OTH` / pre-1977 `Undesirable`) -> Triggers VA `§ 3.12` COD review. — **`Bad Conduct` (`BCD`) — CRITICAL COURT-MARTIAL SPLIT:** Determine from the promulgating order / Block `25`/`28` whether the `BCD` was adjudged by a **Special Court-Martial (`SPCM`)** (NOT a statutory bar under `§ 3.12(c)(2)`—evaluated under `(d)(2)` and eligible for `§ 3.12(e)` compelling circumstances!) vs. a **General Court-Martial (`GCM`)** (hard statutory bar under `§ 3.12(c)(2)`!). — `Dishonorable` (Enlisted) or `Dismissal` (Officer) -> Adjudged by `GCM` (`§ 3.12(c)(2)` statutory bar). — `Uncharacterized` (separations initiated `>= Oct. 1, 1982`) -> Check Block `28` under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.12(l)(1)–(3)` `[former § 3.12(k)(1)–(3)]`**: — **`Entry Level Separation` (`ELS`, typically `< 180` days):** **AUTOMATICALLY "other than dishonorable" under `§ 3.12(l)(1)`!** (If VA denied an `ELS` on COD grounds, file immediate CUE!). — `Void Enlistment` (`§ 3.12(l)(2)`) or `Dropped From the Rolls` (`§ 3.12(l)(3)`): Reviewed under `(c)` and `(d)`.

**Blocks `25`, `26` & `28` (*Separation Authority, `SPD` Code & Narrative Reason*):** — **`In Lieu of Trial by Court-Martial` (`AR 635-200 Ch. 10` / `USMC SOTS` / `SPD KFS` or `JFS`):** Verify in the separation packet whether charges were actually **referred to (or threatened with referral to) a General Court-Martial** (`§ 3.12(d)(1)(i)` non-exempt bar) vs. only a **Special Court-Martial**! If the OMPF lacks proof of pending GCM charges, VA **cannot** apply `§ 3.12(d)(1)(i)`! — **`Pattern of Misconduct` / `Minor Disciplinary Infractions` / `Commission of a Serious Offense` / `Drug Rehabilitation Failure` (`AR 635-200 Ch. 14` / `SPD JKA, JKB, JKQ, JKN, JPC, KKC`):** Governed post-June 25, 2024 by **`§ 3.12(d)(2)(i)–(ii)`** and **fully eligible for `§ 3.12(e)` compelling circumstances**! — **`Personality Disorder` / `Adjustment Disorder` (`AR 635-200 Ch. 5-13 / 5-17`, `SPD JFX / JFV`):** Classic DoD administrative label frequently masking undiagnosed in-service **PTSD, MST, TBI, or bipolar/psychotic illness**—prime evidence for `§ 3.12(e)(2)(i)` or `§ 3.354(b)` insanity!

blocks.text: Gate 2: Multi-Enlistment 38 C.F.R. § 3.13 Unconditional-Discharge Screen *(Check BEFORE Litigating § 3.12!)*

items: **Audit Every Enlistment Contract (`DD Form 4`) & `DD-214` Block `18`:** Did the veteran complete the obligated term of an earlier enlistment (`§ 3.13(c)`)—or discharge early in post-Vietnam service to reenlist when eligible for honorable separation (`§ 3.13(a)(3)`)—and **immediately reenlist without a physical break in active service**?

**Apply `38 U.S.C. § 101(18)(B)` & `38 C.F.R. § 3.13(a)–(c)` (*Holmes v. Brown*, `10 Vet. App. 38 (1997)`; `§ 5107(b)` equipoise confirmed in *Newman v. McDonough*, `35 Vet. App. 310 (2022)`):** — **Rule:** Instead of suffering an adverse `"conditional discharge"` stitch under `§ 3.13(a)–(b)`, Period 1 is deemed **unconditionally discharged or released under conditions other than dishonorable (`§ 3.13(c)` / `(a)(3)`)** for all disabilities incurred or aggravated during Period 1—**even if Period 2 ended in an `OTH`, `BCD`, or `General Court-Martial` Dishonorable Discharge** (absent `38 U.S.C. § 6104` treason/subversion/mutiny/spying forfeiture)! — **CUE Check (RO CUE (§ 3.105(a)) / Board CUE (38 U.S.C. § 7111)):** If a prior RO or Board decision barred benefits across *all* service based on a composite single `DD-214` displaying an `OTH` in Block `24` while ignoring `"CONTINUOUS HONORABLE ACTIVE SERVICE"` in Block `18`, plead **CUE** for multi-decade back pay on all Period 1 disabilities (complete the [Board CUE Pre-Filing Gate](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate) if attacking a BVA decision).

blocks.text: Gate 3: Statutory vs. Regulatory Bar Triage & Dual-Track VA + DoD Upgrade Strategy

Select the highest-yield VA pathway(s) **and** launch a parallel DoD military-board track where warranted (see full clause-by-clause table in [Part 3 Historical Diff: Character of Discharge Evolution (38 U.S.C. § 5303 & 38 C.F.R. § 3.12 Pre- vs. Post-June 25, 2024 Final Rule, 89 FR 32361)](/cfr/modules/character-of-discharge-3.12-evolution)):

items: **Track 3A — Objective Defeat of `§ 3.12(d)(2)(ii)` ("Not Persistent" Defense):** — Pull the *Manual for Courts-Martial* (`MCM`) maximum punishment table for every documented misconduct incident: — Is the offense **"minor misconduct"** (max MCM punishment does **not** include dishonorable discharge or confinement `> 1 year`)? — **Single Offense:** Never "persistent" under `(d)(2)(ii)`! — **Spacing Check:** Were two minor offenses separated by **`> 2 years`**, a minor and serious offense separated by **`> 2 years`**, or two serious offenses separated by **`> 5 years`**? If outside those windows, `(d)(2)(ii)` **fails objectively** even before reaching compelling circumstances!

**Track 3B — `38 C.F.R. § 3.12(e)` Compelling Circumstances Exception (`Eff. June 25, 2024`, `89 FR 32361`):** — **Eligible Bars:** `§ 3.12(c)(6)` (`>= 180`-day continuous AWOL), `§ 3.12(d)(2)(i)` (moral turpitude), and `§ 3.12(d)(2)(ii)` (willful & persistent misconduct). *(Ineligible: `(c)(1)–(5)` including `GCM`, and `(d)(1)(i)–(ii)` discharge in lieu of `GCM` / mutiny).* — Build a 3-part evidentiary brief + private Nexus/IMO addressing: `(1)` `§ 3.12(e)(1)` honest/meritorious service outside the misconduct window; `(2)` `§ 3.12(e)(2)(i)–(vii)` mitigating factors (mental/cognitive impairment **including PTSD, TBI, ADHD, or substance use disorder**, physical trauma/medication side effects, combat/overseas hardship, **MST**, duress/desperation, family obligations, youth/immaturity); and `(3)` `§ 3.12(e)(3)` substantive UCMJ defenses. — **Effective-Date Ceiling Warning:** Standalone `89 FR 32361` reopenings (`VA Form 20-0995`) **cannot pay earlier than June 25, 2024** (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(g)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)`). Always screen Tracks **3C–3E** below if pre-2024 back pay is at stake!

**Track 3C — `38 U.S.C. § 5303(b)` / `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.12(b), 3.354(b)` Insanity Exception *(Defeats ALL Bars + Retroactive!)*:** — Mandatory whenever facing a **General Court-Martial (`(c)(2)`)**, **discharge in lieu of GCM (`(d)(1)(i)`)**, **deserter (`(c)(4)`)**, or **pre-June 25, 2024 back-pay** claim! — Obtain a forensic psychiatric opinion applying VA's **non-criminal** `§ 3.354(a)` standard (*Zang v. Brown*, `8 Vet. App. 246 (1995)`; *Gardner v. Shinseki*, `22 Vet. App. 415 (2009)`; [`VAOPGCPREC 20-97`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index))—proving disease-based prolonged behavioral deviation concurrent with the offense(s) (never let an examiner apply criminal *M'Naghten* "right vs. wrong" tests, and pair newly obtained brig/inpatient STRs with **`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)`**!).

**Track 3D — *Hamill* AMA Explicit-Notice Audit & Pre-2024 *Cropper* CUE:** — ***Hamill v. Collins*, `166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. 2026)` (`38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)`):** Did the veteran submit any AMA (`>= Feb. 19, 2019`) claim or COD reopening request that VA failed to address with explicit `§ 5104(b)` findings? If so, the AMA claim **remains legally pending and unadjudicated**! — ***Cropper v. Brown*, `6 Vet. App. 450 (1994)`:** Did a pre-2024 final COD denial misclassify a *Special* Court-Martial `BCD` as a `GCM` statutory bar, ignore `ELS` status under `former § 3.12(k)(1)`, or violate extant pre-2024 law? *(Never cite `89 FR 32361` for pre-2024 CUE per *George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` / `§ 20.1403(e)`).*

**Track 3E — Parallel DoD Discharge Upgrade (`DRB` vs. `BCMR`/`BCNR`) & `§ 3.400(g)` Effective Dates:** — **`DRB` (`DD Form 293`, `10 U.S.C. § 1553`):** Strict **`15-year`** deadline from discharge; **cannot** upgrade a `GCM` sentence; **TRAP (`Pub. L. 95-126` / `38 C.F.R. § 3.12(h)`):** a post-Oct. 8, 1977 `DRB` upgrade to *General (Under Honorable Conditions)* lifts `(d)` bars **only** if issued under uniform historical standards and **never** overrides an original `(c)` statutory bar! — **`BCMR` / `BCNR` (`DD Form 149`, `10 U.S.C. § 1552`):** `3-year` deadline routinely waived "in the interest of justice"; **CAN** upgrade `GCM` discharges, change Narrative Reason (`Personality Disorder -> Secretarial Authority / Medical Retirement`), and **conclusively binds VA under `38 C.F.R. § 3.12(f)`**! Plead DoD **Liberal Consideration** (*Hagel* `2014`, *Carson* `2016`, *Kurta* `2017`, and *Wilkie* `2018` memoranda for PTSD, TBI, mental health, and MST). — **`10 U.S.C. § 874(b)` Clemency Trap (`VAOPGCPREC 10-96`):** A Service Secretary's `§ 874(b)` clemency administrative substitution **does NOT** lift a `§ 5303(a)` `GCM` bar—use `10 U.S.C. § 1552` `BCMR` instead! — **Post-Upgrade Filing Clock (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(i)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.400(g)(1)–(3)`):** File an original VA claim within **`1 year` of the military upgrade taking effect** to lock in the `DD-293`/`DD-149` filing date (`§ 5110(i)` / `§ 3.400(g)(1)`), or reopen a previously disallowed VA claim promptly (watching `§ 3.400(g)(3)`'s 1-year-prior-to-reopening cap, and pairing any newly uncovered STRs with **`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)`** to reach the original VA claim date!).

blocks.text: Gate 4: National Guard / Reserve Active-Service & Line-of-Duty (LOD) Audit (38 C.F.R. §§ 3.6, 3.301)

When a prospect served in the Army/Air National Guard or Reserves, verify the **exact statutory duty status on the date of the injury, exposure, or symptom onset** ([Playbook 11](/playbooks/11-guard-reserve-adt-iadt-and-line-of-duty)):

rows: **Any** in-service injury or disease + full statutory presumptions
**YES (`§ 1111` applies):** VA must prove preexistence *and* non-aggravation by clear & unmistakable evidence (*Wagner v. Principi*, `370 F.3d 1089 (Fed. Cir. 2004)`).
Normally classified as **`ADT`** (`§ 3.6(a)(2), (c)(3)`)—injury *or* disease (plus COVID-19 / Homeland Defense / Southwest Border `32 U.S.C. § 502(f)` federalized protections)
Treated as **`ADT`** unless converted by statute (`e.g., 38 U.S.C. § 1164` COVID-19 presumption) or disabled in line of duty under `§ 101(24)`.
**3. Active Duty for Training (`ADT` / `ACDUTRA`, incl. `IADT` Basic/AIT & Annual Training)**
In-service **injury OR disease** incurred or aggravated in line of duty (`+ § 3.6(e)` authorized portal-to-portal travel)

**CRITICAL TRAP (*Biggins* / *Paulson* / *Smith* / *Donnellan*):** **NO `§ 1111` presumption of soundness or `§ 1153` presumption of aggravation** unless the claimant *first* proves at least in equipoise (`38 U.S.C. § 5107(b)` benefit of the doubt; *Newman v. McDonough*, `35 Vet. App. 310 (2022)`) that a disability was incurred or aggravated during `ADT` (`24 Vet. App. 40`; `24 Vet. App. 167`)!

**ONLY:** `(1)` an **injury** incurred/aggravated in line of duty, OR `(2)` **`§ 106(d)` acute myocardial infarction, cardiac arrest, or stroke (`CVA`)** (`+ § 3.6(e)(1)–(3)` direct portal-to-portal travel)

**FATAL DISEASE BAR:** Ordinary diseases (e.g., non-stroke sleep apnea, diabetes, non-traumatic psychiatric onset without injury/assault) during weekend `IADT` **cannot** establish `§ 101(24)` active service unless tied to an `IADT` **injury** (e.g., orthopedic trauma, acoustic trauma, TBI, or physical MST assault) or `TERA` exam!
**5. Pure State Active Duty (`SAD` — Governor's State Funds)**
Verify funding/authority code on orders—many Guardsmen confuse `Title 32 § 502(f)` federally funded disaster/border duty (qualifying!) with pure state-funded `SAD`!

items: **Demand Missing Guard/Reserve Records for `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)` Reconsideration:** Request all `Title 10`/`32` orders, `NGB-23` / Reserve retirement point sheets, unit drill muster rosters, **`DA Form 2173` (Army) / `AF Form 348` (Air Force) / `DD Form 261` Formal Line of Duty (`LOD`) determinations**, and `1973` St. Louis fire / state Adjutant General (`TAG`) archives. Associating an unobtained `DA Form 2173` or `Title 32` order unlocks retroactive compensation back to a prior `"no active service"` denial under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)`**!

**Audit Line of Duty & Secondary Substance Use (`38 U.S.C. § 105(a)`; `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.1(m)–(n), 3.301, 3.310(a)–(b)`):** Under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.1(m)` and `(n)`**, favorable military `LOD` and non-misconduct findings **are binding on VA** **`"unless it is patently inconsistent with the facts and the requirements of laws administered by the Department of Veterans Affairs"`**—whereas adverse `"Not in LOD"` military findings do *not* bind VA! For alcohol/substance-related disabilities, plead **secondary service connection under *Allen v. Principi*, `237 F.3d 1368 (Fed. Cir. 2001)` (`§ 3.310(a)–(b)`)** whenever SC PTSD, depression, or chronic orthopedic pain caused or aggravated the substance use disorder and downstream organ damage!

**Screen `PACT Act` Guard/Reserve Toxic Exposures (`38 U.S.C. § 1168` `TERA`):** Under `Pub. L. 117-168`, Guard/Reserve members exposed to `AFFF`/`PFAS` firefighting foam, burn pits, fuels, degreasers, radiation, or herbicides during `ADT` or `IADT` trigger mandatory **`§ 1168` `TERA` participation memos and medical nexus opinions** whenever claiming a non-presumptive disability!

blocks.text: Gate 5: Immediate Chapter 17 Healthcare Access, Ancillaries & § 5904 Fee Check

Never leave a disabled `OTH` client untreated while a 12-month COD or `BCMR` docket runs—immediate VHA care protects the veteran's life **and** generates contemporaneous clinical diagnoses/nexus records (`Bell` constructive possession):

items: **Enroll Immediately in Statutory `Chapter 17` Healthcare Carve-Outs (`VA Form 10-10EZ` / VHA Eligibility):** — **`38 U.S.C. § 1720D` (`MST` Counseling & Care):** Furnished **regardless of character of discharge** and **without requiring any in-service report** of the sexual assault or sexual harassment! — **`38 U.S.C. § 1720I` (`OTH` Mental & Behavioral Health Care):** Available to former service members with an administrative `OTH` (excluding `GCM`/dishonorable) who either `(A)` served **`> 100` cumulative days** with deployment in a combat theater / contingency / hostility / drone operation **OR** `(B)` experienced **`MST`**. — **`38 U.S.C. § 1720J` (`COMPACT Act` Acute Suicidal Crisis Care):** Zero-cost emergency inpatient/outpatient stabilization at any VA or community facility regardless of enrollment or discharge status (subject to statutory exclusion thresholds). — **`38 C.F.R. § 3.360` (`Pub. L. 95-126, § 2` Line-of-Duty Healthcare) & `38 C.F.R. § 17.34` (Tentative Eligibility):** Unlocks Chapter 17 medical treatment for specific service-connected/line-of-duty disabilities for administrative `OTH` veterans whenever no `§ 5303(a)` / `§ 3.12(c)` statutory bar or `BCD` applies!

**Verify `38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(1)` / `38 C.F.R. § 14.636` Contingency-Fee Posture:** — **Initial Original Claim / Pre-Decision COD Review:** Representation before VA issues an initial AOJ decision on the claim is **pro bono (`$0` fee)** under `§ 5904(c)(1)`. — **Post-AOJ COD Denial (`VA Form 20-0995` Supplemental, `20-0996` HLR, or `10182` Board NOD):** A prior AOJ Administrative Decision denying eligibility on `COD` or `"no qualifying active service"` grounds **satisfies `§ 5904(c)(1)`**, authorizing a compliant contingency fee (`<= 20%` direct-pay withholding) on all past-due Title 38 compensation unlocked once the COD/service gateway and disability ratings are granted! — **DoD `DRB`/`BCMR` Fee Boundary:** `VA` will **not** withhold `§ 5904(d)` direct-pay fees from DoD proceedings (`DD-293`/`DD-149`); ensure any parallel DoD upgrade retainer is separately structured and compliant, with Title 38 contingency fees attaching only to continuous/post-AOJ-decision VA reviews.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Preparation Checklist for Less-Than-Honorable Discharges & Guard/Reserve Eligibility Reviews
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: When VA says 'You are not eligible as a Veteran'—either because of an Other Than Honorable (OTH), Bad Conduct (BCD), or Uncharacterized discharge, OR because your service was in the National Guard or Reserves—one missing piece of military paperwork often changes the entire outcome. This intake checklist helps you and an accredited representative gather the exact service contracts, reenlistment remarks, court-martial vs. administrative separation codes, mental health/trauma markers, Title 10/32 orders, and Line of Duty (LOD) forms needed before filing.
record_clues: Every DD Form 214, DD Form 215, NGB Form 22, enlistment/reenlistment contract, and Official Military Personnel File (OMPF) separation packet—especially DD-214 Block 18 ('Immediate Reenlistment' remarks) and Blocks 24–28.
Any court-martial order showing whether a Bad Conduct Discharge came from a Special Court-Martial (potential regulatory review) rather than a General Court-Martial (statutory bar).

Unit orders showing exact statutory authority (Title 10 vs. Title 32 U.S.C. §§ 316, 502–505 vs. State Active Duty), retirement point statements, drill schedules, and Line of Duty forms (DA Form 2173 / AF Form 348 / DD Form 261).
In-service sick-call notes, stockade/brig evaluations, MST markers, or post-service psychiatric records documenting mental health conditions at the time of separation.
important_cautions: Always Check Prior Enlistments First (§ 3.13): Never spend years fighting a final OTH discharge before checking whether you completed an earlier enlistment and immediately reenlisted—because 38 C.F.R. § 3.13(c) insulates disabilities from the earlier honorable period right away.

Match the Exception to the Exact Bar: The June 25, 2024 'compelling circumstances' rule (§ 3.12(e), 89 FR 32361) helps overcome prolonged AWOL and regulatory misconduct bars (with effective dates no earlier than June 25, 2024 if granted solely under the new rule), whereas General Court-Martial or OTH-in-lieu-of-GCM bars require § 3.13 prior service, § 3.354(b) insanity, or a § 1552 BCMR correction.

Guard/Reserve Proof Gate: An NGB Form 22 by itself shows separation from state Guard status—always pair it with federal Title 10/32 orders, ADT/IADT documentation, and Line of Duty findings to prove qualifying active service under 38 C.F.R. § 3.6.
questions_for_representative: Looking at Block 18 and my enlistment contracts, did I complete an earlier honorable obligation before reenlisting under 38 U.S.C. § 101(18)(B) and 38 C.F.R. § 3.13?
Which specific pathway—June 2024 § 3.12(e) compelling circumstances, § 3.354(b) insanity, DRB (DD Form 293), or BCMR/BCNR (DD Form 149)—fits the exact separation authority on my DD-214?

For my National Guard or Reserve injury, have we pulled my federal Title 10/32 orders and Line of Duty packet so VA evaluates § 3.6 active service (and § 3.156(c) effective dates if those service records were missing earlier)?

McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` / `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)` change-in-interpretation bar! veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Comparing Ways to Seek an Earlier Effective Date (Why CUE Is Usually the Last Resort)
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Many Veterans hear the phrase 'Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE)' and assume it is the only way to fix an old VA decision or recover past-due benefits. In reality, Veterans Law provides multiple distinct legal pathways to look back at an older decision—and almost every other pathway gives the Veteran far friendlier evidence rules (including the 'benefit of the doubt') than CUE. This comparison guide helps you and your accredited representative see side-by-side how newly associated service records (§ 3.156(c)), open or pending claims, wrong-address notice challenges, void rating reductions (§§ 3.105(e)/3.344), Nehmer Agent Orange rules (§ 3.816), AMA continuous pursuit (§ 3.2500), and Regional Office vs. Board CUE motions actually work.
record_clues: You are still within 1 year of a VA Rating Decision (or within 120 days of a Board of Veterans' Appeals decision), meaning direct appeal or continuous-pursuit lanes are still open!

Official military hospital, personnel, or unit records were added to your C-file after an older denial (§ 3.156(c)), or you served in the Republic of Vietnam / Blue Water Navy with a covered Agent Orange condition (§ 3.816).
VA lowered a long-standing rating without 60-day notice or proof of sustained life/work improvement, or left a claimed issue completely unaddressed in a post-February 19, 2019 AMA decision.
An older decision became final with all records already in the file, and VA flatly misapplied a mandatory rating percentage or combined-math table in force on that date.
important_cautions: Preserve Active Appeal Clocks First: If a decision was issued within the past year (or a Board decision within the past 120 days), timely direct review preserves full benefit-of-the-doubt rights—never let an active appeal deadline expire assuming you can 'just file CUE later.'

Why CUE Is the Narrowest Needle: Under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(d)–(e) and George v. McDonough, CUE requires an undebatable error based solely on the record and law at the time; VA's failure to get records, an inadequate C&P exam, a close medical judgment call, or a later court reinterpretation cannot win as CUE.

Board CUE Res Judicata Trap (38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c)): Unlike Regional Office CUE motions under 38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a), once the Board of Veterans' Appeals issues a final merits decision on a CUE motion for a specific Board issue, no second Board CUE motion is allowed on that Board issue.
questions_for_representative: Am I still inside a 1-year AMA review window or a 120-day CAVC judicial appeal window where we can keep my claim open directly?
Before we even consider CUE, do my records fit 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) newly associated service records, a void rating reduction, Nehmer (§ 3.816), wrong-address notice, or an unadjudicated AMA issue?
If CUE is the only remaining option, are we challenging a Regional Office rating decision (§ 3.105(a)) or a Board decision (§ 7111), and has a Board CUE motion ever been filed on that issue before?

title: Zero-PII 5-Gate Special Monthly Compensation (SMC(k)-(t)), Barry Step-Math & Ancillary Grants Audit Worksheet
