toc.text: Preconditions (Mandatory C-File / VBMS Intake Packet)
Gate 1: SMC(k) (x3 Stacking) & Statutory Rate-Ceiling Audit (38 U.S.C. § 1114(k); 38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a))
Gate 2: Extremity Loss of Use (LOU) Screen (38 C.F.R. §§ 3.350(a)(2), 4.63 — *Tucker v. West*)
Gate 3: SMC(s) Housebound Screen — Statutory (100% + 60%) vs. Factual
Gate 4: SMC(l) A&A, *Barry* Multi-Step Calculator, Anti-Pyramiding, SMC(r)/(t) & § 3.552 Trap
Gate 5: High-Dollar Ancillary Grants & Fee/Offset Sweep (Playbook 13)

lines: **ZERO CLIENT PII RULE:** Never enter veteran names, SSNs, claim numbers, or unredacted medical/award text inside this Git repository—copy this worksheet to your secure offline case management folder before screening! Because SMC is **inferred by law** inside every evaluation claim whenever record evidence reasonably raises it (*Akles v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 118 (1991)`; *Buie v. Shinseki*, `24 Vet. App. 242 (2010)`), running all **five sequential gates** below routinely uncovers **`$2,000–$7,000+/month` rate upgrades** plus **`$150,000+` in unclaimed ancillary grants**.

blocks.text: *(Cross-references: Verbatim `SMC` regulations [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.350, 3.352, 3.552(b), 4.63 & 3.810(a) (Special Monthly Compensation Ratings, Aid & Attendance, TBI SMC(t), Loss of Use & Multiple Clothing Allowances)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.350-3.352-smc-evolution); [`Part 3 SMC Evolution Diff`](/cfr/modules/smc-statutory-and-regulatory-evolution); [Master SMC Treatise & Step Math](/docs/smc-complete-treatise-and-step-math); [Playbook 12 (`SMC(l)`, `SMC(r)(1)–(2)` & `SMC(t)`)](/playbooks/12-aid-and-attendance-smc-l-r1-r2-and-smc-t); [Playbook 13 (Ancillary Grants)](/playbooks/13-ancillary-grants-sah-auto-clothing-dea-spina-bifida); [Playbook 04 (Unadjudicated TDIU & Mandatory SMC)](/playbooks/04-unadjudicated-tdiu-informal-claims-smc); [`Surviving Spouse & Helpless Child Diff`](/cfr/modules/survivor-marriage-dependency-evolution); [Procedural Vehicles for Piercing Finality](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality); [Board CUE Pre-Filing Gate](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate); [Master `VAOPGCPREC` Digest](/docs/vaopgcprec-index); [Three-Era Statutory Crosswalk](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk); [Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon); and [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).*
Preconditions (Mandatory C-File / VBMS Intake Packet)

items: **Pull Every Historical & Current Rating Code Sheet:** Notification letters omit internal SMC designators (`K-1`, `S-1`, `L-1`, `M½`, `R-1`, `T`), diagnostic codes, and subordinate ancillary blocks!

**Pull All `VA Form 21-2680`s, C&P DBQs, VAMC `PSAS` Prosthetics Logs & Caregiver (`PCAFC`) Assessments:** Essential for proving functional Loss of Use (`LOU`), bracing, ADL deficits, and TBI supervision.

blocks.text: Gate 1: SMC(k) (x3 Stacking) & Statutory Rate-Ceiling Audit (38 U.S.C. § 1114(k); 38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a))
Audit whether the veteran qualifies for **up to `3` concurrent `SMC(k)` awards (`K-1`, `K-2`, `K-3`)**:

items: **1. Creative Organ (`§ 3.350(a)(1)`, eff. `Aug. 1, 1952`):** SC erectile dysfunction (`DC 7522`, e.g., secondary to diabetes, hypertension, radical prostatectomy `DC 7528`, spinal/radicular nerve injury, or SSRI/PTSD medication!), female sexual arousal disorder (`FSAD`), orchiectomy, hysterectomy, or oophorectomy. — **`VAOPGCPREC 5-89` Surgical Rule (`>= Mar. 23, 1989`):** Prior elective noncompensable sterilization (vasectomy / tubal ligation) **does NOT bar `SMC(k)`** for subsequent SC **anatomical** removal of a creative organ!
**2. Single Hand or Single Foot (`§ 3.350(a)(2)`):** Anatomical loss or functional `LOU` (proceed to **Gate 2**).

**3. Both Buttocks (`§ 3.350(a)(3)`, eff. `Aug. 1, 1956`):** Severe bilateral gluteal muscle damage preventing the veteran from rising from a seated or stooping position and maintaining postural stability without assistance ([Playbook 01](/playbooks/01-penetrating-wounds-scars-vs-muscles)).
**4. Single Eye Blindness (`§ 3.350(a)(4)`):** Light perception only (`LPO`) or anatomical enucleation.
**5. Total Bilateral Deafness (`§ 3.350(a)(5)`, eff. `July 1, 1963`, `Pub. L. 88-20`):** Absence of air and bone conduction in both ears.

**6. Complete Organic Aphonia (`§ 3.350(a)(6)`, eff. `July 1, 1963`, `Pub. L. 88-22`):** Constant organic inability to communicate by speech (e.g., post-laryngectomy `DC 6518` or vocal-cord paralysis `DC 6519`).

**7. Breast Tissue Loss or Radiation (`§ 3.350(a)` intro; `former § 3.350(a)(7)` removed at `68 FR 55467`):** Complete mastectomy (`>= Nov. 1, 2000`, `Pub. L. 106-419`), OR **`>= 25%` tissue loss** (single breast or combined lumpectomy/excision) **OR radiation treatment of breast tissue** (`>= Dec. 6, 2002`, `Pub. L. 107-330`, `68 FR 55467`).

**Statutory Rate-Ceiling Check (`38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)`):** — Combined `0%–100%` schedular/TDIU (`§ 1114(a)–(j)`) or `SMC(s)` (`§ 1114(s)`): Each `SMC(k)` (`up to 3`) adds on top, provided `§ 1114(a)–(j)` or `§ 1114(s)` + `k`(s) does not exceed the `SMC(l)` dollar rate (capped at `(l)`). — Base `SMC(l)` through `SMC(n½)`: `SMC(k)` (`up to 3`) adds on top, **strictly capped at the `SMC(o)` / `§ 1114(p)` dollar ceiling** (`zero` `SMC(k)` add-ons pay above `SMC(o)`, `SMC(r)(1)`, `SMC(r)(2)`, or `SMC(t)`!).

blocks.text: Gate 2: Extremity Loss of Use (LOU) Screen (38 C.F.R. §§ 3.350(a)(2), 4.63 — *Tucker v. West*)
Never wait for physical amputation—audit every severe radiculopathy, peripheral neuropathy, spinal cord, `ALS`, stroke, or orthopedic file under ***Tucker v. West*, `11 Vet. App. 369 (1998)`**:

items: **Lower Extremity `LOU` (`Foot`):** Would remaining function be **equally well served by an amputation with prosthesis**? Check for **complete foot drop** (common peroneal nerve paralysis), inability to balance/propel (`push-off`) without a rigid ankle-foot orthosis (`AFO`), unfavorable ankylosis, non-union of tibia/fibula, or severe trophic/vascular ulceration.

**Upper Extremity `LOU` (`Hand`):** No more effective function than an amputation stump with suitable prosthetic appliance—e.g., inability to grasp, pinch, manipulate, or oppose thumb and fingers (`median`/`ulnar`/`radial` paralysis or contractures).

**Paired `LOU` Upgrade Check:** `2 feet` = **`SMC(l)`**; `2 hands` = **`SMC(m)`**; `1 hand + 1 foot` = **`SMC(l)`**; higher anatomical/above-knee/above-elbow pairings = **`SMC(l½)`–`SMC(o)`** *(Note: under `VAOPGCPREC 30-97`, preexisting NSC paralysis never bars anatomical-amputation SMC!).*

blocks.text: Gate 3: SMC(s) Housebound Screen — Statutory (100% + 60%) vs. Factual
Whenever the veteran is **not** yet receiving `SMC(l)+`, test both `38 U.S.C. § 1114(s)` (`eff. Sept. 1, 1960`) prongs:

items: **Prong 3A — Statutory `SMC(s)` (`100% + 60%`):** — Does the veteran have **ONE single SC disability rated `100%` schedular** OR **TDIU (`§ 4.16`) attributable solely to ONE single SC disability** (*Bradley v. Peake*, `22 Vet. App. 280 (2008)`; *Buie v. Shinseki*, `24 Vet. App. 242 (2010)`)? *(Trap: Multi-disability TDIU fails this prong under *Gazelle v. Shulkin*, `868 F.3d 1006 (Fed. Cir. 2017)`—get an IMO isolating unemployability to a single `70%` PTSD or `60%` back condition!)* — Do the **remaining separate/independent SC disabilities** combine via `38 C.F.R. § 4.25` (not simple addition, *Gazelle*) to **`>= 60%`** (rounded, e.g., `55% -> 60%`)? — **Bitemporal CUE Gate:** Omission of `SMC(s)` on a **schedular `100% + 60%`** code sheet (`>= Sept. 1, 1960`) is **pure math CUE (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive)**! For pre-Nov. 26, 2008 TDIU-based denials (`VAOPGCPREC 6-99` era), *George v. McDonough* (`596 U.S. 740 (2022)`) bars CUE—use `§ 3.156(b)–(c)` or pending claims ([Playbook 04](/playbooks/04-unadjudicated-tdiu-informal-claims-smc)).

**Prong 3B — Factual Housebound (`38 C.F.R. § 3.350(i)(2)`):** — Single `100%` (or TDIU) disability + **substantially confined** as a direct result of SC disability(ies) to the veteran's dwelling and immediate premises (or ward/clinical area) with reasonable certainty of persistence throughout life. — ***Howell v. Nicholson*, `19 Vet. App. 535 (2006)`:** Leaving home **for medical appointments** does **NOT** defeat factual housebound!

blocks.text: Gate 4: SMC(l) A&A, *Barry* Multi-Step Calculator, Anti-Pyramiding, SMC(r)/(t) & § 3.552 Trap
Run this 5-step catastrophic calculator on every polytrauma, `A&A`, or `TBI` file ([Playbook 12](/playbooks/12-aid-and-attendance-smc-l-r1-r2-and-smc-t)):

items: **Step 4.1 — Establish Base `SMC(l)`–`SMC(n)`:** — **Regular `A&A` (`SMC(l)`, `38 C.F.R. § 3.352(a)`):** Under *Turco v. Brown*, `9 Vet. App. 222 (1996)`, the veteran **need NOT satisfy every listed factor**—inability to dress, bathe, feed, toilet, adjust prosthetics, **OR physical/mental incapacity requiring regular care/supervision to protect from hazards of the daily environment** establishes `SMC(l)`!

**Step 4.2 — Cross Out Base Disabilities (*Breniser* / *Amberman* Anti-Double-Counting Gate!):** — List the exact SC disability(ies) used to establish base `SMC(l)–(n)` in Step 4.1. Under ***Breniser v. Shinseki*, `25 Vet. App. 64 (2011)`** and ***Amberman v. Shinseki*, `570 F.3d 1377 (Fed. Cir. 2009)`**, those base disabilities are **"spent"** and **CANNOT** also be counted in Step 4.3! *(Practice Tip: If a veteran has BOTH bilateral foot `LOU` AND `A&A` due to a separate `100%` Parkinson's/PTSD condition, ground base `SMC(l)` on bilateral foot `LOU` so the separate `100%` condition remains free to power a full-step `(f)(4)` bump—or vice versa!)*

**Step 4.3 — Apply Multi-Step `§ 3.350(f)(3)–(4)` Stacking (*Barry v. McDonough*, `101 F.4th 1348 (Fed. Cir. May 16, 2024)`):** — Count every **separate, independent ("unspent") permanent SC disability rated `50%`–`90%`** (plus any `§ 4.25` **combination** of leftover `< 50%` permanent SC disabilities combining to `>= 50%`) -> add **`+ ½` step EACH** (`§ 3.350(f)(3)`). — Count every **separate, independent ("unspent") permanent SC disability rated `100%` schedular** (*excluding `§ 4.16` TDIU*) -> add **`+ 1` full step EACH** (`§ 3.350(f)(4)`). — Sum steps along `L -> L½ -> M -> M½ -> N -> N½ -> O` (capped at **`SMC(o)`**; add any `SMC(k)` up to the `SMC(o)` dollar cap). *(Note: *George* bars standalone CUE on final pre-May 16, 2024 single-step ratings—use pending appeals, `§ 3.156(b)–(c)`, *Hamill* AMA silent omissions, or file an immediate Supplemental/increase claim!)*

**Step 4.4 — Check `SMC(r)(1)`, `SMC(r)(2)` & TBI `SMC(t)` (`~$11,000+/month` Top Tiers!):** — **`SMC(r)(1)` (`§ 1114(r)(1)`; `§ 3.350(h)`):** Did *Barry* step-stacking (or paired `LOU`s) push the veteran to **`SMC(o)`** (or **`SMC(n½) + SMC(k)`** hitting the `(p)` ceiling) **WHILE** also needing regular `A&A`? If yes, **`SMC(r)(1)` unlocks automatically** (provided `A&A` itself wasn't the sole basis without independent paired losses/bumps satisfying `§ 3.350(h)`)! — **`SMC(r)(2)` (`§ 1114(r)(2)`; `§ 3.352(b)(1)`):** Qualifies for `(r)(1)` **PLUS** requires daily personal health-care services by (or under regular supervision of) a **licensed health-care professional** absent which institutionalization would be required. — **`SMC(t)` for Traumatic Brain Injury (`§ 1114(t)`, `Pub. L. 111-275, § 601`, eff. `Oct. 1, 2011` — *Laska v. McDonough*, `37 Vet. App. 460 (Sept. 6, 2024)`):** — Does the veteran have **SC TBI residuals** requiring **regular `A&A` (`§ 3.352(a)`)** (including lay/spousal cognitive supervision, medication management, wandering/safety protection) without which they would require hospitalization, nursing home, or residential institutional care? — **Post-*Laska* Goldmine:** *Laska* **invalidated `38 C.F.R. § 3.352(b)(2)`'s "higher level of care" hurdle**—paying the **full `SMC(r)(2)` rate** (`>= Oct. 1, 2011` statutory floor) **WITHOUT** needing `SMC(o)` and **WITHOUT** needing skilled nursing care!

**Step 4.5 — Audit `38 C.F.R. § 3.552` VA Hospitalization Reductions:** — If VA reduced `SMC(l)`, `(r)(1)`, `(r)(2)`, or `(t)` during inpatient care, verify: `(1)` was care actually **at VA/government expense**? `(2)` did VA wait until at least the **`1st` day of the `2nd` calendar month following the month of admission** (`§ 3.552(b)(1)`)? and `(3)` did VA overlook the **`§ 3.552(a)(2)` continuation exception** (paraplegia involving both lower extremities + bowel/bladder sphincter loss, or Hansen's disease) or fail to restore full A&A immediately on hospital release?

blocks.text: Gate 5: High-Dollar Ancillary Grants & Fee/Offset Sweep (Playbook 13)

items: **`Ch. 21` `SAH` / `SHA` / `TRA` (`VA Form 26-4555`, `~$117,000+`):** Screen bilateral LE bracing/crutches/wheelchair under ***Jensen v. Shulkin*, `29 Vet. App. 66 (2017)`** (`§ 3.809(c)` — does *not* require `SMC` `LOU`!), `<= 20/200` bilateral blindness (`Pub. L. 116-154`, eff. Oct. 1, 2020), `1 LE + organic balance/propulsion`, severe burns, `ALS` (`§ 3.809(d)`), or `§ 1151` (*Kilpatrick*); check `6` lifetime grant uses (`§ 2102(d)(3)`) + `TRA` family-home grant (`§ 2102A`).

**`Ch. 39` Auto Purchase + Adaptive Equipment (`VA Form 21-4502` & `10-1394`, `~$25,000+` + Unlimited Equip.):** Screen `1+` hand/foot `LOU`, `<= 20/200` or `20°` blindness, severe burns (`Pub. L. 111-275, § 803`, eff. Oct. 1, 2011), `ALS`, knee/hip ankylosis (`10-1394` adaptive equip.), and **prior recipients from `>= 30 years` ago** (immediately eligible for a **second full vehicle grant** under `Pub. L. 117-333`, `38 U.S.C. § 3903(a)`, shifting to every `10 years` on Jan. 5, 2033!).

**Multiple Annual Clothing Allowances (`VA Form 10-8678`, `§ 3.810`, `Aug. 1` Deadline):** Count **every** qualifying brace, prosthesis, wheelchair, or SC skin cream damaging distinct garments (`§ 3.810(a)(2)`, *Sursely*) or accelerating damage to a single garment (`§ 3.810(a)(3)`); appeal VHA `Handbook 1173.15` `"non-rigid"` denials to BVA (`§ 20.105`); verify automatic annual renewal (`Pub. L. 117-328, Div. U, § 201`).

**Retroactive `Ch. 35` DEA (`VA Form 22-5490`) & `CHAMPVA` (`VA Form 10-10d` / `10-7959a`):** Calendar the **strict `1-year` post-`P&T`-notice deadline (`38 C.F.R. § 21.4131`)** to capture multi-year retroactive DEA tuition/stipends; verify post-Aug. 1, 2023 elimination of DEA age-26/10-year expiration (`Pub. L. 117-328, Div. U, § 234`); **never** let an unadjudicated `18–23` disabled child cash a DEA payment before establishing `§ 3.356` helpless-child status (`38 U.S.C. § 3562`).

**`Ch. 18` Spina Bifida & Birth Defects (`VA Form 21-0304`, Denver RO):** Screen biological children of Vietnam, Korea DMZ (`Sept. 1, 1967 – Aug. 31, 1971`), and **Thailand (`Jan. 9, 1962 – May 7, 1975`, `38 U.S.C. § 1822`)** herbicide veterans for spina bifida (non-occulta), and biological children of female Vietnam veterans (`§ 3.815`)—zero offset against VA compensation, DIC, DEA, or SSI (`§ 1834`)!

**Offsets & `§ 5904` Fee Check:** Audit `CRDP`/`CRSC`/*Soto* concurrent receipt ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc)), verify post-decision `§ 5904(c)(1)` fee posture on denied `SMC`/ancillary/VHA appeals, and structure retainers to account for non-withheld VHA/vendor disbursements + CAVC `EAJA` fee offsets.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: 5-Step SMC & Ancillary Benefits Audit Worksheet for Severely Disabled Veterans & Caregivers
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: When a Veteran is rated 100% or TDIU—or lives with polytrauma, Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI), spinal cord or nerve paralysis, ALS, Parkinson's, blindness, or advanced cancer—VA Rating Code Sheets routinely miss higher Special Monthly Compensation (SMC) tiers and tens of thousands of dollars in housing, vehicle, clothing, and family education grants. This 5-step worksheet helps Veterans, family caregivers, and accredited representatives audit every layer: (1) missing SMC(k) add-ons and functional Loss of Use, (2) statutory/factual SMC(s) Housebound, (3) Aid & Attendance SMC(l), SMC(r)(1)/(2), and TBI SMC(t) under Laska, (4) multi-step bumps under Barry v. McDonough, and (5) SAH housing, Chapter 39 Auto, multiple Clothing Allowances, CHAMPVA, and retroactive Chapter 35 DEA.
record_clues: Your latest VA Rating Code Sheet (showing any lettered SMC codes like K-1, S-1, L-1, M-1, P-1, R-1, or T) alongside a list of every service-connected Diagnostic Code and percentage.
Medical notes, VA Form 21-2680, PCAFC Caregiver records, or Prosthetics records showing braces (AFOs), wheelchairs, walkers, skin creams, or daily caregiver assistance.
Award notification dates for 100% Permanent & Total (P&T) status—critical for checking the 1-year retroactive Chapter 35 DEA education filing window (38 C.F.R. § 21.4131).
important_cautions: Keep Personal Information Private: Never save Social Security numbers, VA file numbers, or unredacted medical letters in shared or public files—keep your completed worksheet private for your accredited representative.

Respect Statutory Floors & Anti-Pyramiding Rules: TBI SMC(t) cannot precede October 1, 2011; the same extremity or organ impairment cannot be double-counted for both base SMC(l)–(n) and § 3.350(f) step bumps (Breniser / Amberman); and under George v. McDonough (§ 20.1403(e)), Barry and Laska apply via open claims, Supplemental Claims, or § 3.156(c) rather than CUE on final pre-2024 decisions.

Act Within 1 Year of Initial P&T Notice for Retroactive DEA: Under 38 C.F.R. § 21.4131, spouses and eligible children have 1 year from notification of a retroactive P&T grant to file VA Form 22-5490 and recover retroactive college/training stipends.
questions_for_representative: Walking through all 5 gates on my Rating Code Sheet, did VA miss any inferred SMC(k), functional Loss of Use (§ 4.63), SMC(s), Aid & Attendance, TBI SMC(t) (Laska), or multi-step Barry bumps?

Have we checked every ancillary grant tied to my disabilities—Chapter 21 SAH/SHA housing, Chapter 39 Auto/Adaptive Equipment, Sursely multiple Clothing Allowances (§ 3.810), CHAMPVA, and Chapter 35 DEA?
Which filing lane—timely HLR/Board appeal, Supplemental Claim with a VA Form 21-2680, unadjudicated AMA issue audit, or Regional Office CUE on an older math error—protects my earliest effective date?

title: 48-Hour Survivor Post-Mortem Triage & Pre-Filing Gate Checklist (DIC, § 5121A Substitution, § 5121 Accrued & § 3.816(f) Nehmer Estates)
statutes: Pub. L. 116-92, § 622 (NDAA FY2020 SBP-DIC Offset Repeal, eff. Jan. 1, 2023)
keyPrecedents: Padgett v. Nicholson, 473 F.3d 1364 (Fed. Cir. 2007) (en banc)
cFileTriggers: Death of an active firm veteran client with any pending RO, HLR, Supplemental, BVA, CAVC, or Federal Circuit matter
Intake inquiry from a surviving spouse, minor/school/helpless child, dependent parent, or estate executor following a veteran's death
Death certificate listing non-SC primary cause where veteran had SC cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, diabetes, or herbicide conditions
Board decision dated ON OR AFTER the veteran's date of death (void nullity under Smith v. Brown!)
killSwitches: Missing the STRICT 1-year post-death statutory filing bar for § 5121(c) Accrued Benefits and § 5121A Substitution (permanently forfeits non-Nehmer accrued/substitution!)

Substituting at the CAVC/Federal Circuit WITHOUT also filing a timely VA accrued/substitution claim within 1 year of death when remand is required (moots the appeal under Merritt v. Wilkie, 965 F.3d 1357 (Fed. Cir. 2020)!)

Filing a brand-new post-mortem CUE motion expecting § 5121 accrued back pay when the veteran had no CUE claim pending at death (barred by Haines v. West, 154 F.3d 1298 (Fed. Cir. 1998)—valid ONLY for § 3.22(b)(1) hypothetical § 1318 DIC!)
Relying on the deceased veteran's VA Form 21-22a POA or fee agreement instead of executing a new survivor VA Form 21-22a and survivor § 5904 fee agreement (§ 14.631(g))
Adult non-helpless child or estate filing for standard § 5121 accrued benefits without either § 3.816(f) Nehmer class status or § 5121(a)(6) last-sickness/burial expense proof

toc.text: Preconditions (Intake Packet & VBMS Snapshot — Hours 0–24)
Gate 1: Immediate Appellate & Forum Posture Check (Hours 0–48)
Gate 2: Strict 1-Year Statutory Bars vs. Effective-Date Relation-Back Windows
Gate 3: Statutory Payee Hierarchy & Estate Eligibility Audit
Gate 4: Merits Track & Prescribed Form Selection Matrix
Gate 5: Postconditions — Rate Add-Ons, Concurrent-Receipt Offsets & Representation Hygiene

lines: **ZERO CLIENT PII RULE & IMMEDIATE DEADLINE ALERT:** Never enter veteran names, SSNs, VA file numbers, or unredacted death certificates into repository files—execute case-specific checklists offline! Upon notice of a veteran's death, **stop treating the file as a living-veteran Chapter 11 claim immediately**: the veteran's POA extinguishes at death (`38 C.F.R. § 14.631(g)`), appellate jurisdiction shifts overnight, and **missing the strict `365-day` statutory clock under `38 U.S.C. §§ 5121(c), 5121A` permanently destroys non-*Nehmer* accrued and substitution back pay!**

blocks.text: *(Cross-references: Verbatim snapshots [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.22 & 3.312 (Hypothetical § 1318 Total-Disability DIC Evolution & Service-Connected Cause of Death)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.22-dic-hypothetical-evolution) and [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.1000, 3.1010 & 3.816(f) (Accrued Benefits, § 5121A Substitution & Nehmer Survivor/Estate Payouts)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.1000-3.1010-accrued-substitution); [Playbook 08 (DIC & `§ 1318`)](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical); [Playbook 09 (Accrued, Substitution & *Nehmer*)](/playbooks/09-accrued-benefits-substitution-nehmer-estates); [Playbook 06 (*Nehmer* `§ 3.816`)](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc); [Marriage & Dependency Diff (`§§ 3.50–3.57, 3.356`)](/cfr/modules/survivor-marriage-dependency-evolution); [Forms Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon); [Title 38 Statutory Crosswalk](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk); and [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).*
Preconditions (Intake Packet & VBMS Snapshot — Hours 0–24)

items: **Exact Date & Cause of Death Verified:** Obtain the long-form **Death Certificate** (checking *both* Part I Immediate/Underlying Causes and Part II "Other Significant Conditions Contributing to Death") plus terminal hospitalization / autopsy / hospice summaries.

**Freeze Complete VBMS eFolder & VACOLS/Caseflow Snapshot:** Download the latest **Rating Code Sheet**, all pending `526EZ` / `0995` / `0996` / `10182` / Legacy `NOD`–`Form 9` filings, active `VA Form 21-0966` Intents to File, and any pending CAVC / Federal Circuit docket entries.

blocks.text: Gate 1: Immediate Appellate & Forum Posture Check (Hours 0–48)
Identify **where every live issue stood on the exact date of death** and execute the matching forum preservation move:

items: **Scenario 1A — Appeal Pending at CAVC or Federal Circuit:** — File a **`CAVC Rule 43(a)`** (or `Fed. R. App. P. 43(a)`) **Motion to Substitute** an eligible `§ 5121(a)` accrued-benefits claimant (*Breedlove v. Shinseki*, `24 Vet. App. 7 (2010)`). — If the veteran died **after** briefing/submission was complete at the CAVC or Federal Circuit, move simultaneously for ***nunc pro tunc* relief** back to the date of death (*Padgett v. Nicholson*, `473 F.3d 1364 (Fed. Cir. 2007) (en banc)`). — **CRITICAL *MERRITT* TRAP (*Merritt v. Wilkie*, `965 F.3d 1357 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`):** Judicial substitution at CAVC/Fed. Cir. **DOES NOT** satisfy VA's 1-year administrative filing deadline if the court vacates/remands rather than reversing outright! **Always file `VA Form 21P-0847` AND `VA Form 21P-534EZ` (or `21P-535`/`21P-601`) directly with the VA AOJ within `1 year` of death** while the court appeal is pending!

**Scenario 1B — Veteran Died During the `120-Day` BVA Notice of Appeal (`NOA`) Window:** — File a timely **protective CAVC Notice of Appeal** + `CAVC Rule 43(a)` motion to substitute within `120 days` of the BVA decision mailing date (*Pekular v. Mansfield*, `21 Vet. App. 495 (2007)`; *Breedlove*, `24 Vet. App. at 20–21`), **AND** file `VA Form 21P-0847` + `VA Form 21P-534EZ` at the VA AOJ within `1 year` of death!

**Scenario 1C — Veteran Died *Before* the BVA Issued Its Decision (Post-Death BVA Decision):** — Under *Smith v. Brown*, `10 Vet. App. 330 (1997)` and *Landicho v. Brown*, `7 Vet. App. 42 (1994)`, the Board lost jurisdiction over the veteran at the moment of death—making the post-death BVA decision **ultra vires and a legal nullity**! — Move the Board (via Motion to Vacate) or appeal to CAVC within `120 days` to **vacate the void BVA decision** so it carries zero adverse preclusive effect, and file **`VA Form 21P-0847`** within `1 year` of death so the survivor substitutes directly into the still-pending BVA appeal!

**Scenario 1D — Claim/Review Pending at RO, HLR, Supplemental Claim, or BVA Docket (`38 U.S.C. § 5121A`):** — File **`VA Form 21P-0847`** (*Request for Substitution of Claimant Upon Death of Claimant*) within **`1 year` of death** (`38 C.F.R. § 3.1010(b)`). — Confirm whether open-record substitution (keeping Duty to Assist, new nexus opinions, and `§ 1154(b)` combat presumptions under *Reeves v. Shinseki*, `682 F.3d 988 (Fed. Cir. 2012)`) beats waiving substitution for immediate closed-record `§ 5121` adjudication (*Reliford v. McDonald*, `27 Vet. App. 297 (2015)`).

blocks.text: Gate 2: Strict 1-Year Statutory Bars vs. Effective-Date Relation-Back Windows

lines: **NEVER CONFUSE `§ 5110(d)` WITH `§§ 5121(c) & 5121A`:** Missing `1 year` on DIC only shifts the DIC effective date forward; missing `1 year` on Accrued Benefits or Substitution **kills the entire back-pay claim forever** (unless *Nehmer* `§ 3.816(f)` applies)! Do **not** rely on an unperfected `VA Form 21-0966` Intent to File to toll `§ 5121(c)` or `§ 5121A` past 365 days—file the formal application inside 1 year of death!

rows: Effective **first day of the month in which death occurred**!
**Still eligible!** Payable from date of claim (or perfected `VA Form 21-0966` ITF / `§ 3.114` / `§ 1305` date).
Steps into veteran's pending claim/appeal back to **veteran's original effective date** (uncapped!).
Unpaid benefits "due and unpaid" on file at death (uncapped for deaths on/after Dec. 16, 2003 per `Pub. L. 108-183, § 104`).
100% of unpaid *Nehmer* retroactive compensation paid to survivor or **estate**.
**NO 1-YEAR BAR!** *Nehmer* mandate overrides `§ 5121(c)` time and payee bars!

items: Calendar **300-day** and **350-day** hard internal firm stop-dates measured from the exact date of death.

blocks.text: Gate 3: Statutory Payee Hierarchy & Estate Eligibility Audit

Verify the client qualifies in the highest surviving payee tier (see full status matrices in [Part 3 Historical Diff: Surviving Spouse Marriage Validity, Multi-Era Remarriage Cutoffs (§ 3.55) & Helpless Child Status (§ 3.356)](/cfr/modules/survivor-marriage-dependency-evolution)):

items: **Tier 1 — Surviving Spouse (`38 U.S.C. §§ 101(3), 103, 5121(a)(2)(A)`; `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.50–3.55`):** — Valid marriage (`§ 103(c)` / `§ 3.1(j)`, including nationwide post-*Obergefell* recognition and Same-Sex Duration Relief under Instruction `01-22`, `87 FR 68904`), OR **`§ 3.52` Deemed Valid Marriage** (*Dedicatoria* / *Colon* ignorance at marriage + no entitled rival legal spouse). — **Continuous Cohabitation (`§ 3.53`):** If living apart at death, document **absence of surviving spouse's fault at the time of separation** (*Gregory v. Brown*, `5 Vet. App. 108 (1993)` — e.g., veteran's PTSD, abuse, desertion, or nursing-home care). — **Marriage Duration (`§ 1304` vs. `§ 1318(c)`):** Confirm `>= 1 year` marriage OR child born (`§ 3.54(d)`). *(Remember: the `15-year` post-service marriage path in `§ 1304` applies ONLY to `§ 1310` SC-death DIC, NOT `§ 1318` total-disability DIC!)* — **Remarriage Audit (`§ 103(d)(2)` / `§ 3.55(a)`):** Terminated remarriage restores DIC (`Pub. L. 105-178`); ongoing remarriage retains DIC if entered **at age `57+` (`Dec. 16, 2003 – Jan. 4, 2021`)** OR **at age `55+` on or after `January 5, 2021` (`Pub. L. 116-315, § 2009`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.55(a)(9)(iii)`, `87 FR 68360` eff. Nov. 15, 2022)**—audit `2021–2022` denials where raters wrongly applied pre-Nov. 2022 `§ 3.55(a)(10)` age-57 text, and remember `Ch. 35 DEA` / `Ch. 37 Home Loan` remain at age `57+`!

**Tier 2 — Surviving Child(ren) (`38 U.S.C. §§ 101(4)(A), 5121(a)(2)(B)`; `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.57, 3.356`):** — Unmarried child under `18`, schoolchild `18–23` (*note*: schoolchild `18–23` qualifies for DIC under `§ 1314(b)`, whereas `§ 5121` accrued tracks `§ 101(4)(A)` definition!), OR **pre-age-`18` permanently incapable Helpless Child (`§ 3.356`)** (confirm no post-Oct. 31, 1990 non-void/non-annulled marriage under `§ 103(e)` / `§ 3.55(b)`!).

**Tier 3 — Dependent Parent(s) (`38 U.S.C. §§ 1315, 5121(a)(2)(C)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.250`):** — Screen low-income parents for income-tested Parents' DIC (`VA Form 21P-535`) and dependency-at-death accrued benefits.

**Tier 4 — Adult Non-Helpless Child / Deceased Veteran's Estate (`§ 3.816(f)` or `§ 5121(a)(6)` ONLY):** — Confirm **either** (a) **`38 C.F.R. § 3.816(f)` *Nehmer* class entitlement** (pays 100% unpaid retro to adult children or the **estate** when no Tier 1–3 *Nehmer* payee survives!) **or** (b) **`38 U.S.C. § 5121(a)(6)` (`§ 3.1000(a)(5)`)** reimbursement capped at documented **last-sickness and burial expenses** paid by the claimant (`VA Form 21P-601`).

blocks.text: Gate 4: Merits Track & Prescribed Form Selection Matrix

Select **all** applicable tracks simultaneously (filing **`VA Form 21P-534EZ`** for a spouse/child automatically claims DIC, Survivors Pension, *and* `§ 5121` Accrued Benefits, while **`VA Form 21P-0847`** is additionally required to substitute under `§ 5121A`!):

items: **Track A — Direct or Contributory Cause-of-Death DIC (`38 U.S.C. § 1310`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.312(a)–(c)`):** — Screen primary cause (`§ 3.312(b)`) AND **contributory cause (`§ 3.312(c)`)**: did an SC disability debilitate a **vital organ (`§ 3.312(c)(3)`, where `100%` vital-organ evaluation assumes debilitation)** or combine substantially/materially (`§ 3.312(c)(1)`) to hasten death even if omitted from the Death Certificate? — **PACT Act DIC Re-Evaluation (`38 U.S.C. § 1305`, enacted by `Pub. L. 117-168, § 204`) & New Herbicide/Burn-Pit Presumptions (`Pub. L. 117-168, §§ 403–406`):** If DIC was *previously denied* and the cause of death is now presumptive (e.g., hypertension or MGUS under PACT `§ 404`, expanded herbicide locations under `§ 403`, or burn-pit cancers/COPD under `§ 406`), file a **`§ 1305` re-evaluation election** on `21P-534EZ` / `20-0995`!

**Track B — `§ 1318` Actual (`§ 3.22(a)(2)`) or Hypothetical (`§ 3.22(b)(1)–(2)`) `10-Year` Total-Disability DIC:** — Did the veteran hold (or **hypothetically qualify for**) continuous `100%` schedular or `TDIU` evaluations for **`10+` years** before death (`5+` years from discharge, or `1+` year if a Former POW under `§ 3.22(a)(2)(i)–(iii)`)? — **Hypothetical `§ 3.22(b)(1)–(2)` Audit:** If the veteran was under-rated during life, screen historical Rating Code Sheets for **RO/BVA CUE (`§ 3.22(b)(1)` via `§ 3.105(a)` / `§ 7111`)** or **newly associated service department records (`§ 3.22(b)(2)` via `§ 3.156(c)`)** on a lifetime claim that push combined/TDIU ratings to `100%` across the 10-year window! — ***Haines* vs. `§ 3.22(b)(1)` Rule (*Haines v. West*, `154 F.3d 1298 (Fed. Cir. 1998)`):** Remember that a survivor-initiated CUE motion **cannot** recover `§ 5121` accrued back pay unless the veteran's own CUE motion was pending at death, **but CAN** establish prospective/month-of-death `§ 1318` DIC under `§ 3.22(b)(1)`! *(Run the [BVA CUE Pre-Filing Gate](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate) and exclude George v. McDonough `§ 20.1403(e)` change-in-interpretation theories before filing any Subpart O motion).*

**Track C — `§ 5121A` Substitution (`VA Form 21P-0847`) + `§ 5121` Accrued (`21P-534EZ` / `21P-535` / `21P-601`):** — File `VA Form 21P-0847` alongside `21P-534EZ` (spouse/child), `21P-535` (dependent parent), or `21P-601` (reimbursement / non-spouse accrued).

**Track D — `38 C.F.R. § 3.816(f)` *Nehmer* Footnote 1 & Estate Audit:** — If the veteran served in the Republic of Vietnam or qualifying Blue Water Navy waters, audit the entire C-file back to **September 25, 1985** for any prior denied claim or contemporaneous medical diagnosis of a covered `§ 3.816(b)(2)` herbicide condition (*excluding* hypertension, MGUS, and chloracne per [Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc)).

blocks.text: Gate 5: Postconditions — Rate Add-Ons, Concurrent-Receipt Offsets & Representation Hygiene
Verify every dollar of survivor entitlement and lock in compliant representation **before** submitting the filing packet:

items: **`38 U.S.C. § 1311` DIC Rate Add-Ons Screened:** — **`§ 1311(a)(2)` ("8-Year Kicker"):** Extra monthly allowance if the veteran was `100%`/`TDIU` continuously for `8+` years immediately preceding death *and* married to the surviving spouse for those same `8+` years (applies to hypothetical `§ 1318` grants too!). — **`§ 1311(c)` Aid & Attendance / `§ 1311(d)` Housebound:** Submit **`VA Form 21-2680`** (or nursing-home proof) if the surviving spouse or dependent parent has functional/ADL limitations! — **`§ 1311(b)` Minor-Child Add-On & `§ 1311(f)` 2-Year Transitional Benefit:** Verify VA pays *both* the per-child increment (`§ 1311(b)`) and the automatic 2-year Transitional Benefit (`§ 1311(f)`) whenever `>= 1` child under age `18` is on the surviving spouse's award!

**SBP–DIC Full Concurrent Receipt Verified (`Pub. L. 116-92, § 622`):** — Confirm DFAS pays **100% of military Survivor Benefit Plan (`SBP`)** concurrently with **100% of VA DIC** for all periods on or after **January 1, 2023** (zero "Widow's Tax" offset!).

**Ancillary Benefits & Helpless-Child `Ch. 35` DEA Safeguard:** — Trigger **`CHAMPVA` (`38 U.S.C. § 1781`)**, **`Ch. 37` VA Home Loan COE**, **`Ch. 35` DEA**, and **Burial / Plot / Service-Connected Death Burial Allowance (`38 U.S.C. §§ 2302–2308`; `VA Form 21P-530EZ`)**. — **Helpless Child `Ch. 35` Gate (`38 U.S.C. § 3562`; `38 C.F.R. § 21.3023(a)–(c)`):** Ensure any disabled 18-year-old child files for and secures **`§ 3.356` helpless-child status BEFORE** negotiating a first `Ch. 35` DEA check/EFT (protecting concurrent receipt under `§ 21.3023(b)` and avoiding an irrevocable `§ 3562` schoolchild forfeiture if `§ 3.356` were denied!).

**Fresh Survivor POA & `§ 5904` Fee Agreement Executed (`38 C.F.R. §§ 14.631(g), 14.636`):** — Execute a **brand-new `VA Form 21-22a`** signed by the **surviving claimant** (or court-appointed estate executor for `§ 3.816(f)` *Nehmer* estate claims) AND a **new `38 U.S.C. § 5904` fee agreement** in the survivor's own name—never rely on the deceased veteran's extinguished POA or fee contract!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Step-by-Step Survivor Checklist After a Veteran Passes Away (Protecting Deadlines, Substitution & Monthly DIC)
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: In the grief and paperwork following a Veteran's passing, critical VA deadlines can quietly slip by—especially the strict 1-year deadline from the date of death to lock in date-of-death DIC effective dates, open-record Substitution (§ 5121A), and unpaid Accrued Benefits (§ 5121). This step-by-step checklist walks surviving spouses, children, dependent parents, and accredited representatives through the exact records and time-sensitive protections to check: signing a fresh survivor representative appointment, preserving any pending VA or court appeal, checking both service-connected cause of death (§ 1310) and 10-year total-disability DIC (§ 1318), screening for PACT Act or Nehmer Agent Orange retroactivity, and verifying DFAS Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) and burial allowances.
record_clues: The certified death certificate (checking whether contributing service-connected illnesses were omitted), final hospital/hospice discharge summaries, and autopsy reports if performed.
Any VA Rating Decision, Higher-Level Review, Supplemental Claim, Board appeal, or CAVC appeal that was pending—or still within its 1-year / 120-day appeal window—when the Veteran died.
Marriage certificates, prior divorce/death decrees, birth certificates of minor, school-age (18–23), or pre-age-18 permanently disabled ('helpless') children, and funeral/burial receipts.
A Board of Veterans' Appeals decision dated on or after the Veteran's date of death (which must be vacated so the survivor can substitute into the live appeal).
important_cautions: 1-Year Post-Death Deadline Is Strict: Filing VA Form 21P-534EZ and VA Form 21P-0847 within 1 year of death locks in the month-of-death DIC effective date (38 U.S.C. § 5110(d)) AND preserves statutory Substitution and Accrued rights (§§ 5121(c), 5121A). Missing the 1-year mark permanently forfeits non-Nehmer accrued/substitution back pay.
New Representative Form Required: Any VSO or attorney Power of Attorney signed by the Veteran ended at death; the survivor must sign a new VA Form 21-22 or 21-22a.

Dual Filing Required When a Court Appeal Was Pending: If an appeal was at the CAVC or Federal Circuit (or inside the 120-day CAVC appeal window), counsel must protect BOTH court substitution and a formal VA agency substitution/accrued filing within 1 year of death (Merritt v. Wilkie).

Do Not Confuse Post-Mortem CUE With Accrued Pay: A brand-new CUE motion filed for the first time after death cannot pay § 5121 accrued benefits (Haines v. West), though it CAN establish 10-year § 1318 DIC under 38 C.F.R. § 3.22(b)(1).
questions_for_representative: What is the exact 1-year anniversary of the Veteran's passing, and have we submitted both VA Form 21P-534EZ and VA Form 21P-0847 with a fresh survivor VA Form 21-22 / 21-22a?
Did my loved one have any open claim, appeal, unadjudicated issue, or void post-death Board decision into which I can substitute under 38 U.S.C. § 5121A?
Do the final hospital records support contributory service-connected death (§ 3.312(c)), PACT Act DIC re-evaluation (§ 3.33), or 10-year total-disability DIC (§ 3.22)?
Have we also checked non-taxable VA service-connected vs. non-service-connected burial allowances, CHAMPVA health care, Chapter 35 DEA education benefits, and full post-2023 SBP payments?

Probative private IME, DBQ, or lay statement uploaded to VBMS in an AMA 'in-between' dead zone (between AOJ decision and VA Form 10182 NOD, or after NOD before a Board hearing) (Cook v. McDonough; Cash v. Collins)

Board decision issued prematurely BEFORE expiration of the § 20.202(c)(2) docket-modification window (later of 1 year from AOJ decision or 60 days from NOD receipt) without a claimant waiver (Williams v. McDonough)
Post-remand Rating Decision, SSOC, or Board decision repeating the identical defective medical opinion or skipping an ordered specialist examination (Stegall v. West violation)
Legacy appeal marked 'Withdrawn' or 'Closed' in VACOLS between Dec. 12, 1990 and Feb. 6, 2025 despite a timely NOD/VA Form 9 prior to an SSOC or partial grant (Freund v. Collins class restoration)
killSwitches: Filing a VA Form 20-0996 Higher-Level Review against a prior Higher-Level Review decision or against a Board of Veterans' Appeals decision (jurisdictionally barred by 38 U.S.C. § 5104B(b)(2) and 38 C.F.R. § 3.2601(b))
Uploading new medical evidence to VBMS during a Direct Review Board appeal (§ 20.301), during an HLR (§ 3.2601(f)), or AFTER the 90-day Evidence/Hearing window closes expecting the VLJ to read it

Attempting to switch AMA Board dockets under § 20.202(c)(2) AFTER the later of 1 year from the AOJ decision or 60 days from NOD receipt, OR after already submitting evidence or hearing testimony (Brack v. Collins)
Failing to file a protective § 5108 Supplemental Claim (or § 3.155(b) ITF) within 1 year of an adverse CAVC judgment while appealing to the Federal Circuit (38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)(2)(E); MVA v. Sec'y)
Irrevocably opting a multi-decade remanded Legacy Part 19 appeal into AMA when ongoing open-record § 5103A development is still needed (§ 3.2400(c))

blocks.text: Effective **February 19, 2019**, the **Veterans Appeals Improvement and Modernization Act of 2017 (`AMA`, `Pub. L. 115-55`, `131 Stat. 1105`; `84 FR 138`, published Jan. 18, 2019)** replaced VA's single-track Legacy open-record system (`NOD -> SOC -> VA Form 9`) with a modular **three-lane architecture** coupled with **rigid, non-discretionary Board evidentiary windows (`38 U.S.C. § 7113`; `38 C.F.R. §§ 20.300–20.303`)**. Selecting the wrong AMA lane—or uploading a `$4,000` private medical nexus opinion during an `"in-between"` Board dead zone without invoking *Cash v. Collins*—routinely costs veterans years of delay or forfeits multi-year retroactive effective dates.

blocks.text: 1. Tactical Three-Lane Architecture (38 U.S.C. §§ 5104C, 5104B, 5108, 7105; 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.2500–3.2601)

Within **`1 year`** of the mailing of an initial or supplemental AOJ decision (`38 U.S.C. § 5104C(a)(1)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.2500(c)`), a claimant may maintain **continuous pursuit (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)(2)`)** by electing one of three mutually exclusive review lanes *per issue*. Under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.2500(d)`**, **issue-splitting across lanes is expressly permitted**: if a single Rating Decision grants PTSD at an underrated `30%` (where the existing `DBQ` already shows `70%` criteria) while denying sleep apnea for lack of nexus (requiring a new private `IME`), counsel can simultaneously file **`VA Form 20-0996` (`HLR`)** on the PTSD rating and **`VA Form 20-0995` (`Supplemental Claim`)** with the new `IME` on sleep apnea!

rows: **`VA Form 20-0996`** (`1 year` from AOJ decision; **barred** after HLR or BVA)
**`VA Form 20-0995`** (`1 year` from AOJ, BVA, or **CAVC** decision for continuity; anytime `>1 yr` under `§ 5110(a)(3)`)
**Strictly Closed** as of prior AOJ decision (`§ 3.2601(f)`).
**Open:** Requires presenting or identifying **"new and relevant"** evidence (`§ 3.2501(a)`).
**Full `§ 5103A` Duty** (including fetching identified records per `§ 3.2501(b)` + ordering exams).
**None proactively**—*except* mandatory **`§ 20.802(a)` remand** for pre-AOJ DTA error!
`(1)` Clear rater legal/VASRD math error on existing `DBQ`; `(2)` **Fast `90–150 day` DTA conversion** via informal conference!
`(1)` Submitting a new private `IME`/`DBQ`/buddy statement; `(2)` Protective post-BVA or post-CAVC filing (`§ 5110(a)(2)(D)–(E)`).
`(1)` Complex credibility/*Nieves-Rodriguez* weighing; `(2)` Setting up CAVC judicial review (`§ 7252`) & EAJA fees.

blocks.text: A. Lane 1 Deep Dive: Higher-Level Review (VA Form 20-0996; 38 C.F.R. § 3.2601)

items: ***De Novo* Adjudication & Closed-Record Discipline (`§ 3.2601(d)–(f)`):** Conducted *de novo* by an experienced Decision Review Officer (`DRO`) / Higher-Level Adjudicator who did not participate in the prior decision (`§ 3.2601(e)`). While the reviewer owes zero deference to the prior rater's adverse conclusions, **`38 U.S.C. § 5104A` (`§ 3.104(c)`) favorable findings bind the DRO** unless rebutted by clear and unmistakable evidence.

**Mastering the Informal Conference (`38 C.F.R. § 3.2601(h)`):**
• Counsel may request **one** optional telephonic informal conference (`§ 3.2601(h)`) for the sole purpose of pointing out **errors of fact or law** in the prior decision.
• **Operational Rule:** Never attempt to read new post-decision medical findings or unsubmitted lay facts into the phone call—the DRO is barred by `§ 3.2601(f)` from considering them. Instead, prepare a 1-page citation script referencing **exact VBMS document dates and PDF page numbers** already in the eFolder before the appealed rating decision.

**The "DTA Conversion" Gambit (`38 C.F.R. § 3.2601(g)`):**
• Waiting `2–4 years` at the Board merely to get a *McLendon* exam remand or *Barr* exam-adequacy remand is rarely optimal when an HLR can achieve the **exact same remand in `3–5 months`**!
• Under **`§ 3.2601(g)`**, if the DRO discovers during HLR (often prompted by counsel at the `§ 3.2601(h)` conference) that VA committed a **pre-decisional `§ 5103A` duty-to-assist error** prior to the appealed decision and cannot grant the maximum benefit outright, the DRO **must return the claim for corrective development**.
• **Crucial Effect:** Once the HLR issues a `"Duty to Assist Error"` return, **the closed record REOPENS** as an expedited Supplemental development stream—allowing counsel to immediately upload a private nexus opinion, `DBQ`, or `VA Form 21-8940` (`TDIU`) into VBMS before the new rating decision issues!

**Jurisdictional Kill-Switches (`38 C.F.R. § 3.2601(b)`):**
• **No HLR-of-an-HLR:** You **cannot** request an HLR of a decision issued on a prior HLR (`38 U.S.C. § 5104B(b)(2)`). *(Nuance: If an HLR triggers a `§ 3.2601(g)` DTA return and the AOJ subsequently issues a **new supplemental rating decision** after development, that new AOJ decision IS once again eligible for HLR!)*
• **No HLR-of-a-Board Decision & No Contested Claims:** HLR is strictly unavailable to review a BVA decision or simultaneously contested claims (`§ 3.2601(b)`).

blocks.text: B. Lane 2 Deep Dive: Supplemental Claims (VA Form 20-0995; 38 U.S.C. § 5108; 38 C.F.R. § 3.2501)

items:
**`"New and Relevant"` vs. Legacy `"New and Material"` (`§ 3.2501(a)(1)` vs. `Former § 3.156(a)`):**
• Congress deliberately **lowered** the readjudication gate in `38 U.S.C. § 5108(a)` (`38 C.F.R. §§ 3.156(d), 3.2501(a)(1)`):
• **Legacy `"New and Material"` (`former § 3.156(a)`):** Required evidence not previously of record that related to an **unestablished fact** necessary to substantiate the claim **AND raised a reasonable possibility of substantiating the claim**.
• **AMA `"New and Relevant"` (`§ 3.2501(a)(1)`):** **`"New"`** means evidence not previously part of the **actual record** before agency adjudicators (meaning VAMC clinical notes that existed in VistA/CAPRI but were never pulled into the actual VBMS eFolder qualify as `"new"`!). **`"Relevant"`** means **"information that tends to prove or disprove a matter at issue in a claim, including evidence that raises a theory of entitlement not previously addressed"** (aligning with ***Kisor v. Wilkie*, `969 F.3d 1333, 1337–40 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`** that `"relevant"` speaks to a disputed issue without demanding outcome-changing weight!).

**VA's Affirmative `§ 5103A` Duty to Gather `"New and Relevant"` Evidence (`38 C.F.R. § 3.2501` introductory text & `(b)`):**
• A veteran need **not** attach physical copies of medical records to `VA Form 20-0995`. Under `§ 3.2501` (introductory text & `(b)`), if the claimant adequately identifies relevant federal (`VAMC`, `SSA`, `STR`/`JSRRC`) or private records (with `VA Form 21-4142`), **VA must exercise its `§ 5103A` duty to assist (`§ 3.159`) to obtain those records** before deciding whether new and relevant evidence has been presented or secured!

**Post-BVA & Post-CAVC Continuous Pursuit (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)(2)(D)–(E)` & *MVA v. Sec'y*):**
• Unlike Legacy law (where filing a reopening at the RO after a BVA or CAVC denial forfeited the original effective date), **`38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)(2)(D)`** (`within 1 year of a BVA decision`) and **`§ 5110(a)(2)(E)`** (`within 1 year of a CAVC decision`) preserve the **initial claim's effective date** via a `20-0995` Supplemental Claim!
• Under ***Military-Veterans Advocacy v. Sec'y of Veterans Affairs*, `7 F.4th 1110, 1134, 1142 (Fed. Cir. 2021)`**:
• The Federal Circuit **invalidated `38 C.F.R. § 3.2500(b)`**, allowing claimants appealing an adverse CAVC judgment to the Federal Circuit to **simultaneously file a protective `§ 5108` Supplemental Claim within `1 year` of the CAVC decision** (essential because `§ 5110(a)(2)` has no post-Federal-Circuit clause!); and
• The Federal Circuit **invalidated `§ 3.155`'s Supplemental Claim exclusion**, restoring **`VA Form 21-0966` Intent-to-File (`ITF`)** placeholders to Supplemental Claims ([`Master Effective-Date Treatise`](/docs/effective-dates-and-staged-ratings-treatise)).

blocks.text: C. Lane 3 Deep Dive: Board Dockets, 90-Day Evidentiary Windows, *Cash v. Collins* & Docket Switching (38 U.S.C. § 7113; 38 C.F.R. §§ 20.202, 20.300–20.303)
Filing **`VA Form 10182` (`Notice of Disagreement`)** within `1 year` of the AOJ decision requires selecting one of three statutory Board dockets under **`38 U.S.C. § 7113`**:

items:
**Direct Review Docket (`38 U.S.C. § 7113(a)`; `38 C.F.R. § 20.301`):**
• **Evidentiary Scope:** Strictly limited to the evidence of record **at the time of the AOJ decision on appeal** (`§ 20.301`). Written legal argument pointing to record errors is permitted, but new factual/medical evidence is barred.
• **Best Use:** Fastest Board lane when the record at the time of the rating decision already contains a winning private `IME`, an unaddressed `§ 5104(b)` *Hamill* pending claim, mathematical VASRD/`SMC` error, or a glaring *Nieves-Rodriguez*/*Barr* pre-decisional exam defect (`§ 20.802(a)`).

**Evidence Submission Docket (`38 U.S.C. § 7113(c)`; `38 C.F.R. § 20.303`):**
• **Evidentiary Scope:** AOJ record **plus** evidence and argument submitted by the appellant or representative **with the `VA Form 10182` NOD OR within `90 days` following the Board's receipt of the NOD** (`§ 20.303(b)(1)`). No hearing is held, and VA has no `§ 5103A` duty to develop new evidence submitted in that `90-day` window—instead, the VLJ weighs it **in the first instance** (`§§ 20.300(a), 20.801`).
• **Trap 1 — The AOJ-to-NOD `"In-Between"` Gap (*Cook* vs. *Cash*):**
• In ***Cook v. McDonough*, `36 Vet. App. 175, 180–85 (2023)`**, the CAVC held that `38 U.S.C. § 7113(c)` enforces a hard closed-record rule: evidence uploaded to VBMS *after* the AOJ decision but *before* the `VA Form 10182` NOD is filed does **not** automatically roll into the Board's record, though if the Board excludes out-of-window evidence it must give accurate notice (`38 C.F.R. § 20.205(c)`) explaining the exclusion and the right to file a `§ 5108` Supplemental Claim.
• **LANDMARK RESCUE — *Cash v. Collins*, `No. 24-1811 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 5, 2026)`:** Reversing VA's hyper-technical refusal to read gap-period submissions referenced on the NOD, the Federal Circuit held under **`38 U.S.C. § 7113(c)(2)(A)`** (`"evidence submitted... with the notice of disagreement"`) that **when a `VA Form 10182` NOD (or accompanying brief) clearly identifies or incorporates by reference probative evidence submitted during an AMA `"in-between"` window that is already in VA's possession (`VBMS`), the Board MUST consider that evidence without requiring physical resubmission!** *(Firm Protocol: Always attach an addendum to every `10182` explicitly listing and incorporating by date/document ID all post-AOJ submissions in `VBMS` under Cash v. Collins AND re-uploading clean copies inside the `90-day` window as belt-and-suspenders!)*

**Hearing Docket (`38 U.S.C. § 7113(b)`; `38 C.F.R. § 20.302`):**
• **Evidentiary Scope:** AOJ record **plus** testimony presented at the Board hearing **plus** evidence submitted **at the Board hearing or within `90 days` following the Board hearing** (`§ 20.302(a)`). *(If the appellant withdraws the hearing request or fails to appear without good cause, the `90-day` evidence window runs from the date the withdrawal is received or the date of the scheduled hearing per `§ 20.302(b)–(c)`).*
• **Trap 2 — The Post-NOD / Pre-Hearing Dead Zone & VLJ Hearing Notice Duty (*Cook* / `§ 20.705`):** Because Board Hearing appeals frequently wait `2–4 years` for a hearing date, unrepresented veterans and prior VSOs routinely upload medical records *after* filing the `10182` NOD *before* the hearing—a period **excluded** by `§ 7113(b)(2)`! Under ***Cook v. McDonough*, `36 Vet. App. 175 (2023)`** and the VLJ's hearing duties (`38 C.F.R. § 20.705`; cf. *Bryant v. Shinseki*, `23 Vet. App. 488 (2010)`), when pre-hearing submissions sit in VBMS outside the window, the VLJ/Board has an obligation at the hearing (and in accurate notice) to alert the claimant that pre-hearing evidence fell outside the statutory window so the claimant can **formally resubmit it during the hearing or within the `90-day` post-hearing window**! *(Hearing Script: At every AMA Board hearing, formally move on the record to re-submit and incorporate all post-AOJ VBMS documents and immediately upload a consolidated evidentiary packet within `90 days` post-hearing!)*

**Docket Switching (`38 C.F.R. § 20.202(c)(2)`) — *Williams*, *Brack* & *Cardoza*:**
• Under **`38 C.F.R. § 20.202(c)(2)`**, an appellant may modify a `VA Form 10182` to switch Board dockets (by filing a new `VA Form 10182` checking the new docket) until the **LATER** of:
• **`1 year`** from the date the AOJ mailed notice of the decision on appeal; **OR**
• **`60 days`** after the Board receives the initial `VA Form 10182` NOD—

blocks.text: ***PROVIDED*** the appellant has **not yet submitted evidence (`§ 20.303`) or testified at a hearing (`§ 20.302`)** under the original election!

items:
***Williams v. McDonough*, `37 Vet. App. 305, 310–11 (2024)` (Premature Board Decisions Barred):** Because `§ 20.202(c)(2)` confers an affirmative right to switch dockets throughout that `1-year` / `60-day` window, **the Board is prohibited from issuing a final decision BEFORE the `§ 20.202(c)(2)` window expires** unless the appellant expressly waives the remaining modification time!
• ***Brack v. McDonough*, `37 Vet. App. 172 (2024)`, *aff'd sub nom. Brack v. Collins*, `No. 25-1205 (Fed. Cir. Sept. 8, 2026)` (Strict Post-Window Cut-Off):** Conversely, once the `§ 20.202(c)(2)` deadline has expired, docket-switch requests are strictly time-barred—and on the Direct Review docket, the "fair process" doctrine does **not** obligate the Board to delay issuing its decision for `90 days` after VA fulfills a Privacy Act C-file request.
• ***Cardoza v. McDonough*, `37 Vet. App. 407 (2024)`:** If the Board sends an administrative letter refusing to docket or accept a `VA Form 10182` NOD (or dismissing a docket request as untimely), that refusal letter constitutes a **final, appealable Board decision** within CAVC jurisdiction (`120-day` NOA clock!).

blocks.text: 2. Board Adjudication Standards, AOD & *Stegall* Remand Compliance
A. Statutory Architecture of a Board Decision (38 U.S.C. §§ 5104A, 7104)

items: **`§ 7104(a)` (`One Review on Appeal` & Sympathetic Scope):** Decisions of the Board are based on the entire record in the proceeding (bounded by `§ 7113` in AMA appeals) and upon consideration of all applicable provisions of law and regulation, including all **reasonably raised theories of entitlement** (*Roberson v. Principi*, `251 F.3d 1378 (Fed. Cir. 2001)`).

**`§ 7104(c)` (Binding Authorities vs. `M21-1`):** The Board is bound by statutes, VA regulations, and precedent opinions of the VA General Counsel (`VAOPGCPREC`, [`Master VAOPGCPREC Digest`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index)). Under **`38 C.F.R. § 20.105`**, the `M21-1` Adjudication Procedures Manual does **not** bind the Board—**HOWEVER**, under ***Overton v. Wilkie*, `30 Vet. App. 257, 263–65 (2018)`**, if a claimant relies on a relevant substantive `M21-1` provision (such as an exposure concession or stressor rule), the Board **must** address that `M21-1` provision and explain its reasons for following or departing from it!

**`§ 7104(d)(1)` (`Reasons or Bases` — *Gilbert* & *Caluza*):** Every Board decision must include a written statement of the Board's findings and conclusions, and the **reasons or bases** for those findings and conclusions, on all material issues of fact and law presented on the record—analyzing the credibility and probative value of all material favorable evidence and explaining why any rejected favorable evidence was discounted (*Gilbert v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 49, 56–57 (1990)`; *Caluza v. Brown*, `7 Vet. App. 498, 506 (1995)`).

**`§ 5104A` & `§ 20.801(a)` (Binding Favorable Findings):** Any finding favorable to the claimant recorded by the AOJ (`in-service event`, `TERA participation`, `current diagnosis`, `combat service`) binds the Board unless rebutted by **clear and unmistakable evidence**!

**First-Instance Evidence Consideration (*Bernard* Legacy Waiver vs. AMA `§§ 20.300(a), 20.801`):**
• **Legacy Appeals (`Part 19` / `§ 20.1304`):** Under ***Bernard v. Brown*, `4 Vet. App. 384, 393–94 (1993)`**, the Board **cannot** adjudicate pertinent new evidence in the first instance unless `(a)` the AOJ already reviewed it in an `SOC`/`SSOC`, `(b)` the claimant **affirmatively waives initial AOJ consideration in writing**, OR `(c)` the Board grants the full benefit sought.
• **AMA Appeals (`§§ 20.300(a), 20.801`):** Congress eliminated the `SSOC` ping-pong in AMA—the Board is statutorily authorized to evaluate timely `90-day` Evidence/Hearing submissions in the first instance without a *Bernard* waiver!

blocks.text: B. Advancement on the Docket (AOD, 38 U.S.C. § 7107(b); 38 C.F.R. § 20.800(c))

Because non-expedited AMA Evidence Submission and Hearing appeals routinely sit `2–4+ years` in the Board queue, screen **every** Board client at intake for mandatory **Advancement on the Docket (`AOD`)** under `38 U.S.C. § 7107(b)` and `38 C.F.R. § 20.800(c)` (`Legacy § 20.900(c)`):

items: **Age `75+` (`§ 20.800(c)(1)`):** Automatic upon age `75` (though always file a `1-page` written `AOD` notice flagging the veteran's `DOB` when a client turns `75` mid-appeal so Board docketing clerks update the queue flag!).

**Serious Illness (`§ 20.800(c)(1)`):** Active cancer, severe cardiopulmonary/renal failure, `ALS`, terminal illness, suicidal ideation / inpatient psychiatric crisis, or advanced neurodegenerative decline (attach `1–3` corroborating clinical pages).
**Severe Financial Hardship (`§ 20.800(c)(1)`):** Foreclosure/eviction notice, utility shutoff, homelessness/HUD-VASH enrollment, Chapter 7/13 bankruptcy, or repossession.

**Other Sufficient Cause (`§ 20.800(c)(1)`):** Administrative error by VA that caused substantial prior delay (e.g., *Freund* unlawful `VACOLS` closure or lost remand) or federal disaster declaration affecting the veteran's residence.

blocks.text: C. Enforcing Remand Directives (*Stegall v. West* & *D'Aries v. Peake*)

lines: ***Stegall v. West*, `11 Vet. App. 268, 271 (1998)` — Remand Orders Are Law, Not Suggestions:**

* **Core Rule:** *"A remand by this Court or the Board confers on the veteran or other claimant, **as a matter of law, the right to compliance with the remand orders**... and imposes upon the Secretary a concomitant duty to ensure compliance with the terms of the remand."*

* **Substantial Compliance Standard (*D'Aries v. Peake*, `22 Vet. App. 97, 105 (2008)`):** While VA need only demonstrate **substantial** (not rigid literal) compliance, any failure to execute the core substantive instruction of a prior Board or CAVC remand—such as `(1)` ordering an NP/PA exam when the remand specified a board-certified neurologist/orthopedist, `(2)` failing to obtain records identified in the remand, or `(3)` accepting an addendum opinion that **repeats the exact factual error or skips the exact etiological question** identified in the remand—is an automatic *Stegall* violation requiring vacatur!

* **Audit Step:** Whenever a case returns from an HLR `§ 3.2601(g)` DTA return, a Board `§ 20.802` remand, or a CAVC `JMPR`, **place the prior remand order side-by-side with the new C&P addendum line by line** before choosing the next review lane!

blocks.text: 3. Surviving Legacy Part 19 Appeals & *Freund v. Collins* (2026) Class Restoration
A. Legacy Part 19 Mechanics for Pre-Feb. 19, 2019 Appeals (38 C.F.R. §§ 3.2400(b), 19.20–19.52)

Under `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.2400(b) and 19.2`, any appeal stemming from an initial AOJ rating decision issued **prior to February 19, 2019** (that was never opted into AMA via `RAMP` or a post-Feb. 19, 2019 `SOC`/`SSOC` election under `§ 3.2400(c)`)—including multi-cycle Board and CAVC remands of pre-2019 claims—remains governed by **Legacy `38 C.F.R. Part 19`**:

items: **Notice of Disagreement (`NOD`):** Written communication expressing dissatisfaction and desire for appellate review filed within **`1 year`** of mailing of the AOJ rating notice (`VA Form 21-0958` became mandatory for Legacy compensation NODs eff. **March 24, 2015**, `79 FR 57660`).

**Statement of the Case (`SOC`, `Pub. L. 87-666`, eff. Jan. 1, 1963):** Mandatory VA summary of evidence, laws, and reasons. **Goldmine:** If a claimant filed a timely post-1962 Legacy `NOD` and VA **never issued an `SOC`**, the Legacy appeal **never became final and remains legally pending today**!

**Substantive Appeal (`VA Form 9`, `38 U.S.C. § 7105(d)(3)` `[pre-AMA]`; `38 C.F.R. § 19.52(b)`):** Must be filed within **`60 days` from the date the `SOC` is mailed OR within the remainder of the `1-year` period from the date of mailing of the original AOJ decision notice, whichever period ends LATER**.

**Supplemental Statement of the Case (`SSOC`, `38 C.F.R. § 19.31, 19.38`) & Open Continuous Record:** Whenever new evidence arrives in a perfected Legacy appeal prior to Board decision (without a *Bernard* waiver), the AOJ must readjudicate via an `SSOC` with a `30-day` response window—**no second `VA Form 9` is ever required after a timely initial `VA Form 9`!** Moreover, the `§ 5103A` duty to assist and open evidentiary record remain active throughout Legacy Board pendency (`38 C.F.R. § 20.1304` `90-day` post-certification window).

**Opt-In Caution (`38 C.F.R. § 3.2400(c)`):** Electing to opt a Legacy appeal into AMA within `60 days` of receiving an `SOC` or `SSOC` is **irrevocable**—do **not** opt a complex Legacy remand out of `Part 19`'s open continuous record unless an immediate closed-record grant is certain!

blocks.text: B. *Freund v. Collins*, No. 21-4168 (Vet. App. Class Certified Mar. 2026) — Auditing Unlawfully Closed VACOLS Appeals

In ***Freund v. Collins*, `No. 21-4168 (Vet. App. class certified Mar. 2026)`**, the CAVC certified a sweeping `Rule 23` class action covering **`~28,000+` Legacy appeals** improperly closed in VA's Veterans Appeals Control and Locator System (`VACOLS`) between **December 12, 1990 and February 6, 2025**:

items: **The Systemic Agency Error:** Automated `VACOLS` scripts and RO clerks routinely closed timely Legacy appeals as `"Withdrawn"` or `"Failed to File Substantive Appeal"` when `(1)` VA issued a post-`NOD` partial grant or `SSOC` and expected a redundant `Form 9`, `(2)` a claimant filed a timely `Form 9` inside the remainder of the `1-year` rating-notice window rather than `60 days` post-`SOC`, or `(3)` an `SOC` was returned undeliverable or never mailed to counsel ([`Procedural Vehicles`](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality)).

**C-File Intake Protocol:** In **every** C-file containing a `1990–2019` Legacy `NOD`, pull the **`VACOLS` printouts / Caseflow appeal history** alongside every `SOC`, `SSOC`, and `VA Form 9`. Whenever `VACOLS` shows an administrative closure without an explicit written withdrawal by the veteran (`38 C.F.R. § 20.205` `[Legacy § 20.204]`) or a final BVA merits decision, demand **immediate reinstatement of the pending Legacy appeal** with full retroactive continuity back to the original claim!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Choosing Your VA Review Lane: Supplemental Claim, Higher-Level Review & the Three Board Dockets
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Since February 19, 2019, whenever VA issues an initial decision you disagree with, the Appeals Modernization Act (AMA) gives you 1 year to preserve your effective date by choosing one of three paths: (1) a Supplemental Claim (VA Form 20-0995) when you have or want VA to gather 'new and relevant' evidence, (2) a Higher-Level Review (VA Form 20-0996) when a senior reviewer can spot a legal mistake or pre-decision Duty-to-Assist error on the existing closed record (with an optional informal phone conference), or (3) a Board of Veterans' Appeals Notice of Disagreement (VA Form 10182) on one of three dockets—Direct Review (fastest, closed record), Evidence Submission (90-day post-NOD evidence window), or Hearing (testimony before a Veterans Law Judge plus a 90-day post-hearing evidence window).
record_clues: An AMA Rating Decision that skipped a required VA nexus exam, relied on a flawed C&P opinion, or failed to request identified VA or Social Security medical records—often a strong fit for a Higher-Level Review informal conference or Supplemental Claim.

A private medical nexus letter (IME/DBQ) or buddy statement uploaded to VA's system in an AMA 'dead zone'—such as between the Regional Office decision and filing VA Form 10182, or after filing VA Form 10182 on the Hearing docket BEFORE the hearing date (Cook v. McDonough; Cash v. Collins).
A post-remand VA decision that repeated the exact same defective medical opinion or ignored a Board/Higher-Level Review remand instruction (violating Stegall v. West).

An older Legacy appeal marked 'Withdrawn' or 'Closed' in VA's tracking system between December 12, 1990 and February 6, 2025 after a partial grant or Supplemental Statement of the Case despite a timely appeal (Freund v. Collins class).
important_cautions: Barred lane combinations: you can NEVER file a Higher-Level Review against a prior Higher-Level Review decision or against a Board of Veterans' Appeals decision (38 U.S.C. § 5104B(b)(2); 38 C.F.R. § 3.2601(b)).

Strict Board evidence windows: uploading new medical evidence during a Higher-Level Review, during a Board Direct Review appeal, or AFTER the 90-day Evidence/Hearing window closes means the reviewer or Veterans Law Judge cannot consider it in that decision (though you can file a Supplemental Claim within 1 year after a Board denial to have it considered).

Board docket-switching deadline: under 38 C.F.R. § 20.202(c)(2) and Brack v. Collins (2026), you can switch Board dockets only before the later of 1 year from the Regional Office decision notice or 60 days after the Board receives VA Form 10182—and only BEFORE submitting evidence or hearing testimony.

Post-CAVC 1-year protection: if you lose at the Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims (CAVC)—even while appealing further to the Federal Circuit—you must file a protective Supplemental Claim (or Intent to File) within 1 year of the CAVC judgment to preserve continuous pursuit of your effective date (38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)(2)(E)).
questions_for_representative: Based on what is already in my VA Claims File, should we point out a Duty-to-Assist or legal error in a Higher-Level Review, submit a new private nexus opinion in a Supplemental Claim, or appeal to the Board?
If we appeal to the Board on VA Form 10182, which docket (Direct Review, Evidence Submission, or Hearing) prevents my medical evidence from falling into an unreadable 'dead zone'?
If I still have a long-running Legacy appeal (from a pre-February 19, 2019 decision), why might staying in Legacy's open-record system be safer than irrevocably opting into AMA?
Did VA comply substantially with every instruction in my prior Board remand or Higher-Level Review Duty-to-Assist return (Stegall v. West)?

cFileTriggers: Executed VA Form 21-22a Appointment of Individual as Claimant's Representative and § 5904 direct-pay or non-direct-pay fee agreement

Supplemental Claim (VA Form 20-0995) or CUE motion (§§ 5109A / 7111) where VA RO staff erroneously deny attorney fees based on the invalidated >1-year rule of 38 C.F.R. § 14.636(c)(1)(i) (MVA v. Sec'y)

Post-remand VA past-due award on a claim where counsel previously collected CAVC EAJA fees, triggering the mandatory Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c) lesser-fee client refund
killSwitches: Contracting for or charging a fee before VA OGC accreditation (§ 14.629) or before an initial AOJ decision has issued on the claim under 38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(1) (illegal 'claim shark' / premature fee violation under §§ 5901, 5905)

Taking the initial 3-hour Veterans Law CLE BEFORE the date of initial VA OGC accreditation rather than during the first 12 months FOLLOWING initial accreditation (rejected by OGC under 38 C.F.R. § 14.629(b)(1)(iii)!)

Missing the strict 30-day fee-agreement filing deadline or filing in the wrong VA office under 38 C.F.R. § 14.636(g)(3) (direct-pay goes to AOJ/VBA Centralized Intake; non-direct-pay goes to OGC 022D — forfeits VA direct-pay withholding under Ravin v. Wilkie, 956 F.3d 1346 (Fed. Cir. 2020))

Waiting 90 days (60 + 30) to file a CAVC EAJA application after a consent JMPR order that issued an immediate mandate under CAVC Rule 41(b) (fatal expiration of the 30-day statutory EAJA clock on Day 31!)

Accepting a CAVC remand predicated solely on a supervening change in law (Vaughn) or an argument raised for the first time at the CAVC (Robinson v. O'Rourke, 891 F.3d 976 (Fed. Cir. 2018)) without an administrative-error predicate (destroys EAJA prevailing-party status under Sumner!)

Retaining both an EAJA fee (28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)) and a § 5904 contingency fee covering the same representation work without refunding the smaller fee dollar-for-dollar to the claimant (violates Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c) and Carpenter v. Principi, 15 Vet. App. 64 (2001) (en banc))

blocks.text: Ethical, compliant revenue architecture allows a Veterans Law firm to litigate multi-decade retroactive claims and appellate precedents sustainably while maximizing the veteran's or survivor's net recovery. Unlike general civil contingency practice, Veterans Law representation is governed by a **dual federal statutory regime**: **`38 U.S.C. §§ 5901–5905`** and **`38 C.F.R. Part 14`** regulate agency accreditation, power of attorney (`POA`), and past-due contingency/non-direct-pay fees, while the **Equal Access to Justice Act (`EAJA`, `28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)`)** shifts hourly litigation fees onto the federal government at the U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims (`CAVC`) and Federal Circuit—linked together by the mandatory **`Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c)` `"same work"` lesser-fee client refund rule**.
