blocks.text: 1. Accreditation, Power of Attorney (VA Form 21-22a) & Prohibition on Unaccredited "Claim Sharks"

*(Statutory Crosswalk Note: Enacted in `Pub. L. 85-857` (`1958`) as **`former 38 U.S.C. §§ 3401, 3404, and 3405`**, these provisions were renumbered **`38 U.S.C. §§ 5901, 5904, and 5905`** on **May 7, 1991** by `Pub. L. 102-40, § 402(b)(1)`, `105 Stat. 187, 238`; see [Title 38 Statutory Crosswalk](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk)).*
A. Prohibition on Unaccredited Representation (38 U.S.C. §§ 5901, 5905)

Under **`38 U.S.C. § 5901`**, **no individual may act as an agent or attorney in the preparation, presentation, or prosecution of any claim under laws administered by the Secretary unless formally recognized (`accredited`) by VA**.

items: **The Unaccredited `"Claim Shark"` Bar:** Unaccredited for-profit "consulting," "DBQ mill," or "claim coaching" companies are **categorically barred** by `§§ 5901` and `5904(c)(1)` from preparing or prosecuting VA benefit claims or charging fees on initial claims—even if disguised as "medical consulting" or deferred subscription contracts. Under **`38 U.S.C. § 5905`**, whoever wrongfully withholds from any claimant or beneficiary any part of a benefit or claim allowed and due is subject to criminal misdemeanor penalties, and accredited practitioners are barred under **`38 C.F.R. § 14.632`** (Standards of Conduct) from splitting fees with or assisting unlawful unaccredited claim-preparation schemes.

blocks.text: B. OGC Accreditation & Mandatory Post-Accreditation CLE Windows (38 U.S.C. § 5904(a); 38 C.F.R. § 14.629(b))

Attorneys (members in good standing of a State bar, `VA Form 21a`) and claims agents (who additionally pass OGC's written Veterans Law examination and background check) must obtain formal accreditation from the **VA Office of the General Counsel (`OGC`)** *before* representing a claimant on a VA benefit claim (`38 C.F.R. § 14.629(b)(1)`). To maintain accreditation under **`38 C.F.R. § 14.629(b)(1)(iii)–(iv)`** (`73 FR 29852`, pub. May 22, 2008, **eff. June 23, 2008**):

items:
**Initial `3-Hour` CLE Window (`§ 14.629(b)(1)(iii)` — Critical Timing Trap!):** Both newly accredited attorneys and claims agents must complete at least **`3 hours` of State-bar-approved qualifying CLE** covering core Veterans Law topics (representation before VA, claims procedures, basic eligibility, right to appeal, `Ch. 11` disability compensation, `Ch. 13` DIC, and `Ch. 15` pension) **during the first `12-month` period *following* the date of initial accreditation by VA**.
• **Practitioner Kill-Switch:** Because `§ 14.629(b)(1)(iii)` expressly mandates completion *"during the first 12-month period **following** the date of initial accreditation,"* **OGC rejects CLE courses taken *prior* to the date on the OGC accreditation letter!** Never rely on a pre-accreditation CLE course to satisfy Year 1 VA compliance; take the `3-hour` qualifying course *after* OGC issues initial accreditation and submit written certification (title, date, time, provider) to OGC with the annual `§ 14.629(b)(4)` good-standing certification.

**Biennial Ongoing `3-Hour` CLE (`§ 14.629(b)(1)(iv)`):** An additional **`3 hours`** of State-bar-approved Veterans Law CLE must be completed **not later than `3 years` from the date of initial accreditation, and every `2 years` thereafter**, certified in writing to OGC.

blocks.text: C. Power of Attorney Mechanics (VA Form 21-22a; 38 C.F.R. § 14.631)

items: **Individual Appointment + Firm-Affiliate Authorization (`§ 14.631(a)`):** Unlike VSOs (`VA Form 21-22`), VA accredits **individual** attorneys and agents—not law firms as entities. **`VA Form 21-22a`** (*Appointment of Individual as Claimant's Representative*) must name an individually accredited attorney/agent, signed by both the claimant and the representative, with the firm/associate disclosure block checked so accredited partners, associates, and supervised paralegals (`§ 14.629(c)`) can access VBMS.

**Single-POA Exclusivity & Limited-Claim Carveouts (`§ 14.631(e)–(f)`):** A claimant may hold only **one** unrestricted `POA` across all VA claims at a time; filing a new unrestricted `VA Form 21-22a` automatically **revokes** any prior VSO or attorney `POA` unless the new `21-22a` explicitly restricts representation to a specific claim/issue (`§ 14.631(f)`).

**Automatic Extinguishment at Death (`§ 14.631(g)`):** A veteran's `VA Form 21-22a` and fee contract **terminate by operation of law at the moment of the veteran's death**—counsel must immediately execute a **brand-new `VA Form 21-22a` and a brand-new `§ 5904` fee agreement** signed by the eligible `§ 5121A` / `§ 5121` survivor ([Playbook 09](/playbooks/09-accrued-benefits-substitution-nehmer-estates); [`Survivor Triage Gate`](/checklists/survivor-post-mortem-triage-gate)).

blocks.text: 2. Four-Era Chronology of 38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(1) Fee-Charging Triggers (1862–Present)
Under **`38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(1)`**, charging a fee for VA administrative representation is lawful **only** after the statutory trigger in force for that procedural era has occurred:

rows: **Strict `$10` Statutory Fee Cap** across all VA administrative claims (zero judicial review of benefits decisions).

Upheld against Fifth Amendment Due Process and First Amendment challenges in ***Walters v. National Ass'n of Radiation Survivors*, `473 U.S. 305 (1985)`** based on the informal, non-adversarial design of pre-VJRA VA proceedings.

**First Final BVA Decision + `1-Year` Retention Window:** Fees permitted *only* after the Board first makes a **final decision** in the case, *and only* if counsel is **retained within `1 year`** of that Board decision.

Extremely narrow trigger: if no final BVA decision existed on that specific claim—or if the veteran waited `> 1 year` after the BVA decision to hire counsel—paid administrative representation was barred (save on reopening after a final BVA denial under former `§ 14.636(c)(3)`).

**Legacy Notice of Disagreement (`NOD`) Filed `>= June 20, 2007`:** Fees permitted for services rendered *after* a valid Legacy `NOD` was filed on or after **June 20, 2007** (`38 C.F.R. § 14.636(c)(2)`).

**Continuous `"Case"` Scope (***Cameron v. Shinseki*, `26 Vet. App. 109, 114–17 (2012)`**, *aff'd sub nom. Cameron v. McDonald*, `561 F. App'x 922 (Fed. Cir. 2014) (nonprecedential)`):** Once a qualifying `>= June 20, 2007` NOD was filed on a claim stream (e.g., service connection or evaluation), downstream rating-assigning or reasonably raised `TDIU` (*Rice* / *Roberson*) proceedings that remain part of that **same continuous `"case"`** stay fee-eligible without requiring a brand-new post-grant NOD!
**Notice of Initial AOJ Decision (`38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(1)`):** Fees permitted once the claimant is provided **notice of the AOJ's initial decision** under `§ 5104` with respect to the case.

***Military-Veterans Advocacy v. Sec'y of Veterans Affairs*, `7 F.4th 1110, 1135–41 (Fed. Cir. July 30, 2021)`:** **Invalidated `38 C.F.R. § 14.636(c)(1)(i)`** to the extent VA barred fees on non-continuous Supplemental Claims (`> 1 year` after a prior decision) and CUE motions!

blocks.text: Deep Synthesis: *Military-Veterans Advocacy v. Secretary* (7 F.4th 1110 (Fed. Cir. 2021)) & Immediate Supplemental / CUE Fee Eligibility

In VA's January 2019 AMA final rule (`84 FR 138, 174`), VA promulgated `38 C.F.R. § 14.636(c)(1)(i)`, which allowed fees on a `§ 5108` Supplemental Claim (`VA Form 20-0995`) *only* if continuously pursued within `1 year` of a prior decision—treating Supplemental Claims filed `> 1 year` after a final denial (as well as `§§ 5109A / 7111` CUE motions) as brand-new "initial" claims on which attorneys had to work for free unless VA denied the Supplemental Claim/CUE motion *again*.

items: **The Federal Circuit's Invalidation (`7 F.4th at 1135–41`):** On direct `38 U.S.C. § 502` review, the Federal Circuit **vacated that restriction**, holding it violated the unambiguous text of amended **`38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(1)`**. Under the AMA statute, Congress shifted the fee-charging line to notice of `"the agency of original jurisdiction's initial decision under section 5104 with respect to the case"`. Because **every** `§ 5108` Supplemental Claim (`VA Form 20-0995`)—whether filed `6 months` or `30 years` after a prior denial—and **every** `§ 3.105(a)` / `§ 7111` CUE motion or `§ 3.156(c)` reconsideration seeks readjudication/revision of an issue on which VA **already issued an initial AOJ decision**, **the statutory `§ 5904(c)(1)` prerequisite is already satisfied at intake!**

**Operational Rule & Bitemporal *George* Gate:**
• **All Open / Current Retainers:** Accredited attorneys and agents may enter into a valid `§ 5904` fee agreement and collect `20%` direct-pay withholding **immediately upon filing any `VA Form 20-0995` Supplemental Claim or `RO`/`BVA` CUE motion** attacking a prior denied or under-rated issue! *(Conversely, a **brand-new original `VA Form 21-526EZ` contention** never previously adjudicated by VA still lacks an initial AOJ decision and remains strictly fee-exempt until VA issues its initial `§ 5104` decision on that contention).*
• **Bitemporal *George* Note (`38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`):** Under ***George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)`**, *MVA v. Sec'y* governs all post-July 30, 2021 fee determinations and timely-appealed/pending fee disputes (`open-claim`), whereas collaterally attacking a *prior final* pre-July 30, 2021 fee-denial decision via CUE faces `§ 20.1403(e)`'s change-in-interpretation bar.

blocks.text: 3. Fee Agreement Architecture, Direct-Pay (<= 20%) vs. Non-Direct-Pay (<= 33 1/3%), Reasonableness & *Scates* Quantum Meruit
A. Mandatory Contract Clauses & The Strict 30-Day Dual-Office Filing Gate (38 C.F.R. § 14.636(g))

Every `§ 5904` fee agreement must be in writing, signed by both the claimant and the accredited attorney/agent, list the claimant's name and VA file number, identify the specific terms of calculation, and comply with **`38 C.F.R. § 14.636(g)(1)–(3)`**:

items:
**Direct-Pay Contingency Agreements (`<= 20%`, `38 U.S.C. § 5904(d)`; `38 C.F.R. § 14.636(g)(2), (h)`):**
• Must be `(i)` **contingent solely on a favorable outcome** (claim resolved in a manner favorable to the claimant), `(ii)` **capped at `<= 20%`** of `"the total amount of any past-due benefits awarded on the basis of the claim"`, and `(iii)` authorize VA to withhold and pay the fee directly out of the cash past-due award.
• **WHERE & WHEN TO FILE (`§ 14.636(g)(3)`):** Direct-pay fee agreements **MUST be filed with the Agency of Original Jurisdiction (`AOJ`)** (via VBA Centralized Mail Intake Center, P.O. Box 4444, Janesville, WI 53547-4444, `VA QuickSubmit`, or direct VBMS upload—**NOT** OGC!) **within `30 days` of execution**!
• **Sovereign Immunity Kill-Switch (***Ravin v. Wilkie*, `956 F.3d 1346, 1350–52 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`**):** Missing `§ 14.636(g)(3)`'s `30-day` filing deadline strictly forfeits VA direct-pay withholding. Moreover, even if counsel timely complied and VA *erroneously* released `100%` of the retroactive award to the veteran without withholding the `20%` hold, *Ravin* holds that **sovereign immunity bars forcing VA to pay a second time out of public funds**—counsel's sole remedy is private collection from the client! *(For exact fee-base rules on incarcerated awards under **Snyder v. Nicholson**, `489 F.3d 1213 (Fed. Cir. 2007)`, debt-invalidation cash limits under **Gumpenberger v. Wilkie**, `973 F.3d 1379 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`, and `DFAS AEW` CRDP holds, see [Playbook 20, Section 6](/playbooks/20-backpay-offsets-crdp-crsc-severance-recoupment)).*

**Non-Direct-Pay Fee Agreements (`> 20%` up to `33 1/3%`, Hourly, Flat, Hybrid, or Disinterested Third-Party Payer; `38 C.F.R. § 14.636(f), (g)(3), (j)`):**
• VA performs **zero** withholding or collection assistance; counsel collects directly from the claimant (or disinterested third-party payer under `§ 14.636(j)`).
• **WHERE & WHEN TO FILE (`§ 14.636(g)(3)`):** Non-direct-pay fee agreements **MUST be filed with the VA Office of the General Counsel (`OGC (022D)`, Department of Veterans Affairs, 810 Vermont Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20420)** **within `30 days` of execution**!

blocks.text: B. Three-Tier Reasonableness Presumptions (38 C.F.R. § 14.636(e)–(f))

Under **`38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(3)(A)`** (and **`38 U.S.C. § 7263(c)–(d)`** for CAVC fee agreements), all fees must be **reasonable** as measured by the eight factors in **`38 C.F.R. § 14.636(e)`** (extent/type of services, complexity, level of skill/competence required, time spent, results achieved including prospective benefits, level of review to which the claim was taken and stage of retention, customary local/veterans-bar rates, and whether the fee is fixed or contingent):

items: **Tier 1 — Presumption of Reasonableness (`<= 20%`, `§ 14.636(f)(1)`):** Any continuous-representation fee that **does not exceed `20%`** of past-due benefits (direct-pay or non-direct-pay) is **presumed reasonable**, rebuttable **only by clear and convincing evidence** that the fee is unreasonable!

**Tier 2 — Neutral Middle Band (`> 20%` up to `33 1/3%`, `§ 14.636(e), (f)(1)`):** Non-direct-pay fees exceeding `20%` up to **`33 1/3%`** carry **NO regulatory presumption either way** (neither presumed reasonable nor presumed unreasonable)—if challenged before `OGC (022D)`, reasonableness is evaluated *de novo* on the eight `§ 14.636(e)` factors without VA withholding assistance.

**Tier 3 — Presumption of Unreasonableness (`> 33 1/3%`, `§ 14.636(f)(1)`):** Any fee that **exceeds `33 1/3%`** of past-due benefits is **presumed unreasonable**, and the **attorney or agent bears the heavy burden of rebutting that presumption by clear and convincing evidence** before OGC!

blocks.text: C. Discharged / Prior Counsel *Quantum Meruit* & Bifurcated Jurisdiction (*Scates v. Principi*, 282 F.3d 1362 (Fed. Cir. 2002))

When a claimant discharges an attorney/agent mid-stream (or retains sequential representatives across a multi-year claim) before the past-due award issues, ***Scates v. Principi*, `282 F.3d 1362, 1365–69 (Fed. Cir. 2002)`** (*aff'g Scates v. Gober*, `14 Vet. App. 64 (2000) (en banc)`) governs both the **substantive fee cap** and **adjudicative forum**:

items: **Substantive *Quantum Meruit* Allocation (`§ 14.636(e)–(f)`):** Implicit in every attorney-client contingency contract is the veteran's unconditional right to discharge counsel at any time without penalty. Once representation terminates prior to the favorable award, **the `<= 20%` presumption of reasonableness no longer applies**, and the discharged attorney is **not** automatically entitled to the full `20%` contingency share. Instead, VA must calculate a reasonable ***quantum meruit*** fee reflecting **the actual value of the discharged attorney's services and causal contribution to the ultimate award** under the `§ 14.636(e)` factors (weighing the work performed post-discharge by the veteran *pro se*, a VSO, or successor counsel!).

**Bifurcated Forum Jurisdiction (`RO/AOJ` Eligibility vs. `OGC (022D)` Reasonableness Review):**
• **Step 1 — `RO/AOJ` Initial Jurisdiction Over Fee *Eligibility* (`Cox v. West`, `149 F.3d 1360 (Fed. Cir. 1998)`; *Scates*, `282 F.3d at 1367–68`; `38 C.F.R. § 14.636(h)`):** Whether a representative met the statutory prerequisites for direct-pay fee *entitlement* (`§ 5904(c)(1)` trigger, valid `30-day` filing, cash past-due base) must be decided **in the first instance by the RO/AOJ**, NOT by OGC or the BVA! Adverse AOJ *eligibility* or past-due math decisions are appealed through AMA review lanes (`HLR` `20-0996` or `Board NOD` `10182` within `1 year`).
• **Step 2 — `60-Day` Allocation Hold & `120-Day` `OGC (022D)` *Reasonableness* Review (`38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(3)`; `38 C.F.R. § 14.636(i)`):** When multiple direct-pay agreements or discharged counsel exist, the AOJ withholds a single global `20%` pool and issues a **Fee Allocation Notice** giving the claimant and all representatives **`60 days`** before VA releases funds, and **`120 days`** from notice of the final past-due amount to file a motion for **fee reasonableness / *quantum meruit* review with `OGC (022D)`** (`73 FR 29852` shifted reasonableness adjudication from BVA to OGC in the first instance, with OGC's final reasonableness decision then appealable to the **BVA**!).

blocks.text: 4. Equal Access to Justice Act (EAJA, 28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)) Practice at the CAVC & Federal Circuit

Under **`28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)(1)(A)`**, a court *shall* award reasonable hourly attorney fees and litigation expenses to a prevailing veteran/survivor in judicial review of VA action (`CAVC` or `Federal Circuit`), **paid by the government out of agency funds (NOT deducted from the veteran's benefits!)**, unless the government proves its position was substantially justified or special circumstances make an award unjust.
A. The "60 + 30 = 90-Day" Window vs. Immediate JMPR Mandates (28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)(1)(B); CAVC Rules 36, 39, 41)

An EAJA application must be filed **within `30 days` of `"final judgment"`**—defined by `28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)(2)(G)` as a judgment that is *"final and not appealable"*. Mastering the **two distinct CAVC finality clocks** prevents fatal malpractice:

items:
**Contested CAVC Single-Judge Memorandum (`nonprecedential, CAVC Rule 30(a)`) or Panel Decision (`60 + 30 = 90 Days`):**
• **Day `0`:** CAVC enters judgment (`CAVC Rule 36`; note that after a single-judge decision, timely filing a `21-day` motion for reconsideration/panel review suspends judgment finality until resolved).
• **Days `1–60`:** Statutory `60-day` window to appeal to the Federal Circuit runs (`38 U.S.C. §§ 7291(a), 7292(a)`). If no appeal is filed, CAVC judgment becomes final and **mandate issues (`CAVC Rule 41(a)`)** after Day `60`.
• **Days `61–90` (`30-Day` EAJA Window):** Counsel has **`30 days` after judgment becomes final (`CAVC Rule 39(a)`)**—i.e., `90 days` total from judgment entry—to file the complete EAJA application! *(At the Federal Circuit, the `90-day` Supreme Court certiorari period yields a `90 + 30 = 120-day` total window unless mandate/finality is accelerated by stipulation).*

**Consent Joint Motion for Remand (`JMR` / `JMPR`) — Immediate `30-Day` Mandate Trap (`CAVC Rule 41(b)` & *Bly*):**
• When the parties file a consent `JMR` or `JMPR` and waive appellate review so the Clerk's order **serves as the immediate mandate of the Court under `CAVC Rule 41(b)`**, the order is `"final and not appealable"` **on the exact day it is entered**!
• **CRITICAL DEADLINE RULE:** There is **NO `60-day` wait** when an order issues an immediate `Rule 41(b)` consent mandate—**the `30-day` EAJA clock expires `30 calendar days` after the JMPR order date!** *(Historical Note: In ***Bly v. Shulkin*, `883 F.3d 1374 (Fed. Cir. 2018)`**, the Federal Circuit held that if a remand order does *not* legally foreclose appealability, the `60-day` window still applies under `§ 2412(d)(2)(G)`; however, modern CAVC `JMPR` practice expressly incorporates `Rule 41(b)` finality/mandate stipulations—**always** file EAJA within **`30 days`** of a `JMPR` order!).*

**Premature Applications & *Scarborough* Relation-Back Curing (*Scarborough v. Principi*, `541 U.S. 401 (2004)`):**
• Under *Scarborough*, `541 U.S. at 413–19`, `§ 2412(d)(1)(B)`'s `30-day` deadline is a mandatory claim-processing rule (not subject-matter jurisdictional): if a timely EAJA application omits the required allegation that the government's position was `"not substantially justified"`, counsel may **cure the defect by relation-back amendment** after the `30-day` window closes.
• Under CAVC practice (`CAVC Rule 39(a)`), if an EAJA application is lodged **prematurely** (after decision/judgment entry, *before* the `60-day` appeal period expires), the Clerk holds it and **treats it as timely filed on the date judgment becomes final**!

blocks.text: B. Four Substantive EAJA Eligibility Elements

items: **Complete Itemized Application (`28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)(1)(B)`; `CAVC Rule 39`):** Contemporaneous tenth-of-an-hour (`0.1 hr`) billing records identifying exact dates, tasks, and timekeepers, excluding clerical overhead or unproductive/duplicative hours (*Hensley v. Eckerhart*, `461 U.S. 424 (1983)`).

**Net Worth `<= $2,000,000` (`28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)(2)(B)`):** Individual appellant's net worth did not exceed **`$2,000,000`** on the date the CAVC Notice of Appeal was filed (satisfied via net-worth declaration or cross-referencing a granted CAVC *in forma pauperis* motion).
• **Treasury Offset Check (***Astrue v. Ratliff*, `560 U.S. 586 (2010)`**):** Because `§ 2412(d)(1)(A)` awards fees to the `"prevailing party"` (the veteran), Treasury's `31 U.S.C. § 3716` Administrative Offset program intercepts EAJA awards if the veteran owes delinquent federal non-tax debt (e.g., defaulted federal student loans or SBA/child-support offsets); execute a written **EAJA Fee Assignment** with the client so VA/Treasury pays counsel directly whenever zero federal offset debt exists!

**`"Prevailing Party"` Status — The Administrative-Error Requirement:**
• **Controlling Rule (***Sumner v. Principi*, `15 Vet. App. 256, 264–65 (2001) (en banc)`**, *aff'd sub nom. Vaughn v. Principi*, `336 F.3d 1351 (Fed. Cir. 2003)`):** A CAVC remand confers `"prevailing party"` status **only** if the remand was **predicated, explicitly or implicitly, upon administrative error**—either conceded by the Secretary in a `JMPR` or found by the Court!
• **Qualifying Error Remands (***Kelly v. Nicholson*, `463 F.3d 1349, 1353–55 (Fed. Cir. 2006)`** & ***Zuberi v. Nicholson*, `19 Vet. App. 541, 546–48 (2006)`**):** Agency error need not prove entitlement on the ultimate disability merits—a remand for `§ 7104(d)(1)` inadequate reasons or bases, ignoring an alternative diagnostic/service-record theory (*Kelly*), or relying on an inadequate VA medical opinion (*Zuberi*) fully establishes prevailing-party status!
• **Disqualifying Non-Error Remands (*Vaughn* & ***Robinson v. O'Rourke*, `891 F.3d 976, 980–83 (Fed. Cir. 2018)`**):** Remands based **solely** on `(a)` an **intervening / supervening change in statute, regulation, or precedent** issued after the BVA decision (*Vaughn*, `336 F.3d at 1355–60`; *Akers v. Nicholson*, `409 F.3d 1356 (Fed. Cir. 2005)`), `(b)` newly discovered post-BVA evidence, OR `(c)` directing the Board under *Maggitt* discretion to consider **an argument or issue raised for the first time at the CAVC** where the Board committed zero error in not addressing it *sua sponte* (*Robinson*, `891 F.3d at 980–83`) **forfeit `100%` of EAJA fees**! **Always anchor every `JMPR` in at least one concrete BVA `§ 7104(d)(1)` or `§ 5103A` administrative error!**

**Absence of `"Substantial Justification"` (`28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)(1)(A)`):**
• Once alleged by the appellant, the **Secretary bears the burden** of proving the government's position had a `"reasonable basis both in law and fact"` (***Pierce v. Underwood*, `487 U.S. 552, 565 (1988)`**) at **BOTH** the administrative (`BVA`) stage **AND** the judicial (`CAVC` OGC litigation) stage under the totality of circumstances (***Patrick v. Shinseki*, `668 F.3d 1325, 1330–33 (Fed. Cir. 2011)`**).

blocks.text: C. CPI-U Rate Escalation, *Mannino* Midpoint Math, *Richlin* Paralegal Billing & "Fees-on-Fees"

items: **Statutory `$125/hr` Base + `CPI-U` Escalation (`28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)(2)(A)`, `Pub. L. 104-121, § 232`, eff. `Mar. 29, 1996`):**

blocks.text: $$\text{EAJA Attorney Hourly Rate} = \$125.00 \times \left(\frac{\text{Applicable Regional or National CPI-U}}{\text{March 1996 Base CPI-U}}\right)$$ *(Capped at counsel's prevailing market rate; in 2024–2026 practice, `CPI-U` adjustments routinely yield `~$245–$260+/hr` depending on the regional/MSA `CPI-U` index).*

items: ***Mannino* Anti-Interest Midpoint Rule (***Mannino v. West*, `12 Vet. App. 242, 244–45 (1999)`**):** Applying *today's* `CPI-U` index to hours worked in *earlier* years constitutes impermissible interest against the United States. Counsel must calculate the `CPI-U` multiplier using either `(1)` the separate historical `CPI-U` for each year/month services were rendered, or `(2)` the **single `CPI-U` index for the temporal midpoint** between the first and last dates of compensated appellate work!

**Paralegal & Law-Clerk Prevailing Market Rates (***Richlin Security Service Co. v. Chertoff*, `553 U.S. 571, 581–90 (2008)`**):** Non-attorney paralegals, law clerks, and non-admitted practitioners supervised by CAVC counsel are billed at **prevailing market rates** (supported by *Laffey* / *USAO* / *Morimura* / local market surveys, capped below the `CPI-U` attorney rate), **never** restricted to the law firm's internal payroll cost!

**`"Fees-on-Fees"` (***Commissioner, INS v. Jean*, `496 U.S. 154, 161–66 (1990)`**):** Reasonable hours spent drafting the initial EAJA application and litigating any government opposition to EAJA entitlement or quantum are **automatically compensable** without re-litigating substantial justification for the fee phase.

blocks.text: 5. Mandatory "Same Work" Offset & Ethical Refund Rule (Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c))
A. Controlling Federal Statutory Command (28 U.S.C. § 2412 note)

When Congress extended `EAJA` explicitly to the CAVC in the **Federal Courts Administration Act of 1992 (`Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c)`, `106 Stat. 4506, 4513`, Oct. 29, 1992, codified at `28 U.S.C. § 2412 note`)**, it enacted an ironclad anti-double-dipping mandate (identical in structure to Social Security's `42 U.S.C. § 406(b)` / EAJA savings clause recognized in ***Gisbrecht v. Barnhart*, `535 U.S. 789, 796 (2002)`**):

lines: *"Section 5904(d) of title 38, United States Code, shall not prevent an award of fees and other expenses under section 2412(d) of title 28, United States Code. Section 5904(d) of title 38, United States Code, shall not apply with respect to any such award **but only if, where the claimant's attorney receives fees for the same work under both section 5904 of title 38, United States Code, and section 2412(d) of title 28, United States Code, the claimant's attorney refunds to the claimant the amount of the smaller fee**."*

blocks.text: B. Unified Continuous Retainers vs. Segregated Representation Models (*Shaw* & *Carpenter*)

Understanding what constitutes **`"the same work"`** under ***Shaw v. Gober*, `10 Vet. App. 498, 503–05 (1997)`** and ***Carpenter v. Principi*, `15 Vet. App. 64, 74–79 (2001) (en banc)`** (*appeal dismissed for lack of jurisdiction*, `327 F.3d 1371 (Fed. Cir. 2003)`) is a mandatory ethical and trust-accounting gate for every Veterans Law firm:

rows: **Model 1: Unified Continuous Representation (`RO/BVA -> CAVC -> Post-Remand Grant` by Same Counsel/Firm)**

Under ***Carpenter*, `15 Vet. App. at 76`**, when counsel represents a claimant at the CAVC (earning `EAJA` fees on a remand) **and** continues representing the claimant on remand under a `§ 5904` contingency agreement to win past-due benefits on that claim, **the CAVC appeal and post-remand success constitute `"the same work"`** (advancing the single continuous claim to an award)! **Kill-Switch:** *Carpenter* (`15 Vet. App. at 76–79`) **invalidated `"unless remanded"` / "post-remand-only" carveout clauses** inserted into unified contingency agreements to evade the `EAJA` offset—keeping `100%` of both `EAJA` and `20%` of the full past-due award is **unlawful and per se "excessive and unreasonable"** (`38 U.S.C. § 7263(d)`; `38 C.F.R. § 14.636(f)`). **Action:** Immediately upon receiving the second fee, **refund `100%` of the smaller fee (`min(EAJA_fee, §5904_fee)`) directly to the claimant**! *(Note: Out-of-pocket court filing costs reimbursed as EAJA *expenses*—e.g., the `$50` CAVC filing fee—are not attorney "fees" and are not offset unless already paid by the client).*
**Model 2: Segregated CAVC-Only Referral Counsel (`EAJA Only`, `$0` `§ 5904`) + Separate Agency Merits Counsel (`§ 5904 Only`, `$0` `EAJA`)**

Firm A (agency counsel) handles RO/BVA representation under a `§ 5904` contingency retainer (`0` CAVC appearance, `$0` `EAJA`). For the CAVC appeal, the veteran retains independent CAVC specialist Firm B under a **court-only `EAJA`-only retainer** in which Firm B **expressly charges `$0` under `§ 5904` and waives any share of past-due benefits**, returning the case solely to Firm A upon CAVC mandate. Because Firm B receives *only* `EAJA` (for court work) and Firm A receives *only* `§ 5904` (for agency work) **with zero fee-splitting between Firm A and Firm B**, neither `"claimant's attorney"` receives dual fees for the same work. **Trap:** If Firm B takes *any* referral cut of Firm A's `20%` `§ 5904` fee—or if Firm A bills co-counsel `EAJA` hours—`§ 506(c)` **immediately attaches** and mandates refunding the overlapping smaller fee to the veteran!
**Model 3: Post-Remand-Only Initial Retention *(Pro Se or Prior Counsel at CAVC -> Brand-New Post-Mandate Agency Counsel)***

Veteran wins a CAVC remand *pro se* (or via prior CAVC-only counsel who exits at mandate) and **retains a brand-new agency attorney for the first time *after* CAVC mandate** solely for post-remand development. Because the post-mandate attorney never received an `EAJA` fee, `§ 506(c)` does not apply to that attorney (though if prior CAVC counsel *also* filed a `§ 5904` agreement, VA allocates the single `20%` direct-pay cap under *Scates* / `§ 14.636(i)` and prior counsel must still offset its own `EAJA` recovery!).

blocks.text: C. Exact Trust/Operating Accounting Formula for Model 1 Refunds
Whenever a unified-representation claim grants retroactive past-due benefits after an earlier `EAJA` award on the same issue:

items: **Case A (`§ 5904` Contingency Fee `>` Prior `EAJA` Fee):** Suppose counsel previously received **`$6,800.00`** in CAVC `EAJA` fees (deposited into operating revenue when earned at the close of the CAVC case), and VA subsequently awards `$150,000.00` in past-due benefits on remand, disbursing **`$30,000.00`** (`20%`) directly to counsel under `§ 5904(d)`. Counsel **must immediately issue a `$6,800.00` refund check (`the smaller fee`) to the veteran** (leaving counsel with `$30,000.00` net total fees and boosting the veteran's net recovery from `$120,000.00` to **`$126,800.00`**—`84.53%` of the gross award!).

**Case B (Prior `EAJA` Fee `>` `§ 5904` Contingency Fee):** Suppose counsel previously received **`$6,800.00`** in `EAJA` fees, and the post-remand grant yields `$20,000.00` in past-due benefits (`20%` `§ 5904(d)` withholding = **`$4,000.00`**). Counsel **must immediately refund the entire `$4,000.00` `§ 5904(d)` payment (`the smaller fee`) to the veteran** (retaining the `$6,800.00` `EAJA` fee while the veteran nets **`100%` (`$20,000.00`)** of the past-due VA award!).

**Multi-Issue Proration Audit:** If a CAVC `EAJA` award covered Issues `A` and `B`, and VA grants past-due benefits *only* on Issue `A` while denying Issue `B`, counsel still received `EAJA` for the CAVC remand that produced Issue `A`'s award—refund the full overlapping `EAJA` fee (up to `min(EAJA, §5904_A)`) rather than risking an `OGC` / `CAVC` disciplinary violation by unilateral hair-splitting, and track any remaining credit so `EAJA` is never refunded more than once (`cumulative refunds <= total EAJA fee received`).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Understanding Accredited Representative Fees (38 U.S.C. § 5904) & Court-Paid EAJA Refunds
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Federal law strictly regulates who can assist you with a VA benefits claim and when fees can be charged. Veterans Service Organizations (VSOs) never charge fees. VA-accredited claims agents and attorneys are strictly prohibited from charging fees to prepare or file an initial claim—they may charge fees ONLY after VA issues an initial decision on the claim (38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(1)). When an accredited attorney or agent represents you on contingency, fees of 20% or less of past-due benefits are presumed reasonable and eligible for direct VA withholding (while fees above 33.33% are presumed unreasonable). Even better: if an attorney appeals a Board denial to the U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims (CAVC) and wins a remand based on VA error, the Equal Access to Justice Act (EAJA, 28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)) requires the government—not the Veteran—to pay court attorney fees, and if VA later awards back pay for that same work, the attorney MUST refund the smaller of the two fees dollar-for-dollar to the Veteran.
record_clues: VA Form 21-22 (appointing an accredited VSO at $0 cost) or VA Form 21-22a (appointing an individual VA-accredited attorney or claims agent) paired with a written fee agreement.

A VA fee-withholding letter under 38 C.F.R. § 14.636(h) withholding up to 20% of retroactive past-due benefits—or dividing that 20% pool among current and prior attorneys based on actual contribution (Scates quantum meruit).
A CAVC remand order or Joint Motion for Partial Remand (JMPR) followed within 30 days of mandate by an EAJA fee application.
A post-remand VA back-pay award where the attorney previously received EAJA fees for the court appeal, triggering a mandatory client refund of the smaller fee under Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c).
important_cautions: Watch out for unaccredited 'claim sharks': under 38 U.S.C. §§ 5901 and 5904(c)(1), anyone who is not accredited by VA's Office of the General Counsel—or anyone demanding fees or future-increase percentages to prepare an INITIAL claim before VA issues an initial decision—is violating federal law.

Strict 30-day fee-filing and EAJA deadlines for representatives: direct-pay fee agreements must be filed with the VA Regional Office / Intake Center within 30 days of execution (38 C.F.R. § 14.636(g)(3); Ravin v. Wilkie), and CAVC EAJA applications must be filed within 30 days after final nonappealable judgment/mandate—note that consent JMPR orders often issue an immediate mandate under CAVC Rule 41(b), starting the 30-day EAJA clock immediately rather than after 60 days!

Mandatory lesser-fee refund protection: an attorney can NEVER keep both a CAVC EAJA fee and a 38 U.S.C. § 5904 contingency fee for the exact same representation work—federal statute (Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c)) and Carpenter v. Principi require refunding the smaller fee dollar-for-dollar to you.

Supplemental Claim & CUE fee clarification: in Military-Veterans Advocacy v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs (2021), the Federal Circuit invalidated VA's regulatory ban on charging fees for Supplemental Claims or CUE motions filed more than 1 year after an initial decision, though George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e) bar CUE against final pre-2021 fee decisions.
questions_for_representative: Can we verify your active accreditation number on VA's Office of the General Counsel Accreditation Search before signing VA Form 21-22a?

Is your contingency fee capped at 20% of net past-due benefits only (never ongoing future monthly checks), and does our contract state whether case expenses (like private medical opinions) are separate?
If a prior representative worked on my appeal before I switched, does my total attorney fee stay within a single 20% withholding pool allocated fairly under 38 C.F.R. § 14.636(h)–(i)?

If you take my Board denial to the CAVC and recover EAJA fees from the government, how will the mandatory dollar-for-dollar EAJA offset/refund reduce any contingency fee if we later win back pay at VA?

title: Authority Hierarchy, Temporal Versioning Policy & Citation Verification Log
keyPrecedents: Cash v. Collins, No. 24-1811 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 5, 2026)
cFileTriggers: Pre-filing citation check and source-hierarchy audit before submitting a CUE motion, Board brief, or CAVC brief
killSwitches: Citing a nonprecedential CAVC single-judge memorandum decision as binding precedent (violates CAVC Rule 30(a))
Confusing a Federal Register proposed/publication date with the regulation's effective date
Quoting current eCFR text to prove CUE in a historical decision without pulling the contemporaneous CFR edition

toc.text: 1. Hierarchy of Authorities in Veterans Law
2. Mandatory Temporal-Versioning Rules
3. Master Authority Verification & Characterization Audit Table

blocks.text: Synthesized and cross-verified from dual Deep Research audits (Deep Research) and primary Federal Register / judicial checks.
1. Hierarchy of Authorities in Veterans Law

items: **Positive Statutory Text (`Title 38 U.S.C.` & Public Laws; pre-1959 `Veterans' Regulations`):** Supreme controlling authority.

**Enacted `38 C.F.R.` Regulations (Edition in Force on Decision Date):** Binding substantive law unless invalidated—and under *George v. McDonough*, 596 U.S. 740 (2022), even a *later-invalidated* regulation defeats CUE if the adjudicator faithfully applied it while it was in force.

**Controlling Judicial Precedent:** U.S. Supreme Court -> U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit -> precedential panel/en banc decisions of the U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims (CAVC).
• **Nonprecedential Warning (`CAVC Rule 30(a)`):** Single-judge CAVC memorandum decisions (e.g., *Marion v. Collins*) are **not binding precedent**.

**VA General Counsel Precedent Opinions (`VAOPGCPREC`):** Binding on **all VA officials, ROs, and the Board** (`38 U.S.C. § 7104(c)`; `38 C.F.R. § 14.507`), though reviewable by the Federal Circuit/CAVC.

**Adjudication Procedures Manual (`M21-1`):** Binding operational instructions for AOJ/RO raters, **not** binding on the Board or courts (`38 C.F.R. § 20.105`), and frequently reorganized on KnowVA—always record the exact retrieval date and historical change memo.

blocks.text: 2. Mandatory Temporal-Versioning Rules

items:
**Publication Date != Effective Date:** Always verify the **effective date** in the Federal Register preamble:
• **1945 VASRD:** Titled "1945 Schedule", **effective April 1, 1946** (`38 C.F.R. § 3.952`; Part 4 App. A).
• **Auditory & Tinnitus (`§§ 4.85–4.87`):** Maryland CNC & puretone tables published Nov. 18, 1987 (`52 FR 44117`), **effective December 18, 1987**; `§ 4.86` exceptional patterns & `"recurrent"` tinnitus published May 11, 1999 (`64 FR 25202`), **effective June 10, 1999**; `DC 6260` Note (2) single `10%` rule published May 14, 2003 (`68 FR 25822`), **effective June 13, 2003**.
• **Mental Disorders (`former § 4.132` -> `§ 4.130`):** `70%` psychoneurotic tier & `DC 9411` codified Jan. 4, 1988 (`53 FR 21`), **effective February 3, 1988**; DSM-IV unification, `§ 4.129` `50%` rule & `DC 9520–9521` published Oct. 8, 1996 (`61 FR 52695`), **effective November 7, 1996**; DSM-5 update published & **effective August 4, 2014** (`79 FR 45093`; finalized `80 FR 14308`, Mar. 19, 2015).
• **Endocrine System (`§ 4.119`):** Era 2 published May 7, 1996 (`61 FR 20440`), **effective June 6, 1996**; Era 3 overhaul published Nov. 2, 2017 (`82 FR 50802`), **effective December 10, 2017**.
• **Eye & Vision (`§§ 4.75–4.79`):** Era 2 overhaul published Nov. 10, 2008 (`73 FR 66543`), **effective December 10, 2008**; Era 3 clinic-visit overhaul published Apr. 10, 2018 (`83 FR 15316`), **effective May 13, 2018**.
• **Hemic & Lymphatic Systems (`§ 4.117`):** `AL` Amyloidosis (`DC 7717`) published Feb. 8, 2012 (`77 FR 6466`), **effective March 9, 2012**; comprehensive overhaul published Oct. 29, 2018 (`83 FR 54250`), **effective December 9, 2018** (corrected Oct. 11, 2022 at `87 FR 61248`).
• **Infectious, Immune & Nutritional (`§§ 4.88a–4.88b`):** `§ 4.88a` / `DC 6354` CFS published & **effective November 29, 1994** (`59 FR 60902`); comprehensive overhaul published June 18, 2019 (`84 FR 28227`), **effective August 11, 2019**.
• **Muscle Injuries (`§§ 4.55–4.73`):** Published June 3, 1997 (`62 FR 30235`), **effective July 3, 1997**.
• **Spine IVDS vs. General Formula:** IVDS published Aug. 22, 2002 (`67 FR 54345`), **effective Sept. 23, 2002**; General Rating Formula published Aug. 27, 2003 (`68 FR 51454`), **effective Sept. 26, 2003**.
• **`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)` Revision:** Proposed June 20, 2005 (`70 FR 35388`); Final Rule published Sept. 6, 2006 (`71 FR 52455`), **effective October 6, 2006**.
• **Scars (`§ 4.118`):** Interim overhaul published July 31, 2002 (`67 FR 49590`), **effective August 30, 2002**; major 8-characteristic/painful-scar-count overhaul published Sept. 23, 2008 (`73 FR 54708`), **effective October 23, 2008** (clarified Jan. 20, 2012 at `77 FR 2909`); skin/scars update published July 13, 2018 (`83 FR 32592`), **effective August 13, 2018**.
• **Standardized Forms / End of Informal Claims:** Published Sept. 25, 2014 (`79 FR 57660`), **effective March 24, 2015**.
• **Respiratory System (`§§ 4.96–4.97`):** Published Sept. 5, 1996 (`61 FR 46720`), **effective October 7, 1996** (`§ 4.96(d)` PFT rules added Sept. 6, 2006 at `71 FR 52457, 52459`, **effective October 6, 2006**).
• **Cardiovascular System (`§§ 4.100–4.104`):** Era 2 (`LVEF + METs`) published Dec. 11, 1997 (`62 FR 65207`), **effective January 12, 1998** (`DC 7122` Cold Injury published July 14, 1998 at `63 FR 37778`, **effective August 13, 1998**); Era 3 (`METs` General Formula) published Sept. 30, 2021 (`86 FR 54089`), **effective November 14, 2021** (corrected Nov. 9, 2021 at `86 FR 62095` and Nov. 29, 2021 at `86 FR 67654`).
• **Musculoskeletal (`§ 4.71a` / `§ 4.73`):** Published Nov. 30, 2020 (`85 FR 76453`) and corrected Feb. 4, 2021 (`86 FR 8142` renumbering Plantar Fasciitis from `5285` to **`DC 5269`**), **effective February 7, 2021**.
• **Bilateral Factor Exclusion (`§ 4.26(d)`):** Published Apr. 14, 2023 (`88 FR 22914`), **effective April 16, 2023**.
• **Digestive System (`§ 4.114`):** Published Mar. 20, 2024 (`89 FR 19735`), **effective May 19, 2024**.
**Never Project Modern Text Backward in CUE:** Obtain the print/govinfo CFR edition (govinfo covers 1996–present; HeinOnline / Federal Register covers 1936–1995) before filing any CUE motion.

blocks.text: 3. Master Authority Verification & Characterization Audit Table

rows: `166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 4, 2026)` (`No. 24-1543`). Eliminates implicit denial **strictly for AMA decisions** (`>= Feb. 19, 2019`) under `38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)`. Facts arose from an unaddressed request to reopen a character-of-discharge determination, not TDIU. Footnote 6 notes that within 1 year of a silent AMA decision, claimants have an adequate legal remedy via HLR or Board appeal rather than mandamus. Legacy decisions remain governed by *Deshotel* / *Adams* / *Hampton* / *Steele* (*cert. petition pending*, *Steele*, `No. 25-1123`).

`No. 24-1811 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 5, 2026)`. Under `38 U.S.C. § 7113(c)`, when a Board NOD (`VA Form 10182`) clearly identifies or incorporates probative evidence submitted during an AMA "in-between" window that is already in VA's possession, the Board must consider it without requiring physical resubmission.

`605 U.S. 360 (June 12, 2025)` (No. 24-320, 9–0, Thomas, J.). Displaces 6-year Barring Act (`31 U.S.C. § 3702(b)`) cap on **Title 10 DoD CRSC** (`10 U.S.C. § 1413a`). **Not** a Title 38 VA effective-date statute; implemented via **Aug. 20, 2025 DoD guidance** and parallel Court of Federal Claims Tucker Act litigation (e.g., *Christopher Carey v. United States* for claims >\$10,000).

`101 F.4th 1348 (Fed. Cir. May 16, 2024)`. Invalidated VA's single-step ceiling on `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(f)(3)–(4)`, holding veterans at base rates `SMC(l)–(n)` are entitled to **multiple** half-step or full-step intermediate SMC increases (capped at `SMC(o)`) for each separate `50%` or `100%` disability. *(Caution: Attacking final pre-May 2024 single-step ratings via CUE faces `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)` / George v. McDonough change-in-interpretation defenses).*

`971 F.3d 1348 (Fed. Cir. 2020)` & `766 F.3d 1402 (Fed. Cir. 2014)`. VAMC medical records generated within **1 year *after*** a Legacy RO rating decision are constructively received by VA under *Bell* and **`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b)`**, requiring VA to determine whether they constitute new and material evidence and **abating finality** if VA never made that determination!

`33 Vet. App. 252 (2021)`. Precedential decision on mailing an SOC to a claimant's **representative**; rebuts regularity via nonreceipt **plus** evidence of systemic VA mailing irregularity (practitioner affidavits, NOVA declaration, GAO report)—**not** a wrong-address C&P exam case, though burden-shifting framework applies across mailing disputes.

`No. 24-6964 (Vet. App. Dec. 23, 2025) (mem. dec.)`. Single-judge nonprecedential decision (**do not cite as binding precedent under CAVC Rule 30(a)**); illustrates that counsel's bare affidavit of nonreceipt of an HLR decision without systemic/file corroboration fails to rebut regularity.

`7 Vet. App. 271, 274 (1994)` (often mis-cited as `471` or `1995`, which was the Fed. Cir. jurisdictional dismissal `56 F.3d 85`). Holds regularity applies to RO mailings and bare nonreceipt is insufficient.

`926 F.3d 1362, 1370 (Fed. Cir. 2019)`. Construes **pre-March 24, 2015 informal-claim scope** under former `38 C.F.R. § 3.155(a)` when filings point to specific medical records—**not** an exception to the post-2015 Intent-to-File requirement (*cf. Sellers v. Wilkie*, 965 F.3d 1328 (Fed. Cir. 2020) for post-2015 form specificity).

`2 Vet. App. 611 (July 21, 1992)`; `VAOPGCPREC 12-95` (`60 FR 43186`, Aug. 18, 1995). Constructive possession of VA records applies to CUE only for AOJ decisions rendered **on or after July 21, 1992**.

`596 U.S. 740 (2022)`. Later judicial invalidation or reinterpretation of a regulation cannot support CUE against a prior final decision (`38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`—creates a major defense against pre-2008 *Bradley* TDIU-based `SMC(s)` and pre-2024 *Barry* `§ 3.350(f)` CUE claims).

`969 F.3d 1333 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`, *reh'g en banc denied sub nom. Kisor v. McDonough*, `995 F.3d 1316 (Fed. Cir. 2021)`. Defines "relevant" under `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)(1)` as relating to a contested element / basis of the prior denial.

`68 F.4th 1376 (Fed. Cir. 2023)` & `135 F.4th 1353 (Fed. Cir. 2025)` (*cert. pet. No. 25-1123*). Confirm that in **legacy** (pre-AMA) claims, a decision denying a schedular increase can implicitly deny reasonably raised TDIU.

`38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)` (Fed. Cir. appeal `No. 25-1972` voluntarily dismissed Mar. 30, 2026). Bars discounting musculoskeletal/disability ratings for ameliorative medication effects unless the DC explicitly mentions medication. VA's reactive `38 C.F.R. § 4.10` Interim Final Rule (`91 FR 7118`, Feb. 17, 2026) was **rescinded Feb. 27, 2026 (`91 FR 9712`)**—audit any rating issued Feb. 17–27, 2026!

`No. 21-4168 (Vet. App. class certified Mar. 2026)`. Covers ~28,000+ legacy appeals improperly closed by VACOLS automated sweeps (Dec. 12, 1990 – Feb. 6, 2025) despite timely appellate posture; proposed settlement mandates case-by-case VA audit and readjudication.
`604 U.S. 369 (2025)`. CAVC reviews the Board's approximate-balance determination under `38 U.S.C. § 5107(b)` (benefit of the doubt) for clear error.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: How Legal Sources Rank in VA Claims & Why Official Regulation Dates Must Be Checked
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Not everything printed online or inside a VA manual carries the same legal weight. In Veterans Law, Acts of Congress (38 U.S.C.) rank highest, followed by binding federal court precedents (U.S. Supreme Court, Federal Circuit, and precedential three-judge CAVC panels), enacted VA regulations (38 C.F.R.), and active VA General Counsel Precedent Opinions (VAOPGCPREC). Below those sit VA's internal M21-1 Adjudication Procedures Manual (which guides Regional Office raters, though the Board of Veterans' Appeals is not strictly bound by it unless discussed) and single-judge CAVC memorandum decisions. This guide explains how accredited representatives verify that every statute, regulation, and court case actually governed on the exact date of your VA decision.
record_clues: A VA rating decision or representative letter quoting today's online eCFR regulation text to challenge a decision issued 15 or 30 years ago, when the regulation read differently.
A citation to a Federal Register notice date where the new rule did not actually take effect until 30 or 60 days later—or was only a proposed rule that never became law.
A brief relying on a single-judge CAVC memorandum decision ('mem. dec.') as if it were binding law, rather than checking CAVC Rule 30(a) nonprecedential limits.
important_cautions: Publication Date vs. Effective Date: When VA publishes a final rule in the Federal Register, its 'Effective Date' is usually weeks or months after the publication date. Always verify the exact effective date before comparing an older rating decision against a rule change.

Nonprecedential Single-Judge Decisions (CAVC Rule 30(a)): Single-judge CAVC memorandum decisions ('mem. dec.') are nonprecedential under CAVC Rule 30(a)—they may be cited for persuasive reasoning where permitted, never as binding precedent.

Proposed & Rescinded Rules Are Not Enacted Law: Proposed rules (such as RIN 2900-AQ72 on sleep apnea/tinnitus, RIN 2900-AQ82 on mental disorders, or 90 FR 46542 on painful scars) and rescinded rules (such as the February 17, 2026 § 4.10 medication rule at 91 FR 7118, rescinded February 27, 2026 at 91 FR 9712) are not enacted law.

Post-Decision Court Reinterpretations (George v. McDonough): Under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e), a later court decision that changes how an existing statute or regulation is interpreted applies to open claims, timely appeals, and § 3.156(c) service-record reconsiderations, but cannot prove Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) in an older final decision.
questions_for_representative: Have we checked the exact print edition of 38 C.F.R. and 38 U.S.C. that was in effect on the day my VA decision was issued, rather than relying on today's eCFR?
Are the court cases supporting my argument binding precedential panel opinions, and were any relied-upon VA General Counsel opinions later withdrawn?
Does our strategy rely on an enacted regulation in force at the time of the decision, or would an open-claim / 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) route avoid the George v. McDonough CUE bar?
