blocks.text: From `1933` until `November 18, 1988`, the Veterans' Administration operated in "splendid isolation" behind the judicial-review bar of `former 38 U.S.C. § 211(a)`. Enactment of the **Veterans' Judicial Review Act (`VJRA`)**, `Pub. L. 100-687, Div. A, 102 Stat. 4105 (Nov. 18, 1988)`, dismantled that insulation by creating a two-tiered federal appellate architecture ([Three-Era Title 38 U.S.C. Statutory Crosswalk (1933–Present)](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk), [Era Lens 3: The VJRA Revolution, Well-Grounded Claims & 1990s VASRD Overhauls (1988–2000)](/eras/1988-2000-vjra-revolution)):

items: **First-Tier Article I Appellate Review (`38 U.S.C. §§ 7251–7288`):** Exclusive review of final adverse Board of Veterans' Appeals (`BVA`) decisions before the **U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims (`CAVC`)**—originally enacted as `former 38 U.S.C. §§ 4051–4092` establishing the *U.S. Court of Veterans Appeals (`COVA`)*, renumbered to `Chapter 72` by `Pub. L. 102-40, § 402(b)(1), 105 Stat. 187, 238 (May 7, 1991)`, and renamed `CAVC` by `Pub. L. 105-368, § 511, 112 Stat. 3315, 3341 (Nov. 11, 1998)` (effective March 1, 1999). *(Note: `Pub. L. 107-103, § 603(a), 115 Stat. 976, 999 (Dec. 27, 2001)` repealed the VJRA's original post-Nov. 18, 1988 Notice of Disagreement jurisdictional floor).*

**Second-Tier Article III Law-Declaration & Direct Rulemaking Review (`38 U.S.C. §§ 7292, 502`):** Exclusive review of pure questions of statutory, regulatory, and constitutional interpretation—plus pre-enforcement review of VA regulations and `M21-1` manual rules—in the **U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit**, followed by certiorari to the **U.S. Supreme Court (`28 U.S.C. § 1254(1)`)**.

blocks.text: Pair this appellate treatise with [AMA Three-Lane & BVA Litigation Manual](/docs/ama-lanes-and-bva-litigation-manual), [Attorney Fees (`§ 5904`) & EAJA Practice](/docs/attorney-fees-5904-and-eaja-practice), [Part 20 & Part 14 Regulatory Snapshots](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-part-20-ama-evid-windows-and-part-14-fees), [Part 19/20 & Part 14 Evolution Diff](/cfr/modules/ama-part-19-20-and-part-14-fee-evolution), and the [CAVC Appeal, EAJA & Fee Compliance Gate](/checklists/cavc-appeal-eaja-and-fee-compliance-gate).
1. CAVC Exclusive Jurisdiction & Finality Prerequisites (38 U.S.C. §§ 7252, 7261, 7266)

Under `38 U.S.C. § 7252(a)`, the CAVC possesses **exclusive jurisdiction** to review decisions of the Board of Veterans' Appeals. That jurisdiction is bounded by four structural rules that govern every intake and briefing decision.
A. Final Adverse Board Decision Requirement (*Kirkpatrick* & *Breeden* vs. *Maggitt*)

items: **Board Remands Are NOT Final Appealable Decisions:** Under `38 U.S.C. § 7266(a)`, a claimant may appeal only a **"final decision"** of the Board. Because a Board remand neither grants nor denies benefits, **a Board remand order is not a final decision** over which the CAVC can exercise `§ 7252(a)` appellate jurisdiction—even where the veteran contends the remand instructions apply an erroneous legal standard (*Kirkpatrick v. Nicholson*, `417 F.3d 1361, 1364–65 (Fed. Cir. 2005)`; *Breeden v. Principi*, `17 Vet. App. 475, 478 (2004)` (per curiam order)).

**Mixed Board Decisions (Bifurcated Finality):** When a single Board decision denies Issue A (e.g., lumbosacral spine service connection) while remanding Issue B (e.g., radiculopathy or TDIU), the denial of Issue A is immediately final and appealable within `120 days`, whereas remanded Issue B remains non-final before the agency—unless Issue B is inextricably intertwined with a reversed/vacated denial on Issue A.

**Claim-Level Jurisdiction vs. Issue Exhaustion (*Maggitt v. West*):** Once a claimant obtains a final adverse Board decision on a *claim* and timely invokes `§ 7252(a)`, the CAVC has subject-matter jurisdiction over that decided claim. Under *Maggitt v. West*, `202 F.3d 1370, 1377–78 (Fed. Cir. 2000)`, the CAVC possesses case-by-case discretion to entertain newly raised legal arguments supporting that same claim—or to require administrative issue exhaustion where factual development or agency expertise outweighs immediate resolution (cf. *Scott v. McDonald*, `789 F.3d 1375, 1378–81 (Fed. Cir. 2015)`). By contrast, if the Board never adjudicated a **distinct claim or distinct CUE theory** at all, the CAVC lacks `§ 7252(a)` jurisdiction over that unadjudicated matter (*Andre v. Principi*, `301 F.3d 1354, 1361 (Fed. Cir. 2002)`).

blocks.text: B. One-Way Asymmetry of Review (38 U.S.C. § 7252(a))
Congress intentionally designed CAVC review to be **one-directional**:

lines: *"The Secretary may not seek review of any such [Board] decision."* (`38 U.S.C. § 7252(a)`).

blocks.text: If the Board grants service connection, assigns a `70%` evaluation, or awards an earlier effective date, **VA Office of General Counsel (`OGC`) cannot appeal or cross-appeal that favorable Board ruling to the CAVC**. (Conversely, once the *CAVC* enters judgment, *either* the claimant or the Secretary may appeal a pure legal ruling to the Federal Circuit under `38 U.S.C. § 7292(a)`).
C. Inviolability of Favorable Factual Findings (38 U.S.C. §§ 5104A, 7261(a)(4); *Medrano*)

In the Veterans Benefits Act of 2002 (`Pub. L. 107-330, § 401, 116 Stat. 2820, 2832`), Congress amended `38 U.S.C. § 7261(a)(4)` so that the CAVC may set aside or reverse *only* a finding of material fact **"adverse to the claimant."**

items: **Absolute Bar Against Disturbing Favorable Board Findings:** Under ***Medrano v. Nicholson*, `21 Vet. App. 165, 170 (2007)`** and ***Roberson v. Principi*, `17 Vet. App. 135, 139 (2003)` (per curiam order)**, **the CAVC lacks statutory authority or jurisdiction to reverse, vacate, or disturb findings of fact made by the Board that are favorable to the claimant**—full stop. Even if VA OGC argues on appeal that a favorable Board predicate finding (e.g., confirmed in-service injury, current diagnosis, credibility of lay symptomatology, or exposure) lacked a plausible basis, the CAVC **cannot** overturn it.

**Agency-Level Binding Force (`38 U.S.C. § 5104A`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.104(c)`):** Enacted by the Appeals Modernization Act (`Pub. L. 115-55`, eff. Feb. 19, 2019), any favorable finding of fact made by an AOJ rater or the Board is **binding on all subsequent VA and Board adjudicators** unless rebutted by **clear and unmistakable evidence** ([AMA Three-Lane Strategy, Evidentiary Windows & Board of Veterans' Appeals Litigation Manual (38 U.S.C. §§ 5104C, 7104, 7105, 7113; 38 C.F.R. Parts 3, 19 & 20)](/docs/ama-lanes-and-bva-litigation-manual)).

blocks.text: D. Precedential Discipline & CAVC Rule 30(a)

Under *Frankel v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 23, 25–26 (1990)` and *Bethea v. Derwinski*, `2 Vet. App. 252, 254 (1992)`, only published **three-judge panel** and **en banc** CAVC decisions establish binding precedent. Single-judge memorandum decisions (`mem. dec.`) are strictly **nonprecedential (`CAVC Rule 30(a)`)** and may never be cited as binding authority ([Authority Hierarchy, Temporal Versioning Policy & Citation Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)). If an appeal raises an issue of first impression, systemic statutory/regulatory conflict, or split single-judge outcomes, counsel should move for panel consideration under `CAVC Rules 30` and `35`.

lines: **Post-Mortem Substitution at the CAVC (`CAVC Rule 43`):** If an appellant dies while a CAVC appeal is pending (or during the `120-day` NOA window after a final Board decision), an eligible accrued-benefits survivor (`38 U.S.C. §§ 5121, 5121A`) must move to substitute under `CAVC Rule 43` (*Breedlove v. Shinseki*, `24 Vet. App. 7 (2010)`). See [Playbook 09: Accrued Benefits, Substitution & Nehmer Estates](/playbooks/09-accrued-benefits-substitution-nehmer-estates) for the *Merritt* procedural trap when a veteran dies before CAVC mandate issues.

blocks.text: 2. The 120-Day Notice of Appeal (NOA) Clock, *Rosler* Abatement & Equitable Tolling (38 U.S.C. § 7266(a))

Under `38 U.S.C. § 7266(a)`, a Notice of Appeal (`NOA`) must be filed with the CAVC within **`120 days` after the date on which notice of the Board's decision is mailed** (presumed to be the date stamped on the BVA decision unless rebutted by clear evidence of non-mailing or wrong-address mailing under *Ashley v. Derwinski*, `2 Vet. App. 307, 309 (1992)`).
A. *Henderson v. Shinseki* & The Non-Jurisdictional 120-Day Rule

In ***Henderson v. Shinseki*, `562 U.S. 428, 438–42 (2011)`**, the U.S. Supreme Court unanimously held that `38 U.S.C. § 7266(a)`'s `120-day` filing deadline is an **"important procedural" claim-processing rule, NOT a jurisdictional bar**, emphasizing the uniquely pro-claimant structure of Title 38. On remand in ***Bove v. Shinseki*, `25 Vet. App. 136, 140–43 (2011)` (per curiam order)**, the CAVC confirmed two operational consequences:

items: **`§ 7266(a)` Is Subject to Equitable Tolling:** Reinstating the pre-*Bowles* equitable-tolling jurisprudence of *Bailey v. West*, `160 F.3d 1360 (Fed. Cir. 1998) (en banc)` and *Barrett*.

**Waiver / Forfeiture:** Because `§ 7266(a)` is non-jurisdictional, the CAVC will not dismiss an untimely NOA *sua sponte* if the Secretary fails to raise untimeliness—though in practice VA OGC systematically audits NOA dates and files motions to dismiss before the record is transmitted.

blocks.text: B. Controlling Federal Circuit Categories of Equitable Tolling

To establish equitable tolling of `§ 7266(a)`, an appellant must show: `(1)` an **extraordinary circumstance** beyond the claimant's control; `(2)` **causation** (the extraordinary circumstance prevented timely filing); and `(3)` **due diligence** in pursuing appellate rights.

rows: ***Barrett v. Principi*, `363 F.3d 1316, 1321 (Fed. Cir. 2004)`**; ***Arbas v. Nicholson*, `403 F.3d 1379, 1381 (Fed. Cir. 2005)`**

*Barrett* holds mental illness tolls `§ 7266(a)` where the condition rendered the veteran **incapable of "rational thought or deliberate decision making,"** or **incapable of handling their own affairs or unable to function in society** (a medical diagnosis alone is insufficient without functional linkage; corroborate via clinician declarations or hospitalization records). *Arbas* extends the identical functional-incapacity test to **physical** illness or acute hospitalization.

Two landmark rules: **(a)** Homelessness preventing receipt of the mailed BVA decision is an extraordinary circumstance causing late filing; and **(b)** Veterans law applies the **"stop-clock" standard**, requiring proof of due diligence **only *during* the period of extraordinary circumstances** to be tolled—*not* throughout the entire residual `120-day` period after the impediment ends!
***Sneed v. Shinseki*, `737 F.3d 719, 726–28 (Fed. Cir. 2013)`** *vs.* ***Nelson v. Nicholson*, `489 F.3d 1380, 1383 (Fed. Cir. 2007)`**

Under *Sneed*, **complete attorney abandonment** (e.g., counsel abruptly terminating representation immediately before the `120-day` deadline expires, leaving the veteran unable to retain substitute counsel or file) constitutes an extraordinary circumstance. By contrast, under *Nelson*, **"garden-variety" attorney negligence** (missed calendar reminders, late mailing by active counsel) is imputed to the client and **never** tolls `§ 7266(a)`.
**4. Timely Misfiling at VA & Postal Anomalies**
***Santana-Venegas v. Principi*, `314 F.3d 1293, 1297–98 (Fed. Cir. 2002)`**; ***James v. Wilkie*, `917 F.3d 1368, 1372–74 (Fed. Cir. 2019)`**

Under *Santana-Venegas* (and *Jaquay v. Principi*, `304 F.3d 1276 (Fed. Cir. 2002) (en banc)`), misfiling a written expression of intent to appeal to the Court at the **VARO where the claim originated within `120 days`** tolls the clock. Under *James*, the Federal Circuit barred rigid *per se* exclusions (reversing CAVC's categorical rejection of a fallen residential mailbox flag on Day 120): **a veteran has zero duty to file prior to Day 120**, and CAVC must conduct a flexible, case-specific equitable inquiry.

blocks.text: C. Board Motion for Reconsideration Abatement (*Rosler* & *Linville*) vs. AMA Supplemental Claims
When a final Board decision contains an obvious error—or when `120 days` have not yet elapsed—practitioners must distinguish **three** post-Board filings whose clock mechanics differ radically:

items:
**Motion for BVA Reconsideration Within `120 Days` (`38 U.S.C. § 7103`; `38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1000–20.1004`):**
• Under ***Rosler v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 241, 249 (1991)`** and ***Linville v. West*, `165 F.3d 1382, 1385–86 (Fed. Cir. 1999)`** (enforcing `38 C.F.R. § 20.1002`'s USPS postmark rule on reconsideration filings), if a claimant files a Motion for Reconsideration with the Board **within `120 days`** of the mailing of the Board decision, **the finality of the Board decision is abated**.
• If the Board Chairman denies reconsideration, a **brand-new `120-day` CAVC NOA clock** begins on the date the Chairman mails notice of the denial! If the claimant then files a CAVC NOA within `120 days` of the Chairman's denial, the CAVC has jurisdiction over the underlying Board decision (and may review the Chairman's denial to the extent permitted under *Mayer v. Brown*, `37 F.3d 618 (Fed. Cir. 1994)`).
• *Post-120-Day Trap:* A Motion for BVA Reconsideration may be filed at *any* time (`38 C.F.R. § 20.1002(b)`), **but** if filed **more than `120 days`** after the BVA decision (absent equitable tolling of the initial gap), its denial by the Chairman **does NOT revive CAVC jurisdiction** over the underlying BVA decision!

**AMA Post-Board Supplemental Claim Within `1 Year` (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)(2)(D)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.2500(c)(3)`):**
• Following *Military-Veterans Advocacy v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs (`MVA`)*, `7 F.4th 1110 (Fed. Cir. 2021)`, a claimant who receives an adverse AMA Board decision may preserve the continuous-pursuit effective date by filing a `VA Form 20-0995` Supplemental Claim supported by **new and relevant evidence** within **`1 year`** of the BVA decision ([Master Effective-Date & Staged-Rating Legal Treatise (38 U.S.C. § 5110; 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.114, 3.155, 3.400, 3.2500)](/docs/effective-dates-and-staged-ratings-treatise)).
• **CRITICAL KILL-SWITCH:** Filing a `VA Form 20-0995` Supplemental Claim at the AOJ **does NOT abate or toll the `120-day` CAVC NOA deadline** under `§ 7266(a)`! *(Note: While `38 C.F.R. § 3.2500(d)` bars pursuing two administrative lanes simultaneously, **MVA v. Sec'y**, `7 F.4th at 1134` **invalidated `38 C.F.R. § 3.2500(b)`**'s former regulatory bar against filing a protective `§ 5108` Supplemental Claim while a federal-court appeal is pending).*
• **Sequential Safety Valve (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)(2)(E)`):** Always prioritize CAVC review within `120 days` when the closed Board record contains reversible error (preserving `EAJA` fee recovery!). Even if the CAVC later affirms the Board denial, **`38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)(2)(E)` (`38 C.F.R. § 3.2500(c)(4)`)** grants the veteran a fresh **`1-year` window after CAVC disposition** to file a `VA Form 20-0995` Supplemental Claim with new and relevant evidence while still keeping the original effective date alive ([AMA Three-Lane Strategy, Evidentiary Windows & Board of Veterans' Appeals Litigation Manual (38 U.S.C. §§ 5104C, 7104, 7105, 7113; 38 C.F.R. Parts 3, 19 & 20)](/docs/ama-lanes-and-bva-litigation-manual), [Accreditation, 38 U.S.C. § 5904 Contingency Fees, Reasonableness Litigation & Equal Access to Justice Act (EAJA, 28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)) Practice Treatise](/docs/attorney-fees-5904-and-eaja-practice)).

blocks.text: 3. CAVC Standards of Review, Rule 33 JMPR Engineering & Outright Reversal (38 U.S.C. § 7261)
A. Statutory Standards-of-Review Matrix (38 U.S.C. § 7261(a)–(c))

rows: ***Lane v. Principi*, `339 F.3d 1331, 1339 (Fed. Cir. 2003)`** (reinforced post-*Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo*, `603 U.S. 369 (2024)`).

***Gilbert v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 49, 52–53 (1990)`**: Set aside or reversed when there is no plausible basis in the record or the Court holds a "definite and firm conviction that a mistake has been committed" (*Deloach*). Trial *de novo* of facts is barred (`§ 7261(c)`).
**`Clear error`** on evidentiary weighing (*de novo* only if BVA misstated legal test)

***Bufkin v. Collins*, `604 U.S. 369 (2025)`**: `§ 7261(b)(1)`'s directive to "take due account" of VA's application of the benefit of the doubt does **not** create *de novo* appellate reweighing; factual weight assessments are reviewed for clear error.
**`Arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, or otherwise not in accordance with law`**

***Russell v. Principi*, `3 Vet. App. 310, 315 (1992) (en banc)`**. *(Note: Whether a CUE motion satisfied pleading specificity or whether the Board misinterpreted a statute/regulation remains reviewed de novo).*
**Legal adequacy** enabling claimant understanding & judicial review
*Gilbert*, `1 Vet. App. at 56–57`; *Caluza v. Brown*, `7 Vet. App. 498, 506 (1995)`, *aff'd*, `78 F.3d 604 (Fed. Cir. 1996)` (must address all material favorable evidence and credibility).
**Appellant bears ordinary civil burden** of showing prejudice, **WITHOUT initial CAVC fact-finding**

***Shinseki v. Sanders*, `556 U.S. 396, 406–11 (2009)`** **bounded by** ***Tadlock v. McDonough*, `5 F.4th 1327, 1334–38 (Fed. Cir. 2021)`**: CAVC **cannot make initial factual findings** (e.g., weighing conflicting medical or lay evidence in the first instance) to deem a Board error "harmless"!

blocks.text: B. CAVC Rule 33 Joint Motion for Partial Remand (JMPR) Engineering & The *Carter* Waiver Trap

Prior to merits briefing, `CAVC Rule 33` mandates a pre-briefing settlement conference between appellant's counsel and VA OGC Group VII counsel based on a structured **Rule 33 Memorandum**. Roughly `65%–75%` of CAVC appeals resolve via a negotiated **Joint Motion for Remand (`JMR`)** or **Joint Motion for Partial Remand (`JMPR`)**—which confers "prevailing party" status for **EAJA attorney fees (`28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)`)** provided the remand is predicated on administrative error ([Zero-PII 7-Gate CAVC / Federal Circuit Appellate, JMPR, EAJA & 38 U.S.C. § 5904 Fee-Compliance Gate Checklist](/checklists/cavc-appeal-eaja-and-fee-compliance-gate)).

lines: **The *Carter* Restrictive-JMPR Waiver Trap (*Carter v. Shinseki* / *Carter v. McDonald*):**

In ***Carter v. Shinseki*, `26 Vet. App. 534, 541–43 (2014)`**, *vacated on other grounds sub nom.* ***Carter v. McDonald*, `794 F.3d 1342, 1346–47 (Fed. Cir. 2015)`**, the courts established a dangerous trap for careless appellate practitioners. In *Carter*, counsel negotiated a narrow JMR focused on a single evidentiary notice point while omitting other substantive errors in the Board's decision. Although the Federal Circuit ultimately vacated in *Carter v. McDonald*, `794 F.3d at 1346–47`, because VA failed to mail the post-remand 90-day submission letter to the veteran's new attorney (holding that burying an expired notice letter inside a voluminous C-file copy did not cure defective notice), both decisions underscore that **a negotiated JMPR operates as a bilateral stipulation defining the scope of the Board's remand mandate**. If counsel stipulates to a narrow, closed-ended JMPR ("the Board erred *solely* by failing to address X") without reserving open argument/evidence rights—and then fails to raise additional theories on remand—omitted errors can be deemed **abandoned or foreclosed** in a subsequent appeal!

blocks.text: Every firm-approved `Rule 33` JMPR **must** enforce four contractual clauses:

items: **Targeted Partial Vacatur & *Medrano* Shield:** Explicitly vacate **only** those portions of the Board decision that denied the appealed benefits, and state expressly that **all grants and favorable findings of fact remain undisturbed and binding** (`38 U.S.C. § 5104A`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.104(c)`; *Medrano v. Nicholson*, `21 Vet. App. 165, 170 (2007)`).

**Predicate Administrative Error Recital (EAJA Lock):** State clear Board legal or `§ 7104(d)(1)` reasons-or-bases error in the body of the JMPR (never stipulate to a purely "equitable" remand without error, which destroys EAJA "prevailing party" status under *Sumner v. Principi*, `15 Vet. App. 256 (2001) (en banc)`).

**Anti-*Carter* Non-Waiver & Open-Submission Clause:** Expressly stipulate: *"Nothing in this Joint Motion waives any other factual or legal error; on remand, Appellant is free to submit additional evidence and argument (`38 C.F.R. § 20.800` / post-remand window), and the Board must conduct a critical reexamination of the record and address all issues reasonably raised by the appellant or the evidence of record (`Fletcher v. Derwinski`, `1 Vet. App. 394, 397 (1991)`)."*

***Stegall* Compliance Mandate:** Incorporate an express instruction that the Board and AOJ must ensure substantial compliance with the remand directives under ***Stegall v. West*, `11 Vet. App. 268, 271 (1998)`**—establishing reversible legal error if VA ignores the JMPR's exam or rationale instructions on remand.

blocks.text: C. When to Reject OGC's Remand Offer and Brief for Outright CAVC Reversal

When VA OGC spots a fatal flaw in a Board denial where the record overwhelmingly favors the veteran, OGC routinely offers a `Rule 33` remand so the Board can "provide an adequate statement of reasons or bases" or "obtain a clarifying medical addendum." **Accepting an unnecessary remand costs the veteran `1–3+ years` of remand churn and hands VA a roadmap to manufacture negative evidence.**
Counsel must **reject a JMPR and brief for outright reversal (`38 U.S.C. § 7261(a)(4)`)** in two primary scenarios:

items:
**Uncontroverted Record / Only One Permissible View (*Deloach*, *Gutierrez* & *Adams*):**
• ***Deloach v. Shinseki*, `704 F.3d 1370, 1379–81 (Fed. Cir. 2013)`**: Construing Congress's 2002 addition of `"or reverse"` to `38 U.S.C. § 7261(a)(4)`, the Federal Circuit held that where the Board has performed the necessary fact-finding, its adverse finding is clearly erroneous, and the uncontroverted evidence of record permits **only one permissible view of the evidence**, the CAVC has the full statutory power and duty to **reverse outright** and order an award of benefits.
• ***Gutierrez v. Principi*, `19 Vet. App. 1, 8–9 (2004)`**: Reversing a Board denial outright because all competent medical and lay evidence of record supported entitlement, making reversal—not remand—mandatory.
• ***Adams v. Principi*, `256 F.3d 1318, 1321–22 (Fed. Cir. 2001)`**: While CAVC may remand to clarify a genuinely ambiguous exam, **the CAVC may NOT remand merely to give VA a "second bite at the apple" to develop new negative medical evidence** to shore up an unsupported denial!

**Failed Affirmative VA Burden (*Horn* Soundness & `§ 3.344` Void Rating Reductions):**
• Whenever **VA—not the veteran—bears the affirmative burden of proof**, and the existing record fails as a matter of law to satisfy VA's heightened standard, **reversal is mandatory as a matter of law**:
• **Presumption of Soundness (`38 U.S.C. § 1111`):** In ***Horn v. Shinseki*, `25 Vet. App. 231, 243–44 (2012)`**, VA's medical opinion legally failed to prove by *clear and unmistakable evidence* both preexistence and non-aggravation. The CAVC **reversed** the Board's finding rather than remanding for a new VA medical opinion, holding VA does not get a remand to cure its failure to carry an affirmative rebuttal burden ([Substantive Service Connection Treatise: Direct Nexus (§ 3.303), Chronicity Post-Walker, Presumption of Soundness (§ 1111), In-Service Aggravation (§ 1153) & Congenital Defects vs. Hereditary Diseases](/docs/service-connection-direct-soundness-aggravation)).
• **Void Rating Reductions & Severance (`38 C.F.R. §§ 3.105(d)–(e), 3.343, 3.344`):** Where VA reduced a stabilized (`>= 5-year`) or total evaluation without demonstrating sustained material improvement under the ordinary conditions of life and work, the reduction is **void *ab initio***, requiring **outright CAVC reversal and retroactive reinstatement** from the effective date of the unlawful reduction (*Kitchens v. Brown*, `7 Vet. App. 320, 325 (1995)`; [Playbook 05: Void Rating Reductions](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings)).

blocks.text: 4. Federal Circuit & Supreme Court Review (38 U.S.C. §§ 7292, 502)
A. The Jurisdictional Wall of 38 U.S.C. § 7292(d)(2)
Appealing an adverse CAVC decision to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit crosses the sharpest jurisdictional razor's edge in federal appellate practice:

items: **Affirmative Grant (`38 U.S.C. § 7292(a), (c), (d)(1)`):** The Federal Circuit has exclusive jurisdiction to review a CAVC decision with respect to the validity of a decision of the Court on a **rule of law** (`Pub. L. 107-330, § 402`; *Morgan v. Principi*, `327 F.3d 1357, 1361 (Fed. Cir. 2003)`) or the validity or **interpretation of any statute or regulation** relied upon by the CAVC.

**Absolute Fact & Law-to-Fact Prohibition (`38 U.S.C. § 7292(d)(2)`):** Except to the extent an appeal presents a **constitutional issue**, the Federal Circuit **"may not review `(A)` a challenge to a factual determination, or `(B)` a challenge to a law or regulation as applied to the facts of a particular case"** (*Conway v. Principi*, `353 F.3d 1369, 1372 (Fed. Cir. 2004)`; *Fagan v. Shinseki*, `573 F.3d 1282, 1287 (Fed. Cir. 2009)`).

blocks.text: B. Issue-Framing Engineering to Defeat DOJ Motions to Dismiss

Department of Justice (`DOJ`) Commercial Litigation Branch counsel move to dismiss a substantial percentage of veterans' Federal Circuit appeals under `§ 7292(d)(2)`. Survival turns entirely on **isolating a pure rule-of-law or statutory/regulatory construction error** in the CAVC's opinion rather than disputing record weight:

rows: *"CAVC erred in finding the veteran's combat lay statement outweighed by post-service records."*
*"VA's regulation is facially invalid because it imposes an evidentiary burden conflicting with `38 U.S.C. § 1154(b)`'s statutory combat-relaxation mandate."*
*"CAVC erred in affirming that the veteran's knee pain was not a compensable condition."*
*"CAVC misinterpreted `'disability'` in `38 U.S.C. § 1110` by requiring a formal pathological diagnosis rather than functional impairment of earning capacity."*
*"CAVC erred in failing to apply the benefit of the doubt (`§ 5107(b)`) to the PTSD evidence."*
*"CAVC misinterpreted `'approximate balance'` in `38 U.S.C. § 5107(b)` by requiring an exact mathematical tie rather than nearly equal evidence."*
*"CAVC miscalculated the veteran's SMC step rating on this rating code sheet."*
*"CAVC misinterpreted `'an additional'` in `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(f)(3)` as capping veterans at a single half-step SMC bump despite multiple qualifying disabilities."*

***Barry v. McDonough*, `101 F.4th 1348, 1352–54 (Fed. Cir. 2024)`** ([Master Special Monthly Compensation (SMC) Legal Treatise & Multi-Step Rate Architecture (38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)–(t))](/docs/smc-complete-treatise-and-step-math))
*"CAVC erred in finding the AMA notice letter implicitly denied the COD reopening request."*
*"CAVC misinterpreted `38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)` by importing the legacy implicit-denial doctrine into post-Feb. 19, 2019 AMA decisions."*
***Hamill v. Collins*, `166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. 2026)`** ([Procedural Vehicles for Piercing Finality (The Time-Machine Mechanisms)](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality))
*"CAVC erred in refusing to make the Board consider evidence submitted before the `10182`."*
*"CAVC misinterpreted `38 U.S.C. § 7113` where a timely `VA Form 10182` expressly incorporates 'in-between' post-AOJ submissions by reference."*

***Cash v. Collins*, `No. 24-1811 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 5, 2026)`** ([AMA Three-Lane Strategy, Evidentiary Windows & Board of Veterans' Appeals Litigation Manual (38 U.S.C. §§ 5104C, 7104, 7105, 7113; 38 C.F.R. Parts 3, 19 & 20)](/docs/ama-lanes-and-bva-litigation-manual))

blocks.text: C. Strict Article III Deadlines & Direct 38 U.S.C. § 502 Rulemaking Petitions

items: **Strict Jurisdictional `60-Day` Federal Circuit NOA (`38 U.S.C. § 7292(a)`; `28 U.S.C. § 2107(b)`; `Fed. R. App. P. 4(a)(1)(B)`):** Unlike CAVC's `120-day` `§ 7266(a)` claim-processing deadline (*Henderson*), the **`60-day` deadline** from entry of CAVC judgment to file a Notice of Appeal to the Federal Circuit is **strictly jurisdictional** under *Bowles v. Russell*, `551 U.S. 205, 209–14 (2007)` and **cannot be equitably tolled**! (A petition for writ of certiorari to the U.S. Supreme Court under `38 U.S.C. § 7292(c)` and `28 U.S.C. § 1254(1)` must be filed within **`90 days`** of Federal Circuit judgment per `Sup. Ct. R. 13.1`).

**Direct Federal Circuit Pre-Enforcement Challenges (`38 U.S.C. § 502`):** Under `38 U.S.C. § 502`, veterans' organizations and affected claimants may bypass administrative adjudication altogether and petition the Federal Circuit **directly** to invalidate substantive VA regulations, interpretive rules, or generally applicable `M21-1` Adjudication Procedures Manual provisions (`5 U.S.C. §§ 552(a)(1), 553`).
• ***NOVA v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs*, `981 F.3d 1360, 1365–69 (Fed. Cir. 2020) (en banc)`:** Held that `(1)` generally applicable `M21-1` manual rules are reviewable interpretive rules under `§ 502`, and `(2)` `§ 502` petitions are governed by the **`6-year` statute of limitations in `28 U.S.C. § 2401(a)`**—striking down former `Fed. Cir. Rule 15(f)`'s `60-day` deadline!
• ***MVA v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs*, `7 F.4th 1110 (Fed. Cir. 2021)`:** Exercising `§ 502` jurisdiction to invalidate unlawful AMA regulations, including VA's `38 C.F.R. § 14.636(c)(1)(i)` ban on attorney fees for CUE motions and non-continuous Supplemental Claims ([Accreditation, 38 U.S.C. § 5904 Contingency Fees, Reasonableness Litigation & Equal Access to Justice Act (EAJA, 28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)) Practice Treatise](/docs/attorney-fees-5904-and-eaja-practice)).

lines: **Bitemporal *George v. McDonough* Gate (`596 U.S. 740 (2022)`; `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`):** Winning a Federal Circuit `§ 502` regulatory invalidation (*MVA*) or `§ 7292` reinterpretation (*Saunders*, *Barry*, *Hamill*) applies with full retroactive force to **all open, pending, timely-appealed, `§ 3.156(b)`, and `§ 3.156(c)` claims** (*Harper v. Virginia Dep't of Taxation*, `509 U.S. 86, 97 (1993)`). However, under ***George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)`** and `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`, **that judicial invalidation or reinterpretation CANNOT be used to attack a prior final RO or Board decision via CUE (`38 U.S.C. §§ 5109A, 7111`)** if the adjudicator faithfully applied the regulation or settled interpretation extant when the prior decision became final ([Authority Hierarchy, Temporal Versioning Policy & Citation Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log), [Board of Veterans' Appeals (BVA) CUE Motion Pre-Filing Gate Checklist (38 U.S.C. § 7111; 38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1400–20.1411)](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate)).

blocks.text: 5. Extraordinary Writs of Mandamus (28 U.S.C. § 1651(a)) & CAVC Rule 23 Class Actions
A. All Writs Act Mandamus (28 U.S.C. § 1651(a)): *Cheney*, *Martin* (TRAC) & *Wolfe*

Under the **All Writs Act (`28 U.S.C. § 1651(a)`)**, the CAVC may issue extraordinary writs of mandamus "in aid of its prospective appellate jurisdiction" wherever agency action or inaction frustrates a claimant's path to a reviewable Board decision (*Cox v. West*, `149 F.3d 1360, 1363 (Fed. Cir. 1998)`). Every petitioner must satisfy the three-prong test of ***Cheney v. U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia*, `542 U.S. 367, 380–81 (2004)`**:

items: **Clear and Indisputable Right:** The petitioner has a clear and indisputable legal right to the relief sought;
**No Adequate Alternative Remedy:** The petitioner lacks adequate alternative means (such as an ordinary appeal) to obtain the relief; and
**Equitable Appropriateness:** The issuing court, in its discretion, concludes the writ is appropriate under the circumstances.

blocks.text: 1. Unreasonable Agency Delay: The Six-Factor TRAC Standard (*Martin v. O'Rourke*)

For nearly twenty years, the CAVC evaluated delay petitions under *Costanza v. West*, `12 Vet. App. 133, 134 (1999)`, requiring proof of an "arbitrary refusal to act." In ***Martin v. O'Rourke*, `891 F.3d 1338, 1344–49 (Fed. Cir. 2018)`**, the Federal Circuit **abrogated *Costanza*** and mandated the six-factor balancing framework of *Telecommunications Research & Action Center v. FCC (`TRAC`)*, `750 F.2d 70, 80 (D.C. Cir. 1984)`:

items: The time agencies take to make decisions must be governed by a **"rule of reason"**;
Any **statutory timetable** enacted by Congress supplies content for that rule of reason;
Delays are **far less tolerable when human health and welfare are at stake** (weighing heavily in veterans' benefits claims);
The effect of expediting delayed action on agency activities of a **higher or competing priority**;
The **nature and extent of the interests prejudiced** by the delay; and

**Zero Bad-Faith Requirement:** The Court **need not find any agency impropriety or bad faith** behind agency lassitude to hold delay unreasonable! *(Note: Under Mote v. Wilkie, `976 F.3d 1337, 1343–46 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`, CAVC cannot summarily dismiss a delay petition without applying the TRAC factors merely because VA took a minor ministerial step after the petition was filed).*

blocks.text: 2. The "No Substitute for Appeal" Kill-Switch (*Wolfe* & *Lamb*)
Mandamus **cannot** be used to short-circuit an available administrative appeal:

items: ***Lamb v. Principi*, `284 F.3d 1378, 1384 (Fed. Cir. 2002)`** and ***Wolfe v. McDonough*, `28 F.4th 1348, 1354–59 (Fed. Cir. 2022)`**: In *Wolfe*, even though the Federal Circuit agreed on the statutory merits that `38 C.F.R. § 17.1005(a)(5)` unlawfully barred reimbursement of private-insurance **coinsurance** under `38 U.S.C. § 1725` (while upholding exclusion of deductibles), the Federal Circuit **reversed the CAVC's mandamus writ and class certification** under *Cheney* Prong 2 because claimants possessed an **adequate ordinary remedy** via direct administrative appeal to the BVA and CAVC! See [Playbook 22: Emergency Medical Reimbursement (`§§ 1725/1728`) & PCAFC](/playbooks/22-emergency-medical-reimbursement-1725-1728-and-pcafc).

blocks.text: B. CAVC Rule 23 Aggregate Litigation & Landmark Class Actions

In ***Monk v. Shulkin*, `855 F.3d 1312, 1318–21 (Fed. Cir. 2017)`**, the Federal Circuit reversed nearly three decades of CAVC refusal to hear aggregate claims, holding that the CAVC possesses full authority under the All Writs Act (`28 U.S.C. § 1651(a)`), `38 U.S.C. § 7264(a)`, and inherent judicial power to certify **class actions**—prompting promulgation of **`CAVC Rule 23`**. Four landmark precedents define the strategic boundaries of `CAVC Rule 23` practice:

rows: Certified a nationwide class of legacy appellants waiting **`> 18 months`** after filing a timely Substantive Appeal (`VA Form 9`) for VA to certify and transfer their appeals to the Board (`38 C.F.R. § 19.35`), granting classwide `TRAC` relief ordering certification or affirmative explanation.

**CRITICAL JURISDICTIONAL LIMIT:** In a `§ 7252(a)` *appellate* class action (challenging Palomares radiation dose methodology), **CAVC lacks jurisdiction to include class members who have NOT obtained a final Board decision** (such as veterans with pending RO claims or veterans who never filed a claim)! Every member of an *appeal* class must satisfy `§ 7252(a)`'s Board-decision predicate—sharply distinguishing `§ 7252` appeal classes from `§ 1651(a)` mandamus classes protecting *prospective* jurisdiction!
***Beaudette v. McDonough*, `93 F.4th 1361 (Fed. Cir. 2024)`** (*aff'g* `34 Vet. App. 95 (2021)`)

Unanimously affirmed CAVC class certification and held that `38 U.S.C. § 1720G(c)(1)` ("medical determinations") does **NOT** bar Board (`§ 7104(a)`) and CAVC (`§ 7252(a)`) review of **PCAFC Family Caregiver** eligibility and stipend denials/revocations. *Why mandamus succeeded despite Wolfe:* VHA refused to accept NODs or route caregiver appeals to the Board at all, **blocking the gateway to ordinary appellate review** ([Playbook 22](/playbooks/22-emergency-medical-reimbursement-1725-1728-and-pcafc)).
***Freund v. McDonough*, `114 F.4th 1371 (Fed. Cir. 2024)`** & ***Freund v. Collins*, `No. 21-4168 (Vet. App. class certified Mar. 18, 2026)`**

**Defeating VA "Pick-Off" Mootness & Restoring Closed VACOLS Legacy Appeals:** After automated VACOLS sweeps silently deactivated tens of thousands of timely perfected legacy appeals (`VA Form 9`) due to mail-logging lags, VA reactivated the named petitioners' files and claimed mootness. In *Freund*, `114 F.4th at 1378–83`, the Federal Circuit vacated dismissal under the **"inherently transitory" mootness exception** and held systemic VACOLS closures satisfied `Rule 23` commonality and adequacy. On **March 18, 2026**, CAVC certified the nationwide class (`Dec. 12, 1990 – Feb. 6, 2025` VACOLS closures for purported lack of timely Substantive Appeal), establishing a mandatory **Audit Track (`~28,258` files)** and **Notice Track (`~64,599` files)** that restore **original legacy claim effective dates** ([Historical & Modern VA Forms, Service Records & Rating Code Sheet Lexicon (1945–2026)](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon), [AMA Three-Lane Strategy, Evidentiary Windows & Board of Veterans' Appeals Litigation Manual (38 U.S.C. §§ 5104C, 7104, 7105, 7113; 38 C.F.R. Parts 3, 19 & 20)](/docs/ama-lanes-and-bva-litigation-manual)).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Appealing a Board Denial to Federal Court (CAVC & Federal Circuit): Deadlines, Remands & Writs
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: When the Board of Veterans' Appeals issues a final decision denying all or part of a claim, you can appeal outside VA to an independent federal court: the U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims (CAVC). Unlike VA Regional Offices and the Board, the CAVC does not take new medical evidence—instead, it reviews the existing Board record to decide whether the Board misapplied the law, failed to provide adequate 'reasons or bases' (38 U.S.C. § 7104(d)(1)), or committed clear factual error, often vacating and remanding flawed Board decisions (with government-paid EAJA attorney fees). Decisions of the CAVC can be appealed within 60 days to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit on pure questions of statutory or regulatory interpretation (38 U.S.C. § 7292).
record_clues: A final Board of Veterans' Appeals decision accompanied by VA Form 4597 ('Your Rights to Appeal Our Decision'), which starts the 120-day clock to file a CAVC Notice of Appeal (38 U.S.C. § 7266(a)).

A 'mixed' Board decision that granted one issue (or made favorable factual findings, which are binding on VA under 38 U.S.C. § 5104A and Medrano v. Nicholson) while denying a higher percentage or earlier effective date.
A Joint Motion for Partial Remand (JMPR) negotiated between your appellate attorney and VA General Counsel at the CAVC Rule 33 conference.
Severe illness, hospitalization, homelessness, or VA mail misdelivery that caused a Notice of Appeal to arrive after Day 120 (potentially supporting equitable tolling under Henderson v. Shinseki).
important_cautions: Critical 120-day CAVC trap: filing an AMA Supplemental Claim (VA Form 20-0995) after a Board denial does NOT pause ('toll') the 120-day deadline to appeal to the CAVC! (Only a timely Motion for Board Reconsideration filed within the 120-day window pauses the CAVC clock under Rosler v. Derwinski.) Meanwhile, under AMA, you have up to 1 year after a Board denial to file a Supplemental Claim with new and relevant evidence—meaning many Veterans consult a CAVC appellate attorney well before Day 120.

Board remands cannot be appealed to the CAVC: if the Board remanded an issue back to the Regional Office for another exam or development, that remanded issue is not a 'final decision' and cannot be appealed to the CAVC yet (Kirkpatrick v. Nicholson).

Narrow JMPR waiver trap & benefit-of-the-doubt limits: if your attorney signs an overly narrow Joint Motion for Partial Remand without preserving other arguments and favorable findings, unmentioned arguments on that issue can be waived on remand (Carter v. Shinseki). Also note that under Bufkin v. Collins (2025), the CAVC does not re-weigh close evidence from scratch under the benefit-of-the-doubt rule—making legal and reasons-or-bases challenges essential.

Extraordinary writs (mandamus) cannot bypass regular appeals: the CAVC grants All Writs Act petitions only for extraordinary, unreasonable agency delays where no ordinary administrative appeal path solves the problem (Martin v. O'Rourke; Wolfe v. McDonough).
questions_for_representative: What is the exact 120th calendar day from the mailing date stamped on my Board decision, and should we file a CAVC Notice of Appeal before Day 120 or file a Supplemental Claim with new medical evidence within 1 year?

Does my Board decision contain favorable factual findings (such as conceding an in-service injury or diagnosis) that are legally protected from being overturned by the CAVC or VA on remand (Medrano v. Nicholson; 38 U.S.C. § 5104A)?

If VA's lawyer offers a Joint Motion for Partial Remand (JMPR) at the CAVC, does the draft agreement preserve my right to submit new evidence and argue additional errors on remand (Carter v. Shinseki) while establishing EAJA fee eligibility?

If the CAVC affirms a Board denial—or while a legal issue is appealed within 60 days to the Federal Circuit—should we also file a protective Supplemental Claim or Intent to File within 1 year of the CAVC judgment to protect my effective date?

blocks.text: Winning substantive service connection or a `100%` disability evaluation is only half of a Veterans Law firm's representation: **effective-date selection and historical staging** routinely separate an `$8,000` award from a `$280,000+` retroactive recovery (and determine the corresponding `38 U.S.C. § 5904` past-due fee base). Regional Office (`RO`) raters and the Board of Veterans' Appeals (`BVA`) systematically commit four recurring effective-date errors: `(1)` defaulting to the **date of a VA C&P examination** rather than the date entitlement factually arose; `(2)` ignoring the **`1-year` prior lookback** on increased-rating and TDIU claims (`§ 5110(b)(3)` `[former § 5110(b)(2)]` / `§ 3.400(o)(2)`); `(3)` misapplying **`§ 3.114(a)` liberalizing-law**, **PACT Act**, and **AMA continuous-pursuit (`§ 3.2500`)** rules; and `(4)` failing to assign **staged ratings** across multi-year appeals.

blocks.text: 1. Master Architecture of 38 U.S.C. § 5110 & 38 C.F.R. § 3.400
A. Historical Codification & The Baseline Two-Variable Formula (§ 5110(a)(1))

Modern effective-date law originates in **`Pub. L. 87-825` (`76 Stat. 948`, enacted Oct. 15, 1962, effective December 1, 1962)**, codified from `1959` through `May 6, 1991` as **`former 38 U.S.C. § 3010`** and renumbered **`38 U.S.C. § 5110`** on **May 7, 1991** by `Pub. L. 102-40, § 402(b)(1)` ([Three-Era Title 38 Statutory Crosswalk](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk)). *(Practitioner Kill-Switch: Section `7` of `Pub. L. 87-825` bars using post-1962 liberalized effective-date provisions to award payments prior to December 1, 1962).*

Unless a specific statutory exception in `§ 5110(b)–(n)` or a finality-piercing rule (`38 C.F.R. §§ 3.105(a), 3.156(c), 3.816`) governs, **`38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)(1)`** and **`38 C.F.R. § 3.400` (introductory text)** set the default effective date at the **LATER** of two dates:

items: **Date of Receipt of the Application** (or active `38 C.F.R. § 3.155(b)` Intent to File / pre-March 24, 2015 informal claim); **OR**

**Date Entitlement Arose ("Facts Found")** — the earliest date the evidence of record (medical *or* competent lay evidence) establishes that the legal criteria for service connection or a specific evaluation tier were factually met.

lines: **Cardinal Litigation Rule — "Date Entitlement Arose" Is NEVER "Date of the VA C&P Examination" (*Swain* & *McGrath*):**

* ***McGrath v. Gober*, `14 Vet. App. 28, 35 (2000)`:** The date a medical diagnosis or nexus opinion is written down is merely the date of *documentation*, not necessarily the date the disability first manifested or worsened. Adjudicators must weigh lay testimony, private records, and retrospective medical inferences to determine when entitlement factually arose.

* ***Swain v. McDonald*, `27 Vet. App. 219, 224–25 (2015)`:** Even where a VASRD code requires a specialized objective test—such as Maryland CNC speech discrimination / puretone audiometry under `38 C.F.R. § 4.85(a)`—`§ 4.85(a)` is an *evaluative* rule, **not an effective-date rule**! When a veteran files a claim (or experiences observable hearing/functional decline during a pending appeal) and VA does not administer the confirmatory C&P test until years later, VA **cannot** mechanically assign the C&P examination date without adjudicating when the compensable impairment factually began.

blocks.text: B. Complete Subsection-by-Subsection Statutory Map of 38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)–(n)

lines: **Statutory Citation Disambiguation (`§ 5110(b)(2)` vs. `(b)(3)` & `§ 5110(f)` vs. `(n)`):**

1. **`Pub. L. 112-154, § 506(a)` (`126 Stat. 1165`, Aug. 6, 2012):** Inserted a temporary `2-year` Fully Developed Claim (`FDC`) incentive (`Aug. 6, 2013 – Aug. 5, 2015`) as current **`§ 5110(b)(2)`**, redesignating the classic `1-year` increased-compensation lookback (`Pub. L. 94-71`, `1975`) from `former § 5110(b)(2)` to **`§ 5110(b)(3)`** and the `1-year` permanent-and-total pension lookback from `former § 5110(b)(3)` to **`§ 5110(b)(4)`**. Because pre-2012 Federal Circuit/CAVC cases (*Harper*, *Gaston*, *Dalton*) and `38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2)` authority notes cite `§ 5110(b)(2)`, **always cite `38 U.S.C. § 5110(b)(3) [former § 5110(b)(2)]`** in briefs!

2. **`§ 5110(f)` vs. `(i)` vs. `(n)`:** Subsection **`(f)`** governs adding existing dependents within `1 year` of reaching a **`30%+` combined rating**; subsection **`(n)`** governs `1-year` lookbacks for **marriage, birth, or adoption** (`§ 3.401(b)`); and subsection **`(i)`** governs **`10 U.S.C. §§ 1552/1553` military record corrections and discharge upgrades** (`§ 3.400(g)`).

rows: Initial claim or timely-pursued Supplemental Claim
**Later** of date of receipt of claim/ITF OR date entitlement factually arose (*Swain*, `27 Vet. App. 219`; *McGrath*, `14 Vet. App. 28`).
AMA review option filed within **`1 year`** of AOJ `(A)–(C)`, BVA `(D)`, or CAVC `(E)` decision
Preserves initial claim/ITF application date, still bounded by "facts found" (*MVA v. Sec'y*, `7 F.4th 1110 (Fed. Cir. 2021)`).
Supplemental Claim (`§ 5108`) filed **`> 1 year`** after prior decision
No earlier than receipt of Supplemental Claim (or its active ITF), *unless* `§ 3.156(c)`, CUE, `§ 3.114(a)`, PACT, or *Nehmer* applies.
Original disability compensation claim received within **`1 year` after discharge/release**
**Day following discharge or release** (assuming disability existed at/within 1-yr window). **NO equitable tolling** (***Arellano v. McDonough*, `598 U.S. 1 (2023)`** `9–0`).
Original Fully Developed Claim (`FDC`) received **`Aug. 6, 2013 – Aug. 5, 2015`** (`Pub. L. 112-154, § 506`)
Up to **`1 year` prior** to receipt of original FDC (sunset Aug. 6, 2015 upon standardization of `VA Form 21-0966` ITF).
Claim or ITF for **increased disability compensation** (including **TDIU** & **SMC**) received within **`1 year`** of ascertainable worsening
**Earliest date factually ascertainable** increase occurred within `1 year` prior to complete claim or ITF (*Harper*, `10 Vet. App. 125`; *Gaston*, `605 F.3d 979`; *Dalton*, `21 Vet. App. 23`).
**Wartime Disability Pension (`Ch. 15`)** claim received within **`1 year`** of becoming permanently & totally (`P&T`) disabled
Date veteran became `P&T` disabled if `P&T` severity prevented applying for `>= 30 days` immediately after onset ([Playbook 21](/playbooks/21-overpayment-waivers-incompetency-and-wartime-pension)).
**`38 U.S.C. § 1151`** VA medical care / VR&E injury claim received within **`1 year`** of injury/aggravation
**Exact date injury or aggravation was suffered** (if filed `> 1 year` later, date of claim receipt).
**Survivor DIC (`Ch. 13`)** or **Survivors Pension** claim received within **`1 year`** of veteran's death
**First day of the month in which death occurred** (even if veteran died on the `31st` of the month!).
Child's separate DIC claim (`(e)(1)`) within **`1 year`** of entitlement arising, or child turning `18` (`(e)(2)`)
First day of month child's entitlement arose (`(e)(1)`), or statutory age-`18` / school-attendance transition date (`(e)(2)`).
Proof of existing dependents submitted within **`1 year` of notification** of a rating action establishing **`>= 30%`** combined SC
**Relates back to the effective date of the qualifying `30%+` rating** (frequently worth years of retroactive dependency add-ons!).
Award or increase pursuant to a **liberalizing Act or administrative VA issue**

Facts found, **never earlier than effective date of the Act/issue**, and **max `1 year` prior** to claim/ITF or VA-initiated review (*McCay*, `106 F.3d 1577`; *Ortiz v. McDonough*, `6 F.4th 1285`). *(Superseded for PACT DIC re-evaluations by `38 U.S.C. § 1305` notwithstanding `§ 5110`!)*
Improved Pension deferred/reduced on anticipated income where actual lower `IVAP` proof arrives **before end of next calendar year**
Retroactive adjustment per facts found for that calendar/medical-expense year ([Playbook 21](/playbooks/21-overpayment-waivers-incompetency-and-wartime-pension)).
Readjudication following **`10 U.S.C. § 1552` (BCMR/BCNR)** correction or **`10 U.S.C. § 1553` (DRB)** discharge upgrade

Original VA claim within `1 yr` of upgrade: **date upgrade application filed** (`DD-149`/`DD-293`); reopened disallowed VA claim: **latest** of `(1)` upgrade filing, `(2)` prior disallowed VA claim, or `(3)` `1 yr` prior to VA reopening *(unless `§ 3.156(c)(3)` pre-existing STRs pierce the cap — [Playbook 03](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c))*.
Active-duty death report/finding by Service Secretary (claim within **`1 year`** of report/finding)
First day of month of death fixed in report (excluding periods covered by active-duty pay/allotments).
Surviving spouse / child reinstatement within **`1 year`** of final annulment decree (`(k)`) or death/divorce ending remarriage (`(l)`)
Date judicial annulment/divorce decree became final or date of subsequent spouse's death.
Proof of **marriage, birth, or adoption** received within **`1 year`** of the event
**Exact date of marriage, birth, or adoption** (assuming veteran already held `>= 30%` SC on that date).

blocks.text: 2. Legacy Continuous Prosecution (§ 20.1103) vs. AMA Continuous Pursuit (§ 5110(a)(2)(A)–(E), § 3.2500)
A. AMA Lane-Switching Mechanics (38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)(2)(A)–(E); 38 C.F.R. § 3.2500)

Effective **February 19, 2019** (`Pub. L. 115-55`; `84 FR 138, 170`), Congress replaced single-track Legacy appellate prosecution with **AMA continuous pursuit**. An initial claim's filing date (or ITF date) remains continuously alive across multiple sequential reviews so long as the claimant files a permitted action **within `1 year`** after notice of each decision:

items: **After an Initial or Supplemental AOJ Decision (`§ 5110(a)(2)(A)–(C)`):** Within `1 year`, file `(A)` a Higher-Level Review (`VA Form 20-0996`, `§ 5104B`), `(B)` a Supplemental Claim with new and relevant evidence (`VA Form 20-0995`, `§ 5108`), **or** `(C)` a Board Notice of Disagreement (`VA Form 10182`, `§ 7105`). *(Note: You cannot file back-to-back HLRs on an HLR decision—switch to `0995` or `10182`).*

**After an AMA Board (`BVA`) Decision (`§ 5110(a)(2)(D)` & `§ 7266`):** Either appeal to the CAVC within **`120 days`** (`38 U.S.C. § 7266(a)`) **OR** file a **`§ 5108` Supplemental Claim (`VA Form 20-0995`)** with new and relevant evidence within **`1 year`** of the BVA decision (`§ 5110(a)(2)(D)`). *(An HLR is barred after BVA review under `§ 5104B(b)(2)`).*
**After a `CAVC` Decision (`§ 5110(a)(2)(E)`):** File a **`§ 5108` Supplemental Claim (`VA Form 20-0995`)** with new and relevant evidence within **`1 year`** after the CAVC decision!

blocks.text: B. The Two Judicial-Appeal Continuous-Pursuit Traps (Legacy vs. AMA + *MVA v. Sec'y*)

rows: **Trap 1: Legacy CAVC Affirmance Break** · *(Appeals NOT in AMA)*

In a **Legacy** appeal, a CAVC affirmance (once mandate issues) renders the underlying BVA denial **final** (`§ 7291`), permanently severing Legacy continuous prosecution! Unlike AMA, filing a reopening request within 1 year after a Legacy CAVC affirmance **does NOT preserve the original claim date**—any subsequent grant takes the **date of reopening** unless `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)` service records or CUE applies ([Procedural Vehicles Piercing Finality](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality)).
**Trap 2: AMA Post-CAVC (`§ 5110(a)(2)(E)`) vs. The Federal Circuit Gap (*MVA v. Sec'y*)**
`38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)(2)(E)`; ***Military-Veterans Advocacy v. Sec'y of Veterans Affairs*, `7 F.4th 1110, 1131–45 (Fed. Cir. 2021)`**

Under AMA, `§ 5110(a)(2)(E)` preserves continuous pursuit for `1 year` after a **CAVC** decision via a `§ 5108` Supplemental Claim—**even after a CAVC affirmance**! **HOWEVER**, Congress omitted a `1-year post-Federal Circuit / SCOTUS` subparagraph in `§ 5110(a)(2)`! Originally, VA promulgated `38 C.F.R. § 3.2500(b)` (barring concurrent Supplemental Claims while a Federal Circuit appeal was pending) and `§ 3.155` intro language (barring ITFs for Supplemental Claims), trapping veterans whose Federal Circuit appeals lasted `> 1 year` past the CAVC judgment. · • **The *MVA v. Sec'y* Rescue (`7 F.4th at 1134, 1142`):** On July 30, 2021, the Federal Circuit **invalidated both `38 C.F.R. § 3.2500(b)`'s concurrent federal-court bar and `§ 3.155`'s exclusion of Supplemental Claims from the ITF framework** (as well as `§ 14.636(c)(1)(i)`'s fee restriction on `>1-yr` Supplemental Claims). · • **Mandatory Appellate Protocol:** Whenever a firm appeals an AMA CAVC affirmance to the Federal Circuit (`§ 7292`), **calendar `Day 330` from the CAVC decision** and file a **protective `VA Form 21-0966` Intent to File AND/OR `VA Form 20-0995` Supplemental Claim** (with new and relevant evidence) **within `1 year` of the CAVC decision** so the initial AMA effective date survives even if the Federal Circuit affirms `18 months` later!

blocks.text: C. Intent-to-File Consumption (§ 3.155(b)) vs. Pre-2015 Informal Claims (*Pacheco* & *Hazan*)

items: **Pre-March 24, 2015 Informal Claims (`former §§ 3.155(a), 3.157(b)`):** Before `79 FR 57660` (eff. **March 24, 2015**, [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: Former 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.155(a) & 3.157(b) Informal Claims (Repealed March 24, 2015)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.155-3.157b-informal-claims-pre-2015)), *any* written communication identifying the benefit sought (`Shea v. Wilkie`, `926 F.3d 1362 (Fed. Cir. 2019)`) or any VAMC/uniformed-services examination or hospitalization report for an already service-connected condition (`former § 3.157(b)`) operated as an informal claim. In ***Pacheco v. Gibson*, `27 Vet. App. 21, 29–30 (2014) (en banc)`**, the CAVC held that where a veteran had a decades-long series of VAMC treatment reports for a `0%` or compensable SC disability, the **earliest** qualifying VAMC report showing worsening—not merely the last report within a year of a formal filing—triggered an unadjudicated `§ 3.157(b)` claim for increase (*see also* ***Hazan v. Gober*, `10 Vet. App. 511, 518–21 (1997)`** on non-abandonment of pending increase claims). *(Citation Disambiguation: Do not confuse pre-2015 informal-claim case law with [`VAOPGCPREC 8-97`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index), `62 FR 15567`, which governs secondary service connection under `§ 3.310` for `38 U.S.C. § 1151` disabilities).*

**Post-March 24, 2015 Single-Active-ITF Consumption Rule (`38 C.F.R. § 3.155(b)(4)–(6)`; *Sellers v. Wilkie*, `965 F.3d 1328 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`):**
• **One Active ITF Per Benefit Type (`§ 3.155(b)(6)`):** A claimant may have **only ONE active `VA Form 21-0966` Intent to File** at a time for each general benefit category (`compensation`, `pension`, or `survivors benefits`). Submitting a second compensation ITF while an earlier compensation ITF is still active marks the second ITF as an **invalid duplicate**—it does **not** extend the 1-year window or create a backup placeholder!
• **Immediate Consumption on First Complete Claim (`§ 3.155(b)(4)–(5)`):** The **first** complete claim (`VA Form 21-526EZ` or, post-*MVA v. Sec'y*, `VA Form 20-0995` Supplemental Claim) received within `1 year` **immediately consumes** the active ITF (covering all conditions filed on that same calendar day). If counsel intends to file an additional claim the next week, counsel **must file a brand-new `VA Form 21-0966` AFTER** submitting the first claim!

blocks.text: 3. Increased-Rating 1-Year Prior Lookback (§ 5110(b)(3) [former (b)(2)], § 3.400(o)(2)) vs. Pending-Claim Increases

When adjudicating an increased evaluation (including **TDIU** under ***Dalton v. Nicholson*, `21 Vet. App. 23, 32–35 (2007)`** and **SMC** as an ancillary rate increase), practitioners must separate the timeline into **three distinct legal zones** anchored around receipt of the complete claim or active ITF:
Zone 1 (> 1 Year Prior to Complete Claim or Active ITF)

items: **Bypass Vehicles:** Screen exclusively for `(a)` pre-March 24, 2015 `former § 3.157(b)` VAMC outpatient/hospitalization reports (*Pacheco*), `(b)` Legacy `§ 3.156(b)` `1-year` post-decision VAMC records (*Lang v. Wilkie*, `971 F.3d 1348 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`), `(c)` newly associated service department records (`§ 3.156(c)`), `(d)` post-Feb. 19, 2019 AMA silent omissions (`§ 5104(b)` / *Hamill v. Collins*, `166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. 2026)`), or `(e)` `§ 3.105(a)` / `§ 7111` CUE ([Playbook 04](/playbooks/04-unadjudicated-tdiu-informal-claims-smc)).

blocks.text: Zone 2 (Within 1 Year *Prior* to Complete Claim or Active ITF — § 5110(b)(3) / § 3.400(o)(2))

items:
**Governing Standard (*Harper*, *Gaston*, *Dalton*):**
• ***Harper v. Brown*, `10 Vet. App. 125, 126 (1997)`:** When medical or lay evidence demonstrates a factually ascertainable increase within the `1-year` window preceding claim receipt, the effective date is the **exact date of that ascertainable increase**; if the increase occurred *more* than `1 year` before the claim and remained static without further escalation during the 1-year window, the effective date defaults to **date of claim receipt**.
• ***Gaston v. Shinseki*, `605 F.3d 979, 983–86 (Fed. Cir. 2010)`:** Affirming *Harper*, the Federal Circuit held that `"an increase in disability had occurred"` within `1 year` prior to the claim requires evidence of **identifiable worsening/escalation during that 1-year lookback window**, not merely proof that the veteran *already* suffered static higher-level severity years earlier. *(Litigation Tip: Audit emergency-room visits, medication escalations, assistive-device prescriptions, flare logs, or **date of work cessation / termination** within the 12-month pre-claim window to satisfy Gaston!).*
• ***Dalton v. Nicholson*, `21 Vet. App. 23, 32–35 (2007)`:** Because TDIU (`38 C.F.R. § 4.16`) is legally an increased-compensation evaluation once service connection is in place, **`§ 5110(b)(3)` `[former (b)(2)]` / `§ 3.400(o)(2)` applies in full to TDIU claims**—meaning a veteran who stops working due to SC disabilities on June 1, 2024 and files a TDIU claim (or ITF) by June 1, 2025 wins a **June 1, 2024** TDIU effective date! (*Dalton*, `21 Vet. App. at 38–40`, also independently bars C&P examiners from rejecting lay symptom onset solely for lack of contemporaneous medical records).

**Exact `eCFR` `§ 3.400(o)(2)` + `§ 3.155(b)` ITF Mechanics (No False "2-Year Pre-ITF" Stacking!):**
• Verbatim `38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2)` (`79 FR 57660`, [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.114, 3.400, 3.2500, 3.654, 3.665, 3.700 & 3.701 (Effective Dates, Liberalizing Laws, Continuous Pursuit, Drill/Incarceration Adjustments, Severance/Separation Recoupment & Benefit Elections)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.114-3.400-3.700-effective-dates-offsets)) awards the earliest factually ascertainable date *"if a **complete claim or intent to file a claim** is received within 1 year from such date, otherwise, date of receipt of claim."*
• **Lawful `~24-Month` Span From Formal Claim:** If worsening occurs on **May 1, 2024**, the veteran submits `VA Form 21-0966` (ITF) on **April 25, 2025** (within `1 year` of May 1, 2024!), and files `VA Form 21-526EZ` on **April 20, 2026** (within `1 year` of the ITF), the **May 1, 2024** effective date is locked in—almost **two full years** before the `21-526EZ` arrived!
• **Kill-Switch:** You **cannot** reach *more* than `1 year` prior to the ITF itself (`§ 3.400(o)(2)` measures `1 year` prior to the ITF when perfected via ITF, or `1 year` prior to the complete claim when no ITF was used—never `1 year` before the ITF *plus* another year!).

blocks.text: Zone 3 (*After* Claim or ITF Receipt While Claim/Appeal Is Pending — § 5110(a)(1) / § 3.400(o)(1))

items: **Rule (*Swain* & *Chotta*):** Once the claim or ITF has been received, `Gaston`'s 1-year lookback hurdle **disappears**; under `§ 5110(a)(1)` and `§ 3.400(o)(1)`, any increase occurring while the claim or appeal is pending takes effect on the **date the factual criteria were met** (lay testimony of worsening, surgery date, CPAP prescription, work cessation), **never** reflexively delayed to a later VA C&P exam (*Swain*, `27 Vet. App. at 224`). Under ***Chotta v. Peake*, `22 Vet. App. 80, 84–86 (2008)`**, when lay or clinical evidence suggests higher historical severity during an unexamined multi-year gap, VA's duty to assist (`§ 5103A(d)`) requires requesting a **retrospective medical opinion** assessing historical disability levels!

blocks.text: 4. Liberalizing Laws & VA Issues (38 U.S.C. § 5110(g); 38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)) vs. PACT Act & *Nehmer*
A. What Qualifies as a "Liberalizing Law or VA Issue" (*Spencer*, *Routen*, *Ortiz v. McDonough*)
Under `38 U.S.C. § 5110(g)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)`, not every favorable legal development triggers a `1-year` liberalizing lookback:

items: ***Spencer v. Brown*, `17 F.3d 368, 372–73 (Fed. Cir. 1994)` & *Routen v. West*, `142 F.3d 1434, 1440–42 (Fed. Cir. 1998)`:** A liberalizing law or VA issue must be a **statute enacted by Congress** or an **administrative regulation/issue promulgated by the Secretary** that brings about a **substantive change** creating a new basis of entitlement or removing an evidentiary hurdle. **Judicial decisions** of the Supreme Court, Federal Circuit, or CAVC reinterpreting existing statutes or regulations (e.g., *Barry*, *Laska*, *Walker*) **are NOT `§ 3.114(a)` liberalizing laws**—courts declare what the statute/regulation *always* meant!

***Ortiz v. McDonough*, `6 F.4th 1285, 1292–97 (Fed. Cir. 2021)`:** Reversing *Foreman v. Shulkin*, `29 Vet. App. 146 (2018)`, the Federal Circuit held that `38 C.F.R. § 3.304(f)(3)` (`75 FR 39843` / `41092`, eff. July 13, 2010—relaxing stressor corroboration for fear-of-hostile-military-activity PTSD) **IS a liberalizing VA issue under `§ 3.114(a)`**, confirming that regulatory amendments eliminating corroboration or evidentiary proof barriers qualify even when the underlying diagnosis (`PTSD`) already existed! *(Citation Note: Always distinguish **Ortiz v. McDonough**, `6 F.4th 1285 (Fed. Cir. 2021)` on `§ 3.114(a)` from **Ortiz v. Principi**, `274 F.3d 1361 (Fed. Cir. 2001)` on `§ 5107(b)` benefit-of-the-doubt equipoise).*

blocks.text: B. Strict Effective-Date Mechanics Under § 3.114(a)(1)–(3) (*McCay v. Brown*)
In ***McCay v. Brown*, `106 F.3d 1577, 1580–82 (Fed. Cir. 1997)`**, the Federal Circuit established the three ironclad temporal boundaries of `§ 5110(g)` / `§ 3.114(a)`:

items: **Continuous Substantive Eligibility:** The claimant must have met all substantive eligibility criteria **on the effective date of the liberalizing Act/issue**, and that eligibility must have existed **continuously** from that date through the date of claim or administrative determination (`§ 3.114(a)` intro).

**Absolute Statutory Floor (`§ 5110(g)`):** The effective date can **NEVER precede the effective date of the liberalizing Act or VA issue** (*McCay*, `106 F.3d at 1581`). *(If the disease was not diagnosed until *after* the Act's effective date, `§ 3.114(a)` continuous eligibility on the Act's effective date fails and standard `§ 5110(a)`/`(b)` rules govern).*

**`Within 1 Year` (`§ 3.114(a)(1)`) vs. `More Than 1 Year` (`§ 3.114(a)(3)`):**
• **Reviewed within `1 year` of the Act/issue's effective date** (`(a)(1)`): Effective on the **effective date of the Act or VA issue**.
• **Claim/ITF or VA review `> 1 year` after the Act/issue's effective date** (`(a)(2)–(3)`): Retroactive **up to `1 year` prior to receipt of the claimant's application/ITF** (or date of administrative determination on VA-initiated review), capped no earlier than the Act's effective date!

blocks.text: C. Contrast Matrix: § 3.114(a) vs. PACT Act (Pub. L. 117-168) vs. *Nehmer* (§ 3.816) & § 1305 DIC

rows: Floor = effective date of Act/regulation (e.g., **June 25, 2024** for `89 FR 32361` COD overhaul; **Jan. 2, 2025** / **Jan. 10, 2025** for `§§ 3.320a–3.320b` burn-pit IFRs). Up to **`1 year` prior** to claim/ITF if filed `> 1 year` later (`§ 3.114(a)(3)`).
**PACT Act Veteran Disability Claims** · *(`Pub. L. 117-168`, enacted **Aug. 10, 2022**)*
`Pub. L. 117-168` (`136 Stat. 1759`); VA Aug. 2023 extension notice; `38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)(3)`

• **Filed (or ITF submitted) on or before `August 14, 2023`** *(extended from Aug. 9, 2023 due to `va.gov` portal volume)*: Effective **August 10, 2022**, provided the presumptive condition existed on Aug. 10, 2022 (or date of post-Aug. 10, 2022 diagnosis if later). · • **Filed `after August 14, 2023`:** Governed by **`38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)(3)`**—eligible for up to **`1 year` prior lookback** from receipt of the claim or active ITF (never earlier than **Aug. 10, 2022**), provided the PACT presumptive condition existed continuously from Aug. 10, 2022!

**SUPERSEDES `§ 5110(g)`!** Where a prior DIC claim was denied and the survivor elects re-evaluation under a post-Aug. 10, 2022 presumption (including PACT hypertension/MGUS or burn-pit cancers), payment takes effect *"notwithstanding section 5110"* **all the way back to the original denied DIC claim** ([Playbook 08](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical))!
***Nehmer* Herbicide Class Claims & Blue Water Navy**

**OVERRIDES `§ 3.114(a)`** for covered Republic of Vietnam / `§ 1116A` offshore herbicide conditions denied or pending `>= Sept. 25, 1985`—paying back to the **original denied/pending claim date** (or date disability arose), *except* that PACT-added **hypertension and MGUS** (and newly added Thailand/Laos/Cambodia/Guam locations outside `§ 1116A`) are excluded from *Nehmer* class retroactivity ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc)).

blocks.text: 5. Staged Ratings Across Multi-Year Appeals & The §§ 3.343 / 3.344 Stabilization Distinction
A. Mandatory Staging on Both Initial (Fenderson) and Increased-Rating (Hart) Appeals

items: **Initial Service-Connection Appeals (***Fenderson v. West*, `12 Vet. App. 119, 126 (1999)`**):** Whenever service connection is initially granted following a multi-year claim or appeal, VA **cannot** fixate solely on the veteran's current severity at the time of the final C&P examination (`"snapshot rating"`). Separate **"staged" disability percentages** must be assigned for distinct historical periods whenever the evidence demonstrates fluctuating or progressive severity from the effective date forward. *(Citation Precision: Always cite **Fenderson v. West**, `12 Vet. App. 119 (1999)`—never mis-cite as "Fenderson v. Gober").*

**Increased-Rating Appeals (***Hart v. Mansfield*, `21 Vet. App. 505, 509–10 (2007)`**):** Extended *Fenderson* in full to **claims for increased evaluation** (spanning Zone 2's `1-year` pre-claim lookback through Zone 3's entire multi-year appellate pendency), requiring staged evaluations whenever disability severity rose or fluctuated across distinct intervals.

blocks.text: B. What *Reizenstein* & *Singleton* Actually Held on Retrospective Staged Downgrades (§§ 3.343(a) & 3.344)

A classic appellate trap arises when the Board grants a multi-year retroactive appeal via staged ratings that **step UP and then step DOWN** inside the same decision—for example, awarding `100%` from `2014 to 2020` (`6 years`!) and `50%` from `2020 to present`:

items:
**Why `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.343(a)` and `3.344` Do NOT Apply (*Reizenstein* & *Singleton*):**
• ***Reizenstein v. Shinseki*, `583 F.3d 1331, 1336–38 (Fed. Cir. 2009)`:** Held that `38 C.F.R. § 3.343(a)` (requiring proof of "material improvement" before reducing a total disability rating) applies **prospectively** to reductions of *ongoing, running awards* upon which a beneficiary relies for living expenses—**NOT** to a temporary retrospective `100%` stage assigned simultaneously alongside a lower subsequent stage in a single retroactive decision.
• ***Singleton v. Shinseki*, `659 F.3d 1332, 1341–44 (Fed. Cir. 2011)`:** Extended *Reizenstein* to **`38 C.F.R. § 3.344`** (`5-year` stabilized-rating heightened proof under [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.105(d)–(i), 3.343, 3.344, 3.951, 3.953 & 3.957 (Rating Reductions, Stabilization & Statutory Protections)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.105e-3.344-3.951-3.957-reductions) and [Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings)), holding that even when an earlier retrospective stage exceeds `5 years` in duration (`e.g., 2014–2020`), `§ 3.344`'s "sustained improvement under the ordinary conditions of life" standard does **not** govern a retrospective staged rating, nor does staging violate Fifth Amendment due process.

**HOW TO WIN ANYWAY — The Affirmative Evidentiary & Reasons-or-Bases Burden:** Even though `§§ 3.343(a)` and `3.344` do not apply to retrospective staging, *Singleton* and *Fenderson* do **not** give the Board license to guess or manufacture an arbitrary downgrade date! To step a staged rating *down* on Date `X`, the Board must cite **affirmative, adequate medical/factual evidence** (`Chotta`, `22 Vet. App. at 84`; `38 U.S.C. § 5107(b)` equipoise; `§ 7104(d)(1)` reasons or bases) demonstrating that the veteran's symptomatology *actually improved* below the higher DC criteria on Date `X` (and did not merely reflect temporary medication masking barred under *Ingram* where the DC lacks medication language, or a single isolated "good day" exam!). Conversely, once a running award *is* placed into active monthly payment, any *subsequent* VA proposal to reduce a `5-year+` running tier triggers the full void-ab-initio shield of `§§ 3.105(e)` and `3.344` ([Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings))!

blocks.text: 6. Bitemporal *George v. McDonough* Matrix (CUE vs. Open-Claim Only)

Before attacking a historical effective-date error, screen every theory through ***George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)`**, **`38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`**, and the [`Mandatory Board CUE Pre-Filing Gate`](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate):

headers: Operational Pleading Rule (`CUE` vs. Open / Finality-Piercing Vehicle)
rows: **Ignoring Undisputed `1-Year` Post-Discharge Filing (`§ 5110(b)(1)`) or `1-Year` Post-Death DIC Filing (`§ 5110(d)`)**

Positive statutory text since **Dec. 1, 1962** (`Pub. L. 87-825`). If the C-file date-stamp proves receipt within `1 year` of discharge/death and undisputed record facts show the disability existed, assigning claim-receipt date is textbook **RO/Board CUE (`§ 3.105(a)` / `§ 7111`)**.

Positive statute since `Pub. L. 94-71` (`1975`). However, because CUE bars re-weighing debatable facts (`§ 20.1403(d)(3)`), CUE succeeds only where **undisputed** contemporaneous records (e.g., inpatient surgical/test results in VA possession post-July 21, 1992 per [`VAOPGCPREC 12-95`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index)) left **zero room for debate** that the higher DC criteria were met on an earlier date within the `1-year` window. On open/pending claims, invoke `§ 5107(b)` equipoise!
**Unadjudicated Pre-Mar. 24, 2015 `§ 3.157(b)` VAMC Report (*Pacheco*) or AMA `§ 5104(b)` Silent Omission (*Hamill*)**
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** *(Pending Unadjudicated Claim — No CUE Burden!)*

Better than CUE: an unadjudicated pre-March 24, 2015 `§ 3.157(b)` report (where no subsequent final decision adjudicated the increase) or a silent post-Feb. 19, 2019 AMA omission (*Hamill v. Collins*, `166 F.4th 1030`) remains **legally pending**, adjudicated under `§ 5107(b)` benefit of the doubt ([Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log); [Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon))!
**Post-*MVA v. Sec'y* (`2021`) Concurrent Supplemental Claim (`§ 3.2500(b)`) or Supplemental ITF (`§ 3.155`)**
**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** *(for pre-July 30, 2021 final decisions)*

Under *George* and [`VAOPGCPREC 25-95`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index), faithful application of `38 C.F.R. § 3.2500(b)` or `§ 3.155` *before* the Federal Circuit invalidated them on **July 30, 2021** (`7 F.4th 1110`) **cannot** constitute CUE against a prior final pre-July 30, 2021 decision; applies to all open/pending claims and post-July 30, 2021 filings.
**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** *(for `2018–2021` final decisions under Foreman)*

Final `2018–July 2021` denials applying *Foreman v. Shulkin* are shielded from CUE by `§ 20.1403(e)` change-in-interpretation rules; pursue via open appeal, `§ 3.156(c)` service records, or a new `VA Form 20-0995` (`1-year` lookback under `§ 3.114(a)(3)`).

Associating missing STRs, unit/deck logs, or military clinical files mandates reconsideration and carries the effective date back to the **original previously denied claim** ([Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) Service Department Records (Pre-Oct. 6, 2006 vs. Current)](/cfr/38-cfr-3.156c), [Playbook 03](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c)).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: How VA Effective Dates & Staged Ratings Work: Avoiding the 'Date of C&P Exam' Mistake
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: When VA grants service connection or a higher disability percentage after years of claims or appeals, two questions control your retroactive back pay: (1) What is the lawful effective date (38 U.S.C. § 5110; 38 C.F.R. § 3.400)? and (2) Did your symptoms fluctuate or worsen across different periods so VA must assign 'staged ratings' (separate percentages for distinct time slices under Fenderson v. West and Hart v. Mansfield)? A classic VA error is setting your effective date on the day a C&P examiner saw you—confusing the date a doctor wrote down your symptoms with the earlier date your claim/Intent to File was received or the date your disability actually arose or worsened.
record_clues: A VA Rating Decision or Award Letter setting the effective date on the exact date of a VA C&P examination or private DBQ rather than the claim date, Intent to File date, or day after military discharge (if filed within 1 year of separation).

An increased-rating or TDIU grant ignoring VA or private medical notes showing the disability clearly worsened within the 12 months BEFORE the claim or Intent to File was received (1-year lookback under 38 U.S.C. § 5110(b)(3) and 38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2); Dalton v. Nicholson).

A PACT Act grant omitting the August 10, 2022 effective-date backstop on a claim or Intent to File submitted on or before August 14, 2023—or omitting up to 1 year of pre-claim lookback under 38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)(3) on post-August 14, 2023 PACT filings where diagnosis predated the claim.
A multi-year appeal assigning one low percentage for the entire early period and stepping up only on the date of a recent exam without evaluating earlier medical and lay evidence for staged ratings.
important_cautions: Strict 1-year post-discharge rule (Arellano v. McDonough): in 2023, the U.S. Supreme Court held that the 1-year window after military separation to get an effective date back to the day after discharge (38 U.S.C. § 5110(b)(1)) is strictly fixed and CANNOT be extended through equitable tolling.

No 'double' 2-year lookback & no duplicate Intent to File: on an increased-rating claim, the 1-year lookback under 38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2) reaches at most 1 year prior to your complete claim OR active Intent to File (never 1 year before an Intent to File plus another year), and filing a second VA Form 21-0966 Intent to File for the same general benefit while an earlier one is still open has no effect (38 C.F.R. § 3.155(b)(6)).

Court decisions are NOT 'liberalizing laws': under Spencer v. Brown and Routen v. West, a new court decision reinterpreting an existing statute or regulation does NOT qualify as a 'liberalizing law or VA issue' under 38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a), and under George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e), cannot establish Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) against an older final decision.

Retrospective staged step-downs inside a single retroactive grant do not trigger 5-year stabilization notice rules (Singleton v. Shinseki), though VA must still back any staged step-down with solid medical evidence and clear reasons.
questions_for_representative: Why did VA pick the date of my C&P examination as my effective date instead of my Intent to File date, claim date, or the earlier date my medical records and lay statements show the condition existed or worsened (Swain v. McDonald)?
For my increased-rating or TDIU claim, do my VA or private clinical notes show ascertainable worsening during the 12 months BEFORE my claim or Intent to File under 38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2)?
If my appeal spanned several years, should we request Fenderson / Hart staged ratings for each distinct time period supported by my treatment records?
Did newly associated official military or unit records play a role in granting my claim, which could unlock an effective date all the way back to an earlier denied claim under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)?

Francway v. Wilkie, 940 F.3d 1304 (Fed. Cir. 2019) (en banc)
