blocks.text: 1. Three-Element Direct Service Connection (38 U.S.C. §§ 1110, 1131; 38 C.F.R. § 3.303(a)–(d))
A. Reconciling *Shedden*, *Hickson*, and *Caluza*

Under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.303(a)`**, service connection may be granted for any disability resulting from disease or injury incurred in or aggravated by active service, evaluated upon "the entire history of the veteran's service as shown by official records and other pertinent medical and lay evidence." The Federal Circuit and CAVC express the governing tripartite test in two complementary formulations—***Shedden v. Principi*, `381 F.3d 1163, 1166–67 (Fed. Cir. 2004)`** and ***Hickson v. West*, `12 Vet. App. 247, 253 (1999)`** (refining ***Caluza v. Brown*, `7 Vet. App. 498, 506 (1995)`**, *aff'd per curiam*, `78 F.3d 604 (Fed. Cir. 1996)`):

items:
**Element 1 — Current Disability:** Competent evidence of a present disability.
• **Timing Rule (*McClain* & *Romanowsky*):** Under ***McClain v. Nicholson*, `21 Vet. App. 319, 321 (2007)`**, Element 1 is satisfied if the claimant had the disability **at the time the claim was filed OR at any time during the pendency of the claim**—even if the condition temporarily resolves before a C&P examination or Board decision (potentially warranting staged ratings). Under ***Romanowsky v. Shinseki*, `26 Vet. App. 289, 293–94 (2013)`**, a clinical diagnosis recorded shortly *before* claim filing is probative evidence of a current disability at filing and cannot be ignored merely because symptoms were in remission on the day of a later VA exam.
• **Functional Pain Without Formal Pathology (*Saunders*) vs. Psychiatric DSM-5 Carve-Out (*Martinez-Bodon*):** Under ***Saunders v. Wilkie*, `886 F.3d 1356, 1368 (Fed. Cir. 2018)`**, "disability" in `§ 1110` means **functional impairment of earning capacity**; thus, orthopedic or somatic pain that causes functional loss satisfies Element 1 even without an identified underlying pathological diagnosis. **Critical Exception:** In ***Martinez-Bodon v. McDonough*, `28 F.4th 1241, 1246 (Fed. Cir. 2022)`**, the Federal Circuit held that because **`38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125(a)` and `4.130`** explicitly require a mental-health diagnosis conforming to the **DSM-5**, psychiatric claims **cannot** use *Saunders* to establish Element 1 without a formal DSM diagnosis ([VASRD Historical Diff: Mental Disorders & PTSD (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125–4.130, DC 9400–9440)](/cfr/modules/mental-health-dc-9400-9411)).

**Element 2 — In-Service Incurrence or Aggravation:** Medical or, in certain circumstances, lay evidence of in-service incurrence or aggravation of a disease or injury (reinforced for combat veterans by **`38 U.S.C. § 1154(b)`**, where satisfactory lay evidence consistent with combat service suffices absent clear and convincing evidence to the contrary).

**Element 3 — Causal Nexus:** Competent evidence of a causal link ("at least as likely as not" / `50%` equipoise under `38 U.S.C. § 5107(b)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.102`; reviewed on CAVC appeal for clear error under ***Bufkin v. Collins*, `604 U.S. 369 (2025)`**) between the present disability and the in-service disease, injury, or event.
• *Note on Shedden's Terminology:* *Shedden* explained that while "service connection" is often used colloquially for Element 3, strictly speaking "service connection" denotes the overall three-element entitlement, whereas Element 3 is the **causal relationship (nexus)** between current disability and in-service event (`381 F.3d at 1166–67`).

blocks.text: B. 38 C.F.R. § 3.303(b) Chronicity & Continuity Post-*Walker v. Shinseki* (2013)

For two decades (`1993–2013`), CAVC precedent (*Savage v. Gober*, `10 Vet. App. 488 (1997)`) permitted veterans to bypass a medical nexus opinion for *any* condition under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.303(b)`** by showing either "chronicity" in service or continuous post-service symptoms.

In ***Walker v. Shinseki*, `708 F.3d 1331, 1338–39 (Fed. Cir. 2013)`**, the Federal Circuit **abrogated *Savage*** and confined `§ 3.303(b)` strictly to the **enumerated list of "chronic diseases" in `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(a)`** ([Playbook 07](/playbooks/07-statutory-presumptions-chronic-tropical-pow-als)):

rows: **ONLY `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(a)` listed chronic diseases** (e.g., arthritis, cardiovascular disease, psychosis, organic nervous system disease/sensorineural hearing loss/tinnitus per *Fountain v. McDonald*, `27 Vet. App. 258 (2015)`, malignant tumors, peptic ulcers).

If the `§ 3.309(a)` disease was shown as **chronic** (*definite and persistent*, not merely isolated/acute) in service, subsequent manifestations of the **same chronic disease** at any later date—however remote—are service-connected **unless clearly attributable to intercurrent causes** (no new medical nexus opinion needed!).
**ONLY `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(a)` listed chronic diseases** noted in service without established in-service chronicity.

If a condition noted during service was *not* clearly chronic at discharge, continuous post-service symptoms linked to the `§ 3.309(a)` condition establish SC without satisfying the `1-year` presumptive manifestation window of `§ 3.307(a)(3)`.
**ALL non-`§ 3.309(a)` conditions** (e.g., orthopedic strains, meniscal tears, radiculopathy, OSA, GERD, non-psychotic mental disorders such as MDD/GAD/PTSD).

`§ 3.303(b)` does **not** apply as a standalone legal shortcut; the claim proceeds under **`§ 3.303(a)`**. **HOWEVER**, under ***Jandreau v. Nicholson*, `492 F.3d 1372, 1377 (Fed. Cir. 2007)`**, ***Barr v. Nicholson*, `21 Vet. App. 303, 308–10 (2007)`**, and ***Buchanan v. Nicholson*, `451 F.3d 1331, 1336–37 (Fed. Cir. 2006)`**, a layperson is **competent to report observable continuous symptoms** (pain, limping, ringing in ears, panic attacks), the Board **may never reject lay testimony solely due to the absence of contemporaneous post-service treatment records**, and a medical nexus examiner **must account for credible lay continuity** (*Dalton v. Nicholson*, `21 Vet. App. 23 (2007)`)!

blocks.text: C. 38 C.F.R. § 3.303(d) Post-Service Initial Diagnosis (*Cosman* & *Combee*)

Under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.303(d)`**, *"Service connection may be granted for any disease diagnosed after discharge, when all the evidence, including that pertinent to service, establishes that the disease was incurred in service."*

items: **Presumptive Periods Never Foreclose Direct SC:** As held in ***Cosman v. Principi*, `3 Vet. App. 503, 505 (1992)`** and ***Combee v. Brown*, `34 F.3d 1039, 1043–44 (Fed. Cir. 1994)`** (codified in **`38 C.F.R. § 3.307(d)`**), presumptive provisions (`§§ 3.307–3.309`, `3.317`, `3.320`) are evidentiary shortcuts—**not ceilings**. Even when a disease (e.g., multiple sclerosis, cancer, psychosis, or delayed-onset PTSD) is first diagnosed 20 years after separation and long after any presumptive period expired, VA **must** adjudicate direct service connection under `§ 3.303(a)` and `(d)` whenever in-service symptoms or exposures are linked via medical nexus.

blocks.text: 2. Entrance Examination Architecture: 38 U.S.C. § 1111 Soundness vs. 38 U.S.C. § 1153 Aggravation

Every preexistence ("EPTS — Existed Prior to Service") dispute begins with **one binary factual audit** of the service entrance physical examination (`SF 88` / `DD Form 2808` *Report of Medical Examination*, distinct from the self-report medical history form `SF 93` / `DD Form 2807-1`!):
A. Threshold Rules on Entrance Exam "Notations" & Lost Records (§ 1111)

Under **`38 U.S.C. § 1111`** (`extended to peacetime service after Dec. 31, 1946 by 38 U.S.C. § 1132`), *"every veteran shall be taken to have been in sound condition when examined, accepted, and enrolled for service, except as to defects, infirmities, or disorders noted at the time of the examination, acceptance, and enrollment."*

items: **Recruit Self-Report Questionnaires Do NOT Defeat Soundness (*Crowe v. Brown*):** In ***Crowe v. Brown*, `7 Vet. App. 238, 245 (1994)`**, the CAVC held that a recruit's check-mark or historical mention of a past childhood condition (e.g., childhood asthma, murmur, or knee sprain) on the **medical history questionnaire (`SF 93` / `DD Form 2807-1`)** is **NOT** a clinical "notation" of a defect when the examining physician evaluates that body system as **"Normal"** on the official **Report of Medical Examination (`SF 88` / `DD Form 2808`)**! Only an affirmative clinical abnormality recorded by the entrance examiner strips `§ 1111` soundness.

**Missing, Incomplete, or Fire-Destroyed Entrance Examinations:** Where an entrance physical examination was lost, destroyed (e.g., in the **1973 NPRC St. Louis fire**; see [`VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon`](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon)), or left blank, VA **cannot** presume a condition was noted at entry. Unless contemporaneous induction records affirmatively record an entrance clinical notation of the condition, the **`§ 1111` presumption of soundness attaches in full** (with heightened Board explanation duties under *O'Hare v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 365 (1991)`). *(Note: For Guard/Reserve `ADT` without a formal entrance exam, `§ 1111` generally requires having been "examined, accepted, and enrolled," and `§ 1111` does **not** apply to `IADT` per *Smith v. Shinseki*, `24 Vet. App. 40 (2010)`—see [Playbook 11](/playbooks/11-guard-reserve-adt-iadt-and-line-of-duty)).*

blocks.text: B. 38 U.S.C. § 1111 Two-Prong Clear-and-Unmistakable Rebuttal (*Wagner v. Principi* & *Vanerson*)

For decades prior to 2004, `38 C.F.R. § 3.304(b)` departed from the text of `38 U.S.C. § 1111` by stating that VA could rebut the presumption of soundness merely by showing clear and unmistakable evidence that the condition **existed prior to service**—omitting the statutory requirement that VA *also* prove lack of in-service aggravation (`VAOPGCPREC 3-2003` attempted to defend following the narrower regulation).

In ***Wagner v. Principi*, `370 F.3d 1089, 1096 (Fed. Cir. 2004)`**, the Federal Circuit **invalidated that omission in `38 C.F.R. § 3.304(b)` (and `VAOPGCPREC 3-2003`)**, holding that the plain text of `38 U.S.C. § 1111` is unambiguous: when no preexisting disorder was noted at entrance, **VA bears the burden of proving by CLEAR AND UNMISTAKABLE EVIDENCE BOTH**:

items: **Prong 1 (Preexistence):** The disease or injury existed prior to entrance into active service; **AND**
**Prong 2 (Zero Aggravation):** Any in-service worsening was **NOT aggravated** by active service (or that there was zero increase in disability during service).

blocks.text: VA formally amended `38 C.F.R. § 3.304(b)` to conform to *Wagner* at **`70 FR 23027` (published & effective May 4, 2005; applicable to open claims)**.

items: **What "Clear and Unmistakable Evidence" Means (*Vanerson v. West*):** Under ***Vanerson v. West*, `12 Vet. App. 254, 258–61 (1999)`**, "clear and unmistakable evidence" under `§ 1111` is an **onerous, undebatable standard**—meaning the facts and medical principles cannot be misinterpreted and allow **no room for reasonable debate** when viewing the entire record as a whole. Crucially, while underlying factual findings are reviewed for clear error, **whether the evidence of record rises to the level of "clear and unmistakable evidence" sufficient to rebut `§ 1111` is a question of law reviewed *de novo* by the CAVC** (`12 Vet. App. at 261`)!

**Claimant Has ZERO Threshold Burden on Aggravation Under `§ 1111`:** Unlike `§ 1153` (where the claimant must first show in-service worsening of a *noted* condition), under `§ 1111` (*Wagner*, `370 F.3d at 1096`), if VA proves Prong 1 (preexistence) and the claimant merely points to in-service symptoms or disability, **the veteran does NOT have to prove permanent worsening before the burden shifts**—VA itself must affirmatively prove *lack of aggravation* by clear and unmistakable evidence!

lines: **THE *GEORGE v. McDONOUGH* BITEMPORAL CUE BOUNDARY (`596 U.S. 740 (2022)`):** Remember that *George v. McDonough* itself arose out of a 1977 BVA denial under **pre-*Wagner* `38 C.F.R. § 3.304(b)`**! The Supreme Court held (`596 U.S. at 747–53`) that when a pre-June 1, 2004 RO or BVA decision **faithfully applied the then-extant text of `§ 3.304(b)`** (finding clear and unmistakable preexistence without requiring VA to disprove aggravation), *Wagner*'s subsequent invalidation of `§ 3.304(b)` on June 1, 2004 (`70 FR 23027`, eff. May 4, 2005) **cannot support a CUE motion** (`38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`; `VAOPGCPREC 25-95` — Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)).
* **How to Win Pre-2004 Soundness Cases Despite *George*:**

1. **Reopen / Supplemental Claim + `§ 3.156(c)` Service Records ([Playbook 03](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c)) or `§ 3.156(b)` 1-Yr VAMC Records ([Playbook 04](/playbooks/04-unadjudicated-tdiu-informal-claims-smc)):** Any open, pending, or `§ 3.156(b)/(c)` reconsidered claim applies *Wagner* with full retroactive force!

2. **Prong-1 CUE Sword (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive):** Even under pre-2004 `§ 3.304(b)`, VA *always* had to prove **Prong 1 (preexistence)** by **clear and unmistakable ("undebatable") evidence** (`38 C.F.R. § 3.304(b) (1977)`). If the pre-2004 RO/BVA relied on speculative medical conjecture ("probably EPTS") or treated a self-report history box as an entrance notation (*Crowe*) without undebatable proof of preexistence, **that violated the extant pre-2004 regulation itself and REMAINS CUE-SAFE**!

blocks.text: C. Outright CAVC Reversal Remedy (*Horn v. Shinseki* & *Adams v. Principi*)

One of the highest-value appellate weapons in Veterans Law is **outright CAVC reversal**—rather than vacatur and remand—when VA relies on a legally insufficient medical opinion to rebut `§ 1111` soundness.

In ***Horn v. Shinseki*, `25 Vet. App. 231, 239–44 (2012)`** (relying on ***Adams v. Principi*, `256 F.3d 1318, 1321–22 (Fed. Cir. 2001)`** and *Miller v. West*, `11 Vet. App. 345, 348 (1998)`), the CAVC established two lethal litigation rules:

items: **Equivocal / Speculative Examiner Language Fails `§ 1111` as a Matter of Law:** If a VA C&P examiner opines that an unnoted condition *"likely," "probably,"* or *"at least as likely as not"* existed prior to service, uses unexplained conclusory assertions, or fails to provide undebatable medical principles disproving in-service aggravation, that opinion is **legally incapable** of rising to "clear and unmistakable evidence."

**NO Second Bite at the Apple (Reversal, Not Remand):** When VA has had a full opportunity to develop the record to carry *its own* statutory affirmative burden under `38 U.S.C. § 1111` (just as in unlawful rating reductions under [Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings)) and its evidence falls short of "clear and unmistakable," **remanding for a new VA medical opinion impermissibly gives the Secretary a second bite at the apple to build evidence *against* the veteran** (`Horn`, `25 Vet. App. at 243–44`). Instead, the CAVC **reverses the Board's rebuttal finding outright**, ordering that the `§ 1111` presumption of soundness stands **unrebutted as a matter of law** (leaving only Element 1 current disability and Element 3 post-service nexus if contested)!

blocks.text: D. 38 U.S.C. § 1153 & 38 C.F.R. § 3.306: Aggravation of *Noted* Preexisting Conditions

When—and **only** when—a preexisting injury or disease **was clinically noted** as an active defect or disorder on the entrance physical (`SF 88` / `DD Form 2808`), `§ 1111` does not attach to that condition, and adjudication shifts to **`38 U.S.C. § 1153`** (`former § 353`) and **`38 C.F.R. § 3.306(a)–(c)`**:

rows: Claimant bears the initial burden (`50%` equipoise under `§ 5107(b)`) of showing an **increase in disability during active service**: · • ***Davis* Temporary Flare-Up Rule:** Temporary or intermittent flare-ups of **symptoms** alone during service, without an underlying worsening of the disability itself, do **not** establish `§ 1153` aggravation unless the underlying condition worsened. · • ***Maxson* No Mandatory "Permanent" Post-Service Hurdle:** Conversely, VA **may not** require objective proof of "permanent" measurable worsening persisting decades after discharge as an extra-statutory barrier; the question is whether the condition **increased in disability during service** based on the entire medical and lay history (*Joyce* confirmed both medical and lay evidence can prove the in-service increase).

Once an in-service increase in disability is shown (`50%` equipoise), **aggravation by service is presumed by law** without the veteran needing a causal nexus linking the worsening to a specific military trauma!

• **Wartime Service & ALL Peacetime Service After Dec. 31, 1946 (`§ 3.306(b)`):** VA can rebut the presumption of aggravation **ONLY by a specific finding based on CLEAR AND UNMISTAKABLE EVIDENCE** (obvious/manifest medical facts and principles) that the increase in disability was due to the **natural progress** of the disease! *(Note: `Pub. L. 93-177` / `38 U.S.C. § 1137` & `§ 3.306(b)` aligned post-1946 peacetime service with wartime `clear and unmistakable` rebuttal—removing the old 6-month peacetime service gate that previously sat in `§ 3.306(c)`! Note `§ 3.306(b)(2)` combat/POW rule: due regard must be given to combat or POW hardships, though temporary symptom flare-ups still require underlying worsening).* · • **Pre-Dec. 7, 1941 Peacetime Service Only (`§ 3.306(c)`):** Uses the historical lower "available evidence of a nature generally acceptable as competent" natural-progress standard.

blocks.text: *(Rating Deduction Note under `38 C.F.R. § 4.22`: When SC by aggravation is granted, VA deducts the preexisting entrance degree of disability **only if** that pre-service baseline was **compensably ascertainable (`>= 10%`)** at entry; if the pre-service condition was mild/`0%` or unascertainable, the veteran receives the **full schedular evaluation** without deduction, and if post-service severity reaches `100%` total disability, **zero deduction** is permitted under `§ 4.22`!)*
3. Congenital / Developmental *Defects* vs. Hereditary / Familial *Diseases* (38 C.F.R. § 3.303(c))

Few provisions in `38 C.F.R. Part 3` generate more unlawful Regional Office denials—and more **high-dollar CUE victories (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive)**—than **`38 C.F.R. § 3.303(c)`**, which states:

lines: *"Congenital or developmental defects, refractive error of the eye, personality disorders and mental deficiency as such are not diseases or injuries within the meaning of applicable legislation."*

blocks.text: A. The Controlling Dichotomy: Static *Defects* vs. Progressive Genetic *Diseases* (VAOPGCPREC 82-90, 67-90, *Winn*, *Terry*, *O'Bryan*, *Quirin*)
For decades, VA examiners and raters saw the words *"genetic," "hereditary," "familial,"* or *"congenital"* in a medical textbook and reflexively denied service connection under `§ 3.303(c)`.

In two landmark binding precedent opinions issued **July 18, 1990**—**[`VAOPGCPREC 82-90`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index) (`55 FR 45711`, Oct. 31, 1990)** and **[`VAOPGCPREC 67-90`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index) (`55 FR 43253`, Oct. 26, 1990)**—subsequently endorsed by the Federal Circuit and CAVC in ***Winn v. Brown*, `110 F.3d 56, 59 (Fed. Cir. 1997)`**, ***Terry v. Principi*, `340 F.3d 1378, 1382–86 (Fed. Cir. 2003)`**, ***Quirin v. Shinseki*, `22 Vet. App. 390, 394–97 (2009)`**, and ***O'Bryan v. McDonald*, `771 F.3d 1376, 1378–80 (Fed. Cir. 2014)`**, the courts established the bright-line legal test:

items: **Non-Compensable Congenital / Developmental *Defect*:** A **static structural or anatomical abnormality** existing from birth or development that is **more or less stationary in nature and largely incapable of improvement or deterioration** (e.g., pure uncomplicated refractive myopia/astigmatism, extra digit, static pilonidal dimple without infection, pure DSM personality trait without superimposed disorder, intellectual developmental disability). Because a true static defect is not a "disease or injury" under `§§ 1110, 1111`, **the `§ 1111` presumption of soundness does not apply to pure defects** (*Winn*; *Terry*).

**Compensable Hereditary / Familial / Genetic *Disease*:** Any condition—**even if 100% genetically determined at conception!**—that involves a **pathological process capable of improving or deteriorating (progressing) over time**! Under `VAOPGCPREC 82-90`, `VAOPGCPREC 67-90`, *Quirin*, and *O'Bryan*, **every progressive genetic or familial disorder IS a "disease" under `38 U.S.C. §§ 1110` and `1111`**!

blocks.text: B. Master Classification & Litigation Matrix (§ 3.303(c) Screening)

headers: Does `§ 1111` Soundness Apply if Unnoted on `SF 88` / `DD 2808`?
rows: **Retinitis Pigmentosa, Leber's Optic Atrophy (*O'Bryan*), Keratoconus, Fuchs' Dystrophy**
**Compensable Hereditary *Disease*** (progressive degenerative pathology; explicitly analyzed in `VAOPGCPREC 67-90` & *O'Bryan*, `771 F.3d 1376`)

Even if VA proves genetic preexistence via DNA/family history (Prong 1), **VA must still prove by clear & unmistakable ("undebatable") evidence that active service did NOT aggravate progression** (Prong 2)! Speculative examiner remarks lose under *Horn*!
**Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (`HCM`), Brugada / Long-QT Arrhythmias, Marfan Aortopathy**
**Compensable Hereditary *Disease*** (capable of worsening, hypertrophy, remodeling, and decompensation)
Physical training (`PT`), deployment exertion, and adrenergic stress frequently accelerate cardiac remodeling; VA almost never has *undebatable* medical proof of zero service aggravation.
**Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (`ADPKD`), Hereditary Hemochromatosis, Sickle Cell Disease (*vs. asymptomatic trait*), Wilson's Disease**

Categorical post-July 18, 1990 RO/BVA denials calling ADPKD, hemochromatosis, or sickle cell disease a "congenital defect under `§ 3.303(c)`" violate binding `VAOPGCPREC 82-90` -> **prime CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive CUE target**!
**Charcot-Marie-Tooth (`CMT`) Hereditary Neuropathy, Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (`EDS` with progressive joint/vascular deterioration), Muscular Dystrophies, Huntington's Disease**

Challenge any C&P opinion conflating genetic etiology with "congenital defect." Under *O'Bryan*, genetic origin at conception proves *at most* Prong 1 preexistence—never "defect" status and never Prong 2 non-aggravation!
**Optic Nerve Hypoplasia (*Quirin*), Pes Planus ( Congenital Flatfoot ), Spondylolisthesis / Spina Bifida Occulta, Bicuspid Aortic Valve, Chiari Malformation**
**Fact-Specific Inquiry (*Quirin*, `22 Vet. App. at 395–97`)** — Board cannot assume "defect" by label; requires medical evidence on whether the condition is **capable of improving or deteriorating**
**YES if progressive disease**; if truly static defect, proceed to **Superimposed Injury/Disease Rule** below!

Under *Quirin* (`22 Vet. App. at 396`) and *Monroe v. Brown*, `4 Vet. App. 513, 515 (1993)`, **even if** the baseline structural anomaly is a static defect, if active-duty rucking, trauma, or infection **superimposes an acquired disease or injury** (e.g., degenerative arthritis, plantar fasciitis, disc herniation, infective endocarditis, or symptomatic syringomyelia) onto that defect, **the superimposed disability IS fully compensable**!
**Excluded *as such*** unless an acquired psychiatric disorder is **superimposed**
Excluded *as such*, **EXCEPT** superimposed `§ 4.130` disorders (`PTSD`, `MDD`, `GAD`, psychosis, bipolar)

Under ***Carpenter v. Brown*, `8 Vet. App. 240, 245 (1995)`** and `38 C.F.R. § 4.127`, service connection **must be granted** when a service-related acquired psychiatric disorder (e.g., PTSD from combat or MST; [Playbook 16](/playbooks/16-ptsd-stressors-and-mst-corroboration)) is **superimposed upon** a personality disorder! Always audit historical "personality disorder" discharges for misdiagnosed in-service PTSD, bipolar disorder, or MST markers ([Playbook 10](/playbooks/10-character-of-discharge-insanity-upgrades)).

blocks.text: 4. Bitemporal CUE vs. Open-Claim Audit Summary (George v. McDonough Gate)

Before selecting a procedural vehicle ([Procedural Vehicles Piercing Finality](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality); [`Mandatory Board CUE Pre-Filing Gate`](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate)), classify the historical causation error against this bitemporal gate:

items:
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (Safe for RO CUE `§ 3.105(a)` & Board CUE `§ 7111`):**
• **Post-July 18, 1990 `§ 3.303(c)` Categorical "Congenital Defect" Denials of Progressive Hereditary Diseases:** Directly violates extant, binding `VAOPGCPREC 82-90` and `VAOPGCPREC 67-90` (`38 U.S.C. § 7104(c)`).
• **Post-June 1, 2004 (*Wagner*) / Post-May 4, 2005 (`70 FR 23027`) `§ 1111` Denials Without Undebatable Proof of Both Preexistence AND Non-Aggravation.**
• **Pre-2004 `§ 1111` Denials Lacking Clear & Unmistakable Proof of *Preexistence* (Prong 1):** Even pre-*Wagner* `§ 3.304(b)` required clear and unmistakable evidence of preexistence (and *Crowe* confirmed recruit history checkboxes on `SF 93` are not clinical entrance notations).
• **Ignoring Listed `§ 3.309(a)` In-Service Chronicity Under `§ 3.303(b)`:** Undisputed STR chronicity of a `§ 3.309(a)` disease denied for lack of a post-service nexus opinion.

**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) (Use `§ 3.156(b)` *Lang*, `§ 3.156(c)` STRs, *Hamill* Explicit Notice, or Supplemental `20-0995` — DO NOT File CUE):**
• **Pre-June 1, 2004 `§ 3.304(b)` Soundness Denials Where Preexistence *Was* Undebatable and the Adjudicator Relied on Pre-*Wagner* `§ 3.304(b)` to Omit VA's Non-Aggravation Burden:** Explicitly barred from CUE by ***George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)`** and `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`.
• **Pre-2018 Denials of Undiagnosed Pain Before *Saunders v. Wilkie*, `886 F.3d 1356 (Fed. Cir. 2018)`** (where prior CAVC precedent *Sanchez-Benitez v. West*, `13 Vet. App. 282 (1999)` had barred pain-alone SC). Reopen via Supplemental Claim (`VA Form 20-0995`) or capture pending Legacy/AMA claims!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Direct Service Connection, the Presumption of Soundness, In-Service Aggravation & Hereditary Diseases
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: To establish direct service connection, VA generally looks for three things: a current disability, an in-service injury, event, or illness, and a medical link between them (38 C.F.R. § 3.303). Two powerful statutory protections prevent unfair 'preexisting condition' denials: if a condition was NOT recorded on your military entrance physical, you are presumed to have entered service in sound condition unless VA proves by clear and unmistakable evidence BOTH that the condition existed before service AND that service did not aggravate it (38 U.S.C. § 1111; 38 C.F.R. § 3.304(b)). And if a condition WAS noted at entrance, worsening beyond natural progression during service establishes in-service aggravation (38 U.S.C. § 1153; 38 C.F.R. § 3.306). In addition, VA law distinguishes static congenital birth defects from progressive hereditary or genetic diseases, which CAN be service-connected if they first manifest or worsen in service.
record_clues: A military entrance clinical examination (Standard Form 88 or DD Form 2808) marking the relevant body system 'Normal', paired with a VA denial claiming the disability 'existed prior to service (EPTS)'.

A self-reported childhood history check-mark on a medical history questionnaire (SF 93 or DD Form 2807-1) where the entrance physician found no clinical abnormality, yet VA treated the history note as an entrance defect.
A VA examination opinion stating a condition 'likely preexisted service' without clear and unmistakable proof, or failing to address whether active duty aggravated the condition.

A VA denial labeling a progressive genetic or familial disease—such as retinitis pigmentosa, keratoconus, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, Charcot-Marie-Tooth neuropathy, or polycystic kidney disease—as an uncompensable 'congenital defect' under 38 C.F.R. § 3.303(c).
important_cautions: Critical Supreme Court limit on older decisions: before Wagner v. Principi (decided June 1, 2004) and VA's May 4, 2005 amendment to 38 C.F.R. § 3.304(b) (70 FR 23027), the printed regulation omitted the lack-of-aggravation prong. In George v. McDonough (2022), the Supreme Court held that applying that pre-2004 regulation cannot be challenged as Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) in a final pre-Wagner decision under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e), though open claims, Supplemental Claims, and 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) service-record reviews can apply current law.

Temporary flare-ups vs. aggravation: for conditions noted on an entrance exam, temporary symptom flare-ups during service that return to the pre-service baseline without lasting worsening do not establish in-service aggravation under 38 U.S.C. § 1153.

Continuity of symptoms and psychiatric diagnoses: under Walker v. Shinseki, the 38 C.F.R. § 3.303(b) chronicity/continuity shortcut applies only to chronic diseases listed in 38 C.F.R. § 3.309(a), and under Martinez-Bodon v. McDonough, mental health service connection requires a formal DSM-5 diagnosis under 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125(a) and 4.130.
Preserve Board review rights carefully: under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c), claimants receive only one final merits CUE decision per prior Board decision issue.
questions_for_representative: Can we inspect my actual military entrance clinical exam (SF 88 or DD Form 2808) to verify whether a doctor clinically noted any defect at enlistment?

If my claim was denied as 'existed prior to service' before June 2004, should we pursue a Supplemental Claim with new and relevant medical evidence—or newly obtained military records under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)—rather than a CUE motion barred by George v. McDonough?
Did VA misclassify a progressive hereditary or genetic disease as a static 'congenital defect' under 38 C.F.R. § 3.303(c)?
If my condition was noted at entrance, do my service medical records or post-deployment exams show lasting worsening beyond natural progression under 38 C.F.R. § 3.306?

title: Master Special Monthly Compensation (SMC) Legal Treatise & Multi-Step Rate Architecture (38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)–(t))
cFileTriggers: Rating Code Sheet displaying 100% schedular (or single-disability TDIU) plus >= 60% separate SC disabilities without SMC(s-1)
Catastrophic or Aid & Attendance Code Sheet capped at a single intermediate § 3.350(f)(3)-(4) bump despite multiple distinct 50%+ or 100% disabilities (Barry v. McDonough)
Prostatectomy (DC 7528), erectile dysfunction (DC 7522), hysterectomy/oophorectomy, mastectomy/breast radiation, or foot-drop (DC 8521) rated without SMC(k)
Severe bilateral neuropathy, ankylosis, or orthopedic joint failure rated at 40%-80% without functional Loss of Use (LOU) analysis under § 4.63 and Tucker v. West
AMA post-Feb. 19, 2019 rating decision omitting reasonably raised SMC despite clinical evidence of Aid & Attendance, housebound status, or extremity LOU (Hamill v. Collins)

Relying on TDIU (§ 4.16) rather than a 100% schedular evaluation to claim a full-step bump under 38 C.F.R. § 3.350(f)(4), or relying on multi-disability TDIU to satisfy the single-total-disability prong of statutory SMC(s) (barred by Bradley, Buie, and Gazelle)

blocks.text: While standard schedular evaluations (`10%–100%`, `38 U.S.C. § 1114(a)–(j)`) compensate average impairment in civil earning capacity (`38 U.S.C. § 1155`), **Special Monthly Compensation (`38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)–(t)`)** is Congress's supra-schedular statutory system compensating **non-economic anatomical loss, functional loss of use (`LOU`), loss of bodily integrity, housebound confinement, and personal caregiving dependency**. Under official 2026 VA compensation tables (effective December 1, 2025, veteran alone), monthly tax-free compensation climbs from **`$3,938.58/month`** at `100%` schedular (`§ 1114(j)`) to **`$6,877.12/month`** at `SMC(o)`/`(p)` and **`$11,271.67/month`** (over **`$135,260/year` tax-free** before dependency add-ons) at `SMC(r)(2)` and `SMC(t)`.

A. Three-Era Statutory Crosswalk (1933–Present)

When auditing multi-decade C-files or pleading Clear and Unmistakable Error (`CUE`) under `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.105(a), 20.1404(b)`, counsel must cite the exact statutory designation in force on the date of the challenged decision ([Three-Era Title 38 Statutory Crosswalk](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk)):

rows: `Veterans' Regulation No. 1(a), Part I, par. II(k)–(p)` *(wartime)* & `Part II` *(peacetime)*
`Pub. L. 73-2` (`48 Stat. 8`); `Pub. L. 79-182` (`1945` SMC overhaul); `Pub. L. 82-427` (`1952` creative organ `(k)` & `(r)` A&A predecessors)
Peacetime awards paid `80%` of wartime SMC rates until equalized in `1973–1974` (`Pub. L. 93-177` / `Pub. L. 93-295`).

All `1959–Aug. 5, 1991` RO Code Sheets, BVA decisions, and early COVA cases (*Payne*, *Akles*) cite `38 U.S.C. § 314`. *(Note: `Pub. L. 102-40` renumbered `§ 3203 -> § 5503` on May 7, 1991, 91 days before `§ 314 -> § 1114`!)*

Modern `Ch. 11` four-digit numbering (`+800` arithmetic rule). `38 U.S.C. § 1151` (`former § 351`) and `38 U.S.C. § 1160` (`former § 360`) paired-organ awards qualify for SMC "as if" service-connected ([`VAOPGCPREC 30-97`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index)).

blocks.text: B. Why SMC Is Mandatory & Inferred by Law (*Payne*, *Akles*, *Bradley*, *Buie*)
Unlike initial service-connection claims (`38 U.S.C. § 5101(a)`), **entitlement to SMC never requires a separate, explicit claim** once the underlying disability is before VA for adjudication:

items: ***Payne v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 85, 87 (1990)` & *Akles v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 118, 120–21 (1991)`:** Whenever a claimant seeks compensation or an increased evaluation and the medical evidence or rating percentages of record reasonably raise potential entitlement to `38 U.S.C. § 1114` (`former § 314`) / `38 C.F.R. § 3.350`, VA has an **affirmative, mandatory duty** to infer, develop, and adjudicate SMC—or provide adequate written reasons or bases (`38 U.S.C. § 7104(d)(1)`) explaining why SMC is not warranted. VA policies requiring claimants to "specify" SMC on an application form are unlawful (*Akles*, `1 Vet. App. at 121`).

***Bradley v. Peake*, `22 Vet. App. 280, 294 (2008)` & *Buie v. Shinseki*, `24 Vet. App. 242, 250–51 (2010)` *(decided Mar. 23, 2010, amended Apr. 21, 2011)*:** SMC is an **ancillary evaluation issue** part and parcel of every claim for disability compensation and every duty-to-maximize audit, regardless of the chronological sequence in which individual disabilities were service-connected or increased.

blocks.text: C. Piercing Finality & Effective-Date Mechanics on Omitted SMC

When an audit of historical Rating Code Sheets ([VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon)) reveals missed SMC, match the era and factual posture to the lowest-burden procedural vehicle ([Procedural Vehicles Piercing Finality](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality), [Playbook 04](/playbooks/04-unadjudicated-tdiu-informal-claims-smc)):

items: **1-Year Increased-Rating Lookback (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(b)(2)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2)`):** Because SMC is legally a rate increase on existing service-connected disabilities (*Akles*; *Bradley*), a newly filed claim or `VA Form 21-2680` establishing LOU, housebound status, or A&A takes an effective date up to **1 year prior to claim receipt** if it is factually ascertainable that the statutory criteria were met during that 1-year lookback window.

**Mathematical / Undebatable RO or Board CUE (`38 U.S.C. §§ 5109A, 7111`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a)` — CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive):** When the contemporaneous Rating Code Sheet or undisputed C&P examination *already* established every statutory element—e.g., schedular `100%` + independent disabilities combining to `>= 60%` with zero `SMC(s)` award, or `DC 7528` radical prostatectomy / `DC 5165` foot amputation with zero `SMC(k)` award—VA's omission is undebatable **CUE** yielding full decades-long retroactivity (*remembering `VAOPGCPREC 12-95`'s July 21, 1992 *Bell* constructive-possession cutoff for unassociated VAMC notes*).

**Legacy Non-Finality (`< Feb. 19, 2019`): `§ 3.156(b)` (*Lang*) vs. Implicit Denial:** Under *Deshotel v. Nicholson*, `457 F.3d 1258 (Fed. Cir. 2006)`, a Legacy rating decision adjudicating the underlying disability may implicitly deny reasonably raised SMC if context alerted a reasonable claimant; however, if VAMC clinical records relevant to the rated condition were generated within **1 year *after*** a post-July 21, 1992 Legacy RO decision and VA never issued a new-and-material determination, **finality never attached** under `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b)` (*Lang v. Wilkie*, `971 F.3d 1348 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`). Similarly, newly associated STRs or military clinical charts trigger full reconsideration back to the original claim under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)`** ([Playbook 03](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c)).

**AMA Explicit-Notice Non-Finality (`>= Feb. 19, 2019` — *Hamill v. Collins*, `166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. 2026)`):** Under `38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)`, the implicit-denial doctrine is **abolished** in all Appeals Modernization Act (`AMA`) decisions. Whenever an AMA rating decision grants or increases a disability while **staying completely silent** on reasonably raised `SMC(k)`, `SMC(l)`, `SMC(s)`, `SMC(t)`, or *Barry* step bumps, **that SMC issue was never denied and remains legally pending** anchored to the original AMA claim / Intent to File!

blocks.text: 2. SMC(k) Add-On Architecture (38 U.S.C. § 1114(k); 38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a))

Unlike `SMC(l)` through `SMC(t)`—which replace standard `§ 1114(a)–(j)` percentage pay—**`SMC(k)` is a flat-rate monthly add-on (`$139.87/month` per award in 2026)** payable on top of `0%` through `100%` schedular/TDIU evaluations, `SMC(s)`, or `SMC(l)` through `SMC(n½)` awards.
A. All Eight Statutory Losses & Regulatory Nuances (§ 3.350(a) & (a)(1)–(6))

lines: **Regulatory Numbering Precision (`Former § 3.350(a)(7)` Removal at `68 FR 55466, 55467`):** When `Pub. L. 106-419, § 302` (`114 Stat. 1822, 1853`, Nov. 1, 2000) first authorized `SMC(k)` for complete mastectomy in women veterans, VA promulgated `former 38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a)(7)` (`67 FR 6872, 6873`, Feb. 14, 2002). After **`Pub. L. 107-330, § 102`** (`116 Stat. 2821`, **effective December 6, 2002**) broadened `§ 1114(k)` to cover `>= 25%` breast tissue loss or breast radiation treatment, VA **removed separate subparagraph `(a)(7)`** (`68 FR 55466, 55467`, Sept. 26, 2003, retroactive eff. Dec. 6, 2002) and placed the breast criteria directly into the **introductory paragraph of `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a)`**, leaving numbered subparagraphs `(a)(1)` through `(a)(6)`.

rows: **One or More Creative Organs** *(Anatomical Loss or LOU)*

Covers erectile dysfunction (`ED`, `DC 7522`, including secondary to diabetes, radical prostatectomy `DC 7528`, vascular disease, spinal cord injury, or SSRI/antihypertensive medication), female sexual arousal disorder (`FSAD`), orchiectomy, complete testicular/ovarian atrophy (`(a)(1)(ii)`), and hysterectomy / bilateral oophorectomy. **Single-`k` Rule:** Loss/LOU of *both* testicles, *both* ovaries, or multiple creative organs yields **only ONE `SMC(k)`** (`"one or more creative organs"`). **Elective Sterilization Unlock ([`VAOPGCPREC 5-89`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index)):** Under binding `VAOPGCPREC 5-89` (`54 FR 38033`), a **prior elective noncompensable vasectomy or tubal ligation does NOT bar `SMC(k)` for a subsequent SC *anatomical loss* of a creative organ** (e.g., post-vasectomy Agent Orange prostatectomy/orchiectomy or post-tubal-ligation hysterectomy), because the statute compensates loss of bodily integrity independent of preexisting procreative capacity! *(Contrast pure functional LOU without anatomical loss, where VA audits whether erectile/creative function was extinguished solely by NSC causes).*
Amputation or functional inability to grasp/manipulate equivalent to below-elbow amputation with prosthesis (*Tucker*). Two hands jump directly to **`SMC(m)`** (`§ 1114(m)`).

Amputation or absence of effective balance and propulsion equivalent to below-knee amputation with prosthesis (*Tucker*), including complete common peroneal nerve paralysis with foot drop + trophic changes (`§ 4.63(b)`). Two feet (or 1 hand + 1 foot) jump to **`SMC(l)`** (`§ 1114(l)`).

Established when severe bilateral damage by disease or injury to **`Muscle Group XVII`** (gluteus maximus/medius/minimus, `DC 5317`) renders the veteran **unable to rise from a seated or stooped position and maintain postural stability without assistance** (hands on knees/furniture, cane, or third-party aid). Note: *both* buttocks must be severely impaired to yield **one** `SMC(k)` award.

Visual acuity reduced to **light perception only (`LPO`)**, no light perception (`NLP`), or anatomical enucleation (`DC 6061–6066`)—inability to recognize test letters at `1 foot` and inability to perceive objects, hand movements, or count fingers at `3 feet`. *(Check `38 U.S.C. § 1160(a)(1)` / `§ 3.383` paired-organ jump to `SMC(l)`–`(n)` if the opposite eye is NSC blind!)*
**Deafness of Both Ears** *(Absence of Air & Bone Conduction)*

Profound bilateral total deafness (`100%` under `§ 4.85` / `DC 6100` with **complete absence of both air and bone conduction** bilaterally). *(Pair with `§ 3.350(e)(1)(iii)` & `(f)(2)` if vision is also impaired).*

**Organic** disability of the organs of speech (`DC 6519` laryngectomy, vocal cord paralysis, tracheal/laryngeal trauma or malignancy) that **constantly precludes communication by natural speech**. Use of an artificial electrolarynx or esophageal speech prosthesis **does NOT defeat `SMC(k)`**, whereas purely psychogenic/conversion mutism without organic speech-organ pathology is excluded from `(a)(6)`.
**Breast Tissue Loss (`>= 25%`) or Breast Radiation** *(Women Veterans)*

Anatomical loss of **`25%` or more of tissue** from a single breast OR from both breasts in combination (`DC 7626` radical, modified radical, simple, or **partial mastectomy / wide excision**), **OR receipt of radiation treatment of breast tissue** (`>= Dec. 6, 2002`; between `Nov. 1, 2000` and `Dec. 5, 2002`, `Pub. L. 106-419` covered complete mastectomy only). Unilateral and bilateral breast loss together authorize **one** `SMC(k)` unless paired with distinct non-breast `(k)` losses.

blocks.text: B. The 3-k Maximum (K-1, K-2, K-3) & Statutory Rate Ceilings (§ 1114(k))

A veteran may receive up to **three concurrent `SMC(k)` awards (`K-1`, `K-2`, `K-3` = `$419.61/month` in 2026)** for distinct qualifying losses (because four extremity losses or paired eye/limb losses automatically convert into higher `SMC(l)`–`(o)` base tiers). However, `38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a)` enforce **two strict statutory rate ceilings**:

items:
**Ceiling 1 — Combined with `0%–100%` (`§ 1114(a)–(j)`) or Housebound `SMC(s)` (`§ 1114(s)`): Capped at `SMC(l)` (`$4,900.83` in 2026):**
• When `1` to `3` `SMC(k)` awards are added to a `0%–100%` schedular/TDIU rating (`$3,938.58` at `100%`) or to **`SMC(s)` (`$4,408.53`)**, total compensation **cannot exceed the `SMC(l)` rate (`$4,900.83`)**.
• **2026 Arithmetic Check:** Even at `SMC(s)` + `3k`, `$4,408.53 + ($139.87 × 3) = $4,828.14`, which sits **`$72.69/month` below `SMC(l)` (`$4,900.83`)**—meaning **all three `SMC(k)` awards pay out 100% in full on top of both `100%` and `SMC(s)`**!

**Ceiling 2 — Combined with `SMC(l)` Through `SMC(n½)`: Capped at `SMC(o)` (`$6,877.12` in 2026):**
• When `1` to `3` `SMC(k)` awards are added to a base or intermediate rate between `SMC(l)` (`$4,900.83`) and `SMC(n½)` (`$6,514.44`), total compensation **cannot exceed `SMC(o)` (`$6,877.12`)** (provided the `(k)` condition is **not** one of the conditions already used to establish the `(l)`–`(n½)` base!).
• *(Example: `SMC(n½)` `$6,514.44` + `3k` `$419.61` = `$6,934.05`, which hits the `SMC(o)` cap and is truncated to **`$6,877.12`**; whereas `SMC(n½)` + `1k` = `$6,654.31` and `SMC(n½)` + `2k` = `$6,794.18` pay in full—and **`SMC(n½) + 1k` + Regular A&A unlocks `SMC(r)(1)` (`$9,826.88`)** under `38 U.S.C. § 1114(r)`!)*
• **No `SMC(k)` Above `SMC(o)`:** Once a veteran reaches `SMC(o)`, maximum `SMC(p)`, `SMC(r)(1)`, `SMC(r)(2)`, or `SMC(t)`, `SMC(k)` no longer adds extra dollars (`§ 1114(k)`).

blocks.text: 3. Loss of Use (LOU) Legal Standard (38 C.F.R. §§ 3.350(a)(2), 4.63 & *Tucker v. West*)

Thousands of veterans with intact limbs—suffering from severe diabetic/radicular peripheral neuropathy, gunshot nerve/muscle trauma, failed total joint arthroplasties, or complex regional pain syndrome (`CRPS`)—legally qualify for **`SMC(k)`** (single hand/foot) or **`SMC(l)`–`(m)`** (bilateral feet/hands) without amputation.
A. The Functional Prosthesis-Equivalence Standard (*Tucker v. West*, 11 Vet. App. 369 (1998))

Under `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.350(a)(2)` and `4.63` (verbatim text in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.350, 3.352, 3.552(b), 4.63 & 3.810(a) (Special Monthly Compensation Ratings, Aid & Attendance, TBI SMC(t), Loss of Use & Multiple Clothing Allowances)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.350-3.352-smc-evolution)), **Loss of Use (`LOU`)** of a hand or foot exists whenever:

lines: *"no effective function remains other than that which would be equally well served by an amputation stump at the site of election below elbow or knee with use of a suitable prosthetic appliance."*

blocks.text: In ***Tucker v. West*, `11 Vet. App. 369, 372–73 (1998)`**, the CAVC reversed a Board denial that focused merely on whether the veteran retained *some* motion or weight-bearing ability without comparing that residual function to a prosthetic limb:

items: **Mandatory Comparative Inquiry:** Adjudicators and C&P examiners **cannot** deny LOU merely because a joint moves or the veteran walks short distances with a cane/AFO brace; they **must explicitly compare** actual remaining function against what a below-elbow (`hand`: **grasping, pinching, manipulation**) or below-knee (`foot`: **balance, propulsion, weight-bearing push-off**) prosthesis could accomplish (*Tucker*, `11 Vet. App. at 373–74`; and under *Payne* and *Akles*, severe stacked joint ratings—such as `DC 5257/5260/5261 + 5258/5259` knee stacking under *Lyles v. Shulkin*, `29 Vet. App. 107, 118–19 (2017)`—can reasonably raise `§ 3.350` LOU, noting under *Lyles* and `38 C.F.R. § 4.68` that once extremity LOU SMC is awarded, separate schedular musculoskeletal ratings for that same lost-use extremity's manifestations are subsumed and cannot be stacked on top!).

**Per Se / Presumptive LOU Rules (`38 C.F.R. § 4.63(a)–(b)`):**
• **`§ 4.63(a)` Structural / Ankylosis Per Se LOU:** `(i)` **Extremely unfavorable complete ankylosis of the knee**, `(ii)` **complete ankylosis of two major joints** of an extremity (e.g., ankle + knee, or wrist + elbow), or `(iii)` **shortening of a lower extremity of `3½ inches (8.9 cm)` or more** **must** be taken as LOU of the hand or foot!
• **`§ 4.63(b)` Common Peroneal Nerve / Foot-Drop Per Se LOU:** **Complete paralysis of the external popliteal (common peroneal) nerve (`DC 8521`)** with consequent **foot drop**, accompanied by characteristic organic changes including **trophic and circulatory disturbances** (skin thinning/ulceration, hair loss, temperature/color changes, muscle atrophy), **must** be taken as LOU of the foot! *(Crucial nuance: Even without trophic changes or complete peroneal nerve severance, functional inability to balance and propel still establishes LOU under the general *Tucker* comparative test!)*

**Upper-Tier LOU Escalators (`SMC(m)` & `SMC(n)`):**
• **Preventing Natural Knee or Elbow Action (`§ 1114(m)`; `§ 3.350(c)(1)(ii)–(iii)`):** When LOU extends above the foot/hand to involve knee or elbow pathology (or above-knee / above-elbow amputation) such that natural knee/elbow action would be prevented with prostheses in place, bilateral leg LOU jumps from **`SMC(l)` (`$4,900.83`)** to **`SMC(m)` (`$5,408.55`)**!
• **Amputation Prerequisite Exception at `SMC(n)` (`§ 1114(n)`; `§ 3.350(d)`):** At `SMC(n)` (`$6,152.64`), actual **anatomical amputation** so near the hip/shoulder as to prevent prosthetic use is required for *lower* extremities (`§ 3.350(d)(2)–(3)`—with a strict caveat that if reamputation at a higher level would allow a prosthesis, `(n)` is not met), **EXCEPT** that **functional LOU of both arms** preventing natural elbow action (`§ 3.350(d)(1)`) and **blindness without light perception in both eyes** (`§ 3.350(d)(4)`) achieve **`SMC(n)` without amputation**!

blocks.text: B. Anatomical Loss vs. Preexisting Non-Service-Connected Paralysis (VAOPGCPREC 30-97)

Under binding **`VAOPGCPREC 30-97`** (`62 FR 63604`, Dec. 1, 1997), `38 U.S.C. § 1114(l)–(n)` states **"anatomical loss *or* loss of use"** in the disjunctive. Therefore, where a veteran with **preexisting non-service-connected (`NSC`) paraplegia** (who already lacked lower-extremity function) subsequently suffers bilateral hip disarticulation compensable under `38 U.S.C. § 1151` (or service connection), the veteran is **unconditionally entitled to `SMC(n)`** based on **anatomical loss**, regardless of prior NSC loss of use!
4. The SMC(l) -> SMC(o) Ladder, *Barry v. McDonough* Multi-Step Math & Anti-Pyramiding
A. Master Statutory & Intermediate Rate Architecture (2026 Rates, Eff. Dec. 1, 2025, Veteran Alone)

Intermediate half-step rates authorized under `38 U.S.C. § 1114(p)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(f)` equal the **arithmetic mean** between the two adjacent statutory tiers (adjusted annually by statutory COLA):

rows: Baseline total disability evaluation (`+ $139.87` per `SMC(k)` up to `3k`).
Single `100%` (or *Bradley* single-disability TDIU) **+** (`>= 60%` separate combined SC **OR** factual permanent housebound).
Loss/LOU of **both feet**; **1 hand + 1 foot**; bilateral blindness **`5/200` or less**; permanently **bedridden**; **OR Regular Aid & Attendance (`§ 3.352(a)`)**.
Intermediate rate between `(l)` and `(m)` (e.g., `1` foot + `1` above-knee leg `(f)(1)(i)`, or `SMC(l)` + one `50%+` `(f)(3)` bump).

Loss/LOU of **both hands**; **both legs** preventing natural knee action; **1 arm + 1 leg** preventing natural elbow & knee action; bilateral blindness **`LPO`**; OR bilateral blindness rendering in need of **Regular A&A**.
Intermediate rate between `(m)` and `(n)` (e.g., `SMC(m)` + `50%+` `(f)(3)` bump, or `SMC(l)` + `100%` `(f)(4)` + `50%+` `(f)(3)` bumps).

Loss/LOU of **both arms** preventing natural elbow action; **anatomical loss of both legs** (or **1 arm + 1 leg**) so near hip/shoulder as to prevent prostheses; anatomical loss of **both eyes**; OR bilateral blindness **`NLP` (no light perception)**.
Intermediate rate between `(n)` and `(o)` *(Critical: **`SMC(n½) + SMC(k)` + Regular A&A unlocks `SMC(r)(1)`** under `§ 1114(r)`!)*.

`(i)` Anatomical loss of both arms preventing prostheses; `(ii)` **Two or more distinct `(l)–(n)` rates** (no condition counted twice, `§ 3.350(e)(1)(ii)`); `(iii)` `60%+` bilateral deafness + `20/200` SC blindness (`(e)(1)(iii)`) or total blindness `NLP` + `60%+` deafness (`§ 1114(o)`); `(iv)` **Paraplegia**: bilateral lower-extremity LOU + loss of anal & bladder sphincter control (`§ 3.350(e)(2)`, `Code O-2`); **OR** reaching the `(p)` ceiling via *Barry* `(f)(3)–(4)` bumps!

Composite rate (`$6,877.12` + `$2,949.76` allowance) for veterans at **`SMC(o)`**, **max `SMC(p)`**, or **`SMC(n½) + k`** who need **Regular A&A** (`§ 3.352(a)`) while not hospitalized at U.S. Gov't expense ([Playbook 12](/playbooks/12-aid-and-attendance-smc-l-r1-r2-and-smc-t)).

**`SMC(r)(2)`:** Composite rate (`$6,877.12` + `$4,394.55`) for `(o)` / max `(p)` / `(n½ + k)` veterans needing daily **higher-level care** (`§ 3.352(b)(1), (3)`) avoiding institutionalization. **`SMC(t)` (`>= Oct. 1, 2011`):** Identical `$11,271.67` total rate for **SC TBI residuals** needing **Regular A&A** (`§ 3.352(a)`) avoiding institutionalization—**no `(o)` or licensed professional required** (*Laska v. McDonough*, `37 Vet. App. 460 (2024)`).

B. *Barry v. McDonough* (101 F.4th 1348 (Fed. Cir. 2024)) & Iterative § 3.350(f)(3)–(5) Step Math

For decades prior to May 16, 2024, VA's `M21-1` manual unlawfully capped `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(f)(3)` and `(f)(4)` at **one single bump**, no matter how many additional severe `50%+` or `100%` disabilities a catastrophically disabled veteran suffered. In ***Barry v. McDonough*, `101 F.4th 1348, 1353–56 (Fed. Cir. May 16, 2024)`**, the Federal Circuit reversed the CAVC and held that the unambiguous text of `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(f)(3)` (and parallel `(f)(4)`) **mandates a cumulative step increase for *each* separate, independent qualifying disability or combination**, constrained only by the statutory `SMC(o)` / `§ 1114(p)` dollar ceiling (`$6,877.12` in 2026)!
Exact Mechanics of the Five § 3.350(f) Step Rules:

items: **`§ 3.350(f)(1)` & `(f)(2)` (Anatomical / Sensory Intermediates):** Specific asymmetric limb-level combinations (e.g., `1` foot + `1` leg preventing knee action = `SMC(l½)`) and bilateral blindness + unilateral/bilateral deafness steps (`38 U.S.C. § 1114(p)`).

**`§ 3.350(f)(3)` — Half-Step Bump (`+½ Step` per Independent `>= 50%` Single or Combined Disability):**
• **Trigger:** Each additional single permanent SC disability—**or `38 C.F.R. § 4.25` combination** of permanent SC disabilities (e.g., `30% + 30% = 51% -> 50%`!)—independently ratable at **`50%` or more** (and < `100%`), separate and distinct from the base `SMC(l)–(n)` disability(ies).
• **Step Effect:** Advances `(l) -> (l½) -> (m) -> (m½) -> (n) -> (n½) -> (o)` (`+1` half-step per independent `50%+` unit!).
• **Non-Consumption Packing Rule:** Never waste two separate `50%` disabilities by combining them together into one `80%` unit (`1` half-step); under *Barry* and VA's duty to maximize (*Buie*), **each standalone `50%`, `60%`, `70%`, or `80%` permanent disability triggers its own separate `+½` step**, while leftover `<50%` permanent ratings (`40%`, `30%`, `20%`, `10%`) combine via `§ 4.25` (and `§ 4.26` bilateral factor if paired!) to form additional `>= 50%` half-step bundles!

**`§ 3.350(f)(4)` — Full-Step Bump (`+1 Full Step` per Independent `100%` Schedular Disability):**
• **Trigger:** Each additional single permanent SC disability independently ratable at **`100%` schedular** (*explicitly `"apart from any consideration of individual unemployability"`—**TDIU (`§ 4.16`) CANNOT trigger `(f)(4)`**!*), separate and distinct from the base `SMC(l)–(n)` disability(ies).
• **Step Effect:** Advances a full statutory tier—e.g., `(l) -> (m) -> (n) -> (o)` or `(l½) -> (m½) -> (n½) -> (o)`!

**`§ 3.350(f)(5)` — Three-Extremity Bump:** Anatomical loss or LOU of **three extremities** entitles the veteran to the next higher rate (whether statutory or intermediate), capped at `§ 1114(p)` (`$6,877.12`).

blocks.text: C. Anti-Pyramiding & The Double-Counting Bar (*Amberman* & *Breniser*)

Both `38 C.F.R. § 4.14` (general VASRD anti-pyramiding) and the explicit text of `38 U.S.C. § 1114(o)` (`"no condition being considered twice"`) and `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(f)(3)–(4)` (`"separate and distinct and involve different anatomical segments or bodily systems from the conditions establishing entitlement under 38 U.S.C. 1114(l) through (n)"`) strictly prohibit **double-counting the same disability or functional manifestation**:

items: ***Amberman v. Shinseki*, `570 F.3d 1377, 1380–81 (Fed. Cir. 2009)`:** Under `38 C.F.R. § 4.14`, two defined diagnoses cannot be compensated twice if they share overlapping symptomatology/manifestations; anti-pyramiding focuses on **functional manifestations**, not diagnostic labels.

***Breniser v. Shinseki*, `25 Vet. App. 64, 74–77 (2011)`:** Landmark CAVC precedent defining the boundary between `SMC(l)` and `SMC(o)`/`SMC(r)(1)`:
• **The Illegal Double-Count (*Breniser* Trap):** Suppose a veteran has bilateral lower-extremity LOU (`SMC(l)` under `§ 1114(l)`), and *because of that exact same bilateral lower-extremity paralysis*, cannot dress, bathe, or transfer without Regular Aid & Attendance. The veteran **cannot** claim a *second* `SMC(l)` rate for A&A under `§ 3.350(e)(1)(ii)` to jump to `SMC(o)` and `SMC(r)(1)`—nor can the veteran use the underlying `40%–80%` lower-extremity radiculopathy/amputation ratings a second time to fuel a `§ 3.350(f)(3)–(4)` step bump! Once lower-extremity LOU establishes base `SMC(l)`, those lower-extremity ratings are **consumed**.
• **The Lawful Dual-Rate Unlock (`SMC(o)` -> `SMC(r)(1)`):** By contrast, if the veteran has `(1)` bilateral lower-extremity LOU (`SMC(l)` #1) **AND** `(2)` **either** loss of anal and bladder sphincter control (`38 C.F.R. § 3.350(e)(2)` `Code O-2`), **OR** an **independent need for Regular A&A (`SMC(l)` #2) caused *solely* by a separate, distinct SC disability** (e.g., SC Parkinson's upper-limb tremor/dementia, SC `100%` PTSD/cognitive hazard incapacity, or SC blind/cardiopulmonary helplessness wholly independent of the legs), *"no condition [is] considered twice"*—entitling the veteran to **`SMC(o)` (`§ 3.350(e)(1)(ii)`) + A&A = `SMC(r)(1)` (`$9,826.88/mo`)**!

blocks.text: D. Bitemporal *George v. McDonough* Gate on *Barry* (Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) for Pre-May 16, 2024 CUE)

Under ***George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)`** and **`38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`** ([`VAOPGCPREC 25-95`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index)), a judicial decision overturning VA's longstanding regulatory interpretation **cannot** establish CUE against a prior **final** RO or Board decision rendered before May 16, 2024 (Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)). Consequently:

items: **Final Pre-May 16, 2024 Decisions:** Do **not** waste a one-shot Board CUE motion (`§ 20.1409(c)`, see [`Board CUE Pre-Filing Gate`](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate)) attacking a final 2015 single-step award solely under *Barry*. Instead, screen aggressively for **open-claim / non-finality vehicles**—`§ 3.156(b)` *Lang* 1-year post-decision VAMC records, `§ 3.156(c)` newly associated military clinical/STR records, AMA `§ 5104(b)` *Hamill* silent omissions (`>= Feb. 19, 2019`), or pending Legacy/AMA appeals—where ***Barry* applies retroactively across the entire open period**!

**Post-May 16, 2024 Decisions & New Supplemental Claims:** Any decision issued **on or after May 16, 2024** that caps `(f)(3)`/`(f)(4)` at a single bump commits **reversible error (and CUE if final)**; for closed pre-2024 files with no finality exception, file an immediate `VA Form 20-0995` / increase claim invoking `§ 5110(b)(2)`'s 1-year lookback where worsening occurred.

blocks.text: 5. Housebound SMC(s) (38 U.S.C. § 1114(s); 38 C.F.R. § 3.350(i))

`SMC(s)` (`$4,408.53/month` in 2026—**`+$469.95/month` (`+$5,639/year`)** above `100%`) requires **first** a **single** service-connected disability rated as total (`100%`), **plus** **either** Statutory `60%` (`§ 1114(s)(1)`) **or** Factual Housebound (`§ 1114(s)(2)`).
A. Prong 1 (§ 1114(s)(1) & § 3.350(i)(1)): Statutory "Total + 60%" Housebound
*(Note: Despite its nickname, a veteran qualifying under `§ 1114(s)(1)` **need NOT be confined to the home**—he or she may travel freely!)*

items:
**Single-Disability TDIU Satisfies the `"Rated as Total"` Prong (*Bradley v. Peake*, `22 Vet. App. 280 (2008)`):**
• Invalidating [`VAOPGCPREC 6-99`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index) (formally **withdrawn at `75 FR 11229`, Mar. 10, 2010**), *Bradley* held that **`38 C.F.R. § 4.16` TDIU attributable *solely* to ONE single service-connected disability** satisfies `"a service-connected disability rated as total"` under `§ 1114(s)`, provided remaining separate SC disabilities independently combine to `>= 60%`!
• **The Multi-Disability TDIU Bar (*Buie*, `24 Vet. App. at 250–51`; *Gazelle v. Shulkin*, `868 F.3d 1006 (Fed. Cir. 2017)`):** Conversely, a TDIU grant predicated on the combined effect of *multiple* SC disabilities **cannot** satisfy the single-total-disability prong—**unless** medical/vocational development (or an `M21-1` *Bradley* audit under *Buie*'s duty to maximize) proves that **one single SC condition (`e.g., 70% PTSD` alone) independently caused unemployability** while the remaining SC conditions independently combine to `>= 60%`!
• **Bitemporal CUE Guardrail:** Pure mathematical omission of `SMC(s)` on a **schedular `100% + 60%`** Code Sheet is **CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive safe back to 1960** (`Pub. L. 86-663`). By contrast, attacking a final **June 7, 1999 – Nov. 25, 2008** RO/Board denial of *TDIU-based* `SMC(s)` via CUE is **barred by `VAOPGCPREC 6-99` + *George v. McDonough*** (Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)).

**Combined-Table Math & Separate Bodily Systems (*Gazelle v. Shulkin*, `868 F.3d 1006, 1010–12 (Fed. Cir. 2017)`):**
• Under *Gazelle*, multiple separate disabilities under `§ 1114(s)(1)` must combine to **`60%` or more under VA's `38 C.F.R. § 4.25` Combined Ratings Table** (including the `§ 4.26` bilateral factor if paired independent extremities are present—e.g., `50% + 20% = 60%`, whereas `30% + 30% = 51% -> 50%` fails, **not** `30 + 30 = 60` arithmetic addition!).
• Under `§ 3.350(i)(1)`, the `60%+` disabilities must be separate and distinct from the `100%` disability (note: a temporary `100%` surgical convalescent or active-cancer rating under `§§ 4.29, 4.30` or `DC 7528` **does** trigger temporary statutory `SMC(s)` during every month the `100%` + `60%` ratings run concurrently!).

blocks.text: B. Prong 2 (§ 1114(s)(2) & § 3.350(i)(2)): Factual "Permanently Housebound"

When a veteran has a single `100%` schedular (or single-disability TDIU) evaluation **without** `60%` in additional ratings—or where all disabling manifestations stem from that single `100%` condition (e.g., severe agoraphobic `100%` PTSD, severe `100%` COPD/heart failure, or `100%` ALS/MS not yet needing A&A)—`§ 1114(s)(2)` awards `SMC(s)` if the veteran is **"permanently housebound"** (`substantially confined as a direct result of service-connected disabilities to his or her dwelling and the immediate premises, or, if institutionalized, to the ward or clinical areas`, reasonably certain to continue for life).

items: ***Howell v. Nicholson*, `19 Vet. App. 535, 540 (2006)`:** Reversing VA's hyper-literal reading, the CAVC held that **"leaving one's house for medical purposes cannot, by itself, serve as the basis for finding that one is not substantially confined"** under `§ 1114(s)(2)`! Document on `VA Form 21-2680` and lay declarations that the veteran leaves the home/yard *only* for medical treatment or only with extraordinary third-party transport/escort.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Plain-English Guide to Special Monthly Compensation (SMC) Ladder & Multi-Step Rate Math (38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)–(t))
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: VA's 100% schedular rate is NOT the ceiling of disability compensation. When a Veteran suffers anatomical loss or functional Loss of Use of organs, senses, or limbs, becomes housebound, or needs daily Aid & Attendance, 38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)–(t) replaces or supplements standard table math with Special Monthly Compensation (SMC). Historically, VA's computer software and manuals capped intermediate half-step (§ 3.350(f)(3), for independent 50%+ disabilities) and full-step (§ 3.350(f)(4), for independent 100% disabilities) increases at just ONE single step. On May 16, 2024, in Barry v. McDonough, the Federal Circuit struck down that one-bump cap—holding that EACH separate and distinct 50%+ or 100% disability adds its own incremental step up the SMC ladder toward the SMC(o) / maximum SMC(p) ceiling (which can in turn unlock higher-level Aid & Attendance under SMC(r)(1)).
record_clues: A Rating Code Sheet awarding SMC(l), SMC(m), or SMC(n) alongside TWO OR MORE separate 50%+ or 100% disabilities where VA granted only a single half-step or full-step increase (Barry v. McDonough).

Up to three separate SMC(k) add-ons stackable on top of 0%–100%, SMC(s), or SMC(l)–(n) (capped so total monthly pay does not exceed SMC(o) or SMC(p) limits) for erectile dysfunction, prostatectomy, reproductive/breast tissue loss, aphonia, unilateral eye/hearing loss, or Loss of Use of a hand/foot.

100% schedular (or single-disability TDIU) plus 60%+ in separate disabilities with no statutory Housebound SMC(s) paid, OR actual factual 'substantially confined to the home/ward' status overlooked under § 3.350(i)(2).
Severe bilateral nerve damage, foot drop with AFO braces, or ruined joint function rated 40%–80% without checking functional 'Loss of Use' under 38 C.F.R. § 4.63.
important_cautions: Anti-Pyramiding / No Double-Counting (Amberman & Breniser): You cannot use the exact same disability or overlapping functional impairment twice—every 50%+ combination or 100% disability used for a § 3.350(f)(3)–(4) step bump must be completely separate from the conditions used to establish your base SMC(l)–(n) rate.

TDIU Limits in SMC Math: Under § 3.350(f)(4) and Buie / Bradley / Gazelle, a full-step increase under § 3.350(f)(4) requires an independent 100% schedular disability (not TDIU), and statutory SMC(s) based on TDIU requires that ONE single disability alone warranted TDIU.

CUE vs. Open/Supplemental Claims After Barry & Laska: Under George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e), Barry (May 16, 2024) and Laska (September 6, 2024) cannot be used to assert Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) against final pre-decision ratings—use a Supplemental Claim, timely appeal, § 3.156(c) service records, or check for an unadjudicated AMA issue (Hamill v. Collins).

Am I missing any SMC(k) add-ons (up to three) or statutory/factual SMC(s) Housebound compensation?
If multiple Barry step increases raise my rate to SMC(n½)+k or maximum SMC(p) and I also need regular Aid & Attendance, does that unlock SMC(r)(1) higher-level care?
Did a post-February 19, 2019 AMA decision fail to give explicit notice on reasonably raised SMC (Hamill v. Collins), keeping my earlier effective date alive?

blocks.text: Under **`38 U.S.C. § 7104(c)`** (`former 38 U.S.C. § 4004(c)`, see [Three-Era Title 38 Statutory Crosswalk](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk)) and **`38 C.F.R. §§ 2.6(e)(8), 14.507`**, written legal opinions designated as precedent opinions by the VA General Counsel (`VAOPGCPREC`) occupy **Tier 4** of the Veterans Law hierarchy of authorities ([Authority Hierarchy, Temporal Versioning Policy & Citation Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).

Unlike the `M21-1` Adjudication Procedures Manual—which binds Regional Office (`AOJ`) raters operationally but does **not** bind the Board of Veterans' Appeals (`38 C.F.R. § 20.105`)—an active `VAOPGCPREC` opinion **legally binds both Regional Offices and the Board of Veterans' Appeals** unless and until it is superseded by statute/regulation, invalidated by the Federal Circuit/CAVC/Supreme Court, or formally withdrawn by VA OGC.
1. Bitemporal CUE Mechanics & The *George v. McDonough* Mirror Rule

Because `VAOPGCPREC` opinions are binding substantive law within VA under `38 U.S.C. § 7104(c)`, they cut **both ways** in Clear and Unmistakable Error (`CUE`) litigation ([Procedural Vehicles for Piercing Finality (The Time-Machine Mechanisms)](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality); [Board of Veterans' Appeals (BVA) CUE Motion Pre-Filing Gate Checklist (38 U.S.C. § 7111; 38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1400–20.1411)](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate)):

items: **Offensive CUE Sword (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive):** If an active, binding `VAOPGCPREC` opinion was in force on the date of a final RO or Board decision (from its internal OGC issuance date forward under `38 C.F.R. § 14.507(b)`), and undisputed facts of record triggered its rule—for example, refusing separate knee instability (`DC 5257`) and limitation-of-motion (`DC 5260`/`5261`) ratings after `VAOPGCPREC 23-97`, or rejecting a progressive hereditary disease as a "congenital defect" after `VAOPGCPREC 82-90`—**failure to apply that extant `VAOPGCPREC` is textbook CUE** (`38 U.S.C. §§ 5109A, 7111`).

**Defensive CUE Shield (*George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` & `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)` — Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)):** Conversely, if an RO or Board decision *faithfully followed* a restrictive `VAOPGCPREC` that was active and binding on the date of the decision—for example, `VAOPGCPREC 6-99` barring single-disability TDIU from satisfying the `100%` prong of `SMC(s)` prior to *Bradley v. Peake*, `22 Vet. App. 280 (2008)`—a later court invalidation or OGC withdrawal **cannot** establish CUE against that prior final decision (`VAOPGCPREC 25-95`; *Jordan v. Nicholson*, `401 F.3d 1296 (Fed. Cir. 2005)`). To capture retroactive back pay across a pre-withdrawal era, practitioners **must** unlock an open claim via `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b)` (*Lang*), `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)` service records, or an unadjudicated pending claim!

blocks.text: 2. Citator Status Taxonomy
Every opinion in this digest has been Shepardized against `va.gov/ogc/precedentopinions.asp`, *Federal Register* withdrawal notices, Title 38 statutory amendments, and CAVC/Federal Circuit precedent:

items: **`Active-Binding`:** Remains in full force on all VA adjudicators and the Board under `38 U.S.C. § 7104(c)` and `38 C.F.R. § 14.507`.
**`Active-Binding (Modified / Clarified)`:** Core holding remains binding, while a subsidiary prong was refined by later regulation or appellate precedent.
**`Invalidated in Part by Court / Superseded by Regulation`:** A controlling Federal Circuit or CAVC decision struck down a central legal premise, prompting a corrective `38 C.F.R.` amendment.
**`Withdrawn by VA OGC`:** Formally stripped of precedential status by VA OGC notice published in the *Federal Register*—**never cite as active law**.
