**Kill-Switch Screen:** Foreshadowed `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`, *Jordan*, and ***George v. McDonough*, 596 U.S. 740 (2022)**. Pivots counsel away from doomed CUE filings toward `§ 3.156(b)–(c)` or pending-claim pathways.
Addresses BVA jurisdiction to review the timeliness of a Legacy Substantive Appeal (`VA Form 9`) and agency waiver when the AOJ treated an appeal as timely without adjudicating timeliness.
**Legacy Appeal Shield:** Pair with *Percy v. Shinseki*, `23 Vet. App. 37 (2009)` and *Freund v. Collins* (2026 VACOLS class action) when VA belatedly claims a decades-old Legacy appeal was untimely.

blocks.text: B. Domain II — Musculoskeletal, Knee Stacking & Auditory Anti-Pyramiding (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.14, 4.71a, 4.87)

rows: Assigning **separate ratings** for knee recurrent subluxation/lateral instability (`DC 5257`) AND degenerative arthritis (`DC 5003`) or limitation of motion (`DC 5260`/`5261`) **does not violate `38 C.F.R. § 4.14` anti-pyramiding** because instability and motion loss represent distinct disabilities.

**High-Yield CUE Sword (`>= July 1, 1997`):** Raters routinely subsumed knee arthritis/ROM into `DC 5257` (or vice versa). Undisputed C&P findings of both instability and compensable ROM/X-ray arthritis establish RO/Board CUE ([VASRD Historical Diff: Spine & Musculoskeletal Joints (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.40, 4.45, 4.59, 4.71a)](/cfr/modules/orthopedic-spine-joints)).

Clarifies `VAOPGCPREC 23-97`: when a veteran is rated under `DC 5257` (instability), a separate rating under `DC 5260`/`5261` (including via `§§ 4.40, 4.45, 4.59` functional/painful motion) requires limitation of motion meeting at least the criteria for a `0%` or compensable ROM code, or painful motion under `§ 4.59`.

**Stacking Multiplier:** Pair with *Lyles v. Shulkin*, `29 Vet. App. 107 (2017)` confirming `DC 5257` never bars separate `DC 5260`/`5261` or meniscal (`DC 5258`/`5259`) evaluations where symptoms are distinct.

A veteran **may receive separate ratings under BOTH `DC 5260` (limitation of leg flexion) AND `DC 5261` (limitation of leg extension) for the exact same knee joint**, because flexion loss and extension loss constitute distinct functional impairments.

**Triple-Stack Knee Audit (`>= Sept. 17, 2004`):** Allows simultaneous `DC 5257` (instability) + `DC 5260` (flexion) + `DC 5261` (extension) on a **single knee** (triggering bilateral factor if opposite leg is also SC)! Ignoring compensable extension lag alongside flexion loss post-Sept. 17, 2004 is classic CUE.

When evaluating unilateral SC hearing loss under `38 C.F.R. § 4.85`, an opposite **non-service-connected (`NSC`)** impaired ear must be assigned Roman Numeral `I` (normal) unless `38 U.S.C. § 1160` (`§ 3.383`) paired-organ hearing loss applies (*Boyer v. West*, `210 F.3d 1351 (Fed. Cir. 2000)`).

**Paired-Organ Screen:** Fixes NSC ear at `I` when the SC ear is `0%` (`I–IX` on `Table VII`), *except* effective **Dec. 6, 2002 (`Pub. L. 107-330, § 103`; `69 FR 48149`)**, **`38 U.S.C. § 1160(a)(3)` / `§ 3.383(a)(3)`** unlocks full bilateral `Table VII` rating whenever the **SC ear is `>= 10%` compensable (`X or XI` on `Table VII`) AND the NSC ear meets `§ 3.385`** ([VASRD System 03 Historical Diff: Auditory System, Maryland CNC & Puretone Tables, Tinnitus Three-Era Evolution (DC 6260), Meniere's & Vestibular Stacking (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.85–4.87, DC 6100–6260)](/cfr/modules/03-auditory-hearing-tinnitus-4.85-4.87))!
Held that `38 C.F.R. § 4.87, DC 6260` authorizes only a **single `10%` evaluation** for recurrent tinnitus regardless of whether perceived in one ear, both ears, or in the head.

**CUE Trap Blocker:** Upheld in *Smith v. Nicholson*, `451 F.3d 1344 (Fed. Cir. 2006)` and codified in Note (2) to `DC 6260` (`68 FR 25822`, eff. June 13, 2003). Do **not** file bilateral tinnitus stacking CUE motions!

blocks.text: C. Domain III — Special Monthly Compensation (SMC) & Loss of Use (38 U.S.C. § 1114)

rows: Articulates the statutory purpose of `38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)` (`former § 314(k)`, `SMC(k)` creative organ): a **prior elective, noncompensable sterilization** (e.g., tubal ligation or vasectomy) **does NOT bar entitlement to `SMC(k)`** for a subsequent service-connected **anatomical loss** of a creative organ (e.g., hysterectomy, salpingo-oophorectomy, or orchiectomy), because the statute compensates anatomical loss independent of preexisting procreative capability.

**Foundational `SMC(k)` Unlock:** Distinguish **anatomical loss** (where prior elective sterilization is **no bar** under `5-89`) from pure **loss of use** (`ED`/`FSAD`), and audit every surgical/oncological file (hysterectomy, prostatectomy, orchiectomy) where raters wrongly denied `SMC(k)` ([Playbook 04](/playbooks/04-unadjudicated-tdiu-informal-claims-smc)).

A claimant with preexisting non-service-connected paraplegia who suffers bilateral hip disarticulation compensable under `38 U.S.C. § 1151` is entitled to statutory **`SMC(n)`** (`38 U.S.C. § 1114(n)`) based on anatomical loss, regardless of prior NSC loss of use.

**Anatomical vs. Functional SMC Distinction:** Proves that **anatomical amputation** satisfies `§ 1114(l)–(n)` unconditionally even where preexisting NSC paralysis already eliminated lower-extremity function!

*(Historical Rule)* Had barred using a `100%` TDIU award (`§ 4.16`) to satisfy the "service-connected disability rated as total" requirement for statutory housebound **`SMC(s)`** (`38 U.S.C. § 1114(s)`).

**CRITICAL CITATOR TRAP:** Judicially repudiated by ***Bradley v. Peake*, 22 Vet. App. 280 (2008)** and **formally withdrawn at `75 FR 11229` (Mar. 10, 2010)**. Single-disability TDIU + `60%` independent SC grants `SMC(s)` on all open claims, *but* `VAOPGCPREC 6-99` + *George* blocks CUE on final `1999–2008` denials!

blocks.text: D. Domain IV — TDIU & Extraschedular Referrals (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.16, 3.321(b)(1))

rows: "Unemployability" in `38 C.F.R. § 4.16` is synonymous with inability to secure and follow a **substantially gainful occupation**; while governed by an objective standard ("average person" impairment), VA must consider the individual veteran's **educational and occupational history**, excluding age (`§ 4.19`) and NSC disabilities.

**Core TDIU Doctrine:** Prevents BVA/examiners from inventing a hyper-theoretical sedentary job divorced from the veteran's actual education and work background ([VASRD Historical Diff: TDIU (§ 4.16), May 2024 Digestive (§ 4.114) & Pending Sleep Apnea/Tinnitus Proposals](/cfr/modules/tdiu-digestive-respiratory-diffs); *Ray v. Wilkie*, `31 Vet. App. 58 (2019)`).

Whenever evidence of record reasonably raises an extraschedular evaluation under `38 C.F.R. § 3.321(b)(1)` or `§ 4.16(b)`, the Board **must address** whether referral to the Director, Compensation Service is warranted (and cannot assign an extraschedular rating in the first instance without referral).

**Board Remand Engine:** Supports CAVC vacatur when the Board ignores reasonably raised `§ 4.16(b)` referral for unemployable veterans below the `60% / 70%-40%` schedular thresholds. *(Note: `82 FR 57830`, eff. Jan. 8, 2018 amended `§ 3.321(b)(1)` to eliminate *Johnson* collective extraschedular ratings).*
**`Active-Binding (Modified in Part by Regulation)`** *(`82 FR 57830` & Thun)*

blocks.text: E. Domain V — Presumption of Soundness, Congenital Defects vs. Hereditary Diseases (38 U.S.C. § 1111; 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.303(c), 3.304(b))

rows: Construes `38 C.F.R. § 3.303(c)`: non-compensable "congenital or developmental **defects**" are structural/static abnormalities largely incapable of improvement or deterioration, whereas **hereditary or familial progressive "diseases"** ARE compensable diseases under `38 U.S.C. § 1110` if they first manifest in service or are aggravated by service!

**Massive CUE & Merits Weapon:** Raters for decades unlawfully denied genetic/familial conditions (hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, retinitis pigmentosa, polycystic kidney disease, Charcot-Marie-Tooth, Ehlers-Danlos) by mislabeling them "congenital defects" under `§ 3.303(c)`. Post-1990 categorical denials on this ground are prime **CUE** candidates!
**`Active-Binding`** *(Endorsed by Fed. Cir. / CAVC in Winn, Terry, Quirin)*

Companion to `VAOPGCPREC 82-90`: confirms that hereditary diseases (specifically analyzing retinitis pigmentosa) are subject to the presumption of soundness (`38 U.S.C. § 1111`) and service connection by in-service incurrence or aggravation (`§ 1153`) if progression exceeds natural history.

**Soundness Rebuttal Pairing:** Combine `VAOPGCPREC 67-90` and `82-90` with *Wagner v. Principi* (`370 F.3d 1089 (Fed. Cir. 2004)`): if a genetic disease was unnoted at entrance, **VA** bears the clear-and-unmistakable burden of proving *both* preexistence (e.g., via genetic etiology) **and** zero service aggravation (*Horn v. Shinseki*, `25 Vet. App. 231 (2012)`).

Analyzed `38 U.S.C. § 1111` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.304(b)`, correctly noting statutory history required disproving aggravation, **but** erroneously concluded VA was bound to follow the narrower regulatory text of `§ 3.304(b)` requiring only clear and unmistakable evidence of preexistence.

**CITATOR TRAP:** The Federal Circuit in ***Wagner v. Principi*, 370 F.3d 1089 (Fed. Cir. 2004)** **invalidated** the portion of `§ 3.304(b)` and `VAOPGCPREC 3-2003` omitting the lack-of-aggravation prong; VA amended `§ 3.304(b)` at `70 FR 23027` (May 4, 2005). Cite *Wagner*, not `3-2003`, for the active burden!
**`Invalidated in Part by Court / Superseded by Regulation`** *(Wagner, 2004; `70 FR 23027`)*

blocks.text: F. Domain VI — Secondary Service Connection, Obesity, Substance Abuse & § 1151 (38 C.F.R. § 3.310)

rows: (1) Obesity *per se* is not a "disease or injury" under `38 U.S.C. §§ 1110, 1131` and cannot be rated as a standalone SC disability; **HOWEVER**, (2) **obesity may serve as an "intermediate step"** establishing secondary service connection under `38 C.F.R. § 3.310` when an SC orthopedic/mental/endocrine condition causes weight gain (or prevents exercise) that proximately causes or aggravates a third disability (e.g., **obstructive sleep apnea, hypertension, diabetes, GERD, or contralateral joint disease**)!

**Cornerstone Secondary SC Play:** Develop three explicit nexus links in the private IMO/DBQ: `(a)` SC condition caused/aggravated obesity (immobility, SSRIs/corticosteroids, PTSD binge eating); `(b)` obesity was a substantial factor causing/aggravating the downstream condition; and `(c)` the downstream condition would not have occurred (or worsened) to the same degree absent the SC disability.

Secondary service connection under `38 C.F.R. § 3.310` **applies fully to disabilities proximately due to or aggravated by a `38 U.S.C. § 1151` disability** (VA medical malpractice / unforeseen treatment injury).

**`§ 1151` Multiplier:** Whenever a veteran holds a `§ 1151` award (e.g., surgical nerve damage) that later causes secondary depression, gait derangement, or cardiovascular decline, claim full `§ 3.310` secondary compensation (`>= Feb. 11, 1997` CUE-safe).

*(Historical Rule)* Construed the `Pub. L. 101-508` (`1990`) alcohol/drug-abuse bar in `38 U.S.C. §§ 105(a), 1110, 1310` to prohibit secondary SC or DIC for alcohol/drug abuse (and resulting organ damage, e.g., cirrhosis) even when caused by service-connected PTSD.

**CITATOR TRAP:** **Overturned in core part by *Allen v. Principi*, 237 F.3d 1368 (Fed. Cir. 2001)**, *reh'g denied*, `268 F.3d 1340`, which held `§ 1110` bars only *primary* willful-misconduct substance abuse, **allowing secondary SC (`§ 3.310`) when an SC disorder (like PTSD/chronic pain) causes or aggravates alcohol or drug abuse and downstream organ disease** (`38 C.F.R. § 3.310(b)` codified at `71 FR 52744, 52747`, pub. Sept. 7, 2006, eff. Oct. 10, 2006)!
**`Invalidated in Part by Court / Superseded by Regulation`** *(Allen, 2001; `71 FR 52747`)*

blocks.text: G. Domain VII — Character of Discharge (COD), Willful Misconduct & Insanity (38 U.S.C. § 5303; 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.12, 3.354)

rows: Construes **`38 U.S.C. § 5303(b)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.354(a)` insanity**: insanity requires behavior resulting from **disease** (excluding pure personality disorder or mere voluntary intoxication *unless* accompanied by an underlying psychosis, bipolar/mood disorder, PTSD, or organic brain disease) that renders the servicemember prolongedly maladjusted, devoid of normal social judgment, or unable to conform conduct at the time of the offense(s) leading to an OTH/BCD discharge.

**COD Gateway Unlock:** Even when a veteran has a statutory or regulatory COD bar and cannot secure a DRB/BCMR upgrade, proving `§ 5303(b)` insanity at the time of the misconduct **completely removes the COD bar** for compensation and healthcare (`Zang v. Brown`; supplemented by VA's June 25, 2024 `38 C.F.R. § 3.12` compelling-circumstances rule, `89 FR 32361`).

A **substituted administrative discharge** granted as executive clemency by a Service Department Secretary under **`10 U.S.C. § 874(b)`** does **not** remove the absolute statutory bar under **`38 U.S.C. § 5303(a)`** for a discharge/dismissal pursuant to sentence of a **general court-martial** (`GCM`).

**Discharge-Upgrade Forum Screen:** Distinguish `10 U.S.C. § 874(b)` clemency substitutions (which leave a GCM conviction bar intact) from full **`10 U.S.C. § 1552` BCMR/BCNR record corrections** vacating or setting aside the GCM sentence, or `§ 5303(b)` insanity!

blocks.text: H. Domain VIII — Toxic Exposure, Presumptions & Duty to Assist (38 U.S.C. §§ 1116A, 5103A)

rows: Clarified that `M21-1` asbestos adjudication instructions did not create an irrebuttable regulatory presumption of service connection, while requiring case-by-case evidentiary development of in-service asbestos exposure and medical nexus *(Note: pre-VCAA "well-grounded claim" framing under `former § 5107(a)` was superseded Nov. 9, 2000 by `Pub. L. 106-475`)*.

**Asbestos / TERA Bridge:** Historically governed Navy/shipyard asbestos claims; today, pair with **`38 U.S.C. §§ 5103A(d) & 1168` (`PACT Act` TERA medical nexus mandate)** whenever MOS/shipboard asbestos exposure is conceded!
**`Active-Binding (Modified in Part by Statute)`** *(`Pub. L. 106-475` & `§ 1168` TERA)*

Interprets retroactive effective-date mechanics of **`38 U.S.C. § 1116A(c)`** (*Blue Water Navy Vietnam Veterans Act of 2019*, `Pub. L. 116-23`, eff. Jan. 1, 2020) and its alignment with *Nehmer* (`38 C.F.R. § 3.816`) for previously denied offshore herbicide claims filed between Sept. 25, 1985 and Jan. 1, 2020.

**Retroactive Effective-Date Audit:** Audit every post-2020 Blue Water Navy grant ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc)) where the RO lazily assigned a `Jan. 1, 2020` or `ITF` effective date despite an earlier post-1985 claim or death!

blocks.text: I. Domain IX — Survivor DIC, § 1318 Tort Offsets, Marriage Recognition & Substitution (38 U.S.C. §§ 103, 1318, 5121A)

rows: Under **`38 U.S.C. § 1318(d)`**, VA must offset `§ 1318` survivor DIC by the total amount received by the survivor under a judicial judgment, FTCA settlement, or compromise for the veteran's death, regardless of how state law labels the tort damages (e.g., "pain and suffering" vs. "pecuniary loss"), excluding amounts paid solely to non-DIC third parties or estate debts.

**Wrongful-Death Settlement Structuring:** Essential pre-settlement audit rule whenever a `100%` P&T / TDIU veteran dies of non-SC causes and the surviving spouse pursues a medical-malpractice, Camp Lejeune (`CLJA`), or asbestos wrongful-death settlement alongside `§ 1318` DIC ([Playbook 08](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical))!
Addressed post-*Windsor* effective dates (`3-2014`) and `38 U.S.C. § 103(c)` state-residency marriage validity (`4-2014`) for same-sex spouses prior to *Obergefell v. Hodges*, `576 U.S. 644 (2015)`.

**Bitemporal Marriage & Duration Screen:** *Obergefell* superseded state-residency bans nationwide eff. June 26, 2015, and **Secretary Instruction `01-22` (`87 FR 68904`, eff. Oct. 11, 2022)** counts pre-*Obergefell* marriage-type relationships toward 1-year DIC (`§§ 1304, 1318(c)`) and 8-year kicker (`§ 1311(a)(2)`) duration ([Part 3 Historical Diff: Surviving Spouse Marriage Validity, Multi-Era Remarriage Cutoffs (§ 3.55) & Helpless Child Status (§ 3.356)](/cfr/modules/survivor-marriage-dependency-evolution)).
*(Historical Rule)* Addressed dismissal/abatement of pending BVA appeals upon a claimant's death following *Padgett v. Nicholson*, `473 F.3d 1364 (Fed. Cir. 2007)`.

**CITATOR TRAP:** Rendered obsolete for deaths **`>= October 10, 2008`** by **`Pub. L. 110-389, § 212` (`38 U.S.C. § 5121A` Substitution)** and **formally withdrawn at `75 FR 11229` (Mar. 10, 2010)** ([Playbook 09](/playbooks/09-accrued-benefits-substitution-nehmer-estates)).

blocks.text: J. Domain X — Separation/Severance Recoupment & Wartime Pension Net Worth (38 C.F.R. §§ 3.700, 3.274–3.276)

rows: Distinguishes **`10 U.S.C. § 1212` Disability Severance Pay (`§ 3.700(a)(3)`)**—which is recouped **solely** from VA compensation payable for the specific severance disability(ies)—from **`10 U.S.C. §§ 1174/1174a` Nondisability Separation Pay / `SSB` (`§ 3.700(a)(5)`)**, which mandates withholding against **all** VA disability compensation regardless of condition.

**Recoupment Isolation Audit:** Prevents raters from raiding independent non-severance SC compensation (e.g., `70%` PTSD) to recoup a `10%` orthopedic `DSP` award ([Playbook 20](/playbooks/20-backpay-offsets-crdp-crsc-severance-recoupment)). *(Read with post-Sept. 30, 1996 after-tax net cap & post-Jan. 28, 2008 `§ 1212(d)(2)` combat-zone non-recoupment).*

Assets transferred by a claimant (or fiduciary) into an irrevocable self-settled **"special needs" or living trust** that retains expenditures for the claimant's benefit **remain includable** in net worth for Improved Pension (`38 U.S.C. § 1522`); only complete relinquishment of all ownership, control, and beneficial enjoyment removed assets pre-2018.

**Pension Trust & Lookback Screen:** Explains why pre-Oct. 18, 2018 pension planning required outright gifts or third-party-only trusts—and since **Oct. 18, 2018 (`83 FR 47246`, `38 C.F.R. § 3.276`)**, *even* outright `< FMV` transfers of covered assets within **`36 months`** trigger up to a `5-year` transfer penalty ([Playbook 21](/playbooks/21-overpayment-waivers-incompetency-and-wartime-pension); [`Part 3 Pension Diff`](/cfr/modules/pension-net-worth-and-effective-date-diffs)).

Before citing *any* `1989–2015` `VAOPGCPREC` opinion in a brief, cross-check this quarantine ledger so you never rely on rescinded agency precedent:

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Binding VA General Counsel Legal Opinions (VAOPGCPREC) & Why Some Older Opinions Were Withdrawn
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: When a tricky legal question arises inside VA, VA's top lawyer—the General Counsel—can issue a formal Precedent Opinion (abbreviated 'VAOPGCPREC'). Under federal statute (38 U.S.C. § 7104(c)), active VA General Counsel Precedent Opinions are legally binding on every VA Regional Office rater AND on every Veterans Law Judge at the Board of Veterans' Appeals. Many landmark Veteran protections come directly from active VAOPGCPREC opinions: allowing separate knee ratings for instability and limited motion (VAOPGCPREC 23-97 & 9-98), protecting progressive hereditary diseases from being dismissed as 'congenital defects' (VAOPGCPREC 82-90), and recognizing obesity as an intermediate link in secondary claims (VAOPGCPREC 1-2017). At the same time, courts later struck down several older restrictive General Counsel opinions, forcing VA to formally withdraw them.
record_clues: A knee rating decision refusing to grant separate percentages for lateral knee instability (DC 5257) alongside painful or limited flexion (DC 5260) and extension (DC 5261).

A denial calling a progressive genetic or familial disease (such as retinitis pigmentosa, hereditary neuropathy, or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy) a non-compensable 'congenital defect' under 38 C.F.R. § 3.303(c).

A secondary claim for sleep apnea, hypertension, or diabetes denied without evaluating whether service-connected pain, immobility, or medication caused weight gain/obesity as an intermediate step (VAOPGCPREC 1-2017).
An older 1990s or 2000s denial citing a VAOPGCPREC number (such as VAOPGCPREC 6-99 on TDIU/SMC(s) or VAOPGCPREC 7-99 on secondary substance use) that courts later invalidated.
important_cautions: Never Rely on a Withdrawn Opinion: Several older VAOPGCPREC opinions (including 6-99, 7-99, 4-99, 13-94, 2-2007, and 2-2008) were formally withdrawn or invalidated by federal courts and are no longer valid law.

Why George v. McDonough Matters for Old Opinions: Under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e) and George v. McDonough, 596 U.S. 740 (2022), if an older final VA decision faithfully applied a restrictive VAOPGCPREC opinion that was still active at that time before a court struck it down, you generally cannot overturn that old decision via Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE)—though you can file an AMA Supplemental Claim or check for pending claims or § 3.156(c) service records.

Pre-July 21, 1992 VAMC Record Rule: Under VAOPGCPREC 12-95, constructive possession of VA medical records under Bell v. Derwinski applies to CUE motions only for decisions issued on or after July 21, 1992.
questions_for_representative: Does an active binding VA General Counsel Precedent Opinion (such as VAOPGCPREC 23-97, 82-90, 20-97, or 1-2017) directly require VA and the Board to recognize my legal theory?
If my older VA denial relied on a VAOPGCPREC opinion that a federal court later struck down, should we pursue a Supplemental Claim or pending/service-record audit rather than a CUE motion?
Did VA overlook a binding General Counsel opinion that was already active and in force on the exact date of my rating decision?

blocks.text: 1. Regulatory & Statutory Landscape

items: **Launch of the 1945 VASRD (Effective April 1, 1946):** Although titled the *1945 Schedule for Rating Disabilities*, it took effect **April 1, 1946** (`38 C.F.R. § 3.952`; `38 C.F.R. Part 4, App. A`), creating the foundational 4-digit Diagnostic Code system designed around massive numbers of WWII combat casualties (shrapnel, GSW, cold injury/trench foot, tropical disease, "psychoneurosis").

**Pre-1959 Statutory Citations & Savings Protection (`38 C.F.R. § 3.953`):** Prior to **January 1, 1959** (effective date of `Pub. L. 85-857`, `72 Stat. 1105`, enacted Sept. 2, 1958), Title 38 U.S.C. did not exist as a positive-law title. Rating sheets from 1945–1958 cite **Veterans' Regulation No. 1(a), Part I** (wartime service connection) or **Part II** (peacetime service connection) (briefly consolidated by the Veterans' Benefits Act of 1957, `Pub. L. 85-56`, `71 Stat. 83`, eff. Jan. 1, 1958). Even from January 1, 1959 until 1991 (`Pub. L. 102-40`, `105 Stat. 187`, eff. May 7, 1991 for `3000`–`4000` administrative/appellate sections; `Pub. L. 102-83`, `105 Stat. 378`, eff. Aug. 6, 1991 for `300`–`500` benefit sections), compensation statutes carried earlier section numbers (e.g., `38 U.S.C. § 310` instead of `§ 1110`; `§ 314` instead of `§ 1114`; `§ 3010` instead of `§ 5110`). Crucially, **`38 C.F.R. § 3.953(a)–(b)`** preserves statutory grandfathering under `Pub. L. 85-56` and `Pub. L. 85-857`, protecting disability compensation/service connection payable on **December 31, 1957** (`Pub. L. 85-56`) or **December 31, 1958** (`Pub. L. 85-857`) against termination or reduction absent fraud, clear and unmistakable error as to fact/law, or material misrepresentation, alongside the general 10-year service-connection shield in **`38 C.F.R. § 3.957`**.

**Pre-1962 Appellate & Informal Claim Mechanics:** Before `Pub. L. 87-666` (`76 Stat. 553`, enacted Sept. 19, 1962, eff. Jan. 1, 1963), there was **no Statement of the Case (SOC)** procedure; veterans appealed via `VA Form P-9` / `Form 1-9` within one year of notification (see [`Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon`](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon)). Meanwhile, VA's 1961 Part 3 recodification (`26 FR 1561, 1571`, published and effective Feb. 24, 1961) formally codified `38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b)` making VA hospital admissions and outpatient exam reports automatic informal claims for increase (see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: Former 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.155(a) & 3.157(b) Informal Claims (Repealed March 24, 2015)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.155-3.157b-informal-claims-pre-2015)).

blocks.text: 2. Signature C-File Artifacts to Look For

items: **`VA Form 8-526`:** Often completed right at the separation center before demobilization. Every symptom written in the veteran's own handwriting on a discharge `8-526` is an **explicit formal claim**! If the veteran listed five conditions on the `8-526` and the 1946 rating sheet only adjudicated three, the other two may have remained **legally pending** (subject to pre-AMA implicit denial analysis under *Deshotel*/*Adams*).

**Separation Physicals & Hospital Summaries:** `WD AGO Form 38`, `AGO Form 53-55` (Enlisted Record and Report of Separation), `WD MD Form 55` clinical records, and `DD Form 214` (introduced in 1950 for Korean War era).

**Carbon-Copy Rating Code Sheets:** Sparse 1-page sheets with virtually zero narrative "reasons or bases" (narrative explanations on RO ratings were not required until Feb. 1, 1990 under `38 U.S.C. § 3004(b)`, renumbered `§ 5104(b)` in 1991).

blocks.text: 3. High-Yield Retroactive Opportunities & Bitemporal Era Traps

items: **The WWII / Korea Penetrating Wound Goldmine (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive):** Mass demobilization boards routinely granted `0%` or `10%` under `DC 7800–7805` (scars) for gunshot, mortar, and artillery shrapnel wounds when separation exams on the *same desk* recorded retained metallic foreign bodies (`SFB` / `MFB`), muscle hernia, loss of deep fascia, surgical debridement, or through-and-through muscle tracks across `Muscle Groups I–XXIII` (`DC 5301–5323`). Because the separation physical was **physically in the C-file** at the time of the 1946 or 1953 rating, this avoids the *Bell* constructive-possession bar (`VAOPGCPREC 12-95`, `60 FR 43186`, Aug. 18, 1995) and supports pure **RO CUE** (`38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a)`), quoting the verbatim historical `38 C.F.R. § 4.56` text in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 4.56 Muscle Injuries (Pre-July 3, 1997 vs. Current)](/cfr/38-cfr-4.56).

**1973 NPRC St. Louis Fire Overlap (`§ 3.156(c)` Open Reconsideration):** Millions of Army (discharged Nov. 1, 1912 – Jan. 1, 1960) and Air Force (discharged Sept. 25, 1947 – Jan. 1, 1964, surnames Hubbard–Z) records burned on July 12, 1973. If a Korean War veteran was denied in the 1970s/1980s for "no STRs due to fire," and morning reports, VA hospital admission summaries, or Surgeon General's Office (`SGO`) index extracts are later located and associated, **`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)(1)(iii)`** (see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) Service Department Records (Pre-Oct. 6, 2006 vs. Current)](/cfr/38-cfr-3.156c)) unlocks an open-record reconsideration effective date back to the post-fire denied claim!

**Bitemporal *George v. McDonough* Gate (`596 U.S. 740 (2022)`; `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`):** When attacking a final 1945–1961 decision via CUE, anchor your argument strictly to the unambiguous text of `Veterans' Regulation No. 1(a)` / `Pub. L. 85-857` and the contemporaneous 1945 VASRD edition in force on the rating date—never on a post-decision judicial reinterpretation or invalidated regulation (`§ 20.1403(e)`). Conversely, if finality is pierced via `§ 3.156(c)` newly associated service records or an unadjudicated discharge `8-526` claim, modern precedent and benefit-of-the-doubt (`§ 5107(b)`) apply in full.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Era 1 (1945–1961): Post-WWII & Korean War Rating Decisions
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: After World War II, VA launched the modern 4-digit Diagnostic Code rating schedule effective April 1, 1946. Rating sheets from 1945 through 1961 were typically one-page carbon copies with almost no written explanation, and decisions before January 1, 1959 cited World War II 'Veterans' Regulations' rather than modern Title 38 law numbers. Many separating service members filled out VA Form 8-526 right at the separation center—and if VA left a listed condition undecided or rated a deep gunshot or shrapnel wound only as a surface scar, those historical records still matter today.
record_clues: A discharge-center application on VA Form 8-526 listing multiple injuries or illnesses in handwriting, paired with a 1-page carbon-copy rating sheet that decided some conditions and stayed silent on others.
Discharge and separation records such as AGO Form 53-55, WD AGO Form 38, NAVPERS 553, or an early Korean War DD Form 214 (introduced in 1950).

Pre-1959 rating sheets citing 'Vet. Reg. No. 1(a)' or 1959–1961 sheets citing three-digit Title 38 section numbers (§ 310 or § 314), or mentions of records lost in the July 12, 1973 National Personnel Records Center (NPRC) St. Louis fire.
important_cautions: Older laws use different numbers than today's statutes (for example, Vet. Reg. No. 1(a) before 1959, § 310 from 1959 to 1991, and § 1110 today), and Congress protected disability compensation payable on December 31, 1957 or December 31, 1958 under special grandfathering rules (38 C.F.R. § 3.953).

For Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) reviews of decisions issued before July 21, 1992, VA hospital records that were not physically inside the Regional Office claims folder generally do not count as part of the record, and later court reinterpretations cannot establish CUE under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e) (George v. McDonough).

Reconstructing burned or misplaced military hospital, morning report, or Surgeon General index records to request reconsideration under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) follows different rules than CUE—and under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c), claimants get only one final merits CUE decision per prior Board decision issue.
questions_for_representative: Did my original VA Form 8-526 list any symptoms or injuries that the 1940s or 1950s rating sheet never addressed?

Were my separation physical and military surgical records physically inside my VA Claims File when the original rating was issued, or can newly located service/morning-report records be submitted under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)?
Does a pre-1959 statutory savings clause (38 C.F.R. § 3.953) or 10/20-year protection rule (38 C.F.R. §§ 3.951, 3.957) protect any historical evaluation in my file?

title: Era Lens 2: Pre-VJRA Closed Era & Vietnam War Adjudications (1962–1988)
statutes: Pub. L. 87-666, 76 Stat. 553 (enacted Sept. 19, 1962, eff. Jan. 1, 1963 — SOC & Appellate Procedure)
Pub. L. 87-825, 76 Stat. 948 (enacted Oct. 15, 1962, eff. Dec. 1, 1962 — Effective Date Reforms)
38 U.S.C. § 211(a) (former judicial review bar; replaced/renumbered § 511(a) by Pub. L. 102-83)
keyPrecedents: Nehmer v. U.S. Dept. of Veterans Affairs, 712 F. Supp. 1404 (N.D. Cal. 1989)
cFileTriggers: Timely Notice of Disagreement (NOD) in C-file with NO Statement of the Case (SOC) ever issued
0% or low compensable SC rating followed by VAMC admission/outpatient treatment reports (38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b))
Post-Sept. 25, 1985 Vietnam veteran claims denied for skin/chloracne, cancer, neuropathy, or heart disease (Nehmer)
1970s Vietnam combat GSW/fragment ratings ignoring muscle groups or PTSD (DC 9411 added eff. Apr. 11, 1980)
killSwitches: Assuming constructive possession of VAMC records not physically in the C-file for CUE against a pre-July 21, 1992 decision (barred by VAOPGCPREC 12-95)

Applying modern Caluza/Shedden medical-nexus jargon or post-decision judicial reinterpretations (George v. McDonough, 596 U.S. 740 (2022); 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)) to allege CUE in final pre-1988 RO decisions

toc.text: 1. Regulatory & Statutory Landscape
2. Signature C-File Goldmines of the 1962–1988 Era
3. Critical Bitemporal & Evidentiary Traps

blocks.text: 1. Regulatory & Statutory Landscape

items: **"Splendid Isolation" (`former 38 U.S.C. § 211(a)`):** Until November 18, 1988, VA benefit decisions were **completely insulated from federal judicial review** (save for constitutional challenges to statutes), and attorneys were capped at a **$10 fee** (`former 38 U.S.C. § 3404(c)`), leaving veterans represented almost exclusively by overburdened VSOs or pro se. Note also that throughout `1962–1988`, Title 38 carried pre-1991 `Pub. L. 85-857` section numbers (`§ 310` for wartime SC, `§ 314` for compensation/SMC rates, `§ 3010` for effective dates as reformed by `Pub. L. 87-825`, `76 Stat. 948`, enacted Oct. 15, 1962, **effective Dec. 1, 1962**, and `§ 4005` for NOD/SOC appeals).

**Creation of the NOD -> SOC -> Form 9 Pipeline (`Pub. L. 87-666`, `76 Stat. 553`, enacted Sept. 19, 1962, eff. Jan. 1, 1963):** Established the mandatory **Statement of the Case (SOC)**. Once a claimant filed a written Notice of Disagreement (NOD) within 1 year of a rating notice, VA was **statutorily required** to issue an SOC before the claimant's 60-day clock (or remainder of the 1-year period) to file a Substantive Appeal (`VA Form 1-9` / `Form 9`) could even begin to run!

**Broad Informal Claims & `38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b)`:** Throughout 1962–1988, `38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b)` (see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: Former 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.155(a) & 3.157(b) Informal Claims (Repealed March 24, 2015)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.155-3.157b-informal-claims-pre-2015)) automatically converted **every VA hospital admission report or VA outpatient examination report** regarding an already service-connected condition into an **informal claim for an increased rating** on the date of admission/examination.

**Recognition of PTSD (`DC 9411`, Effective April 11, 1980):** Following DSM-III (1980), VA added Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (`DC 9411`) to `38 C.F.R. § 4.132` effective **April 11, 1980** (see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125–4.130 Mental Disorders, Traumatic Stress (§ 4.129), Eating Disorders (DC 9520–9521) & Former § 4.132 Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.132-mental-disorders-pre-1996)). Prior Vietnam psychiatric claims were often mischaracterized as non-compensable "personality disorders" or "situational maladjustment" despite documented combat trauma.

blocks.text: 2. Signature C-File Goldmines of the 1962–1988 Era

items: **Unperfected NODs Missing an SOC:** Audit every post-1962 letter from the veteran expressing dissatisfaction with a rating or denial. If it met the broad pre-AMA definition of an NOD (`former 38 C.F.R. § 19.118` / `§ 20.201` — "disagreement and desire for appellate review") and **VA never issued an SOC**, the 1960s/1970s/1980s rating **never became final** (*Tablazon v. Brown*, 8 Vet. App. 359 (1995))!

**Dormant `§ 3.157(b)` VAMC Reports:** Whenever a Vietnam or Korean War veteran held *any* service-connected disability (including `0%`), check if a VAMC hospital summary (`VA Form 10-1000`) or outpatient report (`10-2545` / progress notes) **physically entered the C-file** (or was received by VA) showing worsening without a follow-on rating action.

**Missing Inpatient Clinical Records vs. Outpatient Health Record (`§ 3.156(c)`):** During the Vietnam War, field hospital and evac hospital **inpatient clinical packets** (e.g., 24th Evac Hospital, USS *Sanctuary*, USS *Repose*, Yokosuka/Clark AFB surgical records) were stored separately at NPRC from the thin outpatient Dental/Health jacket (`DD Form 722`). Thousands of 1970s Vietnam claims were denied or rated `0%` because VA only requested the outpatient jacket! Associating those inpatient clinical files today triggers **`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)`** (see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) Service Department Records (Pre-Oct. 6, 2006 vs. Current)](/cfr/38-cfr-3.156c)) back to the 1970s claim!

***Nehmer* Class Claims (Sept. 25, 1985 Forward):** Any claim received or pending on or after **September 25, 1985** from a qualifying herbicide-exposed veteran for a condition later added to `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(e)` (including ischemic heart disease, Parkinson's, B-cell leukemias, prostate/respiratory cancers, peripheral neuropathy, bladder cancer, hypothyroidism, parkinsonism—noting `M21-1 VIII.i.2.B.1.c` excludes chloracne, hypertension, and MGUS from `§ 3.816` class retroactivity) must be audited under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.816`**.

**Unlawful Rating Reductions (`38 C.F.R. § 3.344`):** In the 1970s and 1980s, ROs routinely cut `50%` or `70%` stabilized (5+ years) psychiatric or orthopedic ratings based on a single cursory C&P exam without reviewing the entire medical history or finding sustained improvement under the ordinary conditions of life and work. Under *Brown v. Brown*, 5 Vet. App. 413 (1993), such reductions are **void *ab initio***—restoring the prior rating back to the date of reduction without needing to prove CUE!

blocks.text: 3. Critical Bitemporal & Evidentiary Traps

items: **No *Bell* Constructive Possession Before July 21, 1992:** For a **CUE** motion attacking a 1962–1988 decision, you **cannot** rely on VAMC records that stayed strictly inside the VAMC medical center and were never placed in the VARO claims folder (`VAOPGCPREC 12-95`, `60 FR 43186`, Aug. 18, 1995). Look instead to whether those VAMC records triggered an unadjudicated **`§ 3.157(b)` informal claim**!

***George v. McDonough* (`596 U.S. 740 (2022)`) & `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)` Gate:** Later judicial invalidation of a regulation cannot establish CUE against a final 1962–1988 decision (which is why *Nehmer* class stipulations under `38 C.F.R. § 3.816` were uniquely necessary to override final `§ 3.311a` denials!). Whenever a 1962–1988 decision is kept **open** via an unperfected NOD (*Tablazon*), pending `§ 3.157(b)` claim, `§ 3.156(c)` service record reconsideration, or *Brown* void *ab initio* reduction, `§ 20.1403(e)` does **not** apply.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Era 2 (1962–1988): Vietnam Era & Pre-Court VA Decisions
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: From 1962 until November 1988, no independent federal court reviewed VA benefit denials, and lawyers were barred from charging more than $10—meaning most Veterans navigated claims alone or with busy service organizations. At the same time, two protective rules existed during this era: starting January 1, 1963, if you sent a written Notice of Disagreement (NOD), VA had to mail back a formal Statement of the Case (SOC) or your appeal stayed open; and VA hospital or outpatient exam reports for an already service-connected condition automatically counted as informal claims for a higher rating under former 38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b).
record_clues: A letter or VA Form 21-4138 sent within one year of a 1963–1988 rating decision disagreeing with the outcome, with no Statement of the Case (SOC) in the file.
A 0% or low service-connected rating followed by VA Medical Center admission summaries (Form 10-1000) or clinic reports showing the condition worsened.

Vietnam inpatient evacuation hospital or surgical ship charts (stored separately from the thin outpatient health jacket), post-September 25, 1985 Agent Orange denials, or pre-1980 combat trauma labeled 'personality disorder' before PTSD (Diagnostic Code 9411) was added in April 1980.
important_cautions: For Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) motions challenging pre-July 21, 1992 decisions, VA medical center records that were never placed into the Regional Office claims folder cannot be used to prove CUE—though they should be checked as possible unadjudicated informal claims under former 38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b).

Later court reinterpretations of a regulation cannot establish CUE against a final 1962–1988 decision under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e) (George v. McDonough), whereas open claims, missing-SOC appeals, void reductions (38 C.F.R. § 3.344), Nehmer herbicide rules (38 C.F.R. § 3.816), and newly associated military records (38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)) are not CUE motions.

Remember that under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c), once the Board of Veterans' Appeals issues a final merits decision on a CUE motion for a specific Board issue, a second CUE motion on that Board issue is barred.
questions_for_representative: Is there any written disagreement letter in my C-file after January 1, 1963 where VA never issued a Statement of the Case?
Did VA only pull my thin outpatient health record in the 1970s while missing separate military hospital inpatient surgical charts that could support reconsideration under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)?

If I had an Agent Orange condition denied or claimed on or after September 25, 1985, or a 5-year rating reduced on a single exam, do Nehmer (38 C.F.R. § 3.816) or stabilized-rating rules (38 C.F.R. § 3.344) apply?

title: Era Lens 3: The VJRA Revolution, Well-Grounded Claims & 1990s VASRD Overhauls (1988–2000)
statutes: Pub. L. 102-40, 105 Stat. 187 (May 7, 1991) & Pub. L. 102-83, 105 Stat. 378 (Aug. 6, 1991) (Title 38 Renumbering)
keyPrecedents: Russell v. Principi, 3 Vet. App. 310 (1992) (en banc)
Caluza v. Brown, 7 Vet. App. 498 (1995), aff'd, 78 F.3d 604 (Fed. Cir. 1996)
cFileTriggers: 1990s denials stating 'Claim is not well grounded'
Post-July 21, 1992 rating decisions ignoring VAMC treatment notes in VistA/CAPRI
Ratings rendered across publication-vs.-effective-date windows around Nov. 7, 1996 (Mental Health) or July 3, 1997 (Muscle Injuries)
killSwitches: Attacking a 1990–2000 'not well grounded' denial as CUE solely because VA refused to provide a C&P exam (lawful under pre-VCAA Grottveit/Caluza law and barred by Cook v. Principi)

Confusing Federal Register publication dates with effective dates (e.g., 61 FR 52695 pub. Oct. 8, 1996 vs. eff. Nov. 7, 1996; 62 FR 30235 pub. June 3, 1997 vs. eff. July 3, 1997) or violating 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e) / George v. McDonough

toc.text: 1. Regulatory & Statutory Landscape
2. High-Yield Opportunities in 1988–2000 Decisions
3. Critical Era & Bitemporal Traps

blocks.text: 1. Regulatory & Statutory Landscape

items: **Creation of Judicial Review (`Pub. L. 100-687`, `102 Stat. 4105`, Nov. 18, 1988):** Established the U.S. Court of Veterans Appeals (renamed CAVC on Mar. 1, 1999 by `Pub. L. 105-368`), mandated BVA "reasons or bases" (`former § 4004(d)(1)` -> `§ 7104(d)(1)`), and authorized paid attorney representation following a first BVA final decision (if NOD was filed on or after Nov. 18, 1988); written RO decision notices (`former § 3004` -> `38 U.S.C. § 5104`) followed via `Pub. L. 101-237, § 115` (effective **Feb. 1, 1990**).

**Two-Step 1991 Title 38 Renumbering (`Pub. L. 102-40` & `Pub. L. 102-83`):** Early COVA opinions (`1–2 Vet. App.`) cite pre-1991 section numbers that Congress renumbered in two stages during 1991:
• **May 7, 1991 (`Pub. L. 102-40, § 402`, `105 Stat. 187`):** Renumbered administrative, claims, and appellate chapters (`§ 3007 -> § 5107`, `§ 3010 -> § 5110`, `§ 3404 -> § 5904`, `§ 4004 -> § 7104`, `§ 4051 -> § 7251`).
• **August 6, 1991 (`Pub. L. 102-83, §§ 4–5`, `105 Stat. 378`):** Codified Department organization (`former § 211(a)` superseded by `§ 511(a)`) and renumbered substantive benefit chapters (`§ 310 -> § 1110`, `§ 314 -> § 1114`, `§ 410 -> § 1310`, `§ 521 -> § 1521`).

**The "Well-Grounded Claim" Trapdoor (Nov. 18, 1988 – Nov. 8, 2000):** Under former `38 U.S.C. § 5107(a)` (`§ 3007(a)`), a claimant bore the threshold burden of submitting a "well-grounded" (plausible) claim—including **competent medical nexus evidence** (*Grottveit v. Brown*, 5 Vet. App. 91 (1993); *Caluza v. Brown*, 7 Vet. App. 498 (1995), *aff'd*, 78 F.3d 604 (Fed. Cir. 1996))—**before VA's duty to assist (including providing a C&P exam) ever attached**!

**July 21, 1992 *Bell* Cutoff:** Decisions issued **on or after July 21, 1992** are charged with **constructive possession** of VA medical records generated before the decision (*Bell v. Derwinski*, 2 Vet. App. 611 (1992); `VAOPGCPREC 12-95`, `60 FR 43186`, Aug. 18, 1995).

**1989–1997 Major Regulatory & VASRD Overhauls (Always Separate Publication vs. Effective Dates!):**
• **March 1, 1989 & September 4, 1990 (`38 C.F.R. § 4.16` TDIU):** `54 FR 4281` (published Jan. 30, 1989, **effective March 1, 1989**, adding former `§ 4.16(c)`) and `55 FR 31579` (published Aug. 3, 1990, **effective September 4, 1990**, codifying the Census poverty-threshold marginal employment rule in `§ 4.16(a)`).
• **December 31, 1990 (`38 C.F.R. § 3.655` Missed C&P Exams):** Published Nov. 29, 1990 (`55 FR 49521`), **effective December 31, 1990**, distinguishing original claims from increased-rating/reopened claims.
• **November 7, 1996 (`38 C.F.R. § 4.130` Mental Disorders):** Published Oct. 8, 1996 (`61 FR 52695`), **effective November 7, 1996** (adopting DSM-IV, eliminating former `§ 4.132` and former `§ 4.16(c)` — see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125–4.130 Mental Disorders, Traumatic Stress (§ 4.129), Eating Disorders (DC 9520–9521) & Former § 4.132 Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.132-mental-disorders-pre-1996)).
• **July 3, 1997 (`38 C.F.R. §§ 4.55, 4.56, 4.73` Muscle Injuries):** Published June 3, 1997 (`62 FR 30235`), **effective July 3, 1997** (modernizing `DC 5301–5323` — see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 4.56 Muscle Injuries (Pre-July 3, 1997 vs. Current)](/cfr/38-cfr-4.56)).

**1997 CUE Act (`Pub. L. 105-111`, `111 Stat. 2271`, Nov. 21, 1997):** Created statutory BVA CUE (`38 U.S.C. § 7111`; implemented at `38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1400–20.1411`, `64 FR 2134`, published Jan. 13, 1999, **effective Feb. 12, 1999**) and codified RO CUE (`§ 5109A`).

blocks.text: 2. High-Yield Opportunities in 1988–2000 Decisions

items: **Post-July 21, 1992 *Bell* Constructive Possession CUEs:** If an RO rated a condition at `10%` in 1994 while VAMC orthopedic or surgical notes from 1993 (not yet printed into the paper C-file) documented ankylosis, statutory housebound criteria, or loss of use of a foot (`SMC(k)`), those VAMC records **were constructively before the rater**!

**Anti-Pyramiding Errors After *Esteban* (1994) & *DeLuca* (1995):** Raters continued lumping painful scars, muscle group damage, and peripheral nerve injuries into one low code despite *Esteban v. Brown*, 6 Vet. App. 259 (1994), or failing to account for functional loss due to pain/flare-ups on joint exams under *DeLuca v. Brown*, 8 Vet. App. 202 (1995) (note: *DeLuca* inadequacy of exam is a duty-to-assist error, *not* CUE, unless the C&P report *itself* documented the reduced painful ROM in degrees that warranted a higher schedular rating!).

**Bypassing 1990s "Not Well Grounded" Denials via `§ 3.156(c)`:** While you rarely win CUE against a 1995 "not well grounded" denial, **many 1990s claims were deemed "not well grounded" only because in-service STRs or combat unit logs were missing from the C-file**! If STRs, deck logs, or JSRRC records were later associated, **`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)`** completely sweeps aside the 1995 "not well grounded" denial and restores the 1995 effective date!

blocks.text: 3. Critical Era & Bitemporal Traps

items: **Never Attack Lack of a C&P Exam in 1990–2000 as CUE:** Double kill-switch—both because pre-VCAA law denied exams to non-well-grounded claims (*Grottveit*) and because duty-to-assist errors can never constitute CUE (*Cook v. Principi*, 318 F.3d 1334 (Fed. Cir. 2002) (en banc)).

***Karnas v. Derwinski* Transitional Rule (1996/1997 VASRD Changes):** If a claim was pending across the **Nov. 7, 1996** mental health change or **July 3, 1997** muscle injury change, VA was required under *Karnas v. Derwinski*, 1 Vet. App. 308 (1991) to apply whichever version of the regulation was **more favorable** to the veteran (for the period after the amendment's effective date, while applying only the old rule prior to the amendment's effective date).

***George v. McDonough* (`596 U.S. 740 (2022)`) & `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)` Gate:** Under `§ 20.1403(e)`, a post-decision judicial reinterpretation (e.g., *Bradley v. Peake* in 2008 or *Barry v. McDonough* in 2024) applies to **open/pending** 1990s claims (including Legacy claims kept non-final under *Lang* `§ 3.156(b)` or *Tablazon* missing SOCs), whereas attacking a **final** 1990s decision via CUE must rest on regulatory/statutory commands that were settled at the time of that decision.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Era 3 (1988–2000): Early Court Review & 'Not Well Grounded' Denials
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: The Veterans' Judicial Review Act of November 18, 1988 created independent court review for the first time and required written explanations on VA decisions. However, between November 1988 and November 2000, the law also enforced a strict hurdle called the 'well-grounded claim' rule: if a Veteran did not already have medical evidence linking a condition to service, VA routinely dismissed the claim as 'not well grounded' without providing a VA medical exam. Starting July 21, 1992, VA also became legally responsible for VA hospital records that existed when it decided a claim even if they had not been copied into the paper claims folder.
record_clues: A 1990s Regional Office or Board denial letter stating your claim was 'not well grounded'—especially if military medical or unit records were missing at the time.
A rating decision dated on or after July 21, 1992 that overlooked findings already recorded in VA Medical Center computer or hospital charts.
Rating decisions issued near major 1990s schedule updates, such as the November 7, 1996 mental health update or the July 3, 1997 muscle-injury update (published June 3, 1997).
important_cautions: A 1990–2000 'not well grounded' denial usually cannot be overturned via Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) merely because VA declined to schedule a C&P exam—under the law in effect before November 9, 2000, VA did not owe an exam until a claim was well grounded, and duty-to-assist errors are not CUE.

Always separate a regulation's Federal Register publication date from its effective date (for example, 38 C.F.R. § 4.56 was published June 3, 1997 but took effect July 3, 1997), and note that post-decision court reinterpretations cannot establish CUE against final decisions under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e) (George v. McDonough).
Congress created Board CUE motions on November 21, 1997, subject to 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c)'s strict limit of one final merits CUE decision per prior Board decision on an issue.

blocks.text: 1. Regulatory & Statutory Inflection Points

items: **Veterans Claims Assistance Act of 2000 (`Pub. L. 106-475`, `114 Stat. 2096`, Nov. 9, 2000):** Eliminated the "well-grounded claim" barrier and codified `38 U.S.C. § 5103` (VCAA notice) and `§ 5103A` (duty to assist, including low-threshold medical nexus exams under `38 C.F.R. § 3.159(c)(4)` and *McLendon v. Nicholson*, 20 Vet. App. 79 (2006)).

**2006 Expansion of Paid Representation (`Pub. L. 109-461`, `120 Stat. 3403`, enacted Dec. 22, 2006):** For NODs filed on or after **June 20, 2007**, accredited attorneys and agents could charge fees right after the RO decision/NOD rather than waiting for a final BVA decision.

**2006 `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)` Overhaul (`71 FR 52455`, published Sept. 6, 2006, eff. Oct. 6, 2006):** Clarified mandatory retroactive effective dates under `§ 3.156(c)(3)` back to the previously denied claim (see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) Service Department Records (Pre-Oct. 6, 2006 vs. Current)](/cfr/38-cfr-3.156c)).

**Major VASRD & Presumptive Amendments (Publication vs. Effective Dates):**
• **August 30, 2002 & September 23, 2002:** Interim Scars (`38 C.F.R. § 4.118`, `67 FR 49590`, published July 31, 2002, **effective Aug. 30, 2002**, converting area thresholds to `sq. in. / sq. cm.`) and Interim Spine IVDS (`DC 5293`, `67 FR 54345`, published Aug. 22, 2002, **effective Sept. 23, 2002**, incapacitating-episode duration formula).
• **September 26, 2003:** Spine Formula (`38 C.F.R. § 4.71a`, `68 FR 51454`, published Aug. 27, 2003, **effective Sept. 26, 2003**) — goniometer ROM degrees + separate radiculopathy ratings under Note (1) (see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 4.71a Spine Evolution (Former DC 5285–5295 vs. Modern DC 5235–5243)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.71a-spine-evolution)).
• **October 23, 2008:** Scars & Disfigurement (`38 C.F.R. § 4.118`, `73 FR 54708`, published Sept. 23, 2008, **effective Oct. 23, 2008**; clarified Jan. 20, 2012 at `77 FR 2909`) — 8 disfigurement characteristics under `DC 7800` and count-based painful/unstable scar ratings under `DC 7804` (see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 4.118 Scars & Disfigurement (DC 7800–7805, 1946–Present)](/cfr/38-cfr-4.118)).
• **July 12, 2010:** PTSD Stressor Liberalization (`38 C.F.R. § 3.304(f)(3)`, `75 FR 39843`, **published July 13, 2010, effective July 12, 2010**) — VA/contract psychiatrist confirmation of fear of hostile military or terrorist activity eliminates JSRRC corroboration for non-combat veterans in theater.
• **August 31, 2010:** *Nehmer* Herbicide Expansion (`75 FR 53202`, published & **effective Aug. 31, 2010**) — added **Ischemic Heart Disease (IHD)**, **Parkinson's disease**, and **hairy cell / B-cell leukemias** to `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(e)`.
• **August 4, 2014:** DSM-5 Mental Health Transition (`79 FR 45093`, interim final rule published & **effective Aug. 4, 2014**; adopted final Mar. 19, 2015, `80 FR 14308`).
• **August 13, 2018:** Skin & Scars Revision (`83 FR 32592`, published July 13, 2018, **effective Aug. 13, 2018**).

blocks.text: 2. The March 24, 2015 Hard Wall (Death of Informal Claims)

Effective **March 24, 2015** (`79 FR 57660`, published Sept. 25, 2014 — see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: Former 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.155(a) & 3.157(b) Informal Claims (Repealed March 24, 2015)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.155-3.157b-informal-claims-pre-2015)), VA abolished the decades-old informal claim regime:

items: **Before March 24, 2015:** `21-4138` statements, letters from VSOs/congressional offices, and VAMC hospital/outpatient reports (`§ 3.157(b)` for already-SC conditions) triggered valid informal claim effective dates.

**On or After March 24, 2015:**
• Claims **must** be filed on prescribed standardized forms (`VA Form 21-526EZ` for initial/increase; `VA Form 21-0966` Intent to File preserving up to 1 year to submit the complete form).
• `38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b)` was **completely repealed**. VAMC medical records dated March 24, 2015 or later **never** initiate an informal increased-rating claim on their own.
• **Pre-2015 Informal-Claim Scope vs. Post-2015 Forms (*Shea v. Wilkie* vs. *Sellers v. Wilkie*):** Note that *Shea v. Wilkie*, 926 F.3d 1362, 1370 (Fed. Cir. 2019) is **not** an exception to the post-2015 Intent-to-File requirement—it construed **pre-March 24, 2015 `38 C.F.R. § 3.155(a)`** informal-claim scope (holding that where a pre-2015 filing refers to specific medical records containing a reasonably ascertainable diagnosis, it raises an informal claim for that condition). For **post-March 24, 2015** standardized forms (`21-526EZ`), *Sellers v. Wilkie*, 965 F.3d 1328 (Fed. Cir. 2020) governs: a claimant must minimally identify the sickness, disease, or injuries for which benefits are sought on the prescribed form rather than relying on unreferenced medical records.

blocks.text: 3. Screening Opportunities & Bitemporal Traps

items: **The `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b)` 1-Year Post-Decision VAMC Goldmine (*Beraud* & *Lang*):** Even after March 24, 2015 killed informal claims, **every Legacy rating decision issued before February 19, 2019** remained subject to `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b)`! Under *Beraud v. McDonald*, 766 F.3d 1402 (Fed. Cir. 2014) and *Lang v. Wilkie*, 971 F.3d 1348 (Fed. Cir. 2020), if a VAMC generated relevant clinical records within **1 year *after*** a Legacy RO decision and VA never issued a determination on whether those records were new and material, **that Legacy decision never became final**!

**Bitemporal *George v. McDonough* Gate (`596 U.S. 740 (2022)`; `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`):** Because `§ 3.156(b)` (*Lang*) or `§ 3.156(c)` keeps/reopens the historical claim on direct merits rather than CUE, intervening judicial reinterpretations (such as *Bradley v. Peake* (2008) on TDIU-anchored `SMC(s)` or *Barry v. McDonough* (2024) on multi-step `§ 3.350(f)` SMC) apply **retroactively without triggering the `§ 20.1403(e)` change-in-interpretation CUE bar**!

**Audit the Feb–March 2015 Window:** Any VAMC exam, hospital admission, `21-4138`, or eBenefits incomplete saved application initiated *before* March 24, 2015 is governed by the old informal-claim rules.

**Legacy Implicit Denial Still Applies:** For any rating decision issued **prior to February 19, 2019** (and non-RAMP), VA can still raise *Deshotel*/*Adams*/*Hampton*/*Steele* implicit denial if a related pending claim was omitted. Check *Hamill v. Collins*, `166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. 2026)` once you cross February 19, 2019!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Era 4 (2000–2018): Duty-to-Assist Era & The 2015 Standard Form Wall
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: On November 9, 2000, Congress passed the Veterans Claims Assistance Act (VCAA), ending 'not well grounded' dismissals and requiring VA to help gather records and provide medical nexus exams when basic clues exist. Two major date boundaries define this era: first, on March 24, 2015, VA ended informal letter and hospital-report claims, requiring standardized forms (such as Intent to File Form 21-0966 and Form 21-526EZ); second, for Legacy Regional Office decisions issued before February 19, 2019, relevant VA Medical Center records created within one year after a decision could keep that claim legally open under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b) if VA never reviewed them.
record_clues: Written statements (Form 21-4138), unemployability evidence, or VA hospital exam reports dated BEFORE March 24, 2015 versus standardized Form 21-526EZ / 21-0966 filings ON OR AFTER March 24, 2015.
VA Medical Center treatment notes created within 365 days AFTER a 2000–2018 Regional Office rating decision for the exact condition decided.

Ratings for spine conditions (updated September 26, 2003), scars and Traumatic Brain Injury (updated October 23, 2008), non-combat PTSD fear stressors (updated July 13, 2010 per 75 FR 39843 & 75 FR 41092), or 2010 Agent Orange additions (ischemic heart disease, Parkinson's, B-cell leukemias).
important_cautions: March 24, 2015 is a strict regulatory cutoff: VA medical notes or informal letters dated on or after March 24, 2015 do not start a claim without a prescribed VA claim form or Intent to File.

Once a 2000–2018 decision becomes truly final, a failure in VA's duty to assist (such as an inadequate C&P exam) cannot establish Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE), and later court reinterpretations are barred in CUE under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e) (George v. McDonough)—which is why checking whether the claim stayed open under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b) or § 3.156(c) matters first.

In pre-February 19, 2019 Legacy decisions, VA may argue a related unmentioned issue was 'implicitly denied,' and Board CUE motions remain limited by 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c) to one final merits CUE decision per prior Board issue.
questions_for_representative: Did I receive VA Medical Center care for my claimed condition within one year after my pre-February 19, 2019 rating decision that could have kept the claim open under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b)?
Were any written statements, unemployability clues, or VA exam reports received before the March 24, 2015 informal-claim cutoff never adjudicated?
Did VA apply the exact spine, scar, TBI, or Nehmer effective-date rule in force on my 2000–2018 decision date?

blocks.text: 1. Appeals Modernization Act (AMA) Architecture (Effective Feb. 19, 2019)

items:
**Three Review Lanes (`Pub. L. 115-55`, `131 Stat. 1105`; `38 U.S.C. § 5104C`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.2500`, `84 FR 138`, published Jan. 18, 2019, effective Feb. 19, 2019):**
• **Supplemental Claim (`VA Form 20-0995`):** Requires "new and relevant" evidence (`38 U.S.C. § 5108`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(d)`, a lower threshold than Legacy "new and material"); triggers full duty to assist.
• **Higher-Level Review (`VA Form 20-0996`):** Closed-record de novo review by senior adjudicator; no new evidence permitted, though HLR "duty to assist error" return converts the claim back into a Supplemental development lane!
• **Board Appeal (`VA Form 10182`):** Direct Review (closed record), Evidence Submission (90-day window), or Hearing (testimony + 90-day post-hearing evidence window).

**Continuous Pursuit (`38 C.F.R. § 3.2500(c) & (h)`):** Protects the original effective date continuously so long as a valid lane election is filed within **one year** of each AOJ decision or **within one year of a Board denial** (`Supplemental Claim`).
• **CRITICAL TRAP:** Continuous pursuit **stops at the CAVC/Fed. Cir.** Filing a `20-0995` Supplemental Claim within 1 year of a **CAVC affirmance** does **not** preserve the earlier effective date (*see* `38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)(2)(D)-(E)`). Always evaluate whether to file a Supplemental Claim within 1 year of the *Board* decision or seek CAVC vacatur/remand!

blocks.text: 2. Landmark Judicial Shifts (2020–2026) & Bitemporal Scope

items: ***Lang v. Wilkie*, 971 F.3d 1348 (Fed. Cir. 2020):** VAMC clinical records generated within 1 year *after* a Legacy RO rating decision are constructively received under `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b)`, preventing finality from attaching unless VA adjudicated whether they were new and material.

***George v. McDonough*, 596 U.S. 740 (2022):** Later judicial invalidation or reinterpretation of a VA regulation (`38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`) does **not** make prior reliance on that regulation "clear and unmistakable error" (establishing the core bitemporal split between Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) doctrines and CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive doctrines).
***Arellano v. McDonough*, 598 U.S. 1 (2023):** `38 U.S.C. § 5110(b)(1)` (the 1-year post-discharge filing window for discharge-day effective dates) is **not subject to equitable tolling**.

***Barry v. McDonough*, 101 F.4th 1348 (Fed. Cir. May 16, 2024):** Overturned VA's single-step ceiling on `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(f)(3)–(4)`, holding veterans at base `SMC(l)–(n)` can receive **multiple** half-step and full-step intermediate SMC increases (up to `SMC(o)`) for each independent `50%` or `100%` disability *(open-claim / continuous-pursuit / `§ 3.156(b)–(c)` safe; CUE on final pre-May 2024 ratings faces `§ 20.1403(e)` / George defenses)*.
***Bufkin v. Collins*, 604 U.S. 369 (2025):** CAVC reviews the Board's approximate-balance determination under the `38 U.S.C. § 5107(b)` benefit-of-the-doubt standard for clear error.

***Ingram v. Collins*, 38 Vet. App. 130 (2025) & Rescinded `38 C.F.R. § 4.10` Medication IFR (`91 FR 7118`, rescinded `91 FR 9712`, Feb. 17–27, 2026):** Reaffirmed that VA **cannot discount disability ratings based on the ameliorative effects of medication** unless the Diagnostic Code explicitly accounts for medication. VA issued an Interim Final Rule on Feb. 17, 2026 (`91 FR 7118`) attempting to reverse *Ingram*, **rescinded it on Feb. 27, 2026 (`91 FR 9712`)**, and abandoned its Federal Circuit appeal (`No. 25-1972`) on Mar. 30, 2026—flag any rating rendered **Feb. 17–27, 2026** (or earlier/later) that discounted symptoms due to medication!

***Soto v. United States*, 605 U.S. 360 (June 12, 2025):** Unanimously abolished the 6-year Barring Act (`31 U.S.C. § 3702`) cap on retroactive **Title 10 DoD Combat-Related Special Compensation (CRSC)** (`10 U.S.C. § 1413a`), followed by **Aug. 20, 2025 DoD guidance** and parallel Court of Federal Claims Tucker Act claims (e.g., *Christopher Carey v. United States* for >\$10,000 arrears).

***Hamill v. Collins*, 166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 4, 2026) (`No. 24-1543`) & *Cash v. Collins*, No. 24-1811 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 5, 2026):** *Hamill* abolished the **implicit denial doctrine** for all AMA-era decisions (`>= Feb. 19, 2019`) under `38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)` (noting in fn. 6 that within 1 year of a silent AMA decision, HLR or Board appeal is the proper remedy over mandamus). *Cash* held under `38 U.S.C. § 7113(c)` that a Board NOD (`VA Form 10182`) identifying probative "in-between" AMA evidence already in VA's possession compels Board consideration without physical resubmission.

***Freund v. Collins*, No. 21-4168 (Vet. App. class certified Mar. 2026):** Landmark CAVC class action covering ~28,000+ legacy appeals improperly closed by VACOLS automated sweeps (Dec. 12, 1990 – Feb. 6, 2025) despite timely appellate posture.

blocks.text: 3. PACT Act (Pub. L. 117-168, 136 Stat. 1759, Aug. 10, 2022) & Effective Dates

items: **Expanded Herbicide Locations & Conditions (`38 U.S.C. §§ 1116, 1116A`):** Added Thailand (any U.S./Royal Thai base), Laos, Cambodia (Mimot/Krek), Guam, American Samoa, Johnston Atoll, plus **hypertension** and **MGUS**.

**Gulf War / Post-9/11 Burn Pit Presumptions (`38 U.S.C. § 1120`) & TERA (`§ 1168`):** Added 23+ respiratory and cancer presumptions and mandated Toxic Exposure Risk Activity (TERA) medical nexus exams.

**Retroactive Effective Date Nuances & OIG Error Pattern:**
• Under `38 C.F.R. § 3.114` (liberalizing law) and PACT Act transition rules, claims filed (or covered by an Intent to File) by **August 14, 2023** could receive an effective date back to **August 10, 2022** (assuming disability existed then). **VA OIG documented \$20.4 million in underpayments** caused by raters assigning claim-receipt dates rather than `Aug. 10, 2022` or `§ 3.114(a)` 1-year lookbacks!
• **Crucial *Nehmer* Exclusions vs. Inclusions:** `M21-1 VIII.i.2.B.1.c` explicitly **excludes hypertension, MGUS, and chloracne** from `38 C.F.R. § 3.816` *Nehmer* class retroactivity. Conversely, check whether **RVN / Blue Water Navy (`Procopio` / `Pub. L. 116-23`)** claims for classic *Nehmer* `§ 3.309(e)` conditions qualify for full `§ 3.816` retroactivity back to post-1985 denied claims, OR whether `§ 3.156(c)` newly associated unit/deck records carry even a PACT-granted claim back to an original denial (*Emerson*)!

blocks.text: 4. Regulatory & VASRD Status Check (Enacted vs. Unfinalized Proposals Through Late 2026)

items: **ENACTED — Musculoskeletal (`85 FR 76453`, published Nov. 30, 2020, eff. Feb. 7, 2021):** Objective assistive-device rules for knee instability (`DC 5257`), updated prosthetic minimums, added plantar fasciitis (`DC 5285`), and added Compartment Syndrome (`DC 5331`, each affected muscle group rated separately).

**ENACTED — Bilateral Factor Exclusion (`88 FR 22914`, published Apr. 14, 2023, eff. April 16, 2023):** Added `38 C.F.R. § 4.26(d)` excluding bilateral disabilities from the `10%` bilateral bonus whenever including them causes combined math to round down from `100%` to `90%`.

**ENACTED — Digestive System (`89 FR 19735`, published Mar. 20, 2024, eff. May 19, 2024):** Created `DC 7206` for GERD (esophageal stricture/dysphagia model) and updated `DC 7319` IBS (`10%/20%/30%` Rome IV frequency model). Pre-May 19, 2024 ratings are protected against schedule-based reductions (`38 U.S.C. § 1155`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.951(a)`).

**ENACTED — Character of Discharge (`38 C.F.R. § 3.12`, `89 FR 32361`, published Apr. 26, 2024, eff. June 25, 2024):** Overhauled `§ 3.12(d)` regulatory bars and created the **"compelling circumstances"** exception for prolonged AWOL and moral turpitude discharges.

**NOT FINALIZED (Still Proposed as of Late 2026):**
• **Sleep Apnea (`DC 6847`) & Tinnitus (`DC 6260`) (`RIN 2900-AQ72`, `87 FR 8474`, Feb. 15, 2022):** Proposed rule eliminating standalone `10%` tinnitus and `50%` CPAP sleep apnea ratings has **NOT** been published as a Final Rule. Current criteria (`10%` standalone `DC 6260`; `50%` CPAP `DC 6847`) **remain active law**.
• **Mental Disorders (`38 C.F.R. § 4.130`, `RIN 2900-AQ82`, `87 FR 8498`, Feb. 15, 2022):** Proposed domain-based WHODAS overhaul (`10%` minimum floor) has **NOT** been published as a Final Rule. Existing `§ 4.130` (`0/10/30/50/70/100%`) remains active law.
• **Painful Scars (`DC 7804`, `90 FR 46542`, Sept. 29, 2025):** Proposed note requiring objective evidence of pain upon examination/demonstration has **NOT** been published as a Final Rule. Existing `DC 7804` painful scar criteria remain active law.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Era 5 (2019–Present): Modern AMA Lanes, PACT Act & Recent Rulings
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Starting February 19, 2019, the Appeals Modernization Act (AMA) replaced the old multi-year appeal process with three review options—Supplemental Claims (Form 20-0995), Higher-Level Reviews (Form 20-0996), and Board Appeals (Form 10182)—allowing you to protect your original effective date by pursuing a review option within one year of each VA or Board decision. This era also includes the August 2022 PACT Act toxic-exposure expansions, the June 2024 Character of Discharge update, and major 2024–2026 court rulings on explicit decision notices, medication effects, Special Monthly Compensation steps, and Combat-Related Special Compensation back pay.
record_clues: An AMA decision letter dated on or after February 19, 2019 that stayed completely silent on a claimed or reasonably raised condition (which courts held in 2026 cannot be 'implicitly denied' under 38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)).

A PACT Act grant where VA assigned the date your form arrived instead of looking back up to one year (or to August 10, 2022 for timely 2022–2023 Intent to File claims), or a survivor DIC denial eligible for PACT re-evaluation under 38 C.F.R. § 3.33.

A rating issued around February 17–27, 2026 that lowered an evaluation because medication reduced symptoms (under a short-lived 38 C.F.R. § 4.10 interim rule at 91 FR 7118 that VA rescinded 10 days later at 91 FR 9712).
important_cautions: Deadline caution: While filing a Supplemental Claim within 1 year of a Regional Office or Board denial preserves continuous pursuit under 38 C.F.R. § 3.2500, filing a Supplemental Claim after a Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims (CAVC) affirmance does NOT preserve the original effective date—and CAVC appeals carry a 120-day filing window from a Board denial.

Do not confuse online rumors about proposed rules with active law: proposed changes to sleep apnea (DC 6847) and tinnitus (DC 6260) under RIN 2900-AQ72, mental health under RIN 2900-AQ82, and painful scars under 90 FR 46542 remain unfinalized proposals (not enacted law), and the February 2026 medication rule (91 FR 7118) was rescinded.

Under Arellano v. McDonough (2023), the 1-year post-discharge filing window for a day-after-discharge effective date cannot be extended by equitable tolling, and Board CUE motions remain governed by 38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1403(e) and 20.1409(c).
