4. Bitemporal Pathway Selection & Kill-Switches

blocks.text: A VA rating decision or Statement of the Case **never becomes final**—and its 1-year appellate clock **never begins to run**—if VA failed to mail notice in strict compliance with `38 U.S.C. § 5104(a)` (`former § 3004(a)`, enacted by `Pub. L. 101-237`, eff. Feb. 1, 1990; renumbered by `Pub. L. 102-40`, May 7, 1991) and `38 U.S.C. § 7105` (`former § 4005`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.103`) (*Hauck v. Brown*, 6 Vet. App. 518 (1994)). Likewise, summary denials for "failing to report" for a C&P exam (`38 C.F.R. § 3.655`) frequently harbor either defective exam notice or illegal disregard of existing evidence.
1. C-File Red Flags (Audit Triggers)

items: **Returned Mail Scans:** Search VBMS / paper C-file for scanned envelopes, `VA Form 20-8992` / `21-0820` Report of General Information notes saying *"Mail returned undeliverable"*, or handwritten `"RTS"` notations.

**Chronological Address Audit:** Build a mini-table of every address appearing in the C-file (`DD-214` mailing address, `21-526`, `21-4138`, change-of-address cards, VAMC `10-10` admission facesheets, VSO `21-22` POA forms) in the 24 months prior to a denial. Compare character-by-character against:
• The C&P exam scheduling letter (if preserved), AND
• The Rating Decision / SOC notification letter (and copy to representative!).

**Summary `§ 3.655` Denials:** Any rating decision reading *"Veteran failed to report for examination without good cause; claim denied"*—especially on an **original** claim where STRs + medical evidence were already in the file, or an **increased-rating / reopened / supplemental** claim where exam notice went to an outdated address!

blocks.text: 2. Substantive Rules on 38 C.F.R. § 3.655 (Failure to Report for C&P Exam)
Since **December 31, 1990**, `38 C.F.R. § 3.655` establishes a sharp dichotomy based on **claim type**:

rows: Claim **shall be rated based on the evidence of record**! It **cannot** be automatically denied solely as punishment for missing an exam!
Rater issued a knee-jerk automatic denial despite STRs + medical evidence already establishing SC or a partial rating -> **CUE (`§ 3.105(a)`)** if existing evidence undebatably warranted a grant!
**Increased-Rating or Reopened / Supplemental Claim (`§ 3.655(b)` second sentence)**
May be denied for failure to report *only if* claimant failed to report **without good cause**!
Exam notice went to a wrong/outdated address ("good cause" per `§ 3.655(a)` examples includes illness, hospitalization, or death in immediate family, plus lack of notice!).
Requires **60-day pretermination notice**; if veteran expresses willingness to report before cut, VA must reschedule!
RO reduced or stopped an existing award after a single missed reexamination without issuing `§ 3.655(c)` / `§ 3.105(e)` 60-day advance notice -> **Void reduction**!

lines: **Exact Federal Register History of `38 C.F.R. § 3.655` (Publication vs. Effective Date — Verbatim Snapshot at [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 3.655 Failure to Report for VA Examination (Pre-Dec. 31, 1990 vs. 55 FR 49521 & AMA)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.655-examinations-evolution)):**
* **Pre-December 31, 1990:** Former `38 C.F.R. § 3.655` governed 1-year "abandonment" for failure to report.

* **1990 Overhaul (`55 FR 49521`):** Published **November 29, 1990**, **effective December 31, 1990** (revising `§§ 3.326, 3.327, 3.330, 3.655` to separate original claims rated on the record from reopened/increased-rating claims denied for failure to report without good cause; subsequently amended at `58 FR 46865`, Sept. 3, 1993; `80 FR 18117`, Apr. 3, 2015; and `84 FR 138, 171`, Jan. 18, 2019, eff. Feb. 19, 2019 substituting "supplemental" for "reopened"). *(Citation Guardrail: Do not confuse `55 FR 49521` on `§ 3.655` with `55 FR 31579`, published Aug. 3, 1990, eff. Sept. 4, 1990, which amended `38 C.F.R. § 4.16(a)` TDIU marginal employment!)*

blocks.text: 3. Rebutting the Presumption of Regularity (Notice of Decisions & Exams)

Under *Ashley v. Derwinski*, 2 Vet. App. 307, 309 (1992) and *Mindenhall v. Brown*, 7 Vet. App. 271, 274 (1994), VA enjoys a rebuttable **presumption of regularity** that it properly mailed decisions and exam notices to the latest address of record.
Step 1: Claimant Produces "Clear Evidence" of Irregularity
Any of the following satisfies "clear evidence" to **burst the presumption**:

items: **Wrong / Typo Address on the Letter:** Missing apartment number, transposed digits, wrong city/ZIP, or using an older C-file address when a newer address was already in the claims folder (*Crain v. Principi*, 17 Vet. App. 182 (2003); *Davis v. Principi*, 17 Vet. App. 29 (2003)).

**Returned Undeliverable Mail + Alternate Address Available:** When a decision letter comes back undeliverable and **any other plausible address** exists in the claims file or VAMC records (*Cross v. Brown*, 9 Vet. App. 18, 19–20 (1996); *Woods v. Gober*, 14 Vet. App. 214 (2000)), VA cannot sit on the returned envelope—it must check its records and remail!

**Representative Nonreceipt + Systemic Mailing Irregularity (*Romero v. Tran*, 33 Vet. App. 252 (2021)):** *Romero* specifically governs mailing an SOC/decision to a claimant's **accredited representative** (rather than wrong-address C&P notices), holding that nonreceipt **combined with** clear evidence of systemic VA mailing irregularity (practitioner affidavits, NOVA declaration, GAO report) bursts regularity.
**No Copy of Notice Letter in C-File + Corroborating Procedural Anomalies:** E.g., rating sheet marked `"File Only — Do Not Notify"` or blank address block.

blocks.text: Step 2: Burden Shifts to the Secretary

Once clear evidence bursts the presumption, the burden shifts to VA to establish by affirmative evidence that the decision was **actually mailed properly or actually received** by the claimant (*Ashley*, 2 Vet. App. at 309; *Romero*, 33 Vet. App. at 262). If VA cannot prove proper mailing/receipt, **the appeal period never started**—the veteran can file a timely Notice of Disagreement / appeal **today** on a 1979 or 1998 rating decision!
4. Bitemporal Pathway Selection & Kill-Switches

items: **Pathway A — Defective Decision Notice (Pending Appeal / Non-Final Decision — Bypasses *George*!):** File a timely NOD / direct response asserting the prior RO decision never became final due to defective `§ 5104(a)` mailing notice, supported by exhibits of the address discrepancy or returned envelope. Because the claim remains **open on direct review**, **benefit of the doubt (`§ 5107(b)`), full duty to assist, and post-decision judicial precedents apply without triggering *George v. McDonough*, 596 U.S. 740 (2022) / `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`**!

**Pathway B — Defective Exam Notice + Later Re-filing:** If a later decision *validly* noticed and adjudicated the exact same condition before Feb. 19, 2019, check whether that later decision closed the pending claim (*Adams* / *Williams*)—if the later decision *granted* service connection and simply set the effective date as the *new* claim date while overlooking that the earlier claim was still pending from defective notice, appeal/challenge the effective-date assignment (or raise CUE under `§ 3.105(a)` if final and undebatable on the face of the C-file!).

**Kill-Switch (Bare Nonreceipt & `CAVC Rule 30(a)` Nonprecedential Warning on *Marion v. Collins*):** Never rely solely on an affidavit from the veteran or representative saying *"I have good mail-handling habits and never received the decision"* (*Mindenhall*, 7 Vet. App. at 274; see [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)). Note that *Marion v. Collins*, No. 24-6964 (Vet. App. Dec. 23, 2025) (mem. dec.) is a **single-judge nonprecedential memorandum decision (`CAVC Rule 30(a)` — do NOT cite as binding precedent)**, illustrating that counsel's bare affidavit of nonreceipt of an HLR decision without systemic or C-file corroboration fails.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Mail Sent to the Wrong Address, Returned VA Letters & Missed C&P Exam Denials
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Normally, if you do not appeal a VA decision within 1 year, that decision becomes final because courts presume VA properly mailed it to your latest address of record. However, if your VA Claims File (C-file) shows VA mailed a Rating Decision, Statement of the Case (SOC), or Compensation and Pension (C&P) exam scheduling notice to an outdated, mistyped, or incomplete address—especially when another part of VA (such as your VA Medical Center) already had your current address—the 1-year appeal clock may never have legally started. In addition, under 38 C.F.R. § 3.655(b), when a Veteran misses an exam on an original compensation claim, VA is prohibited from denying the claim automatically just for missing the appointment and must instead evaluate the claim on the evidence already in the file.
record_clues: Scanned envelopes or mail-room sheets in your C-file stamped 'RETURN TO SENDER,' 'UNDELIVERABLE,' 'MOVED LEFT NO ADDRESS,' or 'UNCLAIMED.'
A street number, apartment unit, or ZIP code typo on a VA decision cover letter compared to the address you wrote on your claim form, VA Form 21-4138, or VA Medical Center registration.

An older rating decision denying your initial disability claim solely because you 'failed to report for a scheduled VA examination' or calling the claim 'abandoned' without evaluating your service medical records.
A gap in your C-file where you filed a timely Notice of Disagreement (NOD), or never received the decision letter, and VA closed the file without mailing notice to all required addresses.
important_cautions: More Than 'I Never Got It' Is Required: Courts presume official government mail was sent properly unless concrete evidence—such as a wrong address in the C-file, returned-mail stamps, or missing mailing records—rebuts that presumption (Mindenhall v. Brown; compare nonprecedential CAVC Rule 30(a) single-judge discussions such as Marion v. Collins, No. 24-6964 (Vet. App. Dec. 23, 2025) (mem. dec.)).

Check Whether a Later Decision Closed the Claim: Under pre-February 19, 2019 Legacy rules, a later rating decision that validly notified you at your correct address and decided the exact same disability issue could start the finality clock from that later date—whereas post-February 19, 2019 AMA decisions require explicit issue notice under 38 U.S.C. § 5104(b) (Hamill v. Collins).

Original Claims vs. Increase/Supplemental Claims (§ 3.655): Effective December 31, 1990 (published November 29, 1990 at 55 FR 49521), § 3.655(b) requires VA to decide an original compensation claim on the existing record after an unexcused missed exam, whereas claims for increase or supplemental/reopened claims may be denied if an exam was missed without good cause.
questions_for_representative: Can we compare the mailing address on the old VA decision letter and exam scheduling notice against every address listed in my VAMC medical records and claim forms on that date?
Are there any scanned returned-mail envelopes in my VBMS eFolder showing VA knew the notice was undeliverable?
Was my claim an original compensation claim that VA denied outright for missing a C&P exam without rating the service records already in the file under 38 C.F.R. § 3.655(b)?
Did any later properly mailed VA decision explicitly adjudicate that same condition, or could the original claim still be legally pending?

title: Playbook 03: Newly Associated Service Department Records (38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c))
keyPrecedents: George v. Shulkin, 29 Vet. App. 199 (2018), vacated in part on other grounds
cFileTriggers: Early denial stating 'Service medical records negative for...' or 'No corroborated stressor in service' followed years later by a grant
Condition ALREADY service-connected via a later liberalizing rule (§ 3.304(f) PTSD or PACT Act), where newly found unit/STR records now corroborate the original denied claim (Emerson)
NPRC NA Form 13055 / St. Louis 1973 fire memo in C-file
Late-associated inpatient clinical packet, deck logs, morning reports, JSRRC/CRUR response, DA Form 20, or upgraded DD-215
Supplemental Claim granting SC on date of 20-0995 / reopened claim despite newly associated STRs or unit logs
killSwitches: Prior denial was solely for 'no current diagnosis' while in-service event was ALREADY conceded, OR VA already evaluated the newly associated record in an intermediate reopening denied for lack of diagnosis (Blubaugh / Kisor)
Newly submitted record is a private post-service record, buddy statement, or VA medical record rather than an official 'service department record'
Record did not exist at the time of the prior VA decision (unless it is a JSRRC/DoD archival verification or NPRC fire reconstruction under § 3.156(c)(1)(ii)-(iii))

toc.text: 1. C-File Red Flags (Audit Triggers)
2. The Three-Element Test Under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)(1) & (3)
3. Effective Date & Staged Rating Mechanics (§ 3.156(c)(3)–(4))
4. Legal Pathway Selection, Post-Grant Reconsideration & Kill-Switches

blocks.text: `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)` is the premier **"time-machine" provision** in Veterans Law. Unlike CUE, it requires **no showing of undebatable error**, permits **contemporary medical nexus opinions** to link the newly associated service record to a current disability, and mandates an effective date reaching all the way back to the **original previously denied claim** (or date entitlement arose, whichever is later).
1. C-File Red Flags (Audit Triggers)
Whenever a veteran was **denied decades ago** and **granted much later** (or is currently denied for lack of in-service documentation), audit the two VBMS upload/receipt dates:

items:
**Compare the Evidence List on Denial #1 vs. Grant #2:**
• Did Denial #1 list *only* the DD-214 or outpatient health jacket (`"SMRs negative for back trauma"`), while Grant #2 followed receipt of **inpatient hospital clinical records**, **Reserve/National Guard drill STRs (`LOD` line-of-duty reports)**, **ship deck logs**, **morning reports**, **military police blotters**, or a **JSRRC / CRUR stressor report**?
• **Classic Rater Error:** When granting on the later Supplemental/Reopened claim, RVSRs routinely default to the date of the Supplemental Claim (`VA Form 20-0995` / `21-526EZ`) and completely forget to check whether `§ 3.156(c)(3)` mandates the **1972, 1984, or 1996 original claim date**!

**Proactive Archive Hunts (When Records Still Haven't Been Pulled):**
• **Inpatient Clinical Records (NPRC / St. Louis):** Stored by hospital name and year, *not* always merged into the veteran's outpatient STR folder!
• **1973 NPRC Fire Cases:** SGO (Surgeon General's Office) hospital admission punch-card index extracts, unit morning reports, pay vouchers, and VA hospital folders.
• **DD Form 215 Corrections / Awards:** Retroactive Purple Heart, CIB, CAR, or Air Medal citations verifying combat stressors previously rejected as uncorroborated.
• **Classified / Declassified DoD Exposure Records (`§ 3.156(c)(1)(ii)`):** Project 112 / SHAD, Edgewood Arsenal, mustard gas, radiation logs, Camp Lejeune / Thailand / Johnston Atoll military unit histories.

blocks.text: 2. The Three-Element Test Under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)(1) & (3)
To unlock the earlier claim's effective date, prove:

items: **Official Service Department Record:** Generated by a military branch, DoD, Coast Guard, PHS/NOAA, JSRRC/CRUR, NARA/NPRC archival holdings of military unit records, or `§ 3.156(c)(1)(iii)` reconstructed NPRC fire records. (*Note:* Even if publicly accessible in National Archives in 1980, what matters is when it was **associated with the VA C-file**—*Emerson v. McDonald*, 28 Vet. App. 200 (2016)).
**Not Associated With the C-File at the Time of the Prior Decision:** Verify VBMS date stamps or paper C-file date-received stamps on the reverse/bottom margin of the STR pages.

**"Relevant" & Basis of Award "All or in Part" (*Vigil*, *Blubaugh*, *Kisor*):**
• **Relevance (*Kisor v. McDonough*, 995 F.3d 1316 (Fed. Cir. 2021)):** The newly associated record must speak to a **matter that was in dispute** in the prior denial (e.g., if the prior denial rejected in-service stressor, exposure, or injury, and the new record corroborates that stressor, exposure, or injury).
• **"All or in Part" (*Vigil v. Peake*, 22 Vet. App. 63 (2008)):** The service record **does NOT need to establish service connection all by itself**! Even if VA also needed a brand-new 2025 C&P medical nexus opinion to connect the newly found 1971 sick-call slip to the veteran's current arthritis, the grant is still based *"in part"* on the 1971 service record—triggering `§ 3.156(c)(3)`!

blocks.text: 3. Effective Date & Staged Rating Mechanics (§ 3.156(c)(3)–(4))

items:
**Effective Date Formula:** The **LATER** of:
• The date VA received the **previously decided claim**, OR
• The **date entitlement arose** (i.e., the earliest date the disability existed and met compensable/service-connected criteria).

**Critical Corollary for PTSD / Chronic Conditions:** Even if a formal PTSD diagnosis first appeared on a VA exam years later, audit contemporaneous lay evidence, employment history, VAMC notes, Social Security disability records, or private medical notes back to the original claim date to prove **"entitlement arose"** at (or shortly after) the original claim (*Mayhue v. Shinseki*, 24 Vet. App. 273 (2011) — watch out for when the veteran provided sufficient information for VA to request JSRRC records!).

**Retroactive Staged Ratings (`§ 3.156(c)(4)`):** Once `§ 3.156(c)(3)` sets an effective date in (say) 1982, VA must assign staged disability percentages (`10%`, `30%`, `50%`, `70%`, `TDIU/100%`) across the entire 1982–2026 period!

blocks.text: 4. Legal Pathway Selection, Post-Grant Reconsideration & Kill-Switches

items:
**Reconsideration EVEN AFTER Service Connection Was Already Granted (*Emerson*, 28 Vet. App. at 208; `M21-1 X.ii.2.B`):** Even if VA **already granted** service connection years later via a liberalizing rule (e.g., `2010` PTSD stressor relaxation under `38 C.F.R. § 3.304(f)` or `2022` PACT Act presumption), newly associating official service department records that corroborate the **original** 1975 or 1992 denial still compels `§ 3.156(c)` reconsideration and a retroactive effective date back to that original claim!
• **Filing Practice Tip:** When submitting newly obtained service department records under AMA on `VA Form 20-0995`, **explicitly label the top of the cover brief and form**: *"REQUEST FOR RECONSIDERATION AND EARLIER EFFECTIVE DATE UNDER 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) (NOT A STANDARD § 3.2500 SUPPLEMENTAL EFFECTIVE-DATE CLAIM)"* so intake processors do not assign the `20-0995` receipt date!

**Direct Appeal / HLR / Supplemental Claim of Effective Date:** If VA just granted service connection within the last year using a wrong modern effective date despite newly associated STRs/JSRRC records, file an **HLR (`20-0996`) or Board Appeal (`10182`)** within 1 year challenging the effective date under `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)(3)` (see verbatim snapshot [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) Service Department Records (Pre-Oct. 6, 2006 vs. Current)](/cfr/38-cfr-3.156c)).

**If the Later Grant Already Became Final Years Ago:**
• Can VA's failure to apply `§ 3.156(c)(3)` in a now-final grant be attacked via **CUE (`§ 3.105(a)`)**? **YES**, where the newly associated service records and continuous disability since the original claim were undebatably in the record at the time of that grant! Alternatively, if yet *additional* relevant service records are associated, file directly for `§ 3.156(c)(1)` reconsideration (*George v. Shulkin*, 29 Vet. App. 199 (2018)).

**The *Blubaugh* Intermediate-Denial Exhaustion Trap (`773 F.3d at 1314`):** If VA associated the missing service record during an **intermediate** reopening and denied that reopening for *lack of a current diagnosis*, `§ 3.156(c)` reconsideration was exhausted in that intermediate decision—a *third* claim granted years later when a diagnosis finally appears will not reach back to Claim #1.

**The *Mayhue* Address/Unit Info Trap:** Under *Mayhue v. Shinseki*, 24 Vet. App. 273 (2011), if VA could *not* locate unit records in Claim #1 ONLY because the veteran failed to provide unit name/dates (`§ 3.156(c)(2)`), and the veteran first supplied the unit name/dates in Claim #2 enabling JSRRC verification, VA may limit the effective date to Claim #2. Always verify whether the veteran's `DD-214` or personnel file (`OMPF`) *already* listed the unit during Claim #1!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Missing Military, Hospital & Unit Records Found Years Later (38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) Retroactive Reconsideration)
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Many Veterans were denied service connection decades ago—for combat injuries, in-service surgeries, PTSD stressors, or toxic exposures—simply because key official military records were sitting in a separate archive, misfiled, classified, or thought lost in the 1973 St. Louis National Personnel Records Center (NPRC) fire. Under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c), if VA later receives relevant official service department records that existed when VA previously denied the claim, VA must reconsider that earlier claim. Even if your condition was already granted years later on a reopened or Supplemental Claim, newly associated service records that help prove the original claim can push your effective date all the way back to the original claim date (or when the disability arose, if later)—without needing to prove Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE).
record_clues: An early VA denial stating 'Service medical records are negative for treatment' or 'No in-service stressor corroborated,' followed years later by VA granting the exact same condition.
An NPRC NA Form 13055 or 1973 St. Louis fire notice in your Claims File (C-file), later supplemented by reconstructed morning reports, hospital admission indices, pay records, or personnel files.

Military inpatient clinical packets (stored separately from outpatient health jackets), Navy deck logs, Air Force unit histories, DA Form 20 personnel files, DD-215 corrections, or Joint Services Records Research Center (JSRRC) / Defense Department combat verifications added to your C-file after the first denial.
A Supplemental Claim (VA Form 20-0995) award that set your effective date on the date you reapplied, even though newly obtained service records were part of the evidence.
important_cautions: Why the Original Denial Reason Matters (Blubaugh & Kisor): Section 3.156(c) applies when the newly associated service records are 'relevant'—meaning they relate to a disputed reason why the earlier claim was denied (such as proving an in-service event or injury). If VA already conceded the in-service event in the original decision and denied solely because you had no current medical diagnosis at that time, newly found service event records generally will not change that earlier effective date.

Official Service Records Only: Post-service private doctor notes, lay buddy statements, Social Security records, and post-discharge VA Medical Center (VAMC) treatment notes are valuable evidence, but they are not 'official service department records' under § 3.156(c).

2005 Proposal vs. October 6, 2006 Final Rule: VA proposed clarifying § 3.156(c) on June 20, 2005 (70 FR 35388) and finalized it effective October 6, 2006 (published September 6, 2006 at 71 FR 52455), consolidating former § 3.400(q)(2) effective-date rules.
questions_for_representative: Can we compare the exact 'Evidence' list on my earliest VA denial against every military hospital packet, deck log, personnel record, or unit log now in my VBMS eFolder?

Even though I am already service-connected today, did VA grant my condition later under a new law (like the PACT Act or relaxed PTSD rules) before checking whether newly associated service records corroborate my original denied claim (Emerson v. McDonald)?
What exact reason did VA give for my original denial—missing proof of an in-service event/injury, or lack of a current diagnosis—and how do the newly associated service records address that gap?

If VA granted service connection based on newly associated service records, do we have medical or lay evidence across the past decades so VA can assign accurate staged ratings back to the original claim?

title: Playbook 04: Unadjudicated TDIU, Pre-2015 Informal Claims (§ 3.157(b)), Mandatory SMC & AMA Explicit Notice
cFileTriggers: Pre-March 24, 2015 claim for rating increase accompanied by evidence veteran stopped working, received SSA disability, or had Voc Rehab (Ch. 31) infeasibility letter
Pre-March 24, 2015 VAMC hospital admission or outpatient exam showing worsening of an already-SC disability with no subsequent rating action (§ 3.157(b))
Rating code sheet showing one 100% disability (or single-disability TDIU) PLUS separate SC disabilities combining to 60%+ with no SMC(s) awarded
Post-Feb. 19, 2019 AMA decision that stays completely silent on a claimed or reasonably raised issue
killSwitches: Relying on § 3.157(b) or non-form informal claims received ON OR AFTER March 24, 2015
Legacy pre-Feb. 19, 2019 subsequent rating decision explicitly or implicitly (Deshotel/Adams/Hampton/Steele) adjudicating the pending claim
Assuming TDIU premised on MULTIPLE combined disabilities satisfies the 'single 100% disability' prong of statutory SMC(s) (foreclosed under Bradley/Gazelle)
Attacking a final pre-2008 decision under Bradley or a final pre-May 2024 decision under Barry via CUE without confronting George v. McDonough, 596 U.S. 740 (2022) and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)

toc.text: 1. Archetype A: Reasonably Raised Unadjudicated TDIU (*Roberson* & *Rice*)
C-File Red Flags
2. Archetype B: Historical 38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b) VAMC Reports & § 3.156(b) Post-Decision VAMC Abatement (*Lang*)
Part 1: Pre-March 24, 2015 § 3.157(b) Informal Claims for Increase
Part 2: 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b) 1-Year *Post*-Decision VAMC Finality Abatement (*Lang v. Wilkie*, 2020)
3. Archetype C: Mandatory Statutory SMC (38 U.S.C. § 1114(k), (l), (s)) & Multi-Step Bumps (*Barry*)
High-Probability SMC Audits
4. Archetype D: Post-Feb. 19, 2019 AMA Silent Omissions (*Hamill v. Collins*, 2026)

blocks.text: Massive retroactive awards frequently hide in plain sight when VA **received a valid informal or inferred claim**—or had **statutory facts on its own code sheet requiring SMC** (`38 U.S.C. § 1114`, `former § 314` prior to `Pub. L. 102-83`, Aug. 6, 1991)—and simply failed to adjudicate it.
1. Archetype A: Reasonably Raised Unadjudicated TDIU (*Roberson* & *Rice*)

Under *Roberson v. Principi*, 251 F.3d 1378 (Fed. Cir. 2001) and *Rice v. Shinseki*, 22 Vet. App. 447 (2009), a request for Total Disability based on Individual Unemployability (`38 C.F.R. § 4.16` — `40 FR 42535`, Sept. 15, 1975; `54 FR 4281`, pub. Jan. 30, 1989, eff. Mar. 1, 1989; `55 FR 31579`, pub. Aug. 3, 1990, eff. Sept. 4, 1990) is **part and parcel** of an initial or increased-rating claim whenever:

items: A veteran is seeking service connection or a higher rating, AND
The record contains **cognitive, clinical, or lay evidence of unemployability** attributable to the disability(ies).

blocks.text: C-File Red Flags

items: Veteran wrote on a `21-4138`, `21-526`, or C&P intake sheet: *"Lost my job because of my back/PTSD"*, *"Haven't worked since 1998"*, or *"On Social Security Disability (`SSDI`)"*.
VAMC notes or Chapter 31 (`VR&E`) records state *"Employment not currently feasible"*.

RO granted `70%` PTSD in 2004 (meeting `§ 4.16(a)` schedular threshold!) while C&P exam stated `"Unemployed x 5 years due to PTSD"`, and RO neither awarded TDIU, deferred TDIU, nor sent `VA Form 21-8940`!
• **Trap Check (Legacy vs. AMA Implicit Denial):** In **Legacy (pre-Feb. 19, 2019)** decisions, check whether the rating decision denied a schedular `100%` increase under circumstances that implicitly denied reasonably raised TDIU (*Deshotel v. Nicholson*, 457 F.3d 1258 (Fed. Cir. 2006); *Hampton v. McDonough*, 68 F.4th 1376 (Fed. Cir. 2023); *Steele v. Collins*, 135 F.4th 1353 (Fed. Cir. 2025); *cf.* *Comer v. Peake*, 552 F.3d 1362 (Fed. Cir. 2009)). In **AMA (on/after Feb. 19, 2019)** decisions, under ***Hamill v. Collins*, 166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 4, 2026) (`No. 24-1543`)**, silent omission **never** denies TDIU—it **remains legally pending**!

blocks.text: 2. Archetype B: Historical 38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b) VAMC Reports & § 3.156(b) Post-Decision VAMC Abatement (*Lang*)
Part 1: Pre-March 24, 2015 § 3.157(b) Informal Claims for Increase

Before **March 24, 2015** (`79 FR 57660`, published Sept. 25, 2014 — see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: Former 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.155(a) & 3.157(b) Informal Claims (Repealed March 24, 2015)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.155-3.157b-informal-claims-pre-2015)), `38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b)(1)` (`26 FR 1571`, Feb. 24, 1961) mandated that once service connection was in effect (even at `0%`!), **VA's receipt of a VA hospital admission report or VA outpatient examination report** showing worsening **operated as an informal claim for increased compensation** on the date of admission/examination.

items: Identify the date service connection was **first granted** (e.g., `10%` knee or `0%` scar/sinusitis in 1974).

Pull VAMC treatment/admission records between 1974 and **March 23, 2015** showing objective worsening (also checking pre-2015 written filings pointing to VAMC records under *Shea v. Wilkie*, 926 F.3d 1362 (Fed. Cir. 2019)).

Check whether **any rating decision** was issued on that condition after that VAMC report:
• **If NO subsequent rating decision adjudicated that condition until decades later:** That `§ 3.157(b)` informal claim remained **unadjudicated and pending**!
• **If a subsequent Legacy rating decision adjudicated that exact condition:** Normally, a later final adjudication terminates an earlier pending informal claim for increase (*Williams v. Peake*, 461 F.3d 1349 (Fed. Cir. 2006)), UNLESS the later grant failed to apply the mandatory 1-year lookback under `38 U.S.C. § 5110(b)(2)` (`former § 3010(b)(2)`) / `38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2)` / `§ 3.157(b)` (potential **RO CUE**).

blocks.text: Part 2: 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b) 1-Year *Post*-Decision VAMC Finality Abatement (*Lang v. Wilkie*, 2020)
Even for **initial service-connection denials** (where `§ 3.157(b)` never applied because SC was not yet granted!) and even **between March 24, 2015 and February 18, 2019**:

items: Under *Beraud v. McDonald*, 766 F.3d 1402 (Fed. Cir. 2014) and ***Lang v. Wilkie*, 971 F.3d 1348 (Fed. Cir. 2020)**, if a **VAMC generated clinical treatment records** relevant to the denied/rated issue within **1 year *after*** a post-July 21, 1992 Legacy RO decision, VA constructively received those records during the 1-year appeal window under `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b)`.

Unless VA issued a formal determination deciding whether those post-decision VAMC notes constituted new and material evidence, **the Legacy RO decision NEVER BECAME FINAL**—meaning a grant 10 or 25 years later must assign an effective date anchored to that original non-final claim!

blocks.text: 3. Archetype C: Mandatory Statutory SMC (38 U.S.C. § 1114(k), (l), (s)) & Multi-Step Bumps (*Barry*)

lines: **Full `SMC(k)–(t)` & Ancillary Suite:** For complete multi-step math, *Breniser*/*Amberman* anti-pyramiding rules, `SMC(l)`/`(r)(1)`/`(r)(2)`/`(t)` (*Laska v. McDonough*, `37 Vet. App. 460 (2024)`), `§ 3.552` hospitalization reductions, and `SAH`/`Auto`/`Clothing`/`DEA` grants, see the **[Master SMC Legal Treatise & Step Math](/docs/smc-complete-treatise-and-step-math)**, **[Playbook 12 (A&A, `SMC(r)` & `SMC(t)`)](/playbooks/12-aid-and-attendance-smc-l-r1-r2-and-smc-t)**, **[Playbook 13 (Ancillary Grants)](/playbooks/13-ancillary-grants-sah-auto-clothing-dea-spina-bifida)**, and the **[SMC & Ancillary Audit Worksheet](/checklists/smc-and-ancillary-audit-worksheet)**.

blocks.text: VA must consider and award SMC **even when never claimed by the veteran** whenever record facts establish entitlement (*Akles v. Derwinski*, 1 Vet. App. 118 (1991); *Buie v. Shinseki*, 24 Vet. App. 242 (2010)).
High-Probability SMC Audits

items:
**`SMC(s)` Statutory Housebound (`100% + 60%` Rule — `38 U.S.C. § 1114(s)` / `former § 314(s)`):**
• Veteran has **one single disability rated 100%** (either schedular `100%`, OR **TDIU attributable solely to ONE single service-connected disability** under *Bradley v. Peake*, 22 Vet. App. 280 (2008)!), **PLUS** additional separate/independent service-connected disabilities combining to **`60%` or more**.
• **Pure Math CUE (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive):** When the Rating Code Sheet itself shows schedular `100%` PTSD + `50%` Sleep Apnea + `20%` Lumbar (`50 + 20 = 60%` combined!) and omits `SMC(s-1)`, that is an airtight, mathematical **RO CUE**!
• **The *Bradley* Angle & *George v. McDonough* Guardrail (Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) pre-2008):** If VA granted TDIU citing multiple disabilities, check whether one disability *alone* caused unemployability. *(Bitemporal Caution: Attacking a final **pre-Nov. 26, 2008** decision via CUE under *Bradley* faces a `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)` / *George v. McDonough*, 596 U.S. 740 (2022) change-in-interpretation defense; always check first for open/pending claims, `§ 3.156(c)` service records, or *Lang* `§ 3.156(b)` non-finality!)*

**Multi-Step Intermediate & Full-Step SMC Increases (`38 C.F.R. § 3.350(f)(3)–(4)` — *Barry v. McDonough*, 2024):**
• Under ***Barry v. McDonough*, 101 F.4th 1348 (Fed. Cir. May 16, 2024)**, veterans receiving base `SMC(l)–(n)` are entitled to **multiple** half-step (`§ 3.350(f)(3)`, per independent `50%+` disability) and full-step (`§ 3.350(f)(4)`, per independent `100%` disability) rate bumps, capped at `SMC(o)`. Audit every catastrophic injury / A&A code sheet for suppressed multi-step bumps (noting the same `§ 20.1403(e)` / *George* CUE bar on final pre-May 16, 2024 ratings vs. full retroactive application on open, pending, or `§ 3.156(b)–(c)` claims).

**`SMC(k)` Loss of Use of Creative Organ / Extremity (`38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)`):**
• Radical prostatectomy (e.g., Agent Orange prostate cancer!) or erectile dysfunction documented as secondary to diabetes/PTSD SSRIs on the C&P exam itself while rater granted `DC 7528` or `DC 7522` at `0%` and forgot to check the `SMC(k)` award box!

**`SMC(l)` Aid & Attendance / Housebound-in-Fact:**
• VAMC nursing-home/homebound documentation or C&P exam certifying inability to dress, bathe, manage prosthetics, or protect oneself from hazards of daily environment (`38 C.F.R. § 3.352(a)`).

blocks.text: 4. Archetype D: Post-Feb. 19, 2019 AMA Silent Omissions (*Hamill v. Collins*, 2026)
Under ***Hamill v. Collins*, 166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 4, 2026) (`No. 24-1543`)**, audit every AMA-era rating decision (dated **February 19, 2019 or later**) side-by-side against:

items: Every box/row listed on the veteran's `VA Form 21-526EZ` or `20-0995`, AND

Every secondary condition or extraschedular/TDIU/SMC issue reasonably raised on the DBQ/C&P exam (e.g., DBQ checks *"Radiculopathy: Yes — Mild right sciatic nerve"* during a lumbar spine claim, and the AMA rating decision grants `20%` lumbar spine while saying **zero words** about radiculopathy!).

**Result under *Hamill*:** Because `38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)` prohibits denial by silence under the AMA, that radiculopathy or TDIU claim **was never denied**—demand immediate adjudication with an effective date anchored to the original AMA `21-526EZ` / ITF! *(Practice Note: If within 1 year of the silent AMA decision, pursue HLR or Board appeal per *Hamill* fn. 6 rather than a mandamus petition; see [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).*

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Overlooked Unemployability (TDIU), Pre-2015 Informal Claims, Mandatory SMC & Silent AMA Decisions
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Not every past VA oversight requires proving Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE). Sometimes a Veteran raised a claim or entitlement in the record—and VA simply never decided it. Before March 24, 2015, written statements, VA hospital admissions, or VA outpatient exam reports showing worsening of an already service-connected disability could act as an informal claim for increase (former 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.155(a), 3.157(b)). Likewise, when a Veteran seeks a higher rating and the record shows service-connected disabilities prevent substantially gainful work, VA must consider Total Disability Based on Individual Unemployability (TDIU) as part of that claim. And for decisions issued on or after February 19, 2019 under the Appeals Modernization Act (AMA), if VA stays completely silent on a claimed or reasonably raised issue instead of giving explicit written notice under 38 U.S.C. § 5104(b), that issue may remain legally open and pending.
record_clues: A pre-March 24, 2015 claim for an increased rating where your VA medical notes, Social Security disability award, or Chapter 31 Voc Rehab records showed you could no longer work due to service-connected conditions, yet VA never mentioned TDIU.

A VA Medical Center (VAMC) hospital admission or VA outpatient examination report dated before March 24, 2015 documenting worsening of an already service-connected condition (even a 0% rating), with no follow-up VA rating decision.

A Rating Code Sheet showing one single disability rated 100% (or TDIU caused solely by one disability) PLUS separate service-connected disabilities combining to 60% or more, with no statutory Housebound Special Monthly Compensation [SMC(s)] paid.
A rating decision issued on or after February 19, 2019 that decides one condition while staying completely silent on a related issue, secondary condition, TDIU, or SMC raised by your claim or exam.
important_cautions: March 24, 2015 Standardized Forms Cutoff: VA repealed former § 3.157(b) and non-form informal claims effective March 24, 2015 (published September 25, 2014 at 79 FR 57660). VA medical visits or loose letters dated on or after March 24, 2015 do not start a claim without a standardized VA claim form or Intent to File (VA Form 21-0966).

Legacy 'Implicit Denial' vs. Post-2019 AMA Explicit Notice: In pre-February 19, 2019 Legacy decisions, a later decision could sometimes implicitly close out a related pending issue if a reasonable person would have understood it was denied—whereas for AMA decisions on or after February 19, 2019, courts enforce strict explicit-notice rules (Hamill v. Collins).

TDIU & Statutory SMC(s) Single-Disability Rule: Under Bradley v. Peake and Gazelle v. Shulkin, TDIU counts as the 'single 100% disability' for statutory SMC(s) only if unemployability is warranted by one single disability alone—not a combination of multiple disabilities.

Judicial Reinterpretation CUE Bar (George v. McDonough): Under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e), later court rulings reinterpreting a statute or regulation (such as Bradley in 2008 or Barry v. McDonough in 2024) apply to open, pending, or timely appealed claims, but cannot be used to allege CUE against an older final decision.
questions_for_representative: Do my pre-March 24, 2015 VAMC hospital or outpatient treatment records trigger an unadjudicated informal claim for increase under former 38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b)?

When I sought higher ratings in the past, was there evidence in my file that my service-connected disabilities kept me from working (Roberson / Rice), and did any later Legacy decision implicitly close that TDIU issue?
Did any AMA rating decision issued on or after February 19, 2019 stay silent on a claimed or reasonably raised TDIU, secondary, or SMC issue without giving explicit § 5104(b) denial notice?
Does my Rating Code Sheet show a single 100% disability alongside 60% or more in separate disabilities where mandatory statutory SMC(s) was overlooked?

title: Playbook 05: Void Rating Reductions & Protected/Stabilized Ratings (§§ 3.344, 3.951, 3.957)
cFileTriggers: Any rating code sheet lowering an existing disability percentage (e.g., 50% -> 30%, 100% -> 70%, 30% -> 10%)
Severance of service connection (<10 years under § 3.105(d) or >=10 years under § 3.957)
Reduction of a rating in effect for 5+ years based on a single routine C&P examination
Reduction lacking 60-day advance notice under 38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e) when overall combined payment dropped
killSwitches: Staged ratings assigned simultaneously in an INITIAL award are NOT reductions of stabilized ratings (Fenderson v. West, 12 Vet. App. 119 (1999); though watch out where temporary/convalescent vs. stabilized 5-year periods accrued!)
Reduction of a rating DID NOT reduce total combined monthly compensation (exempts § 3.105(e) 60-day notice, though § 3.344 substantive rules STILL apply if stabilized 5+ years!)
Proven fraud by the claimant (the sole statutory exception to 10-year § 3.957 and 20-year § 3.951(b) protections, alongside lack of qualifying military service/COD under § 3.957)

toc.text: 1. The Statutory & Regulatory Protection Matrix
2. C-File Red Flags (Audit Triggers)
3. Bitemporal Pathway Selection: Void Restoration vs. CUE

blocks.text: Whenever a C-file shows VA **reduced a previously granted evaluation** or **severed service connection**—even 30 or 40 years ago, and even if the veteran never appealed—stop immediately and audit the reduction. Under *Brown v. Brown*, 5 Vet. App. 413 (1993), *Kitchens v. Brown*, 7 Vet. App. 320 (1995), and *Murphy v. Shinseki*, 26 Vet. App. 510 (2014), a rating reduction executed without strict observance of VA's regulatory safeguards is **void *ab initio*** (legally invalid from inception), compelling **full restoration of the prior rating retroactive to the date of the unlawful reduction—without needing to satisfy CUE**!
1. The Statutory & Regulatory Protection Matrix

*(See verbatim primary-source regulatory text in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.105(d)–(i), 3.343, 3.344, 3.951, 3.953 & 3.957 (Rating Reductions, Stabilization & Statutory Protections)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.105e-3.344-3.951-3.957-reductions) and pre-1991 statutory section numbers in [Three-Era Title 38 U.S.C. Statutory Crosswalk (1933–Present)](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk)).*

rows: Any duration (if total monthly compensation drops)

VA **must** issue **proposal-to-reduce notice** with detailed reasons, give **60 days** to submit evidence / **30 days** to request a predetermination hearing (`§ 3.105(i)`), AND make reduction effective **last day of the month in which a 60-day period after final notice expires** (*Murphy*, 26 Vet. App. at 515).

Burden rests on **VA** to prove prior grant was **clearly and unmistakably erroneous** (with medical certification that prior diagnosis was clearly erroneous) + **60-day proposal notice** and delayed effective date!

Schedular `100%` cannot be reduced without exam showing **material improvement** under ordinary conditions of life and work (`§ 3.343(a)`; *Ternus v. Brown*, 6 Vet. App. 370 (1994)). TDIU cannot be reduced without **clear and convincing evidence of actual employability** (`§ 3.343(c)(1)`), nor solely for engaging in substantially gainful employment unless maintained for **12 consecutive months** (`§ 3.343(c)(2)`).
Same or higher evaluation in effect **5 years or more**

**(1)** Exam must be **full and complete**, reviewing the **entire medical history**; **(2)** Must show **sustained improvement** (not temporary remission!), so a **single exam** cannot justify reduction of episodic conditions unless all record evidence concurs; **(3)** Improvement must hold up under **ordinary conditions of life and work**!
SC in force **10 years or more** (effective date of SC to effective date of severance)

Service connection **cannot be severed** except upon proof of **fraud** or clear military-record proof of lack of requisite service / character of discharge. *(See also **`38 C.F.R. § 3.953(a)–(b)`** protecting compensation/SC payable on **Dec. 31, 1957** under `Pub. L. 85-56` and **Dec. 31, 1958** under `Pub. L. 85-857`)*.
Continuous rating at or above a % for **20 years or more**
Rating **cannot be reduced below that percentage** except upon proof of **fraud**—even if the veteran makes a complete medical recovery or the original grant was CUE!
Any existing rating on effective date of a VASRD change
A change in the Rating Schedule (e.g., May 19, 2024 GERD `DC 7206` overhaul) **can NEVER by itself reduce** an existing disability rating!

blocks.text: 2. C-File Red Flags (Audit Triggers)

items: **The "Single C&P Exam" Reduction of PTSD / Back / Asthma:** Veteran held `50%` or `70%` PTSD from 1978 to 1985 (`7` years -> stabilized under `§ 3.344(c)`!). In 1985, VA scheduled one 20-minute routine C&P exam where the examiner did *not* have or review the complete C-file (*Stern v. McDonough*, 34 Vet. App. 51 (2021)) and noted *"Veteran doing somewhat better today"*, so RO cut `70% -> 30%`. **Void *ab initio*!**

**Missing Predetermination Notice (`§ 3.105(e)`):** RO issued a single rating decision cutting `40% -> 10%` effective immediately (or first of next month) without ever sending a `Proposed Rating Reduction` letter offering 60 days for evidence and a 30-day predetermination hearing!

**20-Year Retroactive Crossover Trap (`38 U.S.C. § 110`):** Under `§ 3.951(b)`, the 20-year clock runs from the **effective date** of the evaluation—including when a retroactive award (e.g., CUE or appeal) grants `50%` from 1995 to 2016! Once 20 continuous years attach, VA cannot cut below `50%`.

blocks.text: 3. Bitemporal Pathway Selection: Void Restoration vs. CUE

items:
**Direct Motion / Claim to Restore Void Reduction (Preferred — Bypasses *George* CUE Bars!):**
• Under *Brown v. Brown*, 5 Vet. App. 413, 421–22 (1993) and *Kitchens v. Brown*, 7 Vet. App. 320, 325 (1995), a reduction violating `§ 3.344`, `§ 3.343`, or `§ 3.105(e)` is **not merely erroneous—it is void *ab initio***, meaning the claimant does **not** have to meet the strict `§ 3.105(a)` CUE standard or confront `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)` / *George v. McDonough*, 596 U.S. 740 (2022) change-in-interpretation defenses (though practitioners routinely plead **BOTH** voidness *ab initio* under *Brown*/*Kitchens*/*Murphy* **AND**, in the alternative, CUE under `38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a)` / `§ 7111` for belt-and-suspenders protection!).

**Remedy — Outright Reversal, Never Curative Remand (*Schafrath*, *Kitchens*, *Horn*, *Murphy* & *Stern*):** Unlike ordinary compensation claims where an inadequate exam triggers a remand for a new exam, whenever VA bears the affirmative burden of proof—as in rebuttal of soundness (*Horn v. Shinseki*, 25 Vet. App. 231, 243–44 (2012)), severance (`§ 3.105(d)`), or rating reductions (`§§ 3.105(e), 3.343, 3.344`)—**the sole lawful remedy for VA's failure to carry its burden is outright reversal and reinstatement of the prior rating/service connection retroactive to the date of the unlawful reduction, NEVER a remand to let VA gather better evidence against the veteran** (*Schafrath v. Derwinski*, 1 Vet. App. 589, 595–96 (1991); *Kitchens*, 7 Vet. App. at 325; *Murphy*, 26 Vet. App. at 517; *Stern*, 34 Vet. App. at 59)!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: When VA Reduced a Long-Standing Disability Rating or Cut Off Service Connection Without Required Safeguards
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: VA law places strict guardrails around lowering an existing disability rating or severing service connection—and those protections grow stronger the longer a rating has been in place. Under 38 C.F.R. § 3.344, once a disability rating has remained at the same percentage for 5 years or more, VA cannot lower it based on a single routine examination; VA must review the entire medical history and show sustained improvement under the ordinary conditions of daily life and work. At 10 years, service connection itself is protected against severance absent fraud or lack of qualifying military service (§ 3.957), and at 20 years, a continuous evaluation cannot be reduced below its lowest level over those two decades absent fraud (§ 3.951(b)). When VA reduces monthly pay without following mandatory notice or medical-improvement rules, courts treat the unlawful reduction as legally void from the start—meaning the earlier rating can be restored without having to meet the steep standard for Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE).
record_clues: A VA Rating Code Sheet showing an existing percentage lowered (for example, 70% down to 30%, or discontinuance of Total Disability Based on Individual Unemployability [TDIU]) after a single short Compensation and Pension (C&P) exam.

A rating that had been in effect at the same level for 5 or more years before the effective date of the reduction, or a rating continuously in force at or above a certain percentage for 20 or more years.

A reduction that lowered your actual monthly compensation check without VA first sending a 60-day proposed reduction letter under 38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e) (and, from January 21, 1992 onward, notice of your 30-day predetermination hearing right under § 3.105(i)).

A letter severing (cutting off) service connection after 10 or more years from the original effective date, or lowering an existing rating solely because VA updated the Rating Schedule criteria (§ 3.951(a)).
important_cautions: Staged Ratings vs. Reductions: When VA grants a claim for the first time and assigns higher and lower 'staged' percentages across past years in the same initial award, the 5-year stabilization rules of § 3.344 generally do not apply unless a rating actually remained in effect for 5 years.

Combined Payment Exception to Advance Notice: If VA lowered one individual disability percentage but your total combined monthly compensation payment stayed the exact same, VA was not required to send a 60-day advance notice under § 3.105(e)—though § 3.344's medical-improvement rules still apply if that specific rating was stabilized for 5+ years.

Historical Effective Dates Matter: Predetermination hearing rights under 38 C.F.R. § 3.105(i) took effect on January 21, 1992 (published December 19, 1991 at 56 FR 65846), so pre-1992 reductions must be checked against the procedural rules in force on that date.

Board CUE Caution (38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c)): Void-reduction restoration is a distinct legal pathway from a Board CUE motion; never rush into a Board CUE filing without counsel because the Board allows only one final merits CUE decision per prior Board decision issue (excluding without-prejudice pleading dismissals under § 20.1404).
questions_for_representative: How many years and months had my disability rating been in effect between its original effective date and the effective date when VA actually lowered my payment?
Did VA send a 60-day proposed reduction notice under 38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e) before cutting my monthly check, or did VA skip required notice or ignore a timely hearing request?
Does the C&P examination VA relied on review my entire longitudinal medical history and show sustained improvement under ordinary life and work conditions as required by 38 C.F.R. § 3.344?
Can we seek restoration of the prior rating as a void reduction (Brown v. Brown / Kitchens / Stern) rather than framing the request as a CUE motion?

title: Playbook 06: Nehmer Herbicide Retroactivity (§ 3.816), 1-Year Chronic Presumptions & CRSC (Soto)
keyPrecedents: Nehmer v. U.S. Dept. of Veterans Affairs, 494 F.3d 846 (9th Cir. 2007)
Procopio v. Wilkie, 913 F.3d 1371 (Fed. Cir. 2019) (en banc)
cFileTriggers: Republic of Vietnam (including 12-nautical-mile territorial seas / Blue Water Navy) service + ANY post-Sept 25, 1985 claim or medical diagnosis in file for a § 3.309(e) herbicide condition
Survivor of Vietnam veteran who died of IHD, lung/prostate/bladder cancer, diabetes complications, or Parkinson's after a prior claim was filed
Chronic disease (§ 3.309(a): arthritis, hypertension, peptic ulcer, psychoses, organic nervous disease, etc.) manifesting to 10%+ within 1 year of discharge but denied for 'no in-service treatment'
Military retiree (20-year or Ch. 61) with combat-related disabilities whose CRSC back pay was capped at 6 years

Assuming hypertension, MGUS, or chloracne receive § 3.816 Nehmer class retroactivity (explicitly excluded under M21-1 VIII.i.2.B.1.c!)

blocks.text: This playbook covers three statutory/class mechanisms that routinely produce high-six-figure awards by overriding ordinary effective-date rules or abolishing statutory time caps.
1. *Nehmer* Class Retroactive Effective Dates (38 C.F.R. § 3.816)

Under the *Nehmer* consent decree and `38 C.F.R. § 3.816`, veterans who served in the **Republic of Vietnam** (including **Blue Water Navy** offshore territorial seas under *Procopio* / `Pub. L. 116-23` / 2020 N.D. Cal. *Nehmer* enforcement order!) and their survivors enjoy extraordinary retroactive effective dates for **covered herbicide diseases** (`§ 3.816(b)(2)` / `§ 3.309(e)`).
A. The Two *Nehmer* Retroactive Pathways (§ 3.816(c)(1) & (2))

items:
**Previously Denied Claims (`§ 3.816(c)(1)` — "Footnote 1" Claims):**
• If VA **denied** compensation for a covered herbicide disease in a claim **received on or after September 25, 1985** (or pending on Sept. 25, 1985), the effective date of a later *Nehmer* grant is the **date VA received that prior denied claim** (or the date the disability arose, whichever is later)—**even if decades passed and the veteran never appealed**!

**Coding / Diagnostic Lookback Rule ("Footnote 1" Medical Evidence Trap):**
• Even if the veteran did **not** name the exact *Nehmer* condition on a post-Sept. 25, 1985 claim (e.g., veteran claimed "shortness of breath / chest pain" or "hypertension" in 1994), if **medical records in the file at the time of that claim or prior to the new presumptive rule** showed a diagnosis of **Ischemic Heart Disease (`CAD`/`IHD`)**, VA **must** treat it as a previously denied *Nehmer* claim!

**Claims Filed Before Regulatory Effective Date (`§ 3.816(c)(2)`):**
• Pending claims when a new herbicide presumption took effect relate back to claim receipt or date disability arose.

***Nehmer* Survivor & Estate Payouts (`§ 3.816(f)`):**
• Uniquely in all of Veterans Law, when a *Nehmer* class member dies before receiving owed *Nehmer* retroactive benefits, VA must pay **100% of the unpaid retroactive compensation** (without the 1-year `§ 5121(c)` filing bar or pre-Dec. 16, 2003 2-year accrued-benefits cap of `38 U.S.C. § 5121`!) to the surviving spouse, children (**including adult independent children**), parents, or **even the veteran's estate**! See [`Playbook 09: Accrued Benefits, Substitution & Nehmer Estates`](/playbooks/09-accrued-benefits-substitution-nehmer-estates) and verbatim [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.1000, 3.1010 & 3.816(f) (Accrued Benefits, § 5121A Substitution & Nehmer Survivor/Estate Payouts)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.1000-3.1010-accrued-substitution).

**Mandatory *Nehmer* Exclusions, Survivor `§ 1305` DIC Escape Hatch & PACT Act OIG Audit Check:**
• **`M21-1 VIII.i.2.B.1.c` Exclusions:** **Hypertension**, **MGUS**, and **chloracne** are **excluded** from `38 C.F.R. § 3.816` *Nehmer* class retroactivity! For living veterans, PACT Act hypertension and MGUS claims are governed by PACT Act statutory effective-date rules (`Aug. 10, 2022` or `38 C.F.R. § 3.114` 1-year lookbacks)—unless an independent finality-piercing rule (`§ 3.156(c)` newly associated service records, `§ 3.156(b)` *Lang* non-finality, or `§ 3.309(a)` 1-year post-discharge CUE) applies. **HOWEVER, for surviving spouses/children**, if DIC was *previously denied* before August 10, 2022 and the death is now presumptive under PACT Act `§ 404` (hypertension/MGUS), **`38 U.S.C. § 1305` (`PACT Act § 204`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.33`) mandates retroactive DIC back to the original denied DIC claim**—see [`Playbook 08: Survivor DIC & § 1318`](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical)!
• **VA OIG \$20.4 Million PACT Error Pattern:** Audit every 2022–2026 PACT Act award to verify the rater did not overlook a pre-August 14, 2023 Intent to File or `§ 3.114(a)` 1-year retroactive lookback back to **August 10, 2022**.

blocks.text: 2. Overlooked 1-Year Post-Discharge Chronic Diseases (38 U.S.C. § 1112; 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.307, 3.309(a))

lines: **Expanded Presumptions Playbook:** For full coverage of `§ 3.309(a)` chronic diseases, `§ 3.309(b)` tropical diseases, `§ 3.309(c)` Former POW presumptions, `§ 3.318` ALS (`20%` minimum), radiation (`§§ 3.309(d), 3.311`), Camp Lejeune, and *Shedden*/*Hickson* continuity traps, see **[`Playbook 07: Statutory & Regulatory Presumptions`](/playbooks/07-statutory-presumptions-chronic-tropical-pow-als)**.

blocks.text: Historically, RO raters summarily denied post-service claims whenever **Service Treatment Records (STRs) were silent**, forgetting that **40+ enumerated "chronic diseases" in `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(a)`** require **ZERO in-service manifestations** if they manifest to a compensable degree (`10%` or more) within **1 year of separation** (3 years for Hansen's disease / TB; 7 years for MS)!
Classic Overlooked § 3.309(a) Conditions

items: **Arthritis** (degenerative/osteoarthritis or rheumatoid manifesting to `10%` within 1 year of discharge)
**Cardiovascular-renal disease** (including **hypertension** and arteriosclerosis!)

**Organic diseases of the nervous system** (including **sensorineural hearing loss**, **tinnitus**, **epilepsy**, **peripheral neuropathy**, and **migraines** when organically rooted—*see Walker v. Shinseki*, 708 F.3d 1331 (Fed. Cir. 2013) restricting continuity-of-symptomatology under `§ 3.303(b)` strictly to `§ 3.309(a)` chronic diseases!)
**Peptic / duodenal ulcers**, **calculi** (kidney/bladder/gallbladder), **malignant tumors**, **diabetes mellitus**, **psychoses**.

blocks.text: **CUE Trigger:** If private or VAMC records in the C-file at the time of an early denial undisputedly showed a `§ 3.309(a)` chronic disease rated at `10%+` severity within 12 months of separation (after 90+ days active wartime/post-1946 service) and no affirmative clear evidence rebutted the presumption (`§ 3.307(d)`), denying for "negative STRs" is classic **RO CUE (`38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a)`)**!
3. Uncapped CRSC Arrears After *Soto v. United States*, 605 U.S. 360 (2025)

Whenever your client is a **military retiree** (20+ year regular/reserve retiree OR **Chapter 61 medical retiree**—even with <20 years of service!) and holds combat-related VA disabilities (Purple Heart, armed conflict, hazardous service, instrumentality of war, or **presumptive Agent Orange / Gulf War / radiation combat-related conditions**):

items: **The Historical Trap:** Until June 12, 2025, Navy/Army/Air Force CRSC boards invoked the Barring Act (`31 U.S.C. § 3702(b)`) to confiscate all retroactive CRSC older than **6 years** prior to the veteran's CRSC application.

**The *Soto* Holding (`605 U.S. 360 (2025)`):** The U.S. Supreme Court unanimously held that `10 U.S.C. § 1413a` provides independent settlement authority, **completely eliminating the 6-year Barring Act time bar** on CRSC claims.

**Practice Checklist & Forum Split (DoD Guidance vs. Court of Federal Claims):**
• **Aug. 20, 2025 DoD Guidance & Past Partial CRSC Grants:** Did the retiree apply for CRSC in 2015–2025 and get cut off at 6 years of back pay despite holding VA combat-related ratings back to 2003 (when CRSC began) or retirement? Under DoD's **August 20, 2025 implementation guidance**, demand full retroactive recalculation from the military department CRSC board / DFAS; for disputed or delayed pre-6-year arrears exceeding **\$10,000**, evaluate parallel Tucker Act (`28 U.S.C. § 1491`) litigation in the U.S. Court of Federal Claims (e.g., *Christopher Carey v. United States*).
• **Pair Every VA Retroactive Win With a Follow-On CRSC Application:** When a Chapter 61 or 20-year retiree wins a 15- or 20-year VA effective date via CUE, `§ 3.156(c)`, or *Nehmer*, immediately file/amend their branch CRSC packet to unlock a **second uncapped retroactive payout** from DFAS! *(Note: Remember `CRDP` vs. `CRSC` tax-free optimization—Chapter 61 retirees with <20 years do NOT get CRDP, making CRSC pure net new tax-free recovery up to their longevity retirement cap!)*

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Agent Orange Retroactive Effective Dates (Nehmer), One-Year Chronic Diseases & Combat-Related Retiree Pay
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Normally, when Congress or VA adds a new presumptive illness, benefits cannot go back earlier than the date the new law took effect. For Vietnam-era herbicide Veterans and their families, however, federal court orders codified in 38 C.F.R. § 3.816 (the Nehmer class action rules) require VA to look back to earlier denied claims—or even earlier medical diagnoses already in the file—filed or pending on or after September 25, 1985 for covered Agent Orange conditions. This guide also explains two related retroactive checks: the 1-year post-discharge chronic disease presumption (38 C.F.R. § 3.309(a)) and Combat-Related Special Compensation (CRSC) arrears for military retirees after the U.S. Supreme Court's decision in Soto v. United States.
record_clues: A DD-214, deck log, or personnel record showing service in the Republic of Vietnam or its 12-nautical-mile territorial seas (Blue Water Navy) between January 9, 1962 and May 7, 1975, paired with an older VA denial or VA medical note mentioning ischemic heart disease, prostate or bladder cancer, Type 2 diabetes, Parkinsonism, or hypothyroidism.

A survivor or family estate record where a Vietnam Veteran passed away from a covered herbicide illness after having filed an earlier disability claim, even if no surviving spouse or dependent child remains.

An older rating denial stating 'not shown in service treatment records' when medical records within 12 months of military discharge documented a listed chronic condition (such as arthritis, hypertension, peptic ulcer, or organic nervous disease) at a 10% or higher level.
A Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) or military branch CRSC award letter that capped retroactive combat-related retiree pay at six years under the Barring Act (31 U.S.C. § 3702).
important_cautions: Not every herbicide condition triggers Nehmer class retroactivity: VA excludes PACT Act additions such as hypertension and monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS), as well as chloracne, from 38 C.F.R. § 3.816 retroactive class rules.

Location rules differ between Nehmer class membership (focused on Republic of Vietnam and Blue Water Navy service) and expanded PACT Act herbicide locations such as Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Guam, American Samoa, and Johnston Atoll, which generally follow statutory liberalizing-law effective dates unless direct service records apply.
Claims that were both filed and finally denied before September 25, 1985—with no later claim pending on or after September 25, 1985—do not qualify under the Nehmer cutoff.

Under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c), once the Board of Veterans' Appeals issues a final merits decision on a Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) motion on a specific Board issue, no second CUE motion is allowed on that Board issue—so Nehmer and 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) service-record pathways should always be checked first.
questions_for_representative: Does my VA Claims File (C-file) contain an earlier denied claim—or an earlier medical diagnosis or VA hospital code—on or after September 25, 1985 that could anchor an earlier Nehmer effective date under 38 C.F.R. § 3.816?

If my loved one served in Vietnam or Blue Water Navy waters and has passed away, can surviving family members or the estate request a Nehmer retroactive payee review under the post-December 2, 2021 version of 38 C.F.R. § 3.816(f)?
Did my medical records within the first year after discharge show a 10% compensable chronic condition under 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.307 and 3.309(a) that an earlier decision overlooked?
If I am a military retiree receiving CRSC whose retroactive payment was previously capped at six years, how can we check eligibility for unpaid arrears following Soto v. United States?

title: Playbook 07: Overlooked Chronic, Tropical, ALS & Former POW Statutory Presumptions (38 U.S.C. § 1112; 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.307, 3.309, 3.318)
cFileTriggers: Legacy or pre-VCAA denial stating 'Condition not shown in STRs' or 'No nexus to service' when post-discharge records show manifestation to >=10% within 1 year (or 3/7 years)
Diagnosis of ALS (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis) at ANY point post-discharge after >=90 days continuous active service (38 C.F.R. § 3.318)
Former Prisoner of War (FPOW) C-file with denied anxiety, dysthymia, heart disease, stroke, neuropathy, IBS, ulcer, or osteoporosis
Tropical theatre service followed by malaria, dysentery, amebiasis, leishmaniasis, or schistosomiasis
killSwitches: Active Duty for Training (ADT) or Inactive Duty Training (IADT) without >=90 days continuous active military, naval, air, or space service (§ 3.307(a)(1))
Condition manifested within 1 year ONLY to a 0% noncompensable degree rather than the mandatory >=10% compensable threshold (§ 3.307(a)(3))
Invoking § 3.303(b) chronicity/continuity of symptomatology for a condition NOT listed in § 3.309(a) (foreclosed by Walker v. Shinseki, 708 F.3d 1331 (Fed. Cir. 2013))

toc.text: 1. Presumptive Categories & Statutory Manifestation Windows
2. Evidentiary Mechanics That Unlock Retroactive Wins
3. Pathway Selection: Closed-Record CUE vs. § 3.156(c) vs. Supplemental Claim

blocks.text: Across the pre-VJRA (`1946–1988`) and early post-VJRA eras, RO rating boards routinely denied claims with a rubber-stamped line—*"Not shown in Service Medical Records"*—completely overlooking that **`38 U.S.C. § 1112` and `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.307, 3.309, 3.318` require ZERO in-service clinical documentation** when a qualifying disease manifests to a compensable degree (`10%+`) within its statutory presumptive window.
1. Presumptive Categories & Statutory Manifestation Windows

rows: **`>= 10%` within 1 year of separation:** Arthritis (degenerative/rheumatoid), cardiovascular-renal disease (incl. hypertension, arteriosclerosis, myocarditis), diabetes mellitus, peptic/duodenal ulcers, psychoses, epilepsies, organic diseases of the nervous system (sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus, neuropathy, migraines if organic—*Fountain*), calculi (kidney/bladder/gallbladder), malignant tumors, lupus, sarcoidosis, Hodgkin's, leukemias, etc.
• **Within 3 years (`>= 10%`):** Hansen's disease (leprosy) and active tuberculous disease. · • **Within 7 years (`>= 10%`):** **Multiple sclerosis (`MS`)**.
**At ANY time after separation** (even 40+ years later!), unless affirmative evidence establishes a separate intercurrent cause (`100%` minimum evaluation under `DC 8017`!).

**`>= 10%` within 1 year** (or standard incubation period): Malaria, bacillary/amebic dysentery, amebiasis, blackwater fever, cholera, dracontiasis, filariasis, leishmaniasis, loiasis, onchocerciasis, oroya fever, pinta, plague, schistosomiasis, yaws, yellow fever, and resultant therapy complications.
**Any period** of captivity/internment as an FPOW

**`>= 10%` at ANY time post-service:** Psychosis, **any of the anxiety states**, dysthymic disorder (depressive neurosis), organic residuals of frostbite, post-traumatic osteoarthritis, **atherosclerotic / hypertensive heart disease** and complications, **stroke** and complications, and *(eff. Oct. 10, 2008)* osteoporosis if PTSD is diagnosed.

**`>= 10%` at ANY time post-service:** Avitaminosis, beriberi (incl. beriberi heart disease), chronic dysentery, helminthiasis, malnutrition (incl. optic atrophy), pellagra, other nutritional deficiencies, **irritable bowel syndrome (`IBS`)**, **peptic ulcer disease**, **peripheral neuropathy** (unless due to infectious disease), **cirrhosis of the liver**, and *(eff. Sept. 28, 2009)* osteoporosis.

blocks.text: 2. Evidentiary Mechanics That Unlock Retroactive Wins

items:
**Symptoms Count Even Before Formal Diagnostic Label (`§ 3.307(b)`):**
• Under `38 C.F.R. § 3.307(b)`, manifestation within the 1-year / 3-year / 7-year window **does not require a contemporaneous textbook diagnosis** if factual, clinical, or competent lay evidence shows **characteristic symptoms of `>= 10%` severity** within the presumptive period that a later medical examiner identifies as the onset of the chronic disease (e.g., documented optic neuritis, paresthesias, or foot drop within 7 years of discharge later diagnosed as **Multiple Sclerosis**!).

**`§ 3.303(b)` Chronicity & Continuity of Symptomatology (*Savage* & *Walker*):**
• Under *Walker v. Shinseki*, 708 F.3d 1331 (Fed. Cir. 2013), `38 C.F.R. § 3.303(b)` (in-service chronicity OR continuous post-service symptomatology without needing an Etiology/Nexus medical opinion) applies **exclusively to the chronic diseases enumerated in `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(a)`**.
• For non-`§ 3.309(a)` orthopedic conditions (e.g., an ankle sprain or lumbar strain prior to radiographically confirmed degenerative arthritis), claimants must proceed under `§ 3.303(a)` or `§ 3.303(d)` direct service connection using lay symptom continuity as factual foundation for a medical nexus opinion!

**High Threshold for Government Rebuttal (`38 U.S.C. § 1113`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.307(d)`):**
• Once presumptive service and manifestation within the statutory window are shown, VA can rebut the presumption **only** via *"affirmative evidence to the contrary, or evidence to establish that an intercurrent injury or disease which is a recognized cause of any of the diseases or disabilities has been suffered between the date of separation from service and the onset of any such diseases or disabilities"* (`§ 3.307(d)`). Speculative examiner statements cannot rebut a statutory presumption.

blocks.text: 3. Pathway Selection: Closed-Record CUE vs. § 3.156(c) vs. Supplemental Claim

items:
**Evidence of Presumptive Manifestation Was Already in the Closed Record -> File CUE (`38 U.S.C. §§ 5109A / 7111`):**
• Example: Veteran discharged after 3 years active duty in June 1971; VAMC or private records **already in the C-file** (or constructively possessed in VAMC files on/after July 21, 1992 per *Bell*) documented blood pressure readings meeting `10%` under `DC 7101`, an active duodenal ulcer (`DC 7305`), or X-ray degenerative arthritis (`DC 5003`) in February 1972; RO denied in 1973 solely because *"STRs negative."* **Textbook RO CUE (`38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a)`)!**

**Missing Separation / TDRL / Military Hospital Records Associated Later -> File `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)` Reconsideration:**
• If Temporary Disability Retired List (`TDRL`) exams, military inpatient charts, or FPOW repatriation records (`VA Form 10-564-D` / military debriefings) are newly associated, demand reconsideration back to the original denied claim under [Playbook 03](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c).

**Private First-Year Records Located Today -> File Supplemental Claim (`§ 3.2501`):**
• Private post-service medical records do **not** trigger `§ 3.156(c)` effective-date retroactivity, nor can unsubmitted private records establish CUE, though they establish prospective service connection immediately.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Overlooked Presumptions for Post-Discharge Chronic Illnesses, Tropical Diseases, ALS & Former POWs
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Even when military medical records do not mention an illness during active duty, federal law (38 U.S.C. § 1112 and 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.307, 3.309, and 3.318) presumes certain conditions are service-connected if they appear to a compensable degree within specific timeframes—or at any time after service for conditions like Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) and many Former Prisoner of War (FPOW) disabilities. In older decisions, raters sometimes denied claims simply because Service Treatment Records were silent, overlooking that post-service records within the statutory window satisfied the presumption.
record_clues: An older VA denial letter stating 'not shown in service treatment records' or 'no medical nexus to service' when private or VA medical records within 1 year of discharge (or up to 3 or 7 years for specific illnesses like multiple sclerosis or tuberculosis) showed a listed 38 C.F.R. § 3.309(a) chronic disease at a 10% or higher severity.

A diagnosis of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS / Lou Gehrig's disease) at any time after separation following at least 90 days of continuous active military, naval, air, or space service (38 C.F.R. § 3.318).

Military records confirming Former Prisoner of War captivity alongside a denied claim for anxiety, dysthymic disorder, heart disease, stroke, peripheral neuropathy, irritable bowel syndrome, peptic ulcer, cirrhosis, osteoporosis, or nutritional deficiency (38 C.F.R. § 3.309(c)).
Service in a tropical theater followed by malaria, bacillary dysentery, amebiasis, leishmaniasis, schistosomiasis, or unexplained recurrent fevers (38 C.F.R. § 3.309(b)).
important_cautions: Minimum active-service and severity gates apply: the 1-year chronic and tropical presumptions under 38 C.F.R. § 3.307(a) require at least 90 days of continuous active service (pure Active Duty for Training or weekend drills alone do not qualify) and require the condition to manifest to at least a 10% compensable level—not 0%—within the presumptive window.

Under the Federal Circuit's decision in Walker v. Shinseki, the 'chronicity' and 'continuity of symptomatology' shortcuts in 38 C.F.R. § 3.303(b) apply only to the specific chronic diseases listed in 38 C.F.R. § 3.309(a); unlisted conditions require medical nexus evidence under 38 C.F.R. § 3.303(a) or (d).

Exact rating dates matter for ALS: VA raised the minimum evaluation under Diagnostic Code 8017 from 30% to 100% effective January 19, 2012 (published December 20, 2011 at 76 FR 78823), while also directing raters to evaluate Special Monthly Compensation for progressive limb, speech, swallowing, and breathing complications.

Before considering any Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) filing, remember that 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c) allows only one final merits CUE decision per prior Board of Veterans' Appeals decision on an issue, and later shifts in court interpretation cannot establish CUE under George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e).
questions_for_representative: Is my diagnosed condition—or an underlying nerve, vascular, arthritic, or psychotic disorder—on the official list of chronic diseases in 38 C.F.R. § 3.309(a)?

Do my private doctor records, hospital charts, or lay statements from the first 12 months after discharge show symptoms severe enough to meet at least a 10% rating under the rating schedule in effect at that time?
If ALS (Diagnostic Code 8017) is service-connected, has VA evaluated all progressive extremity, speech/swallowing, respiratory, and Aid and Attendance needs for Special Monthly Compensation?
If I am a Former POW or served in a tropical theater, should we review earlier denials against the expanded presumptive lists in 38 C.F.R. § 3.309(b) and (c)?

title: Playbook 08: Survivor DIC — Direct/Contributory Death (§ 1310), Hypothetical § 1318 Entitlement (§ 3.22) & PACT Act § 1305 Re-Evaluations
statutes: 10 U.S.C. § 1450(c) (repealed eff. Jan. 1, 2023 by Pub. L. 116-92, § 622)
keyPrecedents: Nat'l Org. of Veterans' Advocates, Inc. v. Sec'y of Veterans Affairs, 314 F.3d 1373 (Fed. Cir. 2003)
cFileTriggers: VA Form 21P-534EZ / 21P-534 / 21P-535 DIC denial citing death certificate alone while omitting terminal VAMC/ICU records
Deceased veteran rated 70%-90% combined (or <10 years at 100%/TDIU) where CUE, void reduction, or § 3.156(c) STRs push 100%/TDIU past 10 continuous years
Previously denied pre-Aug. 10, 2022 DIC claim involving hypertension (PACT § 404), expanded Agent Orange locations, or Gulf War/post-9/11 burn-pit conditions
Rating Code Sheet omitting the § 1311(a)(2) 8-year kicker, § 1311(c)-(d) spouse A&A/Housebound, § 1311(f) 2-year child transitional benefit, or § 1311(a)(3) pre-1993 pay-grade rate
Pre-2023 or post-2023 military retiree survivor award where DFAS maintained an unlawful 10 U.S.C. § 1450(c) SBP-DIC offset
killSwitches: Pleading open-ended Green v. Brown / Cole v. West hypothetical § 1318 entitlement without a lifetime claim + § 3.22(b) CUE or § 3.156(c) predicate (barred by 65 FR 3388, NOVA, Rodriguez & Tarver)

Relying on a post-decision judicial reinterpretation (e.g., Bradley or Barry) to prove § 3.22(b)(1) CUE against a final lifetime rating (barred by George v. McDonough, 596 U.S. 740 (2022) and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e))

Invoking Bell v. Derwinski constructive possession of VAMC records to attack a pre-July 21, 1992 lifetime decision via § 3.22(b)(1) CUE (barred by Damrel v. Brown, 6 Vet. App. 242 (1994) and VAOPGCPREC 12-95)

Death caused by the veteran's intentional willful misconduct (§ 1318(b) / § 105(a)), UNLESS suicide resulted from a service-connected mental unsoundness (38 C.F.R. § 3.302) or organ failure was secondary to an SC disorder under Allen v. Principi
Claiming the § 1311(a)(2) 8-year kicker when the veteran held 100%/TDIU for 8+ years but was married to the surviving spouse for fewer than those same 8 continuous years

Pursuing § 1318 DIC alone when § 1310 direct/contributory SC death is provable and the survivor received a wrongful-death/FTCA tort settlement (triggers mandatory § 1318(d) dollar-for-dollar offset under VAOPGCPREC 3-97)
