blocks.text: Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (`DIC`, `38 U.S.C. ch. 13`, `former ch. 13 §§ 401–423`; see [Three-Era Title 38 Statutory Crosswalk](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk)) is the cornerstone tax-free monthly survivor benefit for surviving spouses, minor/school-age/helpless children, and low-income dependent parents (`38 U.S.C. § 1315`). Regional Office (`AOJ`) raters routinely deny valid DIC claims by treating the four-line state **Death Certificate** as conclusive proof of etiology, overlooking **contributory** vital-organ impairment under `38 C.F.R. § 3.312(c)`, ignoring **`38 C.F.R. § 3.22(b)` CUE / `§ 3.156(c)` hypothetical `10-year` total-disability reconstruction**, or misapplying **`38 U.S.C. § 1305` (`PACT Act § 204`)** retroactive effective dates.

lines: **Run Parallel Post-Mortem Triage:** Every deceased-veteran intake involves **two distinct claim tracks** that must be screened simultaneously within **1 year of death**: **(1) the survivor's own Chapter 13 DIC claim** (this Playbook) and **(2) the deceased veteran's unpaid lifetime compensation** via `38 U.S.C. § 5121A` Substitution, `§ 5121` Accrued Benefits, or `38 C.F.R. § 3.816(f)` *Nehmer* Estate payouts ([Playbook 09](/playbooks/09-accrued-benefits-substitution-nehmer-estates) and [`Survivor Post-Mortem Triage Gate`](/checklists/survivor-post-mortem-triage-gate)).

blocks.text: 1. Preconditions: VBMS, Death Certificate & C-File Audit Triggers

Before selecting a DIC theory, pull the complete deceased veteran's VBMS eFolder, **every historical Rating Code Sheet** ([VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon)), and terminal medical records:

items:
**Core Survivor Claim & Ancillary Forms:**
• **`VA Form 21P-534EZ`** (*Application for DIC, Survivors Pension, and/or Accrued Benefits*, or legacy `VA Form 21-534` / `21P-534`), **`VA Form 21P-535`** (dependent parents DIC under `38 U.S.C. § 1315`), **`VA Form 21-0966`** (Intent to File), and **`VA Form 21-2680`** (Surviving Spouse Aid & Attendance / Housebound under `§ 1311(c)–(d)`).
• **Marriage & Dependency Proof (`38 C.F.R. §§ 3.50–3.57, 3.356`):** Marriage certificate, prior divorce/annulment decrees, continuous cohabitation or `§ 3.52` deemed-valid marriage affidavits, post-57 / post-55 remarriage dates, and pre-age-18 helpless-child medical proof (see [`Survivor Marriage, Remarriage & Dependency Evolution`](/cfr/modules/survivor-marriage-dependency-evolution)).

**Terminal Clinical vs. Death-Certificate Triggers (`§ 1310` / `§ 3.312`):**
• State **Certificate of Death** listing only an immediate terminal mechanism (*"cardiopulmonary arrest," "respiratory failure," "sepsis," "natural causes"*) in **Part I** while omitting or burying service-connected diabetes, COPD, ischemic heart disease (`IHD`), hypertension, chronic kidney disease, cirrhosis, or PTSD in **Part II ("Other Significant Conditions")**.
• Terminal **VAMC / ICU / Hospice Discharge Summaries**, **Autopsy Reports**, **`DD Form 1300`** (*Report of Casualty*), or toxicology/psychiatry notes documenting multi-organ decompensation or service-connected mental unsoundness (`38 C.F.R. § 3.302`).

**Rating Code Sheet Triggers (`§ 1318` / `§ 1311` / `§ 1305`):**
• Veteran died of a **purely non-service-connected cause** (e.g., motor vehicle accident, non-presumptive malignancy, acute infection) after holding `100%` schedular or `TDIU` (`§ 4.16`) for **fewer than 10 years on paper** (e.g., `7`–`9.5` years), **OR** holding `70%–90%` combined while factually unemployable (`VA Form 21-8940` / VAMC vocational notes / SSA disability records in file).
• Any **previously denied DIC claim** in the eFolder where the veteran had herbicide exposure (including Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Guam, Blue Water Navy, or **PACT Act `§ 404` hypertension / MGUS**), burn-pit / Southwest Asia deployment (`38 U.S.C. § 1120`), Camp Lejeune water exposure (`38 C.F.R. § 3.307(a)(7)`), or Former POW captivity (`38 U.S.C. § 1318(b)(3)`).
• Veteran died **before January 1, 1993** at pay grade **`E-7` through `O-10`** (`§ 1311(a)(3)` higher pay-grade rate audit), or held `100%`/`TDIU` for **`>= 8` continuous years** while married to the surviving spouse (`§ 1311(a)(2)` kicker audit).

blocks.text: 2. Bitemporal Pathway Gate (Lowest-Burden Vehicle First)

Always sequence survivor DIC theories from **lowest evidentiary burden and broadest effective-date reach** to **highest finality-piercing burden**, strictly respecting *George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` and `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`:

rows: **PACT Act / Presumptive DIC Re-Evaluation** (`38 U.S.C. § 1305` [added by `Pub. L. 117-168, § 204`]; `38 C.F.R. § 3.33`; *Nehmer* `38 C.F.R. § 3.816(d)`)
Statutory exposure + presumptive cause/contributor of death (no nexus opinion needed)
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive *(statutory override of `§ 5110` finality)*
**Relates all the way back to the original previously denied DIC claim** (`§ 1305(a)(3)`; `§ 3.33(d)(1)`), or month of death if filed `<1 yr` after death! Zero `§ 1318(d)` tort offset.
Mechanical duration audit on Code Sheet (`10 yr` total, `5 yr` from discharge, or `1 yr` FPOW) + non-willful-misconduct death
Zero medical-nexus proof of cause of death required; unlocks full DIC + `§ 1311(a)(2)` 8-year kicker (if married 8 yrs). *(Watch `§ 1318(d)` tort offset!)*
**Direct / Secondary / Contributory SC Death** (`38 U.S.C. § 1310`; `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.310, 3.312(a)–(c)`)
**Equipoise (`38 U.S.C. § 5107(b)`)** — *de novo* survivor merits claim (*Hupp*, `21 Vet. App. at 352`) with full `§ 5103A` Duty to Assist
Prior lifetime denials of the veteran **do NOT bind the survivor**! Avoids `§ 1318(d)` wrongful-death tort offset (`VAOPGCPREC 3-97`) and works even with `<10` yrs at `100%`.
**Equipoise (`§ 5107(b)`)** using newly associated official military/JSRRC/unit records on a lifetime claim ([Playbook 03](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c))
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive *(bypasses CUE & George bars)*
Retroactively establishes `10+` years of `100%`/`TDIU` prior to death **without needing undebatable CUE**; simultaneously unlocks `§ 1311(a)(2)` 8-year kicker!
**`§ 3.22(b)(1)` Void Reduction or Lifetime CUE Reconstruction** (`38 C.F.R. §§ 3.22(b)(1), 3.105(a), 3.344`; `38 U.S.C. § 7111`)
Void *ab initio* ([Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings)) **OR** strict 3-prong *Russell*/*Fugo* CUE on closed lifetime record
**CUE:** Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) for later judicial reinterpretations; CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive for extant rules
**Bypasses *Haines v. West*!** While a survivor cannot initiate CUE for `§ 5121` accrued back pay, `§ 3.22(b)(1)` **expressly empowers** a survivor to prove lifetime CUE to win `§ 1318` DIC!

blocks.text: 3. Proof Elements & Doctrinal Mechanics
A. Primary vs. Contributory Service-Connected Death (38 U.S.C. § 1310; 38 C.F.R. § 3.312(a)–(c))

Under `38 U.S.C. § 1310(a)` (`former 38 U.S.C. § 410(a)`), DIC is payable whenever a veteran dies from a service-connected (or compensable `§ 1151`) disability. Under `38 C.F.R. § 3.312(a)`, death is service-connected if a service-connected disability was **either the principal OR a contributory cause of death**.

items:
**Principal Cause of Death (`§ 3.312(b)`):**
• The service-connected disease or injury, singly or jointly with some other condition, was the **immediate or underlying cause of death** or was **etiologically related** thereto (e.g., service-connected diabetes mellitus causing end-stage renal disease or fatal myocardial infarction; service-connected hepatitis C causing hepatocellular carcinoma).

**Contributory Cause of Death (`§ 3.312(c)(1)–(4)` — The High-Yield Litigation Engine):**
• Even when a **non-service-connected** event is the immediate cause of death (e.g., pneumonia, surgical shock, COVID-19, stroke, or non-SC cancer), DIC must be granted under `§ 3.312(c)(1)` if a service-connected disability:
• **"Contributed substantially or materially"** to death;
• **"Combined to cause death"**; or
• **"Aided or lent assistance to the production of death."** *(Showing merely that it "casually shared" in producing death is insufficient).*
• **Vital Organ Impairment (`§ 3.312(c)(3)`) vs. Static Musculoskeletal Conditions (`§ 3.312(c)(2)`):** Service-connected disabilities involving active processes affecting **vital organs** (cardiovascular, pulmonary, renal, hepatic, central nervous system) receive heightened probative weight when evaluating whether they debilitated the veteran or lowered physiological reserve against an acute non-SC insult—and where such an active vital-organ condition is rated **`100%` disabling**, ***"debilitation may be assumed"*** (`§ 3.312(c)(3)`). Conversely, minor or quiescent/static musculoskeletal disabilities (`§ 3.312(c)(2)`, even if rated `100%`) generally do not contribute unless medical proof demonstrates they materially accelerated fatal decline (e.g., severe service-connected paraplegia/immobility causing fatal pulmonary embolism, decubitus sepsis, or obesity-mediated cardiopulmonary failure under `VAOPGCPREC 1-2017`).

**Overcoming Terse Death Certificates (*Lathan* & *Dyment*):**
• Attending physicians and county coroners complete death certificates within minutes to authorize burial, routinely listing only terminal cardiac/respiratory arrest rather than underlying chronic pathophysiology.
• Under ***Lathan v. Brown*, 7 Vet. App. 359, 365–67 (1995)** and ***Dyment v. Principi*, 287 F.3d 1377, 1380–82 (Fed. Cir. 2002)**, VA **cannot** rely on the omission of a service-connected condition from the death certificate to deny DIC without evaluating the totality of terminal clinical records—and where record evidence indicates a service-connected vital-organ condition may have contributed materially to death, VA's duty to assist requires an adequate medical nexus opinion analyzing the mechanics of `§ 3.312(c)` (which need **not** be expressed with absolute medical certainty; `"at least as likely as not"` satisfies `§ 5107(b)`!).

***De Novo* Survivor Merits Independence, Combat Relaxation & Secondary Suicide/Substance Deaths:**
• **Prior Lifetime Denials Do Not Bind the Survivor (*Hupp v. Nicholson*, `21 Vet. App. 342, 352 (2007)`):** A survivor's `§ 1310` DIC claim is an **original, independent claim**. Even if the veteran applied for service connection for heart disease or lung cancer during life and let a denial become final, the survivor establishes service connection for the cause of death ***de novo*** (without needing CUE or `new and relevant` evidence to reopen the veteran's dead lifetime claim!), armed with `38 U.S.C. § 1154(a)–(b)` combat/service consideration and `§ 5107(b)` Benefit of the Doubt.
• **Suicide & Secondary Substance-Abuse Deaths (*Myore* & *Allen*):** Under `38 U.S.C. § 105(a)`, willful misconduct bars `§ 1310` DIC (*Myore v. Nicholson*, `489 F.3d 1207, 1213–14 (Fed. Cir. 2007)`). **Two major exceptions defeat the bar:**
• **Mental Unsoundness Suicide (`38 C.F.R. § 3.302`):** Suicide resulting from "mental unsoundness" caused by a service-connected disorder (PTSD, major depression, TBI, chronic intractable SC pain syndrome) is **not** willful misconduct and establishes service-connected death!
• **Secondary Substance Abuse (*Allen v. Principi*, `237 F.3d 1368 (Fed. Cir. 2001)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.310(a)`):** Fatal cirrhosis, pancreatitis, cardiomyopathy, or accidental overdose caused by alcohol or substance use disorder **proximately secondary to service-connected PTSD, depression, or chronic SC pain** is compensable under `§ 1310` (see [`VAOPGCPREC 7-99` citator note](/docs/vaopgcprec-index)).

blocks.text: B. Non-SC Death & Hypothetical 10-Year Total Disability (38 U.S.C. § 1318; 38 C.F.R. § 3.22)

*(See verbatim historical and current regulatory text in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.22 & 3.312 (Hypothetical § 1318 Total-Disability DIC Evolution & Service-Connected Cause of Death)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.22-dic-hypothetical-evolution)).*

Enacted originally as `former 38 U.S.C. § 410(b)` (`Pub. L. 95-479`, Oct. 18, 1978), recodified at `former § 418` (`Pub. L. 100-687, § 1403`, Nov. 18, 1988), and renumbered **`38 U.S.C. § 1318`** (`Pub. L. 102-83`, Aug. 6, 1991), Section `1318` mandates payment of DIC **"in the same manner as if the veteran's death were service connected"** even when the veteran died of a **100% non-service-connected cause**, provided the death was *not* the result of the veteran's own willful misconduct (`§ 1318(b)`) and the veteran was `"in receipt of or entitled to receive"` compensation at death for a service-connected disability **rated totally disabling** (`100%` schedular **or** `TDIU` under `38 C.F.R. § 4.16`!) under any of **three duration tracks**:

items: **The `10-Year` Rule (`§ 1318(b)(1)`; `§ 3.22(a)(2)(i)`):** Continuously rated totally disabling for **10 or more years immediately preceding death**;

**The `5-Year` Post-Discharge Rule (`§ 1318(b)(2)`; `§ 3.22(a)(2)(ii)`):** Continuously rated totally disabling from the **date of discharge or release from active duty** and for **not less than 5 years** immediately preceding death; or

**The `1-Year` Former POW Rule (`§ 1318(b)(3)`; `§ 3.22(a)(2)(iii)`):** Added by the *John William Rolen Act* (`Pub. L. 106-117, Title V, § 501`, `113 Stat. 1573`, enacted & eff. **Nov. 30, 1999**)—veteran was a **Former Prisoner of War (`FPOW`)** whose SC disability was continuously rated totally disabling for **not less than 1 year immediately preceding death**.

blocks.text: The Doctrinal Arc of "Entitled to Receive" (1997–2009 Bitemporal History)
Understanding why open-ended "hypothetical entitlement" died—and how `§ 3.22(b)(1)–(2)` replaced it—is essential to avoiding malpractice:

items: **Era 1 — Open-Ended *De Novo* Hypothetical Entitlement (`1997–Jan. 20, 2000`):** In ***Green v. Brown*, 10 Vet. App. 111 (1997)**, ***Wingo v. West*, 11 Vet. App. 307 (1998)**, and ***Cole v. West*, 13 Vet. App. 268 (1999)**, the CAVC construed `"entitled to receive"` in `§ 1318(b)` to allow a survivor to prove *de novo*—from records in the C-file or VA custody—that the veteran *hypothetically should have been rated* `100%` or `TDIU` for 10 years prior to death, **without proving CUE** in a prior final rating decision. *(See also Wanner v. Principi, 17 Vet. App. 4 (2003), rev'd in part on jurisdictional VASRD grounds, 370 F.3d 1124 (Fed. Cir. 2004)).*

**Era 2 — The January 21, 2000 Rulemaking (`65 FR 3388`):** Published and effective **January 21, 2000** (`65 FR 3388`), VA overhauled `38 C.F.R. § 3.22(b)` expressly to overturn *Green*, *Wingo*, and *Cole*. Amended `§ 3.22(b)` restricts `"entitled to receive"` strictly to cases where **the veteran filed a disability compensation claim during his or her lifetime** AND satisfies an enumerated regulatory basis—chiefly:
• **`§ 3.22(b)(1)` (Lifetime CUE):** The veteran would have received total disability compensation for the `10`/`5`/`1`-year period **but for Clear and Unmistakable Error (`CUE`)** committed by VA in a decision on a claim filed during the veteran's lifetime;
• **`§ 3.22(b)(2)` (`§ 3.156(c)` Service Department Records):** VA reopens/reconsiders a lifetime claim after death based **solely on newly associated service department records** (`38 C.F.R. §§ 3.156(c), 3.400(q)(2)`), yielding a retroactive total rating spanning the required period; or
• **Administrative Nonpayment / Withholding Tracks (`§ 3.22(b)(3)(i)–(vi)`) & Pending Claims (`§ 5121`/`§ 5121A`):** Under `§ 3.22(b)(3)(i)–(vi)` (`70 FR 72220`), `"entitled to receive"` also covers cases where the veteran held a total disability rating for the required period that was unpaid solely due to `(i)` dependents' apportionment, `(ii)` `§ 5314` overpayment/indebtedness offset, `(iii)` unwaived military retired pay, `(iv)` `10 U.S.C. § 1174(h)(2)` separation-pay recoupment, `(v)` unknown whereabouts, or `(vi)` `§§ 5308–5309` alien withholding. Separately, winning a retroactive `10-year` total rating post-mortem on a claim pending at death via `§ 5121` accrued benefits or `§ 5121A` substitution establishes `§ 3.22(a)(2)` entitlement directly (`70 FR 72213–14`).

**Era 3 — Facial Validity & Retroactive Application (*NOVA*, *Rodriguez* & *Tarver*):**
• In ***Nat'l Org. of Veterans' Advocates, Inc. (NOVA) v. Sec'y of Veterans Affairs*, 314 F.3d 1373 (Fed. Cir. 2003)** (following an earlier remand at `260 F.3d 1365 (Fed. Cir. 2001)` requiring VA to harmonize `§ 3.22` with `38 C.F.R. § 20.1106`), the Federal Circuit upheld `65 FR 3388` as a valid interpretation of `§ 1318(b)`.
• In ***Rodriguez v. Peake*, 511 F.3d 1147 (Fed. Cir. 2008)** and ***Tarver v. Shinseki*, 557 F.3d 1371 (Fed. Cir. 2009)**, the Federal Circuit held that amended `§ 3.22(b)` **applies retroactively even to DIC claims filed BEFORE January 21, 2000**, foreclosing open-ended *Green*/*Cole* hypothetical arguments across all eras.

blocks.text: Three Winning § 3.22(b) Reconstruction Plays Today

items: **Play 1 — Unadjudicated `Roberson` / `Rice` TDIU CUE (`§ 3.22(b)(1)`):** Veteran died in 2024 of a car accident; held `100%` from 2018–2024 (`6` years), and held `70%` PTSD from 2011–2018 while VAMC records in the C-file (post-July 21, 1992 *Bell* constructive possession) undebatably established inability to work due to PTSD during a 2012 increased-rating adjudication where the RO failed to adjudicate TDIU ([Playbook 04](/playbooks/04-unadjudicated-tdiu-informal-claims-smc)). Proving CUE in the 2012 RO decision under `§ 3.22(b)(1)` extends total disability from `2012 -> 2024` (`12` continuous years), **unlocking both `§ 1318` DIC and the `§ 1311(a)(2)` 8-year kicker**!

**Play 2 — Late-Arriving `§ 3.156(c)` Service Records (`§ 3.22(b)(2)`):** Veteran filed a PTSD or orthopedic claim in 2009 that was denied for lack of stressor/in-service documentation, was granted `100%` in 2019 (`5` years before a 2024 non-SC death), and post-mortem NPRC/JSRRC unit records corroborate the 2009 stressor ([Playbook 03](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c)). Under `§ 3.22(b)(2)`, reconsidering the 2009 claim with `100%`/`TDIU` medical staging back to `<= 2014` satisfies the `10-year` clock **without proving CUE**!

**Play 3 — Void Rating Reduction Restoration ([Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings)):** If VA unlawfully reduced a `100%` or `TDIU` evaluation within 10 years of death in violation of `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.105(e), 3.343, or 3.344`, restoring the void reduction *ab initio* bridges the gap and establishes `10` continuous years of total disability!

blocks.text: C. DIC Rate Architecture (38 U.S.C. § 1311), SBP Repeal & PACT Act § 1305 Re-Evaluations

items:
**Flat Rate vs. Pre-1993 Pay-Grade Election (`§ 1311(a)(1)` vs. `§ 1311(a)(3)`):**
• Under the *Veterans' Benefits Act of 1992* (`Pub. L. 102-568, § 102`, eff. **Jan. 1, 1993**), Congress replaced military pay-grade DIC tables with a uniform flat monthly base rate (`§ 1311(a)(1)`) for deaths occurring **on or after January 1, 1993**.
• **Pre-1993 Death Audit (`§ 1311(a)(3)`):** Whenever a veteran died **before January 1, 1993** (e.g., in a *Nehmer*, `§ 1305`, or `§ 3.156(c)` retroactive DIC grant, or an ongoing widow's award), VA **must** pay whichever is **greater**: `(i)` the legacy military pay-grade table rate (`E-7` through `O-10` routinely pays **hundreds of dollars more per month**!) **or** `(ii)` the modern `§ 1311(a)(1) + (a)(2)` flat + kicker rate!

**The `"8-Year Kicker"` & Vigilant Marriage-Overlap Audit (`38 U.S.C. § 1311(a)(2)`):**
• Adds a substantial COLA-indexed monthly supplement (`~$330+/month` in 2025–2026) if the veteran was `"in receipt of or was entitled to receive"` compensation for a SC disability **rated totally disabling (`100%` or `TDIU`) for a continuous period of at least 8 years immediately preceding death**.
• **CRITICAL MARRIAGE-OVERLAP RULE:** The final sentence of `38 U.S.C. § 1311(a)(2)` mandates: ***"In determining such period, only periods in which the veteran was married to the surviving spouse shall be considered."*** Both conditions—total disability **AND** legal/deemed-valid marriage to *that* surviving spouse—must overlap continuously for the **8 years immediately preceding death**!

**Mandatory DIC Monthly Add-Ons (`§ 1311(b), (c), (d), (f)`):**
• **`§ 1311(b)` (Dependent Children):** Monthly add-on for **each** child of the veteran under age 18 (or helpless child / schoolchild where applicable).
• **`§ 1311(c)` (Surviving Spouse Aid & Attendance) & `§ 1311(d)` (Housebound):** Monthly supplements (`~$400+` for A&A; `~$195+` for Housebound) when the surviving spouse resides in a nursing home, is blind, or requires regular assistance with activities of daily living (`38 C.F.R. §§ 3.351, 3.352` — always screen elderly surviving spouses with **`VA Form 21-2680`**!).
• **`§ 1311(f)` (2-Year Transitional Child Benefit):** Enacted by `Pub. L. 108-454, § 301` (eff. Jan. 1, 2005), pays an **automatic extra monthly flat benefit** (`~$350+/month`, COLA-indexed) on top of `§ 1311(b)` for the **first 2 years** following commencement of DIC entitlement whenever the surviving spouse has **one or more children under age 18** (terminating after 24 months or when the youngest child turns 18, whichever occurs first).

**Complete Repeal of the SBP-DIC `"Widow's Tax"` (`Pub. L. 116-92, § 622`; `10 U.S.C. § 1450(c)`):**
• Historically, `10 U.S.C. § 1450(c)` (and `38 U.S.C. § 1318(e)` equating `§ 1318` DIC with `§ 1311(a)` DIC) forced DFAS to confiscate military Survivor Benefit Plan (`SBP`) annuities dollar-for-dollar by the amount of VA DIC.
• Section `622` of the **NDAA for FY 2020 (`Pub. L. 116-92`)** repealed the offset in three steps: **(i) `Jan. 1, 2021`:** SBP offset capped at `2/3` of DIC + Special Survivor Indemnity Allowance (`SSIA`); **(ii) `Jan. 1, 2022`:** SBP offset capped at `1/3` of DIC + `SSIA`; **(iii) `January 1, 2023 – Present`:** **100% complete repeal**—surviving spouses receive **100% of military SBP AND 100% of VA DIC concurrently** with zero offset! *(When winning retroactive pre-2023 DIC for a retiree spouse, audit DFAS recoupment math across the pre-2021, 2021, 2022, and post-Jan. 1, 2023 windows and verify employee SBP-premium refund credits!)*

**PACT Act DIC Re-Evaluations & Original-Claim Effective Dates (`38 U.S.C. § 1305` & `38 C.F.R. § 3.33`):**
• **Statutory Precision (`§ 204` vs. `§ 404` of `Pub. L. 117-168`):** Practitioners frequently refer colloquially to "PACT Act § 404 DIC re-elections" because **Section `404`** of `Pub. L. 117-168` (`136 Stat. 1782`, Aug. 10, 2022) added **hypertension and MGUS** as herbicide presumptions (`38 U.S.C. § 1116(a)(2)(L)–(M)`—which are excluded from `§ 3.816` *Nehmer*!). However, the overarching statutory DIC re-evaluation mandate was enacted by **Section `204`** of `Pub. L. 117-168` (`136 Stat. 1776`, eff. Aug. 10, 2022), codified at **`38 U.S.C. § 1305`**, and implemented at **`38 C.F.R. § 3.33`** (`88 FR 82264`, published Nov. 24, 2023, eff. **Jan. 23, 2024**).
• **Super-Retroactive Effective-Date Mandate (`§ 1305(a)(3)`; `§ 3.33(d)(1)`):** Whenever a previously submitted DIC claim was evaluated and **denied before** a law, regulation, or federal court decision/settlement taking effect **on or after August 10, 2022** established or modified a presumption of service connection (covering PACT Act `§ 404` hypertension/MGUS, `§§ 401–403` Thailand/Laos/Cambodia/Guam herbicides, `§ 406` / `§ 1120` burn-pit cancers/COPD/interstitial lung disease, and future presumptions), the survivor may elect re-evaluation (e.g., via `VA Form 20-0995` or `21P-534EZ`), and ***"notwithstanding section 5110 of this title,"*** VA **must** grant DIC **"effective as if the establishment or modification of the presumption of service connection had been in effect on the date of the submission of the original claim"**!
• **Audit Goldmine:** Unlike living-veteran PACT Act hypertension claims (capped at Aug. 10, 2022 absent an independent finality exception; [Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc)), a widow whose Vietnam-veteran husband died of hypertensive heart/renal disease or stroke and whose DIC claim was denied in **1998** wins **nearly 30 years of retroactive DIC back to 1998** under `38 U.S.C. § 1305(a)(3)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.33(d)(1)`!

blocks.text: 4. Invariants / Kill-Switches

items: **Dead *Green* / *Cole* Open-Ended Hypothetical Entitlement:** Never argue that `§ 1318` DIC is warranted simply because C-file evidence could support a *de novo* retrospective `100%` rating without a lifetime claim + `§ 3.22(b)(1)` CUE or `§ 3.22(b)(2)` `§ 3.156(c)` records (*NOVA*, `314 F.3d 1373`; *Rodriguez*, `511 F.3d 1147`; *Tarver*, `557 F.3d 1371`).

**The *George v. McDonough*, *Cook* & *Damrel* CUE Bars Inside `§ 3.22(b)(1)`:**
• Under *George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` and `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`, you **cannot** establish `§ 3.22(b)(1)` CUE in a final lifetime decision by invoking a *post-decision* judicial reinterpretation (Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)), nor can an inadequate lifetime examination or `§ 5103A` duty-to-assist failure establish `§ 3.22(b)(1)` CUE (*Cook v. Principi*, `318 F.3d 1334 (Fed. Cir. 2002) (en banc)`; `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(d)(1)`). Always check `§ 3.156(c)` (`§ 3.22(b)(2)`), void reduction restoration ([Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings)), or `§ 1310` contributory death instead!
• Under *Damrel v. Brown*, `6 Vet. App. 242, 246 (1994)` and `VAOPGCPREC 12-95`, *Bell v. Derwinski* constructive possession of VAMC records applies **only to lifetime AOJ/Board decisions rendered on or after July 21, 1992** ([Procedural Vehicles Piercing Finality](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality)). Also complete the [`Board CUE Pre-Filing Gate`](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate) to avoid BVA subsumption (`§ 20.1400(b)`) or one-shot res judicata (`§ 20.1409(c)`).

**The `§ 1318(d)` Wrongful-Death Tort Offset Trap (`VAOPGCPREC 3-97`):** Under `38 U.S.C. § 1318(d)` and [`VAOPGCPREC 3-97`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index), if a surviving spouse or child receives money/property from **any judicial award, FTCA judgment, or private tort settlement** for the veteran's death (e.g., asbestos, medical malpractice, auto crash), **`§ 1318` DIC is suspended dollar-for-dollar** until the entire settlement is recouped—regardless of state-law "pain and suffering" labels! By contrast, **`§ 1310` direct/contributory SC death carries NO `§ 1318(d)` private-tort offset** (offsets apply to `§ 1310`-style awards *only* if entitlement rests on `38 U.S.C. § 1151(b)` malpractice). Always prove `§ 1310` contributory death whenever a wrongful-death settlement exists!

**Marriage Duration & Remarriage Cutoffs (`38 U.S.C. §§ 103(d), 1304, 1318(c)`):** Verify 1-year marriage (or child born of/before marriage, or marriage `<15` years after the period of service in which the fatal disability arose under `§ 1304(2)` for `§ 1310` DIC!) and remarriage age thresholds (**age `57`** eff. Jan. 1, 2004 via `Pub. L. 108-183`; **age `55`** eff. Jan. 5, 2021 via `Pub. L. 116-315`) in [`Survivor Marriage, Remarriage & Dependency Evolution`](/cfr/modules/survivor-marriage-dependency-evolution).

blocks.text: 5. Postconditions: Effective Dates, Ancillaries, Offsets & Fees

items:
**Effective-Date Verification Matrix:**
• **Filed Within 1 Year of Death (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(d)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.400(c)(2)`):** Effective date is the **first day of the calendar month in which the veteran died**! *(Verify whether an Intent to File `VA Form 21-0966` or Social Security survivorship application filed under `38 U.S.C. § 5105` / `38 C.F.R. § 3.153` locked in the 1-year post-death window!)*
• **Previously Denied DIC Re-Evaluated Under New Post-Aug. 10, 2022 Presumption (`38 U.S.C. § 1305(a)(3)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.33(d)(1)`):** Effective **as if the presumption had been in effect when the original denied DIC claim was submitted** (reaching back to the month of death if that original denied DIC claim was filed within 1 year of death!).
• ***Nehmer* Herbicide Death (`38 C.F.R. § 3.816(d)`):** Relates back to the prior post-Sept. 25, 1985 denied DIC claim (or month of death if filed within 1 year) per [Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc); unpaid *Nehmer* DIC if the surviving spouse subsequently dies is payable down the `§ 3.816(f)` chain ([Playbook 09](/playbooks/09-accrued-benefits-substitution-nehmer-estates)).
• **First-Time Liberalizing DIC Claim (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(g)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)`):** Up to **1 year prior** to receipt of claim/ITF, no earlier than the liberalizing law's effective date (e.g., **August 10, 2022** for PACT Act claims backed by a pre-Aug. 14, 2023 ITF).

**Mandatory Ancillary Survivor Unlocks (Audit Every Grant Letter!):**
• **Chapter 35 Survivors' & Dependents' Educational Assistance (`DEA`, `38 U.S.C. §§ 3500–3566`):** Up to 36 months of tax-free college/vocational stipends for the surviving spouse and eligible children (with modernized post-Aug. 1, 2023 delimiting-date repeal under `38 U.S.C. § 3512`!).
• **CHAMPVA Comprehensive Health Care (`38 U.S.C. § 1781`)** (if not TRICARE-eligible).
• **Chapter 37 Surviving Spouse VA Home Loan Guaranty & Funding-Fee Exemption (`38 U.S.C. § 3701(b)(2)`).**
• **Service-Connected Burial Allowance Upgrade (`38 U.S.C. § 2307`):** Whenever DIC is granted under **`§ 1310`** (service-connected death—*note: `§ 2307` requires `§ 1310` SC death rather than `§ 1318` non-SC death!*), claim the statutory SC burial reimbursement (`$2,000+`) and National Cemetery plot/transportation benefits.

**Attorney Fees (`38 U.S.C. § 5904` & `EAJA`):**
• Because a survivor's first `VA Form 21P-534EZ` is an **original claim** separate from the veteran's lifetime claims (*Hupp*), paid `§ 5904(c)(1)` contingency fees attach **only after VA issues an initial AOJ decision on the DIC claim**—**EXCEPT** where the survivor is pursuing a Supplemental Claim / HLR / Board appeal / `§ 1305` re-evaluation of a **previously denied DIC claim**, in which case an initial AOJ decision already exists and `§ 5904` contingency representation attaches immediately! Always offset any `28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)` EAJA award dollar-for-dollar against `§ 5904` fees for the same appellate work ([Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Survivor DIC Monthly Benefits: Service-Connected Cause of Death (§ 1310), the 10-Year Total-Disability Rule (§ 1318) & PACT Act Re-Evaluations
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) is a tax-free monthly benefit paid to eligible surviving spouses, dependent children, and low-income parents. Importantly, there are TWO completely separate paths to qualify—and VA denials often check only part of the picture: (1) Direct or Contributory Death (38 U.S.C. § 1310; 38 C.F.R. § 3.312), where a service-connected condition (including PACT Act or Agent Orange presumptions) was either the primary cause of death OR contributed substantially and materially to death—even if left off the death certificate; and (2) Total-Disability DIC (38 U.S.C. § 1318; 38 C.F.R. § 3.22), paid regardless of the cause of death when the Veteran held (or was legally entitled to receive) a 100% or TDIU rating for at least 10 continuous years before death (5 years from military discharge, or 1 year for Former POWs). In addition, under PACT Act § 204 (38 U.S.C. § 1305; 38 C.F.R. § 3.33), survivors whose earlier DIC claims were denied before a post-August 10, 2022 presumption (such as hypertension or burn-pit cancers) can re-elect DIC with retroactive effective dates back to the original denied DIC claim.
record_clues: A DIC denial letter (VA Form 21P-534EZ) relying solely on the one-page death certificate without reviewing final hospital/ICU records showing how service-connected heart, lung, kidney, diabetes, or mental health conditions hastened death (§ 3.312(c)).

A Veteran who died of a non-service-connected cause at 70%–90% (or with fewer than 10 years at 100%/TDIU), where correcting a Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) in a lifetime decision (§ 3.22(b)(1)) or adding missing military records (§ 3.22(b)(2) / § 3.156(c)) pushes 100% or TDIU past the 10-year mark.

A previously denied DIC claim where the Veteran died of complications from hypertension, MGUS, expanded Agent Orange service (Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Guam, Blue Water Navy), or Gulf War / post-9/11 burn-pit illnesses (38 C.F.R. § 3.33).

A granted DIC award missing the extra monthly 8-year 'kicker' (§ 1311(a)(2)), surviving spouse Aid & Attendance / Housebound add-ons (§ 1311(c)–(d)), the 2-year transitional benefit for minor children (§ 1311(f)), or full military Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) restoration after Congress repealed the SBP-DIC offset effective January 1, 2023.
important_cautions: How Post-2000 'Hypothetical' § 1318 DIC Works (38 C.F.R. § 3.22(b)): Since VA amended § 3.22 on January 21, 2000 (65 FR 3388, upheld in Rodriguez and Tarver), if the Veteran did not already hold a 10-year 100%/TDIU rating at death, a survivor cannot argue open-ended 'hypothetical' entitlement from scratch—entitlement under § 3.22(b) requires showing a prior lifetime VA claim plus either CUE in a final lifetime decision (§ 3.22(b)(1)), newly associated official service department records (§ 3.22(b)(2)), or a specified military retired-pay/withholding nonpayment rule.

Judicial Reinterpretation CUE Limit (George v. McDonough): When using § 3.22(b)(1) CUE to challenge a deceased Veteran's final lifetime decision, later judicial reinterpretations cannot establish CUE under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e), and pre-July 21, 1992 lifetime decisions are evaluated on the physical C-file record at that time (Damrel v. Brown).

8-Year DIC Kicker Marriage Requirement: To receive the extra monthly § 1311(a)(2) 8-year allowance, the Veteran must have been rated totally disabled (100% or TDIU) for 8 continuous years immediately preceding death AND married to the surviving spouse for those exact same 8 continuous years.

Wrongful-Death Settlement Offset Difference (§ 1318 vs. § 1310): If a survivor received a civil wrongful-death or Federal Tort Claims Act (FTCA) recovery, 38 U.S.C. § 1318(d) requires offsetting non-service-connected § 1318 DIC, whereas proving direct/contributory service-connected death under § 1310 avoids the § 1318(d) non-FTCA private-tort offset (VAOPGCPREC 3-97).
questions_for_representative: Did VA obtain the final hospitalization, ICU, or autopsy records to evaluate whether a service-connected condition (especially one affecting a vital organ at 100% under § 3.312(c)(3)) contributed substantially and materially to death?

If my spouse's DIC claim was previously denied before August 10, 2022, does a PACT Act presumption (such as hypertension or burn-pit cancer) qualify me for retroactive re-evaluation back to my original DIC claim date under 38 U.S.C. § 1305 and 38 C.F.R. § 3.33?

If my spouse had fewer than 10 years at 100%/TDIU on paper at death, was there a void rating reduction, newly associated service record (§ 3.22(b)(2)), or lifetime CUE (§ 3.22(b)(1)) that would establish 10 continuous years of total disability?

Did my DIC award letter properly include all applicable § 1311 add-ons (8-year kicker, spouse Aid & Attendance/Housebound, minor-child transitional benefit), and was my claim filed within 1 year of death for a date-of-death effective date (§ 5110(d))?

title: Playbook 09: Accrued Benefits (§ 5121), Post-Mortem Substitution (§ 5121A), CAVC Rule 43 & Nehmer Class Estates (§ 3.816(f))
statutes: Pub. L. 108-183, § 104 (repeal of 2-year accrued cap eff. Dec. 16, 2003)
keyPrecedents: Nat'l Org. of Veterans' Advocates, Inc. v. Sec'y of Veterans Affairs, 809 F.3d 1359 (Fed. Cir. 2016)
Padgett v. Nicholson, 473 F.3d 1364 (Fed. Cir. 2007) (en banc)
cFileTriggers: Death of a veteran while ANY initial claim, Supplemental Claim (0995), HLR (0996), Board appeal (10182 / Form 9), or CAVC appeal/NOA window is pending
Unadjudicated informal claim (pre-Mar. 24, 2015), Roberson/Rice TDIU issue, or post-Feb. 19, 2019 AMA issue lacking § 5104(b) explicit notice (Hamill) open at date of death

Deceased Republic of Vietnam / Blue Water Navy / Korean DMZ veteran with a post-Sept. 25, 1985 denied claim or in-file diagnosis for a § 3.309(e) Nehmer condition (even if only adult children or an estate survive)
BVA decision issued AFTER the veteran's date of death, or VA adjudication of VA Form 21P-534EZ without Reliford substitution-waiver notice
killSwitches: Relying on the deceased veteran's VA Form 21-22a POA or fee agreement after death (agency terminates immediately at death; counsel MUST obtain a new 21-22a and fee agreement from the survivor)

Missing the strict 1-year post-death statutory filing deadline for § 5121 accrued benefits (§ 5121(c)) or § 5121A substitution (38 C.F.R. § 3.1010(b)), OR substituting solely at the CAVC/Federal Circuit without also filing a formal VA accrued/substitution application within 1 year of death when a remand is needed (moots the appeal under Merritt v. Wilkie, 965 F.3d 1357 (Fed. Cir. 2020)!)

Filing a brand-new post-mortem § 5109A or § 7111 CUE motion to recover § 5121 accrued benefits when the veteran had NO CUE claim pending at death (categorically barred by Haines v. West, 154 F.3d 1298 (Fed. Cir. 1998))

Attempting § 5121A substitution or § 5121 accrued recovery for an adult non-helpless child or estate (ineligible under § 5121(a)(2) except for § 5121(a)(6) last-sickness/burial reimbursement OR § 3.816(f) Nehmer class awards!)
Invoking § 5121A open-record substitution when the veteran died BEFORE October 10, 2008, or overlooking the 2-year accrued payment cap for non-Nehmer deaths BEFORE December 16, 2003
Assuming PACT Act hypertension or MGUS qualifies for § 3.816(f) Nehmer estate/adult-child payout (explicitly excluded by M21-1 VIII.i.2.B.1.c)

blocks.text: Under general Veterans Law principles, a veteran's claim for lifetime disability compensation extinguishes upon death unless saved by statute (*Zevalkink v. Brown*, `102 F.3d 1236, 1243–44 (Fed. Cir. 1996)`). Yet when a veteran dies with a multi-year appeal pending, an unadjudicated informal/TDIU/AMA claim sitting in the C-file, or a previously denied Agent Orange condition, **hundreds of thousands of dollars in unpaid lifetime compensation** hang in the balance.

Capturing those funds—while simultaneously protecting the survivor's prospective monthly DIC ([Playbook 08](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical))—requires choosing with surgical precision among **three distinct statutory/regulatory post-mortem vehicles**: **(A) `38 U.S.C. § 5121A` Substitution**, **(B) `38 U.S.C. § 5121` Accrued Benefits**, and **(C) `38 C.F.R. § 3.816(f)` *Nehmer* Class Survivor/Estate Payouts**.

lines: **Immediate 48-Hour Post-Death Intake Rule:** A veteran's Power of Attorney (`VA Form 21-22a`) and representation authority **terminate by operation of law at the moment of death**. Execute the [`Survivor Post-Mortem Triage Gate`](/checklists/survivor-post-mortem-triage-gate) immediately: sign a **new `VA Form 21-22a`** (and updated fee agreement) with the eligible survivor/executor, calendar the **strict 1-year post-death statutory bar** (`§§ 5121(c), 5121A(a)(1)`), and check for running **`120-day` CAVC Notice of Appeal (`NOA`)** deadlines!

blocks.text: 1. Preconditions: VBMS, Docket & C-File Post-Mortem Triggers

*(See verbatim primary-source regulations in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.1000, 3.1010 & 3.816(f) (Accrued Benefits, § 5121A Substitution & Nehmer Survivor/Estate Payouts)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.1000-3.1010-accrued-substitution) and form/code-sheet conventions in [Historical & Modern VA Forms, Service Records & Rating Code Sheet Lexicon (1945–2026)](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon)).*

items:
**Prescribed Post-Mortem VA Forms:**
• **`VA Form 21P-0847`** (*Request for Substitution of Claimant Upon Death of Claimant*) — primary form to step into a pending claim, HLR, or Board appeal within **1 year of death**.
• **`VA Form 21P-534EZ`** (*Application for DIC, Survivors Pension, and/or Accrued Benefits*) — simultaneously claims DIC **and** `§ 5121` accrued benefits (and triggers VA's duty under *Reliford* to address `§ 5121A` substitution if a claim was pending!).
• **`VA Form 21P-601`** (*Application for Accrued Amounts Due a Deceased Beneficiary*) — used by non-spouse/parent/adult-child payers seeking **`§ 5121(a)(6)` last-sickness and burial expense reimbursement**, or when claiming accrued amounts without DIC.

**Pending-Claim & Docket Audit Triggers (What Counts as "Pending at Death"?):**
• Any active initial claim (`21-526EZ`), AMA Supplemental Claim (`20-0995`), Higher-Level Review (`20-0996`), Board appeal (`10182` or Legacy `VA Form 9` / unissued `SOC` after post-1962 `NOD`), or CAVC appeal pending on the date of death.
• **Hidden Unadjudicated Claims Open at Death:** Even if VBMS shows *"No Active Claims"* on the date of death, a claim was **legally pending at death** if the C-file contains:
• A pre-March 24, 2015 informal claim (`former § 3.155(a)` / `§ 3.157(b)` VAMC hospitalization report) or pro se symptom entry (`Shea v. Wilkie`) never adjudicated ([Playbook 04](/playbooks/04-unadjudicated-tdiu-informal-claims-smc));
• Reasonably raised `Roberson`/`Rice` **TDIU** during an open rating stream;
• A defective-address decision that never became final under `§ 3.103` / *Mindenhall* ([Playbook 02](/playbooks/02-wrong-address-defective-notice-cp-exams)); or
• A post-February 19, 2019 AMA claim/issue omitted from explicit `38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)` decision notice under ***Hamill v. Collins*, 166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. 2026)** ([Procedural Vehicles Piercing Finality](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality))!
• ***Nehmer* Class Audit Trigger (`§ 3.816(f)`):** Service in the Republic of Vietnam (land or `12-nm` Blue Water Navy territorial seas, Jan. 9, 1962 – May 7, 1975) or Korean DMZ + **any** post-Sept. 25, 1985 denied claim or in-file diagnosis ("Footnote 1") for a `§ 3.309(e)` covered herbicide disease ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc)).

blocks.text: 2. Bitemporal Pathway Gate & Master Three-Track Architecture

headers: Track A: Post-Mortem Substitution (`38 U.S.C. § 5121A`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.1010`)
Track B: Accrued Benefits (`38 U.S.C. § 5121`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.1000`)
Track C: *Nehmer* Class Survivors & Estates (`38 C.F.R. § 3.816(f)`)
rows: Claimant died **on or after October 10, 2008** (`Pub. L. 110-389, § 212(c)`)
**Any date of death** *(Note: deaths **< Dec. 16, 2003** capped at **2 years** of benefits; uncapped **`>= Dec. 16, 2003`** per `Pub. L. 108-183, § 104`)*
**Any date of death** (even 1980s–2000s deaths!), with **ZERO 2-year cap** across all eras
**NO 1-year post-death filing bar!** Payable whenever class entitlement is identified (`§ 3.816(f)`)

Strictly `§ 5121(a)(2)`: · 1. Surviving spouse; · 2. Minor (`<18`), helpless (`§ 3.356`), or school (`18–23`) children; · 3. **Dependent** parents. · *(Adult independent children & estates **BARRED**!)*
Same `§ 5121(a)(2)` hierarchy; if none exist, `§ 5121(a)(6)` pays **ONLY reimbursement of last sickness & burial expenses** to the person who bore the expense!

Broad `§ 3.816(f)(1)(i)–(iv)` hierarchy: · `(i)` Spouse at death (**even if remarried**); · `(ii)` **ALL children (INCLUDING adult independent children!)**; · `(iii)` **ALL parents (regardless of dependency)**; · `(iv)` **Deceased class member's ESTATE!**
**OPEN RECORD:** Substitute steps into veteran's shoes; can submit **new private IMOs, lay statements & DBQs**, and triggers VA's `§ 5103A` Duty to Assist!
**CLOSED RECORD:** Strictly frozen to `"existing ratings or decisions or... evidence in the file at date of death"` (*Zevalkink*; *Jones*) + constructive VA records.
**OPEN CLASS RECORD:** Full retroactive staging from service/medical records & post-mortem *Nehmer* review ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc)).

**Superior (`open-claim` preserved!):** Substituting into a live claim/appeal keeps it **non-final**, so favorable judicial precedents (*Bradley*, *Barry*, *Hamill*) apply **without** *George* (`§ 20.1403(e)`) CUE bars! Can also substitute into a CUE motion *filed by the veteran before death*.

**Restricted (*Haines v. West* bar!):** Survivor **CANNOT initiate** a new `§ 5109A`/`§ 7111` CUE motion to collect `§ 5121` accrued benefits (*Haines*, `154 F.3d 1298`), though survivor CAN collect on a CUE motion pending at death.
**Bypasses CUE & *Haines*!** `§ 3.816(c)–(f)` vacates prior post-Sept. 25, 1985 herbicide denials by consent decree without needing CUE!

blocks.text: 3. Proof Elements & Doctrinal Mechanics
A. Standalone Accrued Benefits (38 U.S.C. § 5121 [former § 3021]; 38 C.F.R. § 3.1000)

items:
**The "Pending Claim or Existing Decisions" Prerequisite (*Zevalkink* & *Jones*):**
• Under `38 U.S.C. § 5121(a)` (`former 38 U.S.C. § 3021(a)`, [Three-Era Statutory Crosswalk](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk)), periodic monetary benefits to which an individual was entitled at death `"under existing ratings or decisions or... based on evidence in the file at date of death"` and `"due and unpaid"` are paid to the highest living `§ 5121(a)(2)` class.
• In ***Zevalkink v. Brown*, 102 F.3d 1236, 1241–42 (Fed. Cir. 1996)** and ***Jones v. West*, 136 F.3d 1296, 1299–1300 (Fed. Cir. 1998)**, the Federal Circuit held that an accrued-benefits claim is **derivative** of the veteran's claim: unless unpaid benefits were already awarded before death, **the veteran must have had a claim pending (or a non-final appeal window open) on the date of death**.
• **What Counts as `"Evidence in the File at Date of Death"` (`§ 3.1000(d)(4)`):** Includes all records physically in the C-file plus records in **constructive VA possession** (VAMC clinical records, military service records, SSA records already held by VA, etc.), **excluding** post-mortem medical nexus opinions unless `§ 5121A` substitution is invoked.

**Repeal of the Historical 2-Year Payment Cap (`Pub. L. 108-183, § 104`):**
• Prior to December 16, 2003, `38 U.S.C. § 5121(a)` brutally capped accrued recoveries at **2 years** of retroactive benefits—forfeiting 8 years of back pay if a veteran died during a 10-year appeal!
• Section `104(a)` & `(d)` of the *Veterans Benefits Act of 2003* (`Pub. L. 108-183`, `117 Stat. 2656`) **repealed the 2-year cap in full for claimants dying on or after December 16, 2003**, unlocking 100% of uncapped past-due lifetime compensation. *(If auditing an older death occurring **before Dec. 16, 2003**, the 2-year cap still applies to `§ 5121`—pivot immediately to `38 C.F.R. § 3.816(f)` if herbicide-related!)*

**The Three-Way Survivor CUE Matrix (*Haines v. West*, `154 F.3d 1298 (Fed. Cir. 1998)`):**
• **Rule 1 — Survivor CANNOT Initiate CUE for `§ 5121` Accrued Back Pay:** In *Haines v. West*, `154 F.3d at 1300–02`, the Federal Circuit held that `38 U.S.C. §§ 5109A` and `7111` do **not** authorize a survivor to initiate a post-mortem CUE attack on a final lifetime rating decision in order to manufacture `"due and unpaid"` accrued benefits under `§ 5121`.
• **Rule 2 — Survivor CAN Pursue a CUE Motion Filed by the Veteran Before Death:** If the *veteran* filed a valid `§ 5109A` or `§ 7111` CUE motion during life and died before final resolution, that CUE claim was **pending at death**, allowing an eligible `§ 5121(a)(2)` survivor to substitute (`§ 5121A`) or take accrued benefits (`§ 5121`) upon proving CUE!
• **Rule 3 — Survivor CAN Initiate Lifetime CUE Under `38 C.F.R. § 3.22(b)(1)` for `§ 1318` DIC:** *Haines* bars CUE **only** for `§ 5121` lifetime back pay; `38 C.F.R. § 3.22(b)(1)` explicitly authorizes a survivor to prove CUE in a lifetime decision to establish `10-year` total disability for the survivor's own monthly `§ 1318` DIC ([Playbook 08](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical))!

blocks.text: B. Post-Mortem Substitution (38 U.S.C. § 5121A; 38 C.F.R. § 3.1010) & The *Reliford* Waiver Choice

Enacted by **`Pub. L. 110-389, § 212` (`122 Stat. 4151`, Oct. 10, 2008)** for deaths **on or after October 10, 2008**, and implemented at **`38 C.F.R. § 3.1010`** (`79 FR 52977`, published Sept. 5, 2014, eff. **Oct. 6, 2014**; upheld in ***Nat'l Org. of Veterans' Advocates, Inc. (NOVA) v. Sec'y of Veterans Affairs*, 809 F.3d 1359 (Fed. Cir. 2016)**), Section `5121A` revolutionized survivor litigation:

items:
**Open-Record Shoes of the Veteran (*Reeves* & *Breedlove*):**
• By filing **`VA Form 21P-0847`** (or `21P-534EZ` requesting accrued/substitution) within **1 year of the veteran's death**, an eligible `§ 5121(a)(2)` survivor steps directly into the pending claim or appeal at its exact procedural stage (*Breedlove v. Shinseki*, `24 Vet. App. 7, 18–20 (2010)` (per curiam)).
• Under ***Reeves v. Shinseki*, 682 F.3d 988, 993–94 (Fed. Cir. 2012)**, an eligible survivor has standing to substitute on appeal without having first prosecuted a separate standalone `§ 5121` accrued claim, inheriting the veteran's evidentiary presumptions (such as `38 U.S.C. § 1154(b)` combat relaxation) and full open-record development rights—including submitting **new post-mortem private medical nexus / staging opinions**!

**Tactical Gem — When to WAIVE Substitution Under *Reliford v. McDonald*, `27 Vet. App. 297 (2015)`:**
• In *Reliford*, the veteran died with a positive nexus opinion already placing the record in `§ 5107(b)` equipoise; instead of granting `§ 5121` accrued benefits on the closed date-of-death record, VA automatically treated the widow's `21-534` as a `§ 5121A` substitution, ordered a **new post-mortem VA medical opinion that came back negative**, and denied the claim!
• The CAVC reversed, holding that `§ 5121` and `§ 5121A` are distinct statutory pathways and **VA must notify an accrued claimant of the right to WAIVE `§ 5121A` substitution** (`27 Vet. App. at 303–05`).
• **Practitioner Decision Rule:**
• **Substitute (`§ 5121A` — 95% of cases):** Whenever the date-of-death record lacks a medical nexus, diagnosis confirmation, stressor proof, or higher-rating staging evidence that you can supply via a post-mortem private IMO/DBQ.
• **Waive Substitution & Demand Closed-Record `§ 5121` Adjudication (*Reliford* — 5% of cases):** Whenever the file **on the date of death** already contains uncontroverted or equiponderant favorable medical evidence entitling the claimant to win under `§ 5107(b)`, and reopening the record risks VA shopping for a hostile post-mortem C&P opinion!

blocks.text: C. The CAVC & Board Death-Timing Matrix (CAVC Rule 43, *Smith*, *Breedlove*, *Padgett* & *Phillips*)
When a client dies near or during appellate review, the **exact date of death relative to the BVA decision and CAVC docket** dictates the mandatory litigation motion:

rows: **1. Died *BEFORE* BVA Decision Issued** *(without prior substitution)*
**Legal Nullity (*ultra vires*):** BVA lacked jurisdiction over a deceased appellant (`38 C.F.R. § 20.1302(a)`)
*Smith v. Brown*, `10 Vet. App. 330 (1997)`; *Landicho v. Brown*, `7 Vet. App. 42 (1994)`; *NOVA*, `809 F.3d at 1364`

**(a)** Move BVA (or appeal to CAVC if needed) to **vacate the void BVA decision** so it poses zero res judicata bar; **AND** · **(b)** File **`VA Form 21P-0847`** within **1 year of death** to substitute into the still-pending appeal! *(Remember [`VAOPGCPREC 2-2007`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index) was withdrawn at `75 FR 11229`!)*
**2. Died *AFTER* BVA Decision During `120-Day` NOA Window** (`38 U.S.C. § 7266`)
Valid BVA decision that will become **final roadblock** unless timely appealed
*Breedlove v. Shinseki*, `24 Vet. App. 7 (2010)`; *Pekular v. Mansfield*, `21 Vet. App. 495 (2007)`; *Merritt v. Wilkie*, `965 F.3d 1357 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`; **`CAVC Rule 43(a)(2)`**

**Mandatory Dual-Forum Filing:** · **(a)** File **NOA + Motion to Substitute + new survivor `21-22a`/fee agreement** in **CAVC** within 120 days of BVA decision (plead equitable tolling if death delayed filing); **AND** · **(b)** File **`VA Form 21P-0847` + `21P-534EZ`** at the **VA AOJ** within **1 year of death** (judicial substitution alone moots on remand under *Merritt* if no timely formal VA claim was filed!).
*Phillips v. Shinseki*, `581 F.3d 1358 (Fed. Cir. 2009)`; *Reeves*, `682 F.3d 988`; *Merritt*, `965 F.3d 1357`; **`CAVC Rule 43(a)(1)`**

File **`CAVC Rule 43(a)(1)` Motion to Substitute** (attaching death certificate, marriage/dependency proof, and new survivor `21-22a`) **AND** file **`21P-0847` + `21P-534EZ`** at VA within **1 year of death** (*Merritt*). Preserves merits remand **and EAJA fee standing** (*Phillips*)!
**4. Died *AFTER* Case Submitted to CAVC / Fed. Cir. (or No `§ 5121` Payee Exists Post-Submission)**

Substitute under `Rule 43(a)(1)` **AND/OR** move the Court to enter judgment ***nunc pro tunc* effective the day before the veteran's death**! Crucial if no `§ 5121(a)(2)` payee exists (crystallizing `§ 5121(a)(6)` reimbursement & EAJA standing) or for pre-Oct. 10, 2008 deaths.

blocks.text: D. *Nehmer* Class Retroactive Survivor & Estate Payouts (38 C.F.R. § 3.816(f))

Whenever a deceased veteran served in the **Republic of Vietnam** (including `12-nm` **Blue Water Navy** offshore waters under `Pub. L. 116-23` / `VAOPGCPREC 3-2019`) or covered *Nehmer* cohorts and had a post-September 25, 1985 denied claim or in-file "Footnote 1" diagnosis for a covered herbicide condition ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc)), **`38 C.F.R. § 3.816(f)` completely supersedes the harsh restrictions of `§§ 5121` and `5121A`**:

items: **No 1-Year Filing Bar & Unlimited Retroactivity:** Even if the veteran died in 1995 and the family contacts your firm 30 years later, VA **must** audit the C-file and pay **100% of the unpaid retroactive compensation** from the prior post-Sept. 25, 1985 claim/diagnosis date to the veteran's death (`§ 3.816(c), (f)`).

**Dramatically Broader Payee Chain (`38 C.F.R. § 3.816(f)(1)(i)–(iv)`):** VA must pay the first living class in order:
• **`(i)` Surviving Spouse at Death:** Payable **regardless of current marital status** (even if the widow remarried at age 35 and lost `§ 1310` DIC!).
• **`(ii)` Child(ren) in Equal Shares:** Payable **regardless of age or marital status**—meaning **40- or 60-year-old independent adult children** (natural, adopted, or household stepchildren at death) recover full six-figure *Nehmer* awards despite being completely barred under `§ 5121(a)(2)`!
• **`(iii)` Parent(s) in Equal Shares:** Payable **regardless of financial dependency**.
• **`(iv)` The Deceased Class Member's Estate:** If no spouse, child, or parent survives at the time of payment, VA **must pay the deceased class member's probate estate** (via court-appointed executor/administrator or state small-estate affidavit procedures where accepted)!

**Mandatory Exclusion Screen (`M21-1 VIII.i.2.B.1.c`):** Remember that PACT Act **hypertension**, **MGUS**, and **chloracne** are **excluded** from `38 C.F.R. § 3.816` *Nehmer* class status ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc)). An adult child or estate **cannot** use `§ 3.816(f)` to collect unpaid lifetime hypertension compensation (though a surviving spouse **can** use `38 U.S.C. § 1305` to win multi-decade retroactive **DIC** if hypertension caused/contributed to death and a prior DIC claim was denied; see [Playbook 08](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical)!).

blocks.text: 4. Invariants / Kill-Switches

items: **Expired Power of Attorney Trap:** Filing an NOA, `20-0995`, or `21P-0847` signed by counsel under the *deceased veteran's* `VA Form 21-22a` without obtaining a **new `VA Form 21-22a` signed by the survivor/claimant** results in jurisdictional dismissal for unauthorized filing!

**Confusing the `§ 5110(d)` 1-Year DIC Effective-Date Rule With the `§§ 5121(c) / 5121A` Absolute Bar:** Filing a DIC claim (`21P-534EZ`) `14 months` after death merely forfeits month-of-death DIC retroactivity (paying DIC from claim receipt forward). Filing a `§ 5121` accrued claim or `§ 5121A` substitution request `14 months` after death **permanently extinguishes the entire accrued/substitution claim forever**!

***Haines v. West* Post-Mortem CUE Trap:** Never file a new post-mortem `§ 5109A` or `§ 7111` CUE motion expecting `§ 5121` accrued back pay (*Haines*, `154 F.3d 1298`). Check instead for **(1)** an unadjudicated lifetime claim (`Shea`, `Roberson`, *Hamill* `§ 5104(b)`), **(2)** `§ 3.816(f)` *Nehmer* class status, or **(3)** `§ 3.22(b)(1)` CUE solely as the predicate for `§ 1318` DIC ([Playbook 08](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical)).

**Single Substitute Representative, Preferred-Class Forfeiture & Successive Substitution (`38 U.S.C. § 5121A(a)(1)–(2)`; `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.1000(a)(1)(ii), 3.1000(c)(2), 3.1010(a), 3.1010(g)(4)–(5)`):** Upon the death of a veteran with no surviving spouse and multiple eligible minor/helpless/school children, only **one** person may be treated as the formal substitute to prosecute the claim (`§ 5121A(a)(2)`; `§ 3.1010(a)`), while resulting accrued benefits are paid in equal shares to all eligible children (`§ 3.1000(a)(1)(ii)`—*note: `§ 3.1000(a)(2)` governs death of a surviving spouse*). If a preferred-tier survivor waives or misses the 1-year deadline, lower-tier survivors are barred (`§§ 3.1000(c)(2), 3.1010(g)(4)`); **however**, if a timely-substituted survivor **dies while the substituted claim/appeal is still pending**, **`§ 3.1010(g)(5)`** grants the next eligible class member a fresh 1-year window from the *substitute's* death for successive substitution!

blocks.text: 5. Postconditions: Payment Cutoffs, Retiree Arrears (Soto) & Attorney Fees

items:
**Exact Payment Boundary & Seamless DIC Handoff (`38 U.S.C. § 5112(b)(1)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.500(g)(1)`):**
• Lifetime compensation won via `§ 5121`, `§ 5121A`, or `§ 3.816(f)` pays from the veteran's effective date **through the last day of the calendar month PRECEDING the month of death** (veterans do not receive compensation for the month in which they die).
• If the surviving spouse files `21P-534EZ` within 1 year of death, **DIC begins on the first day of the month OF death** (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(d)`), leaving **zero unpaid gap days**! *(Audit the veteran's bank account for any Treasury reclamation of a posthumously deposited month-of-death VA check vs. `38 U.S.C. § 5122` month-of-death surviving-spouse check rules).*

**Parallel DFAS Retiree Arrears & Uncapped CRSC (*Soto v. United States*, `605 U.S. 360 (2025)`):**
• Whenever a `§ 5121A`, `§ 5121`, or `§ 3.816(f)` award retroactively increases a **military retiree's** lifetime VA compensation, audit whether VA withheld money for military retired-pay offset (`38 U.S.C. §§ 5304–5305`). File a follow-on **Arrears of Pay (`AOP`, `10 U.S.C. § 2771`, `SF 1174`)** and **uncapped `CRSC` (`10 U.S.C. § 1413a`)** claim with DFAS / the service branch CRSC board under *Soto* ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc))—remarkably, **`10 U.S.C. § 2771` DFAS arrears pay out to designated beneficiaries, spouses, adult children, parents, or legal representatives without `§ 5121` minor-child restrictions**!

**Attorney Fees & EAJA Alignment (`38 U.S.C. § 5904` & `28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)`):**
• **Execute a New Fee Agreement Immediately:** Sign a new `38 U.S.C. § 5904` contingency fee agreement (and `VA Form 21-22a`) with the substituting survivor and file within 30 days at VA (`38 C.F.R. § 14.636(g)`). When substituting under `§ 5121A` into a claim that already had an initial AOJ decision during the veteran's life, `§ 5904(c)(1)` fee eligibility carries forward seamlessly; if filing an original standalone `§ 5121` or `§ 3.816(f)` claim with no prior decision on that issue, paid `§ 5904(c)(1)` representation attaches only after an initial AOJ decision on that claim.
• **EAJA Survivorship & Offset:** Upon `CAVC Rule 43` substitution (or *Padgett* *nunc pro tunc* relief), the substituted survivor maintains full standing to recover **`28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)` EAJA fees** (*Phillips*, `581 F.3d at 1368`), subject to the mandatory dollar-for-dollar `§ 5904` same-work offset ([Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Recovering Unpaid Back Pay After a Veteran Passes Away: Substitution (§ 5121A), Accrued Benefits (§ 5121) & Nehmer Estates
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: When a Veteran passes away while a VA claim, appeal, or review window is still open, the past-due compensation VA owed the Veteran during their lifetime does not automatically vanish—but strict deadlines and family-priority rules apply. For deaths on or after October 10, 2008, an eligible surviving spouse, minor/school/helpless child, or dependent parent can request 'Substitution' within 1 year of death (38 U.S.C. § 5121A; 38 C.F.R. § 3.1010) to step directly into the Veteran's shoes and submit new medical evidence or nexus opinions, rather than being locked into 'Accrued Benefits' based only on evidence already in the file at death (38 U.S.C. § 5121; 38 C.F.R. § 3.1000). Even broader rules apply to Republic of Vietnam / Blue Water Navy Agent Orange ('Nehmer') awards under 38 C.F.R. § 3.816(f), which can pay full retroactive back pay to adult children or the Veteran's estate with no 1-year filing deadline.
record_clues: A Veteran passed away within the past 12 months while an initial claim, Supplemental Claim, Higher-Level Review, Board appeal, or 1-year/120-day appeal window was still open.
An older unadjudicated pre-2015 informal claim, overlooked TDIU issue, or silent post-February 19, 2019 AMA issue was still legally pending on the date the Veteran died.
A Board of Veterans' Appeals decision issued ON OR AFTER the Veteran's date of death (which is legally void and leaves the appeal pending for substitution!).

A deceased Republic of Vietnam or Blue Water Navy Veteran had a post-September 25, 1985 claim or diagnosis for a covered Agent Orange condition (such as ischemic heart disease, prostate/bladder/lung cancer, Parkinson's, or diabetes), even if only adult children or an estate survive (§ 3.816(f)).
important_cautions: Strict 1-Year Post-Death Deadline (§ 5121 & § 5121A): Standard accrued-benefits and substitution requests MUST be filed with VA within 1 year of the Veteran's death (unlike § 3.816(f) Nehmer class payouts, which have no claim deadline). Also, if a case is pending at a federal court (CAVC or Federal Circuit), the survivor must BOTH substitute at the court AND file a timely VA accrued/substitution claim within 1 year of death to prevent mooting a remand (Merritt v. Wilkie).

Power of Attorney Ends at Death: A deceased Veteran's VA Form 21-22a or VSO appointment terminates the moment the Veteran dies; the surviving family member must sign a brand-new appointment form to authorize a representative.

No Post-Death Brand-New CUE Motions for Accrued Pay: Under Haines v. West, a survivor cannot file a brand-new Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) motion after death to collect § 5121 accrued back pay unless the Veteran's own CUE claim was already pending at death (post-death CUE is used instead to establish 10-year § 1318 DIC under § 3.22(b)(1)).

Adult Children & Estates Eligibility Difference: Under standard § 5121 / § 5121A rules, non-helpless adult children over 23 (or 18 if not in school) cannot substitute or collect accrued pay (beyond reimbursing last-sickness/burial expenses under § 5121(a)(6))—whereas § 3.816(f) Nehmer Agent Orange awards DO pay adult children and estates (note: PACT Act hypertension and MGUS are not Nehmer § 3.816(f) conditions).
questions_for_representative: Are we within 1 year of my loved one's death so we can file VA Form 21P-0847 (or VA Form 21P-534EZ) immediately to lock in 38 U.S.C. § 5121A open-record substitution rights?
Have I signed a new survivor VA Form 21-22 or 21-22a so you have legal authority to view the VBMS file and represent me?
If my loved one's appeal was at the CAVC (or inside the 120-day CAVC appeal window) at death, have we protected BOTH judicial substitution (CAVC Rule 43) and a timely VA agency filing?

If only adult children or an estate survive, did the Veteran serve in the Republic of Vietnam / Blue Water Navy with a covered Agent Orange condition eligible for a § 3.816(f) Nehmer estate/adult-child payout?

title: Playbook 10: Character of Discharge (§ 3.12 Overhaul), Conditional Discharges (§ 3.13), Insanity (§ 3.354(b)) & DRB/BCMR Upgrades
cFileTriggers: DD Form 214 Block 24 showing Other Than Honorable (OTH), Undesirable, Bad Conduct (BCD), or Uncharacterized separation
DD Form 214 Block 18 Remarks showing 'Immediate Reenlistment' or 'Continuous Honorable Active Service From...' across multiple enlistments
Special Court-Martial (SPCM) BCD misclassified by an RO rater as a statutory General Court-Martial (GCM) bar under § 5303(a) / § 3.12(c)(2)
AWOL calculation >= 180 days that improperly included authorized leave, return to military control, or military/civilian confinement
STRs, brig/stockade records, Article 15/court-martial packets, or post-service psychiatric records showing PTSD, TBI, bipolar disorder, psychosis, or MST at time of misconduct
AMA post-Feb. 19, 2019 Supplemental Claim or reopening request on COD ignored or silently omitted from VA's decision notice (Hamill v. Collins)
DRB (DD Form 293) vs. BCMR/BCNR (DD Form 149) upgrade decision followed by a VA award ignoring § 3.400(g) or § 3.156(c) effective dates
killSwitches: Invoking post-June 25, 2024 38 C.F.R. § 3.12(e) compelling circumstances (89 FR 32361) to claim CUE on a pre-June 25, 2024 final COD denial, or expecting a § 3.114(a) liberalizing effective date earlier than June 25, 2024

Pleading § 3.12(e) compelling circumstances against a General Court-Martial (§ 3.12(c)(2)), OTH in lieu of GCM (§ 3.12(d)(1)(i)), conscientious objector (§ 3.12(c)(1)), officer resignation for good of service (§ 3.12(c)(3)), deserter (§ 3.12(c)(4)), alien release (§ 3.12(c)(5)), or mutiny/spying (§ 3.12(d)(1)(ii)) bar

Relying on a post-Oct. 8, 1977 DRB upgrade (10 U.S.C. § 1553; § 3.12(h) [former (g)]) alone to overcome a § 3.12(c) statutory bar (such as 180+ continuous days AWOL) instead of escalating to a BCMR/BCNR (10 U.S.C. § 1552; § 3.12(f) [former (e)]) or proving § 3.354(b) insanity / § 3.12(e) compelling circumstances

Relying on 10 U.S.C. § 874(b) Service Secretary executive clemency discharge substitution to lift a General Court-Martial statutory bar (barred by VAOPGCPREC 10-96; requires 10 U.S.C. § 1552 BCMR sentence correction or § 3.354(b) insanity)

Pleading § 3.354(b) insanity based solely on a pure personality/character disorder or voluntary acute intoxication without an underlying mental disease (Struck v. Brown; Zang v. Brown; VAOPGCPREC 20-97)
