blocks.text: Threshold **"veteran" status** under `38 U.S.C. § 101(2)` requires active military, naval, air, or space service terminated *"under conditions other than dishonorable"* (*Holmes v. Brown*, `10 Vet. App. 38, 40 (1997)`; *D'Amico v. West*, `209 F.3d 1322 (Fed. Cir. 2000)`; ***Newman v. McDonough*, `35 Vet. App. 310 (2022)`**—abrogating the pre-VCAA *Aguilar*/*Holmes* preponderance hurdle and holding that **`38 U.S.C. § 5107(b)` benefit-of-the-doubt equipoise** governs threshold veteran-status and COD/insanity determinations; see [Three-Era Title 38 Statutory Crosswalk](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk)). Veterans separated with an **Other Than Honorable (`OTH`)** (historically *"Undesirable"*), **Bad Conduct (`BCD`)**, **Dishonorable (`DD`)**, or **Uncharacterized** discharge are routinely turned away at intake—yet **five distinct statutory and regulatory pathways** allow counsel to establish full compensation eligibility and, in four of those five pathways, capture **multi-decade retroactive effective dates** pre-dating VA's **June 25, 2024** Character of Discharge (`COD`) overhaul (`89 FR 32361`).

lines: **Paragraph Redesignation Alert (`89 FR 32361`, pub. Apr. 26, 2024, eff. June 25, 2024):** VA's 2024 Final Rule inserted a new **`38 C.F.R. § 3.12(e)` (*Compelling circumstances exception*)** and **redesignated former paragraphs `(e)–(k)` as `(f)–(l)`** (`§ 3.12(f)` `[former (e)]` BCMR upgrades; `§ 3.12(g)` `[former (f)]` pre-Oct. 8, 1977 DRB upgrades; `§ 3.12(h)` `[former (g)]` post-Oct. 8, 1977 DRB upgrades; `§ 3.12(i)` `[former (h)]` special review programs; `§ 3.12(l)` `[former (k)]` uncharacterized separations). Always cite **both** current and `[former ...]` paragraph letters when briefing cross-era claims. For verbatim pre- and post-June 25, 2024 regulatory text and structural diffs, see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.12, 3.13, 3.354, 3.400(g), 3.6 & 3.301 (Character of Discharge Evolution, Insanity, Upgrades, ADT/IADT & Line of Duty)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.12-3.13-3.354-cod-insanity) and [Part 3 Historical Diff: Character of Discharge Evolution (38 U.S.C. § 5303 & 38 C.F.R. § 3.12 Pre- vs. Post-June 25, 2024 Final Rule, 89 FR 32361)](/cfr/modules/character-of-discharge-3.12-evolution). Run the [`COD & Guard/Reserve Intake Audit`](/checklists/cod-and-guard-reserve-intake-audit) at initial screening, and pair Guard/Reserve duty-status issues with [Playbook 11](/playbooks/11-guard-reserve-adt-iadt-and-line-of-duty).

blocks.text: 1. Preconditions: DD-214, OMPF & VBMS Administrative Triggers

Before accepting a prior VA COD denial at face value, obtain the complete **Official Military Personnel File (`OMPF`)** (enlistment contracts `DD Form 4`, separation packet, court-martial promulgating orders, Article 15s) and VBMS **Administrative Decision** ([VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon)):

items:
**`DD Form 214` Block-by-Block Audit (`1979–Present` Format; Equivalent Boxes on Older `DD-214` / `NAVPERS 553`):**
• **Block `12` (`Record of Service`) & Block `18` (`Remarks`):** Look for total prior active service exceeding the final enlistment contract, or remarks stating ***"Immediate Reenlistment,"*** ***"Continuous Honorable Active Service From [Date] to [Date],"*** or ***"SOLDIER HAS COMPLETED FIRST FULL TERM OF SERVICE."*** A single consolidated `DD-214` masking an earlier honorable reenlistment is the **#1 CUE goldmine in COD law (`38 C.F.R. § 3.13`)**!
• **Block `24` (`Character of Service`):** `Honorable` or `Under Honorable Conditions (General)` binds VA favorably (`§ 3.12(a)`), *unless* issued via a post-Oct. 8, 1977 DRB upgrade where a `§ 3.12(c)` statutory bar remains (`§ 3.12(h)`). `Under Other Than Honorable Conditions`, `Undesirable`, `Bad Conduct`, `Dishonorable`, or `Uncharacterized` (`§ 3.12(l)`) triggers a formal VA COD determination.
• **Blocks `25` (`Separation Authority`), `26` (`Separation Code / SPD`), `28` (`Narrative Reason`) & `29` (`Dates of Time Lost Under 10 U.S.C. § 972`):**
• Distinguish **Special Court-Martial (`SPCM`) BCD** from **General Court-Martial (`GCM`) BCD/DD** via the Court-Martial Order (`CMO`)—`DD-214` Block `24` says `"Bad Conduct"` for both!
• Distinguish administrative **OTH in lieu of trial by GCM** (e.g., Army `AR 635-200, Ch. 10` / `SPD KFS`, which triggers non-waivable `§ 3.12(d)(1)(i)`) from misconduct/pattern-of-misconduct separations (`AR 635-200, Ch. 14` / `MILPERSMAN 1910-140`, which fall under waivable `§ 3.12(d)(2)`!).
• Audit **Block `29` (`Time Lost`)**: Verify whether `180+` lost days reflect a **single continuous AWOL (`>= 180` consecutive days)** versus *multiple shorter AWOLs* or **military/civilian confinement (`CONF`)**!

**Clinical & Procedural Triggers in STRs / VBMS:**
• Post-deployment behavioral collapse, brig/stockade psychiatric evaluations, emergency room overdoses, MST markers, TBI blast exposures, or Axis I diagnoses (PTSD, schizophrenia, bipolar I/II, major depression) preceding or contemporaneous with the misconduct (`§ 3.354(b)` & `§ 3.12(e)(2)`).
• Post-February 19, 2019 (`AMA`) `VA Form 20-0995` or `21-526EZ` requesting COD reopening where VA issued a letter or decision that failed to explicitly adjudicate the COD issue under `38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)` (*Hamill v. Collins*, `166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. 2026)`).

blocks.text: 2. Bitemporal Pathway Gate (Escaping the June 25, 2024 § 3.114(a) Floor)

Reopening a denied COD determination solely under the **June 25, 2024 liberalizing rule (`89 FR 32361`)** caps the earliest possible effective date at **June 25, 2024** (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(g)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)`). Always screen the **five retroactive pathways** in descending order of back-pay reach and lowest burden:

rows: **Unbroken Reenlistment / Unconditional Discharge Rescue** (`38 U.S.C. § 101(18)(B)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.13(a)–(c)`)
**YES** *(for all disabilities incurred/aggravated in the earlier completed period!)*
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive *(extant since Oct. 8, 1977 `Pub. L. 95-126`)*
**Date of original denied VA claim** via `§ 3.105(a)` / `§ 7111` **CUE** (or `§ 3.156(c)` if `DD-4` contracts were missing from C-file)!
**VA Insanity at Time of Offense** (`38 U.S.C. § 5303(b)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.354(a)–(b)`; `VAOPGCPREC 20-97`; *Newman* equipoise)
**YES — Eliminates ALL `(c)` statutory (including GCM & desertion!) and `(d)` regulatory bars**
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive *(de novo on Supplemental/STRs; CUE only if undebatable on closed record)*
**Original claim date** if proven via newly associated STRs/brig records (`§ 3.156(c)`), or date of Supplemental Claim (`§ 3.2500`).
**AMA Explicit-Notice Failure / Pending Claim** (`38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)`; *Hamill v. Collins*, `166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. 2026)`)
Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) *(keeps AMA claim non-final)*
**Date of the unaddressed AMA claim** (note: `§ 3.12(e)` liberalizing criteria still take effect June 25, 2024, while `§ 3.354(b)` / extant merits reach full claim date).
**BCMR (`§ 3.12(f)`): YES (all bars).** **Post-1977 DRB (`§ 3.12(h)`): `(d)` bars ONLY, NOT `(c)` statutory bars!**
Later of **date of DRB/BCMR application** or **1 yr prior to VA reopening** (`§ 5110(i)` / `§ 3.400(g)`)—**OR original VA claim** if factual record correction triggers `§ 3.156(c)` (*Spencer*)!
**Pre-2024 Regulatory Misapplication CUE** (*Cropper*; pre-2024 `§ 3.12(d)`) **vs. Post-June 25, 2024 Compelling Circumstances (`§ 3.12(e)`)**
**NO** (`§ 3.12(e)` applies **only** to `(c)(6)` 180-day AWOL & `(d)(2)` moral turpitude / willful & persistent)
Pre-2024 misapplication: CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive; **`89 FR 32361`: Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114)**
Pre-2024 CUE: prior decision date; **`§ 3.12(e)` liberalizing reopening: NO EARLIER THAN JUNE 25, 2024** (`§ 3.114(a)`).

blocks.text: 3. Proof Elements & Doctrinal Mechanics
A. Statutory Bars (§ 5303(a) / § 3.12(c)) vs. Regulatory Bars (§ 3.12(d)) & The 2024 Overhaul (89 FR 32361)

*(Link to verbatim text in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.12, 3.13, 3.354, 3.400(g), 3.6 & 3.301 (Character of Discharge Evolution, Insanity, Upgrades, ADT/IADT & Line of Duty)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.12-3.13-3.354-cod-insanity) and side-by-side comparison in [Part 3 Historical Diff: Character of Discharge Evolution (38 U.S.C. § 5303 & 38 C.F.R. § 3.12 Pre- vs. Post-June 25, 2024 Final Rule, 89 FR 32361)](/cfr/modules/character-of-discharge-3.12-evolution)).*

items:
**The Six Statutory Bars (`38 U.S.C. § 5303(a)` [`former § 3103(a)`]; `38 C.F.R. § 3.12(c)(1)–(6)`):**
• **`(c)(1)` Conscientious Objector:** Refused to perform military duty, wear the uniform, or comply with lawful orders. *(Non-waivable under `§ 3.12(e)`).*
• **`(c)(2)` Sentence of a General Court-Martial (`GCM`):** Absolute statutory bar unless overcome by `§ 3.13` prior period, `§ 3.354(b)` insanity, or `10 U.S.C. § 1552` BCMR upgrade (`§ 3.12(f)`).
• **CRITICAL `GCM` vs. `SPCM` Distinction:** A **Bad Conduct Discharge (`BCD`)** adjudged by a **Special Court-Martial (`SPCM`)** is **NOT** a statutory bar under `§ 5303(a)` / `§ 3.12(c)(2)`! An SPCM BCD must be adjudicated under the **regulatory bars of `§ 3.12(d)`**—meaning an SPCM BCD for drug possession or minor offenses **IS eligible for the `§ 3.12(e)` compelling-circumstances exception**! Whenever an RO summarily labels any `"BCD"` a `"statutory court-martial bar"` without pulling the Court-Martial Order (`SPCMO` vs. `GCMO`), reverse on HLR/appeal (or RO CUE if `SPCM` was on the face of the record)!
• **`(c)(3)` Officer Resignation for the Good of the Service:** Statutory bar applicable strictly to commissioned/warrant officers (e.g., `AR 600-8-24` resignation in lieu of GCM—enlisted `Ch. 10` discharges fall under regulatory `§ 3.12(d)(1)(i)` instead). *(Non-waivable under `§ 3.12(e)`).*
• **`(c)(4)` Deserter:** Requires affirmative military record proof of desertion (`10 U.S.C. § 885`—intent to remain away permanently or shirk hazardous/important service), not mere administrative "dropped from rolls" (`DFR`) shorthand without a desertion finding. *(Non-waivable under `§ 3.12(e)`).*
• **`(c)(5)` Alien During Hostilities:** Affirmatively shown that the alien requested release during hostilities (`§ 3.7(b)`). *(Non-waivable under `§ 3.12(e)`).*
• **`(c)(6)` Continuous AWOL `>= 180` Days Resulting in OTH (`38 U.S.C. § 5303(a)`):**
• **Strict Computation Rules:** The `180` days must be **continuous** (consecutive). **Exclude** authorized leave, periods after return to military control, travel time authorized upon apprehension/surrender, and **military or civilian confinement** (once apprehended into custody, the member is no longer AWOL). Two separate 110-day AWOLs separated by 3 days of military control equal `220` lost days in `DD-214` Block `29`—**but `0` continuous 180-day bars under `§ 3.12(c)(6)`**!
• **Compelling Circumstances Eligible (`§ 3.12(c)(6)(i)`):** Unlike `(c)(1)–(5)`, Congress expressly built a compelling-circumstances escape valve into `§ 5303(a)` for `180+`-day AWOL, now governed by **`§ 3.12(e)`**!

**Restructured Regulatory Bars (`38 C.F.R. § 3.12(d)(1)–(2)`, eff. June 25, 2024; Validity Upheld in *Garvey v. Wilkie*, `972 F.3d 1333 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`):**
• `89 FR 32361` eliminated the archaic *"homosexual acts involving aggravating circumstances"* bar (`former § 3.12(d)(5)`) and split remaining regulatory bars into two strict categories:
• **`§ 3.12(d)(1)` — Compelling Circumstances NOT Applicable:**
• **`(d)(1)(i)` Discharge in Lieu of Trial by GCM:** Acceptance of an OTH (or equivalent) discharge in lieu of trial by **General Court-Martial** (note: discharge in lieu of *Special* Court-Martial does **not** trigger `(d)(1)(i)`!).
• **`(d)(1)(ii)` Mutiny or Spying:** Mutiny or espionage.
• **`§ 3.12(d)(2)` — Compelling Circumstances (`§ 3.12(e)`) IS Applicable:**
• **`(d)(2)(i)` Offense Involving Moral Turpitude:** Clarified to include, generally, conviction of a **felony** (or civilian/UCMJ equivalent carrying `>1 year` confinement / dishonorable discharge).
• **`(d)(2)(ii)` Willful and Persistent Misconduct:** Replaced vague subjective standards with **bright-line temporal & *Manual for Courts-Martial* (`MCM`) thresholds**:
• *One-time isolated misconduct* is **never** "persistent" (preserving *Cropper v. Brown*, `6 Vet. App. 450 (1994)`).
• *"Minor misconduct"* means an offense whose maximum *MCM* sentence if tried by GCM would **not** include a dishonorable discharge or confinement `> 1 year`.
• Conduct is **"persistent"** ONLY if: `(A)` two+ instances of *minor* misconduct occur within **2 years** of each other; `(B)` an instance of *minor* misconduct occurs within **2 years** of *more serious* misconduct; or `(C)` two+ instances of *more serious* misconduct occur within **5 years** of each other.

blocks.text: B. Pathway 1 — Unbroken Reenlistment & Conditional Discharges (38 U.S.C. § 101(18)(B); 38 C.F.R. § 3.13(a)–(c))

Prior to 1979, and frequently in modern Navy/Army administrative practice, servicemembers who reenlisted early ("short-term discharge" to accept a new contract or commission) without a physical return to civilian life received **no `DD-214`** at the end of Contract #1. Years later, when the servicemember received an OTH or GCM BCD at the end of Contract #2, DoD issued **one consolidated `DD-214`** covering the entire multi-contract span with Block `24: Other Than Honorable`.

items:
**The Statutory Rescue (`38 U.S.C. § 101(18)(B)`, added by `Pub. L. 95-126`, Oct. 8, 1977; `38 C.F.R. § 3.13(c)`):**
• Even where no unconditional discharge certificate was issued (`§ 3.13(a)–(b)`), a servicemember **shall be considered to have been unconditionally discharged or released** from active service upon completing the period of service for which they were originally obligated (`§ 3.13(c)(1)`), where non-issuance resulted from an intervening enlistment/reenlistment (`§ 3.13(c)(2)`), and the member was eligible for a discharge under conditions other than dishonorable at that point (`§ 3.13(c)(3)`).
• Furthermore, in post-Vietnam peacetime/all-volunteer service (`§ 3.13(a)(3)`), an immediate discharge issued *to reenlist* when eligible for honorable separation is **already an unconditional honorable discharge** locking in the date of early reenlistment!

**Textbook CUE Weapon (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive):** Any disability incurred or aggravated during Enlistment #1 is **100% immune** from even a **General Court-Martial Dishonorable Discharge** in Enlistment #2! If `DD-214` Block `18` (*"Continuous Honorable Active Service..."*) or `DD Form 4` enlistment contracts were in the C-file when an RO or Board barred *all* active service, file **`38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a)` / `38 U.S.C. § 7111` CUE** (or, if `DD Form 4` contracts were never obtained by VA, submit them under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)`** [Playbook 03](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c) to capture the original claim effective date without the CUE standard!).

blocks.text: C. Pathway 2 — VA Insanity at Time of Offense (38 U.S.C. § 5303(b); 38 C.F.R. § 3.354(a)–(b))

Under `38 U.S.C. § 5303(b)` (`former § 3103(b)`) and `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.12(b), 3.354(b)`, if it is established to the satisfaction of the Secretary that the veteran was **insane** at the time of committing the offense(s) leading to the court-martial, discharge, or resignation, **every statutory bar (`§ 3.12(c)`, including GCM and desertion!) and every regulatory bar (`§ 3.12(d)`) is completely eliminated**.

items:
**VA's Broad, Non-Criminal Definition (`§ 3.354(a)` — *Zang*, *Gardner*, *Struck* & `VAOPGCPREC 20-97`):**
• VA insanity is **NOT** criminal *M'Naghten* / UCMJ Article `50a` lack-of-mental-responsibility, and a military court-martial's finding of mental competency to stand trial **does NOT bind VA**!
• Under ***Zang v. Brown*, 8 Vet. App. 246, 252–54 (1995)**, ***Struck v. Brown*, 9 Vet. App. 145, 152–54 (1996)**, and [`VAOPGCPREC 20-97`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index), a person is insane under `§ 3.354(a)` if, **due to a disease** (excluding constitutional psychopathic / pure personality disorder unless psychosis is engrafted, and excluding mere voluntary intoxication *absent* an underlying mental disease), the person:
• Exhibits *"a more or less prolonged deviation from his normal method of behavior"*; **OR**
• *"Interferes with the peace of society"*; **OR**
• *"Has so departed (become antisocial) from the accepted standards of the community to which by birth and education he belongs as to lack the adaptability to make further adjustment to the social customs of the community in which he resides."*
• **No Strict Direct-Causation Requirement (*Gardner v. Shinseki*, `22 Vet. App. 415, 419–21 (2009)`):** Overturning restrictive BVA practice, *Gardner* held that VA insanity is **markedly broader than the Model Penal Code**—*"due to disease"* modifies the *behavioral state* (`prolonged deviation`), **not** a criminal-law requirement that the mental disease directly compelled the specific criminal act, so long as the veteran was insane at the time of the misconduct leading to separation!

**Duty to Obtain All Procurable Records & Adequate Psychiatric Opinions (*Cropper*, *Stringham*):**
• Under `§ 3.354(b)`, VA must base its decision on *"all the evidence procurable relating to the period involved"* (including STRs, brig/stockade logs, pre-enlistment records showing baseline "normal method of behavior," and post-service VAMC notes), provide a medical nexus/insanity opinion applying `§ 3.354(a)` when reasonably raised, and state adequate reasons or bases (*Cropper v. Brown*, `6 Vet. App. 450, 452–54 (1994)`; *Stringham v. Brown*, `8 Vet. App. 445, 448–49 (1995)`). *(Note: Under Paulson v. Brown, 7 Vet. App. 466 (1995) and McKnight v. Gober, 131 F.3d 1483 (Fed. Cir. 1997), pre-VCAA notice/status hurdles historically tripped pro se claimants, whereas post-VCAA D'Amico overruling and 38 U.S.C. § 5103A mandate full VA record procurement on COD!).*

blocks.text: D. Pathway 3 — AMA Explicit-Notice Non-Finality (*Hamill v. Collins*, 166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. 2026))

As documented in [Procedural Vehicles for Piercing Finality](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality), the Federal Circuit's landmark opinion abolishing the implicit-denial doctrine under the AMA—***Hamill v. Collins*, 166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 4, 2026)**—**literally arose out of an unaddressed AMA request to reopen a Character of Discharge determination!**

items: Whenever a claimant submitted an AMA `VA Form 20-0995` or `21-526EZ` on or after **February 19, 2019** contesting or reopening a COD bar and VA issued an administrative letter or rating decision that failed to satisfy all explicit-notice elements of `38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)` on the COD issue, **the AMA COD claim never became final and remains legally pending**.

blocks.text: E. Pathway 4 — DRB (10 U.S.C. § 1553) vs. BCMR/BCNR (10 U.S.C. § 1552) Upgrades & Effective Dates

items:
**Forum & Liberal Consideration Selection (`DD Form 293` vs. `DD Form 149`):**
• **Discharge Review Board (`DRB`, `10 U.S.C. § 1553`, `DD Form 293`):** **15-year statute of limitations** from discharge; reviews propriety and equity (right to personal/video hearing); **cannot** upgrade a **General Court-Martial (`GCM`)** discharge (can review SPCM BCDs granted via clemency/administrative channels depending on branch rules, not GCM sentences).
• **Board for Correction of Military/Naval Records (`BCMR`/`BCNR`, `10 U.S.C. § 1552`, `DD Form 149`):** **3-year limit** from discovery of error/injustice, **routinely waived "in the interest of justice"**; full authority to upgrade **any** discharge (including setting aside/upgrading GCM characterizations via clemency, changing narrative reasons to **Medical Retirement (`Chapter 61`)**, or erasing AWOL lost-time entries!).
• **Mandatory Statutory & DoD "Liberal Consideration" (`10 U.S.C. §§ 1552(h), 1553(d)(3)`):** Leverage the four foundational DoD memoranda—**Hagel** (`Sept. 3, 2014`, PTSD), **Carson** (`Feb. 24, 2016`, TBI & *de novo* waivers), **Kurta** (`Aug. 25, 2017`, MST, sexual harassment, broader mental health, and civilian/post-service evidence sufficiency), and **Wilkie** (`July 25, 2018`, equity/clemency/rehabilitation)—now reinforced by statutory mandates requiring clinical/mental-health advisor review!

**THE `Pub. L. 95-126` UPGRADE TRAP (`§ 3.12(f)` `[former (e)]` vs. `§ 3.12(h)` `[former (g)]`):**
• **`BCMR`/`BCNR` Upgrade (`10 U.S.C. § 1552` -> `38 C.F.R. § 3.12(f)` `[former (e)]`):** An upgrade to **Honorable OR General (Under Honorable Conditions)** issued by a **`BCMR`/`BCNR`** is **final and conclusive on VA** and **sets aside BOTH `(c)` statutory bars AND `(d)` regulatory bars**!
• **Post-October 8, 1977 `DRB` Upgrade (`10 U.S.C. § 1553` -> `38 U.S.C. § 5303(e)(1)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.12(h)(1)–(3)` `[former (g)]`):** An Honorable or General discharge issued on or after October 8, 1977 by a **DRB** sets aside **`(d)` regulatory bars** (provided `(h)(1)–(3)` individual case review + uniform published standards are met, which modern standard DRBs satisfy—unlike 1977 Carter Special Discharge Review Program upgrades under `§ 3.12(i)` `[former (h)]`), **BUT DOES NOT SET ASIDE A `§ 3.12(c)` STATUTORY BAR!** Thus, if the veteran had **`180+` continuous days AWOL (`§ 3.12(c)(6)`)** or **desertion (`§ 3.12(c)(4)`)**, a DRB upgrade alone leaves the statutory bar standing unless counsel **(a) petitions the `BCMR`/`BCNR` under `10 U.S.C. § 1552` (`§ 3.12(f)`)**, **(b) proves `§ 3.12(e)` compelling circumstances** (for `(c)(6)` AWOL), or **(c) proves `§ 3.354(b)` insanity**!
• **The `10 U.S.C. § 874(b)` Clemency Trap ([`VAOPGCPREC 10-96`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index)):** A substituted administrative discharge granted as executive clemency by a Service Secretary under **`10 U.S.C. § 874(b)`** does **NOT** lift a `§ 5303(a)` **General Court-Martial** bar; you must obtain a **`10 U.S.C. § 1552` BCMR correction** (`§ 3.12(f)`) or establish `§ 3.354(b)` insanity!

**Effective Dates After Upgrade (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(i)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.400(g)` vs. `§ 3.156(c)` *Spencer*):**
• **Standard Upgrade Rule (`§ 5110(i)`; `§ 3.400(g)`):** Where VA entitlement arises *because of* a `10 U.S.C. § 1552` or `§ 1553` discharge upgrade, the effective date is the **latest** of: `(1)` **the date the application for upgrade/correction was filed with the service department**, `(2)` the date VA received a previously disallowed claim, or `(3)` **1 year prior to the date of reopening** of the disallowed VA claim! *(Practice Imperative: **Always file a VA claim / Supplemental Claim within 1 year of the DRB/BCMR upgrade decision**—otherwise the `(3)` 1-year lookback forfeits the entire multi-year DRB/BCMR processing period!)*
• **Super-Retroactive `§ 3.156(c)` Override (*Spencer v. West*, `13 Vet. App. 376 (2000)`):** If the BCMR did not merely grant equitable clemency on character of discharge, but **corrected underlying military facts** (e.g., voided an unlawful separation to grant constructive active duty as in *Spencer*, expunged erroneous AWOL days, or issued a `DD-215` corroborating combat/MST stressors) alongside newly associated OMPF records, invoke **`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)`** ([Playbook 03](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c)) to demand the **original VA claim effective date**!

blocks.text: 4. Invariants / Kill-Switches

items: **The `June 25, 2024` `89 FR 32361` Non-Retroactivity & *George* CUE Bar:** Never plead CUE (`§ 3.105(a)` / `§ 7111`; see [`Board CUE Pre-Filing Gate`](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate)) against a pre-June 25, 2024 final COD decision by citing the 2024 `§ 3.12(d)(2)` 2-year/5-year misconduct metrics or `§ 3.12(e)` compelling circumstances (*George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)`; `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`). Pre-2024 CUE requires proving undebatable error under **pre-2024 law** (e.g., ignoring `§ 3.13` prior honorable service, miscounting non-continuous AWOL, mislabeling an SPCM BCD as a GCM bar, or treating a single isolated minor infraction as "persistent" contrary to *Cropper*).

**Non-Waivable Bars Under `§ 3.12(e)`:** `§ 3.12(e)` compelling circumstances **cannot** waive `§ 3.12(c)(1)–(5)` (conscientious objector, GCM, officer resignation for good of service, deserter, alien release) or `§ 3.12(d)(1)(i)–(ii)` (OTH in lieu of GCM, mutiny/spying). Pivot immediately to **`§ 3.13` prior enlistment**, **`§ 3.354(b)` insanity**, or **`10 U.S.C. § 1552` BCMR upgrade (`§ 3.12(f)`)**.

**Pure Personality Disorder / Standalone Voluntary Intoxication Exclusion (`§ 3.354(a)`):** Under *Zang*, *Struck*, and `VAOPGCPREC 20-97`, antisocial/borderline personality disorder alone—or acute voluntary intoxication without an underlying Axis I/organic mental disease—cannot establish `§ 3.354(b)` insanity (though **substance use disorder (`SUD`), ADHD, and impulsive behavior DO qualify as `§ 3.12(e)(2)(i)` compelling circumstances** on post-June 25, 2024 COD claims!).

**Uncharacterized Entry-Level Separations (`§ 3.12(l)` `[former (k)]`):** For separations initiated `>= Oct. 1, 1982`, an **Entry Level Separation (`ELS`, `<180` days)** is treated as **under conditions other than dishonorable** (`§ 3.12(l)(1)`)! Only *Void Enlistments* (`§ 3.14`) or *Dropped From Rolls* (`§ 3.12(l)(2)–(3)`) require special scrutiny (and watch `24-month` minimum-active-duty rules under `38 U.S.C. § 5303A` / `38 C.F.R. § 3.12a`, which **exempt** any veteran discharged for a disability incurred/aggravated in line of duty OR holding a compensable SC disability!).

blocks.text: 5. Postconditions: Chapter 17 Healthcare Carve-Outs, Effective Dates & Fees

items:
**Immediate Chapter 17 VHA Healthcare Access (Even While Compensation COD Is Denied or Pending!):**
• **`38 U.S.C. § 1720D` (MST Care):** Free VHA counseling and medical/mental treatment for **any** physical or mental condition related to **Military Sexual Trauma (`MST`)**, **frequently available regardless of OTH/BCD character of discharge or `§ 5303A` length of service**!
• **`38 U.S.C. § 1720I` (Mental & Behavioral Health for OTH Veterans):** Urgent and ongoing VHA mental/behavioral healthcare for former servicemembers with an **OTH** administrative discharge (excluding GCM or statutory bars) who served `>100` active days and either deployed to a combat theater/hostile-fire area, operated unmanned aerial vehicles in combat, or experienced sexual assault/harassment.
• **`38 U.S.C. § 1702` (`former § 602` Psychosis / Mental Illness Presumption), `§ 1710(e)` Toxic-Exposure Care & `38 C.F.R. § 3.360` (`Pub. L. 95-126, § 2`):** `§ 1702` presumes service connection **for Chapter 17 medical treatment purposes** if a veteran of wartime/Persian Gulf service develops an active psychosis (or post-Gulf War mental illness) within **2 years after discharge** (and before statutory end dates). Moreover, under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.360`**, even when a `§ 3.12(d)` regulatory bar blocks *monetary compensation*, VA **must** still authorize **Chapter 17 healthcare** for disabilities incurred or aggravated in line of duty during active service (`38 U.S.C. § 5303(a)` statutory bars and BCDs block `§ 3.360` care unless `§ 1720D`, `§ 1720J` acute suicidal crisis stabilization, or `§ 3.354(b)` insanity applies!).
• **`38 C.F.R. § 17.34` Tentative Eligibility:** Authorizes immediate emergent/provisional VHA mental and medical care while a formal VBA COD determination is pending!

**Effective-Date & Ancillary Audit Upon Winning COD:**
• Verify the RO did not reflexively assign **June 25, 2024** (`§ 3.114(a)`) if entitlement was independently established via **`§ 3.13` prior honorable period**, **`§ 3.354(b)` insanity**, **`§ 3.400(g)` DRB/BCMR application date**, **`§ 3.156(c)` newly associated OMPF/STRs**, or **`§ 5104(b)` *Hamill* pending AMA status**.
• Audit restoration of **Chapter 31 VR&E**, **Chapter 33 GI Bill** *(note: `38 U.S.C. §§ 3011, 3311` strictly require a **full `"Honorable"`** discharge—neither a `General` discharge nor a VA `§ 3.12` COD grant unlocks GI Bill without a DRB/BCMR upgrade to full **Honorable**, unless `§ 3.13` establishes a prior unconditional Honorable period!)*, **Chapter 37 VA Home Loan**, and **`Chapter 61` / `CRSC` ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc))**.

**Attorney Fees (`38 U.S.C. § 5904` vs. Pro Bono / Hourly DRB-BCMR Rules):**
• A prior VA administrative decision denying benefits on COD grounds constitutes an **initial AOJ decision** under `38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(1)`—meaning `20%–33.3%` contingency fees attach immediately upon filing a `VA Form 20-0995` Supplemental Claim, `20-0996` HLR, `10182` Board appeal, or CUE motion before VA!
• Separate **Title 10 DRB/BCMR** petitions (`10 U.S.C. §§ 1552, 1553`) are *not* governed by Title 38 `§ 5904(d)` VA direct-pay withholding; structure engagement agreements cleanly to separate Title 10 military-board work from Title 38 VA representation, and offset any CAVC `EAJA` (`28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)`) award dollar-for-dollar against `§ 5904` fees for the same appellate work ([Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Less-Than-Honorable Discharges (OTH & BCD): Prior Honorable Enlistments (§ 3.13), June 2024 Compelling Circumstances (§ 3.12), Mental Health 'Insanity' (§ 3.354) & Military Upgrades
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Having an Other Than Honorable (OTH), Undesirable, Bad Conduct (BCD), or Uncharacterized separation on your DD-214 does NOT automatically lock you out of VA disability compensation or health care. First, if you completed an earlier enlistment honorably and immediately reenlisted without a break in service, 38 C.F.R. § 3.13 protects benefits earned during that earlier period regardless of how your final enlistment ended! Second, effective June 25, 2024 (89 FR 32361), VA overhauled 38 C.F.R. § 3.12—expanding the 'compelling circumstances' exception (§ 3.12(e), weighing combat hardship, PTSD/TBI/MST, age, and length of service) to cover prolonged AWOL and regulatory misconduct bars. Third, under 38 U.S.C. § 5303(b) and 38 C.F.R. § 3.354(b), VA uses a broad, non-criminal medical definition of 'insanity' due to disease (such as severe PTSD, bipolar disorder, psychosis, or TBI) that lifts even General Court-Martial bars—and Chapter 17 mental health care (§§ 1720D MST, 1720I OTH mental health) can be available immediately.
record_clues: DD-214 Block 18 ('Remarks') noting 'Immediate Reenlistment' or 'Continuous Honorable Active Service From [Date]'—showing you completed an earlier enlistment before the enlistment that ended in an OTH or BCD (§ 3.13).

DD-214 Block 24 showing an OTH or a Special Court-Martial (SPCM) Bad Conduct Discharge—often misread as a General Court-Martial bar—or an AWOL count near 180 days that mistakenly counted confinement or authorized leave.

Service medical records, stockade/brig notes, Article 15 packets, or post-service psychiatric records showing untreated PTSD, TBI, Military Sexual Trauma (MST), depression, bipolar disorder, or psychosis when the in-service misconduct occurred.
A Discharge Review Board (DRB, DD Form 293) or Board for Correction of Military/Naval Records (BCMR/BCNR, DD Form 149) upgrade decision.
important_cautions: June 25, 2024 Effective-Date Floor (89 FR 32361): VA published the revised Character of Discharge rule on April 26, 2024, taking effect June 25, 2024 (note: VA rejected and never enacted an earlier July 10, 2020 proposed standalone moral-turpitude definition at 85 FR 41471). Reopening an old denial solely under the liberalized 2024 rule cannot carry a compensation effective date earlier than June 25, 2024 (§ 3.114(a)), nor can the 2024 rule prove CUE in a pre-June 25, 2024 final decision.

Bars Where 'Compelling Circumstances' (§ 3.12(e)) Does Not Apply: Section 3.12(e) applies to prolonged AWOL (180+ continuous days) and moral-turpitude / willful-and-persistent misconduct bars, NOT to a General Court-Martial sentence (§ 3.12(c)(2)) or an OTH discharge accepted in lieu of a General Court-Martial (§ 3.12(d)(1)(i))—those require § 3.13 prior-enlistment protection, § 3.354(b) insanity, or a 10 U.S.C. § 1552 BCMR/BCNR correction.

DRB vs. BCMR/BCNR Upgrade Power After 1977: Under Pub. L. 95-126 and § 3.12(f)–(h), a post-October 8, 1977 Discharge Review Board (DRB) upgrade does not automatically override a statutory § 3.12(c) bar (like 180+ days continuous AWOL), whereas a full BCMR/BCNR correction under 10 U.S.C. § 1552 does.

Insanity Exclusion for Pure Personality Disorders / Voluntary Intoxication: Under § 3.354(a) and VAOPGCPREC 20-97, VA's insanity exception requires behavior caused by an actual disease or injury—not a standalone personality disorder or simple voluntary intoxication unconnected to an underlying mental disease.
questions_for_representative: Does my Official Military Personnel File (OMPF) or DD-214 Block 18 show an earlier completed enlistment before an immediate reenlistment that already qualifies me as a Veteran under 38 C.F.R. § 3.13?
Can I file a Supplemental Claim (VA Form 20-0995) to have my OTH or Special Court-Martial discharge reviewed under the June 25, 2024 'compelling circumstances' factors in 38 C.F.R. § 3.12(e)?

If my discharge involved a General Court-Martial or OTH in lieu of General Court-Martial, do my psychiatric or TBI records support the 38 C.F.R. § 3.354(b) insanity exception or a parallel BCMR/BCNR petition (DD Form 149)?
While we work on compensation eligibility, can I enroll right now for VA MST counseling (§ 1720D), OTH mental/behavioral health care (§ 1720I), or Chapter 17 health care (§ 3.360)?

blocks.text: National Guard and Reserve claims fail at the Regional Office (`AOJ`) far more often than Regular Component claims—not because entitlement is absent, but because raters misread **`NGB Form 22`** state separation summaries as proof of *"zero active service,"* conflate **`Title 32` full-time operational Guard duty (`32 U.S.C. § 502(f)`)** with non-federal **State Active Duty (`SAD`)**, overlook favorable binding **Line of Duty (`LOD`)** determinations (`38 C.F.R. § 3.1(m)`), or unlawfully reject secondary alcohol/drug-related organ damage caused by service-connected PTSD or chronic pain (*Allen v. Principi*, `237 F.3d 1368 (Fed. Cir. 2001)`).

lines: **Pair With COD Screening & `§ 3.156(c)` Reconsideration:** Whenever a Guard/Reserve file also involves an `OTH`/`BCD` or multi-period active/reserve service, run [Playbook 10](/playbooks/10-character-of-discharge-insanity-upgrades), [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.12, 3.13, 3.354, 3.400(g), 3.6 & 3.301 (Character of Discharge Evolution, Insanity, Upgrades, ADT/IADT & Line of Duty)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.12-3.13-3.354-cod-insanity), [Part 3 Historical Diff: Character of Discharge Evolution (38 U.S.C. § 5303 & 38 C.F.R. § 3.12 Pre- vs. Post-June 25, 2024 Final Rule, 89 FR 32361)](/cfr/modules/character-of-discharge-3.12-evolution), and the [`COD & Guard/Reserve Intake Audit`](/checklists/cod-and-guard-reserve-intake-audit). Crucially, because Guard/Reserve unit orders and `LOD` packets are notoriously absent from initial VA STR pulls, **associating missing `LOD` or `Title 32` orders decades later triggers `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)` reconsideration** back to the original denied claim ([Playbook 03](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c))!

blocks.text: 1. Preconditions: The NGB-22 C-File Trap & Guard/Reserve Record Triggers

Before evaluating the medical merits of any Guard or Reserve claim, audit the VBMS eFolder against the member's state Adjutant General (`TAG`) / Reserve Personnel Center (`ARPC`, `HQ RIO`, `PERS-9`, `CG PSC`) holdings ([VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon)):

items:
**The Classic `NGB Form 22` C-File Trap:**
• **`NGB Form 22`** (*Report of Separation and Record of Service*) documents **only termination from a state National Guard enlistment**—it is **NOT** a federal `DD Form 214` and frequently omits individual `ADT` school tours, `Title 32 § 502(f)` operational orders, `IADT` drill injuries, and short `Title 10` call-ups!
• Whenever a prior VA denial states *"No qualifying active duty shown on NGB-22,"* immediately FOIA/request:
• All **`DD Form 214`s** (issued for `IADT`/`AIT` basic training `>= 90` days, `Title 10` federal mobilizations, and `>= 90`-day `Title 32` active-duty tours);
• Complete **`Title 10` (`10 U.S.C. §§ 12301–12304`)** and **`Title 32` (`32 U.S.C. §§ 316, 502–505`)** movement/activation orders, travel vouchers (`DD Form 1351-2`), and **Retirement Point Accounting (`NGB Form 23` / `ARPC Form 249-2-E` / `LES` pay stubs)** proving exact `ADT` vs. `IADT` drill dates; and
• Formal and informal **Line of Duty (`LOD`) Investigation Packets**: Army **`DA Form 2173`** (*Statement of Medical Examination and Duty Status*), Air Force **`AF Form 348`**, DoD formal **`DD Form 261`** (*Report of Investigation — Line of Duty and Misconduct Status*), or Navy/USMC **`JAGMAN` LOD** endorsements, plus civilian emergency room transport records from drill weekends!

**Line-of-Duty & Substance-Use Red Flags:**
• Any post-October 31, 1990 denial citing `38 U.S.C. § 105(a)` or `38 C.F.R. § 3.301(d)` (*"alcohol/drug abuse is willful misconduct"*) where the veteran **already held (or simultaneously established) service connection** for PTSD, major depression, TBI, MST, or chronic orthopedic/neuropathic pain!

blocks.text: 2. Bitemporal Pathway Gate (Lowest-Burden Vehicle First)

Sequence Guard/Reserve and Line-of-Duty pathways to bypass `§ 1111` soundness traps and *George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` CUE bars ([Procedural Vehicles Piercing Finality](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality)):

rows: **Newly Associated `LOD` Reports, `Title 10`/`32` Orders, or Guard STRs** (`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)`; *Vigil*; *Emerson*)
CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive *(bypasses CUE & George bars)*
**Relates all the way back to the original denied VA claim** ([Playbook 03](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c)) even if contemporary nexus opinion is added!
**Favorable In-File `LOD` Ignored by RO/BVA** (`38 C.F.R. § 3.1(m)–(n)`; `§ 3.105(a)` / `§ 7111` CUE)
Undebatable error ignoring a favorable `DA Form 2173` / `AF Form 348` / `DD Form 261` already in C-file
**Original denied claim effective date** via RO/Board CUE (`§ 3.1(m)` makes favorable military LOD **binding** on VA!).
**PACT Act Toxic Exposure (`TERA` / `§ 1119` / `§ 1120`) for Guard/Reserve** (`38 U.S.C. §§ 1119, 1168`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.320`)
Presumptive deployment (`Title 10`) OR documented `TERA` participation during `Active Duty` / `ADT` / `IADT` (`§ 1168` nexus exam)
Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114) *(eff. Aug. 10, 2022, unless paired with `§ 3.156(c)` unit logs!)*
Up to **Aug. 10, 2022** (`§ 3.114(a)`)—or **original claim date** if newly associated Guard exposure/maintenance logs trigger `§ 3.156(c)` (*Emerson*)!
**Secondary Substance Abuse & Organ Sequelae** (*Allen v. Principi*, `237 F.3d 1368 (Fed. Cir. 2001)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.310(a)–(b)`)
**Equipoise (`§ 5107(b)`)** medical nexus proving SC mental/physical condition caused or aggravated SUD & organ damage
Open/Supplemental: CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive; **1999–2001 CUE: Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) (`VAOPGCPREC 7-99`)**
Date of Supplemental/open claim (or CUE **only** if final post-*Allen* decision ignored undisputed secondary nexus without weighing).

blocks.text: 3. Proof Elements & Doctrinal Mechanics
A. The Three-Tier Duty Matrix (38 U.S.C. §§ 101(21)–(24), 106(d); 38 C.F.R. § 3.6(a)–(e))

Under `38 U.S.C. § 101(2)` and `§ 101(24)` (see [Three-Era Title 38 Statutory Crosswalk](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk)), *"active military, naval, air, or space service"* encompasses **three distinct tiers** with dramatically different disease, injury, and presumption rules:

rows: Regular Component full-time duty; **Reserve/Guard `Title 10` federal call-up** (`10 U.S.C. §§ 12301–12304`, *excluding* training-only orders); **AGR (`Title 10`)**; Academy cadets/midshipmen.
**Injury OR Disease** incurred or aggravated in line of duty + full `§ 3.309` / PACT presumptions (subject to minimum service days).
**YES (`§ 1111` & *Wagner*)** — VA must prove *both* preexistence AND non-aggravation by clear & unmistakable evidence!
Covered round-the-clock (`24/7`) from induction to separation (unless AWOL/confined under `§ 3.1(m)`).
**Tier 2: `Active Duty for Training (ADT / ACDUTRA)`** (`38 U.S.C. §§ 101(22), 101(24)(B)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.6(c)`)

Reserve `AT` (2-week annual training), **`IADT`/`AIT` basic/initial skill schools**, service schools, and **National Guard full-time `Title 32 U.S.C. §§ 316, 502, 503, 504, 505` duty** (`§ 3.6(c)(3)`), including **`Title 32 § 502(f)`** operational missions & `Title 32 AGR`!
**Injury OR Disease** incurred or aggravated in line of duty during the `ADT` window.
**NO (`Biggins`; `Paulson`; `Smith`)!** Claimant must first prove `§ 101(24)` veteran status by proving in-`ADT` incurrence or `§ 3.306` aggravation!
**YES (`§ 3.6(e)`)** — Authorized direct travel to/from `ADT` covers **injury** OR acute MI, cardiac arrest, or stroke!

Weekend drills / Battle Assemblies (`37 U.S.C. § 206`), unit training assemblies (`UTA`s), prescribed additional training/flight drills, and **National Guard `32 U.S.C. §§ 316, 502–505` drills**. *(Excludes work/study in connection with correspondence courses & muster duty).*

**STRICTLY:** **(1) `"Injury"`** incurred/aggravated in line of duty, **OR (2) Acute myocardial infarction, cardiac arrest, or cerebrovascular accident (`stroke`)** (`§§ 101(24)(C), 106(d)`, `§ 3.6(a)(3), (e)(3)`, eff. Nov. 1, 2000). **NO general chronic disease!**
**NO** — Claimant bears burden of proving in-`IADT` injury (or `§ 101(24)(C)`/`§ 106(d)` cardiac/stroke event) or aggravation.
**YES (`§ 3.6(e)(1)–(3)`)** — Authorized direct travel to/from `IADT` covers **injury** OR acute MI, cardiac arrest, or stroke!

blocks.text: Critical Doctrinal Nuances Inside the Duty Matrix:

items:
**The `ADT` Presumption-of-Soundness Catch-22 (*Biggins*, *Paulson*, *Smith*, *Donnellan* & *Acciola*):**
• Because `38 U.S.C. § 1111` grants the presumption of soundness only to a *"veteran,"* and a Guard/Reserve member with **pure `ADT` service** becomes a *"veteran"` under `38 U.S.C. §§ 101(2), 101(24)(B)` **only if disabled by an injury or disease incurred or aggravated during `ADT`**, the CAVC holds that **`§ 1111` soundness does NOT apply to `ADT` claims unless veteran status is first independently established** (*Biggins v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 474, 477–78 (1991)`; *Paulson v. Brown*, `7 Vet. App. 466, 469–70 (1995)`; *Acciola v. Peake*, `22 Vet. App. 320, 324 (2008)`; *Smith v. Shinseki*, `24 Vet. App. 40, 46–48 (2010)`).
• **The Aggravation Trap (*Donnellan v. Shinseki*, `24 Vet. App. 167, 173–75 (2010)`):** For a preexisting condition claimed as aggravated during `ADT` (`38 U.S.C. § 1153`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.306(a)`), the claimant cannot rely on `§ 3.306(b)`'s clear-and-unmistakable rebuttal shield; instead, **the claimant must affirmatively prove** (under standard equipoise `§ 5107(b)`) **permanent worsening during `ADT` beyond natural progression** (not a mere temporary flare-up of symptoms!).
• **Practitioner Escape Hatch:** Always check whether the client **also** had a separate period of **Tier 1 `Title 10` Active Duty**! Once a claimant establishes `ADT` incurrence/aggravation (or analyzes a Tier 1 `Title 10` tour), full `§ 1111` *Wagner v. Principi*, `370 F.3d 1089 (Fed. Cir. 2004)` protections attach to every Tier 1 `Active Duty` period!

**`IADT` Cardiac/Stroke Expansion (`Pub. L. 106-419, § 301`, eff. Nov. 1, 2000; `38 U.S.C. §§ 101(24)(C), 106(d)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.6(a)(3), (e)(2)–(3)`):**
• Prior to November 1, 2000 (`66 FR 48558, 48560`, Sept. 21, 2001; `67 FR 49584, 49585`, July 31, 2002), a Guardsman who suffered a massive heart attack or stroke during a drill PT test was denied because atherosclerotic heart/cerebrovascular disease was classified as a `"disease"` rather than an `"injury."` Under `38 U.S.C. §§ 101(24)(C), 106(d)(1), (4)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.6(a)(3), (e)(2)–(3)`, **acute myocardial infarction, cardiac arrest, and cerebrovascular accident (`stroke`)** occurring during `IADT` (or portal-to-portal travel) are statutorily compensable!
• **Framing Orthopedic, Acoustic, Assault (`MST`), & Toxic Traumas on `IADT` as `"Injury"`:** Remember that under `§ 3.6(a)(3)` and `(d)`, physical trauma, **acoustic trauma / noise-induced sensorineural damage**, heatstroke/frostbite, lightning/electrical shock, **Military Sexual Trauma (`MST` physical/sexual assault — `M21-1` recognizes personal/sexual assault trauma during `IADT` as an `"injury"` causing PTSD!)**, and acute chemical/toxic cellular trauma (e.g., *C-123* Agent Orange reserve aircrew `38 C.F.R. § 3.307(a)(6)(v)`) can establish an in-`IADT` **"injury"**!

**Portal-to-Portal Direct Travel Rules (`38 U.S.C. § 106(d)(1)–(4)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.6(e)(1)–(3)`):**
• Covers injury (or `§ 3.6(e)(3)` `"covered disease"`: acute MI / cardiac arrest / stroke) incurred **while proceeding directly to or returning directly from** authorized/required `ADT` or `IADT` (`§ 3.6(e)(1)–(2)`).
• Under **`38 U.S.C. § 106(d)(2)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.6(e)(2)`**, VA weighs six factors: `(i)` hour of departure, `(ii)` scheduled arrival/release hour, `(iii)` mode of travel, `(iv)` itinerary (no major personal detours/frolics!), `(v)` manner of travel, and `(vi)` immediate cause of disability/death. **Statutory Burden Warning (`38 U.S.C. § 106(d)(3)`):** Unlike regular in-camp LOD presumptions, **`38 U.S.C. § 106(d)(3)` places the affirmative burden of proof on the claimant** in portal-to-portal travel claims—document exact Google Maps route miles, drill schedule sign-in/out rosters, and police crash timestamps!

blocks.text: B. National Guard Title 10 vs. Title 32 (§ 502(f)) vs. State Active Duty (SAD) & The PACT Act

items:
**Decoding the Three National Guard Authorities:**
• **Federal Mobilization (`Title 10 U.S.C. §§ 12301(a), 12302, 12304`):** Federalized **Tier 1 `Active Duty`** (`§ 3.6(b)`). Confers full veteran status, `DD-214`, `§ 1111` presumption of soundness, and overseas `§ 1119` / `§ 1120` Gulf War / post-9/11 burn-pit presumptions.
• **Full-Time National Guard Duty (`Title 32 U.S.C. §§ 316, 502, 503, 504, 505`):** Federally funded duty under state Governor command—classified by **`38 U.S.C. § 101(22)(C)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.6(c)(3)` as Tier 2 `Active Duty for Training (ADT)`** (even when operational rather than classroom training!).
• **`32 U.S.C. § 502(f)` Operational Missions:** Post-9/11 airport security (`Operation Noble Eagle`), Southwest Border missions, FEMA hurricane/disaster response (Katrina, Maria), DC Capitol security, and **2020–2022 COVID-19 pandemic response** were overwhelmingly executed on **`Title 32 U.S.C. § 502(f)`** orders! Raters who mistake `§ 502(f)` orders for "State Active Duty" commit clear legal error—**both injuries AND diseases** (including severe COVID-19 residuals, orthopedic injuries, and PTSD) incurred or aggravated on `Title 32 § 502(f)` orders establish full service connection (`§ 3.6(c)(3)`)! *(Also check `38 C.F.R. § 3.7(o)` for Guard service where a disability was incurred).*
• **Pure State Active Duty (`SAD`):** Activated strictly by a state Governor under **state law and 100% state funds** (e.g., local blizzard/riot call-up not converted to federal `Title 32 § 502(f)` FEMA reimbursement). **Not** qualifying federal service under Title 38 (remedy lies in state workers' compensation)—**always verify whether FEMA/DoD retroactively converted initial `SAD` orders into `Title 32 § 502(f)` orders** (as happened nationwide in March 2020 for COVID-19!).

**PACT Act (`Pub. L. 117-168`) Toxic Exposure Expansions for Guard & Reserve (`38 U.S.C. §§ 1119, 1168`):**
• **Presumptive Burn-Pit / Herbicide Deployments (`§§ 1116, 1119, 1120`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.320`):** Guard/Reserve units deployed on `Title 10` (or qualifying `ADT` in covered Thailand/Guam/Johnston Atoll/SW Asia/Djibouti airspace or waters) receive identical `23+` burn-pit and expanded herbicide presumptions ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc)).
• **Toxic Exposure Risk Activity (`TERA`) Participation (`38 U.S.C. § 1168`):** Section `303` of the PACT Act expanded `TERA` lookup (` DoD ILER` Individual Longitudinal Exposure Record) to Guard and Reserve members who were exposed to PFAS firefighting foam (`AFFF`) at Guard airbases, jet fuel (`JP-8`), solvents (`TCE`), depleted uranium, burn pits, or radiation during **`Active Duty`, `ADT`, or `IADT`**, mandating a `§ 1168` VA toxic-exposure medical nexus opinion when disability + `TERA` participation are shown (while still respecting `§ 3.6(d)` `IADT` injury vs. `ADT` injury/disease thresholds!).

blocks.text: C. Line of Duty (38 U.S.C. § 105(a); 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.1(m)–(n), 3.301) & Secondary Substance Abuse (*Allen v. Principi*)

items:
**Asymmetric Binding Force of Service-Department `LOD` Determinations (`38 C.F.R. § 3.1(m)–(n)`):**
• **Presumption of Line of Duty (`38 U.S.C. § 105(a)`):** Every injury or disease incurred during active military, naval, air, or space service is **presumed** to have been incurred in line of duty unless caused by the veteran's own **willful misconduct** or (for claims filed after October 31, 1990) **abuse of alcohol or drugs**, or incurred while deserting / materially AWOL (`§ 3.1(m)(1)`) or confined under court-martial/civil sentence (`§ 3.1(m)(2)`).
• **THE ASYMMETRIC BINDING RULE (`§ 3.1(m)` & `§ 3.1(n)` — Massive Litigation Weapon!):**
• **Favorable Military `LOD` BINDS VA:** Under the plain text of `38 C.F.R. § 3.1(m)` and `§ 3.1(n)`, a service-department finding that an injury, disease, or death **occurred `"in line of duty"`** (or was **not** due to misconduct) ***"will be binding on the Department of Veterans Affairs unless it is patently inconsistent with the requirements of laws administered by the Department of Veterans Affairs"*** (e.g., where the military found `"In LOD"` despite undisputed `0.22` BAC single-car intoxication prohibited by `38 U.S.C. § 105(a)`). Ignoring a valid favorable `DA Form 2173` or `AF Form 348` in the C-file is **CUE**!
• **Unfavorable Military `"Not in LOD"` Does NOT Bind VA:** Notice the one-way wording of `§ 3.1(m)–(n)`! If a Guard commander summarily checked `"Not in Line of Duty"` (or failed to complete an `LOD` packet at all), VA is **NOT** bound by that adverse/missing finding and **must** independently adjudicate line of duty under `38 U.S.C. § 105(a)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.301`!

**Willful Misconduct vs. The Complete Bitemporal History of Substance-Abuse Claims (`1944–Present`):**
• **General Willful Misconduct (`§ 3.1(n)(1)–(3)`; `§ 3.301(a)–(c)`):** Requires deliberate or intentional wrongdoing with knowledge of—or **wanton and reckless disregard** of—its probable consequences, which is the **proximate cause** of the injury (`§ 3.1(n)(3)`). Mere negligence, carelessness, poor judgment, or technical violation of traffic/police ordinances (`§ 3.1(n)(2)`) is **NOT** willful misconduct! Simple drinking of alcohol is not willful misconduct unless acute intoxication proximately and immediately causes the accident (`§ 3.301(c)(2)`).
• **Era 1 (`Pre-November 1, 1990` Claims):** Under `former § 3.301(c)(2)`, while *primary* alcoholism was treated as misconduct for standalone ratings (*Traynor v. Turnage*, `485 U.S. 535 (1988)`), **organic diseases resulting from chronic use of alcohol** (e.g., alcoholic cirrhosis incurred in service!) were expressly **compensable** (`"will not be considered of willful misconduct origin"`) on claims filed **on or before October 31, 1990**!
• **Era 2 (`November 1, 1990` `OBRA 1990` Bar — `Pub. L. 101-508, § 8052`):** Effective for **claims filed after October 31, 1990**, Congress amended `38 U.S.C. §§ 105(a), 1110, 1131` (implemented at `38 C.F.R. § 3.301(d)`, `60 FR 27407, 27408`, May 24, 1995; gender-neutral wording update at `87 FR 26125`, May 3, 2022) to bar line-of-duty / direct service connection for **primary** abuse of alcohol or drugs (and organic diseases caused by *primary* voluntary substance abuse). *(Note: `66 FR 18195, 18198` [Apr. 6, 2001] added the `§ 3.300(c)` tobacco cross-reference to `§ 3.310(a)`, while `71 FR 44913, 44918` [Aug. 8, 2006] was an unrelated omnibus rulemaking that did not amend `§ 3.301` or `§ 3.310`).*
• **Era 3 (`1999–2001` Overreach & *Allen v. Principi* Breakthrough):**
• In [`VAOPGCPREC 7-99`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index) (`June 9, 1999`), VA OGC unlawfully overextended `OBRA 1990` to bar **secondary** service connection even when service-connected PTSD caused alcohol abuse and fatal cirrhosis.
• In ***Allen v. Principi*, `237 F.3d 1368, 1376–81 (Fed. Cir. 2001)`**, *reh'g denied*, `268 F.3d 1340`, the Federal Circuit **invalidated `VAOPGCPREC 7-99` in core part**, holding that `38 U.S.C. § 1110` precludes compensation **only** for willful-misconduct / **primary** alcohol or drug abuse—it **does NOT bar compensation when alcohol or drug abuse is a secondary disability (or symptom) proximately caused or aggravated (`Allen v. Brown`, `7 Vet. App. 439 (1995) (en banc)`) by a service-connected mental or physical condition under `38 C.F.R. § 3.310(a)–(b)`** (`71 FR 52744`, pub. Sept. 7, 2006, eff. Oct. 10, 2006)!
• **How to Plead *Allen v. Principi* Secondary Substance-Use Chains Today:**
• **Mental-Disorder Rating Incorporation:** Where an SC mental disorder (`PTSD`, `MDD`, `TBI`) causes self-medication (`Alcohol Use Disorder` / `Opioid Use Disorder`), the substance use disorder cannot be rated separately from the mental disorder (`§ 4.130` pyramiding rule), **but its occupational/social impairment merges directly into a higher `70%` or `100%` `§ 4.130` evaluation**!
• **High-Value Physical Organ & Intermediate-Step Chains (`§ 3.310(a)–(b)`):** Once medical nexus evidence shows an SC condition (`PTSD`, `anxiety`, **or chronic intractable SC spine/radiculopathy pain!**) caused or aggravated alcohol, opioid, or nicotine dependence (`38 C.F.R. § 3.300(b)` for secondary tobacco claims!), **every resulting physical organ disability is separately compensable**, including:
• **Alcoholic cirrhosis / chronic liver disease / portal hypertension / hepatocellular carcinoma**;
• **Chronic pancreatitis & secondary diabetes mellitus**;
• **Alcoholic cardiomyopathy, atrial fibrillation, & hypertension**;
• **Alcoholic peripheral neuropathy & cerebellar ataxia**;
• **Obesity / weight-gain intermediate chains (`VAOPGCPREC 1-2017`) -> Obstructive Sleep Apnea (`OSA`) or GERD**; and
• **Survivor DIC (`38 U.S.C. § 1310`)** for fatal cirrhosis or accidental overdose secondary to SC PTSD/pain ([Playbook 08](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical))!

blocks.text: 4. Invariants / Kill-Switches

items: **Routine `IADT` Chronic-Disease Kill-Switch (`38 U.S.C. § 101(24)(C)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.6(a)(3), (d), (e)`):** Never plead direct chronic disease onset (e.g., essential hypertension, hypothyroidism, idiopathic MS, or osteoarthritis without trauma) during a 2-day `IADT` drill weekend—`§ 3.6(a)(3)` and `(e)(3)` cover **only `"injury"`** or **`§ 101(24)(C)` / `§ 106(d)` acute myocardial infarction, cardiac arrest, or stroke**. Check immediately whether symptoms manifested or worsened during a 2-week **`ADT` (`AT`)** tour or **`Title 32 § 502(f)`** order (`§ 3.6(a)(2), (c)` covers diseases!), or arose from an acute drill **injury**!

**Pure `ADT` Soundness Mispleading (*Smith* & *Donnellan*):** Never argue in a CAVC or Board brief that VA failed to rebut the `§ 1111` presumption of soundness on a pure `ADT` claim where the claimant lacks independent veteran status—you will lose under *Smith v. Shinseki*, `24 Vet. App. 40 (2010)` and *Donnellan v. Shinseki*, `24 Vet. App. 167 (2010)`. Instead, develop an affirmative private IMO proving permanent `§ 3.306(a)` aggravation beyond natural progression during the `ADT` tour!

**Pure Governor-Funded State Active Duty (`SAD`):** Confirm federal funding/statutory authority (`Title 10` or `Title 32 U.S.C. §§ 316, 502–505`) before litigating; pure state-funded `SAD` without federal conversion cannot confer Title 38 eligibility.

**Primary Post-1990 Substance Abuse & The `VAOPGCPREC 7-99` / *George* CUE Bar:**
• Standalone primary alcohol/drug abuse (not caused or aggravated by an SC disorder) remains statutorily barred for claims filed after October 31, 1990 (`38 U.S.C. §§ 105(a), 1110`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.301(d)`).
• Under *George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` and `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`, **do NOT file a CUE motion** ([`Board CUE Pre-Filing Gate`](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate)) attacking a final `June 1999 – 2001` RO/Board decision that faithfully applied [`VAOPGCPREC 7-99`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index) before *Allen v. Principi* invalidated it—reopen via `§ 3.156(c)` missing service records or a Supplemental Claim (`VA Form 20-0995`) instead!

blocks.text: 5. Postconditions: Effective Dates, Drill-Pay / Severance Offsets & Fees

items:
**Effective-Date Verification:**
• **Late-Associated `LOD` (`DA Form 2173` / `AF Form 348` / `DD Form 261`), `Title 10`/`32` Orders, or Guard STRs (`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)(3)`):** Audit every Guard/Reserve grant! If VA previously denied for *"no active service"* or *"no in-service injury"* while holding only an `NGB-22`, and later granted after associating `LOD` or `Title 32` orders, **demand the original denied claim's effective date** under `38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)(3)` ([Playbook 03](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c); *Vigil v. Peake*, `22 Vet. App. 63 (2008)`).
• **1-Year Post-`ADT`/`Title 10` Filing (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(b)(1)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.400(b)(2)`):** A claim received within **1 year after release from a qualifying `Active Duty` or `ADT` tour** where disability was incurred/aggravated takes the **day following release from that tour** as its effective date!

**Guard/Reserve Drill-Pay Waiver, Combat Severance & Retirement Offsets:**
• **Annual Drill-Pay Waiver Math (`38 U.S.C. § 5304(c)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.700(a)(3)` — `VA Form 21-8951` / `21-8951-2`):** Drilling Guardsmen and Reservists **cannot** receive VA disability compensation and military drill/AT pay **for the exact same day**—**NOT** the entire year! A standard drilling reservist performs ~`48` `UTA`s (`4` drill days = `1` day of VA pay per `UTA`) + `15` `AT` days = **`~63 days/year`**, waiving **only `63/360`ths (~2 months) of VA compensation** while keeping **nearly 10 months of tax-free VA pay PLUS 100% of military drill pay**! Always counsel drilling clients **never** to waive their entire VA award!
• **Combat-Zone Disability Severance Non-Recoupment (`10 U.S.C. § 1212(d)(2)`):** If a Guard/Reserve member was medically separated (`IDES`/`MEB`) with disability severance pay for a disability incurred in a **combat zone** or during **combat-related operations** (post-Jan. 28, 2008 NDAA FY 2008 `Pub. L. 110-181, § 1646`), VA is **statutorily prohibited from recouping** that severance pay—and under `10 U.S.C. § 1212(d)(1)`, VA also cannot recoup severance pay if the severed condition is `0%` or non-contributory to the combined rating!
• **`20-Year` ("Gray Area" Age `60`) & `Chapter 61` Reserve Retirees (`CRDP` `10 U.S.C. § 1414` & `CRSC` `10 U.S.C. § 1413a` / *Soto*):** Once a Guard/Reserve retiree reaches retirement pay receipt age (typically age `60`, or earlier reduced age for post-2008 deployments) with `>= 50%` VA combined rating, verify automatic **`CRDP`** restoration—or, for `Chapter 61` medical retirees (`<20` good years) or combat-injured retirees, file **`CRSC`** with **uncapped pre-6-year retroactivity under *Soto v. United States*, `605 U.S. 360 (2025)`** ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc))!

**Attorney Fees (`38 U.S.C. § 5904` & `EAJA`):**
• Prior VA denials for *"lack of veteran status / no active duty on NGB-22"* or *"willful misconduct under § 3.301(d)"* satisfy the initial-AOJ-decision prerequisite of `38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(1)`, enabling immediate contingency fee agreements on `§ 3.156(c)` reconsiderations, Supplemental Claims, HLRs, and Board appeals (subject to dollar-for-dollar `EAJA` same-work offset; see [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: National Guard & Reserve Claims: Active Duty vs. Training (ADT & Drill/IADT), Title 32 Orders & Line of Duty Investigations
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: National Guard and Reserve members are frequently denied VA benefits with a boilerplate letter saying 'No qualifying active military service'—often because VA looked only at a state NGB Form 22 and never obtained federal activation orders, training orders, or military Line of Duty (LOD) determinations. Under 38 U.S.C. § 101(24) and 38 C.F.R. § 3.6, you do NOT need a Title 10 overseas deployment to earn VA disability compensation if you were disabled by: (1) any injury or disease incurred or aggravated during Active Duty for Training (ADT, such as basic training, AIT, annual 2-week training, or federally funded Title 32 U.S.C. §§ 316, 502–505 duty, including § 502(f) operational missions); OR (2) an injury—or an acute heart attack, cardiac arrest, or stroke (§ 106(d))—during weekend drills (Inactive Duty Training / IADT) or authorized direct portal-to-portal travel to and from training.
record_clues: A VA denial stating 'Not a Veteran' or 'No active service' when your C-file contained only an NGB Form 22 without your Title 10 / Title 32 orders, drill attendance/retirement point sheets, or training clinic records.

A favorable military Line of Duty (LOD) report—such as Army DA Form 2173, Air Force AF Form 348, or DD Form 261—confirming an injury or illness happened 'In Line of Duty' during training or drill (binding or highly probative evidence that also triggers 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) if added to your C-file later!).

Federally authorized Title 32 U.S.C. § 502(f) National Guard orders (such as post-9/11 airport security, border missions, hurricane response, or federal COVID-19 response) mislabeled by VA as pure state duty.
A heart attack, cardiac arrest, stroke, orthopedic trauma, acoustic trauma, or toxic exposure injury during weekend drill (IADT) or authorized direct travel to/from ADT or IADT (§ 3.6(d)–(e)).
important_cautions: Pure Governor State Active Duty (SAD) vs. Title 32 Duty: Pure state-funded, Governor-controlled State Active Duty (with no federal Title 10 or Title 32 U.S.C. §§ 316, 502–505 authority) is covered by state workers' compensation rather than federal VA compensation—so checking the exact statutory authority printed on your orders is essential.

Disease vs. Injury on Weekend Drills (IADT): Unlike Active Duty for Training (ADT), routine weekend drills (IADT) cover physical 'injuries' (including toxic/acoustic injury mechanisms) PLUS acute myocardial infarction, cardiac arrest, and stroke (retroactively effective November 1, 2000 under Pub. L. 106-419), but do not cover ordinary chronic diseases manifesting during a drill weekend.

How Aggravation Works on ADT (Smith & Donnellan): On pure ADT claims where Veteran status has not yet been established, the § 1111 presumption of soundness does not apply—meaning the claimant must show with medical or lay evidence that a pre-existing condition actually worsened during ADT under § 3.306.

Secondary Alcohol/Substance Conditions After 1990 (Allen v. Principi): While primary alcohol/drug abuse claims filed after October 31, 1990 are barred (§ 3.301(d)), alcohol/substance disorders or organ damage caused or aggravated by a service-connected condition ARE compensable under § 3.310—though under George v. McDonough (§ 20.1403(e)), Allen cannot be used to file CUE against a final 1999–2001 decision that applied pre-Allen agency precedent.

blocks.text: Aid and Attendance (`A&A`) tiers represent the single largest monthly compensation multipliers in Title 38—scaling from **`$4,900.83/month`** at `SMC(l)` (`38 U.S.C. § 1114(l)`) to **`$9,826.88/month`** at `SMC(r)(1)` (`§ 1114(r)(1)`) and **`$11,271.67/month`** (veteran alone, effective Dec. 1, 2025) at `SMC(r)(2)` (`§ 1114(r)(2)`) and Traumatic Brain Injury **`SMC(t)` (`§ 1114(t)`)**. Two watershed 2024 judicial decisions—***Barry v. McDonough*, `101 F.4th 1348 (Fed. Cir. May 16, 2024)`** (multi-step bumps into the `SMC(r)(1)` gateway) and ***Laska v. McDonough*, `37 Vet. App. 460 (Sept. 6, 2024)`** (striking down `38 C.F.R. § 3.352(b)(2)`'s licensed-professional barrier to `SMC(t)`)—have unlocked thousands of previously blocked `~$10,000–$11,271+/month` claims.

blocks.text: 1. Preconditions: VA Form 21-2680, PCAFC Caregiver Files & Code-Sheet Triggers

Before pleading any `A&A` tier, pull the complete **VBMS eFolder**, **CAPRI/VistA VHA clinical records** (including Geriatrics & Extended Care and Caregiver Support Program notes), and **every internal Rating Code Sheet** ([VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon)):

items:
**Clinical & VHA Caregiver Triggers (`Bell` Constructive Possession Goldmines):**
• **`VA Form 21-2680`** (*Examination for Housebound Status or Permanent Need for Regular Aid and Attendance*) or Neurological/PTSD/TBI DBQs checking assistance with bathing, dressing, feeding, toileting, prosthetic adjustment, medication management, mobility/transfers, or supervision against environmental hazards.
• **VHA `PCAFC` Stipend Files (`38 U.S.C. § 1720G`; `38 C.F.R. § 71.20`):** Enrollment in VHA's *Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers* (`PCAFC`) requires a clinical VHA interdisciplinary finding that the veteran needs personal care services for `>= 6` continuous months due to an inability to perform one or more `ADL`s or a need for **supervision, protection, or instruction**. Because VHA `PCAFC` evaluations sit inside VA medical records, they are **constructively before VBA raters** (*Bell v. Derwinski*; [`VAOPGCPREC 12-95`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index)) and **reasonably raise `SMC(l)` / `SMC(t)`** (*Akles v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 118 (1991)`)!
• **VAMC `HBPC`, `H/HHA`, Bowel/Bladder & Polytrauma Notes:** Home-Based Primary Care (`HBPC`), Homemaker/Home Health Aide (`H/HHA`) authorizations, `BRADEN` fall/ulcer scores, neurogenic bowel/bladder catheterization regimens, or Polytrauma/TBI Clinic notes (`DC 8045`) documenting executive dysfunction, wandering, stove/driving hazards, impulsivity, or memory cueing.

**Rating Code Sheet SMC Designator Audit:**
• Inspect the `SMC` block at the bottom of the Rating Code Sheet:
• `SMC (L-1)` (`§ 1114(l)` Regular A&A) paired with uncounted independent `50%+` or `100%` schedular disabilities (`Barry` `SMC(r)(1)` candidate!).
• `SMC (O-1)` / `(O-2)` (`§ 3.350(e)(2)` paraplegia + anal/bladder sphincter loss) or `P-1`/`P-2`/`P-3` intermediate steps without `R-1` or `R-2` despite `A&A`.
• `10%`, `40%`, `70%`, or `100%` `DC 8045` Traumatic Brain Injury (or co-morbid `TBI + PTSD/dementia` rated as `100%`) receiving only `100%`, `SMC(s)`, or `SMC(l)` despite spousal caregiving that prevents nursing-home or assisted-living placement (`SMC(t)` candidate!).
• Award lines showing `"Hospitalized — SMC Reduced"` (`38 C.F.R. § 3.552`) that persisted *after* the veteran was discharged home!

McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` bar** ([Procedural Vehicles Piercing Finality](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality)). Always sequence your procedural vehicle in this exact order:
