blocks.text: 3. Proof Elements & Doctrinal Mechanics
A. SMC(l) Regular Aid & Attendance (38 U.S.C. § 1114(l); 38 C.F.R. § 3.352(a), (c))

*(Link to verbatim text in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.350, 3.352, 3.552(b), 4.63 & 3.810(a) (Special Monthly Compensation Ratings, Aid & Attendance, TBI SMC(t), Loss of Use & Multiple Clothing Allowances)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.350-3.352-smc-evolution)).*

items:
**Holistic, Disjunctive `ADL` Standard (*Turco v. Brown*, `9 Vet. App. 222, 224 (1996)`):**
• `38 C.F.R. § 3.352(a)` enumerates six core indicators: `(1)` inability to dress or undress; `(2)` inability to keep oneself ordinarily clean and presentable; `(3)` frequent need of adjustment of special prosthetic or orthopedic appliances; `(4)` inability to feed oneself through upper-extremity incoordination or extreme weakness; `(5)` inability to attend to the wants of nature (toileting/continence); **OR** `(6)` **physical or mental incapacity requiring care or assistance on a regular basis to protect the claimant from hazards or dangers incident to his or her daily environment**.
• **The *Turco* Rule:** In *Turco*, `9 Vet. App. at 224`, the CAVC held that `§ 3.352(a)` is explicitly **disjunctive and holistic**—a claimant **need NOT exhibit every listed inability**, and **"regular" aid and attendance does NOT require "constant" (`24/7`) need**! Requiring assistance with bathing and dressing three or four times per week, or regular daily cognitive hazard monitoring, fully satisfies `"regular"` A&A when viewed in connection with the veteran's condition as a whole.
• **Permanently Bedridden Alternative (`§ 3.352(a)`):** Requires that the essential character of the SC disease/injury *actually requires* remaining in bed (excluding voluntary bedrest or physician-prescribed convalescent rest). Never let an examiner conflate `"bedridden"` with `"regular A&A"`—`§ 3.352(a)` expressly prohibits basing A&A on whether the veteran stays in bed!

**Cognitive & Psychiatric `"Hazards of Daily Environment"` (`§ 3.352(a)`):**
• Raters routinely fixate on physical paralysis while overlooking cognitive/mental A&A. Document concrete safety incidents in spouse/caregiver declarations: leaving burners/stoves on, forgetting or double-dosing insulin/medications, wandering/getting lost, falling on stairs due to vertigo/ataxia/orthostatic hypotension, or severe psychotic/dissociative/dementia disorientation.

**Unlicensed Spouse / Family Caregiving (`38 C.F.R. § 3.352(c)`) & Medical Nexus Rigor (*Prejean* & *Martinez*):**
• Under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.352(c)`**, performance of A&A by a **spouse, child, or household relative** fully qualifies—zero professional licensing or out-of-pocket payment is required for `SMC(l)`!
• **Sole-SC Causation Rule:** Unlike NSC Pension A&A, compensation `SMC(l)` requires that **service-connected disability(ies) alone** necessitate regular A&A (excluding NSC aging/arthritis). Under ***Prejean v. West*, `13 Vet. App. 444, 448–49 (2000)`**, any private `VA Form 21-2680` or IMO **must** provide a **thorough, reasoned medical rationale** connecting objective clinical findings on SC conditions directly to the specific `§ 3.352(a)` functional deficits (conclusory check-boxes without clinical reasoning will be discounted). *(Procedural note: Under *Martinez v. Wilkie*, `31 Vet. App. 170 (2019)`, VA is not statutorily required to proactively mail an unfavorable C&P copy prior to decision, so counsel must actively pull VBMS `21-2680` C&P uploads immediately after exam completion to submit rebuttal IMOs before rating!).*

blocks.text: A veteran needing Regular A&A (`§ 3.352(a)`) cannot jump straight from `SMC(l)` (`$4,900.83`) to `SMC(r)(1)` (`$9,826.88`) without **first** crossing one of **three statutory gateways** in `38 U.S.C. § 1114(r)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(h)(1)–(2)` (see full math in [Master SMC Treatise § 4](/docs/smc-complete-treatise-and-step-math)):

items:
**Gateway 1 — Dual `(l)–(n)` Entitlements (`§ 1114(o)` / `§ 3.350(e)(1)(ii)` & `(e)(2)`):**
• **Paraplegia `Code O-2` (`§ 3.350(e)(2)`):** Bilateral lower-extremity LOU **+** loss of anal and bladder sphincter control = automatic `SMC(o)` + A&A -> **`SMC(r)(1)`** (and **immune** from `§ 3.552` hospitalization reduction!).
• **Paired Independent `(l)–(n)` Conditions (*Breniser* Boundary):** E.g., bilateral foot LOU (`SMC(l)` #1) **+** Regular A&A (`SMC(l)` #2) caused **solely by a separate, distinct SC condition** (such as SC Parkinson's upper-extremity/cognitive impairment or SC heart failure). Under ***Breniser v. Shinseki*, `25 Vet. App. 64, 74–77 (2011)`**, if the A&A need relies *in whole or in part* on the bilateral foot LOU, `(e)(1)(ii)` fails—the IMO **must** isolate the non-extremity SC condition as independently sufficient for `§ 3.352(a)` A&A!

**Gateway 2 — Post-*Barry* Multi-Step Bumps to Max `§ 1114(p)` (`$6,877.12`):**
• Under ***Barry v. McDonough*, `101 F.4th 1348 (Fed. Cir. 2024)`**, a veteran at base **`SMC(l)` Regular A&A** who stacks **6 half-steps** (`§ 3.350(f)(3)` `>= 50%` units), **3 full-steps** (`§ 3.350(f)(4)` `100%` schedular units—*not TDIU*), or any equivalent mix (`e.g., two 100%s + two 50%s`) reaches **"the maximum rate authorized under subsection (p)" (`$6,877.12`)**, which under the plain text of **`38 U.S.C. § 1114(r)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(h)(1)` automatically converts into `SMC(r)(1)` (`$9,826.88/mo`)**!

**Gateway 3 — The `SMC(n½) + SMC(k)` Special Bridge (`§ 1114(r)` & `§ 3.350(h)(2)`):**
• Even **one half-step short of `SMC(o)`**, a veteran at **`SMC(n½)` (`$6,514.44`) + at least one `SMC(k)` (`$139.87`)** (e.g., `ED` `DC 7522`) who needs Regular A&A **immediately qualifies for `SMC(r)(1)` (`$9,826.88/mo`)**!

blocks.text: Once any of the three gateways above is met, advancing from `(r)(1)` to **`(r)(2)` (`+$1,444.79/month`)** requires proving **all three** strictly construed (`§ 3.352(b)(6)`) elements:

items: **Daily In-Home `"Personal Health-Care Services"` (`§ 3.352(b)(3)`):** Services requiring professional health-care training/skills—such as **administration of injections, placement/management of indwelling or intermittent catheters, sterile wound/ulcer dressings, physical/occupational therapy, tracheostomy/ventilator suctioning, PEG tube feeding, or digital bowel disimpaction programs**—performed **daily** in the veteran's home.

**Licensed Provider OR `"Regular Supervision"` of a Spouse/Relative (`§ 3.352(b)(4)–(5)` — Critical Practitioner Lever!):**
• A spouse or household relative performing those daily health-care services **QUALIFIES for `SMC(r)(2)`** under `§ 3.352(b)(4)–(5)` **if** `(a)` the relative follows a **prescribed regimen** of personal health-care services ordered by a licensed health-care professional (`MD`, `DO`, `RN`, `NP`, `PA`, `PT`), **AND** `(b)` **the licensed health-care professional consults with the unlicensed caregiver at least ONCE EACH MONTH to monitor the regimen (`"The consultation need not be in person; a telephone call will suffice"` — `§ 3.352(b)(4)`)**!
• *Action Step:* Enlist the veteran's VAMC `HBPC` nurse or private treating physician to write the daily home-care regimen into the medical chart and log a scheduled **monthly telephone check-in** with the caregiving spouse!

**Institutionalization-Avoidance Nexus (`§ 3.352(b)(1)(iii)`):** Medical certification that, **in the absence of** such daily higher-level care, the veteran **would require hospitalization, nursing home care, or other residential institutional care**.

blocks.text: C. Traumatic Brain Injury SMC(t) (38 U.S.C. § 1114(t)) & ***Laska v. McDonough*, 37 Vet. App. 460 (2024)**

Enacted by **`Pub. L. 111-275, Title VI, § 601`** (`124 Stat. 2864, 2884`, Oct. 13, 2010, **effective October 1, 2011**) and codified nearly seven years later at **`38 C.F.R. §§ 3.350(j), 3.352(b)(2)`** (`83 FR 20735`, pub. May 8, 2018, **eff. June 7, 2018**), **`SMC(t)` pays the full `SMC(r)(2)` monthly rate (`$11,271.67/month` in 2026)** to TBI veterans **without** requiring `SMC(o)`, limb loss, or multiple ratings!
How *Laska v. McDonough* (37 Vet. App. 460 (Sept. 6, 2024)) Demolished VA's SMC(t) Roadblock:

items: **VA's Unlawful 2018 Regulation (`38 C.F.R. § 3.352(b)(2)(ii)`):** When VA promulgated `83 FR 20735` in 2018, VA inserted an extra-statutory requirement into `§ 3.352(b)(2)(ii)` demanding that TBI veterans prove a need for `"higher level of care"` (`§ 3.352(b)(3)`—daily skilled medical procedures by or under monthly supervision of a licensed health-care professional). Because severe TBI residuals typically demand **cognitive/behavioral supervision, cueing, and safety monitoring** by a spouse rather than sterile surgical dressings or injections, VA denied `95%+` of `SMC(t)` claims!

**The Landmark Holding in *Laska v. McDonough*, `37 Vet. App. 460 (2024)` (`No. 22-1018`, decided Sept. 6, 2024; originally docketed and argued as *Haskell v. McDonough* before surviving spouse Margaret Laska substituted):**
• A precedential CAVC panel **invalidated `38 C.F.R. § 3.352(b)(2)`'s `"higher level of care"` requirement**, holding it manifestly contrary to the plain text of **`38 U.S.C. § 1114(t)`**!
• Under `§ 1114(t)` and *Laska*, a veteran wins **`SMC(t)` (`$11,271.67/mo`)** upon proving **three plain statutory elements**:
• **Regular Aid & Attendance for SC TBI Residuals:** As a result of service-connected **`TBI` residuals (`DC 8045`)**, the veteran needs **Regular Aid & Attendance under `38 C.F.R. § 3.352(a)`**—explicitly including **unlicensed spouse or family caregiving (`§ 3.352(c)`)** for cognitive supervision, memory prompting, medication management, behavioral/impulse safety, fall prevention, or ADL assistance! *(Note: Where SC TBI and co-morbid SC PTSD/dementia cannot be clinically disentangled by an examiner, apply *Mittleider v. West*, `11 Vet. App. 181 (1998)` to attribute inseparable cognitive symptoms to the SC TBI!)*
• **Ineligibility for `SMC(r)(2)`:** The veteran is not otherwise eligible for `§ 1114(r)(2)` (e.g., lacks `SMC(o)`/`(p)` or lacks skilled `§ 3.352(b)(3)` nursing care).
• **Institutionalization Avoidance Absent Regular A&A:** **In the absence of such regular aid and attendance**, the veteran **would require hospitalization, nursing home care, or other residential institutional care** (including assisted-living facilities, memory-care units, or residential brain-injury group homes—the veteran could **not** safely live independently if the family caregiver were removed!).

blocks.text: D. 38 U.S.C. § 5503(c) & 38 C.F.R. § 3.552 VA Hospitalization Reduction Defense

To prevent duplicate federal expenditure when VA itself furnishes inpatient nursing/medical care, `38 U.S.C. § 5503(c)` (`former § 3203`) and `38 C.F.R. § 3.552` reduce A&A awards during prolonged federal hospitalization—creating **four high-frequency RO errors** that counsel must audit:

items:
**The `"First Day of the Second Calendar Month"` Grace Window (`§ 3.552(b)(1)–(2)`):**
• Discontinuance of `SMC(l)` A&A, `SMC(r)(1)`, `SMC(r)(2)`, or `SMC(t)` is **NEVER immediate upon admission** (except readmission within `<6 months` after an **against-medical-advice [`AMA`] or disciplinary** discharge under `§ 3.552(b)(3)`!).
• Reduction takes effect on the **last day of the month following the month of admission**—meaning the reduced rate begins on the **first day of the SECOND calendar month after admission** at VA / U.S. Government expense!
• *Calendar Math:* Admitted to a VAMC or VA Community Living Center (`CLC`) on **March 2** -> **100% full `SMC(r)/(t)` (`$11,271.67`) is payable for ALL of March AND ALL of April** -> reduction takes effect **May 1**! If discharged on **April 29**, **zero reduction ever occurs**! *(Note: Under `§ 3.552(k)(2)`, if initial A&A entitlement arises *on or after* hospital admission, A&A payment is deferred until hospital release unless exempt under `(a)(2)`).*

**Exact Hospitalization Fallback Rates (`§ 3.552(d)–(i)`):**
• **`SMC(r)(1)` / `(r)(2)`:** Drops to the underlying `SMC(o)` / max `SMC(p)` (`$6,877.12`)—*unless* that `SMC(o)` itself depended on a second `SMC(l)` A&A rate, in which case **`§ 3.552(g)(1)–(3)`** governs: base `(l)` + separate A&A drops to **`SMC(m)`** (`(g)(1)`); base `(m)` + separate A&A drops to **`SMC(n)`** (`(g)(2)`); base `(n)` + separate A&A **retains `SMC(o)`** (`(g)(3)`)!
• **`SMC(l)` A&A + `§ 3.350(f)` Step Bumps (`§ 3.552(i)`):** Reduces during hospitalization to **`SMC(s)` (`$4,408.53`)** (including `SMC(r)(1)` achieved solely via `SMC(l)` A&A + *Barry* `(f)(3)–(4)` bumps, or `SMC(t)` where underlying TBI + co-morbidities equal `SMC(s)` or `100%`).

**Absolute Statutory/Regulatory Exemptions (`§ 3.552(a)(1)–(3)`):**
• **Paraplegia + Sphincter Loss (`§ 3.552(a)(2)` — `Code O-2`):** **ZERO hospitalization reduction** ever applies when A&A is based on **paralysis of both lower extremities together with loss of anal and bladder sphincter control**, OR **Hansen's disease**! *(Trap Warning: `§ 3.552(a)(2)`'s `5/200` blindness exemption applies **only to NSC Pension**, NOT to SMC compensation!)*
• **Non-VA Expense Care:** Private hospital or private nursing-home stays paid by **Medicare, private insurance, or personal funds** (not under VA contract/expense) **do NOT trigger `§ 3.552`**!

**Mandatory Immediate Restoration on Hospital Release (`§ 3.552` — Classic RO CUE):**
• Full `SMC(l)` / `(r)(1)` / `(r)(2)` / `(t)` **must be restored effective the exact date of release/discharge** from VA hospitalization (including authorized `30+`-day convalescent leaves). Raters routinely forget to lift the hospitalization withholding code for months or years after discharge—a textbook **RO CUE (`§ 3.105(a)`)**!

blocks.text: 4. Invariants / Kill-Switches

items: **Hard `October 1, 2011` Statutory Floor on `SMC(t)` (`Pub. L. 111-275, § 601(c)`):** Never request `SMC(t)` for any period prior to **October 1, 2011**, even on an open 2007 Iraq/Afghanistan TBI appeal—stage the award as `SMC(l)` (or `SMC(r)(1)` if *Barry* bumps apply) prior to Oct. 1, 2011, stepping up to `SMC(t)` on **October 1, 2011**!

**The *Breniser* Double-Counting Bar (`25 Vet. App. 64`):** Never plead `SMC(o)` / `SMC(r)(1)` under `§ 3.350(e)(1)(ii)` when the veteran's A&A need is caused in whole or in part by the exact same extremity/blindness condition establishing base `SMC(l)`–`(n)`. Pivot to **Gateway 2 (*Barry* `(f)(3)–(4)` bumps from distinct ratings)** or **`§ 3.350(e)(2)` bowel/bladder loss (`Code O-2`)** instead!

**The *George v. McDonough* (`596 U.S. 740 (2022)`) / `§ 20.1403(e)` CUE Bar:** Never file a CUE motion attacking a final pre-May 16, 2024 single-bump rating under *Barry* or a final pre-Sept. 6, 2024 `SMC(t)` denial under *Laska*. Unlock non-finality via `§ 5104(b)` *Hamill*, `§ 3.156(b)` *Lang*, or `§ 3.156(c)`, or file an immediate `VA Form 20-0995` Supplemental Claim!

**TDIU Exclusion Under `§ 3.350(f)(4)`:** Remember `§ 3.350(f)(4)`'s full-step bump requires a **`100%` schedular** evaluation (`"apart from any consideration of individual unemployability"`). If an independent `70%` disability underpins TDIU, use it as a **`+½` step under `§ 3.350(f)(3)`** instead!

blocks.text: 5. Postconditions: Effective Dates, PCAFC Non-Offset, Ancillary Unlocks & Fees

items:
**Zero Offset Between `SMC(l)/(r)/(t)` & VHA `PCAFC` Family Caregiver Stipends (`38 U.S.C. § 1720G`):**
• **Massive Household Multiplier:** Monthly VHA `PCAFC` stipends paid directly to a spouse/family caregiver under `38 U.S.C. § 1720G` (`38 C.F.R. pt. 71`) are **separate VHA health-care support payments—NOT Title 38 duplicate disability compensation**! A qualifying TBI or polytrauma household legally collects **100% of tax-free `SMC(t)` or `SMC(r)(2)` (`$11,271.67+/month`) PLUS 100% of the monthly `PCAFC` Level 1 or Level 2 caregiver stipend** with **zero dollar-for-dollar offset** (only VHA *in-home contract aide hours* may be coordinated with clinical need, never VBA `SMC` cash pay!).

**Automatic High-Dollar Ancillary Unlocks ([Playbook 13](/playbooks/13-ancillary-grants-sah-auto-clothing-dea-spina-bifida)):**
• Upon winning `SMC(l)`–`(t)` or extremity/vision LOU, immediately trigger: **`~\$121,000+` `Ch. 21` Specially Adapted Housing (`SAH`)** (for bilateral lower-extremity LOU, blindness, severe burns, or certain single-extremity + A&A/balance combinations), **`~\$26,000+` `Ch. 39` Automobile + unlimited adaptive equipment grants** (including the 10-year second auto grant under `Pub. L. 117-333`), **multiple annual `§ 3.810` Clothing Allowances** (*Sursely*), and **`P&T` `Ch. 35` DEA / `CHAMPVA`** retroactive effective-date audits!

**Military Retirement (`CRDP` / `CRSC`) & Attorney Fees (`38 U.S.C. § 5904` & `EAJA`):**
• For military retirees (`Ch. 61` medical retirees especially!), stepping up from `100%` (`$3,938.58`) to `SMC(r)(2)`/`SMC(t)` (`$11,271.67`) increases VA waiver against military retired pay—immediately file/amend **`CRSC` (`10 U.S.C. § 1413a`)** for combat/instrumentality TBI or polytrauma to recover **uncapped retroactive retired-pay offsets under *Soto v. United States*, `605 U.S. 360 (2025)`** ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc))!
• Because SMC is part and parcel of underlying compensation claims (*Akles*), any prior AOJ rating decision on the underlying TBI or SC disabilities satisfies `38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(1)` for contingency fees on Supplemental, HLR, or Board SMC upgrades (offsetting any CAVC `EAJA` award dollar-for-dollar for the same work; see [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Aid & Attendance (SMC(l)), Higher-Level Care (SMC(r)(1)/(2)) & Traumatic Brain Injury Caregiver Compensation (SMC(t))
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Special Monthly Compensation (SMC) pays substantially higher monthly rates above 100% when service-connected disabilities leave a Veteran needing regular daily help from another person ('Aid and Attendance' under 38 C.F.R. § 3.352(a)—such as help bathing, dressing, toileting, taking medications, adjusting prosthetics, or staying safe from physical or cognitive hazards). Basic Aid & Attendance starts at SMC(l), steps up through intermediate rates when combined with separate 50%+ or 100% disabilities (Barry v. McDonough), and reaches higher-level care under SMC(r)(1) and SMC(r)(2). Crucially, for Veterans with service-connected Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI), Congress created SMC(t) (paid at the top SMC(r)(2) dollar rate)—and in Laska v. McDonough (September 6, 2024), the Veterans Court struck down VA's extra rule demanding 'licensed health-care professional' skilled nursing, confirming that regular family/lay Aid & Attendance preventing institutionalization satisfies SMC(t).
record_clues: A VA Form 21-2680 physician exam, DBQ, or VAMC record documenting need for help with dressing, bathing, toileting, feeding, prosthetics, fall prevention, or supervision against everyday hazards.

Enrollment in VA's Family Caregiver Program (PCAFC), Home-Based Primary Care (HBPC), or VA Homemaker/Home Health Aide services in your medical chart while your Rating Code Sheet still pays only standard 100% or SMC(s).

A service-connected Traumatic Brain Injury (DC 8045) where VA denied SMC(t) (or paid lower SMC(l)) because your spouse or family member provides daily cognitive/supervisory care rather than a licensed nurse (Laska v. McDonough).

A Veteran receiving SMC(l) for Aid & Attendance who ALSO has multiple independent 50%+ or 100% service-connected disabilities that step the award up toward SMC(o) / maximum SMC(p)—unlocking SMC(r)(1) under Barry v. McDonough.
A reduction of Aid & Attendance during a VA hospital stay applied too early (before the first day of the second calendar month following admission) or never restored on discharge (§ 3.552).
important_cautions: October 1, 2011 Statutory Floor for TBI SMC(t): Congress set the effective date of 38 U.S.C. § 1114(t) at October 1, 2011 (Pub. L. 111-275, § 601(c)); no SMC(t) payment can take effect prior to October 1, 2011.

Judicial Reinterpretation CUE Bar (George v. McDonough): Under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e), the 2024 court rulings in Barry v. McDonough (multi-step § 3.350(f) bumps) and Laska v. McDonough (TBI SMC(t) family-care standard) apply to open claims, timely appeals, Supplemental Claims, and § 3.156(c) service-record reconsiderations—not as Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) against older final decisions.

No Double-Counting the Same Disability (Amberman & Breniser): A disability already used to establish your base SMC(l) award cannot be counted a second time to trigger an extra § 3.350(f) step bump or a second SMC(l) rate.

Service-Connected Requirement & VA Hospitalization Rule (§ 3.552): Compensation Aid & Attendance (SMC(l)) must be needed due to service-connected disabilities alone (not non-service-connected aging), and prolonged VA/government hospitalization triggers special discontinuance rules starting the second calendar month after admission (§ 3.552(b)).
questions_for_representative: Do my VAMC caregiver (PCAFC), Home-Based Primary Care, or VA Form 21-2680 records show regular need for Aid & Attendance or supervision due to my service-connected conditions?
If I have a service-connected Traumatic Brain Injury and need regular family/caregiver help to remain safely at home instead of in a facility, should we pursue SMC(t) under Laska v. McDonough?

If I already receive SMC(l), do I have additional completely separate 50%+ or 100% service-connected disabilities that warrant multiple step increases (and potential SMC(r)(1) eligibility) under Barry v. McDonough?
If VA reduced my Aid & Attendance during an inpatient hospital stay, did VA follow the exact calendar-month timing and discharge-restoration rules in 38 C.F.R. § 3.552?

Confusing Jensen v. Shulkin, 29 Vet. App. 66 (2017) (§ 3.809 SAH assistive-device locomotion standard) with Walker v. Shinseki, 708 F.3d 1331 (Fed. Cir. 2013) (§ 3.303(b) chronicity restriction)

Claiming Ch. 18 Spina Bifida benefits for spina bifida occulta (§ 1802) or for herbicide locations outside Vietnam, Korea DMZ, and Thailand (§§ 1805, 1821, 1822 — Laos, Cambodia, Guam, American Samoa, and Johnston Atoll were NOT added to Ch. 18 by the PACT Act)

blocks.text: Winning a `100%` Permanent and Total (`P&T`), Loss of Use (`LOU`), blindness, burn, `ALS`, or Special Monthly Compensation (`SMC`) award is only half of catastrophic-injury representation. Properly audited **ancillary grants and derivative family benefits** routinely deliver **`$150,000–$300,000+` in tax-free lump sums, home/vehicle adaptations, recurring annual stipends, and retroactive family education/healthcare reimbursements** that general practitioners leave unclaimed on the table.

*(Cross-references: Verbatim `SMC` regulations [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.350, 3.352, 3.552(b), 4.63 & 3.810(a) (Special Monthly Compensation Ratings, Aid & Attendance, TBI SMC(t), Loss of Use & Multiple Clothing Allowances)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.350-3.352-smc-evolution); [`Part 3 SMC Statutory & Regulatory Evolution Diff`](/cfr/modules/smc-statutory-and-regulatory-evolution); [Master SMC Legal Treatise & Step Math](/docs/smc-complete-treatise-and-step-math); [Playbook 12 (`SMC(l)`, `SMC(r)(1)–(2)` & `SMC(t)`)](/playbooks/12-aid-and-attendance-smc-l-r1-r2-and-smc-t); [Playbook 04 (Unadjudicated TDIU & Mandatory SMC)](/playbooks/04-unadjudicated-tdiu-informal-claims-smc); [`Surviving Spouse & Helpless Child Evolution Diff`](/cfr/modules/survivor-marriage-dependency-evolution); [`SMC & Ancillary Audit Worksheet`](/checklists/smc-and-ancillary-audit-worksheet); [Three-Era Statutory Crosswalk](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk); [Master `VAOPGCPREC` Digest](/docs/vaopgcprec-index); [VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon); and [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).*
1. Preconditions: VBMS / VHA / Loan Guaranty Forms & Code-Sheet Triggers

Unlike standard disability ratings adjudicated solely inside VBA's `VBMS` compensation lane, ancillary benefits span **four separate VA administrations/divisions** (VBA Compensation, VBA Loan Guaranty, VBA Education/Denver RO, and VHA Prosthetics/`CHAMPVA`). Audit every `100%`, `TDIU`, `SMC`, `ALS`, orthopedic bracing, burn, or herbicide C-file for these exact forms and triggers ([VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon)):

rows: **`VA Form 26-4555`** *(VBA Compensation certifies medical eligibility -> Loan Guaranty SAH Agent disburses)*
Bilateral LE bracing/wheelchair/walker (`Jensen`), `1 LE + balance/propulsion` disorder, `<= 20/200` bilateral blindness, severe burns, `ALS` (`§ 3.809(d)`), or loss/LOU of both hands (`SHA`).
**`VA Form 21-4502`** *(Vehicle Purchase + Equip., VBA)*; **`VA Form 10-1394`** *(Adaptive Equip. Only, VHA PSAS)*
Loss/LOU of 1+ foot or hand, `<= 20/200` or `20°` field blindness, severe burn scar contractures, `ALS`, knee/hip ankylosis (`10-1394`), or prior auto grant `>= 30 yrs` ago (`Pub. L. 117-333`).
**`VA Form 10-8678`** *(VHA Prosthetic & Sensory Aids Service — `PSAS`, **`Aug. 1`** annual cutoff)*

Any prosthetic limb, wheelchair, crutches, or rigid/hinged/velcro brace tearing shirts/pants, OR prescribed topical cream/ointment for SC skin condition irreparably staining outergarments (*Sursely*).

Rating Code Sheet granting `100%` schedular or `TDIU` with `"Basic Eligibility to Dependents' Educational Assistance Established From [Date]"` (or improperly omitting `P&T` despite static disability!).
**`VA Form 21-0304`** *(VBA Denver Regional Office — dedicated national `Ch. 18` hub)*
Biological child with spina bifida (Vietnam, Korean DMZ, or **Thailand** herbicide veteran parent) OR non-chromosomal birth defect (female Vietnam veteran mother).

lines: **`38 U.S.C. § 1151` Beneficiaries Qualify for `SAH`, `Auto`, and `Clothing Allowance` (*Kilpatrick*):** Under ***Kilpatrick v. Principi*, `327 F.3d 1375 (Fed. Cir. 2003)`** (and `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.808(b), 3.809(a), 3.810(a)`), veterans compensated "as if service-connected" for VA medical/surgical malpractice or vocational rehabilitation injury under `38 U.S.C. § 1151` are **statutorily eligible** for `Ch. 21` `SAH`/`SHA`, `Ch. 39` Auto/Adaptive Equipment, and `§ 1162` Clothing Allowances! *(By contrast, `§ 1151` total disability during life does **not** unlock `Ch. 35` DEA or `CHAMPVA` unless `§ 1151` **caused or contributed to the veteran's death** under `38 U.S.C. §§ 1781(a)(3), 3501(a)(1)(A)–(B)`!).*

blocks.text: 2. Bitemporal Pathway Gate (Inferred Subordinate Issues vs. Application-Gated Grants)

items:
**Mandatory Subordinate / Inferred Ancillary Issues (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive / AMA Explicit § 5104(b) Notice):**
• Whenever a Rating Decision grants `100%` schedular or `TDIU` with no routine future examination (`38 C.F.R. § 3.327`), VA **must** adjudicate `Ch. 35` DEA basic `P&T` eligibility (`38 C.F.R. § 3.807`). Likewise, when VA grants `SMC` for extremity `LOU`, qualifying blindness, or `ALS` (`38 C.F.R. § 3.318`), VA is operationally required to address subordinate `Ch. 39` (`§ 3.808`) and `Ch. 21` (`§§ 3.809–3.809a`) certification.
• Under **AMA (`>= Feb. 19, 2019`)**, if a claimant checked or reasonably raised `P&T`/`SAH`/`Auto` and the decision notice stays silent, the ancillary issue **remains legally pending** under `38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)` (*Hamill v. Collins*, `166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. 2026)`).

**Application-Gated Lump Sums & Liberalizing Statutes (Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114)):**
• Actual disbursement of `SAH`/`SHA` (`26-4555`), `Ch. 39` Conveyance (`21-4502`), `Clothing Allowance` (`10-8678`), and `Ch. 18` (`21-0304`) requires a formal application. Statutory expansions (`Pub. L. 111-275` eff. Oct. 1, 2011; `Pub. L. 116-23` eff. Jan. 1, 2020; `Pub. L. 116-154` eff. Oct. 1, 2020; `Pub. L. 117-333` eff. Jan. 5, 2023) cannot generate CUE or payments predating their statutory effective dates (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(g)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)`).

***George v. McDonough* (`596 U.S. 740 (2022)`) CUE Bar (Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)):**
• Judicial invalidations of restrictive VA ancillary interpretations—such as *Sursely v. Peake* (`2009`, multiple clothing allowances), *Kilpatrick v. Principi* (`2003`, `§ 1151` `SAH`/`Auto`), and *Jensen v. Shulkin* (`2017`, `§ 3.809` lower-extremity `LOU`)—apply fully to open/pending appeals and new annual/supplemental filings, **not** as `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)` CUE against final pre-precedent denials that faithfully applied extant regulations.

blocks.text: 3. Program-by-Program Merits & Pleading Playbook
Program 1: Chapter 21 Specially Adapted Housing (SAH), SHA & TRA (38 U.S.C. §§ 2101–2102B; 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.809–3.809a)

items:
**The *Jensen v. Shulkin* Assistive-Device Breakthrough (`29 Vet. App. 66 (2017)`):**
• Raters routinely commit legal error by denying `SAH` unless the veteran already holds `SMC(l)`/`(m)` amputation-equivalent `LOU` under `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a)(2)`.
• In ***Jensen v. Shulkin*, `29 Vet. App. 66, 73–76 (2017)`**, the CAVC **rejected** importing `§ 3.350`'s strict `SMC` `LOU` standard into `38 U.S.C. § 2101(a)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.809`! Under *Jensen* and `§ 3.809(c)`, lower-extremity "loss of use" for `SAH` exists whenever bilateral lower-extremity pathology deprives the veteran of perambulation **without the regular and constant use of braces (`AFOs`), crutches, canes, or a wheelchair as their normal mode of locomotion**—even if **"occasional locomotion by other methods"** (such as shuffling a few steps unassisted inside a bathroom) remains possible!
• *(Citator Guardrail: Never confuse *Jensen v. Shulkin*, `29 Vet. App. 66 (2017)` on `§ 3.809` assistive-device locomotion with *Walker v. Shinseki*, `708 F.3d 1331 (Fed. Cir. 2013)` on `§ 3.303(b)` chronicity!)*

**Ryan Kules Act Lifetime Uses (`6x`) & `2030` Supplemental Refresh (`Pub. L. 116-154`, `134 Stat. 690`, eff. Oct. 1, 2020):**
• Veterans may split their `SAH`/`SHA` cap across **up to `6` separate lifetime grant uses** (`38 U.S.C. § 2102(d)(3)`), capturing biennial/annual construction-cost escalations on unused balances.
• Under **`38 U.S.C. § 2102(f)`** (enacted by `Pub. L. 116-154, § 3`, **phased in starting October 1, 2030**), `10` years after receiving a prior grant, veterans who exhausted their aggregate cap will unlock a **supplemental `SAH`/`SHA` refresh up to `50%` of the prevailing statutory maximum**!

blocks.text: Program 2: Chapter 39 Automobile Purchase & Unlimited Adaptive Equipment (38 U.S.C. §§ 3901–3904; 38 C.F.R. § 3.808)

items:
**Qualifying Conditions (`Full Vehicle Purchase + Equipment` vs. `Adaptive Equipment Only`):**
• **Full Conveyance Purchase Grant (`VA Form 21-4502`, `~$25,000+` paid to seller) + Unlimited Adaptive Equipment (`38 U.S.C. § 3901(1)(A)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.808(b)(1)–(4), (6)`):**
• Loss or **permanent loss of use (`LOU`)** of **one or both feet**, OR **one or both hands** (*Tucker v. West*, `11 Vet. App. 369 (1998)`—foot drop / peroneal paralysis with `AFO` brace qualifying for `SMC(k)` `LOU` **simultaneously unlocks the `$25,000+` `Ch. 39` Auto Grant**!);
• Permanent bilateral visual impairment (`<= 20/200` central visual acuity in both eyes, OR widest visual field `<= 20 degrees` in both eyes) — *note: the veteran does **not** have to drive personally; a caregiver/spouse may drive the vehicle for the blind/disabled veteran!*;
• **Severe burn injuries** (`Pub. L. 111-275, § 803`, eff. **Oct. 1, 2011**; `§ 3.808(b)(4)` — deep partial-thickness or full-thickness burns causing scar contractures that preclude effective vehicle operation); OR
• **Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (`ALS`)** (`38 C.F.R. § 3.808(b)(6)` — automatic eligibility!).
• **Adaptive Equipment ONLY (`38 U.S.C. § 3902(b)(2)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.808(b)(5)` — `VA Form 10-1394`):**
• **Ankylosis of one or both knees, or one or both hips** (without full `SMC(k)` foot `LOU`) unlocks **unlimited VHA-paid adaptive equipment** (power seats, hand controls, left-foot accelerators, lifts, power steering/brakes, air conditioning) on up to `2` vehicles within any `4-year` period (`38 U.S.C. § 3903(b)`), though **not** the vehicle purchase price itself unless counsel proves functional `LOU` of the foot!

**Second & Recurring `10-Year` Full Auto Purchase Grants (`AUTO for Veterans Act`, `Pub. L. 117-333, § 2`, `136 Stat. 6121`, enacted Jan. 5, 2023; `38 U.S.C. § 3903(a)`):**
• Congress ended the 75-year "once-in-a-lifetime" conveyance limit in **two statutory phases** (`38 U.S.C. § 3903(a)(2)–(3)`):
• **Phase 1 (`Jan. 5, 2023 – Jan. 4, 2033` — Immediate `30-Year` Bridge):** Any eligible veteran whose prior `Ch. 39` vehicle purchase grant was paid **`30 years` or more ago** (e.g., Vietnam, Gulf War, or early peacetime amputees/`LOU` veterans paid on or before `1996`!) is **immediately eligible right now** for a brand-new `$25,000+` vehicle purchase grant!
• **Phase 2 (`Beginning January 5, 2033` — Recurring `10-Year` Cycle):** Starting `10 years` after enactment of `Pub. L. 117-333`, **every** eligible veteran can receive a new full vehicle purchase grant **every `10 years`** once a decade has elapsed since their prior grant!

blocks.text: Program 3: Multiple & Recurring Annual Clothing Allowances (38 U.S.C. § 1162; 38 C.F.R. § 3.810; VA Form 10-8678)

items:
**Stacking Multiple Annual Allowances (*Sursely v. Peake*, `551 F.3d 1351 (Fed. Cir. 2009)` & `76 FR 70883`, eff. Dec. 16, 2011):**
• Under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.810(a)(2)`**, a veteran earns **separate annual tax-free lump-sum allowances** (`~$1,000+` *each* per year) for every qualifying prosthetic/orthopedic appliance (including wheelchairs) or physician-prescribed topical SC skin medication that independently damages a **distinct type of outergarment** (e.g., `Allowance #1` rigid/hinged knee brace tearing trousers + `Allowance #2` shoulder/back brace or wheelchair tearing shirts/jackets + `Allowance #3` prescribed corticosteroid/calcipotriene ointment staining collars/sleeves!).
• Under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.810(a)(3)`**, multiple qualifying appliances/medications affecting a **single type of garment** (e.g., bilateral `AFO`s/knee braces + wheelchair both destroying trousers) **also** unlock multiple allowances when together they wear/tear that garment at an **accelerated rate** requiring faster replacement than a single appliance!

**Defeating VHA Prosthetics' (`PSAS`) Unlawful "Rigid Appliance" Denials (`38 C.F.R. § 20.105`):**
• Local VHA `PSAS` offices routinely deny `VA Form 10-8678` by citing internal `VHA Handbook 1173.15` lists and labeling velcro-strapped, carbon-fiber, or hinged braces "flexible / non-rigid."
• **Appellate Cure:** Neither `38 U.S.C. § 1162` nor `38 C.F.R. § 3.810(a)(1)` contains the word **"rigid"**—the sole statutory standard is whether the appliance **"tends to wear out or tear"** the veteran's clothing! Appeal VHA denials to the Board (`VA Form 10182`, attaching photos of frayed trousers/shirts and a brief invoking `38 C.F.R. § 20.105`, under which internal VHA manuals **do not bind the Board**!).

**`August 1` Filing Cutoff & `Pub. L. 117-328` Automatic Renewal (`Div. U, § 201`, Dec. 29, 2022):**
• File initial or *additional-allowance* `VA Form 10-8678` claims with the local VAMC `PSAS` on or before **August 1** of that benefit year *(Exception: under `38 C.F.R. § 3.810(c)(1)`, if filed within `1 year` of the rating grant establishing SC for the underlying disability, VA pays the prior benefit year retroactively!)*. Under `Pub. L. 117-328, Div. U, § 201`, once approved for static devices/skin medications, annual clothing allowances **renew automatically each year** without re-filing!

blocks.text: Program 4: Retroactive P&T Unlocks for Ch. 35 DEA (§ 3.807, § 21.4131) & CHAMPVA (§ 1781)

items:
**The `1-Year` Post-Notice Election Goldmine for Retroactive `Ch. 35` DEA (`38 C.F.R. § 21.4131(d)` / `(f)`):**
• Suppose a veteran wins a `100%` `P&T` (or `TDIU P&T`) appeal in `2026` with an effective date of `2018`, and their spouse or child attended college/trade school between `2018` and `2025`.
• If each dependent files **`VA Form 22-5490` within `1 year` of the date of VA's `P&T` notification letter**, `38 C.F.R. § 21.4131` lets them elect a **retroactive `Ch. 35` DEA commencing date all the way back to the `2018` `P&T` effective date**—generating up to `36` (`45` pre-Aug. 1, 2018) months of lump-sum tax-free stipends (**`$35,000–$55,000+` per dependent**)! Missing the `1-year` post-notice window caps DEA retroactivity to at most `1 year` prior to receipt of `22-5490`!
• **No `Age-26` / `10-Year` Expiration Post-Aug. 1, 2023 (`Pub. L. 117-328, Div. U, § 234`; `38 U.S.C. § 3512(g)`):** Dependents who first become eligible, turn `18`, or finish high school **on or after August 1, 2023** have **zero delimiting-date expiration or age-26 cutoff**!
• **Helpless Child Sequencing Warning (`38 U.S.C. § 3562`; `38 C.F.R. § 21.3023`):** Never let a disabled `18–23` child cash a `Ch. 35` DEA payment *before* securing `38 C.F.R. § 3.356` helpless-child status—an adjudicated `§ 3.356` helpless child receives `Ch. 35` DEA **concurrently** with dependency/DIC (`§ 21.3023(b)`), whereas a non-`§ 3.356` schoolchild triggers an **irrevocable lifetime bar** to schoolchild dependency/DIC upon negotiating their first DEA payment (`§ 21.3023(c)(1)`; see [Part 3 Historical Diff: Surviving Spouse Marriage Validity, Multi-Era Remarriage Cutoffs (§ 3.55) & Helpless Child Status (§ 3.356)](/cfr/modules/survivor-marriage-dependency-evolution))!

**Retroactive `CHAMPVA` Medical Reimbursement (`38 U.S.C. § 1781`; `38 C.F.R. §§ 17.271–17.276`):**
• Non-TRICARE-eligible spouses and children of `100%` `P&T` veterans should file **`VA Form 10-10d`** immediately upon receipt of the `P&T` award, then submit **`VA Form 10-7959a`** with itemized provider bills/EOBs from the entire retroactive `P&T` period to recover out-of-pocket hospital, surgical, deductible, and prescription payments!

blocks.text: 4. Postconditions: Effective Dates, Offsets & § 5904 Fee Structuring

items:
**Attorney Fees on Denied Ancillary & VHA Appeals (`38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(1)`; `38 C.F.R. § 14.636`):**
• Initial preparation of `VA Form 26-4555`, `21-4502`, `10-8678`, `22-5490`, or `21-0304` before an initial AOJ/VHA decision is **pro bono (`$0` fee)**.
• Once VBA, Loan Guaranty, or VHA (`PSAS` Clothing Allowance / `CHAMPVA`) issues an **initial denial** (or under-evaluates a `Ch. 18` Spina Bifida level at Level `I` instead of Level `III`), a compliant `§ 5904` contingency fee agreement (`<= 20%` standard reasonable presumption) attaches to post-decision AMA Supplemental (`20-0995`), HLR (`20-0996`), or Board (`10182`) review!

**Direct-Pay (`§ 5904(d)`) Disbursement Nuance:**
• While VBA withholds `20%` direct-pay fees from cash lump-sum compensation, `Ch. 18`, and `Ch. 35` DEA back pay paid to the claimant, **VHA `PSAS` Clothing Allowances** are disbursed through VHA fiscal channels without automated `VBMS` fee withholding, and **`Ch. 39` Auto (`21-4502`) / `Ch. 21` `SAH` (`26-4555`)** funds are paid to auto dealers, escrow agents, or construction builders rather than as unrestricted cash back pay to the veteran. Draft fee agreements explicitly excluding third-party vendor/escrow disbursements where required (or relying on **CAVC `EAJA` fees (`28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)`)** on judicial remand of denied `SAH`/`Auto`/`Clothing` appeals!).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Overlooked Housing, Vehicle, Clothing & Family Grants: SAH Home Adaptation, Auto Grants, Multiple Clothing Allowances, Retroactive DEA & Spina Bifida
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: When a Veteran reaches severe disability tiers—such as 100% Permanent and Total (P&T), Loss of Use of a hand or foot, severe balance/locomotion impairment, blindness, or severe burns—monthly compensation is only part of what Congress authorized. High-dollar 'ancillary' benefits are frequently left off VA rating decisions unless someone checks for them: Specially Adapted Housing (SAH / SHA, Chapter 21) grants to build or remodel an accessible home, Chapter 39 Automobile & Adaptive Equipment grants, MULTIPLE annual VA Clothing Allowances (§ 3.810) when more than one brace/prosthetic or prescription skin cream ruins your clothes, retroactive Chapter 35 Dependents' Educational Assistance (DEA) and CHAMPVA health care for spouses and children, and Chapter 18 benefits for biological children with spina bifida (or covered birth defects of female Vietnam Veterans).
record_clues: A 100% P&T or SMC Rating Code Sheet that makes no mention of Chapter 35 DEA (§ 3.807), CHAMPVA, Specially Adapted Housing (§§ 3.809–3.809a), or Automobile/Adaptive Equipment (§ 3.808).

VA Prosthetics or C&P notes showing regular reliance on braces (AFOs/KAFOs), crutches, canes, walkers, or a wheelchair for bilateral lower-extremity or balance conditions (Jensen v. Shulkin SAH standard).

A prior VA automobile purchase grant paid 30+ years ago (eligible for a second vehicle grant starting January 5, 2023 under the AUTO for Veterans Act, Pub. L. 117-333!), or hip/knee ankylosis qualifying for recurring adaptive equipment.

VA Prosthetics denying a Clothing Allowance (VA Form 10-8678) because a prescribed brace wasn't 'rigid,' or paying only ONE annual clothing allowance when multiple braces/wheelchairs/skin creams damage different garments (Sursely v. Peake).

A multi-year retroactive 100% P&T award where your spouse or college-aged children paid tuition while your appeal was pending—triggering a strict 1-year window to claim retroactive Chapter 35 DEA stipends (38 C.F.R. § 21.4131)!
important_cautions: Strict 1-Year Deadline for Retroactive Chapter 35 DEA (38 C.F.R. § 21.4131): When VA grants retroactive 100% P&T status covering past years in which your spouse or child attended college/training, they must file VA Form 22-5490 within 1 year of the P&T rating notice letter to capture multi-year retroactive DEA stipends.

Disabled Child Chapter 35 Election Trap (38 U.S.C. § 3562): Never have an 18-to-23 disabled child cash a Chapter 35 DEA check before adjudicating lifetime § 3.356 helpless-child status first, or schoolchild dependency can be permanently barred if § 3.356 fails.

Second Automobile Grant 10-Year vs. 30-Year Phase-In (Pub. L. 117-333): Between January 5, 2023 and January 4, 2033, a second Chapter 39 automobile purchase grant requires 30+ years since the prior grant; the 10-year recurring cycle opens on January 5, 2033 (though adaptive equipment has no one-vehicle limit).

Chapter 18 Spina Bifida Statutory Scope: Chapter 18 excludes spina bifida occulta (§ 1802) and currently covers qualifying herbicide service in Vietnam, the Korean DMZ, and Thailand (January 9, 1962 – May 7, 1975)—the 2022 PACT Act did not add Laos, Cambodia, or Guam to Chapter 18.
questions_for_representative: Since my 100% P&T award was backdated, are we within the 1-year window under 38 C.F.R. § 21.4131 for my spouse or college-aged children to claim retroactive Chapter 35 DEA education benefits?

Do my braces, assistive mobility devices, Loss of Use, blindness, or burn injuries qualify me for a Chapter 21 Specially Adapted Housing (SAH/SHA) grant (Jensen v. Shulkin) or Chapter 39 Auto/Adaptive Equipment?

Do I use multiple orthopedic appliances, prosthetics, or prescription skin creams that damage separate articles of clothing—qualifying for multiple annual Clothing Allowances under 38 C.F.R. § 3.810 (Sursely v. Peake)?
Did I receive a VA automobile grant more than 30 years ago that now qualifies me for a second vehicle grant under Pub. L. 117-333?

title: Playbook 14: Secondary Service Connection (§ 3.310(a)), Incremental Aggravation (§ 3.310(b) / Ward v. Wilkie), Medication Side Effects & The Obesity Intermediate Step (VAOPGCPREC 1-2017 / Walsh)
keyPrecedents: Allen v. Brown, 7 Vet. App. 439 (1995) (en banc)
cFileTriggers: C&P opinion or BVA decision denying § 3.310(b) secondary aggravation for lack of 'permanent worsening' or 'permanent increase beyond natural progression' (violates Ward v. Wilkie, 31 Vet. App. 233 (2019))

Veteran with SC orthopedic pain, lumbar/knee immobility, PTSD/MDD, or psychotropic/corticosteroid therapy denied secondary Obstructive Sleep Apnea (DC 6847), Hypertension (DC 7101), or Diabetes Mellitus Type II (DC 7913) where BMI >= 30 / weight gain appears in VAMC vitals (Garner / Walsh / VAOPGCPREC 1-2017 trigger)

VAMC Pharmacy (CAPRI/VistA) chronic prescriptions for NSAIDs (meloxicam, ibuprofen, naproxen), SSRIs/SNRIs (sertraline, fluoxetine, venlafaxine), atypical antipsychotics, corticosteroids, or opioids without secondary claims for GERD (DC 7206), CKD (DC 7530), Erectile Dysfunction (DC 7522 + SMC(k)), TMJ/bruxism, or DMII

C&P examiner refusing to address § 3.310(b) baseline severity by writing 'cannot determine baseline without resort to mere speculation' without exhausting clinical/lay history (violates El-Amin, Jones, and Sharp)

Service-connected above-knee amputation (or bilateral above-ankle amputations) with uncompensated ischemic heart disease or hypertension (automatic SC under 38 C.F.R. § 3.310(c)), or SC TBI (DC 8045) followed by Parkinsonism, seizures, dementia, depression, or pituitary deficiency (automatic SC under 38 C.F.R. § 3.310(d))
killSwitches: Filing a standalone claim for 'obesity' as a primary or secondary rated disability — obesity per se is not a 'disease or injury' under §§ 1110/1131 and functions strictly as an unrated 'intermediate step' in a § 3.310 causal/aggravation chain (VAOPGCPREC 1-2017)

Assuming a secondary service connection grant under § 3.310 inherits the primary disability's effective date or qualifies for the 1-year increased-rating lookback of 38 U.S.C. § 5110(b)(2) / 38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2) — squarely barred by Ellington v. Peake, 541 F.3d 1364 (Fed. Cir. 2008) and Ross v. Peake, 21 Vet. App. 528 (2008)

Filing a CUE motion against a final pre-June 2019 RO/BVA decision based on Ward v. Wilkie, or against a final pre-Feb. 2020 decision based on Walsh v. Wilkie — judicial reinterpretations are barred from CUE by George v. McDonough, 596 U.S. 740 (2022) and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e) (use Supplemental Claim, § 3.156(b), or Hamill AMA non-finality instead)

Citing withdrawn/invalidated VAOPGCPREC 7-99 as barring secondary SC for PTSD/pain-induced alcohol or drug abuse (invalidated by Allen v. Principi, 237 F.3d 1368 (Fed. Cir. 2001) and superseded by 71 FR 52747)

Citing VA's unfinalized proposed Sleep Apnea rule (RIN 2900-AQ72, 87 FR 8474 / 89 FR 74162 — proposed, not finalized) or VA's rescinded Feb. 17, 2026 § 4.10 medication Interim Final Rule (91 FR 7118, rescinded Feb. 27, 2026 at 91 FR 9712) as active law

blocks.text: In law-firm disability practice, **secondary service connection (`38 C.F.R. § 3.310`)** is the single most reliable engine for transforming low-rated orthopedic or mental-health awards (`10%–30%`) into `100%` schedular, `TDIU` (`§ 4.16`), Statutory Housebound **`SMC(s)`** (`§ 1114(s)`), and Creative-Organ **`SMC(k)`** (`§ 1114(k)`) entitlements. Under `§ 3.310(a)`, a disability that is proximately due to, the result of, or aggravated (`§ 3.310(b)`) by a service-connected disease or injury **"shall be service connected" and "considered a part of the original condition"** for compensation entitlement.

lines: **Single Source of Truth & Orthogonal Links:** Do not duplicate multi-paragraph regulatory text in pleadings without checking the exact CFR edition in force on the rating date. Consult [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 3.310(a)–(d) (Secondary Service Connection, Aggravation of Nonservice-Connected Disabilities, Amputation Cardiovascular Presumption & TBI Secondary Illnesses)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.310-secondary-aggravation-evolution) for verbatim pre- and post-October 10, 2006 text of `38 C.F.R. § 3.310(a)–(d)` (`71 FR 52744`, `78 FR 76196`). Pair this playbook with the [Direct SC, Soundness & Aggravation Treatise](/docs/service-connection-direct-soundness-aggravation), the [`VAOPGCPREC` Master Digest](/docs/vaopgcprec-index), [Playbook 11](/playbooks/11-guard-reserve-adt-iadt-and-line-of-duty) (*Allen* secondary substance abuse), [Playbook 17](/playbooks/17-section-1151-va-malpractice-and-ftca-interplay) (`§ 1151` secondary chains), and the [Master SMC Treatise](/docs/smc-complete-treatise-and-step-math).

blocks.text: 1. Preconditions: VBMS / VHA Pharmacy, Vitals & Code-Sheet Audit

Before drafting a `VA Form 21-526EZ`, `20-0995` Supplemental Claim, or private Independent Medical Opinion (`IMO`) instruction letter, extract four datasets from the VBMS eFolder and VHA `CAPRI`/`VistA` (`Blue Button`) clinical chart ([VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon)):

items: **Active Primary SC Anchor (`Rating Code Sheet`):** Confirm at least one already-service-connected (or concurrently claimed) disability—including any **`38 U.S.C. § 1151`** disability, which supports full `§ 3.310` secondary service connection under binding **[`VAOPGCPREC 8-97`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index) (`62 FR 15567`, Feb. 11, 1997)**!

**VHA Longitudinal Vitals (`BMI` & Blood Pressure Trajectory):** Pull chronological VAMC weight/`BMI` readings (`BMI >= 30.0` clinical obesity; `25.0–29.9` overweight intermediate progression) alongside orthopedic flare-ups, surgeries, PTSD/MDD onset, and sleep-study (`PSG` / CPAP `DC 6847`), `HbA1c` (`DC 7913`), or blood-pressure (`DC 7101`) diagnoses.

**VHA Active & Historical Medication Ledger (`Pharmacy Outpatient Profile`):** Map every chronic medication prescribed to treat an SC disability (dosage, start date, duration) against downstream organ, metabolic, dental, or sexual-dysfunction diagnoses.

**Prior Negative Secondary C&P Addenda:** Screen every prior negative VA medical opinion for **three classic legal errors**:
• Addressing **only direct causation (`§ 3.310(a)`)** while ignoring **aggravation (`§ 3.310(b)`)** (*El-Amin v. Shinseki*, `26 Vet. App. 136 (2013)`);
• Demanding **"permanent worsening"** or **"worsening beyond natural progression"** in a `§ 3.310(b)` opinion (*Ward v. Wilkie*, `31 Vet. App. 233 (2019)`); or
• Dismissing obesity as *"merely a lifestyle/metabolic risk factor, not an SC disease"* without analyzing the `VAOPGCPREC 1-2017` / *Walsh* / *Garner* intermediate chain!

blocks.text: 2. Bitemporal Pathway Gate (George v. McDonough & Regulatory Effective Dates)

Because `38 C.F.R. § 3.310` combines decades-old en banc judicial rules (*Allen v. Brown*, `1995`), prospective regulatory presumptions (`§ 3.310(d)` TBI eff. `Jan. 16, 2014`), and modern CAVC reinterpretations (*Ward*, `2019`; *Walsh*, `2020`), select your finality vehicle strictly from this bitemporal table ([Procedural Vehicles Piercing Finality](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality)):

rows: **En Banc Secondary Aggravation (`Allen v. Brown`, `7 Vet. App. 439`)**
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** (`>= Mar. 17, 1995` for flatly refusing to recognize secondary aggravation as a legal theory)
Open appeal; `§ 3.156(b)` (*Lang*); or RO/Board CUE if undisputed record established SC aggravation and adjudicator held `§ 3.310` covered causation only.
**Incremental / Non-Permanent Aggravation (`Ward v. Wilkie`, `31 Vet. App. 233`)**
**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)** for pre-June 14, 2019 final decisions
**DO NOT file CUE on pre-June 2019 "no permanent worsening" denials!** File `VA Form 20-0995` Supplemental Claim with a *Ward*-compliant IMO, or check *Hamill* (`§ 5104(b)`) / `§ 3.156(b)`.
`1-2017` causation (`>= Jan. 6, 2017` undisputed record): CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive; **Pre-2020 *Walsh* aggravation of obesity: Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE)**
`VA Form 20-0995` Supplemental Claim + 3-link IMO (fastest path), active appeal (`0996`/`10182`/`CAVC`), or *Hamill* silent-omission audit if raised post-Feb. 19, 2019!
**Prime RO/Board CUE Sword!** If C-file/VAMC records (`Bell` post-July 21, 1992) showed qualifying SC amputation + IHD/HTN and rater denied nexus, file CUE!
**Prospective / Liberalizing Rule (§ 3.114)** (`38 C.F.R. § 3.114` 1-yr lookback to `Jan. 16, 2014` floor; CUE-safe for post-Jan. 16, 2014 denials ignoring `(d)`)
Supplemental Claim / `§ 3.114` audit (`>= Jan. 16, 2014` for presumptive shortcut; earlier dates require `§ 3.310(a)` medical nexus).
Direct `21-526EZ` / `20-0995` or CUE against any post-Feb. 11, 1997 refusal to grant secondary SC off a `§ 1151` disability.

blocks.text: 3. Merits Mechanics: Causation (§ 3.310(a)), *Ward* Aggravation (§ 3.310(b)), Medications & Obesity
A. § 3.310(a) Proximate Causation vs. § 3.310(b) Aggravation (*Wallin*, *Allen*, *Ward*, *El-Amin*)

items: **Tripartite Causation Test (`§ 3.310(a)` — *Wallin v. West*, `11 Vet. App. 509, 512 (1998)`):** Requires `(1)` a current disability; `(2)` a service-connected disability; and `(3)` medical evidence establishing a nexus (`>= 50%` probability) showing the secondary condition was **proximately due to or the result of** the SC condition (e.g., lumbar IVDS `DC 5243` -> bilateral sciatic radiculopathy `DC 8520`; right knee instability -> altered gait -> contralateral left knee/hip osteoarthritis).

**Mandatory Dual-Theory Duty (*El-Amin v. Shinseki*, `26 Vet. App. 136, 140–41 (2013)`):** Because `§ 3.310` encompasses *both* initial causation (`(a)`) and aggravation (`(b)`), a VA C&P examination that opines an SC disability *"did not cause"* a secondary condition—while failing to address whether the SC disability **aggravated** it—is **legally inadequate** whenever the record suggests potential worsening!

***Ward v. Wilkie*, `31 Vet. App. 233, 238–40 (2019)` — Death of the "Permanent Worsening" Myth:**
• Following *Allen v. Brown*, `7 Vet. App. 439, 448 (1995) (en banc)` and VA's October 10, 2006 rulemaking (`71 FR 52744, 52747`; verbatim text in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 3.310(a)–(d) (Secondary Service Connection, Aggravation of Nonservice-Connected Disabilities, Amputation Cardiovascular Presumption & TBI Secondary Illnesses)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.310-secondary-aggravation-evolution)), VA's `M21-1` manual and DBQ templates unlawfully instructed examiners that `§ 3.310(b)` aggravation required **"permanent worsening beyond natural progression."**
• In ***Ward v. Wilkie*, `31 Vet. App. 233 (2019)`**, the CAVC **invalidated the "permanent worsening" requirement**, holding that neither `38 U.S.C. § 1110` nor `38 C.F.R. § 3.310(a)–(b)` requires permanence: **ANY incremental, measurable additional disability (including recurrent/intermittent increases in pain or functional loss) above the non-service-connected baseline proximately caused by an SC condition is compensable!**

**Baseline Severity Mechanics & Defeating Lazy *"Jones Speculation"* Cop-Outs (`§ 3.310(b)`):**
• Under `38 C.F.R. § 3.310(b)`, the pre-aggravation **baseline level of severity** is established by medical evidence created before the onset of aggravation or by the **earliest medical evidence created at any time between the onset of aggravation and the receipt of medical evidence establishing the current severity** of the NSC condition. VA deducts that baseline *only* if it is ascertainable; if baseline severity was `0%` / sub-compensable, full schedular compensation applies.
• **Attacking *"Cannot Speculate on Baseline"* C&P Opinions:** Examiners routinely try to dodge `§ 3.310(b)` by stating *"I cannot determine baseline severity or separate natural progression without resorting to mere speculation."* Under ***Jones v. Shinseki*, `23 Vet. App. 382, 390 (2010)`** and ***Sharp v. Shulkin*, `29 Vet. App. 26, 33–36 (2017)`**, that excuse is **legally invalid** unless the examiner `(i)` reviewed **all procurable clinical and lay evidence** (including spouse/veteran testimony of pre- vs. post-onset symptom frequency), `(ii)` explains **specifically what data is missing**, and `(iii)` demonstrates that the limitation reflects the **limits of medical science at large** rather than the examiner's personal failure to analyze the history!

blocks.text: B. High-Yield Medication Side-Effect Chains & *Ingram v. Collins* (2025–2026)

Disability caused or aggravated by **medications prescribed to treat a service-connected condition** is compensable under `38 C.F.R. § 3.310(a)–(b)` on the exact same footing as direct anatomical causation:

rows: **GERD (`DC 7206`)**, **Peptic/Duodenal Ulcer (`DC 7304–7305`)**, **Chronic Kidney Disease / Renal Dysfunction (`DC 7530` — up to `60%–100%`!)**, upper GI bleeding/anemia (`DC 7700`). *(Note May 19, 2024 Digestive VASRD overhaul at `89 FR 19735`—see [VASRD Historical Diff: TDIU (§ 4.16), May 2024 Digestive (§ 4.114) & Pending Sleep Apnea/Tinnitus Proposals](/cfr/modules/tdiu-digestive-respiratory-diffs)).*

**Erectile Dysfunction (`DC 7522` `0%` + statutory `SMC(k)` `~$139+/mo` creative-organ add-on!)** or **Female Sexual Arousal Disorder (`FSAD` + `SMC(k)`)**; **Bruxism / Secondary TMJ Disorder (`DC 9905`)**; **Metabolic Syndrome / Weight Gain -> Obesity Intermediate Chain (`OSA`, `DMII`, `HTN`)**; **Tardive Dyskinesia**.

**Diabetes Mellitus Type II (`DC 7913`)** + tertiary diabetic peripheral neuropathy (`DC 8520`), nephropathy, retinopathy; **Hypertension (`DC 7101`)**; **Avascular Necrosis (`AVN` of femoral head -> hip replacement `DC 5054`!)**; **Osteoporosis**.

**Central or Mixed Sleep Apnea (`DC 6847`)** (respiratory drive depression & upper-airway hypotonia); **Opioid-Induced Bowel Dysfunction / Functional Constipation / IBS (`DC 7319`)**; **Daytime Sedation (`TDIU` vocational multiplier)**; **Hypogonadism / ED (`SMC(k)`)**.
**Erectile Dysfunction (`DC 7522` + `SMC(k)`)**; gout (`DC 5017` from thiazide hyperuricemia); chronic ACE-inhibitor cough/angioedema.

lines: **Medication Amelioration Quarantine (*Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)` & Rescinded `91 FR 7118`):** When evaluating the primary or secondary musculoskeletal/systemic disability itself, under ***Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)`**, raters and examiners **may NOT discount a veteran's disability rating based on the ameliorative symptom-masking effects of medication** unless the specific Diagnostic Code explicitly incorporates medication into its rating criteria! Quarantined Alert: VA's reactive February 17, 2026 `38 C.F.R. § 4.10` Interim Final Rule (`91 FR 7118`) attempting to overturn *Ingram* was **formally rescinded 10 days later on February 27, 2026 (`91 FR 9712`)** ([Authority Hierarchy, Temporal Versioning Policy & Citation Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)). Audit any rating decision issued in February 2026 that cited the rescinded `91 FR 7118` IFR!

blocks.text: C. The Three-Link Obesity Intermediate-Step Chain (VAOPGCPREC 1-2017, *Walsh* & *Garner*)

Under binding **[`VAOPGCPREC 1-2017`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index) (Jan. 6, 2017; `84 FR 13755`)**, while obesity *per se* is not a standalone ratable "disease or injury" under `38 U.S.C. §§ 1110, 1131`, **obesity is a valid "intermediate step" establishing secondary service connection under `38 C.F.R. § 3.310`**! Two subsequent precedential CAVC decisions dramatically expanded its reach:

items: ***Walsh v. Wilkie*, `32 Vet. App. 300, 306–08 (2020)`:** Held that `VAOPGCPREC 1-2017` is **not limited to cases where an SC condition *initially caused* obesity**—VA **must equally adjudicate whether the SC condition *aggravated* preexisting overweight/obesity** as the intermediate link!

***Garner v. Tran*, `33 Vet. App. 241, 247–50 (2021)`:** Held that VA and the Board **must address the obesity intermediate-step theory** whenever it is explicitly argued **OR reasonably raised by the record**—identifying three classic record triggers: `(1)` orthopedic/pain-induced immobility or reduced exercise capacity; `(2)` psychiatric symptoms (PTSD/MDD anhedonia, hyperphagia/binge eating, inability to sustain diet/exercise); and `(3)` weight-gain side effects of SC medications!

blocks.text: Exact Three-Link Proof Blueprint for Your Private IMO (VAOPGCPREC 1-2017 + *Walsh*)

Instruct every medical expert drafting an obesity-chain nexus opinion (for **Obstructive Sleep Apnea `DC 6847`**, **Hypertension `DC 7101`**, **Type II Diabetes `DC 7913`**, **GERD `DC 7206`**, or **weight-bearing hip/knee/ankle degeneration**) to address **all three links explicitly**:

items: **Link 1 (Primary SC -> Obesity Causation or Aggravation):** The veteran's service-connected disability(ies) (e.g., lumbar spine/knee orthopedic exercise intolerance, PTSD/MDD emotional eating and cortisol dysregulation, hypothyroidism, or `SSRI`/`quetiapine`/`gabapentin`/`prednisone` pharmacotherapy) *at least as likely as not* **caused OR aggravated** the veteran's obesity (cite objective VAMC `BMI` climb from `X` to `Y` following SC injury/Rx).

**Link 2 (Obesity -> Target Disability Substantial Factor):** The obesity was a **substantial factor** in **causing OR aggravating** (`Ward` incremental worsening!) the target secondary disability (e.g., pharyngeal fat-pad deposition and reduced lung volume narrowing the upper airway in `OSA DC 6847`; insulin resistance in `DMII DC 7913`; neurohormonal/sympathetic activation in `HTN DC 7101`).

**Link 3 ("But-For" Proximate Nexus):** The target secondary disability **would not have occurred—or, under *Walsh* and *Ward*, would not have worsened to the same degree—but for** the service-connected disability's causation or aggravation of the veteran's obesity!

lines: **Quarantine Watchlist — Proposed Sleep Apnea Rule (`RIN 2900-AQ72`):** VA published a **proposed (unfinalized)** rule in February 2022 (`87 FR 8474`, `RIN 2900-AQ72`; supplemental notice `89 FR 74162`, Sept. 2024) proposing to restrict `50%` CPAP ratings under `DC 6847`. **That proposed rule has NOT been finalized**—current `38 C.F.R. § 4.97, DC 6847` (`50%` for medically required breathing assistance device such as CPAP) **remains binding active law**, and filing an ITF (`VA Form 21-0966`) / `21-526EZ` / `20-0995` now locks in grandfathering protection under `38 U.S.C. § 1155` and *Karnas v. Derwinski*!

blocks.text: 4. Statutory/Regulatory Secondary Presumptions & Special Chains

items:
**Secondary Alcohol / Substance-Use Disorder & Organic Sequelae (*Allen v. Principi*, `237 F.3d 1368 (Fed. Cir. 2001)`):**
• While `38 U.S.C. §§ 105(a), 1110` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.301(d)` bar *primary* direct service connection for willful-misconduct alcohol or drug abuse, the Federal Circuit in ***Allen v. Principi*, `237 F.3d 1368, 1376–81 (Fed. Cir. 2001)`** (invalidating `VAOPGCPREC 7-99` and codified in `38 C.F.R. § 3.310(a)–(b)` at `71 FR 52747`) held that **alcohol or substance-use disorder caused or aggravated by an SC disability (e.g., self-medication of SC PTSD, MDD, or chronic orthopedic pain) IS compensable as part of the primary condition AND unlocks secondary service connection (and `§ 1310` DIC!) for all downstream organic sequelae**: hepatic cirrhosis (`DC 7312`), hepatocellular carcinoma, chronic pancreatitis (`DC 7347`), alcoholic peripheral neuropathy, gastritis, and cardiomyopathy ([Playbook 11](/playbooks/11-guard-reserve-adt-iadt-and-line-of-duty)).

**Automatic Amputation -> Cardiovascular Presumption (`38 C.F.R. § 3.310(c)`):**
• Enacted at **`44 FR 50339, 50340` (Aug. 28, 1979)**: **Ischemic heart disease or other cardiovascular disease** (including hypertension, `DC 7101`, arteriosclerosis, `DC 7005`, cardiomyopathy) developing in a veteran who has a service-connected amputation of **one lower extremity at or above the knee** OR service-connected amputations of **both lower extremities at or above the ankles** *"shall be held to be the proximate result of the service-connected amputation or amputations"*—**zero medical nexus opinion required**!

blocks.text: 5. Invariants / Kill-Switches & Postconditions (Effective-Date Traps & Ancillary Unlocks)
A. Fatal Invariants / Kill-Switches

items:
**The *Ellington* / *Ross* Secondary Effective-Date Trap (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)` vs. `§ 5110(b)(2)`):** Under ***Ellington v. Peake*, `541 F.3d 1364, 1369–70 (Fed. Cir. 2008)`**, ***Ross v. Peake*, `21 Vet. App. 528, 532–35 (2008)`**, and ***Roper v. Nicholson*, `20 Vet. App. 173, 180–81 (2006)`**, although `§ 3.310(a)` states a secondary disability is *"considered a part of the original condition,"* a secondary service-connection claim is an **original/supplemental claim for a separate disability—NOT an "increased rating" claim**! Therefore:
• It does **NOT** inherit the primary disability's earlier effective date; and
• It does **NOT** receive the `1-year` pre-claim lookback of `38 U.S.C. § 5110(b)(2)` / `38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2)`!
• **How to Capture Earlier Secondary Effective Dates Lawfully:** Audit the C-file for `(a)` an **earlier pre-March 24, 2015 informal claim** (`former § 3.155(a)` / *Shea v. Wilkie*, `926 F.3d 1362 (Fed. Cir. 2019)`) or `VA Form 21-526EZ` pointing to VAMC notes of the secondary symptom; `(b)` **sympathetic scope (`Clemons`)** where a neurological/psychiatric/orthopedic symptom was part of a pending primary appeal; or `(c)` **AMA silent omission (`§ 5104(b)` / *Hamill v. Collins*, `166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. 2026)`)** ([Playbook 04](/playbooks/04-unadjudicated-tdiu-informal-claims-smc)).

**Anti-Pyramiding Check (`38 C.F.R. § 4.14` & `§ 4.130`):** Secondary mental disorders (`MDD`/`anxiety` secondary to orthopedic pain) merge into a **single combined `§ 4.130` mental-health evaluation** if the veteran already holds SC PTSD—though adding secondary somatic/depressive symptoms frequently pushes a `30%–50%` mental rating up to `70%` or `100%` + `TDIU`!

blocks.text: B. Postconditions & Downstream Multipliers
Upon granting secondary SC under `§ 3.310(a)–(d)`, immediately audit ([`SMC & Ancillary Audit Worksheet`](/checklists/smc-and-ancillary-audit-worksheet)):

items: **`SMC(k)` (`§ 1114(k)`):** Mandatory inferred add-on for `SSRI`/antihypertensive/diabetic/prostate **Erectile Dysfunction (`DC 7522`)**, `FSAD`, or severe secondary peripheral neuropathy causing **foot-drop / functional loss of use of a foot or hand** (*Payne v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 85 (1990)`).

**`SMC(s)` (`§ 1114(s)`) & *Barry* Intermediate Steps:** Secondary `OSA` (`50%`), `GERD`, radiculopathy (`20%+20%` bilateral), or depression (`50%–70%`) routinely supplies the **`>= 60%` independent combined rating** needed to unlock Statutory Housebound **`SMC(s)`** atop a `100%` schedular or single-disability *Bradley* `TDIU` award—or additional `50%`/`100%` half-step and full-step bumps under ***Barry v. McDonough*, `101 F.4th 1348 (Fed. Cir. 2024)`** ([Playbook 12](/playbooks/12-aid-and-attendance-smc-l-r1-r2-and-smc-t))!

**Survivor `§ 1310` Direct/Contributory DIC:** Secondary `OSA`, `IHD` (`§ 3.310(c)`), `DMII`, renal failure, and *Allen* cirrhosis are leading causes of death that unlock lifetime tax-free survivor **DIC (`38 U.S.C. § 1310`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.312`)** even when the veteran had NOT held `100%` P&T for 10 years under `§ 1318` ([Playbook 08](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical))!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Secondary Conditions, Incremental Aggravation, Medication Side Effects & Weight Gain as an Intermediate Link
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Service connection does not stop with the injury that happened in uniform. Under 38 C.F.R. § 3.310, a new health condition is compensated as service-connected if an already service-connected disability—or the prescription medication used to treat it—either caused the new condition (§ 3.310(a)) or aggravated a non-service-connected condition above its baseline level (§ 3.310(b)). Under Ward v. Wilkie, secondary aggravation includes any measurable or incremental additional disability without requiring 'permanent worsening.' In addition, when service-connected pain, limited mobility, mental health symptoms, or medications contribute to weight gain/obesity that in turn causes or aggravates conditions like sleep apnea, hypertension, or Type 2 diabetes, obesity can serve as a valid intermediate link in the causal chain (VAOPGCPREC 1-2017; Walsh v. Wilkie).
record_clues: A VA exam or denial letter rejecting secondary aggravation because there was 'no permanent worsening' of an underlying condition (conflicting with Ward v. Wilkie).

VA medical center vital signs showing weight gain or Body Mass Index (BMI) of 30 or higher alongside service-connected knee/back pain, PTSD, depression, or weight-inducing medications, paired with obstructive sleep apnea, hypertension, or diabetes.

Long-term VA or private pharmacy records for anti-inflammatory pain relievers (NSAIDs), antidepressants (SSRIs/SNRIs), corticosteroids, or opioids alongside acid reflux/GERD, chronic kidney disease, erectile dysfunction, or jaw clenching.

A service-connected lower-limb amputation at or above the knee (or both ankles) followed by heart disease (§ 3.310(c)), or service-connected Traumatic Brain Injury followed by Parkinsonism, seizures, dementia, depression, or pituitary hormone deficiency (§ 3.310(d)).
important_cautions: Obesity itself is not assigned a standalone VA disability percentage; rather, under VAOPGCPREC 1-2017 it functions strictly as an intermediate step linking a service-connected disability to a ratable secondary condition such as sleep apnea or diabetes.

Effective dates for newly claimed secondary conditions generally run from the date of the secondary claim or Intent to File—they do not automatically inherit the primary disability's original effective date or the 1-year increased-rating lookback of 38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2) (Ellington v. Peake).

Under George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e), later judicial clarifications like Ward v. Wilkie (2019) or Walsh v. Wilkie (2020) apply to open claims and Supplemental Claims, not Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) motions attacking older final decisions.

Beware of unfinalized or rescinded rules: VA's sleep apnea proposal (RIN 2900-AQ72, 87 FR 8474) remains a proposed rule that is not enacted law, and VA's February 17, 2026 medication rule (91 FR 7118) was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712).
questions_for_representative: Do my pharmacy and treatment records support a secondary claim—either through direct causation or incremental aggravation under 38 C.F.R. § 3.310(a)–(b)—for side effects of my service-connected medications?

If service-connected orthopedic pain, limited exercise capacity, or mental health symptoms contributed to weight gain before I developed sleep apnea, diabetes, or high blood pressure, what medical nexus evidence should we gather for an intermediate-step claim?
Did a prior VA examiner improperly demand 'permanent worsening' or refuse to estimate my pre-aggravation baseline severity?

Do any automatic secondary rules apply to my case, such as cardiovascular conditions after qualifying lower-extremity amputations (§ 3.310(c)) or neurological/endocrine conditions after TBI (§ 3.310(d))?
