blocks.text: Modern Southwest Asia, post-9/11, and occupational toxic-exposure litigation turns on **three legally distinct statutory engines** that VA examiners and Regional Office (`AOJ`) raters routinely conflate:

items: **Engine 1 (`38 U.S.C. § 1117`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.317`):** **Undiagnosed Illnesses & Medically Unexplained Chronic Multisymptom Illnesses (`MUCMIs`)** + `9` infectious diseases (`6-month` chronicity, **zero nexus required**; pre-Aug. 10, 2022 `10%` floor superseded eff. Aug. 10, 2022 by `Pub. L. 117-168, § 405(a)` `"to any degree at any time"`!).

**Engine 2 (`38 U.S.C. §§ 1119–1120`; `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.320, 3.320a, 3.320b`):** **Burn Pit & Particulate Matter (`PM2.5`) Presumptive Cancers & Respiratory/Hematologic Diseases** (`0%` floor, **zero manifestation deadline**, **zero nexus required**).

**Engine 3 (`38 U.S.C. §§ 1168 & 5103A(d)(2)`):** **Non-Presumptive Toxic Exposure Risk Activity (`TERA`) Direct Causation** (mandatory `ILER` audit + synergistic `§ 1168(a)` medical nexus opinion governed by `38 U.S.C. § 5107(b)` equipoise).

blocks.text: *(Cross-references: [`Part 3 Toxic, Gulf War, PACT & § 1151 Evolution Diff`](/cfr/modules/toxic-gulf-pact-1151-evolution); [Playbook 06 (*Nehmer* Exclusions & *Soto* CRSC)](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc); [Playbook 07 (`§§ 3.309(a)–(d)`, ALS, Radiation & Camp Lejeune)](/playbooks/07-statutory-presumptions-chronic-tropical-pow-als); [Playbook 08 (Survivor DIC & `§ 1305` PACT Re-Evaluations)](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical); [Playbook 03 (`§ 3.156(c)` Service Records)](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c); [Playbook 11 (Guard/Reserve `ADT`/`IADT` Exposure)](/playbooks/11-guard-reserve-adt-iadt-and-line-of-duty); [2019–2026 AMA & PACT Era Lens](/eras/2019-2026-ama-pact-modern-era); [May 2024 Digestive & Respiratory VASRD Diffs](/cfr/modules/tdiu-digestive-respiratory-diffs); [Master `VAOPGCPREC` Digest](/docs/vaopgcprec-index); [VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon); and [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).*
1. Preconditions: VBMS, Deployment & ILER Audit Triggers
Pull the complete VBMS eFolder and screen these exact records before selecting a pleading track:

items:
**Qualifying Deployment & Exposure Proof:**
• **`DD Form 214` / `DD Form 215`**, Guard/Reserve **`Title 10` mobilization orders** ([Playbook 11](/playbooks/11-guard-reserve-adt-iadt-and-line-of-duty)), **`DA Form 2-1`**, flight logs, ship deck logs (Persian Gulf, Red Sea, Arabian Sea, Gulf of Aden, Gulf of Oman), Hostile Fire / Imminent Danger Pay (`HFP`/`IDP`) LES entries, Post-Deployment Health Assessments (**`DD Form 2796`** / **`DD Form 2900` `PDHRA`**), and DoD Burn Pit Registry questionnaires.
• **VBMS `TERA` Memorandum & `ILER` (`Individual Longitudinal Exposure Record`) Extract:** Audit whether the RO generated the mandatory **Toxic Exposure Risk Activity (`TERA`) Memorandum** and queried `ILER` + the Defense Occupational and Environmental Health Readiness System (`DOEHRS`). Missing deployment locations (e.g., classified temporary duty at **Karshi-Khanabad (`K2`), Uzbekistan** or **Syria**) or omitted MOS chemical hazards make any downstream `§ 1168` medical opinion legally defective.

**High-Value C-File Audit Red Flags:**
• Prior denial of **IBS (`DC 7319`)**, **fibromyalgia (`DC 5025`)**, **CFS (`DC 6354`)**, or chronic multi-site joint/muscle pain/headaches/fatigue where the C&P examiner wrote *"less likely than not related to Gulf War service"* (*Gutierrez* / *Stewart* legal error!).
• Pre-August 10, 2022 denial of **asthma, chronic rhinitis, or chronic sinusitis** because symptoms manifested `> 10 years` after separation (`86 FR 42724` interim trap eliminated by `38 U.S.C. § 1120`!) or rated `0%` noncompensable (`10%` floor eliminated!).
• Post-2022 diagnosis of **leukemia, multiple myeloma, `MGUS`, `MDS`, myelofibrosis (`§ 3.320b`)**, **bladder/ureter cancer (`§ 3.320a`)**, or **urethral/paraurethral/male breast cancer (`89 FR 51224`)**.

blocks.text: 2. Bitemporal Pathway Gate (CUE vs. § 3.114 Liberalizing Floor vs. § 3.156(c))

rows: **Final pre-2022 RO/Board decision denied `§ 3.317` `MUCMI` (`IBS`, `CFS`, `fibromyalgia`) in a `1990+` Iraq/Kuwait/Saudi/Persian Gulf veteran solely for "lack of nexus" despite `>= 10%` severity for `>= 6` months**

**RO CUE (`§ 3.105(a)`) or Board CUE (`§ 7111`):** Demanding an etiological nexus for a listed `§ 3.317(a)(2)(i)(B)` `MUCMI` violated unambiguous extant regulation (*Gutierrez*, `19 Vet. App. at 8–9`)—not shielded by *George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)`.
**Living veteran granted a PACT Act `§ 1120` / `§§ 3.320–3.320b` presumptive condition (or Afghanistan `§ 1117(f)` `MUCMI`) after a final pre-Aug. 10, 2022 denial**

**Hard Statutory Floor (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(g)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)`):** *Nehmer* (`§ 3.816`) **does NOT apply** to `§ 1120` burn-pit presumptions! Presumptive back pay cannot predate **August 10, 2022** (for PACT Act; **Jan. 2, 2025** for `§ 3.320a`; **Jan. 10, 2025** for `§ 3.320b`) *unless* you win **direct SC** via newly associated `§ 3.156(c)` service records!
**Newly associated `DD-2796`, deployment orders, deck logs, or unit environmental records (`K2`, burn-pit proximity, MOS hazard logs) placed in file after a prior direct-SC denial**

**`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)` Reconsideration ([Playbook 03](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c)):** Pair newly associated official service records with a **direct `§ 1168` / `§ 3.303(a)` nexus IMO** to unlock an effective date back to the **original pre-2022 claim** (`§ 3.156(c)(3)`)—piercing the Aug. 10, 2022 PACT floor!
**Surviving spouse/child previously denied DIC before Aug. 10, 2022 where veteran's death is now covered by PACT Act (`§ 1120`, `§ 1117(f)`, `§§ 3.320a–3.320b`)**

**`38 U.S.C. § 1305` (`PACT Act § 204`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.33`) Re-Evaluation ([Playbook 08](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical)):** Unlike living veterans, previously denied DIC claimants receive retroactive DIC **all the way back to the original denied DIC claim**!

blocks.text: 3. Engine 1: Persian Gulf War Undiagnosed Illnesses & MUCMIs (38 U.S.C. § 1117; 38 C.F.R. § 3.317)
A. Geographic Scope & The Pre- vs. Post-PACT Afghanistan Trap

items: **Classic `§ 3.317(e)(2)` Southwest Asia Theater of Operations (`>= Aug. 2, 1990`):** Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, the neutral zone between Iraq and Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates (`UAE`), Oman, the Gulf of Aden, the Gulf of Oman, the Persian Gulf, the Arabian Sea, the Red Sea, and the airspace above these locations.

**PACT Act `§ 405` Statutory Expansion (`38 U.S.C. § 1117(f)`, eff. Aug. 10, 2022) vs. `38 C.F.R. § 3.317` Lag:**
• **Pre-August 10, 2022 Trap:** Prior to the PACT Act, **Afghanistan** was covered **only** under `38 C.F.R. § 3.317(c)` for `9` specific infectious diseases (`75 FR 59970`, Sept. 29, 2010: brucellosis, *Campylobacter jejuni*, Q fever, malaria, *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*, nontyphoid *Salmonella*, *Shigella*, visceral leishmaniasis, and West Nile virus)—**NOT** for `§ 3.317(a)` undiagnosed illnesses or `MUCMIs`!
• **On/After August 10, 2022 (`Pub. L. 117-168, § 405(b)`, `136 Stat. 1783`):** Congress enacted **`38 U.S.C. § 1117(f)`**, expanding `§ 1117` `MUCMI` and undiagnosed-illness eligibility (`>= Aug. 2, 1990` or `>= Sept. 11, 2001` as applicable) to active service in **Afghanistan, Israel, Egypt, Turkey, Syria, and Jordan**!
• **Statute Trumps Stale CFR Text (`0%` Floor + `6` New Countries + No Sunset):** Although VA's conforming revision to `38 C.F.R. § 3.317` (`89 FR 79815`, Oct. 1, 2024, `RIN 2900-AR75` — *proposed / not finalized*) lagged behind the statute—leaving stale `10 percent or more` and pre-PACT country text in `eCFR`—**positive statutory text in `38 U.S.C. § 1117(a)(1) & (f)` controls immediately from August 10, 2022**: `(a)` replacing the legacy `10%` manifestation threshold with **"became manifest to any degree at any time"** (`0%` floor!), `(b)` adding those `6` countries, and `(c)` **permanently abolishing the former December 31, 2026 manifestation sunset** (`87 FR 6038`)!

blocks.text: B. Qualifying § 3.317(a) Disabilities, Thresholds & Appellate Weapons
To establish presumptive service connection under `38 U.S.C. § 1117` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.317(a)(1)`:

items: **Severity & Chronicity Floor (Pre- vs. Post-Aug. 10, 2022 Trap):** Under `§ 3.317(a)(4)`, a qualifying chronic disability must have persisted for **`6 months` or more** without affirmative evidence attributing it to an intercurrent post-service cause (`§ 3.317(a)(7)`). **Watch the bitemporal `10%` trap:** for decisions prior to **August 10, 2022**, `38 U.S.C. § 1117(a)(1)` required manifestation to a **compensable degree of `10%` or more**; effective **August 10, 2022**, `Pub. L. 117-168, § 405(a)` amended `§ 1117(a)(1)` to cover disabilities manifesting **"to any degree at any time"**—making any post-Aug. 10, 2022 denial that relies on stale `eCFR` `§ 3.317(a)(1)(i)`'s `10%` threshold unlawful!

**Two Substantive Prongs (`§ 3.317(a)(2)(i)(A)` vs. `(B)`):**
• **Undiagnosed Illness (`§ 3.317(a)(2)(i)(A)`):** Objective or lay-observable chronic signs/symptoms (`§ 3.317(b)` — fatigue, skin symptoms, headache, muscle pain, joint pain, neurological signs, neuropsychological signs, upper/lower respiratory signs, sleep disturbances, GI signs, cardiovascular signs, abnormal weight loss, menstrual disorders) that cannot be attributed to any known clinical diagnosis.
• ***Joyner v. McDonald*, `766 F.3d 1393, 1395 (Fed. Cir. 2014)`:** **Pain alone** (such as chronic multi-joint, neck, or muscle pain without somatic pathology on imaging) qualifies as an undiagnosed illness under `§ 3.317`!
• **Medically Unexplained Chronic Multisymptom Illness (`MUCMI`, `§ 3.317(a)(2)(i)(B)`):** A **diagnosed** illness defined by a cluster of signs or symptoms without conclusive pathophysiology or etiology, **expressly including by law**:
• **Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (`CFS`, `DC 6354`)**;
• **Fibromyalgia (`DC 5025`)**; and
• **Functional Gastrointestinal Disorders (`FGIDs`)** (`76 FR 41696`, pub. July 15, 2011, **eff. Aug. 15, 2011**), including **Irritable Bowel Syndrome (`IBS`, `DC 7319` — up to `30%` under the May 19, 2024 Digestive VASRD `89 FR 19735`!)**, functional dyspepsia, functional vomiting, functional constipation, functional abdominal pain syndrome, and functional bloating (*excluding structural GI diseases like IBD/Crohn's, ulcerative colitis, or celiac disease*).

**Three Controlling Precedents That Destroy Defective `§ 3.317` Denials:**
• ***Gutierrez v. Principi*, `19 Vet. App. 1, 8–9 (2004)`:** A claimant under `§ 1117` / `§ 3.317` is **NEVER required to prove a medical nexus** to service or to a specific environmental toxin! Whenever a C&P examiner opines *"fibromyalgia/IBS is less likely than not caused by Gulf War service,"* the opinion is legally irrelevant and non-responsive—once service in a covered location and a `6-month` chronic diagnosis of `CFS`, `fibromyalgia`, or `IBS`/`FGID` (at `>= 10%` pre-Aug. 10, 2022, or to *any degree* `>= Aug. 10, 2022` under `§ 1117(a)(1)`) are shown, **entitlement is automatic by operation of law** (absent affirmative proof of an intercurrent supervening cause like traumatic abdominal surgery).
• ***Goodman v. Shulkin*, `870 F.3d 1383, 1386–88 (Fed. Cir. 2017)` & *Stewart v. Wilkie*, `30 Vet. App. 383, 390–93 (2018)`:** For conditions *outside* the three per se `MUCMI` categories, whether a diagnosed multisymptom illness has "inconclusive pathophysiology or etiology" is a **case-specific medical question**—an examiner cannot reject `MUCMI` status merely because *risk factors* exist if neither the exact etiology nor pathophysiology in *this veteran* is conclusive (*contrast conditions with partially understood pathology like diabetes, MS, or OSA excluded under `§ 3.317(a)(2)(ii)`—plead those under Engine 3 `§ 1168` TERA!*).

blocks.text: 4. Engine 2: Burn Pits, PM2.5 & PACT Act Presumptions (38 U.S.C. §§ 1119–1120; 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.320, 3.320a, 3.320b)
A. Two Covered Location & Date Windows (38 U.S.C. § 1119(c)(1))

items: **Window A (`On or after August 2, 1990`):** Active military, naval, air, or space service in **Bahrain, Iraq, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, or the United Arab Emirates (`UAE`)**, **plus the airspace above** any of those locations *(Note: unlike `§ 3.317(e)(2)`, `§ 1119(c)(1)(A)` omits surrounding open seas unless the servicemember entered territorial land/airspace—use `§ 1168` TERA for shipboard exhaust/incinerators on open seas!)*.

**Window B (`On or after September 11, 2001`):** Active military, naval, air, or space service in **Afghanistan, Djibouti, Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, or Uzbekistan** (explicitly covering **Karshi-Khanabad (`K2`) Air Base**), **plus the airspace above** any of those locations.

blocks.text: B. Complete Presumptive Disease Architecture (0% Floor & Zero Time Limit!)

Under **`38 U.S.C. § 1120(b)`** and **`38 C.F.R. §§ 3.320, 3.320a, 3.320b`** (`88 FR 60336`, pub. Sept. 1, 2023, **eff. Oct. 31, 2023**), Congress **eliminated both the `10%` severity floor and the `10-year` post-service manifestation cap** that had crippled VA's `2021` `PM2.5` interim rule (`86 FR 42724`). Even a **`0%` noncompensable diagnosis** (e.g., `0%` chronic rhinitis without polyps or `<50%` nasal obstruction under `DC 6522`) **must be granted service connection**, unlocking lifetime VHA health care, future increased ratings, and secondary service connection (`§ 3.310`, e.g., secondary obstructive sleep apnea `DC 6847`!).

rows: **11 Statutory Cancer Categories:** `(1)` Brain cancer; `(2)` Gastrointestinal cancer of any type; `(3)` **Glioblastoma**; `(4)` Head cancer of any type; `(5)` Kidney cancer; `(6)` Lymphoma of any type; `(7)` Melanoma; `(8)` Neck cancer of any type; `(9)` Pancreatic cancer; `(10)` **Reproductive cancer of any type**; `(11)` Respiratory (breathing-related) cancer of any type (absorbing the `9` rare respiratory cancers from `87 FR 24421`, Apr. 26, 2022).

Active cancer / treatment = **`100%`** (`6-month` post-treatment convalescence before mandatory C&P re-exam); **always audit residuals + `SMC(k)`** (`prostatectomy`, `orchiectomy`, `hysterectomy`, `>= 25%` breast tissue or radiation, `laryngectomy` aphonia)!

**12 Statutory Respiratory Diseases:** `(1)` **Asthma that was diagnosed after service**; `(2)` Chronic bronchitis; `(3)` Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (`COPD`); `(4)` Constrictive bronchiolitis or obliterative bronchiolitis; `(5)` Emphysema; `(6)` Granulomatous disease; `(7)` Interstitial lung disease (`ILD`); `(8)` Pleuritis; `(9)` Pulmonary fibrosis; `(10)` Sarcoidosis; `(11)` **Chronic sinusitis**; `(12)` **Chronic rhinitis**.

**Asthma Trap:** Statutory text says *"asthma that was diagnosed after service."* If asthma was diagnosed *in service*, claim **direct SC (`§ 3.303(a)`)**; if preexisting before service, claim **in-service aggravation (`§ 3.306`)**!

Added **urethral cancer**, **paraurethral gland cancer**, and *(from June 17, 2024 through Sept. 29, 2025)* **male breast cancer**. **CRITICAL SEPT. 30, 2025 REVERSAL TRAP:** Effective **September 30, 2025**, VA prospectively rescinded automatic sub-regulatory presumptive status for **male breast cancer** (grandfathering veterans already granted prior to Sept. 30, 2025).

**Post-Sept. 30, 2025 Male Breast Cancer Pleading Mandate:** Never concede VA's policy reversal! Plead **BOTH**: `(1)` statutory preservation that **breast cancer in males is a `'reproductive cancer of any type'` under plain text of `38 U.S.C. § 1120(b)(2)(H)`** (`Loper Bright` statutory-text challenge to VA's narrowing), **AND** `(2)` **direct `§ 1168` TERA nexus** backed by an oncologist IMO!
**Urinary bladder cancer** (including overlapping sites of the bladder) and **ureter cancer** (including ureteric orifice and urachus) for `§ 1119(c)` veterans.
Closes the genitourinary gap alongside kidney (`§ 1120(b)(2)(D)`) and urethral (`89 FR 51224`) cancers! (`§ 3.114` floor: **Jan. 2, 2025** unless direct TERA nexus proved).

**Acute leukemias**, **chronic leukemias** (incl. `CLL` / `CML`), **multiple myelomas (explicitly including `MGUS`!)**, **myelodysplastic syndromes (`MDS`)**, and **myelofibrosis** for `§ 1119(c)` `PM2.5`-exposed veterans.
Major hematologic breakthrough (`DC 7703, 7712, 7718, 7719`)! Note `MGUS` alone typically rates `0%` asymptomatic unless symptomatic/evolving into smoldering or overt multiple myeloma (`100%`).

blocks.text: 5. Engine 3: Non-Presumptive 38 U.S.C. § 1168 TERA Nexus Litigation

For *every* non-presumptive condition—such as **Obstructive Sleep Apnea (`OSA`, `DC 6847`)**, **hypertension** (in non-herbicide veterans), **autoimmune/neurological/hepatic/thyroid disorders**, or **CONUS/shipboard/MOS exposures**—PACT Act Section `303` enacted **`38 U.S.C. § 1168`** and **`38 U.S.C. § 5103A(d)(2)`**:
A. Triggering Mandatory § 1168(a) TERA Examinations Beyond Overseas Burn Pits

Whenever `(1)` the veteran has a current disability, `(2)` the record reflects participation in **any Toxic Exposure Risk Activity (`TERA`, `38 U.S.C. § 1710(e)(4)(C)`)**, and `(3)` record evidence is insufficient to grant outright, VA **must** order a medical examination and nexus opinion that **explicitly considers the total potential exposure through all applicable deployments AND the synergistic, combined effect of all toxic exposure risk activities** (`38 U.S.C. § 1168(a)(2)`):

items:
**High-Yield Occupational / CONUS `TERA` Pathways:**
• **PFAS / `AFFF` Aqueous Film-Forming Foam:** Military firefighters (`DoD` crash-rescue MOS), flight-deck crews, and airbases with documented `PFAS` groundwater plumes (linked to kidney/testicular cancer, thyroid disease, ulcerative colitis, dyslipidemia).
• **CONUS & Overseas Base Contamination:** **Fort McClellan, Alabama** (`PCBs` / Monsanto plume, chemical-corps training—no statutory presumption yet, making `§ 1168` + `ILER`/MOS proof essential!), **Camp Lejeune** non-presumptive conditions ([Playbook 07](/playbooks/07-statutory-presumptions-chronic-tropical-pow-als)), **George AFB / Kelly AFB / Wurtsmith AFB** (`TCE`/perchloroethylene degreasers).
• **Jet Fuels (`JP-8` / `JP-4` / `JP-5`), Solvents, Shipboard Asbestos (`VAOPGCPREC 4-2000`), Heavy Metals/Lead (indoor firing ranges / artillery / mechanics), & Depleted Uranium / Radar.**

**Narrow `§ 1168(b)` Exception:** VA may decline a `§ 1168(a)` exam **only** if it determines there is *no indication of an association* (e.g., pure acute orthopedic trauma or standalone `§ 4.130` psychiatric disorders without neurotoxicological/secondary linkage)—and VA **must submit a written report to Congress** justifying exemptions (`§ 1168(b)`).

blocks.text: B. Destroying Boilerplate Negative § 1168 C&P Opinions on Appeal

Contract C&P examiners routinely rubber-stamp negative `TERA` opinions citing generic `National Academies` (`NASEM`) tables and claiming *"scientific literature does not conclusively prove a causal link."* Attack these opinions on three precedential grounds (`VA Form 20-0996` HLR or `VA Form 10182` Board appeal):

items: **Impermissible Elevation of the `§ 5107(b)` Standard of Proof:** Requiring epidemiological certainty (`"conclusive proof"` or `"established positive association"` in population studies) conflates the standard for Congress creating a *nationwide statutory presumption* with individual direct service connection under **`38 U.S.C. § 5107(b)` ("at least as likely as not" equipoise)** (*Stefl v. Nicholson*, `21 Vet. App. 120, 124 (2007)`; *Polovick v. Shinseki*, `23 Vet. App. 48, 53 (2009)`).

**Violation of Statutory Synergistic-Exposure Mandate (`38 U.S.C. § 1168(a)(2)`):** If the veteran had *multiple* exposures (e.g., Iraq burn pits + `JP-8` fuel handling + `AFFF` foam) and the examiner analyzed only burn pits in isolation—or ignored the `ILER` / `TERA` memo—the exam violates `§ 1168(a)(2)` as a matter of law.

**Dual-Track Pleading for Sleep Apnea (`DC 6847`):** Never rely on a bare `TERA` theory for `OSA` alone! Always plead **both** `(a)` **secondary service connection (`38 C.F.R. § 3.310`)** to presumptive **chronic rhinitis (`DC 6522`) / chronic sinusitis (`DC 6510–6514`) / asthma (`DC 6602`)** (upper-airway nasal resistance collapsing pharyngeal patency during sleep, or corticosteroid/weight-gain intermediate link under `VAOPGCPREC 1-2017`) **AND** `(b)` direct `§ 1168` `TERA` particulate airway inflammation! *(Watchlist Guardrail: VA's Feb. 15, 2022 proposal to curtail `50%` CPAP ratings under `DC 6847`, `RIN 2900-AQ72` / `87 FR 8474`, remains **proposed / not finalized**—current `50%` CPAP criteria govern!)*

blocks.text: 6. Postconditions: Effective Dates, CRSC (*Soto*) & Fee Checks

items:
**August 10, 2022 PACT Floor & `38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)` 1-Year Lookback:**
• Claims/ITFs filed on or before **August 14, 2023** secured the **August 10, 2022** statutory effective date (assuming diagnosis existed on Aug. 10, 2022). For claims filed *after* August 14, 2023, audit **`38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)(3)`**—especially for **`§ 3.320a` (eff. Jan. 2, 2025)** and **`§ 3.320b` (eff. Jan. 10, 2025)**: any claim filed within `1 year` of Jan. 2 / Jan. 10, 2025 (or at any time thereafter, looking back `1 year` prior to receipt of claim if medical criteria were met!) unlocks up to **12 months of pre-filing liberalizing back pay**!

**Mandatory Post-Grant `CRSC` Audit for Military Retirees (*Soto v. United States*, `605 U.S. 360 (2025)`):**
• Presumptive Gulf War (`§ 3.317`) and PACT Act (`§§ 1119–1120`) disabilities incurred via Southwest Asia / post-9/11 combat-zone hazards (`instrumentality of war` / `hazardous service` / `armed conflict`) routinely qualify for tax-free **Combat-Related Special Compensation (`10 U.S.C. § 1413a`)**—crucial for **Chapter 61 medical retirees** with `< 20` years of service who are barred from `CRDP`, with **zero 6-year Barring Act cap** after *Soto* ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc))!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Gulf War Undiagnosed/Multisymptom Illnesses, PACT Act Burn Pit Presumptions & Toxic Exposure (TERA) Exams
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Veterans who served in Southwest Asia or expanded post-9/11 theaters—and Veterans from any era exposed to occupational or environmental hazards—have three distinct paths to service connection that VA examiners sometimes confuse: (1) Gulf War presumptions under 38 U.S.C. § 1117 and 38 C.F.R. § 3.317 for undiagnosed illnesses and Medically Unexplained Chronic Multisymptom Illnesses (chronic fatigue syndrome, fibromyalgia, and functional gastrointestinal disorders like irritable bowel syndrome), which require NO medical nexus opinion; (2) PACT Act airborne-hazard and burn-pit presumptions (38 U.S.C. § 1120 and 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.320–3.320b) covering more than two dozen respiratory conditions and cancers; and (3) direct Toxic Exposure Risk Activity (TERA) medical nexus exams under 38 U.S.C. § 1168 for non-presumptive conditions linked to jet fuel, PFAS firefighting foam, solvents, radiation, or burn pits.
record_clues: A DD-214, deployment travel voucher, flight log, or Individual Longitudinal Exposure Record (ILER) showing service on or after August 2, 1990 in Southwest Asia/Somalia, or on or after September 11, 2001 in Afghanistan, Djibouti, Syria, Jordan, Egypt, Lebanon, Yemen, or Uzbekistan (K2).

A VA exam denying fibromyalgia, chronic fatigue syndrome, irritable bowel syndrome, or chronic unexplained joint/muscle pain because 'there is no medical nexus linking the condition to Gulf War service.'
A pre-August 10, 2022 denial of asthma, rhinitis, or sinusitis because symptoms started more than 10 years after discharge or were rated below 10%.

A diagnosis of urinary bladder or ureter cancer (§ 3.320a, effective January 2, 2025) or leukemia, multiple myeloma, MGUS, myelodysplastic syndrome, or myelofibrosis (§ 3.320b, effective January 10, 2025), or a negative TERA medical opinion that ignored military occupational specialty chemical exposures.
important_cautions: Different effective-date rules apply to living Veterans vs. Survivors: unlike Vietnam Nehmer claims, PACT Act burn-pit presumptions for living Veterans generally cannot take effect earlier than August 10, 2022 (or January 2025 for newly added §§ 3.320a–3.320b cancers) under 38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a), whereas previously denied Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) survivor claims re-evaluated under 38 U.S.C. § 1305 and 38 C.F.R. § 3.33 can reach back to the original DIC claim date.

Statutory text overrides lagging print regulations: the PACT Act (August 10, 2022) statutorily removed the Dec. 31, 2026 Gulf War deadline and added Afghanistan, Israel, Egypt, Turkey, Syria, and Jordan to 38 U.S.C. § 1117, even while VA's October 1, 2024 conforming regulation (89 FR 79815) remains a proposed rule that is not finalized. Similarly, RIN 2900-AQ72 (sleep apnea) remains an unfinalized proposed rule.

Conditions with a known or partially explained pathology (such as diabetes, multiple sclerosis, or obstructive sleep apnea) do not qualify as unexplained illnesses under 38 C.F.R. § 3.317(a), so representatives typically pursue them through a § 1168 TERA nexus opinion or § 3.310 secondary connection.

Failures to order a TERA exam or search ILER records are duty-to-assist errors addressed through open review lanes (Higher-Level Review, Supplemental Claim, or Board appeal), not Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) motions (Cook v. Principi; 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c)).
questions_for_representative: Does my diagnosed condition already qualify as a presumptive Gulf War multisymptom illness (§ 3.317) or PACT Act burn-pit respiratory/cancer condition (§§ 3.320–3.320b) where no medical nexus opinion is needed?
Have we requested my Individual Longitudinal Exposure Record (ILER) and military occupational exposure history before attending a 38 U.S.C. § 1168 TERA medical exam?

If VA denied my PACT Act or Gulf War condition before August 10, 2022 (or before January 2025 for newly added blood and bladder cancers), should we file a Supplemental Claim and check the liberalizing effective-date rules?
If I am a surviving spouse whose DIC claim was previously denied, am I eligible for retroactive re-evaluation back to my original DIC filing date under 38 U.S.C. § 1305 and 38 C.F.R. § 3.33?

Cir. 2012))

blocks.text: Psychiatric disability claims (`DC 9400–9440`, `38 C.F.R. § 4.130`) routinely drive `70%` (`TDIU` gateway under `§ 4.16(a)`), `100%` schedular, Statutory Housebound **`SMC(s)`**, and Regular Aid & Attendance **`SMC(l)`** awards. Yet Regional Offices (`ROs`) unlawfully deny thousands of valid trauma claims every year by misapplying **`38 C.F.R. § 3.304(f)`**—demanding non-existent official military police reports in Military Sexual Trauma (`MST`) claims, botching `JSRRC` unit searches, or illegally imposing `§ 3.304(f)` PTSD stressor-corroboration hurdles onto **Major Depressive Disorder (`DC 9434`)** and **Generalized Anxiety Disorder (`DC 9400`)**!

lines: **Single Source of Truth & Orthogonal Cross-References:** For the verbatim chronological text of `38 C.F.R. § 3.304(f)` across its `1993` (`58 FR 29110`), `2002` (`67 FR 10330`), `2008` (`73 FR 64208`), and `July 13, 2010` (`75 FR 39843` / `75 FR 41092`) overhauls, consult [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.303(a)–(d), 3.304(b) & (f), and 3.306(a)–(c) (Direct Service Connection, Chronicity, Congenital Defects, Presumption of Soundness, Aggravation & Four-Era PTSD / MST Stressor Evolution)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.304f-ptsd-evolution). For historical vs. current `§ 4.130` rating criteria (`DSM-III -> DSM-IV -> DSM-5` and quarantined unfinalized proposal `RIN 2900-AQ82`), consult [VASRD Historical Diff: Mental Disorders & PTSD (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125–4.130, DC 9400–9440)](/cfr/modules/mental-health-dc-9400-9411). Pair this playbook with [Playbook 03](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c) (`§ 3.156(c)` `JSRRC`/`CID`/`NCIS` retroactive effective dates), [Playbook 10](/playbooks/10-character-of-discharge-insanity-upgrades) (June 2024 `§ 3.12(e)` MST compelling-circumstances COD rescue & `DRB`/`BCMR` Kurta upgrades), and the [Direct SC Treatise](/docs/service-connection-direct-soundness-aggravation).

blocks.text: 1. Preconditions: OMPF Personnel File, 21-0781, CID/NCIS & Clemons Scope Audit

Never evaluate a PTSD or MST denial from the `DD Form 214` and STRs alone. Before pleading, obtain and cross-index four archival sources ([VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon); [`C-File Audit Protocol`](/checklists/c-file-audit-protocol)):

items: **Complete Official Military Personnel File (`OMPF`) from NPRC:** Including `DA Form 20` / `DA Form 2-1` (Army), `NAVPERS 1070/604` & `605` enlisted evaluations/awards (Navy), `MCTFS`/SRB page 3 & 11 entries (USMC), and `AF Form 910` EPRs (Air Force)—tracking **exact semi-annual performance/conduct grades**, unit transfers, MOS reclassifications, `Article 15` / `NJP` dates, and campaign/expeditionary medals.

**Stressor Statements & VHA Vet Center / `§ 1720D` MST Records:**
• Review historical `VA Form 21-0781` (combat/non-combat) and `21-0781a` (personal trauma)—consolidated by VA into the modern unified **`VA Form 21-0781`** (*Statement in Support of Claim for Service Connection for PTSD*).
• Request **Vet Center readjustment counseling records** (which VHA stores *outside* standard `CAPRI`/`VistA` unless specifically authorized by the veteran!) and VHA MST Coordinator (`38 U.S.C. § 1720D`) positive-screen notes.

**Military Law Enforcement & Sexual Assault Archives (`§ 3.156(c)` Triggers):** Check whether VA ever requested **Army `CID`**, **Naval `NCIS`**, **Air Force `AFOSI`**, Provost Marshal blotters, **DoD `DSAID` / Restricted-to-Unrestricted `DD Form 2910` SAPR reports**, or **`JSRRC` / `CRUR` (Center for Research of Unit Records)** operational logs!

**Full Psychiatric Diagnostic Inventory (*Clemons* Check):** List **every** DSM-5 diagnosis recorded by VHA, Vet Center, or private clinicians (`PTSD`, `MDD`, `GAD`, `Panic Disorder`, `Persistent Depressive Disorder`, `Bipolar`, `Somatic Symptom Disorder`, `Adjustment Disorder`, secondary `AUD`/`SUD`).

blocks.text: 2. Architecture of 38 C.F.R. § 3.304(f) & The Five Stressor Relaxations

Under the unrelaxed introductory baseline of **`38 C.F.R. § 3.304(f)`** (`58 FR 29110`, May 19, 1993; *Cohen v. Brown*, `10 Vet. App. 128, 138 (1997)`), service connection for **PTSD (`DC 9411`)** requires **(1)** medical evidence diagnosing PTSD in accordance with **`38 C.F.R. § 4.125(a)` (`DSM-5`)**; **(2)** a link, established by medical evidence, between current symptoms and an in-service stressor; and **(3)** **credible supporting evidence that the claimed in-service stressor occurred**—**UNLESS** the claim qualifies under one of **five regulatory stressor relaxations (`(f)(1)–(5)`)** (verbatim text in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.303(a)–(d), 3.304(b) & (f), and 3.306(a)–(c) (Direct Service Connection, Chronicity, Congenital Defects, Presumption of Soundness, Aggravation & Four-Era PTSD / MST Stressor Evolution)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.304f-ptsd-evolution)):
Detailed Mechanics & Traps Across (f)(1)–(4)

rows: **`§ 3.304(f)(1)` — In-Service PTSD Diagnosis** (`73 FR 64208`, **eff. Oct. 29, 2008**; finalized `74 FR 14491`, Mar. 31, 2009)

If the evidence establishes a **diagnosis of PTSD during active service** and the claimed stressor is related to that service, **the veteran's lay testimony alone** establishes the stressor absent clear and convincing evidence to the contrary (consistent with service circumstances).

Check mental-health clinic STRs, deployment combat-stress detachments, and `MEB`/`PEB` narratives. *(Prospective rule eff. Oct. 29, 2008—cannot assert `(f)(1)` as CUE against pre-Oct. 29, 2008 final denials).*

If the veteran **engaged in combat with the enemy**, lay testimony alone establishes the combat stressor absent clear and convincing evidence to the contrary. Under ***Pentecost v. Principi*, `16 Vet. App. 124, 128–29 (2002)`** and ***Suozzi v. Brown*, `10 Vet. App. 307, 311 (1997)`**, combat is proven **EITHER** by individual combat awards (`CIB`, `CAR`, `CMB`, `CAB`, Purple Heart, valor medals) **OR** by unit/MOS records showing the veteran's unit received enemy fire, mortar/rocket attacks, or hostile action while the veteran was present!

**CUE-Safe (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive):** `38 U.S.C. § 1154(b)` (`former § 354(b)`) dates back to `1941`! If an earlier `DD-214` / `DA Form 20` already in the C-file listed a `CIB`, `CAR`, or Purple Heart and the RO denied PTSD for "unverified combat stressor," file **RO/Board CUE**! If unit logs arrive later, invoke **`§ 3.156(c)`** ([Playbook 03](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c)).

**`§ 3.304(f)(3)` — Fear of Hostile Military or Terrorist Activity** (`75 FR 39843`, pub. **July 13, 2010**, corrected from "July 12" typo at **`75 FR 41092`** [July 15, 2010] to **eff. July 13, 2010**)

Applies to veterans who did *not* personally engage in direct combat (`(f)(2)`)—e.g., fobbit/supply/aviation/medic/Navy/DMZ personnel—whose stressor relates to **fear of hostile military or terrorist activity** (IEDs, incoming mortars/rockets, sniper threat, body/casualty handling, drone/SCUD alerts) when: · 1. **A VA psychiatrist or psychologist, or a psychiatrist or psychologist with whom VA has contracted**, confirms the claimed stressor is adequate to support a PTSD diagnosis (`DSM-5` Criterion A) and symptoms are related to it; **AND** · 2. The stressor is consistent with the places, types, and circumstances of service, with no clear and convincing contrary evidence.

**THREE CRITICAL `(f)(3)` RULES:** · 1. **Private IMO Trap (*NOVA*, `669 F.3d 1340 (Fed. Cir. 2012)`):** The Federal Circuit upheld VA's rule that a **private** clinician's report *alone* **cannot** satisfy `(f)(3)` stressor relaxation! **HOWEVER**, under ***Sanchez-Navarro v. McDonald*, `774 F.3d 1380, 1384–86 (Fed. Cir. 2014)`**, **VA adjudicators** (not examiners) decide whether the claimed stressor is consistent with service, and once consistency is shown (plus a private diagnosis or lay symptoms), **VA is legally obligated under `38 U.S.C. § 5103A(d)` to schedule a VA psychiatric exam**! (*Acevedo v. Shinseki*, `25 Vet. App. 286 (2012)` governs exam adequacy). · 2. **CUE Temporal Floor:** **NEVER** cite `(f)(3)` to allege CUE in a final pre-July 13, 2010 non-combat PTSD denial (`38 C.F.R. § 3.114` floor = **July 13, 2010**)! · 3. **`Gagne` JSRRC Rule:** For non-`(f)(3)` unit stressors, under ***Gagne v. McDonald*, `27 Vet. App. 397, 405 (2015)`**, VA cannot give up after a single failed `JSRRC` request—it must submit **multiple targeted 60-day window searches** until further requests are futile!
If the veteran is a former `POW` (`§ 3.1(y)`) and the claimed stressor is related to POW internment, lay testimony alone establishes the stressor absent clear and convincing contrary evidence.

Pair with automatic POW presumptive anxiety/dysthymic/psychosis rules under `38 U.S.C. § 1112(b)` / `38 C.F.R. § 3.309(c)` ([Playbook 07](/playbooks/07-statutory-presumptions-chronic-tropical-pow-als)).

blocks.text: 3. 38 C.F.R. § 3.304(f)(5): Personal Assault & Military Sexual Trauma (MST) Litigation

Codified on **March 7, 2002 (`67 FR 10330`)** following ***Patton v. West*, `12 Vet. App. 272 (1999)`** and ***YR v. West*, `11 Vet. App. 393 (1998)`** (originally numbered `(f)(3)`, redesignated `(f)(4)` in 2008 and **`(f)(5)`** in July 2010), `§ 3.304(f)(5)` recognizes that in-service sexual assault, domestic battery, hazing, and homophobic/racial violent assaults are overwhelmingly **unreported in official military channels** due to retaliation, stigma, and command pressure.
A. Three Controlling Appellate Pillars in MST Litigation

items:
***AZ v. Shinseki*, `731 F.3d 1303, 1315–18 (Fed. Cir. 2013)` — Silence of STRs/Military Logs Is NEVER Negative Evidence:**
• In a landmark precedential opinion surveying empirical DoD sexual-assault underreporting data (`80%–90%+` unreported), the Federal Circuit held that **VA and the Board may NEVER treat the absence of an official service record, STR entry, or military law-enforcement report of an in-service sexual assault—or a servicemember's failure to report the assault to family/friends—as pertinent affirmative evidence that the assault did not occur**, nor use non-reporting to impugn the survivor's credibility! Any BVA or C&P rationale citing *"no report in STRs"* as a reason to doubt the stressor commits reversible legal error!

***Menegassi v. Shinseki*, `638 F.3d 1379, 1382–83 (Fed. Cir. 2011)` & *Patton v. West*, `12 Vet. App. 272, 280 (1999)` — Medical Opinions as Marker Corroboration:**
• Under *Menegassi* (clarifying *Moreau v. Brown*, `9 Vet. App. 389 (1996)` and *YR v. West*, `11 Vet. App. 393 (1998)`), while a post-service medical nexus opinion resting *solely* on the veteran's uncorroborated verbal account does not by itself corroborate a PTSD `(f)(5)` stressor, **a psychiatrist's or psychologist's clinical opinion evaluating documented in-service or post-service behavioral changes ("markers") and explaining that those behavioral shifts are clinically consistent with an in-service sexual assault CAN ITSELF constitute the "credible supporting evidence" required to corroborate the stressor under `§ 3.304(f)(5)`**! *(Note: Under *Hall v. Shinseki*, `717 F.3d 1369, 1373–74 (Fed. Cir. 2013)`, `(f)(5)` relaxes how corroboration is proven—it does not eliminate corroboration entirely for `DC 9411` PTSD, making the *Menegassi* clinical marker-interpretation opinion and the Section 4 Non-PTSD Bypass below essential!)*

**Heightened Notice & Development Duty (`§ 3.304(f)(5)` Last Two Sentences; *Gallegos v. Peake* & *Bradford v. Nicholson*):**
• Under the mandatory text of `§ 3.304(f)(5)`, ***Patton*, `12 Vet. App. at 283–85`**, ***Bradford v. Nicholson*, `20 Vet. App. 200, 205–06 (2006)`**, and ***Gallegos v. Peake*, `22 Vet. App. 329, 334–36 (2008)`**, VA **may not deny** a personal-assault PTSD claim for lack of stressor corroboration without **first explicitly advising the claimant** that alternative evidence from non-service sources or behavioral changes can corroborate the stressor and **giving the claimant an opportunity to identify and submit** such evidence (and requesting `CID`/`NCIS`/`AFOSI`, Vet Center, or civilian records identified by the veteran).

blocks.text: B. Master C-File & OMPF Behavioral Marker Audit Matrix (§ 3.304(f)(5))
When building an MST brief or instructing a *Menegassi* forensic psychologist, construct a **Before-vs.-After Chronological Marker Table** from these hidden file indicators:

headers: Concrete Pre- vs. Post-Assault Behavioral Markers to Extract
rows: Sudden, unexplained drop from `4.0 / Excellent` proficiency/conduct marks to `2.8–3.2` or adverse supervisor comments (*"withdrawn," "attitude changed," "tardy," "distracted"*) following the timeframe/duty station of the assault.

First-time `Article 15` / `NJP` cluster (minor disrespect, missed formation, alcohol incident, short `AWOL` to escape perpetrator), **request for transfer to another unit, ship, barracks, or MOS**, or sudden early separation (`homosexuality` pretext, `"personality disorder,"` `"unsuitability,"` or pregnancy discharge).

Visits within days/months of the timeframe for **STI/STD panels, pregnancy tests, emergency contraception**, bruising/lacerations/jaw/rib/wrist sprains attributed to *"fell down stairs / sports injury,"* or sudden repetitive sick-call visits for **unexplained pelvic/abdominal/GI pain, insomnia, panic/hyperventilation, tension headaches, or rapid `15–40+ lb` weight loss or weight gain**!

Sudden post-discharge alcohol/substance self-medication (*Allen* chain), relationship/marital breakdown, sexual aversion/dysfunction (`FSAD` / `ED`), inability to work around male/authority supervisors, civilian crisis-center or pastoral counseling, or diary/letter entries.

Statements from a barracks roommate, battle buddy, sibling, parent, or ex-spouse—even if the veteran **never named the assault at the time**, lay witnesses are **100% competent** (*Jandreau*) to describe the dramatic personality shift (*"went from outgoing honor graduate at AIT to locking her door, crying, and drinking heavily in late 1994"*), which your *Menegassi* psychologist then clinically links to the MST!

blocks.text: 4. THE GOLDEN STRATEGIC BYPASS: Non-PTSD Acquired Psychiatric Disorders from MST (§ 3.303(a) vs. § 3.304(f))

lines: **The Single Most Powerful Doctrine in MST Litigation (*Patton* + *Clemons*):** **`38 C.F.R. § 3.304(f)` APPLIES EXCLUSIVELY TO POSTTRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER (`DC 9411`)!** It does **NOT** govern *any* other acquired psychiatric disorder under `38 C.F.R. § 4.130`!

items:
**Controlling Legal Authority (*Patton v. West* & *Clemons v. Shinseki*):**
• In ***Patton v. West*, `12 Vet. App. 272, 280 (1999)`**, the CAVC squarely held that `38 C.F.R. § 3.304(f)` governs **only PTSD**; claims for **any other psychiatric disorder** resulting from an in-service personal assault are governed by **standard direct service connection under `38 C.F.R. § 3.303(a)`**!
• In ***Clemons v. Shinseki*, `23 Vet. App. 1, 5 (2009)`**, the CAVC held that a veteran's claim for "PTSD" or mental-health benefits **encompasses ALL acquired psychiatric disorders** supported by the medical record—meaning the RO and Board **must adjudicate entitlement to Major Depressive Disorder (`DC 9434`), Generalized Anxiety Disorder (`DC 9400`), Panic Disorder (`DC 9412`), Persistent Depressive Disorder (`DC 9435`), Somatic Symptom Disorder (`DC 9422`), or Chronic Adjustment Disorder (`DC 9440`) as part of the exact same pending claim**!

**Why This Wins Cases With ZERO External Stressor Corroboration:**
• Under `38 C.F.R. § 3.303(a)` ([Direct SC Treatise](/docs/service-connection-direct-soundness-aggravation)):
• **Element 1 (Current Disability):** A formal `DSM-5` diagnosis (`§ 4.125(a)` / *Martinez-Bodon*) of **`MDD` (`DC 9434`), `GAD` (`DC 9400`), `Panic Disorder` (`DC 9412`), or `Adjustment/Somatic Disorder`**.
• **Element 2 (In-Service Event):** Established by **the veteran's credible lay testimony alone** (`38 U.S.C. § 5107(b)`; *Buchanan v. Nicholson*, `451 F.3d 1331 (Fed. Cir. 2006)`; *AZ v. Shinseki*, `731 F.3d 1303 (Fed. Cir. 2013)` barring any negative inference from non-reporting)—**ZERO independent marker or third-party stressor corroboration is legally required**!
• **Element 3 (Medical Nexus):** A psychiatrist/psychologist nexus opinion linking the `MDD` / `GAD` / `Panic Disorder` *"at least as likely as not"* to the credibly reported in-service assault.
• **Identical Dollar Payout (`38 C.F.R. § 4.130`):** Because **every** `§ 4.130` mental disorder (`DC 9400–9440`) is rated under the **exact same General Rating Formula for Mental Disorders** (`0% / 10% / 30% / 50% / 70% / 100%`), winning `70%` or `100%` for MST-induced `MDD` (`DC 9434`) under `§ 3.303(a)` pays the **exact same monthly compensation and retroactive back pay** back to the original PTSD claim date (*Clemons*) as `DC 9411` PTSD!

blocks.text: 5. Invariants / Kill-Switches & Postconditions (§ 3.156(c), § 3.12(e) COD & Unlocks)
A. Fatal Invariants / Kill-Switches

items: **Pre-July 13, 2010 `§ 3.304(f)(3)` CUE Bar:** Never file CUE against a pre-July 13, 2010 non-combat PTSD denial using `(f)(3)` fear-of-hostile-activity (`75 FR 39843` / `75 FR 41092`). Instead, check whether `(a)` newly associated `JSRRC`/deck-log/morning-report records unlock **`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)`** back to the original claim date, or `(b)` a co-existing `MDD`/`GAD` diagnosis in the prior record was left unadjudicated!

**DSM-5 Diagnostic Floor (*Martinez-Bodon*):** Under `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.125(a), 4.130` and *Martinez-Bodon v. McDonough*, `28 F.4th 1241 (Fed. Cir. 2022)`, ensure the clinician explicitly states a **formal DSM-5 diagnosis** rather than listing "anxiety/trauma symptoms" alone.

**Quarantine Unfinalized `RIN 2900-AQ82` Proposal:** Never cite VA's February 2022 **proposed (unfinalized)** mental-health rating schedule (`RIN 2900-AQ82`, `87 FR 8498`) as active law; current `§ 4.130` occupational-and-social-impairment criteria govern all adjudications.

blocks.text: B. Postconditions: Effective-Date Multipliers, COD Rescue & Ancillary Unlocks

items: **`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)` Retroactive Effective-Date Jackpots ([Playbook 03](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c)):** Whenever `JSRRC` / `CRUR` operational histories, Navy ship deck logs, Army morning reports, or **newly associated `CID` / `NCIS` / `AFOSI` / SAPR investigative files** are added to VBMS after a prior PTSD/MST denial, `§ 3.156(c)(1) & (3)` mandates reconsideration with an effective date **all the way back to the original denied claim** (potentially 10–40+ years of back pay)!

**Character-of-Discharge (`COD`) & Upgrade Rescue for MST Survivors ([Playbook 10](/playbooks/10-character-of-discharge-insanity-upgrades)):**
• **June 25, 2024 `38 C.F.R. § 3.12(e)` Compelling-Circumstances Exception (`89 FR 32361`):** Explicitly lists **sexual abuse/assault (`MST`) and mental impairment** as compelling circumstances overcoming `180+`-day AWOL (`§ 3.12(c)(6)`) and moral-turpitude / willful-and-persistent misconduct (`§ 3.12(d)(2)`) OTH discharges directly inside VBA—plus **`38 U.S.C. § 5303(b)` insanity** (`§ 3.354`) and liberal consideration before DoD `DRB`/`BCMR` under the **Hagel (`2014`), Kurta (`2017`), and Wilkie (`2018`) Memoranda** (`10 U.S.C. §§ 1552, 1553`; [`COD Intake Audit Gate`](/checklists/cod-and-guard-reserve-intake-audit)).

**Downstream `TDIU`, `SMC(k)`, `SMC(s)` & Secondary Chains ([Playbook 14](/playbooks/14-secondary-service-connection-aggravation-obesity)):**
• A `70%` PTSD/`MDD` grant immediately satisfies the single-disability schedular threshold for **`TDIU` (`38 C.F.R. § 4.16(a)`)** (and unlocks *Bradley* **`SMC(s)`** if other SC disabilities combine to `>= 60%`!).
• Audit secondary `SSRI`/trauma **`FSAD` / `ED` (`SMC(k)`)**, secondary **Obstructive Sleep Apnea (`DC 6847`) via the *Walsh*/*Garner* obesity intermediate step**, secondary **migraines (`DC 8100`)**, secondary **GERD/IBS (`DC 7206`/`7319`)**, and *Allen* secondary substance-use sequelae!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: PTSD Stressor Rules, Military Sexual Trauma (MST) Markers & Non-PTSD Mental Health Claims
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Under 38 C.F.R. § 3.304(f), how VA verifies an in-service traumatic event ('stressor') for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) depends on which of five pathways applies: (1) PTSD diagnosed during active service, (2) combat service, (3) fear of hostile military or terrorist activity, (4) Former Prisoner of War captivity, or (5) in-service personal assault or Military Sexual Trauma (MST). Because assaults are rarely reported in official military channels, § 3.304(f)(5) and federal court rulings (AZ v. Shinseki; Menegassi v. Shinseki) forbid VA from treating the absence of an official report as evidence the assault did not happen, and allow corroboration through 'markers'—subtle changes in behavior, work performance, health visits, or statements to friends and family. Equally important, non-PTSD mental health diagnoses such as Major Depressive Disorder or Generalized Anxiety Disorder are governed by direct service connection (38 C.F.R. § 3.303(a)) rather than § 3.304(f)'s PTSD stressor corroboration rules.
record_clues: A VA denial discounting a Veteran's account of Military Sexual Trauma or personal assault because no contemporary military police or medical report appeared in Service Treatment Records.

A PTSD denial for 'uncorroborated stressor' when VA or private records simultaneously diagnosed Major Depressive Disorder (Diagnostic Code 9434), Generalized Anxiety Disorder (Diagnostic Code 9400), or Panic Disorder (Diagnostic Code 9412) linked to service.

Personnel or medical file clues ('markers') such as a sudden drop in performance evaluations, uncharacteristic disciplinary actions (Article 15 / non-judicial punishment), requests to transfer units or duty stations, emergency clinic or screening visits, significant weight changes, or an early 'personality disorder' discharge.

Service on or near a base, convoy route, ship, or airspace exposed to mortar, rocket, IED, or sniper threats where PTSD was denied before July 13, 2010, or denied later without an exam by a VA or VA-contracted psychiatrist or psychologist (§ 3.304(f)(3)).
important_cautions: Key effective date for 'fear of hostile activity': VA's liberalizing rule in 38 C.F.R. § 3.304(f)(3) took effect July 13, 2010 (published at 75 FR 39843 and formally corrected from July 12 to July 13, 2010 at 75 FR 41092). Because it is a prospective liberalizing rule, it cannot be used to prove Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) in final decisions issued before July 13, 2010, and it specifically requires confirmation by a VA or VA-contracted psychiatrist or psychologist (upheld in NOVA v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs).

Newly obtained official military unit histories, deck logs, morning reports, or military investigative files (CID/NCIS/AFOSI) that corroborate a previously denied PTSD or MST stressor can unlock retroactive reconsideration back to the original claim date under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c).

VA's February 15, 2022 mental health rating proposal (RIN 2900-AQ82, 87 FR 8498) remains an unfinalized proposed rule and is NOT enacted law; existing DSM-5 criteria under 38 C.F.R. § 4.130 remain in force.

Under George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1403(d)–(e) and 20.1409(c), disputes over how an adjudicator weighed marker evidence cannot establish CUE, and only one final merits CUE decision is allowed per prior Board decision issue.
questions_for_representative: If my PTSD claim was denied for lack of stressor corroboration, did the examiner also diagnose depression, anxiety, or another DSM-5 mental disorder that should have been evaluated under 38 C.F.R. § 3.303(a) (Clemons v. Shinseki / Patton v. West)?

Have we requested my complete Official Military Personnel File (OMPF)—including performance marks, transfer requests, and disciplinary records—to identify behavioral markers under 38 C.F.R. § 3.304(f)(5)?
Could official unit logs, deck logs, or archival stressor records trigger retroactive reconsideration of an earlier denial under 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c)?

If my stressor involved fear of hostile military or terrorist activity, did a VA or VA-contracted psychiatrist or psychologist evaluate whether the event is consistent with the places, types, and circumstances of my service under § 3.304(f)(3)?

title: Playbook 17: 38 U.S.C. § 1151 VA Medical Malpractice, Unforeseen Facility Injuries (Viegas), Ancillary Limits & FTCA (§ 3.362) Offset Engineering
cFileTriggers: VAMC operative report, oncology/radiology delay, medication overdose, post-op sepsis/nerve injury, or VHA Institutional Disclosure of Adverse Event in VistA/CAPRI
Missing or unsigned VHA informed-consent record (38 C.F.R. § 17.32 / iMedConsent) prior to an invasive VAMC procedure (Hatfield v. McDonough)
Physical injury caused by defective VAMC facility equipment, wheelchair lift, exam table, or restroom grab bar while receiving VA care (Viegas v. Shinseki)
Aggravation of orthopedic/mental disability during a Chapter 31 VR&E training placement or § 1718 Compensated Work Therapy (CWT) assignment (no VA fault required!)
Pre-Oct. 1, 1997 § 1151 / former § 351 claim still pending via § 3.156(b) or unadjudicated informal claim (governed by Brown v. Gardner no-fault causation!)
Parallel Standard Form 95 (SF-95) FTCA administrative tort claim requiring pre-settlement § 3.362(b)/(c)/(e) gross-offset and survivor-allocation structuring
killSwitches: Filing a § 1151 claim for malpractice committed by a non-VA private provider under a 38 U.S.C. § 1703 Community Care / MISSION Act contract, § 1720 contract nursing home, or non-VA § 8153 facility (expressly barred by 38 C.F.R. § 3.361(f) — pivot immediately to state-law medical malpractice before state SOL expires, unless a VA employee's referral delay caused the harm!)

Assuming a 100% P&T § 1151 award or § 1151 death unlocks Chapter 35 DEA (§ 3501 / § 3.807), CHAMPVA (§ 1781), S-DVI / VALife (§§ 1922, 1922B; Alleman), or § 2307 SC burial allowance (Mintz) — strictly barred because § 1151 confers 'as if' compensation, NOT actual service connection

Allowing a veteran or surviving spouse to sign a lump-sum FTCA settlement without modeling the 38 C.F.R. § 3.362(b) GROSS offset (which recoups attorney fees too!), failing to allocate survivor damages to non-DIC heirs under § 3.362(c), or needlessly designating SAH/Auto language triggering § 3.362(e)

Missing the strict 2-year federal statute of limitations on SF-95 FTCA tort claims (28 U.S.C. § 2401(b)), or conversely assuming § 1151 is time-barred after 2 years (§ 1151 has ZERO statute of limitations!)

Reopening a finally denied pre-Oct. 1, 1997 § 1151 claim via Supplemental Claim instead of checking first for pending-claim finality abatement (§ 3.156(b)) or CUE (reopening on/after Oct. 1, 1997 forfeits Brown v. Gardner no-fault causation under 38 C.F.R. § 3.361(a)!)

blocks.text: Under **`38 U.S.C. § 1151`** (`former 38 U.S.C. § 351`), a veteran (even one with **zero service-connected disabilities**) who suffers "additional disability or death" proximately caused by VA medical/surgical care, C&P examination, **`Chapter 31` `VR&E`**, or **Compensated Work Therapy (`CWT`)** receives tax-free monthly Chapter 11 compensation (`0%–100%`, `TDIU`, and **`SMC(k)–(t)`**) or Chapter 13 survivor `DIC` **"in the same manner as if such additional disability or death were service-connected."** Unlike Federal Tort Claims Act (`FTCA`) suits, **`§ 1151` has ZERO statute of limitations** and applies the claimant-friendly **`38 U.S.C. § 5107(b)` "at least as likely as not" equipoise standard**!

*(Cross-references: [`Part 3 Toxic, Gulf War, PACT & § 1151 Evolution Diff`](/cfr/modules/toxic-gulf-pact-1151-evolution); [Master SMC Legal Treatise & Step Math](/docs/smc-complete-treatise-and-step-math); [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.350, 3.352, 3.552(b), 4.63 & 3.810(a) (Special Monthly Compensation Ratings, Aid & Attendance, TBI SMC(t), Loss of Use & Multiple Clothing Allowances)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.350-3.352-smc-evolution); [Playbook 12 (`SMC(l)`, `SMC(r)(1)–(2)` & `SMC(t)`)](/playbooks/12-aid-and-attendance-smc-l-r1-r2-and-smc-t); [Playbook 13 (`SAH`, `Ch. 39 Auto`, `Clothing` & Ancillary Grants)](/playbooks/13-ancillary-grants-sah-auto-clothing-dea-spina-bifida); [Playbook 08 (Survivor DIC & `§ 1318`)](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical); [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.22 & 3.312 (Hypothetical § 1318 Total-Disability DIC Evolution & Service-Connected Cause of Death)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.22-dic-hypothetical-evolution); [Playbook 09 (`§ 5121` Accrued & `§ 5121A` Substitution)](/playbooks/09-accrued-benefits-substitution-nehmer-estates); [Three-Era Statutory Crosswalk](/docs/title-38-statutory-crosswalk); [Master `VAOPGCPREC` Digest](/docs/vaopgcprec-index); [VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon); and [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).*
1. Preconditions: VBMS, VistA/CAPRI & SF-95 Audit Triggers
Screen every catastrophic VAMC surgical complication, delayed cancer diagnosis, medication error, VAMC equipment fall, or `Ch. 31` `VR&E` injury for these exact records:

items:
**Pleading Forms (`1-Year` Retroactive Lookback Gate):**
• Living veteran: **`VA Form 21-526EZ`** (explicitly specifying *"Compensation under 38 U.S.C. § 1151 for [condition] resulting from VAMC [facility] care on [date]"*). If filed **within `1 year` of the date the injury/aggravation occurred**, **`38 U.S.C. § 5110(b)(3)` / `38 C.F.R. § 3.400(i)`** locks in the **exact date of the VA medical injury** as the effective date!
• Survivor: **`VA Form 21P-534EZ`** (within `1 year` of death -> effective first day of month of death under `§ 5110(d)` / `§ 3.400(c)(2)`).
• Parallel `FTCA` Tort Track: **`Standard Form 95` (`SF-95`)** filed with the **VA Office of General Counsel Torts Law Group** within the **strict `2-year` accrual deadline** (`28 U.S.C. § 2401(b)`).

blocks.text: 2. Bitemporal Pathway Gate: The October 1, 1997 Statutory Fault Divide

headers: Substantive Standard & Bitemporal CUE / Reopening Rules
rows: **Claim received BEFORE `October 1, 1997`** *(and either still open/pending or attacked via CUE)*

**NO-FAULT CAUSATION:** In *Gardner*, SCOTUS unanimously struck down `former 38 C.F.R. § 3.358(c)(3)`'s fault requirement—requiring **only** additional disability/death resulting from VA treatment (not natural disease progression). · • **Bitemporal *George* Warning:** Attacking a *final pre-Dec. 12, 1994* denial via standalone CUE faces *George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` (`§ 20.1403(e)`). **Instead**, check whether 1-year post-decision VAMC treatment notes abated finality under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.156(b)` (*Lang*)**! · • **CRITICAL TRAP (`38 C.F.R. § 3.361(a)`):** Reopening a finally denied pre-1997 claim on or after Oct. 1, 1997 subjects the reopened claim to **post-1997 fault/unforeseeability**!
**Claim received ON OR AFTER `October 1, 1997`** *(including Supplemental Claims to reopen)*

**FAULT OR UNFORESEEABILITY REQUIRED (Medical Care) / NO FAULT (`VR&E` & `CWT`):** Must prove `"additional disability"` (`§ 3.361(b)`) proximately caused by VA fault (`§ 3.361(d)(1)`), lack of `§ 17.32` informed consent, or an `"event not reasonably foreseeable"` (`§ 3.361(d)(2)` — *Viegas*), OR direct causation by `Ch. 31 VR&E` / `§ 1718 CWT` (`§ 3.361(d)(3)`).

blocks.text: 3. Three Substantive Causation Engines (38 U.S.C. § 1151(a); 38 C.F.R. § 3.361)

First, establish **`"additional disability"` (`§ 3.361(b)`)** by comparing the veteran's actual post-treatment clinical condition with the condition that VA shows would have existed from the natural progression of the underlying disease (*Look v. Derwinski*, `2 Vet. App. 157 (1992)`). Then prove **any ONE** of these three statutory proximate-cause prongs at **`§ 5107(b)` equipoise**:
Prong 1: VA Fault, Diagnostic Delay (*Roberson*) or Defective Informed Consent (*McNair* / *Hatfield*) (§ 3.361(d)(1))

items: **Active Negligence / Error in Judgment (`§ 3.361(d)(1)(i)`):** Carelessness, negligence, lack of proper skill, error in judgment, or similar fault in furnishing care, surgery, medication, or C&P examination (e.g., severing a recurrent laryngeal or peroneal nerve outside standard surgical planes, prescribing nephrotoxic drugs despite stage-4 CKD labs, or tearing a rotator cuff during an aggressive C&P range-of-motion exam).

**Acts of Omission & Diagnostic Delay (*Roberson v. Shinseki*, `607 F.3d 809, 813–16 (Fed. Cir. 2010)`):**
• When VAMC clinicians fail to follow up a pulmonary nodule on a CT scan, elevated PSA, or positive fecal occult blood test until cancer metastasizes, your private specialist IMO **must satisfy both *Roberson* elements**: `(a)` a reasonable provider under the standard of care **should have diagnosed/treated** the condition earlier, **AND** `(b)` timely diagnosis/intervention **at least as likely as not would have prevented** the stage progression, radical surgery, or terminal outcome!

**Lack of Informed Consent (`38 C.F.R. §§ 3.361(d)(1)(ii) & 17.32`; *McNair* vs. *Hatfield*):**
• Under `§ 3.361(d)(1)(ii)`, furnishing surgical/medical treatment **without informed consent** (`38 C.F.R. § 17.32`) establishes proximate fault **even if the surgeon performed the procedure with flawless technical skill**!
• **Navigating the *McNair* / *Hatfield* Divide:** In ***McNair v. Shinseki*, `25 Vet. App. 98, 104–07 (2011)`**, the CAVC held that a *"minor, immaterial deviation"* in the consent process (such as omitting one foreseeable risk) is excused if a reasonable patient in similar circumstances would still have consented. **HOWEVER**, in ***Hatfield v. McDonough*, `33 Vet. App. 327 (2021)` (*Hatfield I*) and `36 Vet. App. 97 (2023)`**, the CAVC held that *McNair*'s reasonable-patient exception **NEVER applies when VA made NO attempt to obtain or document `§ 17.32` informed consent**! Always pull the raw `iMedConsent` audit trail—a missing consent form wins `§ 1151` under *Hatfield*!

blocks.text: Prong 2: Event Not Reasonably Foreseeable & Facility/Equipment Defects (*Viegas*) (§ 3.361(d)(2))

items: Even when **zero VA negligence occurred**, `§ 1151(a)(1)(B)` and `§ 3.361(d)(2)` award full compensation if the additional disability/death was proximately caused by **"an event not reasonably foreseeable"**—judged by what a **reasonable health-care provider** would have foreseen (rare idiosyncratic anaphylaxis/paralysis not recognized as a known complication of the procedure, as opposed to routine disclosed surgical risks).

**The *Viegas* Premises & Equipment Doctrine (*Viegas v. Shinseki*, `705 F.3d 1374, 1378–83 (Fed. Cir. 2013)`):**
• VA historically denied injuries caused by broken hospital beds, wheelchair lifts, exam tables, or bathroom grab bars, claiming `§ 1151` required direct hands-on clinician treatment.
• The Federal Circuit **reversed**, holding that `"hospital care, medical or surgical treatment, or examination"` encompasses the VA's maintenance of the **physical facility and medical equipment** used during care: when a veteran at a VAMC for medical treatment is injured because a **restroom grab bar detaches from the wall**, that mechanical failure is an **"event not reasonably foreseeable"** compensable under `§ 1151`!

blocks.text: Prong 3: Chapter 31 VR&E & § 1718 CWT Injuries — Zero Fault Required! (§ 1151(a)(2); § 3.361(d)(3))

items: Under `38 U.S.C. § 1151(a)(2)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.361(d)(3)` (expanded to `CWT` eff. Nov. 1, 2000 by `Pub. L. 106-419, § 403(b)`), any additional disability or death proximately caused by the pursuit of **`Chapter 31` Vocational Rehabilitation** or **`38 U.S.C. § 1718` Compensated Work Therapy (`CWT`)** requires **ZERO proof of VA fault or unforeseeability**—only direct causation between the training/work activity (e.g., lifting requirements in a `VR&E` apprenticeship or `CWT` shop herniating a lumbar disc) and the disability!

blocks.text: 4. Covered vs. Excluded Care Settings (§ 3.361(f) — The Community Care Kill-Switch)

lines: **The `38 U.S.C. § 1703` Community Care / MISSION Act Trap (`38 C.F.R. § 3.361(f)(1)–(3)`):** Under `38 U.S.C. § 1151(a)(1)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.361(f)`, `§ 1151` covers care **"furnished by a Department employee or in a Department facility"** (over which the Secretary has direct jurisdiction, including VBA/contract C&P examinations conducted for VA adjudication). By explicit regulation, `§ 1151` **EXCLUDES**:
1. **Private Community Care / MISSION Act providers under `38 U.S.C. § 1703` contracts (`§ 3.361(f)(1)`)**;
2. **Non-VA contract nursing homes under `38 U.S.C. § 1720` (`§ 3.361(f)(2)`)** and State Veterans Homes;
3. **Non-VA sharing-agreement facilities under `38 U.S.C. § 8153` outside VA direct jurisdiction (`§ 3.361(f)(3)`)**; and
4. **Pure domiciliary residential custody** untethered to active medical/hospital care (*Mangham v. Shinseki*, `23 Vet. App. 284, 288–90 (2009)`).
**Two Immediate Intake Saves When Injury Occurred in `§ 1703` Community Care:**

* **Save 1 (State Tort Referral):** Private `§ 1703` doctors are **not** federal employees shielded by the FTCA—immediately refer or co-counsel a **state-court medical malpractice action** before the state `1–3 year` statute of limitations runs!

* **Save 2 (VHA Administrative Referral Delay):** If **VA employees** at the VAMC negligently delayed approving the `§ 1703` Community Care consult for months while a tumor or retinal detachment progressed, *that VAMC administrative/clinical delay* **IS** furnished by a Department employee and **DOES** support both `§ 1151` and `FTCA` (*Roberson*)!

blocks.text: 5. Exact 38 U.S.C. § 1151 Ancillary & Derivative Benefits Matrix (EPIC-02 Trap 1)

Because *Alleman v. Principi*, `349 F.3d 1368, 1371–73 (Fed. Cir. 2003)` and *Mintz v. Brown*, `6 Vet. App. 277, 282–83 (1994)` hold that `§ 1151` pays Chapter 11/13 compensation *"as if"* service-connected **without** converting the disability into *actual* `§ 101(16)` service connection for other Title 38 chapters unless Congress expressly included `§ 1151`, audit every `§ 1151` award against this primary-source table:

rows: `38 U.S.C. § 1151(a)`; **`VAOPGCPREC 30-97`** (`62 FR 63604` — even preexisting NSC paraplegia does not bar `SMC(n)` for `§ 1151` bilateral hip amputation!).
**`VAOPGCPREC 8-97`** (`62 FR 15567`, Feb. 11, 1997) — any downstream physical or mental disability proximately caused or aggravated by a `§ 1151` disability is compensable under `§ 3.310`!
**Survivor `DIC` — `10-Year` `100%` Rule (`38 U.S.C. § 1318`) When Death Is Unrelated**

**`VAOPGCPREC 80-90`** (`July 18, 1990`) & `38 U.S.C. § 1318(b)` (`former § 410(b)`): `10+` continuous years of `100%`/`TDIU` `§ 1151` entitlement prior to death unlocks full `§ 1318` DIC even when death is from an unrelated cause!

**`38 U.S.C. § 1151(c)`** (added by **`Pub. L. 108-454, § 304`**, eff. Dec. 10, 2004); **`38 C.F.R. § 3.808(b)`** (`71 FR 44913`, Aug. 8, 2006) — full vehicle grant + recurring `Pub. L. 117-333` rules ([Playbook 13](/playbooks/13-ancillary-grants-sah-auto-clothing-dea-spina-bifida))!
**`38 C.F.R. § 3.810(a)`** explicitly covers appliances/topical skin medications for a disability *"compensable under 38 U.S.C. 1151"* (*Sursely* stacking applies!).

`38 U.S.C. §§ 3501(a)(1), 1781(a)` & **`38 C.F.R. § 3.807`** require disability/death arising out of *active military, naval, air, or space service* (*contrast `38 U.S.C. § 1160` paired organs, which DO unlock DEA under Kimberlin v. Brown, `5 Vet. App. 174 (1993)`!*).
***Alleman v. Principi*, `349 F.3d 1368 (Fed. Cir. 2003)`** (`§ 1151` disability does not confer Chapter 19 insurance eligibility).

***Mintz v. Brown*, `6 Vet. App. 277 (1994)`** bars the higher `§ 2307` SC burial grant (*though standard `§ 2302`/`§ 2303` non-SC burial/plot allowance IS payable because the veteran was in receipt of VA compensation!*).

blocks.text: 6. Postconditions: FTCA Dual-Track Interplay & 38 C.F.R. § 3.362 Offset Engineering
A. Why Catastrophic Malpractice Cases Should Often Pursue BOTH FTCA (SF-95) AND § 1151

items: **`FTCA` (`28 U.S.C. §§ 1346(b), 2675`):** Strict **`2-year` administrative filing bar** (`28 U.S.C. § 2401(b)`); governed by state malpractice law (and state non-economic damage caps!); pays an **immediate tax-free lump sum** (pain & suffering, lost wages, life-care plan); attorney fees capped at **`20%` administrative (`§ 2672`) / `25%` federal-court litigation (`28 U.S.C. § 2678`)**.

**`38 U.S.C. § 1151`:** **ZERO statute of limitations**; governed by uniform federal `§ 3.361` + **`§ 5107(b)` equipoise** (defeating harsh state tort caps and tort-reform hurdles!); pays **lifetime COLA-indexed `100%` / `SMC(l)–(r)(2)` monthly annuities** + `SAH` + `Ch. 39 Auto`; **`§ 5904` fees** (`20%` of past-due retroactive award prior to FTCA offset date).

blocks.text: B. Three Mandatory Pre-Settlement 38 C.F.R. § 3.362 Offset Rules (Judgments/Settlements >= Dec. 1, 1962, § 3.363)

items:
**The `§ 3.362(b)` Veteran GROSS-Offset Trap (Attorney Fees Are Recouped!):**
• Under **`38 U.S.C. § 1151(b)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.362(b)`**, when a living veteran recovers an `FTCA` settlement/judgment for the same injury, VA withholds prospective monthly `§ 1151` payments starting the month after the FTCA award becomes final until VA has recouped **the ENTIRE gross veteran share—INCLUDING the `20%–25%` FTCA attorney fees**! *(E.g., on a `$500,000` FTCA settlement where the veteran nets `$375,000` after a `25%` litigation fee, VA still withholds the full **`$500,000`** before monthly `§ 1151` checks resume!)* Never accept a modest `$75,000–$150,000` FTCA nuisance offer without modeling whether immediate `§ 1151` monthly cash flow is superior!

**Preserving Survivor `§ 1151` `DIC` via `38 C.F.R. § 3.362(c)` Settlement Allocation:**
• Unlike `§ 3.362(b)`, **`38 C.F.R. § 3.362(c)`** offsets a surviving spouse's `§ 1151` `DIC` **ONLY** by the portion of the FTCA settlement/judgment compensating **harm suffered by that individual DIC-eligible survivor** (received individually or distributed via the estate for that survivor's harm, plus proportional attorney fees)!
• **Drafting Play:** In multi-beneficiary FTCA wrongful-death/survival settlements with DOJ/OGC, explicitly allocate separate, bona fide state-law shares to **(a) adult non-DIC children** for their independent loss of parental companionship/guidance and **(b) the decedent's estate survival action** (if distributed under the will/intestacy to non-DIC heirs or used to pay estate debts/funeral expenses)—every dollar legitimately allocated to non-DIC beneficiaries is **100% exempt from offsetting the widow's monthly `§ 1151` `DIC`**! *(Compare `38 U.S.C. § 1318(d)` / `VAOPGCPREC 3-97` in [Playbook 08](/playbooks/08-survivor-dic-direct-and-1318-hypothetical)).*

**Keeping `Ch. 21` `SAH` & `Ch. 39` Auto Un-Offset Under `38 C.F.R. § 3.362(e)` (`>= Dec. 10, 2004`):**
• Under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.362(e)(1)`**, an FTCA settlement reduces `Ch. 21` `SAH`/`SHA` (`~$117,000+`) or `Ch. 39` Auto (`~$25,000+`) grants **ONLY if the settlement agreement *"includes an amount that is specifically designated for a purpose for which benefits are provided under 38 U.S.C. chapter 21 ... or chapter 39"***! When drafting FTCA release/settlement stipulations with Assistant U.S. Attorneys, **never** insert line-item designations for home modifications or adapted vehicles unless DOJ requires it—general lump-sum damages offset monthly Chapter 11 compensation under `§ 3.362(b)` while leaving the veteran's **`$140,000+` in immediate `SAH` + `Ch. 39` grants completely untouched**!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Additional Disability or Death from VA Medical Care (38 U.S.C. § 1151) & Federal Tort Claims Act Offsets
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: When VA hospital care, medical or surgical treatment, a VA examination, Veteran Readiness and Employment (Chapter 31) training, or Compensated Work Therapy causes an additional disability or death, 38 U.S.C. § 1151 pays monthly VA disability compensation or Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) 'as if' the injury were service-connected. For medical claims filed on or after October 1, 1997 (38 C.F.R. § 3.361), the claimant must show the additional harm resulted either from VA carelessness, negligence, lack of proper skill, error in judgment, or lack of informed consent—OR from an 'event not reasonably foreseeable' (including equipment/facility accidents during care under Viegas v. Shinseki). Unlike a Federal Tort Claims Act (FTCA) claim, § 1151 has no filing deadline, though any FTCA tort settlement triggers mandatory dollar-for-dollar monthly withholding offsets under 38 C.F.R. § 3.362.
record_clues: VA medical center surgical notes, delayed cancer/imaging follow-ups, medication errors, post-operative nerve or infection complications, or a formal VA 'Institutional Disclosure of Adverse Event' in your medical chart.
A missing, unsigned, or incomplete VA informed-consent form (38 C.F.R. § 17.32) prior to an invasive VA procedure (Hatfield v. McDonough).

An injury caused by a malfunctioning VA wheelchair lift, exam table, or hospital fixture while receiving VA care (Viegas v. Shinseki), or an injury/aggravation during Chapter 31 VR&E training or Compensated Work Therapy (where no VA negligence is required).
A Standard Form 95 (SF-95) Federal Tort Claims Act administrative claim or settlement agreement alongside a § 1151 compensation or survivor DIC award.
important_cautions: Community Care exclusion and state deadlines: under 38 C.F.R. § 3.361(f), harm caused by a non-VA private doctor or hospital under a MISSION Act / Community Care referral (38 U.S.C. § 1703) or contract nursing home generally is NOT covered by § 1151 (unless a VA employee's own negligence or referral delay caused the harm), and private state-law malpractice claims have strict state statutes of limitations—just as federal FTCA claims have a strict 2-year deadline on Standard Form 95 (28 U.S.C. § 2401(b)).

'As if' service connection does not unlock every ancillary benefit: even a 100% Permanent and Total § 1151 award does NOT establish eligibility for Chapter 35 Dependents' Educational Assistance (DEA), CHAMPVA family health coverage, VA Service-Disabled Veterans Insurance / VALife, or the § 2307 service-connected burial allowance (though Special Monthly Compensation, Specially Adapted Housing, and Chapter 39 Automobile grants CAN apply).

FTCA gross-offset trap: under 38 C.F.R. § 3.362(b), VA withholds monthly § 1151 compensation against the ENTIRE gross FTCA judgment or settlement—including the portion paid in tort attorney fees—unless survivor damages are properly structured among non-DIC family members under § 3.362(c).

Pre-October 1, 1997 claims: reopening a finally denied pre-Oct. 1, 1997 § 1151 claim forfeits the older Brown v. Gardner no-fault standard under 38 C.F.R. § 3.361(a), so representatives check pending-claim status before reopening, while remembering 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c)'s single final merits CUE rule per Board issue.
questions_for_representative: Was the provider or facility that caused the injury a VA-operated facility/employee covered by 38 U.S.C. § 1151, or a private Community Care provider where state malpractice deadlines may be running?
Have we requested my complete VA medical center chart, iMedConsent informed-consent records, and any Adverse Event or Root Cause Analysis disclosures?

If we are considering both a Standard Form 95 FTCA tort claim (2-year deadline) and a 38 U.S.C. § 1151 claim, how would the 38 C.F.R. § 3.362 gross-settlement offset affect my long-term monthly VA checks?

Could the injury also qualify for actual Secondary Service Connection under 38 C.F.R. § 3.310 (for example, surgery performed to treat an already service-connected disability), which DOES unlock Chapter 35 DEA and CHAMPVA?
