blocks.text: 1. Preconditions: VBMS / C-File Forms, DBQs & Code-Sheet Triggers

Pull the complete **VBMS eFolder**, **CAPRI/VistA Polytrauma & Neurology records**, **DoD blast/deployment logs**, and **every internal Rating Code Sheet** ([VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon)):

items:
**Track A (`DC 8045` TBI) File Triggers:**
• **DBQs & Clinical Evaluations:** *Initial* vs. *Review Evaluation of Residuals of TBI (`DBQ NEURO Residuals of TBI`)*; VHA **Comprehensive TBI Evaluation (`CTBIE`)** / Polytrauma Second-Level Screening notes; Neuropsychological testing batteries (`WAIS-IV`, Trail Making, California Verbal Learning Test); DoD **`MACE`** (*Military Acute Concussion Evaluation*), post-deployment **`PDHA` (`DD Form 2796`) / `PDHRA` (`DD Form 2900`)**, blast/IED incident reports, purple heart / combat action citations, or medevac records (`§ 3.156(c)` triggers!).
• **Rating Code Sheet Red Flags:**
• Pre-Oct. 23, 2008 hyphenated **`8045-9304` (`10%`)** ("post-concussion syndrome / brain disease due to trauma") with unrated contemporaneous headaches, vertigo, tinnitus, or diplopia.
• Post-Oct. 23, 2008 **`DC 8045` (`0%` or `10%`)** when any DBQ facet box shows `Level 2`, `Level 3`, or `Total`.
• Hyphenated **`9411-8045` (`50%` or `70%`)** ("PTSD with TBI") collapsing all TBI residuals into a single mental health code.

**Track B (`DC 8510–8730` Peripheral Nerves) File Triggers:**
• **DBQs & Electrodiagnostics:** *Thoracolumbar Spine DBQ*, *Cervical Spine DBQ*, and *Peripheral Nerves Conditions DBQ*; `EMG/NCS` (electromyography / nerve conduction velocity) studies; MRI reports documenting neural foraminal stenosis or nerve-root impingement at **`L2–L4`** (femoral/obturator) **and** **`L4–S3`** (sciatic), or **`C5–T1`** (cervical radicular groups); physical therapy prescriptions for an **ankle-foot orthosis (`AFO`)**, cane, walker, or wrist splint.
• **Rating Code Sheet Red Flags:**
• Post-Sept. 26, 2003 spine code (`DC 5237`–`5243`) with **zero** `85xx`/`86xx`/`87xx` nerve codes despite positive radiculopathy checkboxes on the Spine DBQ.
• Lower-extremity radiculopathy coded solely as `10%` or `20%` `DC 8520` (sciatic) when the Spine DBQ *also* checked anterior thigh numbness, decreased patellar (`L4`) reflex, or quadriceps (`L2–L4`) extension weakness (**missed `DC 8526` femoral nerve!**).
• Cervical radiculopathy affecting multiple nerve roots coded at `10%` `DC 8515` (median) instead of **`20%` minimum `DC 8510–8512`**, OR dominant (`Major`) vs. non-dominant (`Minor`) percentages reversed (`38 C.F.R. § 4.69`).

blocks.text: 2. Bitemporal Pathway Gate & Invariants (kill_switches)

Sequence your finality vehicle from **lowest evidentiary burden to highest**, strictly separating plain-text regulatory errors (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive) from later judicial reinterpretations (Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) under *George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` and `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`; see [Procedural Vehicles Piercing Finality](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality)):

rows: **AMA Silent-Omission Non-Finality (`>= Feb. 19, 2019`)** (`38 U.S.C. § 5104(b)`; *Hamill v. Collins*, `166 F.4th 1030 (Fed. Cir. 2026)`)
AMA Spine DBQ checked radiculopathy (`DC 8520`/`8526`/`8510`) or TBI DBQ raised `DC 8100` migraines / `SMC(t)` / `SMC(k)` and AMA rating decision silently omitted the issue!

**Claim remains legally pending (Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) doctrines apply in full!)** back to original AMA claim / ITF date ([Playbook 04](/playbooks/04-unadjudicated-tdiu-informal-claims-smc)).
Declassified IED/blast logs, `MACE` concussive screenings, medevac charts, line-of-duty reports, or military inpatient `EMG`/neurology records newly associated with eFolder.
**Mandatory reconsideration (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive)** back to original denied TBI or spine/nerve claim date ([Playbook 03](/playbooks/03-service-department-records-38-cfr-3-156c)).
VAMC Polytrauma, `CTBIE`, or `EMG` records created within **1 year after** a Legacy RO decision never adjudicated for new-and-material status (*Lang v. Wilkie*, `971 F.3d 1348 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`).
**Abates Legacy finality** -> all modern precedents (*Laska*, *Duran*, *Ingram*, *Johnson*) apply retroactively to original claim date!
Challenging an inadequate non-specialist TBI exam (*Barr*), a speculative Note (1) "intertwined" opinion (*Mittleider*), *Ingram* medication discounting, or post-*Laska* `SMC(t)`.
Up to **1 year prior** to ITF / `21-526EZ` / `20-0995` if ascertainable clinical worsening existed during lookback year.

**ONLY plain-text, closed-record errors:** `(a)` post-Oct. 23, 2008 TBI highest-facet math error; `(b)` post-Sept. 26, 2003 undisputed radiculopathy omitted in Legacy code sheet; `(c)` `Major`/`Minor` swap (`§ 4.69`); `(d)` `DC 8405` *tic douloureux* capped at `10%`; `(e)` post-Jan. 19, 2012 ALS `< 100%`.
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive** back to challenged decision date (pass [`Board CUE Pre-Filing Gate`](/checklists/board-cue-pre-filing-gate) before any `§ 7111` motion!).

blocks.text: Fatal Invariants (kill_switches — Stop Immediately If Triggered)

items: **Never Plead Exam Inadequacy as CUE (*Cook* Bar):** Neither an unqualified generalist conducting an initial TBI exam nor a lazy C&P examiner checking *"symptoms cannot be separated"* without rationale constitutes CUE—both are `§ 5103A` duty-to-assist errors barred from CUE by *Cook v. Principi*, `318 F.3d 1334 (Fed. Cir. 2002) (en banc)`. Litigate them via **Supplemental Claim (`20-0995`)** or timely **HLR/Board appeal**.

**Hard Effective-Date Floors:** Never cite the `10-facet` TBI table (`73 FR 54693`) for periods **before October 23, 2008**, `SMC(t)` (`Pub. L. 111-275, § 601(c)`) **before October 1, 2011**, `DC 8017` `100%` ALS (`76 FR 78823`) **before January 19, 2012**, or `§ 3.310(d)` TBI secondary presumptions (`78 FR 76196`) **before January 16, 2014**.

**Upper-Extremity Multi-Nerve Stacking Trap (`§ 4.124a` Note):** Do **not** demand separate concurrent `DC 8514` (radial) + `DC 8515` (median) + `DC 8516` (ulnar) ratings on the *same* arm for multi-root cervical radiculopathy—`§ 4.124a`'s Combined Nerve Injuries Note requires consolidating them into **`DC 8510–8513` Radicular Groups** (contrast with the **lower extremity**, where `DC 8520` sciatic + `DC 8526` femoral **do** stack!).

blocks.text: 3. Track A Execution Recipe: Traumatic Brain Injury (DC 8045) Audit & CUE Engine
Step A1 — Pre-Oct. 23, 2008 DC 8045-9304 (10%) Audit
When screening a C-file with an Iraq/Afghanistan, Gulf War, Vietnam, or training head injury rated at `10%` under `DC 8045-9304` prior to October 23, 2008:

items: **Check Pending-Claim / Staged-Rating Straddle (`73 FR 54693`):** If the claim or appeal was **pending on October 23, 2008** (or kept open via `§ 3.156(b)` *Lang* VAMC records within 1 year of a late-2007/2008 decision!), VA was legally required to assign a **staged rating** applying the `10-facet` table from **October 23, 2008 forward**!

**Audit Missed Pre-2008 Hyphenated Focal Codes (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive):** Pre-2008 `DC 8045` capped *only* `"purely subjective complaints"` (`DC 9304`) at `10%`. If the pre-2008 closed C-file contained a confirmed clinical diagnosis of **post-traumatic migraines (`DC 8045-8100`, `30%` or `50%`)**, **peripheral vestibular vertigo (`DC 8045-6204`, `10%` or `30%`)**, **post-traumatic seizures (`DC 8045-8910`–`8914`)**, **cranial nerve palsy (`DC 8205–8212`)**, or **tinnitus (`DC 6260`, `10%`)**, and the rater lumped everything into a single `10%` `DC 8045-9304` code, plead **RO CUE (`§ 3.105(a)`)** (or `§ 3.156(c)` if military head-trauma records were missing).

blocks.text: Step A2 — Post-Oct. 23, 2008 10-Facet Highest-Score Math Audit (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive)

Pull every post-Oct. 23, 2008 TBI DBQ and audit Section II (*Assessment of Cognitive Impairment and Other Residuals of TBI*) line by line against [`System 13 Diff Section 3`](/cfr/modules/13-neurological-tbi-nerves-4.120-4.124a):

items:
**The Highest-Facet Rule Is Mechanical:**
• **ANY single facet at `Level 1`** -> **`10%`**
• **ANY single facet at `Level 2`** (including `Facet 7` *Subjective Symptoms*: `3+` moderately severe subjective symptoms interfering with instrumental ADLs!) -> **`40%`**
• **ANY single facet at `Level 3`** -> **`70%`**
• **ANY single facet at `Total`** -> **`100%`**

**Classic Rater Errors Supporting Immediate CUE / HLR Reversal:**
• **Facet Averaging / Majority Counting:** DBQ checks `9` facets at `0` or `1` and **`1` facet at `Level 2` (`40%`) or `Level 3` (`70%`)**, and the rater assigns `10%` -> **undebatable `§ 3.105(a)` math CUE**!
• **Violating Note (2) (Illustrative Examples):** Rater refuses to credit a checked `Level 2` or `Level 3` facet because not every bulleted clinical example in the table was documented -> reversible legal error (Note (2) states examples do *not* all need to be present).
• **Violating Note (4) ("Mild TBI" Cap Fallacy):** Rater caps chronic residuals at `10%` because in-service `MACE` labeled the blast concussion `"mild TBI"` -> plain error under Note (4).

blocks.text: Step A3 — Note (1) Comorbid TBI + PTSD (§ 4.130) & DC 8100 Unbundling Strategy

Raters routinely collapse `DC 8045` TBI into `DC 9411` PTSD (`"9411-8045, 70%"`), costing the veteran a separate **`40%` or `70%` TBI rating** (often the exact `60%+` independent disability needed to unlock **`SMC(s)`** or **`100%` schedular**!). Attack bundled ratings using this two-prong blueprint:

items: **Attack Bare "Inextricably Intertwined" Checkboxes:** Under *Mittleider v. West*, `11 Vet. App. 181, 182 (1998)` and `DC 8045` Note (1), VA may combine TBI and a mental disorder **only** when a qualified specialist provides a reasoned medical explanation proving why specific manifestations cannot be delineated without resort to speculation.

**Surgical Partial-Facet Unbundling (Win Even When Cognitive/Mood Facets Overlap!):** Even if `Facet 1` (memory/concentration), `Facet 2` (judgment), `Facet 3` (social interaction), and `Facet 8` (neurobehavioral irritability) overlap `DC 9411` PTSD:
• **Neurological Motor/Visuospatial/Aphasic Facets (`Facets 5, 6, 9`)** are organic brain-injury deficits absent from `§ 4.130` PTSD criteria—any `Level 2` (`40%`) or `Level 3` (`70%`) score on `Facet 5`, `6`, or `9` supports a **standalone `DC 8045` rating alongside `DC 9411` PTSD**!
• **Post-Traumatic Migraines (`DC 8100`, up to `50%`):** Always claim migraines as a **distinct secondary/residual diagnosis under `DC 8100`** rather than leaving headaches inside `Facet 7` (*Subjective Symptoms*), unless `Facet 7` (`40%`) exceeds `DC 8100` (`10%/30%`). Under ***Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)`**, ensure the examiner records **unmedicated baseline** prostrating frequency/duration without discounting for sumatriptan, gepants, Botox, or CGRP inhibitors, and under ***Pierce v. Principi*, `18 Vet. App. 440 (2004)`**, document missed work/FMLA usage for `50%`!

blocks.text: Step A4 — Initial TBI Specialist Qualification Gate (M21-1 & 2007–2015 Cohort)

items: Under binding `M21-1` adjudication policy, an **initial diagnosis of TBI** must be rendered by one of **four board-eligible/certified specialists**: `(1)` **Physiatrist**, `(2)` **Psychiatrist**, `(3)` **Neurosurgeon**, or `(4)` **Neurologist**.

Whenever an initial TBI claim was denied based on a negative C&P exam signed by a **family practitioner, internist, nurse practitioner (`NP`), or physician assistant (`PA`)** without a confirming specialist diagnosis:
• File a **Supplemental Claim (`VA Form 20-0995`)** or **Board appeal (`VA Form 10182`)** challenging examination adequacy under *Barr v. Nicholson*, `21 Vet. App. 303 (2007)`.
• If the initial non-specialist C&P exam occurred between **2007 and 2015**, check VBMS correspondence to see whether VA sent (or failed to send!) a **2016 Secretarial Equitable Relief (`38 U.S.C. § 503`)** re-examination notice offering retroactive effective-date protection!

blocks.text: Step A5 — High-Dollar TBI Unlocks: § 3.310(d) Secondary Presumptions & SMC(t)

items:
**Audit All 5 `38 C.F.R. § 3.310(d)` Presumptive TBI Secondary Illnesses ([Playbook 14](/playbooks/14-secondary-service-connection-aggravation-obesity)):**
• **Following *Moderate or Severe* SC TBI (check acute `LOC > 30 min`, `PTA > 24 hrs`, `GCS <= 12`, or positive intracranial CT/MRI!):**
• **Parkinsonism / Parkinson's disease (`DC 8004`)** — *at any time* (`30%` baseline retained on top of separate extremity/bulbar ratings under *Duran v. McDonough*, `36 Vet. App. 230 (2023)`!).
• **Unprovoked seizures (`DC 8910–8914`)** — *at any time*.
• **Presenile Alzheimer's, frontotemporal, or Lewy body dementia (`DC 9310`/`9326`)** — if manifest within **`15 years`** of TBI.
• **Hypothalamo-pituitary hormone deficiencies (`§ 4.119`: hypogonadism + `SMC(k)`, hypothyroidism `DC 7903`, growth hormone/adrenal insufficiency)** — if manifest within **`12 months`** of TBI.
• **Following *Mild, Moderate, or Severe* SC TBI:**
• **Depression (`DC 9434`)** — if manifest within **`12 months` of mild TBI** OR within **`3 years` of moderate/severe TBI**!

**Screen Every A&A-Eligible TBI Veteran for `SMC(t)` (`$11,271.67/month`):**
• Under `38 U.S.C. § 1114(t)` and ***Laska v. McDonough*, `37 Vet. App. 460 (Sept. 6, 2024)`** (invalidating `38 C.F.R. § 3.352(b)(2)`'s `"higher level of care"` / licensed-professional requirement), a veteran who `(1)` needs regular Aid & Attendance (`§ 3.352(a)` — including **cognitive supervision, medication cueing, or protection from daily household/wandering hazards**!) due to SC TBI residuals, `(2)` does not otherwise qualify for `SMC(r)(2)`, and `(3)` **in the absence of such regular A&A** (provided by an **unlicensed spouse, family caregiver, or VHA `PCAFC` caregiver**) would require hospitalization, nursing home care, or other residential institutional care is entitled to **`SMC(t)` paid at the full `SMC(r)(2)` rate** ([Playbook 12](/playbooks/12-aid-and-attendance-smc-l-r1-r2-and-smc-t))!

blocks.text: 4. Track B Execution Recipe: Peripheral Nerve Radiculopathy & Multi-Nerve Stacking (DC 8510–8730)
Step B1 — Lower-Extremity Multi-Nerve Stacking on the *Same* Leg (DC 8520 + DC 8526 + DC 8528/8529)

Raters overwhelmingly default to assigning a single `DC 8520` (sciatic) rating per leg on Thoracolumbar Spine claims. Because `38 C.F.R. § 4.124a` contains **NO lower-extremity "radicular group" consolidation code**, distinct lower-extremity nerves with non-overlapping anatomical functions **stack concurrently on the exact same leg** without violating `§ 4.14` (*Esteban v. Brown*, `6 Vet. App. 259, 261–62 (1994)`):

items:
**High-ROI Lower-Extremity Audit Example:** Bilateral lumbar `L2–S1` spondylosis with `25°` forward flexion (`40%` `DC 5242`) + bilateral moderately severe sciatic radiculopathy (`40%` Left `DC 8520` + `40%` Right `DC 8520`) + bilateral moderate femoral radiculopathy (`20%` Left `DC 8526` + `20%` Right `DC 8526`):
• All **four** lower-extremity nerve ratings (`40% + 40% + 20% + 20%`) combine **first** and receive the **`+10%` `§ 4.26` Bilateral Factor** (`40` + `40` = `64` -> `64` + `20` = `71` -> `71` + `20` = `77` + `7.7` bilateral = `84.7` -> **`85%`** from leg nerves alone; combined with `40%` lumbar spine = `91%` -> **`90%`** before any cervical/tinnitus/mental rating—or **`100%` + `SMC(s)`** if `TDIU` or another `50%` exists!).

blocks.text: Step B2 — Upper-Extremity Radicular Group Ceiling vs. Single-Nerve Upgrade (DC 8510–8516)

Apply the **`§ 4.124a` Combined Nerve Injuries Note** and ***Slaughter v. McDonough*, `29 F.4th 1351 (Fed. Cir. 2022)`** with surgical precision on Cervical Spine (`DC 5237`/`5242`/`5243`) and upper-extremity claims:

items: **The Anti-Stacking Ceiling (`§ 4.124a` Note & `M21-1`):** When cervical radiculopathy affects **two or more** upper-extremity nerves/roots on the *same* arm (e.g., `C5–C6` radial/median thumb paresthesias + `C8` ulnar 4th/5th finger numbness), VA **cannot** stack `DC 8514 + 8515 + 8516` on that arm. Instead, VA rates a single **Radicular Group (`DC 8510` Upper `C5–C6`, `DC 8511` Middle `C7`, `DC 8512` Lower `C8–T1`, or `DC 8513` All Groups)**.

**The Hidden `10% -> 20%` Upgrade Goldmine (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive):**
• Look closely at the `Mild` column in [`System 13 Diff Section 5.C`](/cfr/modules/13-neurological-tbi-nerves-4.120-4.124a): Mild Median (`DC 8515`) or Ulnar (`DC 8516`) neuropathy pays only **`10%`**, whereas **Mild Radicular Group (`DC 8510–8513`) starts at `20%` (`Major` AND `Minor`)** (and Moderate jumps from `30%/20%` up to **`40% Major / 30% Minor`**)!
• **Audit Trigger:** Whenever a Cervical Spine DBQ checks involvement of **multiple nerve roots** (e.g., both `C5–C6` AND `C7` or `C8–T1`, or checks both median and ulnar distributions) and the rater assigned a single `10%` `DC 8515` per arm, demand reclassification to **`DC 8510`/`8511`/`8512` (`20%` minimum per arm; `40%/30%` if moderate!)**.

**The *Slaughter* Service-Connection Shield (`29 F.4th 1351`):**
• VA **cannot** invoke the Combined Nerve Injuries Note when one nerve injury is **service-connected** (e.g., SC carpal tunnel `DC 8515`) and a second nerve injury in the same arm is **non-service-connected** (e.g., NSC cubital tunnel)—and even when multiple nerves are SC, the radicular group rating can **never** be used to assign a *lower* evaluation than the single nerve representing the `"major involvement"`.

**Verify Dominant (`Major`) vs. Non-Dominant (`Minor`) Handedness (`38 C.F.R. § 4.69`):** Confirm the veteran's dominant hand (or ambidextrous status -> more severely injured arm MUST be `Major`!). Assigning `30%` instead of `40%` for moderate `DC 8510` on a right-handed veteran's right arm is an instant **RO CUE**.

blocks.text: Step B3 — Cross-System Stacking Without § 4.14 Pyramiding
Audit every peripheral-nerve case across these four orthogonal rating layers:

items:
**Orthopedic Spine (`§ 4.71a` Note (1); *Chavis v. McDonough*, `34 Vet. App. 1 (2021)`):**
• Rate Thoracolumbar ROM (`DC 5237–5242`, up to `40%/50%`) **and** Cervical ROM (`up to 30%/40%`)—or `DC 5243` IVDS incapacitating episodes if higher overall (*Chavis*)—**concurrently** with bilateral upper radiculopathy, bilateral lower sciatic + femoral radiculopathy, **neurogenic bladder (`DC 7512`: `20%/40%/60%` for daytime frequency or absorbent pads!)**, **bowel sphincter impairment (`DC 7332`: `10%/30%/60%/100%`)**, and **neurogenic erectile dysfunction (`DC 7522` `0%` + `SMC(k)`)** ([`Orthopedic Spine Diff`](/cfr/modules/orthopedic-spine-joints)).

**Bilateral Factor Math & `§ 4.26(d)` Exclusion Audit:**
• Compensable left + right upper-extremity nerves trigger `+10%` bilateral factor; compensable left + right lower-extremity nerves trigger `+10%` bilateral factor. For periods **on or after April 16, 2023 (`88 FR 22914`)**, verify `38 C.F.R. § 4.26(d)` automatically drops the bilateral factor if—and only if—an anomalous rounding interaction would drop `95%` down to `94%` ([`TDIU & Bilateral Exclusion Diff`](/cfr/modules/tdiu-digestive-respiratory-diffs)).

**Muscle Group Injuries (`38 C.F.R. § 4.55(a)` & `DC 5301–5323`):**
• On GSW, shrapnel, or surgical trauma files ([Playbook 01](/playbooks/01-penetrating-wounds-scars-vs-muscles), [`Muscle Injuries Diff`](/cfr/38-cfr-4.56#redline-diff)), verify whether damaged muscle groups control **different movements** from the injured peripheral nerve (`§ 4.55(a)`). If distinct (e.g., `DC 5314` Group XIV anterior thigh muscle wound + `DC 8520` sciatic posterior/distal nerve palsy), **stack both**!

**`SMC(k)` Loss of Use of a Foot or Hand (`38 U.S.C. § 1114(k)`; `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.350(a)(2), 4.63`):**
• Under *Tucker v. West*, `11 Vet. App. 369 (1998)` and `§ 4.63`, whenever complete or severe `DC 8520` sciatic (`60%/80%`) or `DC 8521` common peroneal (`40%`) foot drop eliminates effective balance/propulsion (such that amputation + prosthesis would equally serve, e.g., rigid `AFO` dependence with absent push-off), OR severe upper-extremity nerve palsy eliminates functional grasping/pinching:
• Award **`SMC(k)`** for *each* affected hand or foot (up to `3` `SMC(k)` awards—or transition to **`SMC(l)`/`(m)`** if bilateral lower-extremity or bilateral hand LOU exists!).
• Ensure the underlying nerve rating is **no lower than the amputation/LOU floor** (`40%` for one foot under `DC 5167`; `70%/60%` for one hand under `DC 5125`)!

blocks.text: 5. Postconditions: Effective Dates, Ancillary Grants & Net-Recovery Audit
Before closing any neurological, TBI, or radiculopathy award, verify every downstream contract postcondition ([`SMC & Ancillary Audit Worksheet`](/checklists/smc-and-ancillary-audit-worksheet)):

items:
**Effective-Date Verification (`§ 5110` / `§ 3.400` / `§ 3.114`):**
• Confirm staged effective dates capture `(a)` the **1-year lookback** prior to ITF/claim receipt (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(b)(2)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2)`) when VAMC/private `EMG`, `MRI`, migraine logs, or TBI evaluations predate the claim; `(b)` **October 23, 2008** on straddling TBI claims; `(c)` **October 1, 2011** floor on `SMC(t)` awards; and `(d)` original AMA claim date on silent radiculopathy/SMC omissions under *Hamill v. Collins*.

**Mandatory Ancillary Unlocks ([Playbook 13](/playbooks/13-ancillary-grants-sah-auto-clothing-dea-spina-bifida)):**
• **Bilateral Lower-Extremity LOU (including regular/constant `AFO` + cane/brace use per *Jensen v. Shulkin*, `29 Vet. App. 66 (2017)`):** Immediately file **`VA Form 26-4555`** for **`Chapter 21` Specially Adapted Housing (`SAH`, `> $120,000+` indexed grant)**!
• **Single Hand or Foot LOU (`SMC(k)`):** Immediately file **`VA Form 21-4502`** for the **`Chapter 39` Automobile & Adaptive Equipment Grant** (`Pub. L. 117-333` 10-year recurring grant rule) + annual **Clothing Allowance (`VA Form 10-8678`)** for rigid `AFO`/wrist braces (*Sursely* multiple-garment rule!).
• **`100% P&T` / `SMC(t)` Unlock:** Verify **`Chapter 35` DEA** & **`CHAMPVA`** (`38 U.S.C. § 1781`) for dependents, and flag `10-year` **`38 U.S.C. § 1318` DIC** protection for the surviving spouse.

**Offsets, Competency & Attorney Fee Audit:**
• **TBI Incompetency Defense (`38 C.F.R. § 3.353`):** High-facet `DC 8045` (`Level 3` / `Total` judgment or memory) or `SMC(t)` awards frequently trigger proposed VA financial-incompetency ratings—protect the veteran's right to a pre-determination hearing, independent financial-management evidence, or spouse fiduciary selection without withholding retroactive back pay.
• **Military Retiree & Severance Offsets:** Audit **`CRDP`** (`>= 50%` combined SC for 20-year retirees) vs. tax-free **`CRSC` (`10 U.S.C. § 1413a`)** on blast/IED TBI and combat spine/nerve injuries—applying ***Soto v. United States*, `605 U.S. 360 (2025)`** to recover uncapped retroactive CRSC arrears ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc))—and confirm non-recoupment of combat disability severance pay (`10 U.S.C. § 1212(d)(2)`).
• **`§ 5904` + EAJA Same-Work Offset:** Reconcile `20%` direct-pay contingency fees against any CAVC `EAJA` award (`28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)`) for the same appellate work.

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Traumatic Brain Injury (10-Facet Table), Separate Physical Residuals & Nerve Radiculopathy Ratings
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Since October 23, 2008, VA evaluates Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI, Diagnostic Code 8045 under 38 C.F.R. § 4.124a) across three distinct areas: (1) a 10-facet cognitive/residual table where the SINGLE highest-scored facet sets the cognitive rating (0%, 10%, 40%, 70%, or 100%—never an average!), (2) emotional/behavioral disorders under § 4.130, and (3) distinct physical/neurological conditions—such as migraines (Diagnostic Code 8100), dizziness/vertigo (Diagnostic Code 6204), tinnitus (Diagnostic Code 6260), vision changes, or nerve damage—which Note (1) requires VA to rate separately unless the exact same symptom would be counted twice. This playbook also explains how radiating nerve pain/weakness from neck or back injuries ('radiculopathy', Diagnostic Codes 8510–8730) is rated separately from spine range of motion.
record_clues: A post-October 23, 2008 TBI Disability Benefits Questionnaire (DBQ) checking Level 2 (40%), Level 3 (70%), or Total (100%) on even one of the 10 TBI facets while the Rating Code Sheet assigned only 10%.

A combined 'PTSD with TBI' rating where VA folded physical TBI residuals—like migraines, balance/vestibular issues, double vision, or motor/speech deficits—into the mental health rating without separate Diagnostic Codes.

A pre-October 23, 2008 TBI rating capped at 10% under former Diagnostic Code 8045-9304 despite separately diagnosed migraines, cranial nerve palsy, tinnitus, or vertigo—or a Veteran who never requested a post-2008 Note (5) TBI review.

A post-September 26, 2003 neck or back exam recording radiating numbness, tingling, or weakness down the arms or legs (sciatic AND femoral nerve involvement, or multi-root cervical radiculopathy) that was omitted or under-coded on the Rating Code Sheet, or severe TBI supervision needs omitted from Special Monthly Compensation at the SMC(t) rate.
important_cautions: Key effective-date floors: the 10-facet TBI rating table took effect October 23, 2008 (published September 23, 2008 at 73 FR 54693) and cannot establish Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) or back pay prior to October 23, 2008. Likewise, TBI Special Monthly Compensation under 38 U.S.C. § 1114(t) (SMC(t)) took statutory effect October 1, 2011.

Nerve combination rules on the upper vs. lower extremities: in the leg, separate sciatic (Diagnostic Code 8520) and femoral (Diagnostic Code 8526) radiculopathy ratings can combine, whereas in the same arm, multi-root cervical radiculopathy affecting radial, median, and ulnar nerves is rated as a single combined Radicular Group (Diagnostic Codes 8510–8513, with higher Major vs. Minor dominant-hand tiers under 38 C.F.R. § 4.69) rather than three separate arm nerve codes.

Exam-adequacy errors vs. CUE: an initial TBI exam performed by a non-specialist or an inadequately explained 'inextricably intertwined' PTSD/TBI opinion is a duty-to-assist error addressed in open claims/appeals—not CUE (Cook v. Principi)—and later court rulings like Laska v. McDonough (2024, invalidating extra-statutory skilled-care hurdles in 38 C.F.R. § 3.352(b)(2) for SMC(t)) are subject to George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1403(e) and 20.1409(c).

Quarantined rulemakings: VA's November 12, 2024 neurological rating notice (RIN 2900-AQ73, 89 FR 88917) remains a proposed rule that is not enacted law, and the February 17, 2026 § 4.10 medication rule (91 FR 7118) was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712).
questions_for_representative: Does my TBI examination sheet show a Level 2 (40%), Level 3 (70%), or Total (100%) box checked on any single TBI facet, and were my migraines, vertigo, vision, and tinnitus rated separately under Note (1)?
If my TBI was combined with PTSD, did the examiner provide a medical explanation for why specific cognitive vs. emotional symptoms could or could not be separated?

On my neck or back Rating Code Sheet, did VA separately rate every affected peripheral nerve (such as both sciatic and femoral nerves in the legs, or the appropriate Radicular Group and dominant-arm column in the arms)?
If service-connected TBI requires regular daily supervision, reminders, or Aid and Attendance from family to stay safe at home, should we evaluate entitlement to SMC(t) under Laska v. McDonough?

title: Playbook 19: Extraschedular Referrals (§ 3.321(b)(1)), Analogous Code Selection (§ 4.20 / Webb) & Temporary 100% Hospital/Convalescent Audits (§§ 4.28–4.30)
cfrCitations: 38 C.F.R. § 4.10 (91 FR 7118 Feb. 17, 2026 IFR rescinded at 91 FR 9712 Feb. 27, 2026)
keyPrecedents: Nat'l Org. of Veterans' Advocates, Inc. v. Sec'y of Veterans Affairs, 927 F.3d 1263 (Fed. Cir. 2019)
cFileTriggers: C&P exam or lay record documenting assistive devices (wheelchair, walker, cane, braces), frequent falls, or hospitalizations uncaptured by goniometric ROM criteria (§ 3.321(b)(1) / Spellers v. Wilkie)

McDonough*, and **(Track C)** `38 C.F.R. §§ 4.28–4.30` temporary `100%` awards paired with automatic *Bradley* `SMC(s)`.

*(Cross-references: Verbatim regulatory text in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.1–4.31 Subpart A General Rating Policy & Two-Era § 3.321(b)(1) Extraschedular Evolution](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.1-4.31-general-policy-snapshots), [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. § 4.16 Total Disability Based on Individual Unemployability (1975–Present Evolution & Former § 4.16(c))](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-4.16-tdiu-evolution), [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.105(d)–(i), 3.343, 3.344, 3.951, 3.953 & 3.957 (Rating Reductions, Stabilization & Statutory Protections)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.105e-3.344-3.951-3.957-reductions), and [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: Former 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.155(a) & 3.157(b) Informal Claims (Repealed March 24, 2015)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.155-3.157b-informal-claims-pre-2015); doctrinal synthesis in [`Part 4 Subpart A General Rating Policy (§§ 4.1–4.31)`](/cfr/modules/subpart-a-general-rating-policy-4.1-4.31), [`TDIU, § 4.26(d) & Digestive Diffs`](/cfr/modules/tdiu-digestive-respiratory-diffs), [Master SMC Treatise & Step Math](/docs/smc-complete-treatise-and-step-math), [VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon), [Master `VAOPGCPREC` Digest](/docs/vaopgcprec-index), [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log), [Playbook 04 (TDIU, `§ 3.157(b)` & SMC)](/playbooks/04-unadjudicated-tdiu-informal-claims-smc), and [Playbook 05 (Void Rating Reductions)](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings)).*
1. Design-by-Contract Preconditions & Invariants (kill_switches)
A. Preconditions (VBMS / C-File Form, Clinical & Code-Sheet Triggers)
Screen the VBMS eFolder, Rating Code Sheets ([VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon)), and VistA/CAPRI medical files for these exact triggers:

items: **Forms & Filings:** `VA Form 21-526EZ` (post-Mar. 24, 2015 claim for increase / temporary total), `VA Form 21-0966` (Intent to File within 1 year of hospital admission or surgery), `VA Form 20-0995` / `20-0996` / `10182` (AMA review lanes), `VA Form 21-8940` (TDIU pivot), and legacy `VA Form 10-7131` / `10-564-D` VAMC hospital exchange slips (`< Mar. 24, 2015`).

**Code-Sheet Notation Triggers:**
• **Hyphenated `xx99-xxxx` Analogous Codes (`§ 4.27`):** E.g., `7599-7522`, `8599-8520`, `5299-5257`, `7399-7346`, or `6899-6845` capped at `0%`, `10%`, or `20%`.
• **`Paragraph 28` / `Paragraph 29` / `Paragraph 30` Entries:** Internal code-sheet shorthand for `§§ 4.28, 4.29, and 4.30` awards—audit start dates, end dates, absence of `SMC (S-1)`, and post-expiration percentage drops!

**Clinical Record Triggers:**
• Prescription of **wheelchair, walker, crutches, cane, AFO brace**, frequent falls, or dizziness/syncope during orthopedic/hearing/neurological claims where the assigned DC evaluates only goniometric range of motion or audiometric thresholds (*Spellers v. Wilkie*).
• **VAMC or VA-approved inpatient discharge summaries exceeding `21` continuous days** for an SC physical or psychiatric condition (`§ 4.29`).
• **Operative reports** (inpatient or outpatient ambulatory surgery) or **orthopedic cast-application notes** immobilizing at least one major joint (`shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip, knee, ankle`) for an SC disability (`§ 4.30`).

blocks.text: B. Bitemporal Pathway Gate & Fatal Invariants (kill_switches)

Before selecting a procedural vehicle ([Procedural Vehicles Piercing Finality](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality)), enforce the *George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` / `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)` boundary:

rows: Deciding whether schedular criteria are "inadequate" (*Thun* Step 1) and whether symptoms cause "marked interference with employment" (Step 2) requires discretionary weighing of facts—**never CUE** (`§ 20.1403(d)(3)`). Litigate via **Board appeal (`10182`), HLR (`20-0996`), CAVC remand**, or non-finality (`§ 3.156(b)–(c)` / AMA *Hamill* `§ 5104(b)`).

**Kill-Switch (`82 FR 57830`, eff. Jan. 8, 2018):** VA abolished collective *Johnson* extraschedular ratings effective Jan. 8, 2018, upheld in *Thurlow v. Wilkie*, `30 Vet. App. 231 (2018)` and *NOVA v. Sec'y*, `927 F.3d 1263 (Fed. Cir. 2019)`. Post-Jan. 8, 2018, pivot collective functional unemployability to **`38 C.F.R. § 4.16(b)` extraschedular TDIU**!

*Webb* (`71 F.4th 1377`) invalidated VA's demand for literal anatomical preconditions in analogous ratings on June 27, 2023. Cannot support CUE against final pre-June 2023 decisions (*George*), **but governs all open/pending/appealed claims and new Supplemental Claims (`20-0995`)**.

When VAMC hospital (`>21` days) or surgical/cast records were constructively in the record (`>= July 21, 1992` *Bell* / [`VAOPGCPREC 12-95`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index)) alongside a timely claim (or pre-Mar. 24, 2015 `§ 3.157(b)` report) and satisfied every objective criterion, omitting `100%`—or omitting statutory **`SMC(s)`** (`>= Nov. 26, 2008` *Bradley*) when other SC ratings combined to `>= 60%`—is **undebatable RO/Board CUE**!

Cutting a veteran **below** their pre-surgical running evaluation upon expiration of `§ 4.29`/`§ 4.30` without `§ 3.105(e)` 60-day advance notice is **void *ab initio*** ([Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings))—requiring **zero CUE burden** for full retroactive restoration!

blocks.text: 2. Track A — Extraschedular Referrals (38 C.F.R. § 3.321(b)(1)) Litigation Recipe
Step 0: Exhaust All Schedular Maximization Tools First (*Morgan v. Wilkie*)

Under ***Morgan v. Wilkie*, `31 Vet. App. 162, 166–68 (2019)`**, extraschedular referral under `§ 3.321(b)(1)` is an exceptional safety valve triggered *only* after VA has exhausted every standard schedular mechanism to compensate the veteran's actual symptoms:

items: Check **separate non-pyramiding Diagnostic Codes (`§ 4.14` / *Esteban*)** (e.g., rating neurological radiculopathy, gait instability `DC 5257`, flexion `DC 5260`, extension `DC 5261`, or painful scars `DC 7804` separately).

Check **unmedicated baseline functional impairment (`§ 4.10` / *Ingram v. Collins*, `38 Vet. App. 130 (2025)`)** (and screen out any decision tainted by VA's rescinded 10-day Feb. 17–27, 2026 IFR, `91 FR 7118`, rescinded at `91 FR 9712`).
Check **`§ 4.7` higher-of-two-evaluations** and **`§ 4.20` higher-ceiling analogous codes** (Track B below).
Plead **schedular maximization as Primary Relief** and **`§ 3.321(b)(1)` referral in the Alternative**!

blocks.text: Step 1: Execute the Three-Step *Thun* Referral Framework (*Thun*, *Spellers*, *Anderson*)

Under ***Thun v. Peake*, `22 Vet. App. 111, 115–16 (2008)`, *aff'd sub nom. Thun v. Shinseki*, `572 F.3d 1366 (Fed. Cir. 2009)`** and [`VAOPGCPREC 6-96`](/docs/vaopgcprec-index), neither the RO nor the Board has jurisdiction to assign an initial extraschedular rating in the first instance; instead, they must refer the claim to the **Director, Compensation Service** whenever Steps 1 and 2 are met:

items:
***Thun* Step 1 (Schedular Inadequacy Comparison — *Spellers v. Wilkie*, `30 Vet. App. 211 (2018)`):**
• Compare the **severity and type** of the veteran's actual SC symptoms against the specific criteria of all applicable Diagnostic Codes.
• **Winning CAVC Remand Pattern (*Spellers*):** In *Spellers*, `30 Vet. App. at 216–18`, the Board denied `§ 3.321(b)(1)` referral for a back/hip disability rated on range of motion despite record evidence that the veteran required a **cane/walker, could not walk more than one block, and had difficulty standing/sitting**. The CAVC vacated: goniometric ROM tables measure *joint excursion*, **not** reliance on assistive ambulation devices or inability to sit/stand! Always isolate functional impacts *wholly absent* from the DC text (e.g., wheelchair/cane reliance prior to diagnostic codes expressly adding assistive devices, frequent syncope, incontinence, medication sedation, or episodic bedrest in non-incapacitating-episode codes).

***Thun* Step 2 (Exceptional Factors — Disjunctive `"OR"` Test!):**
• Show that this unusual disability picture exhibits governing norms such as **(a) marked interference with employment** (missed workdays, demotion, inability to perform physical/cognitive tasks, workplace accommodations—*even if the veteran is still employed and NOT totally unemployable!*) **OR (b) frequent periods of hospitalization**.

***Thun* Step 3 (Director Award & De Novo Board Review — *Anderson v. Shinseki*, `22 Vet. App. 423 (2009)`):**
• Once Steps 1 and 2 are satisfied (or reasonably raised without adequate Board reasons or bases), the RO/Board **must refer** the file to the Director, Compensation Service (`§ 3.321(b)(1)`).
• **Crucial Post-Referral Appellate Rule (*Anderson*, `22 Vet. App. at 427–29`; *cf. Wages v. McDonald*, `27 Vet. App. 233, 238–39 (2015)` on `§ 4.16(b)`):** While the Board cannot *bypass* the Director initially, **once the Director issues a decision denying extraschedular relief (or assigning an inadequate percentage), the Board reviews the Director's decision *de novo***—owing zero deference to the Director and possessing full authority to award or increase the extraschedular rating itself!

blocks.text: Step 2: Navigate the January 8, 2018 (82 FR 57830) Collective-Impact Split

rows: **Pre-`January 8, 2018` Period** *(e.g., Legacy Board appeal or CAVC remand covering pre-Jan. 8, 2018 staged periods where raised)*
***Johnson v. McDonald*, `762 F.3d 1362 (Fed. Cir. 2014)`**; ***Yancy v. McDonald*, `27 Vet. App. 484 (2016)`**

Former `§ 3.321(b)(1)` used the plural *"service-connected disability or disabilities"*, requiring collective extraschedular consideration when the synergistic effect of multiple SC conditions was argued or reasonably raised (*Yancy*) for staged periods prior to Jan. 8, 2018.
***Thurlow v. Wilkie*, `30 Vet. App. 231 (2018)`**; ***NOVA v. Sec'y*, `927 F.3d 1263 (Fed. Cir. 2019)`**

Amended `§ 3.321(b)(1)` restricts extraschedular evaluations strictly to **"an individual"** single SC disability (`Thurlow` held applying the amended rule to claims pending on/after Jan. 8, 2018 is lawful for post-amendment periods). · **MANDATORY PIVOT:** Whenever multiple `<60%/<70%` SC disabilities *collectively* destroy employability post-Jan. 8, 2018, pivot immediately to **`38 C.F.R. § 4.16(b)` Extraschedular TDIU** (`VA Form 21-8940` + vocational expert report — see [VASRD Historical Diff: TDIU (§ 4.16), May 2024 Digestive (§ 4.114) & Pending Sleep Apnea/Tinnitus Proposals](/cfr/modules/tdiu-digestive-respiratory-diffs)), which *expressly* aggregates all SC disabilities!

blocks.text: 3. Track B — 38 C.F.R. § 4.20 Analogous Code Selection & *Webb v. McDonough* Playbook

Unlisted conditions (peripheral dysautonomia/POTS, rare autoimmune/connective-tissue disorders, post-surgical visceral syndromes, pelvic floor dysfunction, complex regional pain) are frequently parked by raters under a dead-end analogous code (`xx99-xxxx` under `§ 4.27`) that caps out at `10%` or `20%`.
Four-Step Analogous Re-Engineering Protocol:

items: **Decode the Hyphenated Code Sheet Entry (`§ 4.27`):** Pull the internal Rating Code Sheet ([VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon)). Locate every `xx99-xxxx` code and check the **maximum schedular ceiling** of the second 4-digit code.

**Build a Comparative *Lendenmann* Matrix (`3 Vet. App. 345, 350–51 (1992)`):** Identify an alternative VASRD Diagnostic Code with `30%`, `50%`, `60%`, or `100%` tiers and map all three mandatory factors side-by-side in your brief/IMO:
• **Factor 1 — Functions Affected:** Does the candidate DC measure the exact physiological/occupational function impaired (e.g., orthostatic syncope/cardiac output vs. peripheral nerve paralysis vs. voiding frequency)?
• **Factor 2 — Anatomical Localization:** Does the candidate DC sit in the same organ system or anatomical region?
• **Factor 3 — Symptomatology:** Do the candidate DC's symptom descriptors match the veteran's actual clinical manifestations?
• *(Appellate Hook: Whenever a claimant proposes a plausible alternative analogous DC or the record shows the assigned DC poorly matches one of the three factors, the Board commits reversible `§ 7104(d)(1)` error if it fails to compare both codes across all three *Lendenmann* factors!)*

**Defeat Literal Prerequisite Denials Under *Webb v. McDonough* (`71 F.4th 1377 (Fed. Cir. 2023)`):**
• **The Trap:** VA agrees to rate an unlisted disorder by analogy to `DC XXXX`, but then denies the `20%`, `30%`, or `60%` tier because the veteran lacks an **organic/anatomical hallmark unique to the named disease** (just as VA denied `20%` under `7599-7522` in *Webb* because medication-induced erectile dysfunction lacked physical *"penile deformity"*, or denies `DC 7206` GERD analogy because non-GERD esophageal dysmotility lacks acid-induced `"esophageal stricture"`).
• **The *Webb* Strike:** Cite *Webb*, `71 F.4th at 1381–83`: under `38 C.F.R. § 4.20` (and `§§ 4.7, 4.21`), an unlisted disability is rated by analogy *precisely because it is not the listed condition*. Requiring literal satisfaction of a disease-specific structural prerequisite renders `§ 4.20` a nullity; once `DC XXXX` is selected as closely related, VA must evaluate whether the unlisted disorder's **functional impairment and symptomatology** match (or `§ 4.7` more nearly approximate) the compensable tier!

blocks.text: 4. Track C — Temporary 100% Hospitalization (§ 4.29) & Convalescence (§ 4.30) Audit Engine

Thousands of dollars in tax-free `100%` + `SMC(s)` back pay go unclaimed every year because veterans undergo VAMC or private surgeries, joint replacements, cast immobilizations, or `22+`-day inpatient psychiatric/medical admissions for already-service-connected conditions without filing a timely `§§ 4.29/4.30` audit.
Step 1: Verify Objective Substantive Triggers (§§ 4.28, 4.29, 4.30 & *Hudgens*)

items:
**Inpatient Admission Exceeding `21` Continuous Days (`38 C.F.R. § 4.29`):**
• Count exact admission-to-discharge calendar days in a **VA medical center, VA domiciliary hospital ward, or VA-approved/contracted hospital** (`22` days minimum!).
• Verify from the admission note and discharge summary that **active treatment or observation of a service-connected disability** (e.g., inpatient PTSD residential trauma program, heart failure admission, osteomyelitis/cellulitis IV antibiotics) began on day 1 (or identify the exact later hospital day SC treatment was instituted and continued `>21` days following an NSC admission under `§ 4.29(b)`).
• **Payment Span:** `100%` runs from the **first day of continuous SC hospitalization** through the **last day of the month of hospital discharge (regular discharge or release to non-bed care) or the last day of the month of termination of SC treatment/observation** (`§ 4.29(a)`), plus optional `1–3` months post-discharge convalescence (`§ 4.29(e)`) and up to `3` further months upon VSCM approval (`§ 4.29(f)`).

**Post-Surgical or Non-Surgical Cast Convalescence (`38 C.F.R. § 4.30`):**
• Unlike `§ 4.29`, **`§ 4.30` covers surgeries or casts performed in ANY licensed private OR VA hospital or outpatient ambulatory surgical center** (`<21` days or same-day outpatient!) for an SC disability, provided **any ONE** of three triggers is met:
• **`§ 4.30(a)(1)`:** Surgery necessitating **at least `1 month` (`30+` days) of convalescence** (documented by surgeon return-to-work / post-op restriction notes: rotator cuff repair, spinal fusion/laminectomy, meniscectomy/ACL reconstruction, hernia/bowel resection, radical prostatectomy);
• **`§ 4.30(a)(2)`:** Surgery resulting in **severe postoperative residuals** (incompletely healed surgical wounds/drains, therapeutic immobilizing casts/splints, required crutches/wheelchair preventing navigation, or strict therapeutic confinement to the home); **OR**
• **`§ 4.30(a)(3)`:** **Immobilization by cast, without surgery, of one or more major joints** (`shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip, knee, ankle` — note that rigid prescribed walking boots/splints that functionally immobilize a major joint like a cast should be briefed with physician certification of cast-equivalent immobilization!).
• **Payment Span & Extensions:** `100%` begins on the **exact date of hospital admission or outpatient surgery/cast** and continues for **`1, 2, or 3 months` from the first day of the month following hospital discharge or outpatient release** (`§ 4.30(a)`), plus **`1–3` additional months** (`up to 6 mos`) upon medical proof of ongoing convalescence (`§ 4.30(b)(1)`).
• **Prosthetic Joint Replacement Check (*Hudgens v. McDonald*, `823 F.3d 630 (Fed. Cir. 2016)` & `85 FR 76453`):** Always check whether surgery implanted a hip/knee/shoulder/ankle prosthesis (`DC 5051–5056` — [VASRD Historical Diff: Spine & Musculoskeletal Joints (38 C.F.R. §§ 4.40, 4.45, 4.59, 4.71a)](/cfr/modules/orthopedic-spine-joints)):
• Before **February 7, 2021** (`85 FR 76453`), `DC 5054/5055` mandated **`1 full year` (`12–13 months`) at `100%`**—and under *Hudgens*, **partial knee replacements** also unlocked `DC 5055` for claims filed/pending prior to July 16, 2015 (`80 FR 42040`)!
• On or after **February 7, 2021**, total joint replacements under `DC 5054/5055` receive **`4 months` at `100%`** following surgery (extendable via `§ 4.30(b)` if severe residuals persist!), while partial replacements/resurfacing procedures qualify directly under **`§ 4.30`**.

blocks.text: Step 2: Lock In the Effective Date (§ 3.400(o)(2) vs. Legacy § 3.157(b))

items:
**Modern Rule (Treatment On or After `March 24, 2015`, `79 FR 57660`):**
• Because VA repealed `former 38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b)` effective March 24, 2015, even a surgery performed *inside a VAMC* **does NOT automatically file a claim**!
• Under **`38 U.S.C. § 5110(b)(2)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2)`**, the veteran **MUST submit an Intent to File (`VA Form 21-0966`) or formal claim (`VA Form 21-526EZ` / `20-0995`) within `1 year` of the date of hospital admission or surgery** to capture the day-1 retroactive `100%` effective date! *(Practice Tip: If a client had a 3-month convalescence starting `11` months ago, file an immediate `21-0966` TODAY before the 1-year `§ 3.400(o)(2)` window closes!)*

**Legacy Goldmine (VAMC Admission/Surgery Before `March 24, 2015` — `Former 38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b)`):**
• For any **VA hospital admission or VA surgical report** prior to March 24, 2015 for an **already-service-connected disability** (even `0%` SC!), `former § 3.157(b)` (`26 FR 1571`) treated the VAMC medical report itself as a **mandatory informal claim for increase/temporary total benefits on the date of admission** ([Playbook 04](/playbooks/04-unadjudicated-tdiu-informal-claims-smc); [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: Former 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.155(a) & 3.157(b) Informal Claims (Repealed March 24, 2015)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.155-3.157b-informal-claims-pre-2015))! If VA never adjudicated `§ 4.29`/`§ 4.30` on that pre-2015 VAMC surgery/admission, demand immediate retroactive payment via **pending unadjudicated claim** or **RO CUE (`§ 3.105(a)`)**!

blocks.text: 5. Postconditions: Automatic *Bradley* SMC(s) & Void Post-Convalescent Reductions
Never close a `§§ 4.28–4.30` (or `DC 5054/5055/7528`) audit without running both postcondition checks:
Postcondition 1: Mandatory Temporary Statutory SMC(s) (*Bradley v. Peake*, 22 Vet. App. 280 (2008))

items: **The Rule (`38 U.S.C. § 1114(s)(1)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.350(i)(1)`):** Statutory Housebound `SMC(s)` (`$4,408.53/mo` vs. `$3,938.58/mo` in 2026 = **`+$469.95/month` net gain**) does **NOT** require that the `100%` disability be permanent! Whenever a veteran receives a temporary `100%` evaluation for **one single SC disability** under `§ 4.28`, `§ 4.29`, `§ 4.30`, `DC 5054/5055`, or active cancer (`DC 7528`), check the Rating Code Sheet for the veteran's *other* permanent SC disabilities ([Master SMC Treatise & Step Math](/docs/smc-complete-treatise-and-step-math); [`SMC & Ancillary Audit Worksheet`](/checklists/smc-and-ancillary-audit-worksheet)).

**Automatic Trigger (CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive):** If those separate, independent permanent SC disabilities combine to **`60%` or more** under `§ 4.25` (including any `§ 4.26` bilateral factor on paired non-surgical extremities), **VA is statutorily required to pay `SMC(s)` for every single month the temporary `100%` evaluation is in effect** (*Bradley*, `22 Vet. App. at 293–94`)! Raters routinely pay `100%` under `Paragraph 29/30` while forgetting to code `SMC (S-1)`—creating an effortless, pure-math **RO CUE (`§ 3.105(a)`)** on any final award!

blocks.text: Postcondition 2: The Post-Convalescent Unlawful Reduction Trap (38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e) & *Foster*)
Audit the exact rating percentage VA assigned **the day after** the `§ 4.29` or `§ 4.30` temporary `100%` period expired:

items: **Lawful Expiration to Pre-Surgical Baseline (Exempt from `§ 3.105(e)`):** Suppose a veteran held a running **`20%`** right shoulder evaluation, underwent rotator cuff surgery, received `100%` under `§ 4.30` for `3` months, and automatically reverted to **`20%`** on month `4`. Under the concluding text of `§§ 4.29` and `4.30`, reverting to the pre-existing `20%` baseline at the end of a fixed temporary period is **exempt** from `38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e)` 60-day advance notice (though the veteran can still appeal for a `30%+` post-surgical residual rating!).

**VOID Reduction *Below* Pre-Surgical Running Baseline (`§ 3.105(e)` & `§ 3.344` Violated!):** Suppose that same veteran held a running **`30%`** knee or **`40%`** lumbar spine rating before surgery (especially if in effect `5+` years under `§ 3.344(c)`!), received `3` months of `§ 4.30` `100%` convalescence, and at month `4` VA dropped the rating from `100%` straight down to **`10%`** (*below* the `30%/40%` pre-surgical running award!) **without** issuing a `§ 3.105(e)` proposal-to-reduce letter, affording 60 days to submit evidence, and waiting 60 days post-final notice (*or* discontinued a `DC 7528` post-treatment cancer `100%` without the mandatory 6-month C&P exam and `§ 3.105(e)` 60-day notice enforced in ***Foster v. McDonough*, `34 Vet. App. 338, 346–49 (2021)`**, noting *Foster* distinguishes `§ 3.105(e)` notice compliance from `§§ 3.343/3.344` stabilized-rating improvement rules):
• **Remedy ([Playbook 05](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings)):** That cut below the pre-surgical baseline is **void *ab initio***! Demand immediate **outright reinstatement** of the `30%/40%` baseline (or `100%` under *Foster* until lawful `§ 3.105(e)` effective date) retroactive to the unlawful reduction date—**with zero CUE burden**!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Unusual Disability Impacts (Extraschedular Referrals), Analogous Ratings & Temporary 100% Hospital/Surgical Pay
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Sometimes VA's standard rating tables do not fit a Veteran's real-world condition—either because an exceptional single disability causes work interference like frequent falls, wheelchair reliance, or repeated flare hospitalizations not captured by standard range-of-motion numbers (extraschedular referral under 38 C.F.R. § 3.321(b)(1)), or because the condition has no exact Diagnostic Code and must be rated 'by analogy' to a closely related code (38 C.F.R. § 4.20). Separately, §§ 4.29 and 4.30 ('Paragraph 29' and 'Paragraph 30') provide temporary 100% compensation when a service-connected disability requires more than 21 days in the hospital, surgery needing at least 1 month of convalescence or leaving severe postoperative residuals, or non-surgical cast immobilization of at least one major joint.
record_clues: Medical or lay evidence showing reliance on a wheelchair, walker, cane, or braces, frequent falls, or work absences that the standard Diagnostic Code criteria do not measure (Thun v. Peake; Spellers v. Wilkie).

A hyphenated '-99' analogous code on your Rating Code Sheet where VA denied a higher percentage solely because your unlisted condition lacked a literal anatomical feature of the borrowed code (rejected in Webb v. McDonough).
Hospital discharge summaries showing 22 or more continuous inpatient days for a service-connected disability without a temporary 100% award under 38 C.F.R. § 4.29.

Surgical operative reports or orthopedic clinic notes documenting service-connected surgery (with >=1 month recovery) or major-joint cast immobilization without a temporary 100% award under 38 C.F.R. § 4.30—or a post-surgery rating dropped below your pre-surgery percentage without 60 days' advance notice under 38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e).
important_cautions: January 8, 2018 change to § 3.321(b)(1): before January 8, 2018, § 3.321(b)(1) allowed collective extraschedular referrals across multiple disabilities (Johnson v. McDonald). Effective January 8, 2018 (82 FR 57830, upheld in Thurlow v. Wilkie and NOVA v. Secretary), § 3.321(b)(1) applies strictly to a single disability, while combined multi-disability unemployability goes through 38 C.F.R. § 4.16(b) extraschedular TDIU.

Post-March 24, 2015 filing window for temporary 100% claims: after VA repealed former 38 C.F.R. § 3.157(b) effective March 24, 2015, VA surgical or hospital reports no longer act as automatic informal claims—so a complete claim or Intent to File must generally be received within 1 year of the hospitalization or surgery under 38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2) to lock in full retroactive convalescent pay.

Non-referral for § 3.321(b)(1) extraschedular review involves fact-specific weighing rather than Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE), and under George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. §§ 20.1403(e) and 20.1409(c), Webb v. McDonough (2023) cannot establish CUE in final pre-2023 decisions (and only one final merits CUE decision is allowed per prior Board issue).
VA's February 17, 2026 § 4.10 medication Interim Final Rule (91 FR 7118) was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712) and is not active law.
questions_for_representative: Does my condition cause exceptional work interference—like assistive-device use, falls, or flare-related absences—that warrants referral to the Director of Compensation Service under 38 C.F.R. § 3.321(b)(1) (or § 4.16(b) if multiple disabilities combine to prevent work)?
If my condition is rated under a hyphenated '-99' analogous code, is there a closer Diagnostic Code based on function, anatomical location, and symptoms under 38 C.F.R. § 4.20 and Webb v. McDonough?
Have we filed an Intent to File or claim within 1 year of my service-connected surgery, joint cast immobilization, or 22+ day hospital stay to secure temporary 100% benefits under §§ 4.29–4.30?

During any months I received a temporary 100% convalescent or hospital rating, did my other permanent service-connected disabilities combine to 60% or more to trigger statutory SMC(s) under Bradley v. Peake?
