blocks.text: Winning a `100%` rating or a multi-decade retroactive effective date is only half of the representation contract: **unlawful VA/DFAS withholdings, Chapter 61 concurrent-receipt traps, gross-vs.-net severance recoupments, and `38 U.S.C. § 5904(d)` fee-base errors** routinely siphon tens or hundreds of thousands of dollars out of a favorable award. Every grant must pass a post-decision offset and fee-withholding audit.

*(Cross-references: Verbatim offset & effective-date rules in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.114, 3.400, 3.2500, 3.654, 3.665, 3.700 & 3.701 (Effective Dates, Liberalizing Laws, Continuous Pursuit, Drill/Incarceration Adjustments, Severance/Separation Recoupment & Benefit Elections)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.114-3.400-3.700-effective-dates-offsets); verbatim waiver/pension/competency rules in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.274–3.279, 3.272(g), 3.353, 3.105(h)–(i), 3.500(b), 1.963 & 1.965 (Pension Net Worth & 36-Month Lookback, Deductible Medical Expenses, Competency Due Process & Overpayment Waivers)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.274-3.279-3.353-1.965-pension-competency-waivers); [Master Effective-Date & Staged-Rating Treatise](/docs/effective-dates-and-staged-ratings-treatise); [`Part 3 Pension Net-Worth & Effective-Date Diffs`](/cfr/modules/pension-net-worth-and-effective-date-diffs); [Playbook 21 (Overpayment Waivers `§ 5302`, Incompetency `§ 3.353` & Wartime Pension)](/playbooks/21-overpayment-waivers-incompetency-and-wartime-pension); [Playbook 06 (*Nehmer* & Uncapped `CRSC` / *Soto*)](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc); [Playbook 11 (Guard/Reserve `ADT`/`IADT`)](/playbooks/11-guard-reserve-adt-iadt-and-line-of-duty); [Playbook 17 (`§ 1151` & `FTCA` `§ 3.362` Gross Offset)](/playbooks/17-section-1151-va-malpractice-and-ftca-interplay); [Master SMC Treatise](/docs/smc-complete-treatise-and-step-math); [`Post-Grant Award Letter & Withholding Audit Checklist`](/checklists/award-letter-and-withholding-audit-checklist); [Master `VAOPGCPREC` Digest](/docs/vaopgcprec-index); [Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon); and [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).*
1. Preconditions: VBMS, DD-214, DFAS & Award-Letter Triggers
Pull these exact documents from VBMS and the client before closing any retroactive grant:

items:
**Separation & Retirement Source Records:**
• **`DD Form 214` (`Blocks 18, 24, 26 & 28`)** and any **`DD Form 215`** correction: Screen Separation Program Designator (`SPD`) codes—**`JFL` / `JFM` / `SFJ`** (Disability Severance Pay under `10 U.S.C. § 1212`), **`JEB` / `SEB` / `SFK`** (Permanent/Temporary Disability Retired List `PDRL`/`TDRL` under `10 U.S.C. ch. 61`), or **`JBK` / `JGH` / `JCC` / `KBK`** (Involuntary Separation Pay `ISP`, Special Separation Benefit `SSB` `10 U.S.C. § 1174a`, or Voluntary Separation Incentive `VSI` `10 U.S.C. § 1175`). Record the exact separation date and exact dollar entry in Block 18 (`Remarks`), plus **`DA Form 199` / `AF Form 356` / Navy PEB** combat-related (`V1`/`V3`/`10a`/`10c`) findings!
• **`DFAS Retiree Account Statement (RAS)`** (or Coast Guard `PPC` statement): Check Gross Retired Pay, `VA Waiver` (`38 U.S.C. § 5305`), `CRDP` restoration amount, `SBP` premium deductions, and federal tax withholding.

**VBMS Financial & Withholding Artifacts:**
• **VA Award Letter (`Payment Summary` & `Withholding` table):** Flag every line showing `"Withholding for Military Retired Pay"`, `"Disability Severance Pay"`, `"Separation Pay"`, `"Readjustment Pay"`, `"Drill Pay Adjustment"`, or `"Incarceration Adjustment"`.
• **`DFAS Audit Error Worksheet (AEW)`:** Electronic reconciliation worksheet transmitted between DFAS (or Coast Guard PPC) and VA's Hines ITC whenever a military retiree wins retroactive VA benefits.
• **`VA Form 21-8951` / `21-8951-2`:** Annual *Notice of Waiver of VA Compensation or Pension to Receive Military Pay and Allowances* (Reserve/National Guard drill-pay audit).

blocks.text: 2. Bitemporal Pathway Gate (CUE-Safe vs. Administrative Recalculation vs. DoD/COFC)

rows: **Illegal VA recoupment of post-Jan. 28, 2008 combat-zone Disability Severance Pay (`§ 1212(d)(2)`), pre-tax gross recoupment (`> Sept. 30, 1996`), or non-severance disability over-withholding (`§ 3.700(a)(3)`)**

**VA Regional Office / HLR / BVA:** Audit request, AMA `HLR` (`20-0996`), `Supplemental Claim` (`20-0995`), or **`RO CUE` (`38 C.F.R. § 3.105(a)`)** demanding full refund of unlawfully recouped VA compensation!

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive:** Statutory/regulatory math and non-recoupment mandates (`Pub. L. 104-201, § 653`; `Pub. L. 110-181, § 1646`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.700(a)(2)–(3), (5)`) leave zero adjudicative discretion—violating them on undisputed `DD-214`/PEB facts is classic `§ 3.105(a)` CUE!
**Missing `CRDP` restoration (`10 U.S.C. § 1414`) or stalled `DFAS AEW` hold**
**VA <-> DFAS `AEW` Reconciliation** (no separate retiree application needed for `CRDP`, though `HLR`/audit forces VA to release improperly held post-AEW balances).
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive:** `Pub. L. 110-181, § 642` codified `100%` TDIU full `CRDP` retroactively to `Dec. 31, 2004`.
**Chapter 61 `< 20-year` medical retiree or combat retiree owed `CRSC` (`10 U.S.C. § 1413a`)**

**Service Branch CRSC Board (`DD Form 2860`)** + **`28 U.S.C. § 1491` Court of Federal Claims** Tucker Act suit for disputed arrears `> $10,000` ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc)).

**Uncapped Retroactivity (*Soto v. United States*, `605 U.S. 360 (2025)`):** Eliminates the 6-year `31 U.S.C. § 3702(b)` Barring Act cap back to statutory inception (`Jan. 1, 2008` for `< 20-yr` Ch. 61 retirees per `Pub. L. 110-181, § 641`).
**AMA `HLR` / `NOD` (`VA Form 10182`)** within `1 year` of RO fee decision (`60 days` on multi-attorney `§ 14.636(i)` allocation notices).
Governed by binding Federal Circuit statutory constructions (*Snyder*, *Ravin*, *Gumpenberger*).

blocks.text: 3. Military Retiree Concurrent Receipt Matrix (38 U.S.C. §§ 5304–5305 vs. CRDP vs. CRSC)

Under **`38 U.S.C. §§ 5304(a)(1) & 5305`** and **`38 C.F.R. § 3.750`**, a military retiree cannot receive full DoD retired pay and VA disability compensation concurrently *unless* an explicit Title 10 exception restores the waived retired pay (**`CRDP`**, `10 U.S.C. § 1414`) or pays a special tax-free combat supplement (**`CRSC`**, `10 U.S.C. § 1413a`).

rows: **Regular `20+` Year Longevity Retiree, `TERA` (`15–19` Yr, `10 U.S.C. § 1293 note`), or Reserve "Gray-Area" Retiree Reaching Retirement Pay Age (`60` or reduced early age)**
**No `CRDP`!** Dollar-for-dollar `§ 5305` waiver reduces taxable DoD retired pay by the VA award (**tax-free swap** only), *unless* disabilities are combat-related -> **file `CRSC` (`>= 10%`)**!

**Automatic `CRDP` (`10 U.S.C. § 1414(a)`)!** Restores `100%` of waived longevity retired pay automatically (no application required). Under **`Pub. L. 110-181, § 642`** (`eff. Dec. 31, 2004`), **`100%` `TDIU` (`§ 4.16`) fully qualifies** for `CRDP`!

Compare taxable `CRDP` vs. tax-free `CRSC` during **DFAS Annual Open Season** (`Jan.`): evaluate marginal tax bracket **PLUS** `USFSPA` former-spouse divorce division (`10 U.S.C. § 1408` divides disposable retired pay/`CRDP`, *not* `CRSC`!) and `SBP` premium deductions.
**Chapter 61 Medical Retiree (`PDRL`/`TDRL`) With `20+` Years Qualifying Service**
**No `CRDP`!** File **`CRSC` (`DD Form 2860`)** for any `>= 10%` combat-related disability.

**`CRDP` Capped at Longevity Portion (`10 U.S.C. § 1414(b)(1)`):** Restores retired pay *only* up to the `2.5% × YOS` (or `2.0%` Blended Retirement) longevity ceiling; any excess Chapter 61 disability-percentage multiplier remains offset!
Verify DFAS applied the full `2.5% × YOS` ceiling; model `CRSC` election if combat-related ratings match the longevity cap tax-free.
**Chapter 61 Medical Retiree (`PDRL`/`TDRL`) With `< 20` Years of Service** *(THE #1 CONCURRENT-RECEIPT TRAP!)*
**ZERO `CRDP` (`10 U.S.C. § 1414(b)(2)`)!** Dollar-for-dollar `§ 5305` offset wipes out DoD retired pay up to the VA rate.
**ZERO `CRDP` (`10 U.S.C. § 1414(b)(2)`)!** Even at `100%` P&T or `SMC`, `< 20-yr` Chapter 61 retirees are **categorically barred from `CRDP`** (unless `TERA`-retired)!

**MANDATORY `CRSC` FILING (`DD Form 2860`, `10 U.S.C. § 1413a`):** Expanded to `< 20-yr` Ch. 61 retirees eff. **`Jan. 1, 2008`** (`Pub. L. 110-181, § 641`). Pays tax-free monthly `CRSC` (capped at the **`2.5% × YOS` longevity ceiling**, `10 U.S.C. § 1413a(b)(3)`) for Purple Heart, armed conflict, hazardous service, instrumentality of war (including **Agent Orange, burn-pit/Gulf War & radiation presumptions** when tied to qualifying exposure!), or simulated war—with **uncapped arrears** under ***Soto v. United States*, `605 U.S. 360 (2025)`** ([Playbook 06](/playbooks/06-nehmer-herbicide-presumptions-crsc))!

blocks.text: 4. Disability Severance Pay (10 U.S.C. § 1212) vs. Separation Pay (§ 3.700) Three-Gate Recoupment Audit

Never assume a VA severance/separation withholding on an award letter is lawful. Run **all three statutory gates** against verbatim [`38 C.F.R. § 3.700(a)(2), (a)(3) & (a)(5)`](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.114-3.400-3.700-effective-dates-offsets):
Audit Gate A: Combat-Zone / Combat-Related Non-Recoupment (10 U.S.C. § 1212(d)(2); 38 C.F.R. § 3.700(a)(3))

items:
**The Rule (`Pub. L. 110-181, § 1646`, `122 Stat. 472`; `74 FR 26956`, pub. & eff. June 5, 2009, **retroactively applicable to separations `>= Jan. 28, 2008`**):** VA is **strictly prohibited (`$0` recoupment)** from deducting Disability Severance Pay (`DSP`) from VA compensation if:
• The member separated from the Armed Forces under Chapter 61 **on or after `January 28, 2008`** *(Fatal Cutoff: `Pub. L. 110-181, § 1646(c)` bars this exemption for separations on or before Jan. 27, 2008)*; **AND**
• The disability for which `DSP` was awarded was incurred in line of duty in a **combat zone** (designated by Executive Order) **OR** incurred during the performance of duty in **combat-related operations** as designated by the Secretary of Defense (armed conflict, hazardous service, instrumentality of war, or simulated war—broader than geographic combat deployment!).

**Remedial Action When DoD/VA Missed the Combat Code:** Inspect `DD-214 Block 18` and PEB `DA Form 199` (`V1`/`V3` codes). If the severance condition resulted from parachute jump, tactical field training (`simulated war`), armored vehicle/artillery (`instrumentality of war`), or combat theater deployment on/after Jan. 28, 2008—and VA recouped `DSP` because `DD-214` omitted the combat-related remark—petition the service branch **BCMR/BCNR (`DD Form 149`)** for a `DD Form 215` combat-related determination, then file an RO audit / `§ 3.105(a)` CUE claim forcing VA to **refund 100% of every dollar previously withheld**!

blocks.text: Audit Gate B: Severance-Disability Isolation Math (§ 3.700(a)(3)) vs. Total-Award Separation Pay (§ 3.700(a)(5))

items:
**Critical Program Divide (`VAOPGCPREC 12-96` & `38 C.F.R. § 3.700`):**
• **Non-Disability Separation Pay (`ISP`, `10 U.S.C. § 1174`), `SSB` (`10 U.S.C. § 1174a`, `§ 3.700(a)(5)`), & Lump-Sum Readjustment Pay (`§ 3.700(a)(2)`):** Recouped from **100% of the veteran's monthly VA disability compensation** across **ALL** service-connected conditions until the net balance is repaid *(whereas **`VSI`**, `10 U.S.C. § 1175(e)(4)`, is offset directly by **DFAS** from the annual `VSI` installment, NOT withheld by VA!)*.
• **Disability Severance Pay (`10 U.S.C. § 1212`, `§ 3.700(a)(3)`):** VA may recoup **ONLY** from compensation payable for **the exact disability (or disabilities) for which military `DSP` was granted**—VA **cannot** raid compensation payable independently for non-severance SC disabilities!

**Exact `§ 3.700(a)(3)` & `M21-1` Two-Method Incremental Recoupment Cap:**
• Once VA makes its *"initial determination of the degree of disability"* (first regular Part 4 schedular rating, excluding temporary `§§ 4.29/4.30` hospital/convalescent ratings), monthly recoupment **cannot exceed** the monthly rate payable for that initial severance rating, and when non-severance SC disabilities coexist (or ratings later increase), VA must compare **(Method 1) standalone rate for the initial severance rating** against **(Method 2) incremental difference (`Total Combined Rate` minus `Combined Rate of Non-Severance Disabilities Alone`)** and withhold the **lesser** amount (most advantageous to the veteran):
• *Zero-Increment Example (`70% + 10% = 70%`):* Veteran has `70%` PTSD (non-severance) and `10%` lumbar strain (severance disability). Under `38 C.F.R. § 4.25`, `70% + 10% = 73% -> rounds to 70%`. Because the veteran already receives the full `70%` rate from non-severance PTSD alone, the `10%` severance disability adds **`$0.00` incremental compensation**—VA must withhold **`$0/month`** while paying the full `70%` check!
• *Partial-Increment Example (`50% + 20% = 60%`):* Veteran has `50%` PTSD (non-severance) and `20%` knee (initial severance rating). `50% + 20% = 60%` combined. Compare standalone `20%` rate vs. `(60% rate minus 50% rate)`: VA must pay at least the full `50%` non-severance rate and withhold **at most** the lesser of the `20%` standalone rate or the `60% - 50%` incremental difference! And if that severance knee later worsens from `20%` to `60%`, `§ 3.700(a)(3)` **caps monthly recoupment at the initial `20%` schedular severance rate**!

blocks.text: Audit Gate C: Post-Sept. 30, 1996 After-Tax Net Cap & *St. Clair* / Pub. L. 114-292 Tax Refunds

items: **Federal Income Tax Exclusion (`Pub. L. 104-201, § 653`, `110 Stat. 2583`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.700(a)(2), (a)(3) & (a)(5)`):** For any Readjustment Pay, Disability Severance Pay, Separation Pay (`ISP`), or `SSB` **paid after `September 30, 1996`**, VA can recoup **ONLY the after-tax net amount** (`gross payout minus flat federal income tax withheld by DFAS`, typically `20%`–`28%`!). Auditing old awards where VA keyed the gross `DD-214 Block 18` figure instead of deducting federal tax withholding immediately cuts `20%+` off the recoupment debt!

***St. Clair* (`26 U.S.C. § 104(a)(4)`) & Combat-Injured Veterans Tax Fairness Act (`Pub. L. 114-292`):** Under ***St. Clair v. United States*, `778 F. Supp. 894 (E.D. Va. 1991)`** *(frequently mis-referred to in informal practice notes as "Stinson," which is an unrelated `508 U.S. 36` Sentencing Guidelines case!)*, lump-sum military `DSP` becomes tax-exempt under `26 U.S.C. § 104(a)(4)` when VA awards service connection for the same injury. Between `Jan. 17, 1991` and `2016`, DFAS computers erroneously withheld federal taxes on `130,000+` tax-exempt `DSP` payouts, prompting Congress to enact **`Pub. L. 114-292` (`Dec. 16, 2016`)** reopening IRS `Form 1040-X` refunds. **Recoupment Rule:** Even if a veteran separately recovered an IRS tax refund under *St. Clair* or `Pub. L. 114-292`, `38 C.F.R. § 3.700(a)(3)` still measures VA recoupment strictly by *"the total amount of the severance pay less the amount of Federal income tax withheld from such pay"* at separation (unless zero tax was withheld at separation because DFAS coded it tax-exempt up front)!

blocks.text: 5. Reserve Drill Pay (§ 3.654), OWCP/FECA (§ 3.708) & Felony Incarceration (§ 5313 / § 3.665)
A. Reserve & National Guard Drill-Pay Pro-Rata Math (38 U.S.C. § 5304(c); 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.654, 3.700(a)(1)(iii))

items:
**The `1/30th` Per-Day Rule (`VA Form 21-8951`):** Reservists and Guardsmen cannot receive VA disability compensation and active/inactive-duty training pay for the **exact same day**, *but* they only waive **`1/30th` of one month's VA compensation for each day of active duty or each Inactive Duty Training (`IDT`/`UTA`) drill period**!
• One standard weekend drill (`4 UTAs` — Saturday morning/afternoon + Sunday morning/afternoon) = **`4 days`** of VA compensation waived; a standard Reserve year (`48 UTAs` + `15 days` Annual Training) = **`63 days`** (`2.1 months`) of VA compensation waived!
• **Practitioner Audit:** Because 1 day of military drill/AT base pay almost always exceeds `1/30th` of monthly VA compensation (even at `100%`!), **always elect to waive VA compensation for the `63` training days** rather than waiving military pay—and immediately file an HLR/audit whenever VA mistakenly suspends the veteran's **entire `365-day` award** as an "active-duty return" instead of posting a `63-day` pro-rata debt!

blocks.text: B. Federal Employees' Compensation Act / OWCP Election (5 U.S.C. § 8116; 38 C.F.R. § 3.708)

items: **Same-Injury Bar vs. Distinct-Condition Dual Receipt:** Under `38 C.F.R. § 3.708(a)–(b)` (for civilian federal employment injuries `>= Sept. 13, 1960`), a veteran **may concurrently receive `100%` of both `OWCP`/`FECA` wage-loss/schedule awards AND VA disability compensation** whenever they compensate **different injuries or anatomical conditions** (e.g., VA `70%` combat PTSD + Postal Service `OWCP` torn rotator cuff)!

**Aggravation Increment Rule:** An irrevocable election is triggered **only** when `OWCP` and VA compensate the **same disability**—and if a civilian federal workplace injury *aggravates* a preexisting SC disability (e.g., `20%` SC back aggravated to `60%`), the veteran can retain the preexisting `20%` VA baseline while electing between `OWCP` and only the incremental `40%` VA increase!

blocks.text: C. Felony Incarceration Reductions, Halfway Houses & Family Apportionment (38 U.S.C. § 5313; 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.665–3.666)

items:
**Trigger & Conviction-Date Anchor (`§ 3.665(a), (c)–(d)`):** Reduction begins on the **`61st day`** of incarceration in a federal, state, local, or state-contracted private penal institution (*Wanless v. Shinseki*, `618 F.3d 1333 (Fed. Cir. 2010)`) **following conviction of a felony**:
• **Disability Compensation (`§ 3.665(d)`):** Ratings of **`20%–100%`** (including `TDIU`/`SMC`) drop to the **`10%` statutory rate**; a **`10%`** rating drops to **one-half of the `10%` rate** (`DIC` similarly drops to half the `10%` compensation rate). *Contrast Wartime/Survivors Pension (`38 C.F.R. § 3.666`):* Pension terminates **completely (`$0`)** on the `61st day` of imprisonment for **either a felony OR a misdemeanor**!
• **Pre-Conviction vs. Post-Verdict Trap (*Mulder*):** Pre-trial detention before a guilty plea/verdict does **NOT** trigger `§ 5313`, *but* under ***Mulder v. McDonald*, `805 F.3d 1342 (Fed. Cir. 2015)`** (*aff'g Mulder v. Gibson*, `27 Vet. App. 10 (2014)`), the 60-day clock starts on the **date the guilty plea or verdict is accepted**, NOT the later sentencing date!
• **Exemptions (No Reduction):** Misdemeanor convictions (for compensation!), civil commitment / forensic psychiatric hospitalization prior to felony conviction, parole, work-release, or **residing in a residential reentry center / halfway house (`38 U.S.C. § 5313(a)(2)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.665(b)`)**!

**Mandatory Family Rescue — Dependent Apportionment (`38 U.S.C. § 5313(b)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.665(e)–(h)`):**
• All or part of the withheld `90%+` compensation (`full awarded rate minus the 10% rate paid to the veteran`) **may be apportioned (`VA Form 21-0788`) to the veteran's spouse, children, or dependent parents** on the basis of individual financial need! VA is legally required (`§ 3.665(a)`) to notify both the veteran and dependents of this right; if dependents apply within **1 year** of notice, the apportionment relates back to the **`61st day`** of incarceration (`§ 3.665(f)`).

**Day-of-Release Full Restoration (`§ 3.665(i)`):** Full `100%` compensation resumes on the **exact date of release** (including transfer to a halfway house or work-release!) **if** VA is notified within **1 year** following release!

blocks.text: 6. Postconditions: Engineering 38 U.S.C. § 5904(d) 20% Direct-Pay Fee Withholdings Across Offsets

Under **`38 U.S.C. § 5904(d)(1)–(3)`** and **`38 C.F.R. § 14.636(g)–(h)`**, VA directly withholds and pays an accredited attorney/agent up to **`20%` of `"the total amount of any past-due benefits awarded on the basis of the claim"`** (*contingent on filing the fee agreement within the **strict `30-day` window** of **`§ 14.636(g)(3)`**—missing that `30-day` filing rule forfeits direct VA payment even on a valid retainer under ***Ravin v. Wilkie*, `956 F.3d 1346, 1350–52 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`**!*). Audit every fee notice against these four Federal Circuit rules:

items:
**Incarceration Reductions Do NOT Shrink the Statutory `"Award"` (*Snyder v. Nicholson*, `489 F.3d 1213, 1217–20 (Fed. Cir. 2007)`):**
• VA historically tried to calculate an attorney's `20%` fee on the tiny `$100+/month` `10%` incarcerated payout (`§ 5313`) rather than the `70%` or `100%` rating won on appeal.
• In *Snyder*, the Federal Circuit **reversed**, holding that `"past-due benefits awarded"` under `§ 5904(d)` means the **unpaid sum of the monthly ratings assigned from the effective date through the award decision** (less any prior ratings already in effect), *before* `§ 5313` payment withholding—so VA must calculate `20%` on the **full awarded rating** and pay it out of the non-apportioned retroactive pool! *(Note: In ***Jackson v. McDonald*, `635 F. App'x 858 (Fed. Cir. 2015) (nonprecedential)`**, rev'g `26 Vet. App. 460`, the Federal Circuit noted in a nonprecedential order that *Snyder* distinguishes the gross "award" from net "payable" cash where `§ 14.636(h)(3)` applies; always anchor briefs on binding *Snyder*, *Ravin*, and *Gumpenberger*!)*

**Overpayment / Debt Invalidation Fees Apply ONLY to Actually Withheld Cash (*Gumpenberger v. Wilkie*, `973 F.3d 1379, 1382–85 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`):**
• When counsel invalidates an unlawful `$196,000` VA debt ([Playbook 21](/playbooks/21-overpayment-waivers-incompetency-and-wartime-pension)) after VA had recouped `$38,000` from monthly benefits, `"past-due benefits"` under `§ 5904(d)` equals **ONLY the `$38,000` actually withheld and retroactively restored in cash** (`20% = $7,600`), **NOT** the `$158,000` uncollected debt balance that VA merely canceled on paper! Structure debt-defense retainers (`non-direct-pay` flat/hourly or hybrid post-decision clauses complying with `§ 14.636(e)–(h)`) accordingly.

**Military Retiree `DFAS AEW` Holds & `38 C.F.R. § 14.636(h)(3)` Cash-Payable Trap:**
• Under `38 C.F.R. § 14.636(h)(3)(i) & (iii)`, direct-pay `20%` withholding requires an award resulting in **cash payment** from which the fee can be deducted, and explicitly flags awards subject to military retired-pay waivers (`§ 5305`) or severance recoupments.
• **Mandatory `AEW` Audit:** When a `20+` year retiree jumps from `< 50%` (or `0%`) to **`>= 50%` / `100%` (`CRDP`-eligible)**, VA initially withholds `100%` of the retroactive VA award pending DFAS's **`Audit Error Worksheet (AEW)`**. Once DFAS confirms `CRDP` entitlement (`10 U.S.C. § 1414`), the `§ 5305` waiver lifts and VA owes the full net retroactive cash payout—**calendar a `45-day` post-grant `AEW` check** to verify VA ran its *Fee Allocation / Release* calculation on the restored post-`AEW` retroactive benefits rather than leaving counsel's `20%` fee at `$0` based on the temporary pre-`AEW` withholding! *(Conversely, for a `< 20-yr` Chapter 61 retiree whose VA award is completely offset dollar-for-dollar by prior DoD retired pay and who recovers arrears separately from DoD via `CRSC`, `§ 14.636(h)(3)` yields `$0` VA cash withholding because `CRSC` is a Title 10 DoD payment!)*

**Prior-Rating Step Deductions, `§ 1151` `FTCA` Offsets & `EAJA` Same-Work Refunds:**
• **Step Increases (`§ 14.636(h)(3)(ii)`):** Past-due benefits equal the difference between the newly awarded combined rate (including `SMC` and dependents!) and the prior combined rate actually paid during each historical month.
• **`§ 1151` `FTCA` Tort Offset ([Playbook 17](/playbooks/17-section-1151-va-malpractice-and-ftca-interplay)):** If an `FTCA` judgment became final *before* the `§ 1151` grant and absorbs `100%` of retroactive `§ 1151` payments under `38 C.F.R. § 3.362(b)`, no net cash is payable by VA for the post-judgment months—secure `§ 1151` effective dates predating the FTCA judgment or account for the FTCA fee (`28 U.S.C. §§ 2672/2678`).
• **Mandatory `EAJA` + `§ 5904` Lesser-of-Two Client Refund (`Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c)`, `106 Stat. 4513`):** Whenever counsel recovers CAVC `EAJA` fees (`28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)`) for court remand work **AND** later collects a `§ 5904(d)` contingency fee covering **the same work** on remand, counsel **must refund the smaller of the two fees dollar-for-dollar to the veteran**!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Auditing Back-Pay Withholdings: CRDP vs. CRSC (Soto), Severance Pay Recoupment & Drill Pay
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Winning a retroactive VA rating or earlier effective date is only half the battle—many Veterans are shocked when their VA Award Letter withholds thousands of dollars for military retired pay, Disability Severance Pay, Separation Pay, Reserve drill days, or felony incarceration. This playbook explains the rules governing Concurrent Retirement and Disability Pay (CRDP, 10 U.S.C. § 1414), Combat-Related Special Compensation (CRSC, 10 U.S.C. § 1413a—including the U.S. Supreme Court's 2025 ruling in Soto v. United States removing the 6-year Barring Act cap on retroactive CRSC arrears), after-tax and combat-zone limits on severance/separation pay recoupment (38 C.F.R. § 3.700), Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) Audit Error Worksheet holds, and dependent apportionments.
record_clues: A DD-214 (Blocks 18, 24, 26, or 28) listing Disability Severance Pay, Involuntary Separation Pay (ISP), Special Separation Benefit (SSB), or Voluntary Separation Incentive (VSI) alongside a VA Award Letter withholding table.
A DFAS Retiree Account Statement (RAS) showing a 'VA Waiver' deduction, or a VA Award Letter holding back retroactive pay pending a DFAS Audit Error Worksheet (AEW) reconciliation.

A Chapter 61 medical retiree (or 20-year retiree) with combat, hazardous-duty, instrumentality-of-war, or simulated-war disabilities whose retroactive CRSC back pay was previously capped at 6 years before Soto v. United States, 605 U.S. 360 (2025).

VA Form 21-8951 / 21-8951-2 Reserve drill-pay adjustment notices, or a felony-incarceration reduction past Day 60 where eligible spouse/child dependents were not notified of apportionment rights (38 C.F.R. §§ 3.665–3.666).
important_cautions: Chapter 61 medical retirees (<20 years) do NOT get CRDP: under 10 U.S.C. § 1414(b)(2), automatic CRDP at a 50%+ VA rating requires a 20-year (or TERA/Reserve gray-area) retirement—Chapter 61 medical retirees with under 20 years must apply to their military branch on DD Form 2860 for CRSC (10 U.S.C. § 1413a) to restore offset retired pay.

Disability Severance Pay vs. Separation Pay recoupment: under 38 C.F.R. § 3.700(a)(3), Disability Severance Pay is recouped ONLY from monthly compensation attributable to the specific severance disability (leaving independent VA disabilities untouched), AND is 100% exempt from recoupment if separated under Chapter 61 ON OR AFTER January 28, 2008 for a combat-zone or combat-related injury (10 U.S.C. § 1212(d)(2)). By contrast, nondisability Separation Pay / SSB (§ 3.700(a)(5)) is recouped across all VA compensation—but for any payout after September 30, 1996, VA can recoup ONLY the net after-tax amount, never the pre-tax gross!

Direct-pay attorney fee limits: under Federal Circuit precedent, accredited representatives forfeit VA direct-pay withholding if the fee agreement is not filed within 30 days (Ravin v. Wilkie), and cannot collect a 20% direct-pay contingency fee on the uncollected face value of a canceled overpayment debt (Gumpenberger v. Wilkie).

Under George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e), later judicial reinterpretations cannot support Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) against older final decisions, and under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c), only one final merits CUE decision is allowed per prior Board decision issue.
questions_for_representative: If VA is recouping separation or disability severance pay paid after September 30, 1996, did VA deduct the federal income taxes withheld so it recoups only the net after-tax amount under 38 C.F.R. § 3.700?

If I was medically separated under Chapter 61 on or after January 28, 2008 for a combat-zone or combat-related injury, is VA unlawfully recouping exempt disability severance pay under 10 U.S.C. § 1212(d)(2)?

As a military retiree (including Chapter 61), should I file DD Form 2860 with my service branch for tax-free CRSC—and if DFAS previously capped my CRSC back pay at 6 years, how do I pursue uncapped arrears after Soto v. United States (2025)?
Has DFAS completed its Audit Error Worksheet (AEW) audit so VA releases the rest of my withheld retroactive compensation?

title: Playbook 21: VA Overpayment Debt Defense & Waivers (§ 5302 / § 5112(b)(10)), Incompetency & Fiduciary Defense (§ 3.353) & Wartime Aid & Attendance Pension (Ch. 15)
statutes: 38 U.S.C. § 5302(a), (c) (amended by Pub. L. 117-328, Div. U, § 254, enacted Dec. 29, 2022)
Pub. L. 118-42, Div. A (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2024, enacted Mar. 9, 2024 — NICS judicial-order restriction)
keyPrecedents: Hartness v. Nicholson, 20 Vet. App. 216 (2006) (overruled by Chandler)
cFileTriggers: VA Debt Management Center (DMC) First Demand Letter or benefit award withholding notice under 38 U.S.C. § 5314
VA Form 5655 (Financial Status Report) requested or filed in response to an alleged compensation, pension, dependency, drill-pay, or severance overpayment

Committee on Waivers and Compromises (COWC) dismissal between Dec. 29, 2022 and Jan. 26, 2026 rejecting a § 5302(a) waiver request filed 181-365 days after debt notice under the stale 180-day eCFR text
C&P Mental Disorders or TBI DBQ checking 'No' to 'Is the veteran capable of managing his or her financial affairs?' or Rating Decision proposing incompetency under 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.105(h), 3.353(e)
Fiduciary Hub appointment letter imposing up to a 4% fiduciary commission (§ 5502(b)) or evidence of fiduciary misappropriation triggering mandatory § 6107 benefit reissuance

VA Form 21P-527EZ (Veterans Pension), VA Form 21P-534EZ (Survivors Pension), VA Form 21-2680 (Aid & Attendance / Housebound), VA Form 21P-8416 (Medical Expense Report), or VA Form 21P-0969 (Income and Asset Statement)
Assisted-living, memory-care, nursing-home, or in-home custodial care contract where unreimbursed medical expenses (UMEs) exceed annual retirement/Social Security income
Wartime veteran rated 10%-50% service-connected entering assisted living or memory care without § 3.701 / M21-1 VI.ii.1.A.2.a greater-benefit payment (or written election) of Aid & Attendance Pension
killSwitches: Pleading a § 5302(a) equitable waiver ALONE without simultaneously contesting the underlying creation, validity, and calculation of the debt (forfeits non-time-barred § 3.105(e) voidness and § 5112(b)(10) sole-administrative-error defenses)

Missing the 30-day window from the DMC First Demand Letter under 38 C.F.R. § 1.912a(c) (lifts the automatic recoupment stay, allowing VA to withhold monthly benefits while waiver/validity review is pending)

Missing the jurisdictional 1-year waiver deadline from notice of indebtedness under 38 U.S.C. § 5302(a) (or 180 days for pre-Dec. 29, 2022 notices) absent proof of delayed actual receipt due to VA/postal error under § 1.963(b) (former § 1.963(b)(2))
Finding of fraud, misrepresentation, or bad faith under 38 U.S.C. § 5302(c) and 38 C.F.R. § 1.965(b) (absolute statutory bar to equitable waiver)

Charging a direct-pay § 5904(d) contingency fee on the unrecouped face value of an invalidated debt rather than already-withheld dollars actually restored (barred by Gumpenberger v. Wilkie, 973 F.3d 1379 (Fed. Cir. 2020)), or charging pre-AOJ-decision preparation fees on an initial 21P-527EZ/534EZ Pension claim (§ 5904(c)(1))

Relying on Hartness v. Nicholson, 20 Vet. App. 216 (2006) to claim § 1521(e) Housebound Special Monthly Pension at age 65+ without a single permanent 100% disability (overruled by Chandler v. Shinseki, 676 F.3d 1045 (Fed. Cir. 2012))

Transferring excess covered assets for less than fair market value (gifts, irrevocable trusts, non-liquid annuities) within 36 months prior to a Ch. 15 Pension claim on or after Oct. 18, 2018 (triggers up to a 60-month penalty period under 38 C.F.R. § 3.276)

blocks.text: Three urgent financial-protection and elder-care emergencies routinely land on a Veterans Law firm's desk—often involving existing compensation clients whose livelihoods or autonomy are suddenly threatened: **(1) VA Debt Management Center (`DMC`) demand letters** threatening `100%` or partial monthly benefit recoupment over alleged dependency, drill-pay, severance, or reduction overpayments; **(2) proposed `38 C.F.R. § 3.353` incompetency findings** triggered when a `70%`/`100%` PTSD or TBI examiner casually checks `"No"` on financial capability; and **(3) Wartime Veterans & Survivors Aid & Attendance (`A&A`) Pension (`38 U.S.C. ch. 15`)** claims where memory-care or assisted-living costs (`$5,000–$8,500+/month`) wipe out a wartime household's retirement income.

blocks.text: 1. Preconditions: VBMS, DMC & Clinical Intake Triggers (c_file_triggers)

Immediately pull the complete **VBMS eFolder**, **DMC accounting ledger**, **Rating Code Sheets**, and **CAPRI/VistA clinical notes** ([VA Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon)) whenever intake reveals any of these triggers:

items:
**Overpayment & Debt-Collection Triggers (`Domain A`):**
• **VA Debt Management Center (`DMC`) `First Demand Letter`** (`St. Paul, MN`) or Regional Office notice citing `38 U.S.C. § 5314` and scheduling benefit offset or Treasury Offset Program (`TOP`) referral.
• **`VA Form 5655`** (*Financial Status Report*) packet, `VA Form 21-686c` (*Declaration of Status of Dependents*) divorce/stepchild removal lag, Reserve drill-pay audit (`VA Form 21-8951`), or severance/separation recoupment adjustment ([Playbook 20](/playbooks/20-backpay-offsets-crdp-crsc-severance-recoupment)).
• **Committee on Waivers and Compromises (`COWC`) Decision** issued after **December 29, 2022** dismissing a waiver request as `"untimely (> 180 days)"` when Congress had already expanded `38 U.S.C. § 5302(a)` to **`1 year`**!

**Incompetency & Fiduciary Triggers (`Domain B`):**
• **C&P Mental Disorders or TBI DBQ** checking **`"No"`** to *"Is the veteran capable of managing his or her financial affairs?"*—especially following an award of `70%` or `100%` PTSD, schizophrenia, dementia, or `DC 8045` TBI.
• **Proposed Incompetency Letter** citing `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.105(h), 3.353(e)` (starts the critical **`60-day` evidence / `30-day` predetermination hearing** clock!), Fiduciary Hub field-examination notice, `up to 4%` fiduciary fee authorization (`38 U.S.C. § 5502(b)`), or allegations that an appointed fiduciary diverted client funds (`38 U.S.C. §§ 6106–6107`).

**Wartime Pension & Aid & Attendance Triggers (`Domain C`):**
• **`VA Form 21P-527EZ`** (*Application for Veterans Pension*), **`VA Form 21P-534EZ`** (*Application for DIC, Survivors Pension, and/or Accrued Benefits*), **`VA Form 21-2680`** (*Examination for Housebound Status or Permanent Need for Regular Aid and Attendance*), **`VA Form 21P-8416`** (*Medical Expense Report*), and **`VA Form 21P-0969`** (*Income and Asset Statement*).
• **Assisted-Living, Memory-Care, or Home-Care Contracts** documenting recurring custodial/`ADL` care expenses alongside `DD-214` wartime service (`>= 1 day` during WWII, Korea, Vietnam, or Gulf War) or an existing `10%–50%` service-connected evaluation where `Ch. 15` A&A Pension pays more (`38 C.F.R. § 3.701(a)–(c)`; `M21-1, Part VI, Subpart ii, 1.A.2.a`).

blocks.text: 2. Bitemporal Pathway Gate (Sequencing Clocks, Deadlines & *George* Boundaries)

Each of these three practice domains carries strict statutory clocks and bitemporal traps under *George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` and `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)` ([Procedural Vehicles Piercing Finality](/docs/procedural-vehicles-piercing-finality)):

rows: **Debt Creation / Validity Attack** (`§ 3.105(e)` voidness; `§ 5112(b)(10)` sole admin error)
**No `1-year` waiver bar** if reduction was void *ab initio* (*Brown*; *Murphy*) or timely appealed (`0995`/`0996`/`10182`) or attacked via extant-rule CUE (`§ 3.105(a)`).
**Always plead Track 1 (Debt Invalidity) FIRST** alongside Track 2 (Waiver); extinguishing debt creation voids the entire balance as a matter of law.
**`30 calendar days`** from date of DMC `First Demand Letter`.
File written debt-validity dispute + `§ 5302` waiver + oral hearing request **within `30 days`** to freeze monthly benefit recoupment until written decision!
**`§ 5302(a)` Equitable Waiver Deadline** (`Pub. L. 117-328, Div. U, § 254`; `90 FR 54234`)
**Pre-Dec. 29, 2022:** `180 days`. **On/After Dec. 29, 2022:** **`1 year`** from notice of indebtedness (codified in undivided `§ 1.963(b)` eff. **Jan. 26, 2026**, replacing `former § 1.963(b)(2)`).
Challenge any `2023–2025` COWC dismissal that enforced the stale `180-day` eCFR text against a post-Dec. 29, 2022 notice; invoke `§ 1.963(b)` actual-receipt rescue if VA/postal error delayed mail!
**`30 days`** for predetermination hearing stay; **`60 days`** for rebuttal evidence; **anytime** to restore competency (*Sanders*, `17 Vet. App. 329`).
Demand `§ 3.105(h)` hearing within `30 days` to halt fiduciary appointment; if already final, file a **new/initial claim** to restore competency (*Sanders* — no `"new & relevant"` hurdle!).

**Pre-Oct. 18, 2018:** Facts-and-circumstances test, **zero** transfer penalty. **On/After Oct. 18, 2018:** Bright-line cap (`$163,699` eff. Dec. 1, 2025) + **`36-month` lookback** on `< FMV` transfers made **on/after Oct. 18, 2018**.
Pre-Oct. 18, 2018 asset transfers **never** trigger a `§ 3.276` penalty; for modern claims, deduct `§ 3.278` `UME`s first to drive `IVAP` to `$0` inside net worth!
*Chandler v. Shinseki*, `676 F.3d 1045 (Fed. Cir. 2012)` overruled *Hartness*, `20 Vet. App. 216 (2006)` on `§ 1521(e)`.
`§ 1513(a)` age `65+` waives `P&T` for basic Pension (`§ 1521(a)`) + Regular `A&A` (`§ 1521(d)`), **not** the single `100%` disability requirement for `§ 1521(e)` Housebound.

blocks.text: 3. Domain A — VA Overpayment Debt Defense (38 U.S.C. §§ 5302, 5112(b)(10); 38 C.F.R. §§ 1.911–1.970, 3.500(b)(2))

*(Link to verbatim text in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.274–3.279, 3.272(g), 3.353, 3.105(h)–(i), 3.500(b), 1.963 & 1.965 (Pension Net Worth & 36-Month Lookback, Deductible Medical Expenses, Competency Due Process & Overpayment Waivers)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.274-3.279-3.353-1.965-pension-competency-waivers)).*
A. The Mandatory Two-Track Pleading Rule (*Schaper*, *Farless*, *Narron* & *Edwards*)

Under **`38 U.S.C. § 5314`**, VA cannot lawfully offset compensation or pension benefits until it affords the beneficiary written predisposition notice of **both** the right to **dispute the existence/amount of the debt** and the right to **request an equitable waiver** (*Schaper v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 430, 435–36 (1991)`; *Farless v. Derwinski*, `2 Vet. App. 555, 558 (1992)`). In ***Narron v. West*, `13 Vet. App. 223, 227–28 (1999)`**, the CAVC held that debt-validity disputes and timely waiver requests are procedurally intertwined conditions precedent to final recoupment, and in ***Edwards v. Peake*, `22 Vet. App. 57, 63–65 (2008)`**, the Court required VA and the Board to sympathetically read *pro se* debt correspondence to recognize implicit waiver requests.

items: **Ironclad Firm Rule:** **NEVER file a `VA Form 5655` / `§ 5302` waiver request in isolation!** Filing a waiver alone implicitly concedes that the debt was lawfully created. Always file a **simultaneous Two-Track Response**: **(Track 1)** an AMA `VA Form 20-0995` / `20-0996` / `10182` (or `§ 3.105(a)` invalidity challenge) attacking the **creation and calculation** of the debt at the Regional Office, **AND (Track 2)** a protective **`§ 5302(a)` equitable waiver + oral hearing request** with `DMC`/`COWC`.

blocks.text: B. Track 1 — Attack Debt Creation, Validity & Calculation (No 1-Year Waiver Bar!)

items:
**Void *Ab Initio* Underlying Reduction or Severance (`38 C.F.R. §§ 3.105(d)–(e), 3.343, 3.344` — [`Playbook 05`](/playbooks/05-Void Rating Reduction (§ 3.105(e))s-stabilized-ratings)):**
• Whenever an overpayment stems from a rating reduction, severance of service connection, or discontinuance of pension/dependency executed **without** strict `60-day` predetermination notice, `30-day` hearing rights (`§ 3.105(i)`), and delayed effective-date calculation (`last day of the month in which a 60-day period after final notice expires` under `38 U.S.C. § 5112(b)(6), (b)(9)`), the underlying reduction is **void *ab initio*** (*Brown v. Brown*, `5 Vet. App. 413 (1993)`; *Murphy v. Shinseki*, `26 Vet. App. 510 (2014)`). Reinstating the prior award **extinguishes `100%` of the resulting debt as a matter of law**.

**Sole Administrative Error (`38 U.S.C. § 5112(b)(10)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.500(b)(2)`; *Jordan v. Brown*, `10 Vet. App. 171 (1997)`):**
• Under `38 U.S.C. § 5112(b)(10)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.500(b)(2)`, when an erroneous award is based **solely on administrative error** by VA (and not an act of commission or omission by the beneficiary), reduction or discontinuance takes effect on the **date of last payment**—meaning the adjustment is **strictly prospective and ZERO retroactive overpayment debt can be created**!
• **The Two-Prong *Jordan* Test (*Jordan v. Brown*, `10 Vet. App. 171, 174–75 (1997)`):** Counsel must prove:
• **Zero Payee Omission / Timely Disclosure:** The veteran or survivor timely reported the change (e.g., uploaded `VA Form 21-686c`, `VA Form 21-4138`, or divorce decree in VBMS, or disclosed Reserve status/severance pay on `DD-214` / `21-526EZ`, yet VA waited `3` years to process the dependency removal); **AND**
• **Absence of Actual or Constructive Knowledge:** The payee neither knew nor reasonably should have known that the continuing direct deposits were erroneous (e.g., complex blended combined-rating/COLA award tables, obscured award letters lacking `§ 5104(b)` itemization, or cognitive impairment).

**Audit Statutory Calculation & Recoupment Errors ([`Playbook 20`](/playbooks/20-backpay-offsets-crdp-crsc-severance-recoupment)):**
• Verify whether VA illegally created a "debt" by recouping **combat-zone Disability Severance Pay** barred by `10 U.S.C. § 1212(d)(2)` (eff. Jan. 28, 2008), recouping **pre-tax gross** rather than **after-tax net** readjustment, severance, or separation/`SSB` pay (`38 C.F.R. § 3.700(a)(2), (a)(3) & (a)(5)`), forfeiting an entire year's compensation instead of **daily pro-rata Reserve drill-pay days** (`38 C.F.R. § 3.654` — typically `63` training days/year), or applying the wrong end-of-month vs. end-of-year dependency discontinuance rule (`38 U.S.C. § 5112(b)(2)` / `38 C.F.R. § 3.501`).

blocks.text: C. Track 2 — Equitable Waiver (38 U.S.C. § 5302(a); 38 C.F.R. §§ 1.963, 1.965)

items:
**Critical Two-Clock Architecture (`30-Day` Freeze vs. Two-Era `180-Day -> 1-Year` Waiver Deadline):**
• **Clock 1 — The `30-Day` Recoupment Freeze (`38 C.F.R. § 1.912a(c)`):** Submitting a written waiver request (or written dispute of existence/amount or oral hearing request) within **`30 days`** of the DMC `First Demand Letter` **automatically stays all benefit withholding** until the `COWC` conducts any requested hearing and issues a written decision! *(If filed on Day `31–365`, the waiver is still timely, but VA may begin monthly withholding pending decision—ask DMC immediately for a hardship compromise/reduced monthly installment plan while the waiver is adjudicated!)*
• **Clock 2 — The Bitemporal `180-Day -> 1-Year` Statutory Expansion (`Pub. L. 117-328, Div. U, § 254` & `90 FR 54234`):**
• **Before December 29, 2022:** `38 U.S.C. § 5302(a)` imposed a strict **`180-day`** deadline from the date of notification of indebtedness.
• **Enacted December 29, 2022 (`Pub. L. 117-328, Div. U, § 254`, Cleland-Dole Act):** Congress amended `38 U.S.C. § 5302(a)` to expand the waiver filing window to **`1 year`** (`365 days`) from the date of notification of indebtedness.
• **Regulatory Alignment (`90 FR 54234`, pub. Nov. 26, 2025, eff. Jan. 26, 2026, `RIN 2900-AS18`):** Nearly three years later, VA consolidated `former § 1.963(b)(1)–(2)` into undivided **`38 C.F.R. § 1.963(b)`**, updating the regulatory text from `"180 days"` to **`"one year"`** while preserving the vital **actual-receipt rescue clause**: if the payee establishes that **actual receipt** of the debt notice did not occur within a reasonable period after mailing through no fault of the payee (wrong address, hospital stay, postal failure), the **`1-year` clock runs from the date of actual receipt**!
• **High-Yield `2023–2025` Audit Alert:** Whenever a client's waiver request on a post-Dec. 29, 2022 debt notice was summarily rejected by `DMC`/`COWC` between **2023 and January 2026** because a clerk relied on the unamended `"180-day"` `eCFR` text, challenge that dismissal immediately—the **self-executing statutory `1-year` text of `38 U.S.C. § 5302(a)` controlled over the stale regulation**!

**Proving the `6` `"Equity and Good Conscience"` Factors (`38 C.F.R. § 1.965(a)`) & *Cullen* Reasons-or-Bases Mandate:**
• First clear the **`§ 5302(c)` / `§ 1.965(b)` Gate:** Establish zero **fraud, misrepresentation, or bad faith** (unfair or deceptive dealing design; mere negligence or misunderstanding of VA rules is *not* bad faith!).
• Under ***Cullen v. Brown*, `5 Vet. App. 510, 512–13 (1993)`**, ***Smith v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 267, 279–80 (1991)`**, and ***Kaplan v. Brown*, `9 Vet. App. 116, 119–20 (1996)`** (reviewing Board waiver denials under `38 U.S.C. § 7261(a)(3)(A)`'s arbitrary-and-capricious / abuse-of-discretion standard), the Board **must explicitly analyze all six `§ 1.965(a)` factors** with adequate reasons or bases (`38 U.S.C. § 7104(d)(1)`):
• **Fault of Debtor (`§ 1.965(a)(1)`):** Document timely reporting (`21-686c`/`21-4138` fax/VBMS receipts), mental/cognitive limitations, or confusing consolidated direct deposits.
• **Balancing of Faults (`§ 1.965(a)(2)`):** Weigh debtor fault directly against **VA's multi-year processing delay**—even partial debtor fault justifies partial or total waiver when VA sat on reported dependency/income data for years!
• **Undue Hardship (`§ 1.965(a)(3)`):** Complete **`VA Form 5655`** line-by-line with verified rent/mortgage, utilities, groceries, prescriptions, co-pays, transportation, and minimum debt service—proving collection would deprive the veteran and family of **basic necessities** (*Cullen*, `5 Vet. App. at 513`).
• **Defeat the Purpose (`§ 1.965(a)(4)`):** Show recoupment undermines the very subsistence/rehabilitative purpose for which Title 38 compensation or pension was awarded.
• **Unjust Enrichment (`§ 1.965(a)(5)`):** Establish absence of windfall where funds were consumed in ordinary good-faith household living expenses.
• **Changing Position to One's Detriment (`§ 1.965(a)(6)`):** Document irreversible financial commitments made in reliance on VA's award (e.g., signing an assisted-living lease, retiring from work, or purchasing home medical adaptations).
• **Demand an Oral `COWC` Hearing (`§ 1.911a` / `§ 1.966`):** Debtor credibility on good faith and financial hardship wins waivers—always request a personal/virtual `COWC` hearing.
• **Attorney Fee Trap (*Gumpenberger v. Wilkie*, `973 F.3d 1379 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`):** Under *Gumpenberger*, invalidating or waiving an *uncollected* `$50,000` debt yields **`$0` in `"past-due benefits"`** for `38 U.S.C. § 5904(d)` direct-pay withholding; direct-pay `20%` contingency fees attach **only to cash already withheld/recouped by VA and restored to the client** (plus CAVC `EAJA` fees if won on judicial remand). Draft compliant non-direct-pay or fixed/flat fee agreements when defending *unrecouped* debt balances!

blocks.text: 4. Domain B — Incompetency & Fiduciary Defense (38 U.S.C. §§ 5502, 5507, 6107; 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.353, 3.105(h))

*(Link to verbatim text in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.274–3.279, 3.272(g), 3.353, 3.105(h)–(i), 3.500(b), 1.963 & 1.965 (Pension Net Worth & 36-Month Lookback, Deductible Medical Expenses, Competency Due Process & Overpayment Waivers)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.274-3.279-3.353-1.965-pension-competency-waivers)).*
A. The Clinical DBQ Trap & Collateral Stakes (4% Commissions, Retro Locks & Pub. L. 118-42 NICS Rules)

During `70%` or `100%` PTSD, Major Depressive Disorder, or `DC 8045` TBI C&P exams, examiners routinely equate psychiatric occupational impairment or impulsivity with financial incapacity and check **`"No"`** on the DBQ financial-competency box—triggering three severe consequences:

items: **Involuntary Fiduciary Control & `Up to 4%` Commissions (`38 U.S.C. § 5502(b)`; `38 C.F.R. pt. 13`):** VA strips the veteran of direct control over monthly compensation and **freezes retroactive back-pay lump sums** pending a Fiduciary Hub field exam; if VA appoints a paid professional fiduciary instead of a spouse/family member, that fiduciary can skim **up to `4%` of the veteran's monthly VA benefits**!

**Brady Act (`NICS`) Reporting & the March 9, 2024 `Pub. L. 118-42` Judicial-Order Shield:**
• Historically, a final `§ 3.353` administrative incompetency rating caused VA to report the beneficiary to the FBI's National Instant Criminal Background Check System (`NICS`) as `"adjudicated as a mental defective"` (`18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(4)`), stripping Second Amendment firearm rights without any court hearing.
• **Current Statutory Restriction (`Pub. L. 118-42`, *Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2024*, enacted Mar. 9, 2024, continued in subsequent appropriations riders):** Congress prohibited VA from using appropriated funds to report a beneficiary to `NICS` based on a VA administrative incompetency/fiduciary determination **unless there is an order or finding of a judge, magistrate, or other judicial authority of competent jurisdiction that such person is a danger to themselves or others**!
• *Practitioner Warning:* Never grow complacent because of the `Pub. L. 118-42` appropriations rider—appropriations restrictions must be renewed unless permanently codified in Title 38, pre-2024 legacy `NICS` entries may require affirmative relief petitions, and **fiduciary seizure of retroactive back pay + `4%` commissions remain in full force**!

blocks.text: B. Due-Process Shield (38 C.F.R. §§ 3.105(h), 3.353(e)) & Benefit-of-the-Doubt Rebuttal (*Sanders*)

items:
**Mandatory `60-Day` Predetermination Notice & `30-Day` Hearing Stay (`§§ 3.105(h), 3.105(i), 3.353(e)`):**
• VA **cannot** finalize an incompetency rating without first issuing a **Proposed Incompetency Notice** detailing the evidence and affording **`60 days`** to submit rebuttal evidence and **`30 days`** to request a **predetermination oral hearing**.
• **Immediate Action within `30 Days`:** File a written demand for a **`§ 3.105(h)`/`(i)` predetermination hearing** within **`30 days`** of the proposal letter—this **legally bars VA from finalizing incompetency** until the hearing is held and all rebuttal evidence is weighed!

**Substantive Standard & Explicit Presumption of Competency (`38 C.F.R. § 3.353(a)–(e)`; *Sanders v. Principi*, `17 Vet. App. 329 (2003)`):**
• **Definition (`§ 3.353(a)`):** A mentally incompetent person is one who, because of injury or disease, **lacks the mental capacity to contract or to manage his or her own affairs, including disbursement of funds without limitation**. Physical disability alone (quadriplegia, blindness, ALS speech loss) **never** constitutes incompetency!
• **Sole Rating-Agency Authority (`§ 3.353(b)(1)`):** Rating agencies hold sole authority to make official determinations of competency and incompetency for VA benefit disbursement and insurance purposes—Fiduciary Hub personnel cannot invent incompetency (and advance due-process notice is excused under `§ 3.353(e)` only where a court of competent jurisdiction has already declared the beneficiary incompetent).
• **Definite Medical Opinion & Consistency Mandate (`§ 3.353(c)`):** Unless medical evidence is *"clear, convincing and leaves no doubt as to the person's incompetency,"* the rating agency **cannot** find incompetency without a *"definite expression regarding the question by the responsible medical authorities,"* weighed across **all evidence of record** with a consistent relationship between disability percentage, commitment/hospitalization facts, and incompetency.
• **Presumption in Favor of Competency (`§ 3.353(d)`):** Under the plain text of **`38 C.F.R. § 3.353(d)`** and ***Sanders v. Principi*, `17 Vet. App. 329, 336–37 (2003)`**, ***"Where reasonable doubt arises regarding a beneficiary's mental capacity to contract or to manage his or her own affairs, including the disbursement of funds without limitation, such doubt will be resolved in favor of competency."*** Even a `50/50` equipoise between a C&P DBQ check-box and positive real-world financial evidence **compels a finding of competency as a matter of law**!
• **The Rebuttal Evidentiary Pack:** Counter a `20-minute` C&P check-box by submitting: **(a)** a private treating psychiatrist/psychologist letter specifically addressing `§ 3.353(a)` contractual/financial capacity; **(b)** `6–12` months of clean bank statements, autopay utility/mortgage ledgers, and a clean credit report (`Equifax`/`Experian`/`TransUnion`) showing zero delinquencies; and **(c)** lay declarations from the veteran, spouse, CPA, or banker confirming independent budgeting (note: voluntarily delegating bill-paying mechanics to a spouse while retaining contractual comprehension *proves prudent management*, not incompetency!).

**Restoring Competency Anytime (*Sanders* New-Claim Rule) & Mandatory `§ 6107` Misuse Reissuance:**
• **Restoring Competency (`Sanders`, `17 Vet. App. at 332–33`):** A request to lift an existing incompetency rating and restore competency is **legally treated as an initial/new claim** (analogous to an increased-rating claim)—meaning the veteran can file to restore competency at any time with updated clinical/financial proof!
• **Temporary Fiduciaries (`38 U.S.C. § 5507(d)`) & Mandatory Reissuance of Misused Funds (`38 U.S.C. §§ 6106–6107`):** Under `§ 5507(d)`, temporary protective fiduciary appointments cannot exceed **`120 days`**. Crucially, if a VA-appointed fiduciary misappropriates or misuses *any* part of a beneficiary's VA benefits (`§ 6106`), **`38 U.S.C. § 6107` (as broadened by `Pub. L. 116-315, § 7005`, `134 Stat. 4932, 5059`, enacted Jan. 5, 2021)** mandates that **VA MUST reissue and pay the full misused amount directly to the beneficiary or successor fiduciary—regardless of whether VA was negligent in vetting or monitoring the rogue fiduciary**!

blocks.text: 5. Domain C — Needs-Based Wartime Veterans Pension & Survivors Pension with Aid & Attendance (38 U.S.C. §§ 1502, 1513, 1521, 1541; 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.2, 3.3, 3.271–3.279)

*(Link to verbatim text in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.274–3.279, 3.272(g), 3.353, 3.105(h)–(i), 3.500(b), 1.963 & 1.965 (Pension Net Worth & 36-Month Lookback, Deductible Medical Expenses, Competency Due Process & Overpayment Waivers)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.274-3.279-3.353-1.965-pension-competency-waivers) and pre-/post-2018 regulatory diffs in [Part 1 & Part 3 Historical Diff: Effective Dates (§§ 3.155, 3.400(o)(2), 3.2500), Severance Recoupment (§ 3.700), Wartime Pension Net Worth/Lookback (§§ 3.274–3.279, 83 FR 47246) & Debt Waiver Deadlines (§ 1.963(b), 90 FR 54234) (1962–2026)](/cfr/modules/pension-net-worth-and-effective-date-diffs)).*
Gate 1 — Qualifying Wartime Active Duty (38 C.F.R. §§ 3.2, 3.3(a)(3); 38 U.S.C. § 5303A)

The veteran must hold a discharge **other than dishonorable** ([Playbook 10](/playbooks/10-character-of-discharge-insanity-upgrades)), **no combat or overseas deployment is required**, and active service ([Playbook 11](/playbooks/11-guard-reserve-adt-iadt-and-line-of-duty)) must satisfy:

items: **Duration:** **`>= 90` days** of active duty (or, if enlisted after **Sept. 7, 1980** / entered as an officer after **Oct. 16, 1981**, completion of the **`24-month`** continuous active-duty minimum or the full period for which called/ordered to active duty under `38 U.S.C. § 5303A`, unless discharged early for disability/hardship); **AND**

**At Least `1 Day` Within a Statutory Wartime Period (`38 C.F.R. § 3.2`):**
• **World War II:** `December 7, 1941` – `December 31, 1946`
• **Korean Conflict:** `June 27, 1950` – `January 31, 1955`
• **Vietnam Era:** `February 28, 1961` – `May 7, 1975` *(for veterans who served **in the Republic of Vietnam**)*; **`August 5, 1964` – `May 7, 1975`** *(for all other active-duty service anywhere in the world)*
• **Persian Gulf War:** **`August 2, 1990` – `present`** *(open-ended until terminated by Presidential proclamation or law)*

blocks.text: Gate 2 — Age 65+ Statutory P&T Shortcut (38 U.S.C. § 1513(a)), *Chandler* Boundary & Survivors A&A

items:
**Veterans Age `65 or Older` (`38 U.S.C. § 1513(a)`, enacted by `Pub. L. 107-103, § 207(a)` [2001]):**
• Wartime veterans **age `65 or older`** are **statutorily exempted** from proving permanent and total (`P&T`) non-service-connected disability or unemployability to qualify for **basic Veterans Pension (`§ 1521(a)`)**! *(Note: Under `Pub. L. 110-157` [2007], VA cross-matches IRS/SSA and National Directory of New Hires [`NDNH`] wage databases to verify income).*
• **Pairing Age `65+` with Regular Aid & Attendance (`§ 1521(d)`; `38 C.F.R. §§ 3.351(b)–(c), 3.352(a)`):** Once a `65+` wartime veteran submits **`VA Form 21-2680`** proving a need for **Regular Aid & Attendance** (`>= 2` `ADL` deficits, daily cognitive/dementia safety supervision against hazards of the daily environment, `5/200` blindness, **OR** status as a **patient in a nursing home** for mental/physical incapacity under `§ 3.351(c)(2)`), the veteran unlocks the **maximum Veterans `A&A` `MAPR` tier** (`$29,093/yr` = **`$2,424/mo`** single veteran; `$34,488/yr` = **`$2,874/mo`** veteran with `1` dependent, effective Dec. 1, 2025)!
• **The *Hartness* -> *Chandler* Trap on `§ 1521(e)` Housebound SMP:** While *Hartness v. Nicholson*, `20 Vet. App. 216 (2006)` had briefly allowed `65+` veterans to claim `§ 1521(e)` Housebound Pension without a single `100%` disability, the Federal Circuit **overruled *Hartness* in *Chandler v. Shinseki*, `676 F.3d 1045, 1050–52 (Fed. Cir. 2012)`**, holding that `§ 1513(a)` waives `P&T` only for `§ 1521(a)`—meaning `§ 1521(e)` Housebound SMP still requires **either** a single permanent `100%` disability (`+ 60%` separate OR permanent confinement to the dwelling/premises). Whenever an elderly client cannot meet `§ 1521(e)`'s single-`100%` hurdle, target **`§ 1521(d)` Regular Aid & Attendance** instead!

**Surviving Spouses (`38 U.S.C. § 1541`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.351(b)–(c)`):**
• An unremarried surviving spouse of a wartime veteran needs **zero disability and zero minimum age** to qualify for basic Survivors Pension (`$11,699/yr` eff. Dec. 1, 2025), and qualifies for the **maximum Survivors `A&A` `MAPR` (`$18,697/yr` = `$1,558/mo` eff. Dec. 1, 2025)** upon **`VA Form 21-2680`** proof of Regular A&A or nursing-home patient status!

blocks.text: Gate 3 — Bright-Line Net Worth & 36-Month Transfer Lookback (83 FR 47246, eff. Oct. 18, 2018; 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.274–3.276)
Effective **October 18, 2018** (`83 FR 47246`, pub. Sept. 18, 2018), VA replaced subjective net-worth adjudication with an objective Medicaid-indexed formula:
$$\text{VA Net Worth} = \text{Covered Assets (Veteran + Spouse)} + \text{Annual Income (IVAP after § 3.278 UME Deductions!)}$$

items: **Annual COLA-Indexed Bright-Line Limit (`§ 3.274(a)–(b)`):** Tied to the Medicaid maximum Community Spouse Resource Allowance (`CSRA`) and adjusted every **December 1** by the Social Security COLA: `$123,600` (`Oct. 18, 2018`), `$159,240` (`Dec. 1, 2024 – Nov. 30, 2025`), and **`$163,699` (`Dec. 1, 2025 – Nov. 30, 2026`)**.

**Exempt Assets Excluded From Net Worth (`38 C.F.R. § 3.275(b)`):**
• **Primary Residence + Marketable Lot up to `2 Acres` (`87,120 sq. ft.`):** Remains **`100%` exempt regardless of dollar value**—and **stays `100%` exempt even after the veteran or surviving spouse moves into an assisted-living facility or nursing home**! *(Crucial Trap: Rental income from the home counts toward gross income, and if the home is **sold**, the net cash proceeds immediately convert into countable assets unless reinvested into another primary residence within the **same calendar year** under `§ 3.275(b)(1)`!)* Acreage exceeding `2 acres` is countable *unless* unmarketable due to zoning restrictions, lack of access, or conservation easements.
• **Personal Effects & Family Transportation Vehicles:** Household goods, clothing, jewelry, and vehicles used for family transportation (excluding speculative collectibles, boats, or RVs).

**The `36-Month` Asset-Transfer Lookback & Penalty Formula (`38 C.F.R. § 3.276`):**
• Applies **only** to transfers for **less than fair market value (`< FMV`)**—gifts to children, transfers into irrevocable trusts, or purchases of non-liquid annuities where the claimant cannot liquidate principal—executed **within `36 months` prior to claim receipt AND on or after October 18, 2018**.
• **The `"Covered Asset"` Exemption Shield (`§ 3.276(a)(2), (b)` — Huge Practitioner Win!):** VA **does NOT penalize every gift**! A penalty attaches **only to `"covered assets"`**—the portion of transferred assets that, had they been retained, **would have pushed total Net Worth over the `$163,699` bright-line cap**! *(Example: Widow has `$50,000` in savings, `$0` IVAP after memory-care UMEs, and gifted `$40,000` to her daughter `12 months` ago. Had she kept the `$40,000`, her Net Worth would be `$90,000 < $163,699` -> **Covered Asset = `$0` -> ZERO transfer penalty**!)*
• **Penalty Divisor & `5-Year` Cap (`§ 3.276(e)`):** Divide excess transferred covered assets by the **Monthly Penalty Divisor** = **`MAPR for a veteran with 1 dependent in need of A&A ÷ 12`** (**`$2,874/month`** eff. Dec. 1, 2025 [`$34,488 ÷ 12`]; `$2,795/month` in the 2025 rate year), **drop fractional months** (round down!), cap at **`60 months` (`5 years`)**, and start the penalty on the **first day of the month following the last transfer**. Under `§ 3.276(e)(5)`, returning all or part of the gifted assets within **`60 days`** of penalty notice (with `90 days` to submit proof) recalculates or extinguishes the penalty!

blocks.text: Gate 4 — Unreimbursed Medical Expense (UME) Zeroing of IVAP (38 C.F.R. §§ 3.278–3.279)

Many middle-class wartime families mistakenly assume `$40,000–$60,000/year` in Social Security and retirement pensions disqualifies them from VA Pension. Walk every family through the **`§ 3.278` `UME` Dual-Zeroing Math** (using **Dec. 1, 2025 – Nov. 30, 2026** rates):

items: **Facts:** Widowed Korean/Vietnam wartime veteran (single, no dependents) has **`$48,000/year`** (`$4,000/month`) in Social Security + pension income and **`$130,000`** in bank savings. Without care costs, `$48,000` income + `$130,000` savings = **`$178,000` Net Worth** (`> $163,699` cap -> **denied**!) and `$48,000 > $29,093` `MAPR` (**`$0` benefit**!).

**Enter Memory Care / Assisted Living (`VA Form 21-2680` + `VA Form 21P-8416`):** Veteran moves into memory care costing **`$66,000/year`** (`$5,500/month`). Under **`38 C.F.R. § 3.278(d)(3)`**, **`100%` of assisted-living / memory-care room, board, and care charges count as deductible `UME`s** whenever the facility provides or contracts for health care or custodial care (`§ 3.278(d)(3)(iv)(A)`)—or a physician, PA, certified nurse practitioner (`CNP`), or clinical nurse specialist (`CNS`) certifies in writing on `VA Form 21-2680` / clinical statement that the claimant must reside in the protected facility to obtain third-party/family care (`§ 3.278(d)(3)(iii)–(iv)`)! Medicare Part B/D & Medigap premiums also count (`+$2,400/yr` -> `$68,400` total UMEs; even using `$66,000` alone):
• **`5%` Basic `MAPR` Deductible (`§ 3.272(g)`):** `5% × $17,441` (single veteran basic `MAPR`) = **`$872`**.
• **Deductible `UME`s:** `$66,000 - $872` = **`$65,128`**.
• **Countable Income (`IVAP`):** `$48,000 (Gross Income) - $65,128 (Deductible UMEs)` = **`-$17,128` -> floored at `$0` `IVAP`!**

**Dual Unlock Result:**
• **Net Worth Drops Below Cap:** `$130,000 (Assets) + $0 (IVAP)` = **`$130,000 < $163,699`** (**Net Worth PASSED!**).
• **`100%` Maximum Tax-Free `A&A` `MAPR` Payable:** `$29,093 (Max A&A MAPR) - $0 (IVAP)` = **`$29,093/year` (`$2,424/month` tax-free!)** paid every month!

blocks.text: E. Compensation vs. Pension Auto-Switching (38 U.S.C. § 5304(a); 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.700(a)(4), 3.701)

Under `38 U.S.C. § 5304(a)` and `38 C.F.R. § 3.700(a)(4)`, a veteran cannot receive Disability Compensation and Wartime Pension concurrently—**but NEVER needs to forfeit or sever service connection to collect the higher `A&A` Pension**!

items: **Assumed Greater-Benefit Payment (`38 C.F.R. § 3.701(a)–(c)`; `M21-1, Part VI, Subpart ii, 1.A.2.a`):** While `§ 3.701(a)–(c)` preserves a beneficiary's right to elect either benefit in writing (`(b)`) and bars retroactive switching prior to election receipt except as otherwise provided (`(c)`), under `M21-1, Part VI, Subpart ii, 1.A.2.a` when entitlement to both Compensation and Pension is established VA **assumes election of and pays the greater benefit**—e.g., paying **`$2,424/mo` (`$2,874/mo` if married) in Wartime `A&A` Pension** over a `20%` (`~$347/mo`) or `40%` (`~$774/mo`) SC award while keeping all service-connected ratings intact on the Rating Code Sheet! *(Best Practice: Always include an explicit written statement electing the greater benefit alongside `VA Form 21P-527EZ` to satisfy `§ 3.701(b)–(c)` strictly).*

**Two-Stage Bridge Strategy:** File **`VA Form 21P-527EZ` + `21-2680` + `21P-8416`** immediately to start `$2,424–$2,874/month` cashflow within months while simultaneously prosecuting a PACT Act / secondary / `100%` + `SMC(l)` compensation claim ([Playbook 12](/playbooks/12-aid-and-attendance-smc-l-r1-r2-and-smc-t)). The moment `100%` SC + `SMC(l)` (`$4,900.83+/mo`) grants, VA automatically switches to the higher `SMC` award and pays the **net retroactive difference** above the Pension dollars already paid!

blocks.text: 6. Invariants / Kill-Switches

items: **Never Plead Waiver Without Contesting Debt Creation (*Schaper* / *Narron*):** Always pair Track 1 (`§ 3.105(e)` voidness + `§ 5112(b)(10)` sole administrative error) with Track 2 (`§ 5302(a)` waiver). If the `1-year` waiver clock already expired, Track 1 debt-invalidity remains alive!

**Hard `§ 5302(c)` / `§ 1.965(b)` Fraud & Bad-Faith Bar:** Any finding of fraud, intentional misrepresentation, or bad faith kills equitable waiver outright—anchor every `VA Form 5655` submission in documentary proof of good-faith disclosure or honest confusion.

**`§ 5904(c)(1)` Initial-Claim Fee Prohibition on Pension & *Gumpenberger* Debt-Fee Limit:** Under `38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(1)`, **attorneys and agents are strictly prohibited from charging a fee to prepare or file an initial `VA Form 21P-527EZ` or `21P-534EZ` Pension application** prior to an initial AOJ decision on that claim (fees attach only to post-AOJ-decision `0995`/`0996`/`10182` appeals!). And under *Gumpenberger*, `973 F.3d at 1384–85`, direct-pay `§ 5904(d)` contingency fees never attach to unwithheld debt balances.

**Post-Oct. 18, 2018 Asset-Protection Trusts & Annuities Trap (`§ 3.276`):** Transferring excess covered assets (`> $163,699` net worth) into an irrevocable trust or immediate annuity within `36 months` before filing `21P-527EZ`/`534EZ` triggers up to a **`60-month` penalty**! Always run the `UME -> IVAP -> Net Worth` worksheet *before* any family executes a gift or trust transfer.

blocks.text: 7. Postconditions: Effective Dates (§ 5110(b)(4) / § 5110(d) / § 3.31), Medicaid $90 Cap & Post-Grant Audit

items:
**Exact Pension Effective-Date & `§ 3.31` Payment-Date Rules ([Master Effective-Date & Staged-Rating Legal Treatise (38 U.S.C. § 5110; 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.114, 3.155, 3.400, 3.2500)](/docs/effective-dates-and-staged-ratings-treatise)):**
• **Veterans Pension (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(a), (b)(4)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.400(b)(1)(ii)`):** Defaults to **date of receipt of `ITF` (`VA Form 21-0966`) or `21P-527EZ`**—*except* under **`§ 5110(b)(4)` / `§ 3.400(b)(1)(ii)(B)`**, where a veteran who files within **`1 year`** of becoming `P&T` disabled AND proves that an **incapacitating disability** (stroke, dementia crisis, ICU stay) **prevented filing a claim for at least the first `30 days`** wins up to a **`1-year` retroactive effective date**! *(Remember `38 C.F.R. § 3.31`: actual monthly cash payment commences on the **first day of the calendar month following** the effective date).*
• **Survivors Pension `1-Year` Post-Death Lookback (`38 U.S.C. § 5110(d)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.400(c)(2)`):** If `VA Form 21P-534EZ` (or an `ITF` perfected within `1 year`) is received within **`1 year` of the veteran's death**, the effective date reaches all the way back to the **first day of the month in which the veteran died**!

**Medicaid Nursing-Home `$90/Month` Reduction (`38 U.S.C. § 5503(d)`; `38 C.F.R. § 3.551(i)`):**
• If a **single** veteran having **neither spouse nor child** (or a surviving spouse having **no child**) resides in a **Medicaid-approved nursing facility** where Medicaid pays part/all of the stay, VA Pension (including `A&A`) reduces to **`$90/month`** (retained by the resident as a personal-needs allowance, exempt from Medicaid nursing-home share-of-cost!) effective no sooner than the last day of the calendar month following the month Medicaid coverage begins. *(Private-pay assisted living / memory care **never** triggers the `$90` cap!)*

**Mandatory Post-Grant Audit ([Zero-PII 6-Gate Post-Grant VA Award Letter, Offset, Ancillary & § 5904(d) Fee-Withholding Audit Checklist](/checklists/award-letter-and-withholding-audit-checklist)):**
• Upon any debt-cancellation/refund, restored competency release of withheld funds, `§ 6107` misuse reissuance, or retroactive `Ch. 15` `A&A` award, verify dollar-for-dollar restoration of previously recouped installments, termination of Treasury (`TOP`) referrals, removal of fiduciary `4%` fee codes, accurate `UME` projection carry-forwards (`§ 3.272(g)`), and compliant `§ 5904` / `EAJA` fee accounting ([Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Defending Against VA Overpayment Debts, Proposed Incompetency & Wartime Aid & Attendance Denials
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Few letters from VA cause more distress than a Debt Management Center (DMC) overpayment demand, a proposal to declare a Veteran 'incompetent' to manage their own finances, or a denial of Wartime / Survivors Pension when assisted-living or memory-care bills are piling up. This playbook walks through the two-track defense against VA overpayments (challenging whether the debt was lawfully created at all AND requesting an 'equity and good conscience' waiver), protecting your right to manage your own funds under 38 C.F.R. § 3.353, and qualifying for Chapter 15 Wartime or Survivors Pension with Aid and Attendance by deducting unreimbursed care expenses under 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.272(g) and 3.278.
record_clues: A VA Debt Management Center First Demand Letter—where responding within 30 days pauses benefit recoupment under 38 C.F.R. § 1.912a(c), and filing VA Form 5655 within 1 year preserves a waiver under 38 U.S.C. § 5302(a) and 38 C.F.R. § 1.963(b).
A waiver dismissal issued between December 29, 2022 and January 26, 2026 rejecting a waiver filed 181–365 days after the debt letter based on outdated 180-day regulatory text.

A C&P exam checking 'No' to financial competency or a VA letter proposing incompetency under 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.105(h) and 3.353(e) (or evidence a VA-appointed fiduciary misused funds, triggering mandatory VA reissuance under 38 U.S.C. § 6107).

An assisted-living, memory-care, nursing-home, or in-home care contract (reported on VA Form 21P-8416 alongside VA Form 21-2680) where high annual care costs reduce countable income for Wartime Pension or Aid and Attendance—even for a wartime Veteran currently receiving a modest 10%–50% compensation check (greater-benefit rule under 38 C.F.R. § 3.701).
important_cautions: Never ask for a waiver alone without also checking debt validity: asking for a waiver concedes a debt exists and asks VA to forgive it, whereas challenging debt validity—such as an unlawful reduction lacking 60-day notice (38 C.F.R. § 3.105(e)) or an erroneous award caused SOLELY by VA administrative error (38 U.S.C. § 5112(b)(10))—wipes out the debt as unlawful and has no 1-year waiver deadline.

Protect the 30-day stay and 1-year waiver clocks: disputing or requesting a waiver within 30 days of the DMC First Demand Letter stops VA from withholding monthly benefits while your case is decided, and the statutory waiver deadline is 1 year from notice of indebtedness for notices on/after December 29, 2022 (180 days before December 29, 2022), barred completely if there was fraud, misrepresentation, or bad faith.

Pension asset-transfer trap (October 18, 2018): gifting or transferring excess assets for less than fair market value within 36 months BEFORE applying for VA Pension on or after October 18, 2018 triggers up to a 5-year penalty period under 38 C.F.R. § 3.276 (whereas pre-October 18, 2018 transfers are exempt). Also note that age-65+ Housebound Special Monthly Pension still requires a single permanent 100% disability plus 60% additional or permanent housebound status (Chandler v. Shinseki).

Representation fee rules: nobody can charge a fee to prepare an initial VA Pension application before an initial VA decision (38 U.S.C. § 5904(c)(1)), and attorneys cannot charge a 20% direct-pay fee on uncollected debt balances (Gumpenberger v. Wilkie).
questions_for_representative: On my VA overpayment letter, are we still within the 30-day window to freeze monthly benefit withholding—and should we challenge the legal validity of the debt (such as sole VA administrative error under 38 U.S.C. § 5112(b)(10)) alongside a 1-year equitable waiver request?

If VA proposed to find me financially incompetent, how do we request a predetermination hearing within 30 days and gather statements from my doctor and family showing I manage my finances (38 C.F.R. § 3.353)?

Would Wartime Pension with Aid and Attendance pay more each month than my current 10%–50% disability compensation once my assisted-living or in-home care expenses are deducted under 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.278 and 3.701?
Before moving any savings or property prior to a VA Pension claim, how does VA's bright-line net-worth cap and 36-month transfer penalty under 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.274–3.276 work?
