blocks.text: Veterans Law firms routinely leave six-figure non-Part-4 recoveries on the table—or forfeit CAVC `EAJA` fees—when VHA's Office of Community Care (`OCC`) denies `$50,000–$500,000+` private emergency hospital and air-ambulance bills under **`38 U.S.C. §§ 1725 / 1728`**, or when VHA's Caregiver Support Program (`CSP`) denies or slashes monthly **`PCAFC` (`38 U.S.C. § 1720G`)** caregiver stipends. Following ***Wolfe v. McDonough*, `28 F.4th 1348 (Fed. Cir. 2022)`** and ***Beaudette v. McDonough*, `93 F.4th 1361 (Fed. Cir. 2024)`**, both domains are prime BVA and CAVC litigation dockets.

*(Cross-references: Verbatim `§§ 17.1002, 17.4000` & related regulatory snapshots in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.159 (Duty to Assist & Medical Exams), 17.120, 17.1002–17.1005 & 17.4000–17.4020(c) (Emergency Care & Community Care 72-Hour Notice), Part 71 (PCAFC Caregivers) & §§ 21.40–21.282 (Chapter 31 VR&E & Retroactive Induction)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.159-17.1002-17.4000-21.282-evidence-emergency-pcafc-vre); AMA & fee evolution in [Part 19, Part 20, Part 14 & Part 17 Historical Diff: Legacy vs. AMA Appeals (57 FR 4104 vs. 84 FR 138), Board CUE Subpart O (64 FR 2134), Four-Era § 14.636 Fee Rules (1862–2026) & §§ 17.1002/17.1005 Emergency Reimbursement (83 FR 974 / 88 FR 10835)](/cfr/modules/ama-part-19-20-and-part-14-fee-evolution); [CAVC, Federal Circuit, Writs & Class Actions Treatise](/docs/cavc-federal-circuit-writs-and-class-actions); [AMA Lanes & BVA Litigation Manual](/docs/ama-lanes-and-bva-litigation-manual); [Attorney Fees (`§ 5904`) & `EAJA` Practice Treatise](/docs/attorney-fees-5904-and-eaja-practice); [`CAVC Appeal, EAJA & Fee Compliance Gate`](/checklists/cavc-appeal-eaja-and-fee-compliance-gate); [Playbook 23 (`Ch. 31` VR&E & *Rudisill*)](/playbooks/23-vre-chapter-31-retroactive-induction-and-rudisill); [Playbook 12 (`SMC(l)`, `SMC(r)` & `SMC(t)`)](/playbooks/12-aid-and-attendance-smc-l-r1-r2-and-smc-t); [Playbook 20 (Offsets & `§ 5904(d)` Fee Base)](/playbooks/20-backpay-offsets-crdp-crsc-severance-recoupment); [Playbook 21 (Overpayment Waivers)](/playbooks/21-overpayment-waivers-incompetency-and-wartime-pension); [Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon); and [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).*
1. Preconditions: VHA OCC, Billing, Ambulance & PCAFC Intake Triggers

Demand both the **VBMS Compensation eFolder** and the **VHA Office of Community Care (`OCC`) / Caregiver Support Program (`CSP`) administrative record** (`FOIA/Privacy Act` to the local VAMC Privacy Officer + VHA Payment Operations in St. Paul/Denver) whenever intake reveals:

items:
**Emergency Medical & Ambulance Billing Artifacts (`§§ 1728, 1725, 1703`):**
• **`VA Form 10-583`** (*Claim for Payment of Cost of Unauthorized Medical Services*), institutional hospital **`UB-04` (`CMS-1450`)**, physician/air-ambulance **`CMS-1500`**, itemized billing ledgers, and third-party **Explanation of Benefits (`EOB`)** or Medicare Remittance Advice (`MSN`/`RA`) breaking down billed charges, contractual adjustments, **deductibles**, **copayments**, and **percentage-based coinsurance**.
• **VHA `OCC` / `Optum` / `TriWest` Denial Codes:** Boilerplate denials citing *"Other Health Insurance (`OHI`) made payment"*, *"Veteran not an active VA health-care participant within 24 months"*, *"72-hour emergency notification not received"*, *"Condition not service-connected"*, *"Does not meet prudent layperson criteria"*, *"Post-stabilization care unauthorized"*, or *"Timely filing limit exceeded"*.
• **ED Triage & Hospital Transfer-Center Logs:** Emergency Department intake nursing triage vitals/chief complaint (establishing symptoms *at presentation* under `§ 17.1002(b)`), physician stabilization notes, and hospital transfer-center phone logs showing VAMC bed unavailability (`"VAMC on diversion / no ICU or telemetry bed available"`).

**PCAFC Caregiver Stipend Artifacts (`38 U.S.C. § 1720G`; `38 C.F.R. Part 71`):**
• **`VA Form 10-10CG`** (*Application for the Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers*), **Centralized Eligibility and Appeals Team (`CEAT`)** decision letters, `Katz ADL` / clinical functional assessments, VHA Clinical Appeals (`VHA Directive 1041`) records, and reassessment tier-reduction or `60-day` advance revocation/discharge notices (`38 C.F.R. § 71.45`).

blocks.text: 2. Bitemporal Pathway Gate (§ 1728 Conversion -> AMA Lanes -> CUE / *George* Bar)
Rank available procedural vehicles from **lowest legal burden to highest**:

rows: **1. Retroactive `§ 1728` Conversion After VBA SC / `P&T` Grant (`38 C.F.R. § 17.126(b)`)**

Whenever VBA grants service connection (or `100% P&T`) *retroactively* covering an earlier emergency episode—even if VHA previously issued a final `§ 1725` denial—file under **`38 U.S.C. § 1728`** within **`2 years` of the date VBA notified the veteran of the SC / `P&T` award** (`§ 17.126(b)`)!

**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive (Independent Statutory Claim):** Does not collaterally attack the prior `§ 1725` denial; opens a fresh `2-year` statutory entitlement window (`§ 17.126(b)` covers SC care rendered within 2 years prior to the rating decision!).

**`1 year`** from any VHA `OCC` (`§§ 1725/1728`) or VHA `CEAT` (`PCAFC` `§ 1720G`) decision (`38 C.F.R. § 3.2500` / `Part 20`), or **at any time** via `VA Form 20-0995` with new and relevant evidence (e.g., transfer-center logs, physician stabilization opinion, or final OHI `EOB`). For historical `May 2011 – Feb. 2024` `PCAFC` denials lacking `§ 5104(a)` appeal-rights notice, invoke *Beaudette* defective-notice / AMA review!
**Full Retroactive Judicial Precedent Applies:** *Staab*, *Wolfe*, *Veteran Warriors*, and *Beaudette* govern **100% of open, pending, timely-appealed, and `20-0995` Supplemental claims**!
Reserved strictly for undisputed factual/statutory misapplications under the law as then understood (e.g., denying `§ 1728` for a condition already listed as SC on the VBA code sheet).

**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) for Reinterpretations:** Under ***George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)`** & `38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)`, *Staab*, *Wolfe*, and *Beaudette* **cannot** be used via CUE to reopen a final pre-precedent decision! *(Note: VA's special 1-year `§ 17.1004(f)` coinsurance re-adjudication window under `88 FR 10835` closed on **Feb. 22, 2024**—use `20-0995` with new and relevant evidence or `§ 1728` conversion instead!)*

blocks.text: 3. Emergency Medical Reimbursement Matrix (§ 1728 vs. § 1725 vs. § 1703 & § 1720J)
A. Rule #1 of Intake: Always Screen 38 U.S.C. § 1728 BEFORE 38 U.S.C. § 1725!

Practitioners and VHA payment clerks routinely default to `§ 1725` and walk straight into fatal `24-month` VHA-user, `90-day` filing, and OHI deductible/copayment traps that **do not exist under `38 U.S.C. § 1728`** (see [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.159 (Duty to Assist & Medical Exams), 17.120, 17.1002–17.1005 & 17.4000–17.4020(c) (Emergency Care & Community Care 72-Hour Notice), Part 71 (PCAFC Caregivers) & §§ 21.40–21.282 (Chapter 31 VR&E & Retroactive Induction)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.159-17.1002-17.4000-21.282-evidence-emergency-pcafc-vre)):

rows: **(1)** Adjudicated **SC disability** (`§ 17.120(a)(1)`); **(2)** **Adjunct** condition aggravating an SC disability (`§ 17.120(a)(2)`); **(3)** **ANY disability (SC or non-SC!)** of a veteran rated **`100% P&T`** (`§ 1728(a)(2)(D)`; `§ 17.120(a)(3)`); OR **(4)** **ANY care** needed by an active **`Ch. 31` VR&E** participant (`§ 1728(a)(2)(C)`; `§ 17.120(a)(4)`)!
**Non-service-connected (`NSC`)** emergency medical condition where no other VA authority (`§ 1728`, `§ 1703`, `§ 1720J`) covers the care (`§ 17.1002(a)–(f)`).

Authorized Community Care emergency treatment for VHA-enrolled/eligible veterans (`§ 17.4010`) when VA is notified within **`72 hours`** (`§ 17.4020(c)`). *(Also check **`38 U.S.C. § 1720J` [`COMPACT Act`, `§§ 17.1200–17.1230`]** for `$0`-cost acute suicidal crisis care regardless of VHA enrollment!)*
**NONE!** Veteran need **never** have used VHA healthcare within the prior 24 months!
**STRICTLY REQUIRED (`§ 1725(b)(2)(B)`; `§ 17.1002(d)`):** Must be VHA-enrolled AND have received VA care within **`24 months`** before the emergency!
VHA enrollment (or statutory exemption under `§ 17.4005`/`§ 17.4010`); **no** strict `24-month` visit bar if `72-hr` notice is met!
**PAYS ALL THREE (`§ 1728(b)`; `38 C.F.R. § 17.129`)!** Reimburses **deductibles, fixed copayments, AND coinsurance** in full!
**PAYS COINSURANCE ONLY (*Wolfe*; `§ 17.1005(a)(5)`)!** **Deductibles & fixed copayments are BARRED** (`§ 1725(c)(4)(D)`).
VA pays the community provider directly at contract/Medicare rates; **zero** OHI cost-share owed by the veteran (only standard VA copay, if any).
**`2 YEARS` (`38 C.F.R. § 17.126`):** Within `2 years` of care (`§ 17.126(a)`) OR within **`2 years` of VBA SC/`P&T` grant notice** (`§ 17.126(b)`).
**`90 DAYS` (`38 C.F.R. § 17.1004(d)`):** Within `90 days` after the *latest* of discharge, death in stay/transport, OR **final exhaustion of third-party/OHI payment (`§ 17.1004(d)(3)`)**!
**`72 HOURS` (`38 C.F.R. § 17.4020(c)`):** Hospital, veteran, or family must notify VHA centralized portal/hotline within **`72 hours`** of start of care!

blocks.text: B. Six Substantive Rules Governing § 1725 & § 1728 Litigation

items:
**The `"Prudent Layperson"` Standard (`§ 1725(f)(1)`; `§ 17.1002(b)` & `§ 17.120(b)`):**
• Emergency status is judged **exclusively by acute symptoms at initial presentation**—whether a *prudent layperson with an average knowledge of health and medicine* could reasonably expect the absence of immediate medical attention to place health in serious jeopardy or cause serious impairment to bodily functions or organs.
• **Reversible VHA/Board Error:** Denying reimbursement because the *final discharge diagnosis* proved non-lethal (e.g., veteran rushed to ER with crushing substernal chest pain and diaphoresis, discharged 18 hours later with `"esophageal spasm / panic attack"`). Pull the **ED nursing triage note** to win outright!

**Stabilization Cutoff & The `"No Available VA Bed"` Exception (`38 C.F.R. § 17.1002(c)` & `§ 17.120(c)`):**
• Unauthorized reimbursement normally stops at the point of **clinical stabilization** (when transfer to a VAMC can occur without material clinical deterioration).
• **Crucial Exception (`§ 17.1002(c)`):** VHA **must continue paying post-stabilization inpatient care** if a VAMC or contracted facility **was not feasibly available or could not accept the transfer** (e.g., VAMC lacked an ICU/cardiac bed or declined transfer), *provided* the non-VA facility contacted VA reasonably promptly upon stabilization! Always subpoena/request the private hospital's **Transfer Center log**!

**Satisfying the `24-Month` Active VHA User Gate (`§ 1725(b)(2)(B)`; `§ 17.1002(d)`):**
• Audit VAMC `VistA`/`CPRS` records for *any* qualifying healthcare episode within the `730 days` preceding ER presentation: VAMC primary-care/specialty visits, **telephone/video telehealth clinical encounters**, **VA mail-order pharmacy prescription fills/renewals** managed by a VA provider, VA-authorized `§ 1703` Community Care appointments, or Vet Center readjustment counseling!

**Never Conflate `72-Hour` `§ 1703` Notice With `90-Day` `§ 1725` or `2-Year` `§ 1728` Filing:**
• Missing VHA's **`72-hour` centralized notification (`38 C.F.R. § 17.4020(c)`)** only prevents VHA from *pre-authorizing* the admission under the `§ 1703` Veterans Community Care Program—it **NEVER** bars a timely **`90-day` `§ 1725` claim (`§ 17.1004(d)`)** or **`2-year` `§ 1728` claim (`§ 17.126`)**! And under **`§ 17.1004(d)(3)`**, when Medicare or private OHI adjudicates or appeals the hospital claim for months after discharge, the `90-day` `§ 1725` clock **does not start** until the veteran *finally exhausts* third-party recovery!

**Surgical OHI Cost-Sharing Precision (*Staab*, *Wolfe*, *Kimmel* & `88 FR 10835`):**
• ***Staab v. McDonald*, `28 Vet. App. 50 (2016)`** struck down VA's total bar against veterans whose OHI paid *any* fraction of an emergency bill (codified by Interim Final Rule **`83 FR 974`**, pub. & eff. `2018-01-09`). VA responded in `2018` by amending `38 C.F.R. § 17.1005(a)(5)` to bar **all** `"copayment[s], deductible[s], coinsurance, or similar payment[s]"`.
• ***Wolfe v. Wilkie*, `32 Vet. App. 1 (2019)`**, ***rev'd*, *Wolfe v. McDonough*, `28 F.4th 1348 (Fed. Cir. 2022)`**: Plead the Federal Circuit's three-part holding with exact precision:
• *Mandamus Reversed:* CAVC erred in issuing a class-wide writ of mandamus because AMA/BVA administrative appeals (`-> CAVC Direct Review`) provided an adequate ordinary remedy.
• *Deductibles & Fixed Copayments Excluded:* Under `38 U.S.C. § 1725(c)(4)(D)`, both **fixed copayments** (flat dollar fee per visit) and **annual deductibles** ARE excluded `"copayment[s] or similar payment[s]"`—VA **cannot** reimburse them under `§ 1725`!
• *Coinsurance MUST Be Paid:* **Percentage-based coinsurance** (e.g., `20%` Medicare Part A/B or private insurance share of a `$150,000` surgical/air-ambulance bill = `$30,000`!) is **NOT** a `"similar payment"` and **MUST be reimbursed by VA**!
• Following *Wolfe* and the Federal Circuit's `38 U.S.C. § 502` mandate in ***Kimmel v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs*, `No. 22-1754, 2022 WL 16337653 (Fed. Cir. Oct. 25, 2022) (nonprecedential order)`**, VA promulgated **`88 FR 10835` (pub. `2023-02-22`, eff. `2023-04-24`)**, amending **`38 C.F.R. § 17.1005(a)(5)`** to pay **coinsurance** (and opening a 1-year `§ 17.1004(f)` retroactive filing window through Feb. 22, 2024 for emergency care rendered between Feb. 1, 2010 and Feb. 22, 2023).

**Provider Balance-Billing Extinguishment (`§ 1725(a)(2)(A)` & `(e)`) & Delayed Air-Ambulance Cap (`88 FR 10032` -> `2029`):**
• **Liability Extinguished (`§ 1725(a)(2)(A), (e)`, `§ 17.1005(a)(4)`):** Payment by VA under `§ 1725` (typically at `70%` Medicare rates when VA is primary payer) **legally extinguishes the veteran's entire personal liability** to the hospital or ambulance company (apart from non-reimbursable OHI deductibles/copayments)—stopping illegal balance-billing in its tracks!
• **Emergency Air/Ground Ambulance Watchlist (`38 U.S.C. §§ 111(b)(3), 1725, 1728`; `38 C.F.R. § 70.30`):** On Feb. 16, 2023, VA published **`88 FR 10032`** to slash non-contracted Beneficiary Travel (`Part 70`) special-mode ambulance payments to the lesser of actual charges or the **Medicare Part B Ambulance Fee Schedule**. **CRITICAL DELAY:** VA delayed `88 FR 10032` first to Feb. 16, 2025 (**`88 FR 90120`**, Dec. 29, 2023) and then **delayed its effective date until `February 16, 2029` (`89 FR 88888`, pub. Nov. 12, 2024)**! Reject any premature VHA attempt to apply the delayed `88 FR 10032` `Part 70` Medicare cap prior to **Feb. 16, 2029**!

blocks.text: 4. PCAFC Family Caregiver Stipend Litigation (38 U.S.C. § 1720G; 38 C.F.R. Part 71)

lines: **`CFR` Citation Trap (`38 C.F.R. Part 71` vs. `Part 17`):** `PCAFC` is codified in **`38 C.F.R. Part 71` (`§§ 71.10–71.60`)** (`85 FR 46226`, pub. `2020-07-31`, eff. `2020-10-01`)—**NOT** `38 C.F.R. §§ 17.4000–17.4040` (which governs the `§ 1703` Veterans Community Care Program, including `§ 17.4010` community-care eligibility and `§ 17.4020(c)` `72-hour` emergency notice)! Always cite **`§§ 71.15, 71.20, 71.40 & 71.45`** in `PCAFC` briefs!

items:
**Judicial Review Unlocked (*Beaudette v. McDonough*, `93 F.4th 1361 (Fed. Cir. 2024)`, *aff'g* `34 Vet. App. 95 (2021)`):**
• For over a decade (`2011–2021`), VA refused to allow BVA appeals on `PCAFC` claims, claiming `38 U.S.C. § 1720G(c)(1)` (*"decisions ... affecting the furnishing of assistance or support ... shall be deemed to be medical determinations"*) barred Board and CAVC jurisdiction.
• The Federal Circuit **unanimously affirmed CAVC's class-wide mandamus order**, holding that `§ 1720G(c)(1)` insulates only narrow clinical choices regarding *how* support is furnished, whereas **all `PCAFC` eligibility, stipend tier-level, effective-date, reassessment, and revocation determinations are fully reviewable through the AMA (`VHA HLR / Supplemental / Board Form 10182 -> CAVC`)**!

**Substantive `PCAFC` Eligibility & Tier-2 Proof Contract (`85 FR 46226`; `38 C.F.R. §§ 71.15, 71.20, 71.40`):**
• **Threshold Rating (`§ 71.20(a)(2)`):** Single or combined SC disability rating of **`70%` or higher** (for all service eras as of Oct. 1, 2022).
• **`6-Month` Personal Care Requirement (`§ 71.20(a)(3)` & *Veteran Warriors*):** Veteran must need in-person personal care services for a **minimum of `6 continuous months`** based on *either*:
• **(a) Inability to perform an `ADL` (`§ 71.15`):** Dressing/undressing, bathing, grooming, adjusting prosthetics/orthotics, toileting, feeding, or mobility *(Note: In ***Veteran Warriors, Inc. v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs*, `29 F.4th 1320 (Fed. Cir. 2022)`**, the Federal Circuit **invalidated** VA's ultra-restrictive `"each and every time"` ADL definition in `§ 71.15`—reject any `CEAT` denial demanding 100%-of-the-time physical dependence on a single ADL!)*; **OR**
• **(b) Need for Supervision, Protection, or Instruction (`§ 71.15`):** Functional impairment at home impacting ability to maintain personal safety on a **daily basis** (dementia, severe TBI, active psychosis/dissociation, seizures, fall risk).
• **Level 1 (`62.5%`) vs. Level 2 (`100%`) Monthly Stipend Math (`38 C.F.R. § 71.40(c)(4)`):** Calculated from the annual **`OPM` `GS-4, Step 1`** rate (including **locality pay** for the veteran's residence ZIP code!) divided by 12:
• **Level 1 (`62.5%` of `GS-4, Step 1`):** Meets baseline `§ 71.20` eligibility (`~$1,800–$2,300+/month` tax-free depending on locality).
• **Level 2 (`100%` of `GS-4, Step 1`):** Veteran is **`"unable to self-sustain in the community"`** (`§ 71.15` — requires personal care services *each time* completing **3 or more ADLs** with full caregiver dependence, OR requires supervision, protection, or instruction on a **continuous daily basis**, paying `~$2,900–$3,700+/month` tax-free + **`CHAMPVA`** health coverage for uninsured Primary Caregivers!).

**`60-Day` Advance Notice + `90-Day` Post-Discharge Continuation (`§ 71.45`) & Legacy Cohort Protection Through `Sept. 30, 2028` (`90 FR 46477`):**
• Under **`38 C.F.R. § 71.45(a)(1)(iii) & (b)(1)(ii)(A)`**, VA-initiated revocations (noncompliance) or discharges (clinical `§ 71.20` non-eligibility, absent fraud or safety emergencies) require **`60-day` advance written notice prior to the effective date of revocation or discharge**, **PLUS `90 days` of post-discharge stipend/benefit continuation** (`§ 71.45(b)(1)(iii)`) following the effective date of qualifying discharges (reassessment non-eligibility, veteran death, or institutionalization).
• **Legacy Cohort Freeze (`90 FR 46477`, pub. Sept. 29, 2025, eff. Sept. 30, 2025):** For **Legacy Participants and Legacy Applicants** (approved or applying before Oct. 1, 2020, `§ 71.20(b)–(c)`), VA extended transition and reassessment protections (`87 FR 57602` -> **`90 FR 46477`**) through **`September 30, 2028`**—barring VHA from discharging or reducing a legacy caregiver's stipend based on reassessment before **Sept. 30, 2028**! *(Quarantine Note: VA's Dec. 6, 2024 `PCAFC` NPRM at **`89 FR 97404` [`RIN 2900-AR96`]** remains **proposed / not finalized**—never cite its proposed criteria as enacted law!)*
• **Zero Offset With `SMC(l)` / `SMC(r)(1)` / `SMC(t)` ([Playbook 12](/playbooks/12-aid-and-attendance-smc-l-r1-r2-and-smc-t)):** `PCAFC` stipends (`Ch. 17`, paid to the caregiver) **stack `100%` concurrently** with `SMC(l)`, `SMC(r)(1)`, and TBI `SMC(t)` (`Ch. 11`, paid to the veteran)!

blocks.text: 5. Invariants (Kill-Switches)

items: **`§ 1725` Deductible / Copay Pleading Trap:** Never plead for reimbursement of OHI **deductibles** or **fixed copayments** under `§ 1725` (*Wolfe*, `28 F.4th at 1358–62`); isolate **percentage coinsurance** under `§ 17.1005(a)(5)` or establish SC / `100% P&T` / `Ch. 31` status to unlock full deductible + copay + coinsurance recovery under **`§ 1728` (`§ 17.129`)**.

**Missing the `2-Year` Post-SC-Grant Clock (`§ 17.126(b)`):** Whenever a firm wins a retroactive SC or `100% P&T` award in Compensation, immediately audit the prior period for unpaid/out-of-pocket ER or ambulance bills and file `VA Form 10-583` under `§ 1728` within **`2 years` of the rating notification letter**.
**Single-Signatory `PCAFC` Retainer Error:** Signing only the Veteran on a `PCAFC` appeal when the **Primary Family Caregiver** is the legal payee of the `§ 71.40(c)(4)` monthly stipend!

blocks.text: 6. Postconditions: Arrears Payees & Structuring § 5904 + EAJA Fee Recovery

items:
**Exact Payee & Cash-Flow Mechanics (`§§ 1725/1728` vs. `PCAFC`):**
• **`§§ 1725 / 1728` Awards:** If the veteran already paid the hospital or OHI coinsurance out-of-pocket, VHA disburses a **lump-sum cash reimbursement directly to the veteran**; if the hospital/ambulance bill remains unpaid, VHA pays the **non-VA provider directly**, extinguishing the veteran's debt (`§ 1725(a)(2)(A)`).
• **`PCAFC` Stipend Arrears (`38 U.S.C. § 1720G(a)(3)(A)(ii)(V)`; `38 C.F.R. § 71.40(c)(4)`):** Monthly stipends and retroactive tier-increase/grant arrears (running back to the `VA Form 10-10CG` receipt date!) are paid **directly to the Primary Family Caregiver**, *not* the veteran. Always execute **`VA Form 21-22a`** and a representation agreement signed by **BOTH the Veteran AND the Primary Family Caregiver**!

**Firm Fee Engineering (`28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)` `EAJA` + `38 U.S.C. § 5904` Non-Withheld Clauses):**
• **Why `§ 5904(d)` `20%` Direct-Pay Withholding Often Fails in VHA:** VHA (`OCC` / `CSP`) disburses medical and caregiver payments outside VBA's `VBMS-Awards` check-splitting engine, and when VHA pays an unpaid `$180,000` hospital bill directly to a provider, **zero cash is payable to the veteran** from which VA could withhold a direct-pay fee (*cf. Gumpenberger v. Wilkie*, `973 F.3d 1379 (Fed. Cir. 2020)` & `38 C.F.R. § 14.636(h)(3)`).
• **Compliant Two-Pillar Fee Contract ([Attorney Fees & `EAJA` Treatise](/docs/attorney-fees-5904-and-eaja-practice)):**
• **CAVC `EAJA` Fee Shifting (`28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)`):** Primary revenue engine on BVA denials of `§§ 1725/1728` (especially provider-paid hospital/ambulance bills!) and `PCAFC` appeals—recovering full CPI-U hourly fees from the United States without reducing the client's medical reimbursement or caregiver stipend by a single cent!
• **Non-Withheld Contingency Clause (`<= 20%` or `<= 33.3%` under `38 C.F.R. § 14.636(e)–(f)`):** Draft the retainer to attach strictly to **retroactive cash lump sums actually disbursed to the Veteran or Primary Family Caregiver** (e.g., `$55,000` retroactive `PCAFC` Level 2 stipend arrears or `$32,000` out-of-pocket coinsurance refund), file within the mandatory **`30-day` window** (`§ 14.636(g)(3)`; *Ravin v. Wilkie*, `956 F.3d 1346 (Fed. Cir. 2020)`), and enforce the **`Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c)`** lesser-of-two client refund whenever both `EAJA` and `§ 5904` fees cover the same CAVC representation phase!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Non-VA Emergency Hospital & Ambulance Bills (§§ 1728 vs. 1725 / Wolfe) & Family Caregiver (PCAFC) Appeals
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: When a medical crisis sends a Veteran to the nearest civilian emergency room or air ambulance, VA Health Administration (VHA) billing denials often cite confusing rules about 'Other Health Insurance,' '72-hour notification,' or 'no VA visit within 24 months.' This playbook explains how to check the much stronger reimbursement statute FIRST—38 U.S.C. § 1728 (covering service-connected emergencies, 100% Permanent & Total Veterans for ANY emergency, and active Chapter 31 VR&E participants)—before turning to 38 U.S.C. § 1725 (which covers non-service-connected emergencies, including percentage-based Medicare/insurance coinsurance after Staab v. McDonald and Wolfe v. McDonough) or COMPACT Act acute suicidal crisis care (38 U.S.C. § 1720J). It also explains how Veterans and family caregivers can appeal PCAFC Caregiver Support denials, stipend tiers, or reassessments to the Board of Veterans' Appeals and CAVC after Beaudette v. McDonough (2024).
record_clues: A VHA Office of Integrated Veteran Care / Community Care denial letter citing 'Other Health Insurance (OHI),' '72-hour notification missed,' 'not an active VA user within 24 months,' or 'timely filing exceeded.'
Hospital (UB-04) or ground/air ambulance bills paired with a Medicare or private insurance Explanation of Benefits (EOB) showing unpaid 20% coinsurance.

A retroactive VA rating decision granting service connection or 100% Permanent & Total status effective BEFORE the date of an earlier denied civilian emergency room visit (unlocking 38 U.S.C. § 1728).
A VA Form 10-10CG Family Caregiver (PCAFC) denial, Tier 1 (62.5%) vs. Tier 2 (100% stipend) placement, or reassessment discharge notice under 38 C.F.R. Part 71.
important_cautions: Always screen 38 U.S.C. § 1728 before § 1725: if the emergency was for a service-connected condition (or an adjunct condition aggravating it), OR you were rated 100% Permanent & Total, OR you were in active Chapter 31 VR&E, § 1728 has a 2-year filing window (38 C.F.R. § 17.126), NO 24-month prior-VA-visit requirement, and reimburses deductibles, copayments, AND coinsurance. By contrast, under § 1725 (non-service-connected emergencies), VA reimburses percentage-based coinsurance (Wolfe; 88 FR 10835), while fixed copayments and deductibles remain barred by 38 U.S.C. § 1725(c)(4)(D).

Three different emergency clocks: do not let VA confuse the 72-hour notification rule for authorized Community Care network payment (38 C.F.R. § 17.4020(c)) with standalone reimbursement claims under § 1725 (90 days under 38 C.F.R. § 17.1004(d)) or § 1728 (2 years under 38 C.F.R. § 17.126).

PCAFC Caregiver rules & quarantined proposals: PCAFC regulations live in 38 C.F.R. Part 71 (NOT Community Care §§ 17.4000–17.4040), Legacy Cohort caregiver protections were extended through September 30, 2028 (90 FR 46477), and VA's December 6, 2024 PCAFC notice (89 FR 97404, RIN 2900-AR96) is a proposed, unfinalized rule—not enacted law. Likewise, VA's non-contracted ambulance fee cap rule (88 FR 10032) has been delayed until February 16, 2029 (89 FR 88888) and is not yet in effect.

Under George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e), later court rulings like Staab, Wolfe, Veteran Warriors, or Beaudette cannot be used to claim Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) against final decisions issued before those rulings.
questions_for_representative: Does my emergency hospital or ambulance bill qualify under 38 U.S.C. § 1728 (service-connected condition, 100% P&T status, or active Chapter 31 VR&E) rather than the stricter rules of 38 U.S.C. § 1725?

If my non-service-connected emergency bill falls under 38 U.S.C. § 1725, does my Explanation of Benefits show unpaid percentage-based coinsurance (reimbursable under Wolfe v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. § 17.1005) rather than a flat copayment or deductible?
Did VA wrongly deny my emergency claim for missing the 72-hour Community Care notice (38 C.F.R. § 17.4020(c)) when I filed timely under § 1728 or § 1725?

For our VA Form 10-10CG Family Caregiver (PCAFC) denial or stipend-tier dispute under 38 C.F.R. Part 71, should we file a Supplemental Claim with functional ADL/supervision evidence, a Higher-Level Review, or a Board appeal under Beaudette v. McDonough?

Waiting until AFTER a Ch. 31 case is closed / declared 'Rehabilitated' to request 38 C.F.R. § 21.282 Retroactive Induction (M28C.IV.C.2 requires an open active Ch. 31 case and alignment between past coursework and the approved IWRP vocational goal!)

Invoking Rudisill v. McDonough, 601 U.S. 294 (2024) for a veteran with only ONE single unbroken period of active service (single-period veterans switching from Ch. 30 to Ch. 33 remain bound by § 3327(d)(2)'s 36-month / remaining-entitlement cap!), or pleading Rudisill as CUE (§ 20.1403(e) / George bar) instead of filing VA Form 22-1995 for a Rudisill review

blocks.text: Chapter 31 Veteran Readiness and Employment (`VR&E`, `38 U.S.C. §§ 3100–3122`; `38 C.F.R. Part 21, Subpart A`) and multi-period GI Bill litigation (`38 U.S.C. chs. 30, 33 & § 3695`) deliver **three massive client and law-firm wins**: **(1)** **`38 C.F.R. § 21.282` Retroactive Inductions** reimbursing `$30,000–$150,000+` in past tuition/loans while restoring `36 months` of `Ch. 33` Post-9/11 GI Bill entitlement; **(2)** **VRC Vocational Infeasibility findings** simultaneously unlocking `24–30` months of `Ch. 31` Independent Living (`IL`) equipment/home modifications *and* serving as dispositive `38 C.F.R. § 4.16` `TDIU` proof; and **(3)** **`48-month` (`+12 months`) GI Bill restoration** under ***Rudisill v. McDonough*, `601 U.S. 294 (2024)`**.

*(Cross-references: Verbatim `§ 21.282` & related regulatory snapshots in [Verbatim CFR Snapshot: 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.159 (Duty to Assist & Medical Exams), 17.120, 17.1002–17.1005 & 17.4000–17.4020(c) (Emergency Care & Community Care 72-Hour Notice), Part 71 (PCAFC Caregivers) & §§ 21.40–21.282 (Chapter 31 VR&E & Retroactive Induction)](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.159-17.1002-17.4000-21.282-evidence-emergency-pcafc-vre); [AMA Lanes & BVA Litigation Manual](/docs/ama-lanes-and-bva-litigation-manual); [Evidence, Medical Exams & Lay Credibility Treatise](/docs/evidence-medical-exams-and-lay-credibility); [Attorney Fees (`§ 5904`) & `EAJA` Practice Treatise](/docs/attorney-fees-5904-and-eaja-practice); [`CAVC Appeal, EAJA & Fee Compliance Gate`](/checklists/cavc-appeal-eaja-and-fee-compliance-gate); [Playbook 04 (Unadjudicated `TDIU`, `§ 3.157(b)` & `SMC`)](/playbooks/04-unadjudicated-tdiu-informal-claims-smc); [Playbook 22 (`§§ 1725/1728` Emergency Care & `PCAFC`)](/playbooks/22-emergency-medical-reimbursement-1725-1728-and-pcafc); [Playbook 13 (Ancillary Grants — `SAH`, `Auto`, `DEA`)](/playbooks/13-ancillary-grants-sah-auto-clothing-dea-spina-bifida); [Playbook 17 (`§ 1151` Malpractice & `Ch. 31` Voc-Rehab Injuries)](/playbooks/17-section-1151-va-malpractice-and-ftca-interplay); [Playbook 20 (Offsets & `§ 5904(d)` Fee Base)](/playbooks/20-backpay-offsets-crdp-crsc-severance-recoupment); [Forms & Code-Sheet Lexicon](/docs/forms-and-codesheet-lexicon); and [Authority Verification Log](/docs/authority-verification-log)).*
1. Preconditions: CWINRS, Counseling Records (CER) & Multi-Tour DD-214 Triggers

VR&E maintains its own electronic case-management system (**`CWINRS` / `e-VA` Counseling & Evaluation Record [`CER`] folder**) that is **not always automatically uploaded into `VBMS`**! Submit a specific `FOIA/Privacy Act` demand for the complete `Chapter 31 CER / CWINRS` file and `Ch. 30/33` `TIMS` education folder whenever intake reveals:

items:
**Chapter 31 `VR&E` Forms & `CWINRS` Triggers:**
• **`VA Form 28-1900`** (*Application for Veteran Readiness and Employment*), **`VA Form 28-1902w`** (*Rehabilitation Needs Inventory*), **`VA Form 28-1902b`** (*Counseling Record — Narrative Report*, where the Vocational Rehabilitation Counselor [`VRC`] records `EH`, `SEH`, and **reasonable feasibility** findings!), and **`VA Form 28-8872`** (*Individualized Written Rehabilitation Plan [`IWRP`]* or *Individualized Independent Living Plan [`IILP`]*).
• **Retroactive Induction Financial Artifacts (`§ 21.282`):** Historical Rating Code Sheets showing a retroactive SC grant (`>= 10%` or `>= 20%`) overlapping prior college/vocational terms, university bursar itemized tuition/fee ledgers, bookstore/supply receipts, federal/private student loan disbursements, and `Ch. 33` / `Ch. 30` *Certificates of Eligibility (`COE`)* showing exhausted months.

***Rudisill* GI Bill Audit Triggers (`Ch. 30` + `Ch. 33`):**
• **Multiple `DD Form 214`s**—or a single `DD-214` whose **Block 18 (`Remarks`)** notes *"Immediate Reenlistment"* (`>= 2` separate qualifying active-duty periods, enlisted-to-officer commissioning, or active-duty tour + post-9/11 Reserve/Guard `Title 10` mobilization!), **`VA Form 22-1990` / `22-1995`**, and any VA Buffalo/Muskogee Regional Processing Office (`RPO`) `COE` capping `Ch. 33` at remaining `Ch. 30` months (`36-month` cap instead of `48 months`).

blocks.text: 2. Bitemporal Pathway Gate (Direct Application -> AMA Lanes -> CUE / *George* Bar)

rows: **`§ 21.282` Retroactive Induction (Cash Tuition Refund + `Ch. 33` GI Bill Restoration)**

**Direct Request to Assigned `VRC` (`M28C.IV.C.2`):** Submit itemized bursar ledgers, transcripts, and `COE` **while the `Ch. 31` `IWRP` case is actively open** (before `"Rehabilitated"` closure!). Appeal any VRC/VR&E Officer denial within `1 year` via `AMA HLR` (`20-0996`), `Supplemental` (`20-0995`), or `BVA` (`10182`).
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive:** Governed directly by `38 C.F.R. § 21.282` and `M28C.IV.C.2`—no CUE standard required on an active `Ch. 31` plan!

**Automatic VA Review** if last education decision was **on/after `Aug. 15, 2018`**; **Manual Filing on `VA Form 22-1995`** (*Request for Change of Program*, explicitly checking **`"Rudisill Review"`**) for pre-`Aug. 15, 2018` decisions or immediate enrollment + **`38 U.S.C. § 3031(i)`** delimiting-date extension (`remaining time + 90 days`)!

**Open-Claim Only (George-Restricted for CUE) for `CUE`:** Under *George v. McDonough*, `596 U.S. 740 (2022)` & `§ 20.1403(e)`, **do NOT file a CUE motion** on a pre-Apr. 16, 2024 RPO decision—file **`VA Form 22-1995`** for a restorative *Rudisill* review!
**Post-`Jan. 1, 2013` Discharge Wrongly Denied Under Repealed `12-Year` Bar (`38 U.S.C. § 3103(g)`)**
**`AMA HLR` (`20-0996`)** within `1 year`, `20-0995` Supplemental Claim, or **`RO CUE` (`§ 3.105(a)`)** on a post-Jan. 5, 2021 denial.
**CUE & Open-Claim Retroactive:** Violating the unambiguous statutory text of `Pub. L. 116-315, § 1025` (`38 U.S.C. § 3103(g)`) on a post-2021 decision is classic statutory CUE!

Cross-file in Compensation via `21-526EZ` / `20-0995` + `21-8940`—**AND** audit historical C-files under *Bell v. Derwinski*, `2 Vet. App. 611 (1992)` (constructive possession) + *Roberson* / `§ 3.156(b)` / *Hamill* ([Playbook 04](/playbooks/04-unadjudicated-tdiu-informal-claims-smc))!

**Mixed Retroactive & Prospective Scope:** Constructively possessed `Ch. 31` infeasibility notes trigger unadjudicated pending `TDIU` (*Roberson* pre-2015; *Hamill* post-Feb. 19, 2019) and reversible `§ 7104(d)(1)` BVA error on open appeals!

blocks.text: 3. Chapter 31 Entitlement, SEH & The Two-Era 12-Year Delimiting Gate (§§ 3102–3103)

items: **`>= 20%` Combined SC Rating (`§ 3102(1)`):** Requires an **Employment Handicap (`EH`, `§ 21.51`)**—an impairment of the veteran's ability to prepare for, obtain, or retain employment **consistent with his or her abilities, aptitudes, and interests** (`AAI`), to which SC disabilities *materially contribute*. *(Key Litigation Weapon: A veteran currently working a high-paying job that **aggravates** their SC spine/PTSD—or mismatches their `AAI`—**STILL HAS AN `EH`**! VRCs commit reversible error whenever they deny `Ch. 31` merely because the veteran is currently employed!)*

**`10%` SC Rating (`§ 3102(2)`), Pre-2013 `> 12-Year` Extension (`§ 3103(c)`), or `> 48-Month` Program Extension (`§ 3105(c)`):** Requires a **Serious Employment Handicap (`SEH`, `§ 21.52`)**—a **significant** impairment of ability to prepare for, obtain, or retain employment (`§ 21.52(b)` factors: neuropsychiatric symptoms, pattern of short-lived jobs/unemployment, inability to utilize prior occupational skills, need for special workplace accommodations).

blocks.text: B. The Two-Era 12-Year Delimiting Date Gate (38 U.S.C. § 3103)

rows: **`12-Year` Basic Period Applies:** Expires `12 years` after the *later* of active-duty separation or first VA notice of a compensable (`>= 10%`) SC rating (`§ 21.41(a)`).

**Mandatory `SEH` Bypass (`38 U.S.C. § 3103(c)`; `38 C.F.R. § 21.44`):** VA **must extend** eligibility past `12 years` whenever the veteran establishes a **Serious Employment Handicap (`SEH`, `§ 21.52`)** and has not been rehabilitated (or under `§ 3103(b)`/`§ 21.42` if a medical condition prevented timely participation)! Submit an independent vocational expert report proving `SEH`!

**Era 2: Discharged or Released *On or After* `January 1, 2013`** (**"Forever `VR&E`"** — **`Pub. L. 116-315, § 1025`**, `134 Stat. 4932, 4960`, enacted `Jan. 5, 2021`, adding **`38 U.S.C. § 3103(g)`**)
**`12-YEAR` BAR COMPLETELY ABOLISHED (`38 U.S.C. § 3103(g)`)!** Zero expiration date—lifetime `Ch. 31` eligibility with `>= 20%` SC + `EH` (or `10%` SC + `SEH`)!

**Stale `eCFR` Alert:** `38 C.F.R. §§ 21.41–21.44` still contain un-updated `12-year` regulatory text! Whenever a VRC mistakenly denies a post-`Jan. 1, 2013` veteran (`>= 20%` SC + `EH`) for lacking an `SEH` past 12 years, demand immediate `HLR` reversal under **`38 U.S.C. § 3103(g)`**!

blocks.text: 4. High-Dollar Retroactive Induction (38 C.F.R. § 21.282 & M28C.IV.C.2) & April 2021 § 3695 Sequence Rule
A. Three-Element Proof Contract for § 21.282 Retroactive Induction

Under verbatim [`38 C.F.R. § 21.282`](/cfr/modules/38-cfr-3.159-17.1002-17.4000-21.282-evidence-emergency-pcafc-vre) and **`M28C.IV.C.2`** (overhauled in **April 2021** to replace narrow legacy "retroactive reimbursements" with full `Ch. 33`/`Ch. 30` entitlement restoration), VA will retroactively induct a veteran into `Ch. 31` for past training periods when **all three elements** are met:

items: **Compensable SC Rating in Effect During the Past Terms (`§ 21.282(c)(1)–(2)`):** A `>= 20%` SC rating (or `10%` SC rating with `SEH`) was legally in effect during the past semesters—**including via a later retroactive VBA Compensation rating grant** whose effective date spans those past academic years!

**`EH` / `SEH` & Initial Evaluation Met (`§ 21.282(c)(3), (6)`):** The veteran met `§ 21.51` (`EH`) or `§ 21.52` (`SEH`) entitlement criteria during those past terms and has completed an initial `§ 21.50` evaluation.

**Coursework Aligns With the Approved `IWRP` Vocational Goal & Prior Benefits Reconciled (`§ 21.282(c)(4)–(5)`; `M28C.IV.C.2`):** The VRC determines that the past credits/courses were **reasonably needed to achieve the currently approved `IWRP` (`VA Form 28-8872`) vocational goal** (e.g., past B.S. credits funded by `Ch. 33` or student loans were mandatory prerequisites for the `Ch. 31`-approved M.S., J.D., CPA, or PA-C track!), with any overlapping VA education benefits reconciled (`§ 21.282(b), (c)(5)`).

blocks.text: B. Double Financial Payoff of § 21.282 + The April 1, 2021 § 3695 Sequence Rule

items: **Payoff 1 — Direct Lump-Sum Cash Reimbursement:** VA reimburses the veteran directly in cash for all verified past out-of-pocket **tuition, mandatory fees, required textbooks, and supplies**—**including tuition paid via federal or private student loans** (only non-repayable scholarships/Pell Grants are deducted!)—plus any positive **`Ch. 31` Subsistence Allowance differential**!

**Payoff 2 — Month-for-Month `Ch. 33` / `Ch. 30` GI Bill Restoration:** VA reclassifies past GI Bill semesters as `Ch. 31` training and **restores `100%` of the consumed `Ch. 33` Post-9/11 GI Bill (or `Ch. 30` MGIB) months back to the veteran's `COE`** (subject to accounting reconciliation between `Ch. 33` MHA and `Ch. 31` `P911SA` rates)!

**Mandatory Sequence Rule (`38 U.S.C. § 3695(b)`, VBA Policy eff. `April 1, 2021`):**
• **Use `Ch. 31` VR&E FIRST -> `Ch. 33` GI Bill SECOND:** Prior `Ch. 31` months **DO NOT COUNT** against `Ch. 33`! A veteran can complete a `36–48+` month `Ch. 31` degree and still keep **`36 full months` of untouched `Ch. 33` Post-9/11 GI Bill** for graduate school! *(Keep at least `1 day` of unexpired `Ch. 33` entitlement while in `Ch. 31` to get paid the higher `Ch. 33` `E-5 with dependents` BAH housing rate [`P911SA`, `38 U.S.C. § 3108(b)(4)`] instead of the lower statutory `Ch. 31` subsistence rate!)*
• **Use `Ch. 33` GI Bill FIRST -> `Ch. 31` VR&E SECOND:** Prior `Ch. 33` months **DO deduct** from the `48-month` `Ch. 31` cap (`48 - 36 = 12 months` left)—rescue these clients by either **(a)** securing a **`§ 21.282` Retroactive Induction** (wiping out prior `Ch. 33` usage!) or **(b)** proving **`SEH` under `38 U.S.C. § 3105(c)` & `38 C.F.R. § 21.78`** to extend `Ch. 31` beyond `48 months`!

blocks.text: 5. Independent Living (IL, § 3120 / § 21.160) & TDIU (§ 4.16) Litigation Synergy

Whenever a VRC issues a formal **Vocational Infeasibility Letter (`VA Form 28-1902b`)** finding under `38 U.S.C. § 3106(d)` and `38 C.F.R. §§ 21.53(d), 21.160` that achievement of a vocational goal is **not currently reasonably feasible** due to SC disabilities, execute **both prongs immediately**:

items:
**Prong 1 — Demand a `24-to-30-Month` `Ch. 31` Independent Living (`IILP`) Plan (`38 U.S.C. §§ 3105(d), 3120`; `38 C.F.R. §§ 21.160–21.162`):**
• Requires `SEH` + SC disabilities rendering vocational goals currently infeasible (`§ 21.160`).
• Funds up to **`24 months`** (extendable to **`30 months`** under `§ 3105(d)(1)`, and further for catastrophic post-9/11 injuries under `§ 3105(d)(2)`) of **home accessibility modifications** (ramps, widened doorways, roll-in showers—stacking alongside or bridging `Ch. 21` `SAH`/`SHA` grants in [Playbook 13](/playbooks/13-ancillary-grants-sah-auto-clothing-dea-spina-bifida)!), assistive computers, ergonomic/mobility devices, and specialized services enabling the veteran to live independently at home rather than in an institution. *(Note: `IILP` does **not** pay monthly `Ch. 31` subsistence allowance—making Prong 2 `TDIU` indispensable!)*

**Prong 2 — Weaponize the VRC Infeasibility Finding to Win `100%` `TDIU` (`38 C.F.R. § 4.16`):**
• **Constructive VA Possession (*Bell v. Derwinski*, `2 Vet. App. 611, 612–13 (1992)`):** Because VR&E is an operating administration component within VBA, a VA VRC's `28-1902b` infeasibility determination is **constructively part of the Compensation record** the moment it is created (triggering unadjudicated `TDIU` audits in [Playbook 04](/playbooks/04-unadjudicated-tdiu-informal-claims-smc))!
• **Reversible `38 U.S.C. § 7104(d)(1)` Board Error:** Under ***Moore v. Derwinski*, `1 Vet. App. 356, 359 (1991)`**, ***Gleicher v. Derwinski*, `2 Vet. App. 26, 28 (1991)`**, ***Beaty v. Brown*, `6 Vet. App. 532, 537–38 (1994)`**, ***Bowling v. Principi*, `15 Vet. App. 1, 6–10 (2001)`**, and ***Ray v. Wilkie*, `31 Vet. App. 58, 72–74 (2019)`**, the Board cannot rely on a medical C&P examiner's check-box assertion that a veteran can perform `"autonomous sedentary work"` while ignoring or failing to reconcile **VA's own vocational specialist (`VRC`) determination that even vocational retraining is infeasible due to SC disabilities**!

blocks.text: 6. *Rudisill v. McDonough*, 601 U.S. 294 (2024) (Ch. 30 + Ch. 33 48-Month GI Bill Restoration)

items:
**The `7–2` Supreme Court Holding (`601 U.S. 294`, Apr. 16, 2024, Jackson, J., *rev'g en banc* `55 F.4th 879 (Fed. Cir. 2022)`):**
• Veterans with **two or more separate, qualifying periods of active-duty service** who separately earned **both** Montgomery GI Bill (`38 U.S.C. ch. 30`, `36 months`) and Post-9/11 GI Bill (`38 U.S.C. ch. 33`, `36 months`) benefits are **NOT** forced to relinquish `Ch. 30` or accept `38 U.S.C. § 3327(d)(2)`'s remaining-months cap when switching to `Ch. 33` before exhausting `Ch. 30`!
• Instead, `§ 3327(d)(2)` governs **only** single-period veterans swapping `Ch. 30` for `Ch. 33`. Multi-period veterans are governed solely by **`38 U.S.C. § 3322(h)(1)`** (barring concurrent same-semester receipt) and **`38 U.S.C. § 3695(a)`**—meaning they may use `Ch. 30` and `Ch. 33` **in any order** up to the **`48-month` aggregate ceiling** (typically **`12 months` `Ch. 30` + `36 months` `Ch. 33`**, unlocking an extra **`12 months`** of tax-free tuition + `BAH` worth `$40,000–$120,000+`!).

**Post-*Rudisill* Filing & Delimiting-Date Recalculation Protocol:**
• **Verify Two Separate Qualifying Periods First:** Check all `DD-214`s (including `Block 18` *"Immediate Reenlistment"* entries on a single `DD-214`, enlisted-to-officer transitions, or active tour + post-9/11 Reserve/Guard `Title 10` call-up). **Kill-Switch:** A veteran with **only ONE single unbroken enlistment** who never reenlisted remains capped at `36 months` under `§ 3327(d)(2)`!
• **`Aug. 15, 2018` Automatic vs. `VA Form 22-1995` Manual Trigger:** VA automatically re-adjudicates files with an education claim decision **on or after `August 15, 2018`**. For decisions **before `August 15, 2018`** (or any client needing an expedited updated `COE`), file **`VA Form 22-1995`** online and explicitly select **`"Rudisill Review"`**.
• **Expired Delimiting-Date Rescue (`38 U.S.C. § 3031(i)`):** Because many pre-2013 veterans saw their `10-year` (`Ch. 30`) or `15-year` (`Ch. 33`) delimiting dates expire while VA enforced its unlawful `36-month` cap, VA applies **`38 U.S.C. § 3031(i)`** to issue a **new prospective expiration date** equal to the entitlement window remaining at the veteran's original forced election **plus `90 days`**!

blocks.text: 7. Invariants (Kill-Switches)

items: **Premature `Ch. 31` Case Closure:** Never let a VRC close an active `Ch. 31` file as `"Rehabilitated"` before submitting and adjudicating a **`38 C.F.R. § 21.282` Retroactive Induction** package (`M28C.IV.C.2`)!

**Zero-Day `Ch. 33` Exhaustion Trap (`38 U.S.C. § 3108(b)(4)`):** Always switch a veteran from `Ch. 33` into `Ch. 31` with **at least `1 day` of remaining `Ch. 33` entitlement** (or restore `Ch. 33` via `§ 21.282` / *Rudisill*!) so the veteran qualifies for the dramatically higher `Ch. 33`-equivalent **`P911SA` (`E-5 with dependents` BAH)** monthly housing rate throughout `Ch. 31`!

**Single-Period *Rudisill* Filing Error:** Never promise `48 months` under *Rudisill* without verifying at least **two separate qualifying periods of service** (`reenlistment` or `second active-duty call-up`)!

blocks.text: 8. Postconditions: Downstream Ancillaries & Structuring § 5904 + EAJA Recovery

items:
**Downstream Statutory Unlocks Triggered by `Ch. 31` Enrollment:**
• **`38 U.S.C. § 1728(a)(2)(C)` Full Emergency Medical Coverage ([Playbook 22](/playbooks/22-emergency-medical-reimbursement-1725-1728-and-pcafc)):** Active `Ch. 31` participation automatically unlocks `§ 1728` unauthorized emergency medical reimbursement (including `100%` of OHI deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance!) for *any* condition necessary to prevent interruption of the rehabilitation program!
• **`38 U.S.C. § 1151` Vocational-Rehabilitation Injury Protection ([Playbook 17](/playbooks/17-section-1151-va-malpractice-and-ftca-interplay)):** Any additional disability caused by `Ch. 31` training or rehabilitation (`38 C.F.R. § 3.358` / `§ 3.361`) is compensable "as if" service-connected!

**Firm Revenue Architecture (`EAJA` + `§ 5904` Contingency Back-Pay):**
• **CAVC `EAJA` Fees (`28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)`):** BVA denials of `Ch. 31` `SEH` extensions, `§ 21.282` Retroactive Inductions, `IILP` Independent Living plans, and *Rudisill* `Ch. 30/33` appeals generate full CAVC `EAJA` fee awards upon remand or reversal ([Attorney Fees & `EAJA` Treatise](/docs/attorney-fees-5904-and-eaja-practice)).
• **`§ 5904` Cash-Arrears & Companion `TDIU` Back-Pay:** Pair every `Ch. 31` representation with **(a)** a compliant `38 C.F.R. § 14.636(e)–(h)` fee clause covering lump-sum `§ 21.282` cash tuition/subsistence reimbursements actually paid to the veteran (filed within `30 days`), **AND (b)** a standard `20%` direct-pay `§ 5904(d)` Compensation agreement on the companion **`100%` `TDIU` (`§ 4.16`)** claim won via the VRC's `28-1902b` infeasibility narrative—always refunding the smaller fee to the veteran for any overlapping CAVC work under **`Pub. L. 102-572, § 506(c)`**!

veteranOverlay.plain_english_title: Chapter 31 VR&E ('Forever VR&E' & Retroactive Induction), Independent Living & Rudisill 48-Month GI Bill Rules
veteranOverlay.what_this_means: Chapter 31 Veteran Readiness and Employment (VR&E, 38 U.S.C. §§ 3100–3122) is one of VA's most powerful benefits—covering full tuition, books, equipment, subsistence stipends, or Independent Living home/assistive services for Veterans with a 20%+ disability rating and an Employment Handicap (or a 10% rating and a Serious Employment Handicap). Even better: (1) Congress abolished the old 12-year VR&E deadline for Veterans discharged on or after January 1, 2013 ('Forever VR&E,' 38 U.S.C. § 3103(g)), (2) Retroactive Induction (38 C.F.R. § 21.282) can restore Post-9/11 GI Bill months or reimburse prior out-of-pocket/student-loan tuition paid while a retroactive VA rating was pending, and (3) under the U.S. Supreme Court's 2024 decision in Rudisill v. McDonough, Veterans with multiple separate periods of qualifying service who earned both the Montgomery GI Bill (Chapter 30) and Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33) can access up to the combined 48-month cap rather than 36 months.
record_clues: A VA Form 28-1900 Chapter 31 denial citing '12-year eligibility period expired' (either for a post-January 1, 2013 discharge where no 12-year bar exists, or for an earlier discharge without properly evaluating a Serious Employment Handicap extension).

A Veteran currently in an open Chapter 31 VR&E program who previously used Post-9/11 GI Bill months or took out student loans for coursework matching their approved VR&E vocational goal during a period covered by a retroactive VA disability rating (38 C.F.R. § 21.282).

A VR&E counselor's written determination (VA Form 28-1902b) that employment is 'not currently reasonably feasible' due to service-connected disabilities—potent evidence supporting both Independent Living services (38 U.S.C. § 3120) and TDIU (38 C.F.R. § 4.16).

Multiple DD-214s (or DD-214 Block 18 'Immediate Reenlistment' remarks / Guard-Reserve Title 10 activations) showing two or more qualifying periods of active service for up to 48 total GI Bill months under Rudisill v. McDonough, 601 U.S. 294 (2024).
important_cautions: Sequence matters—use Chapter 31 VR&E BEFORE Chapter 33 GI Bill whenever possible: under VA's April 1, 2021 policy on 38 U.S.C. § 3695, months used in Chapter 31 VR&E FIRST do not deduct from your Post-9/11 GI Bill, whereas using Chapter 33 FIRST counts against initial Chapter 31 entitlement unless restored via Retroactive Induction (§ 21.282) or extended for a Serious Employment Handicap (§ 3105(c)).

Request Retroactive Induction BEFORE your VR&E case closes: VA's VR&E manual requires an open, active Chapter 31 case to process a § 21.282 Retroactive Induction request, and retroactive induction cannot precede the effective date of your qualifying Chapter 11 disability rating.

Rudisill requires TWO OR MORE qualifying periods of service: Veterans with only ONE single unbroken period of active service who relinquish Chapter 30 for Chapter 33 remain capped at 36 total months under 38 U.S.C. § 3327(d)(2). Also, pursue Rudisill restoration by filing VA Form 22-1995 for a Rudisill review—not a Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) motion (barred for judicial reinterpretations under George v. McDonough and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e)).

Do not let a VR&E counselor cite outdated 12-year text still printed in 38 C.F.R. §§ 21.41–21.44 if your last discharge or release from active service was on or after January 1, 2013—federal statute 38 U.S.C. § 3103(g) controls.
questions_for_representative: Since I was discharged on or after January 1, 2013 (or have a Serious Employment Handicap if discharged earlier), did VA wrongly deny my VA Form 28-1900 Chapter 31 application under the old 12-year rule?

While my Chapter 31 VR&E case is still open, do my past college courses align with my approved Individualized Written Rehabilitation Plan (IWRP) so I can request Retroactive Induction under 38 C.F.R. § 21.282 to restore GI Bill months or reimburse tuition?

If my VR&E counselor found that working is not currently reasonably feasible due to my service-connected disabilities, have we requested Independent Living services (38 C.F.R. § 21.160) AND submitted that letter in support of TDIU (38 C.F.R. § 4.16)?
Do my DD-214s or reenlistment contracts document at least two separate periods of qualifying service eligible for up to 48 months of combined GI Bill benefits under Rudisill v. McDonough?
